users.query:
Perhaps old age has tempered my expectations (I turned 40 last week), but I don't feel any sense of let down after 10+ hours of  roaming the streets of Chicago.  Given the enormous expectations gamers have expressed, it's easy to see why so man people have felt let down.  Expectation is the precursor to disappointment, sadly.  In that light, take these one and two star reviews with a grain of salt.  No, it's not perfect, but no game is.

There's been a lot of discussion about graphics.  To my eyes it's a gorgeous game, especially on the ps4.  It doesn't top InFamous Second Son, but it's still a beautiful rendition of Chicago.  A lot of the game mechanics appear to be borrowed from Ubisoft's stable of games:  hacking from Deus Ex, the cover system from Splinter Cell, etc., but they've all been integrated rather nicely.  I found the controls largely fluid, at least while on foot and during gun play. The voice acting was solid, the soundtrack acceptable, and there's simply a ton of stuff to do. 10 hours in and I haven't even completed a Act 1.

There are, however, plenty of mis-steps in my estimation.  Yes, the driving is atrocious.  Prepare to fishtail...everywhere.  The lack of customization is surprising, whether it be clothing, cars, or anything else.  I noticed little things, like the time not showing on your smart phone/profiler, which struck me as odd.  I had some major frame rate drops during the intro mission, too.  The missions can be very challenging, so prepare to die and fail a lot.

There's a great sense of paranoia running through Watch_Dogs, especially when other players can hack your game.  We live in a world where virtually no one appears to have any right to privacy:  the NSA, spying, hacking, data centers (I drive past the Bluffdale, UT data center everyday), wi-fi everywhere. There's no way to protect yourself.  Someone's always just a click away from digitally intruding on our lives.  In that regard, Watch_Dogs has plenty to say about modern society and the big, wide gray areas we all inhabit.

I've enjoyed this game a lot.  Give it a try.  Give in to the paranoia.

cands.text:
this game may have been 'ground breaking' in 2008.  in 2012, however, it's a complete and utter bore.  i'm not quite sure why so many people seem to love it.

as others have adequately stated, this isn't really a game.  it's a series movies occasionally interrupted by three minuntes of run-and-cover.  and geez, some of those cut scenes are obnoxiously long.  we're talking 15-20 minutes long.  sure, you can skip them, but 9 times out of 10, that only leads you to ANOTHER cut scene.  it seems the guys who made this 'game' want to be movie directors.  if that's the case, then go make movies.

also, there's a lot of juvenile humor - fart jokes and other scattalogical 'humor.'  and hey, let's futher pander to the teenage demographic buy selling copies of playboy at the in-game gun shop.  that makes sense.

the only good thing i can say about this game is that it graphically holds up pretty well.  for its age it looks a lot better than some games released in the last year.  but that's about it.

the entire experience smacks of self-indulgence:  look at our fancy cut scenes! look at our fancy ability to change camera angles during cut scenes!  we're so cinematic! look how awesome we are!  honestly, i don't care how awesome you think your cut scenes are if your game in boring to play.

in short, if you want a fun stealth game, pick up either of the batman games or deus ex: human revolution.  those are incredibly fun stealth games that, you know, have a point.  and by point i mean they let you actually play the game.

Uncharted 2 is one of my all-time favorite games.  I was a new Playstation owner when that game came out, so whenever I play it, it takes me back to the good old days.  Uncharted 3 was ok, I thought and not up to 2's standards.

With the PS4 now 3+ years old, I was excited to see what Naughty Dog would and could do for its star franchise with a beefier system. So, how's it fair?

Pretty good for the most part.  The graphics are stunning, as you would expect.  Lighting, character animations, etc.  Everything looks great.  The guns sounds are much better, too.  I'm glad they didn't just recycle sounds from the older games.

The story is pretty interesting.  We learn some things about Nathan Drake.  He's not who he's always claimed to be.  The cast of characters is solid.  Elena Rose and Nolan North should go down in history as the greatest voice acting duo for a married couple.  Their chemistry is excellent.  It's a bummer Chloe wasn't around this time.  She's a great character and a nice foil for Nathan.

My only issue with the game is the pacing.  The first 3 hours of the game I didn't much more than walk around and climb things.  I know platforming is a major part of the franchise, but there seemed to be an excessive amount of it this time around.  There seemed to be very long periods of nothing between the action.  I found myself thing, "let's get on with it already."  Also, way too much driving.  It was nice to have a car, but I felt I spent too much time just driving to the next checkpoint.  And what's with the sliding?  Too much of that, too.

But when U4 was firing on all cylinders, it was pure magic.  There are some truly excellent sequences that deliver the type of run-and-gun action we've come to expect from the franchise.  There was a lot of verticality we didn't get in previous games, which was nice.  The maps were a lot more open, allowing for various approaches and techniques to take out the baddies.  You can blast your way through, or take a more stealthy approach.

If this is the end of Nathan Drake, and I can't imagine it is, it's a fine send off.  If it isn't, I look forward to the next installment.

I really didn't have any expectation I fired up Murdered: Soul Suspect the other day (I got as part of the Square Enix 2 Humble Bundle, which is amazing).  I knew going in that I wasn't really a fan of "interactive storytelling" games as I don't believe they're really "games."  I thought it might be something like Alan Wake, which I wasn't that big of a fan of either.  I guess what I'm trying to say is that I though I'd give it a try, but I was pretty ambivalent about it all.

Well, turns out I'm pleasantly surprised by my experience with this game.  The set us is pretty simple:  find out who killed you and why.  Sure, it's more than that as there's a smattering of side missions, collectables, etc, but the main thrust is solving your own murder in the small town of Salem, which, of course, is appropriately spooky and populated by other dead folks and demons.  As expected, Murdered is about atmosphere.  The Unreal Engine is really showing it's age here.  It doesn't look all that great for a game released in 2014,  but there's a certain charm to it.  The voice acting is more than fine and while it's not really "scary," it is intriguing and I wanted to find out what happened and why..  That's a good thing.  It's one of those games where you look down at your watch and realize a couple of hours have passed without you even realizing it.

It does feel like more of a game than I was expecting.  Sure, most of the time you're analyzing clues, walking around crime scenes, possessing people and listening in on their thoughts (and occasionally "influencing" them), but I found it largely compelling, and kind of fun.  I don't believe you should pay for than a $10 for it, so if it gets below that price (which is currently is at Humble Bundle), than go for it.  Unfortunately, the early reviews probably sank Murdered chances for success, but don't let the so-called Professional Critics dissuade you from giving it a try.  Just don't expect heavy action, shooting, etc, etc.

as the popularity of multiplayer/on-line gaming continues to rise, it's no surprise that a game devoted solely to on-line finally became a reality. and as others have mentioned, it's a much needed game and hopefully a portent of things to come.

when i first started playing, i really didn't care for it very much.  the graphics weren't on par with COD, Killzone 2, or even BFBC 2. it's instantly noticeable.  they're not bad by any means, they should, however, be better.  secondly, the sound design is average best.  most of guns i've shot and i've heard shot sound like toy guns. considering the jaw-dropping sound design of BFBC2, i was disappointed.  lastly, it's incredibly frustrating to empty an entire clip into someone only to have the turn around and one-shot kill you.  i nearly threw my controller through the TV on a number of occassions. 'i shot that guy in the face 15 times! and he didn't die!!!' was a common shout coming out the basement.

but i perservered.  and i was rewarded.

thankfully, leveling up doesn't take to terribly long.  it's pretty quick actually.  i was able to add attachments to my guns, get better body armor, etc, etc, and most importantly, figured out how to shoot the enemy in the face and actually kill them. i realized that given the number of players on the battlefield, if you only had to shoot the enemy once or twice to kill them, the map would be a huge pile of bodies, all the time. therefore, you have to hit them MANY times for them to go down.  sure, it's still frustrating sometimes, but it is what it is.

the most rewarding aspect of MAG is the objective-based, teamwork mindset. and MAG definitely requires teamwork. objectives are clearly laid out and you get points for following orders and objectives. if you buy this game and don't have a headset, get one. without it the game is infinitely less rewarding. it's pretty exciting to head in to battle with your squad while your squad leader is telling you which way to go and from which side to flank. it's also great to bring buddies back to life with your magical blue mist aerosol medical kit [good move by the game developers to give more points for revives than for kills]. shouting a few 'hooras' to your teammates after winning a tough battle is great, as is hearing your platoon leader direct a string of expletives to a band of snipers hiding at the back of the map and not contributing.  speaking of poor teammates, yes, you can kick them off your squad by vote, even in the middle of the game. awesome.

i've read a lot of posts on the official MAG boards and it seems the developer, zipper, is very dedicated to this game. hopefully we'll get more maps [sorely needed], more character upgrades, and a MAG 2.

it's not a perfect game, but it's a fun and highly addictive game. and most importantly, it's an important, and needed, step in the great world of competitive, on-line gaming.  if you're not sure about it, rent it. buy it used, or borrow it from a friend. i'm pretty sure you'll end up buying it.

VALOR!

spec ops: the line isn't your average shooter.  and in this case, it's a good this.  granted, it's still a fairly linear affair - there are plenty of corridors, hallways, etc - but yager did something admirable by attempting, and largely succeeding, at making a story-driven game where choice and consequence are ever-present and one's man decent into madness is effective and compelling.  and yes, it's based on joseph conrad's "the heart of darkness" (as is coppola's "apocalypse now").

spec ops: the line is a 3rd-person, cover-based shooter that takes place in the weeks and months after a massive sandstorm has.  your squad is tasked with tracking down LT konrad (a nod to joseph conrad, of course), head of the 33rd infantry battalion. the battles take place all over dubai - in sandsweept highways, spacious skyscrapers, aquatic centers, and vacant building.  the gameplay, in my opinion, is very similar to the uncharted series.  even the guns sound relatively the same.  i did experience some issues with trying to take cover.  if you're not lined up perfectly, you go to cover or vault when you don't want to or vice-versa.  this results in a lot of frustrating and unnecessary deaths.  but for the most part the cover system works well, slow-motion head shots are satisfying, and the guns adequate if not spectacular.

the art design is gorgeous.  all of dubai in the distance is fuzzy and sort of hazy, adding to the sense of paranoia and dis-ease.  the color palette reminded me a lot of "enslaved: odyssey into the west." it really is gorgeous with soft blue, green and pink hues. the soundtrack is excellent for this kind of shooter. it's a toned down heavy metal, but it's never obnoxious and never feels like it interferes.

the voice acting is solid, though any game voiced by nolan north immediately makes me think i'm playing nathan drake.  but even so, he's is usual great self, as are christopher reid (of kid n' play fame) and omid abtahi as lugo and adams, respectively.

the only drawback, in my opinion, to this game is the six hour campaign.  it's great while it lasts, but it's over all too soon.  i've not played the multiplayer, so i can't comment on it. i wish developers would spend more time making longer campaigns and less time on multiplayer (can any really hope to out do CoD of battlefield at this point?).

if you can find spec ops: the line for under $20, i highly recommend you buy it.  it's a satisfying game and a strangely compelling journey that when it's over will have you asking more questions and wanting to play it again.

I'm glad to see games like this are making a comeback. Well, I'm not sure if they ever went away, but it's nice to see games that require human interaction.  As you already know, Mille Bornes is a classic card game.  We found that the kids younger than 10 weren't all that interested, but kids over 10 seem more engaged. We like that games don't take overly long to play. You can get a few games in after baths or homework.  But like I said, the best part is that is that you need to play with other people.  Recommended.

crysis 2 is a fantastic shooter. it's easily one of my favorite games.  i've played through the campaign seven or eight times now and it just never, ever gets stale. being able to choose how to play (stealthy or balls-to-wall), the incredible graphics (the lighting and scale are fantastic), and customizable weapons all contribute to the experience.  but part of what makes the gameplay so exceptional is the equally exceptional score.  simply put, this is amazing, amazing stuff.

there are so many beautiful moments in the score that it'd be impossible to cite them all, but as others have mentioned, 'morituri' is probably the score's standout moment.  it's elegant and heartbreakingly beautiful.  other great moments for me were 'battery park' and 'shadowzone.' again, just beautiful.  the orchestral parts are heavy on the violin, which is a nice juxtaposition to the game's environments and settings.  you'd expect a game with a guy in a supersuit to be a bit more bombastic than it is.  and even when boris slavov mixes some electronica into the orchestral arrangements, it just feels right.  it's never intrusive or over-the-top.  it's a perfect compliment to the struggle of man vs. machine as alcatraz, the protagonist, becomes one with the suit.

all in all, i can't praise this score enough. here's hoping mr. slavov helms the crysis 3 and homefront 2 scores.  those games will be all the better for it.

if you're new to the game score genre, some other great scores to check out are 'la noire,' 'red dead redemption,' the uncharted series, 'assassin's creed 2,' and 'skyrim.'  i wish game composers received the same accolades film composers do because they're very much equals, and often superior.

i'm freely admit i'm a  GI JOE fanboy, so keep that in mind when reading this review.

i really didn't know what to expect from this game. trailers aren't always indicative of actual gameplay and the videogame community seemed bound and determined to hate this game before it was even released and without even playing it, but i took a chance and bought it anyway. what can i say, i'm a fanboy.

i finished the campaign last night and here are my thoughts:

the good:

1) it's GI JOE!
2) there's a decent mix of old [duke, scarlett, snake eyes, heavy duty, ripcord, shipwreck/parrot] and new [sgt. flash, kamakura] characters, including one character built just for the game [agent helix]. i would have preferred a line up of classic joes, but the inclusion of the newer joes by no means lessens the game.  and being able to play the cobra characters is fun, too [firefly, destro, baroness]. kind of fun to play the baroness and scarlett side-by-side.
3) each joe's special moves are pretty fun.  i was fond of scarlett's homing arrows and beach head's motion-detected, homing mines. they're both very effective against the enemy. other's were less interesting, but fun all the same.
4) the 3rd person co-op mode is a lot more fun than COD's split screen.
5) the boss battles are challenging, but not inordinately so.
6) there are plenty of trophies to be won, even if most are pretty easy to achieve.
7) some have complained about the graphics -- but the story more embraces the cartoon than the larry hama-penned comics.  i didn't have any problems with the graphics.  they were suitable, colorful and fun.
8) i liked the storm shadow-trained red ninjas. kind of corny, but kind of cool.
9) good nostalgia factor.
10) buy it on amazon and you can unlock scarlett's classic uni.
11) accelerator suit mode!

the not-so-good:

1) the voice acting is horrendous.  i mean truly bad. if it were so-bad-it's-good, i'd be ok with it, but it's not.  the 'jokes' are lame. the characters flat. the dialogue is equally bad.
2) the player has no control over the camera. there were a few times i had no idea what i was shooting at until i took the most circuitious rout down a hallway just to find out. no good.
3) it's fairly short [but does offer some decent replay value].  there are three environments, six missions in each.
4) price point -- it's WAY overpriced for what you get. if you want to buy it, wait a few months until the price drops to $19.99 or buy it used.
5) somewhat repetitive game play.  this is a classic shooter, nothing more, nothing less.  the developers could have spent a bit more time and come up with some a more clever storyline, or more engaging missions, but like i said, it's a straight up duck & cover, run & gun shooter.
6) scarlett is cross-eyed in the cut scenes.  i don't know what that's all about, but that should have been fixed.

all in all, this is a game directed probably at the 11-15 year old crowd, but i had a good time with it. if you're looking for a sophisticated shooeter like COD:MW, or BioShock, this isn't it.  nor should it be.  but that doesn't make it a stupid or unworthy game.  just take it for what it is. having said that, if this were a $[...] game, i'd give it four stars.  but since it's overpriced, it's a solid three.

I really have no idea why this game is so compelling.  All you really do is drive a truck.  Sure, there are additional things to do like by garages, hire drivers, expand your fleet, etc, but this game is all about the driving.  And it does that really, really well.

For a game released in 2013, the graphics aren't really anything to write home about.  It looks like a PS3 game released in 2009.  It's not a bad thing, just a thing.  I assume this is because the developers are an independent studio without the resources of a developer with publisher backing.  Don't expect great textures, but again, you don't need them.

The driving is really, really fun.  I really don't know why.  You just drive.  Pick a job off the job board and drive.  All the jobs require you haul some specific product or resource from point A to point B.  You can gain extra XP by transporting fragile or explosive payloads.  You also have to drive carefully.  Failure to follow the rules of the road will result in penalties and/or fines.  You better turn your lights at night, signal when you turn and drive on the correct side of the road.  If you don't, you'll pay the price.

Honestly, it's not a game I can marathon because it's fairly repetitive; but I love sitting down for 30 minutes and completing 3-4 jobs, earning a little money and making sure my driving team is keeping busy.  I also think the menus could be a bit more friendly.  They can be tricky to navigate, in my opinion.

Yes, the game is playable on keyboard and XBox 360 controller, but I suspect a wheel is really the way to go.  I've not played with a wheel, but I'm doing just fine with a controller and some minor tweaking.

Kudos the developers for creating a compelling game.  It goes on sale fairly often, so pick it up and drive.

I've long since given up on Call of Duty multiplayer, so this review is based on the campaign and other features.

I loved the campaigns in Black Ops 1 and 2.  To me they were a lot of fun and I've played through them many times on PS3 and PC.  Given Treyarch's track record, I was excited to take another dive into this world.  Unfortunately, it's a trip I kind of regret.

Firstly, BO3 is set some 30 years after the events of BO2, so no Mason, Woods, etc.  There's only an quick reference to Raul Menendez, but other than that, this is pretty much a stand alone campaign.  And honestly, it's a pretty rote and boring campaign.  Sure, it's nice to look at, the guns feel beefy and weighty (a good thing!), the power core mechanic can be fun and interesting, but for the most part it's just run around a shoot people in the face because...reasons.  For all of our biotic abilities, there's very little we can do other than blast robots in various ways or become Faith from Mirror's Edge.  There's just absolutely nothing fun about it.

As for the story, I have no clue what it was about.  With a budget as big as EA/Activision must have (they just dropped billions to buy Candy Crush. Say what?!), surely they could find someone to craft a decent story.  Additionally, the could find decent voice actors.  The current crop of voice actors isn't "bad," per say (an average actor can only do so much with mediocre writing while and exceptional actor can do wonders for mediocre writing), but practically every line of dialogue comes from the Vin Diesel School of Acting, or slightly schizophrenic in how characters' tenor and temper dramatically shifts from one line to the next.  And it's not helped by the fact the dialogue is near "Homefront" level of bad.  Meathead 1 and 2 speak only in cliches and hyperbole.  Rinse, repeat.  I can't imagine what a first draft looked like if this is the finished product.  It's that bad.

What I found disappointing is that again there's not offline multiplayer progression.  That offline component is why I still play BO1 five years after it was released.  You can set up bot matches and it's all well and good, but without the allure of challenges and progression, it's just not that fun.

There's also some sort of time trial feature that's almost exactly like Mirror's Edge. I tried it.  It felt tedious.  You might like it.

Multiplayer: I didn't try it.

Zombies:  I didn't try it.  I'm sure other people can help you with that.

So, here's my theory about why these past few entries in the series haven't really resonated for me and perhaps you.  COD4 and MW2 and BO1/2, were at least in some way, based on real events:  Iraq, WW2, the Cold War, Vietnam, etc.  These are events that most of us are familiar with and for that reason, I think they resonate.  We can point to Stalingrad, Khe Sanh, etc, and say, "Ah, yes. I know these places."  I think this is the problem with "future war" settings, and particularly the campaigns for Ghosts, Advanced Warfare, and now BO3 is that they don't resonate because we have no frame of reference.  Sure, it might be exciting to be Adam Jensen in a shooter, but ultimately it feels a bit soulless.  I think the franchise would be well-advised to go back to WW1 or WW2.  Heck, be bold and go back to the Civil War.  More isn't always better.  In fact, it's often worse.

It seems the general public has grown a bit weary of the "future" when it comes to FPS's (to wit:  COD: AW, BO3, Titanfall), and especially the mantra of  "more is better" (I think most people would agree that Bad Company 2 was a vastly superior shooter to BF3 and BF4).

So, developers, take a cue - we want a fun campaign, good guns, good maps.  Less is more when it comes to features.  Fun is king!

Singularity, for the most part is a great game.  It came out in during a time when shooters had flooded the market.  Everyone was trying to capitalize on COD's success.  Some were more successful than others and Singularity should have probably made a bigger dent than it did. But that's what happens when you're trying to infiltrate a crowded market.

Why three stars?  There's one game-breaking sequence that has made me rage quite dozens of times.  I don't know what genius thought the sewer sequence when you're bombarded by these god-forsaken exploding ticks was a good idea.  It seriously the worst sequence of any game I have ever played - ever.  They come at you by the dozens, are somehow impervious to shotgun shells, slow your running and then kill you.  I honestly hated this part more than anything I have ever hated in a video game.  The first time I played this game, I died two dozen times before completely giving up on it for three or four years.  It was that terrible an experience.

It's a real shame because the rest of the game is fantastic.  It has some fun mechanics, good gunplay, fun story and while linear, is still a lot of fun.

And it was completely ruined by one stupid sequence.

i started off as a FPS guy [resistance, killzone2, COD, BFBC2, etc] and gradually moved to games like uncharted 2, assassin's creed, and red dead redemption.  i don't generally do RPGs [FF, dragon age, fallout 3= 'cos i find them to be a bit tedious.  so now you know what i like and play and if you like and play those kinds of games, hopefully this review will be helpful to you.

the premise is pretty straightforward - you're a contestant on a reality TV game show.  each episode as six races/challenges ranging from straight up races against seven other drivers, elimination races [where the last place driver is eliminated every 30 seconds or so], demolition races [avoiding power plays automatically triggered - gas tanks dropped from helicopters, exploding bridges, etc, or trailing and passing a semi dropping explosive barrels in your path], air strike/revenge [avoiding missles launched from a helicopter], and finally the elite race, in which you race against the cream of the crop.  the object is to collect credits to get new cars and then finish in the top 3 of the elite race to move to the next episode.  there are 12 episodes in all, so roughly 70 races.

the gimmick is to fill your power meter by drifting, drafting and jumping [air time]. the meter is split in three sections - the first two trigger power plays designed to take your opponents or open shortcuts on the track [little icons will appear above competitors to let you know when they're in the path of a power play.  if you fill your meter all the way, you can trigger multiple power plays for maximum damage, or trigger a route change by blowing up an air traffic control tower, or cargo ship, or power plant cooler.  consequently you have the potential of making each of the three laps in a given race different.  it's a neat trick. not all the races have route changes, however.

the cars look great and handle great.  i found drifting to be pretty easy once i figured it out.  the tracks don't usually vary much as most locations have three for four different tracks built into it.  the graphics are great, too. the colors are crisp, the explosions great. i didn't have any frame rate issues, either.  i haven't tried the online component yet [i'm kind of burned out of multiplayer after 500 hours of BFBC2], but i assume it's reasonably fun.

in short, i wasn't sure if i was going to like racing games.  i can unequivocally say that i love this one. some of the races are a bit easy and i don't think i ever had to run the same track more than 3 times to finally win, but that for me didn't detract from the enjoyment.

i was lucky to buy it via amazon.com for $19.99 and it's the best twenty bucks i've spent in the last month. highly recommended.

About five or six years ago Namco Bandai released this little gem of a game.  In the intervening years, people seem to refer to this game as a "hidden gem," "overlooked," etc.  All those descriptors are true.  It really is one of the most under appreciated games in recent memory.

I loved this game for many reasons, but above all, I loved it for the relationship between Monkey and Trip.  Andy Serkis and Lindsey Shaw are simply superb in this game.  In fact, Lindsey Shaw was so good that I'm really, really surprised she hasn't done more voice work since.  Maybe she's been approached and decided not to.  I dunno.  Whatever the case may be, I really wish she'd lend her talents more often.  She's great.

Andy Serkis, of course, is no slouch.  With a resume that includes Lord of the Rings and the upcoming Star Wars, his bona fides are beyond question and he's amazing in his role of Monkey.  For a big brute of a thing, Monkey is grounded in reality and very, very human.  This, of course, is thanks to Mr. Serkis.

I won't go into plot or gameplay, though I believe both are superb, because to do so would potentially rob you of the experience.  I will say, however, that its one of those games that stays with you long after you complete it.  It's a beautiful world filled with engaging, yet simplistic gameplay and anchored by two extraordinary actors.

If you've not played this yet, I highly recommend it.

Well, it's come to this.  On the 9th iteration of the Call of Duty is pretty much a shell of its former self.  What was once an exciting and innovate campaign, has become a slog of regurgitated ideas, uninspired level design, and painfully boring firefights.  Nowhere will you find anything as exciting as "Death from Above" or "All Ghillied Up."  I don't necessarily lay all the blame at the foot of IW or Raven or any of the developers involved with the game.  I blame the consumer just as much, if not more (including myself).

Let's talk about the campaign.  Yes, on the PS4, Call of Duty: Ghosts looks pretty good.  It's nowhere near AC IV or Killzone: Shadow Fall, but it's fine all the same.  My complaint is that there isn't a single mission in Ghosts that you haven't played before.  As each level came to a close, I could say, "yep, did that in MW or Black Ops or MW3."  As the campaign came to a close, I couldn't think of a single mission I wanted to replay.  I was kind of like, "that's it?"  I was disappointed.

I didn't find the story particularly compelling, even though it was written by a legitimate Hollywood screenwriter with a cabinet full of awards.  Though maybe that's the problem.  As is usually the case, the dialogue is mostly ham-fisted and delivered with all the enthusiasm of rectal exam.  It sounds like the voice actors are sitting in a studio reading lines.  Maybe they aren't, but i suspect they are.  Compare that to Naughty Dog games where they do motion capture with the voice actors actually acting our their parts.  The difference is night and day.

I don't know if Call of Duty can be saved.  I suppose it doesn't really matter. People will buy it regardless.  But, with the billions each release makes, I'd like to hope they'd fine new ways to innovate and improve.  Unfortunately, Activision seems content to rest on its laurels and release a new game every year with nothing more than a fresh coat of paint.

Vote with your wallets and don't buy another Call of Duty game.

In the age of ubiquitous electronic devices, it's nice to know that board games are still popular enough to be made and, you know, require and encourage human interaction.

I think this game is definitely designed for the 4-7 age group, especially with its bright colors and tactile pieces.  Older kids more accustomed to more sophisticated games and iPad/iPhone games will probably take a pass o this one.  It's definitely fun for the right age group and anything that encourage memory and recall is a-ok with me.

I don't know that "The Greatest Day Ever" has the staying power of Candyland, Chutes and Ladders, or Sorry!, but personally I think it's great that there are still new board games out there.  Here's hoping the trend continues.

Before heading the chance to review this game, I had no idea Melissa and Doug had ventured into board games.  It looks like it was a good decision because the kids had a lot of fun with it.

What we liked is the fact that since its a matching game, even the littler ones can play along.  No reading comprehension required.  The colors are bright and vivid and it's easy to play.  It's also a quick game, so no major time investment needed.  As others have noted, it might have been better had it been a four player game, but the the two player aspect gives a little more immediacy to it.  It's great for parent/child interaction.  It's prices right, too!

As I'd usually the case with M&D products, quality is top notch and built to last.  This is a great game to add to your collection.

Bad Company 2 is my favorite game.  I've got well over 1,000 hours and 50,000+ kills on it.  Battlefield 3 I didn't enjoy at all.  So much so I didn't even bother buying Battlefield 4 until I picked it up on PC for $5.  I was wiling to give Hardline a try, but after this, I'm done with the Battlefield franchise for good, which makes me sad.  But what can you do?

So, what were the problems?  Lag, lag, lag.  Wow.  The lag.  I played multiplayer for about 90 minutes and it was constant rubberbanding, teleporting, getting shot through closed elevators (not even joking - I died in an elevator about five seconds before the door even opened) and more insta-deaths than I can count.  I either had 100% health or 0% health.  No middle ground.  It didn't matter if I got shot in the arm, the leg, the toenail, the hair, the armpit, the stomach - one shot death.  Every. Single. Time.  I could empty an entire magazine in someone's back and they'd turn and kill me with 100% health.  Believe me, I have the video.  It makes playing absolutely zero fun.

On the positive side, the maps seems to be pretty well thought out, if a bit on the small side in some cases.  It seems like this time around EA/Visceral is going for a more frenetic, chaotic pace with eyes set on competitive tournaments. It's now a twitch shooter.  Run and gun and hope you see the other guy first.  That's all well and good, but part of the fun of Battlefield was that you had a nice balance of long range fights, CQC, and vehicles  (tanks, dune buggies, atvs, jets, choppers).  With Hardline you have cars which are taken down way too quickly and little birds.  And what bothered me the most is that there was no Rush game mode.  This will appeal to some people, I'm sure, but it just wasn't my cuppa, as it were.

As far as the campaign, well, it's pretty good.  Definitely a step up from BF3 and BF4, which were, ahem, terrible.  Kudos to Visceral for trying something new.  The dialogue's a bit stiff as it usually is in shooters, but for the most part it's well done.  Nice presentation, decent length, some replayability.  And anything with Kelly Hu is a-ok with me.  But BF is about the multiplayer and unfortunately for me it was a catastrophe.  Maybe others have had better experiences, but I'm glad I spent $3 on the redbox and not $60 retail.

**UPDATE**  I decided to give it another go tonight and it's even worse.  The hit detection is atrocious.  To wit:  I was shooting an enemy in the back as he was running away from me.  10-12 hit markers, minimum.  He turned and one-shot killed me in the arm.  I'm sorry, but this is just Call of Duty with 64 players.  There's no strategy, no planning, no teamwork, no nothing.  Just run and gun, horrible hit detection, horrible lag.

Crysis 2 is one of my favorite games of all-time, so I had big expectation for Crysis 3.  Does it live it?  Well, for the most part, but I have to admit that for all it's great parts, I also have some misgivings.

It's well known that Crysis is famous for its visuals.  That's certainly true here, though I did find the textures a little bit muddier than I was expecting.  Crysis 2's lighting was nothing short of magnificent, but I find it lacking here.  It may be due to the PS3's limitations, but it's disappointing, in my opinion.  What I do like, though, is that six of the seven levels in Crysis 3 are fairly large arenas of battle, giving you plenty of room to maneuver as you like and approach situations via multiple routes. You can pick the enemy off one by one or go in guns blazing. In this regard, it's much more like Crysis 1 than Crysis 2.  Developers seem to take less and less freedom from players these days, so this is a nice change and much appreciated.

The nanosuit is largely unchanged, but instead of collecting Ceph DNA to upgrade your suit, you'll find scattered throughout the levels nanosuit kits that will upgrade your lethality.  The SCAR is still the primary weapon, but there's a nice variety of guns and nice updates like varying ammo/arrow times (incendiary, explosive, etc).  Hacking has also been introduced to Crysis 3, but again, it's so incredibly easy that you wonder why it was added in the first place.  I give Crytek credit for trying to bring something to a shooter other than mindless "monster in the closet" shooting.  There are plenty of great battles to be had, but they don't come right away.  It takes a little while to get things going, but when they do, it's a great and fun shooter.

However, there are some issues that I need to address.  First and foremost is the very choppy frame rate.  I seem to be getting a lot stutter in this game.  I understand that CryEngine 3 is designed for high end PCs, but Crysis 2 ran infinitely smoother than this iteration.  It was almost to the point of distracting.  It very rarely runs smoothly (interesting enough, this isn't an issue in the multiplayer).  Secondly, it's unbelievably easy on regular setting.  I only died once, and that is when I fell off a ledge and neglected to engage the nanosuit's armor.  Using the bow gives you an unfair advantage because it doesn't drain energy.  You'll end up using the bow most of the time because it's basically shooting fish a barrel.  If you have any experience with FPSs, start on veteran mode.  Also, the AI is still a bit wonky - it's not unusual to see enemy Cell and Ceph running in place against a wall.  But hey, it  just makes them a little easier to take down.

And what of the multiplayer?  Well, it seems like it will have legs to last a while longer than, say, "Medal of Honor," "Homefront," "Resistance," and the like. There a good eight or nine game modes.  The most interesting, as others have mentioned, is Hunter mode.  It brings some real tension and frazzled nerves, but the rounds are over WAY to quickly.  The longest Hunter round I've played was about 75 seconds.  The traditional modes are all there - deathmatch, team deathmatch, etc, etc.  My biggest complaint with the multiplayer is that the bow is a one-shot kill.  This encourages campers to sit in the corner with invisibility and a bow.  It's frustrating that my 50 bullets do less damage than 1 arrow, even though I have a metal suit on.  But hey...

Lastly, I don't know what it with video game dialogue writers, but I've yet to play a shooter in which the majority of the principle players don't speak in "Bro."  I think developers severely underestimate their audience.  Crysis 3 has some major groaners.  It's a small criticism, but I'd like to see better dialogue.

All and all, I enjoyed this game a lot and recommend you buy it.  Given amazon's pricing history, this should go on sale for $39.99 in the near future.  At that point, it's a must buy.

Having playing Grid 1 and 2 (as well as Dirt 2 and 3 and F1 2012), I felt like I had a pretty good handle on Codemasters games and believed I had a reasonably good expectation of Grid Autosport.  When I was finally able to play the game (I bought the game and the season pass for less than half of Amazon's current price), I was pleasantly surprised by just how much I loved this game.  I expected to like it, but I absolutely loved it.

The driving in this game is very, very solid.  The cars uniformly handle beautiful.  Very minimal fishtailing.  In fact, it's the first racing game I've ever felt fully comfortable playing from the cockpit view.  I generally go 3rd person, but 1st person in this game is breathtaking.  I love watching the replays at the end of the race.  Many have commented on the graphics, but a free hi-res texture pack is available in the steam store.  The game looks like fantastic.  I didn't notice any issues on my moderately-powered 650Ti graphics card.  I had no screen tearing, stuttering frame rates or anything else for that matter.  Everything was super smooth.

I would personally rank this game up with Shift, NFS:Hot Pursuit and Dirt 2 as some of the racing games I've had the most fun with.

I'm probably in the minority when I say I loved the original Watch Dogs.  I've played it 3 times on the PS4 and once on the PS3.  I have it on my PC, but lack the hardware to run it smoothly.  Most people hated the protagonist, but I didn't mind him.  I loved the missions and the hacking, but hated the driving.

So, how does Watch Dogs 2 fare?  Pretty good!  San Francisco looks great.  It's a beautiful world and you'll recognize a lot of real world places.  It feels like a real world place, although far less populated than than in real life.  The protagonist this go around, Marcus, is much happier person than Aiden Pierce.  He laughs!  So that's new.

After about ten hours into it, I feel like I have a pretty decent handle on what's going on.  This game, it feels, is a lot more reliant on hacking, though the mission structure hasn't dramatically changed.  There's plenty of stuff to hack, too.  You'll come across plenty of opportunities to you use your phone, jumper or quadcopter to pick up research points (skill points), money drops, etc.  The driving is vastly improved, but it's still not great.  I noticed a bit of input lag.  There are no fixer contracts this time around, but you can be an Uber type driver and take people on various missions.  There are sailboat and off-road races, too.  It's a pretty robust world.

You trigger the missions from your cellphone.  There are main missions and side missions.  You can sort of pick which order you want to do them.  Talking with various people in the world will trigger various activities.  There's certainly a lot to do and collect and you'll probably spend 15-20 hours driving around taking photos and finding collectibles.

The AI is much more unreliable in this game.  Sometimes they see you, sometimes they don't.  You can get spotted by an AI and fail the misssion, restart it, do the exact same thing and the AI won't spot you.  The AI, somehow, can manage to spot a body on a rooftop even though there's no line of sight.  The stun guns sometimes permanently knocks people out, sometimes it puts them to sleep for a set period of time before they wake up.  I don't really know why that is, but its frustrating.  I restarted a hideout at least 20 times because the AI was all over the map.  I couldn't progress because the rules kept changing.  It was very frustrating.  I've gotten stuck in the world twice, too.  Once resulted in my death, the other in a hard restart.

So, all in all, it's a very fun game.  Likeable characters, plenty of ways to perform missions, lots of neat gadgets (you 3D print your gears and guns), a more diverse wardrobe (even though its strictly cosmetic, but its there) a beautiful city and plenty to do.  You can't ask for much more in a game than that.

I hope this helps!

three albums in and ed harcourt hasn't quite found his footing.  it's not that he hasn't written some memorable tracks, because he certainly has. rather he's yet to write a memorable album.  'strangers,' however, is ed's best work to date and the closest he's come to penning a truly memorable album.  it's a positive step forward from his last album 'from every sphere.'

'storm is coming' is a raucous opener and a signpost that this ed harcourt album is different from past efforts.  is it a hint of things to come? maybe. it's swirling guitars and hammering paino lend a nice climactic tone to the song. 'born in the 70's' is one of ed's poppier numbers, in a good way. it's funny outro gives a nice little middle finger to anyone who finds reason to hate on the hippy decade.  the album's other stand out track, 'loneliness' is another nice little pop nugget. loneliness isn't normally something to scream about, but it's nice to hear ed belt it out.

like ed's other albums, the listener gets the feeling he's just about either a) run out of ideas, or b) on the verge of clawing through to the surface of musical greatness.  it's simply (as if it were indeed simple) a matter of honing on the good stuff and getting rid of the not-so-good stuff.  there's a great album (and probably more than one) in ed's head, and given the rate at which he releases albums, we could only be a year or two away. let's hope so because ed's one heckuva talent.

this is my first time reading any john grisham novel.  i know, i know.  the guy is fairly ubiquitous these days, but i just never got around to it.  however, i'm a huge baseball fan and when i saw that he'd written a baseball-centric novel, i couldn't pass it up.

honestly, i don't really quite know what to think.  on the one hand, it's a somewhat interesting story that managed to keep my attention.  on the other hand, the writing was passable at best.  if i had to venture a guess, i'd say it's 6th grade level. the prose never sparkled, the characters seems right out of central casting, and the dialogue was ho-hum.  i can't remember once thinking, 'wow, that a great sentence/paragraph and/or exposition.'  it was just all so flat and superficial.

what bothered me most was that grisham appears to place greater stock in name-checking baseball's immortals than he does developing an interesting, thought-provoking story. every time the story diverts to the past, it just felt like he was trying to wow me with his baseball knowledge--and it felt very forced.

baseball is a fertile field to explore in literature.  there's an impressive library already devoted to it.  'calico joe' doesn't live up to its predecessors, but it makes for a decent beach read.

I'm not sure if my order got mixed up or not, but I received cashew pieces instead of whole cashews.  Not a big deal to me since I love cashews in any form -- whole, pieces, dust, whatever.  In fact, I had to give half the jar to my mother because I knew I'd eat the entire thing in about two days.

They tasted great - nice roast, nice flavor, very fresh.

This collection, along with the Ultimate Stealth Pack, is a terrific collection for anyone who's not played these games.  I've played  Sleeping Dogs on PC and PS3, Tomb Raider on PC and PS3, Just Cause on PC.

Sleeping Dogs - wow, what an underrated game.  Long story short, you're an undercover cop infiltrating the Triads.  The story is a but pulpy and gritty, but it's a lot of fun.  You can level up your cop and criminal abilities separately, which is great.  It's an open-world game with plenty of collectables and things to do - races, money stashes, hacking, side quests, even karaoke! The cars, I need to say, handle beautifully (so, so much better than GTA IV).  The one struggle I have is remember combos for all the kung-fu you learn throughout the game.  The voice acting is generally pretty good with some pretty well known actors and actresses taking lead roles.  It's a beautiful-looking game with great fighting, gun play and action.  This one will probably take you 15-20 hours to complete.  Longer if you go for all the collectables.

Tomb Raider - I had never played any of the previous TR iterations prior to this one, so I didn't really have any expectations or preconceived notions about what it should be.  But even had I, there's no escaping the fact this game is amazing.  First of all, Camilla Luddington is absolutely fantastic as Laura Craft - tough, vulnerable, daring and determined.  She's wonderful.  The game play is a blast.  The platforming is great.  The gun play is solid.  Lots of collectables to be had as well.  If you're a fan of the Uncharted series, TR is the perfect compliment.  Plan on 15+ hours on this one, more if you go for the collectables.  There's plenty of replay value here, too.

Just Cause 2 - this game, I admit, is pretty silly -- but in a good way.  It's completely over the top and completely ridiculous, but that's entirely the point.  JC2 is an action movie come to life: outrageous stunts (you'll have a lot of fun with the grapple hook), big guns and bigger explosions.  The world is vast and open and there's just so much to do by way of destruction.  Honestly, the story felt completely secondary to the action, but again, that's perfectly OK.  This game is pretty much as long as you want it to be, but plan on 40-50 hours.

For $10 a game, this is a great set of games to add to your collection.  Highly recommended.

Vegan Cooking for Dummies is truly the one stop instruction manual to conform your kitchen and your body to a healthy vegan oasis.  Many people have a negative preconceived connotation about vegan lifestyles such as the cost of organic food selections, the fear of foreign tastes or lack thereof, and the thought of always being hungry due to missing animal proteins.  Through reading Vegan Cooking for Dummies all of these negative ideas are wiped out and the reader is left with a sense of urgency to get started on their new lifestyle right away.

There are topics in the book that help the transition from non-vegan to a vegan.  These topics include how to transition your whole household to vegan as well as what natural supplements, through food, should be consumed to keep your body in top performance.  For example, there is a whole section within chapter two that discusses what calcium rich foods to eat to help maintain healthy bone structures instead of consuming dairy as well as what plants to eat for protein, Iron, Zinc, and vitamins B-12, B-2, and D.  Other topics include delicious recipes, how to change your outlook on grocery shopping, as well as changing your outlook on caffeine.  Many individuals are addicted to caffeine and the affect of it.  Through proper diet the need for caffeine will diminish and the same endorphins can be obtained through a large glass of fresh squeezed juice
.
The recipes are very simple to follow and even if you have never cooked a day in your life you can still make a fantastic meal.  Many of the same items can also be used throughout a lot of the recipes, such as nutritional yeast flakes and Bragg's Liquid Aminos, so the cost of groceries over time will decrease as items are bought in bulk.  Furthermore, the recipes in the book range from breakfast to dinner to hot drinks and condiments.  There will be something in there for your whole family to enjoy. A few favorites in my house are Pumpkin Pancakes, Green Smoothie, Ginger Soy Dressing,  7-Layer Dip, Eggless Salad Sandwich,  Jicama, Apple, Pineapple Salad with Avocado Dressing, Spinach Mushrooms, and Twice-Baked Sweet Potatoes.

I just realized that Geekerella is going to be part of a series! This was an amazing Cinderella retelling with a clear ending, so I'm excited to see where the story will go from here.

First of all, the cover for this book is gorgeous! I feel like it encompasses all the best parts of the story. Secondly, I loved the main characters. Elle, Darien and Sage were incredible and I would love to be their friend! Thirdly, the author has created a world within a world. Starfield has a fandom just like Star Wars and Star Trek, and I wish it was something that existed in our reality and not just a fictional one. Ashley Poston really delivers a story you can believe in. Also, she references Firefly! I flarking love that show and was royally pissed when it was cancelled. #bringbackfirefly

I was pretty mad at Elle a few times. She would frequently view situations as hopeless or acted like her dreams weren't worth fighting for. Sage, Darien, Cal--everyone else was quick to come to her defense, but she took the abuse because she felt like she deserved it. I would cringe whenever her stepmother or Chloe would verbally attack her, but she was their punching bag and allowed herself to be pummeled. I really wanted Elle to fight back.

When Chloe lies at the end, why doesn't anyone call her out on it?? It would have been so easy to check! Argh. (This isn't spoilery because Chloe lies a lot and is just a horrible person in general, but you'll know exactly what I mean when you get there...)

Despite Elle's inability to defend herself and what she believes in, I found this book to be incredibly enjoyable. I loved learning about Starfield while also watching Elle and Darien dance around each other for weeks. It was fun to know who they were to each other before they did, and I liked watching everything fall into place.

I feel like I should say more about this book, but I don't want to give too much away, so if you enjoy retellings, Cinderella, fanfiction, science fiction, cosplay, conventions, or just a fun story--this is definitely for you!

I like to wear fuzzy socks on a daily basis. I just love how they feel on my feet! I tend to get cold pretty easily, so socks like this help keep my toes from getting frostbite. These look and feel great, but they only reach to the top of my calf. I was expecting them to go over my knee. Maybe I have thick calves? I don't know. It's possible. I've never worn over-the-knee socks before, so I wasn't sure how they would fit. These will serve their purpose just fine, but I will look at larger/longer options in the future.

Red or pink... it doesn't really matter. I seriously doubt a child is going to care. It's more of a parent preference, I think. My son ended up with a pink castle, but it doesn't bother him at all. He jumped right inside and started playing with it. The color didn't matter, nor should it. It's a great product for an awesome price. Yes, instructions would have been nice, but it really wasn't all that hard to figure out. It's pretty self-explanatory if you look at it for more than two seconds.

It's also a lot bigger than I was expecting! Hooray for that. I am able to sit comfortably inside of it with my son, and we even have a little room to spare.

It worked well for a professional football game! I was able to fit enough stuff for myself and my kid, and they said it met all the specified requirements.

We purchased this about a year ago, and it's still holding up just fine! Normally, we have to buy a new shower curtain every year due to wear and tear, but I see nothing wrong with this one. It's interesting to look at, matches a lot of different things, and is educational for our son and visitors.
My husband needed a small bag to take to and from work... this is perfect!
It's simple and convenient to have around, but it snaps shut too easily! I've almost fallen a few times. I would not recommend this for children.
These buttons really are big, but they're perfect. We use them for sorting by color and shape, and also for a few math lessons. Who needs a universal remote when you can have universal buttons?

This is my first book by Amity Hope! The Rules of Rebellion was cute and managed to tackle a tough topic: bullying. In high school, Kylie's sister was body-shamed and bullied so intensely, she begged her parents to let her move in with an aunt. I liked that the author addressed such a serious issue, and brought attention to something so important.

As for the story itself, I started off incredibly confused. Kylie has three older siblings, three girlfriends with three boyfriends, and then Leo. Leo also has three or four older siblings, so it all became a bit too much. There were a lot of names being thrown around in the beginning, and I kept getting them mixed up. Was Meg dating Adam, Nate or Luke? Which guy lived out of town? Did he date Julia or Maddie? Wait, no... Maddie was one of the sisters...

I was almost finished with the book before I started to sort people out. It didn't help that the secondary characters (other than Allie) didn't get addressed very often. They were just fluff for the story and didn't really have any defining characteristics of their own. I think if they had been fleshed out a tad more, I wouldn't have felt so lost when names were tossed around.

I will admit to being super judgmental of Kylie's parents. They wanted to control every male aspect of their daughter's lives, and I felt like they went a little overboard. You can tell two teenagers to keep their hands in "safe places" until you are blue in the face, but you can't watch them forever. I'm pretty sure hands will wander, because that's what teenagers (and adults) do. I think parents should trust their kids, and be confident in their ability to make good decisions. They shouldn't be terrified to bring a love interest home with them.

However, Maddie's circumstances did warrant a little extra protectiveness, and I can see why her parents were on edge when it came to boys. It just sucked for all of Maddie's sisters.

I loved the idea of having a list to cross off. I am a big fan of lists and love how it feels when I complete one. It's like I've accomplished something spectacular! I wish I had made lists like this in high school, because I think it might have made me take a few more chances and try new things.

Leo was adorable, and I loved his projects. I think he and I would have gotten along smashingly, but only after I punched his dad in the face. He's sweet, considerate, but lacked the ability to say what was important. A little more honestly on both sides, and this book would have turned out a lot differently.

This review got away from me, so I guess I had more to say than I thought. I liked the book and thought it was fun, but I wasn't wowed by their story. There were too many things nagging at me while I read this, so it took away from my overall enjoyment.

I absolutely loved this book! I'm so happy it was the first book I finished in 2018! It was a great way to start the year, and it means I'm going to have very high standards for everything else I read. I hope they are all just as marvelous!

The entire book has an underlying sadness to it. The grief is palpable and constant. It shows you how different people choose to heal and manage their emotions, but it also shows you that the pain never completely leaves.

The characters are ridiculously relatable. I didn't feel like I was reading a fictional story. I felt like I was reliving someone's life experiences. It was really realistic and there were times I thought, "I do that, too!" Another awesome example: Matt reads Harry Potter and James Dashner. He also reads a romance book and isn't ashamed that he enjoyed it.

The relationship between Matt and Leah was sweet and sincere. They went through their rainbow of emotions, and it was beautiful to watch them come together. The newness of their feelings was light and refreshing, while their circumstances gave it a darker edge.

Leah also has the best Best Friend. I thought it was hilarious, and so very true, when the author included a bathroom scene with the two of them. They can have an entire conversation while taking turns peeing into a toilet, and it's not awkward or weird. It shows just how comfortable they are with each other, and it takes a long time to develop that kind of friendship and ease with another person.

There are literal laugh-out-loud moments, sweet and endearing moments, and moments when you want to take some of their pain away. It was a captivating, emotional, and hilarious story that I plan to read again and again.

This review is going to be for White Hot and Wildfire. I devoured these books (barely sleeping), and I'm not sure where one ended and the other began.

Words cannot express how much I love this series! It's seriously one of my all-time favorites. They are books that I will read again and again until I'm old and gray, and even then their audiobooks will be played at an insanely loud volume to compensate for my nearly nonexistent hearing.

I love the relationship Nevada and Conner have. He wants to protect her and keep her safe, but he isn't macho about it. He wants Nevada to be her own person and make choices without his influence. He knows that she is capable of defending herself (even if he wants to murder all of her enemies), so he doesn't try to keep her away from danger. He sees her as an equal, and I absolutely love that. They are repeatedly there for each other, and I adored the progression of their relationship. It was perfect.

The family dynamic in this series is incredible. I love the Baylor family and its many members. Grandma Frida is hysterical, and you know you'll laugh when she's around. There is a small age gap between some of the members, and I think Ilona does a wonderful job highlighting those differences. Teenagers are angsty and emotional. They're also prone to rash decisions and heightened feelings. Nevada is always concerned about what is best for them, but really they are all devoted to each other. They fight like family, but their love for each other is always there.

The villains are even superbly written. I don't think I had an issue with any character (except morally), because they were all detailed and driven. There was a reason behind everything, even if we don't know what those reasons are.

The magical aspect is phenomenal. It's new and refreshing, but also detailed and descriptive. I'm not confused by how it works, and you can tell the author put a lot of work into the why and how of it all.

Bonus: I never knew what was going to happen! If the characters were surprised, so was I. I didn't know anything before they did, and I wasn't able to guess things before they happened.

Magic, steamy romance, action, family, monsters, pacifist bears--this series has it all and more! If you haven't read the first book, Burn for Me, stop reading this right now and go find it!

The family dynamic in this series is incredible. I love the Baylor family and its many members. Grandma Frida is hysterical, and you know you'll laugh when she's around. There is a small age gap between some of the members, and I think Ilona does a wonderful job highlighting those differences. Teenagers are angsty and emotional. They're also prone to rash decisions and heightened feelings. Nevada is always concerned about what is best for them, but really they are all devoted to each other. They fight like family, but their love for each other is always there.

The villains are even superbly written. I don't think I had an issue with any character (except morally), because they were all detailed and driven. There was a reason behind everything, even if we don't know what those reasons are.

The magical aspect is phenomenal. It's new and refreshing, but also detailed and descriptive. I'm not confused by how it works, and you can tell the author put a lot of work into the why and how of it all.

Bonus: I never knew what was going to happen! If the characters were surprised, so was I. I didn't know anything before they did, and I wasn't able to guess things before they happened.

Magic, steamy romance, action, family, monsters, pacifist bears--this series has it all and more! If you haven't read the first book, Burn for Me, stop reading this right now and go find it!

I received an ARC from NetGalley in exchange for an honest review. My thoughts and opinions are my own.

I read this with my son and we both really enjoyed it! I love that the story allows Argyle Fox to make mistakes and learn from them. His mother cautions him in the beginning, but (like most children) he's determined to try despite her warning.

We're always telling our son to think about things. We ask a lot of questions to try and encourage him to find his own solutions. Why did that happen? Where does that come from? It's so fun to watch his little mind come up with answers. Mama Fox doesn't just give her son a solution, but tells him to think of one, which he eventually does.

I did have two minor issues with the book, but only because they didn't really make sense. One of the examples was a soccer ball being blown into a tree by the wind, but I've personally never experienced a spring breeze with such force. The other illustrations were more believable. The second thing was Argyle Fox wrapping his new idea and labeling it "Top Secret." The next page has him running outside with the package, but then it's open and he's using it, so why wrap it at all?

It's an incredibly cute story about a child that needed to fail in order to succeed.

I am remembering so clearly how he looked when he was eight, when he was eleven, when he was seventeen. Sawyer and I were only together for a few months before he left, but he was my golden boy for so long before that he would have taken the guts of me with him even if wed never been a couple at all.

I feel like I've lived Reena's entire life! The audiobook wasn't any longer than others I've listened to, but it still felt like I grew up with her. I loved the alternating chapters! The before and after really helped shaped the overall story. Obviously, we know Reena ended up pregnant and had a baby, but we simultaneously get to see what her life is like now, and the events that led up to that world-changing moment.

I didn't always agree with Reena or her decisions, but I did understand them. She was a young adult trying to find herself, and mistakes are a part of the process. I could look at some of her choices and think about how I would do things differently, but that's because I've already lived through that part of my life and learned from my mistakes.

I didn't love Sawyer, but I don't think I was supposed to either. He was a troubled teen with parental problems (that are never really explained), and he also struggles with addiction. His life is lacking substance, so he seems to just float from one place to the next. I understand now why he left, but I really wish he had never gotten involved with Reena. It was selfish and impulsive on his part.

On the other hand, Reena shouldn't have gotten involved with Sawyer. I don't have enough fingers to list the reasons why, but friends and family showing concern is a big one. Also, I've never seen someone so motivated to graduate and follow their dreams, so I was more than a little peeved when Sawyer became more important than school. He just kept taking things from her, slowly and without concern.

I didn't like how easy it was for Sawyer to wiggle himself back into her life in a major way, nor did I agree with how Reena treated those around her that had been there since his absence. I felt cheated. I know Reena deserved better than what she was getting, even if he seemed changed and understanding. He went about it the wrong way, and again she just let him without much consequence. I never understood her strong emotional attachment to him, other than the fact that he's her daughter's father and she has loved him since they were children. The middle (her actual relationship with him) was weird for me. What did he do to deserve so much from her?

I may have said, "I didn't," more than a few times, but I truly enjoyed this book. It was remarkably realistic, and I felt like their situation could have happened to anyone. While I didn't agree with a lot that happened, that doesn't mean it wasn't possible. The writing was beautiful, the secondary characters were prominent people within the story, and the narrator was captivating. I kept going back for more even when I wanted to yell at the characters for their stupidity. Life is about learning, and some lessons are harder than others.

cands.text: So this book was really good up until the point when they finally get their big romantic scene...and it turns out to read like a really bad porno. The story itself was engaging and suspenseful and I was connected to the characters from the beginning. I just couldn't believe it culminated in a sex scene that was neither romantic nor hot. The author works in a number of positions and acts but there is absolutely no emotion, no chemistry coming from the couple. The relationship had reflected a lot of sweetness and devotion up until then, to have it so tawdry just felt completely wrong. I wound up skimming the last few paragraphs of the lengthy scene in order to get back to the story, only to discover that that was it. The author leaves us with a bunch of questions and unresolved issues from the actual plot. The claim that this isn't a cliffhanger is definitely not true. It's also not an HEA but instead a HFN. To add insult to injury, the page count on my ereader reflected a long book but this was actually followed by a bonus book that bloated the length. I've had some other disappointment with Lisa Lace and this is the straw that broke the camels back; she's definitely off my reading list.

This is a sweet book with a very leisurely pace. While there is a bit of angst or sadness it doesn't have to do with the relationship to any great degree. This is more about the evolution of a relationship and the way it helps two men to flower under the other's love and care. The sex takes place completely off screen so, while they have a plenty of loving and enthusiastic sex, there is an extremely low heat factor to the story. Two things I found myself noticing and loving most were all the mentions of yummy baked goods and all the ways that Matthew's bear incorporated its characteristics into his human side. This is probably my least favorite of the three Baking Bears books so far (but this is out of an excellent series) but I still enjoyed it's warmth and sweetness.

Cute concept with a sweet, fairytale-like story. There's zero angst or dramatic tension, just a nice, cozy romance. Pretty much insta-lust/love with a fated mates concept that, in this case, seems to click for both shifter and human parties. Sex is doesn't dominate the book and is passionate but not kinky or erotica flavored. No cliffhanger but a set series setup. The one thing that bugged me is that the BBW aspect was harped on over and over. I know she's overweight; I don't need to keep hearing about it and how the guy is so okay with it that he loads her plate up with food for her when he thinks she didn't get enough (all of this is coming from someone who is BBW so I'm not coming from a place of prejudice). I will probably check out others on Kindle Unlimited at times when I'm looking for something light and quick.

There are so many comments on how sweet this book is--which is too true--but what most fail to mention is how very hot and sexy it is. All that stiff correctness can hide a lot of smoldering passion! So many, many sexy times. Now aside from that there was a great romance--frustrated by Ian's guilt and sense of propriety and duty. Nicky was a great character, the sort of laughing, funny, free-spirited person that everyone loves to be around; he certainly charmed me.  These two make such a contrasting couple but one that has a fiery spark of passion and love. Many have commented on the way the author worked around the problem of making an HEA for them during this historical period and, while I think I have some questions/reservations about it, I was pleased with it. As far as the historical details and such....I have never been a person who liked or read historicals but I was completely taken with this one. The details about the holiday, the games of the time, the conventions of speech and behavior. etc. were interesting but not overwhelming. I don't know enough to know if everything was accurate, but I strongly suspect that a lot of research went into it.  It was fun to read close to Christmas although their celebration is not Christmas the way we know it. There also a surprising amount of wit employed by both men and a secondary character Loews.  I love K.A. Mitchell's work but had held off reading this one because of the historical setting--boy am I glad that a friend changed my mind!

This is a great book that is technically paranormal but feels like a fantasy read too. One thing I liked was that there was much more romance than sex. The two are thinking sexy thoughts and dying to get at each other but so much action and adventure is happening that they (and the reader) are frustrated again and again (in a good way). Lachlan was a total hottie and completely captivated the heroine and me! Maggie is a strong character who, while sometimes really afraid, pushes through and takes things as they come with a brave, gutsy attitude. The high drama of fighting the dark sorcery of Rhurkan and the machinations of the Celtic gods was gripping. I like the system(s) of magic and the idea of the mage and dragon fusion. This book has got it all and was fast paced enough to keep me riveted. A warning though, the story doesn't end in this book. We get to a good jumping off point but there are several more books to go (which frustrated me because I didn't realize it until the end of the book). I can't wait to read the next one!

This was not one of the stronger books of the series to me. It's more like an adventure story than a her typical horror-favored books. While there are a lot of sacrifices and exclamations of love, the book feels somehow less romantic than others. There is certainly less sex in it--mostly by virtue of their travel situations. Although I feel silly saying it, it feels like the series is getting too "out there" with this and the last book. The series started in a horror vein with bits of paranormal thrown in (cool), then the sorcery part grew (okay, great), but now we have gods and fish people and ancient civilizations? Nope, not so much. There is also a LOT of sadness and angst to this story, which I didn't like. For the first time we get Griffins as narrator, alternating with Whyborne, and he is carrying around a lot of grief, anxiety, and pain. I also felt like the author did painstaking research on the gold rush, Alaska, and frontier/boom towns and then decided to devote a lot of the book to showing us all that; unlike her earlier historical details, this felt a little overwhelming. There is yet another magical threat (maybe) that comes into play that will probably lead into the next book. While disappointed in this one, I would never be able to get enough of the series and can't wait to read the next.

This was an enjoyable story but almost YA in feel. There is no real sex until the end, just pining, stolen kisses, and a bit of frotting. The storyline is a little muddled, there is almost too much going on. There were times that things seemed to be heading in one direction and then stopped. There were inexplicable illnesses, mysterious origins, a quest, and more. I kept wondering how a king could manage to be away so long. Despite all this, I was fond of the MCs and secondary characters. I thought that the concept of the Oracle and the priestess was cool and the wedding traditions were very original and charming. I would definitely read other works by this author and could easily see other stories set in this world--maybe the guard finds someone?
