I received a free copy of this book in exchange for a fair and honest review.
There were a lot of great things about this book: the characterization of Adrien and Jasper, the courtship between the two, and the sexy sequences. What disappointed me though, was the way that the end leaves some questions unanswered. This a Romeo and Juliet story in a town where the tiger and wolf shifters literally get along like cats and dogs. A lot is made of this with a big buildup and a number of confrontations. Working around the taboo has them finding secret ways to talk and meet and lets us see a real development to the relationship. Where I was disappointed was the ending. I felt like we were just getting to the point where there was going to be a dramatic crisis, a relationship obstacle or any number of kinks, twists, or turning points, but, instead, the story just wraps up quickly. I really enjoyed the story but just thought that there was going to be more. This is a standalone so I know my questions won't get answered and assume that the happy-for-now turns into a happily-ever-after.

The first thing that you need to know about the book is that the sexual assault at the beginning of the book is horribly graphic. Way more detailed than it had to be to tell the story. It made me feel ill. Beyond that the book, which had a good plot concept, had a lot of problems. I think the author had dreamed up a full and rich fantasy world and felt like she had to convey every element of that to the reader. The way this got done was information dumps to Jared. The POV was also wonky. We start out with Jared and Steve as POV characters and then suddenly include the POV of very minor characters like Silas. I also bristled at the way Steve operates as the alpha-to-be. At one point he decides that Jared needs to move and tells Jared casually that he has people packing Jared's stuff as they speak. What?! There is a lot of high-handed stuff like that going on. Added to all this were some editing errors. I put the book down out of frustration and went on to something else, intending to come back, then realized late that it was just languishing on my ereader and I wasn't motivated to go back to it. I'm interested enough that I would check out other things the author does but don't see myself heading back to this one. This was a 2.5 that I decided to round down to balance all the other glowing reviews.

Rating 2.5
This wasn't a bad book but it was just pretty surface. There was no character development and the heroine spent over half the book taking naps. There was a lot of sex but I found myself skimming for some reason. I was completely turned off when she's all gung-ho to have sex the morning after rough sex when she's all raw and sore and talks about how painful and pleasurable it is. Ugh. I also found his behavior to be very immature and rude--although it's supposed to be because he is so conflicted and tortured. Not sure whether I will give the next book in the series a look or not. Like I said, this wasn't bad but it didn't distinguish itself in any way, although it's length probably contributed to that.

Although there was nothing wrong with this book, it didn't hold my attention enough to finish it. I couldn't get past the idea of her fall in love and sleeping together after they'd known each other about 6 hours (most of which she'd been asleep). I get it from his point of view but from her's it just makes me roll my eyes and lose respect. I wasn't invested enough to follow through on the storyline.

Rating 2.5 I was disappointed in this after reading the first book, A Most Unusual Courtship. The first book had a nice bit of lightheartedness to it and this one--other than Daniel's occasional comments and cane jabs--didn't. It was also more focused on the mystery of the plagued than the romance. There really wasn't much romance, especially anything physical with the exception of a few kisses. The excuse that Gerald is old fashioned and wants to wait for the wedding wore thin then when we finally get to the wedding night almost nothing happens--they might as well have been teenagers! The secondary mystery of Gerald's stalker, while creepy, was not mysterious at all. However thing that frustrated me the most was how Gerald was portrayed almost as a female in the book. You would expect that Leo's mother, as the grand dame of the family to handle all the details of the ceremony. Instead Gerald meets with her endlessly about details like flowers and invitations. He even takes notes as Leo's mother gives him explanations of wedding traditions and customs. The ceremony itself also plays up his feminine role. Add to that the fact that Leo and Gerald's friend Harry are constantly having to protect him or rescue him from situations, and the strong and independent Gerald of the first book is gone. While I would read a third book in the series based on the first, this will not be a reread for me the way that one was.

There was so much that I liked about this story! I thought it was great the way we started with their friendship and the hidden crushing on each other, making the relationship the most important thing in an fantasy/sci-fi story that was great all on its own. Their feelings for each other and their shy and tentative behaviors are just so sweet! Aside from their budding romance (not without its perils and drama) is a bit of danger from within and without to spice up the tale. Shiloh's imagining of what it would be like to have the (sometimes) control over cold and yet have the bearer fully feel its effects is masterful. Love the clever way that she uses the symbolism of the power of cold!  I just wanted to hug Kyle. Oh and what about flighty and fabulous Travis! I would love for him to get a story as well. As is usual for Hollis this is a sweet/low heat/no sex storyThis refuge for people with strange powers seems a fertile source for a series--please, please!

This book did so many things right. First of all was the sweetness, the real romance, rather than just sex. The sex came in its own time, just right in the story, and was plenty sexy. The kid, Chloe, was actually cute without being sappy and acted like a real three year old and not overly precocious like so many stories do. The manny situation felt realistic, not invented for the sake of a story, and included the details of really caring for the child as well, showing rather than telling how Oliver feels for her and provides great care. The pregnancy labor has funny bits as well as those realistic bits like Oliver's response to offers of pain medication. For those who are animal people, there are lots of sweet animal moments. Unicorns. It's a warm picture of two men and one adorable girl becoming a real family. There are believable stumbling blocks in the relationship. Really it was just a great story. It was my first foray into the series and, while the connection to Cafe Om was very tenuous, I look forward to jumping in to read the others in the series.

Just as suspenseful and sexy as the first one. This is really a couple who has to fight for their relationship. This is a story that works very hard to pull them apart, putting their relationship into a crucible, even as external pressures because almost unbearable. I was so angry at Stephen's job yet understood why he had to stand by it, it like so many pieces of the story, seemed to have no good answer. The hits close to home are difficult--there isn't any drama-for-the-sake of drama in the book. The sex and sexual tension is even more explosive in this volume than before. I was so happy with where the book ended but very sad that it was the last of the full-length novels in the series (but don't miss the short stories in between, the other novels set in this same world, or the author's other books!). Great writing and storytelling!

I very nearly didn't finish this book since my mind kept drifting while reading. The pacing was extremely slow and the writing was wooden. I felt like the author was trying to pad his word count by going over the same points again and again. While the two men were supposed to be struggling with so much emotion, I never could feel it. I also felt they had no chemistry and continued to be awkward--and in Fian's case quite cold and standoffish--thoughout the story. The ending also gave us quite a cliffhanger, something sure to exacerbate both men's PTSD. There were just lots of loose ends, things that came up but were never seen to completion or addressed again. I really only kept going for the baby stuff. With a one month gestation there wasn't much to the mpreg piece besides the delivery (I forgot that this series has an anal delivery--OUCH!). The ending was quite sweet, the way that Kellan's usually are. There is obviously going to be another book in the entry but I don't see myself picking it up. Kellan has done other things that I have liked so this may just be an aberration.

This was a tough book to rate for me. I think that I have to divide it into rating the romance part, the mpreg part, and the police/mystery part. Sorry this is so long. Here goes:

The romance: The romance was very sweet. It started with a lot of thinking about each other and moved gently from there. This wasn't one of those books where the couple falls into bed right away or has nasty, sweaty sex when they do get together. I think part of this was probably the pregnancy (thank God because I hate pregnancy sex!), but another piece was just the tender way that the couple explored their relationship. While they were very attracted to each other from the start and felt right with referring to each other as "my alpha" and "my omega" very soon, their entire relationship was always more about the feelings and emotions than the passion. I found that quite endearing. So lots of points for the loving, fairly low angst/drama romance.

The mpreg: For those who want a very realistic, detailed pregnancy experience, this is the story for you. There are a lot 0f exhausted days, back aches, and food restrictions (Pete jokes that he plans to take a taxi straight from the hospital to a sushi restaurant). The birth is a kind of blow by blow of pain, epidurals, embarrassment, and bodily fluids. There is also quite a bit about post-partum challenges too. I feel like poor Aiden must have bought every What To Expect When You're Expecting kind of book and sat there with a notebook and highlighter--or possibly he has his own posse of experienced moms to fill him in on stuff. I think that those that have given birth will find this the piece (a really big piece) of the book really great since it reflects their own moving experience. I've never had kids so I was a little overwhelmed in parts, even though I usually enjoy mpreg very much.

The police/mystery: Sigh. This is where it all fell apart for me. There were so many unbelievable sentiments and occurrences that I felt the credibility was severely strained. What was up with the ramen, how did he even know about the pregnancy? Why in world would you keep that teddy bear?! At one point Pete is passed a note relating to the crime in a restaurant and gives it to Ozzy when they catch up outside. Ozzy reads it then thinks 'well I'm off tonight' and doesn't even go back in the restaurant to try and catch and interrogate the guy. What cop does that? There were several procedural things that didn't ring true to me but perhaps Aiden had done research or sounded things out with an expert and it was all in line with reality. I figured out the mystery ahead of the cops and it wasn't that complicated. I do have to say that I like the idea of the cold case unit for a series and I really loved the characters and banter of the group.

Both Pete and Ozzy are great characters. They really come across as real people with good hearts and loving natures. I like how the author built Pete a solid background as an award winning photographer who was used to danger because of his job. The drama surrounding the families was a little over the top (especially given Pete's good financial situation).

So for me it was a mixed bag, somewhere between an "okay" and a "like" because the cop part pulled it down. The writing is good and the characterization is strong so no problems there. It is completely possible to read this without having read the first in the series (I did as a matter of fact). I think it's worth it for fans to give it a try, especially if you really want an in-depth pregnancy story.

Rating 3.5
There were a number of good things about this book but some others that didn't do it for me. I thought that the love came WAY too soon. I'm also not crazy about bosses who immediately become lovers--especially when they were pretty much hiring you because they were hot for you already. On the plus side...The action/suspense elements were well done and I would love to know more about what's going on there. The mysteries about the other brothers are intriguing and there are good setups there for further books in the series. The sex was particularly athletic. I'm not dying for the next book in the series but may pick it up when I'm in between reads.

Not sure that I like the shift to a vampire mating/beloved story although there looks to be another one set up for the next book. I was a little more bothered by the breakneck speed of the relationship this time. That has always been a feature of this series but I found it more irksome in that, hello, vampires! Scott asks no questions including whether Hugo intends to turn him into a vampire, make him a slave, or harm him in any way. Hugo is way over the top possessive and smothering but Scott seems to just accept it. While I love a good rescue story, this felt a little creepy to me. Again, I may be feeling this way because we are dealing with vampires. In addition to these concerns, though, are the problems with the editing. This was worse than we've had in past entries in the series (it's a consistent problem with Stetke's writing). Run-on sentences, misspellings, and an almost complete lack of commas kept pulling me out of the flow of the story. I usually give these and Stetke's other works higher ratings and I will still eagerly await the next installment. Please, no more vampires--we could maybe mention the next union, hinted at here, in passing in the next werewolf book?

I didn't bother to finish this story that had a number of WTF moments. One thing that kept aggravating me was that no one seemed to have phones. Bobby seems to have no way to contact Jonathan except to wait for him to knock on his window. He knows the guy's parents so why not call them and get Jonathan's number? There is a moment where Bobby should have called 911 or some other form of help but, again, no mention of a having a cell or landline. He fails to keep in touch with his parents because, obviously, he has no phone to call or text them. Ridiculous. I also had to roll my eyes when the unborn baby was able to communicate with Bobby. Really? Jonathan was also a big douche, unwilling to commit and coming for booty calls. There were also many inconsistencies and some plot holes as well. Again, it wasn't even worth finishing.

Having read book 3 first, it was nice to go back and get the quiet healer's love story. In such a short piece there wasn't time for a lot of character development but her backstory was was done. I had less a sense of Narath; he seemed a stock Brion character to act as the hero. It was nice to see Diego interacting with his friends, acting outside his role as the fierce Commander. One niggling thing that bothered me is the way they ran off to have sex/binding when he'd just brought a shipment of wounded warriors to the ship for healing--I guess she must have had particularly gifted assistants or other healers on the ship? This was an enjoyable read but the true must reads are the longer works in the series.

Short, hot, and fun! It's about the electric moment when two men who've been crushing on each other for months (one a wolf shifter) realize that they're mates. The explosive passion of two men completely in sync with each other is done really well. The club setting adds to the ambiance with the kind of hot dancing foreplay and grinding that's totally yummy. The bondage part alluded to in the blurb is very minimal (which I appreciated because that's not my thing). I would like more of the story after what is just their first night together. I've read the second in the series and it overlaps rather than expands on this story (and it's also very good). A great quick, naughty read.

In terms of the plot and the steam, this book was right on target. Where it lost me though was Toby. Toby was a poor friend--the type that only calls when he's had a fight or broken up with whoever his current boyfriend is--to Jason, who seemed very caring and steadfast in return. Toby also seemed to be the type get in a snit if he was not getting his way at all. He snapped at Jason over nothing and whines to Dalton a number of times. As a couple....everything is dialed up to 10 with them. They are all over each other, are in agony when apart, and declare their love and devotion constantly. There is definitely insta-lust and, while not insta-love, the intense feelings come pretty fast. I think if you like fated mates stories then this will really appeal. The pregnancy lore and logistics seemed a little shaky but there is a sweet post-cesarean scene to round out the mpreg part. For those who like it, there is a whole chapter devoted to "pregnancy sex yes or no?". There is a danger/drama piece inserted to add tension to the story, since there is no relationship conflict and the story needed something. It felt a little shaky to me and we never really got any real explanation or resolution of it. Altogether, this was a quick read with some good heat and lots of fated mates feel, followed by a pregnancy experience with the backaches, swollen ankles, and pregnancy sex thrown in. I think I would read another in the series, especially if it was about poor long-suffering Jason and his crush Spenser. I have voluntarily reviewed an Advance Reader Copy of this book.

This was a hard book to rate. It had many of the trope urban fantasy/paranormal elements that I like: unusual magic creature as main character, detective/mystery elements, a crazy deadline, and a main character who presses on despite exhaustion and overwhelming stresses. Unfortunately, Kalos "Kal" was almost incompetent. He was, by his own admission, disorganized and fond of overly simple/linear thinking. He has resources that he wastes, can't locate, or forgets constantly. His backstory is never fully explained (maybe it's meant to be teased out over the course of the series?) and that becomes very annoying. There are too many players and bad guys to the point that they all become red herrings. The magic didn't make sense to me and we are never given proper worldbuilding. The role of Nadia and her relationship to Kal was also weird. He acts like an idiot or a jerk around her but she keeps coming back to him for very important things like the meaning of her mother's necklace. I wouldn't give something that was an heirloom, the only key to my mother, and something you think may be magical to my sort of shady neighbor. The mystery piece of the story was hard to follow for me and the final interaction with the party responsible made no sense at all. Many threads are still unresolved and I can only assume that they will wrap up in future installments. On the plus side, I must say that I very much liked Argos and Gunner, secondary characters, and would have loved to see more of them. There was also something interesting about Kal, even though I often lacked respect for him and wondered how he'd managed to recover all the artifacts that he had. I'm not sure whether I will follow up on the next book in the series. I have a lot of urban fantasy waiting on my ereader and others are calling to me more than this one. I may circle back to the series later with the hopes that it becomes stronger, with a more firmly established and competent lead, and better worldbuilding.

users.query: Material is soft, good color, fits a 6 yr old very well, but the material was a little thinner than expected.

cands.text:
Really well made, much better than the usual quality we've come to expect from mass produced costumes. However, that being said, it's still inferior quality when compared to regular kids clothes from Old Navy or Target. The material feels the equivalent of a 50/50 cotton/polyester mix.  The color is as vibrant as seen on your computer screen, and we were very happy with this costume.

Our 2 yr old is at the 50th percentile for height (34 inches) and weight, and this 2T sized dress was just a tad too big around the middle, but length was perfect.  It made layering clothes under it easy.
Very comfortable and soft, but be aware that the shoe is very wide.  My wife said she felt like she was wearing a very soft and cushy clown shoe.  Hooray for Amazon's great return policy

Well constructed, fits as expected, color looks great.
The shoelaces are sturdy and stay tied.
My 5 year graduated to "tie-shoes" from velcro shoes when he started Kindergarten and he loves them.
You never know how shoes will fit buying online, but with Amazon offering free return shipping, there's no risk.

Wish teaching him how to tie his shoes was as easy as ordering from Amazon.

I first bought this for my son when he was 6 yrs old and thought it was a good fit. When he chewed through the first one over a span of 2.5 yrs, I bought another "youth" size as a replacement. However, when I saw this in the package, it first looked too small to fit my now 9 yr olds mouth.  But it actually is a perfect fit.

Molds well, my son likes the blue color, and the optional strap is a nice bonus. Just hoping it will survive my son chewing on it when he's on the sidelines and not actively sparring.

I first bought this for my son when he was 6 yrs old and thought it was a good fit. When he chewed through the first one over a span of 2.5 yrs, I bought another "youth" size as a replacement. However, when I saw this in the package, it first looked too small to fit my now 9 yr olds mouth.  But it actually is a perfect fit.

Molds well, my son likes the blue color, and the optional strap is a nice bonus. Just hoping it will survive my son chewing on it when he's on the sidelines and not actively sparring.

Shoes are too cute.  Fits as expected.  Hard to ask a 3 year old how comfortable shoes are or about the arch support, but she wears them without complaining all day, so guess that's about as good of a recommendation you can expect from a toddler.

They're easy to put on and off, and the Velcro stays in place.

Pros:
Well crafted, good quality materials
Fits a 6 year old well with room to grow (4 ft tall, about 45 pounds)
Usable pockets in vest

Cons:
None

Summary:
Overall, a very well made costume with quality materials and stitching.  The shirt/vest gets constant use from my son, his friends, and his little sister and has held up well over the past 9 months with no tearing or fraying.  The foam sword has also held up surprisingly well, despite my son using it to beat pretty much everything in the house, including me.  Money well spent.
For the little kid that loves construction and building, this is perfect.  Good Lego quality toy with well designed and durable pieces.
Nice background noise.  It's consistent and even toned, no weird volume issues or tonal variations.  Good for putting infants to sleep!  And the track is 70 minutes long.  Not bad for under a dollar.

Pros:
- Star Wars obsessed 5-year old son LOVES it
- Good quality cotton, very soft

Cons:
- none

Summary:
It boggles my mind that a movie made in the late 70's could have the appeal it does to kids in this modern age. Another mystery is how every other main actor's careers took off except for Mark Hamill... Anyway, my 5 yr old son is all things Star Wars, and he loves his sheets and pillow.  The cotton is very soft, and woven very well.  It's better quality than the usual stuff you see at Wxxmart or Txxget.  The color is nice and neutral.  It fits a deep twin mattress very well, and we're very happy with the quality of the sheet set.  We bought the matching comforter and that is also very well made.

The padded back strap prevents blisters
The footpad is nicely padded as well
The velcro front strap stays put, works well, and hasn't lost the grippiness
Dries out well when it gets wet... which if your toddler is like mine and loves Peppa Pig, always magically finds "muddy puddles" to stomp around in
Looks super cute

The padded back strap prevents blisters

The velcro front strap stays put, works well, and hasn't lost the grippiness
Dries out well when it gets wet... which if your toddler is like mine and loves Peppa Pig, always magically finds "muddy puddles" to stomp around in
Looks super cute

Sturdy, easy to fold, excellent color, holds a large suitcase without collapsing or wobbling around.  The back bar doesn't do a whole lot, but does prevent our guests from ramming their suitcase into the wall.

I bought this after my 4 year old dropped our first iPad and cracked the glass.  I needed something more than the faux-leather case that I was previously using because that obviously did nothing.  I figured if this case meets military specs, it hopefully can withstand the force of a 4-year old.

Pros:
1. Looks durable.  Feels durable.
2. The iPad is surrounded 360 degrees.
3. The screen protector (part of the case) isn't that obtrusive and not really noticeable.  I haven't noticed any problems with the iPad's touch response.
4. My iPad has survived a 4.5 foot drop onto concrete while in this case.

Cons:
1. The flimsy stand, which looks like an after thought, lasted all of one week before it broke off.
2. The case is relatively heavy, and pretty much doubles the weight of the iPad
3. The various covers are annoying (designed to cover the camera, the charger port, the speaker port, and the headphone port).  I just cut them all off.

Summary:
Like most parents, I bought the iPad for me, but it has since been usurped by my 4-year old son.  After he shattered the screen on the first one, I decided to invest a bit more in a case so that I didn't have to pay the ridiculous amount of money Applecare wants for warranty service if my son managed to destroy another iPad.  After reading about every kid-proof case out there, I settled on this one, and am quite happy with it.  This case would have gotten 5 stars had the stand lasted more than a week before snapping in two.  It really is the Achilles heel of the whoel thing.  While the rest of the case is designed to withstand a parachute jump into a war zone, the stand is a thin piece of brittle plastic that clips onto the case.  Two days ago, my son dropped it from the SUV onto the garage floor and the iPad just bounced a couple times.  Definitely worth the money.

And unlike other kid-proof cases out there in the market, I can keep my iPad in this case and just take it to work.  I can pull this iPad out of my briefcase at work and not look ridiculous because my iPad is surrounded by 8 inches of foam, or it looks like a little toy, or any number of crazy contraptions out there.

So far has survived 9 month's worth of daily abuse being attached to a little kid's backpack without falling apart.  There's no better endorsement than that.

Good heavy duty rubbery plastic material.

Well constructed.  Good value for the price.  The last one I had lasted 3 years with year round use in the North Carolina sun, rain, and the occasional snow storm, before the fabric just disintegrated.

What is it with little boys and the fascination with yellow school buses?

This bus is well made, durable, cute, and rolls extremely well.  Paint has held up and the wood is very forgiving of the punishment it gets from my son.
The screen protector is easy to put on, but I find that it rips and tears much easier than other brands that I've used.

Fits very well and is very comfortable.  I'm 5'11", 190 lbs.  The shirt is loose enough but cut close to the body so that it doesn't look like I'm wearing a wetsuit. There isn't so much fabric that it doesn't "sail" around in the pool either.  Dries quick.  Definitely provides UV protection and I don't put any sunscreen on my chest/abdomen when wearing this shirt and I haven't suffered any sunburn yet.  The material is a little thicker than the rashguard I bought from Target and this looks more durable at a lower price!  The stitching is nice and hasn't unraveled after near daily use last summer.  I've worn it a few times as an exercise shirt and worked OK, but definitely not a true performance wicking workout shirt.

2 yr old daughter loves it. My 6 yr old son also uses it as a play set for his Star Wars characters. So the doll house gets double usage. As others have mentioned, the plastic staircase always falls off leading to moments of frustrated screaming by the two year old, who can't figure out how to put it back together.

Also, the dollhouse will play music, but you can barely hear it. Fresh batteries make no difference. Quite annoying.

It's easy to assemble, just 8 bolts onto 8 nuts, and feels pretty solid despite the light weight. The arms/uprights are not flimsy and don't wobble much. The paint/coating looks durable, we'll see how it lasts the winter.  Overall, pretty happy with it.

Pros:
1. It's a Birkenstock.  Very comfy and every other reason why you want to buy one.

Cons:
1. The color of Tobacco brown is more like light tan.  From the picture, I was expecting a dark brownish color.  Not a big enough deal for me to ship the sandles back

Summary:
Very comfy sandals.  Molds to your foot after a week or two of wearing it.  A nice alternative to flip flops (I just can't stand that flip flop noise).

My wireless modem on my Acer laptop died for no reason one day. So here comes this mini-USB modem to the rescue. Setup took about 10 minutes, and I was up and running in no time. Speeds are comparable to what I had with my built in modem. Fires up immediately upon getting the laptop out of sleep mode and I haven't had any trouble with it at all.  Very happy with this item.  I was a bit worried about buying it because it was so much cheaper than its competitors, but I haven't had an issue to date and I'm glad I saved that money

This was purchased to replace the original battery charger that got lost during the last vacation.  This replacement works and looks just like the one that came with the camera.  Charges the battery well and there is no indication that it's doing anything else other than that.  The battery behaves normally and I have no worries that it will overcharge the battery or short circuit it or any number of bizarre things aftermarket items have been known to do.

users.query: Andie Mitchell does a very nice job of describing the pain of food addiction.  She describes overeating as a child and teenager, and then later as a college student.  In college, she made the committment to lose a serious amount of weight, which eventually resulted in a 135 lb weight loss.  After her substantial weight loss, she gets a job on a movie set, and realizes that she is accepted for who she is and the work she does and not for how she looks.  She openly describes her relationship issues with parents, girlfriends, co-workers, and men.  She realizes eventually that she has substituted an addiction to physical excercise as her replacement for food before she tempers the exercise to reasonable levels.  In the end, she comes back to food by creating a blog and working toward spreading the word about healthy eating, exercise and healthy choices.  My only criticism of the story is the excessive amount of time early in the book where she describes gooey, rich foods and how she both loves and hates them.  It just felt like the book was a bit padded there to make it longer.  But I think Mitchell has done an excellent job of describing how trapped she became by her choices until she made the very difficult decision to change her choices.  Her book is positive without being Pollyanna-ish.  I was rooting for her the entire time!!!!

If you haven't read any of the other books out there about about eating and exercising right, this will be a good book to get you inspired.  I thought the book was actually quite repetitive, but what Dr. Katz makes very clear is that we DON'T need to be on expensive pharmaceuticals if we make better lifestyle choices.  He shows how exercise and diet can revolutionize our attitude toward our own health and he demonstrates how we control much of our health ourselves.  His goal is to get readers to recognize that we need to take personal responsibility in caring for our bodies (and our minds) and we can save money and extend our lives.  Obviously, he prescribes pharmaceuticals when people need them, but his main point is that we can significantly reduce our dependence on drugs by living with more energy (exercise) and healthy eating.

This was a fascinating novel of a morbidly obese college professor who hasn't gone out of his New York apt in years, whose story is interlaced with a former student of his and the student's son. As the professor decides to invite the former student to his home, he hires a maid service to clean the many years worth of dust.  His involvement with the maid becomes a turning point for him to start focusing on something other than himself.  The professor has made assumptions about the lives of others which turn out to not be true at all.  This book really illustrates that our friends and acquaintance's  situations are often very different than we think they are.  As the story slowly unfolds, you see a tale of loneliness, longing, procrastination, and action by all the characters.
  The book was utterly charming, extremely well-written, unpredictable, and absolutely worth reading.  I will follow this talented author for anything else she writes.  I think this book would be an excellent choice for both young and mature readers.

I loved this debut novel where the protagonist announces to the reader that she is going to kill herself in 30 days.  The book counts down to her final day as she wraps things up, and you are never sure if she is actually going to go through with it in the end.  The writing was superb.  I really enjoyed the inner dialog where Clementine has her comments about people and situations that were crazy amusing.  Do yourself a favor and read this book.  I will absolutely look for future books by this author!!!

This was an absolutely fascinating documentary that followed 6 diabetic individuals who changed their eating habits drastically, under medical supervision.  I would have liked a little more information on how the patients were selected, and how much diabetic education they had prior to their trip to Patagonia, AZ.  It was astonishing to see the dramatic effect their diets had on their health.  Not every patient was willing to make the necessary adjustments to ensure their good health, of course.  I was extremely impressed with the results and thought the food they were eating looked quite delicious. There is an additional segment that really discusses the food.  I highly recommend this if you are diabetic or have someone in your family who is.  It certainly shows the relationship between diet and health.

I really like this book for it's quirky characters!  How could you not like a book that has a feral bird child who has been raised in a cage?  A young man who has a secret passion for eating insects?  A thoroughly unlike able therapist?  an illusionist?  A crazy mother?  A wacko but psychic girlfriend, who is taking care of a morbidly obese sister and an angry, angst ridden teenage brother?  And a wonderful, warm dad who just wants his son to be happy?

This novel was more character driven than plot driven, as events unfold in NYC as Sept 11, 2001 draws near.  Zal tries so hard to be normal!  He puts himself into a wide variety of social situations that are terribly difficult for him so that he can find out how others people live.  Yet he has been crippled by his unstable mother who loved birds, but rejected him.  Luckily, he is adopted by a man who loves him and only wants the best for him.  I think the underlying story would have been interesting, whatever the storyline, because the author did such an exquisite job of character development.  I have mentioned above almost every character in the book, and each one is memorable!  I will definitely read more work from this author.

This novel of extreme living and extreme loss is fascinating.  Peggy listens to her father and his friends discuss survival scenarios but doesn't think too much about it because it is such an ordinary part of her life.  Her mother goes on a business trip, and suddenly her father tells her that they must leave and go to a safe place.  After they arrive at the disappointing destination, her father tells her that they are the last two people alive on earth.  They live like this for eight years, until one day, she sees another set of shoes and knows that three people are alive.
  This novel was unexpected, in so many ways.  Claire Fuller created a world that had constricted so severely for Peggy and her father, and yet, to the reader, there is a bit of an idyllic quality to that world.  Throughout the novel, there is an underlying tension because the reader knows that father James has lied to his daughter and is living out his own fantasy.  But how will it end?  I highly recommend this novel to fans of YA, but also to anyone who is looking for a wonderful debut novel, and a new author to anticipate!

I had high hopes for this book, but in the end, it didn't keep my interest.  I just had trouble staying focused on what the author was saying.  But in fairness to the author, I have found that sometimes a book like this doesn't appeal to me at one point in my life, but even 3 or 4 months later, I may find it riveting.  I may give this book another chance in a few months!

This novel had been recommended to me by several people, so it has wonderful word-of-mouth feedback.  This book, more than almost any other I have read about being in France during the Nazi Occupation, really makes you feel the fear, the hunger, and the depression of living in that world.  Kristen Hannah tells the story through two (sister) narrators, which was very effective.  Sisters often can be rivals for parental attention, which can affect their behaviors in ways both large and small.  This novel contrasted the choices made by each of these sisters and the consequences of those choices.  I don't want to give anything away, but this is a ver powerful novel that I would certainly recommend highly.  One of the best books I've read in a long time!

I bought the electronic version of this book to read to my 4 year old grandson on the iPad.  He just loved it.  It is a fairly long book with lucious illustrations.  It gives both a verbal and visual sense of coziness and blissful sleeping, as portrayed on the cover of the book.  I think this is a delightful book about that rather difficult process of getting kids to get under the covers and GO TO SLEEP.

This book was different in mood and story than other books I have read for a very long time.  Although it jumps back and forth in time from the backstory that takes place in Sara's diary to a present day disappearance, McMahon does a great job of melding the stories.  Sara, who has lost several children and has a wonderful relationship with her 8 year daughter, but perhaps struggles in her marriage, watches her daughter follow her husband out into the snow.  Hours later, when the husband returns, he is alone and completely unaware that his daughter had run out after him.  The daughter is found dead in the bottom of a deep well.  The darkness  and grief that enfolds Sara is really the rest of the novel.  The story streams on with an old hag, curses, insanity, and violence.  It reminded me of early Stephen King books, where it was hard to draw the line between the real and the supernatural, between real and imagined fears.  I will absolutely read more books by Jennifer McMahon.  Maybe it's time to get back to horror.

I purchased this book because a friend of mine had it and it contains about 3 designs that I want to make.  The cover photo doesn't do it justice, because the designs inside are much more wearable for various body types than the one selected for the cover.  Can't wait to make the lovely one featured in brown in the book.  I would definitely recommend this book for someone looking for some designs that will look good for many years to come.

This is a delightful book about many sheep, two women, and the life they have made on a farm.  The author is a reluctant farmer, but has a committed relationship to her partner and to her writing career.  She isn't convinced that the farm life is for her, but she grows to love and know the sheep they raise, and describes the animals, the mistakes they make, and the choices they make with much love.  She starts getting interested in the wool provided by the sheep and starts knitting, which she had avoided for years.  After finishing this book, I wanted to go visit a farm and scratch some sheep.  She made me fall in love with the idea of living near sheep.  I have been completely engrossed with pictures of sheep (and learning more about the different breeds)ever since.  And the love she has for her partner shines through the entire book!  I recommend this book to others.  I was totally charmed!

I had to re-purchase this book because all of the Mrs. Piggle-Wiggle books were some of my absolute favorites as a child.  I want to start reading the short chapters to my grandson.  For anyone who has never read Mrs. Piggle-Wiggle, she bakes cookies for the neighborhood children, let them run wild in her yard and encourages them to dig for Pirate Treasure in her backyard, and she is an absolute master at teaching children lessons through encouraging their bad behavior.  The wonderful thing is that most of the moms in the neighborhood know this, so they call Mrs. Piggle-Wiggle, and ask her if she has a "cure" for some obnoxious behavior that their darling child has, such as not wanting to bathe, or saying bad words, or refusing to share with others.  Mrs. Piggle-Wiggle's methods are fascinating and basically fool-proof, because by the time the child is "cured", the child himself is disgusted with his own behavior.  The book also has illustrations of the cures.  Unforgettable stories!!!!!!  I highly recommend this book.

"Lost and Found" is a collection of three stories beautifully illustrated by Shaun Tan.  The stories themselves were short, almost poetic in their simplicity.  I found them to be a bit dark for a young audience, but insightful for an adult audience.  I found the illustrations to be gorgeous in their complexity.  I had the impression that the book was directed at children, so I sat down to show it to my two year old grandson who loves books.  He was completely enthralled with the illustrations, but quite uninterested in the text.  He kept going back to the book to look at it again.
  I think that adult fans of Shaun Tan's artwork would want to add this volume to their collection.

This is a cute little book for someone who is looking for a quick, yarn-related story.  The main character seemed a bit naive in her lack of sensiblity of self-danger when a murder takes place in her shop.  That aside, it was entertaining to read about her love for yarn, ordering yarn, knitting for relaxation, etc.  All of those things that we knitters love about the fiber, make us occasionally read about other knitters in other cities, no matter what the story line.

I bought a Kindle version of this book to read to my 3 year old grandson on my i-Pad.  He loves it and requests me to read it over and over and over.  Very appealing illustrations for kids and adults.  I recommend this book for young (under age 5) children.

A perfectly sane woman.  An angry husband.  An obsessive psychiatrist.  The Civil War.  A handsome soldier inmate. A lonely child.  A cruel nurse.  How can you NOT like this book?  It has all the elements that we love and fear in life.  It hasn't been all that long since we could involuntarily commit people to mental institutions in the U.S. and this book reminds us how frightening that is, as it is nearly impossible to convince others of normality.  Iris is so normal that other inmates recognize that there is nothing wrong with her, but her only real hope of escaping from the asylum is to befriend a child and enlist his help.  He is reluctant because she is friendly with a soldier who seems to be suffering from PTSD or something, and the child is worried about Iris' safety.  I really enjoyed this book and would recommend it!!!!

Uncontrollable laughter while you are reading a book is a pleasure, but a tad embarrassing when in a group of total strangers.  Worse yet, I tried reading this book while at a conference where I was supposed to be listening to the (rather dull) speaker.  Another mistake! She is hilarious. She spells out 45 lessons that she has learned from knitting.  Her descriptions of flinging the knitting across the room, using words our children shouldn't be exposed to, and opening another glass of wine while reading a lace pattern, for example, are all things that most knitters can relate to.  Read it and LAUGH in recognition!

It can make a nice background while you are doing another activity, like gardening or sewing.  I recommend this disc for anyone who would like a top quality recording of monks in a monastic setting.

Post-apocalyptic novels are a dime a dozen these days. "The Last Policeman", by Ben Winters, takes a different approach- it's a PRE-apocalyptic novel.  The world is going to end, and everyone knows it.  An asteroid is heading to earth, and no one can alter it's course. In six months, it's all over.  People are killing themselves left and right.  Those that aren't are cashing in their 401k's to live large until the end.

Amidst the crashing economy and gradual shut-down of technology, Hank Palace does his job.  He's a cop, a detective, all he ever wanted to be.  When one of the suicides he is sent to check out gives him a weird feeling, Hank decides to spend his remaining time pursuing justice, even though he may be the only one left who believes in it.  This book will leave you feeling both unsettled and strangely satisfied.  Winters asks questions about the value of life when we are going to die, and answers them bluntly.  The story stands on its own, but is the first of a planned trilogy. Good, because you'll want to see this through the end.

Davis Vann is an amazing writer.  This novel has only 4 characters, and takes place over about 3 days during an annual deer hunt.  As the father spots a poacher through the sight on his rifle, a chain of events is set into motion.  Told entirely from the point of view of the 11 year old boy, this novel fascinates as much as it horrifies the reader.  Vann tells the story of an angry, violent family.  The descriptions are graphically vivid.  The setting is hot and humid.  The events are frightening.  Be prepared for a very intense short novel that shows how a person's background and upbringing creates the person he eventually becomes.  To be honest, I was glad when I finished the book due to the intensity of the story.

From reading the reviews before I ever decided to read this book, it was pretty clear that the majority of readers either loved it or hated it. After reading it, I fall into the camp that loved it. I can understand how the reader has to suspend disbelief to get over the initial hump of a woman knowingly bringing home an escaped convict with her and her son. However, the mom, Adele, is such a lonely, broken soul in desperate need of love that one can believe she might do such a thing. I was also confused that the book was described as sexy and sensual, but is narrated from the point of view of Adele's 13 year old son, Henry. The author does indeed pull this off, though. And Frank, the aforementioned escaped convict, surprisingly turns out to be an almost too good to be true "good guy" character. I did wonder how things could wrap up in a way that would leave me satisfied at the end, but they did. I definitely recommend this one, but will choose who to recommend it to, as it is not for all.

I feel ambiguously about this novel, as it was interesting and well written, however, not exactly "happy" subject matter. I had a sense of foreboding from the beginning, as I knew that things could not end well for all parties. The ending was a mixed bag, but left me feeling quite sad for most of the main characters.

I hated the last half of this book...it made no sense. I just kept thinking that it would all come together and make sense at some point, and it never did. Thankfully, the movie was very different from the book.
I'm afraid that I don't share the enthusiasm of most about this novel. I found it to be a dark and depressing work from beginning to end.

I have read several other books by Robert McCammon and have really enjoyed them, so I was quite surprised that I disliked this one as much as I did. I found it to be very dark and depressing from the beginning. It seemed that nothing positive happened in the protagonist's life until the very end, and even that was a mixed bag. Had it not been for the glowing reviews of this book, I would have given up on it shortly after I started it. But I stuck it out, thinking that it would get much better...unfortunately, it did not.
Saw the movie first and loved it, which often means I don't appreciate the book as much. This was a definite exception. I loved this book!

I found this book to be surprisingly enjoyable. It moved along at a brisk pace, with plenty of unexpected twists and turns. And at it's heart, it's a story about the love of books and bookstores. Lots for a reader to appreciate.

Compelling nonfiction. I didn't expect to be so emotionally moved by this book, but I had a visceral, emotional reaction to the chapters that described the human drama of the poor souls trying to survive the sinking of the Lusitania, especially when mothers and their children where involved. Just an enormous tragedy any way you look at it. I also found the book educational, as I thought the sinking directly and immediately led to the US getting involved in WWI, but there was (inexplicably, in my opinion) a 2 year gap between those events. There is also the backstory of whether British intelligence actually allowed this disaster to happen in the hopes of getting the Americans into the war. We will probably never know for sure.

I absolutely adored this book! I loved the curmudgeon, Ove, from the first page to the last. This is one of those rare novels that can make you cry and laugh (out loud...a lot). Even though there is sadness within the pages it is overwhelming uplifting. I would recommend this one to all readers, and even non-readers. Go ahead, I dare you not to fall in love with Ove.

Although there was a healthy bit of humor injected into it, this one seemed much heavier, and frankly, depressing at times. I also would have preferred that the ending wrapped things up a little more.

This book is imaginative and makes you ponder what might be awaiting us after we pass on. It can be on the depressing side at times, as the main character's life on Earth was not the happiest, but it is ultimately an uplifting story with a happy ending. If nothing else, it will make you think.

I was very disappointed in this final book of the century trilogy. I had a hard time with this one for a number of reasons. Firstly, the time period was much less interesting to me than the previous two. Secondly I did not find the characters as engaging as their parents and grandparents, whose lives were explored in the other two novels. And thirdly, though I could recognize his political leanings in the first two installments, his extreme political bias was on full display in this one and it tainted everything for me. What a letdown!

This was a good introduction to the historical figure of Vlad Dracula, or Vlad Tepes (The Impaler). The author gives a fairly detailed account of his life and times, as well as a crash course on the geo-politics at that time in Wallachia (now part of Romania). He differentiates between fact and fiction, and in the case where accounts and details are provided by legend only, he lets the reader decide what to believe. The only complaint that I have is that the book contained a lot of typos, as well as grammatical issues. Often there were changes in tense during the middle of a sentence. I found these issues to be very distracting and interrupted the flow of the book.

I bought this one thinking it was a true crime book, but it really was a book about Mormonism and fundamentalist Mormon sects. Knowing almost nothing about Mormonism, it was fascinating to learn the origins and history of their religion, and downright scary to take a closer look inside the fundamentalist, polygamist sects. I already had a very unfavorable opinion of polygamy, but now I find it frightening, for the females involved, and for society in general. Girls are often ""given"" for wives as young as 13 and 14, and are often related (sometimes closely) to the men that become their husbands. In many of these communities, they have legal way out, as the police force and judges are all fundamentalist polygamist themselves. It was very eye-opening to learn how these groups get away with the crime of polygamy. The men have only one officially recognized wife, while the rest are ""spiritual"" wives. These spiritual wives are seen by the state as being single mothers once they start having children, and they begin collecting welfare. It was staggering to learn how much money they are able to bilk from the government in this manner. And they do it happily, as they see the government as their enemy. Our tax dollars at work! It was also eye-opening to find out that groups like the ACLU are helping these polygamists, saying that they are just practicing their beliefs. But who is standing up for the young girls who are being systematically abused. I personally think that when someone's religion allows for, and even encourages pedophilia, that is where we, as a society have to draw the line. At that point, it's not a religion, but a crime.

His name is James Borden,a lawyer from New York, and he won't leave her side until she's opened the letter. The letter contains an offer from his employers for funding an investigation business, a 100 thousand dollar cheque and the addition of a partner, a Lucia Garza.

I was all jazzed up and excited to read this book many years ago when Oprah had announced on her show that "House of Sand and Fog" was the next selection in her book club.

The book sounded like a great read, so I jumped right in and read the book in a few short days. After I finished reading this book, I couldn't figure out what all the fuss was about.

Sure Andre Dubus III can write, there isn't any doubt about that, HOWEVER, the storyline, some of the events that take place in this novel, and even the actions of some of the characters, seemed way off center.

Take for instance the main character, Kathy, who doesn't bother opening and reading the several attempts by the county to let her know about a tax problem against her home.... Because she ignores the letters, the county takes away her home and it is auctioned off for sale. Come to find out the county had made a mistake/error regarding the supposed tax issue. If Kathy had only dealt with the letters the county sent her in the first place, then perhaps she wouldn't have been in the predicament she found herself in in the first place.

Kathy also has an affair with a married cop named Les in the novel, whom falls in love with her. Les ends up getting all caught up in Kathy's drama and crossing the line illegally by terrorizing & holding the new family that purchased her home in the auction hostage. Les' actions are truly unfathomable to me.

I found both Kathy & Les to be very frustrating characters to read about in this novel, which is why I am giving the book such a low rating.

This is the 1st novel I've read by Jill Shalvis and it won't be my last. In fact, I look forward to reading Instant Temptation as well as Instant Attraction that pertain to the two other Wilder brothers mentioned in Instant Gratification.

I like Ms. Shalvis's writing style. She is witty and knows how to write a great story with a great cast of characters and just the right amount of steamy, sex scenes without being over the top raunchy. This novel was wonderful to read. I finished it in two days.

The only draw back was how stubborn the lead female character was in letting her guard down-- It became a little old after awhile. Otherwise, this novel was fabulous.

I bought "Black Duck" based on the book's description and also based on all the great reviews it has received thus far. I loved the book the entire way through. "Black Duck" is geared for kids ages 9-12 according to the description with the main characters being teenage boys.

I enjoyed how the author intermixes the past with the present in "Black Duck" by making some chapters in the present day and other chapters in the past. Janet Taylor Lisle is able to bring to life what rum-running during the prohibition may have been like on the New England coast in 1929 by using a cast of fictional characters and how prohibition may have effected a community. The story is told through the eyes of Ruben Hart, who was a teenager during 1929.

Currently Ruben Hart is an elderly man. He is approached by a young boy named, David Peterson, whom wants to be a journalist when he grows up. Young David has his sights on writing a story about the the rum-running days and this is where he crosses paths with Ruben Hart. David is set on interviewing Mr. Hart about the rum-running days as he has heard that Mr. Hart knows something about those days. The interview happens over the summer vacation and David learns/hears quite a story from Mr. Hart & quite a tale it is. The two become friends by the end of the novel.

"Black Duck" is a good story with well developed characters!! The story is intriguing and keeps you wanting to know more about what will happen next!!

This was my 1st experience reading anything written by Joyce Carol Oates and I was extremely disappointed after hearing so many glowing reviews regarding her writing. All the stories in this collection were dark, sinister and quite frankly very creepy.

This is a fast novel to read and could be easily read in one day. It was a very predictable read, which isn't something I like in a book because it makes for a boring read if you can figure out what is going to happen in the novel long before it ends. The characters are likeable enough, but kinda of feel 2 dimensional and safe... Not too much depth to them. The story is simple as well. Overall, this novel isn't a bad read nor a great one. It is a forgettable novel and one I will not remember much about in the future. I wouldn't recommend or buy for friends or family.

I recently finished reading this nonfiction book & enjoyed reading it very much. What I enjoyed most about this book is how very readable it was. I am not very well schooled, if you will, in terms of religion or various religious thought/beliefs, so felt this book was perfect for the layperson (like myself) who wanted to know more about the Dead Sea Scrolls, where they came from and why they are an important part of history.

This book is also written as a series of questions and answers; A format which I also found to be a wonderful way in which to present the topic of the Dead Sea Scrolls. This book is also a short and fast read and very much too the point with regards to the topic at hand.

I received this book a few years back from a friend of mine as either a birthday gift or Christmas gift. Anyway, I read this book and found it to be very enjoyable, witty and fun! A must read for every young female out there that needs some humor! This book is a fast read. So kick back and enjoy.

I'd say this is the best mystery novel I've read by Diane Mott Davidson so far... I've only read three of her books in all and not in any chronological order. With that said, I was hooked from the start of this novel all the way through to the very end. This novel had a lot of red herrings in it and this kept me guessing as to the murderer's identity until the end. I had figured out who the killer was well before it was announced in the two previous novels I had read by Diane Mott Davidson, so it was a perk not to know who it was during this novel until the very end.

The only major drawbacks for me about this novel was Goldy's relationship with her ex-husband, John Richard Korman, and her son, Arch. John Richard Korman is Goldy's abusive ex-husband who still bullies her and she does nothing about it that does her any good. John Richard Korman just gets out of prison in this novel and was physically abusive towards Goldy during their marriage... So, why would Goldy want the child she loves near her abusive ex-husband, even if he is her son's father? Plus Arch's character is plain annoying.

The 1st 40 to 50 pages of this novel were pretty slow. I almost gave up reading this novel because it started off so slowly... I'm glad I didn't though because it ended up being a very fascinating novel that I couldn't put down. You don't have to be a photography fan or know much about Louis Daguerre to enjoy this book.

What I liked most about this novel was the story telling done by Dominica Smith. The novel opens as Louis Daguerre is an old man and going mad due to inhaling mercury vapors from all the daguerreotypes he has done during his lifetime. Daguerre thinks the world is coming to an end, so sets about taking his last 10 great pictures before the world ends with the help of a friend. From there we learn about Daguerre's life, where he grew up, his career, the love of his life who spurned him, but whom he seeks out to see one last time before the world ends.... and so on.

This book is truly a wonderful; read.

I really enjoyed reading this novel quite a bit largely because the storyline was well written and filled with many red herrings. Also, I'm an avid reader of cozy mystery novels and love spending time in bookstores, so reading this novel was a no brainer for me.

Murder of a Bookstore Babe is your typical cozy mystery with the leading character being a female amateur sleuth. In this case, the leading lady & amateur sleuth is school psychologist Skye Denison, who also spotlights as a consultant for the local police department. For the most part, I enjoyed the character of Skye Denison as well as the rest of the characters... Some of the characters were a bit annoying, but nothing one couldn't get past. Murder of a Bookstore Babe started off a bit slow, but picked up speed and kept my attention throughout the rest of the novel.

I look forward to reading other novels  by Denise Swanson in the near future.

"Murder Most Frothy" is the 4th book in the Coffeehouse Mystery Series. I read the first three books in this series and loved them, BUT have found myself sorely disappointed with "Murder Most Frothy". I just finished reading this book recently and am still marveling at how bad it is.

The following summarizes what I don't like about "Murder Most Frothy":

* Claire Cosi, the leading character in this series, spends the entire novel in the Hamptons. Cosi is the manager of The Village Blend Coffeehouse in bustling New York and will someday be co-owner of this business with her ex-hubby...... I like The Village Blend Coffeehouse setting and was disappointed to see the entire novel set outside The Village Blend Coffeehouse and its usual characters (i.e. Tucker her assistant manager, Detective Mike Quinn, etc.)

* Claire makes a lot of stupid/dumb solo moves in this novel in attempts to help find the person trying to murder her friend that seemed really out of character for Claire. Sure she's made some dumb moves in past novels, but not like in this novel.

* Plus Claire jumps to some dumb conclusions about pieces of information she does stumble upon without considering further investigation to see if in fact what she thinks is going is in fact really going on.

* Dialogue in some areas of the book were really lacking. In order to help move the story along, writers usually use dialogue to convey information to the reader, not loads and loads and loads of descriptive paragraphs instead when dialogue can be used.

* I also founding the incessant use of parentheses throughout the novel to be rather annoying feature too.

* Also the ending of the book was completely unbelievable and unrealistic to me.

I'd already read Marjane Satrapi's books Persepolis 1 & Persepolis 2, which I really enjoyed reading a lot.. So I wanted to read another one of her books. I decided to read Embroideries by Marjane Satrapi as it sounded really appealing to me as a graphic novel. It did not disappoint. I loved the writing and artwork contained with in this graphic novel.

I received this novel as a free Kindle download.... And believe me I can see why they are giving this novel away for free. THE STORYLINE IS WAY TO LONG AND DRAWN OUT!!

You have two people very much in love with each other, but can't seem to reconnect due to past hurts and preconceived notions that are holding them back. The bulk of the storyline focuses what each of the main character is thinking and feeling. Their same feelings and thoughts are rehashed over and over again throughout the bulk of the novel, which makes for a frustrating read...

As I was reading this novel, I kept thinking to myself, "Geez, get on with it already and just get together" about the main characters as you knew by the end of novel they would get married and live happily ever after. By the time you do near the end of this novel, the two main characters do get married to each other. From there the author, rushes to add a few broad brush strokes about the happy couple, which is so cheesy!!! The author had spent so much time building up the reasons why it took so much time for the main characters to get together and then just hurries to finish the novel once they were together that the end of the novel didn't feel right. The ending felt rushed and unfinished making the novel seem unbalanced. I think less time could have been spend on why the main characters felt they couldn't be together and more time on their lives together once they became a couple.

This is an interesting book to read about the discrimination that took place in Quakertown, Texas in the 1920s. The characters in the book are fictional according to the author's note at the end of the book, but the event of an entire community of African-Americans being forced to relocate by the white community in order to create a new public park in the area where the African American community resided is based on true events. This book was well written and  touches on the racial tensions at the time.

This is a very quick, easy, and fun read for those looking for light entertainment and an escape from reality for a few hours! This is a book that can help pass the time while traveling or on vacation as well.

Nice storyline, that captures your attention at the start of this novel and holds it through the end of this novel. Take one smart  advertising executive, Leslie Stewart, with an IQ that places her in the genius category and one suave, ladies man, attorney Oliver Russell, whom is running for governor of Kentucky. The two meet when the advertising firm Leslie Stewart works for decides to do pro bono work in order to help Oliver Russell in his run for Governor of Kentucky. Stewart & Russell fall in love quickly and become engaged to be married. Shortly before they are to be married, Russell flies to Paris on business and marries his former girlfriend. Stewart reads about the marriage in the local paper and is crushed although she takes the news in stride.

From that day forward Stewart vows to take revenge on Russell for breaking her heart. But in a cruel twist of fate, even the best laid plans don't always guarantee the desired outcome and can back fire!

I  finished listening to the unabridged audio version of The House of Velvet and Glass by Katherine Howe and narrated by Heather Corrigan this past weekend.

This was my first experience with anything written by Katherine Howe and I am unsure at this point in time whether or not I'll try reading another novel written by Ms. Howe as I wasn't very impressed with The House of Velvet & Glass.

I did think, however, that Heather Corrigan did a splendid job narrating The House of Velvet & Glass and will look forward to hearing her narrate other audiobooks in the future.

The House of Velvet & Glass by Katherine Howe falls into the historical fiction genre. The setting of this novel primarily takes place roughly a century ago on the East Coast of the USA in Boston, Massachusetts. Topics/themes for this novel include the Titanic, the sinking of the Lusitania, World War 1, Spiritualism, Scrying/Divination, family loss, and also a family scandal to name a few of the topics touched upon in this novel.

I liked the premise of The House of Velvet & Glass and many of the themes/topics touched upon within it, as I do enjoy reading historical fiction. I thought, for the most part, that The House of Velvet & Glass was a very slow novel overall.... Some of the scenes did pick up and were interesting, but for much of the novel, I felt it was boring/slow and it felt disjointed as it moved between time periods. I also felt that the ending of The House of Velvet & Glass was very flat. There is an abrupt gap of two years where the novel goes from 1915 and then jumps to 1917 in the next chapter. The novel ends in an unexpected way that wasn't fulfilling to me. The ending was very anticlimactic to say the least. The House of Velvet & Glass just didn't resonate very well with me.

This is this first book I've read by Hungarian Author Sandor Marai and I thoroughly enjoyed reading it. I finished reading "Embers" in three days as I couldn't put it down. This book was that captivating. There was an element of suspense/mystery as to why two friends whom had been friends since boyhood hadn't seen each other in 41 years. What was the cause of them not seeing each other or corresponding with each other during that time?

This book definitely makes one think about the true nature of friendship and has you thinking about what it means  to be friends with someone. Honor and love are also topics touched upon in this novel and also leaving you to think about what each of these terms really mean.

The only reason I didn't give this book a 5 out of 5 stars was because I thought it would have been more interesting to have heard Konrad speak and explain his side of the story as to why he left so hastily 41 years earlier. Instead, "The General" gives mostly long monologues to Konrad explaining the chain of events that occurred and why he felt these events happened as they did. Since Konrad says nothing, we are left to presume that what his friend "The General" has said is true as we only see Konrad through "The General's" eyes for most of this novel.

Otherwise this book is phenomenal and would highly recommend reading it.

Geez, Meryl Streep is phenomenal in her role as the editor-in chief to elite fashion magazine "Runway" and plays the perfect boss from hell. I can't imagine any other actress for this role! Also nice to see actress Anne Hathaway mature as an actress and move beyond "The Princess Diaries".

This movie is fast paced, humorous, and a total chick flick at heart. I loved every second of this movie.... Sure its no Oscar Nominee, its not meant to be anything other than just pure entertainment.

The acting & action were good in this movie, but it was a bit too violent for my taste.

This movie is all about revenge vigilante style, when a parent witnesses a brutal slaying of his eldest son and realizes the justice system may not give the appropriate retribution... So, he takes matters into his own hands.

I recently finished reading Aromatherapy For Everyone by P. J. Pierson & Mary Shipley. This book is a great introduction to the wonderful world of aromatherapy and it makes a wonderful book for someone wanting to learn more about the benefits of aromatherapy.

Here's more of what I loved about this book:

1) Provides a brief introduction/history of aromatherapy and how aromatics and essential oils work.

2) How to use, apply, and store essential oils.

3) Well organized table of contents, index, and color photographs of the plants that make the essential oils.

4) Essential Oils are listed in alphabetical order with a short paragraph about each essential oil along with its therapeutic uses, its applications, which essential oils it blends well with, extraction method of each oil, which parts of the plant are used to make the essential oil, safety precautions, and fun facts!

5) Author biographies are included at the end of the book.

6) A bibliography for further reading is also included as well.

This is the first book I've read about aromatherapy. Although, I can't attest to how factual the information is in Aromatherapy For Everyone, it does appear like the authors do know their topic quite well.

I like how well organized Aromatherapy For Everyone is. It is well written, easy to understand, short, to the point and will make a great reference book to keep in my permanent collection.

I truly think that the French Press is the way to go in terms of making & enjoying a fresh cup of coffee. I have owned several French Presses over the years, but they have all had a glass carafe to them verses a carafe made of stainless-steel.

I just received my Bodum French Press a week ago and have used it several times already. Bodum makes great French Presses and this one seems to be made well too. I like the stainless-steel look as it is really popular these days in terms of kitchen appliances. This French Press is sturdy and well made, without being heavy. I also like that the carafe isn't made of glass, so one doesn't have to worry about the carafe breaking.

The only concern I have regarding this carafe is that the base of the plunger, where the filter is attached, is made of plastic... I am concerned that perhaps this may not hold up well over time and need to be replaced. Only time will tell I suppose. If it hadn't been for this small detail, I'd have probably given this French Press a five star rating.

I first read and enjoyed Bob Morris's mystery novel titled Jamaica Me Dead. So, I immediately purchased Bahamarama right after finishing Jamaica Me Dead in hopes that it was just as good.

What a disappointment to say the least!!! I guessed who dunnit by page 140, which was less than halfway through Bahamarama... I've never read a mystery novel, where I guessed whodunnit and why so early on in the game. Also, the novel started out fun and fast paced with lots of action and very witty, but got boring in the middle partly due to the fact that I was bored cause I figured all out.

The only redeeming features were the humor and that Zack Chasteen and his sidekick, Boggy, are likable characters.

Just used this on a 10 day trip to patagonia and it held up great besides the pocket material (more on that later).  All in all this is my favorite pack for size, versatility and comfort.

Pros:
Shorter profile height, so the top compartment doesn't get caught on tree branches
Folding pouches works great vs zippers but doesn't compress as well advertised
Buckle system is great for fast access
Generous water bottle pocket depth
Colors make your pack easy to pick from a group of bags
Minimal padding just in the right places allows for excellent airflow across your back.  Osprey packs have too much going on.
Detachable 15L is great
Hidden rain cover works great, easy to access
Horizontal compression straps are much better than having a bunch of various loops/straps for backpacking/hiking.

Cons:
One ice pick loop
Material for water bottle pockets isn't very durable, I already have multiple holes in it.  Hopefully these don't expand.
Needs an extremely compressible sleeping bag (kelty one is great but $$)
Detachable 15L portation is sewn at one end instead of a buckle.
No way to fit the Kelty PDSI and a sleeping back in the same compartment

So the stretchy material for the various exterior pockets is the only weak point.  I was cautious when setting down my pack but by the end of the trip, I have multiple holes in mine.  I don't think these will tear unless I really stuff the pockets.... Looking at the other backpacks in my group, some had the same material with the same issue.  Kelty should know that this material tears and picked something more durable.
comfy, but the soles are coming off after 3 months.  Otherwise, they look great and provide good traction and are easily cleaned.

great bag with all the features you would want.  extremely compact when in the stuff sack
