users.query:
Wash Me Away is such a powerful read that made me stop and think because of how real the storyline felt. While I was reading this book I lost myself in Addies journey. The author did an amazing job with the development of the characters. Depression and suicide ideation isn't an easy subject matter to write about but the author did an amazing job on it. I felt the authenticity and struggle these characters had through her words. I loved that the story also provided resources for anyone seeking help. Wash Me Away is told in First person and is told through Addies POV. While this books deals with serious issues, it also gives us a remarkable story on how these issues can be overcome and life can become enjoyable again.

Addie is living with her Aunt Jane and Uncle Gil after losing her father in a storm. Addies life is not at all what her aunt and uncle thought. She has never spoken to anyone about her life with her father Thomas. Just before she is scheduled to start school at Burton Academy, her aunt and uncle want her to speak to a counselor about her feelings. Unbeknownst to Addie, she befriends Leo who also attends the Academy. Addie is not used to having friends but on her first day she becomes friends with not only Leo but Julia and Miyagi. The four become very close and establish an easy and natural friendship. They help Addie focus on her new life rather than her past life. Of course I helps that Leo is around, even though he has a girlfriend.

Addies character is one that I loved. Even though she was damaged by her past we see her grow throughout the story. It is not easy for her to see her friends have loving parents when she lost her mother and a young age, and life with her father was nothing like people thought. At her new home Addie finds letters from her mother and she begins to learn the truth about her family. I loved the eagerness and focus Addie takes when she reads these letters. Just when she starts to get comfortable tragedy strikes the group of friends. Miyagis sister, Willow commits suicide. They are all having a hard time dealing with it, but the reasons for her suicide leaves Julia and Addie confused. Addie starts to see that Willow and her have more in common that she thought. Addie learns of a family secret that changes her already shattered existence.

We do not get Leos POV but you can see how special Addie is to him. Even though he has a girlfriend, there was no doubt for me on where his heart and head are really focused. The connection and chemistry between these characters is strong

You know you're not like most girls.
From this angle, it appears Im like most of the girls Ive met.
I don't mean like that. God not, you're beautiful. What I mean is you're different because you are easy to talk to.

Addie will have to find a way to accept the truth which can very well be the last straw to her already fragile mind. The things this poor girl has endured and lived through will break your heart. I loved the way the author wrote this entire story and how well the characters were woven in perfectly. Each of the friends are dealing with issues of their own and I loved how their strange friendships helped them to deal with the realities of their own lives. I loved how they find solace and peace together. Addie and her friends journey is one youll want to get on and one you will not regret.

cands.text:
4.5   out of 5 
Grab your tissues because you will need it!  This author touches on real life issues like bullying, abuse, poverty and children with special needs.  I was immediately drawn into this story and the well-developed characters.  There was never a moment with in this story that I felt disengaged or disconnected.  This book is emotional. There were parts where I cried, screamed and felt enraged but those moments were foreshadowed by the overwhelming sense of hope, love and second chances.

Adam is returning home after leaving 11 years and hes trying to mend his broken heart.  Adams mother has cancer and the life he envisioned for himself is no longer an option.  I loved Adam. He was such a caring and loving character.  Even though his first and only love Lily broke his heart, it didn't stop it from beating again with he runs into her and her son after 11 years.  I adored how the author didn't make his character bitter or angry with Lily, yes he was hurt but all he wanted to do was hug her and help.

Lily, God I just wanted to reach into my Kindle and hug the ever loving stuffing out that character.  She has suffered so much abuse not only at the hands of her mother but also by the people in her town.  This woman was not broken though she was strong, loving and loved her son fiercely.  Max is a child with special needs, they do not have much but the love they after for one another makes up for the other things.  Lily has always loved Adam but shes confused and hurt by his disappearance. Max bought so much depth into this story, I fell in love him and kept wanting to read more about him.

This story was so different than what I expected. The relationship between Adam and Lily happens over time but during that time. I loved reading how Adam and Max formed  a connection and bond with one another.  Slowly the truth about what really happened between them 11 years ago comes to light and when Adam finally learns about the horrible truth hes determined to right the wrongs of that fateful night.  Learning the truth about Lily broke me, I too wanted to jump right in to help right those wrongs.

This story was remarkably writing and despite all the wrongs the author balances them off with the good that comes from it all.  I loved how the author focused on the couple and didn't add unnecessary angst into this story. You will fall in love with this book and come out believing in love and the goodness in people.  This is the first book in this series and there are more stories to come and I cant wait to read them all.

This book was beautifully written and left me speechless. Mental Illness is sometimes hard to explain but Louise Gornall did an amazing job with bringing agoraphobia and OCD to light. I thought how can an author sift through a teens everyday life and bring this heavy issue to the forefront without confusing it with average teenage drama? I was seriously blow away. This author did that. She took my mind right into Norahs struggles. Her attacks, feelings and anxieties.

What was special about this book was that we got to see the main characters illness but also her struggle to just be normal. Norah knew where she would go wrong, laugh at herself and chastise herself for being different. I felt for this character and how fragile her mind was. The author doesnt only show the mental side of Norah but also shows readers that she is still a person with feelings and has dreams despite her condition.

Luke comes into her life at an awkward moment in her life and while most guys would run, he didnt. I loved that the author also wrote his character as imperfect. He makes mistakes but finds something real and deep within Norah and wants to get to know her. He researched Norahs illness and found ways to get around them to make Norah comfortable.

I loved how Norah and Lukes relationship wasn't overdone with angst and drama. It had just the right amount to balance out. The authors words and depictions had me so engulfed in this story that I never once got bored. Under Rose Tainted Skies is a heart-wrenching book filled with promise, understanding and acceptance. This is definitely one youll want to pick up.

This author has a talent for writing brilliant and powerful love novels where I cant help but fall in love with her characters and their stories. I have waited for Noahs book since we got Sawyers book and I will say this is was so worth it wait. We get laughs, tears, drama, angst and some really hot cowboy loving.

Noahs Journey is a fast read but it was wonderful and enjoyable. The prologue was hard and shaped the man Noah was today. For years Noah lived with the guilt that he did something wrong that made his girlfriend up and leave him. He lived his life with his heart closed off and not willing to offer any woman a chance to hurt him again. But he started to trust and open his heart with his friendship with Alena. With Alena he was willing to take a risk and see where things would go. With Alena he was willing to take a risk and see where things would go. Just when he lets his guard down, his ex-girlfriend comes back to town with a secret that will alter Noah and Alenas life!!

Stacey, I wanted to throat punch. As soon as I read the first page, I knew she was a manipulative, cold hearted witch. She holds something over Noahs head that makes him makes rash decisions. Alena on the other hand, I loved. This woman was the total package, classy, gorgeous, proud a confident (me I would have decked Stacey but I am not classy). She was very understanding with Noah, and I wished she would have been tougher at times. Alena knows that he has to deal with the secret that Stacey has revealed but Noahs detachment puts a wedge in their relationship. She loved Noah and wanted what was best for him and did not want to add more stress to his already difficult time.

Noah is not perfect, he makes mistakes and he unintentionally hurts Alenas. You can tell that Noah is confused and has a lot going in his life. He doesnt realize the damage he is doing to his relationship with Alena and how he is hurting her until his brothers and family tell him. Noah is forced to try to repair the damage his actions have caused but is too late? Will Noahs ex-girlfriends return cause him to lose the only woman that has ever truly loved him?

What I love the most is how this author creates stories and characters where they are not picture perfect. Each couple has a journey they have to take in order to find their happiness. The Epilogue was epic! I really loved it. When I got to that part my heart melted and I fist-pumped and shouted. I cant wait to see what is next for this author.

4.5 stars out of 5 stars

I have to admit at first I wasn't really into this story, but once I got really into it I became absorbed. I think the author did an amazing job writing and plotting this story by giving us a slow build to these characters journey. One that is filled with anguish, pain and some very funny comebacks that brought tears to my eyes. I enjoyed how this author gradually gives us a romance story that at first glance seems to be impossible.

Richard Van Ryan is in one word terrible. Lets just say his reputation proceeds him. He is a tyrant, womanizer and treats people beneath him including his PA Katy poorly. When his heartless and womanizing ways stands in the way of him getting a job he really wants he enlists the help of Katy. The plan is simple he is going to portray himself as a changed man, a man that has fallen in love and engaged to be married. Here is the thing Richard hates Katy. He treats her badly and is constantly belittling and demeaning her. It is a good thing that Katy feels that same way but she needs this money for more than selfish reasons.

I really couldn't stand Richard at first. I wanted to throat punch him and kick him in the junk many times. He didn't care about anyone but himself. The last thing I expected was getting this slow build up where underneath all the arrogance, we got to see the real man. He developed real feelings and often showed a tender, sexy and funny side with Katy. Spending time with Katy helped him to be the man he truly was proud to be. When you see the way this man slowly falls for Katy your heart will skip a beat. This brut of a man does things that not even he thought he was capable of doing.

Katy was so much more than she presented, I know this from the very first introduction. She is gentle, kind, considerate and is loyal. I easily found myself relating to her character. She was not career driven and her only need for money was completely self-less. I understood her pain, lack of self-confidence and reservation. When Katy took the role of Richards finance we see another side to her character. One that will not take his verbal lashings and his mistreatment anymore. Richard never stood a chance.

The conflict and the slow building romance worked so well in this story. I really felt like I was experiencing this story through their eyes and am so glad I really got to know these characters. Their sexual chemistry heated my kindle and I got lost in their little moments, kisses and light touches. What started as a contract turned into so much for Richard and Katy, but what happens after the 6 months are over? Will Richard go back to his old ways or will he be fighting for something more than he even imagined? This was an enjoyable read and even though it was slow starting for me I really ended up loving it.

I adore Mariah Dietzs writing style and I jumped at the opportunity to read this book. The Weight of Rain is different than her previous work but it does hit home. I enjoyed the underlying message in the book, which is about bullying and verbal abusive. There are a lot of different characters in this book and they each of them have a story of their own however the story is told by Lo (Lauren). I really loved that there is a slow build up to this great love story.

The story does start a little slow, but I realized as I kept going that this was how the author intended it to be so we can be introduced to the kaleidoscopic of characters in this book. Los characters was hard to get a read on at first, but slowly I got to see that there is more to this character than I first thought. It was hard for me to see why she would have a one night stand with a guy she just met at a party. Of course the number he gave her is wiped off the next morning. She cant remember his name and he hasn't called her either. Lo is in college and is an extremely talented artist. With the help of her friend she finds the perfect job, a nanny.

What I loved a lot about this book was the relationship between Lo and Mercedes. Mercedes is 10 years old, raised by her father Kash and Uncle King. She is spoiled and a feisty young girl. The start of their relationship is tense but slowly the two form a bond that I found endearing and loving.

Months go by, and Lo finally meets the infamous Uncle King. King and Lo are both in for a shock. Yep you guessed it! Hello one night stand! King I want to go on the record and state I did not like very much at first. He is the typical bad boy of BMX and he treats Lo like crap at first. There is a very good reason for Kings reaction (which we learn later on during the story) and it broke my heart.

The story picks up when King and Lo meet again and needless to say things are strained, interesting and at times witty. King and Lo have a connection and even though neither wants to mention that night, they are drawn to each other. What develops over time is not only a romance, a bond and a love story but also a family. I loved all these characters came together, and formed a very unique family that supported each others dreams and goals. King and Lo come face to face with the knowledge that someone close to them kept them apart for months and are left with more questions than answers. Can they get past this deception? This was a really great story one you don't want to miss out on.

If you are into soulmates, humor, scorching hot chemistry and a second chance romance all tied up with very little drama than this book is for you.  Forget You Not was a fast paced read that sucked me right in at every page.  I loved the comradery and banter with the side characters and their friendship.

Lark and Rowen haven't seen each other since one beautiful and promising night.  Right from the start we see how these two are meant to be together but Rowen has a promise to fulfill and has to walk away.  Now I know everyone is like, really but his reasons are good and for all the years that hes been away, Lark is the one that consumes his every thought.  Now hes back home and  walks right into the bar his little Vixen is at and his dreams are about to come true, not!

This story was so great. The chemistry and banter between Lark and Rowen was so much fun.  Lark isn't the same shy girl Rowen met, a broken heart will do that too.  Shes interested in one thing, getting the goods and going their separate ways.  Well Rowen isn't going to let fate get away again.

This book had so many funny  moments and equal amounts of alpha male to keep readers on their toes.  This was a quick read one that was enjoyable, light and hot.  I enjoyed the connection the characters had even when they were fighting with one another.  I adored Lark and Rowens characters. They brought so much life to this story.  Rowen is in for a fight and he knows that Lark is his soulmate and how high her walls are. Hes determined to march on them walls and bring them down.  I absolutely adored this story and highly recommend it.

4.5 Stars out of 5 Stars

Under Her Skin was an emotional, poignant and promising read. I read the blurb and thought I knew what I was getting into but I was not expecting to feel such an array of feelings. This book got me thinking and remembering just how harsh and volatile relationships can be but with the right person it can be beautiful.

We follow Uma and Ivan ,two people with trouble pasts that are not only drawn together but have a connection neither can explain. Uma is a fighter, survivor and lives with an ugly reminder of how trusting a man can have bad consequences. Uma and Ivans relationship was built on each knowing and understanding that they are both hiding from something ugly. Ivan was so different he understood Uma s need to go slow. He was patient and didn't mind taking the back seat and letting her drive.

Uma and Ivan were both able to free themselves of their pasts when they were together. They both felt no judgements and at peace. I felt what each character was feelings while I read the authors words. I felt their excitement, fears and hopelessness. I enjoyed and understood why and how Uma needed to be the one in control. Her struggle to overcome her fears and her self loathing and how she gets through her day was just so well written. I could feel it all.

Their relationship is slow and steady just as is their sexual relationship. Ivan is an alpha male but when hes with Uma hes sensitive and their moments together were so special and passionate. Dont get me wrong Ivan lets her be in control but his mouth was so dirty, I loved it. Under her Skin was incredible journey and Im so glad I took it.

OK so for a debut book Ashley Suzanne did an AMAZING job, I connected with the characters in this book as if I was there.  I could not stop once I started and I was not disappointed at all, this book had some many great components that make a book special, funny moments, angst and WTF moments.  Mira, Danny, Skylar and Khylee are best friends and are finishing up College and enjoying life, and when tragedy strikes they are left to pick up the pieces.  And when you think things are at all good and done....BAM you are like WTH happened, I loved it and can not wait for the next book

I read the synopsis for this book and I was eager to get my hands on it. I absolutely loved how the author tells this story in dual POV. Both of these characters are complicated and both just want to live life with no attachments. The prologue was an emotional one where we get to see Callies loving relationship with Derrick, the love she lost.

Callie is character that I fell for immediately. For the past 3 years she has lived in a constant state of depression and blaming herself for the accident that took her fiancs life. Her parents have dictated her life for all these years and now she if finally free. She is moving to Boston with her best friend Sierra and is ready to live again, but she wants to be single. I could feel Callies pain from her loss but also her willingness to try to be a normal 20 year old young woman by being free and making her own decisions. When Sierra and her boyfriend Evan show up to move her to Boston they bring one of Evans friends along with.

Malcolm (OH MY WORD) I love this character. With Sierra constantly talking about Callie, he is definitely interested and decides he is going to make that drive to Pennsylvania, see this woman and then go back to his free loving ways. Yeah, Right! As soon as Malcolm lays eyes on Callie he has this instant want. Malcolm does not do relationships and he has never had a problem with sending women on their way once they are finished. So, he definitely questions why in the world he cannot stop thinking about Callie.

Callie and Malcom do have an intense and powerful connection, but since neither wants to be in relationship they choose to remain friends. There is some angst and drama in this story but it is also a beautiful love story. Malcolm was totally possessive and at times he made poor decisions. Callie on the other hand knew finding a love like the one she lost was a gift, one that she did not want to lose. Their plan to remain single is tested. Callie is still fighting her past demons. Can Malcom accept Callie despite the ghosts in her past? Can Callie get past his man-whore ways? Come take the journey with a very strong Callie and a determined Malcolm, it is one you do not want to miss.

3.5 Stars

I have mixed feelings about this story.  I enjoyed some aspects of this book but there are some that I didnt.  Ive never read a book from this author before so Im not familiar with her writing style.  I love a good mystery romance and and Im always up for some humor in a book, but I felt like I had a hard time really connecting with and becoming completely emerged within the story and the characters.

Neve and Duke are working together to restore a cabin and each bring special knowledge on this project.  Neve is a strong character and somewhat cold, I just couldn't connect with her.  I understand why the author made her this strong, working in a male dominant world could make a woman tough, however she was so tough that I needed to see that soft and endearing side to her.  Duke was a mystery to me as well. I just couldn't really figure him out but if I had to say which character I liked best it would be him.

Neve and Dukes banter was the highlight for me in this book. Their exchanges were out right funny and entertaining.  There was a lot of inner dialogue in the story and it took a while for the story to pick up.  I found that I skimmed through parts just so I could get more of their banter and interaction.  The added mystery is this book was also a highlight when things slowly came into play.  I found myself loving those parts so much more than Duke and Neves time together.  This was not a heavy read and for me the focus was more on the mystery of the book than on the couple.  So if you are looking for a good mystery book with a slight romance , this would be your book.  The mystery part and banter was captivating and enjoyable.

Ruin is unlike any book Ive read by this author. There is no alpha male and its based on a true story.  Our hero and heroine are different, special and both suffer from real issues.  The title is so fitting as is the warning the author gives in the start of this book. Its beautifully tragic and so worth the journey.  Alexander and Maybells story unfold from past to present. It is painful, innocent and has a strong presence of promise and hope.  The author starts off with an emotional start and it just kept up with that pace throughout in this beautifully written story.

Alexander and Maybell have experienced and dealt with viciousness their entire lives. Being different left them wide open to the butt of many jokes.  The author describes and shows readers just how cruel, malicious and hurtful bullying can be.  It was hard to read but it was necessary as well. I cried so many times.  Alexander has always watched Maybell, her quirkiness and her unique beauty lured him in.  For years hes always been in the shadows but what brings them together will ruin Maybell.

I loved Maybell. Despite what she went through in life she preserved and she did what made her happy in life.  Love and friendship were never part of her life and when she needed a friend she wasn't there, but the familiar face from school was.  I loved Alexander and Maybells relationship, each had an innocence Ive yet to read in a typical love story.  Theyve both experienced pain and yet find happiness with the moments they shared.  Alexanders mind will break you. His remorse and guilt plagues him and he knows when Maybell finds out the truth about their connection it will ruin her.

Im not sure how to explain this love story without giving anything away, because its a journey to be taken spoiler free.  The fact that I knew this was based on real life I found myself anxious to know who it was about and how things would turn out.  The issues and struggles the two main characters go through are real and these characters thrive in life!  As this story unfolds and the truth is slowly revealed I couldn't help but want more and more.  I swear even though there was ugly in this book, it was beautiful.  The love and innocence Alexander and Maybell find with each other despite their uniqueness is something everyone looks for today.  They experience so many firsts together.  Im glad this story was written. The message is clear, you can achieve anything in life if you want it.  Bullying is cruel, vicious and unwanted, think before you speak.

4.5   out of 5 

Molly McAdams the queen of the ultimate ugly cry, love triangles and gut clenching angst, so how I could I not read this?  If Molly comes out with a book you can bet shes an insta buy.  I love her unique writing style even when she has the power to reduce me to a newborn infant who doesnt get fed at when they are supposed to.  I know when I see her name I am going to be feeling it for days.  This book is another hit for me! It was beautifully ugly and I would not change a thing of it.  I was thoroughly invested in this book from page 1 and it just went from there. I was literally unable to put my kindle down.  I See You was written between past and present, it might seem confusing to some but to get the real feelings of these characters it was necessary.

This book is about Rorie (Aurora), Jentry and Declan and their tumultuous relationship and love.  Rorie is out for a night of fun at College. She wants to let go of her good girl persona and just have fun.  She agrees to a hook up with a hot, tattooed GOD and both agreed to only that one night, the only problem is Rorie cant get over that night.  Rorie is determined to find her one nightstand but she gets herself into trouble and this is where she meets Declan. The man who saves her and who will become the man to steal her heart.  Rories love Declan is real and but her heart and soul belong to the man that stars in her nightly dreams.  FATE can be a Biotch! Smack you right in the face when you least expect it.  Just when Rorie accepts her life with Declan, Jentry appears and cue the angst people. I love it!

I felt so sorry for Rorie because you could tell she tried so hard to do the right thing but the hearts wants what the heart wants.  She knows that once the truth is revealed someone she loves will get hurt and she cares from the both.  It was not easy for her to choose between her heart and what was right and it really takes a toll on her emotionally and mentally.

I really loved Jentry. I am not down playing Declan by any means but Jentry was a force to reckon with.  His presence was overwhelming just as his heart was. Jentry was caring, protective and loved Rorie so fiercely that he would give up his life for her.  Where Declan would stand down and let Rorie be walked over, Jentry was a lion protecting what was his, even when no one knew the truth behind their relationship.  By the time I finished this book I was an emotional wreck.  I swear I thought I was going to have no hair left and that ending was just so perfect. I would highly recommend this.

4.5 Stars out of 5 Stars

Just like her previous book This Is The Route Of Twisted Pain, MariaLisa deMora took me on another wonderful journey.  A journey of acceptance and love.  Every time I read a book by this author Im left feeling emotionally satisfied.

We learned a little bit about PoBoy in this book. I knew his past was dark but I was glad to learn more about his harsh past.  What I didn't know was just how painful and raw it would be.  The club, his brothers and his family are his priority.  Theres nothing he wouldnt do for his club even if it means to deny his true identity.

I love how the author takes her time introducing these very complex characters.  There are three in this book Poboy, Wrench and Chrissy.  We get know each characters back story and are really able to connect with them on a personal level.  Each character has a purpose and in this particular story I got to see why they truly had a special connection.

Chrissy, Poboy and Wrench each have a story to tell and each story screamed to be told.  I enjoyed how we get in their heads and get to know their feelings, fears and fantasies.  These three are hot, sexy and infectious. While this story brings three people together with the promise of love and acceptance we also get some suspense as an added bonus, after all this is an MC read.  We are introduced to new characters in this book, not only friends but enemies.  Just when I thought things would settle the author brings thing up a notch.  Yes this story focuses on Poboy but it also focuses on Wrench and how they both feel about their true identities and if they will be accepted by the MC and the brothers. Highly recommend!

4.5 Stars out of 5 Stars

Amity Cross never ceases to amaze me. Every book I read from her makes me come back for more. This book was different than her other series but it hooked me from start to finish. I was not sure if a writer writing about another writer would work, but it sure did. I loved the titles of each chapter and how much the characters and plot were intriguing and well developed.

I really felt connected to Luxs character. I really saw myself in her. Lux is an awkward young woman, her parents gave her up when she was young and she moved from foster home to foster her entire life.  She is shy and reserved and finds peace in her writing. Lux gets lost in her writing, creating a fantasy world where she is the heroine, fighting for justice and the leading male is in love with her. With love and support from her one and only friend, she publishes her series, but never gets notices. She volunteers at comic book convention hoping become noticed, and noticed she does get.

Jude is the opposite of Lux, he is the star of the weekly TV series Naturals and attends a comic book convention at his home town. He gets stuck in the elevator with a sensitive young woman, who does not recognizes him. Jude is intrigued with the young womans curiosity and her innocence. Trying to pass the time he discovers she is a writer, and before they are rescued he is able to get her card, before the paparazzi swarm in.

Lux never thought she would see Jude again, until she is offered the opportunity to writer for the TV series, Naturals.  Lux ups a leaves her home in Australia and moves across the globe to Atlanta. This opportunity will open doors for Lux, and bring her into the world she has always dreamed of. Immediately, Lux feels self-conscious uneasy and nervous, she is nothing like all the big wigs around her. She was not sure was wanted for her talent or because of Judes insistence. Lux is attracted to Jude and is glad to get the chance to know him, but all that changes at the blink of an eye.

You want to talk about whiplash, well I have it. Jude, lord the man came with his baggage and drama with his co-star and on and off again girlfriend Tessa. Tessa was determined to make Lux miserable and would torture her at every chance. Cue the drama, angst and all that stuff I love while reading.

The story is told in part by Lux POV, but we are gifted Judes POV towards the end which I LOVED. This book was well written and the flow of the story was just awesome. I really fell in love with these characters and their journey. If you are looking for a read that has some quirky moments, drama, angst and some steamy scenes, than this book is one youll want to pick up.

This book is intense because it dealt with some real issues; alcoholism, drug abuse and cheating. Some might find these topics a no-go but lets be real  THESE ARE REAL LIFE ISSUES. Nicos story is an emotional read and lord knows it tested my patience many times, but I am glad I stuck it out. If youve read Gabes book you know a little about Nico and Jill. Their journey transpired over years and Nico has put Jill though so much pain, but she loved him.

What would you do if you walk into your boyfriends apartment, heavily pregnant only to find him in bed with another woman? For Jill that was the finally straw, Nico has broken her heart and promises too many times, now she has to focus on her baby and no longer the man. Things for Jill go from bad to worse that day, but she manages to pull through and move on with her life. I am going to tell you why I loved this characters. Her heart still loved the man but her focus was solely on their daughter. Jill has not seen nor spoken to Nico in over a year, until she gets a phone call from Italy. Nicos mother has cancer and her only wish is to see her granddaughter.

You know that saying you have to hit rock bottom for a person to get better? That is the case with Nico.  Not even seeing the pain, disgust and hurt in Jills eyes was Nico able to see all the wrong he did. NO what broke Nico was almost losing Jill and their unborn child because of his destructive ways. Nico has always managed to win Jill back, but this time it was different, Jill was done. During the course of a year, Nico seeks help for his addictions and move back home to Italy, only seeing glimpses of his daughter, Nicola. So I know I should hate this characters, and let me assure you I did, but what changed for me was his remorse, his sense of guilt and his determination to make things right. Although he loved Jill and his daughter, he knew his addiction damaged their relationship and it was his turn to give Jill want she wanted.

There is so much pain and devastation between Jill and Nico that even a simple conversation is volatile. I loved how the author slowly wrote Nico and Jills journey, not leaving any of the ugly out. I truly appreciated and connected with the characters and their story. It was not a simple to forgive, it took work, a lot of work but their connection and bond is very intense. Nico and Jill have their work cut out, but can you forgive infidelity? Can you get past constant disappointments? How strong and powerful is love? Is it enough to forgive and move forward?

Let me start off by saying this book might have some triggers, so please keep that in mind. Charlies Whiskey brings a lot to the table. We have a female baseball player, MC , bad ass alpha biker and an abusive and dangerous ex. Im not a huge fan of instant love but this author handles this in a different way and it really worked for me.

This book deals with a slew of emotions that a survivor of abused person would battle daily. I felt Charlies highs and lows throughout this book. Her character is clearly well researched and developed. Charlie would be a sassy, strong and valiant person one minute and the next scared, insecure and distant. Whiskey was everything a woman starting over after coming out of an abusive relationship would want and need. Heres the thing the second Whiskey laid eyes on Charlie his natural instincts took over and told him she was his. Whiskey was not pushy. I think thats what drew me to his character. He understood why she would experience so many confusing moments. He didn't give up but stood his ground.

What I appreciated most was how the author didn't overplay the MC life in this book. Yes Im a huge MC book lover and the darker and grittier the better, but in this book there was just enough to keep me satisfied. With keeping the MC life to a minimal it let me focus more on the characters story. Whiskey and Charlie take the time to wade through their feelings and allow Charlie to truly heal. They both experienced pain on different levels but together they slowly. Whiskey was sent to keep Charlie safe from her ex of a nutso and boy was the dude wacko. Working through their feelings and guarding against a past hell bent on getting Charlie back, Whiskey and Charlie discover just how perfect they are together. But can feelings get in the way of keeping Charlie safe? Can Charlie truly let go of the past and look to a promise of a life with Whiskey?

Charlies Whiskey is a entertaining and promising read. I felt like I wasn't left hanging and yes at times Charlie gave me whip lash but I liked her. Would I read another book from this author yes and I believe we might see a book 2 in this series. This book was not all tissues and heart pounding moments. I loved how the author incorporated baseball into this story and used it frequently. Bottom line take a chance on this book, it will not disappoint.

I am a huge fan of Dawn Martens. Dawn Martens has done a terrific job with this series thus far and this one certainly didn't disappoint. I love the characters and the story development in this book. It was engrossing and captivating and I could not get enough.

Untouch Me is about Lilly and Vinny Zippos story but what makes this series even more special is how the author also lets readers see stories unfold for other characters in this Trilogy. All the characters lives blend into each of these stories even though the story focuses on Lilly and Zippo. Let me tell you I love Dawn, I say this because the writing in this book brought out every emotion from me. I wanted to throw my Kindle several times, I cried, screamed, laughed and fell in love with Lilly and Zippo. This book picked up right where the first one left off and I really loved how she takes readers to the past. We get to see how Lilly and Zippos relationship unfolded over the years, all their ups and downs that led them to the present.

Zippos character is hard not to love and also hard to hate. I mean everyone makes mistakes but he continues to make the same mistakes and hides it. Zippo loves Lilly but he is hiding a secret so devastating that he knows it will cost him his true love. Zippo changes and hides things from Angel and Mason Reaper but his actions show them that there is something really wrong. Zippos knows about the friendship and loyalty Lilly has with Eden and even though he understands why she keeps things a secret, he uses that to push Lilly away. The problem with Zippos plan was Lillys strong will and determination to not play the back and forth game with him anymore.

I loved Lilly. She is loyal, supportive, kind, tender and sweet. She loves Zippo with all her heart. Lilly knows keeping Edens secret was wrong but she was protecting her and wanted to keep her safe. When Zippo walks out on her again when she is pregnant with his child, she has had enough. She is done with the back and forth nonsense. It is a hard battle for her because her heart wants Zippo. Lillys walls are up but when Zippo really sees that he cant be without Lilly or his child and puts in the effort to fix things, her walls start to crumble. When Zippos secret is revealed at the worst possible time, Lilly is left shattered and broken.

Zippo never imagined his secret would come out the way it did. He does his best to right his wrongs, Lilly, Eden and Hilary have an amazing bond and have each others back when their worlds are torn apart. The same goes for Zippo, Angel and Reaper. They love these girls but their pasts have a way of keeping them apart.

There are secrets, betrayals and danger to all in the club. The story not only covers Lilly and Zippo but also an unknown person determined to bring down Angel and the club. The evil forces are at work with rats in the club. With relationships in turmoil the boys are so wrapped up in their lives they fail to see the real danger knocking on their doors. Can Lilly forgive Zippo for his secret? Can Zippo right his wrongs and win Lilly back? Can Angel, Zippo and Reaper solve the problems and danger coming to the club or will it be too late? This is one book you don't want to miss out on.

4.5 Stars

I absolutely love this authors writing. You have to understand the Boom theory to understand how this author and her writing works. The Boom and the characters that experience it are incredible and you will fall in love with their story.

Ashlyn and Dillon story was so enjoyable. Their connection and banter held my interest and kept me glued to the story. Ashlyn is known for running men off but one night in Vegas with Dillon changes her game plan. There were so many moments where I found myself smiling and laughing at loud.

Dillon is to die for. This walking sex God of an alpha male knows that Ashlyn is his. I loved that about him, he knows her game and doesnt back down. Ashlyn is funny and feisty, all the things I love in a female lead. She feels for Dillon but is unsure of his past relationship.

Over time the two begin to form an amazing and solid relationship, but Dillons past keeps coming back to cause trouble. What was interesting about this book was not just the dynamics in their relationship but their was an added element of danger that kept me on my toes. It kept things interesting and entertaining. I love that it wasn't just about the couple and sex. This is what I really love about this authors writing style. There was never a dull moment. I was nervous and excited while reading this story. Not everything is hearts and flowers. Dillon has a past and there is danger lurking in the shadows. Can Dillon and Ashlyn find that HEA they both deserved? This is one story that needs to be picked up and read. I cant wait to see what is next in this series.

4.5 Stars out of 4 Stars

If you have read any of C.A. Harms books then you know this author is going to gut you and make you fall in love. She has managed to do it again! The prologue to Ryans love is so heart wrenching that it tore me up. This book exceeded my expectations and I was completely captivated. The author tells the story in alternating POVs which helps in understanding the characters on such a deeper level. This book is one that is filled with so much promise, hope, turmoil, desire and letting go.

Ryan lost the love of his life 3 years ago. He has always known that Claire was meant for him at an early age but losing her so young devastated him. Left to raise their 12 year old daughter was hard for him. When his eyes meet Amber a new comer to Livingston Montana he is filled with emotions he hasn't felt since his wifes passing.

Amber and her best friend Bailey have relocated to Livingston Montana. After her grandmothers passing she purchases the bakery Heavenly Temptations and apartment above the bakery. She is ready to start a new life. The relationship between Amber and her girls is refreshing, supportive and downright hilarious. I laughed so many times because they were just that funny. Sparks fly when Amber lays yes on Ryan.

Ryan was so conflicted about his feelings, and having anything to do with another woman, he loved Claire with all his heart, and just the thought of being with any other woman made him feel guilty. It was hard to watch Ryan finally admitting to move and go forward with his life because you knew he loved his wife. Amber does not want to a stepping stone in Ryans need to get over his wife. She is hesitant to let him into her heart.

It was such as delight to watch Ryan and Amber build a relationship that was not rushed and over time developed into a strong bond. One filled of love and peace. When Ryan and Amber really start to develop a strong bond Ryans daughter has other ideas. The thought of Ryan moving on causes her to lash out more, rebel and causes Amber to rethink their relationship. Their journey is about acceptance and that it is ok to move on in life while never forgetting the past. This story was sweet, refreshing and not filled with unnecessary angst or drama. The next up in this series is Jackson and Baileys story and the bonus chapter at the end of Ryans Love guarantees it is going be get even more interesting with the Sawyer brothers.

One you Cant Forget is a short read but it is filled with drama, angst, suspense and a second chance at love. The author really did a great job with the story line and the character development was also written extremely well. The author tells this story in dual POVs and I love being able to be in their heads. I love a good MC book and unlike some Ive read this one doesnt really have a lot of grit, but the personal drama between the two main characters kept me hooked.

This story is about how despite years of separation (10 in this case) true love will always finds its way back. Emily and Luke were once young and in love, but Luke was the Bad Boy and Emily parents did not want her with him at all. Fast track 10 years and Emily and Luke still have feelings for each other and have never been able to give their hearts away fully to anyone else. When Luke reads an article on a police blog he doesnt believe Emily could do what it says so he sets out to reconnect with her.

Emily and Luke have a connection that is natural, strong and their desire and need for one another is felt on every page. I connected with every interaction and every memory they had. Luke is determined to get her back. I loved how much his inner thoughts showed how much she means to him. I loved how the author shows Emily as a weakness for him. He is nervous and unsure how to react around her when he sees again after those years. Nothing sexier than a man who isn't afraid to show his vulnerable side.

Emily is in trouble with the law, her ex-boyfriend is causing all kinds of trouble in her in her personal and professional life. When she gives into her desires she feels complete, but just as soon as she does she is made to believe that being with Luke will only add to her troubles. I loved seeing Emily getting a back bone and taking control of life. With Lukes dominance and persistence to not let her go again she takes control of what she wants and stands by her man.

If only things are that easy for Emily and Luke. Emilys trouble has yet to run its course, but with Lukes love and support she is ready for this battle. Lukes past is also starting to rear its ugly head. Will Luke and Emily be able to keep their second chance at love? Will Luke and Emilys past ever let them go? This is definitely a great start to a new series and if you love MC books then this one is definitely one youll want to grab. I cant wait to read what comes next. (l

This series by J.M. Walker will suck you in and grip you so tight you will not let go.  I read Grim and fell in love with Angel and Jay, but after reading Stain I have to say that Asher and Meeka stole the show.  I found their love story to be more gritty, drama filled and passion filled.  I will admit the darker side to this story had my upset at times, but I think the author did an amazing job with handling the issues such as PTSD and human sex slave trafficking.  The combining of the Military and an all female MC works beautiful the women are touch and in takes a real rough man to win the heart of the women in the King's Harlot's MC.  The danger, excitement and love felt so real that I could not help but to connect with both of these amazing characters.  I cant wait to get my hands on the next book in this fabulous and gripping series.

4.5 stars

Im such a fan of this author.  She just has a unique writing style that always keeps me invested in the stories and the characters she creates.  Normally Im an emotional wreck from her books (in a good way) but Million Baller Baby it was a refreshing change.  I was all in with humor, football, secrets and a second chance romance.

Rafe and Peytons story blew me away.  Yes there was drama but their story wasn't over shadowed by angst.  Their story started years ago, Peyton and Rafe are thrown together after she takes over as the head of the Carolina Crushers. Let me tell you their chemistry was hot and edgy but the banter between them was even better.  Rafe is good at football but he fumbles big time when his eyes catch the beautiful, feisty and no hold bars new boss. The man is sex on a stick and reeves up Peytons engine.

The author handles their story beautifully she brings the game of football into a love story that felt just as good as a super bowl game.  Nothing went as I expected even when Rafe finds out about his secret child.  I think thats why I loved this story so much, the author took the time to incorporate the child into the story line and made it more like of a familys second chance.  With the teams status on the line, a new child, new team and a chance at love Peyton and Rafe are both in it to win it.  This book had me laughing so many times and little Cullum was an added bonus to this book.  Loved it and cant wait to see whats next from this author.

4.5 STARS

This is a Joanna Wylde book so its pretty much a guarantee that Ill love the story. Its about The Reapers MC so whats not to Like! I love how we get to see the lives of new Reapers members as well as the older ones we have fallen in love with. I loved how we get to see not only the depth of love these men have for their women but also their love for the club. In true spirit Joanna gives readers the grit, intense and emotional side of loving a man in a MC. We also get to see the lighter and playful side of these men.

Tinker has suffered a lost so intense and painful. I truly admired her for her strength because I don't think I would have ever come back from it but she does. She comes back stronger and more put together than before. She leaves her cushy and extravagant life in Seattle to pick up the pieces of her life and care for her ailing father. I loved the relationship she had with her dad and her best friends. I swear I laughed so much when Tinker and Carrie would get together. Gage comes to town in need of a job, one that will allow him to do what the Reapers need. Tinker is immediately attracted to Gage and takes a chance with this stranger.

Gage, gosh I have to say hes right up there with Horse. I haven't felt for the other men in the club like I did for Horse until Gage. He loves his club and has always done right by them but one look at Tinker has him fighting with his heart and mind. Gages need and turmoil for Tinker was felt on every page through the interactions they had. His feelings and need for her were real and having to put those feelings on hold all for the love of his club was painful to read.

This is a book that you have to go slow with to truly appreciate the feelings, backstory and even the ecological story in this message book. Gage is living a life filled with lies. One to a woman who owns his heart mind and soul and another to another woman thats part of a job. Tinker and Gage are meant to be but Gages loyalty to his club and has him pushing Tinker away. I loved that she doesnt sit at home pinning away for him. When Gages lies come to the surface he finds himself in for fight bigger than hes ever fought before.

Gages job for the club and the consequences of that betrayal proves to be dangerous. There were some really gritty moments in this book. Gage and Tinker were like fire together and I loved that Gage was a no hold bars kind of guy. I loved how in this book not only are we dealing with the drama of the MC but also the fight with the elements of nature as well. I loved Reapers Fire and cant wait to see where Ms. Wylde will take the Reapers next.

4.5 Stars out of 5 Stars
Rie Warren has done a great job of intertwining this intense romance novel with some heart pounding and action packed suspense.  I feel like I have travel along with the Bad Boys of X-Ops on these missions. I felt like I was there with them. I did not think I would have the feelings as I did with Walker, but Ms. Warren did it to me again.  The Bad Boys of X-Ops are unique, their missions are dangerous and despite the danger they face, they manage to bring humor to the forefront!!

Im writing a book.
Bullsh*t.  This is porn.
Damn,  Thats some smut you got there.
Smut?  Whats that got to do with us and our missions?
Speak for yourself.
But wheres the plot?
Theres plot there.

In the previous book Justice was the joker, but in this one we get to see a different side to the man.  He is sensitive, fragile and quick headed.  He has been through a lot during his tour as a Marine and he has seen a lot.  I loved how the author added flashbacks of Justices time in the service. We get to see how much that has shaped him into who he is today.  The last thing Justice wants is a woman.  He is skeptical and cautious. Trust does not come easy for him.  He has been hurt in the past by a woman who swore to love him.  His walls are higher than the Great Wall of China, but when he sees Tilly, the man starts to crumble.

She turned confronting me with clear, soft green eyes and hair the color of ripe peaches.  My mouth instantly dried up, and my heart started quaking.

Tilly was perfect for the big bad Justice.  She is strong-willed, independent and goes for what she wants.  Although she is the Ambassadors daughter, she is far from prissy. I love that she gives as good as she gets. She is not afraid to use a gun and climb through the rubble with the rest of the team.  She knows Justice wants her, and she is going to have him even though he pushes her away at every turn.  Besides making it out alive, she now has a new goal and that is Justice.

As much as Justice pushes, Tilly pushes him closer.  I absolutely loved Tilly and Justice. They were perfect together.  She let him do his thing and never questioned his judgement.  Once he lets Tilly in, he is not prepared to let her go or walk away.  These characters are on fire, even in the middle of utter chaos, buildings blowing up and being shot at, they makes things sizzle.

Youre so small, I don't want to 
Give it to me.  Give me all of you.  I can take it.  You know I can.

I read this story all the while hoping that everyone would survive and hoping that Justice and Tilly would make it out together.  Justice is fast paced and packed with action, adventure, danger and some steamy scenes.  I cant wait to get my hands on the next book in this series

Compassion is the perfect title for this Novel.  This novel made me reflect on my life and how much people take for granted.  I was so emotional while I read this book. The subject matter that Ms. Neal touches on are real life issues, issues that are happening today.  We see and hear about these things every day on the news, on our streets, in our own back yards but we do nothing about it. This story made me want to reach out and make a difference.  Compassion is a story that deals with PTSD, military veteran, homelessness, hope and compassion.  It is a story that touched my heart in more ways than I can even explain.  My son is an active marine and I perish the thought that Archer could be my son. I cant even imagine that there could ever be a possibility that he too could get lost in the system.

Jaye and Archer are two people whos lives are completely different, but yet so much alike. They are both living day to day, just going through the motions.  Jaye lost her finance 3 years ago and she has yet to move on from that loss.  Everything she does, everything around her, centers on her lost love.  She is not ready to move on even though everyone around her says it is time.  When is the right time to move on from losing the one person you planned to spend the rest of your life with?  I felt her pain, confusion and frustration and my heart ached for her.  One simple gesture changes her life when she decides to offer a homeless man with beautiful eyes pizza.

Archer, God this man broke my heart.  His inner dialogue alone brought tears to my eyes, his episodes and his coping mechanisms was a test of his inner strength of survival.  Archer is a wounded Army Veteran, who since returning from war has not been able to catch a break.  He is not like how some people think. He is the sweetest man. He is kind, clean, gentle, and wants to make his way in life.  He does not make excuses for his situation. He tries to better himself but no one wants to give him a chance.  When his path crosses Jayes, he meets the one person that is strong enough to give him the chance he desperately needs.

Jaye and Archer together are a force I did not see coming.  This author wrote this couples relationship perfectly to fit their story.  They both were battling their pasts, and needed that one person to take a chance on them and they found that in each other.  I loved that their attraction to one another was there from the start but the relationship itself transpired over months.  I fell in love with Archer and Jaye and the underlining message the author was telling in this story. It is a cruel world out there, but with just one act of compassion you can change a persons whole life. This book truly is so touching and so inspiring. Its really opened my eyes in ways that has me reflecting on how I live my life.  This is a book that everyone should read. It will touch your heart and make you reevaluate your life in more ways than one.

users.query: Read this for book club and was not crazy about it.  Waaaaay too long.  Could have gotten her msg across in half the pages.  Katie shallow and witless and sounds like a middle-schooler.  Only interesting character is Demeter.  Would have been a better book written from her point of view.

cands.text: OK book but could have been about a hundred pages shorter.  Way too much angst and second-guessing on the part of the main character Kathryn who questions her life choices ad nauseum but seems reluctant to take steps to fix her life.  She has been wondering for years what happened to her supposedly best friend Jennifer but when given the chance to take a second look at the incident that is at the heart of the book, she is reluctant to do so.  Spends time watching TV, giving herself pedicures, sleeping late, and generally avoiding the task.  Overall, not a very appealing character in a cast of not very appealing characters.  Kline's writing is good, but the story is pretty lame.

Pretty well written though a few characters were pretty shallow.  If you introduce a shallow character, why write him up at all?  Anyway, as irritating as Louisa is and as unlikeable as Will is, it was still a pretty good read.  I have to say I was surprised by the ending.  I thought it was gearing up to be a "happily ever after" ending and it sure isn't for Will but maybe so for Louisa with all her new money.  Not a bad book to take to the beach.

Update:  Now I have seen the movie and it is soooo much better than the book.  So, give the book a pass and instead rent the movie.

Great read!  Funny, moving, a real page turner.  Not often that I find myself really caring about a fictional character, but the people in this book, particularly Celeste, seem so real that you can totally relate and even worry about them.  Well done, Liane!

This is the first of Karin Slaughter's books that I have read and am not sure if I will read anymore.  Most of the characters were irritating, especially Lena, who seems so conflicted with her personal life that she can't focus on her job.  Not having read the earlier books in what seems to be a series, a lot of the drama was lost on me.  Sounds like Jeffrey cheated on his wife, wife's mother cheated on her husband, wife may or may not be natural daughter of wacko cult patriarch who is now in a wheelchair, men routinely beat and terrorize their wives and daughters, women are victims in general  -- all way too much for me.  I'm back to P.D. James and Dorothy Sayers!

This was my first read by this author.  Main characters are Riley and presumed dead sister Lisa and ne'er do well brother.  Couple of unpleasant characters in the trailer park.  My first impression of Riley was whiney busy body -- a persona she maintains all through the book.  Everything is all about her.  Sister Lisa, supposedly dead, but living large on the west coast and even part of a band (suspend disbelief here), never bothered to come back to face her crime much less let little sister know she was alive.  When we find out the real relationship between Lisa and Riley, it's even harder to understand why she never reached out to her.  All in all, a book about shallow, selfish people.
Characters irritating, book has no ending.  Just stops.  Sounds like she was gearing up for a sequel that never happened.

and not nearly as interesting or entertaining.  I assume JK Rowling wanted to show she could write a "grown up" book, but it certainly is not the page turner her Harry Potter series of books are.  The main character, Cormoran Strike, is moderately interesting, but most of the other characters are pretty shallow -- the vapid models, the hard living, drug using rockers and their groupies, the poofy designer, the dim-witted cops, the grotesque movie producer, the money-grubbing wives, the greedy lawyers -- are pretty one-dimensional.  Also, she could have easily told the whole story in about half the space.  Way too much unnecessary detail that doesn't advance the plot.

I read this as part of our Book Club and last night we discussed it.  Overall, we were not impressed, despite the writer's skill.  The characters were fairly one dimensional, the ending unbelievable, and lots of questions unanswered.  That said, the writer tells the story well, even though the story itself is not very interesting.

I love Liane Moriarty's writing style --- witty, concise, descriptive - but I did not enjoy this book as much as some of  her other books, particularly Big Little Lies.  Still, she weaves a good story with interesting characters.  The "mystery" of the found baby is pretty obvious after you get into the narrative, but it's still a pretty good read.

Disappointing book.  As some other reviewers have said, it doesn't end, it just stops.  What happened with Francine's will?  What happened to Phoebe?  Main character Samantha sort of a spoiled brat.  Love interest just decides to head for the hills.  Can't say I blame him...  Maybe Grisham is planning a sequel?

I agree with most of the reviewers that Martha Grimes seems to be bored with Richard Jury, but wants to keep those checks rolling in.  Shame on her.  Won't abandon her totally, but will be getting her books from the library.

This is the third (?) book that is a departure for Scottoline from her earlier books about feisty, funny women.  I have read all her books and enjoy her writing, but her last few efforts have, in my opinion, have fallen short of the mark.  C'mon Lisa -- go back to your earlier gang and ditch this new touchy-feely family genre.

I had high hopes for this novel based on all the hype I read about it.  What a disappointment.  The writing is good but the story reminds me of an episode of 90210.  The tease in the beginning regarding the reason behind Thea's banishment is what kept me reading, but it doesn't take long to figure out what she did that resulted in her being sent away.  The characters in general are shallow and mean-spirited, especially the girls at the camp.  The horses in the book are more finely drawn, with personalities and likable characteristics, than are the people.  Thea herself starts out pretty interesting, but her overwhelming preoccupation with sex is off-putting, and her acting out on her raging hormones is unattractive.  The male figures are weak and uninteresting and, note to the Headmaster, sex with an underage girl is called rape.

Liked the book a lot.  Recommended it to my Book Club who also enjoyed it.  All of us are "60-somethings" so we could identify with Rebecca trying to jump start her life/career after years of success.  Only criticism was how could she not know Jim's sister died?  That's what small town life is all about.  But overall an enjoyable read.

Read this book because of a review I had read.  The blurbs on the jacket make it sound like the novel of the century.  It is not.  While the story at first seems compelling, it sort of falls apart after Stella recovers her memory, and the whole custody battle takes over.  It also sorts of stops, rather than ends, which is also a disappointment.  Haven't read other books by this author, so maybe this is not the best one to judge her work.

This is the first book I have read by Jodi Picoult and it was a great introduction to her writing.  All her characters were well drawn and believable.  Some critics find the alternating persons narrative a bit disjointed, but I enjoyed hearing the differing perspectives of the characters.  The ending is a total shocker.  Thought I had the mystery of Alice's whereabouts figured out, but no!  I was totally wrong and didn't see the ending coming at all.  Highly recommended.

At around 750 pages, this novel would have been better if it had been half as long.  Way too much description of everything. My impulse was to say, "OK, OK, I got it!"  Don't need to dwell on the same event ad nauseam.  Also, did not really connect with the characters.  After all the hype, I was disappointed.

I have mixed feelings about this odd book.  I liked the stories of all the dogs, but was very disturbed by a couple of things.  First, the author's mention of her 3 suicide attempts.  I was like, "Say what??"  And it was sort of mentioned just in passing, like mentioning what she had for breakfast.  No explanation or detail, just sort of dropped in the narrative for no purpose.  Second, the killing of her two dogs that got into fights.  I did not get that at all.  Why put them down?  They did not seem to be mortally injured.  Why not keep one and find a home for the other.  Even worse was her idea that if any of her new puppies were deaf, she would have them killed, or as she euphemistically says, "Send them to the farm."  I have a deaf dog and cannot imagine being so cold as to kill the puppies just because they were born deaf.  Sure, don't breed them or show them, but kill them??  No.  Also, waaaaaay too much info about dog shows.  All in all, my take-away was if you can't show your dog, then get rid of it.  Sorry, not my idea of puppy love.

Touching story of young Rachel who is snatched from her family and sent by herself to live in a leper colony on Molokai.  In general, I enjoyed the book, although it dragged from time to time.  Also, a few things were left hanging, such as what happened to Sister Catherine?  I also didn't see much point to including all the info about the Japanese interment camps, other than to draw the parallel between those camps and the leper colony.  Also, didn't see much point in the story of how the Hawaiian Queen was deposed.  Seemed like an aside.  One glaring omission was the actual cause of leprosy and how contagious it is and how it is transmitted between people.  The author at several points seemed to indicate that it was not transmissible from person to person, and I had to Google it to find out the facts.  These few criticisms aside, it is a good story of how badly these people were treated for years.

and I look forward to each new title that arrives.  However, I was disappointed with this one.  Not up to her usual entertaining standards.  Maybe it's because the main character is a man.  Her women characters are very believable, funny, smart, and have intelligent dialogue.  This guy, Dr. Mike Scanlon, is none of the above.  His actions are silly and predictable, his dialogue is stilted, his internal monologues boring.  Leave the guys behind, Lisa, and let's hear more from your great women!
This little device works exactly as promised.  The price was good and has lasted a long while so far.  Recommended.
I love Daniel Green shoes and always buy a size 8.  This shoe, however, runs way large.  Will have to put in an insert in order to wear them.

The latest in the saga of Chet and Bernie is entertaining and although not my favorite is still a good ride.  Chet is his usual charming self.  He talks just like I assume my dog would talk if she could.  What am I saying??  Of course, she talks to me!  If you want an entertaining, not too deep, fun read for the summer, pick up a Chet and Bernie mystery.

OMG, talk about a sugar overdose.  Characters just too good to be true.  Ending so totally predictable.  Language stilted and not very natural.  Nobody talks like this!  Good message, however, give to others without expecting anything in return.  Quick read, can do it in an evening.

Entertaining story, two stories really, intertwined.  Although interesting, there is far too much info about the logistics of setting up the World's Fair in Chicago.  OK, I get it -- it was difficult and frustrating.  More interesting is the story of H. H. Holmes, serial killer and ladies' man.  Would have liked more info about Holmes -- what made him tick, what made him a killer, and more info about his wives and victims.  But, that said, a pretty good read, just too long.
