After a four year hiatus Adam Ant returned recharged in early 1990 with "Room At The Top". He proved he could still crack the top 40, something I'm sure no one thought possible at the time. I remember when this came out, and I remember thinking it was average. Now however, it actually is better than "Vive Le Rock". There's something here, if you listen past the late 80's production gloss that still resonates well today (better than "Vive Le Rock" at least). There are a number of good tracks here like "Rough Stuff", "If You Keep On", "Manners & Physique", "Can't Set The Rules About Love", Bright Lights Black Leather", "Young Dumb And Full Of It" and "Anger, Inc." By far, the worst track is "U.S.S.A."

It's too bad this isn't digitally remastered (due to it being on a different record label from his first six albums). His next album would not be released by the evil record company execs, so we'd have to wait five more years until Adam would re-emerge with "Wonderful".

So, overall, not a bad album, but a little dated with the late 80's production and instrumentation. It's not as timeless as "Prince Charming" or "Friend Or Foe", but worth picking up for the Ant fan.

cands.text:
Adam Ant's first album is a do-it-yourself light punk, pre-new wave album. It is simple and straightforward with flashes of humor. It's unlike anything else he did that followed. As such, it's an okay debut as far as debut albums go, and it's just okay as far as Adam Ant's catalogue goes. There are few gems here on "Dirk Wears White Sox" in terms of melody and memorability. I actually prefer the truncated remixed version of "Cartrouble" at the end of disc. Aside from that, there's "Zerox" and "Friends". There are a few other close calls with "Cleopatra" and "Catholic Day", but overall you have to be a hardcore punk/Adam and the Ants fan to really appreciate this one.

The digital remastering is excellent, the packaging is digipak with photos you haven't seen before and an excellent graphics design concept that spans all the remasters unifying them perfectly. There are actually eight bonus tracks, not seven. At 71 minutes, I found this album to be slightly overlong in terms of listening to it all the way through.

Overall, a good beginning.

I like Genesis, own all their studio works. I like Mike + The Mechanics, own all theirs too. Honestly, as a fan from the beginning, I felt 2004's "Rewired" was average, and I was not disappointed with the idea that the band would never make another album. With the death of Paul Young, I didn't think there would be a "Rewired". "M6" in 1999 was not a great album either. So, with anticipation and bemusement I bought "The Road" knowing full well that Mike Rutherford had not made a great album since 1995's "Beggar On A Beach Of Gold". I knew full well that he had recruited three new vocalists, and the idea intrigued me since their debut album had four different vocalists and was brilliant.

I don't like Mike Rutherford's choices here. Also, I felt that Rutherford's songwriting is seriously lacking here. Not one standout track, really. Not even a "One Left Standing" or "Undertow" like on their last album, "Rewired". No, what's here is formulaic adult contemporary schmaltz--average schmaltz mind you, not bad, not great. There's no edge here like "Silent Running", "Black & Blue", "Word Of Mouth" or "One Left Standing". There's nothing terribly infectious like "All I Need Is A Miracle", "Nobody's Perfect", "Get Up", "Another Cup Of Coffee" or "Now That You're Gone". There's also nothing beautiful or emotionally stirring as "Par Avion", "The Living Years", "Someone Always Hates Someone" or "My Little Island".

What you have here is average adult contemporary pop without an edge. After repeatedly listening to "The Road" I kept thinking that it lakes variety even though there are three different vocalists. I listened to all of Mike + The Mechanics previous albums, in sequential order, leading up to my listening to "The Road", and I have to say that 1985's Mike + The Mechanics truly had variety. Go back and listen to it. Each of the nine tracks could stand on its own merits. Each track meticulously arranged and performed, but more importantly, each track was memorable without sounding over-produced or forced. No schmaltz.

I know Paul Carrack left the band, and Paul Young died, but if I was Mike Rutherford I might have attempted to get the other original players back such as drummer Peter Van Hook and keyboardist Adrian Lee. Plus, why not hunt down original vocalists John Kirby ("Par Avion") and Gene Stashuck ("You Are The One")? It would not have hurt to have those original players back on board since they did such a great job the first time around. No, the only original mechanic here is Mike Rutherford. Everyone else is brand new.

Of the three new vocalists, I think I prefer the one that decided not to be a mechanic, Arno Carstens, "Background Noise", "It Only Hurts For A While" and "Hunt You Down". Of the three tracks, I really only like "Background Noise", but his vocal quality and texture brings a refreshingly new approach to the mechanics. Too bad he didn't stick around.

So that leaves Andrew Roachford who is pleasant, but his vocals are indistinct. He is like every other crooner out there. There is no character to his voice, just a silky smoothness that saps most of the emotion out of each of his songs and makes them all sound alike. I suppose if I had to choose I would pick "The Road" and "I Don't Do Love" as his best moments.

Tim Howar, a musical theater actor. Oh boy. Well, he does a good job, and I think I actually liked his vocals better than Roachford's. His voice is also rather indistinct, and could easily be anyone. His best moments are probably "Heaven Doesn't Care" and "Oh No".

The first single, "Reach Out (And Touch The Sun)" is an okay choice, but it's not going to win over new fans, if there are any left in America. So here's what I'm thinking: Another album with better musical ideas could be rewarding. Or, why not get a set of new singers for the next album? That would keep things interesting. Either way, "The Road" leaves me neutralized. If the band never makes another album, that's fine, and if they do, that's fine too, I'll buy it. I like Mike Rutherford's band. I mean I did buy Genesis without Peter or Phil, and it wasn't all that bad, really. At least Mike Rutherford is making new, original work rather than going back and revamping old Mowtown and r&b classics from his youth like someone else we know.

Here's how "The Road" compares to Mike + The Mechanics previous works:

1985 Mike + The Mechanics: Five Stars
1988 The Living Years: Five Stars
1991 Word Of Mouth: Four Stars
1995 Beggar On A Beach Of Gold: Five Stars
1999 M6: Three and a Half Stars
2004 Rewired: Three Stars
2011 The Road: Three Stars

Most people today don't remember Adam Ant. Those of us who do seem only to remember "Goody Two Shoes." He was/is more than that. In fact, all of Adams' cds have something memorable about them. I chose Friend or  Foe to review because I think it's arguably his best cd. It has the hit  "Goody Two Shoes" on it but it also contains non-hits such as  "Friend or Foe", "Desperate But Not Serious",  "Crack Pot History and the Right to Lie", "Cajun  Twisters" and "Place in the Country." 12 solid tracks all  together. Prince Charming is also very good, and so is most of his early  work. 1995's Wonderful is a fine example of what Adam Ant can do. But,  start with Friend or Foe. It's relentlessly frenetic. Definitely upbeat,  with an emphasis on BEAT. The music on this disc isn't like anything you'll  hear on the radio these days. A must have for any rock collector.

By 1982 Adam Ant had ditched his band The Ants and gone solo. "Friend Or Foe" was his first solo album and probably his best. Following off the mega-success of his previous album "Prince Charming", he and Marco, the only band member he kept, came up with another brilliantly catchy and fun album. Again, in America, unfortunately only "Goody Two Shoes" hit the top 40. There are other greats here, and again, like "Prince Charming", not a wasted note. "Friend Or Foe", "Place In The Country", "Desperate But Not Serious", "Here Comes The Grump", a cover of The Doors' "Hello I Love You", "Crackpot History And The Right To Lie" are all great!

Besides the original 12 tracks you also get an overwhelming 12 bonus tracks, most of which are demo versions of album tracks and forgettable. There's not much difference between the Chris Hughes mix of "Goody Two Shoes" and the original. "Coup d'Etat" was only okay. "And So You Shall" as a demo is funny and shows promise. It's too bad it didn't make a final version. "Yellowbeard" is average fare, same with "I Know They Know" and "Gargoyles Are A Go". "Good Sex Rumples The Clothing" is actually amusing and catchy though it sounds like a blueprint for "Crackpot History And The Right To Lie".

Again, the lyrics come with the booklet and the graphic design and artwork ties in nicely with the other remasters in this series. All in all, another great album!

My fandom of Adam Ant began in 1981 with "Prince Charming" on the then fledgling MTV. They would play "Prince Charming" regularly and I think some videos from "Kings of the Wild Frontier". Back then he was different, novel, and he stood out with those videos and that music. I liked his music. Sadly, or strangely, after "Strip" in 1983 he all but dried up in America as he got out of the business after 1985's weak "Vive Le Rock" album failed to excite sales. But wait, like a Phoenix rising from the ashes, in early 1990 came "Room at the Top". It seemed he was back on top after so many years away. But no. It was a fluke. No follow up, and the record company shelved "Persuasion" since "Manners & Physique" didn't reach gold status in sales. Goodbye Mr. Ant. But noooooo, in early 1995 he switches labels and puts out a stunning turnabout "Wonderful" and has yet another hit (his last). And then, it all just evaporated. Again, no follow through--scrapped demos in 1999 and mental health issues run rampant, and nothing.

Right from its title, you can tell this new Adam Ant album isn't going to be what it should have been. The extra long metaphorical title that only a few will get (including Ant himself). The bloated 70 minute disc with 17 tracks. The do-it-yourself cheap production values of the album (I read he made the whole thing on a laptop). It's just not what I wanted. Maybe what you want, but not me. You see, I liked the perfect production-meets-creativity of "Kings of the Wild Frontier", "Prince Charming", "Friend or Foe", "Strip", "Vive Le Rock" and "Wonderful"--"Manners & Physique" was over-produced and a product of its time, and "Dirk Wears White Sox" under-produced and a product of its time.

So there it is--Ant's new album is more like "Dirk Wears White Sox" for better or worse. The punk attitude is there, the sparse arrangements are there, the out of key singing is there, and so musically, for me, this was a failed comeback. Lyrically, Ant fares better here. I mean, some of these songs seem more personal this time around--"Shrink", "Cool Zombie", "Marrying the Gunner's Daughter", "B.S.", "Cradle Your Hatred", etc. There is passion here, it's just not fully realized from a production/arrangement standpoint. It's demos--unpolished, unrefined, raw.

Now, if you have read any of my other reviews, then you know I will take issue with a 17 track album--mainly because I believe in getting in and out within 40 minutes. Could Ant have trimmed this album down and made it better? Absolutely. In fact, I would suggest you edit out "Valentines", "Darlin' Boy", "Dirty Beast", "Sausage", "Who's a Goofy Bunny?" "How Can I Say I Miss You?" and "How Can I Say I Miss You? (Reprise)". If you program your player to just play "Cool Zombie", "Stay in the Game", "Marrying the Gunner's Daughter", "Vince Taylor", "Punkyoungirl", "Cradle Your Hatred", "Hardmentoughblokes", "Shrink", "Vivienne's Tears" and "B.S." you have a pretty good listening experience without all the fat.

Still, musically, this fell far short of my expectations for Ant after 18 years. It's not bad, but it's not good or great. It's just average Ant. I'll take that because there's no way of knowing if he will ever release another album.

So here's how "Adam Ant is the Blueblack Hussar in Marrying the Gunner's Daughter" compares with Ant's other work:

1979 Dirk Wears White Sox: Three Stars
1980 Kings of the Wild Frontier: Four Stars
1981 Prince Charming: Five Stars
1982 Friend or Foe: Five Stars
1983 Strip: Four Stars
1985 Vive Le Rock: Three Stars
1990 Manners & Physique: Two and a Half Stars
1992 Persuasion: [Still unreleased. Bootlegs. I haven't heard it.]
1995 Wonderful: Three and a Half Stars
2013 Adam Ant is the Blueblack Hussar in Marrying the Gunner's Daughter: Three Stars

As far as greatest hits compilations go, this one by Level 42 is exceptional. 18 tracks covering most of their career including the American hits "Something About You" and "Lessons In Love" from  1986 and 1987 respectively. Level 42 were much more than those two songs  however. They brilliantly combined rock and jazz the way no other band has  been able to do except for Steely Dan. Most Americans probably don't  remember Level 42 by now, but they were a great band. Since most of their  cds are out of print in America this greatest hits package is all you need.  If you can find 1985's World Machine or 1987's Running In The Family, both  of those are very good. Level Best is a must have for any rock collector.

Simply put, The Cure is the most consistent work the band has done since 1989's Disintegration. It may not be as close to perfection as that album was, but it beats 1992's Wish, 1996's Wild Mood Swings and 2000's Bloodfowers for vitality and energy. There could be a slew of alternative radio staples such as Before Three, The End Of The World, Anniversary, alt.end, (I Don't Know What's Going)On and Taking Off. While the 10 minute plus The Promise ought to satisfy anyone who longs for The Cure when they peformed longer songs. My least favorite track is Us Or Them in which Robert Smith felt the need to use the f-word repeatedly to get across the idea that he was angry. The rest of the songs are good, but the bottom line is consistency as a whole album, and that is definitely what The Cure has on it. If I were to compare this album with any previous Cure album it would be 1985's The Head On The Door, which is one of my favorites. My least favorite Cure albums are 1984's The Top and Bloodflowers. There are several songs on The Cure that ought to remind fans of why they liked the band in the first place. So, enough quibbling, just buy the cd!

I wondered if Extreme was going to ever make another cd. I enjoyed Gary Cherone's queer response to VH1's Band Reunited, and how Nuno Bettencourt refused to even be filmed for the show three or four years ago.

Well here they are with Paul Geary managing, and a new drummer in his place. "Saudades De Rock" is pretty good. Better than the dismal and depressing "Waiting For The Punchline", their last cd back in 1995.

There are plenty of good songs this time around, and the humor is back as well. "Star", "Take Us Alive", "Run", "Flower Man", "Interface" and "Peace (Saudade)" are all good songs. "Comfortably Dumb" is a play on Pink Floyd's "Comfortably Numb", updated for the ignorant youth of today. "Flower Man" is yet another criticism of John Lennon's "Give Peace A Chance" which the band explored on the song "Rest In Peace" from their excellent 1992 cd "III Sides To Every Story".

There are some ho-hum tracks like "Learn To Love", "Ghost" and "Sunrise" that detract from the flow of the disc. Still, for a band that's been away for 13 years, this is good stuff. I'd easily place it under "III Sides" and over "Waiting", "Pornograffiti" and their debut.

In the liner notes the band says they're back. I'm hoping this means more cds in the future. Drummer Kevin Figueiredo is a perfect match for the band. And let me say that I do miss rock guitar playing such as you hear here with Nuno's virtuoso performances on several of the tracks. They just don't make music like this nowadays. It's all emo or whine-fest. No one knows how to play their guitars anymore.

Extreme does a good job with "Saudades De Rock" and if you are a hardcore fan looking for that old Extreme vibe with something new, this one is for you.

At this point Adam and the Ants could do no wrong in 1981. This is their most realized and fun work. Of the ten original songs there's not a wasted note. Each song plays perfectly off the last. In America, the only song I saw a video for was "Prince Charming", but there were other great songs like "Scorpios", "Picasso Visita El Planeta De Los Simios", "Five Guns West", "That Voodoo", "Stand And Deliver", "Mile High Club", "Ant Rap", "Mowhok" and "S.E.X." are also as equally campy and entertaining. This is truly a fun album and no one makes music like this anymore.

The six bonus tracks consist of demos, two of which were never fully realized "Showbiz" and "Who's A Goofy Bunny Then?" To me, all of the demos are uninspiring but they let you hear the process. As with the other remasters the packagin is digipak and the artwork and design is great. I agree with the other reviewer here that the remastering isn't as good as "Dirk Wears White Sox", "Friend Or Foe", "Strip" and "Vive Le Rock", and it ranks down there with "Kings Of The Wild Frontier". The booklet comes with the lyrics to all the songs. All in all, a great album.

As a casual Supertramp fan, this compilation serves as an excellent overview of a talented band. All the hits are here as well as some other great songs. The only shame is that this set hasn't been digitally  remastered and repackaged with new liner notes. This is a must have for any  rock collector.

If you read my reviews at all, then you know I'm a punk/new wave/romantic fanatic. I'm always on the lookout for new blood in the old vein. In the past 4 years several bands have brought back that classic sound from the late 70's and early 80's that has sorely been missing since 1990. Rock Kills Kid certainly have been influenced by U2, Duran Duran, Modern English, The Cure, The Smiths, The Psychedelic Furs and A Flock Of Seagulls among others. They compete perfectly with the new breeds The Killers, Interpol, The Music, Keane, Snow Patrol, Blue October, Arcade Fire and Franz Ferdinand to name but a few.

So, how IS the music on "Are You Nervous?" Well, I saw the video for "Paralyzed" on MySpace back in April 2006 and couldn't wait to pick up a copy in May. I've listened to it a dozen times and I have to say I'm looking forward to hearing more from this band. The first half of the disc is perfect with "Parlyzed", "Hideaway", "Midnight", "Are You Nervous?" and "Back To Life". Any of these five tracks should be hits on alternative radio stations across the country. Things stumble a bit on the back five as "Life's A Bitch" misses slightly, while "Run Like Hell" (no, not Pink Floyd's song) and "Don't Want To Stay" keep up the standard set on the first half of the disc. The final two tracks "Hope Song" and "Raise Your Hands" seem like toss offs. Overall, a great listen, and a great full-length debut.

Collective Soul are one of those bands that consistently make good albums. Good albums, but never classic albums. I don't know what it is after eight albums, but they never seem to find that perfect balance between song craft, melody and experimental originality. They're just a solid rock and roll band that never fails to deliver the goods on each successive release.

As a long time fan, I am critical of the band. I am not going to gush with glee every time they come out with something new. I'm not going to race to five stars just because it's Collective Soul. The truth is, the band still have work to do in terms of song writing and originality. They've got the power and energy in spades, but what at first sounds like a great melody soon turns into banality.

So, "Rabbit", or "Collective Soul", if you will. Their eighth album in sixteen years. I have them all. I meticulously listened to each one in chronological order leading up to this release, so everything is fresh in my mind. "Rabbit" is one of their more solid albums, just missing great. I mean, how can you resist the catchy and unusual whistling of "Fuzzy" like J. Geils' "Centerfold" re-incarnated. Or how about rocking out to "Dig", or maybe the U2-ish "You", which sounds like "Miracle Drug". "My Days" sounds like something from the Eddie Van Halen play book. "Understanding" is one of my favorites for its three time changes, something the band hasn't tried before, and probably the most experimental song on the disc. More of that please. "Staring Down" sounds exactly like Collective Soul, and then you get two more rockers "She Does" and "Lighten Up". Now, "Love", "Hymn For My Father" and "Welcome All Again" are probably my least favorite tracks, and I cheated and bought separately "Heart To Heart", "Staring Down (Acoustic)" and "She Does (Acoustic)"--all three tracks pleasant but unimaginative.

So I find myself once again frustrated with Ed Roland and company. I want to shake them up, go into the studio and push them to experiment more. They always kind of reminded me of The Cars, but even The Cars pushed themselves from their fantastic debut to their mega-selling fifth album "Heartbeat City". Where's that creativity gone? In some ways I feel Ed and company keep pumping out the same manufactured Hungry Man frozen dinner specials with slightly different spices. I mean the band is still on an independent label, and this is their third release on an indie, so what gives? Why not surprise us? "Afterwords" didn't even chart! Didn't crack the top 200 albums (their first not to!) What does Ed have to lose at this point? It's not sales!

Here's my comparison chart for "Rabbit" compared to the band's previous work:

1993 Hints, Allegations & Things Left Unsaid: Three Stars
1995 Collective Soul: Three and a Half Stars
1997 Disciplined Breakdown: Three and a Half Stars
1999 Dosage: Four Stars
2000 Blender: Three and a Half Stars
2004 Youth: Three Stars
2007 Afterwords: Four Stars
2009 Rabbit: Four Stars

ELO was huge in the 70's when I was a child, and I had forgotten how many  great songs they had done until I bought this compilation. Great songs like  "Telephone Line", "Don't Bring Me Down", "Calling  America", "Rock and Roll is King", "Turn to Stone"  and "Evil Woman" plus much more. The one thing that stands out  for me is how sophisticated Jeff Lynne's arrangements were. I can hear so  many bands that have ELO in their sound in the 80's and 90's.  This is a  must have for any rock collector.

In a break with my own tradition I did not revisit all of The Fixx's albums prior to listening to "Beautiful Friction". In fact, over the past 30 years I have only owned "Phantoms" on cassette and "Ink" on cd. Otherwise, I bought 1989's "Greatest Hits" and 1999's "Ultimate Collection" which was the superior of the two.

Now, The Fixx were ushered in during the New Wave movement of the early 80's, and were almost immediately picked up by the then fledgling MTV. The New Wave movement in general is one near and dear to me. But, The Fixx I considered more of a singles band than an album band. Like Duran Duran, The Fixx made some really great singles, but when you listened to the parent albums they were very uneven. Still, I really think their best album is 1999's "Ultimate Collection" because it gathers key tracks from all of their albums except 2003's "Want That Life". And when you listen to the "Ultimate Collection" you are hearing the very best The Fixx had to offer and you realize how great of a band they were/are. I don't think there is a weak track on the "Ultimate Collection".

But enough with that. "Beautiful Friction" once again demonstrates that The Fixx can't seem to shake that uneven album syndrome. I don't get all the five star reviews here. At best, "Beautiful Friction" falls somewhere between three and four stars. Every single song isn't solid. I think "Anyone Else", "Beautiful Friction", "What God?", "Second Time Around", "Girl With No Ceiling" and "Small Thoughts" are the standouts here. The rest are all average tracks (not bad, in fact there's nothing bad on "Beautiful Friction", but they're not standout tracks).

In fact, "Anyone Else", the first single, is an excellent choice and has Top 40 potential, but it will not get the promotion it deserves, and this is the current fate of all my favorite New Wave artists--OMD, Depeche Mode, Human League, Wang Chung, Men Without Hats, Duran Duran, ABC, Howard Jones, Thomas Dolby, New Order, Annie Lennox, The Cars, The B-52's, Devo, Blondie, Erasure, Pet Shop Boys, Inxs, Joe Jackson, The Pretenders--they've all released new material in the past seven years, but to no fanfare.

Even though bassist Dan K. Brown has returned to the fold, it hasn't altered the band's course. In fact, with The Fixx, I'm going to say that producer Rupert Hine is needed. He produced arguably the band's best albums--1982's "Shuttered Room", 1983's "Reach The Beach", 1984's "Phantoms" and 1986's "Walkabout". He did some production work on 1991's "Ink". His production touches complimented The Fixx and enhanced their sound, and gave them all their most famous hits to date and their highest charting albums to date. With Hine, the band might finally be complete and ready to return to the top.

So, three and a half stars out of five for "Beautiful Friction". The band isn't firing on all cylinders here, but they certainly aren't dead either. Somewhere in the middle. It's nice to have them back after a nine year hiatus between albums.

The debut album "Please Describe Yourself" from this Scottish band absorbs and makes new the 80's New Wave/Punk revival that other fellow artists like The Killers, Keane, Interpol, The Music, Franz Ferdinand and Snow Patrol have also excelled in. I'm very pleased to have this form of music coming back with a vengeance because it's been gone too long.

First, Dogs Die In Hot Cars (DDIHC) have offered both music and video content. I will begin with addressing the music. Their influences are quite obvious to me, and I completely disagree with any comparisons to Dexy's Midnight Runners (I have their music). No, DDIHC sound more like Talking Heads (the only thing missing from their debut being a cover of "Psycho Killer"), XTC, Oingo Boingo, The English Beat and Madness. Their first single instantly grabbed my attention--the ska flavored "I Love You 'Cause I Have To" video played before me and embedded itself in my brain cells. I bought the cd, and the second single "Godhopping" sounds completely like something Talking Heads would do (maybe on 1985's "Little Creatures"). The lyrics and viewpoints are cleverly written and executed. Themes such as desiring to be popular and desirable are evident in "Celebrity Sanctum", men losing power and control and dominance in the world in "Modern Woman", the joys of being lazy in "Lounger", and the media dictating images of what living a great life should be in "Glimpse At The Good Life" are all inflected with a form of dry humor and irony which is sorely missing from today's radio and video stations.

That brings me to the three videos included here: "I Love You 'Cause I Have To", "Godhopping" and "Lounger". The first two being the strongest with "Godhopping" resembling a Talking Heads video like "Stay Up Late" or "Road To Nowhere" or "Love For Sale". The videos are solid, and they should stick with whoever the director was.

We sure need DDIHC because the music world is missing bands like XTC and Talking Heads. I hope this band sells enough cds to make a second album. I give the debut four stars because I think they can do even better things if they're given the chance to. Still, a very strong debut from this relatively unknown Scottish ensemble. I see that I am only the ninth reviewer of this cd which is a shame. This band should really get more recognition, certainly the same as The Killers. Check this disc out. It also met my time constraint rule with 11 songs clocking in at a fantastic 38 minutes--perfect! If you're looking for something "Somewhat Off The Way", check this cd out, it's a good one. Long live the New Wave/Punk movement.

I think with Appetite for Destruction, GNR did for hard rock/heavy metal what Nirvana did for punk. Before GNR, hard rock was Van Halen, Def Leppard and AC/DC. GNR came along and shook everything down. With "Welcome to  the Jungle", "Sweet Child 'O' Mine" and "Paradise  City" GNR proved that hard rock didn't have to be overproduced and  glossy. It could have a sharp edge to it. After Appetite, GNR progressively  produced lesser and lesser recordings of high quality. For anyone who  collects rock, this is a must have.

It could have a sharp edge to it. After Appetite, GNR progressively  produced lesser and lesser recordings of high quality. For anyone who  collects rock, this is a must have.

Of H&O's 15 studio albums this is truly their most consistent and enjoyable. It pains me to say that most people snicker when H&O are mentioned, but this album is testimony to their place in rock and roll  history. I have all 15 of their cds and all 4 of Daryl's solo cds. To be  fair, Voices, Private Eyes, H2O and Big Bam Boom are all excellent discs  with minimal flaws. However, it is Voices that still sounds like it could  have been made today over the other three mentioned. I am biased towards  the 1980-1984 H&O time period because it seems that was the time they  were making their best music. I was only 7 when Voices was released but I  have repeatedly gone back to it over the last 20 years. I never get tired  of that cd, and if you are NOT a H&O fan, then this is the cd for you.  It has hits: "How Does It Feel to Be Back", "Kiss on My  List", "You Make My Dreams", "You've Lost That Lovin'  Feeling", and the original, non-Paul Young version of "Everytime  You Go Away." It also has some great non-hits: "Big Kids",  "Gotta Lotta Nerve", "Africa" and "Diddy Doo Wop  (I Hear the Voices)". It's not a bloated, 75 minute opus like many of  the cds being released today. It's 40 minutes in length and not a note  wasted. No excessiveness, just a tight pop/r&b/punk/rock cd. Now, if  only the record company would digitally remaster and re-release all 15 cds  like other record companies have done for Billy Joel, Elton John, Genesis,  Led Zeppelin, Pink Floyd, some Cheap Trick. Hall and Oates are an American  classic. They haven't even been inducted into the rock and roll hall of  fame yet, what a shame. Let's not forget that they still hold the record  for most successful duo of all time in rock. Buy the cd and tell me that  it's not great, I dare you.

Less than two years after "La Petite Mort" James follow up with "Girl At The End Of The World", another solid release in a catalog filled will great albums. I don't know yet if I like it as much as "La Petite Mort", but it's pretty close. James continue to defy expectations, and defy pop radio vapidness.

They churn out alternative-friendly hooks and clever lines of poetry. Technically, a band that's been around for 30+ years shouldn't sound this alive, this daring, this bold, but they do. I always look forward to a new James album because I know that I'm going to have little to complain about.

I think my favorites here are "Bitch", "To My Surprise", "Nothing But Love" (which should be a smash hit), "Dear John", "Surfer's Song", "Waking" and "Girl At The End Of The World". The rest are good, but not quite as strong.

Keep the albums coming, James, for you are a very rare breed of band.

Here's how "Girl At The End Of The World" compares to previous James albums:

1988 Strip-Mine: Two And A Half Stars

It's hard being Brian Warner. Back in 1994, when Marilyn Manson released their first album, he was 25, and his vitriolic shock rock anger was relevant and fresh--and authentic. All the trappings of youth frustrated with societal ills. Fifteen years later we get "The High End Of Low", an album filled with the same old same old from Mr. Warner.

Still, there are points of interest here. This isn't "Holy Wood", more like "Mechanical Animals". Marilyn Manson is back to the glam rock musically, but the lyrics are the same doom and gloom as always, just dolled up differently. I don't believe Marilyn Manson has ever made a five star album, but they've sure tried. "The High End Of Low" is better than Manson's last two releases, "Eat Me, Drink Me" (2007) and "The Golden Age Of Grotesque" (2003).

The stand out tracks here are "Pretty As A Swastika", "Four Rusted Horses", "Arma-godd**n-motherf**kin-geddon", "Running To The Edge Of The World", "WOW", "Unkillable Monster", "We're From America" and "15". Half the album. That's the problem with Manson--he is brevity challenged. All of Manson's albums are too long, with too much filler. Imagine "The High End Of Low" as a nine track album, filled with the best cuts, now wouldn't that be a five star album?

The length drags "The High End Of Low" into a coma. By the time you get to "15", you've been numbed. I applaud Manson for returning to some creative ideas like the country & western tinged "Four Rusted Horses", the balladry of "Running To The End Of The World", and the in-your-face posturing (which Manson does best) of "We're From America".

At this point, though, even the religious right must be adjusted to Manson's attempts to shock or push buttons. The fact that Warner turns 40 this year should mean that his themes should broaden. There's only so much you can say about death, religion, military, love, etc. Also, I'd like to the see band really stretch themselves musically. Manson has been turning out the same album for years now with some tweaking.

Here's how "The High End Of Low" compares to Manson's other albums:

1994 Portrait Of An American Family: Two and a Half Stars
1996 Antichrist Superstar: Three and a Half Stars
1998 Mechanical Animals: Four Stars
2000 Holy Wood: Four Stars
2003 The Golden Age Of Grotesque: Two and a Half Stars
2007 Eat Me, Drink Me: Two and a Half Stars
2009 The High End Of Low: Three Stars

Now 28, Fiona Apple burst onto the scene nine years ago with 1996's debut "Tidal". That album was full of beyond-her-19-years insight, musicianship and angst. A powerful debut which was not matched with 1999's "When The Pawn". So, now, six years later, we have "Extraordinary Machine" with all of its internet buzz that it had been shelved unfairly. Was it worth the wait?

Well, yes, actually. It is a refreshing album all the way through. In fact, I think it might arguably be her best thus far. She seems lighter musically while keeping her lyrical bite intact. There are several great alternative songs here like the title track, "O, Sailor", "Tymps (The Sick In The Head Song)", "Waltz (Better Than Fine)" and "Window". The rest of the album is just as solid. Apple flexes her lyrical muscle, creating imaginative word couplets and wordplay as evidenced on the title track where she says, "I mean to prove I mean to move in my own way, and say, I've been getting along for long before you came into the play."

Though I enjoyed this album, I believe the best is yet to come from Ms. Apple. A little more life experience and aging and she may just come up with a Grammy-winning alternative album, or album of the year. A one-of-a-kind talent, "Extraordinary Machine" will be listed in many best of 2005 lists by the end of the year. Let's just hope it doesn't take another six years until the next album.

In 2008, I somehow heard "Walking On A Dream", the song, before "Walking On A Dream", the album, was released. It was a good song. Especially for someone like myself who grew up on New Wave/Post Punk/Punk/New Romantic music during the 1980's. I had not heard of Luke Steele or Nick Littlemore prior to Empire Of The Sun, but then I don't live in Australia. Even now, Empire Of The Sun aren't exactly tearing up the charts in the U.S. Five years is also a very long time between albums, especially your first and second. The duo may have lost most of their fan base by now. But of course, not me.

"Walking On A Dream", the album, did not live up to expectations set by "Walking On A Dream, the song. In fact, the album is wildly uneven, and often times falls prey to bland electronic music. That's not to say that the album didn't have variety, because it did, but there were far too many songs that just didn't really hook you in.

"Ice On The Dune" looks to remedy that situation. It is far more focused musically. Maybe not as diverse, but certainly with stronger melodies, better melodies, and memorable songs. Let me start with my favorite tracks. It's a tie for first place with first single, "Alive" and "Concert Pitch". Second place goes to either "DNA", "Ice On The Dune" or "I'll Be Around". The rest of the album is reasonably good, certainly better than "Walking On A Dream", but still doesn't quite add up to a five star piece of work.

I kept thinking that "Ice On The Dune" is catchy, melodic, with reasonable song writing, but it just misses being five stars. I might even give it three and a half stars, with their first album being two and a half stars. The duo still have room for improvement and experimentation. Will they take it to the next level? It remains to be seen. Will it be another five years until they release their third album? Will there even be a third album? It remains to be seen. They have strong potential to become as classic as, say, New Order, or, Pet Shop Boys, or Thompson Twins, etc.

I liked "Ice On The Dune". I like Empire Of The Sun. I like that they are Australian. I like my Australian artists such as Icehouse, Midnight Oil, Savage Garden, Men At Work, Inxs, Olivia Newton-John, Bee Gees, AC/DC, The Church, Kylie Minogue, Air Supply, Cut Copy, Architecture In Helsinki, Models, etc. I wish there were more.

"Ice On The Dune" is worth purchasing if you already like the band, or if you like electronic/New Wave music, and you want something new.

I know Bryan Adams is considered a light weight in the music business, but the facts remain that he is able to continually make good pop standards. Reckless is a great disc--it has 6 hits "One Night Love Affair",  "Run To You", "Heaven", "Somebody", Summer of  '69" and "It's Only Love." How many records today can boast  that many hits? The music on Reckless has a nice, airy feel to it. It's  uplifting even when the messages are downbeat. It holds a place in my  childhood because I was 12 when it was released in 1984. However, it has  stood the test of time too. Reckless is a great addition to any rock  collector's music collection.

After a 12 year absence, Level 42 return with "Retroglide". Right now it's an import only in the United States, but the import has 11 tracks and is 56 minutes in length. Mark King is the principal band member this time out, with augmentation by his son, Nathan King, Lyndon Connah, Sean Freeman and Gary Husband on drums from 1991's "Guaranteed" and 1988's "Staring At The Sun". Original members Mike Lindup and Boon Gould also make appearances, mainly Lindup on keys and backing vocals on four tracks and Boon sharing song writing duties with King on all 11 tracks, plus a guitar solo on the song "Ship".

That said, if you are a Level 42 fan thinking about what this album sounds like, then I can tell you that it's a mixture of stuff dating back to their debut 1981 album, "Level 42" and blending in some "Running In The Family"/"Staring At The Sun" elements with a new, improved, contemporary sound for today's listeners.

In fact, "Retroglide" goes a long way to make up for the lackluster 1994 album "Forever Now" and even "Guaranteed". This is a stronger, wiser, refreshed Level 42, custom made for their fans who've stuck around these 26 years. The musicianship is top notch, of course, but what about the songs?

Well, that's where I give "Retroglide" three stars. Although the band is back on track, and definitely making a move in the right musical direction, there are only a handful of classics here. By far, the best track is "The Way Back Home" at nearly seven minutes, it has some of the best lyrics and the most memorable melody of the 11 tracks. After that, there are several other good songs like "Dive Into The Sun", "Rooted", "Just For You" and "Sleep Talking" (which I'd pick as another single). The back half of the album isn't nearly as sharp. "Retroglide" and "All Around" aren't too bad, but "Clouds", "Hell Town Story", "Ship" and the bonus track "All I Need" are just average in my not so humble opinion.

So, if like me, you own all of Level 42's work, "Retroglide" will make a nice addition to your collection. If you are new to Level 42 I'd start with "Gold" and decide from there if you are a hardcore fan. After that, check out "Level 42", "World Machine" and "Running In The Family".

I remember when MTV began in August of 1981, and I remember this video well. I was 8 at the time, and this cd holds a special place in my collection. It's a quirky, novel mix of pop music that is better than  average of the music at that time. Released in 1979, this cd sounds a bit  ahead and behind it's time. It's has the classic hit "Video Killed the  Radio Star" but is also has the forethought of the  breast-implant/plastic surgery craze of the 80's and 90's in "Living  in the Plastic Age." Another song "Clean, Clean" displays a  punk/new wave bravado. "I Love You, Miss Robot" is an interesting  synth ambient stab. It's a must have for any rock collector just for the  novelty value alone. It's also interesting to note that Trevor Horn  (vocals) has gone on to produce cds by Yes, Frankie Goes To Hollywood, ABC,  Rod Stewart, Seal, Simple Minds, Art of Noise and Grace Jones. Geoffry  Downes (keyboards) went on to Asia (and is still with that band!).

users.query: My wife is a big fan of the Rabbit wine opener (I prefer cork pullers), so as expected she loves this wine preserver system.  We normally use non-vacuuming bottle stoppers, which only do so much good.  The ability to suck out most of the air has a noticeable effect on how long the wine preserves its flavor.

cands.text:
This product gets the job done.  However, it's current price on Amazon is twice as high as that of the Metrokane 5575 Rabbit Wine Preserver with 2 Vacuum Stoppers.  The Swissmar is plastic, and visibly so.  The Rabbit is stainless steel and just generally looks betters.  Same goes for the stoppers.

On a neutral note, the Swissmar sucks from the interior of the stopper, whereas the Rabbit vacuum device envelopes the top of the stopper.

The only advantage to the Swissmar product over the Rabbit is the champagne stopper.  It seems, however, based on other reviews, that this doesn't prevent the CO2 from escaping the champagne.

Took a while to get used to the mouthpiece, but I now really like not having to open a lid to get to the water, and don't need to worry about a nozzle flipping open.  I was also worried that the design might be hard to clean, but I'm not having any problems keeping it clean.

The suction on this vacuum is not much weaker than our Hoover WindTunnel Pet Cyclonic, and the fact that the Dust Devil is so light makes it quite a bit easier to use (and makes it easier to tip over.)  Like our Hoover (and pretty much every vacuum I've owned), using the attachments for the hose results is greatly diminished suction.

The Dust Devil is not perfect, but it does well for typical household tasks.  Given the price point it deserves 5 stars.

This is a really great little vacuum bottle.  It keeps things hot for a very long time.  That being said, the colors of this particular unit aren't that attractive (subjectively to me and my wife.) As my wife put it, it looks like something you would get as a sales award from Mary Kay.

I really like this sprayer.  I much perfer it to the Ace ones I have.  Pressurizes easily, easy to carry around, and has a good choice of nozzles.  I use this one for lawn broadleaf control.  Perfect for the job.

The main feature of this product is the flexible straw at the end -- the usefulness and efficacy of WD-40 is well known.  The straw is made out of a light metal in interlocking segments, and bends easily without seeming to wear out (I don't feel any heat when I twist it quickly).  I will buy this version of WD-40  over the cans with the old red straws anytime I have the choice.  Flipping the applicator down puts it is spray mode as before.
Not the fanciest brush out there, but it is simple and gets the job done.

1) Viper Underground Steel Tip Darts: Celtic Blood, 22 Grams

3) Fat Cat Bulletz 90% Tungsten Steel Tip Darts with Storage/Travel Case, 23 Grams

These are best for a commercial kitchen.  The handles grip well and the blades are keen, although I haven't had them stand the test of time.  They do look industrial, and the parer and utility knives that I got weren't straight.

This unit was a replacement for my Garmin nuvi 200, and as such is a major upgrade.  The updated, and freely updatable maps are the biggest improvement.  I have found these maps to be quite accurate.  The unit also has a lot more little features and ways to put things on maps such as gas stations.  However, like the nuvi, the Tom Tom is far weaker than Google maps on my iPhone 3GS in terms of finding nearby places.

The biggest downside was relative ease of use.  Much of this I recognize is due to being accustomed to a Garmin, but the relative lack of screen brightness (even at maximum setting) and thinner map lines reduce readability compared to the the physically much smaller nuvi 200.

Other discontents are a much fancier mount that is in practice harder to move around and gives worse haptics to the unit than the much simpler nuvi mount.  I also liked that my nuvi turned on and off automatically when I started and stopped my engine.  The Tom Tom can be set to turn off with loss of power, but not automatically turned on.

The AccuBall is the same size as a lacrosse ball and is intended to be used in a manner similar to how lacrosse balls are currently used in strength and conditioning programs like CrossFit.  It is not a massager in the colloquial sense of the term.  Myofascial release involves some pain.  The goal is not pain relief directly, but rather flexibility and mobility.

As a product oriented towards individuals, I rate this product 5 stars.  I don't use the hand-held configuration, and don't see how you would get enough pressure that way to gain much benefit.  In the standard configuration, I found the ball to be much superior to a lacrosse ball because it is denser and hence harder, giving more of a dig when under pressure.  The ridges are also a nice touch, giving more control to how the ball rolls and perhaps even some sort of additional acupressure-type benefit.  The $15 difference between this and a $5 lacrosse ball is noise in the total cost of ones kit.

As a product oriented towards strength and conditioning gyms, such as a CrossFit box, price begins to matter.  In bulk the $15 difference per unit results in a factor of 4 increase in total costs.  I imagine that not having the reversible yellow core, but rather a single piece at the density of the black ridged material, would cost much less to make.  At $7-$8 a unit, I could see this becoming a replacement for the ubiquitous lacrosse ball.  But not at $20 a unit.

Firoozeh's story will resonate quite stongly with readers, Iranian or otherwise, who have shared some of these experiences, but also maybe with those who haven't.

users.query: Good story. The two lead actors are good actors creating believable people. For a low budget, limited audience film, the production values were pretty good. The story was  engaging and worth the watch.

cands.text: Clever plot. Amusing, and not overdone. The direction appears to be strong with pretty good casting. The story is very tongue in cheek humor. The lead actor is definitely a key to the film's success. Not all of the characters are likeable.

Entertaining, a little stagey as I expected it would be. The writing was very good. A few of the actors were too theatrical, which detracted from their character's  messages. The lead actor was outstanding. Worth a view.
Well done story about teen angst. The two lead actors are both very good actors which makes the plot entertaining and believable. This movie is easy to recommend.

Good special effects. The plot does not make the most sense. The lead actors tried very hard, I think, to make the story work. The film is worth a look to form your own opinion. No movie is all good or all bad, this one sure proves that theory.
Great fun between the actors translates to a  lighthearted story that is entertaining to watch. Not every movie has to have a heavy, deep story to be a good source of temporary amusement.
The story holds up. It was a good chance to view two outstanding actors of their time. I understand the ending was changed to appease the viewing audience and was not the original ending intended.

Disappointing. The film was written, directed and starred the same man. This was probably not the best idea, because the director was not the most objective about his lead actor's (himself) performance. Was the film autobiographical? Most of the actors were entertaining, but winey. The lead actress role was a little over acted, and this made the character somewhat irritating to this viewer.
Realistic dialogue.  Story could have been expanded. Character, others than they leads were pretty much one dimensional. Pleasant short film.

Good mix of humor and gay horror genre. Have seen movie previously and I wanted to own a copy. The casting was a good choice of actors. The movie does not appear to be low budget in technical choices of camera work, sound etc. This one deserves a view to form your own opinion.

Clever story with an imaginative plot. Matt Damon was well cast and believable. The special effects were plausible and not over done. The direction was tight and effective. I watched this one twice, it was that good. I saw things the second viewing that I had missed the first time. Easy to see why this one was considered one of the best for 2015.

Well done with excellent performances by the two lead actors. My only complaint is that the audio was a little fuzzy in a few spots. This film was one of the best in this genre, I have viewed. There are many very poor gay themed films out there to view.

Amusing story with a certain appeal. The actors are a very capable bunch. The story has an appeal to gay and non gay viewing audience members. The late Mr. Reborn was a very good, believable character actor.
The drama camp owner  is very over acted, and it tends to bring the simple plot down somewhat. Otherwise the movie is amusing and moves along quickly. Good looking young cast.
This must have been a made for television feature in Great Britain. Story was very predictable, acting was adequate. Not a complete waste of time.

Entertaining. The movie was entertaining, though it does get a little too slapstick at times. The casting was good, it was nice to see Mr. Statham in something lighter for a change. Miss McCarthy is a talented actress. The movie does leave itself open for sequels.

The author does a very good of bringing two very different people together. As in any relationship, there has to be a lot of growth between the two people especially when they start so far apart from one another. There are very strongly described sex scenes which most readers should enjoy.  There is a good flow to the storytelling. Give this one a read.

Good story. Some of the dialogue is somewhat unbelievable. This almost reads like a romance novel for women. Not a very creative effort by the author. Predictable plot.

.

Well done movie, with an interesting story. It has an ending that might surprise you. All of the actors are well cast, with the exception of the actress that portrays the mother. She is miscast, and her character over acts and is not believable. Thankfully she does not ruin the whole movie. Give the movie a chance.
What a waste of film. Acting is very poor and the plot makes no sense. If the goal of a movie is to entertain, this one misses that goal by miles.

Book is engaging and well put together. The author made the story rather wordy and lengthy. I feel if the story had been  shorter it would not have taken anything away from the story. Characters were well drawn and interesting. You will not be able to read quickly thru this one.

Good story. The main characters are sharply drawn and well described to the reader. Future sequels will probably define the characters even more. There are vivid descriptions of Chicago which add to the color of the story. This is the first sexless, gay mystery I think I have read. The plot was developed well.

Well done book. I guess it was from a first time author, who has not done anything else yet. The story is done with a lot of heart. The two main characters are different and easily grab your interest. The plot developed in an area few people probably don't have much exposure to in their lives. At first the two people parallel closely two real guys who were well known in this genre in real life but then things go in an entirely different direction. The ending is a surprise but wholly satisfying for the reader. Since the author appears to have expertise in this area, another novel in this subject would also be good reading.

Surprised with abrupt ending. Todd Young' s short books are not for every reader, they are graphic and usually focused on only one area within the story. Sometimes they cut off too soon in my opinion, like with this one. The author has a good feel for how the (usually) teen characters really talk to one another. This is not an outstanding writer, but a pretty good one

users.query: This is the style of filter that fits my fridge, so of course, that's what I buy.  But I can say that I have never gotten a filter that didn't work properly, or otherwise presented a problem.  It lives up to the GE name.

cands.text: I bought this filter to get a break on the cost.  The price of big-name filters is ridiculous.  These filters seem to work well, and I would buy the brand again.

It seems that fridge filters have shot up unbelievably in price.  I tried this bargain brand as a substitute for the big-name brands, and it seems to work well.  Certainly, the water tastes as good as before.  But unless you're a chemist, you won't know how the water compares in actual quality.  If you're getting your water from a reputable city supply, my guess is, you'll likely be safe.  (But I'm no expert.)
I ordered this to descale my coffee-maker.  It works well and is easy to use.  I plan to use it to descale other household items.

I have an air cleaner that has this type carbon pad as a pre-filter.  I've found that replacing the carbon pad often really adds to the air cleaner's ability to reduce odors.  The price on this carbon pad is so reasonable, there's really no excuse not to replace it often.  I highly recommend it.

This is the first time I've used the Filtrete Home Odor Reducer Filter, so I was wondering how effective it would be.  It seems to do a very good job of freshening the air in the house.  In these winter months, we need a "breath of fresh air."  I'm sure the freshening effect will diminish as the charcoal becomes saturated, but that will be an incentive to change the filter on the recommended basis -- rather than waiting until it "looks bad."  (The mfg. says the filter lasts for up to three months.)

Filtrete is a name I trust, and these Dust and Pollen Filters live up to expectations.  Unlike with bargain filters, the cardboard frame doesn't bend and buckle when you maneuver the filter into place.  And the filter material seems to effectively clean the air as it passes through.

The TrueAir air filter is a small, handy, fan-driven unit you can use anywhere you have a power outlet.  I've had two for years.  Recently, I ordered this special pet-odor version of the replacement filter.  I can't honestly say it differs from the usual carbon filter, but it works well at cleaning and freshening the air -- pets or no pets.  (In my opinion, carbon is the key to freshening.  As long as a filter has that, I'm happy.)

I've only had my air cleaner for a couple of days, but it seems to do an excellent job.  I wanted to write this review now, however, because I had an encounter with the Customer Service folks at Vornado that was very impressive.  The Vornado unit has several filters, and I had a problem with the simplest of them -- the "permanent filter."  I could not get it properly installed, despite reading the instruction booklet carefully.  (It turns out the booklet is written primarily for the 300 model, so all the illustrations are misleading if you have a 500 model.  The respective filter configurations are significantly different.)  Stumped, I called the Vornado Customer Service number and talked with an extremely helpful young man.  Since he was looking at the same instruction booklet I was, he was equally stumped.  He said he would go get one of the Model 500 units and see if he could figure out the problem.  After an hour or so, he called me back and proudly announced he had found the answer!  Then he stayed with me on the phone as I re-installed the filter.  I couldn't have asked for better service.  I would give the Vornado company an A+, but they lose points for not printing a proper instruction manual.  The Model 500 is different enough from the 300 to deserve its own manual.  I made the error I did because I followed the illustrations in the booklet, which are entirely of the 300.  Still, the PCO500 seems like an excellent product and I look forward to using it for a good long while.
This spout exactly matches the spout I was removing.  Essential, since it must match the existing plumbing configuration.  The quality is good, and installation was trouble-free.

I bought this item because all my spray attachments leaked -- no matter how much I paid for them.  This takes care of the problem handily ... I just installed it between my hose nozzle and spray attachment. Now I can shut off the hose without going back to the faucet.  The convenience is worth the small cost.

These Febreze filters -- for the True Air fan -- do an efficient job of cleaning the air.  The fan is fairly small, so it's not intended for freshening large spaces.  But its size means you can tuck it into those spots where you need some instant air-cleaning.  For example, it's great to keep by the stove when you're cooking.  Your range hood may draw out air, but it doesn't remove odors.  The charcoal in the Febreze filter will make quick work of that for you.  One of the best things about the fan is that it plugs directly into an electrical outlet -- sort of like a very large night light.  Thus it takes up little space and can easily be moved from one spot to another, as needed.  I've had my two for years, and I'd hate to be without them.

I bought this four-way key so I would be sure and get the right size for my faucet.  I figured that between the four of them, one size would have to fit.  I was wrong.  The two small sizes are too small, and the two large sizes are too large.  You'd think American plumbing would be pretty standardized by now, but apparently it isn't.  It's too late to return the item, so I'll just write it off as a bad buy.  But quite honestly, I don't know what I would have done differently.  I don't have a clue as to how to measure the size of my faucet.  So I guess it will be just me and my pliers from here on out!  (P.S. -- I gave the product three stars because I assume the manufacturer made it properly.  I just made a mistake by believing that a four-way key would fit pretty much any standard domestic faucet.)

This little coffee maker is OK, but it really doesn't get the most out of the coffee pod.  The water lazily trickles through, so the result is a bland cup of coffee.  But for those who like bland coffee, the machine works fine.  It's fast and easy to use.

Some time back I ran into an offer of free samples of Barista Prima Coffeehouse Coffee.  When the samples arrived, I fell in love with the brand.  It's rich and delicious.  Now, it's what I use on a regular basis.  Had I not had the samples, I would never have known that this brand I had never heard of would be a stand-out.  It's just a great product for people who love a rich, full-bodied coffee.

Some time back I ran into an offer of free samples of Barista Prima Coffeehouse Coffee.  When the samples arrived, I fell in love with the brand.  It's rich and delicious.  Now, it's what I use on a regular basis.  Had I not had the samples, I would never have known that this brand I had never heard of would be a stand-out.  It's just a great product for people who love a rich, full-bodied coffee.
If you need a quick iced tea, this works well.  Not as good as conventionally made iced tea, but good if time is the issue.
If you hate weak, bland coffee, you'll like this brew.  It has that pure coffee flavor that you expect, but often don't get in common commercial brands.

Boy, the black pepper really adds a zingy touch to this old favorite.  I've always liked Spam, despite its non-glamorous reputation.  (For me, it just needs to be brought to life with a quick zap in the microwave, rather than served cold.)  So it was a treat to find that the liberal addition of cracked black pepper truly kicks things up a notch taste-wise.  It's like that's what Spam has been waiting for all its life -- the perfect spice accompaniment.  And black pepper is it.  Don't worry that the Spam will be too "hot."  Unlike red pepper, black pepper is not about delivering "heat."  It just adds a spicy nip to the taste buds.  If you like Spam, I think you'll like the black-pepper version.

The blurb for this tape touts it as being good for a variety of heavy-duty repairs, including plumbing fixes.  I tried it for the latter, and it simply didn't work.  It failed to create a seal, so the water just poured past it.

Since I've got it, I'll probably try it for other repairs ... perhaps it will work for something that doesn't involve water.  Or perhaps I didn't use it right, but I read and followed the instructions.

An earlier reviewer said he wished he'd used this glue earlier, instead of the cheap kind.  I feel the same way.  The glue gives a very sturdy, long-lasting bond.  And the dispenser is a huge improvement over the less expensive super glues.

These shoes are true to size and very comfortable.  They fit high up on the foot, so they're good for activities like shopping, where you don't want a shoe that's slipping up and down on your heel. I find myself choosing them often ... pretty, neat, but comfortable.

This little bag of charcoal is very handy and well-constructed.  The grommet makes it possible to hang the bag inside a closet and other out-of-the-way places.  Charcoal does a great job of freshening an area.

This fudge struck me as a bit bland.  I guess with the words "clotted cream" in the name, I expected a distinct flavor ... and certainly something rich.  It's like it's missing something fundamental.  Now that I think about it, the taste reminds me of a dish that the cook has forgotten to put the salt in.  It's that kind of bland.  (It seems that without the salt, none of the other flavors in the dish come to the fore.)
Many may enjoy this fudge, but to me, any run-of-the-mill American fudge would offer a more exciting taste experience.
This is delicious coffee, and extremely quick and convenient to prepare.  In less than a minute, you have a brew that's fresh, aromatic, and rich in flavor.

cands.text:
I don't know whether it is the Kindle format or my newer version Kindle or what but reading this book is a challenge.
The books skips from one place to another and I have to really work at find my way back to where I was.
Furthermore, the author gets us bogged down with enormous amounts of tedious trivia about the trek the Americans are basically force marched on as they try to get out of that Albanian hell hole.
There are too many forgettable characters about whom we learn too much.
I would have liked to have learned more about the women....just a couple of nurses get most of the attention and, similarly, just a few of the men are focused upon. There were thirty people in this hapless group but we know very little about most of them and how they fare during this experience.
The story IS a good one but I wish it were better told.

My local store used to carry this delicious juice which is 100% Organic Grape Juice but recently stopped carrying it so I am  thrilled to find it here.

Read this book out of curiosity....trying to decide whether or not to buy it for my pre-teen grandchildren whom I am trying to educate about the horrors of Nazi Germany, Hitler, and WW2.
I had thought I would simply peruse it as a Sample in my Kindle but quickly bought the book for myself.
Now I will buy the hardcover for my grandchildren to pass around.
For a Young Reader book, it was riveting with unexpected twists and turns with touches of humor yet with a serious approach to the subject of pure evil.
I particularly appreciate that the author did not feel like he had to use bad language or racy, sexual, scenes in an attempt to pull in today's youth.
This is simply a very fine book and I recommend it highly.

An amazing book, actually.  The book taken from his letters home and notes/journal he kept during the last year of the war from Normandy to the Battle of the Bulge.
I've read quite a few similar books over the past few years and this is one of the best as the reader is drawn in and captivated by the author and his buddies; although we realize, of course, that the author survives the war, we become concerned for his friends and buddies as he describes them and are saddened when some of them are killed.
Raymond Gantter was a good, decent man who tried to withhold judgement when witnessing terrible behavior; although he does not let the Nazi atrocities off the hook at all, he is compassionate toward the German people during and after the war....to a point.
As the atrocities of the Holocaust and stories of  slavery and forced labor are uncovered, he takes a harder view toward the German citizen.
He is less lenient toward the U.S. military officers who often showed themselves to be selfish, self indulgent, inept and even brutish.
My only complaint about the book is that I would have liked to have known more about the author's life after the war---as he reestablished his little family that he missed so terribly.  Some photos would have been appreciated as there are none, at least in the Kindle version.

Even if you don't enjoy Beatrix Potter's precious, timeless characters, you should still relish this beautifully done set of DVDs based on her classics.
Every, single aspect of these DVDs perfectly subscribes to the original stories.
The musical score is particularly well done.
Highly recommend.

I don't know what to say about this "period" piece. By "period" I mean ----so Seventies; is Neo feminism the term I'm searching for?
The young heroine is determined to have it her way but she's all over the place regarding what it is she wants.
She says she never wants to marry but then she says she'll only marry for "love" and then she falls in love with a great guy who loves her and what does this girl do?  Trade it all in for her brilliant career.
Don't know how autobiographical the story actually is but it made me mad.
Acting was great.

I have feet problems.
Nothing serious but they do tend to hurt occasionally. There is nothing worse than aching feet.
This little shoe is just awesome. It is light weight yet supportive and I can bounce around all day long in them and my feet don't get tired and "sad".
In a word, these shoes give me Happy Feet.
I'm buying quite a few pairs because as sure as God made little green apples, TEVA ---will sooner or later----- stop making them.

Found this book to be very compelling and hard to put down. Reads fast and the reader is pulled along wondering who is going to live and who is not in this horrible accident.
My only question is why the author's family ----who had been associated with the train wreck ------had never mentioned it to him or each other.
I thought perhaps there was some sort of a mystery attached but there was not nor was it cleared up why the family never discussed such a catastrophic event that occurred in their neighborhood and affected, at the very least, the author's ancestor.
I still give the book Five Stars for being well written and moving.

Frankly, nothing can possibly beat the Original TEVA Mush Flip-Flop.
I've worn them for years and they are my standard summertime footwear.
Although I am a woman, I like to get the Men's as they seem to be a bit more "Mushy" than the Women's.
Sometimes I put them in the washing machine to get them good and clean and that also plumps them up a bit.
Not with hot water, however.

cands.text: This is a fabulous tribute to someone she must love greatly. And I adore it. I like to think he heard them along with me in the van on my recent road trip and knew I was thinking of him. I thank her muchly for this absolutely gorgeous paean to true love..
