users.query: If you like the movie Pretty Woman you will love Legal Ease.  The characters were likable, the story line flowed easily and there was your happy ending.  Will I read the rest in the series?  I don't know.  But I would recommend Legal Ease to anyone who wants a nice story with a happy ending.

cands.text: What can I say. I love the story. Yes it is a lot on the Pretty Woman side but it still has an essence of its own. This is my first time reading this author and I feel she is now in my group of gotta read her stuff. You feel what the characters are feeling. You understand why something is happening. It was easy to get caught up in and wanting more. Not just more steamy parts but more of the story and what happens next. So since I do want more it's on to book two in the series.

A Charming Crime was a light feel good read. Nothing heavy or overly dramatic. Just a good start to introduce some interesting characters and a girl learning about her past and special gifts she has been given.

I won't even call this a book.  It is the first 12 chapters of a book and not even enough character or story development to make me to read the rest let alone buy the rest.  There is no resolution of any sort at the end.  Usually a series has an ending of one part of a story and you like that story and the characters so much you want to read what happens next to them. I am still seeking justice for those killed in the plane wreck because all this book did was let you know there was a crime which you get in the title and synopsis.  So read those two things and you have read this book.

Legal Affairs is a book I could not put down.  It is VERY sexy, intelligent and just plain good.  At first I was reading a de ja vu.  Matt and McKayla have what is suppose to be a one night stand and then they are thrown together in a situation where their worlds collide.  I literally had just read another story that began like that (it only got 4 stars).  But the author brings you in as if you are Mac's friend as she tells her story.  I hate stories where the female lead becomes stupid in her actions.  Never fear, Mac is anything but stupid.  She is smart and does what is best for both physically and emotionally.  She is strong.  She accepts her flawed soulmate but will only take so much.  Matt is probably my new favorite alpha male.  He knows what he wants and goes for it.  He is also very likable and is so much a man.  It may take him a while to get the picture emotionally but when he does, watch out.  I can't wait to read more by this author.

I found the authors lack of follow through to be Positively Criminal.  When I purchased this book there was no indication that is was book 2 in a series.  So when you start reading you already feel like you missed out on something.  Once you figure out that you aren't confused the story starts to pull you in.  Then the story stalls.

The story was nothing new.  Boy and girl have the hots for each other and play cat and mouse.  When they do hook up there are lots of dirty words and description but nothing that makes the reader go, "Yeah, they are finally together."

As I continued to get disappointed with the story I started to see how ludicrous and unbelieveable things were.  Seriously, Dr. Miller gives lap dances in her spare time.  She is so good she teaches other girls how to do them and make money.  Yet she feels the need to wear a wig and contacts as a disguise.

This story could have gone so many ways that would have been more interesting but didn't.

Burglary Blue was just the ticket I was looking for. I want something that was a quick read but had enough meat to make me want more. This is the first in a 3 book series. There was a decent suspenseful story line but it had opportunity to be a bit more. I found Lexie and Micheal to be likable characters. The authors did a good job with making them real. Many times in stories such as this the characters are hum drum and boring. I found the characters to be real humorous at times and really caring about each other. I just hope the other stories allow them to grow and the suspense gets fattened up.

As this is the last in the series I am reviewing the story as a whole. The first two "books" in the series captured the attention of the reader. You want to know more about the characters and root for them. Then there are sections where you are thinking oh no don't go there. And since you got them for free you are forced to buy the ending. This is a great marketing ploy. Still of the 3 books Book 3 wasn't as intriguing as the first 2.  Shining Star make the story go from a steamy will they or won't they suspense to a somewhat romantic less steamy yeah we know this is a HEA ending. When the author wrote about the Oscars it was almost like she realized she didn't know hoe to wrap the story up. I feel she should have ended the story there and put in an epilogue instead of trying to recapture the steamy chemistry of the characters.

When I first started reading this book I was a little concerned about the theme of the book.  But the author was able to get me interested and keep me wanting to find out what happens next. She also tied in the previous story/book without you needing to know what the first story truly was all about.  I can also say Ms. Rasey did her research.  As well as providing an interesting read she also provided insight and reason to some lifestyles and acts that many may consider taboo.  I recommend this book.

When I first started reading this book I was a little leary as the first couple of pages were a little strange.  But once you get pasted the prologue be prepar for a thrill ride.  I became obsessed with the characters and wanting to know what was going to happen next.  I recommend this book for those who like romantic suspense.

I was only going to give this story 2 stars but the who done it plot twist earned an OK rating for the story.  I have read other books by Ms. Marton and found Broslin Bride not to be in the same category as her other works.

If you are looking for something that is smokin' hot then this is not the story for you.  There wasn't any grand love story unfolding.  There wasn't a great action adventure or suspense yet I couldn't not finish it.  The characters are just normal people.  There are unsuspected heroes.  I don't think I will be getting the other 2 books in the trilogy as this story was so every day.  I like to read books that provide the excitement and emotions of what you wish you had not of what you already have.

I liked it enough to purchase the rest of the series.  This story had me hooked.  I thought I knew who the killer was before the characters did but I was wrong.  This does not happen often.  If the story didn't end so abruptly I would have probably given it 5 stars.

After reading Playing with Fire all I could say was Wow.  I couldn't wait for Trial by Fire.  Trial by Fire is a good story and a sexy read but it didn't keep me as engaged as Playing with Fire.  The "suspense" was easily solved but the twist and turns the characters had to take still left you with the tension of wanting to know what happens next.

Ms. Lee let us see a little deeper into Nate as well as let him grow.  Erin on the other hand was a little stagnate.  She was stood by her man but her Wonder Woman behaviors left me a little angry with her.

Although this is probably the first Taylor Lee book that I haven't given 5 stars, I still cannot wait for the next installment of the All Fired Up series and other books authored by Taylor Lee.

I loved book 4 of the series and had high hopes for book 5.  The author did not  have to put in the suspense and intrigue.  The story was great with getting to know the characters as average people.  I was all excited with the idea of a spontaneous wedding.  That is what Luke and Anabel are all about.  But to end the story the way it did was very disappointing.  We don't know how Anabel got to the mansion, what happened, or get to see her Dark Prince ride in on his stallion to save her.  If it was meant to be funny because Anabel is getting something she never wanted, it wasn't. There isn't even a tease that there will be more to come.  I had such high hopes for this book and Tracy Ellen you let me down.

I was quite disappointed with this book.  Ms. Grace could have ended it after reading about 30% to 40% of the book.  That is when she revealed who the killer was.  You could tell the Ms. Grace was grasping at straws by trying to use every successful crime T.V. show's gimmick.  We have CSI, Criminal Minds and Law and Order.  The characters had no real depth.  There was very little chemistry between Jennifer and Blake.  The ending was very predictable.  And please, tell me since when do law enforcement officers use the term STAT.  Being a nurse that really began to bug me.  I am really glad this is where the trilogy ends because I don't think Ms. Grace could pull another one out.  There are no more TV shows to mimmick.

Not What She Seems was a good easy read.  By the time I was 50% through I couldn't put it down.  It reminded me a lot of my two favorite movies, Pretty Woman and Cinderella.  The author draws you in by letting you believe that if a woman with all the baggage that Emily had can land a billionaire then there is hope for the rest of us.

The characters are likeable.  The author did a good job in throwing suspicion from one person to the next.  There was  anticipation of would Emily and Steven get together.  But when they did it was a little anticlimactic.  Sparklers fizzled but there weren't no big fireworks.

I found the ending to be VERY disappointing.  I wanted more.  The reader is left hanging high and dry.  I thought to myself, that's it?  Where is the wrap up; the epilogue?  Did Conner get his dinosaur for Christmas.  Did Steven and Emily move to Nebraska and live happily ever after?  How did Steven's parents like Emily. I guess the writer wanted the read to fill in the blanks.

This is the first book I have read by this author let alone the series.  Where the story was good, I mean really what girl doesn't like weddings, I always felt that I didn't know the people involved.  I was the AND guest someone brought as a date.

Then just as I thought I was getting to know Nick and Sam, the story ended.  I don't know if I will go back and read the stories leading up to this one. I already know the outcome of the relationship.

Material Witness was a nice easy read. Where I was curious about who was doing bad things, I can't say it was edge of your seat suspense.  What stood out for me was how the author built the emotions of the characters.  From the first attraction to the final (well let's not give it away)I felt how the characters felt.  Ms. Mondello did something that no other author has done in a while, at one point I had a few tears in my eyes and 1 or 2 actually escaped.  So if you want to read a book with true emotional I would recommend Material Witness.

I am writing this based on all 5 books in the series because they flow together so well and each one provides such a intricate piece to the story that you can't not think of one book without thinking of the next part.  I think it is important to say that this is the first time I have ever read a series of books with the topic of BDSM being part of the story.  The way that Ms. Blackstone doesn't focus on the "kink" it is just there and part of what the characters like.  Yes there are times that I would say to myself "really" or let's move one but the BDSM is not what the story is about at all and should not put the reader off from purchasing this series.

So with that being said I found the Liliana Batchelor series to provide a great story line about learning to trust someone that you love.  Stuart is such a powerful character in everything he does but that is also his undoing.  Lily is not a push over.  She is a strong independent woman who knows what she wants and will fight like hell to get it.  Still they both have flaws act as barriers to their relationship.

Lily has 2 flaws, she runs away when times are tough and her biggest flaw is getting angry with Stuart because he "makes" her do something both in life and in the bedroom.  Lily tends to forget she can say no.  But instead she does it and then turns and gets mad angry with Stuart saying things such as "How could you."  If you read book 5 the scene at the Pavilion during her friends wedding is a perfect example.

Stuart doesn't like to share unless it is on his terms. Don't get me wrong he is a giver but it  is on his terms only.  Others have stated how they disliked Stuart becoming dark and twisted in books 4 and 5.  Ms. Blackstone does an excellent job in the end explaining this character flaw and why it happen.

I would have like to have read more about how Stuart and Lily put the past behind them and how their playtime changed after all was said and done with the demons of Stuart's past.  Stuart stated that the "scenes" he was doing with Lily were cathartic and based on what he did or would do with Megan.  Ms. Blackstone then writes how Stuart and Lily learned how to make scenes that was theirs and not someone else's.  I feel if some of the description of the country side or if the first 7 chapters of book 5 wasn't about a "scene" to make Megan jealous (seriously that was a little long) there would have been time in the book to write about how the relationship changed.  All the reader knows is in the end, love prevailed which is expected in a story about romance and love.

I couldn't wait to get to the end of this book.  Of all of the Edgars Series this one was my favorite.  I found Luke and Abby to be the most real of all of the Edgars characters.  The story kept me engaged.  I wanted to know how they were going to figure out the crime.  And they did it without the clue that was left for them.  It was nice to see the female character making the first "physical" connection.  We don't always have to wait for the male to make a move.  And where the crime was horrific, there wasn't too much time spent on that but on how they were able to solve it and work together as a team.  I really hate to see this series end but I will continue with other of Ms. Ferrell's series because her writing is smart and entertaining.

If you like the movie Sweet Home Alabama you will love this book.  Kit didn't know what she really wanted in life.  And when she saw it was right in front of her for the taking sparks fly.  The suspense wasn't on the edge of your seat suspenseful but I will say I didn't expect the twist of it.  This was a great get lost in a romance story.

Eyes of Jade is packed with action while trying to figure out who done it.  But I would not have described it as a romantic suspense.

The story showed little sparks of attraction between Eve and Jake but I never felt any heat between the two.  As for romance, the things that Jake did for Eve as a big tough FBI agent was more of him being a gentle giant rather than a romantic man.

The writing is good but as I was reading it I found plenty of opportunities where the author could have weaved all of the relationship material that she saved for the end.  Perhaps if she had I wouldn't feel as disappointed in the book.

The best way to describe this story is Will & Grace meets Ghost Whisperer.  I found Ghostly Interests to be a little like a young adult / teen novel.  There was no real suspense and every character in the book talked about the chemistry between Harper and Jared but I just didn't feel it.  Harper has a gift that seemingly makes her an unhappy person.  She is an Eyore.  Negative, no real happy thoughts and in need of an antidepressant.  She has a sexy cop that is willing to accept her, her baggage and meddling friends.  Yet she remains flat.  If.  You are looking for a good suspense.  Look elsewhere.  I will say I was a little surprise of who "dunnit."  But there wasn't enough of a story line revolving around the mystery that made me want to care.

I have studied many items in order to be prepared for this exam.  CCM Certification Made Easy is the best of all of them.  There really is no need to go through and highlight passages because Ms. Cooper Gillingham only wrote the information needed for the test.  Another praise for the author is that I found out 2 weeks before I took the CCM that the format and blue print of the test was changed.  There was nothing available to assist with this change.  Yet Ms. Cooper Gillingham pulled together her 2nd edition and I now feel confident that I succeeded with the changes that were made.  Along with the book Ms. Cooper Gillingham and her partner provide you a website with a workbook and tip sheets and a Community Forum on Facebook to provide you with support and answer questions. .  I have told many staff and co-workers this is the book to get to prepare for on of the most important exams of your career.

Where Forever, Please didn't have the steaminess of the earlier books and the drama was significantly less, it was written the way an ending to a series should end. Everything was tied up and you didn't have any questions of what happened next. I was pleased with the ending and felt content with the life that Hunter and Olivia ended with.

The series showed how the relationship evolved and how the past effects the future but in the end a great partnership can get you a HEA.

users.query: These Rice Puffs are great to have with plain yoghurt, or milk, sweeten with a little rice syrup, or honey and you have a healthy breakfast with no additives. Add some berries and a truly healthful breakfast is in your bowl. I will be buying these regularly.

cands.text: I like these very much, having them every day for breakfast. Were they cheaper, I would enjoy them even more.
This is perfect for my purpose. Take one half cup of Bob's Red Mill Oat Groats, from Amazon, add one cup boiling water and seal.. 12 hours later you have the perfect breakfast.

We cannot eat wheat pasta, but enjoy macaroni. This product is the tastiest, best looking and best cooking rice macaroni we have ever found.  We used to buy a ready made, from the supermarket, but now have something very much better.

Yummy. That is the best description of them, but for those who like reading longer reviews I will try to expand it.
Soft, soggy, tasty, delicious, slices easily with a serrated knife, squashes without one. Dark, fruity, and Yummy.

I have kept these in cool storage, for over 2 years, and the quality has not deteriorated - I use them for MRE supplies, and keep varieties in my Emergency Prepared Storage. The price from Amazon is the best I have found anywhere. I will be purchasing more of these, to eat now, and to store for need.  The ingredients are:  Water, Potatoes, Chickpeas, Tomatoes, Onions, Sunflower oil, salt, ginger, garlic, cornstarch, coriander, chilies & cumin spices. 2 servings per sachet, 130 calories, 4g fat (0 trans fat) 0mg cholesterol, 530mg sodium, 19g carbohydrate, with 4g as fiber and 3g as sugars. 5g protein
Calories per gram - Fat 9; Carbohydrate 4; protein 4; these values make it good for pure balance diets.

Without a doubt these are the best sardines I have tried to date - we have a standing order in for these, and eat them many times a week for a quick luncheon.  Having them packed in water makes them much more palatable than those in olive oil from the same company.

The idea is wonderful - a press for juicing citrus - every home should have one. The reality is a little less cheery - it works, but after it has worked to it's greatest extent, you need to get out the old fashioned twist juicer, and get twisting.

The press takes less than half of the juice out of a standard size orange, the rest has to be on the twist juicer.. Not quite what I anticipated, but what juice it does extract is wonderful.
I have loved mushy peas for the last sixty years, even though the colouring added is quite scary.

One of the staples of my diet, and a regular purchase

Made my body behave oddly. I will not be buying them again.

The world is a risky place - often there are minor glitches in the power grid, that make life difficult; these can last weeks, so having some food put by to give sustenance in such times is a good idea.  These cans are good - the meat tastes great, the stock in the can tastes wonderful and I recommend these for anyone to have on hand, for the times the supplies run out in the stores. We have three months of food stored so should do ok, provided the Zombie invasion doesn't arrive and destroy civilisation, but then, why would I stay at home..

It looks like some cheap bit of plastic, with holes in strange places. I am a musician with way too many years behind me that did not include playing the Ocarina so...  I took the plunge and was amazed at what this little instrument toy can do. I can play about anything withing it's range of notes, it will allow for chromatic inflections, doesn't like to bend easily, like the whistles I perform with, but I reckon a better quality one may have promise. I am glad I bought it, because it is a great little instrument, with accurate pitch, intuitively easy to play, fun to mess around with and guaranteed to bring a smile to the face when you demonstrate that you can get exactly the same sound by moving three different fingers. Nothing else I play can do that so the novelty value is high. The finish of the mouthpiece left a lot to be desired, but two minutes with a craft knife got the manufacturing burrs of the hole. The burrs were not sharp, did not detract from the toy quality, but it looks better without them.
It does not help me - I am a tetraparesic spastic with hyperkinetic motion going on.
This item works well and is comfortable to play with. I am not yet proficient in playing a lap steel, so cannot give a glowing review, but for my novice hands, it makes playing easier.

This item is amazing - it fits my diminutive lady perfectly, looks awesome, and goes very well with the other Victorian Era Clothing she is so fond of. Very rapid dispatch, arrived in one week from the UK.
 Very recommended.

I had one of these fun instruments years ago, so was happy to get one now. The Amazon page showed a picture of a pull apart case for this item. Unfortunately, there was no case in the bubble pack, which was rather disappointing. However, the Little Lady is just as I remembered, with an octave of notes, that can play many tunes - I played for an hour, and amused my family with many tunes.

If you want a fun novelty, this Little Lady is perfect for the purpose - they are not awesome sounding harps - the pitch is high, the sound is small, but mine is in tune, and I can play any one octave tune on it - I have played one on stage, I used one in a tour, with twenty venues and it went down well. People like the instrument, and like seeing someone play a tune on it that they recognize. In the sixties, I busked in Britain with one these - with a dulcimer - I made sufficient money to live comfortably for the summer. Without the Little Lady, I made about half the money. I had made a holder for it, that worked pretty well - I need to make another.

Hopefully I can find a case for this item, as without one, it is very easy to lose it - just over an inch long and quarter inch wide and deep. There is a V shaped loop at the end, that will take a chain - I may attach a watch chain on it, to stop it going missing.

users.query: I liked this story, just not as much as liked the other books by Sellers that I've read. I thought the characters needed a little more development. The plot was great and it was fast moving in the second half of the book. Its definitely worth reading.

cands.text: This was an excellent novel. As in most series, the second is not quite as good as the first. Maybe it's because you already know the characters. The plot was great and had lots of twists and the book was very well-written. There were a few typos, but they didn't detract from the story. I would definitely read the next huntress book by Ms. Sokoloff.

This novel was excellent and an unusual mystery. The characters were wonderful and all the details made them feel very real. The plot was intricate and I really liked the writing style--very readable and not hurried. I look forward to the next book by this fantastic author.

This novel could have been better. The plot was very good, but the characters were flat. They had no personalities. I didn't hate it, but I can't really recommend it either. There are so many mystery authors that are really very good, some even excellent. It seems a shame to spend the time reading something that's just okay.
I liked this book but the first half was a little disorganized and really depressing. It got better and I liked the second half. The plot was good but I would have liked more depth to the characters.

I loved this book from the very first chapter to the very last sentence. The characters were wonderful as was the writing. It didn't feel like you were reading the story, more like you were living it. The settings (Boston area and Texas) were both described very well and the plots were excellent. I liked the way they were woven together. I have no complaints about this novel, but I hope P. M. Steffen writes fast because I can't wait for the next Sky Stone novel.

I liked this book but I thought it was unrealistic; there were way too many people that were way too nice. Also, I didn't like the writing style; it was as simplistic as the characters. The good news is that the story was okay; there was some suspense and it was a fast read.

I liked this novel, but the first half rambled around without much point. The second half was excellent. The characters were great and so was the plot once it got going. I recommend it and will read the next one to see if it's better.

This was a good novel with interesting characters and a good plot. There were a couple of typos, but nothing major and they didn't interrupt the story. The story built up slowly and nicely but the ending seemed a little rushed.

This was a good novel with a very unusual plot. I liked it but there were quite a few typos and grammar errors. They didn't interfere with the readability but it should have been edited before publishing. This is one of my pet peeves. Still, it was a decent read, but maybe not good enough to purchase the second book.

This was an interesting novel with a lot of things going on. Personally, I would have liked fewer characters and more about the characters. When I finished it, I couldn't remember most of their names; there were just so many, many with similar roles. I felt that the story was a little wordy; towards the end I wondered when it was going to end.

I really liked this book.  The characters were great and the suspense was fantastic. There's nothing bad that I could say about it, but for some reason it left me wanting more. More what, I'm not sure of. Maybe more passion from the characters, friends and neighbors. Everyone was too willing to accept the events.
I loved this book--great characters and lots of suspense. The surprising ending was fantastic. I will definitely read more books by this author.

Great novel. The plot was excellent and the characters were well defined and likeable. I especially liked chararcters from Jackson Hole, Wyomng. I couldn't find anything wrong with this novel, except that it could have been longer.

I really liked this novel. The characters were interesting and the plot was great but there were incidents and named characters that did nothing to further the plot. Some were introduced and then forgotten. As I read I thought they were important but they were never mentioned again. This was a minor fault and I recommend the novel for mystery lovers.

What a wonderful book! It was very well written and the characters were unforgettable. They were real people with flaws. This book touched my heart in so many ways. I feel as if I lived this story. I highly recommend this book. I would give it six stars if I could.

I really liked this book and Mr. Simmons is a great mystery author. His books are like a roller coaster ride. Put your cardiologist's number on speed dial. He lets you get to know his characters by having them meander around and interact and you think you've found the primary plot. But then he starts the gradual climb to the summit. Once you get there, he lets you see from the top and then the story moves so fast you can barely keep up with it. Thankfully in the last chapter he slows it down so you catch your breath and slow your heart rate. Wow! I can't wait for the next ride. Thank you, Mr. Simmons, for writing this novel.

I still love the character, Moe Prager.

cands.text:
Boring, tedious, and reads like a bad high school history book. I was really excited to start this one but was quickly disappointed. Way to broad in scope and with little depth due to the long history the author hopes to bring together. It also felt like at times that the author was trying to drop as many names and places as he possibly could. It all ran together.
I bought the Kindle version and of course the maps were at the end. Doesn't help when the author is going on and on about geography with no map to look at.

The last few chapters were better but it didn't save this one. Steer clear on this one.

I think this book deserves a review of the total work and the of the person being written about.

I think the author presented the life of Wallis Simpson without bias and to the point. I have two critiques though:

1. The repeated speculation about her sexuality and possible sexual disfunction. I personally found this part of the book to be very suspect. If you don't know that this person had these issues, is it right to go on and on about them? No facts were present except people looking at pictures of her and trying to make determinations.

2. After WWII, the last 40 years of her life is wrapped up in 30 pages. Did she not do anything during that time?

Finally a quick comment about Mrs Simpson and Edward VIII. Usually when I read biographies, I'm interested the person being written about and I take for granted that they are people with flaws and strengths. To be blunt, I would never want to meet either of these people in real life. Childish, petty, superficial, etc would be words to describe them. Always complaining about money and jewels seemed to be the big things in their lives. To that end they seem well suited for each other. I think they got what they deserved after choosing to get married. Simpson can be excused for the first husband who beat her. The second husband got the complete shaft. She cheats on him with the King and runs him into the ground and then still has the nerve to be friends with him. Mrs. Simpson would have been a perfect character on the Real Housewives show.

Fascinating book. I think it was better than his first book. Religion, philosophy, history, biology are all explored in this opus to the future of humanity.

The author has many ideas about what will happen but does preface that these are only possibilities.

His two books should be read at all universities across the county and studied. It's that good.

Excellent book. I found myself at times thinking this is exactly what happens at my house. Several reviews stated that this was written for women but I never thought that for a minute. Also several reviews stated that the woman in the scenarios set up were the only ones who had to make changes to the relationships they were involved in. I reject that 100% of the time as well.
Lots of good ideas and suggestions. I especially enjoyed the Star Trek reference at the end.

This was an excellent book. Interesting story and with an unusual timeline for most of the book.  The characters were developed very well and the descriptions of things and places was really well done. Just enough but not too much.
The only issue was the very end of the book. I wish there had been a bit more closure.
Five stars for sure.

A complete look at Charles Lindbergh. The writing is steady throughout with the author keeping his opinions to himself.

I think one of the most interesting things about the book is the public's fascination with Lindbergh for so many years. From the flight to the kid napping and through WWII the press was at times relentless.

I also enjoyed how an introvert in childhood was thrust into the limelight with his historic flight. For the rest of his life it seemed that he was trying to get away from the rest of the world. Always building a house or a remote jungle to visit later in life looking for simpler times.

The only other issue I found was the lack of closure for the rest of the family after Charles' death. What happened to his wife and kids? Charles died and that was it. Probably could have been a few pages about the rest of them too.

Recommend

This was a great book. Sometimes with memoirs they end up becoming brag fests about how great the person was or all the things they accomplished. This is not the case with Kate Mulgrew.

She lays it all out in this one and boy does she have some stories to tell. It was hard to put down and I learned a lot about her.
The only complaint with the book is that it stopped in 2000. What has been happening since then?

Highly recommend.

This one started slowly and then got into a good rhythm. I thought the book was going to review the secrets that the president was receiving but it was actually about the book itself and how each president liked the daily brief prepared.

The book is dry and probably geared towards a political junky or someone involved with intelligence.

Every time I read a "classic" I'm always disappointed for a variety of reasons. This one suffered from a lack of character development for sure. There was no connection. There could have been but there wasn't. Maybe that's what the author was going for because the premise of the book is how uniform all the people of earth have become because of the new order. They take pills to feel happy and have relationships just for the heck of it. Everyone is programmed to be a certain way and have a role to fill. That's how the book read.

On the positive side there definitely were some large topics explored that were interesting. I almost feel like this was a Bernie sanders book. Everyone is happy with stuff and they take pills and have no challenges in life because they are given everything. A couple of characters try to buck this but in the end they cannot.

The last fifty pages are the best with the discussion between on of the government officials and John the savage. Lots of great dialogue.

One final question. What was the fascination of "The Ford." Was it how he cranked out cars at his factories. These people became enamored with that and created a whole society based on that concept? The people mention him instead of God but no one really gave the history of how Ford became the guy they all revered.
Worth a look.

The short artilces for most of the book were just great. A wide range of topics were discussed that I enjoyed. The only ding on the book was the ending where Charles gets really involved with discussing the Middle East. Long discussions/articles on Israel that all seemed to run together. Overall, a great analysis on world events from the past 30 years with some very humorous articles in there for good measure.

This one was tough to rate for some reason. I dislike when a book is not titled correctly. The author calls this and optimists guide. I felt the book was pretty depressing. Mass migration due third world countries falling apart and global warming destroying the planet are a few of the light hearted topics discussed.
That being said I thought there was a lot of interesting information within the pages. I especially enjoyed his suggestions for improving the world and America. He's a center left kind of guy and I'm a center right kind of guy but I think we could find some common ground and compromises and get things going again. He mentioned a couple of suggestions that I found very interesting.

1. He was in favor of better border security with a healthy visa program.
2. More local problem solving versus Washington DC and the big, slow federal government trying to fix problems.

The last three chapters are a review of his hometown and for some reason I didn't enjoy them. I felt like everything was roses in his mind about the good old days. He tried to point out failings now and then but it just felt out of place with this book and the previous 90 percent being about accelerations in the world.

Interesting book

Excellent, excellent book. The author is a psychologist and is a diehard liberal so I wasn't sure what to expect. He mentions this in the beginning of the book so I was on guard for the usual Kool aid drinking that sometimes happens.

That being said this was a fantastic book. He goes into great detail about what makes liberals and conservatives tick. He discusses what each does well and what they do not when thinking about morals.

The only drawback to this book is it does contain a lot of terms to keep straight and the philosophers who coined them. They can get overwhelming but their overall ideas are well worth it.

The final twenty or so pages were the best. We need to have conversations and find ways to work together. Each side is wrong and right and that makes it tough.

Highly recommend.

The idea behind this book is a noble one. If we could get more people to "give" and not "take" the world would be a better place. The what's in it for me mentality is what is wrong with the world. Unfortunately it seems to be growing.

I enjoyed it so much I am going to copy an excerpt to share with colleagues at work. Hopefully we can make some changes.

This one goes under the category of interesting topic but fell short. The beginning and the end of the book were interesting but the middle was horribly boring. Long narrative about the Dutch and the political wrangling of the time just went on and on. The characters in the story were also fairly lifeless. It just never gained any traction. Barely 3 stars.

A friend recommended this one stating it was one of the best books ever. Expectations were high starting and they quickly died away with this overwritten novel. I almost stopped reading this a couple of times in hopes that it would improve. It did but not until page 400.

This book reminded me of a Charles Dickens novel. Never ending descriptions and sidebars on topics that were remotely connected to the development of the main characters distracted from the novel. It could have been so much better if it had been half its length.

The King was missing a few men on this one. If you like Dickens, this is your book.

Excellent look at president Nixon. After reading this, I feel like several college classes could be offered on president Nixon. The book is fair, well written and provides enough detail for the causal reader.

His life reads like a Greek tragedy at times. His fatal flaw being that he was not able to look inside and identify his insecurities and how they led him down the wrong path. Love him or hate him, he did make his mark on the world.

Highly recommend.

I did not read the prequels to this novel about the Romulan War. I plan too. So a little bit of this novel contains back stories from those 5 books. I enjoyed this reboot of Admiral Archer and the Enterprise gang very much.

My only slight issue is the storyline featuring Captain Shumar of the Essex and Captain Reed's storyline. In my opinion, they were not necessary to this book at present. Now, maybe something will change in the next book in the series with them but it felt like those to story lines were not locked in with the main story featuring the "Mute Ships."

Looking forward to reading the next book in the series.

This was an excellent book. I knew nothing about these guys trying to reach the North Pole. Excellent writing and I especially enjoyed the detail concerning the crew member's eye inflammation. The author was detailed and accurate in his description. Wonderful tale and just the right  length. Highly recommend.

If you have read anything about Shakelton's adventure to the South Pole then you will enjoy this story as well except going north this time.

Interesting take on foreign policy mainly focusing on the Obama administration.

Only issue I had was his comment about predictions mostly being false and he cites several examples and then he goes on to have a whole chapter of his so called future with Hillary as president.

Interesting book.

A fun book about the early days of paleontology in the western United States in the 1870s. A quick read based on history about two paleontologists who despise one another and are bent on sabotaging each other at every turn.

Fun read.

Ive never watched or heard any of Katy Turs reporting on NBC during the campaign. I was unaware of her involvement in the Trump campaign from the beginning. Im just a political junky and wanted to hear her stories of following the campaign.
She delivered on those and provided some interesting insight of the grueling life of a reporter following a campaign. This campaign was especially brutal but one gets the idea from her stories of the road.
Her style is interesting with little one liners dispersed through the story. At time I felt like the book was a stream of consciousness.
If you are looking to read about the election from a reporters perspective, this is worth your time and a quick read.

A side note that has nothing to do with the writing is the bizarre picture on the front and how that picture of her on the front cover looks nothing like her bio picture on the inside jacket cover. I'm confused as to what the implied meaning of the front cover is??

Recommend

Everything is known, says Gabriel Garcia Marquez. Like almost everything in his book, the statement should not be taken literally. Just as a literal interpretation of the Book of Genesis is not required to appreciate the Hebrew bible, this alternative bible begins to make some sense only when you get the metaphor. Everything is known because human nature is what it is. Because we are human, we make the same mistakes over and over. History repeats. And, it repeats. And, it repeats.

Marquez's man-made bible history tells you that you do not need his or anyone's written history book to know that pre-historic mothers cried for their future warriors even as they nursed them. Marquez wants you to know that you don't need a bible or a crystal ball to tell you that tomorrow's righteous dads will again be sending their brave sons into some bloody conflict somewhere. Everything is known. The past, the present and the future, it's all known. Marquez lays it out for you in this bible. It's not an easy read. Despite brilliant uses of ironic humor, despite a masterful use of language---really more poetry than prose---, despite the occasional hints of hopefulness, the message comes through loud and clear: Life's a bitch and then you die; after that there is nothing.

Now, go have a nice day.

Andrew Lloyd Webber liked the story so much he has based his latest musical on it; you can see it now in London. Literary experts have called it, the very first mystery novel. The book jacket says it is " A gripping tale of murder, intrigue, madness, and mistaken identity". Never out of print since its publication over 140 years ago, the Modern Library Classic introduction to the book tells us: "The Woman in White has lasted, to our great pleasure, because it is a superb storytelling about people who engage our minds and imaginations."

The above facts speak to some of the reasons  The Woman in White is considered a literary classic. To be sure, The Book Club enjoys including an occasional classic in its repertoire. Sort of like training wheels, somehow we seem to believe the reading of select classics will assist our powers of discrimination and taste. However, unlike the timeless pieces of Shakespeare and Twain, the challenge confronting today's reader of the very first mystery novel is to be able to appreciate the work's creativity long after other writers have honed the genre to a point where an original, even a great one, can seem a bit hackneyed.

The Woman in White may not have been as exciting as The Big Sleep or even The DaVinci Code. But, after reading it, we were left with no doubt as to whose shoulders Chandler and Brown were standing when they achieved their great heights.

Midway upon the journey through this book, I found myself within a forest dark, for the straightforward path had been lost. Ah, me!  How hard a thing to say. What was it in this promising tome, erudite, and original, which in the very thought renews the disappointment? So bitter is it, I can dream only of next month's tale. So, speak will I of the things I saw in my travel and travails therein. I cannot well repeat how there I began so full of hope until somehow I abandoned the true way. Or, more correctly put, the way abandoned me. Thereafter, I reached a mountain's peak, at that point where belief terminated, and consternation pierced my heart. Upward I looked, and beheld its portent vested already with shadowy doubts. Then was the fear quickened that my heart's lake would have to endure several more nights of the author's academic pondering.  As though we were predator and prey, he with distressful breath issuing from sea upon the shore turns the water foamy and hot, so did my mind and body wish to flee. And, lo almost where the hope began, the story did nothing but decline. If I had rhymes both rough and stridulous as were appropriate to the dismal hole I would press the juice of my conception more fully, but because I have them not, not without fear I bring myself to speak of the peril of dreams and not fond reflections of Pearl.

Written to commemorate the bicentennial of the US Constitution, the book tells the story of descendants of a family who variously contributed to the creation, the writing, the interpretation, and the defense of that uniquely American document. Framed in typical Michener style as a grand epic novel, and likely planned as one, Legacy lacks the author's usual attention to minutia that provide the context for his characters' actions. In other words, it's short. So short that it, seems incomplete, unfinished, more like an outline than the real deal. Nonetheless, in my view, even Michener Light is far better than most of today's crop of non-story tellers. It's certainly a story worth the read.

This one is different. First, there's the writing style. Forget punctuation. Forget paragraphs. Forget chapter headings. Saramago's prose comes at you like packets of bits and bytes down a fiber pipe. Think Rushdie on steroids. Next, there's Algor Cipriano, the potter. Our introduction to him begins with Algor's ramblings; some are spoken; others are not. His thoughts mold our view of Algor. He is 64, widowed, with a married daughter. He is independent, hard working, loyal and noble. He is a man you can like. But, Algor's worker peasant ways are the old ways. More and more people are moving to high rises in the New Town. The swank population there prefers mass produced items over hand-made pottery. Algor is rapidly becoming obsolete, useless, old. He has two choices: retire to the New Town where he can live in a tiny apartment with his daughter and son-in-law or re-mold himself into something more marketable. His struggle is profoundly moving. He knows that he must change, keep up with modern times, but wait. Wait. As he gets a closer look at the new town Center, he is convinced that the new way is false. It's a trap. Why would anyone want to live in a high-rise cubit---a cave---even if it does have 500 cable channels, a slick Micro-wave oven, simulated rain forest, and an indoor ski jump? The new town residents, in Algor's estimation, are not seeing reality. They are dupes, consumed by consumerism. The Cave is not a pretty tale, but it is one where you'll enjoy the spelunking.

According to an ancient Chinese proverb, the route to wisdom starts when you select words with the proper meaning. Alan Bennett's The History Boys is all about the use of words. The situation is a classroom filled with working class boys all of whom want to break with tradition and pass entry tests that will make them some of the first non-Elites to ever get into Oxbridge---for the uninitiated that's short for Oxford or Cambridge. Even for the best of them, chances are slim. First, there's the little matter of class; at Oxbridge, students and faculty are either highbred or rich, mostly both; a working class resident is most likely to be there as janitor or cook. Then there's the matter of competition; only the best of the best need apply; there are many more applicants than slots. Not to be deterred, the ambitious school administrators have a plan: Use two very different types of tutors. One gives the boys facts, figures, poems, stories, and an appreciation of culture. The other gives them something seemingly more valuable: presentation skills. Together, the teachers hone students who know how to choose words that surprise, stir emotions, and impress. The strategy works, sort of. Through the benefit of hindsight, we learn that the boys do get into Oxbridge; but, Bennett also lets you know that he knows the difference between a "proper" schoolboy who can carefully mouth words to impress and the wise man who makes an impression by choosing his words properly.

As Americans, we have the God given right to be blond, blue-eyed, rich, beautiful and to get what we want when we want it. It's our Manifest Destiny. Gatsby knew that then. And, we know it now.

Much like today, in the America of 1925 all things were possible. The country, having only recently been born yet again following its latest Baptism of Fire, was in its second or third childhood. As in previous reincarnations, progress was fast. The USA was now the most powerful country in the world. Women could vote. Negroes were driving their own cars. Radio, much like the printing press before it and the Internet after it, was providing access to whole new classes of people. Farmers in Iowa.  Pennsylvania Coal Miners. Cowboys. Truckers. They all wanted their piece of the pie. And the pie was growing like wildfire. The stock market was setting record highs on a daily basis. Fully a third of the population was new immigrants. Joe Kennedy, the son of an Irish immigrant, was making his fortune running scotch into the US through Canada. Italian immigrant, Al Capone was getting even richer selling bootleg booze made right here in the good old USA. These newcomers proved that it was possible to get rich overnight. If they could do it, anyone could do it. Why, a poor man could even aspire to becoming president of the USA. Old Abe proved it was possible. In America, a man like Gatsby, if he had enough money, could even win over a Daisy Buchanan. It was possible.

Magical Realism. Our book club was introduced to this new (for us) peculiarly Latin American literary form when we read Gabriel Garcia Marques's One Hundred Years of Solitude and later Saramago's The Cave.  In the De Bernieres rendition, we get Magical Realism on steroids. The Result: Mixed Reviews. Love it or hate it, all of our readers agreed that the author rivals Rushdie in the use of "I'm smarter than you are" references. (I challenge anyone to understand half the references in this book without easy access to  English and Spanish dictionaries, Wikepedia, and an eighty-year old shaman). Sure, when you get the inside joke, it can be really funny (I loved his calling the john an excusado), until you start thinking about all the stuff you are missing ( Do you know why he changes the character's name to Parmendies) . I'm sorry, but when I'm sitting on the beach with a paperback, I don't want to have stop at every other sentence to do Where's Waldo exercises on my laptop. After doing that more than a few times, the Reality for me was that the book lost much of its Magic.

So many folks told our Book Club how much they enjoyed Amy Tan's other works such as The Joy Luck Club and The Kitchen God's Wife, that choosing Saving Fish from Drowning as our September 2007 read was an easy decision. We were ready for a good read. Certainly, the title was intriguing. What could it mean? How will it apply to the story? Tell us more. Writing from the perspective of a dead woman, Bibi Chen, Tan expertly began to reel us in with a quirky story set in odd places filled with unusual characters.  It was exactly what you'd expect from a writer of her renown. For about a hundred pages we were hooked.
About halfway through the book, we began to have some doubts. For some, it started with her use of foreshadowing. Forget subtlety. Think Yogi Berra meets Burma Shave: When you come to a fork in the road, take it. For others, the problem was plot, or more accurately too many sub-plots and no main one. In the end, most of our readers didn't care a fig for any of the characters or the various stories. Mercifully, the book does have an ending. Even better,  there is an Epilog. So if you really want to know if the tribe ever finds their lost God or if they end up massacred by the Myanmar military, or more important, if Harry gets Sally, Tan is there to wrap it all up for you. In Burma Shave lingo, we think her sermon says: Western do-gooders are like so many fishermen who spend their days saving fish from drowning.

Written in 1943, this little book long ago attained the status of timeless classic. Yet, when discussed at our book club, our members could agree on little about the book's interpretation, sensibility, or even if it is appropriate for children. Some viewed it as an innovative form of literature requiring both a narrator and an inquisitor: What did that mean daddy? Where did the Little Prince go daddy? Does he love the rose? Who tamed whom? Some viewed it as a sort of religious work designed to teach our children "what is really important in life".  Do you like butterflies? What sort of voice does she have? On the other hand, some felt that the book allowed children to question the wisdom of adults, especially parents. Is this one of those deals Like Text Messaging where kids get it but adults never can? Others, who knew something about the author's life---why should it matter--- read it as a sort of suicide note disguised as a children's book. It was during these darker moments that one wag commented that any work that can stimulate a discussion this gloomy had to be something really special. And, here's where we all started to agree. This is not a work that speaks for itself. It is, instead, a sort of catalyst that will produce different enlightenments for different readers and narrators. While Saint-Exupery's little book can  open doors to wisdom, you have to enter by yourself. That so many continue to choose to do so is testimony to his greatness as a writer and a teacher.

This may have been what Dante had in mind when he wrote about his journey into Darkness. But, nobody does the dark-side better than Faulkner. When his Addie tells us that the reason for living is to get ready to stay dead a long time you guess that this is no love sonnet. Indeed, as she lay already dead, her family is transporting her decomposing body to Jefferson many miles away. Along the way we learn that all the Bundrens have ulterior motives for wanting to go on the long journey to bury Addie. Addie wants to be buried far from the family she raised but never truly loved; her hunchbacked husband, Anse, wants a new set of teeth (in part because he wants a smile that might attract a new wife); son Cash wants a phonograph (or as he calls it, a "graphophone"), youngest son Vardaman wants to get a toy train; daughter Dewey Dell wants to get an abortion (with the ten dollars that Lafe, the would-be father, has given her); illegitimate son Jewel wants to get away from Anse; and, crazy like a fox son Darl, well, truth is we don't really ever know what he wants but we do know that he has a secret that he would like to express in the most eloquent prose anyone has ever written.

OK. That's the set-up. There's a flood. The mules drown. Jewel's prize horse is sold by Anse. Addie's decomposing body is attracting buzzards. They are all nearly killed in a fire.

 And then, things really go bad.

Predictable is my word for this overly hyped novel. To be sure, the story is cleverly crafted so as to force the reader to read, the story within the story within the story, all the way to the end, end, end. But when I finally got to the end, I found it, well, predictable.

Thinking of writing a journal to leave to your children? This book might inspire you. The writer is a preacher who has plied his trade in the fictional Iowa town of Gilead. The town's name is of some significance. According to the bible, Gilead is a place where one can always find respite. The Gilead of our story may or may not be such a place. That's one of the questions that adds tension to the narrative. The others have to do with faith, redemption and predestination. If you believe in predestination---as a Congregationalist, our preacher should---can you expect a sinner to change? As he writes, our preacher shares his thoughts as he sorts out his beliefs and, more important, his doubts about himself and his religion. At the crux of the problem is Jack. Years ago, while baptizing young Jack, our preacher was distracted; as a result, he always sensed that Jack had received an inappropriate or incomplete blessing. Jack has returned to Gilead. From all we know, this prodigal son was a rotten guy when he left, and he's not so swell now, unless you want to give him credit for having a black wife and an illegitimate child in another town. The preacher is torn. He does not trust Jack; he even fears that Jack is after his own wife. But, he also blames himself for Jack's failures in life. What should he do? Predestination or redemption? His narrative is transforming. In the end, he makes the right choice; at least, that is what he tells himself. Spirituals in Concert

Legacy in the Making comes beautifully packaged as a hard back coffee table book. Inside, youll find impressive photos, illustrations, quotes, scripts and eye-boggling variation of page colors. Ornamentally, its an impressive piece of design. As I read through it though, I could not help but wonder about the books own legacy. Would it make its way into the ranks of the best business books ever written? A few years hence, would other business writers be quoting passages from it? In my humble assessment, the answers are a resounding No. Indeed, theres little about the Japanese concept of ikigaiyour reason for beingat the core of the book that is original or memorable.  We heard and remember more eloquent explorations of the concept before from the incomparable Rick Warren in A Purpose Driven Life. Though in paperback, we keep a copy of Warrens book on our bookshelf next to other originals like Start with Why, From Good to Great, Think and Grow Rich, Built to Last, In Search of Excellence, and the E-Myth. As an attractive display, Legacy might linger on my coffee table for a few weeks, but a year from now it won't be in the company of the memorable.

Written in sparse, simple language, you might be tempted to dismiss the work as banal. But Hemingway, like his friend Picasso, knows the value of pruning so that less is more.
The story is set in Paris between the two great wars. There we find a group of attractive, young, well-educated ex-patriots. Our narrator, Jake, is in love with the beautiful Brett. But Jake's war wound makes him unable to satisfy Brett sexually. Their unhappy predicament spawns an unusual love affair. Jake, in effect, becomes Brett's pimp. Just as fish can be lured more successfully with artificial flies than real worms, the lovers use Brett's exotic looks to lure men for "artificial" love affairs. While never overtly stated, Jake and Brett play their game under strict rules. Brett never falls for any of her "lovers." Jake never denies her choices. Jake is always there for her when she needs him. Like Picasso, Hemingway is a master of the double entender. At the Bullfights, we learn that steers are used to calm the wild bulls; it's a steer that leads the bulls to slaughter; bulls get slaughtered, but the steers get to live another day; a great bullfight is one where, at the climax, the bull and matador are one. At the bullfight, like two Greek gods, Brett and a handsome young matador are inevitably attracted to each other. Jake arranges a meeting and then leaves them. After a brief tryst, the young Adonis leaves Brett because Brett won't marry him. Penniless and alone, Brett calls Jake to her rescue. It's not your typical love story, but it makes a swell book.

Everything is connected. Rachel Carson told us so in The Silent Spring. Now Natalie Angier shows us how and why. What she pulls off is nothing short of brilliant. Our book club voted it the book they'd most like to see included in a general college curriculum. One of our club members, when asked how she felt after finishing the book, shouted "happier and smarter." As one wag put it: the feel good book of the year. To be sure not all our members were so ecstatic. One did not finish; others thought the book too technical. And, then there was the God thing. Let's be clear. The book begs the question but readers made it the centerpiece of our discussion. If everything is connected---physics, chemistry, biology, astronomy---everything--- back to a common origin, then why, how, who, what?  Dogma teaches that the answer is there. Just read your bible; if you ask too many questions, you'll only get confused. Science takes a more, well, scientific approach. As Hamlet put it: There are more things in heaven and earth, Horatio, than are dreamt of in your philosophy. More things, indeed. Our galaxy alone contains 300 billion suns. And, at last count, there are 100 billion galaxies. Statistically speaking, the chances of us knowing even one trillionth of anything of significance is just about zero. There's a lot to learn. And, while acceptance might provide peace of mind, as Natalie Angier shows us, learning and discovery are a lot more fun.

Magical Realism. It's a peculiar literary genre that our book club seemingly likes to include in our book bucket------we have read three others: Senior Vivo, The Cave, and One Hundred Years of Solitude-----but, ultimately, not one that we particularly enjoy.  Like Water for Chocolate was no exception. While some of our sixteen reviewers did appreciate the author's attempt at cooking up hot passions, most felt that what we got was a contrived recipe for so much cold turkey.

This is not a phrase book. It's not a grammar book. It's not a beginner's book. So, what is it? For me it was a fun little read. Period. I can't say I learned much but I did have fun laughing at all the errors... Way too many and fundamental to attribute to typos.

A Walk in the Woods. With a smile still on my face from having just read Bill Bryson's eponymous novel, I had to have these towels. Like Bryson's writing, the towels say Welcome to America, and that always makes me feel good.

Certainly, we know there was a Boss Tweed. We know about the corrupt world he lived in. And, we know there was a waterworks. But, what about the rest? Does it add up? Is it the "immense, extraordinary achievement" that the San Francisco Chronicle says it is?

Because we are dealing with E.L. Doctorow, the novel at first has the ring of real history. From the very first page, the author gives you that "You are there" style he made famous in Ragtime. It's a technique that can put you smack on the rough streets of old New York, where homeless newsboys fight each other for the "rights" to a corner, where dangerous horse carriages careen wildly down cobbled stoned streets, and where evil men, protected by Boss Tweed himself, ply their villainy with paid for impunity.

But, alas, the characters in The Waterworks are not nearly as interesting or believable as those in Ragtime. Perhaps it's the fact that Ragtime is peopled with real historical characters, that makes it a compelling work. Then again, perhaps, Doctorow is not really the mastermind of fiction the Chronicle claims he is. Or perhaps, he just blew this one.

In our view, The Waterworks is definitely not "Doctorow at his best" as proclaimed by the Philadelphia Enquirer, nor is it the "gem of a novel" heralded by the Boston Globe.

Do all mass movements, good and bad, follow similar paths? Eric Hoffer, former longshoreman, drifter, self-educated writer and philosopher, explains the process. There can be no mass movement without deliberate misrepresentation of facts. To be successful, mass movements must be contrary to nature, common sense and pleasure. "We can be absolutely certain only about things we do not understand." True believers are attracted by the prospect of sudden and spectacular change in their conditions of life. Thus, mass movements attract the frustrated and/or unemployed. Those who have the lowest opinion of themselves are ripe for conversion no matter what doctrine is being offered to them.  Hoffer shows how the right words at the right time are critical. "A [mass] movement is pioneered by men of words, materialized by fanatics and consolidated by men of action."  Written in 1951, Hoffer's little book seems totally prescient in today's world filled with extremist views on both sides of the political spectrum. Brilliant.
Inside the shoe, there is a very hard protrusion where the heel piece is crudely stiched to the instep piece. The protrusion gouged my foot. I could not wear them. I returned them. .

While I could find a few things to criticize, and I will, this grill is hard to beat for the price. Because it grills from the top and bottom, it cooks quickly and thoroughly. The non stick surface cleans easily. So, here are my quibbles: No cleaning instructions. No handle to open a hot lid; must use potholders to lift; this can be dangerous. The drip tray does not attach. No "on/off" switch; you start by plugging in; could be dangerous if left on and unattended. Pretty small grill to be called family size; no way it's for a family of four; on the other hand, it does not take up a lot of storage space. Great for a dorm room.

Brands have value. Because of a brand, I don't simply buy tennis shoes, I buy an attitude: Just do it. Because of a brand, I am truly authentic when I buy the Real Thing. When I shop at Whole Foods, my healthy living provides a salve for both body and soul. Brands, according to the author of Friction, got to become Brands largely by advertising to captive audiences using radio, TV and print. But, in the digital world, ads, especially the pop-up variety, are incredibly annoying and mostly ignored. In the digital world, ads are a form of Friction. A new paradigm is needed; instead of harassing on-liners, companies need to empower them. Easier said than done? Yup! For sure, the book does not say its easy. But, it does two really worthwhile things. First, it highlights the problem of Friction; second, it gives good examples of empowerment. One other benefit: the book looks great on my coffee table.

users.query: I received an ARC from the author for an honest review. Mirage was great and an absolute joy to read. Ashley Suzanne's first book and definitely not my last. In fact I messaged her after I finished and asked so when is the next book coming out?! The story of four friends, their friendships, loves, joys and heartbreaks. Mira/Danny/Skyler/Kylee four college friends whose lives all change on the night of graduation from College. Danny & Mira fell in love during college and Danny proposes to Mira. What Mira & Skyler don't realize is that they have very deep emotional feelings for each other. The book takes twists and turns throughout. and what I was not expecting was the Cliffhanger, yep one of those. But you know that's ok. Another fact about the book I enjoyed was the detail that Ashley went into to describe the scenes in the book. The story takes place in Michigan and the characters go to the University of Michigan. There are a lot of little details that I appreciated in the story. I highly recommend this book. Happy Reading.

cands.text: I received an ARC from The Author for an honest review. I loved Stay With Me! It is stories like this on that warm my heart and have me rooting for the couple. And also believing in love at first sight combined with HEA. Hailey & Caleb, well I knew the moment I started to read the book it would be Love At First Sight. It did not take much for me to get hooked on this story. I finished the book within a day. Hailey has grown up as a darling in Hollywood but as she gets older things change for her. She wants to escape her Hollywood existence for a new experience. To be on her own in a small Vermont College town. As the book goes through her experiences, hopes & dreams she realizes that this is the opportunity for her to make herself a better person. Of course her mom (and manager) is a total bitch. The kind that makes you want to reach through your kindle and slap her senseless. I loved all the little nuances of this book the way the author wove the love story of Caleb & Hailey was wonderful. The interactions between all the characters from Caleb's friends and family to the way they all became friends. Hailey no longer feels like a loner. This was a fun read and had me laughing & crying. I highly recommend this book. Also this is turning into a series so expect more great stories from Elyssa Patrick. I would like to take a moment to say Thank You to Elyssa for letting me be a part of the release of this fabulous story. Thanks Hun. Happy Reading y'all.

I received an ARC for an honest review. I was pulled into the story from the very beginning, Amber and Shane are great characters. I love the writing style, the book was a great story of friendship. It's always hard to let someone new into your life. It's a story of finding yourself and what makes you happy. I always love a new story and I am a sucker for a good YA romance. I am definitely looking forward to reading her second book. I highly recommend you give this book a shot. True it's different from what I usually read but I never say no to good story. Happy reading from your favorite book Vixen.

I received an ARC from the author for an honest review. I loved Trust by L. Chapman. What a great book. A bitter sweet romance filled with hopes and dreams. I did not know what to expect when I received this book or began to read it. I was pleasantly surprised. The lead female character is Megan very reserved and shy. She is in London with her friend Jenny getting items for Jenny's upcoming wedding. (I found myself reading the pages with and English accent.) As you get to know these two girls they are very different people but similar at the same time. Very loyal to each other. (I love that) Enter Mark he is good looking and very interested in Megan. As the story continues you get to know Megan better and realize the reasons she is reserved and shy. She has been hurt in the past and does not want to be hurt again. Megan and Mark begin a whirlwind friendship. Megan starts to open up to Mark and pretty soon she is realizing she is falling hard and fast for him. She swears to herself that no one will ever hurt her again. I enjoyed each and every chapter of this book and felt very honored to have the opportunity to read the book and participate in the blog tour. If you have not read Trust, you owe it to yourself to read this simple sweet romance. I am looking forward to more books from this wonderful author. Long live sweet romance!

I received an ARC from the author for an honest review. I really liked this story I was a nice change of pace for me. I liked Beth's writing style. a great weekend book. Another recommended book and author and I am looking forward to the next book in the series. Happy Reading.

I received an ARC from the author for an honest review. Erika Ashby I love you and your books. No Going Back, wow, wow, and I did not see that one coming. A very powerful angry, passionate revealing love story. Seth & Mallory talk about a couple! Loved them. This book was very emotionally powerful for me. I found myself at times not being able to put it down then other times I just had to put it down. Erika writes with passion, humor and intensity. This was book number 2 in the series and I can not wait to see what else Erika has for us in the lives of Seth and Mallory not to mention Jesika & Derek. I have a feeling there are lots more twists and turns ahead for everyone. I know this review is short but by no means does it imply that I did not love the book because I loved the book. But by no means does this mean that the book was not a roller coaster of events and emotions. Thank you Erika for trusting me with a copy of your work and the opportunity to read and review as well.

I was given an ARC by the author for an honest review. Spark was great! I mean the book grabbed me and would not let go! I finished it in one day. The opening pages just sucked me in and I could not stop reading I had to finish this book. The story of Velaney & Eric is great. The way he comes swooping in and rescues her in the opening chapters to the friendship they share and then FINALLY The hot and steamy romance! From the beginning when they met in the hospital room until the very end. Of course you have the ups and downs and twists and turns of a great romance but this story has heart, pardon the pun. AJ has had endless non committed hookups, being the drummer of Runaway Train has its perks! Mia is heart broken by her ex fianc.
