That being said, I don't own or us a Really Right Stuff L plate that the first 2 reviews mention however I am familiar with them. It seems a bit stupid that neither of these customers who were disappointed noticed in the big clear image that the slot where the mounting plate provided is 90 degrees opposite of what they needed for their fancy RRS mount!

I've shot with a number of camera mounting systems that use what is know as the Arca Swiss clamp style mounting plates and 99% of them are designed were the plate mounted to the camera is aligned with the lens axis, that is front to back and not side to side like RRS does. If anyone has a bad design it is Really Right Stuff! Most heads that have the Arca Swiss style clamps have a thumb screw to release or tighten the plate so with a RRS L plate the thumb screw would be in your chin or in the way at the front under the lens! Talk about a design flaw.

So, order this only if you understand that it won't work with a RRS L Plate and don't be as stupid as the first two reviewers!

I purchased this to replace my trusty old heavy Gitzo Reporter tripod and it was needed for several reasons.

1. Needed to be lightweight and compact enough to fit in my checked luggage.
2. Quick to set up or break down even in low light coditions.
3. Sturdy enough for reasonable long exposures under normal conditions mostly with wide angle lenses.
4. Reasonably priced.

This tripod met the above and exceeded all of the above. I am mainly shooting exposures under 1/30th of a second down to 10 seconds or so and obviously I try to shoot when conditions are best such as not extremely windy or an unstable moving surface where a much bigger tripod might be needed. I am also mostly shooting landscapes with wider lenses.

I am using Canon EOS bodies and lenses so the weight is somewhere around 2-6lbs. I would feel comfortable using this tripod with telephoto lenses if the conditions were good, not super windy, etc.

The case supplied is good enough, I took off a small compression strap sewn on to the shoulder strap. Not sure what it was for but it served no purpose for me. I also put on a better shoulder strap as the one supplied is pretty light wight material and not much of a shoulder pad.

Based on this tripod I plan to purchase their largest one later for my 800mm lens and sell the 18 lb Gitzo tele studex!
Just what I needed for the times I want to hook my GoPro Hero3 up to the TV. Also works for my Canon EOS M camera!

I got this since the GoPro out of the box relies on charging the battery while installed in a camera via a USB cable. Great for off use times but not good when you are actually using the camera. The batteries fit in the charger fine and charged quickly and it is nice that it comes with both AC and a DC auto-cigarette lighter connection which really keeps you covered. Have not tested the discharge cycle while filming with the batteries but I have used Wasabi batteries in my Canon 5D mkII with great results.

This is like my 4th eyecup for my Canon 5D mkII. The eyecup just slides off too easily and later you pick up your camera and it is gone. Thinking about putting some rubber cement or something to hold it in place but not be permanent.

One thing I noticed right off with my DJI P-3 Advanced is that the support arm that holds the adjustable mount for a cell phone or tablet had a bit too much flex because it is lightweight plastic. Maybe not so bad for a phone but it really made me feel uneasy if I used my tablet.

This aluminum holder really solves the problem. It is easily switched out with the OEM one and comes with an allen bolt and a wrench so you can tighten it down to the control unit nice and snug. The small slotted screw from your plastic mount can be reused for this one. The part is well made and machined from a solid piece of metal. I chose the blue color because I had added some blue decals indicating what controls do in each setting, it all looks nice like it was designed that way. I highly recommend this upgrade.
I was impressed with the quality of this tripod gimbal head and it works perfectly with my 800mm lens and Canon camera body.
Not bad build quality but too small for my needs. The first time I wanted to use it was for a low shot along a muddy river near some waterfalls. Hard to get the shot if the tripod is so short.

I am now a big fan of Induro and have 2 of their tripods, this head and the gimbal style head for my long lenses. The build quality on the head is good, actions are smooth and the knobs are easy enough for my big old hands even in cold weather.

The quality is good and they hold a good charge and I like that the charger comes with a European plug and also a car charger plug but the batteries have 2 small notches that click into place on tabs on the charger to hold the battery in place while charging and the OEM ones from GoPro don't have any notches so you can't fit the OEM ones in this charger. Wish they had come up with a mounting method that matched the OEM batteries shape.
I got 2 of these for my GpPro kit. They were big enough in size and the price was right.
I got these for my ocean kayak, just have found times when a cleat at the back and front would be handy. Found some stainless steel screws and nuts at the local big box store.
Going to make my epic bike riding video so this will be an important accessory. Fits my standard size handle bar and might fit on some lower parts of the frame, just have not checked yet.
Going to make my epic bike riding video so this will be an important accessory. Fits my standard size handle bar and might fit on some lower parts of the frame, just have not checked yet.

I needed this to make some repairs to my DJI Phantom Drone. The kit comes with lots of the smaller Torx bits as well as some slotted and Phillips. The battery supplied didn't last long so I had to replace it. The light is a nice feature, too. Sure beats having to spin a small screwdriver for long screws.

I got this for 2 applications. I offroad a bit in my Land Rover and this will be great for attaching to the roof rack or to the brush guard of  my ARB bumper. But it also will be good for attaching to the lower front fork of my bicycle for low angle shots as the tubing there on my mountain bike is too big for the typical handlebar mount.
This seems to be well made, very light yet sturdy and should help protect the camera and gimbal from being damaged.

Perfect OEM match for what was in my 1996 Toyota Avalon. Too bad that the one I had to remove was the one next to the firewall and when I got it out found that the threads had stipped leaving debris in the bung hole on the manifold. Ended up having to drive it a mile or so to a shop and let them retap the hole and insert the sensor. Cost me $108 for that so I still think it was less than if they had also removed the sensor and installed a sensor at a marked up price. Oh and the car was really loud without the sensor being installed!

I've been a fan of Julia Child since I was a kid and my mom used to watch these shows on PBS when they were first aired. The quality of the video seems good, it is amazing that she did all of this live. Julia was so not Food Network material and sadly she would never have gotten a show in this day and age of Bobby Flay and EVOO Rachel Ray!
I have a ring flash with several rings for different filter sizes but one of my lenses is smaller than any of the rings I got with the flash. This makes the flash work with the ring.
Well made and easy to install. Didn't come with instructions but I got an email from the vendor telling me how to install it. By then I had already attached it because it's pretty easy to understand,

users.query: I thought the storyline was slow to start with every other chapter dealing with the past or present. I guess this was meant to lead up to the last third of the story.  I almost gave up, but decided to continue.  Finally was drawn into the the novel about 3 sisters, their relationship with each other, their Mother, and with the death of their young brother when they were children.  Family secrets revealed.

cands.text: The author, Kathy Cooperman, has quite a background on reading many books, however, the storyline of her book was not enough to capture my attention.  I only read half of the book and have no interest in finishing.

I could not finish this novel.  The basic story line was interesting, however with a multitude of similes,  well known sayings, and many lists, the book seemed never ending.  If you want to know the story line, read "About the  book".

Slow to start, but moved right along once into it.  A continuing novel of family who sacrifice for their art, but also experience joy, love, sorrow, encouragement, solitude, and learning about confidence all intertwined.
Another book I just will not finish.  Little more than half way through and it seems to go nowhere.  Ready to start another.
Good storyline but I wasn't,I especially interested in the details of playing chess. No further words to say about this book
A quick read: short chapters, repeatedly going from past to present.  Imaginative story telling of a woman trying to find herself.

Almost put the book down half way through.  Basic story line very interesting, but the book lacked continuity, many words either misspelled or words left out.  Only continued as I thought it may improve, but failed.

Sarah Moriarty depicted the coast of Maine with great visualizations, however sometimes at great length.
A complex novel about four siblings inheriting the family summer home: memories of their life, mixed in with current living.  The decision facing them was whether or not to sell their family home.  Some of the characters were left hanging, wondering just what the future held for the individual.

The murder of Harper McDaniel's husband and infant son leads her on a wild ride to Europe to find the killer. Fast moving with unpredictable characters, with an end that has you ready for the continuing thriller.

Taking place in Africa in 1953, it was interesting to read about customs of that time period, witch craft,  and rebels go wanted to drive the white population away.  It was in spring to read of the friendship that developed between a young teenage girl and her family helper's son .
Unfortunately several African words were intertwined with the novel without any definition, some you may be able to figure out.  This is why I gave 4 stars.

I wasn't expecting such a captivating novel when I picked this book.  A  Pastor's  wife, overwhelmed by her life, and a man, betrayed by family and friends , become accidentally marooned in a place in Colorado.  Neither was expecting the other to be present.  Moving frequently between present and past, with twists and turns, spiritual and soul  searching,  this becomes a page turner.

A modern novel, with scattered humor, about a fellow making rash decisions on events in his life, then wants to take personal responsibility to make future changes happen.  You felt unanswered questions of some of the characters in book.

Living in Martha's Vineyard, a cast of characters with different backgrounds and issues become the novel about family, friendship, identity, anxiety and life's struggles.  An interesting read as to how these people coped with their individual problems.

Interesting novel of the life and times of a midwife in West Virginia during the Great Depression.  Me. Harmon wrote of life's trilogy: love, birth and death.  With coal mines mishaps, closings, ; the KKK;  and the lack of physicians or medical care,  many stories are told of Patience Murphy's life as a midwife.

This is an amazing mystery taking place during the 1917-1918 period when there was war in Europe, the influenza outbreak and someone looking for retribution. Friendships, romance, and despair blend together to make for a fascinating read.

An amazing thriller about manipulating monthly labor data in order to boost confidence to temporarily stabilize the economy during the 2012 election. Murder, scheming, deception, compromising info, and threatening those to withhold information make up this novel.  An exciting read with many interesting characters.
Got this for my granddaughter who didn't seem interested in the stories.  Maybe later.
A quick, easy romance novel concerning the possibility of love at first sight with criminal activity threading throughout.  Does this love continue despite circumstances ?
Great historical fiction of a German woman living in the 1300's:  making decisions , not necessarily popular and living with the consequences.  Hard to put down.

The beginning if this novel is dark, about a woman so addicted to alcohol and drugs because of the demons on her life.
She witnesses a murder, where her life really begins to unfold, revealing her past.  Unexpected and wonderful things start to happen as she searches for her true self.
A truly thought out novel about life and the world we live in.

Well written history from the late 1800's to present with years of research.  Thirst for adventure, the force of fear, drove many to the brink of death to see if they could survive.  Both men and women gave this challenge a try to gain notoriety or earn money.  Mrs. Anne Taylor, in the late 1800's was the first person and woman to go over the Falls and survive.  Most of the book deals with the Hill family and their knowledge of the Niagara Falls, their help to others and their own interest in challenging the Falls.
If you have been to the Falls, this book gave more insight to the tourist area.  Would be a great read if you have intentions of visiting Niagara Falls.
Given as a Christmas gift and am sure will be enjoyed by the recipient.

Dr. Addison Carter was hired by an oil company to be their doctor.  Upon arriving to take the position, she is immediately let go as she is a female doctor, not a male as was thought of by her name.  In 1917, female were not accepted as doctors in the eyes of the public.
This novel is about finding her place in a community with her knowledge, compassion and love.  Slow to start, the story line improves as you read along.
Amazing read, with a tangled web of deception:  including a slight touch of humor.  If you like political drama, especially in regards to finance, this book is for you.

This novel is about a young German teenage girl during World War II  who was able to triumph over years of adversity throughout her teenage years. From name changes, parent/ guardian changes and the loss of her memory for a brief time was able to overcome adversity. A vivid picture was written about life during those war years. Empathy and love for some of the characters, disdain for others, lead to a touching sensitive novel.

users.query:
This book is a little different from most YA books I have read. While this book does have supernatural beings, You don't have the everyday YA supernatural creatures (Vampires, werewolves, elves, faeries, etc)

Morgan is a High school student who lost her mom 10 years ago. There is this super huge mystery behind her moms disappearance. Nobody knows if there was foul play or if she left on her own. Nothing but her vehicle was discovered.
While at a party Her best friend Ris dragged her to, she sees this guy who is totally checking her out and ignoring the popular girls. Of course they get mad, vicious, and ultimately cause a scene and reminds Morgan that everyone thinks her dad murdered her mom. What a total A-hole right?
At school Morgan is known as the psychic (some say shes a freak) To Morgan its just logic and luck, but there is more to Morgan than even she knows.

We also learn of a group called the Veneret (a group of beings with supernatural powers) who are very interested in Morgan, who we learn is a Natural. The Veneret people have all kinds of "powers" ranging from Mind control, Moving objects with their mind, reading people, etc.

This book is full of thrills, a bit more of a love triangle more of a love rectangle, and is really fast paced. I wouldn't classify this as a full fledge novel. I personally feel a book should be like 250 pages to be considered a novel, but ya this book is on the shorter end. I think maybe 185 pages or so.

Now while I did really enjoy this book, I was left feeling like something was missing. We don't get a happy ending all wrapped up, but it does leave you wanting the next book. But for me it was more than that I can't put my finger on what was lacking with this book. Maybe because It did get wrapped up in 185 pages, maybe I was seeking more back story, maybe more story in general. I'm not too sure. It was one of those that you finish reading and your like hmmm, I like that, but something was missing. I wasn't satisfied after reading it.

bottom line: If your looking for something a little different with a nice fast pace, then I recommend this book.

cands.text:
The Girl and The Raven is honestly a book I have been putting off for sometime...

WHY?!?!?!?!?!
why did I put this lovely book off for so long? Maybe it had to do with the cover (I'm not a fan). Maybe the fact I've NEVER been interested in demon books (A topic that never interested me before). Whatever it is I want to kick myself in the butt for waiting so long! Such a good good book. I thought ok, maybe I'll like this book. I just didn't know I was going to come out LOVING this book. That came from left field.

Lucy is 16 years old and has just lost her mom. Her uncles (Sheldon and  Bernard) get guardianship of her and she comes to live in her Grandma's house (who is also deceased). The one night things unfold for Lucy. Persephone tells her she is a witch and from there on poor Lucy her whole life changes. Then on top of everything her totally hot crush who is also a supernatural creature, lets her know this crazy Demon guy is her father. So now on top of her Moms death, her grandma's death, and learning she is a witch, she finds out she is also part Demon :/
So now Lucy has to wonder is she as evil as her father? Or is she Good like her grandma and how thin is the line between good and evil?

Really awesome premise. I have to say this is my first witch book. I really enjoy it and can't wait to dive into some more. I really enjoy Lucy. For being a 16 year old with all this sprung on her and keeping her normal life and supernatural life from meeting, she is really mature. I feel at times she makes naive decisions, but she is new to this that is to be expected. I REALLY love the ending. There is this AWESOME action seen that totally had me on my toes. I don't know if this is a series, but honestly I hope not. There are a few things left unanswered, but I'm scared that if the author does go on, I may have to deal with a little but of a love triangle. I totally expected in this book and I am SO glad that was not the case. But the ending kind of had me thinking if the book does go on she may bring that aspect in and it would ruin this book for me if she were to make Lucy choose between Marcus and Dylan.

Character Development is great. I think the author did a wonderful job. I like that I could actually visualize these characters and the emotions they must be going through. Pauline has a beautiful writing style that just flowed together so nicely. I will be sure to check out more of her work!

Bottom Line: This book is packed with emotions from beginning to end. If you need something that will both make you laugh and cry This is a good number. Oh and Marcus is Hot!

Favorite Quote:
"If your trying to scare me off, you're going to have to do better than that. I face down demons, remember?

Copy Provided by Netgalley in exchange for an honest review

I was given a copy from the author through Netgalley in exchange for an honest review

Characters:
Sera: A 16 year old girl who is experiencing crazy lifelike nightmares. Has an awesome younger brother Nate and overprotective parents who try to dictate her every move. High school is her first form of actual public school (thanks to her strict parents).
Kyle: Sera's very Hunky best friend whom she has known for a few years. Someone her parents have now banished her from seeing. He is the troubled teen. A foster child. Dresses as if he is Goth/Punk
Dev: Sera's newest friend. A mysterious guy with an unusual Tattoo that has Sera intrigued since the first time she saw it.
Your average line up right?

But there is definitely more to these characters than what meets the eye! It goes much deeper.
And the worst part of all is...... Everybody but Sera knows whats going on and who they are.

This is based on Hindu Mythology. I have never heard anything about the Hindu religion or the mythology before reading this novel. I love this concept and it is VERY interesting. Something I definitely haven't seen done in the YA genre before which makes this book that much better to me!

My biggest Con is the Love triangle. I know I say this often but I am so over love triangles twilight really just ruined them for me. This particular love triangle sucked because I REALLY enjoyed both of the guys in this book. When you learn of Sera and Dev's story you will then really see why I am so torn between the two (but not giving anything away). To the authors defense the love triangle does go with the story she is bringing to life for us.
So basically the love triangle is part of the myth, it is not just thrown in for our entertainment.

This book started off a little slow for me, but Definitely picks up and when it picks up it does so quickly. Once we learn more about whats going on and whose who the story all comes together more and the action really begins!

One other thing I didn't like is Sera at the beginning of the book. She was very unlikable and sometimes almost pathetic to me. She considered herself ugly, awkward, and gangling. She even went as far as to describe herself as looking like a gargoyle. Yet she had these two beautiful guys pining over her. If that's what looking like a gargoyle gets you, then gees sign me up!
Oh but Sera sure does redeem herself and becomes the bad ass heroine I knew she could be!

I may have disliked the Love Triangle and Sera in the beginning, but I really enjoyed this novel and I will go as far to say I rate this novel an EPIC read. The author put this novel together so well. The execution as a whole is flawless. This is a book I will be recommending to everyone I know (Yes Katrina this means I will be sending you a text gushing about this book)

I also want to take the time to let Everyone know March 13 I will have Amalie Howard on the blog for an an Author interview + giveaway! So be sure to come by and check it out!

By Blood is a book I had never heard of until I started scanning Netgalley for some new novels. Guilty. But I am so glad I ended up running into this little charm of a book.

Emma is your typical 17 yr old girl, with your not so typical family situation (no spoilers). Her father ends up sending her to England for the summer to be with her mom whom she does NOT get along with. On top of that she is stuck taking care of "Vermin" her little half- brother.

One day Emma ends up taking Vermin for a little stroll and some sightseeing.
She meets this girl named Ashley who takes her to an awesome vegetarian restaurant and introduces her to a friend named Simon. After they leave Ashley tells Emma she is a Druid! And OMG after that moment there is not a single dull moment in the book. The characters are SO well developed it felt like I knew each and everyone of them personally. Simon was masterfully created. He is that Charming guy next door but you know something is off about him. Josh is that sweet boy that you hope Emma goes for because he is just developed into this VERY like able nice guy, where Simon is more of a mystery and your sexy bad boy.
One of my favorite things is this novel is wrapped up beautifully with no loose strings.

I was very interested in Druids after reading this novel. I did some research and came up VERY short because in history they covered their tracks well.
This is Not your typical YA book. I love and appreciate the uniqueness of this book.

I will be checking out more from Tracy E. Banghart

I was provided an ARC of this book in exchange of my honest opinion.

I automatically know that when I open a Brenda Novak book, I'm going to love it and I'm going to have tons of feels throughout the book. This one is definitely no exception. I have read all the previous books, and Rileys story has probably been my most anticipated one (Besides for Eve's of course but we finally got her HEA!)

Phoenix has just been released from prison for vehicular manslaughter on a girl Riley had been dating. Now that she is out, she wants to make up for lost time with their son.

I really expected to go into this book, hear Phoenix's story, her do something off the wall like kidnap her son, and some undercover FBI agent get involved and that is who Riley falls in love with. Seriously I had the whole story mapped out in my mind. Of course that is not how things worked out, but from previous novels I expected to dislike her from the get-go.

But FINALLY getting Pheonix's POV it changed everything for me. And I just think it was done so wonderfully.
Great writing, awesome characters, wonderfully thought-out Plot. Novak has a way with words that it just flows so beautifully.
If you haven't checked out the whiskey creek series, I highly recommend it!

Poison Princess
Kresley Cole

Let me start by saying I do NOT read YA, much less YA apocalypse/paranormal. I am an avid romance reader. So me wanting to read this book and liking it so much I couldn't put it down was a big deal! I actually downloaded a free sample and I was hooked I borrowed the book from a friend so I could finish it! I have a love/hate relationship with this book. There are some things I don't understand, a lot of things I found unnecessary, and some things just not explained. In all this how did the Zombies come about? I understand the slavers, the cannabals, the militia. But never once did it ever explain the exsistance of zombies. I don't understand where her school life was necessary at all. Everyone but Jack died. I don't know if it was to show what a spoiled brat she was, the kind of life she lived or what significance it played. What I do know is it took up a lot of chapters. BUT although I didn't find it necessary, it didn't bore me or deture me from the book. I also have a love/hate relationship with Jack. The guy is totally into her, its obvious. but the way that he was sometimes made me angry. But I do believe the good outweighed the bad. Matthew his character is VERY unlikeable and I found myself wanting to slap him a time or two maybe even 3. For as much as she liked him and favored him, I did not feel that connection. Selena pissed me off, finn was cool! As for Evie I liked her, something about her just totally drew me in. I didn't like how she let Brandon treat her at the beginning of the book. A lot of things that happened toward the end I DID NOT expect and I like that twist of events! Needless to say I love this book and I can't wait to get my hands on Endless Knight

In this novel we have Amy who was relatively new to Lucky Harbor. She is a 28 ur old server at the Eat Me Diner. She is your tough girl out of the chocoholics quipped woth a very rough past. At 16 she ended up leaving home and surving on her own. learning to trust know and not to let anyone in.
We start out with her on a Journey that her grandma had once gone on, and found peace. hope. and heart.

We have Matt Bowers an Ex Military / Ex swap, turned Lucky harbors Forest Ranger! also equipped with a rough past Ranger Hot Buns slowly loses his defenses to Tough Girl Amy.

We also meet Riley an 18 yr old runaway who Amy takes under her wing knowing all too well what its like to survive on your own. Shes a very likeable new character :)

You still have Lucielle and her crazy facebook ways! The chocoholics! and even a little mystery :)

Matt bowers Aka Ranger Hot Buns mmmm yummy! love itttt he is hott! especially with the whole rescuing the damsel in distress thing! Amy is very likeable and her story is very real. Made me want to cry for her! the chemistry between her and Matt was electrifying.

I also love how she swooped in for Riley. Had her back all the way :)

I love this book and def recommend! haven't found a lucky harbor book that has left me unsatisfied yet

.5
I recieved this book from the author in exchange for an honest review

I went into this book blindly.  I didn't read any reviews and I had never heard of the author before. Oh boy, how I love discovering Awesome new authors!

Impassioned is about a girl named Harper who is still stuck on her highschool sweetheart who wants to "take a break". One night while out with her friend she meets the incredibly sexy Ethan! He seems perfect. Attentive, gorgeous, and rich. But remember looks can be deceiving.

This book is HOT! Probably one of the sexiest books I have read in a longtime! I love how believeable, real, and well developed the characters are. I could relate to Harper in so many different ways it was crazy! I love how we got to watch Harper grow as an individiual and in each of her relationships.  She goes from this young naive girl with no experience to a grown mature woman who just went through hell and survived it.

My biggest complaint is that this story ended! I enjoyed it so much. I was on an emotional roller coaster. I laughed, yelled, cried, cussed different characters out! This book brought up so many emtions I haven't felt in a long time. Which is a big reason I love reading New Adult novels.

I highly recommend checking this book out

.5
I recieved a copy of this book from the author in exchange for an honest review.

It is SO hard to review a Novella because they are so short you don't want to give anything away.
This is a 62 page New Adult paranormal/fantasy novel.
Which def. Means it is a book with so, e HOTT scenes! That is something I love about the NA books. They have hot scenes yet still keep the story (in other words sex doesnt take over)

Donovan is hot I love him, he is the perfect hero to me! Gosh he is irresistable.
Sahsa is an excellent heroine, I think she took coming into herself very well
A lot of heroines who learn they are more than they had ever known get really flighty and annoying.

So if your lookin for a fun fantasy/paranormal Hot quick read, then this book is for you!

-Courtney

Lately I have been reading book that have left me feeling very mixed and confused on my emotions. Death Is But a Dream is going to be added to the list. I don't think I liked the book as much as I liked the idea of the book. In Netgalley this was posted as a YA. My question is WHY? Plutus was 24 I think and Callie was 28 there were not any YA characters in this book.

When I read the summary I thought this book was going to be AWESOME. I love Greek Mythology, there is a mystery tangled in this, and of course romance. Three things I would have normally enjoyed and for the first 15% of this book I did find myself liking it a whole bunch, but then somewhere along the way it veered in this very wrong direction. So basically I loved the idea of the story, but the execution was ALL wrong. It went from could be bad ass to Corny in 0-5 seconds. I did NOT like how the author portrayed the Gods. She went against everything Greek mythology has taught us. She made Hades nice. Seriously? I just didn't get the feel for it.

Here is the Gist:
Callie Jumps in front of a bus to save a little girls life. Instead she has now thrown off some balance of the world and messed up a lesson for people in the living world. Callie is this badass Detective who dedicates herself to the job. Hades God of the Underworld needs someone to protect his son Plutus (Someone has tried assassinating him several times) so he makes a deal with Callie. Find his sons killer she can go back to her life (Since right now she is in a coma).

One of the biggest things that Erked me was that Callie hated being called Callista. Hades, Plutus, and anyone else who met her Called her Callista. I get it she doesn't like it, but to repeat yourself at least 20x that it is Callie not Callista was annoying. Your halfway dead for freaking crying out loud. who the heck cares whether you like Callie or Callista. You have bigger problems here. Like these weird sort of Shadow monsters trying to kill you.

Then you have this mere mortal standing up to Gods like she's freaking Zeus or Apollo or some special God or Goddess, hell no. You think the Gods in the mythological world would have really ever put up with her smart ass mouth and attitude? I don't think so. Just saying. I don't care if I'm Buffy the Vampire Slayer who might I add is a Real bad ass. If I died and there was the whole meeting the Gods and Goddess of the afterlife, I'm showing some respect. These people could have decided she didn't deserve to live or do whatever they want. But nope the Gods/Goddesses just let this mortal come in and ream them. No No, not okay with me.

The romance seemed fake and forced. I felt zero chemistry between the character.
The who done it was poorly done. We get no back story or anything on the person who did it and all of a sudden it is solved. It felt like the Author was tired of writing and just wrapped it up. Maybe she tried adding too many aspects and kind of forgot to include the bad guy and a background on him/her. Who knows.

Overall if I hadn't said so already, I was pretty disappointed. And Looking at the reviews on Goodreads I think I am  the minority here.

I received this book from Netgalley in Exchange for an honest review

Its no secret, I absolutely loved book one, Shine Not Burn. I didn't think Casey was going to be able to meet those expectations I had for book 2. But holy friggin amazeballs, she once again blew me away!

If you have read Shine Not Burn, you know Candice is a bit of an airhead, but she is so sweet and lovable, and she really believes her knowledge is real (she calls herself the internet MD for crying out loud), you just cant help but love her! I mean the girl thinks when you get eggs from a chicken, you gotta stick your hand up their butt, to fish out the egg, (again with her googling)

I look over at Andie. Please don't tell me shes going to touch chicken poop.
Andies face is totally impassive. Nope.
Phew. Thats a relief.
She is going to touch their eggs, though.
 Then she is going to touch their poop.
She laughs, sounding confused. How so? She takes a sip of her drink as she waits to be educated by me.
I cringe. Ew, Andie. Because the eggs come from their butts, of course.
Andie laughs so hard she spits coffee out at me  Youve got to be kidding me. She wipes tears away. Oh, man, Candice, I sure have missed you.
I frown at her obvious ignorance of all things chicken. I missed you too. But why are you laughing over simple scientific facts? Google is your friend, you know, Andie. You really shouldnt neglect your Googling.

But Candices bone-headedness, and the way she is so naive, makes this book SO much better. There wasn't a page I wasn't rolling on the floor laughing!

Candice is Andies Bff, and she ends up coming to Oregon to be there for the birth of Andie and Macks first baby! Candice is a hairdresser and she owns her own salon, and as I said she is a riot (that is very mildly putting it). She definitely was not prepared for the country way of livin or the weather. I think in the first few chapters, Candice spent more time on her ass lookin up at the Oregon sky than anything.

Candice knew Ian was gorgeous, from Andies wedding, but she knew he was a major jerk, from what Andie had told her about him. Candice didn't like him right off the bat. But what she doesnt know is Ian is brooding and angry over a broken engagement. That happened over 3 years ago. Seriously. She doesnt take to that very well, and lets Ian know it.
At first things between the two are very rocky. When I say rocky, Candice accidentally grazes Ian with a bullet at the shooting range, but she swears its Karma who shot him!

But, Candice is just what the doctor ordered for Ian. She is fun, wild, and carefree, which is exactly what our Ian Mackenzie needs!

The tension between these two, is what really makes this book just come to life for me. These characters have so much chemistry, and Casey builds it up so well. They didn't meet their first night, and get it on, it was a process. But you know the tension is there and that they both want it.

Do not look at his package, Candice. Do not look at his package. My eyes move of their own accord. Oh, you looked at his package! And  oh my  Oh my, my, my  Theres a giant bulge! Hooray for giant bulges and the jeans that let me see them!

Candice really is what makes this book. I just cant say enough positive things about her as a character, Elle casey did a phenomenal job with her. I was actually scared to read her book, being in her head and such, because in book one she was just so dingy, but like I said she is just to lovable.

Another great thing is we got to catch up with Andie, Mack, and their family! It was like a big reunion. I really wish this series could continue on, just because the Mack family feels so much like my own family now, and it was really hard closing the book, not knowing if this was a temporary good-bye or not.

If your looking for a fun, easy, quick, humorous, light read, that will keep you laughing till the end, then definitely pick this book up!

YA

This book is hard to classify. I want to classify it as a middle grade book, but I know I wouldnt want my daughters reading about some of the things these girls talk about (well think about) in this book. But I feel it was a wee bit too immature to be young adult. I couldn't see me in high school enjoying this book. It was full of drama and problems adolescents at their age shouldnt even be worrying about.  Thats something I didn't like..

I don't usually take notes while reading, but with this book I did. I was confused a lot of the time. Just way too many peoples thoughts and POV to keep up with. They should of chose two maybe 3 characters to stick with, but instead we have like 7.

The premise is different, I think it could have been much better. I mean a vaccine that happened to give certain people ESP thats not your everyday situation. It could have come off really well. It was okay, not great but okay. Too much he said she says and drama, oh you think Im fat or I cant believe hes thinking about her or oh my I was cheated on just too many different situations and childish things to deal with. Hence why I wish there was nothing referring to sex in this book. It would make a great middle school book.

I do like the authors writing. Everything was well done and flowed together. I even actually enjoyed the ending a lot.

Defy.... I am very torn with this book.
I REALLY wanted to like this book, and I really did like some aspects. But there was a lot I couldn't get past either. Even rating this book is hard. I want to give it 2.5 stars just because of the  mix emotions I am feeling, but I know this book is worth at least 3 stars.

So you have Alexa aka Alex and her twin brother Marcel. Their family is killed and the army ( and I use army loosely, not like the military branch, just an army for the country) is picking up kids. Boys join the Army and girls get sent to breeding houses (yeah its as bad as it sounds)
Marcel saves his sister from the breeding house by cutting her hair and saying she is a he.

As they grow older they join the Guards to protect this really annoying Prince Damien. This book seems bullet proof, right? Well that's what I thought too.

I love the writing. Sarah Larson has an EXCELLENT writing style and great flow. Although I am torn with this book I will check out her future work.
The plot is great. The idea of the story is awesome. The execution and characters are who I had issues with. Oh and then add a typical YA love triangle to the mix and this book quickly unraveled.
Until the last about 60 pages, it all picked back up again and was wrapped up nicely.

The book started with a lot of promise I was captured turning the pages, well swiping them on my kindle, but anyways going through this book ready to devour it. But then somewhere along the way it got flat, boring, and lost its appeal. The details at times were insignificant.  The dialog between characters were unbelievable and monotone.

Then the worse happened Alex aka Alexa pissed me off! She went all this time hiding the fact she was a girl and did it damn well. Well then she lets her girly emotions get in the way and ruin it all. I don't mind that there was romance, but the girl needs to be careful. If discovered she would get sent to the breeding house. You figure she would be more careful and not get all giddy and blushy around the prince. And at first she didn't. She was a bad ass who did her duty and did it well. Then after an incident happened (can't give too many details, spoiler) its like she did a 360 and became emotional and less careful. It was unbecoming. But I guess you had to work her turning girly in order to have the romance aspect. Who knows.

I hate love triangles especially this one. Its a love triangle not too much to elaborate on!

And again I do like the ending and I like the twist I did not see coming throughout the book. But again I had to force myself to stay focused and to read this to get to the good stuff.

I will be reading book 2 and I will have tons of expectations!

This is an Awesome and yet creepy psychological thriller. So many twist and turns it keeps you on your toes. The first few pages had me snagged!

It isn't one of my favorite thrillers but its still really good. if your into psychological thrillers I def. recommend checking this one out!

Guys! This book is AMAZING! Can I rave about this book enough? Nope! Will my review do this book Justice? Nope!

Ok so we have Miss Lara Jean a Junior in high school, with 2 sisters Margot who is older and Kitten who is younger, and a dad who is raising his three girls as a single father. Margot and Lara are very close, more so than most sisters. After their mother died, Margot is the one who took care of the family. Well Margot has graduated and is now going to college..... Out of the Country. Of course this is very hard on the whole family, but even more so on Lara. She now must take responsibility of the family while dealing with being a junior in High school.
Lara Jean now has even bigger issues.... When she decides she doesn't want to love a boy anymore she writes them a letter to get over it. They are just her way of venting, she doesn't actually send them out. She does the opposite she stashes them away in a Hatbox her mother had given her. Well one day Peter, the boy who stole her first kiss comes up to Lara at school asking about this letter she sent..... What? She didn't send him a letter.... Oh no, Some how all her old letters have gotten sent out to the boys she used to love. Poor Lara Jean.

My Favorite part of this book????? Lara Jean has a family! OH MY GOSH who knew YA characters actually have those? This family also includes a..... DAD... ***GASP*** So rare.

Characters:
Kitten (the youngest sister) is my Absolute FAVORITE second character in this book. She is a little Firecracker. She made me laugh so hard I was crying. Kitten reminds me so much of my youngest child. She has no filter and no problem speaking her mind. Just a in your face personality. BOOM!

Margot- She has a stick up her booty. She doesn't let her emotions show and you can tell she tries hard to be strong for the family. I still love her though.

Lara Jean is just so sweet. I love her so much. Sometimes I felt like I was in this book with her and I jsut wanted to grab and comfort her through her hard times.

Peter I liked him right off the bat. Cocky arrogance and all

Josh is sweet and yet so confused. I love his connection with the family and watching him grow as a character.

This book is so hard to review. I read it Saturday in one sitting and waited till 4/23/14 to write a review so I could collect my thoughts. I still can't put my emotions into words. So you know what?!?!?! Stop reading this and go BUY THE BOOK! You won't regret it.

Ryleigh Andrews basically took EVERYTHING I dislike in characters and a book, threw it all together in this huge boiling pot, and turned it into something I love. How the heck did she do that? Ill tell you how: Her writing is amazing, the story telling is on point, and those characters, I wanted to know them, to meet them, and to love them! Mia, might be a little lucky I don't know her, because I probably would have slapped her a time or two!

Mia is a little hard to like, Im throwing that out there now. There were moments I absolutely loved her and moments I just wanted to throttle her, kind of like a sister! But, I truly understand Mia and where she is coming from in this book. She is a rock star, her wonderful (And I mean wonderful) boyfriend Ethan is a professional Football player. She has insecurities about their relationship due to some sort of past issues. Hey its normal they don't see each other often, both are traveling, both are busy. Mia handles her stresses a little different than some, and I don't agree with her, but I can understand it.

She looked up at his tall body, swallowing the rush of desire she had for this gorgeous quarterback. He smiled at her, his eyes on her lips, and she felt like she had been kissed. She saw hunger in his eyes or was that a reflection of her eyes? Mia Sighed, desperately wanting the real thing.

Ethan, what can I say about Ethan? YOU BROKE MY HEART!!!!! But seriously, I love Ethan. He made a mistake, he is a man and I think I can forgive him. I really need to see him redeem himself in the next book. A lovely thing about this book is we get alternating POVs, so yes while we see Ethan struggle, make mistakes, and do stupid things, (like not visiting Mia in New York when you had a chance,) we can really sympathize with him, see why he did it, and how he felt. Had I not had Ethans POV in this novel, I would probably be bashing him!

His lips were slightly upturned in a soft, sensual smile as he watched her. His Bottom lip was a little bigger than the top and she had an insane desire to tug on it with her teeth.

Andrews really knows how to write steamy scenes. This book has just the right amount of hotness to it. A lot of authors drowned their story out with sex and sex scenes, but Andrews did an A1 job. I have to say my favorite is probably their Skype date. I know that sounds weird, but it was HOT! Go see for yourself!

All in all this is a great start to a series and I cannot wait to continue on this journey with Mia and Ethan. Im already pretty heartbroken and emotionally strung out from this novel, and reading some friends reviews, I know that this is an emotionally charged series, but I come prepared!

It is no secret, I have been in a huge reading slump. Last Years mistake is only the 3rd book I have read in 2 months. Sad I know. While at HEB (a local grocery store) I happened to stumble upon this gem in the produce isle. Seriously. Everything about this book drew me in. The cover, title, The title font, The yellow on the cover, and what really got me was the summary. I am a sucker for second chance romances!

I haven't felt that pull to a book in a very long time. Yes, I have been buying CRAP TONS of books lately, but its more out of guilt and anxiety. With Last Years Mistake, there was a special pull, and I know I needed this book in my life right away. I brought this book home and read it in one sitting!

The Gist:

Kelsey and David meet the summer of their freshman year, while on vacation. These two just kind of click immediately as best friends. Kelsey is your shy girl, who generally closes herself off to new people. Where David is more popular especially with the ladies!

While on vacation, Kelsey learns that David will be moving right down the road from her and attending the same school. From there on, the two are inseparable.. Until one night something rbad happens, and it is totally misunderstood, and Kelsey is made the laughing stock of her school/town.

Ready to start fresh, Kelsey and her family move to their summer vacation spot, and Kelsey takes the opportunity to re-invent herself. But what she doesnt know, is David wasn't ready to let her go. So a year later, he is back and ready to get his girl. The problem is, Kelsey already has a new life, new friends, and a new boyfriend, who basically worships the ground she walks on.

Last Years mistake is told not in alternating points of views, but it alternates between the past and present. I think its really cool, because you still get the back story, but it all slowly unravels, until you get all the details of what really happened in the past.

The writing is excellent, all the characters are really likable and are all very easy to relate to. If your in the mood for a fun, fast paced, second chance romance, then I definitely recommend picking this little gem up!

This book has done something to me no other book has done in a long time. My head is still spinning. I requested this book from Netgalley back in December. I REALLY liked the cover. It was beautiful yet mysterious at the same time. But for some reason I couldn't get myself to open the book. Well recently I went into my local bookstore and saw the Trilogy in hardback, I had never seen them in physical form. They were beautiful and used (which put them at like $6 each in hardback). I didn't grab them at first. I went home and started dead beautiful on my Tablet. I was hooked. I immediately facebook messaged the bookstore owner and asked her to hold the three books for me!

So back to the book. Rene is a young girl who on her 16th birthday discovers her parents bodies in the woods. When she finds her parents they have gauze in their mouth and coins surrounding their bodies. Rene is positive that they were murdered, but the experts ruled their deaths as heart attacks.
Rene's grandfather becomes her guardian, uproots her from her life, and Sends her to Gottfried Academy in Maine. Guys this Academy is nothing like it seems. And I'm not saying anymore. The mystery around Gottfried takes you all the way to the end. So no spoilers from me!

The mystery of this book is probably what had me so intrigued. I couldn't put Dead Beautiful down, it kept me wanting more. This book was so unpredictable to me. I had so many guesses as to what was happening and who everyone was, but I was never right. I had an idea who the good guys and bad guys were, but the moment I felt I was sure, Woon sent me through a loop and totally surprised me. That happened so many times through out the book, it was a breath of fresh air. I will say this book does have a slower pace which I'm not used to, but it worked. I still thoroughly enjoyed it and I never got bored.

Normally I am not a fan of insta-love or even a romance that grows as quickly as Dante and Rene's, but if you get through the whole book the insta-love makes sense and it works. That is probably the biggest spoiler I will give. Now with that being said, don't get the idea that this book is full of romance, because it isn't. I would say this is more mystery than romance.

I love this book, Im glad I already have book 2 and 3 waiting for me because otherwise I would be going crazy.

There are very few books that leave me speechless.
When I say very few I mean 2. Ugly Love by Colleen Hoover and this book,
Lev by Belle Aurora. I read this book a week ago, and I haven't
been able to review it. I can't get all my thoughts and feels
out and do this book justice. Seriously, what do you say about a book
that you feel is utterly perfect? No this isn't your classic novel by Jane Austen or Emily Bronte,
but the emotions, the pain, and the rawness of this book, made it perfect for me.

The reason I love this book so much is hard to put into words.
This is a book about Love. The characters are truly beautiful characters and
they don't let petty things drive them apart. Mina could have walked away so many times, and the same with Lev
but they fought for what they both wanted, and that was eachother. They had all of these outside obstacles going
against them, and instead of the author letting it get in the way of the characters, she made it to where
everything they went through made them stronger together. We got to watch a friendship bloom into
a real love and it was so wonderfully magical.

That is the only way I really know how to explain my feelings on this book. If you haven't read this one, I
definitely recommend it.

Take Me Now has left me very mixed. I love the book I am a sap for a great romance, but something's just really bugged me about this novel as well.

Pros: Eric is a hunk of a Hero. The romance is sweet and leaves you giddy. The characters are well developed in their roles. For example Lauren is a Beezy and Faith Sullivan made her into the ultimate beezy. There is NO liking her in this novel. Some authors try to make you sympathize with the villain. Nope Lauren is the ULTIMATE villain. I like Eric's backstory It makes for the perfect romance between Ivy and him.

Cons: The hero/heroine seemed to have NO backbones it literally pissed me off a few times. Like Seriously Ivy, stand the hell up for yourself don't let all these people push you around. That's definitely my view on Ivy is a pushover. I liked her I would of liked her to fight for herself more and standup to Lauren, Will, and Ryan. I didn't like that Lauren was able to string Eric as her puppet because of a secret. Eric/Ivy gave these three characters (Lauren, Will, And Ryan) way too much power.

Otherwise I loved this book. The romance is sweet. It happens fast, but sometimes it does happen that way. I cannot wait for book 2 to be out. I really want to see what choices Ivy makes and the development of their romance!

This is a very quick read. If it was summer I would def. make this my go to beach read.

Good Vibrations is probably one of my favorite, no, I'm pretty sure it is my favorite self published book. I love indie books and authors, but a lot of times you kind of have to weed through the good and the bad. Good Vibrations is definitely on the good scale. This book was a total random buy at my local bookstore and I REALLY need to get my hands on the rest of the series before I go insane. Luckily I did buy a few of her other books before they all sold out.

Mallory goes to school in Boulder, Co, but has decided to spend her summer in Hawaii with her BFF Sunny (Who I absolutely Adore!) Mallory has gone through a stressful semester as well as a terrible breakup, so some fun in the sun is definitely in order.

Evan catches sight of Mallory while in an intense lip lock with last weeks fling (who is about to be heading back home from Hawaii). Evan does not do relationships, flings are his thing, and he makes that very clear, but what happens when you meet a girl who you want to throw your own rules away for?

This book is such a fun read that left me feeling so good inside! This is a new adult so of course it has some steamy scenes, but I'm sure your can tell that by the synopsis ;)

I absolutely LOVE Scott's writing style everything just flows so well and she's able to paint this perfect picture for you. At times I really felt like I was in Hawaii observing Mallory and Evans relationship. I love an author who can transfer you to their fictional world.

The characters are all very likable and I was really able to relate with some of these characters and that's always a plus in my book. I instantly loved Sunny and I know everyone else will too! By the time I closed this book, I felt like I was leaving my friends back in Hawaii to return to reality and I cannot wait to get the next book and return.

I have recommended this book to everyone I know. If you enjoy romance with two characters who have the right amount of sarcasm then this book is definitely for you!

Ok, so I am more of a newbie when it comes to YA compared to most people. I say this because I haven't even been reading YA for a full year yet. I used to read nothing but Adult contemp romances. I loved that they were steamy without all the New Adult graphics (come on everyone knows what I'm talkin' about with all that NA craziness). Any who, I was never into YA contemporary novels. I don't exactly know why since I read a lot of paranormal/dystopian/fantasy YA romance novels. My point is lately I have been on a YA contemporary kick and I am really enjoying it.

I recently read Anna and the French Kiss (I know, why have I waited so long?!?!) and I REALLY liked it, probably my favorite book this month!

So a bit about this wonderful little book!
Anna is sent away to go to school in Paris by her father who is this big time author whom walked out on the family when he made it big. Going to Paris sounds like a dream come true to me, but for Anna it is the end of the world. She has to leave her best friend, her family, the cute boy who has finally showed interest in her, and the worst part is she gets NO say in the matter. The decision was made for her by her dad. Blah. So she meets Mer her next door neighbor in the dorms who introduces Anna to her group of friends and from there we get to see all sorts of relationships form!

This book is a much slower paced book than I am used to, but still incredibly enjoyable. The slow pace works. It helps with the buildup of friendships, relationships, & getting the whole cultural experience through Anna's perspective.

Characters: There are way too many to name that I liked and disliked (which with the characters you dislike you are supposed to, so it's not like I just disliked this person because they weren't developed correctly, I dislike them because they were developed correctly, if that makes sense!) This isn't an insta-love  in the sense of normal insta-loves. The relationship actually takes time to build and neither characters are professing their love on page 10 of chapter 2 :) but there is an instant attraction which is definitely normal in the real world.

All in all I really like this book it comes highly recommended from me. For all you guys and gals looking for a fun beach/pool read, this is the book I would take. I will be re-reading this on my next trip to Oklahoma. I can see myself sitting in my car for 5 hours with my feet propped up on the dash and listening to music reading this!

users.query: I wanted to craft garage doors in the slide-fold fashion. This book provided me with design resources to continue with my project, which I am in the midst of designing and building. Between the internet (which offers many expensive hardware options to construct slide-fold doors) and the ideas presented in this book, I believe my design will function appropriately using much less expensive technology such as a Stanley sliding door mechanism, some welded hinges, and a bottom channel-guide and bearing design that limits the lateral motion of the hinged panels as they are displaced by the effects of wind or the process of opening and closing. If you are involved in the process of creating or installing transitional elements in homes or commercial facilities, you just might find the information in this book will give you the understanding required to surmount problems before they arise.

cands.text: These pulls are impressively stout for the price. I am building a series of drawers without mechanical glides, so something of a robust handle should be of great benefit to wrestle the wide, full-length drawers.

I welded some square tubing to a triangular ring of gate hinges as well as to a quarter inch steel plate platform. I bolted the bar stools swivel to both the tractor seat and the quarter inch plate. I finished the  legs with rubber  tubing  inserts  that preserve the floor from being scratched.

The swivel is pretty quiet, I believe that it will need to be greased from time to time. This type of seat is good for posture when using a laptop at a table, or for playing the guitar. The swiveling of the seat allows greater mobility and provides a more relaxing seating arrangement, than would a static seat, when playing music.

This implement makes entry and exit of a vehicle much more stabile. It takes up little space and is very well made. My wife is currently at a care center after breaking her hip and relearning how to enter and exit a car. I bought this, showed it to the occupational therapists working with my wife (who were unaware of its existence) and they're very interested in showing it to other clients.

My wife has MS. I am a carpenter. The pictures, captions and text provide inspirational (yet often expensive) architectural options that could be pursued during remodel or new construction. It would be great if the next edition provided "motorized" options that raised and lowered sinks and counter methodologies, as reinventing the wheel is expensive and time-consuming business. Suppliers of these options deliver a paucity of details from which might be pillaged lower-cost options by the owner/builder.

Carpentry is pretty much cut and dried lineal measure with a bit of trigonometry mixed in. The best carpentry is exemplified in wooden boats and vacuum molded free-form shapes. I believe this book is a training manual for union carpenters and, as such, is quite thorough in the many aspects of rectilinear construction, form work, and the like. What would really put this book over the top would be if it were to include such green technologies as evidenced in simple shelter literature and practice, such as straw bale building, a bit of geodesic, some timberframe and the use of repurposed construction material applications. Heck, why not throw in a bit of welding and illustrations of the metal to wood types of interfaces that might spur creativity in the industry instead of simply following the status quo. Someone's got to help people be able to build their own houses through improved understanding of alternative technologies and thereby help dial down the restrictiveness of building codes that make no place for innovation.

Hung some steel rain gutter with this. Riveted the "continuous" gutter pieces together. The use of this tool saved me about $2000. The gutter contractors bid $2500 for our home (we are a bit remote). Instead, another (friendly) contractor had me measure the necessary spans and downspout placements and produced (in 35 foot segments) the appropriate guttering for our house for about $550 including all of the downspouts and hangers and seam sealant. Driving it to our house, over the 5000 foot pass that separates our house from my friend's home was a slow, slow drive with the very flexible gutter loosely tied to the 20 foot 2x6's on the truck rack. Ten miles per hour. There was no one else on the road. Not too bad.

This is my first toolbelt-specific-set-of-suspenders. I riveted 4 - 1 inch "D" rings on 1 inch wide leather loops appropriately sized so that my toolbelt belt could run through them. Then I slid on the bags and D-loops on in appropriate order, followed by clipping the suspenders to the adjustable (laterally) D-rings. It is very comfortable. I don't have to cinch my belt and my toolbelt up extremely tight, anymore. Should have done this years ago. The belt keeps my shoulders and back a little bit warmer than usual, however, I have found that, historically, keeping my back warmer than ambient temperature helps to prevent back pain. The central hanging loop at the intersection of the webbing in the back, provides a great place to hang my entire toolbelt/suspender system (on a conveniently placed nail) so that it is at a height ready for me to "take upon me, once again, the trappings of the carpentry industry." Buy these. There may be better systems, but at this price these are a bargain.

I make slab-topped tables. Prior to purchasing this tool, I have used a 3 1/4 inch planer. While the Makita 6 3/4 inch planer weighs a ton, it makes short work of what was once quite a laborious process. I used to freehand with my chainsaw and then use the 3 1/4 inch planer, a process that required careful blending of the many planer passes that were required to level a slab's surface. I have upgraded to the use of an Alaska chainsaw mill and the Makita. Still a lot of work, but the finishing process is expedited, allowing me to spend more time concentrating on the construction and joinery of the dimensional legs and shelves that I typically install as supporting members for the slab tops . . . dimensional lumber that is also roughed out and finished using the chainsaw and the Makita.

Okay, our vacuum is not the best, but when used in consort with this attachment, the results were disappointing. The brush is soft and, since our blinds are 2 3/8" blinds, they are rather far apart and the brush fit okay between the slats, but when you encounter the supporting and adjusting strings of the blinds the bristles of the brush don't have the flexibility to "push" the dust past the strings to be picked up on the other side when you shift the brush to the other side. That is to say . . . I bought a two dollar feather duster and produced a better finish than this attachment made with our "not too superior" vacuum.

As an aside: Swiffer dusters are really good for the short run, but with any real accumulation of dust they are rendered saturated within a brief period of time. The feather duster was able to easily clean our three large venetian blinds and come back for more while swiffer would have cost about two dollars a window to achieve the same end. The feather duster is still ready to go. The swiffers would be in the land fill.

You don't really need this thing if you know what your doing. There are workarounds for everything, but . . . once in a while this item will allow you to rapidly/safely rip up a bunch of wood that will require very little milling/reworking prior to use. It's really best for creating uniform cuts to save your fingers from splinters that would (eventually) cause your fingers to become less useful due to pinching the sole of your circular saw as you do temporarily, as a fence for ripping. Don't try this unless you are pretty experienced with a saw . . . you could get hurt. This fence will help keep you safe when you are ripping wood. A better guide can be made from clamping a 1x on the surface of your stock, but when your stock is narrow, this fence will help you keep more of your saw upon the stock and give you more stability and accuracy than can otherwise be provided. Save your fingers.
Learn how to use this . . . buy one.
