users.query:
I pretty much swore off this series after the last book and wasn't even anticipating Lover Reborn.  But when I saw it sitting on the library shelf I gave in to the BDB pull despite knowing I would likely be disappointed.  Tohr was, after all, one of my favorites.  And ultimately I was not surprised that it contained Ward's latest annoying habit - dedicating half a book to a past couple/character.  UGH.  If John and Xhex were even a remotely believable mated couple than MAYBE it wouldn't be so brain-numbing to read about their melodrama.  However, this was a pairing that never felt genuine in the first place and enforcing unnecessary complications on them in order to pad another's story was annoying, horribly boring and just plain badly done.  And only cemented that they were never a solid pairing.  Very unfortunate decision on Ward's part, yet again.  A lot of her recent books have contained the same writing errors in judgement that can be found here, as well.  The Take Two of Xhex and John aside, Lover Reborn had too great a uniformity between all the characters in the way they speak, think and interact.  Apparently, the BDB lingo extends to even shellans and secondary characters.  Well, excluding the Chosen.  Verily verily.  And what was up with the questions without question marks.  Sorry Ward but you are not good enough to rewrite what proper punctuation is.  And the sudden unimportance of the Lessening Society is strange and doesn't seem to fit with the entire premise of the BDB world.  Just not buying it.

And though I'm liking Layla for the first time and am intrigued by the direction her story is taking, I do not like the 'let's get pregnant so we have somebody to love' part.  AHH.  Why, oh why?  I do like Quinn and Blay.  Too bad they can't just have an HEA.  But even though the next book might be about them...Ward will screw it up.  Evidence of this is everywhere.  It seems she can't just write a tight, intense and sensible story anymore.

And Tohr?  Well...it could have been worse.  But would have been better if the BDB mansion hadn't already descended to a bad soap opera.  He deserved more.  And more to the point - Autumn/No'one deserved more.  She deserved a true mate.  A bonding scent, possessive, loving Mate.  She got the short straw though and doesn't that seem to make her a perpetuating tragedy?

Now the Band of Bastards is working for me.  But this could just because the BDB has stalled, gotten stale and needs a knew cast of reliable characters.  Maybe, just maybe, focusing outside the BDB mansion will help Ward refocus her writing and storytelling.  Here's hoping....though I sense a Tohr and Autumn Take Two in the future.  Sigh.

cands.text:
Ward has lost all focus on what made her BDB series a success in the first place.  The first books snagged her a substantial and supportive audience.  Her recent books in the series have left those same fans confused and disappointed.  We keep hanging on, hoping that the great romances and basic plot devices would return, that what made this series great would prevail through all the deteriorating dialogue, sideline antics and poor romance hookups.  Unfortunately that hasn't happened and I am now joining the many who have let go.  One has to wonder why Ward can't stay focused and remember that her original premise was what garnered her the audience she now has.  All the contradictions and backtracking, complications and errors, are signs of an average, even bad, writer. Maybe she has overwhelmed herself and not just her audience with her increasingly convoluted plots (not to mention her fixation on poorly conveyed and overused BDB lingo).  If it wasn't broke, Ward, why fix it?  Go back to what worked in the beginning and you will have saved yourself and your fans.

One good note- I liked that vamps from outside little Caldwell were finally introduced.  It was about time.

I'll keep and re-read the first books in the series, as I am still a fan of those.  And I hope Tohr's story gets the reverence and emotional depth and attention it deserves.  However, I no longer trust Ward and will not read it unless the reviews are great and the fans still holding on are happy.

This Review has Spoilers.

Ok, I read this book to follow the series, which seems to be the only reason I've read the last two (hated Phury's book).  I was hoping it would rev me back up and it did, but not as much as I would have liked.  My list of likes and dislikes for Lover Mine:

LIKE:
1. The best part of this book?  Quinn and Blay.  Great sub-story and it kept me totally captivated.  They need to continue this "I love you but I love you not" conflict (poor Quinn, he's so confused) for a at least one more book (where Blay is serious with Saxton the whole time) and then BAM, a hot scene and they have their HEA.
2. Payne's story. I can't wait to see her and V interact and love that there's another kicka** chick hanging with the Brothers.  Also, her and Manny?  Maybe, and sounds good...can't wait to see how Manny fits into everything, so I love that the next book will bringing him in again.
3. Xhex's inner-pain and repression finally breaking through.  It had to happen for any resolution to occur.  She's still tough but after all she's been through, there had to be a breaking point.  And liked that John was there for her the whole way.
4. Lash's downfall.
5. John and Tohr coming to terms.
6. Darius and Tohr's back-in-time subplot.  It opened up more understanding of the characters and gave a glimpse of what John is subconciously remembering from his time as Darius.  The apple tree, in particular, was a nice touch.

DISLIKE:
1. The gratuitous profanity, which at times distracted other than enhanced the scene.  The uncreative chapter beginnings...so many times it was the same!  Especially with Lash and Xhex always "waking up" or "coming to" right at the beginning.  It all became tedious and redundant.
2. Xhex and John did not have the same intensity and passion as all the other Brothers.  Was this a writing problem or a basic forcing of characters that didn't belong problem?  Don't know, but it was disappointing.
3. The overuse of subplots.  The Lessers/Lash got waaaay too much page time.  As did the reality tv producer and his girlfriend subplot.  Was it that necessary to continously go back to those two??  I mean, we didn't even really see or hear from Murhder but we sure got alot of info about seemingly superfluous characters.  They needed to be cut back...alot.  It got in the way.
4.  I really don't like that Quinn is so hung up on his mismatched eyes.  After what everyone else in the series has gone through, that seems so ridiculously minor.  He needs to get over it.
5.  I dislike that alot of Brothers, and their mates, were not given much page space.  We don't even see Beth, John's sister!  I believe this is because JR spent much too much time on the subplots, giving time to tv host, etc and not the people in John's life and the people we have become invested in.  What a wasted use of characters, in general, in this book.
6. Xhex should not have been invited to fight with the Brothers so quickly.  If John and company are not even inducted yet, why is she so suddenly and openly accepted into a supposedly close-knit and secretive group?  Didn't buy it.
7. No'Ones identity was fine by me...what I hated was how she revealed herself.  It happened too quickly and wasn't even interesting.  No suspense at all.  Maybe should have waited until the next book for that reunion.  It felt like JR was just trying to quickly wrap everything up in a nice bow for Xhex right at the end.  Yawn.  And unrealistic.  Hated it.

All that being said, I give the book 3.5 Stars.  Much of what I liked about the book wasn't even between the "main" characters - John and Xhex, which in my mind means their story was unsuccessful overall.  So, can't give it a 4 Star.

However, I am, as always, looking forward to the next book!  This book did get me excited about the next one.

I knew that this was a multiple partner story before I read it.  I picked it up intentionally to see if buying the first book would be worthwhile.  I have decided against it.  There were just too many creep factors for me, personally, to become that involved in the characters or even to find the love scenes all that erotic (in fact, I found them very bland).  The creep factors were:
1. The three men are brothers, which I hadn't expected to be that bothered by but once I started reading I didn't find it intriguing at all or believable.
2.  The female protagonist systemically "corners" each brother and practically begs for sex from each man in turn.  Just not sexy or romantic.
3.  She's 8 months pregnant at the time.
4.  They all call the child "theirs"...he is "their son"...as in they do not know who fathered the baby and so all claim him. Something about this went against my own peace of mind.  Maybe too...cult-like?  Takes me to number 5...
5.  The entire scenario is so unrealistic that even for a book I couldn't suspend my disbelief.  The author writes the 4-way relationship as a pleasant, laid back one, with no jealousy issues or the woman just throwing her hands up and saying "I need space, quit touching me for one freaking minute".  All is perfect in their world, nobody minds sharing and they all know each other's business.  And sure, the heroine is well cared and the men genuinely love her, but at the same time she is overly cossetted.  It left me feeling like she had no real freedom, always surrounded by men hovering over her.  She didn't have enough of an independent spirit for the heroines I usually like reading about.  Oh, and the birth scene was poorly written and also not realistic at all.

Some people will like and have liked this story just fine and are not bothered by any of the things that bothered me.  I tried it and I just didn't like it.

I love Julia Quinn's books and always look forward to each one.  And though I was a bit disappointed with JUST LIKE HEAVEN, the first of the Smythe-Smith books, I still enjoyed it.  Thankfully, though, this installment was an improvement from the first.  Still light-hearted fun with cute characters and entertaining scenarios.  But this one felt more focused.  It had a more defined plot and an added mystery that kept things engrossing.  And the humor was just right, it avoided being used as much as "filler", like I felt the previous book was.  The character of Daniel was down-to-earth, a family man (which is a nice change from some romance books) and yet still had that alpha edge.  And Anne, though at times a bit thickheaded, was still believable and relatable.  I just really loved this story.  Not nail-biting suspense or serious drama or thought-provoking tale.  Just good, laidback fun.  It was so cute, so fun and a perfect use of four hours of leisure time.

I have read all of Lackey's 500 Kingdom books and can't quite decide why I have bothered with them.  They are all very predictable, somewhat stilted and sadly lacking in suspense.  And this latest addition to the series epitomizes everything that has bothered me in the past books.  The villain of "Beauty and the Werewolf" was obvious from the start, all the clues where laid out right in front of the reader AND the characters and yet the characters (all supposedly very clever and experienced) never figure it out until it is "too late"...ugh.  The very stupidity of it irritated me.  Furthermore, the villain was for more interesting and I think had much better chemistry with Bella than the "hero" does.  The romance was very lacking, the relationship between Bella and Sebastian was so platonic and indifferent until the last fourth of the book that it wasn't believable when they suddenly kissed or Bella suddenly proclaimed love.  It was very dry and though the situation could have developed into love it just wasn't written convincingly enough to sell it (Bella spends more time with the villain than the hero, for crying out loud).  And the character of Bella?  She was so abrasive, self-important and bossy.  A shrew.  And though she points this out about herself, in passing, a couple times, that self-reflection doesn't change her for the better.  And why all the other characters think she is "all that and a bag of chips" is beyond me.  She held onto her grudge against the King until the very end, which was ridiculous and all sorts of blown out of proportion.

Ultimately, this series provides some interesting takes on fairy tales and I suppose that's why I stuck with it.  But now?  I'm pretty done.  The Tradition is hammered out in boring detail in every book and each story, in and of itself, is trite and most of the characters have lacked depth (which hurt the romance) and all of the stories have lacked edge-of-your-seat suspense (in fact, this book was downright boring).  What was fun escapist reading in the beginning has transitioned into a test of patience and now I get more irritated by these books than relaxed.

I was aware of what I was getting into, having been told about the book by someone else and recognizing it as an inspirational/Christian regency romance.  However, what I heard from others was so positive, that I was surprised by how very bland this book ended up being.

The book is filled with circular conversations, repeated inner monologues and very s l o w progression.  Nothing, as in really nothing, happens for most of the book, just a lot of fretting and worrying and then rinsing and repeating.  And the characters?  Ugh.  Amelia, who IS the heiress to Winterwood and a very rich woman, never can get a word out in defense of herself, as everyone else is always steamrolling over her and acting as if Winterwood is their right and she allows it, her attempts at showing backbone always aborted.  And the Captain, the reluctant love interest, is the epitome of gentlemanly behavior and defender of virtue that comes across rather...well, bland.  Of course, all the characters but four are somehow shown to be weak (via gambling, drinking, etc), mean-spirited, self-promoting, manipulative and unsupportive in the extreme.  The four characters that aren't this way?  Amelia, the Captain, and the victor and the victor's wife (how original).

The plot is weak.  The writing tedious.  The characters bland.  The end result is uninspiring.  I can say there was good editing and beautiful cover art, combined with a promising premise.  But the execution left much to be desired.  I'm not so sure I'll be able to read another Sarah E. Ladd, no matter how highly recommended to me.

Admittedly, I missed book 5 (I thought I had the order right but nope.)  And that was likely the one that was different, considering it's the only non-Theronai main couple so far.  However, that means there's still been five books of the same dang thing: a Theronai female who doesn't know what she is and doesn't accept the truth for a long time or at the very least believes everything that she is feeling is some kind of magical trick and manipulation or brainwashing.  This theme has gotten old and worn out.  Jackie, the heroine of DYING WISH, is very angsty, her inner monologue a long repetitive track of "I want my old life, I don't accept this, I don't believe what I'm feeling is real, this world isn't for me".  And though I liked that Iain is the first male to actively resist the bonding with a female, it was unfortunate that Jackie chooses him because of that.  It would be nice to see a woman ready-to-go and be accepting while the male has to change his perspective.  In this story, we just get two hard-headed people with repetitive thought processes.

Don't get me wrong, this series is packed FULL of creativity and imagination.  The world itself is complicated and fascinating.  I've enjoyed it.  However, if the next books will just be more of the same...I might be done.  I don't want to spend another 350+ pages listening to female characters come up with one denial after another.

Jackie, like most of heroines of the past, of course comes around in the end.  And the way she does it is so fast you might get whiplash.  One second she's leaving and never coming back, naively and foolishly heading off to comfortable corporate boredom and the next she's done a complete one-eighty and is gung-ho in love and on board.  Her sudden change isn't true to form and a bit off putting.  However, it's hard to complain too loudly since she does it to save Iain.  And the way she does it is great.  I very much liked this resolution, it was imaginative, even if I didn't like how remarkably repetitive the journey was getting there.  And Jackie's ability is, well, super awesome.

There are a handful of characters I would like to continue on with and read about.  And, of course, the plots have thickened considerably and become increasingly complex and incomplete (this is also somewhat frustrating, seems like the story is getting away from the author.)  Just not sure if I should continue on with the series.  Any more digging-in-her-heels heroines will turn me off and yet I foresee that happening.

This book was a mixed bag for me.  I enjoyed it overall but wasn't remotely blown away by it and, in my opinion, the next books in the series are overpriced so I won't be continuing on with it.  A quick look at what did and didn't work:

Pros:  Good storyline and character development.  A plot that moves along with only some humdrum boring parts.  I liked the world building though this could have been given more attention.

Cons:  The continuity issues (some obvious ones that the author definitely should have caught) and grammar mistakes were distracting.  The story is also very predictable and at times improbable or all-too-convenient.  I also found the romance lackluster because it was too much like a cardboard cut-out of every other paranormal/fantasy/sci-fi "mated" trope.  Nothing that original there.

Over-all I enjoyed this book.  It had great imagery and the reader will become engrossed in Joanna's life-long pursuit for answers.  Joanna's final discovery (practically on the very last page, bytheway) is beautifully written and I'm glad her daughter apart of it.  However, I was sorely disappointed by the unrewarding and sudden ending.  Too many characters were left in limbo, there were a lot of holes and questions that lingered.  It was as if the author just excused herself and ended it because it had all become tedious (it was 450 some pages of character development she suddenly dropped).  Very unfortunate.  A sequel is desperately needed to make the ending of this book tolerable.  And I would not buy it without a sequel to go along with it.  I'll return the book to the library and try not to stew too much.

First of all, I love, absolutely love, Showalter's wonderfully rich imagination.  Her Atlantis series and Lords of the Underworld series have proven that she has IDEAS and can even, sometimes, write them down very well.  I find her a refreshing reprieve from the often dark and overly slangy and badmouthed BDB (J.R. Ward's series, which I love).  She is very original in her overall concepts.  However, sigh..., she underdevelops her characters and plots.  Her sex scences are lacking.  Which is surprising, considered how much internalizing the characters do.  I felt the Maddox and Ashlyn had potential but not enough time to fulfill much of it.  And her "fairy godmother" Anya was a cheezy and simple way to make everything better right at the very end, with no real climax to the story.  Also, she tried much too hard to overdevelop her story by adding the second set of Lords half-way through the FIRST book.  Those characters should not have entered onto the scence for a couple more books, at least.  Leave the readers WANTING to learn about them and meet them, just don't throw them in without a by-you-leave and crowd your pages with too many cardboard cutouts.  I wanted to get to know the first characters first, but had no time to really determine who they were or care.

I will continue with this series for a little more and see if Showalter can bring things into better focus.  I'll give her more time because I love the ideas behind her books and know she can write better...well, as long as she doesn't repeat the horribly out-of-character and cheezy dialogue on the last page of Darkest Night.  Ugh.

I have fallen in love with this series and hope it continues for a long while.  I read all four in a week-long binge, buying one after the other, because I couldn't get enough (and instead of writing raving reviews for all four, I decided to just write the one for expediency's sake.)  What a fantastic, creative and wonderful mix of history, adventure, romance, and the supernatural.  The premise is so intriguing and as a history lover,  I was thrilled that this series is not just another modern-urban-fantasy (which seems to overwhelm the literary supernatural market these days.)  The primary characters are interesting on their own, well developed with distinct personalities and then when you put them together they are irresistible as a team and as a couple.  The action is intense in all the books, with a standard yet well grounded Good vs Evil plot.  The story is detailed, well written and just plain fun.  Highly recommended for those looking for a meatier and unusual new twist in romantic supernatural adventures.  And can I just say that the cover art on these books is some of my favorite out there?

I am simultaneously disappointed and intrigued by this story.  The premise was excellent.  And I did grow to care about the characters though I had a difficult time connecting with them initially.  However, there were several issues I had a hard time overlooking:

1.  The writing style.  It took me many chapters to "get into the flow" of the author's peculiar way of writing.  The dialogue in particular often felt wooden and out of place.  Also, there were some truly awful transitions, which was distracting (at one point I actually flipped back to see if I had skipped a page).  And the too obvious attempts at quirkiness often felt uncomfortable and forced.
2.  Predictability.  There wasn't one single surprise in the entire novel.  The "hints" to the plot that the characters missed were rather clumsily done thus making everything obvious to the reader.  Where's the fun in that?  Also, the bad guys and their evil plot had a been-there-done-that feel to it.
3.  Lack of World Building.  The Victorian era setting where the supernatural are a known and, mostly, acceptable entity was only superficially explained in this book.

I wanted to love this book.  And I found certain aspects of it appealing (the soul as an actual quantifiable entity was very interesting).  However, the steam-punk aspect was downplayed and glossed over..  The supernatural element was the most prominent genre but it got muddled by a lack of explanation.  And though this was not a bodice-ripper as some have said (there are a couple short kissing scenes and one love scene at the end but it is not too descriptive) what is there was a bit contrived.  In short, the mixing of genres, which I was excited about, was poorly handled by the author.  Combine this was the three main issues I had with the book and I have to give it 2.5 stars, rounded up because this was the author's first.  This was an entirely uncomplicated book and not necessarily in a good way (it desperately needed some more...soul).  And though I might pick up the next one if I see it on a shelf somewhere, I won't be rushing out to buy it either.

The opener was solid and had my interest right away.  However, it quickly began to dwindle as the characters were introduced and their personalities were shown.  I don't think a single positive thing happens in the first several chapters to anyone (minus the Prologue) nor did a single likeable character stand out enough to make me care much about what was happening (with a possible exception of the younger daughter).  The story contained some surprises that helped me keep reading but over-all, once the interest waned due to the lack of connection to the characters, it was hard to stay focused on the book and it took me longer to read than most stories of a similiar length.  This book was a dreary rather humorless read and it just wasn't able to hold my attention.  However, if I had been in the mood for this type of story I might have had an easier time of it since the author is a skilled writer and the storyline was obviously well thought out.

First of all, I liked Wicked Intentions (Book 1 of the Maiden Lane series) much more than this one.  It had better tensions and character development, more mystery and more passion.  That being said, I still enjoyed this book and am really excited about the third book (mostly because I cannot wait for that story line to continue and see more of those past characters).  I liked that the main characters could be contradictory and unsure of themselves as it made their personalities more realistic, and it was great fun to get to know them.  Elizabeth Hoyt is a treasure and I'm glad I stumbled upon her.

I admit it took me awhile to finally sit down and read past the first few pages of this book.  But once I did?  I was hooked.  What a fun and lovely combination of characters, inventions, intrigues and plots.  I felt that most the characters were well-thought out and that the plot was complex without being convoluted.  And I very much appreciated that the author was detailed and scientific in her approach to her steampunk world.  I thought, as I was reading, that surely this author must have a background that qualifies her to know some of this stuff.  And apparently, after reading the author bio, that is indeed the case.  That expertise shows in the storyline.  It gave the steampunk world and medical devices an added touch of realism that I appreciated.  But also, it wasn't so overly detailed on the science side to be off-putting to a layman.  Over-all, a well-balanced writing style.

If I had any criticisms, it might be that the story could feel slow at times and that it was fairly predictable.  The mystery did offer up a last minute surprise but by the time it came about, it was no longer that much of one.  Also, the hero could be annoyingly wishy-washy in his actions, especially in regards to the heroine, Lady Amanda.  Amanda herself felt like a genuine and solid character.  And lastly, I really wish the author would come out with a prequel that gives readers a chance to see the sister, Emily, and her love story unfold.  It was a little frustrating to come into such a potentially interesting side-story, after the fact.

That being said, I was excited to see a sequel had already come out, as am definitely interested in continuing in this steampunk world.

Too many inconsistencies right from the start and I couldn't like the main character, Erin, which made getting into this book very difficult and I eventually gave up on it.  The author wrote as if she herself didn't know her character and she certainly wrote as if she didn't understand psychology at all.  One page, Erin, can't even recall what lycanthropy means and then a few pages later, during her rather unprofessional questioning of the patient, she is suddenly an expert on "clinical lycanthropy" (what, did she do a quick Wikipedia search before showing up?  Must have).  That is only one of several examples of the inconsistencies this book had just in the first few chapters.  For some readers, they don't catch it or don't care, but for me it's a major distraction.

And as for Erin, she is established as being cold and disdainful from the first pages (she turns her nose up at another doctor for his, in her opinion, lack of professional ethics but then calls mental patients "madmen" and only agrees to see Conner because she's bored and he might be her "pavlov's dog" that helps her career? lol).  There's a fine line an author has to write on if they set up their character with that kind of personality because you still want her to be likable.  For me, Erin with her inconsistencies and superiority, was unlikeable right away and when the author tried to "save" her and make her likable it wasn't believable.

Also, the plot was never engaging and it felt as if the author was trying very hard to wax poetic at times (which was only moderately successful).  There are elements of the story and writing that should have worked well but it just didn't happen here, at least not for me.  But in terms of freebie self-publishing ebooks this was better done than a lot of others out there (thus, 2 stars instead of 1).

Other reviewers have mentioned that the ending was a stretch and I couldn't agree more.  In fact, the ending required a reader to suspend disbelief so much that the entire novel was thrown off balance by it.  Previous to the final maybe 40ish pages the story was well paced and believable despite some minor flaws.  Then, suddenly, nevermind trying for historical realism within a mostly well-crafted historical fiction and let's just be as improbable, even absurd, as possible so that the heroine can have her cake and eat it too.  I was, as you can tell, disappointed by it.

The main character is a young woman and mother named Anna.  She is likeable because of her strengths and her faults.  She is also sometimes unlikeable because of them.  There are some wise observations she has, though, that stood out, one of which is that we don't really know a person even if we see them everyday.  Anna learns this about her friend, Elinor, and ultimately she learns this about the Rector, as well.  Some readers won't like the revelation about him at the end and certainly it was distasteful and I didn't like it either.  However, it didn't negate all the positive attributes he had demonstrated throughout the book and I found him to be a very sympathetic character.  I felt he deserved a more fitting end than how it was left, which basically was the author making a last ditch effort to redeem him after throwing him under the proverbial...cart.

It also sometimes felt as if the author was trying to throw as much plague hysteria into her story as possible.  This poor village is beset with every social and religious syndrome of the plague.  We find isolation, fear, opportunists, insanity, mob madness, witch hunting, murder, flagellants, nihilism, drug and alcohol use, etc.  It made for a good story and was historically accurate as it spanned the spectrum of plague consequences (even including how a village decimated by the plague cannot properly function anymore without the people to run it).  The tale was well written with excellent prose and dialogue.  But sometimes the events felt forced, much like the ending was.

I really think I would have given this book 5 stars if it weren't for the end.  Instead, it falls somewhere in the 3 to 4 star range for me.  Just wish I could alter the last couple chapters....  But I know some readers have and will like it just fine the way it is and I would still recommend it.

.

There was a lot I enjoyed about ZERO AT THE BONE.  For starters, the interactions between D, an assassin with a conscience, and Jack, a surgeon in Witness Protection, were great and their burgeoning relationship was intriguing to read about.  There are some action sequences to keep things from being too boring (bad guys, bullet wounds, crazy revenge scheme against D).  The author does a good job not rushing into a romantic relationship between her protagonists.  Also, the readers get inside the character's heads.  We know what they are thinking and feeling and come to understand each as an individual.  The plot was suitably complicated with no annoying holes (my one beef would be that D uses his brother's house and yet somehow that's not a problem whereas using Jack's ex-father-in-law's sister's cabin is a big deal...ookaay).  Also, the author obviously spent time proofreading beyond spell check (thank you!).  With some changes, this book could easily have been a 4 star or more.  However, there are some problems I had with the story that kept me from really loving it.  A few are mentioned below.

The biggest problem of all was D's accent.  It immediately hurt the book because it was so bad I had to rewrite his lines in my head as I was reading them for it to be bearable.  At first, I tried to read it the way it was written.  But it just sounded entirely ill-suited and unnatural, was poorly written and threw me right out of the story and the character of D.  This is a man who has been travelling the world since age 18, after he joined the military.  Even if his roots originally caused his dialect (which the author never specifies) by the age of 36, after decades removed from it's source, it would have smoothed out, especially considering his line of work would necessitate a less conspicuous sound.  The author could have made his voice sound unique from Jack's, less 'educated', without totally dumbing him down.  Surely someone mentioned this to her before she published?  It's a shame that this book was held back by D's voice because so much about the story was well done.  However, the voice of a character is very important.  It is inescapable and affects the entire reading experience.

The second major problem was the length.  300 plus pages are not a bad thing, most novels are approximately that many.  However, this story wasn't "tight" enough for it to work.  Cut a few paragraphs here, shorten some scenes here and there, and the story wouldn't have dragged as much.

The first time D and Jack have sex is very short and jarring.  This was a smaller issue but stood out all the same.  It was as if the author didn't know how to transition her characters into a sexual relationship, or a relationship beyond the external one, so she got it over with as quickly as possible.  Maybe she should have been less subtle sooner about their mutual attraction to each other?  And really, no lube or preparation?  Yet later in the book when they don't use lube it's suddenly an issue (they have to stop because it hurts and yet it magically didn't hurt the first time).  Be consistent.

Overall, I would recommend this book.  Is it even worth a few bucks to read?  Probably.  Is it worth $6.29?  No.  If you are considering it, look for it elsewhere first (scribd.com would be a good bet, even it it doesn't have the whole thing it will likely give a good sample of it).  That's my advice, anyhow.

I have never read a Lynn Kurland novel but decided to try this book because I enjoy fantasies that have a romantic element.  To be clear, I did not read the previous books in the series and thought that this was a stand alone book within her Nine Kingdoms series (the cover and backcover do not give an unfamiliar reader any indication that it is not a stand alone unless it was in the section that was covered by the library barcode, lol).  I realized fairly quickly, however, that this was a sequel.  And it wasn't all that difficult to catch up to the story since there seemed to be a lot of rehashing.

I think, in some ways, I can offer a more unbiased few of the author's writing and story than some other reviewers since I am not familiar with this author or her series and therefore I am not inclined to be forgiving towards the book.  Because, honestly, this story, which had potential, was very frustrating to read.  The heroine is clueless (about her looks, about her abilities, about her background, about...well, just about everything) and is always doing things (at the drop of a hat, bytheway) that are unusual or special or interesting to the other characters but SHE doesn't seem to think it requires more contemplation about herself and what she does.  And since the hero, Runach, witnesses all of her abilities unfolding but still continues to think she is without magic, it really just makes him look as clueless as her.  He kept saying he would give himself time to think it through "later" when he had time.  What?  You don't have time to think?  Unlikely.  Neither one of the main characters were very believable and thus I didn't connect to them.

As for the writing itself...had clumsy foreshadowing, a shallow plot and was sorely lacking in descriptiveness.  Events occur quickly and without suspense.  And the dialogue?  Repetitive (yes, yes, we get it, he doesn't have magic anymore and she had a terrible upbringing).  And if one more character was going to say to Runach "do you know what she is" but then NOT tell him a dang thing, I was going to throw the book across the room (and he would then say to himself "I'll think about it later", lol).  It felt as if the author was just trying to drag the story out longer to justify needing three books (or maybe it was the only way the author knew how to put in foreshadowing/suspense?).

The end was somewhat abrupt and left a lot of unanswered questions.  Which, of course, is intentional.  However, I didn't really care and won't be picking up the next book to find out how it all ends (the main characters seemed too clueless to have any chance of success in accomplishing their quests but we all know they will).  I love fantasy and romance and wanted to like this book.  But it was poorly executed and over-all lacked depth.

~Spoiler Alert~
What can I say that hasn't already been said by other reviewers?  The story of Winter was fascinating and delicious to read and I was not disappointed in it, despite some plot issues.  In fact, I have so much faith in Hoyt's storytelling ability that I'm holding off my final judgement on some of those issues - perhaps it will not be surprising if the tale of Lord d'Arque (who thus far is written rather shallowly) and his interest in the Foundling Home will be revealed in the next book, LORD OF DARKNESS.  We already know, thanks to the glimpse we got of this book, that some mysteries which started in THIEF OF SHADOWS will be resolved; we have only to wait for it.  And as for the wonderful surprise at the end of THIEF OF SHADOWS...I'm so happy I can still be taken off guard by a book.  I didn't see it coming, though perhaps I should have.  I love that Winter's retirement from crime fighting is not the end of his crime-fighting persona, that that particular tale is far larger than we were originally led to believe.

I also liked that Winter was a virgin, younger than our heroine and that our heroine was able to learn more about herself and personally grow and develop throughout the book.  And if the lovemaking scenes were not as intense as past books in the series, I can live with that.  And if some things felt somewhat contrived, I can live with that too.  Though it is unfortunate and the reason I can't give 5 stars.  Over-all, Hoyt delivered another unique love story between two individuals with totally different backgrounds.  This basic premise works well for her; she has a real talent for creating an intriguing, well-built tension between her characters.  And, as usual, I will be anxiously awaiting the next installment.

Byer's research and writing style shine in this 400+ page tale about the human desires we all have and the lengths we go to in order to find/fuel those desires.  The story is packed full (perhaps too full) with zanny, earthy and legally insane characters that will keep the reader anxiously waiting for their favorite storyline to continue.  The search for Planet X (Pluto) is, at times, a side note, the vehicle used to move the story along, and yet it is still intriguing enough to keep up a decent core narration.  At times, the supposed main character, Clyde, is left in the dust by far more interesting and dialogue rich characters, which can be confusing, and yet at the same time Clyde, who ultimately discovers Pluto, is perhaps the least interesting of them all so the reader doesn't much mind his sidekick statis.  My only true complaint is that the beauty of the stars and the fascinating and complex mystery of the heavens are not fully appreciated by the author, who reduces space to mathematics and apathic characterizations (though, of course, astronomy is largely done through mathematics, it is not what usually captures the imagination).  I enjoyed the book overall and would recommend it to most people.  However, it could be unnecessarily "heavy" and slow moving and most of the meaning is not on the surface of the text and for this reason I would not recommend it to everyone.  The search for Pluto is, when viewed as a metaphor, far more interesting than anything tangible.

Maybe it was the cover, the title, the lack of reviews or the premise but for some reason I was not expecting much of this novella.  However, the price was right (free) and I decided to take a chance because I was just in the right mood to check it out.  J.T. Hall was unfamiliar to me and, I apologize to the author, but I think I thought I would be deleting this one before the first chapter ended.

I was wrong.  Not only was the writing impressive with solid editing but the story was also impressive.  Excellent characterization and descriptions.  The storyline was written convincingly without any over-the-top drama.  The whole thing was surprisingly believable with a nice layer of tension.  There was a small but well-done plot propelling all the characters and bringing them together.  The author even managed to put in a brief flashback that didn't distract from the main story but add to it.  That's hard to do with such limited page space.  Over-all, I enjoyed it very much and am glad I took the chance on it.

FYI:  Three dudes, if you hadn't noticed from the title.  Mild police-related action/violence.  Profanity but not gratuitious.  One descriptive sex scene, BDSM-themed and somewhat prolonged.

A short, cute, and clean romance set in a fantasy world of elves and humans.  The characters were likeable and the worldbuilding was decent.  I did think, however, that the story felt like a sequel or like a book set in a world the author had already set up in a series somewhere...there could have been better clarity and pacing, over-all, in terms of the worldbuilding.

The romance was interesting and mostly fun to read about.  The plot was simplistic and there was a general lack of suspense but there was a mysterious antagonist that attacks Tari more than once, so the author did attempt to write something more than just a romance.  I would have liked to see this part of the story be more tense and uncertain, but there is, really, little actual drama here and the writing was unexciting.  The most drama comes from Tari and Arion making false assumptions about how the other feels (of course).

The editting errors could be distracting, as well, but it wasn't terrible.  Over-all, this was an easy, light romance with a hint of plot and mystery to keep readers turning pages (albeit slowly).

Though, to be fair, LONGBOURN is not as much as a spin-off as one would think by the blurbs.  And I do admit that I would not have picked up this novel without the P&P connection and one that is a new idea compared to zombies and sequels galore.

Unfortunately, despite the interesting concept, the story was lackluster and hard to "get into".  I have read historical fiction/non-fiction and classical literature for many years now and have trudged through some painstakingly slow and long-winded books.  I like to think a short-attention span wasn't the reason I found the story so dull.

For me, the characters just didn't come alive, they were flat, and the plot was thin and predictable.  And not the kind of engaging predictability that P&P has, where we know how it will end for Elizabeth and Darcy but can still anticipate the journey they take to get there.  In LONGBOURNE, the characters, the journey and the destination all feel less rewarding (the flip-side of writing a novel based on, however loosely, Pride and Prejudice - it's hard to live up to the original).

Baker had her own voice and I think it was a good choice to stay away from mimicry.  However, as a counterpoint, it felt as if she did attempt to make up for this by giving the novel a heavier atmosphere.  No Austen wit or humor to be found here, which was a shame as there was good potential for it and the story needed it.  Also, fans of P&P might be unhappy with how little their favorite characters make an appearance and when they do, how little they are seen favorably (Baker might have pushed this too much).

As a concept, the P&P idea isn't new but focusing on the serving class was intriguing and I wanted to find this story fresh and engaging.  But I ended up feeling lukewarm about it and can only say that, though I don't regret reading it, I'm glad I borrowed it.

users.query: This was great until it wasn't. Keep in mind I used it for about a year, but after a year it got stained really easily. It looked dirty all the time and I tried everything to clean it with no good results. I loved the way it looked, a little blingy and since I fish I loved that the back looked like fish scales. It protected my phone fairly well. I dropped my phone a lot and it wasn't enough to keep the tempered glass screen protector from cracking but that was easily replaced. I would say compared to otterbox, it's moderate protection but looks good.

cands.text: I absolutely love this phone case! I love the color, the design, the magnets are strong and hold my phone well. The only bad thing I can say about it is the eyelet/gromet that the wrist strap snaps into fell out almost immediately. Now the wrist strap is just in an unprotected hole that I'm hoping will hold up and not tear through. I would certainly buy it again.

I actually bought two phone cases for my Galaxy S5 and I've used the other one primarily. This one is more of a baby blue in person and I was hoping for more of a teal. Other than that it's great. The magnets are good and strong and hold the phone in well. I bought both of the cases because I wanted to be able to leave my purse in my truck when I wanted to make a quick dash into a store and still have my debit card & ID with me. This works perfectly for that and much more.

For full disclosure 1) In January 2015, I purchased the IGEN Waterproof Case - Universal Protective Cover for my Samsung Galaxy S5 and really liked it so I figured I'd like this too. 2) I was able to purchase this IGEN protective case at a discount in exchange for an honest review.

Let me first say, this is more than a tablet case! This would be a perfect dry bag for taking to water/amusement parks, on a cruise, to the swimming pool, beach, in the rain, anywhere you might be where you need to keep something dry or just need to safely tote small stuff around. I will be using this for my tablet, but also my phone along with anything else I need to tuck away and keep close. The lanyard adjust from approximately 27" to 49" and can be worn around the neck or, extended fully could be worn cross-body too.

Like I said, I really liked my IGEN protective case that I purchased earlier this year for my phone. Please feel free to read my review about it for which I DID NOT receive a discount. (I will try to provide a link below). I totally expected pretty much the same thing but I was wrong. Although I have not had any issues with my protective phone case, this protective tablet case is made of a material that feels more durable, more like rubber. As I said in my other review, my hubby and I fish. Not only do I like to keep my phone with me when I fish, I also have to keep things handy like fishing licenses, cash, room & car keys, etc. This will be my new "go-to" bag for my tablet but also for my phone when we go fishing because it will hold my phone and so much more. I like that the backside of the case is not see-thru except for the camera slot. This will prevent things like money from being seen easily.

So, now that I've covered a few of the awesome ways you can use it, I'll say it's very cool simply as a tablet dry case. It has a window for your camera if you have a camera on the backside of your tablet. I have a Kindle Fire that fits nicely inside and I can still turn it on and off. It operates through the clear screen but you do have to press so your finger makes contact with the table screen (or at least on mine I do). You could use it to record on-the-go but don't want to spend $500 on a fancy little portable camera. Just put the lanyard on with the camera pointing away from you. The lanyard will keep little hands from dropping it as well. You can use the lanyard to attach it to a shopping cart to keep it from being dropped or stolen while your child plays as you shop or as you use it for a grocery list. The case has a nifty strap on the back where you can slip your hand for holding it in a horizontal or vertical position. It can also be worn horizontal by fastening one clip in each grommet or vertical by clipping fastening one clip in one grommet and the 2nd clip to the 1st clip. And the best part is the waterproof case is truly waterproof! The construction of this case is even better than my phone case with a better locking design. The locks close and open easily, but not so easy that they will come open on their own. I don't know if this will change with use but I can update my review if it does.

***As with any product that claims to be waterproof, always test by submerging in water BEFORE using!!

PROS:
SO MANY USES!!
Truly waterproof. If it gets dirty, just wash and dry before removing your device.
Locks operate easily and smoothly
Adjustable lanyard for many ways to wear or attach to objects
Negligible weight added
Has hard plastic grommets to keep snaps from stressing the holes

CONS:
I really can't find any but if I do I will update my review

Link for the phone case I purchased and reviewed.
http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00JPOQ4KW?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_detailpage_o09_s00

I bought this for mysef because it said my HTC Thunderbolt would fit inside with the hard rubberdized case still on. Short story is... IT DID! I was excited. I showed it to my husband who said she wished he could find one that would fit his blackberry with the case on. He had a similar case but it was a snug fit without the case on it. I suggested he try this one and VOILA! So I let him have it and he loves it! It has a belt clip and belt loops so if you want to string your belt through it you can or just clip it on you britches, purse or whatever you wan. It looks good, was much better quality than the one my husband got from the verizon store. There are cheaper cases on amazon but I this one is really worth every penny!

Bought it for hubby as a Christmas gift. He loves it! It's the perfect size for his small laptop. It's durable and he likes that it's a clamshell opening because it makes it easy to get his computer in and out of and he can see everything inside. This is his 2nd case logic case. The first one lasted a year or more. I don't know if he's just rough on cases or what. Hopefully this one will last him a little longer.
Perfect fit for my Galaxy S5, easy to put on, great protection. Better than replacing a cracked screen.

Bought this for my hubby and he loves it! It's a clamshell design so he can lay it on his desk and open the top for easy access to his laptop. It has been very durable and still shows little sign of wear after 10 months.

Bought this for my hubby and he loves it! It's a clamshell design so he can lay it on his desk and open the top for easy access to his laptop. It has been very durable and still shows little sign of wear after 10 months.

It's okay. I have a Jackery Giant+ 12000 mAh that I absolutely love because it charges my Samsung S5 several times on one charge. I was looking for something lighter in weight that I could carry in my purse. This seemed like a good option but it's really not that much lighter. It also took 2 days of charging with my computer USB to fully charge it. I've not had a chance to use it to see how many charges I can get from it so I'll update my review once I've used it a few times. So far I'm only slightly impressed.

Hubby loves it! Fits his new LG G5 perfectly, even with an Otter Box Commuter on. He likes that there are belt loops and a clip. Having the cutout at the bottom where he can give his phone a push upwards and it makes it easier to take the phone out of the case.

I bought this for my husband and I to keep in our tackle box. It's nice that it's laminated and waterproof. It has a good variety of fish you're likely to catch, good descriptions and great pictures. It doesn't have every fish you can possibly catch but definitely the most popular fish. Would make a great gift for anyone you know who likes to freshwater fish.

When I first got this I have to admit I gave it the hairy eyeball. It was thin and folded up in the package but I figured I'd give it a try. Turns out I love this dry bag! My new Galaxy S5 with the "AUMI Dual Layer High Impact Resistant Hybrid Shockproof Gel Rhinestone Bling Armor Defender Case" slid right inside with a little effort but not a big deal. Hubby and I fish and my need for this was because I couldn't find a pretty life proof case that wasn't $80. I find the life proof to be too bulky for my little hands and purse so I was looking for another option. I put my phone in it, lengthened the lanyard and put it around my neck while we loaded fishing gear. When I got in the truck it went right over my rearview mirror which kept me from checking and double checking "did I grab my phone". The lanyard can be shortened to wear as a wristlet too.  Even with my phone inside, there's plenty of room for other stuff behind the phone like my fishing licenses, driver's licenses etc. I'll also be using this on our next cruise instead of carrying a bag. I'll be able to carry my phone or camera, along with my room card and cash, all securely around my neck. If you have kids and are going to a waterpark, this would be good to have your children to wear and enclose your name, cell phone number and a designated meeting spot if you get separated.

One thing I wish they could add or at least offer is a floatation device that could attach in the lanyard loop. If I drop my phone in the Gulf of Mexico, it would be nice to know it would also float instead of sitting dry and secure on the bottom until the next net comes along.

PROS:
Easy to use
Add no noticeable extra weight
Adjustable lanyard
Plenty of room for phone and extras
Very affordable
Can use phone right through the plastic
More uses than just a dry case for a phone

CONS:
Not a flotation device

Awesome! Just awesome! I practice my fishing knots at home and then when I get to the coast and go to tie my knots, I go blank! This is perfect! Waterproof, compact, illustrations are excellent and easy to follow. If you know someone who fishes I high recommend it for them. Would make a great little stocking stuffer.

As full disclosure, I did not purchase this charging cable. It was sent to me by iZopp to product test it.  This is my 2nd item I have by iZopp. I also ordered two USB to double USB for my S5. I'm very impressed with their products so far.

First of all, I'll say it's made to be with iphone, ipad and probably most androids as long as it's not a Galaxy S5, which is what I have. I have still been able to use it. I keep it with my external battery and am always prepared to let someone use it to charge their phone, as long as it's an iphone or android with a normal macro USB (unlike the double USB required for my S5). It fits nicely in the carrying bag that came with my external battery and although it's more than 3' long, you'd never guess it by the size of it when it is rolled up. Best part is, I've been able to stop carrying multiple adapters that came with my battery. I just need two, mine for my S5 and this one that will take care of all of the rest. It came with a Velcro strap that keeps it nicely wound and compact so you're not tangling it with everything in your purse, glove box, car console or wherever you choose to keep it. The quality is very nice and doesn't feel cheaply made. I've pulled on the silicone covers quite a bit and they're still very well attached and shows no sign of coming off at all. I like it so much that, if they come out with one with a USB for the S5 I'm definitely buying at least two. It takes up so much less room than the 3' cord I currently have to carry for my S5 (which I purchased and is also an iZopp product.)

This is the 2nd of this exact camera I've had. The first one, I loved so much, but accidently spilled OJ on it and it fried. So I was looking for the exact same camera and found it!! I carry it everywhere with me, it's always in my purse. It takes wonderful pictures and video. The battery last a very long time during use and when hanging out in my purse. I would highly recommend this little camera to anyone, IF you can find it!

So far... LOVE IT! Hubby and I fish a lot so we load the truck with a lot of gear, which USE to include an enormous rectangle ice chest that took up 2x the amount of floor real estate in our SUV. Now we have the Cube and have reclaimed our floor space. The Cube is taller which is nice because it takes up less floor space and if you have a pick-up or SUV like we do, you should have plenty of room for the height of the cooler. If you have a car, I'd double check the height of your ceiling in your back seat to make sure it will fit. I don't think it would fit in the trunk of any car unless it's laying down, and even then I'm not sure. Another thing I like is it gives you a tall "table" to set your tackle box on (if you fish), or your drinks or maybe even to be used as a prep table if your camping out.

My only complaint is the darn wheels! Why oh why Igloo must you put such wimpy dinky wheels on your coolers? And why oh why must you keep using the metal rod that snaps into a slot and will eventually loosen so the wheel pop out and can't be kept on. Every single Igloo rolling cooler we've purchased with these wheels on them have eventually fallen apart. I'm hoping this will be different. I bought this for hubby for Christmas and we've only taken it out once. Today is 1 month after Christmas so I will update my review as we use it more.

I hate wet salad greens! I have spent more money than I wish to disclose on spinners. I've tried everything from the cheapest spinners to more expensive (Tupperware, Pampered Chef, etc). I have found most of them to be awkward to hold and spin at the same time. This little spinner is PERFECT! The ratchet is so easy to work, I could see someone with joint issues finding this much more comfortable than the others. I love the break on it too.

Here's how I use mine... I put the salad in the basket (in the bowl), put cold water in the bowl and ratchet it a time or two to wash the greens, drain the water and spin the heck out of it until it's dry!!! Be sure to keep your hands on it while it's spinning. The first time I used it I got it spinning and let go to wash my hands and the salad inside was off balance causing it to wobble a bit. Not a big issue, I would just hate for it to fall off the counter and break.

The only thing I would suggest you consider is the size. It's perfect for me because I use it for one huge salad for me, or two smaller salads for me and my hubby. If you have a family of more than two you may want to buy the larger 5 qt spinner.

I read in a couple of other reviews that someone stores their lettuce in the basket/bowl and another who uses the bowl to serve the salad. Sounds like good ideas that I may try.

How 'bout that title?? Well, it really says most of how I feel, but... I bought this for one reason and one reason only. I have a Flip camera and I had noticed that the USB drive on it was starting to bend a little because when I plugged it in, it just kind of dangled from my laptop which also made it easy to bump. To save my flip from any further abuse, I bought this cable and it works like a charm! I only have a laptop, but I could see this being a blessing if you had a desk top computer too. Then I started realizing I could use it for just about anything that has a USB. I can even plug my wireless mouse stick into it and use my mouse still. Basically, anything with a USB that you would normally plug directly into your computer or laptop can be used with this cable. I was hoping I could use it to hook my laptop to my TV, and I can if I only want sound. To get sound and video I had to buy a male to male HDMI cable. If you are questioning quality, don't even give it a second thought! BUY IT! I'm sure you can get one here or on that auction site, shipped from China for a little less but 1. it will take FOREVER to arrive and 2. most of the time you get what you pay for. Hope this helps you decide!

Love, Love, Love this book! We are near the Texas Gulf Coast and a lot of the fish in the book are found on the Florida and Mexico gulf coast. It's got great pictures, great descriptions and even tells you what is edible and what is not. Includes offshore and deep sea fish too! I would buy this book again and just may so I have one in my truck and one on my bedside table! It's definitely the best illustrated and written book on fish in the Gulf of Mexico!! Buy one for the fishing person in your life!

This is a great net for the price! It's HUGE and works extremely well as a pier net. If you fish on piers and catch big fish that you can't pull up with your fishing line, the rope on this is long enough to lower and lift your fish onto the pier. It's big but fits nicely standing on end in my fishing cart between the wall of the cart and my tackle box. If you fish piers and hope to catch big fish, you need one of these! Can be used as a crab net too but works perfectly as a pier net.

Don't make the mistake I made! I have two dogs (a pink one that weighs about 25 lbs. and a blue one that weighs about 55 lbs.) who are not inside dogs, contrary to what they believe. They do come in for cold nights and we have hardwood floors that can become very chilly very quickly. For years and years I've been going to the local thrift shops and buying quilts, blankets, etc. to use as their winter beds. They're cheap and I can throw them away without feeling like I'm wasting money. Last year for Christmas I decided to buy them proper dog beds. Amazon had these beds on the black Friday sale (I don't recall the price) so I bought two. I bought the 29" x 21" for both of them thinking they would be plenty big enough, but not sure since Amazon did not put any information about what size dog each bed size is most suitable for. This size is perfect for my 25 lb. pink one (Mini Australian Shepherd) but not so much for my 55 lb. blue one (Standard Australian Shepherd). He can fit on it but is about a head too long, so now I have to order two more in a larger size. Two because I know my pink one and she will take the bigger bed every time if they're different sizes. As far as the quality, they've been sleeping on the over a month and still have plenty of oomph in them. The gray is great for hiding dirt and hairs. I will update my review as they continue to use them to share how they old up to wear, tear and washings.

This story has everything and enough angst to make the reader squirm.  I loved how these two characters fell in love.  It wasn't instant and yet that special 'spark' was between Matt and Janie from moment one.

Janie is a woman recovering from a huge loss: that of her husband.  She's been through a year of change, loneliness, and growth.  It's when she agrees to a dinner date with Matt that it comes to her how lonely she's become for what she once had, and lost when her husband died.  She's a genuinely good, sweet, kind, and loving mother of grown twin boys.  She's a very  virtuous 42 year old woman who has kept herself to the man she'd married after high school.  The way the writer expresses Janie to us readers it is believable that Janie is REAL.

Matt, for his part is every woman's dream guy.  He's the eldest of 7 sons - yes.....7 and each born about 13 months apart.  He is a successful and respected businessman; somewhat of a workaholic.  He's also been divorced (and hurt badly) twice.  Matt has no plans for marrying ever again.  Then he meets Janie and slowly falls in love.  He's too slow though and Janie returns to Portland after her 2 week dream vacation in New York.

The part where Matt takes Janie to the airport and they part made this reader cry.  I haven't been so moved by a parting scene in a good while.  Janie cried when she got on the plane.  Matt shed some tears as he left the airport.  We ALL shed tears of sadness.  It does take a good writer to convey such emotion as to make this reader cry.

I was also peeved with both Janie and Matt because they should have swallowed their fears and pride......and taken that chance that the other would have been open to continuing the relationship instead of ending it after the 2 weeks.

The good news is there is another book after this one called FIRST CLASS TO PORTLAND and that takes this love story further and into their happily ever after.

I really enjoyed this story and plan to read the 2nd in the series.  This is just wonderful romance at its BEST.  Recommended highly.  Written wonderfully.  Thank you dear authoress.

IZZY (the female lead) really managed to annoy the heck out me.  Sure; she's been abused by the ex-husband but she treats people so badly at times - she's bratty!
Takes a good writer to make me react like this to a character......so it's all good.  Still.....Izzy sure wouldn't be my BFF.  Ever.
I get that she's very beautiful, sexy, and all that.  She just seemed so 'full of herself' a lot of the time.

I love the security team.  The guys are over the top HOT.  I did however, think it very sad that Izzy manages to get cornered by her ex-husband - not once, but twice - and she's supposed to be kept safe by these security guys who just adore her.  First time is when the whole team is in the house and they let Izzy answer the front door (somewhere out front and away from the game their watching on TV) - by herself.  They KNEW the husband was trouble and looking for Izzy.  The second time Izzy's main man (Axel) lets Izzy go alone to her BFF's house and he KNEW Brandon (the ex from hell) was gunning for Izzy.
I wouldn't hire this security team!

Aside from these things: I enjoyed the book.  I especially loved the HOT ex-marines who head-up the security team.  I liked how the romance evolved and came together and by the end.......I was all warm and fuzzy inside.  I even liked Izzy at the end.  Axel......he was very alpha and HOT.  Loved him too.

Looks like there will be more books in the series and I'll be looking into reading the next one.  Thank you dear authoress.

First off; let me say that this truly reminds me of some of the most beloved 'Danielle Steel' novels I've read over the years.  It's rather.....epic, actually.  It was a story that drew me in and even though I had the feeling that it'd end up the way it did.....I felt good about the way it ended.  It was both uplifting and bittersweet.

All along I felt there was something deeper for Cam and Chloe.  I rather felt badly for Cam because he wore his heart on his sleeve and yet hid it so well from Chloe.....or at least he did to a certain point.  Chloe falling for Tyler - yes....I thought it true love.  For Tyler, I thought it was as close to love as he'd ever have for anyone else.  He was sadly....a product of over-expectant parents who didn't give him the love that parents should.  He'd been broken down so many times by his parents that he felt expected to fail.  All the stuff they go through to have a child - the marriage took back seat.  I think what happens was both their faults - not just Tyler.  I did hope Chloe could forgive Tyler but throughout the book she is very dedicated to truth and justice and what Tyler did by lying to her was tough for Chloe to get past.

This book was paced well but I sure would have liked a bit more of the epilogue after Chloe makes her journey to California.  It's like waiting for the pay-off of dessert only to find out there someone forgot the cool-whip!  Can we get more?  I liked Chloe.  I liked Tyler.  I loved Cam.  Can they all be one big family?  Okay....Tyler needed to apologize for hitting Cam - poor Cam who was being nothing but Chloe's friend.  I think another book?  Come on dear authoress - you know those characters are still in your head.  I know they're in mine!

Thank you for a very fine dramatic story.  When I say it is reminiscent of Danielle Steel, I mean it with true sincerity.

users.query: I have read many books on co-parenting with a less-than-ideal Dad. (or Mom)  This one is down to earth and very informative.  It is written focusing on what the children need from co-parents instead of how the co-parents should get along.  After all, both want the best for their children, don't we?

cands.text: I bought this book when I needed to draw up a document for child custody privileges.  It was full of meaningless little snippets, like "will you let your child drive when he/she is 16".  I needed a 'meat and bones' guide to write a document that would hold, and this book didn't help me.  I guess when my children are 16 I'll need that info, but for now it was just a waste of money.

This movie had 4.5 stars, so I thought, Why not?  It is confusing and...boring.  It might be:  <SPOILER> just called a child that wasn't wanted by either parent, both of which are control freaks.  It was looong.  Maisy figured it out...but what are the long-term ramifications?

This is child neglect.  Who would take a newborn baby: put her/him in it's crib, and let it cry it's self to exhaustion and sleep?  Then, purposely wake her/him up, feed her/him, play (Ha Ha), and repeat.  My baby's father insisted on this approach as he had custody of my daughter.  I have had 2 children, slept with them and nursed on demand.  I was not "allowed" to do this with my third child because of her father's insistence he use this "Baby Wise" method with her.  I was astounded how cruel this method was to recommend care for a newborn.  How could ANYONE use this method?  As a parent of 3 and MD, I am amazed this book was ever written.  It goes against the plethora of knowledge gained by REAL studies for newborn care and needs.  I would give this book a -5.  Please don't buy this and use it to torture your newborn..

Introduction.  At first the MantisX looks like an overpriced device comparable to the Targetize product.  Targetize isa  poor copy of the MantisX. The Mantis is an amazing training tool- the Targetize fails to be useful.  Don't be fooled by the words on the box "designed by ex-military and special-forces"  I'm not saying it is a lie, but  the product itself demonstrates they designed a product to quickly separate you from your money-
Please consider I recommend a device like this almost exclusively for dry fire training.  I don't need a device like this for live fire, I have target feedback for that.  Without great details, I have many years as a firearms and marksmanship instructor, and many years as a competitor.  Dry fire is key, and a training device like this aids dry-fire by making it "interesting", provides metrics that can uncover critical shooting errors that we may not be able to detect, and by giving us measurable numbers we can set goals against.

Analysis
The MAantisX is being compared directly with the Targetize in Design, Function, and App performance.

Design:
  The Mantis-X is a single component, no hassle. The Targetize sensor and rail clamp are two components- while removing the device from the pistol the Targetize sensor falls out.  Its not the end of the world, but it is annoying, and you must remove the sensor from the mount to attach the charging cable
 The Mantis-X uses a standard USB micro charging cable.  Targetize uses a proprietary cable.
The Targetize charger cable is magnetic- but not strong enough to keep the sensor attached to the cable (see pictures).  The fit is poor, I had to use a rubber band to keep the cable attached to the sensor to get it to charge. .

Function:
  Mantis-X can be mounted top, bottom, left or right sides, and "front" is irrelevant.  The MantisX performs flawlessly attached to a magazine base.  the Targetize didn't detect vibration or motion (in dry fire) when attached to the magazine base.

This is all important to consider if you ever want to use the device with multiple firearms.  The MantisX gives you that flexibility, the Targetize does not, It doesn't seem that the Targetize can be mounted in any position other than on a front rail under the barrel with the designated "front" end always pointing forward.

Regardless- I almost exclusively use my MantisX attached to a magazine base using a self-adhesive mini rail section.  Mounting the training device to the pistol rail prevents holstering... Mag-base mounting allows you to train with the pistol and your normal carry setup. I only have any problem on a subcompact frame-- but not enough to keep me from training.

App performance:

 the whole point of a device like this is to enable you to analyze the metrics of gun movement pre trigger press, during trigger press, and post trigger press.
 The Mantis-X app can display the shot metrics in multiple relatable outputs.  My preferred view shows exactly what motion is occurring during the trigger press and where the muzzle is at the beginning and end of the trigger press- and that is the magic. The MantisX can show were the error is in the application of the fundamentals of marksmanship.  It shows you when in the execution of the integrated act of firing the error committed.  Targetize apparently doesn't understand this, Mantis-X does.

The Mantis-X has multiple views of the same data.  One view scores shots according to a "pistol correction chart" we've all seen them, and while we may not all agree 100% on all causes of common errors, it is still instructional.  The Mantis-X app correlates the motion during the shot and provides coaching feedback to assist you to break bad habits, to be aware of habitual errors,  and reduce common shooter errors.

The Targetize sensor is not compatible with the Mantis-X app, I didn't expect it to be, but it as worth a try  BECAUSE The Targetize app is not an effective training aid  If the app cant display these metrics in a useful way, the device is pointless. The Targetize picture of shot grouping is not helpful, (see pictures) Targetize app only gives you feedback as a numeric value 1-10, for three metrics, grouping, stability, and precision.
Understand how the technology works- it is a movement sensor (accelerometer).  The device cannot see the target, and it does not know where it is in space- therefore grouping and precision are completely wrong metrics- it can't measure these metrics.
And even if you convince yourself this is still okay- the feedback it gives you is about as useful as your buddy standing next to you saying "good job" or "you suck".  So what?

Conclusions and Summary

Don't be fooled- Mantis-X is not an over-piced version of the Targetize product .  MantisX has an exceptionally well designed app with usefull metrics and coaching tips.  A single piece sensor design, and a standard reliable charging cable.

My biggest concern is that after a bad experience with the Targetize product some costumers will be wary to try the MantisX- but don't be- the MantisX is a far superior product designed by someone that understands how a device like this can improve training. Save yourself the time and frustration- its not worth the small price difference.
