I've used airmouse devices since Gyrations first product, and every increment they sold after. A few years ago I discovered the IPazzPort and have used  since.

The Rii works every bit as good, and functions as a remarkably good universal remote as well.

Let me hit construction, materials, and form factor quickly then I will move on to the functionality.

It is light, thin, narrow, fits well in one hand in remote orientation and is easy to hold in keyboard orientation.  It feels solid, nothing creaks or wiggles or cracks when using it.  The battery charges using a standard mini-usb, it comes with a short usb cable, but no wall adapter (110VAC to 5VDC usb format).  That doesn't bother me because I have a drawer full of wall adapters that have come along with so many devices that I don't need another one.

It has a switch on the side that disables the mouse/keyboard function- which should help draw out the time between charges. The switch does not disable the IR remote.
The keys are rubber on both sides, clearly labeled and logically laid out.  No complaints.  On the keyboard side the mouse functions are in the middle of the keyboard, so the keyboard is just slightly a split keyboard design.  The mouse activation button is right in the center with the left and right mouse buttons where you would expect them when you hold the remote in your hand in remote orientation.  Press the mouse button and just move the remote through the air, it only takes a little movement to move the cursor around the screen.  If you ever use a Wii controller you get the idea, except this is way smoother and easier to control, and doesn't require you to be pointed in any particular direction to work.

The universal remote side is as generic and ordinary as it can get- Awesome!  It is as much like any other remote as you could ask for, nothing is weird, it is laid out as close to any standard as might exist.  It has a button labelled "macro"- I don't know what for, it will not take more than 1 function, so I guess you can use it as just another spare button, weird, but not a big deal.

The universal remote works great, or at least as good as most.  It can do duty as 8 remotes.  I use it with a TV, a Satellite receiver, a BluRay player, and with the Viewtv VT-163.  It works great with everything.

Something you need to know about the IR universal remote function: this is a programmable remote- every function you want must be taught to it and stored in a button.
The Rii Must learn and store the individual IR burst patterns from your original remote:
1. Place the Rii IR end to IR end with whatever remote it is learning from. (Let's just say it is your DVD remote)
2. Put the Rii in learning mode. On the Rii press and hold the DEVICE button (The DVD button would be ideal) until the led lights up steady and stays lit when you release the button- something like 4 seconds? It actually lights up just a bit brighter at this point.
3. On the Rii- press a button to be programmed (let's just say it's the PLAY button) the led starts to blink.
4. On the original remote (your DVD remote) press the PLAY button. Rii will learn that specific IR burst and store it into memory.  the led blinks rapidly a few flashes.  The Rii will stay in program mode so you can continue teaching it more buttons.  About 10 second of inactivity and it exits program mode.

Lather rinse and repeat.

There are no codes that you program that will let the Rii "assume the identity" of another manufacturers remote-

This is a good thing!  Programming may take a few minutes, but it gives you some flexibility that most universals can't

You can program any original function into any key on the Rii.  If your original remote had a button that the Rii doesn't have you can program that feature into a different button.  The Rii doesn't care (as long as you remember what button does what!)

You can combine devices functions under one device button- You could assign functions of your amp, your cable box, and your TV all under one button- lets just say you have cable and not satellite- so go ahead and make this custom group under the SAT device button.  You could program your speaker amplifier volume to the volume buttons, program your cable box channel buttons to the channel buttons, and the TV power to the power button- A lot of universal remotes won't let you do that.

Now the airmouse and keyboard function:

I use the airmouse and keyboard functions with an Android-on-a-stick,  The keyboard works well, with a little more separation between the keys than the IPazzPort.

The voice function works with Google voice search- it really works!  I din't think I would care about that, but after an evening playing I am really starting to like it.  And why not, I like the feature on my phone, why not on my TV?  A similar function can be found on one model of LG smart TV, and actually, so can the airmouse and keyboard.

Also, the Rii has a small speaker in it (like a Wii controller).  Apparently with the right app you could use this much like a telephone handset for voice calls.  I had to go into my Android Sound settings and tell it I want my audio to come out of the main sound device not the Rii.  It would be better if this could be done with a button on the remote- but that would probably require a app, as it is this thing worked right out of the box, I did nothing other than plug the tiny dongle into my Android device and everything worked.  The sound setting was the only extra thing I had to do.

The reasons it isn't perfect, but by no means are these reasons enough not to buy it- just things the manufacturer could consider:

The universal remote side could use a few more buttons.  Maybe just one more generic row.  The Rii has a row of buttons- yellow, green, red, and blue.  These buttons have the  icons for mute, rewind, play/pause, and fast-forward on them.  I wish they did not, and that the above mentioned functions would have their own buttons.  The Sat receiver and my BluRay player use the color buttons for specific functions that can't coexist with the rewind, play, and fast-forward.  (On the BlueRay player I coded the numeric keypad 4= rewind, 6=fast-forward, etc.)  For the Sat- I don't 3 of the 4 keys all that often, so if I really need to , I guess I can just reach into the drawer and pull out the Sat remote, The one key I do use more frequently I programmed it into another key that the Sat remote didn't have

The airmouse function on every airmouse I've used before has had three mouse functions- off, hold-to-move, and free-move.  The Rii only has two- off and free-move.  It isn't too much to get accustomed to, but the hold-to-move is a really nice feature I already miss.  However, all of the other great things about the Rii outweigh this one (missing) feature.

The keys are not back-lit.  I wish they were, but they are not.  I'll live with it- the keys of the original remotes weren't back-lit either.

The keyboard side is missing the "Windows" key that makes a difference for anyone running a desktop OS (Windows or Ubuntu)
The IpazzPort had it, along with a very clever CTRL-ALT key, which made CTRL-ALT-DEL only two keys, the RII requires four keys CTRL-ALT-Fn-DEL to pull of the same thing.
Seriously- not a deal breaker, just a thing to know.

And one final observation, judging by the construction- I believe the Rii is made by the same people that make the IpazzPort, so I don't feel bad comparing the two.

I'm pleased with this purchase. They're a little tricky to fill and the reservoir for the peppercorns and salt could be bigger, but overall they're very good.  The grinding mechanism is fast and efficient. I'm not sure how long they'll last, but so far so good. They were a big hit here for Christmas as my nephews were fascinated by them and wanted to salt and pepper everyone's food. The light on the bottom is very handy, but you do have to be careful when reassembling them to make sure the contacts line up correctly. If you see reviews complaining the light doesn't work, they probably didn't reassemble it correctly. You have to line up the contacts on the top and bottom half when reassembling the unit to make the light work. Battery life seems good so far. I'd recommend them to anyone wanting an easy to use electric peppermill/salt grinder.

I enjoyed this book a lot and was disappointed to find myself at the end. I was finally wrapping my head around all of the time changing angles just when the book ends. It'll get a reread in the near future and I look forward to the sequel.

It's a good enough book. I found some parts quite good, but was a bit disappointed in the lack of bread varieties available in the book. Since all of the recipes in the book rely solely on using starters and not commercial yeast it's not that good for those of us who only bake occasionally. The daily maintenance of a starter can become something of a burden for the occasional baker and the waste of the unused starter can make baking in such a manner quite expensive. Having a yeast based alternative would be nice.

By and large I find many bread baking books to be written by those who are true believers in what they do, and only what they do and this is an example of such a book. We're given no real alternatives for making bread in other ways. You must use the slow rise, natural starter, folding method of kneading, and bake in a cast iron dutch oven, to get good results according to this book. I'm happy to report I've made great tasting bread using store bought yeast, relatively quicker rises, using a mixer to knead the dough and baking it on a baking stone that I mist and have a pan of water in for steam. I strongly suspect that given some time and experimentation that Chad Robertson could have found alternative methods of making his bread that were more practical for the occasional baker and would have yielded good to very good results. It's fine to recommend your exact methods to exactly replicate your bread, but developing a good alternative that's more practical for the real world bakers who only bake a loaf of bread once or twice a month would be nice also. If you want to exactly replicate Tartine bread, then this is the book for you. If you want a good bread book that will let you bake bread occasionally without having to start a week or more in advance and maintain a starter, you might want to look elsewhere.
I'm just starting using it but the plants are looking good so far. The real test will come a month and months from now, but for now things are looking good. It came very nicely boxed and packaged.

If you love Nathalie and you love biscuits then this book is for you. You'll get more biscuit recipes than you'll know what to do with and lots of good little stories. I'd buy it again. It's a good book.

I've got them all on DVD and if I'm not near my DVD player will stream them to whatever device is available. They just always make me laugh. The casting is brilliant, the writing is brilliant, and the timing is impeccable. It's just a very, very well done show. It's a tick edgier than some may like, but it's funny as can be. Mind you my changes aren't quite as extreme as "Romeo and Ethel the Pirate's Daughter" evolving into "Romeo and Juliet" but it's fun to see how the story adapts as the movie progresses.

I wasn't sure about this movie, but I gave it a shot and I was pleasantly surprised by it. There's some good humor and a few twists and turns. It's not one of the best movies I've ever seen, but I was pleasantly surprised by it.

I figured the old one was about out of time so it was a good time to replace it even though it was still working. (It's now stashed as a spare should this one ever blink out on me.) I've liked this movie and watched it before, so I knew what to expect. The video quality was good on he stream and it was a good night of movie watching.

users.query: I cried real tears and laughed out loud throughout this entire book.  It was engrossing and I couldn't wait to turn the next page.  I was enthralled by both Jacob and Dino and direction each character went.  I was conflicted with Dino's character though.  I was actually rooting for him to get revenge on his gang and hoping he would get caught by the police.  The story kept me on edge.  The stand out was of course little Isaiah and his impact on everyone who knew him.  I would definitely recommend this for everyone.  Keith Thomas Walker never disappoints and this is no different.

cands.text: I always miss the Kingdom family between books. I was glad to finally read Josh's story. Like books 1 through 4 of course there is enough drama and intrigue to keep you on the edge of your seat. With this series it's imperative that you read them in order. Enjoy.

I laughed and cried through this entire book.  I laughed a whole lot more.  Gang culture is in no way funny but there were moments in this story that you just HAD to laugh.  KTW is a remarkable story teller and I look forward to each and every book.  Anyone who loves Mr. Walkers books will certainly love this one.  He has a way of making the villain so human you cant help but root for the villain as well as the hero.  Funny how he does that

I love anything Adrienne Byrd writes.  I pretty much knew how this story would turn out but I still loved the characters.  I love how they both rescued each other in the end and how the entire story had a 'feel good' vibe to it.  Its a short steady read but you won't be disappointed.

This was a good read but I hated everyone in this book.  I think there will be a follow up by the way it ended and I hope by then some of the characters will have grown a conscious.  I like reading K.F. Johnson because she takes it there.  If we are supposed to dislike some of these characters - she hit the mark.

OMG! When I got to the end I was shocked.  I thought I knew who the killer was midway through but as usual Keith Thomas Walker threw us a curveball!  It was riveting from beginning to end.  The most lovable characters - even the transgender character had me cracking up, and the characters you're "supposed" to hate come together to make up a spine tingling story.  You will love it.  I did.

Keith Thomas Walker has a way of bringing you into the lives of his very flawed characters to a point where you actually empathize with them.  Especially the bad guys who always seem to have a sad background.  Sometimes the people who seem like they're on your side are not.  Its like yelling at the TV when the good person trusts the wrong person!! The story twists and turns and you can't put it down!  Get it now!!

By the last word of this book my heart was in my throat.  I read it straight through for 2 days and couldn't put it down until I actually passed out sleep.  I took this exciting, inspirational and sometimes frustrating ride with Fire and Sylvia and was so attached to them at the end I became protective of them (from the other characters in the book  crazy, I know).  Theirs was a love so pure and sweet it will make you a little envious.  Ive never read Colin Channer before and didn't know what to expect.  After reading this I went back and found everything he had written that I could get my hands on and just began to devour them.  You will enjoy this once you get a handle on his writing style (which is very poetic and descriptive), I just flew through this book and couldn't wait to find out what would happen next.  I think anyone with a real romantic soul will enjoy this read.

This series has been in my heart since the first book.  I was so intrigued by Midnight in The Coldest Winter Ever and I was hoping and praying for an exclusive story involving him only.  That being said, I was REALLY disappointed in the way this one ended. I hope this is not the end of the story.  I really didn't have much love for the second wife.  I know its his culture and custom and a part of who his character is to take another wife but the American woman in me only saw her only as a side bitch (Im not ashamed of that feeling) and I couldn't find any love for her character.  She was just a chick who invaded another womans marriage.  I thought she brought a certain amount of tension to the household.  Not for him since he got the benefit of sharing a bed with 2 different women. I didn't like that this book began and ended with her.  Her dysfunctional, overly educated pseudo intellectual family members didn't help her cause either. There were a few things unresolved such as the fact that in A Deeper Love Inside, Midnight mentioned that he had 3 wives and I thought we would meet the third wife (side bitch 2) in this book.  I was glued to the other 2 books and couldn't turn the pages fast enough.  This book was no different.  In spite of the back and forth feel of the chapters going in and out of the past and present, I didn't have a hard time following the storyline.  I didn't like not spending more time on Akemis character.  We didn't get to experience her having her children, the sex of the children or anything.  In spite of the very few flaws, all in all this was a very good book.  If you are not familiar with the Midnight series, check out The Coldest Winter Ever and then start the Midnight series including A Deeper Love Inside: The Porsche Santiago Story.  In spite of a few hiccups, I do enjoy this series and Im looking forward to the next installment.

I love Keith Thomas Walker.  I love that in his stories all the characters are a little bit flawed and not rich and beautiful in the "Romance Novel" way [you know: light skinned, long hair, green or hazel eyes].  These characters feel like real people. I also love the very intense issues they all have.  No one is perfect and I can relate to them on a very, basic human level.  It seems that love does conquer all and even the most flawed individuals can have a good heart. I would have definitely fallen for a guy like Marcel in a heartbeat and you will too.  You will find yourself rooting for this couple and hoping that they both find happiness with each other in the end.  I don't want to spoil it for you but I will tell you I had a hard time putting this book down.

Loved it, loved it, loved it.  I've been waiting for this installment of this series and was not disappointed.  I knew Sharon C. Cooper would come through!  I love the characters and was right there in the situation with them.  Very suspenseful and intriguing.  I can't wait for the next installment!  A definite must read!!

I have never read anything by this author and I don't think I'll go back for another helping.  I was sooo bored.  The goody goody girl was just too much for me.  Everything was a misunderstanding and it was so easy to say the wrong thing to her.  She got on my nerves quickly.

This is a nail biting saga.  I love the story and the Kingdom brothers are people I'd like to know.  You don't want them as an enemy.  The love story between Jason and Aviva continues and you just fall more in love with them throughout.  You even see a more human side of Hope that wasn't there before.  All in all I would definitely recommend the Kingdom saga.  You have to start with Abandoned But Not Alone and then For Love and Revenge.  After those 2 then you can start The Ties that Bind.  You don't want to read them out of order!!!
I love the "series" books.  The continuations are always a fun read.  The next story after this is also great.
I'm in love with the Donovans.  These books can't come out fast enough for me.  I've been following the series for a long time.  I think everyone will enjoy the constant suspense.

Short and sweet.  I couldn't put it down.  I had it read in 2 days thirsting for more.  I loved every minute of it.  I have become so involved in this series I can't put any of them down.  I will hate to see them go.

I LOVE the Donovans.  Parker has to be one of my favorites.  This story kept me riveted and I would not put it down.  I'm on pins and needles waiting for the next installment.  A.C. Arthur kept us hanging now I'm biting my nails!!  You will love this one too.

I was riveted to my seat.  A real page turner.  I had a hard time putting this down.  At first I didn't like either one of them but eventually they all became very human to me and I found myself rooting for them even though they were essentially the "bad" guys.  I loved the love story of course as only Donna Hill can deliver.  It was good to see the appropriate people get what they had coming in the end.  The bad guys were bad but the real villains were terrible!!  Another hit.  I can't wait to see what happens next!

I knew I would love this book.  Brenda Barrett creates the most, amazingly complicated characters.  The story was very enjoyable and easy to lose yourself in.  I read this in 2 days because I couldn't put it down.  I'm anxious to read Hazel and Caitlyn's stories.  This is a very enjoyable series so far.

I've never read Carl Weber before and I'm glad I started with this one.  This is a pure adrenalin ride.  You're not sure what to make of the main character - if he's a good or bad guy - but you find yourself cheering for him anyway.  Most of the characters are familiar people you've me in your lifetime. The relationships are complex and entertaining.  I ready this book in 2 days because I couldn't put it down!!!

Loved it.  I just bought it because the title didn't look familiar and I feel like I got a real gift instead.  It was very interesting and I loved the characters.  I think people will just love the main character and want to be her best friend.

I love KTW and everything he writes.  This story was as gripping as the others.  It was very much a teaser and I can't wait for the next installment to see where the story takes us with Monica and Jovan, will they get together or just work together? Will she take him up on his offer to work together?  Hopefully we don't have to wait too long to find out.

This series pulled me in quickly like all of Brenda Barrett's series books.  I fell so hard for Ian.  I found myself rooting for Ian and Ruby all the way.  I love how Ms. Barrett's books are a contrast of good and evil and good always prevails.  I'm looking forward to seeing how the rest of the Band works out.  Excellent cast of characters and excellent story.  You will love it but make sure you start from the beginning with Going Solo (Carson and Alice), you will be hooked after that.

The Cochran/Deveraux will get you hooked in no time.  Its hard to take romance books seriously because all of the characters seem so flawless and perfect, which they are.  They are great looking, rich and extremely educated which is what you want in a romance!!  This is the story of a secret brother that only few people knew about.  This was a great story and I enjoyed every bit of it.

I can't wait for Brick House 2!!  I was riveted throughout this story and found myself rooting for Korah and Brick!!  Keith Thomas Walker never lets me down with the wonderfully flawed characters and the seriously engaging storylines.  I'm curious to see how the son and the assistant pan out.  Hurry up and finish writing it!!!

I was riveted to this entire series.  I didn't care for Kelley's selfish character right off the bat. She expected to have her cake and eat it too and everyone was else was just supposed to accept it.  She cared nothing really about anyone else except getting caught.  I found myself very invested in the characters.  I felt sorry for some, I hated others and loved the rest.  You won't be able to read one and not continue with the rest.  I was curious about the outcome of all of their individual situations.  I love Brenda Barrett's complex characters and her portrayal of family dysfunction is remarkable.  I strongly suggest the entire Three Rivers series.  Its people you know and people you wish you didn't know and you might even see yourself.  A great read.

I'm glad I decided to order this shirt. I'd buy from this maker again. I received the product at a discount/ free for a fair and unbiased review

A page turner with great depth of Characters and Setting with an exciting story. I'm so looking forward to read the rest of Crystal Ward's series.

I got this because I go to conferences and there is always a masquerade theme party. I'm not the type that gets into getting all dressed up in costumes so I figured I could throw this in my suitcase and be covered for the party. The cut out is very intricate and very pretty. If I don't wear my glasses I won't know who is who- but it's a costume party so maybe it won't matter. I received this product at a discount/ free for a fair and unbiased review

The Author's "the glass is half full" approach to life grabbed me from the first page. It's hard to write about your own life but Stevie Dupin makes it seem so easy. His mix of disbelief tempered with humor is truly inspirational. My husband and I went through something similar and I instantly connected with his story. I love the scenes of his childhood, how he went to Hollywood and beyond. The writing is amazing and very smooth. This is the type of book you will read, put on your shelf and take it back down to read again.

This is a great water bottle by Daixers. I read some of the other reviews and a few said it's small. Not of you carry it- to me it's the perfect size. It has a hand lanyard which is so hand when I walk. It is leak proof. I have a few from other places that said they were leak proof. This one really is. It has a nice flip top- easy to open and close.  The outside of the bottle has places to grip the bottle- which is great especially when you're working out, it won't slip out of your hands. I like to see people using refillable water bottles instead of the disposable ones. When you open it to fill it, the mouth is wide enough to add ice to it. I like this product. I received this product at a discount for a fair and unbiased review

This is the cutest wine holder ever! When I saw it I knew it would look great on my new shelves. It comes as pictured- a bronze colored tricycle. I still have to buy a bottle of wine to put in it but I am very pleased with it. The holder is well made and durable. The wheels are stationary so you don't have to worry about it moving. It has great detail- swirl spokes on the wheels and a lovely pattern where the bottle lays. I've been looking for something unique and I found it. I received this product at a discount for a fair and unbiased review

When Jean Joachim writes it's pure magic. Her vivid descriptions of the settings made me feel as though I was there. The story is filled with love, passion, doubts and healing. The family dynamics are wonderful and fun. The characters all come with their own set of flaws and it makes the interactions thrilling to read. I love a good romance and this novel has it all.

I love Historical Western Romance and when I saw the author's profile on Facebook I was intrigued. I bought Christmas Miracles to give her books a try. I'm glad I did- It is a completely enjoyable read. The characters are well developed and easy to relate to. It has that special romance magic of obstacles being thrown in the path of true love. I was able to lose myself in this story, cheering for a happy ending.
A wonderfully tender story with just the right amount of angst. A well written western romance I highly recommend. I love her books

I have a half circle window in my bathroom. I have a shade that is fan shaped in there and I wanted something different. I love the pattern. It is simply elegant. Very Pretty. I measured by taking a piece of string and measuring from the middle if the bottom- Like you were using a compass. This worked out great and it looks amazing. I received this product at a discount for a fair and unbiased review

I absolutely loved this book! The characters are endearing and the story flowed beautifully with a great plot and intricate details.  This book is a winner. I couldn't put it down I just had to see what happened next. The dialogue is so natural and often witty. Can't wait for more!!
so enjoyed this novel. It has everything the chunky cowboy ,the strong woman, and great conflicts. the amazing detail allowed me to feel a part of the story

I love a good romance but this one blew me away. It's a love story set in New York City and by the time I finished reading, I felt as though I had actually been in NYC for the holidays. The descriptions are vivid and the story moves right along. The writing is smmooth as glass and the characters will keep you turning pages. One of Jean Joachim's Best.

Once again Charliann Roberts has done it. A great modern day twist to a mail order bride with many surprises. The author had me guessing at each turn. The characters are well written and the plot holds your attention. I also loved that she included characters from her first book- it felt like a fun reunion.

Rebecca DeMedeiros all I can say is I hope you have more books coming soon. I love historical western romance and I was reading another book that was just okay and I decided to try A Bargain Bride. I was enthralled from the first page and sad when it ended. This novel grabbed my heart and didn't let go. The romantic anticipation and tension were spot on. I loved the characters. I really hope another book is coming out quickly!!

A Betting Bride is romantic, fun and witty. I fell in love with Serena and Alec. The characters were well written and full of personality. I loved the give and take of the whole romance, wondering will they or won't they. This is the second novel I have read by Rebecca De Medeiros and she did not disappoint. A Betting Bride took me away from my stressful days and transported me into a small old west town with plenty of action and romance.
A great story. very well written with a lot of heart. It's one of the better books I have read of late- well done!!

Jess denies God. In his infinite wisdom, he's taken everyone she's ever loved. Moving to the French Quarter was a ploy to erase the guilt she felt for rebuking her faith. Perhaps, if she hadn't met Justin, an angel preoccupied with getting back into God's good graces, and drowning in his hatred for humanity, her plan would have worked.

Justin's general disdain for the human race makes him difficult to like, but some higher power has appointed him her keeper. Justin's convinced he can mend her broken relationship with her maker, but in the process he learns a thing or two about his own humanity.

Never mind falling in love, that's not supposed to happen. In fact, it may even be forbidden. Jess just wants Justin to understand her plight, and he wants to protect her from a world she doesn't know.

If neither are equipped to save the other, then whose soul will live and whose will perish?

A page turner that I spent the whole night reading! Well written and the mix of paranormal and romance keeps you on the edge of your seat!
Hildie McQueen is one of my favorite authors. love this and all her other westerns

I'm not quite sure whether or not I believe in reincarnation but it didn't matter I love the notion that love conquers all. JP Grider wove a beautiful story of unconditional eternal love. Lena has recurring nightmares. She is afraid of her fiance. I enjoyed watching her grow in strength and determination. Of course I was ecstatic about a love that endured for a century. This novel is well written and a joy to read.

users.query: The work of the author is amazing!  I hadn't thought about making living plants into arrangements.  The author explains everything.  Really.  After reading this, I understand how to create some of these arrangements.  The trick is finding some of the rarer plants.

cands.text: I wanted more of a how-to plant book and instead received a picture book.  This is a case of a poor fit.  Someone else might find the cues on styling useful and enjoyable.
Inspiration and fun.  Well worth having on my book shelf.  Some stitch instruction included but not a how-to guide.
Nice enough book. Expected more detailed information, but perhaps there will be enough to get started. Paper is middling quality and binding feels stiff.
This is exactly what I hoped it would be-- pages of patterns, textures and designs. I use mine for art journals and inspirations.
Beautiful, beautiful, beautiful.  An art book more than a how-to.

Out of numerous books and guides to no-ruler quilting, this one might be my favorite. The pallet is fresh and vibrant--  slightly amphed colors, and the circular quilts are wunderbar. Love love love Ms. Wood's aesthethic

It is what just what I expected. If one can coordinate yarn substitutions, these are the classics. Even Foolish Virgins, which I've always admired but will never knit. There are two versions of Kilim. That's what I was after. NIcely printed.

So many craft books are disappointing, so I'm pleased to see new patterns cleverly crafted that I might actually wear.  Further, the book organizes similar sweater styles for you, such as raglan or round yoke.  I purchased mine used, so that compounded my satisfaction.
There are a few items I like, but it's mostly about the pictures and styling.  A nice, pretty book with contemporary country craft stylings.
Pretty but that's about all.  Well, maybe a good coffee table book your guests will like.

The plant is healthy, however I'm disappointed that only two leaves have one slit each. My plant does not look as glorious as most photos. A friend said the brighter the light (not direct), the more the leaves begin to split. If my plant improves, I'll update and add a star. Fingers crossed.
A few stories aren't great; however, prepare for some surprises and hold onto your seat.
I think this is essential reading for those with chronic illness and the ones that love them.

Was completely disappointed with the quality and look of this cover.  Feels like packing material.  The surface is too shiny and rippled to see the constellations from most angles.  I decided to shell out the big bucks for Amazon's Origami cover and am happy I did.

Hands down the best sock book I have ever owned. Inspirational!  Besides authentic and adapted vintage patterns, Bush gives separate instructions on each heel and toe so one can create custom socks.  The instructions are incredibly clear.  The spiral binding allows the book to open flat and adds considerable durability.  (No broken spines.). My socks went from beginner level to intermediate/advanced by following this book, and the patterns/heels/toes are a delight to try and to revisit.  My are now admired for their detail, even by folks who do not knit, and my husband's large, wide feet, with their high insteps sport tailored, gorgeous socks.  A great and fun way to expand sock knitting and produce the most awesome socks around!  I cannot praise this book enough.  I have two copies in various places around the house or in my tote.
These dignified our bathroom's reading material.  We have two, and I may buy more for other areas of the house and office.
Precision color writing, and the colors are juicy.  The pinks are extra rich.

Um, wow.  Visually beautiful.  By the end, even my preteen boy shed a few tears that the story and film amply deserved, not from pity, but from a deeply moving account of the interior life clashing with circumstance.  Magical realism at it's best.  I'm off to read the book.
Read by the author. Makes me miss NY a little, but not enough to go back. True narrative voice of a gen x NYer.

Ah, you know...my son is very pleased...me?  I'm just glad it's not falling apart like a megabloks figure.  I admit the joint articulation is very good...and this seller has a great price.  Can you imagine paying $28 dollars and up for this?
Paper is sturdy enough to use rubbing alcohol blending on my prismacolor pencils. The small size is nice when I want some doodle-like coloring and not an entire page.

Not as airy and thin as pictured. Disappointing, but I thought I'd try them for the price. They're already in the was and that will soften the material. Out of the package the fabric was stiff and coarse. The lace trim around the edges of mine are thicker than pictured as well. Not sure where these will go because they won't look light enough for our bedroom.

Covers what my therapist and I are discussing; the epigenetic influence of trauma on family lineage.  I suppose this theory can work in one's favor if you're born into a blessed and lucky family.  What's most important is becoming aware of one's family story.

All cotton school uniform pant and at a good price.  They are soft and relatively wrinkle free from the dryer.  (No need to iron them unless you need a crease in the front.).  Look good all day, and my son says they are comfortable.  (He is sensitive to anything scratchy.). Just what we wanted.  Upper knee length, (he's 5'6" or so).

users.query: For a $35 guitar, this is perfect.  It is a real (albeit cheap) guitar.  It stays in tune long enough for my 3 year old kid to play with it.  It doesn't sound great, but once tuned, you can play real songs on it.  No regrets.

cands.text: Great feeling, great full sound, nice lows.  Also super affordable.

These strings sounded great, but after a while some of the coating started wearing off and a weird green substance was on the strings.  They still sounded good, but it was weird.  They were a little overpriced, though. I'm currently using DR RARE's.  Half the price and the sound is better (in my opinion).  The DRs also feel alot nicer on the fingers.

These strings sounded great, but after a while some of the coating started wearing off and a weird green substance was on the strings.  They still sounded good, but it was weird.  They were a little overpriced, though. I'm currently using DR RARE's.  Half the price and the sound is better (in my opinion).  The DRs also feel alot nicer on the fingers.
This thing is cheaply priced, cheaply made, but it really has pretty good sound and it works.  I don't expect the durablilty to be great, but come on, I pay like 8 bucks for it.

This is the cheapest case I could find anywhere (both online and in brick-and-mortar stores).  When I opened it I was vastly impressed with the quality.  This thing is going to protect my guitar.  It did smell weird, though.  I think it is from the glue they use.  I aired it out and it is way better now.  Definitely recommended.

Our 1 year old loves it.  I agree that the string is a little short, we're thinking about tying it with another string to make it longer.  Our biggest complaint is that the top note is exactly the same pitch as the second from the top.

Let me start out by saying my wife is an experienced (10+ years) violin teacher and has played violin for most of her life. We bought this violin for our 5 year old son after being unimpressed with the "economy" violin rental for $25 per month.  The rental was Romanian-made and was "valued" at ~$500 by the shop.

This Bunnel violin outfit is a great value and likely one my wife will be recommending to new students.

The violin itself sounds great for a student violin and the fit and finish is nearly perfect. It is very beautiful, and the setup done by Kennedy was very good. The action was perfect, the bridge fit well, and the strings were mostly in tune.

The rest of the outfit is definitely lower quality than the violin, but nothing is junk.  The bow is good.  The case is a little cheap, but should hold up well.  The oblong style is nice to fit music in the side pocket.  The rosin is good. The shoulder rest is very cheap, but should be ok.  It is much better than the foam one my son was using on the rental.  The poorly written description the shoulder rest box was funny.

Overall, what you get in this outfit is impressive, the violin being the most impressive.

The sound quality in these far exceed earbud style headphones.  The bass is truly rich and the mids and trebles are good too.  I love them.  The only comment I have is that the reflecty part that goes behind your neck rubs off easily, as I've only had them for a few months and much of it is gone. I use these very often and the woven material wire is much better and more durable than plastic covered wire.

Recommended.
I love this. The price is right, it is comfortable, and it looks good.
You can't beat the price and it just works.  I wouldn't count on this for continuous use and it isn't too rugged, but it does what it is supposed to do for much less money than the competitor.

This case is lightweight, but is made with cheaper materials.  It would work just fine if you are on a budget, but if you can afford an upgrade, even like $30-$40 will get you a lot nicer case for your money, both in materials and style.  We got this one: http://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B00PLBAKNK (though it doesn't look like it is stock currently)

The look is perfect, the quality is fine. This isn't heavy duty, but if you don't plan on bumping into it, it should last just fine. Fit and finish are good.

The installation was great, except for the mounting screws.  They were way too long.  I had to buy shorter ones from Ace for 20 cents each.
Other reviewers mentioned some club based big box stores had it cheaper, but this is way cheaper than any regular grocer.  Red Star is quality.  The bread is delicious.
Excellent quality. This will let you until and tear with just one hand.
This is very well made, and had a nice wooden handle. It feels like it will last us many years and doesn't look or feel cheap like ones with a plastic handle.

Our son really enjoys playing with this.  Interestingly, it works better with hot wheels cars than with the included car.  The included one works most of the time, but since it is top heavy, sometimes it tips over around the turn.

Overall, I'd recommend it.

I bought this thing purely because (1) it is really small and portable (2) it was cheap--only $280 and (3) because it had amazing battery life.

Just to reiterate what others said, yes the keyboard is small, but it is not impossible.  I've only owned it for 2 days and I'm already almost used to it (and I'm a touch typer).  The only thing that sometimes bothers me is the placement of the right shift key, but I am getting used to it.  Hand size doesn't matter so much as fatness of fingers.  I have relatively big hands (I can palm a men's regulation basketball and dunk it) and it really isn't that bad.  But just to be clear, this computer is not meant to write papers on.

Also, I agree with other reviews as to downloading the updated touchpad driver from elantech.  There are some pretty sweet features with the new driver.

Because of the size of the Solid State drives, the C drive being smaller than D, you should change the registry (aka default drive for installing programs and saving data) from C to D. [...]

The battery life is quite awesome on this little thing.  Yesterday I got around 6 hours and I was playing some video and was always connected to the wi-fi.  The wi-fi is quick to connect and holds the connection very well.

This little thing boots up extremely quick, this is due to the solid state drive...

Also, if you are watching videos online (like on hulu) you need to switch to performance or super performance modes otherwise the video only goes by frames...

If you aren't sure if you wanna buy this, I'd say go with it.  If you have fat fingers, go with the 10 inch model.

If you have any questions, ask away.
Great reliable printer.  I love that it is wireless (even if it doesn't work with my linux computer).  The cheap toner is also a big plus.  Much better than my old inkjet printer.

We love this one.  It just works, is easy to ready, and is really fast at what it does.  The only downside is that you have to know what tempurature your meat is supposed to be, because it has no cheat sheet.

The brass casing is beautiful and the compass works.  At less than 5 bucks, you can't go wrong.  I just wanted a basic compass to have with me for backpacking (best not to put all my faith in electronics, in case of emergency), and this one is light, protects itself, and works.  It fit the bill perfectly.
This works great.  It locks on nicely and easily, the magnet works well to hold and release the lid, and it hasn't failed me yet.
Great toaster.  It is a little bulky, but that's so they can insulate the sides.  Looks great and works great.
The shape wasn't quite right and didn't offer enough support. I like the papi Men's 3-Pack Cotton Stretch Jock Strap much better.

This worked great to remove the inside panel of the sliding door on our Honda Odyssey.  I had to remove the panel to access the inside of the exterior handle to replace the broken one my son broke.  No scratches and the tools seemed sturdy.  It was nice to have all different sizes for different applications.
These are better than standard cheap grips, but I still had numbness in my hands on longer rides.

users.query:
For several generations, the Porter family summers at Ashaunt Point in Massachusetts, a small, blue blood community.  Residents can trace their lineage back to the Mayflower.  But as with every other place, Ashaunt changes over time, as do the residents.  Follow the changes to the land and the Porter family through death, birth, love, war, and the heartache that change inevitably brings.

I really found myself struggling with this book.  The narrative is broken into four distinct time sections, yet within each section, the narrative switches between characters, and jumps forward in time.  It made for a very disjointed read overall.  The book follows one family, and most of the characters appear in multiple, if not all four, sections, yet I found it very difficult to connect to any character.  For example, Helen appears as a child in the first section, a young lady in the second, a middle aged mother in the third, and a dying senior citizen in the fourth.  Yet, I was unable to connect any one of these versions to the others, because I never actually got to know Helen as a character.  It is like when you meet someone as an adult, and see a photograph of them as a child; without knowing the person well, it is hard to see anything of the adult before you in the child in the photo.

The writing itself is quite lovely.  I particularly enjoyed the descriptions of the natural landscape of Ashaunt.  New England is so particular, with specific social quirks and nuances, it was difficult for me to relate.  It was as if I had been given a private view into the life of a Kennedy-esque family, and struggle to understand their everyday lives.  Yet, despite the difference in social standing, at the heart of story were universal truths: love, life, death, illness.  No amount of social standing can allow a family to escape those realities.

Fans of contemporary fiction may connect to this book better than I seemed to be able to.  I found the narrative jarring, and as a result this book failed to hold my attention.

I received a review copy courtesy of TLC Book Tours in exchange for my honest review.

cands.text: I thought this was a good book.  The writing is nice, very descriptive, and flows well.  I also thought the characters were well developed.  I did tire a bit of the shifting narratives, but all in all, this is a very good book.

How did a family produce not one, but three, stunningly talented writers?  And how would these talented women fit in to Victorian ideals of femininity?  We learn the family history of the Brontes, as well as the life experiences that so clearly colored the sisters' writings?  Known originally as Acton, Currer, and Ellis Bell, the girls would end up writing some of the most groundbreaking literary works of the times, and their stories would last throughout the ages.

Jane Eyre has always been one of my favorite pieces of classic literature.  There is something so universal to the story, aspects that resonate with modern readers despite the fact that it was written in a much different time and social climate.  So, given the chance to read more about the live of the author, and her sister, I jumped right on.  And typically, I love biographies, particularly of people I admire, but for me, this book just seemed flat.  I found very little in the book that would be engaging to the intended age group (ages 10 and up).  As an adult, with a vested interest in the subject matter, I was quite bored for the majority of the book, so I imagine many kids would be as well.  The facts of the Brontes lives were presented in a straightforward manner, but it was not until the book discussed the writings of the girls that I became the least bit interested.  The book is almost 200 pages, at the middle grades reading level, yet it took we an entire weekend to read, not because it was difficult, but because I just was not engaged at all by the writing.

Even as a child, I was a voracious reader.  I read any and every thing I could get my hands on.  I had a knowledge of classic literature, and while I was too young to read the works themselves, I adored film adaptations of many classic literary works, even before I was of school age.  So, as a child, this type of literary biography would have certainly appealed to me.  However, I was an unusual child, and kids today have so many other options in terms of reading, I am not sure that this book will appeal much to kids.  Certainly parents would encourage their children to read this, and it could be a great supplement to public school or homeschooling curriculum, but I do not see a child going out of their way to read this, as opposed to more engaging books.

This is a book about 5 sisters from a poor, dysfunctional family.  Each girl has her own issues, and a very distinct narrative voice.  Chapters are narrated by the different sisters, and through this we learn a great deal about each girl.

We also learn something the girls do not know: they are being watched by a mysterious man who is also a narrative voice in the book.  This man has an obsession with the girls, which drives him to hold one of them captive.

This book is an eye opener into the world of child abduction and they thoughts of pedophiles.  This would be a good book for a parent to read with their teens and open up the lines of communication regarding such a serious topic.

I had a hard time maintaining interest in this book, perhaps it was just a little too much like too many other stories out on the market right now.  I just found the characters not as engaging as I would typically like.  Perhaps I was just having a cranky day when I tried to read it, it just did not stick with me.

For as long as she can remember, Lillian has loved mythology stories, and the "monsters" that appear in them. When her sister, Bluebell, goes missing, Lillian realizes that those stories may be more fact than fiction, and life as she knows it may change forever.

I cannot even begin to express how impressed I was with this book. The author, Nara Duffie, completed this book 11 days before her 11th birthday. Yes, you read that correctly! She was 10 when she wrote this. Actually, she started writing it much earlier than that, and took her time polishing and perfecting it. You can tell that this book was written with a tremendous amount of dedication and precision. The characters are very well developed, and the back story unfolds brilliantly in the middle of the present action. I thought the book was full of rich imagery, and I admire the author's imagination.

This book will really appeal to fans of books like Harry Potter and Percy Jackson. I think it is a wonderful book for both young adult and adult readers. Do not let the author's young age deter you; this is better writing than I have seen from may seasoned, adult authors. Bravo Nara!

Sometimes, the world is an amazingly small place.  And sometimes, lives are more interconnected than we could ever imagine.  This novel follows a cast of characters that include an American couple that married during WWII, an elderly German soldier who was disfigured, a blind museum curator, a successful movie director, and worker at a retirement home.  These lives have histories that span the continents, yet somehow, small acts will bind them all together forever.

This book was simply beautiful.  Once I picked it up, I could not stop reading it, and finished in just a few hours.  I really thought it brilliant on so many levels.  The writing itself is so moving, the words tender and honest, poetic without being overly florid.  And the way the stories are woven together, past to present and back again, was like watching an intricate dance.  All the movements were lovely, but the overall essence of the piece is stunning and breathtaking.

I am a huge fan of literature set during the 1930s and 1940s, so the fact that much of this book takes root during that era was a real draw for me.  Yet as the story transports us back and forth between past and present, the thing that stuck with me the most is that human nature has changed so little over the course of time.  All people have choices to make in life, choices that impact countless others in ways unimaginable.  This book help cement in my mind the importance of those small, seemingly everyday moments.  The acts of kindness, or forgiveness, or bravery, which will change the course of history in countless ways.  I also liked the concept of interconnectedness, regardless of race, religion, ethnicity, or socioeconomic status.  There is just so much to love about this book, I wish I could better put it into words.  The best suggestion I can make is to simply read it for yourself.

I received a review copy courtesy of TLC Book Tours in exchange for my honest review

Sometimes, what looks like a picture perfect family is really a portrait of dysfunction.  Violet is your typical rebellious teenager.  As the middle child, she is stuck between an older sister who fled to freedom, and a younger brother who is diagnosed with autism.  And controlling the whole family situation is Mother.  What lengths will Mother go to, in order to keep the family in order?

This book is, in a word, explosive.  For anyone who has encountered a controlling, and mentally ill person, this book rings very true.  Particularly if you have encountered someone with borderline personality disorder.  I thought the mother, Josephine, was an incredibly character, the kind you love to hate.  And my heart just ached for Violet.  Yes, she is troubled, and yes, she does some things that are wrong, but the hurt and manipulation that she endures in unbelievable.

I thought the storyline was well developed.  There were several plot twists that I did not anticipate.  The author writes with a very honest style, one that speaks from places of deep pain and healing.  That is what lends so much depth to this book; you are certain there are parts of the author imbedded in the story.  Fans of psychological thrillers, suspense, and drama will all find something to love in this book.

I received a review copy courtesy of TLC Book Tours in exchange for my honest review.

I really enjoyed the way these stories were interwoven. It reminded me that everyone has a story and you may never realize what someone else is dealing with. Well written, interesting characters, just a great collection.

I found this book to be really relatable, even though my high school and college days are long past.  I think many young adult readers will see pieces of themselves and their personal struggles in this book.  I was easily able to connect, and many other readers will be as well.
This helped me relive the younger years, as a child of the 80s/90s. Well written, well developed characters, kept me engaged throughout.

This is a book detailing years of abuse perpetrated against a young girl.  It is told in the narrative voice of the spirit of the homes in which the girl resided.  Mostly because that spirit is the only one who saw the truth of the situation, and the only one who cared about the girl.

Books like this absolutely break my heart.  I find it hard to comprehend that people actual treat their children this way, yet I know it to be true.  It is clear that this book is more than a little autobiographical.  I hope the act of writing this helped the author heal.

The writing is lyrical and lovely.  The metaphor of insects in place of people is unique, and while it does take some getting used to, it helps deal with the horrors that the firefly  withstood.

Shine bright firefly.
This book is really beautiful.  The photos are simply gorgeous, and I love the different stories presented.  It is like walking back in time.

Set in Kansas in 1885, this book follows the story of Zoe, a widow taking care of the orphaned children of her best friend Addy. Cade is the children's nephew, but he is also Zoe's old flame. He left town years ago, to become a bounty hunter, with a promise to return to Zoe. Tired of waiting, she married, but her husband eventually died. Now, he is in charge of his sister's children, so he returns to town to settle the matter. As it turns out, there are quite a few matters that need to be settled back in town. But can they be?

I was a little nervous about this book when I noticed the setting, as I am not a big fan of westerns. However, I quickly forgot that this book was set in a Wild West-type setting, because the story so quickly becomes engaging. Lori Copeland does an excellent job of hooking the reader, right from the start. Her characters are so relatable; one forgets they are simply characters. In fact, one of the children in the book has a lisp, and all her dialogue is written phonetically, as it would sound with the lisp; I found myself talking like her for a day or two after finishing the book. It is no exaggeration, her characters become so familiar to you, and they are more like old friends.

The story line moved quickly, so there was no real down time in the book. As a result, I found it hard to get to a good stopping place, and would instead find myself reading for hours after I had intended to stop. That is a sign of an engaging plot.

There is a strong emphasis on family in this book, and what a family can look like, since Zoe is not blood kin to the children, but she is still their family. I really liked that sentiment being represented in a Christian book. Also, I liked the fact that the characters were flawed, I think that was part of what made them so relatable. There is also a theme of community in the book that allowed a rich cast of supporting characters to shine at different times.

All in all, I highly recommended this book. While the main storyline was that of romance, the plot and back story were so rich with details that it was more than just a romance novel. While fans of traditional western novels might find it a little too romantic for them, lovers of historical romance will enjoy it, and if you are like me, with little exposure or appreciation to traditional western novels, this is a great way to test the waters. This book is one in the Western Sky Series, so if you have enjoyed others from the series, chances are you will love this one as well.

Very rarely does one person's story unfold without affecting the stories of others.  As children, Monty, BJ, and Erin saw themselves as equals; as they grew and evolved, each child took their own path, illuminating the differences between the three.  Yet no matter where they go and what they choose, they all still seem to have  a bearing on each other.

I am really quite a fan of short story collections where the characters and stories are interwoven.  This book is yet another example of why this style appeals to me.  We get to see the characters from different angles and points of view, which allows us to have a clearer image.  We get to see this trio of characters interact in different ways and with different combinations of people, and we find that each, in some way, is wounded.  Each, in some way, is abused or unloved, and feels less than the others.  They cannot seem to notice that their feelings of inadequacy is probably their greatest uniting factor.

I really thought the characters were well developed.  They each have their own stories to tell, and by breaking them up into short story form, we get intimate flashes of each character.  I particularly loved that, while reading, I had no preconceived notions of the appearance of the characters (for the most part; Monty's enthnicity is described, as is BJs hair), which to me meant these characters could be, and in many ways are, all of us.

This is a very quick read, but it is intensely emotional, with a lot of stuff below the surface.  Even though you will get through it quickly, you will need a little time to digest it.  Fans of short stories, particularly interwoven collections, will enjoy this book.

I received a review copy courtesy of TLC Book Tours in exchange for my honest review.

Tracy was a young girl from South Africa who found herself in the "family way" at the age of fourteen.  Through the book, we learn what it is really like to be a teen mom, how it affects your life in the long run, and how your life need not be the tragic cliche we all associate with teen parenthood.  We also learn that in order to survive, one must have a sense of humor.

I really enjoyed this book.  I felt like Tracy gave an honest and endearing account of her experience as a teen mother.  Our culture is currently obsessed with teen parenting, and the drama that it can create.  One need only to look at MTV's program line up to confirm this.  Yet Tracy shows that, while teen parenting is not what most girls dream of, nor is it the optimal situation, it does not have to mean a death sentence or doom the mother to a life of trashy drama.  I loved that Tracy did what she needed to do to make life as good as possible for her kids.  I also loved the fact that Tracy parents gave her so much support.

A few reviewers have criticized the fact that Tracy talked about her dating life, and (gasp) the fact that she had sexual partners after have a child at such a young age.  Um, hello, what century are you living in?  Why is it wrong for a young, healthy woman to have, and heaven forbid, enjoy sex?  Why is it so awful that she sought out love and partnership?

There are definitely some parts of the slang and some cultural references which we foreign to me, being fairly unfamiliar with South African culture, but that did not hinder my ability to appreciate this book.  It is a nice, lighthearted memoir (not all memoirs have to be heartrending and melodramatic by the way) that made me laugh.  I appreciate the honesty, and really enjoyed the nice easy read.  Memoir fans who appreciate lightheartedness would enjoy the book, as would many fans of the teen mom type reality television shows.

I found that of the books in the Wolves of Mercy Falls series, this was my least favorite.  However, it is still a great book.  The author has the same elegant, captivating writing style, I just was not completely satisfied with this book as a resolution to the series.

Dystopian fiction has started to really grow on me, and books like this are the reason why.  Well written, fast paced, and totally captivating, this book pulls readers in from the first pages.  A solid read for young adult or adult readers.

Every family has its secrets.  When Anna Oh falls in love with a woman, and decides to marry her, a slew of controversy is created, and those secrets surface.  We meet various members of the Oh family, we learn their history, their joys, and their traumas.

Despite his bestseller status, this is my first foray into Wally Lamb.  I have not yet decided if there will be a second.  I found aspects of the book incredible.  I thought that the characters were really well  developed.  Even if you do not always like them (and some are certainly unlikable), you at least understand them, and feel like you know them.  That is a true art form.

However, getting to the point where you do know the characters and care about them was a bit of a struggle for me.  I really plodded through the beginning of the book (and the book is longer than most contemporary novels), and honestly, there were times I thought about giving up.  It was all just a little too verbose for me.  Detail is great, too much detail is grating.

There are a lot of unpleasant topics covered in the story; racism, trauma in various forms (emotional, physical, sexual), homophobia.  Some of these issues are described in a manner that is fairly graphic, and may serve as a trigger for readers with a similar history, so be forewarned.

I think the story and characters were solid, it was just a bit of a difficult journey to get to the end of the book.  I am not completely giving up on Wally Lamb, but someone will have to do a good job of selling me on him in the future, because this was not a fantastic first impression.

I received a review copy courtesy of TLC Book Tours in exchange for my honest review.

When Adelaide and her sister Maggie are kidnapped by white men, then rescued by a group of Cherokee Indians, they have no idea the impact the ordeal will have on their lives.  Both girls are welcomed into the tribe, and both learn to cultivate their powers of prophecy through dreams.  Maggie leaves the tribe and begins her life as a wife and mother, while Adelaide stays with the tribe.  When a white man is brought into the fold by one of the Indians, claiming the man holds the spirit of his slain tribesman and brother, Adelaide realizes she must face her past, in order to have a real future.

Once again, Graham weaves magic in the form of a beautiful historical romance.  I absolutely loved the setting of early America, where the balance of peace between the Native Americans and the white men is always tenuous and dangerous.  I am simply fascinated with the customs and spirituality of native people, and I really enjoyed how that was woven into this story.

The idea of white people being accepted into an Indian tribe seems unusual to me, but when you read about it with these characters, it all seems to make sense.  The characters are deftly written, and one cannot help but love them.  I really loved seeing Jesse develop and grow throughout the course of the story.  There is a strong theme overcoming one's past and healing from wounds both physical and emotional.

The book will appeal to fans of historical romance, particularly those with interests in Native American spirituality.  Fans of Grahams past work will be happy to see her triumphant return with this novel.

I received a review copy courtesy of the author in exchange for my honest review.

No name is ever given for the country in which she resides, nor is her name ever revealed,  but the narrator of this story talks about her life as a mother and wife in a time when it seems the world is going to end.  Turmoil is the state in which they live.  Her husband and son have gone off to fight, but who knows which side they are fighting for, or which side is the right side.  Will this family ever feel normal again?

I have never been one to read much, ok, any, dystopian fiction, so I am not sure if this book is representative of the genre.  What I am sure of is that this book is totally bizarre, and in my opinion defies most rules of writing.  The setting is never really set, the characters are never really developed, and the plot only sort of exists.

The book is described as an illustrated novel, and I find this to be a grave misnomer.  The illustrations look like childish scribbles, and do not really add anything to the experience of the book.  It reads more like a stream of consciousness exercise than an actual novel, though there is at least some resolution at the end of the book.

I think maybe I just did not "get" this book, because it has a lot of great reviews out there.  But to me, it seemed as if this book was just trying too hard to be bold and artistic, to make a statement.  The only statement I got from this book was "you get what you pay for", since I got it as a free download.

This piece is just as gorgeous as I hoped it would be.  The photo truly does not do it justice.  The piece if beautiful and delicately crafted.  Would make a great gift for anyone with a July birthday!
This throw is luxurious and soft.  I felt like I should be riding in a sleigh or something.  It made me feel so fancy!  I highly recommend!

The young Maria Antonia is a member of the Hapsburg family, her mother the Empress of Austria.  She is content to scamper about as a child, until her mother reveals her fate to her.  Mama is attempting to arrange a betrothal between Maria and Louis, the dauphin of France.  Before Maria is acceptable to France, however, she must undergo transformation.  Her appearance, her education, her ability to behave like a Queen, no, a French Queen, but all be improved before the betrothal is even possible.  After many months of hard work, Maria finally learns she is to be wed.  What will it be like, to be the future Queen of France?

For the most part, I really enjoyed this book.  I love the history of Marie Antoinette and often think she was dealt a poor hand in life.  Sure, she was royalty and privileged, but she had absolutely no say in the direction her life had, like most women of the time, yet she was ultimately executed because of that life.  I feel like the book did a good job of showing how helpless and naive Marie was.

The storyline was adequate; it is hard to be original when writing a semi fictionalized version of history, I am sure, but I just felt like I had read or scene all this before, in the same exact tone.  It reminded me very much of the 2006 movie about Marie Antoinette, in fact it felt like some of the writing had literally lifted scenes from the movie.  Perhaps this is just excellent research by both the author of this book and the writer of the screenplay, I cannot be sure.  But for me, it made the book seem just the slightest bit stale.  Still, I found myself somewhat captivated but the book.  I take this to be a good sign of a historical writer; the reader knows what is going to happen, and still finds the book compelling.

The book is a first in a trilogy about Marie Antoinette, so it ends shortly after she becomes Queen.  I am anxious to see how the author handles the next books.  This one is filled with descriptions of things that are most likely what a young teenaged royal would find interesting, fashion, relationships, and pleasing one's parents.  Not too different from today's teens, which might make the book appealing to young adult readers.  It is completely appropriate for this demographic as well as for adults.  I am hoping later books deal with more of the mature intrigues that happened during the reign of Marie Antoinette.

Her whole life, Jane has done what others wanted, or expected, her to do.  Or so she thought.  But when her husband of 22 years leaves her, she is forced to start living life for herself.  Along the way, she finds a ring from the 16th century, inscribed with Latin, and one word in English- JANE.  Lady Jane is the second cousin to the King.  She has so few choices in her life, no choice in her betrothal, no choice in her station in life.  But finally, almost too late, she realizes she does have some control over her life.  What can the Jane from yesterday teach the Jane of today?

I was thoroughly enchanted by this book, and would not have ever guessed it was published by a traditionally Christian publisher.  It is a story with wide mainstream appeal.  I love the juxtaposition of the stories of both Janes.  I found both of the Janes, as well as Lucy, to be characters that really pulled on my heartstrings, they were so well developed and easy to relate to.  Even the parts of the book that were taking place in the 16th century had such universal themes, one did not feel a huge gap due to the time setting.

A lot of times, when stories jump from character to character, or switch time periods, it can feel a but clunky, but not the case with this lovely story.  The two stories really sort of echo each other, not necessarily in plot, but in theme and emotion.  You heart breaks for each Jane in her own time.

I personally am fascinated with anything to do with the British monarchy, particularly in the 15th and 16th centuries, so this was right up my alley.  If you enjoy the writings of Philippa Gregory, I think you will like this as well.  With the modern day element, it will also draw in more traditional romance readers.  Overall, I think this book is suitable for even older teenage readers, as several of the characters are in their teens for the majority of the book.

I am very anxious to read more from Susan Meissner, because this book literally blew me away.

I received a review copy of the book courtesy of the publisher.

The world has changed ever since a virus struck, rendering adults infertile, meaning teenagers are the only ones able to reproduce.  Suddenly, girls start getting pregnant for money, and signing fertility contracts.  For twin sisters Melody and Harmony, this means life will be forever changed for one of them.  But it might not be the one everyone is expecting.  Is it a mere case of mistaken identity, or divine intervention?

Sigh.  It is always difficult to write an unfavorable review of a wildly popular book.  Such is the case for me with this book.  This is a book written for young adults, and even with that audience in mind, I found this book to be incredibly sophomoric.  The use of ridiculous futuristic slang and shallow, stereotypical characters were just a couple of my complaints with this book.

While I thought the concept of the story was good, I thought the execution was a little lackluster.  There could have been so much more done with a storyline involving global adult infertility.  Instead, it reinforced the idea that teenagers were silly, and petty, and if they really are our future then we are all doomed.  I also hate books the force preposterous visions of the future on the readers.  However, I do fully recognize that had someone written about Twitter, Facebook, or blogging in a book published in the 40s it would also have seemed ridiculous, yet here we are.

In short, if you are looking for a light easy read, whether an adult or young adult, this is an ok book, but really, I think there are much betters out there.  I know this review may make me highly unpopular among young adult fiction lovers, and I fully recognize that this book has been getting rave reviews.  Mine just is not one of them.

users.query:
Charles and his parents have just moved to Echo City where they are going to be living in The Bellwether, an apartment building that used to be a hotel. Charles is worried by the state of the building, knowing immediately that it must be haunted. When Charles tries to sleep in his bedroom for the first time, he discovers he is right and there is something in his closet. Luckily, a neighbor gives him a card for Margo Maloo, Monster Mediator. Charles considers himself a journalist and wants to interview Margo, but she is having none of it though she lets him join her in negotiating with the troll who lives in the basement. Charles finds himself in a parallel world to his own, where there are trolls, goblins, ogres and many more monsters than he could ever have dreamed.

Weings graphic novel tosses readers into a new world that is strongly based in our own. With Margo as an expert guide, this book is much less about battling monsters. It is more about how monsters can get along and live alongside humans in a urban setting. Weing has created a complete monster society and ensures with his stories that the monsters are not the bad guys, just easily misunderstood. The writing is clever, the dialogue solid and the pacing is fast.

The art of the graphic novel is modern and filled with plenty of action. The city and characters are filled with diversity that includes humans and monsters in different skin tones. Weing uses the real estate of his panels in smart ways, lengthening them to share more scenic detail, focusing the scope closely when necessary and broadening them for large buildings.

Just the right book for Halloween, expect this and future books to be popular thanks to a wise mix of humor and shivers. Appropriate for ages 8-11.

cands.text:
A grand Gothic graphic novel, this book is surprising and delightfully dark. The story is told in two parallel stories, one in images and one in text. Both stories take place in the same neighborhood and revolve around Thornhill, a home for orphans. Marys story is told in text and is set in 1982 where she is one of the last children to leave Thornhill. As the other girls leave, Mary is left with a girl who has been bullying her for some time and the story builds to a terrible climax. The illustrated story is that of Ella in 2016 who has just moved to town and doesnt have any friends yet. She can see Thornhill, now disused and old, from her house. When she glimpses a girl there, she decides to figure out the story of Thornhill and the girl.

This is the sort of story, you curl up with and read as fast as possible. Happily, Smys writing and illustrations make it almost impossible to leave this book behind for even a moment. The illustrations linger with the reader, haunting in their black and white details. The text invite readers into the past, showing them what being an orphan in was like before rules were put in place to protect children. There is a brilliance to not setting the history piece in the 1800s, but allowing shocking situations of a more modern time to surface.

The art pieces in the book allow the reader to piece together that the girl being described in the text is not the one in the images quickly. The images are done only in black and white, filled often with deep shadows and lit by bright light at other times. They are dynamic and interesting, telling their own wordless story of Ella and her own losses.

Get this into the hands of children who enjoy ghost stories, because this one will haunt readers. Appropriate for ages 9-12.

An enormous chubby monster is heading for the city! News crews are reporting on the disaster as the monster releases stink-ray farts. There are slime missiles of snot and even one big upset tummy effect. Hoses try to push him from the city, but it just ends in a belly flop. But the monster gets back up and continues his rampage. Until two brave people are willing to take on the disaster directly, by picking the terrible toddler up.

Sanders channels Japanese monster films in his text, offering just the right tone of awe and fear into the text. The book is great fun to share aloud, using an announcer voice that just makes the humor even funnier. Sanders offers just enough gross moments for children to be engaged and then moves on to other sources of humor. The switch from monster to toddler is also well handled and will not surprise readers who have been given clear hints about the end.

Santat uses his signature style here. The reactions of the people on the ground to Rodneys gross emissions is particularly effective, as they run in fear or try to survive. Santats illustrations also offer clues to Rodney actually being a human toddler, ones that become more clear as the text progresses.

A funny look at the destructive nature of toddlers that will be appreciated by older siblings and parents alike. Appropriate for ages 4-6.

This picture book is a retelling of the classic Aesop fable. The story is much the same with the added tantalizing feature of a carrot patch to get Hare to slow down and eat and then take a nap.
