I understand the need to limit the amount of fuel spilled, but they're actually counterintuitive!  I spill fuel all the time with those plastic, gimmicky latches and get extremely frustrated.

This can works as expected and as it should.  I haven't spilled any fuel either.  Additionally, while it's a 5 gallon can, you can get about 6 gallons in it.

These are great packing cubes and they rival eBags both in quality and price.  I'd highly recommend these over the alternatives, as I've tried both and can easily say that these are the better option.

Quality of the bag and zippers is great.  They've held up to repeated use without any type of flaw.  Additionally, the bags aren't stiff, so you can conform the bag to fit just about anything (reasonable) inside.  When not in use, it takes up next to no space.

I've used these bags on multiple international trips and not only does it organize by military roller duffel, but it makes it extremely easy to organize my items in quick to grab bags.  I can't tell you enough how much time it has saved when I can just pull out 1 cube, with a days worth of clothes and toiletries and just toss it into my backpack.

Highly recommended!

Also, the size and shape are great.  It can fit into just about any type of suitcase or bag.  When travelling with my family, we can easily organize our stuff from our baby's stuff.  No more jumbled mess of clothes!

(+):  Excellent taste, heat level can easily be adjusted with packet, best slow cooker chili out there
(-):  None

We use this all the time and became disappointed when our local grocery stores stopped carrying it.  Thank you Amazon for coming to the rescue!  And at a better price!

We add a can of kidney beans, chili (pinto beans), garlic cloves and stewed tomatoes to make this chili off the charts!  Everyone who tries it loves it and literally thinks that we slaved away over the stove to make it.

Buy these chili, you won't regret it!

This is the only bag of charms I've ever received that matched 100% to the picture.  The charms are of good quality; not exceptional, but good.  I won't ding a star because they're priced very appropriately for what you're getting.

All in all, it's a great set to any collection, Mother's Day or not.  Highly recommended!

I've had these pens forever and they still work...It's basically the pen that will write correctly each and every time.  Not to mention, they're near indestructible.  Consistent, smooth and waterproof/smudgeproof ink.  You can't ask for a better pen.  I've probably written over 750+ pages of notes with the same pen and it's still working like day 1.

This box of pens will easily out live me.  This is one of the few examples of something made today that was built to last.

As an owner of a Keurig, I was skeptical about buying another coffee maker/system.  But I've heard glowing reviews on this Starbucks machine, including the drinks it's able to produce.  I figured to give it a try and if I was unsatisfied, I'd just return it or give it away to someone.

While I'm not a Starbucks fanatic, I do enjoy some of their drinks.  The included recipe guide, which can also be found on their website, produces drinks that are a near perfect match, if not spot on, to their store counterparts.  I believe this has to do with the 19 bar pressure and the specifically designed Verismo pods and recipes designed around this specific system.

Some people reviewing the product are marking it down for the price of the pods, but that's not any fault of the machine itself.  The pods are more expensive than most K-cups, but comparable in price to the Starbucks branded K-cups.  Additionally, the cost of the unit and the pods easily will pay for itself if you're accustomed to drinking a Starbucks every day.  This machine is more of a special treat than just making a 10-12oz. coffee for the road in the morning.  You can certainly make the large coffee, but it's probably more cost effective to just use your regular coffee maker and/or Keurig.

A few things to note, make sure you rinse the machine (using the 'Rinse' function) after each brew.  It really cuts down, if not, eliminates any hiccups with the machine.  Make sure to empty the pod trash tray as well.  I believe they state it can hold about 10 used cups, but I'd never let it get that full.

No complaints with this machine!  I use it every morning a love it!

Good quality ball at a bargain price!  No complaints so far and the ball has been holding air over the last few days of use.

(+):  High quality, excellent price, well made, far better than all soccer balls at this price point, materials holding up well, even with some pavement use

(-):  No retail packaging; left a bit to be desired, comes deflated, has some initial flat spots until you use it

(+):  One of the best corn snacks I've had, lightly spicy with a hint of lime, easy to take-on-the-go, everyone loves them
(-):  Pricing; definitely expensive but worth the cost

It definitely seems more durable than the other typical MacBook Pro covers you'd find on Amazon.  So far, so good with this one in terms of durability.  It also has a snugger fit, which is good, but I believe I'd end up cracking this cover if it ever had to be removed.

The reason I'm deducting two starts is because of the frosted color.  From a distance, it looks great.  My wife likes the look of the rose gold.  But upon closer inspection and even more apparent when the Apple logo is lit, the frosted look has a spray paint pattern on it.  You can see what appears to be unevenness and "spray patterns" on the cover.  I can best compare it to what an object looks like when you do a light first coat of paint with an aerosol can.

Overall, it's durable and looks nice from the distance, but rather cheap when looking up close.  And considering that you're normally close to your laptop, I'd be hesitant to recommend this product.

I'm new to DE shaving; I've used the Gillette Mach 3/5 razors for years and after much research and advice, I went with the Merkur 37C.

(+):  High quality, polished and has a nice weighted feel.  Includes 1 Merkur razor in the box.  Aggressive shave, but doesn't tear up your face.  I'm a guy that needs to shave every day, but sometimes I'll go 3-4 days without shaving on a long weekend or vacation and would absolutely dread shaving 3-4 days of growth.  This razor easy cuts through that tough growth or light stubble, without any added pressure from my hand.  I can't think of a negative for this razor.

(-):  Can't think of any cons at all; you'll see people recommending razors that are less aggressive, but I jumped straight on this one and have had no regrets.  Why waste the time and money on other razors if you're already looking at this one?

Also, I'd recommend you to buy a razor sample pack on Amazon to find the blades you like best.  Personally, I like the Israeli Personna and Merkur Platinum blades.

Highly recommended!

(+):  Fully USB-powered security camera, IR lighting works well in low light conditions, works with all camera monitoring software, 1MP resolution but the image quality is exceptional (Sony CCD).

(-):  No included software, no IR control abilities, not compatible with Windows 10 (tried multiple machines), says it's indoor/outdoor but there is no way that this could be used outdoors and withstand the elements.

Overall, a decent camera for the price, but wouldn't purchase if you plan on using Windows 10 (works on Vista/7/8). I will update the review if anything changes.

Simply put, AMAZING performance!  I have 2 of these running in SLI and both are overclocked.  No heat issues, even with my cards back to back in my case.  While the cooling technologies have certainly been improving over the years, the EVGA backplates, in my opinion, make a world of difference in allowing extra airflow to cool the card.  Originally, I had 2 EVGA reference design 980Ti's that I returned within the first week because at stock speeds, they were throttling from the heat.  My case has great airflow and is huge (Corsair 750D - full tower), but the reference designed cards were just baking together.  Got these two bad boys instead and I've been flying since!

You can't go wrong with these cards, they're great and definitely a better value when compared to the 970/980 and Titan models.  Additionally, EVGA has one of the best warranties and replacement options on the market today.  While all the big players have comparable online support, EVGA really stands out and takes care of you when you have an issue with a card.  And their "step-up" program is great as well.

Lastly, another thing I noticed about these cards, is that they're lighter than some other designs, but also the weight is distributed fairly evenly across the card.  This really does help with the "sagging" of the card and potentially damage to PCI-E slots.

I highly recommend this EVGA GTX980Ti!

Simply put, excellent build quality and comfort!  I also love the customization of the DPI, both in the UI console and on-the-fly.  While adjusting the DPI on the mouse itself isn't necessarily new, the placement of this is perfect, especially if you play FPS games.  On the aesthetic side of things, the matte black finish is a nice touch and the lighting control is great, especially when paired with a backlit Corsair keyboard.  Mine is paired the K70 RGB and looks great.

Additionally, the comfort of this mouse is exceptional.  The aluminum feels solid and when you use it, you know that you're holding something of quality.  I actually bought this mouse twice, as I have one for my work machine, that I don't even play games on.  The level of comfort and precision this provides actually makes it hard to use any other type of mouse.

Purchasing this mouse won't be a regret.  Trust me.

users.query: Lots of military alpha male-ness here! As with any collection (I assume), there were a couple that felt clich or too mushy to be real. And one or two that felt too short; sometimes its hard to properly develop a character like a wounded veteran in a novella! But even though I enjoyed most of the stories, I have to admit there was no standout. Perhaps because it was overall just a great collection!

cands.text:
Since I write about military characters, I like to read military characters. I hadn't heard of this series before and it sounded interesting because of the veteran angle. I didn't check until I'd finished reading, but this is the fifth book in the series and takes place just days after the Viet Nam war ended.

I'm no history buff, but I do like mysteries. As a mystery, this one had so many twists and threads, I almost couldn't keep track of them all. I can honestly say I didn't know what was coming next, so in that regard, this is a great mystery. However, in the end, I did not understand why exactly Darby Baxter felt so strongly about the baby. Considering that was a central tenet to the story, this is not a good thing to still be wondering after you've finished the book.

I like reading about a character's emotional journey based on what has happened to them. That can be in a mystery or a romance or a "mixed" genre. What these characters are going through is very emotional, and yet I just couldn't seem to get "close" to them.

The way that Pepper was reunited with Darby (whom she thought was dead) was excellent. But after that, I would have expected emotions, romantic sentiments, and physical desires. Colonal Darby Baxter had all kinds of potential to be an interesting character, especially in an unaccustomed state of vulnerability ("she'd never smelled fear on him before"). But I just couldn't feel it. Maybe I needed to have the character background from the other books? At any rate, that's why I would rate this as a 3.5 if I could.

I was attracted to this book for several reasons.

First, I love main characters who are soldiers and/or EMS-type personnel, and the idea of following "first responders" of the 9/11 crises intrigued me.

Second, since I often create and write the stories of soldiers with PTSD (post traumatic stress disorder), I'm logically attracted to characters in that situation, as was the case in this novel. (Austin was on scene during 9/11 and Mercy counseled 9/11 survivors; both carry emotional scars from it.)

The premise also attracted me - two people who already share something in their past reconnecting after a number of years. (Two of my novels have variations of this theme.)

The storyline was good, but not as compelling as I had expected. I found myself wishing for less back-and-forth banter dialogue, keeping the story tighter and moving a bit faster. I would have liked more detailed descriptions of the dramatic things (like a beating and subsequent recovery) and how that affected the characters. I guess you could say I wanted *drama*, but what I got was *introspection*.

The handling of the Christian theme was good, in my opinion. Not overdone, not preachy...it felt like real-world people. The secondary characters were also well done, giving the right amount of interaction to the main characters while not becoming too stereotypical.

I have mixed feelings about the ending. In one way, it was unexpected so it's memorable. (I don't care for the "typical" romance formulas; I like more "meat" in my books, but I also like a happy ending when I'm reading for escape.) I can't help feeling that it was rushed after all the agonizing on the part of the characters throughout the book. It felt like the author needed to wrap up the book quickly, or wanted to get you to buy the next in the series.

Like other reviewers, I was surprised how many typos and grammatical errors I encountered. Simple things like placing an "Austin said" at the end of a quote would have minimized confusion about who was speaking (which happened with regularity), which inevitably interrupted the flow of the story.

Primarily because of the disappointing ending and poor grammar, I'd have to bump this book to a rating of 3.5.

This memoir was missing what is one of the most compelling issues of soldiers coming home (for me): namely, the struggle within (coming to terms with what he did and saw) and the struggle with relationships (those closest to him who WERENT soldiers). There were only a couple mentions of the authors mother and family (I still don't know how many siblings he had and what sex they were) and no mention of a woman in his life.

There was some discussion about how his faith was impacted by what he did (kill a man) and saw, which I also find fascinating, but it just didn't seem deep. There was some discussion about his style of leadership and how he mentored others, and that just felt like a teachable moment. The book had a good old boys club feeling - maybe (not being a man) it just wasn't touchy-feely enough for me!

I admit I first wanted to read this book because of the motorcycle angle (hot biker guys, yum, not to mention I'm a biker myself). I also have a weakness for military (or ex-military) veteran heroes in novels - especially if they're injured (physically and mentally). Throw in a juicy mystery or threat of life and limb, and I'm totally THERE.

And this book had it all.

The tortured hero (in this case both literally and figuratively). A smart-ass heroine. Plenty of fireworks between the two, even as the hero tried to keep his feelings for the heroine at bay. There were several OMG scenes (think torture).

This book has a lot of vernacular and a stream-of-consciousness writing style. I tend to want to write that way in my own work but temper it down because, frankly, it's hard to do well. And when it's not done well, the story is harder to read. Not a problem here! The writing style fit with the personality of the characters and the faster pace of the plot line itself.

Another thing that doesn't usually work for me is multiple points of view, and that's my only thumbs-down on this book. You do want secondary themes, but you don't want them to overshadow the main story. In this case, it was two other members of the Black Knights who are crazy about each other but won't admit it (the subject of the next book in the series, I understand). And, it would also be good to differentiate by dialogue (the stream-of-consciousness style is just too hard to take when EVERY character is using it). At least when there was a point-of-view change, it was clearly delineated by a new chapter.

Yes, there were a few scenes that required a suspension of logic (I was thinking about a scene where he's got a bullet in his shoulder but twenty minutes later he's lifting her off the ground/against the wall), but isn't that what we escape into a book FOR?

Since I was trained as an Army paramedic in a previous life, I am drawn to novels and characters who are in that line of work (and much of my writing is impacted by that experience).

From the description of this book I thought there'd be a bit of humor. A couple chapters in I thought crap, this is going to be another Black Flies (which is a rather dark/depressing novel about a paramedic). But no...I got a pleasant surprise. Although there are scenes about the heavier aspects of the paramedic job, the author didn't dwell in them. The book wasn't so much about being a paramedic as it was about how events in Brian's life impacted him - and it's a love story - which is what I like to read.

Against the odds (not to mention with the help of a woman) Brian manages to claw his way out of a very bad spiral that began with the death of his infant son, subsequent divorce, and interrupted suicide plan.

It's not a long book and it has a rather large "cast," which makes it more of a challenge to develop the characters. I thought the author did a good job of that. At first the animosity between Brian and his ex-wife was too clich, as was the fact that they both found new love, but in the end they found a way to become friends and support each other, which I found refreshing.

My only complaint? Add a "he said," "Mel said" etc. I sometimes could not tell who was speaking, which forced me to stop and re-read. It takes me out of the story and slows me down.

A wounded veteran and a devoted wife. Yep - wife. That's different in a romance...and I liked it. This was not a characters-meet-and-experience-immediate-love/lust story. The characters had been married for a number of years and they knew and understood each other at the deeper level that comes with marriage. They had been through periods of separation (due to military service) and tough times (one very tragic experience in particular). Their marriage vows also created a more committed relationship (particularly for the wife, Aimee).

The veteran (Kyle) is my favorite type of hero. The kind of hero who is tough - and even tougher on himself - but there is something about them that shows their humanity and their vulnerability. (The kind of hero I created in True Surrender.) I liked that he had contradictions of himself.

Kyle's experiences, thoughts and frustrations with his physical disabilities were highly believeable. Aimee's responses to them were at times almost too good to be true. But I liked that she was a strong enough person in her own right, and with her own background of military service.

Many books make use of what I think of as "the big misunderstanding" and that is true of this book as well. Sometimes an author can string that out to the point where you get tired of it. But that didn't happen with this book; even though the action took place over only a few days, it was paced well. The wrap-up was a little too quick, but had a twist I didn't connect earlier that was a pleasant surprise.

A note about the title: I don't typically pick up Christmas-themed titles, although it seems fashionable so there must be others who do. This was so much more than a "Christmas story"! I picked it up because of the wounded veteran angle and I'm glad I did. 4.5 stars!

I can only imagine how much went into this book. So much more could have been said; but it was the right length IMO. Where the author needed to stop and give some background or history on a military situation or event, thats a tricky point; its needed to put the womens experience in context, but it also puts the human story on pause. I admit I got a little impatient to get back to the women.

There was a fairly big cast of characters and I kept getting them mixed up. We don't really spend a big enough chunk of time with any woman to really know her well. Each of the women in the book could have had 50 pages to herself, they are all so interesting!

The book covers the selection process for these women in fair detail. So much so that I found myself longing to move on to the ACTION. (Thats how we are, isn't it?!) Also, somewhere around the train-up period I found myself thinking, I have absolutely nothing in common with these women and I was having trouble feeling connected at all. I mean, these women are dynamos! I don't think I ever wanted to work that hard (physically) even when I was younger (as most of these women are). And though I was trained as a combat medic by the Army, I didn't have near the strong feelings that these women did about serving.

Its a somewhat sad ending. One that makes you think, of everybody, why did Ashley have to die? And of course, the romance writer in me loved her storybook marriage (or maybe I just loved Jason!).

Since I write about military characters with PTSD and other injuries, I was naturally attracted to this book.

It had the potential to be very good. And I really tried to get into it. I especially liked the character of Gerry; I felt the author did a good job developing his voice and the "slippery slope" he found himself on psychologically. The premise was great (a veteran confessing to crimes he can't remember committing - brilliant) and the end twist was good (although it felt rushed). I would have liked to see the secondary characters more developed.

The problem was, it jumped all over the place. It changed point-of-view in the middle of a scene, switched from first-person to third-person with no warning, and was generally hard to follow. There were entire chapters of backstory, or what might be called flashbacks (although I usually think of flashbacks as being shorter), which made it confusing to connect that chapter with what was going on in "present" chapters. I think flashbacks are difficult to do well, and should be used sparingly; otherwise they take the reader out of the story too much.

The story idea was such a great one, but these editorial problems really cut into my enjoyment of this book. It needed a good editor!

Seal at Heart has many of my favorite things: a wounded military man and a strong-willed, no-nonsense heroine, as well as a healer theme. I love military intrigue (the opening scene when the hero's mission goes bad hooked me right away) and exploring the friction and challenges soldiers experience in their personal relationships.

This novel did not disappoint! The voices and military "feel" was authentic - the commitment and camaraderie right-on. (As an ex-Army medic and helicopter pilot, the only thing that was jarring was the fact that the hero could fly a chopper just because he'd had fixed-wing lessons. Flying a helo is HARD, folks!)

Writing a military character (especially a man) in a relationship or romance novel is hard to do. I know (from my own writing) that it's hard to walk the fine line of TELLING rather than SHOWING. These characters aren't often verbose (not a lot of dialogue), and you can show them using exercise or alcohol to "exorcise" the demons only so much before there's not enough to hold the reader's interest.

By and large, the author achieved this delicate balance. There were a few times when I felt she was tipping into the territory of "telling" me too much of what was in the hero's head, and there was a six-week period that flashed by without showing his struggle with his memory that was a bit abrupt. But I thoroughly enjoyed the characters, the story arc, the healer elements, and the climax when we gets his memory back (that's not a spoiler, right? You knew it was a happily-ever-after ending!).

Oh, and if you like a little spice in your novels, this one won't disappoint. But in my opinion, the story was plenty compelling on its own.

I know it's a good book when I'm still thinking about it 10 days after I finished it. I was looking for brutal honesty and the raw emotional toll of war (not a factual history tome), and I got it in this book. Sometimes it was as much what WASN'T written as what was (the chapter near the end with the three young boys is a good example). That is a delicate balance for a writer and it was powerful. (Note: toning down the swear words and tightening up the sentence structure would have made it even more powerful by making it less distractive to read.)

I caught a snippet of a documentary on TV the other night, about a situation where our bombers killed our own soldiers because they "got confused by the smoke." It's dismaying to realize that some things never change. I WANT to believe the Army Reserve is smarter and better organized now than my experience in it 20 years ago, but John's experiences sound uncomfortably familiar - our tools were outdated, our training was under par, and the left hand never knew what the right was doing. I (like the author) joined the National Guard to help pay for college; the recruiters laughed off any suggestion that we'd actually be sent anywhere to fight. What do you expect an 18- or 20-year-old to believe? And when you are immersed in a culture, you tend to adopt that culture's attitudes (especially when you're young) - the military IS a culture. I lost site of some of the morals I'd been brought up with and I'd be willing to bet some of the author's less tasteful personal characteristics may have been 'exacerbated' by this immersion too. I would have liked to know more about who the author was before he went to war, and what happened when he returned home (perhaps that's another book altogether?).

There was one mind-blowing moment in my life when I thought I was being activated to Desert Storm. Thank God it was our armory-sharing MP unit instead - or I might have had the same disillusioning experience!

I don't know too many authors who can pull off a book that is almost half flashbacks, AND told from so many points of view. Im not normally crazy about either, but it works for me here.

Defiant could apply to both the hero and heroine of the main story of the book. Navy SEAL John Nilsson defies his superiors and risks his career. And Meg continually defies John and everyone else to stick to her plan.

For being a smart woman, Meg did some really dumb stuff. And it took a little too long for Meg to finally trust John and work WITH him instead of against him. And some of Johns devotion was almost out of the realm of believability. But the building sexual tension was so well done (including history/flashback) that I was willing to forgive these small transgressions. :-)

As for the side stories: theres a spicy one with two of Johns cohorts that really doesnt impact this story. It was a distraction (although a rather, ahem, interesting one). And the sub-theme with the grandmothers love storywell, I thought for sure that was going to be a tear-jerker but it ended with an HEA, which was more satisfying. And thank goodness the daughter didn't die in the end (oops, sorry - spoiler alert - but you probably guessed that already) because that would have pissed me off!

Full disclosure: I was Army National Guard myself (medic) AND learned to fly helicopters (although not in the Army). So how could I resist a book about a female Army Reserve helicopter pilot? Not to mention Hannahs book Night Road practically devastated me.

This book was even more than I expected. First, it was about a married couple rather than a new love situation. Marriage is hard, and it can so easily go on the rocks, as was the case for Joelene and Michael.

I was irritated with Michael for not supporting Joelene in her military career (he came across as extremely self-centered at first). I was irritated with Joelene for always acting so strong and never letting Michael know how she felt. But it was all so believable in a twelve-year marriage!

I didn't know when I started reading what the extent of Joelenes injury would be. Turns out its so similar to the hero in my novel True Surrender - amputation and a touch of PTSD, even the loss of a close friend - that I couldn't put the book down during that section. And without getting into spoilers, the way Michael stepped up and Joelene regained faith in herself and her husband and family it was the kind of book I write (and like to read): finding courage within to trust and love again.

Awesome!

This book has everything I love in a story: slightly dangerous occupations (my writing regularly features EMS and military characters). War and chaos. A handsome, brooding male character. A love triangle ... and a happy ending (I'm a sucker for those). Evans did a masterful job of using traumatic events and showing how the characters develop because of (or in spite of) them. The 'voice' of each was authentic and even though there were four points of view (telling their stories) I didn't have any moments of confusion like I have in other books. The only weakness: the purpose of the moose-on-fire imagery was unclear to me, other than a vague notion of significance.

A pretty good effort/start to a series featuring Navy SEALS. Was it all realistic? Nah. But thats what we read fiction for (although there was one particular scene when the heroine was TSTL  Too Stupid To Live  that I could have done without). The characters were developed and changed over the course of the story. They had flaws/weaknesses that had to be overcome. The action was non-stop so you couldn't get bored. It was entertaining and kept my attention. And, this was all accomplished *without* a sex scene, which I found refreshing.

The one annoying thing was the changing POV  with no warning you were suddenly in another characters mind, even supporting characters (i.e., the other SEAL team members) for just a paragraph or two. For me, that is always distracting and thus the 4-star rating.

The premise of this book was interesting: three women who posed as boys during the Civil War and are now trying to move on in life (and love). I would have liked to hear more details about that; the characters would allude to an incident that I wanted to know more about. But this book is pretty much all after that. There were interesting twists and a good climax. And of course, the romance which seemed a little dry to me but in the end was fairly satisfying. I wanted more about the heroines experience in the war.

This book actually follows two stories, one happening in 1918 and the other in present day. The way the two womens lives become intertwined - and the way the author wove the two stories together in a dramatic climax - were especially awesome.

What I liked: Both stories star strong female characters, which Im always attracted to. I like reading about female military characters, especially if they get to be the hero (be it physical or mental/emotional). At times the references to military processes and units got a little overwhelming, but the author kept the focus on the personal challenges (in particular the romances) of both women. I especially appreciated the realistic look at the marital strain and problems of the present-day couple.

We don't get to know the two male characters very well, and I missed that a little bit because I enjoy stories told from the male point of view.

My only complaint was that it hopped around a little too much. Back and forth with the two stories was OK once I realized that was how the book was laid out. Then the author added flashbacks of the current couples meeting, dating and marriage. Within that you also had different point of view (his and hers) so I did find myself having to backtrack and re-read in some places, which tends to take me out of the story. It happened more at the beginning which also gave me the impression of a slow start. However, that may have been unavoidable given the overall story idea!

I have great respect for Struecker, who has written a nail-biting suspense about a Spec Ops (Army Ranger) team that also grapples with the issue of faith.

There are a lot of characters in this book, and the point of view bounced around a lot. Add in the team members nicknames, and it got hard to follow at times. The early parts bogged down a bit, felt a little slow with all the characters getting a tidbit.

Sruecker tried to follow family events happening at home (a rebellious teenage son, a troubled pregnancy) as well as the action on the mission, which I think is a pretty talk order given the huge cast of characters. As a result, it was hard to get to really know any one of the characters. JJ, the only Christian on the team, is probably the one the reader most gets to know, along with the team leader (Eric Moyer).

Struecker obviously knows the processes and lingo of Spec Ops (having been an Army Ranger himself), but he did an excellent job of not letting that overshadow the storyline.

As for the storyline it had just the right amount of bad-guy stuff (although a tad bit clich). It moved along very quickly from about the middle of the book.

(spoiler alert here) The ending was very good. I was starting to think it would be a HEA which didn't feel realistic considering how the odds were stacked against this team. But no, the team loses one of their own in the end, and the conversation about faith comes full circle, leaving some (Eric in particular) with grief and survivor guilt.

Excellent action. Less bouncing around amongst characters would have made this a 5-star read.

I really tried to like this book. I mean, I was trained as an Army combat medic myself at the age of 19. Back at my National Guard unit after training, I quickly realized that we had few resources, not a lot of support, and I experienced some of the same frustrations as Michael (albeit not during wartime). It was sobering to realize those problems still exist; with everything our country has been through in the last decade I would have expected better.

Sure, we bitched about stuff. And yeah, there was some sexual stuff going on. When you're young, you don't always have the ability to put your experiences in perspective. And a year seems like a long time.

But the reason I read a memoir is to a) be exposed to the personal transformation of the writer, and b) to learn something useful myself.

There was none of that here. There was very little of what he actually SAW in the operating room, in fact. What did Michael learn about himself from this experience? I don't mean superficial things, like Nyquil is best for getting to sleep. I wanted to see how it changed him and how it impacted his life afterward. If there wasn't any personal growth, I don't see the point of writing a memoir.

I get that his situation wasn't ideal, and I kept reminding myself how young he was. But the only word that kept coming to mind while reading was whiny; in fact, I skipped a chunk around 2/3 of the way through. I wanted more. A whole lot more.

I already had Navy SEAL Chris Kyle's memoir (American Sniper) reserved at the library when the news broke that he'd been killed by a fellow veteran. Given that I write about wounded veterans, I was fascinated by the circumstances of his death, and especially interested in what he had to say in life.

Kyle's writing style is casual; he may be biased but it's not in-your-face. Even if you don't feel the same, you don't mind because he seems like such a decent guy. He tells it like it is without political BS. I liked that he was unapologetic about being a Christian. There's a lot of swearing etc in the military, but it doesn't mean you can't be a Christian. That's real. And it's interesting that he brought his wife's voice/thoughts into it from time to time.

I confess that in my time crunch, I skipped over some of the military stuff in favor of the personal struggles. He's pretty matter-of-fact about them, and I found myself wishing he'd go more in-depth on the personal struggles.

In one chapter he talks about falling into a pit and drinking all the time. He mentions a car crash (totaled his truck but he walked away without a scratch) being his wake-up call. I wanted to know more... what those demons were like "up close" and how he faced them down and crawled back out of that pit (and I'm sure he wouldn't have done it in a "poor me" style either). I suppose no one wants to relive periods like that (I sure don't) but that's what I really wanted to know, and that's what I think makes a memoir stand out. This one is OK but not a stand-out.

But I do have to wonder about the "demons" his fellow veteran was battling that would make him take such an extreme action...

The idea of this story is hilarious. Cynthias dating service for the Hollywood elite leads her to a potential relationship with Hollywoods biggest star (and major player). At the same time, her on-again, off-again boyfriend shows up. AND her teenage crush moves back into town. Its a perfect storm - of the laughing kind.

Unfortunately, it was difficult to read; it would have benefitted from a good edit. Head-hopping and telling instead of showing both take me out of the story. We were told about the teenage experience with Pete not once but twice (almost an exact duplicate). I had to go back and re-read a few times to figure out who was speaking (and I think a couple times the dogs were speaking??). And if it was supposed to be Cynthias story, theres an awful lot about her friend Lolita in it.

I could not get into Pete, and I could not get into the instant sex Cynthia has with him. We didn't know anything about him in present day, so why would she be so into him without knowing who hes become? On the other hand, resisting (and then showing up) the mega-movie star was hilarious.

This was a fun story and I especially liked the scenes when the main character (Tess) was riding (and learning to ride) the motorcycle. I also appreciated that the author gave the characters problems that you and I could totally relate to (they weren't deep, dark, scarred-for-life issues). It was hard to follow sometimes, though: changing tense (from I to she and then an abrupt shift to a different point of view) forced me to backtrack and re-read parts, which took me out of the story. There were a lot of sub-plots that were unresolved at the end, and relationships that were glossed over that I wanted to know more about (such as Tess and her dad: he willed her this Harley but we never find out what their relationship was like). And the title: it wasn't really Chloes secret, it was Monas. But Mona wasn't the main character! Although I figured out who Chloe was early in the book, Monas confession at the end (a darker one) was really a great twist. A thorough edit could have made this a 4-star.

I liked that the characters made a connection that wasn't sexual right off the bat. Refreshing change from so many rocker stories. The voice of Beryl was funny and authentic. Beryl has a special knack for saying the wrong thing and having it turn out right. In fact, Beryls adjustment to New York and finding a new Self had the potential to be so funny in and of itself. Could have done so much more with leaving the Oregon boyfriend, the two fiascos with other men, the interaction with the wealthy socialite, etc before she got in so deep with Gavin.

So my thoughts about the romance it felt forced and rushed. I never really got over how quickly and easily they fell into a romantic relationship via internet chat. One conversation its business, the next its friendly, and the next shes wearing his shirt and sleeping in his bed. (And of course the moment he gets back)

Also, Gavin seems to miraculously snap out of his funk (after less than two months) like Beryl is some miracle drug. He seems too nave for a famous rock star, and his actions aren't always believeable. Also, there is a sub-plot with the mom that was distracting and had nothing to do with the story.

Another great book covering the next "season" of Dianne's life. This one was a bit heavier on the Christian/Spiritual angle; however, I liked that the characters not only talk about God but let their actions SHOW their love of God. I followed the interaction between Cole and Takes-Many-Horses closely so see how those male characters developed with their struggles. The introduction of Portia gave us a character we could "love to hate," even though it's not clear yet what role she'll play (I'll find out in book 3!).

I usually like (even prefer) the male perspective  especially strong male characters that have a vulnerability or weakness, and that is certainly the case with Christian. I especially liked the flashbacks/nightmare scenes. I tried to imagine reading this story as if I didn't already know The Story and I think you almost need to have read Fifty Shades to really get the point of Christians situation. The problem, then, was that it was just so much sex three books in the series,  the movie and then this it all starts to blur together, gets a little too repetitive and in the way of the story. On the other hand, I get that it is the only way Christian knows to communicate, and he does change through the course of the book (sort of a requirement to keep my interest at any level).

users.query:
Update: you can see the original comments below. These little earbuds are obviously not made to last.

After just a few months of use, the ear buds are broken. The volume up button no longer activates so you can not adjust the volume. Unfortunately I figured this out after trying to adjust the volume and turning it down more than 1/2 way. Now I can't get the volume back up and they are pretty much useless. This is disappointing because I really liked the item but I thought they would have survived more than 20-25 uses. Good design but poorly made.

There is a lot to love about these little buds. The fit in the ear is superior to any other buds, wired or wireless, that I have owned. They sit comfortably yet firmly in the ear. These are great for running or cycling. They stay in place and wick away sweat well. They are also easy to pop out with a little handle on the top of the bud. The sound quality is really good. It is not quite as good as some of the high dollar wired buds I have but they are close. There is a good amount of bass and the range of sound is very good. The sound clarity is excellent. I would say that the buds could have slightly better range. When cycling, the signal would occasionally stutter but as you get going the Bluetooth seems to sync a little better and you get pretty consistent sound. The microphone works well and shields noise from wind nicely. I have taken calls on my bike and people on the other end have been able to hear me clearly. The buttons on the bud are well thought out and you can easily find them while running. These charge off of a standard micro USB...so compatibility is great.

If I had one complaint about the ear buds it would be battery life. They claim that you can get 6 hours of consistent use out of them. I have not had that experience. I would say I can get maybe 3-4 hours at most out of them without a charge. That is fine most of the time, but on those century cycling trips or long flights I wish they held a little more juice. I bought two sets of these, one for my wife and she has not had the battery complaint I have so maybe I got a pair with a less effective battery. Regardless, given everything else these are a great little set of wireless buds and I would definitely buy them again.

cands.text:
I got a pair of these with an HTC phone I bought nearly three years ago.  I retired that phone and continued using the set of buds with my new Nokia Windows phone (which rocks BTW). After thousands of miles jogging and cycling, they held up great. Only after stepping on them did I finally crack the plastic on one of the buds.

When I saw these on Amazon, I bought three pairs because they are simply great. I have used them with two different phones and my iPad and they sound very good. Their sound quality is far superior to the white apple buds I have for my iPad. They hold up great. The size of the bud is great for my ears. Lastly, all or the functionality on the cable with volume and picking up a call have worked perfectly with both my phones.

At this price, it is a no brainer.

I really like the Squeezebox.  The Pandora integration alone is worth the purchase.  The sound quality is very good.  The power of the Squeezebox is not all that impressive but the sound is crystal clear and for most people there will be plenty of volume and punch to fill your rooms with nice quality music.  You can find almost any radio station you can dream of (probably including your local stations).  The interface is not 100% intuitive but once you fidget with it for a few minutes, it is simple to get around the menus.

My one complaint is the lack of an included battery pack.  Yes, I know you can buy a battery pack for the Squeezebox, but this is a feature that should have been included.  Not having it really detracts from the main use of this item which is to be a carry from room to room audio player.  We find ourselves leaving the SB in one room instead of toting it out to the porch or into the kitchen because carrying the plug and finding an outlet becomes cumbersome.  I just don't think an additional purchase should be required to take full advantage of an items inherent strength...which in this case is portability.

Otherwise, it is a nice unit...and I will probably be a sucker and buy the battery pack.

These speakers sound very good.  They are great for music, have plenty of power, and produce a full sound. I think a hardcore gamer may want to look into speakers that a bit more robust but for listening to music or watching videos, these have ample power and good sound quality. The sub is smaller than I expected but it does a nice job. At this price point they sound great.

My beef with them is that the little satellite speakers just look cheap. Their goofy shape and flimsy plastic appearance don't do it for me.  They sound good, don't get me wrong but I think their look is less than desirable. My biggest problem with the speaker set is the placement of the power switch. All speakers I have had in the past have a power switch on one of the satellite speakers or perhaps on the front of the sub. These have the power switch on the back of the sub...bizarre!  It is difficult to reach under the desk or in the cabinet and switch them off.  So, I just leave them on all the time.  If you are not a power conscious person, this would probably not bother you but I really see this as a design flaw.

All that being said, these speakers do sound quite good and pack enough punch to satisfy computer music listeners and movie watchers.

I liked these enough that I bought another set for my wife. She took them to her office for her employees to play with in the conference room.

The egg shaped exercise balls are a nifty little idea. They, of course, work as a stress ball but they are superior. Their material and shape make them a good exercise tool. The 3 different levels of difficulty that come in the pack vary quite a bit. The easy is something you can squeeze for an hour. The most difficult will wear your hand out fairly quickly. The egg shape of the ball adds a lot of versatility. You can squeeze it facing one direction and then reverse it to use different hand muscles. You can rotate it around and hit different parts of the hand. You can also pinch it between different combinations of fingers and do several other exercises illustrated in the small paper that comes with the eggs.

If the eggs get dirty, it is no problem to clean them. I dropped one and it rolled under my couch and picked up some dog hair. I just dunked it is water and toweled it off and it was good as new. The durability to this point seems good. I have been using them for several weeks and they don't show any signs of wear.

So, I would recommend these little exercisers. I keep one of the eggs at my desk and one in my car. If you are sitting still might as well be making your hands stronger and releasing a little stress. Plus, they are pretty cute. At least that is what people say when they see mine. Good price on a good product.

My wife bought me this to use after I had surgery to notify her if I needed assistance.  The bell is cute, small and wow is it loud for its size. I mean what can you say...? A bell should be loud when rang and this one is.  My only negative comment is the handle quality could be better...it is a bit cheaply made.

But, all in all, it is a good solid little product.

This was sent back day 1.

Play anything, anywhere is their tag line. But no Bluetooth...really? I understand that the description does not indicate that this speaker is Bluetooth and I blame myself for assuming the obvious. Sonos makes some decent (and yes to us audiophiles it is decent) speakers for smaller areas. They are solid and have good mid range sound. I can't imagine them in a home filled with audio nuts or in a home theater room, but they make better than good entry level stuff at a decent price.

My wife saw a commercial or something online and said she would like this Sonos speaker. She wanted it to play with her phone while she is working around our house, in our yard and in our shop. She also thought it may be good to take to the neighbors...I mean "Play Anything Anywhere Right?" What was the reason she wanted this? Because she was envious of my Marshall Bluetooth speaker and she fell pray to good marketing.

I un-boxed the Sonos and it is quite honestly a nice feeling speaker. It is fairly heavy in the hand and it feels well made. So, I pull out the instructions. "Play Anything...Anywhere..." But, it has to be on a proprietary WiFi. So, I get it. Sonos has a niche. They make decent stuff but then they act like they are going into a portable move-around speaker idea with this and it is literally the same as any other home speaker. You can't take it outside your WI-Fi. You can't even take it far outdoors without a WiFi booster...so why call it anything different than their already existing home placement wireless speakers? It is cheaper and I get it...but the entire idea is misleading.

Lastly, for kicks, I hooked it up. I did the set-up...which was quite easy...and fired it up. Decent sound. Pretty warm feeling audio with decent mid-range. To be honest, it was pretty good for its size. But my Anker which cost 1/2 as much sounded better. I returned the Sonos and bought a Bose for my wife (and yes I think Bose is another overpriced company making slightly better than entry level stuff), and it was far superior.

So, don't assume the obvious. IMO any moveable multi-range speaker (outside of very high end theater speakers) should have some sort Bluetooth connectivity. If it doesn't get a better in home speaker for the same price and don't pretend it is mobile.

UPDATE: After a few months of very gentle use...probably 5-10 uses, the switch on the band has stopped working. If you press it down very hard, the light will flash but the light will not stay on. Apparently a poorly made product. And, of course, it is past the time where they or Amazon will honor a return. Beware.

Original Review---

This is a very cool little safety device. I use it to jog or walk the dogs at night. It is fairly bright and has the option to blink or just provide solid light. It is fairly well made. I look at it like most running equipment. You get a year or two out of it and that is great.

My issue with it is sizing. I am a fairly good sized guy with larger than average arms but overall I am pretty average shaped. The band is too big to fit around my wrist. It will simply slide off. And it is too small to fit around my bicep. Again I have larger than average arms but it does not even come close to fitting. I actually wear mine around my ankle. That is fine for me but I would have preferred that they think about sizing. The band should be more adjustable. Either add a longer strap or add more Velcro. It was like they did not think about sizing.

But as a device it works great and is bright enough to be an effective safety device...as long as you can find a place to wear it.

If you are a true PT fan, you already have this album.  If you are a newbie, this should be on your wish list.

I have been fortunate enough to see PT live and was impressed with their ability to offer all the splendor of their music while maintaining a truly "clean" sound.  I was hesitant when buying this album.  Let's face it...good live recordings are rare.  Porcupine Tree's XM recordings are excellent but could Porcupine Tree do it again?  The answer is yes.

This album has a lot going for it.  It has a wonderful set list including an excellent rendition of "Last Chance To Evacuate Planet Earth."  The quality of the music is excellent.  You won't hear a missed note, but would Steve have it any other way...doubt it.  Lastly, it simply sounds great.  This is not a half baked attempt to answer fan's requests for additional live recordings.  This is a very good quality recording and it is truly a wonderful album.

There is no need to pay any more for another brand. These are nice cables. They are the length they claim to be. they are of good quality and seem durable. the ends are tight fitting and seem solid. Save a little cash. these are as good as any other comparable cable.
These Grinch PJ bottoms are very cute. They are extremely soft and seem at least fairly well made. The design looks just like the picture and they fit true to size. I am happy with the purchase.

This kit is filled with good quality items. The charger works well and is well constructed. The batteries are as good if not better than the original Nikon batteries...at least they have been so far. The seller also included a European power converter which is a bit flimsy but works well.

I bought this kit for a vacation and it is the perfect accessory kit for my little Nikon.

I would certainly buy from this seller again. Nice product, fast shipping.

I will preface this review by saying that I own iPads, iPad minis, a Surface, and have used Galaxy tabs. The Nokia 2520 is without a doubt the best tablet I own.

The 2520 is lightning fast. Apps boot and run without any hesitation. The Windows interface makes iOS look antiquated. When I jump over to the iPad for something, I always think at how the Nokia makes the iPad interface look like an old toy.

The picture on the Lumia is extremely good yet soft. When I first bought it I set the iPad with Retina next to it. Their detail is similar but the Lumia is easier to look at for some reason. The glass has better eye feel, if that makes sense. I have tried using the iPad for reading on vacation and two things happened; it had terrible glare, and after 30 minutes in the sun it would overheat. The Lumia is so much better for reading than the iPad it is not comparable. The non-glare screen is very usable in the sun. The unit itself did not overheat on me in the sun but to be honest, I did not really test it for long durations.

The Lumia is very light, much lighter than a Surface. The battery power is impressive. I would say you can get 12 hours of actual use (depending on what you are doing) and several days in standby mode without a charge. The width of the unit is similar to an iPad possibly 10% thicker. When you hold it in your hand the difference is not really noticeable. It is much thinner and lighter than the MS Surface, but because of it's beveled edges and firm feeling case, I think it feels more sturdy than a Surface.

The sensitivity of the screen is incredible. The on screen keyboard is very versatile however more feature rich (and complex) than the iPad. It takes a couple days to get used to it but once you do it is very productive. The handwriting recognition that is an option built into the keyboard interface is amazing. My handwriting is terrible and it makes very few mistakes interpreting what I am trying to say.

The 2520 is expandable to a point. I inserted a 64 GB Micro Smart Card to store music and movies. I was a little disappointed that it did not support bigger cards but as the tech world moves to the cloud, I guess on-device storage is becoming less and less important. Regardless, I would like to have the ability to plug in a 128GB if I chose but 64 is the max. It also has a USB 3 port and I have never used it.

The sound on the 2520 is excellent. The sound with and without headphones is vastly superior to any of my other devices. The positioning of the speakers is smart and watching movies without headphones is quite easy. It has more sound power as well. I tested headphone volume with this device versus the iPad and Surface using the same ear bugs and this is far better than both. The camera is decent. It takes good pictures and is extremely good for video even in lower light (I use it for Skype). But the camera is not something I use often...I personally don't want to be lugging around a 10" device to take pictures at the beach, etc.

One thing I don't love is the charger. Once again, we as consumers, are required to have a proprietary charger made specifically for this device. It is not charged with a Micro USB, which really surprised me knowing Nokia (I have Nokia phones). But after reading about it, the reason behind the decision was not based on marketing but instead on technical function. Nokia claims that the 2520 can be fully charged from 10% to 100% in less than an hour. This could not be accomplished with a micro USB. Personally I have not tested the specific speed of charging but I will say that I noticed that it is fast. It is drastically faster than the Surface I would say slightly faster than a standard sized iPad and about the same as my Phone.

The complaint I hear the most from users of Windows mobile devices is the lack of apps. And that is a valid complaint. The Lumia has thousands of apps available for it in the Microsoft store and it also has additional apps available (almost all for free) designed by Nokia. My thought is this... I have bought tons of apps for the iPad. But honestly most of them are junk, toys that are fun, gimmicky, or maybe serve a single purpose. That is not saying there are not GREAT iOS apps. There are tons of them. But seriously of the 60 quadrillion apps available in the Apple store I only use about 10 of them regularly. The Windows store does not have near the amount of apps available but I guess it does not bother me because on the Lumia I have MS Office, I have Netflix, I have a great music player, I have an awesome maps application, Facebook, Amazon, etc. The apps and games available may not have the numbers of Apple but they certainly have everything you could need (outside of apps that make fart sounds or have singing cats, etc.).

So, that all being said, The 2520 has replaced all of my tablet devices. It is great for business as well as passing time. I guess the real proof is that I discontinued cell service on my iPads because I really don't use them anymore. Nokia has really created a nice device here.

Update: I have had these bulbs in place for about a year and 5 are already bad. Three are blinking and two are completely dead. Defective in one year versus the 22 years as advertised. All bulbs are either on a LED rated dimmer or straight switch and 15%+ are already dead. I contacted seller and they have no warranty and claim that they don't have sales records from a year ago. I ordered 5 boxes and they somehow don't have a record of that.

When they worked they were nice but I don't plan on replacing LED bulbs every year.

So I would advise against buying this product and I would avoid this seller. Very disappointing.

Original review:
I replaced 24 bulbs throughout my house. The replacement was for multiple reasons. I installed a dimmer in a room and the CFL's were not compatible. I have a room where the home's previous owner used several different bulbs of different types. And, I just had some bulbs out. Also, I wanted to save electricity both for cost savings and environmental reasons.. So I decided to spring for the extra money and replace them with these LED's.

When I ordered the bulbs, I had two concerns; the "color" of the light, and the rumored hum that this bulb type often gives off when incorporated with a dimmer. The light color at full brightness is pretty much indistinguishable from a Incandescent. I replaced a few bulbs in a single room and left the others original. At full power, I could not tell the difference. The color is clear and pretty warm. When dimmed, the light is a lot less yellow than an incandescent. If you have ever seen a Dimmable CFL, it is closer to that. I actually prefer the LED's dimmed light. It is richer and maintains its true color instead of yellowing. And as far as hum, there is absolutely none. They are silent.

These bulbs come on instantly and are at full brightness almost immediately. In comparison to CFL's...well...there is no comparison. These LED's are drastically better. The brightness is about 10% greater than an incandescent at full power.

Now they are pricey at a little over $10 a bulb. That is about 5x that of a quality incandescent. But, in my case, I have rooms with 8-10 recessed floods in them. If you figure that 5 of these LED bulbs use roughly the same amount as one incandescent and that these bulbs will last decades not just a couple years...it makes long term financial sense. Then you figure in the better quality of light and the fact that there is no mercury in them...for me, it was a great decision.

I guess the best compliment is that I just reordered another 8 pack to finish off my basement. These are nice bulbs.

I beat up my Galaxy and had to replace it (thank goodness for insurance). I bought several cases at once hoping to find the perfect combination of durability, looks, and ease of operation. This case is just a bit bizarre and has a couple things I don't like.

First, I do not think the phone is misrepresented in the description. So, I got what I thought I would get (kind of). This case is very solid. It is made of a firm rubber plastic mix and it feels like it could take a pretty good beating. There is a glass face-plate covering the phone screen and, again, it seems very durable. However, the responsiveness of the phone definitely dropped after installing the screen cover. This did not happen with a couple other cases I bought.

The case itself is just a little weird. There is a little hanger on the top left of the phone and it comes with a lanyard to put around your neck or whatever. I thought that it would be possible to remove this little hook but it isn't. It is just kind of a weird idea. The belt clip that comes with the phone is big and bulky like pretty much all phone belt clips but it seems rugged. Like 95% of us, I don't use a belt clip. I put the phone in my pocket. That is where the real problem lies. It is very difficult to get the phone out of your pocket with this case. That little hook adds an extra thing to catch on your pants or suit jacket pocket. Also, the bulkiness of the case makes it hold onto the inside of your pocket.

I will say that of the cases I bought, I think this one would probably be the toughest...or maybe tied for first. It was also packaged very nicely. The quality is not in question. But the strange design kind of turned me off. Maybe if I used a phone belt clip, or wanted to hang my phone around my neck it would be a better fit, but for me it was too cumbersome.

We were looking for a simple record player so my wife and I could play some old vinyl we had laying around. This little unit is pretty cute to look at and it sounds surprisingly good as a stand alone player.

The construction is fairly cheap, made almost completely of light plastic but it seems sturdy. But understand that this is in no way a DJ turntable. The size is a bit smaller than I anticipated. You cannot close the cover with a full sized record on the player (which is clear from the photo in the ad) but I was surprised at the small size. The Jensen also has a built in AM/FM radio which has decent reception but I would bet that the majority of people would not use this feature.

The sound quality is pretty good. I have not tried plugging the player into my receiver via RCA but as a stand alone player, it suffices. It has decent volume and clarity. Overall it is better than I expected sound wise.

The price on this little unit makes it very attractive to the person who wants to play the occasion LP and reminisce about the days of vinyl.

I have been through many carry-on bags over the years. Each of them seemed to have one or two things wrong with them; cheap zippers, small wheels, flimsy handles, poor balance, etc. This bag does not have any of these issues. The bag's general design is great with an easy to access top flap, thick well placed handles, and large durable zippers. The bag itself has a nice sturdy frame that could take a tumble down an escalator (heaven forbid). The bar handle has two lock out positions and is thick and well made. The bag rolls easily. Also, the balance is great. You can let it rest without any fear of it tipping over. Lastly, even with the high durability, this bag is comparably light weight.

Since this purchase I have bought other bags made by Travelpro and have been equally impressed with them. In this price range, you will not find a better bag.

I was one of the die hards who thought that Somewhere in Time and Powerslave were in a class untouchable by future Maiden albums.  I was wrong.  Seventh Son is exceptional.  The production quality is high, the lyrics are very good, the music is so strong but intricate and powerful.  Honestly, this album has no weak points.  If you don't own this album, I pity you.

Testament simply gets better with age. Dark Roots of Thrash is a nice sounding recording with a great set-list. I have seen testament live many times dating all the way back to 1989. They are a band which has gone through many line-up changes over the years but in my opinion, this is their best collection of musicians. The return of Alex Skolnick several years back and the more recent addition of drummer Gene Hoglan has created a "seasoned," super-group.

Testament has always been great live but as the years have passed a couple great things have happened to their live shows. First they have a lot of great albums to pull from when playing live. Second, these guys have become better musicians throughout the years. They are honestly at the top of their game. Third, I think they take it more seriously now...the party years are probably over and this makes for a great, professional, clean, yet fun (and very hard) show.

So, Dark Roots of Thrash has a lot going for it. It follows up an exceptional album, Dark Roots of Earth, and they also play some classics and even a few buried tracks throughout the set. The sound quality is certainly above average and the guys are definitely on the top of their game. Lastly, you get your money's worth with this disk. The set list is huge..19 tracks. This is definitely a "must own," live metal album.

I have been a FFDP fan since they were playing 200 person clubs 10 years ago. Their first 2 albums are masterpieces of hard driven yet soulful metal. So, they have a lot to live up to. It is kind of like hitting a grand slam your first 2 times at bat. It is hard to beat that.

However, this is a great album all the same. Its production value is extremely high. It sounds great at any volume. Jeremy Spencer is, as usual, on the top of his game and the rest of the band is tight. There is a little higher melodic value to the guitar lines which I liked. Sometimes FFDP has a tendency to sound mathematical on their riffs and solos. I am not complaining...they are great. But this album explores a little bit of a melodic side. However, one thing that completely stands out on this album is Ivan. This is his best album without question. In his other albums he has always been versatile and powerful and there has always been moments really showing off his melodic talent. Wrong Side of Heaven has a lot of those transitional vocal moments that really make you appreciate the talent of Ivan.

The title track is a little ballad-like and I am sure it was one of those tunes they expected to be on the radio...and it is. But Ivan is so good on that track that you really come to understand the range of his talent. Then they follow it up with "Burn MFer," and Ivan is back to his fist in the air, heavy, bad ass yet soulful self. It is just a really nice display of his versatility and power.

This is not as good as Way of the Fist, or War Is the Answer but it is still a "must own."

I have several vehicles and up here in the northern US, temperature changes are dramatic. Tires can lose 10lbs of pressure due to temperature change. I had some "high quality," analog gauges and I thought they worked well. However, I noticed a difference in their readings. I asked my mechanic the last time my car was in for service and he showed me how inaccurate these gauges can be. That is not the case with this little digital Tekton gauge.

It is extremely easy to use. You click the trigger to turn it on and pop it on the valve stem. There is a back-lit display that gives the reading. It is easy to read and easy to use. The gauge powers off after a few seconds to conserve battery power.

I love this little tool and I would certainly buy it again.

This is a good quality card and the price is great. The driver is fully supported by Windows 8/8.1 and the video speed is quite good. There are certainly better video cards out there but for a mid level card, you won't beat this price. I am very happy with it.

I bought the basket about 2 weeks ago and have used it half a dozen times. It heats up evenly and is perfect for vegetables.

The grill basket is great for grilling potatoes (pre boil or microwave them a bit), beats, sweet potatoes, etc. But fajita vegetables are simply awesome. Onions, bell peppers, and mushrooms grilled together in the basket is a king's meal and you don't need all that oil and fat. I could also see this basket being useful for grilling smaller meat cuts and shell fish. If you normally skewer shrimp for the grill, this basket could be a handy alternative to that method.

As you would expect with any piece of stainless steel, heat kind of dulls its finish a bit. I am not concerned with this because the basket is easy to clean...it simply will dull a bit after a few uses. One other thing to note, the little slits running through the basket can be sharp so be careful not to knick your finger on it.

Great product, great company, very happy.

I bought a case made by MoKo for a Microsoft Surface. It was pretty good quality so I tried them again when I moved to the Nokia 2520. The case is good looking, solid, durable, and functional. It is a well thought out item.

The case fits the Nokia like a glove. There are 4 little "cups," that fit around the corners of the tablet. Two are slightly shorter than the other two which makes removing the tablet fairly simple. The design of the case is pretty cool. Instead of having some sort of stand or fitting behind the device or a part of the case jutting out to hold the Nokia at an angle, you simply pull the tablet out of the two bottom claws. It then has several positions where the tablet fits snugly holding it at a desired angle. Even though you remove the bottom of the tablet from the claws, the Lumia still feels very secure.

The look of the case is fine. It is a faux leather look and is kind of nondescript. It looks professional and solid. I was not looking for a case to draw attention to the unit and this one looks just fine.

The case fits snugly around the tablet both when the cover is open or closed. There are no moving parts, hinges, etc with the case. It uses sturdy "leather," clasps to hold everything where it should be. The inside it a suede-like material that is soft and easy to clean.

The durability of the case is good. It is not going to help the Lumia if you drop it off of the roof, but it will keep scratches off of the screen and save you if you happen to bump it on the corner of the table. It is also water resistant so if you spill a little coffee on the front of the case, it will quickly and easily wipe off. The case is surprisingly light for its durability. It does not bulk up the tablet really at all.

Lastly, the case is a spot on match with all of the 2520's characteristics and features. You can use all of the tablet's functions; camera, ear buds, volume control, etc without having to remove the tablet from the case. It is well designed for the Lumia. A lot of other cases give you problems when you want to change out the memory card, take a picture, etc. this one fits like a glove.

I am very happy with the case. I would certainly recommend it.

I have a dog that is a ball fanatic...and a toy destroyer. She makes kongs look scared and weak. Her relentless drive to chase and chew makes it hard to buy toys for her. These balls hold up, are a good size to throw, and my dog loves them. Even when other toys have fallen into pieces at the hands of her mighty teeth (all 40lbs of her), these have held up. It is strange because they don't seem that tough but their shape and texture make it hard for her to get ahold of them so she just chews away on them without damage.

I have bought the chuck-it brand before and I loved it. I lost one of the balls in the snow at the park last year and never found it. So, with the intention of replacing it, I saw this 3 pack. The glow in the dark ball seemed like a good idea so I decided to buy the trio of balls. I am very happy I did.

These balls throw very well. They are the right weight that they travel a good distance without throwing out your arm. They bounce well and as an added perk, they make a little whistling noise in the air which helps my dog track them. I was a bit skeptical about the glow in the dark ball but it actually works quite well. If you leave it in the light for a little while, you will get quite a bit of glow out of it. It makes playing in the yard at night possible. My dogs both pick it up without a problem.

Let's say if they had an option for a 6 star dog toy, this would get that rating. Every time I lose one of these, I will replace it with another ChuckIt! ball.
