If you just want to know more about Mary Baker Eddy, this book really gives an inside look at the woman's life and work. "Retrospection and Introspection" (in Misc. Writings) is Mrs. Eddy's autobiography and is a great read.
This is a THICK book - well over 1,000 pages and it is stuffed full of practical wisdom, good information and specific instruction on how to pray more effectively.
I highly recommend this book, as well as Eddy's more well known book "Science & Health, with Key to the Scriptures".

This is one of the most intelligently written NDE (near death experience) books I've ever read. (And I've read a few...) Dannion's story was an amazing one and he told it very well.
It is a compelling book - I found  myself devouring the book cover to cover and then perusing it a second  time.
One of the most interesting things I picked up on in this book is  his experience of returning to this life.
He had been sent down to the  morgue, with a sheet draped over his body, when he came back to life.
And he talked about the moment of decision - whether to go back or to  remain in the next life - and once that decision was made, his body stirred  and he was alive again.
This (to me) was a wonderful proof that there is  no power in the body. It is not the body that makes decisions about life.  Dannion's body was dead but once he decided to return to (this) life, the  body was restored.
The human scene shifted to correspond with the  spiritual reality and the spiritual decisions.
Read the book and draw  your own inspirations, revelations and education. It was a great read and a  book with much depth.

I've used these Filtrete air filters for several years in different houses and I am very pleased with them. Yes, they are pricey but if you're prone to sneezing fits (as I am), they're worth every penny. Supposedly, the filter media is fine enough to capture even wee tiny particulate matter, including smoke and smog.

In addition to breathing easier and filtering out nasty smells from your house (which are huge benefits), I've noticed that using these filters also helps keep the house and tabletops cleaner, and there's less need for that dreaded chore of periodic dusting.

Another significant benefit is the benefit to your heating and cooling equipment. With a central air system costing thousands and thousands of dollars, this is not a small benefit! These high efficiency filters do a fine job of keeping dirt and dust out of the blower housing in your HVAC system. The traditional fiberglass filters (those cheap blue filters) keep small animals and yard waste from entering into your HVAC, but little else. Ever look at a 20-year-old blower housing? Usually they're caked with lots and lots of fine dust. In addition to being gross, that can't be good for an electrical appliance.

I highly recommend these Filtrete filters and I change mine more often than the manufacturer's 90-day recommended interval. And I think they're worth every penny of their hefty price tag.

Mrs. Eddy is one of the most interesting women in American history and you have to admire a woman who, during the Victorian era, in the thoroughly male-dominated field of healing, had the courage to stand up and say, "I've found a way to heal through prayer and I'd like to share what I've learned."

"Christian Healer" focuses on the spiritual development of Mrs. Eddy's healing work and talks about how Eddy came to write "Science and Health" (and revise it, too).

At a time when women didn't even the right to vote or the right to hold property (or many other basic rights), Mary Baker Eddy wrote a book and then self-published it. She then went door to door selling that book. And then she had to find more money to publish more books. But now, more than 130 years after the publication of that first edition, her originally self-published tome on spiritual healing has sold more than 10 million copies. Not too shabby. In the world of literary wonders, this is known as an "evergreen title" and it's every publishers dream come true.

"Christian Healer" does a fine job of documenting how Mrs. Eddy came to write Science and Health. And it's also a very inspiring read and reassures the rest of us that healing through prayer is a practical and effective means for healing "all the ills that flesh is heir to."

Prayer is finally coming into its own as a healing resource in mainstream 21st Century culture but you gotta love Mary Baker Eddy for taking this radical stand 130 years ago. And then devoting her life to producing a written work that would preserve and perpetuate her hard-won knowledge of spiritual healing.

I highly recommend this book and I promise, it's an inspiring and worthy read.

This is the FOURTH palm sander I've owned in my 48 years and this is the first one that I don't want to destroy with a sledge hammer. The paper-change feature on this one is a little bit of heaven. It's easy, it's quick and you won't pinch your delicate lady fingers (or worse). The little red button on the front is what makes it sweet and good. Press that button and the sandpaper slides in easily. On the back, the paper is threaded through a little lever. I love this feature. Oh mercy, do I love this feature.

The dust-catcher does a decent job of trapping sawdust but as often as not, I use it without the rear-bagger dealie.

The other super-nice feature: It is not painful to sand with this sander. Most other sanders vibrate my hands, wrist and arm so bad that it is quite painful and unpleasant. I don't know how they did it, but this sander is almost vibration free.

Speaking as a woman who has sanded about 12 billion board feet of lumber, this is the best palm sander I've seen on the market. I'm very impressed.

When I watched this VHS movie for the first time, I wasn't expecting much.  I very nearly turned it off because the first 15 minutes were boring and slow.  But once they got past the yada, yada, yada and into this woman's life story, it was completely enthralling.
I watched it a second time with the family, fast forwarding past the boring introduction.  The fam also found it very interesting.
The movie is kind of a docu-drama, recreated from the detailed diary of a 1780's midwife.  The details about life back then are just beyond description.
One tidbit - premarital sex wasn't the scandal that we'd expect in those times.  However, a woman would be asked, in the throes on intense labor, to name the father of the baby.  The woman's testimony during these intense moments was considered solid and incontrovertible.  If the baby's father refused to marry the woman, THAT was scandalous.
This movie was filled with those kind of details.  I can't recommend this VHS-tape enough.  One of the best movies I think I've ever seen.

I bought the book while rebuilding the front porch and columns on my 1904 home. It *is* a lot easier to take something apart if you know how it was put together. And we needed to re-create mouldings and millwork that was  destroyed by previous property owners. This book shows how the "old  masters" built these old houses.

I'm an old house purist. And this  book has nearly 200 pages of detailed blue prints and drawings, giving  excellent detail on how old buildings were assembled.  (primarily  residences) It satisfied that craving [us] purists get to make something  the way it was made 100 years ago.

The drawings enabled us to *truly*  restore the beautiful details of our old home.

The book has very *very*  few words, but lots and lots of blueprints and drawings.

Rose
author, California's Kit Homes

users.query: Who would have thought a warren of bunnies would draw me in?  I bought it on recommendation for my daughter, and just to be nosy, I started reading it. The writing style is excellent, and the plot drew me in. Needless to say, I'm not giving it to my daughter as a gift, because it now has "experience". Rabbits...go figure.

cands.text: I didn't read it. My mother did. As one who lived through that era in Germany, it was beautifully written, thought provoking, and a page turner. I'd like to say she gave it to me to read after she finished, but somehow she forgot it was mine. It's making its way around the neighborhood right now.

I took a risk and ordered adult coloring books as Advent Calendar stuffers.  They all are artistic and all loved coloring as kids, but two are in their 20s, and two are teens.  They LOVED THEM!!!  This was a gift to my 14-year-old, and she carries it in her backpack and brings it to school, working on it in lunch time and study hall.  Two of her friends have asked for them for birthday presents, and I am using these as designs for my stained glass windows.  I will be ordering more adult coloring books!

My daughter is an artist...an AMAZING artist. I learned this as I looked through her lined notebook homework, and every other page was a doodle or a drawing. Her art teacher told me to get her a real sketch pad so we didn't have to look at Facebook postings with blue lines and holes. I did. She now saves her best work for this tablet. It's heavier paper, absorbs some of her dryer water color paintings, and it doesn't bleed. She still doodles in her homework pad, but it beats homework.

I read this book solely on the recommendation from an unknown reviewer that it was "one of the scariest books ever written". I started reading it, and within a few pages, I was intrigued. I kept that feeling up to and just into the middle of the story, waiting for something to evolve to make it fantastic. Then it went flat. Based on the others' reviews, I'm guessing there was a connection that flittered by me. There lacked supreme descriptions to draw these bits into one ensemble of a plot. I felt him walking down the path, then treading into another time warp. But the events of that last day just fractured into recitation. I felt no fear. I felt no compulsion to purchase the second book. I had no idea why this was rated as one of the scariest. I was nonplussed.

To say that my German Wirehair loves these treats is an understatement. She obsesses over them. She stalks them. I think she has learned to read the bag, because no matter where I put this bag, she finds it. And then she stares. And points. And if you don't see her stare and point, she comes over to you and nudges your arm, walking over to the bag and looking over her shoulder to ensure you see where her attention is directed. And I think she knows I'm old and forgetful, because even if I JUST GAVE her one of these, she walks back to the bag, hoping I don't remember doing just that. And if I hold it in my hand and make her sit, she will, but the whole time she's doing it, copious amounts of drool are pooling on the floor beneath her. Oh, and I'm not exaggerating at all. I made the mistake of running out, and she helped herself to the empty bag in the trash can, shredding it and licking, yes licking, every part of the interior. I have a feeling I could follow her as she does her morning constitutional and find bits of the bag. She loves them. That. Much. She does not behave this way with people food. Just EOS Dog treats. Go figure.

My daughter has always been interested in animal rehabilitation.  This book caught her eye, but before she could buy it from Wal-Mart, they stopped carrying it.  I got lucky and found it on Amazon, and before Christmas day was over, she had her nose buried in it.  She came down red eyed a couple times but stressed the book was good.  I read it afterwards, and I found the story heartwarming.  The only knock in stars comes from the fact that it is a fast read.

This little stuffed animal was affordable, and my daughter wanted it badly. It arrived on time, but I was disappointed that the manufacturer didn't take better care in stitching it. One of the ears is cocked. My daughter loves the look, so she's happy. But if you have a sewing snob who has a hankering for this flying cat thing, he or she might be disappointed. Still, it was very affordable.

My daughter, 13, pushed me to read the Gary Paulsen books. I did, and I found them moderately enjoyable. They are a fast read for an adult, and I find them to be definitely designed for the lower attention span teenagers. They were good stories, but it seemed to me the author got tired of writing these books and ... just put The End on it. Each story has detail, then just quits. I would recommend it for boys, for teens, and for someone who can't get into a thousand page story.

I bought these for my nephews to take HOME, because I knew it would be a waterworld in my bathroom if they kept them here.  They LOVE them (except the one the dog snatched...he bit off the tail, so the squirter doesn't work anymore), but my sister told me she plans on seeking revenge.  Great value!

But I remembered it to be far better than it really was.  Okay, so I was a teen when I saw the movie and read the book. I'm old and I forgot it. Now?  Meh.  It's not horrible; it's just not great.  My mother and I discussed it after she finished it, and we agreed the biggest problem with the story was that we didn't really like any of the characters.  Patrick was okay but favored the boys. Mama was selfish and miserable because she didn't get to marry the man she really loved, so she made everybody else pay.  Auntie is just all about money. Meggie's oldest brother has anger management issues. Meggie's husband was a jerk. Ralph cheated on God. Meggie's kids weren't special, either.  Her daughter was a crude actress who happened to stumble on a nice guy, but instead of landing him, she toyed with him. These characters might be fiction, but our theory is that Ms McCullough believed she evolved these characters to be admirable. We didn't agree. The only one who was true to herself was Auntie Evil. She knew she was rotten to the core and reveled in it.

The pictures are amazing, but all the shading is done for you. Many of the drawings are pre-shaded, leaving you little option to add your own coloring.  Of all the adult coloring books I've owned, this is my least favorite, and I love Degas' work.
I didn't buy it. My daughter did. I think it's ridiculous, but she's nuts about it. Go figure.

This game is fun, and it as about as inappropriate as a game can get. It's partly about the luck of the draw, but it also allows for that creative spin on what card or cards you toss together to draw the most attention. I will say that we've played this maybe a dozen times, and it's not the go-to game like it used to be. I've heard expansion packs go a long way, but if we lose interest after ten games or so, I'm not sure I'd buy them, either. If you've never played it before and you're not easily offended, buy it. If you have thin skin or a strong sense of propriety, buy some other game.

I was surprised at how much they packed into this book.  The examples, steps and instructions are very well done, but I have another series of how-to-draw books, one of which is for trees, and it has more than twice the pages in it with the same amount of information on each page.  The author is a very talented artist, but I wish the book were twice as thick.

Well, not complete, but this was definitely pictorial. The high contrast in their decorations allowed for ease in seeing how they were put together, but the information was more basic and less comprehensive. Still, it makes a good book for a beginner, so overall I'd recommend it.

This is a great movie based on a true story, and I really, really loved it. I only gave it four stars, though, because I was bothered by Gere's wife's giving the dog away when she moved. I would never hand my beloved puppy to anybody else.

I hope I didn't give it away, but the movie is really a great one to watch!

These are really cute place mats, with lots of attention to detail spent on the bunny faces. I read a couple reviews which suggested hand washing them and laying them flat, so I did. They look great, but they do require ironing after washing them.

All four of my daughters bawled in this movie, including the one who rolls her eyes when I tell her it's time we watch a chick flick.  I won't play spoiler and tell you why they cried, but the plot is excellent, the acting is outstanding, and the people they've chosen aren't all perfect.  Highly recommend this movie!

It's a Ravensburger, which is synonymous with excellent quality. I chose this puzzle for my father because he thinks he's so smart. I figured the mass amount of reds would hinder his solution time. But NOOOOOOO!!! Ravensburger's reds fade into distinct shades and hues, and they match the pony perfectly. It took him two afternoons to complete.  The NEXT puzzle I buy him will be in the thousands...!!!

The book is large in size but extremely thin.  The instructions do not show step-by-step methods to draw the flowers, but it does depict the flower with all its detail, including shading and texture.  The book is the one bearing the fewest pages and fewest examples of all my art books.  If there were maybe ten more pages, I'd give it four or five stars.

My dad lives in a heavily wooded area on a lake about 50 miles from the network stations. He got fed up with the Dish Network and DirecTV games of jacking prices all over the place, loading up the channels with commercials, and nickel and diming customers on equipment, so he gave them the boot. He was worried, because he had two channels of entertainment, at best, before satellite TV. He used his old antenna, this CM 7777, and a smart LED TV, and he received 28 channels with excellent reception. It took about an hour to install, including the mast, but he was watching the evening news that day. If only it were as easy to cancel satellite TV as it was to install the Titan... [:-(

I bought this as a black Friday special, and the savings was amazing! I figured it was grossly overpriced normally, so the BF savings was only nominal. Au contraire. I've looked for this same one in other places and find it just slightly less than Amazon. I WISH WISH WISH I could have purchased four or more of these at that price, because we use it in our garage to categorize tools...flooring, drywall, electric, plumbing, etc.,...and they are very garage-durable. LOVE them!!

Sooooo glad I bought these for my daughter, because somebody else did, too, and now I get to call them my own! The wide variety of darkness is transferred beautifully to my drawing. The medium is centered beautifully in the pencil, so sharpening doesn't cause a lot of breakage. The package snaps back together well, so you can use it again and again without losing your pencils.

This product arrived early and in excellent condition.  However, I'm a moron and didn't read the size of 5x7.  The binding on the book is tight, which is a good thing because it'll withstand numerous times of being opened and closed, and is a bad thing because you can't get all the way into the middle of the book to write.  That being said, it's winter in Minnesota, and everything is stiff.  Large handed writers might have a tough time using this.

users.query: This is basically Saving Private Ryan stretched out over 10 episodes.  The acting, special effects, and most everything else is nearly identical.  This is top-tier and it must have cost a fortune to produce.

cands.text: This is basically Saving Private Ryan stretched out over 10 episodes.  The acting, special effects, and most everything else is nearly identical.  This is top-tier and it must have cost a fortune to produce.

This was a great buy.  I just picked up a used Toyota with two working but really beat up key FOBs.  Spending less than $20 for a pair was so much better than $200 for new FOBs plus programming.  The look and fit was just like the OEM models.  No modifications needed for the guts of my old FOBs.
2 hours of your life you won't get back. There's hardly a plot. This is mostly the female lead running around an alien world fighting with the natives.

The cable is a little stiff and bulky compared to some other HDMI cables I have but seems to work just fine. This was purchased to move a Roku stick from the back of my TV to the site/front to cure some connection issues.  This worked much better than the 4" cable that I got free from Roku.

So far, a nice heavy duty cable.  This was much nicer than buying the charger since I can plug it into any of the dozens of USB chargers we own, including the car.  This should be included with the 3DS!!

This was a stocking stuffer for the TV in the bedroom.  Our Samsung blueray has similar functionality but was starting to get buggy.

It works well and I like the direct Netflix button since that's what we use about 95% of the time.  I originally had it plugged straight into the rear HDMI port and it seemed to struggle/buffer much more than it should to start a program.  Some research showed this might be caused by the TV blocking some of the signal from the wireless router (the screen is between the two).  I picked up an HDMI extension cable and moved the roku stick to the top edge facing the router.  This seemed to cure most of the buffering issue.

My biggest gripe is that the unit gets surprisingly hot.  I originally had it plugged into the AC adapter so I wouldn't have to wait for the unit to boot up when we turned on the TV.  A relatively bright LED shone on the wall that bugged my wife at night and the unit was very hot to the touch.  Now the unit pulls power from a USB plugged into the TV instead.

The interface will automatically start playing the next few shows in a series without user input.  The wife really likes that since she watches TV to "fall asleep" to.  By setting the sleep timer it turns off the Roku and breaks the connection.  When we turn it back on we can resume the show where it left off.

Killer sale price.  I'm not sure when I'll get a chance to try them.  Several of the entrees are actually supposed to feed 3 (strange number).  These are going into our hurricane evacuation kit in the closet,  Other than MRE's this was about the best deal I could find on some long term food storage.  Just boil water and you're eating in about 10 minutes.
Kind of pricey but you get what you pay for.  This keeps the junk my kids track into the back from getting ground into the carpet.

So far the quality seems to be great.  I injected some synthetic grease through the included fitting and the sheave turns freely under load.  I've only used this to pull some shrubs out of the front yard and for a double line pull to pre-tension the winch line.  The sheave pulley is nice and smooth so it should be fine for my synthetic rope.  I recently got one of the TGL recovery straps and was very pleased with the quality so I decided to give this a try.  I'm not disappointed.

FYI...The specs on this knife aren't exactly right.  The weight and other specifics provided indicate it's the LST (weight 1.2 oz) but no length is provided.  When it arrived I realized it's the Ultralight LST (about half the size).  The price difference is pretty slight between the two but I've had an LST for years and it's been sharpened away to a nub.  I thought for under 7 bucks this was a great time to get a replacement.  I was very disappointed when I opened the box to reveal the Ultralight model.  Return shipping is about half what I paid for the knife so I might as well just hang onto it.

The flow rate on the mini and the capacity are significantly less than with the normal Sawyer Squeeze.  Even with these limitations, the mini is significantly lighter and more compact.  I actually bought 2, one for camping and the other to include in my evacuation kit.

Having the tubing connection no the input in addition to being able to thread it onto a bottle is a nice touch if you want to rig up some kind of inline filter setup.  I would prefer though to also have a threaded female connection on the output side so you could attach it to a water bottle directly.  The squeeze now sells an adapter for this purpose but it won't work on the Mini.

The bags are definitely the Achilles heel of this system.  They're easy to puncture or even "pop" if you squeeze too hard.  It's much better to just hang the system, add some tubing to the outlet side, and make a gravity setup.

This works well but it seems to get really hot while it's operating.  You can power this stick by plugging the cord into a spare USB port on your TV or by using the included power supply.  I'd recommend using the USB.  I originally had it plugged into the power supply and as I mentioned it runs hot.  I figure this can't be good for it and that's just a waste of power.  You do have to wait about 30 seconds for it to boot up when you apply power but that's no big deal.

You can get a HDMI extension cable from Roku if you happen to have your TV wall mounted and your HDMI ports are on the back.  It took an e-mail and waiting about a week for it to show up.  I don't know why they just don't include this with all of them.
All indications I have is this is OEM quality for significantly less money.  What's not to like
OEM filter for far less than the dealership price.  What's not to like.

It seems to move less air than the size and noise would indicate.  Battery life is surprisingly good but it seems this fan needs a more efficient blade design.  This really hit the spot when trying to backpack in hot weather.
This knife went back after about 2 days.  Right out of the box it was dull and stiff.  It was nearly impossible to open one handed with either hand.  For the money I expected much more.

So far so good.  I wasn't counting on the difference in size between this battery and the old one.  I guess the "9-cell" description should have clued me in.  The pack has an added "hump" that extends the length of the unit to house the extra cells.  There are a couple of small rubber tabs/feet on the pack as well. The extension lifts the back of the laptop up perhaps 3/4" into a somewhat more natural typing angle.  It also holds the bottom of the laptop off the desk surface, increasing airflow to the cooling fans.  Therefore, in addition to some much needed new battery life, it also aids cooling.

No idea on longevity and it's hard to compare since my old battery had totally failed (0% charging).  I'll update the review if I have any new revelations or catastrophic failures.

This knife is greatly improved over the Bushlore from a few years ago.  The blade is now 1/8" thick with a scandi grind.  It's relatively dull out of the box but a few minutes with some fine paper and buffer will have it hair-popping sharp quickly.  Putting a slight convex to the edge will ensure a more durable blade for hard use.  The carbon steel will rust if left in the sheath but a bit of oil and proper storage will keep it nice looking.

The sheath is beautiful and likely worth as much as you pay for the pair.  Unfortunately I'm a lefty so the sheath isn't really useful for me but still well made.  The slab handle was a bit rough out of the box and left some exposed tang metal in spots.  A bit of work on the belt sander took care of those issues.

Watch some of the youtube videos where they put this knife up against some much more expensive bushcraft models.  Overall, the carbon steel is pretty soft and will chip/nick with hard use.  However, it's easy to resharpen when needed.  Overall, this is a great knife to start out with.  You can abuse it and not be too upset because of the low price.  This 90% solution gives you the base materials to create a very nice bushcraft blade on the cheap with just a bit of work.  You can slice some vegetables, whittle a tent stake, and baton some kindling from wrist sided wood...all with the same blade.

This pad takes quite a bit of huffing and puffing to inflate (maybe 10 or 11 breaths) but is surprisingly comfortable.  The material seems very light and fragile but I've been careful so far (2 uses) and no punctures.  It packs down very small and works well both on the tent floor, a cot, or in the sleeve of a double-layer hammock.

The valve seems to stick out much farther than needed and the "lock" is kind of a silly feature.  I'm afraid this is going to lead to some future damage but only time will tell.

The accord is a staple of american sedans for popularity and reliability.  This model is no different except for a limited span (06/07) they decided to make this slightly sportier version.  The 244HP V6 coupled to the 6spd manual transmission makes this grocery getter much closer in performance to the Acura CL/TL since they share much of the same drivetrain.

The interior amenities on the EX version are great.  Road noise is a bit higher than on previous accords I've owned but that's mostly due to the 50series tires and stiffer suspension.  Overall the engine is nearly inaudible over the stereo even at moderate volumes which makes shifting sometimes a bit challenging.

Like all Hondas I've owned, everything just works.  This 10yr old car has no creaks, rattles, clunks to speak of.  The interior is almost pristine with the exception of the driver's carpet mat that shows a divot from the right heel.  The leather seats and trim look like new after a bit of scrubbing with some conditioner as well as the steering wheel.

My only gripe is the steering wheel.  I would have much preferred the radio controls be located more at the 7 o'clock location like on my Toyotas rather than at the 9 o'clock as they are now.  I normally hold the wheel at this lower location so I have to shuffle my hands back and forth to change the radio settings.  The cruise control buttons are opposite at the 3 o'clock and it would be nice if they were lower on the wheel too.

I got the large for my 65-pound dog and that seems to be a good match.  It took a while to get her interested but after that she loves it.  Assembling it solo is kind of a pain trying to get the screws started in the corners while trying to pull the fabric into position.

The size listed is overall and not just the bed surface.  I was concerned that the claws would snag the fabric and quickly destroy the bed once I saw it was somewhat of an open weave.  So far so good.  My dog jumps on the bed and chews on toys but I don't see any loose threads or other damage.

I bought this for an indel-b 51L fridge and it fits great.  The only problem is the control panel is on the same end as the cooler so the lid obscures the control.  This isn't a big deal since I leave the unit running and rarely change the temperature.  I would like it if the insulation were thicker so I may augment it by adding some additional foam between the fridge and this cover.

I'd prefer an optional color rather than black (my truck has grey interior).  I believe a lighter color might aborb less heat when the unit is in the sun.  Some other reviews indicated the velcro tabs on the lid ripped off but so far I haven't had that issue.  I intentionally don't "seal" the lid by pressing the velcro together.  I might remove or cover those velcro tabs entirely.

There are rubber feet on the bottom that more or less line up with the feet on the cooler.  Unfortunately they're rectangular and the cooler feet are round.  Therefore, they don't exactly sit well into the fridge slider I bought to go with this setup (literally the square peg and round hole).

The cover came with a bundle of straps with clips on one end.  They're intended secure the unit in place for transit but there were no instructions.  The d-rings on the case seem to be a very silly place to try and secure the cooler as opposed to the handles.  Overall, this is a good case for less than half the price of others for the same cooler.  I haven't measured it yet but you can quickly tell the cover adds significant insulation to the setup.  The compressor runs less often and you don't feel the cold leaking from the sides of the unit.

It's tiny and weighs practically nothing.  You can carry this as a primary stove for day hikes or backpacking or even keep it in your gear as a spare.  The pot stand is pretty small so don't expect to balance a huge frypan on there.  Small mug sized cookpots work just fine.  The flame pattern makes a small spot so it's great for a quick boil with small pots.  The flame control allows for simmering but the small pattern means you might still scorch dinner with thin titanium and aluminum pots.

Some reviewers complain that the neck where it connects to the fuel canister gets hot.  I haven't found this to be an issue when boiling a single pot of water.  The small mass means it cools off within just a minute or two after shutoff.

Overall, this isn't a stove for heavy duty group use.  However, for boiling water for a solo meal or hot drink it's fantastic.
Fastest/easiest way to extend the differential breather on my Toyota.  The threads screw right into the housing and makes it easy to connect a section of hose.  Not much else to say on this product.

users.query:
I love this book.  At first I felt a bit overwhelmed when I cracked it open and saw all that was going on in there, but I've come to really enjoy it.

It's not a complete reference for any of these topics, but does have a nice selection for each.  The patterns and recipes are fun and well explained.  I would recommend this book for someone who already does  most of these or for someone wanting to try out several different crafts before choosing a new hobby as the basics are also explained.

cands.text:
This book turned out to be just what I was looking for.  After browsing through many books of this type and reading reviews about how the patterns were difficult or the projects were all made on one pattern, I felt nervous about what I might get, but I can say now that I am quite relieved and have no regrets about buying this book.

To let you know what is inside:

Clothing:  There is one knitting pattern for a nice sweater vest (adorable!)... Sewing patterns for a raincoat, leather vest, winter coat, paw socks, bathrobe (shown on cover), sweatshirt with hoody, a dress, and a jump/pajama suit.

Accessories: Directions for making a very practical nylon/chain collar and matching single or double dog lead, collapsible food/water bowls, equipment bag (grooming, roll style bag), fancy shirt collar, reflective collar, 2 different harnesses, bandana, backpack (for the dog),  waterproof napping bag for hunting/sport dogs (not at all useful for my 5 lb Maltese, but maybe for someone else), lining for a wicker style dog bed, lining for a bicycle basket, and a cover for a metal dog cage. Also has a cool pattern for a human padded belt with a hook for a flexi lead to be used when skiing, hiking, etc. Not sure how this would work, but I might make it to use for walking in the mountains.

The directions are all in the fairly simple difficulty range in my opinion; certainly something for everyone.  Most patterns can be made using stuff I already have on hand as well, which is much appreciated.  One other good thing is that I can use the same waterproof material to make a raincoat, water bowl, and backpack.  All in all, I am very happy with this book.

This book is part of one of my favorite series.  It is 385 pages of smaller-than-normal print, and yet I couldn't put this series down.  It is very well-written and has a good mix of emotions flowing throughout the book.

On a side note, I would recommend this series for an audience above 16 years of age.  The main character is a woman who marries a stranger 'out west' around civil war times only to realize the man is very abusive and heartless.  She finds her way to happiness and salvation, but it is a rough road and I would not recommend this book for the younger teen crowd.

Overall I enjoyed it and will keep this set and will enjoy re-reading it through the years.
I enjoyed this book so much! It has everything a good book should have... suspense, and lots of humor and romance.  Really enjoyable book!
This book was different than the typical plot.  It kept my attention until the very end at which point I ordered two other books by this author.  Really cute enjoyable read!

Good wholesome book, good moral to the story, entertaining to read.  The secret occupation of the main character puts a fun twist to the book, and her decisions that she has to make keep the book moving.

If you are looking for something profound that will tug on your brain or heart, this isn't it.  If you are looking for an enjoyable way to pass some time, this is much better than most of what passes for entertainment today.

For what it is, a light Christian romance, Love on a Dime is a good choice.

Overall, this is a good book.  My one complaint:  There are so many pieces of baggage from the heroine's past that it gets a little overwhelming at times.  Eventually though, Jade turns all of the problems one by one over to God and finds closure and healing.

The dialog is clean, the plot makes sense, and the characters are true to their roles.  Other than a little too much drama in the middle of the story, this is a good read.

New to gluten-free eating, I've bought more than 10 gluten free cookbooks and tried recipes from blogs and online collections that have mostly NOT been anything I wanted to choke down.  This book is a breath of fresh air compared to the gluten free bookshelf in my house! Really great for anyone on a paleo/primal style diet as well.

I bought this book on a whim based on Amazon's suggestion along with positive reviews and got a pleasant surprise when I tried the first recipe for coconut bread in the quick recipes section. While a bit more dense than regular bread, it has a pleasant neutral flavor that went well with fruit as well as with meat. Add to this success the fact that I did not have to labor for hours, but for all of about 5 minutes of prep time before popping it in the oven -- this is something even my little brother could do.

Next was banana bread (which was even better than the coconut bread), coconut cookies (amazing), ham and cheese muffins (more like omelettes than muffins, but still good), and then apple pie (great recipe for the filling too!).

This book is not for someone who wants to avoid eggs as I didn't yet read any recipe without eggs. The recipes I've tried so far have been very adaptable -- e.g. using cow's milk or coconut milk. For most of them I think you can use coconut oil in place of butter.  Many of the recipes give alternates for less sugar (or using stevia, honey, etc). I've already recommended this to a few of my friends who are also new at finding alternatives to wheat and plan to buy more books from this author.

I am not normally interested in devotional inspirational books, preferring to read Christian fiction.  However, I really enjoyed the highly readable little book by Squire Rushnell, and the more I read of it, the more I liked it.

The format is based on true short stories of encouragement, interspersed with brief explanations of how to deal with various new ventures any person might face.  The stories are of well-known as well as lesser-known people facing the obstacles that are common when choosing a career path, reacting to life changes such as job loss or sickness, as well as more short-term decisions.  The premise is that when you are trying to decide which way to go, there are little signs that God puts in your path to show that you are on the right trail.  For the most part, these are not big miracles, but a series of small miracles and what some would call coincidences that lead us toward the direction we should take.

Rushnell has written an easy to read and uplifting book of encouragement and hope to help the reader find their way during times of change and decision making. It is very ecumenical in nature, referring to God all through the book, but leaving the interpretation of who that God is to the reader.  Christian, Jew, Muslim, or Buddhist, all could find this little book a worthwhile read.

I absolutely ADORED reading this book until (almost) the end.  It was fun, witty, down-to-earth, and upbeat all the way throughout the story and I did not miss for one second the drama or nail-biting worries about how the book would come together in the end.  It was well written throughout (almost) the entire book.

One pet peeve that really disappointed me (because it put a damper on the happy ending) is that the Italian hero of the book called the lead character a 'bello woman' right at the end of the book.  The author translated this as beautiful woman.  Now, call me nit picky, but this really bugged me just because it was the only word of Italian in the book and it was wrong.  Unless the lead female character was secretly a man, the word should have been the feminine version 'bella' which actually just means 'nice' or 'cute'.  If she meant to call her 'beautiful' instead, the correct translation is 'bellissima'.  If the book goes to reprint I hope that they fix this little detail.

As much as that little detail irritated ME, I don't think it's a deal breaker and I would definitely recommend this book to anyone looking for a light and happy read.  I will purchase other books by this author (and hope that she stays away from foreign languages or gets a translator from here on out!).  :)

This book successfully combines a number of book types into one highly readable and enjoyable story.  A murder mystery, set in the Wild West, with a main character of mixed heritage, a strong Christian theme, that also has a romance and a LOT of adventure and suspense - what more could you ask for?

The many different threads are woven together into a believable plot, and the characters are portrayed as people I could care about and identify with.

The only reason I am giving this a 4 instead of a 5 is that the separation of church and state issue was treated with a modern political viewpoint instead of that of the 1800's.  Not only was the separation of church and state discussion unnecessary to the story line, but it was inaccurate for the time period.  This is an easy mistake to make in today's political climate, but I have read a number of this author's books and was disappointed that this point was not researched better.

For those who don't know the what the Constitution says, the wording is "Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof."  No restrictions are placed on religions except perhaps that a religious denomination cannot become the state religion. The current re-interpretation of this clause did not come into vogue until used by the ACLU in the mid-1900's.

The trumped up charges leading to the church election against the sherriff stemmed from prejudice and hatred.  That could have been made clear without trying to espouse political viewpoints from a century later.

In every other way though, this was a quality book that was well worth the time invested to read.

I found this book to be just what I was looking for to learn Italian home cooking.  I have some of the other 'Spoon' series in Italian and anticipate their translation into English.  This series is easy to use and authentic... One truly preferred by Italians.  I highly recommended it to anyone interested in making true Italian food.

Firstly, this is the first recipe software that I've had the pleasure to try. I didn't pay a lot for it as I snagged it on Groupon for $20. I'm a housewife and home user, not a pro user.  But I LOVED it.  Here's why:

*Better than Pinterest for collecting recipes from around the web.  The capture feature snags them and saves them in my recipe box, letting me print them to recipe cards or add them to my shopping list and meal plans. This feature worked on an Italian site as well as English so language doesn't seem to be an issue.

*Gives me nutritional information for my recipes (very handy as I'm trying to drop a few pounds) and adjust recipes for different number of servings.

*Various cookbooks are available as in-app purchases that import the recipes directly into your recipe list.

*Most importantly, this software is super easy to learn/use and a snap to set up.  The only snag I had (for which I took off one star) was installing on Mac. At the first installation, the software wouldn't open after installing and had to be uninstalled, reinstalled, and then closed and opened a few times before the bugs worked themselves out. I have been using it for awhile now and it hasn't had that problem again.

*One other cool thing I think is worth a mention is that mobile apps are coming soon (for iphone and ipad so far, I believe - hopefully others soon).

As a serial cookbook and recipe collector, this software has been just what I needed to keep my kitchen in order and help keep my favorite recipes all in one place.  I'm sure we're going to be friends for many years to come. If you can get a copy of Cook'n for a fair price, I'd recommend it!

First the good, then the bad and the ugly.  I enjoyed reading this book about a diabetic Southern cake baker and her career success that brings romance into her life.  I would call this book cute, funny, sweet, and the story told in a comfortable easy-going-down kind of way (much like cake, yum!).  Between each chapter I enjoyed the recipes, facts, and tidbits related to the story itself. For this I've rated the book 4 stars.

Now, the annoying part for which I left off that last star. One of the minor characters in the book is supposedly Italian.  However, the author seems to have used an online translation service, as most of the so-called Italian script makes no sense at all.  At one point I believe the character intends to say he is finished with the conversation but it translates to mean he is no-more (dead).  In another place, one of the end-of-chapter excerpts the author offers "Important Translations for the Savvy Hotel Owner" in Italian and French (the two official languages in our hometown) which had my husband and I scratching our heads.  *climbing on soapbox*  Even in fiction, good research makes good stories.  Research, people!! *hopping off soapbox with a shrug* Sandra, if you're out there and reading this, I loved the story, and look forward to reading more from you, but wish you had used a real translator for the Italian bit. I offer my own services free of charge if you will just let me fix this little detail.

If you don't speak Italian or French and are just in the market for a nice relaxing book, go for this one! The recipes will tempt you, the characters will make you smile and even laugh, and you will close the last page running right back here to look for other stories from this author.

I almost gave up on reading this book at the beginning, but it goes from one star to three if you hold on long enough.  To be fair, I was reading the uncorrected proof, so perhaps some major clean up and overhaul will happen before publication.

The introduction begins as an unfocused rant against the dishonest and superficial practices of the corporate culture. Since I work in an open and honest office, and since my life is too busy to read the ramblings of a stranger with whom I don't identify, this was a pretty annoying way to start.  Throw in some unnecessarily crude language and disparaging remarks about Fox News (which I happen to like), and the first 30 pages made the task of reading this book look pretty dismal.

However, there are some useful observations and exercises in this book, especially if you are caught in an unhappy office environment over which you have some control over the changes that need to be made.  I do agree with the author about the need for open and honest communication, and the need to build trust among co-workers and customers.  This book has some good insight into how to accomplish these goals in a number of innovative ways, some of which can be implemented from middle management or below, at least in creating a sane zone in your immediate work area.

I just have two suggestions:  One to author Susan Scott, sharpen your focus and perhaps clean up the format of the book to allow for more concise comprehension of the subject matter (maybe use better subtitles and bullets?)  The other to readers, to hang on or skim through the muddy parts, as there are some good lessons hidden as you go further.

This book is fabulous!  It's a great choice for anyone wanting to make a change in their diets and not sure what direction to go.

For me personally, I was able to take the information in this book and tailor it to my body specifically - as we are all different.  The green smoothies give me a burst of energy and I'm feeling better than I've felt in a long time.  I don't plan on becoming a vegetarian, but eating enough raw vegetables and getting the right foods can not only beautify us outside, but help our bodies to heal themselves inside.  Pick up this book.  Even if you can only do part of this diet, you'll not regret it!

Fans of Lisa Tawn Bergren's other books will enjoy the fast paced action in this first of a new trilogy set in 1883 Colorado Springs.  Like her earlier books, every page has the characters in constant action.  The plot is out of the ordinary, primarily set in a sanatorium for consumptives (tuberculosis patients) rather than the typical "nice girl meets nice boy in normal life" scenario.

The title 'Breathe' has a double meaning:  The main character must regain her health and learn to breathe freely again physically.  Secondarily, the main character and her brother and sister must take a chance to break out of the expectations of family and society and learn to breathe free, to follow the goals of their own hearts.

The three face multiple challenges, one fighting a deadly disease, another fighting unwanted romantic attention, and the third literally fighting in a boxing ring, all against the backdrop of a newly settled western frontier.  Somehow Lisa Bergren manages to weave all of these plots and subplots into a believable and entertaining story.  From the first scenes of the book to suspicious murders to silver mine claims to mountain chase scenes to the suspenseful ending, this book has an energy that keeps the pages turning.

The author never uses any crude language and everyone keeps their clothes on.  And while the dangers that are faced elicit prayers for safety and strength and faith, the book doesn't lapse into preaching. The setting is different and interesting and well researched by the author, who herself lives in Colorado Springs.  If you are looking for a good clean mystery with a touch of romance, I highly recommend this book.

The plot in this book is an interesting premise, giving a few unexpected twists and turns as the mystery unfolds.  Unfortunately, that is about the only good thing I can say about the book.  The characters are pretty one-dimensional, and their decisions are shallow and impulsive.  The story lurches along at an erratic rate, sometimes too fast and sometimes without full plot development or even explanation.  The romance is too sudden and easy.  The surprises are not foreshadowed at all and often out of character for the people as they are described.  Sorry to say that the Lightkeepers Daughter is pretty disappointing.

A different type of protagonist than I usually read, but this made the story more interesting, not less.  I appreciated the insights into the robe that Jesus wore, as well as good descriptions of the areas visited.  There were some religious aspects of the book, but it didn't feel preachy.

Robin Jones Gunn has been one of my favorite authors for the past 20 years.  The Glenbrooke series has a place on my bookshelf even after most of my other books are now digital.  But this book is different.  It gets real and personal.

If you're looking for a book for yourself or someone you care about who is maybe going through a rough patch... this book is very inspiring and uplifting.  I recommend this, as I would all of RJG's books.

For anyone who feels helpless to make their mark on the world or who just needs a bit of cheering up, this is a lovely book that should be just the thing.  It is a series of true short stories of generous acts.that changed lives.  Very thought provoking and uplifting!

This honey is the richest and best-tasting honey I've ever tasted.  In small amounts, it's quite satisfying.

Taste is only a part of what makes this honey so amazing though.  Used on the face it helps even skin tone. Used on scars, it helps to even them out and fade them.  On cuts it works as a natural anti-septic.  My jar is good until 2016 and because it'll be long gone at my house by then, I plan to start keeping this on hand from now on.  Very impressed.

This helped my kitties to feel calm through 18 hours of flying to their new home.  They were happy and quiet in my carryon.  One spray of this stuff is enough to naturally help them to relax and feel more at ease in new situations.

I also recommend the wall plug-in.

From longtime devotee to well-done period drama: This film is a captivating story that has been thoughtfully arranged for the screen. I absolutely enjoyed every intense and pleasant bit of it alike and will look for more from this producer and these actors.

This is a story set in 19th century England, based on the classic novel by Elizabeth Gaskell. It is a story of a young woman, Miss Margaret Hale (Daniela Denby-Ashe) and her parents who, although not wealthy, come from elegant society south of London. At the beginning of the film they relocate to the northern industrial town of Milton where cotton mills feed the town's population of poor workers and the wealthy and powerful families are those owning the mills. One such mill owner, Mr John Thornton, (Richard Armitage) first meets Miss Hale in a way that puts him in an unfavorable light which only time and Mr Thornton's honorable character can overcome. Miss Hale befriends a working family during this time and is torn between sides when unions clash with mill owners.

Beyond this, I will let you find out the rest for yourself. Buy this movie... I can't imagine anyone being disappointed!

users.query:
I was pretty excited about it when Jollylife asked me to review their Silicone Non-stick Healthy Cooking Baking Mat in exchange for a discount.  I had been shopping around for something similar not too long ago and had given up on finding one.  It never fails, the kids complain about their chicken fingers being soggy on one side or the fries we bake just aren't crunchy all the way around.  I really wasn't too sure about this one and whether or not it would truly work especially if I tried my homemade fries but I was psyched to give it a try.

The minute this arrived we decided the kids needed to have some chicken fries and tater tots for lunch over spring break to test it out.  To my surprise this actually worked.  Because the air gets all the around the food instead of the food sitting flat on a pan, the entire piece of chicken (fries, etc.) gets cooked all the way around.  I noticed an obvious difference with the first batch although the kids didn't say a thing about it.  I will say if you use a lot of seasoning or something that drips easily this does require a bit more cleaning than other pans or silicone mats but nothing that a simple dish scrubby won't solve.  I haven't had an opportunity to make my own fries yet but I am even more psyched now.  Plus with the inexpensive cost being under $10 I think this is totally worth the purchase.

cands.text:
I have to say once this arrived, we tossed our other popcorn aside to give this a try.  The flavor is awesome and honestly tastes better than what I was using previously in my opinion.  The kids haven't noticed a difference except for the fact that they can make the batches easier on their own since it is all pre-portioned.
Read more at http://www.aluckyladybug.com/2015/01/franklins-popcorn-gourmet-popcorn.html#UQbzrqtHjhTM6yKH.99

The BBQ Grilling Mat is a great tool for cooking these burgers on the grill without worrying they will stick and crumble.  You can grill tons of difficult foods like shrimp on the grill or use it for other seafood like salmon and of course vegetables.  It is non stick and helps keep from these tender foods from falling through the grill grates.  You can easily saute foods you normally couldn't as easily with that amazing grill flavor.

It's almost summer time and the kids will be home again soon and my free time is limited because I have to plan out healthier snacks for them to have while constantly on the go in the nice weather.  I think as children we don't want to eat those things we are told are healthy.  Kids want the trendy snacks that they know moms and dads tell them they can't have.  Thankfully I've discovered a way around this.  Yum Yum Fun recently asked me to review their Healthy Bars & Snacks Variety Pack in exchange for a discount.  I figured this was perfect timing to start planning and stocking up on supplies for the break.

We opened the box to see an insane amount of snacks packed inside. They are also perfect size for children to sample the different and healthy alternatives in order to decide what they might like best!  I had trouble keeping the kids from devouring everything until I could get a few pictures!  I absolutely loved how the kids were excited to try each product instead of me having to talk them into a healthy alternative.  And being that school is still in session, the kids decided they'd be taking these snacks for their school snack instead of the normal crap they choose.  I would actually love to try another box to see more of the other products they have available since I saw quite a few offered which the kids might like.  I do feel like this is a bit pricey for a monthly box HOWEVER, the quality in food is well worth it.

5.0 out of 5 stars Evolve into Better Cooking, April 8, 2015
By A Lucky Ladybug "A Lucky Ladybug" (Michigan)
Verified Purchase(What's this?)
This review is from: Ecolution EVRE-1208 8-Piece Evolve Non-Stick Cookware Set, Red (Kitchen)
I have noticed that I am having to use little to no cooking spray and still no worrying about burning my meals. My food has seemed to cook more evenly and much faster than with my older pans. Even though these are all dishwasher safe, I have simply hand washed each piece several times now as well with no scrubbing in the slightest! I have been treating this set as like my most prized possession since it first arrived.

I think this is a great set even (especially) for a beginner in the kitchen! Cost-wise this seems to be right in line with other similar products of its nature but like most cookware sets, I'd love to see it more affordable for the every day cook. I have fallen completely in love.

You literally don't need to have the experience I have to properly cook your foods!  You choose the meat you are cooking and how you prefer it cooked, and the beeping alarm sounds when ready.  I have to say the pricing on these gadgets is very reasonable for the quality especially right now as it is on sale.
Read more at http://www.aluckyladybug.com/2014/09/premium-digital-fork-meat-thermometer.html#qhbpbffsVgllxQY3.99

I love that there aren't just recipes in this cook book but "extras" galore.  This isn't your average cookbook as it looks more like a novel than anything to me.  There are suggestions for making lifestyle changes, ideas on entertaining (and within a budget), enhancers for meals, product resources, and even eco-terms/techniques.  There isn't just an appetizer and entree section but smaller more focused sections like warm and cold vegetable sides from your garden.  There are entrees for different lifestyles and recipes for literally everyone's taste.  So far the only complaint I have is there are no visuals to help when flipping through looking for meals.  While part of me appreciates this because the pictures are fake and propped most times, I also like to see an image to get an idea of what the meal might include.  Other than that, I think this is an amazing resource for any level cook.  This is a REAL cookbook which will help anyone make a change in their families lifestyle.

First and foremost, I love the fact that I do not have to use cooking oil/sprays as these are outrageously expensive in my opinion.  Second, you can cook just about anything in this, not just cupcakes or baking!  I like being able to cook other things like bread rolls, muffins, or even my favorite, omelette tarts. read more [...]

Since my son has come to love fresh muffins from a popular restaurant Fast Food chain (because of my father), I love that I can now make him them at home.  It saves us a ton of money and I can make them exactly how he likes them.  These are even freezer safe so you can prepare foods ahead of time if you'd like.
Read more at http://www.aluckyladybug.com/2014/09/sunsella-little-gems-and-mighty-pops.html#PVo7wHUrkC9dpb71.99

This is a great idea for any household and not just if you are trying to live a healthier lifestyle but to use in all areas of the kitchen!  Get creative!
Read more at http://www.aluckyladybug.com/2014/09/bellemains-stainless-steel-lemon-press.html#MmqfDXP6b18iH3bo. 99

I love to cook and that has become fairly obvious by the amount of gadgets I currently have around my kitchen.  It seems like I've run out of cabinet and draw space fairly quick in our new house and I've even had a friend who recently commented about the lack in space with everything.  When I first saw the chefs limited utensil set, I figured it would be perfect for our kitchen.  I honestly figured it wouldn't necessarily be the best of quality being it was only $30 but I was willing to give it a try.

When this arrived, I fell in love!  I do have to admit there was an extra piece I felt which made putting it together a bit confusing but otherwise this is great.  Each of the tools have this awesome grip which is heat resistant and it takes up little to no space on my counter.  I like the stylish look too which matches the other black accessories in my kitchen!  I would definitely recommend this set!

Although I have not had the easiest time using this gadget on the store bought potatoes I had on hand I have yet to try it with a softer vegetable.  I was super excited to come across the Spiralizer Spiral Slicer.  Not only is this supposed to help create healthy alternatives for most people looking to reduce their calories but it is also supposed to be a super fun way to prepare foods in a decorative way.  Read more at  [...]

This tool works great on a variety of tasks such as mixing dough, mashing potatoes, of course different baking mixtures like cookie dough!  I like that I don't have to pull out my mixer every time I decide to make something from scratch as it is such a pain to watch and clean up.
Best part, this is dishwasher safe so you can toss it in to easily cleanup any messes!  I love how well this works AND how easy it is!
Read more at http://www.aluckyladybug.com/2014/09/sunsella-stainless-steel-steamer-and.html#rOWJVw4Cmtf3cZUr. 99

Not only is this an extremely well made product but it has multiple uses as you see I've discovered.  I think the price is a great one if you could use this product for anything in or around the kitchen.
Read more at[...]

Being the big kitchen freak that I am, I've known for a while that I wanted to update my trivets in my kitchen, especially since we moved.  To be honest most of the time I've been using cloth pads and just haven't been happy with their outdated look or the overall performance.  Then, QooWare asked me if I'd be interested in their Kitchen Foldable Silicone Trivets in exchange for a discount and it was all the motivation I need to scoop up a new colorful set.  I love silicone in the kitchen!  It works so much better than any other traditional product especially when it comes to heat.

These are perfect for keeping pots and pans raised from my granite counter tops and are sturdy so those pots don't slip off and potentially spill.  I was a bit frustrated at the fact that several of the legs "pop out" easily when opening/unfolding the trivets.  They aren't easy to "pop" back in either so this is something I'd be aware of when purchasing.  However this doesn't change the quality or inhibit the function.  You can even use them for more than the kitchen...My boys have been using these to prop up their tablets if they watch a video during breakfast and I can easily place my cell there for easy access while cooking too.  I love how they look all over my kitchen too!  Overall at the $15 price point they are more than worth the purchase.

I love that there aren't just recipes in this cook book but "extras" galore.  This isn't your average cookbook as it looks more like a huge manual than anything to me.  This canning cookbook is now going to be my bible from here on out.  As a homesteader who has canned for at least 5 years now, there are tons of new recipes, equipment, and guidelines to follow in this book.  I truly cannot believe how in depth this guide is and especially wish I had had this as a beginner!  I love not only how easy these recipes are to follow but guidelines to make sure I am creating healthy meals for my family all in one place. The cost is even cheaper than buying a special edition magazine with an 1/8 of the info.  This is one of those all in one resources that is a must in any canners kitchen.

Love them!  Not only do these have soap all ready for use but they are less harsh than buying a plain steel wool pad which can tend to scratch my pans.  These are gentle on the skin too so no worrying about poking or cutting your fingers while using!

With all the holiday entertaining I do, I've made it appoint to purchase several different types of dicers, slicers, and knives to help make my preparation easier. Because I have a ridiculous amount of kitchen gadgets and utensils, I've been looking for something compact yet easy to set up when I need it. When Excellent Doer offered a discount in exchange for a review I was hoping this would be able to replace multiple tools in the kitchen.  Because I already own a Mandoline Slicer which is very basic, I was thrilled to discover this one and all that it had to offer.

I love how this holds all it's extras within the unit AND not to mention all the extras it comes with making it an all in one product for the kitchen.  When shopping around, I knew I wanted one with a catch basin of some sort since my other slicer didn't have any and it always results in a mess on the counter.  This one has perfect drawers to use depending on which portion of the gadget you are using.  My hands have been destroyed over the years from using knives and unsafe slicers so I was thrilled to try something on the safe side of kitchen prep using the safety holder so I never get near the blade.

Here is where my review drops to a 4 star:  There is a pop up section which you can see in my pics for slicing strips as well.  Because it does not completely drop below the devices surface, it catches most foods before they hit the blade you are trying to slice using.  This causes your food to get mangled a bit on the bottom OR makes it difficult to make a smooth slice swipe (dangerous).  The blades (not one but ALL) are extremely dull.  My first slice attempt on a firm tomato cause it to get completely mashed in the process with no realistic slices to see.  The 2nd attempt I went with jalapenos (again firm) and it destroyed them.  After several attempts at different veges and fruits, I've determined this is a fail especially at $25.  IF the company improved the blades this would be well worth the cost and more with everything it comes with.

Being that I come from quite a long restaurant management background, I consider myself to be a self starter in the kitchen.  I love to cook, grill, bake anything and especially from scratch with the freshest and healthiest ingredients I can find.  I am always updating my kitchen and trying out the newest gadgets I can find or cooking up my own creations.  I love being that contact for my friends, family, and followers when they are looking into anything kitchen.

I frequently make pizza from scratch for dinner for my family.  This way everyone can personalize their pizzas without having to cost me an arm and a leg ordering delivery.  PLUS, it enables me to use the freshest ingredients (most of which come from my garden).  Sometimes this can be quite a task besides having to literally make it from scratch, it can be a pain to get through the crust as I am by no means a pizza guru.  The pizza cutter was great since the blade was nice and sharp and flowed through pizza easily.  I love that this allows me to cut a large pizza twice as fast just like when I was in the restaurants.  We've been using it on the kids quesadillas just as easily when we make them.  It can really be used to easily slice anything you might need chopped in bulk too.  For $15 bucks I think everyone should have one in their kitchen even if it is just to better cut the pizzas they order!

I LOVE THIS!!  I had seen one in poor shape at a garage sale a while back and have ever since wanted one for my kitchen.  I was so sick of keeping fruit and vege's on the counter.  When this popped up in my amazon suggestions, I knew I had to have it.  My husband installed it right away and we quickly put it to the test.  As you can see from my photos it holds quite a bit and holds it well.  The baskets haven't fallen out of the ceiling and boy can I store even more than I imagined.  I'd definitely recommend one of these if you are limited on counter space or even just as a pretty display for whatever in your home!

*I have 2 bundles of banana's and about 4 pounds in potatoes hanging from this

So I don't like to keep anything disposable in my house that I really don't have to.  That means paper plates, napkins, paper towels, plastic or paper cups, etc.  As goofy as this is going to sound, I have always wanted a soup thermos probably even since I was younger.  I really don't have a clue why I just always thought they would be a useful product to have around.  And that was before I was into all the green friendly products I am now.  Now that I am older, not only do I have more control over what types of products I let my children use in the house and on the go but my husband and I have started prepping for emergency situations.  We are always on the look out for new products to throw into our emergency kits.

When I first discovered the Xtreme canteen, I was pretty psyched to find it is made with BPA FREE 18/8 food grade stainless steel and can keep things like ice frozen for up to 24 hours and your hot liquids hot for up to 12 hours.  I was even more psyched seeing the beautiful colors they had available to choose from.  So far we've used this once when taking a recent road trip where it kept our beverage cold and icy for the 6 hour drive.  I've cleaned it since then and have it ready near my emergency bag as well so we have it ready if we need it for anything else!  While I do think it seems like its a bit expensive for a purchase of a single bottle but the quality definitely helps make it well worth the purchase.

First and foremost, I do NOT recommend this for play with children as it is not a family friendly game.  There is blood and of course lots of violent situations through the entire game.  The variety of weaponry and graphic nature are cause for quite a bit of explanation to young children.  However, the realistic imagery and detail make for an extreme experience for most adults.

I feel fairly confident in saying that most any little boy (and little girls of course) growing up in this decade are into LEGO's of some form.  Between the LEGO movie and all the amazing creations you can make, they have become a big trend for kids.  It's extremely educational, building skills without even being aware of it.  Though the problem with LEGO's (for parents more specifically) is the insane costs involved in acquiring these and all the LEGO swag for your children.

We've purchased several lego plates from the actual lego store and places like target in the past but they've always been so costly.  When CreativeQT asked if I'd be interested in reviewing their Peel-and-Stick LEGO Compatible Baseplates (in exchange for a discount), I figured it might be a good addition to our large lego collection.  After trying a few base plates in the past which wouldn't function properly with actual name brand legos, we've been a bit hesitant.  When these arrived, the boys were psyched and right away we added a few of them to our lego table and others the boys used to build on as a portable base.

These are completely compatible with the legos we have as you can see from my pictures.  We loved the easy peel and stick instead of having to use glue on our tables and shelves like we've been doing in the past.  We even found this last longer with the kids pulling the legos up and off the plates over time.  To be honest, you pay an arm and a leg for even the smaller sets of LEGO's and base plates like this so adding these to your supplies is highly recommended and saves you tons of money!

This was perfect for what we were looking for, for my son's bday part.  While these might be considered "paper" or cardboard of sorts, they were sturdy enough to set around as decoration and even for my 2 year nephew to grab and run around with without ruining them!  They've now become toys for the kids!

I rarely find a blanket that keeps my butt feeling dry even when it says it will.  Somehow the moisture from the dirt beneath always seems to make it's way through, but not with this blanket!  This is not bulky, heavy, or a pain to lug around by any means.  It's is big enough for your family to lay on quite comfortably and still fold up and take back and forth with you wherever you decide to go.  I've got to say I love how easy it is to refold when done, because you know how hard it can be to get something like this folded back into the original carrying position!  While I have been using this for the boys little league games as a blanket to sit on, we've also used it for our family picnics indoors.  We are planning on taking this to the local fireworks show for the 4th of July this week too!  This is seriously one of the best products for any outdoor lover!  This is going to last a long time and is well worth the cost.  This would make a great gift idea for the outdoorsy person in your life as well especially with how lightweight it is.

users.query: It has many psychic revelations, but the family issues are just as compelling. It was hard to put it down.

cands.text: Loved the book and the characters. Different take on portals for ghosts. Zany family dynamic keeps the book moving and fun.

The writer kept me off balance through the whole book. It kept my interest and didn't follow through with the violence most authors would add to the story. All the main characters are off-dysfunctional families, non-working, living beyond their means-yet they keep you reading. There are no easy fixes or brilliant deductions on the part of Jake, but I couldn't stop until I found out how it ended.

Daughter comes home after fleeing when her mom finally admit she was adopted. Her ex follows bringing all the drama he was trying to protect her from and the murder begins. Which of the new people in town are bad and which are innocent? I love the twists and turns in the plot. A great read.

The flow through lose and return to life is amazing. I stopped reading 65% into this book for some reason, but it was well worth the surprise of what story ended up revealing. I think I may have even enjoyed it more because I let my memory jump in the answers to the confusion I felt as things were explained. It helped me enjoy her discoveries of things from her past as they began to connect as memories of the first of the book began to click in my memory.
