I obviously don't need to tell you that H.G. Wells knows how to write a good story.  In fact, seeing as this is a classic, I probably don't need to tell you anything about this book, as even if you haven't read it already, you've probably already got a good idea of whether or not you're going to read it.

However, since I read it, I'm going to tell you what I thought.

First, this book holds up incredibly well to the test of time.  The science might be a little thin, but the ideology is spot on, and is amazingly introspective.  Wells' vision of the future of 800,000 years from now is a spectacular view of what might happen to mankind should we continue to exist (in some form) for that much longer.  But what's more interesting is how it relates to the mankind of today, and what it might truly mean for us as a people.

But that's all side story, all sorts of literary allusions and whatnot.  What's really great about this tale, as with all Wells stories, is the actual action involved, the story itself.  Here we see a character (who never gets and actual name) learning first hand about the dangers of time travel, as well as the dangers of adventuring at all.  And...we learn that human ingenuity is required, even when facing of against human descendants of millenia from now.
 Simply put, this is a great story, and serves as the inspiration for countless time travel stories that have cropped up since this book was first published.  But it still stands as unique, as something no one could duplicate...as something you really should read.

I'm giving this book 2 stars simply because I'm fairly certain that if I read it all the way to the end, I would have been able to determine that this was a brilliant piece of prose.
However...I made it about 20% of the way in and decided that it's really just not worth it.

There's definitely some interesting things going on, but it's all hiding between rather convoluted English and a not-very-exciting storyline, as well as no real characters to even connect with that the whole thing becomes quite confusing before it even starts.
I'm sure this is somewhat the point, but I found that I really just didn't care enough to get to find that out.

Sorry Mellvile, I found that I agree with the rest of your readers in that I just really don't care about this one.

I'll be honest, I had pretty low expectations for this book.  However, my love of Disney World kept me intrigued, as well as the fact that this series seems to keep going and keep having very dedicated fans.

When it was up for free, I decided to check it out.

My review of this book is quite simple.  This book should be re-written.  There are some incredibly solid/imaginative ideas, but the execution is just pathetic.  There was more than one scene in the book where I didn't even realize how cool the events that were happening should be until I had finished it and attempted to explain the silliness to my wife, realizing that it was actually an awesome scene, just poorly written.

The characterizations are flat, the scene building abysmal, and the overall story really just needs a complete overhaul to be what it should be.

That being said, this is a fantastic idea for a book, much better than I expected going in.  I just wish the idea matched the reality.

I came into this book without any real knowledge or expectations or...well..anything.  I just saw that it was a story told from the perspective of an evil super-villain's henchman and I was sold.

And I'm really truly happy I was.  Henchmen is quite the amazing take on the supervillain back story...as well as an amusing look into how they manage to get so many people to work beside them.  This story follows Steve (or Steven? I forget because his role as nameless henchman seemed much more important to the tale) and we get to see a firsthand account of what it really means to work for someone who is trying to destroy the world...or, in this case, try to overturn the US government.

Actually, once you get into this book, you'll see that the term supervillain might be a bit of a misnomer, at least as far as what we know through Steve's eyes.  Eve, his 7-foot tall Amazonian boss with at least a minor dosing of super-strength, doesn't seem to be doing what she's doing to mean any form of selfish means, but in order to better the world.  This isn't Lex Luthor trying to sink California into the ocean so he can sell real estate on the other side of the San Andreas fault.  This is someone who believes the system is broken and is looking to fix it, through means that might be questionable, sure, but sometimes drastic times require drastic measures...or some other similar overused cliche.

This is where Lahti's brilliance shines.  Not only does he manage to craft a wonderful thought-provoking piece of what might cause someone to turn to supervillainy, while also showing that they aren't completely blameless, even if they might have noble intentions; but he also does so with a hefty dose of humor.  This book is plenty funny and on more than one occasion I was reminded of John Dies at the End (although I must note this is nowhere near as flatout funny as that book...rather superficial reminders).  Comedy isn't the primary purpose here, just a great additional to the voice this book carries.  One of something much larger lying under the surface...which we only begin to get a peek at by the conclusion of this tale.

Simply put, this is a great title and one I can't wait to see how it progresses.  I highly suggest you check it out!

The Scott Pilgrim series is easily falling into a bit of a routine with how it tells its stories. The first 2/3rds of the book tends to move rather slowly, exploring more about Scott's daily life and showing how he's really quite the loser, while the last third of the book finally takes its time to explore the more fantastic parts of his life, including the requisite evil ex-boyfriends.
Volume 4 doesn't seem to stray from this roadmap at all either. However, having the exciting parts at the end of the book does a great job of keeping me coming back for more.
Actually, the 4th book in this series really has come a long way in its methods of storytelling. We see Scott's life becoming quite crazed, even without the usage of subspace and maniacal exes. And we also get to learn more about the mysterious Ramona.
In fact, book 4, if anything, seems to take a sudden turn from the rest of the series in that it really starts telling us a bit about what's going on, and giving us an idea of where the resolution for this whole storyline might be headed.
But only slightly.
Just enough to whet our whistle.
All the same, if you've enjoyed any of the previous Pilgrim books, this one is even better than the preceding three. Definitely give it a read!

I made the mistake of watching the movie based on this book first.  If you haven't enjoyed either version yet, stay away from the movie!  I've heard from friends who read the book first that the movie wasn't very enjoyable after reading the book, but I can tell you for a fact that the book loses a lot of its flavor if you watch the movie first.  (side note: if you're not going to read the book (which is a stupid idea), the movie is totally worth the watch)

This book takes everything you know about the horror genre and does things to it that I can't even mention in mixed company.  It quite literally tells the horror genre to screw off because it's too busy getting high in the bathroom.  Everything about this book is set to make you rethink how you would act in a situation where you're facing off against monsters from another realm.  This isn't a question about whether or not you would be going into that darkened room unaware of what's on the other side, but one that asks you, how hard are you going to kick that monster in the fact whilst lightly peeing your pants.

I can't speak highly enough of what happens between the covers of this book and I highly recommend that you drop whatever book you're reading right now and pick this one up.

Also...Leinenkugels gets a mention...which is always a plus.

I had long been told stories about how Moore was able to translate this pulp character into something truly amazing, but even though I've long been a fan of Moore's work, I just didn't trust it.
How wrong I was...
Moore's Swamp Thing has some serious balls to it and really seems to take a rather outrageous backstory and turn it into something that has a story that needs to be told, while getting out some enviro-issues at the same time.
But what's most important here is that Moore turned the Swamp Thing from a monster into a character who is seeking out the truth, and a character who is truly concerned for what is going on around him, while ultimately being absolutely lost to this new world that he has found himself in.
Also...Constantine makes a pretty good appearance in here, which can never be a bad thing.

Having first read this book about a decade ago, I went in knowing quite a bit about what I was about to experience.  In fact, I went in with something of a bad taste in my mouth, because although I knew of my enjoyment of the majority of the book, my distaste for the end had left me unsettled about the whole thing.

However, based on some recommendations by others, I dug back in.

I'm glad I did.

Very few people can debate that what Danielewski has done with this novel is brilliant.  Inside the covers of this overwhelming tome, he manages to capture many different styles, tones, and images.  His ability to present a well-researched document about something that never existed (or did it?) while also showcasing absolute insanity is, well, simply amazing.  Readers may get annoyed with the use of footnotes and typesetting over the course of this 700 page experiment, but the early stages of this process are really just there to get you ready for the novel as it progresses.  Once you get into the main meat of this tale, you're ready, you're looking for clues, hunting for secrets within the words, within the notes, within the format.  Everything, even down to the fact that this is the second edition, no matter which version you get, is a clue to the answer that you hope you'll understand by the end.

Of course, the end doesn't flat out give you the answer, which, although is part of the reason I kept this book from getting a fifth star, is also part of the sheer beauty of the text.  Although we are given a look into every single possible aspect of this house with a dark secret, as well as the family that lived there, we come out of the experience with very few answers.

The book looks as though it is promising to give answers, what with it's professional and non-fictional tone...but the truth of the matter is that there are no answers.  This is a book about madness, a book about getting lost.  A book about the unknown.

And by definition, the unknown cannot be known.  At least not without changing exactly what it is.

If you've somehow not managed to get your hands on this book yet, I highly suggest you take a month and dig in deep.  And after you're done, there are plenty of sites out there dedicated to cracking all of the little codes Danielewski has hidden in his novel.  Maybe they hold the answers...I'm willing to bet they don't.

I have to admit that I feel a little sheepish in that I haven't read the full unabridged version of this book until this very moment.  I've read versions that contain most of the text, but never the full one.  In fact, it wasn't until rather recently that I realized this.

And it's really sad that I hadn't, as the full novelization is spectacular.  A whole lot of nuance is lost in the abridged versions (and the film).  Baum does a spectacular job of letting us see Oz through Dorothy's eyes, while also causing us to realize that the Lion, Tin Man, and Scarecrow were never in need of the items they wanted.

But even more so, we see this fantastical tale of a whole new world.  A new world that I can't wait to read more about...meaning, for the first time in possibly ever, I'm going to have to work through some more of the books in this series.  Excited to see what comes next.

The author sent me this book and asked if I might be willing to give it a read and a review. And me, being the guy who can't turn down a free book, took him up on it.

Also, me being the guy who doesn't actually do any sort of reading up on books to know what they are about or what sort of genre they are or anything before beginning to read a book, went into it completely unawares of what I was about to find.

I don't know if I can quite suggest you go into this book quite as unaware.

It's a good book, possibly even a great book.  It's incredibly well written, the concept is novel, and I can honestly say that I don't think I've read anything quite like it before.

That being said, there are certain parts of this book that are quite unsettling.  If I hadn't agreed to read and review the book ahead of time, I'm fairly certain I would have set the book down never to pick it up again at numerous stops along the path toward the final resolution.

But the real question here is, should you read it?

If you can handle some unsettling imagery regarding death and dismemberment (not a large amount, mind you, just enough to definitely stick out in your mind), then yes, I would wholeheartedly suggest you read this book.

Now here's the issue...the reasons I would suggest you read this book (outside of the fact that it is quite well written and very good at pulling you deeper into the story, even when discussing rather disgusting events) are reasons I don't know I should actually reveal.  They're something of surprises that you find along the way.  Even the official description of the book doesn't really give you a good idea of what you're getting into.

So, when you start reading it, all you get is that there was some sort of plane crash, and a journal discussing excitement about an event called only G-88.  G-88 is talked about quite heavily throughout the text, but isn't actually explained until the moment the event comes up.  Things actually start to fall into place quite well at that point, but until then, I'll admit that I really couldn't gather how all these pieces fit together.

Or maybe I just didn't want to.

Huls takes a rather standard story type, specifically that of a coming-of-age style road trip and turns it on its side a bit, giving us a glimpse of what the world of white privilege can look like at its worse, at how a couple of young boys can be absolute sociopaths simply because they come up in a house where nothing is really expected of them.

Of how boredom can lead men to absolute insanity...while still allowing them to appear to be completely normal human beings.

Ayahuasca contains two of my least favorite protagonists of all time.  All I wanted was for someone to come around and put a bullet in their heads from nearly page one...But I really had a hard time putting it down, even when I really really wanted to.

So, if you like having yourself challenged in a read, I'd definitely say this is a book for you.  If you like books where the winners are spotless and the bad guys wear black hats, then this probably isn't one you want to pick up.

I bought this camera almost 10 years ago and it's just now where I'm starting to think I might actually want to replace it.  If that's not enough of a recommendation to begin with, I don't know what is.  When I bought this one almost a decade ago, it was one of the few high definition cameras on the market.  Making the decision to attempt shooting an independent film, I purchased this item and loved every second of using it.
It definitely hasn't gotten nearly the amount of use it should have over the years, but the memories that have been captured since the birth of my children and my wedding itself and so many other items, they will be cherished, in pretty close to perfect resolution.
I'm quite happy with the purchase I made years ago, and I'd imagine anyone looking at this camera for purchase today would still find plenty to be happy about with it.

There's something so magical about these books that I just can't seem to completely put them down.  The mixture of story being told and artwork which presents itself seems to fit so perfectly while, at the same time, seem so completely opposite of each other.
In the end, the tale being told is filled with such ironic detachment that I'm not even certain what I should take seriously and what is just crazed dreams occurring within Scott's head.
In fact, the beginning of book 2 does exactly that, almost becoming aggravating in its jerky storytelling methods, until you realize that there's a good reason for this.

I don't remember much from the movie anymore, but I really appreciate that it seems in the books there is a growing evil ex army for Scott as a parallel to Ramona's army.  And Knives seems like the perfect character to lead it.  I'll be interested to see how that plays out as the series progresses.

Nothing I can say about this book will do my absolute love for it any justice.  This book is simply something you must read.
A thinly veiled discussion about depression, The Girl on the Red Pillow does something I never thought possible, and definitely wouldn't have thought possible in such an entertaining and engaging way: make depression humorous and interesting.  Well...it doesn't actually make depression humorous, but allows for humor to exist in a story about the topic.
From the first moment you get to meet the wall building dwarf, to the final moment when Annalee finally comes to terms with her depression and looks toward the future, you will be urged forward as you hope Annalee finds the answer to her troubles, especially if you're someone who has dealt with their own wall-building dwarf.

Read this book.  Plain and simple.

I have to admit that I haven't read much of the Ninja Turtle comics since the original series, but I came across this trade and couldn't turn down a chance to see what these guys were up to in the original medium, now that I've had the opportunity to catch up with them in the animated realm.
Although the tone of this trade paperback seems to match that of the new cartoon series more than the original comics, as well as the colored masks, the action around the turtles is totally within the realm of the old school Eastman and Laird.
Our turtles might not be gritty, but the world they live in definitely is, and it keeps with the rather absolute absurdity of the original as well.  Dimension X reigns supreme as we find the Utrom Krang ready to take over everything, in a much more diabolical manner than the weasely Krang of the 1987 cartoon ever could.
We even get to see a short glimpse of Shredder with his granddaughter (a character I hadn't become aware of until checking out the new cartoon) Karai.

The book might be in color, the masks might not all be red, but perhaps that doesn't matter anymore as the cartoon and movie series are more what people remember from this fantastic genre changing comic book.

No matter what you've come to expect from "your" turtles, this book is sure to give you at least a small portion of it.  It's definitely got me wanting to find another trade book to add to my collection.

Amazon said I haven't said enough yet....So, twenty words are needed before this is complete.

Heroes in a half shell.

Blackbeard's Justice is the third book in Jeremy McLean'sThe Voyages of Queen Anne's Revengeseries and to put it simply, if you liked the first two, you're definitely going to enjoy the third one.

But I don't write simple little reviews like that.

And Blackbeard's Justice doesn't deserve a simple review. This is a nuanced book, especially considering that at it's core it's a swashbuckling adventure novel, but here we get to see the dread pirate Roberts...I mean Blackbeard, deal with the events of the previous book, where he may or may not have killed his close friend in a fit of rage. At the same time, his town has been ravaged by a different set of pirates, who just so happen to be led by Calico Jack, a guy who has some revenge need to begin with, leads some folks who have some revenge need, and just so happens to have a secret identity which plays close to Blackbeard's own personal history, as well as that of several of his crew.

In other words, there's a ton going on here. And McLean manages to keep the story moving forward while also juggling all these different pieces quite expertly. As the main cast of characters continues to grow, we get to see each and every one of them develop their own paths through the narrative. This isn't a crew where everyone follows the protagonist blindly. In fact, one of Blackbeard's biggest issues is that his crew seems to, more often than not, think he's lost it and is in need of some psychiatric help.

Blackbeard's Justice may be more of the same we've come to expect from McLean, but it also does a fantastic job of keeping the series alive. What originally began as a quest to find the answers about a mysterious ship has developed into a look behind the madness of Blackbeard and his crew and an attempt to give the reality of the pirating business a good hard look...while making sure there is still plenty of swashbuckling to go around.

Author: Dawn Gray
Fiction, Paranormal,
This review may contain spoilers
Summary: Author Lily Reynolds had rarely traveled from her home state, but the opportunity to visit one of America's "most haunted cities" was not something she could pass up. Despite anxiety issues that plagued her life, Lily and her friend Kylie set off on what they thought would be a two-week vacation, but turn into an adventure beyond her wildest dreams.
Jared Claverack has lived in New Orleans from the time he was born. She was his to protect at all cost, it was a duty he did ferociously. He was content to walk the streets at night, until his blue eyes connected with a pale-skinned woman from the north, and the occupants of the City of the Dead began to creep from out from the shadows.
Was he strong enough to save her, to keep her from the grasp of the evil he knew lurked in the darkness, or would she become just another one of the city's haunting stories?
The Review
I loved this tale from this author, who is fastly growing to be one of my favourites, This one had me hooked from the start, I loved the character descriptions, very thorough, I really enjoyed the banter between some of the characters, The action kept me up until the wee hours of the night, I would highly recommend this to all my friends and family, I loved the scenic descriptions, made me believe I knew exactly where they were for each scene, even though I have never been to New Orleans. I loved the hero, Jared, *insert big sigh here* He was totally dream worthy, I adored the plotline, Good and evil combine to make a great story, I hope to hear more about the lives of the two main characters and what happened when they returned home to her family, 5/5

cands.text:
I bought this on Amazon for review for Confessions of a bookaholic
Summary: Before Lilyann stepped into her destiny to lead the coven, there was another powerful Moon witch...her grandmother. A teenage witch in Galway, Ireland, Leeny Moon was prepared to take her rightful place in the circle along side of her kin. Until, she witnessed firsthand the forthcoming nightmares she would be expected to face.

The fight between good versus evil begins here...

Blessed Be~
Review
I love having a short story which leads to the main book, the back story always helps when you start reading the main book, in this case Compulsion, I will be reading that one next, I loved this novella, I love the title by the way, just had to say.

We meet Aileen or Leeny as everyone calls her, a teenager on the precipice of joining the local coven where her mother is the head witch, Haunted Moon gave me a great insight into the mind of a witch to be, although this was set in 1947 in Galway Bay, it could easily have been set in our generation of teens.

Leeny has been given her first Grimoire by her mother, This is where we first meet her as she starts writing in it, she is being taught by her mother, Rose, on how a witch uses her powers and abilities to eradicate the bane of the human world, The Vampires, which were accidently brought into this world by an ancestor of Leeny's called Ana, who went a bit mad after her fiance was killed, she conjured him back to life as a vampire, so because of this, the witches use their powers to destroy them, Leeny has to learn how to protect the people in her village and of course her family, which is alot for a young lady to take on, but on top of that, she also has to be initiated into the Moon Coven, the trials and tribulations of training was very insightful, I would love to be able to control Fire, like Leeny and her mum, she is also having to keep on top of her studies at school, during training one night her mother fights with a vampire, Nicholas, which leads Leeny to believe that her mother enjoyed it a little too much, which makes her think maybe being a witch may not be a good thing, Poor Leeny has so much to deal with, she has a sister called Colleen or Colly, who desperately wants to be in the coven, but she is not old enough and so feels that Leeny has been given a gift that she is not using correctly, so starts being mean to Leeny, I felt so Sorry for her, she was so alone for a while, Leeny goes through a patch of not wanting to commit murder or kill vampires, until she comes up against one, I would recommend reading this one, I loved this book and cannot wait to read Compulsion.

Ebook: Vengeance of the Werewolf
Author: Mercedes Ludill
Fiction, Paranormal,
This review may contain spoilers
Summary: Werewolves are living in town. Some are good, some are bad, some are really bad. Vengeance of the Werewolf is filled with suspense of the hunt for the werewolf, explicit sexual situations, gore as only werewolves can inspire. This book isn't intended for younger readers as it is rated R. Wolfcreek's werewolves are raw, dangerous, compassionate, vengeful, vicious, and human. There are no mad beasts here, these monsters know exactly what they are doing as they retain their human control when in beast form.
This book is horror, thriller, and suspense, not to be confused with werewolf romance or erotica.
The Review
Firstly, this is a warning to all out there, who want a romance novel, this is not for you, This is a very graphic novel, that had me hooked from the start, I only usually read romance or erotica, but I was asked to review this, thought I would try it, I like trying new things. Infact I loved this one, If you like your werewolves mean & nasty then this is the one for you, There was a little comic relief now and again by Randy and Ted, two of the main characters, but there were so many characters in this book,  our main character was  Lanny, the local police sheriff, who takes control of a lot of the situations in the book, All the characters are very well written, everything is written very descriptively, which made me feel a little queasy in some of the situations, but I think that is what the writer wanted, I enjoyed reading the Epilogue and would be intrigued to know if there were any signs of a series coming from this book, I would highly recommend this to those who like horror style writing, 4.5/5.

I was given this by the author for an honest review

Summary: Recently-turned vampire Emma Hammond is not only getting used to her undead lifestyle, but also to living with her new and unlikely roommates--her human best friend Tammy, and David, a werewolf. While the girls speculate as to possible drawbacks to having such a fuzzy tenant (shedding and marking of territory, to name a few), nothing will prepare them for the dispute that is to come between the NYC clan of vampires and an upwardly-mobile werewolf pack from the suburbs. Will Emma be able to get out of it with both her undead life, and her blossoming friendship with David, intact? And, perhaps more importantly, will she be able to choose between Alex Thompson, her sire and sometimes lover, and James, a slightly-unhinged vampire with a mysterious past?

The Review
You did it again Donna, I loved it, this is the follow on from New Blood although it could have stood on it's own, I enjoyed it more because I had read the first one, We had all the same characters which was wonderful, with a few extra ones thrown in which added greatly to this book, I loved how Donna made this world for us to inhabit, I want to be just like Emma, she had wonderful friends who stood by her in the end, I loved Tammy who was Emma's best friend, I loved how she saved the day, even though she was just a human, well she was!!!!! I still don't understand Alex, but then I never did in this first book, I understands he loves Emma, after all he made her, but he goes to some extraordinary lengths to protect her, I am really looking forward to the next book in this series, I can't wait to hear how Emma gets on and does Michael ever find out about her? 4/5,

Summary: Samantha and Zander never expected to find each other in the strange little town as fire tore through a church, but the more they were together, the more they found a common link in their past.
Extended description
When Samantha Ricketts finds herself placed in a town half-way across the country, her only worry is how did she get there, but when her life is saved by a handsome and mysterious man, the connection they feel is almost more than she can stand.

Together they tap into the supernatural to uncover the mysteries surrounding the strange town but would they become part of the strange past or fall into it's future.
.The Review
Wow, I don't read ghost stories, as I usually read at night and Yes, I am scaredy cat and would never sleep, but I started this during the day and finished later that day, as it was such a great story, I could not put it down, I just didn't want to, I loved the way it was written and yes I loved the romance, I know it was quick romance between Zander and Samantha but hey it only added to the story, as they, Oh I don't want to give too much away, so I will stop right there, I loved how Dawn got you so involved with the story, I loved the idea and the concept of the S.P.I.R.I.T series, I am saying series, I hope it will be one, I would love for the rest of the group to get love interests, and maybe get some powers too, I loved the powers, storm and fire together are a wicked combination, I loved the telepathy between Zander and Samantha, I also loved how Sam was kick ass and was not scared by the bad ghouls or mostly by Zanders boss Everett, she always came back with a classic line to shut him up, as best as she could  Thankyou Dawn for letting me read this book, let me know when the next one is out, Please, 4/5

Author: Dianna Hardy

Fiction, Paranormal,

I was given this ARC by the author for an honest review

This review may contain spoilers

Summary: The full moon is a week away, and although Lydia is as excited as it gets to run as a wolf for the first time, she is also fighting to keep her independence while trying to understand her role in the lives of the three males that have come to rule hers: compassionate, tender Taylor; impetuous, fun-loving Ryan and distant, cold Lawrence.
There's also a fourth man in Lydia's life. Brendan, her previous "friend with benefits", is tirelessly searching for her. He's about to uncover things that should be kept hidden.
However, the testosterone surrounding her is the last thing she should be worrying about. Her family bear truths about her heritage she's not ready to face ... she may not have a choice, because the greatest danger to them all comes from within. The past never stays buried for long, and among the shadows of their species it is rising with a vengeance, threatening to tear their pack apart for good.
Notes: Book two of a series - it is highly recommended that book one be read first. This is an adult, paranormal fantasy short novel (over 55,000 words) containing scenes of explicit sexual content and some violence, entwined with romantic elements.

The Review
Yowzer, How super excited was I to get my greedy little mitts on this copy, I couldn't wait to get stuck in and I didnt, I started it straight away, I really loved the first book in this series, Releasing the Wolf, so could not believe it when the author sent me this ARC, It has felt like I have waited so long for this one, but it hasn't really been that long, still it was definitely worth waiting for, I couldn't put it down, it had all the characters I fell in love with in the first book, Taylor, Ryan and Lawrence, not forgetting our main female lead, Lydia, this book was more in depth with the relationship between the four, I will not give you any spoilers if I can help it, but it does delve into each separate relationship that Lydia has with each of them, along with their relationship together as a group, as usual from this author, The plotline was awesome, I would give the raunchy stuff a 5 out of 5 too, We also have the baddie from book 1, Amil, but he is really growing on me in a weird way, talking of which, the action was great, I was kept on the edge of my seat with this one, we also meet some new characters, one of which freaked me out abit, I won't say who, you will have to read it, to see what I mean, I didn't want this book to end, but now I am looking forward to Book 3, I would give this one 5/5, put it in your wish list,

Summary: Seven days ago, Elizabeth May tried to commit suicide. She was found by Paul, her husband, who took her under his wing and back to their home. But the attempted suicide is not Elizabeth's main problem - Elizabeth can't remember who she is, or a single thing about her life beyond the past week.
Plagued by nightmares about a familiar black panther, and a terrifying snow leopard, she is convinced that the dreams are trying to show her something important, and is determined to regain her memories, one way or another.
Meanwhile, Pueblo - the demon blood-bonded to the witch, Amy - is going insane trying to find her. Amy disappeared one week ago, and it seems not even their bond is strong enough to penetrate whatever magic hides her.
As Pueblo enlists the help of angels and demons alike, Elizabeth begins to piece together parts of her forgotten life. But what she uncovers may just have her wanting to turn away from who she really is ... for good.
The Review
I liked this one a lot, we got to meet the same characters as in the first book, but now we were focused on Amy & Pueblo, my favourite characters from book 1, I love the bond that each couple seems to have, The author has caught exactly how I would imagine that bond to be like, The plot line was again a work of genius, just like the first one, I loved it so much I have the next book, The Demon Bride on my TBR list, Highly recommend to anyone after a fantastic love story, 5/5

Summary: A family secret kept hidden has been exposed, and the consequences could be deadly.

I loved Haunted Moon, so loved it when Compulsion was finally re-edited and released, I was not disappointed, Compulsion has lived up to all my expectations and more from this author, The characters each had their part to play and the author portrayed them beautifully, I loved the family dynamic even when they were under attack, Lilyann Moon didn't understand why she was left the farm from her beloved grandma, why were they all given the jewellery? Author: Dianna Hardy
Fiction, Paranormal,

I was given this by the author for an honest review
Summary: (Book One of the Eye of the Storm series)
Lydia Martin has always had dreams, the weirdest and hottest of them all involving a faceless, muscle-bound man that speaks like sin and smells like sex. Like any sane person, she always put the dreams down to an overactive imagination, coupled with a higher than average libido.
One night, however, instead of their usual, erotic encounters, she finds him in her dream, chained to a wall and screaming in pain. Not only that, but she thinks she recognises the building he's being held captive in as one that's just a few streets away. Awaking with an irrepressible need to save her fantasy lover, Lydia decides to humour her dream self and head on over to where she thinks he's imprisoned.
What unfolds is beyond even her wildest imaginings, as she's sucked into a dangerous and deadly world she never knew existed ... and it turns out that the man who inhabits her darkest fantasies, isn't the only one that needs releasing.
NOTE: This is an adult paranormal fantasy novella (over 34,000 words) containing scenes of explicit sexual content and some violence, entwined with romantic elements.

The Review
Well I saw the author talk about this on facebook and I thought mmmm sounds just up my street and do you know what? It was, I really loved this book, I am so looking forward to Book 2,  I cannot wait to hear more about The Pack, Ryan, Lawrence and my favourite tortured soul Taylor, The little teaser at the back of the book, OK, The epilogue, promises there will be a lot more to look forward to, This is definitely only for over 18's, Lydia was a very complex character, who did not know what she was, she actually made an appointment to see a therapist, she was having doubts about herself, but pulled herself together when she needed to, She could stick up for herself when it was called for, her dreams were wicked and I hope I get dreams like that, *Hot* I loved all the main male characters, each had their own complexities, Lawrence (the researcher and muscle) Ryan (The Muscle and Leader) and Taylor (The male with issues and the muscle) Did I say Muscle? Yeah there was a lot of it, I could picture each of them in my head and saw the whole book play out as a film, I love when I can picture a book like that, Book 2 will be highly anticipated on my kindle, recommended to all my friends, 5/5

Summary: In a seedy Goth club, a beautiful woman dances, waiting to be set free. Along an unlit street, another woman stumbles, fleeing her pursuer. In a darkened room, a man speaks to demons.
Lust, obsession, terror and humiliation storm into the lives of Star and Satori, proving the age-old maxim - be careful what you wish for.
Starblood, the debut novel by Carmilla Voiez, is a tale of magic and horror.
Blinded by love, Satori, a young magician, attempts a spell that goes horribly wrong, resulting in the demon Lilith returning to Earth. Satori knows he must send Lilith back. The dark goddess brimming with power makes it her mission to wreak havoc on Satori's life by ensnaring Star, the woman he loves, and her friends in a web of chaos and deceit.
`Carmilla Voiez makes Clive Barker look like Stephanie Meyer.' Jef Withonef, Houston Press.
The Review
I liked this book but I did get a little confused, it was probably my own fault, tried to read it while the kids were home, not a good idea, kept getting interrupted, but I really needed to read this one, I have heard such great things about it, so I will say this you really need to give this book your whole attention,  Once the kiddies went to bed, I settled down for the night and got really quite engrossed, I loved Star, I really liked how her character changed throughout the book,  Lilith was a psycho but then she was a demon, I would love to have gotten away with some of the stuff she got away with, I believe she subconsciously was killing bad men, won't say who but two were very bad men, The author made me feel Sorry for Satori/Steve but sometimes I felt like he brought it all on himself, but I can understand why he tried to do what he did, all for Love, gets us all in the end, read this book, you won't regret it, 4.5/5

Ebook: Smoke & Mirrors, Book 2 in the Blood & Light Series
Author: Rue Volley
Fiction, Paranormal,
This review may contain spoilers
I was given this for an honest review by the author
Summary: Book two in the Blood & Light Vampire series takes Rue, our teenage vampire, even deeper into the rabbit-hole that has become her life. This book introduces a deeper look into the vampire city of Valon That all vampires derive from. It begins taking a darker turn as you are invited into their world and their lack of compassion for the human race and, even in some cases, a total disregard for their own kind. As the story twists and turns, you are also introduced to two new vampires, Jonah & Lily. They are the sister/brother team, who run a traveling carnival, luring unsuspecting humans into their lair, not only to seduce...but to feed upon.
Rue faces many dangers in this addition, not only from her own kind...but this new vampire breed...that of the rogues, who serve no one but themselves and their own desires. Rue also struggles with her want to be "normal", as she comes to terms with the fact that she is indeed a vampire of great importance. As she navigates her way through this, she is also coming to realize that Joshua Barrington has seduced her and perhaps stolen her heart.
Please join us as you find yourself sucked deeper into an epic story in the life of one girl, who has good intentions but may indeed be her own worst enemy. Book two is more graphic in nature...with language, sexual situations, and violence. Sure to make you laugh, cry...and realize that sometimes you find yourself standing at the corner of WTF and OMG.
The Review
OMG, Miss Volley has done it again, She had me hooked with the first one Blood & Light but this series just keeps getting better, I love how Josh would do anything for Rue, I was ecstatic when they finally bonded and Rue realised that she loved him,  This plot just keeps getting better and better, Rue really pulls you in, I have laughed and cried with this book, that to me is a great book, I want to get me a Josh, he is just perfect, well to me he is, I love Jonah and Lily, the rogues, did you use Johnny Depp as inspiration for Jonah, he just has that feel to him, like Hunter, from your Hunter's Blood series, I just love Jonah and how they are settling in with everyone, I am really looking forward to book 3 Oil & Water, 6/5

Summary: When witch for hire, Megan Stephens, is assigned to help the local werewolf pack leader find a mate, she thinks the job will be easy. Get in, get it up and get gone. But when she meets Zack Connor, she realizes her future might have a lot more dog jokes in it than she ever imagined.
The Review
I loved this book, The fact that we have witches and werewolves in the same book was great, Zack is the alpha leader in this book, and if he doesn't find a mate, the whole pack will go into disarray, this is where Megan is sent in, hired by his mother to try and sort out Zack, so he can attract his mate, Wolves mate for life and so it has to be just the right woman, Zack can tell when his mate is in the vicinity, he can sense his mate but does not realise who it is, So Megan has to find ways of getting the mate out in the open, so Zack can see her, he believes she is hiding in the office black, they even try doing a fire drill but he can't tell which one she is, I love this story, an alpha wolf who would rather do his daily job than worry about wolf politics, Caroline's writing was amusing, she put plenty of comical moments in this book, I had plenty of giggles and yet, it gave me a little insight to the workings of a wolf pack, 4/5

My favourite so far in this series, I know I have said this on each one but this one is a true love story, there are ups and downs in most stories but Zaureth is a tortured soul who deserves his piece of heaven, I loved Zaureth in the other books, he has suffered in silence for many years, Amy is the one person who brings light to his life even though there is none in hers, he deserves this story, they both do. The story flows perfectly, there is just the right amount of action, love and that awesome happy ending.

My parents lent me this for a plane trip back home (but made me promise to hang onto it for them), and I'm glad they did. It took me awhile to get into it, mostly because it can be so painful watching a main character suffer quite as many indignities as this one has to, but the mystery was fascinating, the time and place were very well rendered, and Pliney really grew on me as he met the challenge of uncovering an increasingly dangerous secret. It was a very satisfying read.

This is a funny, honest, and thoughtful look at what it means to grow a garden when everything around you seems intent on eating it before you can, and your dreams and plans vastly outrun your available time.  It's a relief to hear that I'm not the only gardener screwing up over things like trying to harvest leeks in the middle of winter, and it's instructive to learn along with the author that "There's no such thing as an organic apple in the Northeast."  Alexander is also very funny while describing the human economy surrounding a garden, from possibly psychopathic hired help to the inevitable tensions that arise when a garden becomes part of the family.  Anybody who reads and gardens and has even the slightest sense of humor will thoroughly enjoy this book.

A fun light mystery. I'm not a big mystery reader myself, but I was attracted by the cover and the organic farming idea. However, the characters were well drawn and the mystery well plotted and the writing is actually much better than some popular women's fiction I've tried recently. (This one might also appeal to history buffs and folks near Bucks County, PA just as much as organic farming fans.) The small town setting is perhaps the most charming aspect here -- the author has done a great job establishing a strong sense of place with a set of quirky characters who could conceivably want to murder each other in it. I will probably look for the next book in the series the next time I want a break from heavier reading.

I picked this up and read it quickly because I was in the mood for something light and intrigued by the product description of a cranky Hispanic hero (what can I say ... he sounded like my husband). It's a pleasant, capable mystery that clearly knows and takes full advantage of its setting, and doesn't ignore the class and ethnic differences roiling there. It all seemed plausible and the romance had enough sparks to keep me reading on my tiny old iPhone. It seemed very short, though, and perhaps a bit cozier than my tastes run these days. If you're in the mood for a cozy mystery, literally set in a tea room, this is definitely worth a read. I didn't notice any distracting editing or writing issues, either -- it's quite professionally done.
I will also note that 1) I don't know the author at all, and 2) while I would normally give five stars because there's nothing wrong with it and my failure to "love" it is simply the fault of my own personal taste, Amazon seems to be taking a dim view right now of authors who never give fewer than five stars to other writers... so I'm just liking it, because that's how I honestly feel about it. If you love cozy mysteries and aren't completely right-wing in your political views, I think you will enjoy this book.

This has been the base for quite a few fast and easy meals in our house.  It stands alone, but it's great with greens from the garden layered into the bowl before the soup gets poured in. I often add dried shitake mushrooms or leftover meat or a few frozen shrimp to the broth while it's heating up. My son likes it with dried seaweed added. I've since found this for less at our local food coop, but if I didn't have that, I'd likely stock up here because these little packets are just so handy to have around, especially for a quick meal for one. You WILL need a pot to boil water in to cook this because the noodles require three minutes of boiling. I suppose you could do it in a microwave and somehow get it right, but it's not going to be as easy. (The ones in the cups are better for that.)

This flavor is very nice -- fairly spicy without being hot. I do miss the lemongrass and chili flavor, though. Apparently that only comes in the cups now.

Fair disclosure: The author has become a friend. However, I really enjoyed this lively romance quite apart from that. It kept me so entertained on a flight down to visit the folks in Florida that my seat mates kept having to get my attention for stuff like the flight attendant's ginger ale. I barely noticed the time pass.

Phoebe is a fun character who gives as good as she gets, doesn't dwell on anything that goes badly, and just charges ahead to solve some pretty basic problems like figuring out how to not starve to death and keep a roof over her and her siblings' heads. For an inexperienced girl she sure doesn't mind putting it all on the line to get what she needs, and though the reader can't help wondering whether it's going to work out at times, you don't have to worry about an unhappy ending here.

Weger writes with style and verve. If you enjoy straight romance and a down-to-earth Gulf Coast setting, you're going to be all set with this one!

I think I got this book free or really cheap and didn't have high expectations for it, but it really pulled me in and kept me reading. The author has a plainspoken style and a raw honesty that honors a troubled, fascinating man and a complicated, fascinating relationship. It is heartfelt without ever dipping into sentimentality. I am very glad to have read it.

This is a fascinating exploration of public shaming in an age of social media (and before), with some really compelling case studies. It's both serious in its intent and really entertaining. I laughed out loud at some wonderful sentences, like "It seemed appropriate that we were hiking in a desert canyon, because his punishment felt quite biblical, a public shaming followed by a casting out into the wilderness, although that analogy only went so far because biblical wildernesses tend not to be filled with extremely beautiful movie stars and models walking their dogs." Also: "For the first hundred years, as far as I could tell, all that happened in America was that various people named Nathaniel had purchased land near rivers." Ha! Read it in a matter of hours, too. I got it to do some research, but it was a real delight.

While this is a practical and fun way to garden which I am implementing myself this year, I have to say a few things have NOT been as easy as the book made it sound:

1.  The author suggests mixing all the bed ingredients on a tarp with another person, then dragging it to the beds.  I found that just the ingredients for one 4 x 6 bed were too heavy to lift and drag with my son, and was thankful I hadn't tried to mix all my beds at once as suggested (wouldn't have fit on the tarp anyway).  You're going to need real strong help with this part.  I next tried just mixing the stuff in the beds but that was difficult too.  If you are not a football player or are working alone, getting these beds filled is going to be a bigger challenge than you would guess from your reading.  I also found it took more material to fill my beds than the book suggested, but then I noticed the peat moss and vermiculite bags and bales I bought were not quite as big as the book suggests; those sizes simply weren't available in my area, apparently.

2. Vermiculite is hard to find and expensive, though I agree it's probably worth it.  I've only found it at Agway so far and I live in a fairly agricultural area.

3. I could definitely have used a little more specific help with the compost.  It usually comes in 30 lb or 40 lb bags -- would it have been so hard to suggest how many would probably make up the amount needed for one 4 x 4 bed?  I feel I've pretty much had to eyeball this one, which has meant extra trips to the store.  The instruction to use five different types is a pain too, since most stores around here carry the same three options, including humus that is surely very similar in make-up to the peat mosse.  The author appears to live in some sort of retail compost & vermiculite paradise.

4. Raised beds are not necessarily ideal for drought, which we had here in early spring (that has since reversed itself big time).  The beds dry out so quickly I'm not sure it would even be safe to leave them for a weekend.  I would think people in chronically dry areas might want to modify the mix so it's not quite so light, or dig their square foot beds DOWN, not up.  (Not easy, I know.)

5.  This book must have been rushed through editing; two sections on basil that say pretty much the same thing are clearly redundant.

On the plus side, the approach makes a lot of sense as a way to cope with poor soil, and advice about the individual plants is very good too.  Just make sure that if this is for your poor old Grandma, she gets a lot of strong help (and some extra $$) to get it going.

I have over the years owned an evolution of home stereo equipment.
I own a pair of Super. Fi 5 EBs -- as I needed something "small" and portable.
I've inherited several Beats headphones... for bluetooth capability, or pure novelty... but I *knew* what I was listening to was complete crap.

I never truly had a need for headphones. The EBs did satisfy the basshead in me, and the quality was better than anything I had heard in an earphone or headphone.

I tossed around the idea of buying these for many years. I am glad I finally did! I won't get into the subjective here, but these are the headphones for me. A little bit more fun than flat for me. Flat is optimal, but fun is more important-- and this is why I chose HD650s over HD600s in the long run.

They are great headphones. I power them from:

Modern Denon AVR
(2005?) Onkyo AVR
Schlitt Magni 2

All of which have sufficient power. You can google for hours about what amp you "need":

Plugging them directly into a mobile device, laptop, or older USB soundcard does produce sound. It's not a whisper.
Plugging them directly into my ASUS Xonar PCIE Sound Card also produces sound...
It's also not loud.

Of all my mobile devices, the Ipad Pro seems to be able to slightly elevate the volume more than any other phone or android tablet I have laying around, but nothing in comparison to something purposed to drive headphones.

It's not a joke -- buy an amp. If you have an AVR... I really would be hard pressed to tell you that my Magni 2 / FIIO DAC sounds better than my Denon or Onkyo with a digital input. I can *technically* turn the Magni 2 up all the way on high gain-- I would not dare turn the AVRs past half.

So... YMMV but as far as I'm concerned.. I have two very large and powerful headphone amps in my AVRs and a purpose-built small amp for the road that does a wonderful job at listening volumes.

Buy an amp. Experiment with a parametric EQ if you feel something is missing. It's okay, no one has to know.

Edit:
I will add two bits.

The first pair came defective, and the return process went wonderfully.
There was a slight buzz in one driver at volume with bass. This was my worst nightmare about ordering something like this online.
They cross-shipped, next-day, and I had zero problems with the return.

(This could obviously end badly-- I noticed this within a few days thanks to a popular song about the removal of masks. It is entirely possible someone who cares about their hearing would not have)

I was hoping this book would be as good as "Foreskin's Lament" but I was terribly disappointed.  "Hope" is a boring non stop kvetchy psychosis of Kugel (the main character) who is the stereotype of a worrisome, thinks too much nerdy Jewish Man with the classic affliction of celiac disease and a god awful Mother.  There is nothing appealing about this character or any character in this book.  Even the 3 year old son is portrayed as a sickly screaming unattractive child.  The book starts with a promising premise; that Anne Frank survived and has been hiding out in attics all this time.  Kugel finds her in the attic of the home he just purchased.  Anne is now an old ugly mean bag of bones who stinks up the house.  Kugel, his Mother and Anne are forever having bowel movements in the wrong places.  Not pleasant at all.  Then some nasty throw up session is added to make the book even more disgusting then it already is.  Why Kugel's wife stays as long as she does is beyond me or any reader.  Take Philip Roth's character's and Woody Allen at their possible worst without any intelligence or humor and you have this book.  Seriously awful.
I have had enough of these kind of books.  about slaves, dying babies, depressing times....one too many of these books.  depressing themes.

The book starts of well and with intrigue but gets bogged down.  Just doesn't go anyplace and gets boring.  I had no empathy or feelings towards the main character; in fact she was starting to really annoy the heck out of me.  Book lasted about 60 pages when I put it down.

Kristy Bromberg WOWS me once again. What can I say that will truly do this book or Kristy Bromberg justice? I'm having a hard time finding just the right words to express how much I really loved this book. Aced surpasses all my expectations and then some. For me, Aced is about truly honoring and living out the vows of marriage. For better or worse, in sickness and health...sticking it out when the going gets tough and you don't think you can take one more thing. It's about selfless love and support of family and so, so much more.
Okay, let's start with the negative...the ONLY negative is that I'm so very sad to let go of Colton & Rylee. I could read about them and their family forever. Finishing Aced was bittersweet for me because as good as it was, I'm just not ready to say goodbye. Now, the positives. There's just WAY too many positives to mention. I really wish I was better with my words so I could properly express how much I enjoyed reading Aced. First, it was absolutely worth the wait! Once again, Kristy, brings out every emotion possible. The feel-good-moments, the angst, the tears of joy and sorrow, the laughter, the anger, and the sexy times...every single emotion. Kristy is an AMAZING writer and through her words, her readers are able to really know her characters and feel what they are going through. She has this brilliant way with words that enables us to visualize her characters, scenes, interactions, etc. so vividly in our minds like a movie playing in our heads.

Most obvious in this final book is the growth of Colton Donovan as a man, a husband, a father, a son. I was in awe at just how far this character has come since the beginning of Driven. Still cocky as ever (which I love), but he discovers the strength within himself to be the husband and the light for Rylee when she truly needs him to be HER lifeline. As I was reading, I was reminded of a time in Crashed when Becks says to Rylee, "That lifeline thing goes both ways...Use it. Use him. He won't break if you do...but you just might if you don't." And, that statement means more in Aced than it ever did before! Luckily, like in all the other Driven books, we are treated to several other impactful words of wisdom throughout Aced whether it's from Becks, Andy, Dorothea, Rylee's Mom, Haddie...you name it! All "quoteworthy".

I could go on and on with my review but it would become a lot of rambling I'm afraid. To sum up my review, I LOVED Aced and if you loved Colton & Rylee and the rest of the gang in the other Driven books, then you are going to love Aced! Colton & Rylee truly do come full-circle! Kudos to you Kristy. Well done. You did not disappoint. You did Colton & Rylee good!

Again, there was potential there to like these characters, perhaps with more character development. It disappoints me to say that I didn't enjoy this book like I have some of her others. That being said, I will keep trying with future books because I have really enjoyed some of Ms. Lynn's other books. This one just misses the mark for me personally.

I have enjoyed reading many of Sandi Lynn's books. Sadly, this one did not give me warm, fuzzy feelings. I liked how the book started out and I thought the storyline had great potential. However, I felt like the writing was very choppy with not a lot of flow to it. Story felt rushed to me and I really struggled with forming a connection with the characters. Again, there was potential there to like these characters, perhaps with more character development. It disappoints me to say that I didn't enjoy this book like I have some of her others. That being said, I will keep trying with future books because I have really enjoyed some of Ms. Lynn's other books. This one just misses the mark for me personally.

I loved reading Graham's book. He was always the serious one. Always in control. Until a fiery brunette falls into his office and changes everything. You will easily fall in love with Graham & Mallory. Their story is filled with lots of sexy times, good times and humor. I really enjoyed this book. Definitely a fun and easy read.

Another good, entertaining read. Would've liked to seen some more character development. I felt like I needed more, but there is another one coming out soon. I'm used to seeing more conflict for the couples, so almost feel like Lily and Luke need some "complications" to deal with. Overall, I enjoyed reading this, but need more story.

HOLY S&%T...If you haven't read Meghan March's Beneath series you absolutely need to get started! I've loved each one of the books in this series, but I have to say that Beneath These Lies is by far the BEST one yet (and they are all GREAT)! BTL is nothing that you think it will be and the main characters in this one are nobody you could dream them up to be! Simply put...AMAZING, INTRIGUING, STEAMY HOT. Okay, so...maybe not so simply put!
This one is a DEFINITE read! You won't regret it!
Kudos to Meghan March. You sure know how to write a good story with sexy, Alpha males! Well done!

I had no idea what to expect from this book. This was my first Kylie Scott book. Im thrilled to say that I was NOT disappointed!! I loved this book. OMG...her writing is awesome. I laughed so hard, I teared up. Mostly, I enjoyed the heck out of it! Vaughan and Liddy are hilarious together. Their easygoing, witty banter made this book! The sexiness was hot too, but mixed right in with their unconventional meeting, etc. The supporting characters were great too! Looking forward to reading more about them. LOVED it! Definitely will be reading more!
OMG...this book. I couldn't put it down. Ryan is dreamy for sure and Sofia is a rockstar. These two together are refreshing. Loved this book and their story. Well done Toni Aleo!

Finally, we get Rhett Hennessy's book! It was definitely worth the wait. Loved this book just like I love this series. You will love Ariel too. This book has everything: love, sexiness, suspense, intense...lots of feels. Definitely read this book!
Kristen Proby does it again. I'm so glad she saved Savannah and Ben for last! They were perfect for each other. Such a great book.

Once again, Meghan March has made me fall in love with another couple! I loved this book. Cal and Greer were HOT! I'm not sure anybody writes hot sex stuff like Ms March! And HOLY PLOT TWISTS BATMAN!! She is Queen of the plot twist!
Definitely read this book. It can be read without reading the Dirty Billionaire series first, but personally I think starting with DB first is better! Gives additional insight into characters and storylines. 5 stars all the way!!!

Fenton and Brynne are hot from the very start. This book is full of sexy times, new love and a bit of intrigue and mystery. I definitely recommend this book. Adrianna Locke has quickly become one of my favorite authors.
Loved this book. Ryder and Nicole are great apart and together. A fun, easy read with delicious sexiness too. I really enjoyed this book.

Wow. This one was a tear jerker. But, definitely worth reading. I loved it. Tate is a strong, independent female. And Miles...well, Miles makes you want to just hug him. He's such a tortured soul and feels undeserving of love because of his past. Tate makes him see that loving someone can be beautiful again. Loved this book!

Ok...I admit. After looking at mostly all 5 star reviews for The Retrieval, I hesitated. I thought to myself, "Is it possible that this book is really THAT good?". I mean, almost all 5 star reviews...that's too good to be true. Except, it's not! The Retrieval by Aly Martinez IS REALLY THAT GOOD!

This is book one of a duet about 2 different couples whose lives become very intertwined with the other. And, if you're one of those people who don't like to start a duet or series until book two is released...you're in luck because book 2 was just released this week!

The story is written from multiple POV, which I absolutely loved. You will easily fall in love with all of the characters in this story. Well, most of them. You'll have to read it to find that out!  It's got a bit of everything including love, romance, marriage, humor, second chances, suspense, alpha males, sexy times and a few teary moments.  This book had me intrigued from the very first page and had me sitting on the edge of my seat! I loved everything about The Retrieval!

I have loved all of Ms Proby's book series, but Book one in the Fusion series just might be my favorite one yet! So many good things about this book. First, Jake & Addie are awesome. Love their chemistry. And then we've got the 5 friends. I really enjoyed reading about these 5 strong women. I'm eagerly waiting to read each of their books because I have no doubt they will be great. I've never been disappointed with a Kristen Proby book! Love, love, love this book!

Another book in the Assassins series. This book was so much fun to read. Wren was such a relatable heroine as she deals with her own insecurities, yet she comes across as being very secure to others. This is something many women can relate to. And, Jensen...let's talk about what a wonderful man he is. He is always saying and doing the right things. He is like the perfect guy. What isn't there to love about him? I highly recommend this book.

Omg...Lauren Rowe does it again. I absolutely love Captain! Ryan Morgan is my favorite Morgan brother. He is hot and passionate and cocky yet sweet at the same time. He is everything wrapped up into one man. Ryan and Tessa are super hot together. Explosive. Reminded me a lot of Jonas and Sarah from The Club books. Job well done Lauren Rowe. I really loved this book!
Jennings and Violet were so much fun! I laughed, smiled and loved! Just the right amount of romantic comedy mixed in with some fun sexy times! Loved this book! Highly recommend reading Sure Thing!

users.query: Bought this for my 12 year old Little and she LOVES it! She loved making it--said it wasn't hard, but wasn't too easy either--and took her about an hour.

cands.text: So...this took me 2  hours to put together by myself. But it was worth it!! I put the back on backwards so it's black instead of white and I love it!
My pup LOVES this! She tore up the "tree' part pretty quickly, but had a blast doing so!
It didn't really teach my anything. I guess it could be a nice gift for a younger sibling in or right after college.

It's easy to use, and my dog doesn't seem to mind it at all, but it doesn't hold the hairs very well. I usually end up sitting in a pile of loose hairs, and it doesn't appear to have helped with hair around the house either. Still a good brush, and I'll keep using it anyhow.
This compilation of short stories was great at first--until it became so repetitive I didn't even want to finish it. I hoped so badly to love it, but after finishing it, I can't recommend it.
Definitely for a first-time user. It's kind of loud but it doesn't bother me.
Easy to install, and looks great! Just as pictures. Plus, good price for a Moen product.

So my boyfriend got an XBox One, and of course hooked our entire entertainment center up to it. The actual controller is super touchy and I kept accidentally forwarding/rewinding movies and shows when I just wanted to move the controller out of the way. This is so much easier for me. The buttons actually make sense, and no accidental button pushing!

Definitely for crafting purposes only. A couple already broke, but for the price and how small they are, I wasn't expecting much. Still functional is you're careful with them! I just wanted to put up pictures in my office without destroying the walls, so I did a clothesline type of thing, and it worked out well.
So far, it's sturdy and seems well made. Glad we got this!

I bought this for my parents for Christmas and they LOVE it! They had an electrician install it, and he has an older version installed in his home, so he was able to show my dad how the app works. He also told my dad this version is much nicer than his, and seemed a little jealous haha. The copper color looks beautiful and matched their decor perfectly. According to my dad, this is a must-have!
This is everything I hoped for and more! It's bigger than it looks, yet still small enough to not be too much. I love it!
I'm very happy I bought this set! Just as described, at a great price, and good quality.

My dog doesn't really play with toys, but will occasionally chew one of her bones when no one is watching. I opened this and gave it to her, and immediately took it to her bed and chewed it for almost an hour. Very happy I bought this!

My dog doesn't really play with toys, but will occasionally chew one of her bones when no one is watching. I opened this and gave it to her, and immediately took it to her bed and chewed it for almost an hour. Very happy I bought this!
I was hesitant about this, even with all the other good reviews--but SERIOUSLY. This smells so good, and my dog doesn't even notice. She just thinks she's getting a full on pet/scratch session lol

I've only had this for 24 hours, so actual air cleaning results are TBD. This arrived quickly, and looks beautiful! The highest fan speed gives off a white noise type loudness, but even 1 level below is significantly quieter. I like the white noise, but my dog didn't seem too pleased about it :-P One level down though and she was fine.
It's bigger than I expected, but still a great design!

This is exactly what I needed! It was easy to program my TV, DVD player, and even my streaming box. I bought the streaming box for less than $20 at WalMart about 5-6 years ago, and of course it came with a crappy little remote. Well the remote was only about 1/2 functional as of 2 years ago, so I tried contacting the manufacturer, searched message boards, and tried a few other universal remotes and my only option was to buy the exact crappy remote new from the manufacturer for $10 +S&H. So when I tried this one, it was with zero expectation and it actually worked! I have never been more excited over a remote in my life!
practice a couple times before needing to use it and you'll be fine!
Really strong! It's not very flexible, so it was awkward on my wrist, but I bought it for my dad and it fit his wrist just fine. It'll definitely come in handy (..or rather, hand-free)!
The pockets are indeed extra deep (I have a 13" mattress with a 2" memory foam topper). Soft, good material, and true to color.
It's an awesome idea, but the holes are a little too big and doesn't quite keep the tea from filling my mug anyhow. Still super funny to me, tho!
Sturdy and seems to be a good product...but my dog won't play with it.

My boyfriend and I recently moved into a new apartment in which my box spring didn't fit in the elevator or stairwell. This was perfect for us! Lightweight enough, and we got into our apartment with no trouble at all. Set up was super simple, and when we move out we won't have that giant headache again! It's sturdy, quiet, and we've both been sleeping great.

users.query: I love my slow cooker.  It is large enough to cook a large roast and vegetables.  It does tend to get a bit hot so you have to remember to add plenty of liquid.  I especially like the locking lid feature- makes it really convenient when taking it to carry-in dinners, etc.

cands.text: Nice, heavy whisks. Displayed in a crock on my counter with other utensils. Look great with my stainless steel kitchen. Worth every penny!

I love my Kitchen aide Artisan stand mixer, but when getting it out to mash potatoes got to be too big a hassle, I went on the hunt for a handheld mixer.  This one is great- works well and stores well.

I purchased 4 pan rack / organizers (varying types) to help unclutter my pull-out pantry drawer which held 2 sets of stainless steel- one Emeril and one Cuisinart.

I placed this rack on its side for lids and smaller saut pans. I am able to store 2 lids in some of the slots. Then I placed this rack sitting upright so I can stack the larger skillets. I am very pleased with the outcome- the drawer looks so much neater.  My only complaint is my largest skillet barely fits. It's a very tight squeeze.

We ordered this fan for our bedroom/bathroom. It runs fairly quietly and is more powerful than another Lasko model that we have elsewhere in the house. It is also compact and does not take up a lot of floor space
This was exactly what I needed! My thick, heavy queen sized Croscill comforter fit in with no difficulty. The container is plastic but substantial enough to last a while.

Got this as a Christmas gift for a daughter in law.  It is convenient (small enough to tuck away in a purse or tote bag) but sturdy enough to hold a camera steady for great pictures using a timer or for videoing.

My husband and I watched this and he liked it a bit more than I did (violence and language probably being the main reasons.) In general, we like movies by both Wahlburg and Washington. Of course, it was heavy on the action. This one was a little confusing at first and took a while to get into the story. For that reason I gave it 4, rather than 5, stars

Of course, it was heavy on the action. This one was a little confusing at first and took a while to get into the story. For that reason I gave it 4, rather than 5, stars

I truly love Karen Nueburger's sleepwear because it is always so soft and comfortable. This nightshirt did not disappoint- silky soft against the skin.  It did run a little larger than expected though.  I typically wear an XL so that's what I ordered... it's pretty loose, but that's okay to sleep in.

I bought this blender to use for making frozen drinks... margaritas, daquiris, etc.  I looked at the machines specifically for making "frozen concoctions", but settled on this one because of the price difference and also because the other machines were too large for my kitchen counter.  I'm very happy with it.  I used ice straight from the refrigerator ice-maker, along with either liquid or frozen mixers.  The end result was smooth and creamy, just like the ones from commercial machines - no little ice chunks to clog your straw! This blender has an ice-crushing feature that automatically pulses while in use to prevent overheating the motor. I did find that adding a little extra liquid (juice or even water) helped to keep it running smoothly.  Great buy.
