I purchased this some years ago and finally the strap split.  So I had to order another one, it's very sturdy and I just love it.

users.query: We got the first one from a win on Facebook. My daughter loved the series. She has already read this book, and is on book 3. Book 4 comes out soon, and I will be getting it.

cands.text:
I received this book in exchange for my honest review.

First off, this is book three and book 1 and 2 must be read prior to understand what's going on better in 3. If you have read the previous books then there is no way you won't want to read this. Three is even better than the first book! I love the bet that Astrid makes with Erik at the end! Happy reading! Again, my only complaint...it's too short! Just put the 3 or so parts together and make a novel. Enough with the suspense of waiting! Ha ha
I absolutely enjoyed all the danger, laughs, shifting and lovemaking this book had to offer. I will be getting book 2 and 3 for sure!

I really liked this book a lot. The end has me wanting to buy book 2 and 3 because it's left on a cliffhanger. I was easily able to follow the characters on their journey and picture all the scenes. It was fun to get lost in this book by L. Filloon.
I just finished reading this, and I liked it very much and am looking forward to book 2 in the series! I can't believe it left off with a cliff hanger!

Read this in the box set. It's best to read this series back to back because there is no recap of the previous book in the next book. I finished this within 2 days. Would have been less, but life gets in the way. This is the best book of a series start I have read in a while, aside from Carlotte's Sanctuary series. She has such unique ideas on stories! This is about a family of back woods mages that are on the run from a rival mage clan. It's really unique to read that each mage get's their power from the power name they are given. I'm in love with this series, and do not want it to end.

Really enjoyed this book. Yet again another cliffhanger. My only con is the the book does not do a recap of the previous book, or have more physical descriptive recaps of the characters. I mean there are some about hair color and height of main characters. Oh, and FYI this one had me crying a litter! Good read overall.

I received this book direct from the author. This has no effect on my review.

This is book 3. If you've read this far it means you love the series, and loved this book. You cannot read this one without reading book 1 and 2. Otherwise you would be lost trying to follow what happens. I loved this book. I just wish there was an epilogue to show more of what happens after everything. I know there is a book just about Gabriel so maybe that's my follow up to the story. Happy reading!

I was given a free ARC of this book in exchange for my honest review. So, this Draglen brother is my favorite by far! This is the fourth book in the series. I recommend reading them all, and in order. I skipped Layern, and was a bit baffled at times because I lacking the knowledge of what happened in the previous book. This book has a different POV than the other three books. I actually enjoyed the new take on it. Gemi, a dragon shifter, is very aggressive, and has been following his future wella for six months before approaching her. This is because she is a witch. Witches and Dragons are enemies. It has great "adult scenes". Also, something new, it had danger and violent action. I loved when Gemi and Shalisi were out in positions of dire peril. It made for a riveting read. If you haven't read this series yet, please do. Some scenes had me laughing out loud, others made me want a nice night with my other half.
I loved ever page of Shooting Stars by Karina Halle! I am looking forward to getting my hands on the third chapter in the desirable series.

First off I definitely should have read the first and second book prior to the third. Not reading the first two made a lot of things confusing, and maybe left out certain meanings to things said or done. I liked the concept of the book, and the visual I got with the details. In ways there were too many details. There could have been more dialect. I could skip pages here and there, and still know what was going on. A really good book makes me want to read every word. It was an okay quick read though. I read it in one night. Zoey has great writing ideas, and an eye for detail for surroundings.

This is the first book in the series I've read. I adored it for it being a contemporary! My fav is historical. I recommend this book for a good short read! The cover is very inviting as well. High fives to Erika Wilde on this great story!

I am a huge fan of Charlotte Abel's writing!  I read book 1 a while back. I can't believe I waited this long to read book 2. Now I need 3. Charlotte builds an intricate story world for us to live in. It's really neat how "New Eden" is it's own place yet also in Colorado. I was engrossed in the book as soon as I picked it up. It's a take on shifters I love to read about. I love the details with well developed characters. This is a must read for those who like shifter books.

This book was full of mixed emotions. In the beginning it opens up with twin sisters who are both pregnant and due around the same time. What surprised me was it was more about one of the babies and not the twins. It was a good book though and had me hooked page for page.

Don't like it as much as the previous, but it was a great addition to the Rougemont series! I enjoyed the "rough" characters and their colorful backgrounds! I enjoyed her writing style very much! Could add a bit more whitty comments in this one to make me laugh though like the first book of the series.
I enjoyed this book and thought how funny it was neither of them knew who the other was til closer to the end. I want to read more of her books.

This is the "third" book of the Rougemont series, and I adored it! There was one small part I thought the book could do without to speed it along. It was just a flashback of a fond memory between Drew and Lisa when they were younger towards the front of the book. I loved the fact that Moriah put Phillip in as a possible candidate for Lisa. It makes me want to read Phillip's story, and I wonder if Christian and Madeline will have a story. I thought it had a perfect ending to a perfect book. A witty book as always, and that's what I love because it makes me giggle at those parts. ;)

I could not put this book down! As soon as I finished book 1 I started book 2, Awaken. Kristen has me hooked. It is mythology, paranormal, contemporary, mystery, suspense and romance all in one! She captures the right amount of details to keep everything freely moving and interesting in the book. I can't predict what's going to happen next, and I love that! I love the sea, so I love reading this series. No, so far no one has a fish tale. It reminds me a little of Percy Jackson, but a girl instead of a guy. Pick this book up, there are several more to read after it and all re-releasing soon!

This book reminded me of the tv series Beauty and The Beast. I like that show, so its very easy to like this book. Not a whole lot of juicy sex scenes,  but the action and suspense makes up for it. I'm a hopeless romantic so I enjoyed the ending.  I look forward to the next Winter sisters book.
I really enjoyed the flow of this story. I liked how I was not totally able to predict the whole story. It was very sweet. I won't mind reading book 2.

As with the 3 previous Sanctuary series books I loved this one. However, I did feel like something more dire should have happened. I know this was a continuance book, but I think another bigger plot could have this series go on for another 3 or 4 books. Same fantastic writing was  displayed in this was as was before. Gabriel's Gift captured me, and held me hostage until I finished it through. I can't wait to read Paul's story one day, and Rose's story. One of my favorite scenes is at the end of the book, but I can't tell you why. ;)

I felt there wasn't enough to keep me totally interested to give it 4 stars. I love books about Indians and shifters. This wasn't what I expected. It does however make for a great folk tale or legend story.

This book was deserving of five stars! It is best read back to back with no other books in between. Charlotte gives a unique outlook on mages. I read all 3 books and 2 short stories in 8 days. It was too good to put down. There are some predicable plots, but also some unexpected twists and turns. The author also graciously included her first book of Sanctuary series(I've already read that one previously) and a prelude to the Sanctuary series. Channie's Daddy does something to anger a royal mage. It triggers a mage war to come. Channie's family packs up to live in a place with magically disabled people. There, a prophecy is born from a Book of The Dead and a powerful mage is revealed, but not until much turmoil is suffered. This series made me laugh, giggle, sigh and cry. This is one series I'd be happy to reread and "relive". The author created a story that came alive in my mind, and now I have to come down from a book "high". Thank you Charlotte for sharing this story.

A notorious rake and a shy blue stocking with many meetings in a library. "What a lovely novel." Or, is it "fiction"? This was a lovely book indeed. I can relate to Louisa on several levels. And I adore ALEX. I was kept entertained by the two weeks of party festivities whilst following the drama between Lord Xavier and his Coz, Lord Lockwood. Theresa, it appears LA Signora smokes way too many cigarillos. :) Didn't read book 1. Book 2 can be a stand alone. I saved this for a Christmas time read, but really it could have been read anytime.
I received this book in exchange for my honest review. For a novella this was a very enjoyable read, and funny turn of events. Just the right amount of story mixed with the right amount of romance.
I haven't gotten to use it yet. I did score it for a good price though. I wanted this because it's an open face but used like a bait cast.

users.query: Wow! This band has released a real powerful gem here. Every song is great but I especially like Termination, Sidewinder and Empires Never last. The singer is great with quite a range. I'm glad I discovered this band. Amerigus needs to discover these guys. I recommend to start with the DVD. It's a great show.

cands.text: Solid CD from these prog metal rockers. Great riffs from the guitar department. I really like this band and I think they are on the threshold of making a classic CD. The second song is the best. Awesome Amerigus.

I always admired Ambrosia from a distance. I liked their singing and musicianship but I was always afraid of being accused of being a sissy for liking them. Anyhow, I finally broke down on the advise of other proggers and purchased this one. I have to say that I was shocked. These guys actually rock out. This music kind of reminds me of Kansas at the same time in the early 80s. I highly recommend this one.

This is a great DVD that features the entire World's Apart album and that would be enough. However there is a lot more including gems like Careful Where You Step, Humble Stance and a host of other great tracks. The band is in great form and they put on a great show. I really wish I could see them live but I seriously doubt they will ever get down this south. The whole package is nice including CDs of the concert and great photos. It's also amazing to see Saga of the early 80s in the Live in England segment. Excellent package Inside Out!

Great DVD that captures a great band. I am especially impressed with vocalist Rob Sowden- he is a remarkable frontman. I am also really impressed with John Mitchell's fascinating guitar work. The set list is quite a bit different than their previous DVD. I really like the songs from Immortal- "Waiting for the Flood" and "Friday's Dream" . The Visitor songs are great also. Thanks Arena for this great DVD.

This is an amazing Cd of hard rock prog tinged tunes. Ray Alder is awesome on vocals. This might be his best effort. And , that is really saying a lot because he's done such great work with Fates. The band is also solid creating some great songs. The drummer is especially interesting. This CD is worth checking out and I would love to see these guys continue. If they do, I have a feeling the best is yet to come.

This is a great live show featuring some great songs. Careful Where You Step opens the show in grand fashion. They also do songs from Full Circle which an ignoramus underrated on Amazon. They do Time Bomb and it rocks. I don't care what fools say-for my money, Saga is the best prog band out there. Fools criticize them because their musical vistas are limited by Weird Al ventures and metal bore fandangalos.

this is an outstanding CD featuring great prog tunes. I can't stop listening to it. My favorites are Frequency and The Province but all songs are great. And to top it off they throw in a great bonus DVD. This is a great show that has some new songs on it as well as classics. Sleepless Incidental is incredible with its spine tingling ending and The Seventh House will bring you to tears. This is a no brainer- 5 stars all the way for this fabulous release.

Awesome music, great vocalist make this a true winner. And add Matin Orford as a special guest and you've got yourself a great prog mix. This band is a great listen. The first 2 songs are more than worth the purchase. Nice that they did Ant's song and did it well.
Great CD from Queensryche.  The drumming is fantastic as always and the songs are great.  This incarnation of the band is relevant and worthy of the name.
GREAT ROCKING CD FROM THIS AWESOME GROUP. OFTEN UNDERAPPRECIATED GROUP. CHECK OUT ALL OF THEIR ALBUMS. I CONTEND THAT THERE IS NOT ONE WEAK ALBUM IN THEIR DISCOGROPHY. THIS ONE IS THEIR BEST.

This is an incredible new CD from SAGA. I found myself listening to this over and over again on a long road trip. Great instrumentals throughout the CD and the prog tinged rock keeps the listener's interest. These guys continue to impress and have not run out of gas. Highly recommended for the music. The bonus DVD is worthless and almost led me to dock a star- "The Making of Trust" is short and gives little insight into this terrific music.
This band captures an old 70s Trick of the Tail era sound while forging a unique modern quality. Vocals are great and the music is superb with a lot of spirit. This is truly a band to watch.
This band captures an old 70s Trick of the Tail era sound while forging a unique modern quality. Vocals are great and the music is superb with a lot of spirit. This is truly a band to watch.

This is an excellent example of great music. This CD puts Pallas in a position to take command of the other progressive greats out there such as IQ and Arena. Pallas has taken their time to construct dramatic, pasionate pieces of music that are both aggressive and beautiful. I would like to thank all the members of the band but a special note must be to Ronnie Brown. Brown is a killer keyboard player with interesting ideas all over the CD. During the fabulous "Too Close to the Sun" Brown seems to be channeling Genesis circa late 70s- what an incredible sound. In "Bringer of Dreams" he flies on the keyboard. Amazing musicianship throughout. It's wonderful how Pallas has really kept the prog going with "The Cross and the Crucible" and now with "The Dreams of Men". Absolutely essential for anyone that enjoys progressive music. Purchase this one now proggers!!!
Powerful statement from the band. This is rock at its finest. I saw them on this tour and boy were they awesome. Unfortunately, after this album, things started to go sour.
Gift from my wife for X-Mas. I like this band's approach. The EPIC songs are interesting and this band has a lot of promise. I will get more of their CDs in the future.

I have been a harsh critic of this band and their tendancy to go too far. This CD is a pleasant surprise and actually a shock because I was expecting it to stink after their previous "train wreck of thought". Three things struck me on this new CD:

1. They don't go too far with jams and excessive wankarama

2. Jordan finally fits into the band...instead of trying to outplay everyone on keys

3. The songs are melodic in the tradition of Awake

Really a good strong effort from the band.

I have been a harsh critic of this band and their tendancy to go too far. This CD is a pleasant surprise and actually a shock because I was expecting it to stink after their previous "train wreck of thought". Three things struck me on this new CD:

1. They don't go too far with jams and excessive wankarama

2. Jordan finally fits into the band...instead of trying to outplay everyone on keys

3. The songs are melodic in the tradition of Awake

Really a good strong effort from the band.

Good rock with some prog tinges that reminds me of the band Enchant. And, that's a good thing. The vocalist is powerful but at times delivers some weak performances. The first song is a good rocker but the vocals sound too Scorpionish. After that it gets much better ending on a great note with Critical Mass (Part 1-3). Definitely worth checking out and makes me interested in hearing their other CDs.

I love this CD. I guess it is the whole package, the mystery, and the great songs. The music proves the excellent musicianship-something I used to argue all the time. Eric Carr is a tremendous drummer. Ezrin really understood Kiss. (Destroyer and The Elder are tremendous;Revenge stinks)

Richard Matheson is my favorite author. This book is just one of many that he has written that is both captivating and creative. He has written books of many different genres. His westerns are great. I never thought I would like a western book.

From the first bass notes this CD takes you on a journey and moves you in ways only the greats like Genesis and Yes could. Of note is the outstanding creative vocals of Nichols that really stick with you long after you listen. Also, Mike Holmes really does some of his best guitar work of his long stellar career. And ofcourse I must mention the maestro Orford-absolute brilliance. Even staunch Pebozo who seems to think only bands in the 70s can make sincere progressive music likes this band. These guys are awesome. I would recommend all their CDs.

This new Saga CD put to rest my sadness that Sadler has left. I still miss Sadler but the new singer is dynamic and solid even leading to a  fresh sound. It reminds me of when Ray Wilson took over for Phil McLovin in Genesis. I just hope fans like fickle pickle Pedroza will give it a chance. All songs are good but my favorites are Crown of Thorns, Let it Go, Avalon and the captivating Step Inside with its triumphant chorus. This has to be the CD of the summer. Great job Saga!

SOME GREAT COMPOSITIONS HERE...NICE GREER VOCALS...WALSH AT TIMES SOUNDS FAR AWAY FROM THE MUSIC...NOT QUITE SURE THIS IS A GROUP EFFORT BUT NEVERTHELESS THIS IS A FUN LISTEN AND REMINDS ME OF THE GLORIOUS 70'S...SO TAKE OUT THE CHUCA SHOES, THE RINESTONE JACKETS, THE CORDOROY PANTS AND ENJOY. BUT AFTER IT'S OVER YOU WAKE UP WITH A NASTY HANGOVER AND WONDER WHAT'S LEFT FOR KANSAS...???
Fantastic American prog metal band that makes you want to explore more of their CDs. I like how they fuse many styles and keep it interesting. I highly recommend this to open minded music lovers.

users.query: The Blueberry Lane series is phenomenal.  My only problem is I let too much time pass between series reads and I forget details about each sibling/cousin love story and then have to re-read after finishing the current one. Which is perfectly fine since it's all at my fingertips on my beloved Kindle. I follow Katy in each of her series and genres, including her new Radish endeavor, and never am I disappointed. The only thing that I sometimes want in this one is an epilogue, although each successive book contains bundles of "updates/epilogue to satisfy inquiring and nosy minds such as mine. Bravo, Ms Regnery.

cands.text: I've been reading lots and lots of romances on my Kindle for about 3 years now.  As most folks, I have my favorites, and favorite authors that I keep tucked away to read and re-read again and again.  This series, and Julie Richman is now amongst my top five favorites.  I started with just the first book in the series, and after devouring it, decided to just buy the boxed set to finish reading the series.  Ms Richman has created the utterly near perfect male character in Schooner Moore.  And the unique, laugh-out-loud and sexy relationship between Schooner and Mia, not to mention the rich, character-developed, unique story of Mia's life between the time she and Schooner separated as mere teens and reunited 24 years later, is absolutely spell-binding.  Julie Richman can weave a story that weaves right into your bone and blood, and become a part of you.  This is a series I highly recommend to any romance reader.  It has just the perfect touch of heart-rendering romance, spice and heat, and so many aaah moments you can barely stand it.  Thank you, Julie, for a series to dwell in my heart for a long time to come!!!

The one thing I know for certain I'll have when I read one of Ms Lane's books is pure, unadulterated flaring, flaming, LOVE and emotion.  My very very favorite part of this 2nd in this wonderful Sugar Rush series was at the very end, the things that both Hannah and Evan say to each other, but mainly Evan's amazingly "heart-shattering" (appropriate given the circumstances) profession to Hannah.  Ms Lane can dialogue romance like no other.  After the Spiral of Bliss series (which I am unashamed to admit I read a multitude of times), I've found few other authors who can express feelings of the heart as can Nina Lane.  Sweet Escape flows wonderfully into the "Sugar Rush" theme, and Evan, as the second of the famous Stone Brothers, does not disappoint on any level.  Especially refreshing is how the author entwines each of the former characters into the current storyline, giving the reader bits and pieces of more of the family dynamic, the Rainesville community connection, and wraps it up in a nice, sweet package!!!  I cannot wait for the next installment and the story of the next Stone brother!!

This is the second book of this series I've inhaled and cannot wait to afford to get each and every one of this series.  It always amazes me how authors are able to even think of these plots and stories and then so amazingly flesh them out with characters, twists, turns, settings, events, places, and create such a story of wonder and emotion-altering feeling.  Just as with The Color of Heaven, I'd never given a lot of thought to "out-of-body" experiences, or paranormal happenings and how, if real, they can shape our whole being.  The story of Carla, her marriage and her daughter, and how her life was edged by, affected by, and ultimately altered by Aaron as he struggled for his life on a deserted island after surviving a plane crash.  Their love and the unbelievably amazing story is so emotional and special.  Ms MacLean's writing genius is so inspiring and amazing and I have run out of adjectives!!!

If I had to name one thing I did not like about this book, it would be that it ended MUCH too quickly!  I am incredibly fond of this series  I especially like the ongoing story for each of the five friends - - Bree, Cypress, Amelia, Ace, and Blade.  Most readers going from mid-1st book, 400 First Dates, into 325 First Fights, are either rooting for the couple, Bree and Cypress to make it, and for Amelia to have happiness.  Will it be her ex or Ace?  And now Blade has met someone but he doesn't expect it go long-term, where he has finally realized he wants to be.  This is just an excellent read in the trials and tribulations of love, interests, relationship, and life.  Ms Todd knows how to tell the basic girl-meets-boy-and-then-what-they-do with real style, passion, and with a manner to keep the reader wanting more.  I am anxious for the 3rd installment in this series.
Read and reread the first in the series, then couldn't buy #2 and #3 fast enough. Evan and Emma became a part of me.

Msg Katy never fails to please to the max. Whenever I have a new Katy Regnery book on my kindle, I get so excited that I fly through, missing lots of little details while trying to get to the good parts. In Don't Speak, getting to the good part was so worth the nail-biting wait.  This one was every bit as the first 4 modern fairytales, but so much more filled with the feel for the North Carolina coastal lifestyle, of which I had little knowledge.  This book had it all -- the fairy godmother, rags to riches story, and lots and lots of toe curling, swooning love.  You just wanted to wrap up Erik and steal him away. Thank you, Msg Regnery for continuing to give us beautifully-written, richly warm and cuddly emotion, and HEAs  we love. This is a must-read for sure.

After reading each book in this series, I declare it my favorite.  Now that I've read Ginger's Heart, it IS my favorite . . . at least until Don't Speak is released.  I love Katy's writing style, how she sees into the heart and mind of both the woman and the man in the crazy conflicting, confusing thing that is love and relationships.  This one, as has the others, has everything most of us want when reading a romance, especially one that is considered a "fairy tale" romance.  Your heart just bled for Ginger as she experienced so much angst and confusion.  She truly was a "lone" one with very few she could turn to in time of turmoil, and Cain became her everything.  The things he said to Ginger just took away my breath and made me swoon.  The Epilogue was truly epic, and gave you just enough to not spend time wondering and pondering on how everything truly worked out.  A true HEA that satisfied the soul.  Rock on Katy and write on!!!

I couldn't wait to read (and listen via Audible) to this final in the Driven Series (although thankfully, Bromberg gives us 3 more in this collection to carry on the storyline with other characters), but at the same time wanted to do it slowly because I didn't want the whole magic to end.  Rylee and Colton's story has been so  . . . so . . . everything!!  Highs, lows, mountaintop highs, deepest caves low, and everything in between.  Rylee goes through so much, and after attaining the only thing she has left in her heart's desires, she sinks to the depths of despair and has to climb her way up from the pit with the help of those who love her most and by her sheer strength and will.  And Colton, who has become a number 1 book boyfriend and hero, the ever present, speed demon/eye candy hunk of man/tells it like it is, does not let Rylee down, and rises to be the man that was always within him but took a woman like Rylee to step forward.  Ms Bromberg has easily made a fan out of me with this series.  I have yet to read Raced, but I'm one-clicking it after I write this review, and then will work through the 3 "afterthought" companion books.  I do wish this series was offered in Kindle Unlimited, but alas, I had to break the piggybank. It was highly worth it.  The series, and this conclusion book, gives you everything you look for in a romance novel, and even some you never thought you wanted.  I applaud Ms Bromberg for this debut series, and wish her every best on a wonderful literary career!!!

What an awesome book.  I fell in love with Jax and Lexi during their airport texting, and only fell harder with each chapter.  They both showed what love is all about in a way that takes your breath and leaves sighing.  Skye Jordan writes a winner!!!

I could almost use the same review for each of Katy's books, except that each one seems to have that special magical ability to actually see and know the characters with all their flaws, idosyncracies, tics, tats, habits, speech patterns, and unique identities.  I'm sure most of us who read this one love love loved Etienne's whispers en francais.  Kate was so mature and responsible and unbelievable when she learned some of the background behind their tragic parting, in wanting to discuss it with him and get it all out in the open.  There was so much that kept the young couple from testing their youthful love.  But the true magic in this book was how their abiding love kept them somehow connected over many years, although by a very fragile thread, and how fate's abounding joy works to bring the magic to sparkling life for them again.  Ms Regnery's books NEVER let me down and I can always count on each one to renew and energize the true concept of love in my heart and soul!

I really got into and enjoyed Book One of this series. Youthful love, ambitions and dreams, selfishness and selflessness.  The one thing that kept me from taking this one into my heart, and I feel certain it was Ms Jakson's intent to weave the conflict and turmoil as any good writer would, but my focus throughout was on the fact that Christian was  defiantly bound to acquire and claim the child he all but demanded be put death.  When I read all the reviewers claim to "love Christian _ _ how could you not _ _ I wondered if there read something I didn't see.  Christian was, in this book, a selfish, thoughtless, irresponsible jerk of a man who simply wanted whatever he wanted with no thought to what he did to Elizabeth, the woman he so claimed too be. I don't think he deserved Lizzie, but she did deserve a loving daddy.  I've held off purchasing Book Three in the series because the synopsis indicates that this coupe just cannot seem to get it together. I am going to go for it and hope that Christian grows some honest meatballs, and Elizabeth grows the strength and conviction to herself and her children that we know she has.  Ms Jackson is an awesome writer and I'll give her every chance.

I simply do not know how it took me this long t devour this series.  The probably ARE enough word to describe the emotions that flood one while reading and savoring this novel -- I just don't know them all.  What romance-reading woman doesn't search and single the story that gives every single component of deep, immense, near-perfect example of rue, selfless abiding love? Doesn't provide every sigh-inducing magnetic confession and revelation whispered in her ear by a devilishly hunk of man??? Ms Bromberg gifts it all to us with a big red bow of spice, erotic pleasure, twinkling wit and humour, with all the parts of romance we never even thought to desire.  I believe the author may just be "the whole alphabet" of romance writing!!

Admittedly, I bought this book because it was free, and the blurb and reviews weren't awful.  I really liked the plot and especially the characterization. The relationship between Bee and Stephan was quite remarkable, as was Ms Lilley's way of offering dribs of Bianca's past.  Even knowing that James was going to put Bianca through a pepper grinder with his fame and fortune, not to mention his personal proclivities, and yet I couldn't help but root for him a little.  I was, of course disappointed at the cliff-hanger, even though I'd read in the reviews that there was one. I'm curious enough to buy the next instalment.

I was gifted this book by a wonderful reader and reviewer of indie romance after it was so highly recommended. And it lived up to every recommendation and then some.  A very, very ong span of rollercoaster riding and chunks of bittersweet, gritty life passed between the lovely Brecks ("B") Kennedy and the multifaceted Jamie Shaw.  Misunderstandings, miles, boyfriends, girlfriends, times, and any number of things kept this couple from being together. Despite the length of gaps, the miles of separation, engagement, even a marriage, nothing could keep them from each other whenever they were an arm's length apart.  Their love was bigger than all that separated them but could not outlast the timing they faced.  Until . . . A Love Letter to Whiskey . . .  Phenomenal read is all I can say!!!

I am always be certain that I'll fill out all 5 stars when I read a Lauren Blakely book. She never disappoints.  Even when I'm reading part of a series, each book will be in a different setting entirely, but I KNOW I'm gonna love every word. McKenna and Chris were perfect for each other from their first moments together. Their dialogue, mutual physical attraction, interests were all a terrific foundation on which to build a solid, if not quick, full-out loving relationship. McKenna had to work her way around and through the heartbreak that her creep of an ex-fiancee inflicted on her then returned to pour salt in her wounds. Chris was man enough to know she needed to work it out but knew he wanted and needed her to be his.  Pushing a trophy husband contest wasn't an ideal way to get over on her scuba ex, but it was a way for Chris to get close to her, until it was no longer necessary and have every chance to ruin a great could-be love. Terrific ending, and can't wait to move onto Blakely's next hit.

I purchased both the Kindle and audio versions of this.  I mainly listened to the audio version, with a little backup of reading parts I missed along and along.  While I had to see this one completely through to the end, I have to say that my frustration level with Alexa/Lexi/Lex just about hit my limit several times.  I've never been in this type of relationship (thank goodness), so I really could not understand how she kept falling back into him knowing she was going to get hurt and stomped upon again and again.  While the jumping back and forth in time is unique and [kind of] facilitates the storyline, it made it sort of hard to keep up with where we are with this so-called relationship and with all of Jack's other women.  I'm sure there are countless women involved in similar types of situations, and the heart wants what it wants, but this was the most flabbergastingly frustrating relationship I've read in some time, and I read A LOT!  I have always lked Ms Linde's writing and storytelling, so I couldn't give up on the book although a few times I thought about it.  I also felt the very end was a little bit of a let-down, but then so much of Jack's selfish, narcissistic ways were as well, but made for interesting reading.  I think this would be a good book to give a daughter coming into womanhood to learn what NOT to do with men.

If you don't sob your guts out after reading this book, you have no heart!!!  I've been doing a LOT of romance reading the last several months, and this is by far the one that has stuck with me the hardest and longest!  B.A. Wolfe has done a marvelous job with her debut book!  Since I'm a 60-year old grandmother, I can honestly say that the book would appeal to any age and touch any heart!

Already loved Julianne MacLean's Color of Heaven series, and now I have a whole new genre in which to enjoy this wonderful author's work.  Mail Order Bride elicited so many different emotions and emotional responses than many other romance novels.  I became utterly disgusted with Briggs when he just thought of himself and so heartlessly treated Sarah with disdain.  Part of me understood, but it was his pig-headed stubbornness ruling him that made me so frustrated with him!  But any book that raises your ire the way Briggs did is a good one, and I can tell you that this series is epic!  After reading so many "modern day" contemporary romances, when you switch gears and read a western historical one, you have to alter your thinking and look at things a little differently.  Briggs and Sarah's quick attraction to one another was probably not as common for folks like them during that time, and so it made Briggs' ultimate treatment of Sarah such a cold-hearted one to me, but I was so proud how he redeemed himself and how the two of them overcame their prejudices, misunderstandings and hurts and became just them.  Ms MacLean can really depict a woman's thoughts and a man's just as well, which cannot be that simple to do.  I can't wait to read more of this series.

From the very first Aly Martinez book that was recommended and gifted to me by another author, I have gobbled up each one I could. Each of her series are so different from the other, with steadfast, abiding theme of abiding love and devotion. The dual story of Elisabeth and Roman and then Claire, is unique, and the mystery of how they are connected is revealed in shock and amazement. The steadfast way Roman is determined to win his Elisabeth is commanding, yet you can't help but want to clobber his stubborn refusal to truly communicate his full thoughts and feelings with her.  It just goes more fully to the deep and eternal connection this couple shares. I cannot wait to get started on Claire and Luke/Heath's story in Transfer to see how little Tess fits in both couples' lives.

I listened to the Audible version and then followed up with Kindle version.  The narrator's were absolutely perfect for the unique characters and for the twisting and winding plot that Ms Renshaw wove into this book.  Addison and Wilder met, fell into each other with spark and flash, and were totally meant to be together. Except that fate and fickle life had other ideas. They struggled with their love while awaiting things to right themselves in order for them to be together. It was a beautiful story of love and patience overcoming odds thrown into their path, however unimportant one might see them to be. It was well-written with a nice HEA and all we want in romance.

When I first noticed there were only 9 chapters, I was disappointed, but the intensity, passion and flood of feeling in those 9 chapters is remarkable. Especially exciting is that the next instalment comes out TODAY!!!

Bella Andre, if nothing else, knows love - - every nuance, feel, molecule, spice and ingredient that makes up that illusive emotion that drives and rules most humans. And she and describe the physical, passionate part of it with reckless abandon and heart-clashing adoration and thunder. In this case, with Brooke and Race, the almost magical instantaneously of their attraction and passion created an amazing g read that one wants to just be absorbed into one's molecular makeup. The sweetness and genuineness of Brooke mixed with the life-tumbled scarred soul of Race makes for some steamy and bone-jarring emotions that lead to such a satisfying and compete conclusion.  She included every part imaginable into the conclusion that a HEA could contain.  Bravo and once again, I cannot wait to read her again.

I've read and enjoyed Clare James' books, but wasn't sure if this one would be for me.  I was wrong to wonder because even as racy as it is, to this 63-year old, it was pretty yummy.  I did feel a few times that Stevie was a little too immature for her age, but then again she did have a little on her plate to deal with.  I fell in love with Gabe and hated that Stevie was in a dilemma with two men.  Ms James handled the triangle quite adeptly and I thoroughly enjoyed the outcome and anxious to read the next installment in the series.

It ended too quickly!!!  I wanted more more more.  When Vaughn Stone makes up his mind what he wants, he certainly goes after it and gets it.  And Paige is definitely in for trouble.  I could definitely handle being stuck in a sleeping bag with Vaughn for days on end with no trouble whatsoever.  That man has staying power like none other I've heard of!!!!  The tender way he took care of Paige while they were stranded was so endearing.  Fabulous read.  This team can collaborate like none other!!

Christian was a spoiled, wealthy, selfish young man who had no concept of love other than self-love, until Elizabeth enters his life.  Like a shiny new toy, Christian only knows he must have her, conquer her. His sour spirit nearly destroys the sweet beauty, and it takes her hurt and humiliation for him to find that illusive emotion, love, of which everyone always refers.  When he actually realizes that love has wedged its way into his heart, he sadly realizes that she may be lost to him, he sets out to do whatever it takes to let her know that he genuinely loves her and wants them to be together now and always. Elizabeth, a gentle beauty, kind, sweet and full of love for Christian, cannot refuse him, and they share one ultimate first night together.  Have already one-clicked the next installment of Christian and Elizabeth's saga, and cannot wait to read what is in store for this couple.

users.query: This will hold a lot of corks!  It is beautiful and decorative.  Definitely a conversation piece.  I have a lot of corks saved up from many years of drinking wine.  I never wanted to throw them away so just put them wherever I could find a spot, mostly in drawers where they get damaged.  Now I can have them on display and look at them whenever I want to.  I love the grapevine wirework design with glass beads.  It is very rustic looking, like something you would see in wine country.  It would look great on your bar or close to your wine rack.  It is very well-made of sturdy metal.  It is easy to drop the corks in.  The top has a hinge so can easily be opened if you want to remove them.  This would make a great holiday or housewarming gift for any wine drinker.  I received a complimentary product in exchange for a fair and honest review.

cands.text: This is a great idea to have a shatterproof wine glass to bring outside with you.  It is especially good around a pool since you are not supposed to have glass around pools.  It is also great for picnics, camping or the beach.  I bring it out with me on my deck and I don't have to worry if it falls off the table because it will not shatter like glass.  It comes apart and has a nice carrying bag so does not take up much room in transit.  When it is together and you are drinking from it, you would not ever know that it comes apart.  It looks like real glass from far away.  It is a lot nicer than drinking out of those red plastic solo cups.  I received a complimentary product in exchange for a fair and honest review.

This is a very well-made and sturdy growler.  It is airtight and easy to close.  It has a handle to carry it by.  It looks great.  It is unbreakable so it is great for the beach or camping.  This will hold more than a blender full of margaritas.  After blending them, I poured the Margaritas in there and when getting to our destination I just poured them over ice.  This is a lot better than making Margaritas outside in the middle of no where.  I have also used it for it's intended purpose: beer.  You can drink beer right out of it and reclose it to save the rest for later.  Since it is dark and airtight, I am going to use it to store olive oil in when I don't need it for an outdoor adventure.  I received a discounted product in exchange for a fair and honest review.

This is a handy little bottle.  It is smaller than most so it is easier to carry or to throw it into you bag.  It is a very nice looking and sturdy bottle.  It is unbreakable and will not rust.  The cap secures the contents very well so there are no leaks.  It comes with an extra top with a straw attached.  This is very handy while exercising or on-the-go.  Both tops have easy to carry handles.  It is very easy to clean.  Overall, this is a great bottle and will last a very long time.  I received a discounted product in exchange for a fair and honest review.

This is a very nice looking and sturdy bottle.  It is unbreakable and will not rust.  The cap secures the contents very well so there are no leaks.  It comes with an extra top with a straw attached.  This is very handy while exercising or on-the-go.  Both tops have easy to carry handles.  It is very easy to clean.  Overall, this is a great bottle and will last a very long time.  I received a complimentary product in exchange for a fair and honest review.

This is a great card case.  It is made of high quality leather and looks very refined and professional.  It comes in a very nice gift box that would be suitable to give to anyone.  It has 3 different compartments so it would be great for a convention where you can give and receive business cards and keep them separate.  It has an extendable cord so you can clip it to your purse or a belt loop and not lose it, but will always be handy.  It would also be good when going out at night and not wanting to bring a purse with you.  I will easily fit your pocket with your driver's license, a few credit cards and some cash.  Overall, this is a great accessory with many uses.  I received a discounted product in exchange for a fair and honest review.

This is a beautiful and functional item.  It is made of solid copper and looks great.  It will keep your drink cold for a long time.  It is the right size.  It is sturdy and well-made. I have used it for both hot and cold beverages and it works very well for either.  It has a nice handle that makes it easy to hold.  It will last a lifetime!  Since it is copper it is unbreakable so you don't have to worry about breakage like you would for a glass or ceramic mug.  When not in use I have it on display in my kitchen.  It goes great with a rustic decor.  I love this mug.  I received a complimentary product in exchange for a fair and honest review.

I love these organizers!  They make packing so much easier.
