This is the same as the review for the gray tunic. I purchased this bat wing sleeve pullover loose shirt in a size large. I expected it to fit in a certain way but it is meant for a shorter and more petite build. I'm only 5'6" and a size 8 but was thankful to see the other reviews regarding how the sizes run. This hits me right between the waist and hip. I wouldn't wear it with leggings unless you were going to be super casual. If it were a bit longer you could pull off wearing it with leggings and boots to the office BUT it isn't that long so you'd have to wear it with slacks or something else more appropriate.
The construction is pretty solid. The seams appear strong. The color and design and just like the picture. It's super cute and I've gotten compliments on it already. This is definitely a winner. I would advise washing in cold water and hanging it to dry.
I would definitely recommend this shirt with the warnings that I gave above. It's good and the price is great.

My sons old case broke apart so I looked and found the Sanoxy leather case. My son loves it! He says the best feature is the ability to rotate the screen 360* is amazing. I enjoy the fact that it's well made and will keep his iPad 2 protected.

I recommend this one.
I love this ring and it matches my pendant and earrings perfectly. I will wear it awhile and see how it holds up.

Got this as an add-on to my order. The price was unbeatable for this figure that normally runs in the teens $xx.xx.

The detail of the face and clothing is great and looks like the character that my son plays on the screen. I cannot comment yet on articulation due to it being wrapped for Christmas.

For the price that I paid, this is a great deal. Look for it as an Add-on!
I returned it for a different figure, however, the quality and craftsmanship was excellent. This is why I ordered the one my son actually wanted.

I really like the style of this top. The color is like a turquoise blue and not very green. Every time I wear it, I receive compliments. It is well made and I had no issues with the stitching like other reviewers. It's a bit shorter than expected. It does not sit at the hips. It is right under the waist and will hang off of one shoulder. The fabric is thicker than jersey or comparable to a substantial jersey. Light enough for summer but not too heavy. The only problem that I had other than the length was the tag. It poked me relentlessly so I removed it. I think it may have been made of sandpaper. All in all, four stars! I will be buying more in different colors.

Got this set not too long ago and I really like it. The skin cover comes loose far too often but the charger and the usb data cable are frickin awesome to have. All in all, for the price, it's worth the skin cover not being perfect! LOVE IT and would buy again in a second!

It works alright but is too tall for my closet (my issue for not checking dimensions). The reason for taking a star away is that the top bar for hanging my shirts constantly falls down. Other than that, it's great.

What a steal! We got these on sale and my son wanted some "skate shoes". I trust the Teva brand and felt better getting a brand I was familiar with. When they arrived and he opened the box, he was thrilled with the look. They fit well and I was glad for the reviewer that advised going 1/2 a size up because that gave my boy just enough room to grow.

This is a great buy! Five stars.
Got little white bugs on my wildflowers. Ordered this and within ONE DAY they were gone! Love Dyna-Gro's Neem Oil. Will always be a customer.

***Update:  After 17 months I'm having to replace this due to the kids doing the dishes and "passing" the carafe across the kitchen and it landing in the rinsing sink on the corner of the base. It really only chipped in a spot that will cause any liquid to pour out from the bottom. It's a tough little thing and well made to not completely shatter at that mistreatment. Heaven only knows what other abuses were suffered when they did dishes when I was not around! Oh...we figured out our own way to pour to avoid the accursed "drip"!
I really love this replacement carafe by Medelco. It's perfect size for my Mr Coffee 4 cup coffee maker w/the little piece added to the top to make it fit precisely. The carafe is well made, sturdy, affordable and a good fit.***

My problem is that when yo attempt to pour, it will drip in the cup and EVERYWHERE else. I'm not deducting more stars because quite honestly, the original did the same.

Good that I don't have to skip a beat. LOL

Great animated adaptation of the comic. This is definitely a favorite of mine!
5 stars.

I love that I have this to connect my wii to my new hd flat panel television.

I took this out of the package and immediately connected it from the wii to the television component plugs. It worked immediately upon turning on both units and after changing the wii settings from 480i to 480p, my resolution was wonderful. Streaming on netflix is much better as well! The cord is short, which is ideal because of the way my tv stand is set up. I don't like clutter and there is just enough cord to reach everything and keep it tidy.

The delivery of this item was incredibly fast. I ordered it yesterday afternoon and received it late this morning from OnTrac. Amazon continues to come through for me and so far, MiniSuit has giving me a quality product!

Thanks!!!!

I was very please when I received these pants. I have them in Egg Plant as well and could not wait to wear these when I saw them. The price is right. They are very subdued in the design. There are very tastefully sized colored stones on the faux pockets that add a bit of flare to the pants. I'm 5'6" & they fit fine. Not too long and definitely not too short. I'm a thick girl and they fit fine w/ a bit of stretch to them.

I recommend these.

users.query: One was broken and unusable, another was cracked but I'm using it.

cands.text: Only used a few times and the nozzle fell off of the end of the hose.  Totally useless now, and it's a week out of the return window.  I shouldn't have purchased something that only had 2-1/2 stars!

Works OK but I agree with the other reviewers--seems flimsy, the lights are way too bright, it only has one live connector into a socket (the other is 3 small plastic pieces which go into the bottom socket) which makes it a bit unsteady.  I'm using it because I haven't seen anything much better.
Easy to use.  Seems sturdy.  Would be 5 stars if alarm were a bit louder.  A good product for the price.
Just too flimsy for me.  And the color is much lighter than shown on website.  Cheap compared to other solutions, in cost and quality.
Works very well, GREAT price, reasonable shipping time.  Very pleased.
Very weak signal, difficult to change the battery, rather bulky.  Received from my wish list, but would never buy for anyone else.
I didn't think the quality was equal to the price.  Returned it.
Looks great, works great, arrived on time and in perfect condition, and is a nice complement to stainless steel appliances. What more could you want?
These are very useful. I use them in both the kitchen and in the office--I can actually use every outlet in my power strip now.  These are excellent quality, each with the UL certification tag.
Really pleased with this product.  Works very well, the price is GREAT, and the shipping time was reasonable.

None of these types of devices costing under about $90 work all that well, unfortunately.  But if you want something very affordable, for emergency or infrequent use, this is better than a couple of others I've tried.
Works very well and a great space-saver. Glad I bought it.

Love the feel and basic design of this wallet, especially for the price.  However, I could not use it because the card slots were all about 1/8" too narrow for my Visa and other credit cards, and for my drivers license.  Perhaps these wallets are sewn a little differently by different machines or people, but this one seems well sewn and well made.  It's simply a tad too narrow to make it easy to insert and remove cards--you have to wiggle the card in and really pull and wiggle it to get it out.  Also, the tightness means that even if you can get a couple of cards in the slots, you cannot use all 4 card slots at the same time--it's just too tight!

Cheap price, and very cheaply made.  The coil cord was "tweaked" and out of shape.right out of the package.  I may use it until I find something better, as it's not worth returning.  I was hoping to like this enough to give as holiday stocking stuffers, but it's not worth even the inexpensive price.

This is a beautifully made phone--quite heavy, not flimsy like most other "traditional" phones these days.  However, I only gave it 3 stars because even at its highest setting, the volume is much lower than my old, flimsy phone that was half the price.  But I'll keep this as it's simply a secondary phone that I use with MagicJack, mostly to call myself when Ii can't find my cell phone!  Maybe it's just this one phone, too, that has such low volume--but I don't care enough to send it back and get another one.  It's good enough.

I've tried two other antennas in the past few months.  Both were OK but I still had weak signals on a few channels.  This antenna totally did the trick--I found double the number of channels when I re-scanned, and everything I wanted comes in strong and clear.  It was easy to assemble and install on my roof.  A quality project and I recommend it highly
Perfect for "dry goods"--easy to pick up with one hand but still holds plenty.

This is a nice phone in many ways.  I bought it to replace an AT&T speaker phone the I regularly sed with the external speaker and had no problems hearing.  I found this Panasonic phone easy to program and it has a sleek look and feel, and good clarity.  However, even when the speaker volume is at the highest setting you need to have your ear within four or five inches of the handset or desk console in order to hear comfortably.  The manual warns to use the external speaker feature in a "quiet environment," but even in a totally quiet room this feature is inadequate.  And it's totally useless if there's any noise at all in the area.  Perhaps it's just this one piece of equipment rather than every one of these phones, but the "quiet environment" comment in the manual leads me to think the manufacturers know the speaker is inadequate.  If you're not going to use the speakerphone feature, this is a great phone.

This is definitely a quality machine.  Whether it's worth the trouble of assembling, disassembling and cleaning the removable parts is a question of how much time you have, what you're using it for, etc.  I use it sometimes for my hard kitchen and bathroom floors but it doesn't replace an old-fashioned mop for getting into corners, along baseboards, etc.  However, I do use it regularly to "spot-clean" my very light carpeting and throw rugs.  Much easier than getting down on hands and knees to use a spray spot-cleaner, so I do it more often--my carpets look much nicer.  It actually pulls more cat hair and other debris out of my carpet than my regular upright vacuum does--but it means you have wet debris in the rollers and bin, which is a bit messy to clean out.

Overall, this is a somewhat pricey investment considering it does not, for me, completely replace my regular mop or vacuum.  But I do use it often enough, and it seems sturdy enough, that I'm sure the cost will be worth it in the long run.  And my rugs do look very nice!

Got these while recovering from a foot problem that caused me to only be able to wear flip flops.  My foot is healed but I continue to wear these around the house with my flip flops because they're so warm and comfy, and I can slip my flip-flops on and off when putting my feet up to read or watch TV.  Much easier than slippers, and I can also wear the flip flop/sock combo outside to get the mail, etc., even if the pavement is wet.  Love them.
East to install, easy to use.  This is installed on top of carpet and it works perfectly.
Very well made and stylish for the price.  Nice lining, good zipper.  Sturdy adjustable strap.  Nice size.

These are very inexpensive, but look nice and really do the job.  The size makes them most appropriate for smaller doors, back doors, etc.  Would be great for an RV.  I like that they can be hosed down quite forcefully, and come clean easily.

This is tiny, and the clips don't hold on my laptop, but it works just fine siting on the desk behind my computer.  I wanted it only for increasing the volume over my horrible built-in speakers (not for listening to music) and for my uses it gets plenty loud with no distortion.  Works very well for You Tube videos, movies, and listening to the news on the computer.  Easy plug-and-play set-up.

users.query: After years of neglect I've finally gotten around to reorganizing and restocking my workshop. Our rural community is sorely lacking in convenient hardware stores so I like having plenty of options on hand. This is a fine set of pocket hole screws and the included organizer is sturdy and secure. Having these types of options on hand are a real plus when taking on a project.

cands.text: In setting up a new workbench I wanted to go with a new set of wrenches replacing a rather hodgepodge set that seems to inevitably happens. These seem to be of high quality and I love the packaging. These neatly fit in a bench drawer while in their own 'organizer' and I expect these to be a lifetime purchase.

During the process of reorganizing and upgrading my workshop I wanted a complete set of quality pliers and these really fit the bill. I bought the vise grip style and this set. Craftsman is hard to beat and this set is no exception. They look great and work great.

This is the dandiest organizer/tote we have found. we don't go shopping without it. You can really load it up neatly with purchases and carry them in safely and securely. It holds plenty of 'stuff' and keeps things safe and secure. Built to last.

Product arrived on time and in good shape. It is what it is and serves it's purpose while costing less than local hardware outlets. If you are planning a project rather than needing one in a bind this is the way to go.
Crap Period. In setting up my new workshop these looked as if they would be very handy to have. Not so much. I'm using them in a secondary local and still find them ineffective.

Nice basic driver set.  Between home and business tools always seem to be in the wrong place. This set will go along way in solving the problem. I like the color coding and handles. It came with a 'rack' that could be attached to wall or tool board but frankly this went straight to the trash and the drivers went in tool bags. Stanley isn't the best but good as a tool bag supplement.

Nice basic driver set.  Between home and business tools always seem to be in the wrong place. This set will go along way in solving the problem. I like the color coding and handles. It came with a 'rack' that could be attached to wall or tool board but frankly this went straight to the trash and the drivers went in tool bags. Stanley isn't the best but good as a tool bag supplement.
Decent hobby hardware but pricing was on the high end and shipping was less then satisfactory.

Very nice. I'm very active with outdoor work and recreation and never found a phone holder that was secure enough. This pack is large enough for phone (Samsung G4) and additional items ie pens, knife and Id. Seems very sturdy tho time will tell. Also love the fact that don't have to belt off to put it on or take it off.

It's a real joy these days when purchasing a product, receiving it and putting it to use all exceed your expectations. Immediately upon opening this package I was WoWed. The product is beautiful. The quality of materials and workmanship is truly impressive. Soft supple leather, quality zippered compartments and great stitching. The multiple compartments are just what I was expecting and wanted.. Lots of products look good but don't really perform. This bag does both. The adjustable strap makes for a perfect fit, secure and easy to get to. I look at a product like this and think of it as a legacy to be passed down and used by multiple generations, it will only look better with age. We are going on vacation in a couple of weeks and this dandy bag will be perfect.
This two pack is exactly what I was looking for and the design is classic. Mounting hardware is included and effective. Good price as well.
Love this stylish and practical pocket calendar.  Has everything I want and some I don't need but have proved to be handy. Price was very reasonable and shipping prompt
Love Craftsman tools and these are no exception. Formerly used 'Visegrip' brand and they are good but these are an upgrade. Having more than one pair is essential.

Product arrived in timely fashion and in good condition.  All parts were included, assembly was literally a snap.  We had this rack up and in use within minutes of receiving it. The only part that required a tool were the wheels and a small disposable wrench was included with the parts.  It doesn't get any easier or convenient.
Easy and quick fit on my Dewalt tablesaw.. We have a use for the sawdust and this does a good job of collection. Price was right

Needed to have a holder that would easily hang and replace a recessed holder in  a restroom at our business. This unit stuck right on and allowed the roll to hang right over where the now unusable unit is. In initially installing it it does not give one a warm fuzzy feeling about it staying up without anything but the adhesive backing but it has stayed where it belongs and is stable. I do wish there had been a screw on option but so far so good.

Whats to like or dislike? These are basic window points with a push tool. This is the first time I have used this type of product and it went okay. but I was slightly disappointed in the design of the tool itself. The tool fits the point but not to the degree that I thought it would.

Made major points with the wife for this purchase. Placed this in the laundry area and it has eased her work and made things much more efficient.  Assembly was simple and fast. All parts were included and packaging was ok.
I received this as a gift. Although it will not fit my own needs I can still admire the quality of materials and workmanship. I look forward to giving it proudly as a gift.

We used this on the bottom edge of a single garage door. So far it is doing well. I did not make use of the included hardware but rather used construction adhesive. We don't use this door often and wanted a better bottom seal. Can't give any comment regarding how this product will hold up however I still have plenty left over to do it again.

Not really much to like or dislike here. It fits and does what it is designed to do. What more can you expect from a skimmer hose.  It did seem alittle pricey but this was certainly the easiest to find and delivery was fast.

Had a bit of a disagreement with our HVAC guy regarding the AC at our business and this very reasonably price unit resolved the situation with the push of a button. Received the unit promptly and in good condition. Popped the batteries in and away you go. Seems very well designed for both easy of usage and durability. I don't anticipate heavy usage but it one of those tools I'm glad I have in my bag.

This is my third pair of this style and feel certain it won't be my last. I really love the fit, and style of the Timberland boots.  This is absolutely my 'go to boot" .  I have tried a couple of other brands and have been disappointed by them all.  I have some serious back problems and these boots really make things better.

I looked at the usual retail outlets for these and came up empty. However as usual amazon came through.  We have a theater which means lots of trash and heavy items being put in our trash receptacles, i.e. drinks with ice.  Can liners were always falling into the cans creating a huge mess.  These bands are easy to use and eliminates a real pain in the neck.  I would recommend these to anyone wanting less mess and the security of knowing the liner will stay where you put it ..I cannot at this point speak as to their durability but it appears they will hold up well.  I will be buying more immediately just to have spares.  We don't want to be without these handy bands.

We make good use of this style shelving for numerous applications and these liners make the shelving unit better in some of those uses. fit is perfect and nothing falls through or gets hung up on the wire shelving. These are a real upgrade from a shelving unit without liners.

users.query: This is a well made, sturdy skimmer.  I especially like the leading edge when getting things off the bottom.

cands.text: Well made and easy to use. Makes for a clean, professional installation.
Well made and looks good.  Easy to clean.  The hummers like it too.
This is a good looking knife and it seems to have taken an edge well.  Time will tell about how well it keeps the edge.  So far, so good.
This is so pretty.  It is well made too, and the hummers love it.
Hard to lose this. It is bright. Floats too, even with camera attavhed.
Good product at a good price, but that's not the best part.  This vendor not only has good products, they have good service.  My supplies were just what I needed and arrived as promised.
This unit not only looks good but it works well.
Excellent brush.  It is well made and had a good sweeping action.
Excellent brush.  It is well made and had a good sweeping action.
This is a good line for most applications, but did not work well with the winch on my boat.
This is a great way to make connections. Easy to use and tight connections
Good quality and it's nice to have a spare when you need it.
Bought this for our son and his wife.  They were doing DIY projects on their new home without proper tools.  I have one of these and love it, so of course it was my choice for them.
It's a filter and nothing more.  That is great and it works
Great tool.  Also, entertains the grand kids as they are really helping me.
This is a well made journal.  It's very attract, too.
Well made cables. These cables look and feel like they should last awhile.
Nothing special except the price, which is excellent. These are good quality clamps.
Good protection at a reasonable price. Holding up well through the season.
Perfect for the task.  Easy to use and the presentation is outstanding.
Good manual, but did not have complete wiring diagram for my model.

An incredible account that shows that "science"does not mean truth. This book is pretty technical and not to be read as entertainment.  It is full of facts and figures that support the position that anthropology is not interested in what is true about ancient man.  Jack Cuosso is a brave man and an excellent researcher.  He's probably a good dentist as well.
This book is about being healthy using vinegar intentionally in your diet.

users.query:
I was able to read this book as a stand alone without any trouble, though it is a part of a series.

Born to Die is a mystery that mainly features a nurse by the name of Casey who has noticed a series of SIDS deaths relating to babies born at the hospital she works at.  With the help of Danny, a resident who is in love with her, she determines to find out if there is something wonky going on.

While going over the documents Danny has managed to sneak out of the hospital at a bar one night, she catches the eye of Detective Al Warner and there is a connection between the two of them.  They see each other again and Casey shares the details with Al, who is on medical leave and advises he will help her.

This book was not horrible; I found myself continuing because I wanted to see "whodunit".  I had a suspension from the start though of who that person was, and I was right.

That being said, it was at times hard to read simply because quite frankly, a lot of the men were depicted as not very respective of women.  And this connection between Al and Casey wasn't very believable.

Again, not terrible and you find yourself wanting to know the end result.  I didn't hate the book.  However, aspects of some of the characters was a bit off putting to me.

cands.text:
This time we get the story of Dee, who has moved back to the town she was raised in with her grandmother - who happens to be one of the "Gray-Haired Knitting Detectives."  She has left her abusive husband and is basically trying to keep a low profile, and move on with her life.

Her husband shows up and demands that she return home, but Dee refuses.  At the insistence of her new friends and her grandmother, she files for an order of protection from her husband.  A few days later, her husband is found dead - murdered.

Another case for the Gray-Haired Knitting Detectives!

I love these books.  They are truly what a cozy mystery should be, and this third book in the installment (all of which can be read as standalones) is no exception.

The characters are fun.  I like Dee's sass.  I like Tommy who has a major crush on her.  And of course I love Izzy, Noel, Jack, Damien and all the "detectives."

Maybe it wrapped up just a little too quickly at the end, but it didn't take away from my enjoyment of the story.  Yea, the mysteries are good but the fun in this series are the characters and their interaction with each other.

I'm sad that this is the last in the series - maybe the author will revisit them in the future?  One can only hope.

...(yes, Im deciding this is a genre now).  It is hard for me to pinpoint anything that I disliked about this book!

This book is told from the perspective of a strong, female lead by the name of Acadia.  She sees what is happening; has in fact been preparing for it  in a way.  She never expected that the emergency situation she was preparing for would be a zombie apocalypse!  She witnesses the beginning of it first hand, and in peculiar circumstances.  Acadia is a widow, and with some pressure from her friends, has gone out for a night at a bar with the sole intent of getting laid.  However, that event is overshadowed by the beginning of the spread of the disease.

Acadia takes new friends she makes that evening to the ranch she and her deceased husband shared.  What follows is not only a good read, but an interesting read.  Plans are formulated and put into action as a select few of Acadia, her family, and friends prepare for what is sure to be a cataclysmic event!

I loved so much about this book:  The storyline.  Our strong female lead.  Our hero who is much more than he seems on the outside.  A cast of strong supporting characters who you like, who are funny, and a few you absolutely hate.  It has everything that a good zombie book should have.  Highly recommend!

I'm a big fan of mysteries, and this one did not disappoint.

The book is set in England in 1939 during WWII. Dr. Benjamin Bones and his wife, Penny, who are on the verge of divorce, are being sent to her hometown of Birdswing due to the war, and how the government is working to have doctors in practical locations so no town goes without.

Penny feels that this will help their marriage, but Ben is thinking on the drive there that nothing can save it. Their car breaks down and again, due to the war, they are in pitch black dark because it is lights off to avoid the enemy from seeing the town. While they walk to get help, they are run over by another vehicle, and Penny is killed. Dr. Bones is injured.

Dr. Bones is forced from his depression of feeling helpless by local town member Lady Juliet. Lady Juliet is a no-nonsense, giant of a woman. She is estranged from her husband, who married her for her money. She (in a way) browbeats and manipulates Dr. Bones until he feels forced to get up and recover in order to do his job.

Soon, he mysteriously receives a note that says, "Sorry, it was supposed to be her, you weren't meant to be hurt."

What follows is Ben and Juliet's attempts to solve Penny's murder, while being surrounded by many wonderful colorful supporting characters. The local air warden also serves as a constable. His job as air warden is more important to him, and he is bumbling. His sister, anxious to get away from him, moves in with Dr. Bones to help with the office work as well as being a housekeeper/cook.

The interaction between Ben and Juliet is the highlight of this story. They fumble, they snipe, they laugh. I should mention that Juliet feels like a bit of an outcast; a woman who stands 6 feet tall and feels as if she towers over all men that surround her. She has been teased about this throughout her life, which is why she is so headstrong.

A great whodunit, wonderfully written, that kept me on the edge of my seat. I didn't want to put it down because I was dying to know whodunit!!

In this book, Liz and Nate are preparing for their wedding. Just a few days before they are scheduled to be married, Liz receives a harried call from her friend and bridesmaid Olivia - who claims to have found a dead body in her elderly aunt's home.

After going to investigate, Liz finds out that Aunt Dean's home isn't exactly as it appears...it's a bit of a bordello. Local, rich businessmen rent rooms for their mistresses and spend time with them, when possible, in the home.

A dead body does show up the next day, not far from the home - a congressional candidate.

First, I was able to read this well as a stand alone; I have read books 3 and 4 in this series with no issues.

The author's writing is very true to the South and our dialect. Further, she has written another fun, interesting mystery. Things can get a bit confusing - trying to remember which john goes with which mistress - but it doesn't take away from the story. To me, the characters are the fun in these books.

And do you think the wedding goes off without a hitch? I'll never tell - you should just read the book, especially if you love a good murder mystery.

This is the third in the Liz Talbot Mystery Series, and the first one Ive read.  I was able to read it as a stand alone without any issues.

The stories are set in South Carolina, which serves very well for this novel.  Liz owns a detective agency with her partner, Nate, who lives in Greenville while she lives in Stella Maris.  They are a bit of an item as well.  She also has another partner in the form of Colleen, a friend who is dearly departed and serves as her guardian angel (in a sense).

The story starts as Liz is hired by an influential Charleston family to find their daughter who has been missing for a month.  With this being a mystery, I don't want to give anymore away than what you read in the synopsis.

All I can say is  I must now purchase all the other books in this series as this is one of the best mysteries Ive read.  I loved the characters, their interactions with each other, the locale.  I even loved reading about how Liz takes her notes and organizes them (yea Im a bit of a nerd when it comes to organizing things).  Her family is also a great set of characters, specifically her father who acts like a true Southern father should, what with guns and shovels and fire at his disposal.

This is a mystery that grabs you from the start and makes you want to keep reading until you find out everything.  The writing is smart, funny, and interesting.  To be a mystery writer has got to be a huge challenge, and Susan M. Boyer meets that challenge.

Will Liz and Nate find out what happened to the daughter?  Will they be able to work out the differences their long distance relationship has?  Will her dad get rid of the rats inhabiting his backyard?  Buy the book and find out!

All her books are different in various ways. If I were to read them without knowing the author, I wouldn't know the same woman wrote them all. I think that says a lot.

This book is not quite what you think it is. And I am generally good at figuring out a bit in advance what shocker might pop up, but this time I didn't. Which was pretty awesome, because it meant that my mouth dropped open when it happened.

At first, I did have a hard time with the main character - mainly because I was jealous. Yes, I was jealous of a book character! Does that tell you how good the writing is?

You've got a bit of everything in this one: romance, erotic sex scenes, hot men, a strong female lead, secrets, and dare I say chick lit as well.

You think you know what this book will be about but really...you don't. You aren't sure initially whether you like the main character, for she is very flawed. Honestly, she scared me at first.

This book is a bit dark, but it captures you just as any good mystery will. After you get past your initial unease (and don't let it get to you - keep with the book), the story grabs you and holds on. You really cannot quite guess what will happen next, or how it will end.

Highly recommend.

I'm in my 40s and just found the whole book unrealistic.  I know books are an escape but this one was just too unbelievable for me. And the names of the characters were just...out there.  Totally took away from the story because all I could think was, "did she make this name UP?"

This book was truly over the top, laugh out loud funny.

Rosie is 23 years old and living with two friends from college, Delaney and Henry. Delaney's boyfriend Derk is also around quite a bit as well. Rosie majored in English and currently works for a magazine geared to cat lovers, while secretly trying to write a romance novel.

The only problem is, Rosie is a virgin. When her roommates see anything that she writes (lady garden?) they routinely reject anything she uses. With their encouragement, and offers from Henry himself, they urge her to get out there and lose that pesky virginity!

What follows is some of the funniest scenes I have ever read. Rosie's first wax with a woman named Marta is the best scene in the book; I almost peed myself while I read it.

You also get to read about other firsts for Rosie, as well as the variety of men she goes out on dates with, and the hilarious results of each date.

I enjoyed the writing very much and loved how the characters generally didn't hesitate to say what came to mind, like real people do when they are with friends they trust. The characters were also a lot of fun and very easy to like. The story flowed well, and I found it hard to put down.

The only thing that kept me from giving it five stars was that it was maybe a little bit too over the top...I've had some crappy luck dating but the things that happen to Rosie? She might have a little bit too much bad luck to be believable.

Either way - this is a great, fun read; especially if you really need a good, hearty laugh.

I started reading this series of books at the beginning of the year, and I am hooked.  I find them interesting, and I love all the mysteries.  But especially, I love the characters in the books.  If you love mysteries, especially the "paranormal" type, then these are for you.  I cannot wait to get to the next book.

This book tells the story of Ben, bass player and sexy bearded tattooed man who is my new book boyfriend, and Liz, who is the sister of Anne, wife of Mal. Sexy funny drummer extraordinaire. It starts with Liz taking a pregnancy test, which is very hot pink positive. Then we flashback to four months beforewhere we hear about the conception of said pinto bean (this is a phrase my family uses because the babies always look like pinto beans in their ultrasound photos, don't they?).

I loved this storyloved, loved, loved. The chemistry between Ben and Liz is awesome, even when you are reading the text messages they send each other. And Liz is hilarious. I laughed so many times reading this, but I also felt her heartache, because, and I quote the book here (not a spoiler):  "Ugh, boys suck. Such is life. What can you do?"

The sex scenes are off the chart, holy moly, freaking HOT. I found myself with this yearning for my own Ben that literally made me ache. In my lady parts. Ache, I say!

Deep can be read as a stand alone, but this whole series is so wonderfully good  well written, great characters, hard to put down  you really should do yourself a favor and buy them all.

I just finished and once again, Juliet Blackwell does not disappoint!! I adore this book series, and this one is just as good as the others.

First, let me say how much I enjoy her style of writing. I'll admit to being a person, when reading, that skips "details." Do I need to know about the town's history? Or what the heroine is wearing? No, I skip that and move onto the meat of the story. However, I do not skip a thing in these books. She makes the town of San Francisco come alive (and I have been fortunate enough to visit there). The history she includes, and the details of what is there today, make for not only entertaining but interesting reading. And I am drawn to the story associated with potions, herbs, medicinal and natural remedies...everything that Lilly works to "make" I find so interesting.

At any rate, I digress. I don't really like doing reviews that give away anything about the story line. Fans of the series will enjoy this one and it has been worth the wait.

And might I add, I think I am now falling in love with Sailor? Oh yea.

If you love mysteries, and you love books with of a paranormal type genre, you will LOVE this series. All these books are well worth your money and time.

And don't try to stick it into any particular genre.  This is great story telling.  Period.

This book tells the story of JD and Ark, and a woman they find on the streets that they call Blue.  Blue is hiding from people who mean to do her harm; and the people involved are closely related to dark events from JD's past.  A relationship develops amongst the three of them.  Blue wants to feel protected, and being with both men make her feel that way.

I was a bit hesitant going into this one as I am more into books with that have a one-on-one relationship.  However, with these characters and this story it doesn't come across as unbelievable.  JD and Ark were already best friends, and with Blue added into their home, they do seem to be a perfect family.

However, you don't have something going on with three people involved without there being secrets.  And perhaps a touch of jealousy.

I found this book hard to put down.  It was pure entertainment, and as you read, you want to find out how these characters resolve the issues of being three together are created.

There are some very steamy and wonderful love scenes, as well as some that maybe aren't necessarily "loving" but are very hot nonetheless.  The story has many twists and turns, and you are never sure where the story and characters are going.  That is what I like in a story.

Recommended reading for those who love steamy sex, and who like stories a bit on the darker side, and those of you who just want to be taken away and ENTERTAINED.

It is hard to find the words to express all the feels I had from this book. I will start off by saying I think this is the epitome of a great novel. It has everything. A great story, a wonderful couple that serves as the heroine and hero, the best supporting characters who you grow to care about just as much as you do the main characters.

To say I have a book hangover is a gross understatement of the feelings I have after completing this book.

This is the story of Kate, a young lady entering college just a year or so later than most who do right after high school.  Kate is from California, and is one of the most inspiring characters I have ever gotten the please to know.  Yes, you get to know Kate.  Kate is very much a believer of living for the moment, being spontaneous, doing what you enjoy, and living life to the fullest.  She has the ability to be forgiving in situations that most people in this world would not be.

Besides falling in love with Kate, I fell in love with her best friend, Gus.  Her love, Keller.  Her friends  Shelly, Clayton, Pete, Duncan, Stella.  These are a few of the people you meet and get to know in this superb read.

The authors writing is also perfect for the story she tells.  The pace of the story is just right, and you will have problems putting the book down.  And the feels?  Holy crap.  You will have them all.  You will laugh, you will get angry, you will cry and let me tell you, not a few tears sliding down your face.  This book will make you do the ugly cry.  Be prepared because if you don't want others seeing that ugly cry, you probably want to finish it while you are alone.  Or, if you are secure in that ugly cry, finish it (preferably) with a loved one so you can be comforted as well as express how you feel to them.

This book will make you want to be a better person.  It will make you want to live life.  You will not regret reading it at all.

10 out of 5 stars.  Seriously.

Thoroughly enjoyed this book!  Probably my favorite by this author.

It's a bit different from some of her past works, but not in a bad way at all.  I enjoyed all the characters, and identified with Tiffy.  I loved the advice that Fletcher gave about sexy, and I loved some of the things he had to say about how women are treated by certain kinds of men.

Supporting characters were also very strong - Claudio had me laughing in every scene he was in.  Cole was the epitome of "that guy."

Great read that I would recommend to anyone to check out.  Great story line, wonderful characters, awesome writing and hard to put down!

The story takes over from where The Syrian Virgin left off. Anissa is dealing with her feelings about Julien and Michael, while also dealing with moving forward with her college education, as well as worrying about the fate of her family who are in Raqqa.

Some of the issues? Julien's past, which he does not wish to speak to anyone about, including his therapist - specifically, after Anissa finally reveals the truth of her past to him. While he knows that the relationship he has with Anissa is special, Julien's past is one that he wants to open up to Anissa about, slowly. The two of them work on ways that Julien can show that he trusts Anissa while not opening up completely (at first), but their effort backfires and causes even more turmoil between the two of them.

Further, Anissa's sister ends up in a very dangerous situation - and Anissa needs the help of both Julien and Michael in order to assist Maria.

It is hard for me to express how much I enjoyed these two books. Not only are you getting the love story, but you are also being educated about the turmoil in the Middle East, and the atrocities that are happening there. What some people have to endure there, in their home towns, is frightening. You cannot help but want to be like the characters in the book, and find a way to educate people about what is happening. Without wanting to find ways yourself to help in any way possible.

Once again, I found it hard to put the book down. I was drawn into the story, which had a few twists I really did not see coming. I enjoy the characters and like them - and I am totally #teamJulien. There, I said it - I picked a side. Really, I picked that side while reading the first book.

I recommend this book for anyone who enjoys a good, entertaining, interesting story. I recommend it for those who simply want to learn more about our world as well.

This is the story of Beth, sister to Braden (books 1 &2), and Mark, who is a friend and now co-worker of Bradens. Braden and Mark went to law school together, and Beth has had a crush on him since she first met him when they visited her parents home while on break from law school.

Beth is a beautiful, very put together, smart, woman. However, when she is around Mark, she is struck dumb. Further, she turns into a complete klutz. She has actually, without meaning to, physically hurt Mark and herself with her awkwardness while being around him.

Mark has finally realized that he doesnt want to continue with hook-ups with various and sundry women who are also not looking for a commitment. It also doesnt hurt that he finds himself falling for Beth and her endearing awkwardness around him.

This is another wonderfully funny and sexy story from N.M. Silber. The scene where they are putting a computer together is priceless! Again, the books are a series but can be read as stand alones.

This is a great read, and I think if you enjoy feeling a little scared the closer we get to October and Halloween - then you will enjoy this book.

Paige's parents have moved her and her little sister to a new town following the death of their oldest daughter. Paige worshiped her older sister, and feels at a loss. Her mother dotes on her younger sister; her father seemingly ignores everyone and focuses on work. Now she has to start at a new school.

She soon finds herself quickly embraced by a group of what others at the school consider "misfits" (for lack of a better phrase), and opens up to them about gifts that she has. After she confides in them, they confide their own secret about interests that they feel she would only add to. (I don't want to say much, I do not want to give anything away)

Again, I really enjoyed this book. I had a very hard time putting it down, because I wanted to see how Paige saved not only this group of girls, but herself - from themselves. This book was a great combination of mystery, young adult, paranormal and suspense all wrapped into one wonderful package.

I usually struggle when I read books written by one gender who are writing from the point of view of the other gender. However, Matthew S. Cox does an awesome job in this book that is specifically told from Paige's point of view.

Highly recommend this book for lovers of all the genres I mentioned above; or if you just need a good read outside of your normal genre.

Wow. How to explain this read and my feelings...

First, it is titled as a memoir. However, each chapter tells of something different that has happened in Asa's life - from events during her teen years, to her relationships (friends and romantic), to her marriage, to her life as a porn star. It is almost as though you have auto-biographical essays of her life events, along with random thoughts thrown in that make the book damn entertaining.

The writing is really great. There were many times I laughed out loud while reading, as well as having thoughts of "this woman has some great ideas" - especially when it comes to the marriage bed (read the book).

Well written, entertaining, thoughtful at times, funny at times. I thoroughly enjoyed it.

This book also must be for those with an open mind! It contains stories that deal with her job; so if you are a prude, this book probably isn't for you - unless you want to read it to liberate yourself, that is.

Further, if the author decides to write more? I'm in. I want to hear more from her. There is something fabulous about reading an author who is open with her thoughts and feelings about her life and what she wants with no fear of what someone more conservative would think.

This is Book 2 of the Limbo Series, and I have to say...I enjoyed it even more than the first!

This time Parrish has a mystery close to her dad's home.  She is assisted by sexy FBI agent Marco.

In 1973, teenager Cece dies in a car accident.  Or was it an accident?  Cece shows Parrish the details that happened leading up to her death.

Cece starts when she is 16.  Her dad left years ago, and she and her mom live in a trailer park.  Her best friend going up, Erik, has become her boyfriend.  At her mother's insistence, Cece tries out and makes the cheerleading squad.  This gains her attention from Marshall, Mr. All American popular boy in school.  He soon asks Cece out, but she tells him no since she is dating Erik.  However, she does wonder what it would be like to go out with someone else - she has only known Erik.

She breaks up with Erik, who is heartbroken, and starts dating Marshall.  Erik then starts seeing the ex of Marshall - Angie.  Cece knows she has made a mistake, but continues to date Marshall.

Marshall isn't all he appears to be, and after showing his dark side to Cece, which Erik sees for himself - she breaks up with Marshall and reunites with Erik.  Marshall harasses her in an ugly manner at school, shows up at her home, and tries to get back together with Cece.  When she refuses, he becomes even uglier in his attitude with her.

Erik loves music and is in a band, and has a show one evening.  While driving to the show, Cece has her fatal car accident.  But Cece is in limbo - and has unfinished business she needs Parrish's help with in order to move on.

Again, this book had all the elements I personally love - a mystery, romance, even hotter sex this time (because we do move from Cece's last few months into Parrish's life as she solves the mystery), and supernatural themes.  I loved the 70s growing up, as those were my childhood years, and adored the visuals of that time as I read.

The love story between Cece and Erik is heartbreaking but touching, and the chemistry between Parrish and Marco is off the charts.  Marco is a sexy, devilish Italian and OMG I THINK I'M IN LOVE.

This story is a twist on Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs; more adult, more paranormal, and of course the romance is still there.  In this story, Snow has seven brothers who are vampire slayers.  They are royalty whose parents have died and who know must fend for themselves as the land they live in, Fairelle.

Four sons of the deceased king of Fairelle each call upon a djinn to grant one wish to each of them, which the djinn twisted.  One is transformed into a Vampire, another into a Werewolf, another powerful in magick as a Fae, and the last a Nereid who rules the sea.  This story (Book 2 in the Fairelle series, which can be read as a stand alone but reading Book 1 probably would not hurt) tells of the fight over Tanah Darah, where the vampires reside.

Snow has become the caregiver to her seven brothers, who spend much of their time either slaying vampires or training to slay vampires.  She yearns to join them in their battles while also wishing their lives were returned to normal.  She wants to find find her true love and be married.

Prince Sage has been in hiding in the Daemon Wastelands for fifty years.  He is a vampire, and his father was king of Tanah Darah.  His uncle killed Sages father and brother, and now rules there.  He has taken on as allies werewolves and a werebear, his friend Dax.  After seeing the vampire slayers in action against his uncles troops, Sage decides he must recruit them to help take back Tanah Darah.

He doesnt anticipate his plan backfiring, and pissing off the vampire slayers, while falling in love with their sister, Snow.

Though this book has paranormal elements, I enjoyed it because once again, I was taken back in time to when I read historical romances as a teen.  I adored reading those and gave them up at some point, yearning for more contemporary stories.  However, this is yet another book that though a paranormal/supernatural fairy tale is still very much a period piece.  Further, I enjoyed the action of the story, as well as the love story between Snow and Sage.  Snow initially is not a slayer, but her destiny slips into place and she must become one.  Once she does, she has to fight the natural desire of a slayer to kill any vampire in her sights  which includes Prince Sage, who she also has fallen in love with.

The author creates a land that you can picture in your mind clearly; the forest, Snows special cabin, the Daemon Wastelands.  The characters are likeable, and each of the seven brothers have distinct personalities that you cant help but identify with and like.  Initially, when I read the preface, I was worried that I might not be able to keep up with the lands, the characters, the prophecies  but once you started reading the story, the author guided you in a way that made it not only easy to understand, but so interesting.  I did not want to put the book down til I finished.

Highly recommend this one for lovers of the supernatural type of romances.  A fun, exciting read.

Just a fun, quick read. Probably best read prior to any Black Friday shopping. I laughed at several things; the author definitely has a way with words. I think everyone who read this would enjoy it, especially if you ever are brave and head out on Black Friday.

I was drawn to this book as a 45 year old who years for excitement, and being able to do what the heroine in this book did:  take several months off to live life.  Our heroine never married or had children, so she is a bit too dedicated to her job, and apparently was able to have a pension (what is that??), which gives her the luxury of a six month road trip.  How I envy her!

I found the book to be enjoyable, especially considering my life situation.  I don't know if anyone in their 20s or maybe even 30s would enjoy it as much.  It is hard to be in your 40s and date.  It is hard to be in your 40s and feel like you aren't living life and being yourself.

The characters in the book are true to life; though one had a daughter who was really just MEAN.  I have witnessed kids being brats and so forth, but the grown child of one of the heroine's friends takes the cake - you will want to reach into the book and grab her around the throat and shake her!

In a nutshell, you have the heroine who is going thru her "mid-life" crisis.  Her sister, who is going through a divorce after more than twenty years of marriage.  And their good friend who might as well be family who has been hurt in the past, and who is scared to open up to not only the man in her life, but embrace being a grandmother.

Our hero can be a bit of a jerk, but he does come around and realizes that you cannot judge a book by its cover.  And his best friend and the best friend's wife?  Love them.  The only time I didn't was when the wife encouraged our hero to (basically) lie to the heroine.  That really bothered me and I felt it didn't really go along with the character as well as the situation in her life.

A great read for those in their 40s, or maybe 30s, who wonder is this all there is to life - going to work, then coming home?  It will make you think.  And hopefully encourage you to fulfill any dreams you have.

Kyle returns to her home town for the funeral of a childhood friend. She hasn't been home in years thanks to events from the best involving another death. It's been twelve years since she has seen Garin, who was her first love; who she is still in love with. Garin is understandably upset - Kyle moved out of town all those years before, without a good bye or explanation.

They go out to eat dinner after the funeral. Imagine Kyle's surprise when she wakes the next morning in a prison cell...with Garin.

Again, this is a dark read. The writing, as always from Marni Mann, is top notch and entertaining. Plus there is the mystery - what happened all those years ago that Kyle is hiding from Garin? What does she know about their other friend's death from twelve years ago? You are as in the dark as Garin is.

There are twists you don't see coming, which make it hard to put the book down.

I've mentioned twice that it is a dark read; this has some of the most disturbing scenes I have read as far as this kind of genre. I do not consider myself a person to shrink away from certain kinds of scenes, but this book contained some violence that was hard for me to deal with.

It is a great story, and I loved the twists. It is not for the faint of heart, at all.

For you who have been reading Ace's stories, this one starts out with her making a court appearance for a "situation" that occurred at the Walmart. Yes, I know now you want to read it.

This short story was 100% laugh out loud. I could hardly breathe at one point, I was laughing so hard. I can sure sympathize with Ace. And honestly, she has the best one liners around.

If you follow Ace, get this one. If you haven't read these books by Stephanie McAfee - you need to. They are truly laugh out loud, great, fun stories.

I do have a lot of authors I fans of whose books I love, but these books & this author are the most special to me. I have never identified with the character in a book as much as I do Ace.

users.query: I sooooo loved this story, I won't give a synopsis, but I will say this was a great premise, the story line was believable although irritating but that's what made it believable! She made the right choice in the end though I wanted to strangle her throughout the book lol! Especially towards the end smh! But this was a great emotional roller coaster ride that kept me on the edge of my seat, I can't wait for part 2! Great Job Anna! Keep them coming girl because I will continue to read.

cands.text: I truly enjoyed this story, how it flowed, melded together and seemed very much so real. I wasn't happy about the ending because I wanted them to work it out lol, I guess we have to wait for pt 2. Overall, great story and it was done correctly, not to fast or slow, not overly exaggerated it was just right, great read.

This was an okay book, not a page turner but okay.  I thought the main female character was a bit nosey and overstepping her bounds, I'm glad she finally got to the truth, but the story didn't really rope you in, its the kind of book you pick up and read when you have nothing else to do. It's not a bad story at all, it's just not exciting.

Maybe I didn't read the same book, the heroine was very nerve wracking and not likable at all, I'm really trying to see what the two men saw in her, she was kind of selfish, brash, inner self loathing because she was constantly thinking one thing and saying another and just came off as a total itch to me.  The storyline in itself was good, the plot was good, but her interaction with people besides her girls and her control freak 'when I speak people listen' ways just completely made me wish there was another character to dwell on, she really got on my nerves and made the story not click to me.  And the ending, yeah it just didn't fit the rest of the story to me.
Great cute and funny love story! I really enjoyed the characters, just goes to show not to judge a book by it's cover, or it's defense mechanism.

Great Book! I wasn't expecting to like Keisha, I didn't want to like her lol, but I did.  She and Jay had a lot of emotional growing to do, and they did it.  I read this and Mistress twice before leaving this review, great story, not gonna tell it because others already have so do yourself a favor and just get it and read it.  You won't be disappointed!
Loved it! It's a super must read just like Tender Secrets! A lovely tale of friends to lovers, painful secrets, understanding, acceptance and newfound love, Ann does it again.

This is truly a great story! VERY realistic, touching and just overall good, there are enough reviews giving a synopsis of the story so I will leave that to them.  Just know that you won't be disappointed even when you feel like one or more of the characters are wrong or doing to much or just the opposite.  Get it for yourself and read it you will love it.  Great Job Anna Black!!

Loved Chastains and Phillips story! It was about time and long over due.  I do wonder whats going to happen to the new found relationship that was discovered at the end though, that was the only downfall, the questions at the end in regards to her parents and what possibly happened with and to them, otherwise another great read!

I don't know what I was expecting from this book, and I must have gotten the re-edited version because my version was fine.  Anyway, the story kind of took me by surprise by how well it was written.  I've never read from this author before so I was prepared for anything.  The characters and scenarios in this story was very realistic, we all have our group of girls and most of us have been through many ups and downs with each other.  We don't all agree with some of our friends way of life, the things they do or don't do, their naivete, blatant blinders on type of living but we are all still girls.  That's what this book is about, yes you will want to shake some of these girls and yell WHAT IS WRONG WITH YOU?!?!?! BUT we all know someone or even know someone that knows someone that fits these characters and the scenarios in their life.  Just goes to show to never judge a book by it's cover, and if you don't want to be judged or reprimanded for your actions don't run to folks looking for a shoulder to cry on instead of a reality check. I will be looking forward to other titles from this author, this was a very good book.

Okay once again, because other reviewers give synopsis of the story, I will not! You already know what it's about, so I will say it's a GREAT story.  Very true to heart and I LOVE that the big woman gains ground, though she's stubborn to a point and a little naive, she's a great lead character, and the supporting players do their job.  This is a story most can relate too whether they admit it or not. It sheds insight on things that possibly goes unseen in close relationships but that needs to be addressed and dealt with.  Thanks Anna for bringing it back around again! This woman Anna Black is going to be huge! So you see, new authors can stand up and be seen and heard, she has a new following in me!

This was a really great book, though Tracy made me proud and kind of irritated, I loved her rational way of thinking but hated how she thought of herself and how she let her so called friend stagnate her self esteem.  The Love story was very nice, sweet and passionate, I'm glad they stuck it out regardless.

Okay, this was an engaging story! You need to read for yourself to get your own feel, but I liked it.  Though I had more than a few questions like how was Trey getting away with ALLLL of that stuff and nothing ever happened, why didn't Neisha open her darn mouth and say something, and how did her man get away with what he did at the end??? Where did the drama with Raja-Nee and Aaron come from out of left field? It was a few more questions that hopefully the next book will answer. Over all a good story nonetheless.

Funny, mildly suspenseful and just an overall GREAT read! Michelle was going through it trying to figure out her 'straight out of a romance novel' man! She wondered, questioned and even had a few delirious type thoughts and dreams trying to figure out why her 'man' wouldn't have sex with her.  And BOY did she ever find out in the most hilarious way ever! I LOVED Daryl, now THAT'S a man worth many fantasies (fanning self).  Great Job Mr. Lewis, this book was FIRE! I can't wait to read more from you!

I don't even know where to begin, this book was GREAT! It touched on everything, I'm not going to give a preview I will say I LOVED Stan and Prissy's relationship, the relationship with their kids, still don't like Celeste in fact I can't stand her even more lol.  GREAT story, great read, I didn't want it to end, I actually cried at the end because it was so good and loving and funny and HOTTTT! Those Wolf Pack men are something else, even with their flaws and all love it! I love Maureen Smith, I haven't read a book from her yet that I have not liked. GREAT JOB! This is the first book I've read this year and it set the tone for all of the other books that I will read, so I hope my authors come with it because the bar has been set beyond high!

I was quite surprised, this was a good little story that I'm sure some people can relate too.  I know this author will only continue to get better, if a part two comes out I will surely read it.  Good Job.

I don't know what I was expecting but it wasn't this! This was a great story with well read characters, the plot made sense and was well written.  This is my first book by this author but it won't be my last.

This was a great story, nothing like I thought it would be though I must say the two men in this story pissed me off, I can't wait for the sequel! I wish I had waited to read this until the sequel came out because I'm very impatient lol, and this book had me on edge waiting to see Tamia's fate, but I have to wait (sigh) I know somebody better redeem themselves otherwise I might have to jump into this story and smack some people around smh.  GREAT STORY! PLEASE HURRY WITH PART2!

I read this some years ago, it was a good story! Unique was making a way out of no way though once again it's one of those things she really didn't have to do but she was in love with money and taking care of her baby sister, another tale with to much name dropping but that can be overlooked.  I liked the fact that she added in her Mothers mental illness as well as her mans, plus the issue with her sister which was crazy.  It was a great story though, I really enjoyed it.
These reviews cant be real, the storyline was good but the execution sucked. This book was corny, the writing  style and dialogue was very amateurish, not a good book at all.

I absolutely loved this story.  It was about love, sacrifice, compromise, fighting temptations, making decisions and having to stand firm.  Seeing so much of Cinnamon in Aura was so endearing to me, and seeing the love she and MII had for each other despite their differences was very heartfelt and realistic.  Let me just say I don't like Abigail and I'm glad she and Rkoyo can be friends for Amy's sake. I hope there is a part two because I need to see if Aura will be able to continue to fight for her marriage and what that Abigail is going to do, did I say I don't like her lol.  I'm also glad MII stood up to his Mother, she needs Jesus seriously. I love Angelia's writing style and the way she tells the story, it's so realistic and hits home in many ways, I absolutely loved it.

Nice premise, good story line and development, but it was predictable. I knew from when she said they couldn't view the body and that Jay had been cremated that he wasn't dead and would pop up at the end after her and Wayne got close. Something told me to read the reviews in the middle of the book. I realized it's been out for a while and is supposed to have a sequel. What really bothers me is the cliffhanger. I HATE cliffhanger books, especially when there isn't another book. Seeing as though this book has been out since 2015 or longer, I guess there won't be a 2nd book. Well I skipped from 30% to the last chapter, the old back from the dead cliche...time to try something new.

I get where the author was trying to go and what they were trying to do but still, this book confused the crap out of me, it was like walking in on the middle of a conversation with a person who is talking part ways in their head and the other part out loud.  I can't even explain it, I was overall confused.

The story ALMOST had potential, but it was written horribly.  It seemed like the author wrote out ideas for the story and just submitted it, no development, many inconsistencies especially in the timeline, it was very amateurish and mostly unbelievable.  It was rushed and some of the things that happened (the drama) just didn't seem realistic and was way over the top.  The characters were underdeveloped and mostly dumb so they weren't relatable.  The situations they found themselves in just didn't make sense for grown supposedly professional people, who allows the brother of the man that attacked you multiple times to stay with them, get a love letter from them and don't tell their man.  Who just tells their family that they are engaged to someone they aren't even dating?? It's many other things like the way things happened and how rushed it was, the obliviousness of the characters to certain situations, and even the things that were being said. There wasn't enough details about the characters to give you insight into their mindsets, the men all seem like entitled unrealistic whiny wussies, and the females were either confused whores, delusional whores, or just confused and very nave.  It had promise, if this was just an outline and an actual story had been written, but the story as is, well it's simply an unbelievable unrealistic mess.

users.query:
Terrific acting but the direction leaves something to be desired.  Most memorable are the Peter Lorre character, the police commissioner and the miserable old pawn broker.  Lorre's complex character deserves careful dissection.  He lives in abject poverty but, with the help of his poor mother, manages to graduate with high honors with a degree in criminology.  His future--and the future of his family--should be guaranteed except for the fact that our 'hero' is idiosyncratic to the point of deep pathology.  He has a schizoid personality disorder characterized, in part, by truly incredible arrogance and delusions of grandeur.  He commits a murder which is almost a 'thrill kill.'  He thinks he can commit the perfect crime because he is far more intelligent than the police.

Here is where I think the film is misdirected.  It should have, in my opinion, been a study of the unrelenting power of a guilty conscience.  The character should have behaved rather intelligently and coolly until 'done in' by his own guilty soul.  Instead the director produces a character who is so peculiar, weird and unlikeable that he draws attention to himself.  His guilt is a neon sign.  Not just once but over and over.  Ultimately he leaves no room for himself.  Everybody knows he is guilty.

cands.text:
This is a great, but uncomfortable film, about a deeply flawed man.  Dixon Steele.  Although he hasn't written a successful script for some time, is still a highly regarded writer.  He is also a revolving, 360 degree pig.  He is moody, self-centered with numerous flashes of violent anger.  Because, as we learn, Dix had some kind of unspecified military role during the War, we might conclude that Dix' personality is the product of PTSD.  That would be a far too superficial analysis of the labile, non-insightful Dix.

A lovely young woman has been brutally murdered.  She is the same young woman Dix lured to his apartment the previous night on the pretext of her retelling and summarizing a book she's written and would like to see worked into the script of a film.  The whole thing--including the girl--is so shallow and dreary to the world-weary Dix that he tells her to find her own way home.  "Here's some money for the taxi."  He gallantly offers.

The next morning Dix is picked up by the cops and interrogated.  On learning of the girl's death, Dix is neither frightened nor guilty about the fact that, by not seeing her safely home, he has inadvertently delivered her up to death.  Dix, as a matter of fact, is cool, calm, unflustered and uncaring.  He's even too stupid to recognize that his thoughtless behavior NECESSARILY puts him under the police microscope.  Let me emphasize that these are not PTSD symptoms.  They are symptoms of something far darker and deeper...something produced perhaps by twisted DNA.

The woman Dix supposedly loves becomes increasingly frightened of her unpredictable paramour.  She doesn't know whether he's a murderer or not but she does know that he's explosive and dangerous.  She's caught in a classical 'abused woman' scenario.  She needs to get out...and get out now...before he kills her.

I believe Bogart was at his very best when playing deeply flawed characters.  'Treasure of the Sierra Madre' and 'The Caine Mutiny' are other excellent examples.

A complex tragedy that gives the impression of relentless, inevitable fate.  This impression is enhanced by the first moments of the film in which a man is killed and we see the killer 'holed up' in the same hotel room in which he shot his victim.  There are a series of flashbacks in which our protagonist, the killer [played sympathetically by Jean Gabin], reviews the events leading up to the murder.

There is love, mendacity, disgust and bottomless jealousy.  The 'heavy', the murdered man, is truly reprehensible degenerate who adds young women to his score like a gun fighter puts notches on his gun.  Fate, uncontrolled temper and the police play their inevitable roles.  Francoise, our pitiful killer, is far more grieved about revelations about the girl he loved than he is about the killing, itself.

Then again, what if Francoise acted impulsively on a disgusting lie?

This is a tale of almost criminal insight.  Having done a little writing myself, I was overwhelmed by the author's vision.  This is possibly the best work of fiction I've ever read.  It is so beautifully crafted, I wish I hadn't read it.  I wonder how Dubus did it?  Did he start with a basic construction in mind and then ride the winds of logic and illogic?  Did he rely on ancient Greek Tragedies for a guide?  Did he use an outline or did he simply plumb the depths of his own psyche?  I almost feel sorry for an author who could weave such a marvelous tapestry of self-destruction. Personally, I don't have ten percent Dubus skill and depth of knowledge of the human condition.and I'm very glad I don't.

Fate, stupidity, pride, miserable decisions are the clay from which this wonderful story is modeled.  Much of it is illogical but.and I think this is why this book is so very disturbing.the various characters are very real.  If one has personal insight, he can probably see a little [or a lot] of himself here.  We have all screwed up, haven't we?  Hopefullyhopefully.we won't put too many of our screw-ups back to back and produce the ultimate disaster but the possibility is always there..

A highly suspenseful 'whodunit'' or, more accurately, 'Whose going to do it?"  Everybody has a motive, complete with portentous glances, mysterious occurrences, secrecy, greed and lies.  There is heavy, ominous music that both builds the suspense and sometimes misdirects.  The acting and direction are excellent.  I was taken by one extremely brief scene is which a helpful male 'friend' briefly glances at the actress's backside as she turns to walk away.  Was it acting or instinct?

I rented five movies for a long weekend.  Breaking with my usual pattern, I rented fairly recent releases.  Three were terrible, one OK and the fifth, 'An American Crime' superb.

This is anything but an upbeat film in that it is a 'true' story from the 1960's of child abuse and murder.  The acting is wonderful even if the actors are playing monsters.  The film starts with a separated couple, with two children, planning a reexploration of their relationship without he pressure of children.  They leave their two girls with a woman they barely know who already has a house full of children

We watch this stranger-woman as she ranges between depressive and seductive behaviors.  One of her actual daughters gets pregnant--which the woman is mentally incapable of accepting.  She believes, however, that one of her foster daughters has started the 'lie' that her actual birth-daughter is a pregant slut.  The woman undergoes progressive deterioration, punishing her foster daughter brutally for no real reason.  She beats her and burns cigarette butts into her skin.  She has one of her sons throw the hapless girl down the coal skuttle, seriously injuring her.

She then manacles her foster daughter because she 'still requires punishment for being a whore.'  She invites her own children and neighborhood children to brutalize her.  They are all too cooperative and beat, kick and burn her.  They finally carve the initials on her abdomen "I am a prostitute and proud of it."  Her frequent agonizing screams are heard by neighbors who don't want to get involved.

Basically, what is depicted is a sadomasochistic woman descending into depression and psychosis.  There is a trial and conviction.  The woman, and even her own children, are convicted of child abuse.  The woman gets life in prison but is out in twenty years for 'good behavior'.  Heartbreaking.

I think this film can be viewed in a philosophical and even scientific light.  William Golding's 'Lord of the Flies' and some of Sam Peckinpah's movies emphasize their beliefs that chidren are born morally neutral and must be correctly socialized to produce 'safe', civiilized human beings.  Without such socialization children and later adults are dangerous.  In an 'An American Crime', we see an example of negative socialization.  An adult--a psychotic adult--actually gives permission for children to behave in horrific ways. Not surprisingly, just as the marooned children in 'Lord of the Flies', the children engage in barbarous behaviors.

A corollary to this is that the potential for monstrous behavior is just beneath the skin of many of us which probably explains certain otherwise inexplicable individual crimes and mass political/governmental crimes where 'permission' from the highest levels.

Ron Braithwaite author of novels--"Skull Rack" and "Hummingbird God"--on the Spanish Conquest of Mexico
