Loved this sweet love story so much I did not want it to end.

Olivia has just landed a job with a LA Public Relations agency. Her first assignment is to look after actor Austin Ford on a planned vacation with his actress "girlfriend " Cassidy Evans. While on the vacation in Hawaii, Cassidy comes up with a new stunt and is driving Austin crazy. Austin wants his life back and that includes Olivia, but Cassidy has more twists and turns to keep him to herself. Olivia is trying hard to live up to the rules from her boss - no dating clients and make the world believe Austin and Cassidy are a couple. With her job on the line if things go wrong and her heart telling her other things, she feels torn. Will Austin get his life back and Olivia with that???

**ARC provided by author in exchange for an honest review**

GREAT SERIES!!! This book is the last and I must say I will miss this group of friends.

After making a pact last year with her four friends to all have a date for New Year's Eve, Gemma is the only one without. Not only have her friends found dates, they also all found their Mr. Right's this past year. Two of the girls are involved with Carmichael brothers. Because of that, Gemma has been linked in the tabloids to the third brother Greg or Mr. Commitment-Phobic having been seen with him at different functions. As they celebrate the engagement of two of the couples over the holidays at a Carmichael resort, the search is on for the man to kiss. Once the single men hear about Gemma and the New Year's kiss they all try to win her over, but she only has eyes for one. Greg does not want a relationship, but can't seem to stop thinking about Gemma. He knows Gemma is looking for more than casual and will not cross that line. As her privacy and safety are being threatened from being linked to him he feels responsible and helps her with it. Will Gemma consider causal with Greg and risk her heart?  Will Greg win her New Year's Eve Kiss?

Miranda has written a beautiful story about family, friends and happily-ever-after with a lots of spice and suspense. Don't miss this series!!!

DO NOT MISS this story! In Vivian's List you meet Liam and Viv as they start a relationship before he heads back to Iraq. Liam's List is an emotional beautiful story with a little humor along the way of how they dealt with being apart and his return. Liam returns back home from Iraq to Vivian as a different man. He struggles with the blame he puts on himself for want happened during his last tour. As Vivian tries to help Liam cope, she also has to learn to cope. This is their journey as they fight for their love.

I had a hard time putting this story down. The author has you feeling what so many brave soldiers have to deal with after they have fought for us and how their love ones have to fight to get them back. Vivian loves Liam and Liam loves her, but there were some dark times he thought he might lose her. This is a story of growth and love that has you crying, fighting, and laughing along with some very sexy, hot love scenes. You learn so much more about Liam, Vivian and their family and friends. I can wait for the next book with this great group!!!

Copy provided by author

Oh boy this couple's the best!!! I loved this super sweet, sexy novella! This is Damien and Nikki Stark - balancing life and making decisions. This is what most women have to deal with in life. There are so many emotions women go through just trying to get through the day. This is a beautiful story of love, understanding, family, work and balancing it all.

**ARC provided by author**

WOW - There is so much to this book. As this is the first book in a trilogy there is a cliffhanger, so be prepared.

Caleb Stone is a very successful business man who is trying to change his image. Everything about him is a mystery. His first change is a school that is need of help from possibly getting closed. He donates money and his time to help the school. Francesca Radley is a teacher at the school who is extremely headstrong after growing up with parents that tried to dictate her life. Caleb and Francesca butt heads on more than one occasion. Now for image change two - to portray himself in a steady relationship. He soon enters an agreement with Francesca. Caleb has some answers about Francesca's early childhood which she knows very little about and makes that part of the deal. Day by day Francesca sees and tries to learn the Dr. Jekyll and Mr Hyde personalities of Caleb, as she challenges him every step of the way.

The two characters have secrets, strong personalities, and a sexual attraction. Will they survive their fake relationship???

This is Lily's first book and she is off to a great career as a writer. Can't wait for the rest of Caleb and Francesca's stories.

ARC received by author via Fifty Shades Support Group in an exchange for an honest review

I really enjoyed this book a lot! You feel this story from the first page and you can't stop reading. The characters are so real, likable and understandable. I did read Gabe's story in Destined first which I think helps you understand him better. Both Gabe and Mia have different attachments issues stemming from their childhood. Neither one has truly been in love before so the romance is emotional and steamy. For Mia, Gabe was to be a one night no strings, but for Gabe, Mia is so much more. This story takes you on their journey as they fight their way to love.

This story will have you laughing at times, but also pulls on our heartstrings. The writing is super - a Do NOT MISS! What a way for C.J. Fallowfield to start her writing career.

**ARC provided by NetGalley via Beyond the Page Publishing for an honest review**

A sweet, funny novella about an ex football player, now sports writer and the new girl in his apartment building. Once Jake meets Sophie in the elevator he knows he would love to date her.  In the blog Jake writes, he decides to mention Sophie, who he writes about as elevator girl.  Once they learn more about each other, things become messy and it leaves Jake trying to figure out the next play in the game of love and life.

users.query: This was a good way to end the series. The story didn't dragged out and the author made sure she closed the story lines with Tensley and Molly. I'm excited about the other characters getting their own books.

cands.text: I don't know why I waited so long to read this series. I loved the ending their story. It didn't drag out and it was perfect. The other books all helped build the final outcome in this book.
Ms. Harper ended the series with a great plot. I never saw any of it coming. As far as story telling, thus was probably the best book in the series.

This pains me because I love Ms Dawn. However I could not finish this book. Ironically I found the other characters she wrote about to be more interesting. Maybe this series only need one long book for these character instead of three. I lost interest in Beth and D. I became more interested in his children. A series on the whole family would have been more interesting to me.
How did I miss this book?! This was such a great outstanding start to a series. I love characters and can't wait for more.

This book was wonderful. I must admit I was impressed. I didn't think she could pull it off.

The book read very smooth. At times, when the story plot needed to be rushed it was and at times when it needed to be slowed down it was. Loved the imagery and the characters. I'm hoping next book we get Dual POV as I would love to know what Des is thinking sometimes.

Great book! I can't wait until the next one comes out.

This book was definitely different than other things that Ms Dawn has written before. The plot didn't seem as intricate as some of her other book series. Though traditionally, her first book in the series are very lite in plot and development compared to others.

As always, I love the strong female characters she creates. I definitely felt like this book was short. Not a novella but shorter than a good sit down read.

Definitely looking forward to book number 2.

This book was given to me in exchange for an honest review by the author.

Ms. Crane does a good job with continuing her story of Stella Stonewall. There were definitely some twists and turns I did not see coming which I appreciated. The book  wasn't predictable. Can't wait to read the next book.

This series has potential. The first book seems to just be a prequel or set up for the remaining series. This book could have quickly been reduced to a novella. I am not ruling out the series yet. I'll wait until the next book to make my final decision.
Second book was good. First. I appreciated how the author quickly went through four years. I was glad it didn't draw out. I loved the happy cliffhanger. Awesome job on this book.
This was a great sequel. A lot happened in this book and I'm interested to see how the next book pans out. I deducted one star as I felt there where quite a bit of fillers in the beginning.

This series has some potential. I like the fact that the book started off quick and to the point. I also like the fact that it was unpredictable. I thought I had the authors plot figured out but every time I was pleasantly surprised.

I love how all the books are started to intertwine. This was a great book. 4 stars for sure. I only left it T 4 because I still feel like there are too many secrets lefts. I can't wait for the next book.
This was a good book. I liked how this book was in dual point of view. We were able to understand and see the emotional turmoil both  characters went through.

It's a novella. I'm not a fan of novella because of their shortness but I'll put myself through torture just for Ms. Dawn.

With that said if you're a fan of her Forevermore, you'll appreciate the relationship between these two characters. I was a little disappointed because the book seemed to jump years, days, and topics with little to no explanation plus no development between the characters.

I know it's novella but having just finished Moon Mark, I was expecting a little more development. Plus the description reads about a test of her true heart.... Yeah, no test really happens. It just seemed the description really stretched the story a bit.

Love Ms. Dawn but was a little disappointed with the development. Though I did love the Lucifer and Arizona.
Amazing!!!  Can I say it again, amazing!!! Why did this end in a cliffhanger?! I can't wait until the next book. You'll fall in love with Lucien and Lena.
This book was amazing. Finally something outside the box. This was a breath of fresh air to read about something so simple but so true. All characters were believable and relatable.
I definitely thought this was the best book in the series. It really shows you how the main characters have grown since the start.
This was a great sequel. I can't wait for the final book. I loved how Callie grew into the strong heroine. I loved Des's point of view also
Grace Draven did a wonderful job. I loved the story. This sequel match and even exceeded the first book. Can't wait to see what she writes next.

This book definitely has some events that are trigger points for some people. Even I cringed  at a few points. However, I have read the whole series and the first book is probably the worst of it all. Would I recommended this book knowing how the series ends..... yes I most definitely will.
This book is not for the faint at heart. This is your happy immediately fall in love your story. This is angst, this is pain, this is mercy, this is love.

This gas your standard Jay McLean thumbprint on it. A little bit more aghast than I expected but I was surprised by the story layout.

I do love the new set of brothers and I'm looking forward to Logan's story.
Ivy seems to be by favorite Helen Harper female character so far. This was a good book and I am excited about the next few books in the series.
This was a good book and introduction into the series. I can't wait to read the other books in the series.

users.query: I am very pleased that, for once, I was able to read a book totally devoted to Heydrich.  This person (Heydrich), was the most demonic character at the higher echelons of the Nazi hierarchy.  He was ambitious and ruthless.  The authors of this book do a good job in bringing alive this historical figure.  Unfortunately, I have to say that the chapters are rather long (without sub-divisions) and some passages lack clarity.  This book deserves an ample readership.

cands.text: In this quasi encyclopedic book the author brings alive the SS and the men that ran that organization.  I did learn more about Himmler's and Heydrich's character in this book than in their respective biographies.  This learned effort by Mr. Hhne combines scholarship with anecdotes and historical "trivia".  This book will shed light on most readers about the organizational structure, mission and the legacy of horror that the SS left at its wake.  Upon reading this book it was impressed on me the importance of checking budding dictatorships at their outset.

Upfront, I have to admit that I did enjoy this thoroughly researched book.  This biography has a lot of information not only on its subject (Himmler) but on Germans, Nazism in power, "the final solution", and the other leading characters of the Nazi regime, as well.  Some sentences, indeed, full passages, are rather abstruse.  There is a widespread use of speculation by the author regarding Himmler's motivations and actions.  Mr. Padfield also engages into detailed psychoanalysis, mainly regarding Himmler, without being clear how qualified he might be on this field.  Overall, this book is worth reading if you are truly interested in this historical period.

This book was originally written in German and I think the English version is a very good one.  The book can be monotonous at times but, over all, it is vey instructive.  The book filled some gaps I had on the "Nazi" saga after reading the biographies of Hitler, Himmler and, Goering.

  Goebbels was a very effective propagandist and a great orator.  Hitler's aura and mystique was, to a certain extent, the result of Goebbels's propaganda efforts.  Goebbels stood firm behind Hitler up to the bitter end.

  The story is compelling and the narrative is decent.  You will not be disappointed with this biography.

This is the first book from Mr. Lewy that I have read but will not be the last one.  The plight of the Gypsies during the Nazi rule is presented to the readers in a dignified and scholarly fashion.  This is a highly readable book, well argued, and it covers its intended subject with ease, respect and, in a concise manner.  I will not attempt a synopsis here; it suffices to say that the author captures the soul of the ordeal endured by the Gypsies under the Nazi murder machine.  Although the author does not consider that the Gypsies were specifically targeted for what was later to become known as genocide (except the mass sterilizations), he recognizes the grievous harm done to that community due to so called racial considerations and also due to the predominant life style of the Gypsies.  This book deserves five stars.

This is a book quite different to any other book I have read before.  It is probing, controversial and, speculative.  It has a philosophical bent to it and will make you think.

  The book revolves not only about Hitler but also about the Holocaust and the Germans.  Before reading this book, I happened to read Daniel Jonah Goldhagen's "Hitler's willing executioners".  Goldhagen puts the Holocaust's responsibility squarely on the Germans but "Explaining Hitler" goes deeper and entertains the additional possibility that "no Hitler, no Holocaust".

  The book has somewhat long chapters that sometimes feels were written in a haphazard fashion and, as a result of this, it is not a reader friendly book as far as reading mechanics go.

This book was written a few decades back but still has an allure to it.  The book depicts most of the brutalities performed by the members of this infamous organization (the Gestapo that is).  Also, the book brings alive the main characters of the Gestapo and other sister organizations (the SD for example) and paints a background that enables the reader to see the "forrest" in spite of the tall trees.  The prose is beautiful and clear thus making the book highly readable.  Trying to unravel the mind of the Germans, the author engages a bit into German bashing.  This is a book that I am happy to own.

I had read another biography of Adolf Hitler that I thought it was very complete before reading this book, but, upon reading this first tome of Ian Kershaw's two tome biography of Hitler, I realized how much superior, detailed and, balanced, is Mr. Kershaw's effort as compared to the other author's effort.  Mr. Kershaw seemed equally scrupulous and fair in presenting Hitler's failings as he was in presenting Hitler's major accomplishments.  This is a huge book, judged by any standard, that is worthy of your monetary investment at acquiring it and, of your precious time.  Do not miss out on this opportunity of being illustrated about Hitler and his times, by a foremost expert and scholar on the aforementioned subjects.

This book explains how most adult Germans of the Nazi era (1930's and 1940's)were capable of embarking themselves into the genocidal project that with time became known as the Holocaust.

  Antisemitism was the precursor of genocide.  The author mentions how Christianity, sometimes, have been associated with hate against the Jews (portraying them as the killers of Christ and resenting the Jews' "rejection" of Christianity as the True Faith).  Later on in History (mainly during the 19th century), antisemitism gained a pseudo scientific status when Jews were labeled a distinct Race (and an evil and inferior one at that).This new "approach" prevented even converted Jews from escaping persecution.

  Several European countries did embrace antisemitism; in Germany it became pervasive, infecting all strata of the German society.  This widespread German antisemitism defied reason and moderation and it allowed Hitler's genocidal dreams to become a reality.  Because a great deal of Germans were willing to torture and kill Jews, Hitler was able to slaughter six million Jews.

  The author is very methodical while pressing his points. I learned a great deal from this book.  The only reason I did not give this book five stars is my impression that the author could have accomplished the same results with a hundred or one hundred and fifty pages less.  Other than that, it is required reading for any one interested in World War Two.

It took me a few months to finish this 760 pages book but it was time well invested.  This book is a remarkable achievement.  You will find in it the parallel stories of both J. Edgar Hoover and his creature, the FBI.

  J. Edgar Hoover was already on the government's payroll by the presidency of Woodrow Wilson and he remained a Federal employee until his death in 1972 during Richard Nixon's presidential tenure.  He shaped the FBI making it a highly effective investigative law and order organization.  You could say the man and the agency had the same strengths and weaknesses.

  The author, Curt Gentry, excelled at all the imaginable standards with this biographical work.  The book is informative, an eye opener, highly readable and, comprehensive.  This book stands also as a literary jewell.  I wish all biographies were as well researched and written as this one.

I thoroughly enjoyed the way Mr. Johnson presented his warning to American society.  There are dark forces actually trying to take over the world (do you remember those calling for a "New World Order" ?).  Mr. Johnson calls them Imperialists (which they are) but they are better known to us as the Shadow Government, or, the Deep Government.  If you value your freedom, please, read this book.

Vo Nguyen Giap's story is a remarkable one.  This is a man that, with no formal military training, built a crack Army from scratch.  He also led that same Army to victory over two major World Powers, namely, France and the USA.  The author of this book succeeded in writing one of the best biographies I have read.  The author is impartial and fair.  You will be delighted by the artful writing of the author.  Overall, this is a very entertaining and informative book.

This is a good book even if it does not resemble a conventional biography.  The book has scant information on Goering's private life concentrating itself, rather, on Goering's performance at the helm of the German economy during Nazi rule.  The author has a superb grasp of the subject at hand and he does portray an encompassing picture of German economic affairs during World War 2.  Mr. Overy is an accomplished writer; his sentences are elegant and clear.  Nonetheless, the book is difficult to read because the chapters and, even many paragraphs, are overly extensive causing fatigue to the reader.  Overall, it is a good book that taught me a lot about Goering, the Nazis, and the German war effort.

This is the first book on Fascism that I have read so far.  I was curious about Fascism because it was the prevailing political and economic system in both Germany and Italy at the beginning of World War 2 and that war is one of my favorite reading subjects.

  I found the book readable, detailed and, very clear.  The book carries a lot of information for being only an introduction to Fascism.  You will find out that Fascism is a broad term that, nonetheless, did not fully describe any system defined as such (fascist) in any of the countries where it is recognized that it took hold.  Fascism is related to many concepts such as: corporatism, ultra nationalism, paramilitarism, anti-feminism, racism (or at least xenophobia), autarky, totalitarianism, rule by terror, messianic message, tight control of unions and labour, presence of both radical and conservative social and economic measures, cult of personality (of a strong, supreme leader), and bent on welfare and total employment for the "true" nationals.  Sometimes it bordered on Paganism (as in Nazi Germany) and sometimes it was firmly bound to a religion (Catholicism in Franco's Spain and the Christian Orthodox Church in Romania).

  The author also presents an outlook of the current political movements throughout Europe (mostly) that could be termed fascist like.  This is indeed a thorough introduction to Fascism.  Five stars for this book.

I have read various biographies of Napoleon and this one is the one I like best, so far.  Frank McLynn is not afraid of delving into the possible psychological reasons behind people's decisions, actions and, motives.  McLynn is not only thoroughly informed about his subject (Napoleon) but also about Europe in general.  I found myself agreeing with most of McLynn's analyses.  The prose is elegant and highly readable.  McLynn's assesment of Napoleon and his era is fascinating.  Very good history.

Louis Fischer recounts Gandhi's remarkable life while, at the same time, adding his insightful political and spiritual views.  The style is lively and learned.  Gandhi was ahead of his time and humankind still has a lot to learn from him.  This book sure makes justice to Gandhi's timeless message.  Enjoy it.

Robert Spencer has become one of my favorite writers after this effort (Religion of peace?).  He is articulate, reasonable and, has an elegant writing style.

  This book is interesting and well researched.  The author puts to rest a lot of misconceptions about the Judeo-Christian civilization while, at the same time, he indicts Islam for the numerous alleged transgressions of modern civilized ways.

  This is the best book on this subject that I have read so far.

This book is quite pleasing, it is well argued and well written.  If you like "juicy" biographies full of details and trivia you will be disappointed, nonetheless, it still has a wealth of biographical data that makes the book interesting and instructive.  The main focus of the book is on Jefferson's achievements and legacy.  The man (Jefferson) was an intellectual colossus and was never short on peculiar and original ideas; he remains an icon for all Americans that are wary of big government and all Americans that defend the sovereignty of the individual.  I am glad I picked up this book as my starter on Jefferson.

This book must come close to being the most complete and authoritative portrait of Fascism.  Mr. Paxton tackles the very difficult task of defining what Fascism is and what is not.  The author regards the experiences with Fascism of both, Italy and Germany, as the classical examples of that political phenomenon.  Nonetheless, Fascism has many faces and it takes multiple shapes depending on the prevailing cultural and socio-economic conditions of the host country.

  Mr. Paxton delineates and describes a series of stages that Fascism go through and supports his observations with examples from history.  There is a great deal of analysis and scholarship in this book yet, it remains highly readable.  If you want a good perspective on Fascism, this book is for you.

I was surprised to read in the very first review for the book "Fatal Purity: Robespierre and the French Revolution" (on Amazon's webpage for that particular book), under the banner of "No longer the Incorruptible", a scathing attack on the character of Maximilien de Robespierre.  The author of that review went beyond thrashing Robespierre's character into, what I believe it is, an effort to belittle Robespierre's crucial contributions to the French Revolution and the enduring and important message that that event (the French Revolution) evokes on all the persons that read about it.

  First of all, I remember that Ms Scurr took the pain to stress that the book was not meant to absolve nor condemn Robespierre.  After finishing the book, I can attest that she was quite successful at being even handed and fair.  The author of that review, although entitled to his opinion, left the impression (at least on me)that Robespierre, somehow, while embodying all that is evil and, while being utterly devoid of any leadership skills, rose to be the "top man" at the helm of the French Revolution.  The story depicted in the book is quite different from what was written, and omitted, in that review.

  Now, going into the merits of the book, I have to say that it is never dull, it is concise, clear, learned, even enthralling.  Judging by this, Ms Scurr's first literary effort, I can foresee the birth of a star.  Ruth Scurr is a product of both Oxford and Cambridge.  Buying and reading this book is money well invested.

I thoroughly enjoyed this book by Lee Kuan Yew.  Besides being a genious at governing the man is a gifted writer.  The book is full of information for those, like me, that were curious about how this gentleman, along with his associates, pulled out the feat of transforming an underdeveloped society into a model society.  He, almost singlehandedly, achieved what other countries and societies with far more resources only dream of.  Pick this book if you wish to learn and, at the same time, be entertained.

This book have helped me a great deal to come to terms with my life as it is.  It is loaded with useful information.  It has to be read more than once in order to grasp all the important details in it.  It was a blessing to come across this book.  If life does not make sense to you, read this book.

**************************************************************************

  I re-read this book recently and it still made a strong impression on me.  There is a before and after in my life regarding this book.  This book helped me make a perceptual shift in my way of looking at life.  Before reading it, I would concentrate on my problems, on the things that were sour and wrong.  After reading it, I learned about focusing on what is right in my life, on using my strengths to move forward.  I also learned about the importance of appreciation, the ever present availability of choices, the importance of optimism and the importance of forgiveness.  Also, this book warn us about not relying exclusively on affirmations or other "feel good" gimmicks.  The idea is to be proactive, not passive.  I wholeheartedly recommend this great book.

If you want to understand the movement behind Donald Trump, and this movement's trajectory, you ought to read this book.  Pat Buchanan is the spiritual father of the nativist folks that want to defend what has been, culturally, the heart and soul of the American nation.

  This book was written by an outsider, presumably, without axes to grind.  The book is informative and it was written in a lively style.  This biography of Pat Buchanan chronicles the power players, among them Mr. Buchanan, that have moved across the American political firmament in the last twenty years.  After reading this book, you will feel privy to that rarefied world where power brokers try to decide the fate of nations and civilizations.

Esta es una novela muy hermosa y entretenida.  Diferente en varios aspectos a "Gracias por el fuego" y "La Tregua", "La borra del cafe" brilla orgullosamente en el firmamento de la obra de Benedetti con un fulgor unico.  Sin aparente pretension de gran obra, esta novela nos muestra mucho de la realidad de Montevideo (el mundo real y cotidiano) y aun incorpora a Rita, un personaje fantastico que aparece en varias etapas de la vida de Claudio (el protagonista).

  Benedetti usa un castellano exquisito a traves de toda la obra la cual esta dividida conveniente y felizmente en capitulos cortos.

This book is superbly written and very thorough.  The political partnership between James Madison and Thomas Jefferson is recounted and assessed in a magisterial way.  At times, the reader feels that he or she is reading an epic novel written by a wordmaister.  There is a bit of Hamilton bashing in its pages and, in the last section of the book, the authors stray into a social manifesto when they assess Madison's and Jefferson's attitudes regarding racism and slavery.  Overall, this is an excellent book.

users.query: The Chrysalis has three time settings: 17th century Holland, WWII, and modern New York. It's quite good when it talks about the painter of the Chrysalis in the 17th century, WWII (although there should have been more about that), and  the legal fight to decide who owns the painting. The problem I have with this story is that Mara Coyne is an intelligent, talented lawyer, working in one of New York's top law firms, but this confident young woman turns to goo as soon as an old interest looks her way. She is willing to risk everything for this man, including her career. I don't want to give anything away, but there needed to be more consequences for Mara at the end. It had a fairy-tale ending that was too neat.

cands.text: This is much more than the story of a famous painting, the painter Gustav Klimt, and its subject, Adele Bloch-Bauer. It is also about every major player in the Bloch-Bauer orbit, including Freud and famous Viennese painters and musicians. There is so much detail and so many characters that it can get confusing. A mini bio of the many players would have been helpful. The story is at its most interesting when the Nazis descend on Vienna after the Anschluss and WWII begins. The lives destroyed by the Germans is heartbreaking. As for the main subject of the book, the lawsuit filed by Maria Altman, often takes a back seat to less interesting threads. But if you want to know everything there is to know about Adela, Klimt, and the fight to have the Klimt paintings returned to its rightful owners, then this is the book for you.

I am new to Mary Rinehart and really enjoyed this novel. The characters were well constructed and the time period (1930) interesting. I did have a few quibbles, most particularly, the overly complicated plot. Even so, it was so well written that I kept going. My only complaint is that this story definitely needed an epilogue. As others have noted, the murderer is revealed and the book ends. As a result, we have little understanding of motive. But if you are looking for a novel set in a time when making a long-distance call was a big deal and people wrote letters by hand, you will enjoy this story.

Because I was unfamiliar with Mary Rinehart, I went to Wikipedia to read up on her. On her Wikipedia page, the murderer is revealed. So, don't go there until you read the story.

Interesting settings, but not enough suspense. Furst succeeded in creating tension but then let it slip away with descriptions of Paris or dinner entrees. He opened with a good cast of ominous characters but rarely used them to advance the story.

Interesting settings, but not enough suspense. Furst succeeded in creating tension but then let it slip away with descriptions of Paris or dinner entrees. He opened with a good cast of ominous characters but rarely used them to advance the story.
I inherited the 1978 version of this book, and it is one of the best I've read for a general overview of Austen and her times. Great sketches and pictures included.

This story is a modern twist on Pride and Prejudice, and it is thoroughly engaging. The author has the ability to create vivid scenes with a minimum amount of words, and as someone who appreciates crisp writing, this book was a pleasure to read. This retelling is not merely a replay of the modern-day romance of Elizabeth and Darcy, but the story of the strong friendship among the six main protagonists. The arrival of the Wickham-type character adds an interesting twist to the plot. All in all, a very satisfying read.

This is the story of the vicious rape and murder of an eighteen-year-old girl. Although all the clues lead to a reasonable conclusion, it was still unsatisfying. Even though the murderer's past and occupation is used to justify the savagery of the murder, it's hard to swallow. Another pet peeve is the interview technique of the female detective, especially when she interviewed someone who had fought in Iraq and Afghanistan. She kept asking the man how many people he had killed. Seriously? And surviving a burning car that was basically firebombed??? The writing is solid, but there's an "ick" factor that I could not get past.

I enjoyed this story. The lead detective was well developed and believable. My only quibble was with the female reporter hired by the family to find their long-missing grandson. For a smart lady, she did something really stupid. The background of pit closures in the North of England added a perfect backdrop for the story.

Jane and the Madness of Lord Byron is a multi-layered Regency mystery, and the sleuth is none other than Jane Austen. Following the death of Henry Austen's wife, Eliza, Comtesse de Feuillide, Jane and her brother make arrangements to visit the seaside town of Brighton. However, their plans for a quiet interlude fall by the wayside when a stop at a posting inn results in Jane and Henry rescuing a young lady, Catherine Twining, from a forced elopement with the scandal-ridden Lord Byron. When the girl's body is discovered a few days later, a drowning victim, who is sewn into a canvas shroud and deposited in the bed of Lord Byron, the poet becomes the prime murder suspect.

Jane, who had befriended the fifteen-year-old Twining, finds herself in the midst of a murder investigation, one that is thrown into greater confusion when Lady Caroline Lamb, the former and nearly mad lover of Lord Byron, puts in an appearance, as well as his current paramour, Lady Oxford. Jane's investigation takes her to the residence of the Prince Regent. Is the prince or one of his associates involved or did Byron murder the girl who had rejected him?

This novel is interesting on so many levels. It is a tale so rich in Regency minutiae that it is like tapping into a mother lode of information, and Stephanie Barron is very clever in weaving these facts into her story so that you are seeing the beautiful clothes of the era, tasting the food, walking the streets of Brighton, and dancing to music in grand assembly rooms. But the most interesting scenes are those in which Caroline Lamb and Lord Byron are front and center. A conversation between the grieving Byron and his inquisitor, Jane Austen, is fascinating, and scenes of Lady Caroline's growing mental instability are chilling.

If you are a fan of Regency-era novels and mysteries, then you are in for a treat because this book delivers for enthusiasts of both genres.

The book starts out with an interesting bit of history: one of the former owners of a house in Yorkshire was hanged for murder. The new owner wants to know more, and so it begins. Unfortunately, the book never picks up steam b/c it is weighed down with lengthy passages on music, food, wine, contents of bookcases, an unnecessary flirtation, etc. About two-thirds of the way through the book, the mundane turns ridiculous with the introduction of a journal written by the hanged woman during WWII that survived not one, but two, ship sinkings. Although stripped of most of her clothing, the journal (and pen) survived! It goes downhill from there. The ending is unsatisfying, and you end up not liking anyone.

This book is the journal of Rosemary Langheldt who left her job and home in San Francisco to serve with the Red Cross in London and then Germany.  The story is told through letters home and journal entries, and both are highly informative and well written missives.  Mrs. Norwalk recreates what it was like to live in England during the last year of the war.  She is an empathetic observer of the many tens of thousands of men (boys) who stop briefly at her Clubmobile for a donut and a cup of coffee after disembarking in England and re-embarking for the fight on the Continent.  Once Rosemary is transferred to Germany, she sees firsthand the near destruction of many German cities.  Her writings are true to the time:  these people were our enemies a short time ago and they tried to kill the boys who I helped serve.  It also offers an honest appraisal of the Occupation where the black market made many Americans rich.  This book will be of interest to anyone who wants to know about life in England after the Allied landings in June 1944 and the early days of the occupation in Germany.

Interesting story with lots of details about Shanghai between the world wars. But two-thirds of the way through, it starts to lose its sizzle. The main character stops caring, and I found that I did too. With a sequel in the offing, it seems as if the author was ready to move on, and the ending lacks punch. However, it was worth reading.

This is the story of 12-year old Patty Bergen, a Jewish girl living in the South during WWII, who suffers from her father's physical and mental abuse and her mother's disinterest.  When a German POW talks kindly to her while shopping (with prison guards nearby) in her father's clothing store, she is so starved for love that she later assists him when he escapes from a prisoner-of-war camp. Strong characters and a poignant story.

You know how the story is going to go from the opening scene. A hard-nosed business woman is sent to a small Minnesota town to shut it down. Instead, she ends up saving the plan b/c she loves the people and Harry Connick's character. Connick and Zellwegger click, and the supporting cast is just terrific. It's a fun ride.

It's been a while since I laughed out loud at a book, but this is one.  When a 21st lady, Courtney Stone, finds herself in Jane Austen's world, her modern sensibilities run head long into the straight-laced society of early 19th Century.  The passages regarding hygiene, or the lack thereof, are hysterical, especially when she is required to descend into a bathing pool at Bath or "eau de typhus" as she calls it.  I have to admit that I wasn't all that interested in the problems of the modern Courtney Stone but loved to read about her getting her sea legs in Regency society.

There were parts of the beginning of the book that were hysterical, but the same story can  be told only so many times and remain funny. The writing descended into the juvenile. The main character, Judd, is the least interesting character in the book. The others are simply obnoxious. The author pulls out all the stops, but they fall flat. An example is a baby monitor being left in his brother's bedroom where Paul and his wife are trying to create a baby. Anyone who thinks that after years of infertility the sex is anything but goal-oriented is ignorant of the process. So Paul's wife screaming in ecstasy is not only icky, it's completely unbelievable. I made it to 70%, but I could not take one more "feel sorry for me" story. It's too bad; it had a strong start.

The Fox in the Forest was written in 1992. No cell phones, DNA took forever, fingerprints took awhile as well, so the tempo is slower than police work in England in 2016. The writing is very good, especially when Gregson describes the forest; it took on a sinister character of its own. The first half of the book was quite good, but the second half seemed to be a repeat of much of what we already knew. The detectives were a blur--no personality whatsoever--and the ending was only so so. It seemed as if the author was ready to move on. Even so, I liked Gregson's writing and will give another of his mysteries a try.

I have read several of Leon's books, and this was by far the weakest. The pace is sluggish and not particularly interesting. If you've read Leon, you know that she alludes to violence but rarely goes into explicit details of a murder. Death and Judgment is the exception. As others have mentioned, the violence shown on a video is graphic and disturbing. Guido's family is usually a strong point in Leon's books, but that was not the case here. Paola speaks in diatribes, and Chiara is a self-absorbed teenager. The biggest problem is how Leon used Chiara in this book. It simply did not ring true. I encourage any reader to read Leon's books. Just don't start with this one.

The story takes place in Berlin in the months after the end of World War II. After a series of murders, American Nathan Morgan teams up with former Berlin cop Werner Beck to find the killer. I found that Morgan and Beck made a good team, and a Berlin in ruins, the perfect setting for their investigations. The problem with the story is that it is an endless series of murders in which the reader has no emotional investment in the victims. The killer grows frustrated with the lack of press attention to the killings, but leaves clues written in code!

The weakest part of the story centers around Kay, the female interest. We are told a lot about her privileged background, but not a lot about her. Morgan quickly falls for her, but we don't know why. And this woman, who has been given a coveted position in covering the Nuremberg War Trials for a magazine, turns out to be a dim bulb. Author Jones knows how to write male characters, but comes up short on the women. If a man, whom you do not know, stuck his hand up your dress, would you reply: "Excuse me, sir! What do you think you are doing?" Not once, but twice? After slugging the guy, my follow-up would be, "I hope that hurt."  Despite the flaws, it's a decent read, especially if you enjoy books about post-WWII Germany.

This is another solid outing in the Cadfael series. This murder mystery is set in Wales, the birthplace of Cadfael. Cadfael's abbey wants the bones of St. Winifred, a Welsh saint, brought to Shrewsbury, but the local inhabitants don't want their saint to leave Wales. The main proponent of the transfer of Winifred's bones from Wales to England is killed. There are numerous suspects, and the author keeps you guessing until the very end. This is an excellent exploration of the cult of saints that existed at this time.

I'm a big fan of Christopher Fowler's Peculiar Crime Unit series. Part of its charm is that we get to learn about the history of London, and the city comes to life. But in White Corridor, the team of Arthur Bryant and John May are not in London. Instead, they are stuck in a snowstorm in Devon, and stuck they are. With endless descriptions of the weather and failed rescue attempts, the story fails to come to life. Meanwhile, in London, a second murder is being investigated by Bryant and May's peers with frequent consultations by phone with the stranded detectives. Without Bryant and May to lead the investigation, the inquiry is not as interesting. This is a really good series, and I would encourage readers to try another PCU unit. Unfortunately, this one just doesn't work.

In The Mother Tongue, Bryson plays it straight. There is very little of his gentle humor, and I found that a chapter or two a day was all I could digest in one sitting. The book is quite dated as evidenced by the words he uses to define modern technology. They, too, are dated. An update would have been nice. Twenty-plus years is a long time for a language as dynamic as English.

I have read several books on the SOE (Special Operations Executive). For the most part, the agents who, according to Churchill, were supposed to "set Europe on fire" were very often captured shortly after their arrival in France, betrayed, tortured, and gruesomely executed. I was happy to read a story where the operation was, for the most part, a success and the agent survived. Incredibly brave, Virginia Holt volunteered her services time and time and eventually transferred from the SOE to the OSS so that she could continue to "do her bit." The writing is straight forward, but Holt's story is so compelling that it needs little embellishment. It's a good solid read about agents operating in Occupied France.

I put this book down a dozen times because it was so repetitious, but when Backman writes about Ove's relationships with his father and wife, the book rises to a different level. It also has a very satisfactory ending. It's just that it should have been about a third shorter.

Harry Dolan is a fantastic writer--on a par with Michael Connelly. I really enjoyed the story, the pacing, and the writing of The Last Dead Girl. Even though it's a low-key thriller, it keeps you turning the page. My only complaint is that everyone speaks with the same voice. It doesn't matter if you are the murderer or the murdered. You are going to be very matter-of-fact about your destiny. It's as if the entire county had Valium in their water. There are some problems with the ending, but on the whole, a really good read.

this book is really helpful. the author has ADHD so he knows what he is talking about. the section on medication is excellent. my doctor started me on Strattera but i couldn't tolerate it so i told him about another drug mentioned in the book that is off label. i am on that now and it is better. he did not know about this drug before i mentioned it to him so the book was very helpful

seems very pure and nice sweet flavor. obviously it is tart because it is 100% hibiscus but i drink it straight and like it. have not seen my high blood pressure go down which is why i bought it but my wife has cancer so maybe it is just not going to go down till she finishes chemo and we see what comes next.

this is a very nice bell. i thought the price was a little high but the quality is much nicer than what i have seen at new age bookstores etc. the dorja is also very, very nice- and a great meditation tool. i believe i am sensitive to positive energy from rocks, crystals and such and the dorja has really good energy. the sound in the bell is mostly in the higher range as it is a fairly small bell, but it is clear and has good resonance. would buy larger bells from this company if they offered one
cat won't eat these even when i mix it with food. i read the ingredients and they seem ok so i eat them instead for my anxiety and they seem to work! just wished they had worked for the cat...

this is a good book about bi polar. i have struggled with depression and ADHD and books like this help to understand what is what. the section on the medication is very informative. i don't need to fool myself- if i don't have those symptoms i probably don't need that medication. i am trying a medication for the adhd and if it doesnt work i will ask my doctor about some of these others. a good reference
seem to work OK but not very comfortable and have not tried them on a run so not sure if they will stay up. they are well made and not very expensive so i think they are worth the money.
this is very tasty tea- i bought it for the hibiscus but that is only one ingredient- it is very floral and not overly sweet like almost every other beverage usually available when you go out

i really love this cacao powder. i had purchased another brand that i thought was terrific from amazon to use in my morning smoothy. i am trying to get spirulina in my diet daily so i use fruit and veggies to go with it but it is often too sweet. the raw cacao powder helps cut the sweetness and so does cinnamon and ginger. this cacao powder is so rich that when combined with all the fruit it tastes like a creamy milkshake- even when i use orange juice for the liquid. if you use a banana and milk for the liquid it really does taste like a milkshake. i also use peanut butter and WOW does that taste good. my wife has cancer and is on chemo so i need to get ginger into her diet to combat the nausea that chemo can cause. she loves these shakes!

i have a really big head and have never found a nice baseball cap at a regular store. this hat fits my whole head. it comes down far enough that it doesn't feel like it is just sitting on my head and it keeps me warm. the fabric and the construction are very good quality and the color is excellent. i wear it in the rain and on cold days and it is perfect and also very nice looking. the only thing is the bill is long and sort of stiff so i just wear it backwards like the kids do and it makes me feel cool and younger (i am 60) . will get another one if i ever want a different color

well, i thought this was a joke but i have aches and pains for a 61 year old. i went to the local farm and feed store in town and asked if they had horse liniment and they had about 4 brands available. i asked the lady at the counter if any of her customers used any of the brands for their own aches and pains and she replied simply- all of them. use it on the stiff horse and it starts to walk better, it seems obvious well maybe i will try it on my sore shoulder... so the farmers and ranchers all seem to use it too. i bought some and it sits on the nightstand and really works. don't like the minty smell that much but it is not a deal breaker. very soothing so i love it. sent a bottle to my brother for christmas for his torn rotator cuff shoulders and if he likes it too i will continue to send him "horse liniment" for christmas as fun tradition. try it and you will like it

i use this cacao powder almost everyday in a smoothy. i typically use a lot of fruit which can get too sweet. the raw cacao powder balances that so it tastes like chocolate, except much better because the quality is higher. i mainly use this for the nutritional value. i feel like cacao has a lot of calming properties also. there is a reason people like to eat chocolate- but most  has tons of refined sugar. i think i am hooked for life. the other standard in the smoothy is spirulina powder and then fresh ginger. those three go in everything. i usually use orange juice and also almost a teaspoon of cinnamon. what a way to start the day.

It also left brush marks. This brush is much softer, is not losing hair and I don't see the brush marks- and it is made in U.S.A. Won't buy a cheap brush again!

i like this product a lot. not sure if i will purchase again because i still prefer the smoothness of brushing on shellac myself. but this is easier by far. one suggestion. i had the fan running on high because unlike regular shellac this has a somewhat unpleasant odor. well, i got a bit of dust in the finish. next time i will run the fan after i have finished spraying and it has set a little. the other thing is that this can go under lacquer and the stuff in the can (that hasn't been dewaxed can't) so i will try this when i want a laquer finish

this pad is just too thick for me to use as a car seat so i was about to send it back. then i had a three day conference  where i sat most of the day and said the heck with appearances and just took it to each session. saved my butt and my back. i attend these conferences about once a year and will make sure i take it along.
bought this to apply shellac and if you don't thin the shellac it will leave brush marks. need to spend in the $20 dollar range for a better bristle brush was hoping to save some money...

I got very frustrated with the inexpensive flatware we had because the handle on the table spoon would bend when I used it to scoop out ice cream. They looked OK but not very fancy and not heavy enough. So I looked for about a year, no kidding, at about 50 different sets. What I wanted was something special but still everyday, and definetely heavy enough for the ice cream task. I also wanted something that was going to stay shiny for a long time. The reviews convinced me that this could be the ticket on this set. I knew I could buy something for around $60 but nothing seemed like it was just right. This set was $99 and when I asked my wife if I could go ahead and spend that much she said OK. Well, they are just beautiful and very heavy- everything I wanted and my wife loves them too.

wifes rowenta gave up the ghost after 10 years because the cord broke and they couldn't replace it. she bought a sunbeam which she liked but said it wasn't the same as the rowenta she had... so she got this one for christmas. made really well, i don't think you are paying a premium just for the "made in Germany" part of it. all the edges are smooth and she irons a lot so what the heck. i have a bosche 5" orbital sander that i absolutely love. could have saved money on a cheaper unit that would have just left a lot of scratch marks behind. the thing is a joy and keeps me in the shop- why not pay a little extra if you are going to use something a lot.

i bought this book at a local alternative book store about 20 years ago and have read it and reread it hundreds of times. it sits on the counter in the bathroom and i pick it up often. i went to india 35 years ago and hooked up with a different guru who i still consider my real master but these stories are really amazing. when i returned to india a year ago i knew i wanted to visit a few of the ashrams mentioned in the book and was very glad i did. one thing i noticed is that there was a particular smell at the ashram in dehli that i also recognized at the ashram in kainchi- just sort of warm, loving and earthy. he passed away almost 50 years ago and it is hard to believe that his presence, in the form of this smell, would still be there today.

It's string.  It's Kevlar string.  It's tougher than old boot leather.
I bought this to go on a kite reel that surprised me by coming in pre-spooled.  I haven't used any of it yet, but I've used Kevlar string before.  This will go in my travel box, cuz string is handy.
If I have any issues when I do get to use it, I'll update my review.

cands.text:
This is the base hook from which all of the Mustad round bend hooks are derived.
I recommend these hooks to all of my fly tying friends.

Bought as padding for a deer feeder battery in a battery box for my kayak fishfinder.  Excellent quality foam.
The remainder will be turned to fly tying material, lol.

Bought as padding for a deer feeder battery in a battery box for my kayak fishfinder.  Excellent quality foam.
The remainder will be turned to fly tying material, lol.

This is the adhesive recommended to mount a fishfinder transducer.  It is very clear, soft, and holds like all get out.
Good stuff.

I needed a "D"-ring for a dog collar I was braiding.  This covered it.
The bar has a radius to accommodate the curve of a wrist (or a dog's neck).  The shackel is stout, as is the bar, and the shackle bolt is threaded to allow the shackle to be moved to any of the 4 locations provided.
This is probably too strong for what I'm using it for, (the dog only weighs 13 lbs, lol) but it works.

Hmmmm.  Don't remember this one!  I'll have to look for it.  It'll work great to hook my charger to my battery box for my Kayak.
Probably why I bought it in the first place.
It's a cable.  It charges my phone.  And my son's phone.  They are Verizon phones.

Purchased to create poppers for fly fishing.
Clean cut corks, perfect for my purposes.  Made very nice poppers.

I bought this for my son to wear for his new security job.  I'm impressed enough that I wil probably end up getting one for myself.
Don't let the plastic buckle put you off.  It feels like it's made of a glass reinforced nylon, and it isn't flimsy.  The action on it is different, in that it hinges in the middle to close and open, but it makes sense once you use it a couple of times.
The webbing is also nylon, and is much stiffer than other webbing belts I've used, although it is thinner.  I had no problem cutting it to length with a pair of 4" fly tying scissors, and it didn't immediately start to unravel when I cut it.  I made a pass at melting the cut end together with a lighter, but I don't think I was successful, or that it is necessary.
The belt includes 2 elastic loops that I didn't see as being necessary, although I think my son is using one.
My one disappointment with this belt is the way the standing end is treated.  It doesn't have a finisher on it, it just has a "swoopy" curved cut to give a narrower end to thread thru the buckle and your belt loops.  the cut is bonded, but I don't know how well it's going to hold up over time.  I would have rather seen some type of finisher applied to the end.  The belt is stout enough that I'm not going to take any stars away for that.
As always, I have received no compensation of incentive for my review.  It is my own, unbiased opinion.

I had to search a bit to find a web belt that was 1 1/4" wide.  Some of my fishing pants have narrow loops, and I wanted a belt that wasn't leather for a purpose where it was subject to getting wet.
The buckle is sturdy, and seems stronger than a different brand I had fail prior to this purchase.  It holds the cut/buckle end of the belt securely, and doesn't come unbuckled accidently.  The antique brass finish doesn't show scratches or wear.
The belt has a metal endpiece on it, so it doesn't unravel.  It doesn't stretch, so it stays snug at the length you buckle it.
I wear 36" waist pants, and cut 3 1/2" off of the buckle end, and leave about 5" sticking out past the buckle.

I would recommend this to someone looking for a canvas belt.

Nice little spoon-type lures.  Wiggles without having to have a super fast retrieval speed.  The bigger one's cast well on a spin caster, while the smaller one's are more suited to ultra-light gear.
I've caught some pretty nice fish on these.

This jack was the twin to the OEM equipment on my 31 foot Travel Trailer.
Bolted right in to the existing holes and a single hot wire connection.
Wondermus.  Works like a champ!
The reason I had to replace the jack was water got into the motor and switch compartment, thru the manual override hole in the top, and corroded the switch.
The new jack came with a bag to put over the jack head to keep the water out. Ain't that something?
A verty nice unit.  I would easily recommend this.

I like that the point retracts when you press the clip.  I get tired of poking holes in my torso with the others.
The action is smooth, and the grip is comfortable.  This is a mechanical DRAFTING pencil.  It has a long barrel point for use with straight edges, and the lead does not have a spring cushion as I have experienced with other brands.  That is a big plus for me.
All-in-all, I would have to call this the best mechanical pencil I have ever drawn with.  I wish they would have been available back when I was working with a drafting board and velum.
I was expecting something that wound just push right through craft foam. This will require sharpening in order to easily accomplish its porpose

On my new travel trailer, the license plate bracket is 2 clear polystyrene "ears" sticking out of the taillight.  Experience tells me these will get brittle with age and exposure to sunlight.  Bye-bye license plate.
I mounted this Cruiser bracket with 4~#10 panhead sheet metal screws and lots of Lexel clear sealant, after tapping the 4 plate mounting holes for 1/4-20 machine screws with a flat washer and a lock washer each.
I am now confident that my license plate is going nowhere.

I needed cording for a collar to fit my wife's small dog.  Type III paracord was just too big for a 12 lb dog, given the pattern I was weaving.
Type I cord is about the same diameter as the yarn used to knit a baby blanket, just much denser.  It's probably half the cross-section of Type III
I should have used 3/8" buckles, instead of 5/8.  It would have fit much better.
The size of this cording is perfect for more delicate projects.

This is an excellent product, but be aware that the bobbin holder I received is too small to fit a standard bobbin.  It is perfect for the small bobbins that Pearsall's silk comes on, but my Ultra Thread spools are too big for it.  The limbs are dragging on the edge of the bobbins.  I also have a couple of spools of Danville's Flymaster+, which are even bigger bobbins than Ultra's.
I have tried adjusting the limbs, some, by hand, but am still having problems.
It being Thanksgiving weekend, I will have time later to mess with it.  If I can get it to working properly without too much effort, I'll update this review.  I know it is an $9 product, but I didn't expect to have to reconfigure it to fit a standard bobbin,given it is named "Standard".

Direct replacement for the OEM equipment on my Travel Trailer.
These tend to get brittle after a few years and need replacement.  Especially if you are a klutz like I am.

I broke one of these when I was doing the original loading for a brand new trailer.  I broke one of the replacement pair messing with it before I installed it.  The second one I put in without incident.  26 bucks for 2 little pieces of plastic.  Outrageous! If I had another option i'd use it.

This hat replaced a <Big Box Discount Store of your choice> el-cheapo special that I left in a restaurant.
This one is Much, much Better.
The "shape" is stamped into the crown to keep it from becoming misshapen, and the brim has a wire reinforcement in it that you can bend to create the form you wish, within limits.  I prefer the brim sides tilted up just a bit, instead of flat.  Without the wire, I wouldn't be able to do that with a cloth hat.
The cloth is thick and durable and should give me years of comfortable service, if I don't leave it in a restaurant.

I bought 2 of these to replace the 45 year old switches in my carport/garage.  They work like a charm, except some idiot didn't look at the switches and installed them upside down.
Eaton is a well-known product brand, and I received the quality product I was expecting.

***As always, I have neither asked for, nor received, any compensation for my review.  This is my own, un-biased opinion. (And lots of it!)***

I was skeptical.  Too much cheap Chinese-made junk out there.
Distributed by Amazon?  Hmm.  Won't have to wait 2 months for it to get here.
24 month warranty, too?
OK, I'll give it a try.

It arrived promptly, with a wall plug charger and an extra cable in the same shipment (in for a penny...)  All of it is nicely boxed up and presentation is top-notch.  The car charger is sturdy and doesn't feel cheap.  It's supposed to be tri-power, 12V, 9V, & 5V, but I have only used it for 5V in my car.  (I wonder if it will charge the deer-feeder battery for my depth-finder on my kayak?)  My Motorola Droid Turbo recognizes it as a "Turbo Charger" when I plug it in.  That's what I was looking for.  WAY less expensive than Verizon's accesssory.  Like 1/3 the price, and this one does 3 times as much.
It's been running for about 3 weeks in my car, keeping my phone topped off, with no issues.  The different ports do different things, so be sure to plug into the correct one.  (It has been hashed to death in the reviews and questions.  Look for answers there.)
Overall very impressed with the Aukey brand, and will actively look for their equipment when I can.
***As always, I have neither asked for, nor received, any compensation for my review.  This is my own, un-biased opinion. (and lots of it)***

I discovered Ceramic-coated skillets by accident.  We needed a skillet for our travel trailer, and bought one at the big-box store.  What a treat to use and clean.
The only problem was, now we needed a *bigger* skillet/pot for larger meals, french fries and such.  Enter the Wearever 3.5 quart ceramic cook pot.
It's fantastic.  I cooked fried eggs in it.  DRY!  Hashbrowns with cheese?  No problems!  This skillet does what the old Teflon commercials said their cookware would do, without all of the annoying "off-gassing" from teflon!  I'm a convert!  I love these pans!  You will, too!

I have erasers.  I will have erasers for YEARS!
I have bought the 6- and 12-packs of erasers at the department stores before, and they all seemed to have different sized holes in them.  I usually ended up throwing a couple of them away because they wouldn't fit anything.  (Yeah, I could have just held them in my fingers, but that isn't what I bought them for. I have other tools for that.)
These are uniformly great.  They fit snuggly on even my smallest diameter pencils.  They have a heavy wall around the hole, so they don't wobble around when you use them, and come off of the pencil.  The material is denser, so a heavy pressure erasing session (lol) doesn't use up an extraordinary amount of the eraser.
What I didn't expect was for them to actually work better than the E|F and Pentel erasers I was using before.  More complete (completer?) removal of the pencil lines, including colorer pencils, with less pressure and fewer strokes.  To tell the truth, that wasn't even a criteria in my search.  I was surprised.
If I ever have to buy more, Heaven help me, I will stick with the Paper-Mate Brand.

users.query:
I have never read anything from VC. Andrews that I didn't like.
My all time favorite author,  My daughter and I both love her books.  Many books after we read them get given away , or sold, but we both agree, our collection of these books stay with us.

cands.text:
I love VC Andrews, have for years. She is a great writer, I have enjoyed several of her books.
When my daughter, was a teenager, ( 16 ) I let her start reading some of the books, and now she is also hooked.
We both buy her stories and then, exchange with each other, Most books end up in the resale pile, but we both agree our
VC Andrew collection, stays between the two of us.

Curious George, Thanksgiving, book is so wonderful.  We have been watching Curious George, on tv. with the grandkids for years.  All of the kids love the show, ( and I have to admit, I find myself watching it even when the grandbabies are not here.)  I love that they have a city home, and  a country home.  It allows for so many more adventures, and story lines. When we ran across on Amazon, the Curious George, tabbed books, we immediately knew we had to have them all. This story touches base with all the wonderful family traditions that is associated with Thanksgiving, a must for any child.

We loved this game. First time we played it, we were hooked. It was so fun, everybody laughed for hours. As soon as we
played the original game, we had to have all of the expansion packs.

Little Bear, is the most wonderful collection of learning, cartoons, for toddlers and preschoolers, I first discovered little bear, when my oldest granddaughter, who is 9 now, was a baby.  Her and I would watch them every Friday, when she would come to stay with me.  We both fell in love with it.  It is so nice to have a show for them to watch, that is about nothing but friendship, love, curiosity, and learning. Instead of fighting, dark, and sarcasm.  Little bear and his friends, have many many adventures, always doing something to help each other, and take care of one another.  Then there is the shows with his parents and grandparents, which are also just as wonderful. I feel it teaches the kids manners, and patience, and all kinds of social eddicit. All 8 of my grandbabies have grown up watching this wonderful series with me now, and each and everyone has loved them.  Little Bear is just plain good TV.  I even find myself watch them still even when the grandkids are not here.  This series is highly recommended, if I could give them more than five stars I would.

Ok I am publicly admitting, I am a child when It comes to my coloring. I have always loved to color, It truly was my favorite past time with my children, and my grandchildren as well. I have always had my own set of coloring books, and crayons, and everyone understood them are mine, and not to touch them. Please don't get me wrong, because it's important to teach kids to share, when everyone was little, I had 2 different set's of MY coloring books, no matter how many books you buy children they always want to use Grandma's, so one set stays out where they can see, and use them with me, and then I have my secret stash, hidden away, for when I'm by myself.lol  I was elated when they started coming out with the adult coloring books, these things are so cool. I have never really been to excited about coloring with pencils, again I am child, and like my crayons.(my husband regularly laughs at me). When I received my first adult coloring book, it was very evident that I was going to have to switch over to pencils. I really like this set of pencils from KALE. There are 36 pencils in the set, and there are several different shades of most of the colors. Like for green, there are 6 different shades of green, this makes it nice when doing the adult coloring books, because they have a large amount of detail to each of their  pictures, this allows you to get your shading and toning just right. The pencils are all made of recycled material, which, let's face it every little bit of help that we can give our planet, is a plus. The pencils come in a round cardboard container, and there is a pencil sharpener, built right in the top, so you always have it at your fingertips. My oldest granddaughter will be 10 this year, so I think it's time to let her in on grandma's secret stash of cool coloring books. I love that she still enjoys coloring with me, hopefully none of them will grow out of it anytime soon.

This is a beautiful Wine Accessory set from, Antfees.  We have never really been big into wine, but in the last couple of years, we have starting paying a little more attention, to the beverage.  I am by no means any kind of an expert, about wine or wine etiquette, but like I said we have been drinking it a little more often, thanks to a couple of my adult children. They seem to feel that it's important to have some basic knowledge about it. I seen this set of wine accessories, and thought it might be a nice gift for my son and daughter in law.  I was very pleased when it arrived.  It came very quickly after I ordered it. When it arrived it was packaged in a super nice looking gift box.  There are 4 pieces to the set. 1- a aerator/pourer, 2 - a bottle stopper, 3 -a drip ring, and a corkscrew.  The entire set is stainless steel with black accents, every piece looks very elegant.  We have tried the corkscrew, this seemed a little odd to us, because the only kind we have had any experience with is the kind you pick up at walmart, that has the 2 handles, that you pull down. This one works a little differently, but once we figured it out, it worked better than either of the other two we own.  The stopper, works great, we laid the bottle down in the fridge, and no leakage, at all. The drip ring, is a nice addition, but to tell you the truth, if it had not come with the set, it's not something, that I would ever spend money on, just seems, a little silly to me.  I just really liked the look and feel of the entire set, and will be very proud to present this as a gift to my son, and his wife.  I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for a fair and unbiased opinion.

This is also incredibly adorable. What little girl don't like the little mermaid movies. I know both of the girls, could sing every song, with or without the movie playing. Now that my girls are all grown up, all 4 of my granddaughters, love the little mermaid movies, and they love the Barbie Mermaid tales as well. They all have mermaid dolls, and barbie dolls, and one of them has her room decorated in mermaids. So the next logical step, would be for them all to dress like a mermaid. This outfit, is great for them all. I ordered the first one in blue, and then one in lavender, but for the 2 youngest ones, we thought the rainbow pattern was perfect. I love the little shorts that come with this set, especially since one of them is still in pull ups.. The shorts, cover up more than the bikini bottom, that came with the other ones. The fabric is soft and shiney. They love how it shimmers in the sun, "just like a real mermaid, grandma" This outfit does run large, so order smaller than you normally would. The stitching looks good and straight, and solid. I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for a fair and unbiased opinion.

OMG. This is so beautiful. I am a huge penguin fan.  I have always, love them ever since I was a little girl.  This beautiful key chain, is so stunning, with its multitude of rhinestones.  I love it, and highly recommend it to anyone who has a Penguin lover to buy for.

OMG, I was so thrilled when this came in.  I purchased this for my 4 year old granddaughter, who is in love with my little pony everything.  Her favorite (at least for the moment) is Twilight Sparkle pony.  I found this and thought well that would be sweet for her.  When it came in it was so precious.  Not only does Twilight appear on the front as you can see, but on the hood is little pony ears, and fringe that looks like a maine., but the cutest feature, was when I turned it over and on the back they have two little wings attached just as Twilight has.  Definitely 5 stars or more.

For those of you, who have read some of my reviews before, you know that I am a geek when it comes to measuring cups and spoons. I am also somewhat of an addict. I have several sets of my own, I enjoy collecting them. Now don't get me wrong when they have worn out, I do throw them away, and replace them with nice new ones, that I have found. I also buy a set for every bridal shower or wedding gift, that I give. I tie them to the top of the package, instead of bows. They are practical and lots more useful than a bow. I do a similar thing with baby shower gifts, I never buy bows, I always buy a book for the baby, and tie it to the top. This set of measuring cups and spoons from Rebel Tone, is a nice set. It comes in a set of 6, all brightly colored. The set includes :  1 cup, 1/2 cup, 1/3 cup, 1/4 cup, 1 tablespoon, 1/2 tablespoon. Each one also contains the metric increments for those of you who prefer them. Me, I am old fashioned, and like the normal ones, metric just makes my head spins. lol  They are all made of a durable plastic, and they nest down inside of each other for easy storage. The entire set weighs only 3.4 ounces. The only thing that I don't like about this set is that instead of a 1/2 tablespoon, I would really like to have seen a 1 teaspoon, at least that way you can get a little closer to both measurements. A set really is not complete in my opinion if you don't have at least some kind of teaspoon increment. I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for a fair and unbiased opinion. Love my Penguins. I am a huge penguin fan. I ran across this decal, while searching Amazon for penguin stuff, and yeaaa. The decal is wonderful.
It actually has 2 pieces to it, the one you see here, the "LOVE " sign, but it also has a little heart that comes with it. The main decal is 6 inches by 6 inches. It looks wonderful on my truck.

What wonderful childhood memories this brings back. I used to love to yo yo when I was a kid, who didn't right?. I was never very good at it, I could do a few neat tricks with the yo yo's, but nothing too major. I could walk the dog, and do the hold, but other than that, I was not very talented. Still I love to play with them, and I tried and tried to do the other cool tricks, that my brother and sister, had both conquered. Even without mastering the more complicated tricks, I still spent hours and hours, playing with the yo yo s. Now a days, these yo yo's are so much cooler than the ones that we had. I love the bright colors that they come in and the wonderful design. The blue in this yoyo is stunning. My husband calls it cobalt blue, the color of our next car supposedly. This yo yo from Schenzhen TND is made of aluminum, and what looks like clear plastic on the ends. It is 2 inches in diameter, and 1 1/2 inches wide. It weighs in at 2.55 ounces.  I love the smooth feel of the aluminum and it gives it a cool look. This is a butterfly style yo yo. It came with 2 strings, one bright orange, and the other black, both are just over 43 inches long. The string has kind of a twisted braid look to it. The strings come unattached, so you have to load it yourself, it took the hubby a few moments to do this, but it wasn't complicated. I have  been able to walk the dog, with the yo yo, but my husband and his nephew, was playing with it the other night and both were able to do a few tricks, with it. (once they practiced a little) lol. Very nice purchase, this one is actually going my grandson, I will have to buy a few more for the other kids, but I can't wait to see them all playing with these and learning new things. I am all for anything helps to get kids out from in front of the tv and video games.
