Great lights, It really is getting harder and harder to find the mini 100 strand color lights,  I've been looking for a while now, because I needed them for St. Patrick's Day.  Being Irish we go all out for the holiday. Including a tree, with gifts under it for the grandkids. We decorate our tree every year, and then when the day comes, the grandkids, know that the leprechaun has left something for them under the tree. (of course he leaves a lot of green beer, for all the adults). This set is 100 strand of lights, the green color of the lights are actually GREEN! not that aqua, color you get with the led light strands. The length of the strand is 19 feet, with bulbs about every 2 inches. The cord is also green so it hides well in the tree. It has two functions, either steady on or you can have it flashing. They have end to end plugs so you can add more strands if you like. The best feature, if 1 bulb goes out the rest stay on. I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for a fair and unbiased opinion

This  collapsible water bottle from Sanberd, is very cool. I was skeptical as to whether these foldable water bottles were going to be any good, or just a gimmicky waste of money. I happy to say, that I was pleasantly surprised when it came in.  It first arrived in it's own box, (which had a little hole cut out in the corner, so you could see what color it was. When I opened the water bottle was folded up, inside of a clear plastic wrap. The first thing I did, when I opened and unfolded the bottle, was smell it. So many of things, like this, when they come in have a horrible smell to them. (Although I have to admit you get that with plastic more than the silicone.) I am very happy to report that it really had no smell at all. The bottle is made of Silicone as stated, it is 9 inches tall, 2 3/4 inches in diameter (at the bottom), and weighs only 3.4 ounces empty of course. The instructions on the side of the box says to boil the bottle before you use it, in order to sanitize it thoroughly. After doing this I was expecting the bottle to lose it shape somewhat, but nope, it didn't. The bottle has a screw off lid, that opens it up for filling, this opening is not large enough for our regular ice cubes, but I do have ice trays, that are specifically made to give you long skinny ice cubes, to drop down into like plastic water bottles, and they worked perfect for this one. The lid also has a flip top cap, for drinking, so you don't have to take the top off completely, this lid seems to fit very very snug, I have not seen any signs of leakage from either of the top opening. As you can see from the picture you get a nice clip in order to hang it on your belt or backpack. There is also a silicone ring, that once you have emptied your bottle you can roll it all up, and slip this ring around it, to keep it rolled, and compact, for easy storage. This will be wonderful for when I am out walking, but I have a feeling the hubby is going to want some for his bug out bags. I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for a fair and unbiased opinion.

Yea, !! if you have read any of my other reviews, you know that I am a measuring spoon and cup addict.  I just love different ones, I have probably 5 sets in my drawer at the moment, and have no problem looking for more. They are the number 1 gift idea for me to give, when ever I have a bridal shower, or bachlorette party, the recipient always gets a nice set of spoons, and sometimes cups too, taped to the top of their gifts.  All 4 of my children, have all received spoons, and cups, as they were moving out of the house.  I just firmly believe that every household needs a good, set of cups and spoons.  This particular set is just plain cute, and fun.  I love the silicone handles, each a different and bright, cheery color on it.  The spoons are stainless steel, and have nice deep bowls, for scooping with. They are attached together with a heavy duty, stainless steel ring. The ring will open so you can separate the spoons, if need be. This set comes with all the normal measurements, 1 tablespoon, 1/2 tablespoon, 1 teaspoon, 1/2 teaspoon, and 1/4 teaspoon. The spoons, have standard and metric measurements, both of which are stamped on the spoons.  The only negative that I can find with this set, is that I wished the numbers, were a little bit larger, for a easier read, but other than that, I love this set.  I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for a fair and unbiased opinion.

Nice pencil sharpener. I started doing some of the adult coloring books, and if you have tried any of them, then you know that you can not do them with crayons. You have to have colored pencils, or maybe fine, fine, tip markers, or gel pens. There is so many, details in the coloring books,. that no matter how well your crayon is sharpen, it still will be to big. So I have invested in some the really cool sets of color pencils, and gel pens. I can get lost in coloring for hours, and that wears on pencils, you have to sharpen them. This automatic pencil sharpener, from Eagle, is a great for my color pencils. It gives them a nice point, without eating the pencil up. It sharpens very smoothly, and quietly. This sharpener, is 3 1/4 inches high, 3 inches wide, and 5 inches deep. It weighs in at 11.6 ounces. There are little rubber feet, on the bottom, and around the base of the bottom, to help keep it from sliding away on you while in use. The front globe and tray hold your pencil shavings, in, and simply slides off the front for easy emptying. The only negative that I can find with this sharpener, is battery compartment, the cover for it does not fit it well, and the batteries seem to be very very snug in there, had a little trouble getting all 4 AA batteries, in. But once I did the cover is still a little loose. There is a small hole in the back of the sharpener, however it did not come with a cord of anytype. So I'm not sure what that is there for. Other than that, I really like my new sharpener.

These are so wonderful, I purchased them for my husbands den, (or man cave) and when they came in he really loved them.  They look so natural, and really added to the motif in his room. Both of our sons,  seen them and immediately asked me to put them on their Christmas wish lists for their cabins. One like the this one and the other son liked the bear one. Guess Santa has more to deliver.

Wow what a wonderful cheese knife set. We play a lot of cards with company, and cheese and meat trays, are usually a big part of that entertainment. We love to try different types of cheeses. All different, textures, and smells, taste, ect.  This set from Silvero Premium Quality is as nice looking as it is useful. The set includes 4 different cheese tools, and is packaged and displayed very well, could be a great gift, for someone.  The cheese tools are all made of stainless steel, and have  a brushed finish to them. They wash up super easy, just a little soap and water, and no scrubbing.  There is a cheese knife for harder cheeses, 2 spreaders, one for soft, and one for crumbly cheeses, and a fork for serving. They are each about 5 1/2 inches long, and have nice wide handles. Each tool weighs between 1.6 ounces, and 2.4 ounces. When I first opened the box, and saw them, I thought they looked like they were very heavy, and they are not they feel great in your hands, not to big and bulky. The only problem I am having with this set is deciding whether to keep it for yourself, or to put in in my daughter's Christmas present, we got her some wine bottle items, and this would make a great addition to her gift. May just have to break down and order another set.lol I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for a fair and unbiased opinion.

I am old fashion and still using my old cork trivets. They are stained and starting to fall apart, so my daughter told me to give in and buy some new ones. I found this set from Ankway. These are really nice, they are made of silicone, which these days is the way to go with all most everything. The silicone does not have a bad smell, like some of your plastics do, and the silicone can hold up much better, for some things. This set of trivets, come 4 in a pack, you get 2 bright green, and 2 bright blue. They are 7 1/4 inches by 7 1/4 inches and they are 1/4 inch thick. The silicone is a nice soft pliable material, so you can use these as potholders, or trivets, either one. They have a honey comb type weave on them, which worried me a little, because I figured they would be terrible to get clean. I don't have a dishwasher, so I tossed  one in the washer with some towels on gentle cycle and it came out beautifully. They each have a small hole in one of the corners, so that you can hang them up if that is your preference.  I have been doing some baking, and at 400 degrees, you can't even feel a little bit of heat coming thru the pad. I guess my daughter was right it was time to get some new ones. .

OMG.  these glasses are adorable.  I got these for my granddaughter, who has an American Girl Doll.  I was so thrilled when they came in. The frames are a beautiful pink in color, with almost a candy cane stripe to the ear piece.  They are made of plastic, I think she might need to be a little careful with them. We have tried out a couple of these types of card holders. With all the technology now days, I almost wish that I could just memorise my card information, and just have it entered in manually. Seeings how that is not possible, I feel like we need to take as many precautions as possible to protect ourselves. This card holder from FuzzyGreen is a nice aluminum case. When you open it up there are six slots for placing business cards. Each slot will hold several cards, and the slots help to keep them a little more organized.  This case is 4 1/4 inches wide, 3 Inches high, and 3/4 of an inch thick. There is a push button on the front of the case to open it. I think this would be a little bulky for my husband to carry in his pocket, but for my purse, it actually works very well. Storing our business cards was not the reason, that I wanted one of these cases, it was to have the RFID protection, on our credit and debit cards. It wasn't until it came in that I realised that I had missed that point in the description. So all in all this will be a great card holder for business cards, which is what it is for, and I will have to try again for my RFID holder.

 I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for a fair and unbiased opinion. I always do my own research on any product that I order, so I have an idea, (like everyone else) as to whether I should waste my money on it. I rely on the reviews of others to help me make those decisions. When I do a review, I make sure that I have tested the product, and then give an honest opinion on it. I will always try to point out both the positive and the negative points on any product, regardless of the discount that I have received.

I ordered these frames so we could do some cool gifts from the grandkids for the great grandparents. They are a little on the cheaply made side, but really don't look it.  They are made of plastic, and comes in several different colors. This one is white, with a black backing on it. They come packaged in bubble wrap, and then in a box, so they are pretty well protected during shipping.  The picture cover is actually made of  plastic, but is very clear, so you can see the picture with no problem. The back has those little wings, on them for holding the picture in, one one each corner.  It also has a whole in the back for hanging from a screw (not included), or a fold leg for setting on the counter. You need 3AAA batteries, in order to make the recording work.  To record you simply push the button on the back where the microphone is located, record your 10 second message.  To hear the recording, simply push the button on the front right bottom corner.  Ir records very easily, and when you listen to it, it sound pretty good, just a little on the quiet side.  You do not lose your recording, when you have to change batteries, which is a great feature.  When you're recording a little ones voice, you can't exactly re-do it in a couple of years when the batteries have run down. I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for a fair and unbiased opinion.

We decided it was time to upgrade our network. We have been using a 100 Mbps switch, and that needed to take care of 3 computers, and multiple servers. As our system grew, the old switch was a bottleneck in the network. (too much, at one time). We chose this 8 Port Gigabit switch, from Relper, to try and speed up the system. The first thing about this that I liked is that it is very small and compact, so it doesn't take up much desk space. The unit is  5 3/8 inches wide, 1 inch tall, 3 inches deep, and weighs only 9.5 ounces.  There is a 120 v power supply that comes with it. Once we had our system, switched over (ha, ha) speed increased immensely as we was hoping for. My husband says, that to say this basically, we went from a 100 mbps, to a 1000 mbps. Problem solved. yeaaa. I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for a fair and unbiased opinion.

This is a wonderful little lock.  I love how small it is, so it fits onto the luggage zipper very easily, no fighting with it, to get it in and out of place.
You can set your own combination on it, and change it with ease if need be.  It is TSA approved, so they can open the lock to inspect your luggage, if need be, without destroying it. I received this product at a discounted price, in exchange for a fair and unbiased opinion.

users.query: Thor always a good read and I always look for Thor stories. Though I did enjoy this story, it was not quite as exciting as others I've read.  Will still look forward to more of his work.

cands.text: Great storyline. Has a hard time putting it down when necessary.  Enjoy Thor's books...but don't necessarily agree w/his politics...but will continue to keep buying his books

Really enjoyed the collector's three exciting stories.  I am a fan of the late Vince Flynn with the Mitch Rapp series and found Mr. Thor's books w/Scott Harvath series. Very exciting and keeps reader wondering what each chapter is going to bring...excitement & intrigue.
Another great Brad Thor book.  Although fiction, brings home what could be going on behind the scene.  Good depiction of politics and the future of our country.
Brad Thor/Scot Harvath books are one of my favorites....Harvath is a sexy brave character but with compassion!!  Thanks Mr Thor.
Great stories.  I always enjoy the Corps Justice books.  Well written.
Again, even though I've read following books previously, I was still in suspense as I read on.  Knowing a good ending would occur, still kept me reading.  Great read.
Interesting and very good reads. Have many of Clive Cussler's books, paperback, hard cover and now on Kindle.  Very good plots.
Enjoyed this story very much.  Need more like it. Would like to see more Kolt Raynor books.  Would like more with Hawk.

Good read.  Sorry Jack & Bear splitting up, hope another Noble & Bear forthcoming!  Enjoyed the Noble Betrayal.  Least liked was Noble, No Mercy.
But I do like the series of Noble stories I've read.  Looking forward to more

Even though I had read before & did remember as it went along, I enjoyed the action & ultimate successful ending, I enjoyed reading it again. I previously read the book but now reading on my kindle.  Great story...little sci-fi sometimes but good.  Too bad we don't have real groups like the Corporation with what is happening in the world today.
My second experience with Kanon's stories.  Enjoyed this one too.
Separation of Power (Mitch Rapp Novels) Good reading to the end. Keeps you so intrigued that you can't stop reading.
Having read the book where Henley went off the deep end and tried to kill Stevens,  makes it sadder, but it was a  good read.
Took a little time to get into it, but finally did and enjoyed the read.
Very good. Kept my interest to keep reading.  Eric Meyer  books are among my favorite.  Looming forward to more. Thank you.
Enjoyed the Grant Stevens story as usual.  I am always looking for more Grant Stevens & the AT team.  Each one is different & holds the same suspense.  Please keep the sequels coming.
Have read other task force stories but never this one.  Liked it.  Anxious to read more stories by Brad Taylor.
Great plot and keeps you guessing right to the very end.  I probably won't be continuing these ratings if I have to make a complete dissertation about the books.
Enjoyed this book very much.  Since I had read a. couple of the Pike Logan series out of order....still enjoyed the read.
First time with Elkins stories.  Was a little boring going into it but stuck with it & story got more interesting.
Once gain  Juan & company saved the day!  Knew the story would be as suspected but always fun to read & find out how events would work out.
Kept this reader in suspense even knowing Morgan would save the day!  We need & probably have real live men and women who risk their lives every day forties great country of ours.

Glad I bought the book.  Another great Pike Logan saga....with the female solving the puzzle.
Looking forward to more like this.

When I started this, thought I'd made a mistake in choosing it, but knowing who wrote it, couldn't believe it was just a "gory killer" book.  So, kept going.  I Finnish rd this on record time!  Very intriguing & kept me reading.  Finished it at 3am.  Glad to see Stokes & Briggs involved & Greer joining that team.  Thanks for a great read!!!

users.query:
Refreshingly different and poignant, yet an eye-opening reveal. A surprise package -- not anything like I was expecting but so much more in every way. The writing is smooth and beautiful. The characters are a blend of so many out-of-the-ordinary expectations that I was at times mesmerized by their personalities and actions. The story is filled with tenderness, sadness, fun, quirky, and even a bit of scandalous behavior. But don't expect page after page filled with sex because you won't find it here, and what there is takes place in its own due time. Again, kudos to the writer for making it meaningful and a demonstrative relationship in it own special way.

A story of coming of age and of forbidden love that won't easily be forgotten. A book that will definitely be read again. A nice change of pace where nothing was rushed and, at times, felt like I was reading in slow motion. And I don't mean that in a negative way. It worked from start to finish.

cands.text:
A stunning love story that will put readers on an emotional roller coaster. A deep and hard test in the search for ones self. Harder will shred your emotions. It is important to mention that this is not your everyday run-of- the-mill New Adult reading experience. Its a unique journey. A number of very real and difficult topics are addressed in an open and informative manner. Robin Yorks writing is witty and comical at times, even while our characters are surrounded by gut-wrenching circumstances. She writes believable characters with depth and creativity in achingly everyday life situations. This story took hold of my heart and didn't release it until the very end. I wasn't sure what to expect after Deeper. High expectations were a certainty and I certainly wasn't disappointed where Robin York took us.

More than anything else, this is a story of hope. And throughout, this reader continually hoped that both West and Caroline would never look back with regret  but move forward with hope. Even though they don't really know where they are going, there was hope that they wouldnt leave each other behind or alone.

There are so many levels to this amazingly well-written story. Once you begin, you won't be able to put it aside. When Deeper ended, I felt the pain and agony going through both West and Caroline. And as we pick up their story here, the lights are still dimmed and the mood isn't giving us much hope. Back in his hometown of Silt, West is making things much harder than necessary and its causing pain and hurt to more than just him. Hes returned to some of his nasty habits and Caroline is devastated by his actions. Prepare yourself for Caroline and West to trample on your heart before the mending begins bit by bit.

A fresh new voice in the New Adult genre from a much adored and established contemporary romance writer . . . I loved this book! Such a superb read from start to finish.

Publish Date: July 1, 2014
Robin York, Author, who also writes as Ruthie Knox

This is the first book that Ive read by this new-to-me-author, but it won't be my last.  The writing is descriptive and pulls every emotion to the forefront of your mind.  The blurb gives enough information for readers to realize that there is going to be tragedy involved.  More than that though, its an epic love story that feels real and isn't just told  you watch every moment and those moments come to life as they take shape in the evolving commitments and loyalties that last a lifetime.

An added plus is the grand Epilogue that will not only bring you to tears but will also make your heart swell with love and admiration for the truly inspirational love story that the lead character, Dr. Hunter tells in this book.

A must read for your TBR list.

From the lovely cover to the very last word -- a superb reading adventure! The book blurb above says enough . . . so I won't be spoiling this marvelous story by adding any more details concerning the storyline.

I will say that this book is well-worthy of any romance readers time. Theres a stunning combination of bittersweet and second chance for happily-ever-after within its pages. A secondary plot is well blended and runs alongside the main one in the last half of the book  one, the building and ongoing romantic relationship filled with its ups and downs between Lux and Sebastian (Bash), and the other a suspense surrounding the disappearance of a child Lux meets in the open marketplace. I was hooked by the addition of the dark and chilling mystery which was intriguing and cleverly interwoven into the main storyline.

A strong and delightful cast of side characters -- portrayed as Luxs BFFs, Simon, a clothes designer extraordinaire, and Fae, who is close-mouthed and ever-knowlegeable -- add plenty of spark and wit to the narrative as well.

And it would be wrongfully unfair not to pay a special tribute to Jamie, Luxs twin brother. What an admirable and strong individual, who played a very important role in the relationship building between Lux and Bash, while fighting the battle of his life.

This is an outstanding addition to the New Adult genre by a very talented new-to-me-author, Julie Johnson. Im also grabbing her debut romantic suspense novel, Like Gravity to read while anxiously looking forward to what comes next from her.

*I was gifted a copy of this book from the author in return for an honest and unbiased review.*

This debut book is filled with the potential to be a solid and well-contrived adventure in reading. My biggest complaint with it is the lack of spontaneity in the writing style. The dialogue just didn't flow well for me a lot of the time. It has a very structured and robotic tone. There is a great need for the usage of contractions. The entire story gives off a feeling of being force-fed with little emotion to support it.

After running from an abusive home life, Kenna Sloan is hiding behind a wall of toughness, hoping to remain safe and in control of her life. But her roommate has other ideas and arranges a double date to introduce Kenna to her boyfriends buddy, Donovan Alexander, another police officer. Of course, as weve seen in so many of these NA genres, both Kenna and Donovan are tormented by secrets they kept close to the vest.

On a positive note, there is a nice building process to their relationship before moving on to the sexual side. A big plus is the no insta-love even though these two share insta-chemistry. Donovan is a bit contradictory -- one moment he's almost too sweet and syrupy and then the next he's playing alpha that almost becomes over-the-top in my opinion. Kenna is a young college student, who is unexperienced, often fretting and whining over nothing but still remains strong in her own right.

Basically this is a story of putting the past behind you and starting with a clean slate. We all know that is easier said than done. Although it takes awhile, there is some steam to the story and quite a lot of angst. The book also carried with it some very likable characters  as well as some that seemed to serve no purpose whatsoever. There are several parts that are particularly sweet and tender  and also heartbreaking.

Absolutely outstanding from start to finish! A rare and surefire page-turner. Truly loved this brilliantly crafted book so hard. One of the best second chance at love stories ever - that began with a bit of a hate-to-love you theme.

Beautifully draw characters whose emotions run the spectrum. Over-the-top fantastic dialogue with depth and heart. And a strong storyline with plenty of conflict and angst - but not overdone. There's plenty of balance filled with cleverness, sizzle and heat, fun and extraordinary laughable entertainment, as well. I went from tears filling my eyes to laughing out loud in the next minute. I was so caught up by all the different feels and events that added the extra special spark to make this one memorable.

A major HIGH FIVE to HARRY, the boy wonder! That boy stole my heart and I never want it back. The entire secondary cast played their parts to perfection, adding so much support and depth to an already winning tale.

I didn't think JEA could top "When Life Happened" -- but oh how wrong I was. She did it bigtime, too!

Two thumbs up (because that's all I have)!! A standing ovation kind of Epilogue where I felt the need to stand, clap and cheer. This one gets the highest recommendation I can give.

This was my first book by this author. There was a lot to like  a captivating storyline with an older woman/younger man trope. Im usually not a fan of more than a 10-year age difference, but the difference here has such a real feel to it and was so believable that I fell right into it without any trouble. I loved the musical theme involved in bringing Ben and Jill together. The contrast between her developing relationship with Ben and the one she shared with her deceased husband is so different  but she struggles with the age difference. Ben is special ordered to Jills needs in this story that centers around loss, heartbreak, and new beginnings for new love on the horizon.

Jill is the forty-two-year-old widow of a famous rock star, and shes also a Grammy winning composer and a mother. Preparing for a memorial concert to honor his memory, she meets a young and upcoming solo artist.

Ben has just parted ways with his former boy band and on a path for stardom as solo artist. Hes a really good guy with his feet planted solidly on the ground. Hes definitely not your normal bad boy hot rocker. When he meets Jill, hes a goner  and that age difference is no roadblock for him.

What started off as a friendship, grew quickly into a much deeper connection that turned into a burning inferno. Their relationship may have been considered imperfectly cast, but they were perfect for each other.

Jills college-aged daughter is gay and involved with Emily. They are in and out of the picture quite a bit stirring up some dust here and there which adds another level to the drama level. But most of the time, the relationship between mother and daughter is solid and loving. The relationship added a nice addition to the overall theme.

The angst surrounding Bens dark secret seemed a little over-the-top and blown out of proportion in comparison to what it turned out to be. I didn't quite understand the reasoning behind hiding it from Jill or anyone else for that matter. Ben was completely innocent and handled it maturely.

A ton of angsty ups/downs involving the extended family, drugs, marital problems, and some expected plagues that tend to follow celebrities are thrown into the mix as well. A heavy dose of mental illness also comes into play surrounding so many of the characters that the situation quickly seems a bit too redundant and melodramatic. There was a lot of abnormal, no one having escaped without heavy baggage attached to them.

Still, this book has a lot of curb appeal, but it doesnt come without a few flaws. Loose ends left untied, e.g., cosmetic surgery before the big concert planned by Jill, but at the end of the book, shes still complaining about her aging skin, wrinkles, etc. -- and the scheduled surgery that was once a priority was never mentioned again. The writing is not bad -- but a few too many editing issues should have been caught. Needed one last line-by-line edit before hitting publish  a few too many misspelled words and use of wrong words, i.e. potter should be putter, etc.  simple and easy fixes.

SECOND GUESSING is a good all-round tale that deserves a look-see. It provided some laughter, along with the angst-overload, sewn up in an emotional, sweet and tender love story. And a big plus came wrapped in a perfect Epilogue. I just love a solid happily-ever-after, and this author completes the task well.

Prepare yourselves!  This author definitely puts feelings to her words.  Over the past few months, Ive read several books with a similar theme and thought they were good.  But none came close to this one.  Oh geez, this one just messed me up.  I don't remember crying this hard at the end of a book, yet feeling like smiling because something extraordinary just happened.  A truly unforgettable reading experience.

The story surrounds Kate, Keller, and Gus, along with numerous superb secondary characters.

Kate was a person who always saw the bright side of everything.  She made the darkest days in her friend and loved ones lives bright.  And even on the darkest days of her life, she brightened the days for those around her.  Kate was a remarkably admirable and quirky lovable character.  I loved the strengths she exhibited from beginning to ending.  Her originality in style and the independent and self-reliant tendencies she held so solidly were amazing and made her such a unique and memorable character.  But Kate is keeping a secret  a big one.

Gus has been Kates best friend since childhood.  Hes a talented musician on his way to the big time, along with his band of merry music makers.  And he smokes like a fiend  which Kate calls him often.  Hes loyal and true in their friendship.  Theyve only stepped over the line into a one-night-stand once  on the night before he heads one way and she heads across country the other way.  Gus has shared everything with Kate.  Well, except for one secret.

Keller is beautiful  inside and out, as well as smart, friendly and a very hard worker.  As soon as he appeared on the page, my heart fluttered and flipped.  Hes got a magnetism about him that woos all females  and hes honest about it.  He doesnt play games.  Hes got a path to success set out before him.  And hes not looking for a serious relationship.  Well, not until he lays eyes on the new girl in town, who comes in for a coffee and ends up being the best part of his day.  And yes, Keller is keeping a secret, too.

Theres not one negative remark to be made where this book is concerned.  It will require Kleenex.  Youll want to beg and plead before its all over.  Youll be sad and happy, youll laugh and cry throughout.  But when all is said and done, I think youll see the Bright Side.

Simply charming and loaded with romance! Every page was overflowing with extra special touches and all the sweetness love can bring. There wasn't a single thing I would change -- Beth Ehemann didn't miss the slightest opportunity in giving readers perfection in the finale to Kacie and Brody's wonderful love story.

Absolutely a joy to read! I highly recommend the entire Cranberry Inn series.

This is my third book within the last several weeks by a new-to-me-author. And that old saying, "three's the charm" worked really well for me. I wasn't particularly thrilled and wowed by the first or second choices, but this go-round was a totally different experience. A tidal wave of emotions poured from the pages. The writing was authentic and truly enjoyable. I adored everything single line of this story and fell in love with the main characters, the intelligently written words, and the evidence of the authors knowledge and insight into her subject matter. All the elements that make a book remarkable were present and accounted for. And this story made me feel each and every single emotion.

The plot was refreshingly unique and kept me in the moment without distraction. Another college campus for part of the story but it didn't feel like a redo -- this one had depth and meaningful dialogue, along with two characters very different from the other -- yet perfectly compatible in the long run. Just had to come to terms with each other's long-term goals or lack thereof in the case of one. But that one stole my heart and made me hope for a better person to slip from his hiding place. There's loss and sadness lying close to the surface throughout most of this story -- and you'll feel the emotions bubbling within yourself as they are revealed.

Do I recommend this book? Yes, indeed!

WOW! Left me breathless. This is one of THOSE books -- the kind that keeps your mind engaged long after the final word in the Epilogue. Terrific second chance storyline that powerfully pushes through the boundaries of unique -- so much more than just a girl and a boy -- so much more than just a love story.

Don't miss one of the best books of the year!

I love the cute and sassy cover that was first to grab my attention -- but in no way prepared me for what lay ahead. I was consumed from the first page on. Absolutely outstanding! This book was a total surprise  and a novel change from the norm. A ballad of real life. No black and white answers  but plenty of gray areas to challenge your senses emotionally, as well as play havoc with your feelings on morality. Ive purposefully held my review in check trying to convey my praise without divulging any possible spoilers. Some readers will no doubt find hard limits that may be a problem. That being said, I urge you to read this book anyway. Its more than just romance with the possibility of cheating  its more than just a love story  its more than sex  its more than friendship. Its a powerful depiction of real life happening in 3-D technicolor.

At its very core, the story centers on Parker Cruse, a young womanwho hates cheaters! For personal reasons, I hate cheaters, too. I connected with Parker. Its been a lifetime ago, but that hurt has never really been forgotten or forgiven. My motto  once a cheater, always a cheater. I wasn't sure I could read this book. Even after being assured by book buds that I just needed to take it one page at a time and let life happen. I tried hard not to place a lot of emphasis on what the book blurb revealed. I held my nose and jumped into the deep end, and hoped I would still trust those friends when I surfaced. Within this all-consuming reading experience, I found some answers to my own personal demons and so much more. Im glad that I just let life happen and read what now is most assuredly going to hit my list of best reads of 2017.

This second chance romance will own you -- tumultuous, evocative, sexy and addictive. Sometimes life justhappens. Sometimes it hurts, and we cant stop it. We cant control it, no matter how hard we try. And that hurts even more. With emotions running high and intense, the story will burrow deep into your heart. I simply adored Parker. Shes kinda quirky, sassy with a little "devil" in her,and imperfect, but an organizational freak with "responsibility" as her middle name -- and always lovable. Parker is real and she brings life to this story. She's driven and knows exactly how to get a job done well. She's a terrific young woman whose twin sister's betrayal has devastated their relationship and caused rift in the family. Her heart is broken and she's lost the love of her life, or so she thinks. She's never really found her niche or a job that allows her to use the degree she worked so hard to achieve. Living across the road from her parents doesn't allow much adventure for our girl from Iowa either -- and did I mention her insane over-protecting mother?

When temptationcomes knocking on her door,it is one of the funniest scenes I've ever read. Parker fights the attraction with all her might -- really she does! But the chemistry makes things hard to ignore between her and the new neighbor, Gus Westman. Their banter and interactions are so witty and direct that they hit their mark with precision. Gus is suffering his own personal problems. His wife is a workaholic and travels more than she's home. And when she is home, her schedule is filled with uppity clients and girls' night out. Gus is a great guy -- a gorgeous hunk who loves his old sports cap and tight faded tees -- and he gives it his best effort to appreciate and show his love for his wife. He plans trips for the two of them that are always cancelled, and he's built a beautiful home for a family he hopes to share with his wife one day-- if only she would give him the time of day (or night). 

Besides Parker, there's a dynamic cast of characters:Gus, Sabrina, the parents, and sibs, Levi a/k/a TheFuneral Clown,who are all wonderfully drawn. Their parts are meaningful as they each play a major supporting role in humanizing andadding depth tothis story. Prepare yourself to fall in love more than once -- even with Rags, a mischievous Sheepdog. Some you'll lose your heart to deeply --others not so much. It'll be easier loving to hate them. Still, each individual brings their own special meaning to the overall storyline. But the romance plot is predominantly angst-filled and a painful journey to self-awareness and forgiveness interwoven with family, love, loss, secrets, regret, and hope. But don't despair, there are definitely more than enough high-spirited moments interwoven throughout to provide a few belly-laughs from readers, along with some great banter and wit. Altogether, you'll find a truly eye-opening face-to-face with life and all the events that come in and out of our lives at any minute or hour of each day.

WHAM! TOTALLY GOBSMACKED!! Halfway in and Im in a head-on collision with a SHOCKER PLOT TWIST. Be still my mangled heart. Torturous author! I never saw this 360 coming. Without being too specific for fear of including spoilers, this is not your standard romance and certainly not cut and dry. There are twists you won't see coming and ugly demons that must be conquered. Cried my eyes out and felt like Id been slammed in the gut by a 300-lb. defensive lineman. But life happens when you least expect it, and there's nota damn thing you can do about it. And that's all you're getting from me. There's a whole other side to this story and one that will definitely keep you in suspense and emotionally torn. Life goes on and thankfully this author justifies her well-served but merciless gut-punch.

I read each day, and sometimes it feels like Im reading the same old story over and over  just different names/different locations. But this book went way beyond what has becomethe standard. Totally unexpected and uniquely surprising. Whether you believe in destiny or fate, Jewel E. Ann grabbed the bull by the horns and more than met my expectations in creatinga story that shows how life just happens when you least expect it and effectively made it real. She is a powerful writer who builds a profound story that she capably brings to life on the pages, one that captivates from start to finish, and assures youll fall in love with her flawed and endearing characters.

Get yourself a copy of this extraordinary face-to-face with life, and find out how Parker, the girl from Iowa deals with all that confronts her When Life Happened.

Beautiful words, beautiful story, and above all beautiful lessons of self-less love and forgiveness. I would give this story a million stars if I could. It was such a feel good reading experience and not one single teeny tiny nitpick. It was just one of those perfect hits with perfect timing.

Mercy! This one kidnapped my heart and soul and I don't care if I ever get them back. I absolutely loved this book. Emma Scott has created something uniquely extraordinary, special in a deeply emotional way for two of the most lovable and memorable characters Ive been touched by in a long, long time. Not only that, but throughout the pages youll find some of the most priceless and meaningful quotes and dialogue in contemporary romance. This story is written with a magical touch.

Beckett Copeland  to know him is to love him. The moment he presents himself on the page its love at first sight. Even though he's flawed with guilt from an event he created for himself, hes so good and kind, so sweet in an extremely handsome package. He brings all the feels you can imagine. But the boy is badly tormented believing he has no choices, and its going to take a very special person to rescue Beckett from the guilt and agony that drowns him daily.

And then along came Zelda Rossi  never really cared for her name when she was introduced in the Full Tilt series where she worked in Theos tattoo parlor - but that strong and scrappy girl just kept insisting that I love not only her, but her name, too. And I do! A tragedy from her past, for which she continues to blame herself, plagues her future and brings on severe panic attacks. Zelda is the kind of heroine that you want for a best friend. She's loyal, generous and true blue. Both inside and outside, she's a beauty.

Along with our lead characters, there are some extra-special people that play very important roles in providing much needed support. Without these characters, that extra level of extraordinary would suddenly disappear. This story would not have reached the level of perfection that it achieved.

When fate brings Beckett and Zelda together, each is carrying a burdensome weight that must be exposed and shared before healing begins. Blind to his/her own beauty and goodness to the point of self-destruction, each finds it in the other. Together they weather the storms and share memorable lessons of forgiveness and an even more unforgettable multi-leveled story of selfless and tireless support and love that you can ever imagine.

Now on a book high feelin the love, I know Ill be back time and again for a refresher course from these two wonderful examples of how to live life, and more importantly, to love those in your life to the fullest in the most pure, simple, and charitable ways. I found a truly unique reading experience that doesnt come along very often.

An alluring New Adult read by a new-to-me author.  Definitely a fun-to-read story that grabbed me with the blurb and kept me in my chair from start to finish.  Great writing and wonderfully entertaining characters.  This one surprised me in so many good ways  a real treat full of laughs, sizzle, and a big dose of the real thing!

Max Levin is the heir to White Lace Productions, a pornography kingdom.  Hes seen it all and lived it all as he grew up with parents who didn't hide the business.  But as his 24th birthday rolls around, hes not sure that his inheritance is the life he wants in the future.

Everly Parker follows all the rules and has always met her parents expectations.  Shes one test away from her law degree  but her recently deceased grandmother left a bucket list of to dos for Everly and theyve got nothing to do with the law.

Max and Everly sparked from their first encounter.  Even so, the build towards more started slowly beginning with a challenge.  So much fun to watch as the pieces started falling into place with a perfect fit.  I loved both these characters and their story.  A great cast of secondary characters added to the depth and pleasures in RUSH.

In Cynthia Pomranzs debut book, the storyline held great potential in the unique theme and the promise of new love. The writing was easy to follow. But as I got into the story, I struggled with the scenario. I think it might have something to do with my age and the fact that the internet world and online dating is a scary thought for me. I just cant wrap my mind around hooking up this way. Im all about eye-to-eye contact as a first impression. So for me, this idea freaked me a bit.

It was refreshing to read a story involving Jacqueline (Jackie), a more mature career woman who is divorced, has some self-image issues, is separated from her teen-aged daughters, and beginning a new life that hopefully includes romance, as well. After being pushed by her best friend, she tries an online dating service. Oh boy! Variety is the spice of life  and online dating offers it in bulk supply. I found this part of the story most fun-to-read with lots of laugh-out-loud moments and profound, as well. Jackie receives an overload of replies after she posts her profile and she sets about reviewing them and choosing several possibilities. But one particular response catches her eye.

Marc, who posted his handsome face, is a very successful guy. But hes also extremely closed off and secretive. As a reader, I never really understood the totality of why or what his problems were and what they stemmed from. He kept saying he would open up and talk to Jackie about himself, but the talk really never happened. The physical attraction was there from the get-go and it didn't take long before they were involved sexually . . . a bit too fast in my opinion. So many little things were thrown into the story that left so much to the imagination or begging to be resolved. Marc seemed a bit smarmy and shifty to me. For someone who could write such flowery poems and email messages, he was closed off and totally different acting in person. I never felt comfortable with him. But Jackie was attracted and fell head-over-heels. Nothing goes as smoothly as we would have it and, of course, in the world of romance the same applied here. Their newly formed relationship suffers some ups and downs.

Jacqueline presented me with her own set of cause-for-pause. From the beginning I needed to know more about the problems in Jackies marriage and why her daughters were sent away to boarding school if she wasn't onboard with the decision. What made the girls so eager to go away? Why did it seem that her girls had a closer relationship with their father and were disconnected from their mother for long periods of time? There was never any interaction on behalf of the girls between their mom and dad, which just seemed strange to me. Her ex-husband never made an appearance which left so many questions about the family dynamics. For young teen-age girls, I was surprised by the way Jackies daughters treated their mother in a very strained relationship for most of the book, and then suddenly out of the blue and towards the end they throw out the word love. Some of the best moments for me in regards to Jackie were the times she spent with her mother. Their relationship seemed open and natural, unlike the calculated feelings I had where the daughters were concerned.

A major highlight and one I enjoyed immensely is the St. Louis setting which was familiar to me, and made for a nice tour of fond memories and landmarks where I once lived -- a trip to the ballpark to watch those Cardinals in action being one of the fondest.

Just because this one didn't quite send me over the moon doesnt mean I won't look forward to reading more from this new-to-me author.

Note: I received a copy of BECAUSE OF JACQUELINE from the author in exchange for an honest and unbiased opinion.

Deliver will send chills up and down your spine in this romantic thriller because there is a substantial love story.  A fine line between good and evil fills the pages, and it definitely leans towards a much darker and grittier plotline than most.  Readers are wisely forewarned to expect the unexpected.  Thats all Im saying regarding the plotline  each reader should experience every intriguing surprise on their own.

Theres a depth to the characters that I was not expecting.  Each carries his/her own unique and unconventional characteristics.  An unimaginable strength and courage lies within their souls when faced with unfathomable obstacles.  The connection is mesmerizing between the characters and challenges readers to look beyond the mere surface.

My first book by Pam Godwin was tantalizing and torturous  at times almost too much to take in.  Its not an easy book to read or be able to say that you love it.  She writes with a raw fervor that pulls and pushes readers to beg for more.  Godwin definitely delivered a complete package of alluring and spellbinding hours of reading.  I was held captive from start to finish.

Sometimes this reader just wants a solid contemporary romance that is filled with feel-good feelings, smartly written dialogue, sexy romance, and charming characters to win my heart. That's exactly what Julie James's latest release provided in spades. I read it from cover to cover without moving out of my chair.

Our hero isn't thinking clearly when he strikes out to settle a score and crashes Twitter. Soon he finds himself being escorted off an airplane by FBI agents and charged with multiple felonies. After his release from prison, he finds no comfort in being labeled an "ex-con" and as the "Twitter Terrorist." But even more complications arise when he goes and falls in love with a federal prosecutor involved in his case. And wouldn't you know it, she doesn't think her career goals will survive a love connection between an "ex-con" and a "federal prosecutor. Ah - but this ex-con is not only a real charmer with dimples, he's determined, rich, smart, and quite simply irresistible.

In this installment of her FBI series, Ms. James turns up the heat and it is a welcomed addition. Kyle and Rylann have great chemistry. Kyle is a smart and charming. Rylann is strong and witty. Both are strong and well-developed characters.  They approach their relationship as equals. It's fun to watch them spar, tease and tempt one another. Their attraction to each other is never questioned.

Not a major concern but it caught my attention, bugged me a little, and made me wonder: Why this cover of the series, in particular, had its female model clothed in a pantsuit. It didn't hold true to the storyline. Rylann's business suit skirts were not only a turn-on to Kyle throughout the book but also source for the FBI's nickname for her.

After such a marvelous story, the ending was a bit abrupt. I wish there had been a little more spice in the happily-ever-after.

I finished it this morning and was unimpressed. I gave the first two books five star reviews but this one is not happening for me. Too much repetiveness and way way too much sex without plot. Page after page of the same old same old.  And Cary and Eva continue to act like two foolish high schoolers. I'm really annoyed with Eva's conduct in regards to Brett as well. The relationship between Gideon and Eva doesn't feel right this time around.  And well, TMI on Gideon's grooming habits just was unnecessary. Oh well, I've read it now and I wish Sylvia Day had just answered the questions from books one and two, left out all the whacky filler, and just given Gideon and Eva their happy ever after. I paid the price for the product and won't be asking for my money back but, without a doubt, I'm finished with the Crossfire Series.

The cover caught my eye and the book blurb sold it. A stunning debut by Pamela Sparkman in a story of pain, agony, loss and recovery wrapped in love. There's plenty of emotion and turmoil - passionately presented while the heat and sexual relationship remains behind closed doors. The female lead is a virgin who has suffered greatly in her life both physically and with the loss of loved ones. Our hero is simply irresistible and his kindness radiates off the pages. He's the real deal and protects those he loves. A great cast of secondary characters lend their support in making this one even better. I loved Grammy Sophie and the gang of friends who support each other so lovingly and unselfishly when needed.

A truly beautiful love story that is well-written and realistically portrayed. Readers will find the connection between the characters quite surprising and endearing. With the addition of the musical element supplied within the story lies an even sweeter and more meaningful level to this relationship as well.

One of the best lines in the book that has no cliffhanger but a beautiful epilogue summing it all up nicely, "Here's to love, laughter and happily-ever-after."

Theres an abundance of angst attached hereto. It might be a bit of an overload. However, it was a pretty easy read with characters that caught my attention from the beginning and kept me in their spin. Be forewarned though that there is a major cliffhanger that will most likely leave you screaming. Youll have to await the arrival of the next book to find out where the road leads for Prudence and Cash.

Prudence is a musician who travels with her band from England to the US in hopes of signing a record contract. She leaves behind a broken relationship and shes definitely not interested in starting a new one.

Cash Matthews makes his living as an executive producer in the world of television. His path crosses Prus when he hears the band play. He sees, he wants, and he pursues. Of course, Cash has relationship woes as well  and hes definitely not up for anything serious developing either.

Ah  but fate steps forward and plays havoc with their so-called plans. What starts out as two broken souls agreeing to a casual fling over the summer soon becomes much more.

I was drawn to the strong individual portrayed by Pru. I liked that she was a non-whiner who didn't require constant stroking. Cash on the other hand was a bit of a contradiction. What is promoted as his dominant male tendencies seems to lose a bit of its original steam and fizzles a bit. Even so, both characters were interesting and the chemistry between them sparked enough interest to keep me wishin and hopin that they would wake up and smell the roses  before it was too late.

Once again, communication is the key to the success of this relationship and these two seem to have forgotten this important fact. And then time just runs out . . .

Told from both main characters points of view and most times my favorite form of storytelling, I enjoyed venturing inside each ones mind to gain additional depth in both their personalities and thoughts. The author has taken an often told trope and given it her own refreshing and unique take. I enjoyed this book and will be looking forward to continuing on with Prudence and Cashs story in the next installment.

Disappointed - definitely! This train wreck certainly wasn't what I envisioned for two self-proclaimed soul mates and their happily-ever-after. It hurt to watch all the ridiculousness that erupted on the pages of this book. I wasn't gullible enough to fall for it as believable or realistic. What I felt when I fell victim to that crushing cliffhanger at the end of Book One was shock and stress over where this author would take us, but still hopeful and optimistic that the two would definitely get back on track with a meaningful relationship.  I never anticipated all the nonsensical excuses Jax could spew from his mouth in order to try and make himself out to be more than he was. And Lily just bit the green weenie and turned into a sniveling and weak whiner. And Stella - I don't even want to touch that one with a ten-foot pole. All three got a complete make-over in personalities from their original appearances. Some of their actions were deplorable and pathetic. And nothing I read called to me and said, this is a story of soul deep mates who were made for each other and would share a "forever kind of love."

And even though there appears to be a happily-ever-after in a nicely written Epilogue -- I'm not trusting anything in the world of Lily and Jax!
Perfect for the little space I had in mind.  Arrived in mint condition and can't wait to hang it to welcome the spooks and gobblins!

Steamrolled! I did NOT see that coming!! Unbelievably well-written and powerfully surprising. Just when I thought it was all going to be tied up in a neatly packaged conclusion, BOOM the bottom fell out. I must give credit where credit is due and say that Jenni Moen kept the momentum going in this one from the very first word to the very last one.

Ah, but even with that being said, I was disappointed with the way it ended even though I understand the scenario and the "what if" thought processing. The disappointment, however, does not take away from the well-worth-the-read in one well-drawn intriguing and thought provoking story. It earned the five-stars in my opinion.

I chose not to even mention characters or anything else associated with this story to avoid spoilers that might ruin what should most certainly be entered into completely blind by a reader for the maximum punch. My rating should speak for itself -- I highly recommend this one!

A strong and intriguing start in the first installment of K.A. Lindes new Record trilogy. Whats an election without a little scandal or clandestine affairs? Linde has written a political rascal.

North Carolina State Senator Brady Maxwell is running for election to the U.S. House of Representatives when he encounters Liz Dougherty, a bright and daring young college reporter who doesnt support his agenda. Together these two generate the fireworks in this one. There is so much that could go wrong if their secret isn't kept Off the Record.

Ive read some reviews questioning the need for the possible love triangle between Brady, Liz and Hayden. My thoughts are that Hayden, the college newspaper editor, is the third side to the triangle for comparison purposes. Liz herself questions the "arrangement" between her and Brady. He leaves her feeling second string at best. His political career and the upcoming elections take center stage and he wants everything between them kept secret and hidden from sight of the public. And he promises no more. He calls the shots. She even takes on a pseudo name when in contact with Brady. Can Liz really continue this type of relationship. Is this how she really wants her life to be? Hayden, on the other hand, is the light where Brady is the dark. Hayden stands for all the things that Brady cant or won't give her  most importantly the chance at a normal out-in-the-open relationship.

There is a strong cast of secondary characters who pave the way for what looks to be exciting times on the campaign trail in the next two books.

Heather, the young senators press secretary, is overly controlling and way too involved. I have questions about her loyalty and devotion to the young Senator. Theres history between these two from way back and Im not sure I trust her or not. Guess Ill be tuning into installment two to find out if Im worrying over nothing.

Clay Maxwell, the younger brother and a law student at Yale, is quite the flirt and troublemaker. Hes always popping up at the most inopportune times. I think hes got a story to tell as well. He and his older brother don't see eye-to-eye. Is he just jealous or is there something more sinister going on?

And then there is Bradys baby sister, Savannah Maxwell. Just beginning her freshman year at Chapel Hill and assigned to Lizs team on the college newspaper. What kind of trouble will she bring to the table?

Of course, the expected cliffhanger leaves unanswered questions every reader will most certainly find themselves facing at the end of this book. A little longer wait for some of the answers than I would like, but On the Record, the second installment is scheduled for release on August 26, 2014.

There are no words of praise lavish enough to bestow the rank of perfection found in "Defiant," the latest outstanding historical novel written by the incomparable Pamela Clare.  This author holds a magic writing wand in her hand.  The characters come to life on the pages of her books.  Her work is simply outstanding and unforgettable.  If you've never experienced the joys of reading one of her books, I urge you to do so.

Readers have waited with eager anticipation for Connor MacKinnon's story.  Behold -- it has arrived and it's so much more than any reader could have expected.  There's not a teensy weensy itsy bitsy particle of disappointment to be found among the words in this fabulous addition to the "Rangers" series.  Connor and Sarah are magnificently matched and truly joyful to watch as their tender relationship develops into a fiery and passionate mating.  As we've come to expect from this author, the sensual love scenes are exquisitely written with care and realism.  The story is packed with high drama, a heart-wrenching  journey towards survival, and the hope, joys, and sacrifices a family is willing to make for those they love.

Pamela Clare is unquestionably one of the best in presenting the complete package.  She digs deep into her research.  She cares about what's beneath the surface.  She doesn't accept anything less.  Her stories present a true and accurate representation of the history and time period surrounding the storyline.  The proof is in the details.

I stand in awe of Pamela Clare's many talents and charitable acts of kindness.  I'm thankful for the day I discovered her books.  I'm blessed to have enjoyed the time she so freely shares with her readers.  And I look forward to many more wonderful hours of reading pleasure penned by this amazing writer.  Congrats, Pamela!  You've made it to the top of the mountain once again.

users.query: A wonderful contradictions of darkness and light.  A mystery filled with sadness and trauma.  A love that grew despite ugliness around it.

cands.text: I was pulled into this dark romantic mystery.  Such a page turner!  I had to know what was the darkness surrounding the main characters.  This story did not disappoint!
I love emotionally and psychologically charged books.  This book has a raw darkness mixed with a sensual sweetness.  A great dark romance.
I love emotionally and psychologically charged books.  This book has a raw darkness mixed with a sensual sweetness.  A great dark romance.
A satisfying story of love through harsh circumstances. On the edge feelings throughout this book! A perfect ending!  I would love a story on the blind girl in cage!
An intense journey into a depraved, dark, and all consuming sort of possession.  Pain and pleasure seep into the storyline.  Exquisite!
Loved the characters so vulnerable and crazy.  Felt a variety of emotions swirling in a delicate balance of right and wrong.  A journey worth discovering in a excellent book!
Sadist and masochist in love.  This book embraced and tormented the uniqueness of such an intense way to love.  Just amazed and loved this book.
There were moments while reading this book I found myself getting emotional.  The feelings the author conveyed in this story were similar to ones in my own life.  A wonderful story.
A lot of angry hate love in this book! And a lot of drama and betrayal!  No nonsense characters with a lot of edgy deep feelings!
This whole book was all about the buildup of feelings hate and love.  Which is it?  I had to read the whole book to find out which feeling it was for these two characters!
Love the concept of a psychopath finding love unexpectedly.  I really enjoyed the quotes or sayings from some serial killer movies.  An awesome read!
I enjoyed how the story was likened to the beauty and beast plot but it wasn't so glaringly obvious.  One part in this book really had me in tears.  Wonderful!
Loved the characters ands the strong female hero.  Adding mystery and a little bit of darkness really helped the intensity of all the relationships in the book.
A total fantasy of darkness!  So much going on in the grittiness and darkness of the scenes.  And also suspenseful!
Enjoyed how the story developed into a mystery.  Also I appreciate sad characters that turn into happy full filled characters.
The mystery of this story kept me on the edge.  Definitely romantic and so steamy.  Love shifter books! Need more!

I enjoy a book centered around fragile or broken people who learn through another that love is attainable.  The buildup between the lead characters could have been more drawn out but it was still a good story.

I enjoy a heart wrenching and heart breaking tale of loss and love!  And especially when a great love is found through it all.  However the ending in book left me a little disappointed but this book definitely a good read!
Very romantic with the right amount of intrigue and mystery.  I enjoyed the main character. She was the perfect mix of strength and vulnerability.

I was so immersed in this book and it's main character.  The author made her character so vulnerable and lonely.  I had to keep reading so I would know if her character would find clarity!  Amazing book!

My almost 2 year old needs boots for the winter.  These boots fit her good but really difficult to put on with the insert.  It looks like the insert was made for a really narrow foot.  Therefore, these boots get a 4 star.
Enjoyed reading about these two characters fight with themselves about their feelings of love.  Definitely a good book to read!

The gloves were the only nice product out of this package.  The bracelet was the worst.  The construction of it was so flimsy.  The snap to keep bracelet on was just a couple of plastic bumps that would fit into a couple of holes.  Needless to say the bracelet kept falling off.  I definitely would have preferred buying this type of gift at a store instead of online.
I could not put this book down.  I was so hooked on the heroine in this book.  I was rooting for her to have a happy ending. Loved this book.

users.query:
I signed on as a volunteer coach at the National Steinbeck Centers Young Authors Day and learned that the 6-8 graders would be writing about the first chapter of The Red Pony. Yikes, it was time to re-read the short book that I hadnt opened in many years.

Here in the Land of Steinbeck (Monterey, CA), the man is reveredand rightfully so. The Grapes of Wrath and East of Eden are beautiful novels that still move readers, decades after their publication. Cannery Row and Tortilla Flat are whimsical, yet poignant tales from a bygone era of my neighborhood.

As I re-read The Red Pony and thought about todays middle schoolers, I found the story of Jody, the somewhat mischievous 10-year-old farm boy with stern parents, less than riveting. Granted, the themes of death and dying, maturing as a result of difficult experiences, of wanting to please parents and earn their love, are timeless and universal. Steinbeck wrote about them in a simple, yet profound way that continues to make this little book a classic at the middle school level. Nonetheless, I couldn't get past visions of the 31-year-old Steinbeck, not yet a fully formed novelist, scribbling away and honing his skills for the great works to come.

Do I recommend it for middle schoolers? Definitely. Just don't expect Jody Tiflin to grab their interest the way Harry Potter and Katniss Everdeen do.

cands.text:
When a debut novelists work wins the Iowa Short Fiction Award and the New York Times includes the book in its 2014 list of 100 Notable Novels, its worth paying attention. The plot: young, bright and idealistic Laura Freedman has taken a teaching job at a south Texas high school. She struggles with classroom discipline and students whose lives are bleak.

When the story begins, Ms. Freedman has suffered a breakdown and is a resident at Bridges Psychiatric Wellness Solutions in Austin where Wellness Points are earned through strict adherence to the institution's rules and a cheery outlook. This incredibly well-crafted tale is told entirely through email exchanges, student essays, journal entries, short stories and questionable poetry, most in first person, some in second. The pieces are frequently hilarious and almost always dark.

Author Kathleen Founds, who majored in Religious Studies at Stanford, applies her incredible intelligence to deep questions. Her brightest characters often quote or refer toand distortBiblical passages. Some of their writings come off like weird Revelations/Sci Fi parables. Founds does a stellar job of differentiating a rather large cast of characters through their unique voices. The story is so unusual that its hard to know what will happen next. One caveat: this is definitely not a feel-good tale of an inspiring teacher. It does, however, give the reader plenty of literary food for thought on topics like abandonment, the meaning of life and how the actions of others impact an individual.

Ive chatted with Barbara Manning off and on at Central Coast Writers meetings over the last couple of years. My initial impression was of a friendly, attractive and successful older woman from Carmel. When "Anybodys Daughter" came out, I congratulated her, but not being a fan of memoirs, I didn't read it. A couple weeks ago, a local newspaper ran an article about Barbaras work with foster children and the Kinship Center. That got my attention, and I started reading the book, which I found surprisingly well-written and developed.

This is no feel-good story about the life of a well-to-do woman. In fact, Barbaras tale of her horrific childhood reads like a modern day "Oliver Twist." No child should ever have to suffer the poverty, abuse and lack of love she did. While the story is dark, Barbara ends on a triumphant note. For anyone working with foster children, this should be a must-read. For teens in foster situations, it is a story of survival and hope.

You can bet that the next time I see the sweet lady from Carmel, Ill have lots of questions!

I started reading Beyond the Pale on a leisurely Sunday morning and only stopped when I had to be somewhere else. By then I had read 44% and perused all the photos at the end of the book.

In telling the story of his life and the history of Sierra Nevada, Ken Grossman comes across as a very authentic, likeable guy. He admits to being a workaholic whos always searching for ways to improve. His money-saving DIY stories from Sierra Nevadas early days are amazing. Very few craft brewers would be able to build a brewery using tanks from defunct dairies and pumps and pipes from salvage yards.

Grossmans story is an entertaining and educational read for home and craft brewers, craft beer enthusiasts and business people. The book might get a bit technical for someone without some brewing knowledge, but Grossman does a great job of weaving in succinct explanations.

Hollywood: this beer story has all the ingredients for a terrific movie!

The Whitmans of Things Unsaid certainly aren't the Cleavers of Leave It to Beaver. While each character has flaws, the one they all share is overspending. This, of course, leads to a lot of other problems for the parents who live in an upscale retirement home and their 3 adult children with families of their own.

Before you read the first page, you know that the health of the aging parents will continue to decline and that there will be lots of retelling of the past from different characters points of view. As the personalities of the characters and the family dynamics are revealed, the story gets pretty dark at points. What kept me reading was the well-developed plot and wanting to see where it would go. The writing is good, and the way author Diana Paul doles out bits of the characters lives and personalities to create some very complex individuals is perhaps the strongest aspect of the novel.

The book will probably appeal most to Pauls fellow Baby Boomers. Most are dealing, or have dealt, with the needs of aging parents and juggling those with job demands and responsibility to their own spouses and children.

Years from now when I look back on "Mary Coin," undoubtedly, what I will most remember is how much I loved reading it. Up until the last pages, I still wasn't sure exactly how different threads of the story would turn out.

Mary is the protagonist in this eponymous novel, but her story is interwoven with those of Vera Dare, the photographer who, in the 1930's, took Mary's photo and made them both recognizable and that of present-day college professor Walker Dodge who slowly pieces together Mary's life and its unexpected relation to his own. The tale is full of complex relationships and twists and turns as the plot develops primarily in the central California migrant farm camps during the Great Depression. All three characters are, at the core, good people who love their families and struggle with hard choices that they hope will ultimately turn out to be the best ones for their children. Like thousands of real-life Oakies, Mary is dealt a horrible hand of injustices and difficulties. Through it all, her unwavering goal is to ensure survival for her large brood and herself. Her strength even in the most desperate moments is a celebration of the beauty and goodness of the human spirit at its best.

A huge thank-you to Marisa Silver for a terrific, satisfying read!

Just as the cover of Goodnight Brew promises, its a parody for beer people. As such, its a clever and cute take off on Goodnight Moon that will cause anyone with a little brewing knowledge to laugh. The drawings are colorful and appealing. I especially liked the whirling wort hog. Since the book has only been out a couple of months, I encourage author Karla Oceanak and illustrator Alli Ogg to work out a few glitches in the electronic version. One example is the very nice drawing under Goodnight beer lovers everywhere. The illustration explains the beer-making process in a simple, accurate way, but making it large enough to read on an iPad results in fuzzy resolution and the drawing has to be viewed in segments. On the Beer Types & Styles page, the columns run over onto the next page, but reformatting for digital devices is easy enough.

What impresses me most is that I see this little book as a reflection of how far the brewing culture in the United States has evolved. Thirty years ago, very few people would have understood Goodnight Brew. With so many types of brewers today, theres a whole niche of potential readersmany with young children who see Dad or Mom with buckets and malted barley, etc. Kudos to Oceanak and Ogg!

Travels with Barley is a generally entertaining read for aficionados of American beer culture. After author Ken Wells many years as a journalist, the writing is very good, arguably the strongest aspect of the book. Wells emphasizes his middle-class, somewhat blue-collar upbringing, offsetting it with references to his extensive education. (Example: Travels with Barley/Charley)

He alternates between charting his adventures in search of the perfect beer joint and relating stories of Americas beer history. At times, I found the narration a bit too long and meandering. (Example: After reading about the Flora-Bama in the first chapter, I didn't pick up the book for a couple of months.)

A second shortcoming is inevitable with a book of this type: released in 2004, its become outdated. Early on Wells writes that Americans in 2002 (the latest statistics available) consumed 6.35 billion gallons of beer. A few pages later, he says craft brewers have 3.4 percent of the beer market. According to the Brewers Association's latest stats, by 2013, that number grew to 7.8 percent and continues at a vibrant pace. These days, its not unusual for even a modest-sized craft brewery to produce an extremely hopped IPA, a sour beer, a cider and a lager or two in addition to the mandatory ales. As a result, todays craft beer enthusiasts are more educated and sophisticated than those of a dozen years ago, and the beer scene has evolved, contributing to the dated feel of the book.

Giving "Travels with Barley" a break for the passage of time, it still provides some good historical perspective and interesting anecdotes.

Erudite, accomplished and a successful writer capable of penning this complex novel full of beautiful writing, 88-year-old William Gass is a man to admire.  In an age when traditional publishing houses and Hollywood are often interested only in reliable blockbusters, this "Middle C," is a note rarely heard.  It makes for unusual reading in that it breaks so many of the bestseller rules.  The novel is long, the story winding and the tangents numerous.  At times, it's hard to know where Gass or protagonist Yussel-Joey-Joseph-Professor Skizzen and the unconventional punctuation are headed with their riffs.  The third chapter is ten pages of Skizzen's obsession with writing a single sentence correctly--an obsession that goes on until the next-to-last page of the novel.

The writing is often dense which, for me, definitely detracted from the pleasure of reading, but Gass is so knowledgeable and intellectual that he kept me going.  His humor ("At first Joey appreciated her apparently genuine vulgarity in such a crowd of stodges."), his odd characters (the unforgettable Miss Spiky who Skizzen and I couldn't help but like) and an unusual story with plenty of deep thoughts to ponder carried me through to the end.  I don't expect to see "Middle C" at the top of "The New York Times" Best Sellers list, but a big bravo to Gass and Knopf for publishing it.

A novel about a mother and daughter who run a B&B in a summer resort town that comes out in June and has "summer" in the title. Could "The Summer Everything Changed" be anything but a classic beach read?

The somewhat dark plot isn't particularly complex or surprising. The writing isn't majestic (as compared to, say, Barbara Kingsolver, Cormac McCarthy, Mohsin Hamid). At the same time, the characters seem believable and likeable enough that I kept reading. In short, it's the kind of book that would do a good job of helping pass the time on a long flight.

Where Holly Chamberlin deserves accolades is in creating a strong story of teenage domestic abuse. I highly recommend the book to women of all ages who may be suffering from domestic abuse/ violence. Chamberlin portrays strong, intelligent women who, in spite of their strengths still fall prey to abusers.  In the end, she leaves readers with a positive and hopeful message.

Shortly after the widowed Esperanza is told her only child has died in surgery, Saint Judas Tadeo appears as a reflection in her dirty oven window and tells her that twelve-year-old Blanca is still alive and Esperanza must find her. Neither her best friend nor the village priest will believe her story. Since Esperanza never actually saw Blancas body, this Mexican mother is determined to find her daughter at all costs. Convinced that the doctor, who has disappeared, sold Blanca into prostitution, Esperanza is soon exploring seamy brothels and meeting shady characters, with plenty of surprises.

Esperanzas well-written and often funny story is one Gabriel Garca Mrquez would have laughed his way through. Heck, it sounds like something Gabo would have written himself. Likewise, there are echoes of Isabel Allende.  The most surprising thing about Esperanzas Box of Saints is that Mara Amparo Escandn wrote it in English.
