The influence of magical realism, characters like Angel the lucha libre wrestler, the dishes Esperanza cooks are all well-known in Mexico. Esperanzas style of reasoning and expressing herself makes her authentic, genuine and endearing. Like millions of Mexicans, Esperanza has a deep faith in her santitos and the Catholic Church. At the same time, this humble but attractive woman never questions that, given the reason, her saints and God can justify her hanging around prostitutes and pimps.

Like Allende in The House of the Spirits, Escandn gives her characters symbolic namesEsperanza (Hope), Soledad (Loneliness), Blanca (White, as in pure) and Angel, the hero wrestler. Personally, I didn't see the need to make Father Salvador (Savior), and thereby the Catholic Church, so weak.

Overall, a different kind of story that keeps the readers interest.

Ive long enjoyed Jeff Alworths writings on his Beervana blog, in All About Beer magazine and elsewhere. While I eagerly anticipated publication of The Beer Bible, its even more impressive than Id imagined.

I recommend the print version; youll most likely want to mark up this reference book and dog-ear pages. Ive spent quite a few hours over the last month reading it off and on and digesting the encyclopedic information. Before I finished Part One, Knowing Beer, I skipped to Beer Tourism in Part Six. Jumping around work fine, perhaps even better than trying to read straight through this 644-page tome.

Alworth arranges the beer descriptions by styleales, wheat beers, lagers, tart and wild ales. His history of each style gives the reader a grounded perspective of how the style came to its current version. He suggests 5-8 specific beers to try in a style, listing information and mentioning the strongest points of each. With some styles, Ive read right through. For others, Ive had fun reading portions and sharing information with my husband about the particular beer were drinking.

A beer bible could easily become a rote and boring list of information, but Alworth is too good of a writer to fall into that trap. The book is chock full of photos and side bars with interesting tidbits of information. I don't know of any other book on beer that is so current, comprehensive and well written.

If you enjoy reading about the early days of Americas craft beer movement, I highly recommend Bend Beer: A History of Brewing in Central Oregon. The book delivers exactly what the title promises, beginning with Oregons Wild West days and ending in 2014. As a long-time beer blogger (thebrewsite.com) based in Bend, author Jon Abernathy knows his topic well. In this, his first book, he pulls together a great deal of research and many interviews to develop a clear narrative with writing that stays lively and interesting. Numerous photos add to the books appeal.

Perhaps the strongest aspect of Bend Beer is how well Abernathy explains the impact and consequences of events that have shaped U.S. and Oregon brewing history. One example Id never considered: the role the 16th Amendment (1913, establishing a federal income tax) in opening the way for the 18th Amendment (1920, national Prohibition). Before 1913, the federal government had been much more dependent on liquor taxes for revenue.

The section of the book I most enjoyed was roughly the third quarter which begins with the early days of Bends craft beer scene. The pace builds as Abernathy chronicles the early struggles of Bends first two craft breweries, Deschutes and Bend Brewing, and continues with the next half dozen or so that followed. (The list of Central Oregon breweries on Abernathys website currently stands at 27)

Mr. Abernathy, go open a good craft brew and celebrate a job well done!

Author Jonathan Hennessey and illustrator Aaron McConnell have teamed up again to create their third non-fiction graphic novel, and this time, they pulled in professional brewer Mike Smith. Their pooled knowledge and experience are apparent on every page of The Comic Book Story of Beer. Historian Maureen Ogle (Ambitious Brew: The Story of American Beer) might find some details or perspectives to quibble with, but I didnt. Hennessey and Smith have written a seamless and easy to follow history of beer over the millennia. McConnells illustrations are clever, rich and detailed. One example: the female brewer on page 39 in her pink boots. (For non-brewers, thats a shout-out to the Pink Boots Society.) To my knowledge, there's no other published book like it.

An ideal Christmas or birthday gift for homebrewers, beer lovers and comic book fans!

"I simply wanted to write the biggest story I could in the most concise way possible." So says Paul Yoon in the Reading Group Guide that follows "Snow Hunters." Boy, did he accomplish what he set out to do.

In sparse prose that becomes so lyrical at times that it seems almost poetic, he tells the story of Yohan, a Korean POW of the Japanese during the Korean War who is later turned over to an American relocation camp. With no family, friends or home to return to, he relocates to Brazil and works as an apprentice with a Japanese tailor.

There, Yohan wakes up screaming from nightmares. He retreats physically, emotionally and psychologically from situations and people. He goes through days which become years of working and not feeling much of anything, in other words, suffering from PTSD and depression. Ultimately, this is the story of a human being who has been through great horrors and how he finally begins to find love and hope.

Like "The Old Man and the Sea," it is a short, superbly written novel about a humble, solitary man in a great struggle. Yoon's way of stating profound ideas in simple, succinct language from his character's view of the world is reminiscent of Steinbeck.  This novel has so much going for it.

There are, however, two areas where it weakens for me. The plot progress slows at times due to pace of the action and of Yohan's growth/change. Second, Yohan's lack of emotions keeps everyone, including me, at arm's length. In the category of making-the-reader-care-about-the-protagonist, I give the book 3 stars.

Overall, this is a phenomenal debut novel from an exciting, young writer with the literary potential to one day join the ranks of Steinbeck and Hemingway.

"The Time Between" was one of those are novels I read until it was so late I couldn't keep my eyes open. Then I got up the next morning and kept reading until I finished it.

Author Karen White gradually develops a complex plot and fleshes out her endearing characters as she delves deeper into their minds, their actions and the pasts that have molded them. I happily followed protagonist Eleanor as she worked through painful memories and guilt. Like her, I slowly warmed up to her boss, Finn, as we got to know him outside the office. The impervious and crusty 90-year-old Helena has her charming moments. And even the Grinch would have to root for loveable little Gigi.

Eleanor has spent years trying to atone for what she believes is her role in the accident that left her sister in a wheelchair. In addition, she has never properly grieved her father's death, and she has misinterpreted her mother's feelings and thoughts about her. When her boss in Charleston asks her to keep his elderly aunt on Edisto Island company for a few hours on weekends, it's Eleanor's chance to escape the house where she lives with her mother, her newly pregnant sister and the sister's husband for whom Eleanor has feelings. When she walked through the door of the old house on the island where she grew up, she opens a door to many changes in her life and the lives of those around her.

My advice: Toward the end when Helena demands that Eleanor play Chopin's Nocturne in C Minor, go to YouTube and listen/watch Valentina Igoshina play it as you read.

From the start of "This Town," Mark Leibovich demonstrates his considerable writing skills and his insider's knowledge of Washington. The tales he tells so well confirm his nod to local literary tradition which at times compares D.C. to a high school. I'm betting that at this moment there are plenty of folks in D.C. devouring the book which came out today. ("What did he say about me?  What did he say about my friends and the people I'm not friends with?")

The thing is Leibovich does it in such snappy, funny writing that he keeps you reading. He throws out phrases like "peacocking policitians," "garaged yard signs" and "pundit catnip." He breezily refers to insiders by nicknames like "the Tamster," "the Macker" and "the Money Honey." My favorite was that shortly before Romney became the 2012 Republican candidate, voters realized "that they were on the verge of nominating Thurston Howell III."

While Leibovich drops plenty of names, his book isn't just a 400-page version of a tabloid magazine. He has covered his beat (Washington) well and for a long time. No doubt some readers will be disheartened at the cynical and out-for-me attitude of most of the individuals Leibovich describes. Honestly, though, didn't we all pretty much know that already? Others will probably be disappointed that he didn't dish more dirty. But did you really expect the man to go there if he wants to keep his job and his connections?

The book is the solid, well-written result of years of experience. After a while though, it became one more story piled on top of another about smart people with tremendous abilities who almost always succumb to the narcissistic culture of Washington. Leibovich is too smart to offer any suggestions of how we can change it.

In Im Off Then, Hape Kerkeling excels in describing the pilgrim experience on the Camino de Santiago. I read the book after I walked the Camino in May and June of this year. It brought back a plethora of memoriesof a too heavy backpack, constantly aching feet, multiple rainy days of plodding through clay mud with boots that felt weighted with lead. And like Kerkeling, I eventually made two close friendships. We became inseparable, watching out for each other, sleeping in the same albergues, helping one another through the challenging timesand triumphantly walking together into the giant plaza in Santiago de Compostela. In August, 2015, the three of us plan to hike the Swiss Alps.

There were moments when the pace of the book slowed, but that represents the reality of the pilgrimage for many people. Kerkeling didn't have any life-changing spiritual epiphanies, and I dare say, many (perhaps most?) pilgrims today do not. He did have time to think deeply about some timeless topics (the meaning of Life and his own life, is there an afterlife, how he viewed God, etc.) and to journal about his experiences and thoughts. Again, typical of Camino pilgrims. He writes well, although I suspect some of his wit and charm were obscured in translation. I appreciated that Kerkeling came across as more than a celebrity. He opened up and expressed his shortcomings (examples: nonathletic couch potato, impatient with loud, opinionated people).

The biggest caveat I would give a reader considering the Camino is that it has been thirteen years since Kerkeling made his pilgrimage. While much is unchanged, the number of pilgrims has more or less doubled. There are many more albergues and other accommodations and places to eat and buy food. A common remark I heard from repeat pilgrims was that even a few years ago, it was rare to find wi-fi on the Camino. Not anymore.

If you're considering the Camino, I highly recommend reading Im Off Then before you take off.

Ambitious Brew: The Story of American Beer is an ambitious title. No surprise that the book is a hefty 452 pages. The good news is that historian Maureen Ogle achieves her lofty goal and then some in this thoroughly researched and well-organized book. She weaves together the tales of all the major players throughout the history of American beerthe numerous Busches, Millers, Pabsts, Uihleins and many more. The result is a highly engaging book for anyone interested in the topic.

Among all the books on the market today, theres not a more definitive history of beer in the United States. Thats even more laudable considering that Ambitious Brew was published in 2007. The fact that its nearly eight years old is the only bad thing about the book.

Wouldnt it be cool if Ms. Ogle put out a 10th anniversary edition with her take on developments in the U.S. beer sceneparticularly the rapid growth of the craft beer movementover the last decade?

When I decided to walk the Camino, one of the first bits of advice I got from two veterans pilgrims, who didn't know each other, was, "Get yourself a copy of Brierley now."

I'm finally leaving tomorrow! I was going to hold off on writing a review until after I came back, but I've been reading and referring back to "Brierley" for the last three months and can't imagine preparing without the book. My copy is already marked up and dog-eared. I've photocopied the map on the back inside cover and the 33 Stage Summary on page 43 for family and friends.

The only possibly negative thing I've heard about the book came from a pilgrim who walked the Camino last fall. She and her husband said it was indispensable but that so many people carried Brierley that those towns and villages he suggested for spending the night were often heavily crowded in the evenings.

As a Spanish teacher, I recommend Brierley's bilingual checklist and basic phrases for anyone who isn't fluent in the language. I like his attention to outer and inner preparation. His invites the reader to introspective/spiritual reflection in a general way that almost anyone can be open to.

I expect my "Brierley" is going to come home in six weeks considerably worn.

Decir que El murmullo de las abejas me recuerda de Cien aos de Soledad, y La casa de los espritus es colocar la novela en muy distinguida compaa. Y la merece. Las tres novelas relatan grandes historias de varias generaciones de familias y el impacto de verdaderos sucesos histricos en las vidas de los personajes y en sus pueblos. Sin embargo, la mayor comparacin viene siendo el uso del realismo mgico.

En el hermoso lenguaje de la autora Sofa Segovia, cmo no vamos a sentir compasin por un beb, y luego nio, fsicamente diferente a los dems y raro por la manta de abejas que lo acobija? A travs de los eventos y el punto de vista de varios narradores, nos damos cuenta de que lo bello de Simonopio lo trae por dentro. Como la nia Clara, en La casa de los espritus, Simonopio cree muy naturales sus poderes. Como a Clara, frecuentemente, el presente le importa menos que a los dems. Ultimadamente, los dos son nobles ejemplos del amor por sus familias (en el caso de Simonopio, una no biolgica).

La compleja trama y las mltiples historias entretejidas de Abejas me captivaron desde el principio, pero es el ltimo cuarto del libro donde Segovia brilla con una sorpresa tras otra, y tensin cada vez mayor. En el estilo de Stephen King, temprano deja claro quines son el protagonista y antagonista y que los dos van inexorablemente en camino a una pica batalla. Quin ganar y cmo cambiar la vida de todos los personajes? Como en la vida real, las respuestas son imposibles de predeciraun para Simonopio.

There's no doubt Wil Haygood is an experienced journalist and writer who can craft a fine story. He certainly does so in telling the story of Eugene Allen, the exceptional man who served as a White House butler for thirty-four years under eight presidents. In the first section of the book (Allen's story), I was cheering on both Allen and Haygood. The final section of photos showing Allen with family members and dignitaries adds to the appeal of the book. Reading about the years of work to get "The Butler" filmed got me pumped to see movie when it's released in a few weeks.

There were a couple of things about the book that I didn't care for so much. First, it seemed like a long PR roll-out for the movie. Second, it's a good review of the history, roles and successes of African-Americans in the last sixty or so years, but the sections seemed cobbled together to make this 112-page book. The first part is Allen's story. The second part is the movie's story. The third has one-and-a-half-page summaries of the five presidents Allen's fictional version serves in the movie. I can only guess that this part is meant as a primer for movie-goers to read beforehand.

Overall, "The Butler: A Witness to History," is an educational and inspirational read on a subject that we Americans--regardless of color--frequently don't handle well.

Sisters Eleanor and Maddy return for another Pizza Lovers Mystery, this time trying to find the murderer of Maddys troublesome and troubled ex-husband. Theres no shortage of suspects, including Maddys current fianc and even the sisters themselves. Between running their pizzeria and their marginally legal investigation, these good-hearted women stay very busy over the several days during which the story takes place.

The pace of this action-driven whodunit clips along nicely, due in part to the extensive use of dialogue and a nicely developed plot. Author Chris Cavender does a good job of providing quick doses of necessary backstory from previous books for first-time readers. Its an easy and entertaining readideal for a long plane ride or a cold winter day inside.

Protagonist John Cuddy has recently lost his wife and his job with an insurance company. Makes sense to become a private investigator, right? Actually, in Cuddys case, he has some good background for the job, having served in Vietnam during the war and in the military police. He had worked his way up to head of the claims division for the insurance company before being pushed out because he refused to take part in something unethical. When a female teacher acquaintance calls regarding a highly intelligent student who has disappeared, Cuddy is off to investigate. His quest to find the 14-year-old immediately launches Cuddy into intrigue, danger and romance.

The results are an entertaining read. Healy does a great job of steadily deepening the mystery and developing a complex web of backstories for his characters. In turn, the readers perception of the characters and the who-done-it continues to morph. Healy kept me guessing until the very end as to who would ultimately be revealed as the guiltiest partythrough Cuddys hard work and exceptional detective skills, of course.

Originally published in 1984, the book does have a somewhat dated feel at times, but strong storytelling and a good-guy protagonist who the reader wants to root for never go out of style.

In Titan Falls, a small New England community, residents are distrustful of outsiders. Even with money, power and twenty years of marriage to the owner of the paper mill, non-native June McAllister knows shes still not fully accepted. When the latest generation of Snows shows up in a ratty RV to live on the land of their estranged and deceased father, townspeople aren't happy.

One night, a reckless driver causes a fatal accident. Just down the road, Zeke Snows old truck is crashed into a tree, and Zeke is nowhere to be found. What appears to be a clear crime becomes much, much more complicated, and past secrets abound.

Tiffany Baker is a talented writer who spins a complex plot as she gradually reveals the layered lives of characters who all have their share of imperfections and sins. She turns out beautifully crafted sentences that give larger meaning to simple actions. One example: silence fell over the room as the women took their needles, bent their heads, and began to stitch, their needles pricking, prying, and then just as quickly closing the little holes they were making in the fabric of one anothers lives.

As I read, I wavered on the rating to give "Mercy Snow." The mystical aspects of the story reminded me of Latin American magical realism, but at times it got a little too out there for me. I anticipated some plot developments, although there were some good surprises. Finally, I couldn't buy the ending for one character. But ultimately, I went with five stars because there is so much that I liked about the book, and when I finished the last page, I knew this was a novel that I won't forget for a long time.

Made in USA and uses natural food-grade mineral oil and beeswax to condition and protect the wood surfaces in our kitchen. We recently refurbished a wood kitchen rolling cart with chopping block surface and used this product to condition and seal the work surface. The wood readily soaked it up and there was a nice smooth feel to the top. I let it soak in and gave it one more coat for good measure. Don't put synthetic or potentially toxic chemicals on surfaces that come near food -- This is a wonderful wood block conditioner and protectant for surfaces that come in contact with food.

This toys is so cool - the engineering is incredible! It is colorful, durable, and strong. It has ample storage in the 'appliances' behind each door. The doors secure closed nicely. The features are shaped well for small hands to manage well. The burner has a volume control that allows a low or high volume to hear sizzling, bubbling, and timer sounds. The faucet is a nice silver color and the yellow handles turn in 'settings' so they don't spin wildly like some cheaper kitchens do. I like the babydoll high chair incorporated into the countertop. The shelf provides additional storage to keep the pots and phone. The greatest feature is that while this has two levels, the bottom/second level stores completely inside the top level! The front panel of the bottom (refrigerator and dishwasher) fold down flat in the collapsed position but come forward to make the front facing of the bottom unit. The storage between the top level and bottom level are separated, so your child can bake cookies without them falling to the bottom of the unit into the dishwasher. It seems every detail was captured - from all the accessories that include foods like triangle cheese, circular dessert, and square milk carton that the child can learn shapes fitting them into the openings of the skillet lid to the colors and imaginary play. If there is one shortcoming it is that there are not two sets of dinnerware -- the kitchen only comes with one plate and one knife/fork/spoon and tumbler for play meals alone.

Just used this machine for my Halloween cemetery in my front yard. I had chained ghosts with gauze garments I got from Party City for $15 each hanging from the tree over head strung up with fishing line. I had purchased nice, moulded grave markers from Target for about $20 each. Mixed those with the 3/$12 foam ones (from HalloweenSpirit dot com) to make the look go farther without going broke. This fog machine made a fantastic low lying fog covering the entire cemetary and a few feet into my yard effectively and as promised. The machine can only hold about 2 cups of ice (tops) and the machine warms up fast (about a 5 minute wait before fog is generated) -- the fog generated is a good, dense cover and about the time you want it to sustain that, the ice cubes have melted and the fog becomes a billowy, thick cloud that rises and spreads, hiding the props it was supposed to accent. The machine cycles a cool-down cycle for a few minutes about every 10 minutes to avoid overheating.

It was about 80 degrees the Halloween evening we used it. We were having our last bout of warm weather (Indian summer) this fall and the ice needed to be replaced about every 20 minutes. We made sure to use the recommended Chauvet low lying fog fluid -- not all fluids are effective for low-lying fog (I read the cheaper ones are watered down and it's chancey whether you'll get a good fog per reviews). Next year, I will make 4-6 square blocks of ice to fit in the ice container of the fog machine and will hope those will last longer than the chips. My other idea is to see if I can use dry ice in the ice compartment but I'll have to research it first to make sure it won't ruin it.

I'm pleased with the amount of fog that this machine kicked out and the effect it gave when working optimally. It easily covered an area of about 20 x 20' and the wind was not gusty (under 5mph). At 5mph-7mph winds, the fog kicks about and doesn't stay put as well.

The remote that came with is a wired remote (must be connected to the back of machine) and only allows you to basically stand upright next to the machine and hold it in your hand (not very remote if you can't control from a distance). We bought a quart of low-lying fog fluid and using the machine non-stop from 6-9 pm, it used just about a half quart of fluid. I like the effect the fog machine provided - folks loved all our props and kids were wanting to investigate the spooky cemetery!

I put reading books a folding kiddy chair that unfolds into a bed (also sold on Amazon) and my grands make a beeline to play with this thing. I love that it is portable, collapses flat when not in use and is so easy to reassemble on their next visit. smallish but good for my 18mos old grandbaby. Using it as a nap pad and tv chair when she visits since she is outgrowing the crib. cloth coverlet is not removable and shifts around on the foam a bit but this will do nicely for our needs.
Purchased 3. All are equally sturdy, evenly colored. These fit the stem of and matched my existing Anderson handles for my 1996 windows and are functioning perfectly.
I like the LED but the soft white was too yellow and dim for the space I needed. I reverted to the daylight and am very satisfied with the light and energy efficiency.
Super durable and helps keep pool cleaning a minimal process by not kicking the stuff around while vacuuming. Nice coverage and size. Glad to find online when the local shop was out.

users.query: I really enjoyed learning about Emily. I'm really curious to know if she is a real child of Destiny or a victim of circumstances but I'm glad she got to leave home because she was being neglected. I'm also glad she made friends with the princess. I think Emily's modern ideas may get her in trouble. I also enjoyed the ending.

cands.text: i really like emily. the story was very interesting and fast paced. i don't think its like sex and the city. which was a good thing. nobody was hopping into bed with a whole lot of people. the end was surprising and not predictable.

I liked getting to see Alassa's kingdom and family. The rebellion was a very nice twist so was the leader. I never suspected who it was. I think Emily learned more about life outside the school and it was interesting to watch her powers develop.
I enjoyed it. I wasn't sure if I would enjoy especially since its the 2nd arc or whatever. Its in keeping with the rest of the series. Emily still a little naive.

I really liked this one and i enjoy this series. The end had an interesting twist even though I kinda saw it coming. I do what to know how Ali pulled it off this time especially with Jordan. I think Emily is getting a tad obsessed and I wish her family was more supportive.
The spin on  the Romeo and Juliet feud  was nice. Got to see more of Emily outside of magic school. Had all my favorite characters from the other books.

i like this series. this was a good sequel. Emily and Colin's relationship is kinda more serious. This small town is beginning to have a high crime rate. You learn more about Ethan's past but still not who killed him. im looking forward to reading the next book.
Im glad its not the end. It was very suspenseful and I couldn't wait to read what happened next. Im sorry Ellie is an orphan now but a lot of the mysteries from the first two books were solved.

good ending to the series. i wish she'd write another.

The ending was good. It was kind of long and drawn out with all the high school relationship drama even though it took three books. I'm glad that's resolved. i put it down multiple times.

I like that Lisa is becoming a more important character. There were a murders in this book than the first one. i really enjoy reading about the cookie side of the business to even though I don't bake.

users.query:
The touchpad clickers are weak and appear to be failing already.  Otherwise this device works as advertised.  The device works in many modes--laptop like, tablet like, and as a stand for viewing.  All modes work well.  Having the keyboard be the base in tablet mode is strange, but it works.

Boot up is quick and performance is good.  Windows 8 touch is surprisingly cool.

cands.text: Very nice.  I have an old ASUS Zenbook that is similar in design and have loved it for almost two years.  I bought this one for someone else and it appears to be even better.  Good display, keyboard and case.  The touchpad is something that I think requires some configuration.  I have turned off many of the smart gesture capabilities and that make the touchpad more friendly to me.

Very nice.  I have an old ASUS Zenbook that is similar in design and have loved it for almost two years.  I bought this one for someone else and it appears to be even better.  Good display, keyboard and case.  The touchpad is something that I think requires some configuration.  I have turned off many of the smart gesture capabilities and that make the touchpad more friendly to me.
So far so good.  Works as it should.  Everything that I have connected works as it should--mouse, webcam, keyboard, and ethernet.

Nice computer with moderate CPU power but nice battery life.  Lightweight with good screen and touchpad.  No backlit keyboard is surprising but not a problem for me.  I did have some problems with the initial install.  ASUS tech support was simply awful--this should come as no surprise to anyone who has used ASUS tech support.  I had to reinstall.  I believe that the problem was due to a software install that I did not reinstall.  So far everything now works great.  The keyboard does bend a bit in the middle but it doesn't impact anything.  The connectors are not included in this model, unlike my previous ASUS laptop.  You will need either a USB-C connector or USB connector to connect to ethernet (wired) or a VGA monitor.  I had the ethernet one sitting around and it works fine.  Bought a USB-C to USB adapter to give me more ports when I am at home.  USB to VGA has been touchy.
This is my second one.  This one works great.  The other actually ate one stopped working.  The one that works has no problem using high performance discs as well as my mouse and keyboard.

Can't believe that I actually bought a mouse pad.  I was having trouble with my optical mouse on my desk.  My desk is kind of uni-colored so I think it was sub-optimal.  So even though it is embarrassing, my mouse work much better.

These are great keyboards.  If you like chiclet style keyboards, these are great. I have two at my home office and one at my office.  They need very little light to stay powered.  I have no issues with the keyboard.  The mouse is very nice as well.  It is bigger than some, but it has a great feel and unlike some logitech mice, the scroll wheel is not overly sensitive.  Highly recommended

PROS:  Thin, light.  Excellent screen.  Keyboard is good.  Speed is more than ample for large spreadsheets.  Battery life seems good.
CONS:  Touchpad is difficult to master.  I know that I can change the settings to make it easier to use.  I have done this for others with the same ASUS touchpad.  I will get to it.

You need adapters for wired LAN, VGA, and HDMI.  The LAN and VGA adapters are included.  I bought a HDMI cable that has a micro HDMI connector.  Don't buy an adapter if you plan to use the VGA adapter as well.  The HDMI adapter will block the VGA slot.  I bought an extra set of adapters for travel (not very expensive).  The need for adapters is common with ultrabooks and MacBook Air laptops.

I use this laptop as my primary desktop with two external monitors--one via VGA and one via HDMI.  Works great.  I can't speak to reliability since I have only had this a short time, but I have purchased a few of these at my workplace and have found them to be reliable.

This model has the I7 processor and 256GB solid state drive.  You can save considerably if you need less disk space and a slightly slower I5 processor.  I do a lot of database work and wanted the speed and drive capacity.

UPDATE: Year a half later and it goes down as the best laptop that I have ever owned--and I have owned many.  Very happy.
Does the job.  Just wanted an extra mouse at the office when I bring in my laptop.  This guy is just fine.

I love these.  They mostly work.  I had a previous model and part of the screen went bad.  Also, it stopped reading the remote sensor after a couple of year.  I still thought it was worth having another one.
I have been using this on my USB 3.0 laptop for a month or so.  It works without incident.  Very happy so far.

Does the job.  Very light--could bother some.  I use it for travel only so the big issue was battery life.  That seems very good.  It has on on/off switch which I like since I don't use it for long periods.  The USB connector fits snugly in the mouse--also good.  It is very light so it feels a bit different and yes a bit cheap.  Wheel works great for scrolling with a nice click feel so things do go crazy when scrolling.  It is also fairly flat so it is easy to travel with.
Very precise mouse pad.  Had to slow down my mouse.  Slips a bit on my table top which is why I gave it 4 stars.
Very precise mouse pad.  Had to slow down my mouse.  Slips a bit on my table top which is why I gave it 4 stars.
Very precise mouse pad.  Had to slow down my mouse.  Slips a bit on my table top which is why I gave it 4 stars.

This is a nice laptop.  Has reasonable power and battery life and had no problems.  I did have to remove a lot of junk software, but these days that seems par for the course.

Amazon shipped this product quickly.

I have owned this monitor for about a month.  It works fine.  It was easy to setup except that in order to get a reasonable picture I had to manually adjust the settings--not a big deal but it took some time to get it right.  The picture is adequate.  I have used it on gaming machines, DVDs, and HD TV.  It is not even close to my Samsung Touch of Color TV, but it was not in the same price league.  The sound is better than I expected and certainly adequate for a smaller room.

I got it for my "napping room", so I watch and sort of sleep.  For that purpose it does the job.  If you are looking for much more than adequate for a small room, you might want to look elsewhere.

If it holds up, I'll be happy.
An OK phone.  Battery life is a bit less than my iPhone 7.  Fingerprint wake up is a bit inconsistent.  Screen and camera are good.  Not external memory makes it less than ideal.

So far so good.  I have had a lot of failures with Roku devices.  I have three running over the last few years with two failures.  I bought the stick because it was cheaper and I would be less upset when it failed.  I like the Roku interface better than the Amazon stick.  But I can say that the Amazon stick works fine and I have not had a failure.

A good reliable mouse for travel.  To store the usb connector you need to pop open the flat black piece on the top of the mouse.  Easy to do, but not as easy as the ones that just go in the bottom.  It is lightweight which could bother some.  Doesn't bother me.  Feels well made.  Battery has been fine so far, but haven't had it long enough to know the true battery life.  It is very flat, so easy to store in a pocket in my small laptop bag.

Not perfect.  The keyboard is just wide enough for keyboard and mouse.  It does not pull out as far as I would like.  I had a hard time installing the keyboard tray because the screws need to go into metal and they didn't fit well.  I finally found another screw to replace the one that would never fit, but it should not have been that difficult.  The desk itself is fine.

Works fine.  Transfers are fast enough for a travel drive.  I use it to watch and listen to saved mp4s and mp3s.  Works fine for that.  It is a bit bigger  and heavier than other portables, but not that bad.

It fits my laptop and installation was very easy.  The battery appears to be well made.  It takes a full charge without any issues.  Unfortunately, I can't say that I am getting longer battery life.  Don't know if it is this battery or simply that my old battery was still functioning well.  I am not getting the same battery life that I used to get.  My Asus laptop is now getting older but I still like it a lot and didn't want to spend the time and money for a new one.
Very good replacement for the not longer sold Trader Joe's version.  Not quite as strong but this will become my regular decaffeinated tea.

users.query: This was a great read! It may have been fiction but trusting men and love can effect how a person feels by the actions of a parent or parents. This was a good read plus it will may you think long and hard about what influenced your feelings about men, love and trust.

cands.text: I agree with everything that Denise said in her comments on this book. This story is not your usual love story yet it needed to be told. Men do go through a lot of drama as women when it comes to affairs of the heart. We just didn't realize it until this book came out. It is a great read and will stir up alot of emotional baggage carried by both men and women but from a male perspective. Thanks WF for this great story and I am looking forward to the sequel.

This is an awesome and very powerful novel. If you have ever wondered how a child feels when a Mother puts a man or men before them and how abandoned a child feels when she doesn't have her Dad in her life, this is a perfect example. I felt everything that this young lady felt because this author wrote it from the heart with no shortcuts. This book was real and you will not be able to put it down until you finish it! I too hope that there is a sequel but he really doesn't have to because at the end of this book you can tell she is really just beginning to understand that 'My Life Is All I Have'. Great title for an even greater story.

This story was amazing. It had it all from jealousy, spousal abuse, drama, love and a lot of misunderstandings. I could not put this book down until I finished it today. It reminded me of the old saying that you can't judge a book (or in this case a person) by it's cover. Great story!

Great book Lee! It will open your eyes about abusive relationships and how they can and did happen to a male instead of a female in this heart wrenching story. This is a very emotional read and should be read by all! Can't hardly wait for your next book!

This book may have been fiction but I know personally women who have  experienced the situations in this book. This is a great read from the beginning to the end and I was sad too when this story ended. The bright side is the author put an excerpt at the end of this book that lets you know that story is not over at least for one couple. I can hardly wait for the next installment to come out!

This is a wonderful story about old loves, lost loves and forgiveness. It is a great read from the beginning to the end. Stanley takes you in several different directions with the characters in this book and each has a interesting story to tell. I loved it from the beginning to the end. In the end true love conquered all! Great story Stanley!

This novel will have you in tears. It will also have you asking questions about your relationship with your mate and wondering if you missed the signs that your mate may be on on the down low. Great and very emotional read.
This book was awesome. I couldn't put it down until I finished it. After all the drama and just when you feel the couple are going to make it, well the ending will blow you away.

This book was awesome! All of these authors are phenomenal and their stories in this book were great and very touching. I am a big fan of all four so I knew even before I purchased this book that I would love it and I did! Each story made me believe that Miracles can happen if you open your heart and believe.

This is the first book that I have read by this author and I am so glad that I did. This book was full of suspense, drama and romance. I did not put it down until I finished it because it had me on the edge of my seat from the very first page! I am adding this author to my favorite author list.

This book brought me to tears due to all the truths that reflects my life now and in the past. I do know that having and keeping God in your life will change things for the better when you turn it over to him. Thanks Francine for writing and sharing this story!
I loved this historical romance story! Since reading Beverly Jenkins historical romance novels, I have been hooked and Altonya has written a great one too. Great read and informational too.

This book was drama filled from the beginning to the end. Great story and now I am so ready for the sequel to find out how all the drama ends for the Goodlove family. Great christian fiction book even though all this drama could happen and probably has happened in a church or churches somewhere.

I just finished reading Love and Justice and it is a combination of love, pain, sex, mystery and all around true to life story. You won't be able to put it down until you finish it! Rique put all the elements together in this book to keep you reading until you finish it and to pray that he writes a sequel!!!!!
This was a very good read! So much drama yet very entertaining. I loved it from the beginning to the end. I have to admit that the end was shocking but that made the book more interesting.

This book deals with real life love relationships combined with family drama on both sides. Simone and Matthew both learn to stand up for themselves and both find true love. This was a great story and you will not be able to stop reading this story until you finish it.

I read this book in one afternoon because it was so good. Don't be intimidated by the size of the book avid readers! Once you start, the storyline of the characters are so hot and full of drama that you'll continue reading to see how they deal with it all! Be prepared to feel the heat while reading this book and I don't mean from the weather! Great story Jonathan!

This was a great love story about one woman's view on love and marriage after having friends divorce and parents getting divorced. Her heart begins to thaw after she runs into a former flame who is now divorced and tries to rekindle what they had in the past and hoping that she will listen to his reasons why he kept some things from her that caused their break up. She ends up buying a trunk at an antique auction thinking it could possibly have some old documents or letters since her job was working with old documents. Inside is an antique wedding gown and it makes he wonder if it is a sign. Justin Beckett never got over what he had with Samara and despite the fact that he is now divorced, he still believes in love and marriage. His goal now is to make Samara a believer too and take a chance on him for the long haul. Great story!

I loved this story! It is great from the first page to the last. Stephanie's mistrust of men began when she was a young girl because her father left and from her Mom's constant preaching to her to never trust any man but to marry for money. Jack Kaufman ex-Navy Seal and security expert interviews for a security job for her business but also because she has adopted his daughter that he just found out about. She finds out the truth after getting romantically involved with him by a phone call and her ex-fiance Stanley who wants her for her money. They work things out despite all this but the ex goes to deadly measures to try and get her back because his buisness is failing and he needs her money to bail him out. Trust becomes the enemy for them both and almost destroys them all. Great story and you will not out this book down until the last page.

All I can say is that I love the Stallion brother's and this book was amazing.  The youngest Stallion Luke meets his match and realizes that love is a good thing and worth it even with all the drama. Great read!

This great story is about Meghan Howard a Social Worker who has lost her job due to downsizing. Her savings are running low and she is in dire need of a job soon. She walks into a business to get directions and it is a Surrogacy Clinic. A couple there think that she is there to apply but she turns them down. Meghan raised her sister after her parents died and has no desire to become a mother. Businessman Thomas Worthington-Yates lost his wife and unborn child and his in-laws suggest to him to think about surrogacy and implant the last egg that his wife provided before she died. She was their only child and they want a grandchild and a part of her to live on. He is against it but still meets with Meghan thinking that she had agreed to do it. She told him that she had not and he leaves. She later decides to do it but under certain conditions. She wants them to marry because her parents were not married and she felt left out of a lot of things that Father's do with their daughters. She also wants a job so she can go back to school and get her Masters degree. No love was in the equation for either of them at first anyway. This ends up being more than a business propostion which makes the ending very emotional. Great story and you won't be able to put this book down to find out how this ends.

Victor has done it again with another fantastic story!  This story is filled with family drama and the ending will surprise you! Chandelle and Marvin are the main characters in this book but her cousin's Dior and her fraternal twin Dooney add more drama to this mix. Dior is a very unhappy lady and misery loves company and she brings a lot of misery to the once happy couples marriage. Chandelle is a sista that wants material things that she knows her husband can not afford but he goes along with what ever will make her happy until he too has had enough. Lies and deceit turns a happy marriage into a barely there marriage because of secrets and lies. This story will make you angry but it will also make you think about what would you do in this situation. Family is forever but in this case, it is time to let go and let God!

Bakery owner Sophie Mayfield is running the family business with the help of her grandmother Mae. Everyone else in the family wanted to sell the bakery but she was determined to make it a very prosperous business and be able to update the equipment in the process. Fulton Foods has been losing contracts to the Mayfield Bakery and is trying to buy them out but no dice for Sophie nor her grandmother Mae. Eliot Wright works for their family business Fulton Fields and his uncle is pressuring him to stop them at all costs which includes stealing the family recipe book. Eliot goes there and acts like he is the new chef that Sophie hired to do what his uncle wants and finds that he loves baking again and loves the family atmosphere. His uncle gets wind of it and blows his cover and makes threats to Sophie to try and get Eliot to see things his way. In the process of working there he falls in love with Sophie and she ends things with him. Eliot finally realizes that his uncle has been just dangling the CEO job in his face to try and control him and he decides to get back at him and destroy the family business by sending orders their way. He plans to prove to Sophie that he truly loves her and the family business is not more important than his feelings for her. Great love story with a few twists involving others who work at Mayfield Bakery who find love also.

Graphic artist Genevieve L'Esperance has a thriving career and is loving her life in America until she discovers that her visa has run out and INS is looking for her to deport her. She is afraid of going back to her home country because she knows or suspects that her father was killed because he planned to expose the corrupt government and she knows she will be killed if deported. She is dating an older guy named Barry and he offers to marry her but during dinner with his friends, she discovers that he is already married. He claims that he is divorcing his wife and they can be married soon. Barry finally tells her that he loves her but Gen does not feel the same way about him. He convinces her to move out of her penthouse and rent a room from his friends to keep the INS at bay for awhile. She meets the other person renting a room there by the name of Dexter and after a awkward first meeting, they become friends. Barry's divorce is going to take longer than he anticipated so she decides to ask Dexter to marry her. She offers to pay for his last semester of law school in exchange for him becoming her husband of convenience or so she thought. The INS believes their story and they both end up falling in love for real but that does not sit well with Barry. He tries everything he can to break them up even blackmail but love conquers all in the end. Great story!

users.query: I gave it 4 stars because it took me awhile to get into it in the beginning. I also had a hard time with the whole relationship with a ghost! Once I got into the story, I wad hooked. Very different and very well written. I definitely want to read Cade's POV because I feel there is a lot there he didn't tell Briar!

cands.text: This was difficult to rate. I would say more like 3.5-3.75 stars hah. I loved loved the storyline and it really was a good book and I enjoyed reading it. My only problem was that I really had to push through the first half of the book. It was slow and boring and kind of confusing. The last half was great and then over. I would recommend this book just be warned it is slow going at first but well worth it!

I really enjoy Sarah's writing and this was no different! The whole story flowed well and I loved the set up. I haven't read a story with more than 2 character's POV and at first it was a little confusing but I grew to enjoy it. It is definitely a must read!!

I really love that this was a contest that ended up to be a book! I gave 4 stars only because I wasn't a fan of the first two stories. They were very well written, I just wasn't a fan of the story lines to them. Just not my cup of tea. But don't let that discourage you from reading this book! I really enjoyed the rest of the stories! They were phenomenal and the authors are great! I actually wanted more of them! This is a definite must read if you are into apocalypse books! Very well done and put together :)

I have thought hard on how to review this book and came to the conclusion that I can not put into words how much I loved  this story. It was beautiful. Which is weird to say and I can ramble on, but the bottom line is that I highly recommend it. Not a read for everyone and not easily accepted but it really spoke to me. Senna is a strong woman and Issac made her stronger. It brought a lot of emotions and I am so glad I read it.

Brandy does an amazing job bringing to life magical beings in these stories. Paranormal is hard to read and love if the author doesn't do it justice, but these had me hooked! Love doesn't come easy, there is a struggle but it is worth it in the end. The characters are all amazing but my favorite was definitely the bada** Fallon! If you like paranormal, then these are definitely for you!!

So this book was really slow. It was kind of boring until like 60% through it. But it did get interesting and it didn't take me long to finish the last bit of it. I am interested in reading the next one in hopes it is better because majority of the story is in place. I think the author has a great storyline and writes very well. It only has three stars because it took me too long to get into it.

I was anxious to read this after reading what it was about, I haven't read many books like this. The beginning didn't hold my attention, I had to push myself through. But then I got really into it and couldn't put it down! I really like that it was based on a little community coming together to do the best they could to survive and either ride it out or start up a new way of life. I enjoyed all the twists and turns Gary went through and even though I was expecting the end to happen like it did, I still enjoyed the way it came together. It was definitely a great read!

I was instantly hooked on this book! I read it in 2 days! I really love the different takes authors have for similar paranormal subjects. I really loved this idea of guardians for the influencers. Daniel and Anna are awesome and I love how well they work together, like they are one. I really want to read the next in the series!

I LOVED this book so much! I was hooked from the beginning! The author hooks you by starting it off with a secret that you are dying to know. I laughed and cried and yelled at the characters with this book! I love Caleb and Angie and their relationship. But I also love the supporting characters just as much! Especially Em and Joe! The ending was great but I was very sad for it to be over!

I really enjoyed the short story! It was funny and sexy and very well written! The only thing I didn't enjoy was the fast paced relationship and it felt a little rushed. But overall it was a great read and I liked it a lot! Abbie St. Claire is an awesome author!

I really am not good at writing reviews but I try and this one I know will be hard because I can't put into words how I loved this book. This was the first book I have read by this author and it makes me want to read more! I got sucked in right away. Anna and Dante really pulled me and captured my heart, Jude (Dude) took a little but I came around. It was an emotional story with some highs and lows but such a beautiful message. It broke my heart ultimately even with the happy ending, I feel like I connected more to one guy than the other which is why it broke my heart. But overall it was an amazingly beautiful and heart wrenching story that I highly recommend!!

I always love the books that Rene Folsom writes! such a great book, I finished it one day! I only gave it 4 stars out of selfish reasons, I really didn't like the ending. I wish it would have ended with the other brother but, alas I am not the author and she had a different vision! Otherwise she is an amazing author and everyone should read her books ;)

I really liked this book! I just read two books that were emotionally draining and I wanted to go on a book hiatus for a few days, but it was too hard so I started this one. I'm so glad I did! It was refreshing to not read a book full of emotion. While I love the emotional roller coaster books, I also love that this one was to the point. The main characters did bounce back and forth between friends and more than friends but not enough to make you dizzy! I was a little disappointed with the lack of conflict. There was one situation that had me wondering what would happen to Dallas and Carson, but just like that they made up. I just wanted to see a little more challenge. But overall the book was great and I loved the straightforwardness between the main characters and the mild emotion in it.

This book was so amazing. Such an emotional read and was a little hard to get through because of the tears and your heart being ripped out. I love Drew and I felt like I was experiencing everything with her. She is the strongest character I read. Jensen is awesome for being her constant. I read this in one day and want more! Please reach out to someone if you are being abused, no one deserves that.

I am really enjoying these books! I gave it 4 stars only because it lost my attention a few times. It was very well written and a great continuation of Heir to Kale. I loved finding out more of the history and things started to really click. I am really anxious to see what happens in the next book.

I have to admit that it took me awhile to really get into this one. But overall I really enjoyed it. I love all the twists and turns and everything that slowly comes out. Heven definitely has a lot on her plate powers, truth, lies, deception, life, death, everything! Very sad at the loss in this book but excited to read the last book!

I enjoyed this book more than the Apocalypse one! These stories were more along the storyline I enjoy. But, they were both great and had wonderful authors! I loved the first story in this one. I read all of the books in the Soul Seers series! Rene Folsom is a great author! My other favorite was Suburban Zombie! By the title I was a little unsure but it was fantastic! Hilarious and I loved it! Anthony Lance hit a home run on that story! This was a great collection of stories and would highly recommend you read it!

I really loved this book! Very well written and the characters are awesome! I can easily relate to the characters and I love that it is serious, funny, and sexy! The ending was satisfying, but the Epilogue not so much. No I need to read the next one! I cannot wait! This is a must read, very refreshing!

I loved the book but was a little disappointed. I was hoping for a little more suspense and sitting on the edge of your seat, but I still loved the book. My favorite part is that you were blown away by the ending because it is not what you expect! The lack of conflict was the only reason for 4 stars. I still whole-heartedly recommend this series to anyone because it is amazing and Rene is amazing :)
Very good book! My eyes had lots of tears, my heart fluttered and my belly had butterflies! Colleen is such an amazing writer and I love all her books. Excited to read the next book!

Hers made me love Seven James more than any character I ever read in a book, but I love her even more after this book! Seven is a badass woman! She is what women should strive to be, imperfect and confident. It was great to read about what made Seven into who she was in Hers and to see more levels of her. I can say I am definitely surprised at how it all began but it just wouldn't work any other way! So excited to start His next!

I am really loving this series of short stories! This one was definitely hotter than the first, phew. I am still recovering :) It is refreshing to read hot, fun sex stories between a married couple! Being married has a boring sex taboo and this shows it doesn't have too! I love the passion Cari has with the new domineering twist Josh brings! A fun, hot, sexy read! Keep them coming haha

Zero by Renee Folsom- Fantastic! I loved the storyline, and am so glad I don't have a timer haha But I am a little crazy because I want to know who the guy is!!!!

Issac by Michael Loring- This was an awesome story! I loved the Android with human emotions as the basis. I was thinking he would fall for a human at first but he falls for a fellow Androud instead! I loved the ending, but of course wish there was more! I would love to know if they are found!

World Wide Gone by Bart Hopkins- This is definitely something I can see happening in the future! No more internet because it made people fat and lazy! Having an Earth 2 is an interesting idea. I really want to know if Karina waited 12 years!

Life Companion by M.L. Ryan- This was interesting. Scientist creating someone completely compatible to you and you buy them. I liked the twist off Jon and Emma falling in love after their Life Companions fell in love and set then up. It was funny to think yhe whole time it was the other way!

Born Ready by Katheryn Van Pelt-  Really enjoyed this story. It had suspense, some fun and a little love. Alex ran away from a labor camp, boarded Dagon's ship and stole his heart!

Show Me by Magen McMinimy- This was an excellant story. I really liked the bird/human look of Jackal, it was different but cool! I wish there was a little more to the fight between Jackal and Cormac and a little more suspenseful. I know it is a romantic story but it just seemed short. But overall I really enjoyed it!

New Eden by Eaton Thomas Palmer- I really enjoyed this story. I loved the bond between Red and Ona and how that led to finding Red. It is cool that they decided to stay on New Eden!

Love Forgotten by  Stephanie Summers- This was one of my favorites. Technology being used for everything and replacing basic human connections. When Lena goes to another planet that doesn't use all that technology, she falls in love.

What Happens on Destiny 2 by Tara Moeller- I enjoyed this story! Two people who met briefly in college unexpectedly meet again 10 years later.

Brandy by Carrie Avery Moriarty- This was my least favorite. Didn't really Care for the storyline or the writing. But maybe it just wasn't for me. Hope you enjoy it!

This is a must read series! It is short but so amazing. Korah and Dane both have tortured hearts and trouble opening their hearts. They find each other and are smitten but due to their pasts they try so hard not to fall in love. My heart hurt and fluttered and I fell in love with Korah and Dane. I recommend this highly!

I really enjoyed this story!! Hope's family is rich and well into the Manhatten elite. But Hope is far from being into that scene, all she wants is to become an art broker. It is hot and steamy! Kimmie Easley is a great author who can definitely make you feel what she writes!!

users.query: I got this as a free book from one of the deal a day sites and it was a great way to waste a few hours.  The characters are surprisingly likeable and while you do need to suspend your disbelief over the crime scene and police behaviour (on top of the whole Tiff talks to ghosts and Royal is a demon) it is a cute  story to read on a lazy afternoon.

cands.text: Hilarious good crime stopping fun all while managing the kids and nosy neighbors.  Written in a light and easy style, this is the perfect book to unwind with.  Realistic? No.  But highly entertaining and worth the read if you enjoy the genre of crime with some romance thrown in. Fun characters and a highly enjoyable story.

This is a great entry into a series I am looking forward to reading.  Light and simple, the characters have just enough flaws to be genuine.  Not a hard who dun it more of a roll you along, easy peasy one it is still a cute read about a bumbling duo of would be detectives trying to prove that their friend did not leave their dinner party to kill herself.  Thanks to to the help of a friendly police officer who knows their hearts are in the right places they may just manage to solve the case and still have time for dinner.  While I quickly figured out who did it, I still enjoyed their antics enough to keep reading.

I got this book after seeing it on a free site.  I had never read the author prior and had no clue that all of the characters in this book were in other books.  Thankfully, this was written to be a stand alone story.  Although I have to say I want to know more.

I am not a huge fan of horror, although I do love paranormal and at first I thought this was a ghost story of that ilk.  Then, as I started reading it I realized that the ghosts in this book, while very real, were not the kind of ghosts a reality tv show would ever want to film. The ghosts of the past are the strongest in this book.  And how they can come back to haunt you in personal ways.

I don't give spoilers in my review but know this - if you have not read anything else by the author and are looking for a good story that has just the right blend of horror and human emotion as well as interesting characters you won't be disapointed.  There were points where I thought "Oh that is just hookey." And then, just as I was thinking "what a weird turn" it was explained.

There is humour and there is sorrow and there is triumph all packed in a book which shows the greatest thing about the human spirit, even when in moments of extreme fear, is the ability to dig deep and find that extra gear to get out of the fire.

I am going to quickly state I really did end up enjoying this book.  The depth of information presented however was quite in depth at times and seemed a bit more than necessary.  What I really did enjoy was the way that the work and planning and information needed to solve the crime was presented. This was not a simple plot and I greatly enjoyed the fact that it was not a solve it all with one find.  There was romance and mystery and danger.

My biggest issue with this book, besides the occasionally too in depth presentation of the oil world was the large cast of non main characters.  I found myself having to go back occasionally and reminding myself who was who and how they fell into the grand scheme of things.

Overall, a good read but not a quick romance story.  This was almost like two books - a romance novel of the easy variety and a complex mystery.  The melding of the two was awkward at times but in the end I found myself liking it no matter what.

First off - if I could have given 3.5 stars I would have.  It is more than ok but I am not sure how far into really liking it it goes.  Mainly due to the overload of too many types of supernatural bad guys and their descriptions which kinda bogged things down.  Each chapter seems to bring out a new and unknown monster, written as an entry from a made up book that the two hapless new employees of the Dept of Magic find that they need to read to learn the ins and out of their new job which they take with out really knowing that it is not a job they can leave so easily.

I really enjoyed the way the book went from one POV to another between the two characters.  As a matter of fact, Jasmine Farah, a slightly too perfect woman in all that she is capable of as well as being a former beauty queen and her partner Rocco "Rocky" di Angelo who is so poor he lives in a roach motel and barely eats are the main reason I trudged through this book.  The story is good,full of potential.  A super secret government department which dabbles in the paranormal in ways that Spooky Mulder in the X files could only have dreamed of.  The characters are good, if slightly flawed in their personalities.  It is the extra descriptions, the copious amount of bad guys who chase them, the fact that each small act seems to take many pages to describe which weighs the book down.  However, some of the bad guys, famous characters from history, are quite funny and you can't help but see the comedy in the tragedy being told.  There are places where the story gets a big muddy, but if you can get through that you may be surprised at the many directions the story takes before it finally reaches the end.

I was given a free copy in exchange for an honest review.

I really enjoy a well told tale, even one that is well known prior to the reading and the Cold King is no exception.  I found this book on a daily deal and got it for free so I went in not knowing if it would be good or bad.  And, for the most part it was excellent.  I did not find it dark, but rather that it had more colourful characters than some versions of the tale.  While I found one or two editing issues which can easily be overlooked the novel if first rate and very sweet.  It is a romance, a story whose ending the reader will know way before they get there simply due to familiarity with the story.  What makes it unique is the simly told but emotionally filled details.  The need for seperation of the past to fully go on with the future and finding happiness no matter your lot in life is the moral and the characters fill their roles perfectly.  I loved the twists and nuances that set the Cold King apart from other versions of Beauty and the Beast.  A quick and easy read, this story is lovely and gentle and a nice way to lose yourself in a familar childhood tale retold.

There are some stories which you just need to read.  Fenris' is one of them.  I became a huge fan of this fictional character in the Baine Chronicles and was delighted that Jasmine Walt was going to give him his own book series.  This story does NOT disappoint.  Trying to adjust to a quiet life in the country, Fenris is the only shifter in a town of pure humans.  Or is he?  It seems that trouble has found him and he has never been one to back down from helping others.  Well written, this story is a bit more on the romantic side than the Baine Chronicles, but it does have adventure and intrigue and is lovely read, sure to delight old fans and make new ones.

This is a dark book.  Not dark in a demons and hel and fictional evil but dark in a there are humans who do this to other humans and don't care the consequences.  This book is about the human spirit and how it can be corrupt and sick and twisted or it can be loving and wonderful and defy the odds.  This book is not an easy or light read. For Debra Dunbars fans of the imp series there is none of the light hearted humor or devil may care fun. There is no sexy angel to tease or an imp to drink too much.  This is a book which is emotionally raw. Uriel has been missing a while and while gone she went to a dark place in her mind and body. It takes an even darker place and some very courageous young women to pull her out.  Days after reading this book I couldn't put it out of my mind and I am not sure I ever should.  Human trafficking is a real and horrible problem and sadly there are no angels or even demons with their hearts in the right places to save those caught up in it.  spoiler and I don't give spoilers usually but this one needs it - there is a HE of sorts. Not everyone lives and that is hard to read in a story like this.  But there depth of writing and character development is there and this book is wonderfully written for the way it struck both terror and joy in my heart.

Not the best in the series, this one took me a while to finish but when I finally got to the last third of the book it got interesting enough to be sad when it ended. Some character development and also back story and introduction of new characters hopefully with the purpose of tying it all in with the story arc conclusion.

This book should be good.  Interesting plot, lots of action, many possible characters.  However it is not.  It is boring and needs to be trudged through.  I normally read a book like this in an afternoon or two however this on took me much longer as it just wasn't that satisfying of a read.  When folding laundry seems like more fun a book needs a bit of help.

This book has so much potential as a unique and original take on the Beauty and the Beast story. In then hands of a more skilled story teller it could be really good. Instead it is bogged down by poor writing and shallow junior high type characters with little actual depth or likability.  A cursed bi-polar werewolf/man and a woman trapped in the emotional shell of a 12 year old girl make for a hard to believe and care for couple. The most interesting characters are the side ones with sadly little page time.

Jasmine Walt does it again.  This is a fantastic new series which draws the reader into a complex and utterly unique world where the gods and paranormals are the norm and the world is full of intrigue.  As per her norm, the main characters are all tough yet sassy women who may not know exactly where they are going in life but they are willing to grab the bull by the horns and go for it.  While there are hints at romance, that is not what this book is about.  This is pure adventure and intrigue as we follow Malina through her life as a guild assassin.  She has been trained since she was young for the job and it is a huge part of her until secrets are revealed which force her to change perspectives.  The other main characters are all wonderfully written and make you want them to have complete books of their own as well.  I don't like to give spoilers, so please, read it and you be the judge.

This is not your average paranormal book and the characters are not your ordinary type. Set in a far gone period with royal navy ships and women who have proper places this book takes the reader on a beautiful and detailed journey of finding ones place in the world and doing it while being a "proper lady" , albeit one who can start and stop fires with her mind. In her quests to be free of the confines of an arranged marriage she joins the navy and sets about shedding her preformed thoughts and opinions of life as she makes her mark. There are battles and ships and pirates and also friendship. Completely appropriate for teens and pre teens as well as being adult friendly. The ideas are new and unique and beautifully written in a manner which draws you in and captivates you.  My only sadness is the book is stand alone and not past of a series as I am not ready to leave the world created by Melissa McShane.  Gallant gentleman and brave forward thinking women all who converse and fight for what they think is right. I read this all in one sitting as I just couldn't put it down..

I really enjoyed this book.  I wasn't as in love with the series it spun off from but this time the writing is spot on and the world building seems to be much more cemented with back story and flow.  This is the story of Carmella the blood witch and what happens when one night when not in her right mind due to illness she agrees to let a Djinn live in her consciousness to solve a crime. Together with his shape shifting side kick with a slight love of flesh, the work with and through Carmella to figure out just who is taking the djinn from the world.  Set five years after the other series this one shows how everything did NOT go right back together and how the different species were forever altered by the appearance of many different gods and Demi gods as well as different creatures.  I enjoyed reading as Carmella goes from down trodden to  "finding her backbone" and seeing her worth where she thought she had lost it.

This was an interesting suspense/fae/mystery type story.  I enjoyed the fact that the heroine was neither a prude or an idiot, but I do have to wonder about the men in her life - Roan, the mysterious Fae who is all kissing and anger.  And Gabriel, the police inspector who has seen more than he understands and is willing to put his life out for hers. They are lacking in depth and while we get hints to their pasts, it seems we have to take them at face value more than anything.  I think that with a bit more developing of all the characters this can turn into an interesting tale, especially as the lead heroine finds out more about her past and the darkness in it.  I look forward to seeing where this will end up going and will look out for the second book in the series when it comes out.

What can I say, I loved this book.  The lead character, a Blood Mage named Nina is gritty and down to earth.  Her attraction to the King of the Vampires, Greyson is hard to imagine and harder to fight.  I couldn't put this first book down and while I don't normally enjoy books which end on a total cliff hanger I was ok with this one but only because the next book came out literally hours after I finished.  While I did find that some of the world building was weak I found that I liked the characters a lot, even if I wasn't entirely sure how some one who lived chained in a basement for years of her life then a fighting slave for the next decade or so had time to become cultivated enough to learn not only to read, but to love to read.  Also, her loner tendencies and her ability to be so witty and biting in her sarcasm seem a bit at odds.  However, I enjoyed the vampires and the werewolves even if they are not clearly defined in this world and need a bit more background as to why exactly they are at odds.  Hints are given but it seems to all go back to who is in power with no reason why they both will only accept destruction of both races.  The most interesting thing about the whole book is the budding relationship between Nina and Greyson.  Sadly, one is to inexperienced to understand it and one is to blind to see it.  From a writing standpoint it is all over the place and switches narratives from person to person but not always at chapter ends which seems odd.  I think with a good beta team and a few re-writes this could be a great book

Full disclosure here, I read the first book in the series third so I already knew I liked the style of writing.  It filled in gaps and holes I had and also showed just how far the author takes Sydney Rye.  In this book we meet her, not as the detective with a heart for helping she becomes but as Joy we see her not so much as a softer person but as a more naive person.  Someone who hasn't yet learned that what lurks in the shadows is far less scary than what hides in plain sight.  This book is less polished than the future sequels but it fits, as Joy is as well.  I enjoyed the story greatly and recommend it for those who like their books well planned, with just a hint of naughty (there is light bondage mentioned so beware of you are not into it. It is not explicit and does go with the story).  Joy finds a dead body and things spiral out of control, hers and those around her as she struggles to make sense of what she finds and the levels of deceit that surround the death.  All she wanted was a fresh start, and in finding that she finds more than she bargained when she takes a job walking dogs for the rich and famous.

The book begins with Blue and that is fitting.  Blue being the once in a life time dog that is better than any human sidekick one could ask for.

I really loved the first book in this series and as soon as I saw a second in the series on Amazon I grabbed it and read it straight through. A fast read I find finished it in one sitting. The gods are having power issues and only the town's sisters three can save the day. As if that isn't enough of a issue a murdered vampire is found and the on again off again affections of one part time deputies are thrown in the mix.  As usual humor and thrills are high and by the time the book wraps up you find that the story has concluded well but left enough new questions to make you want the next book much quicker than next spring.

This book isn't great literature.  It will never win any prestigious awards.  It is short and quick and sexy and witty and has a dog.  Of the paranormal type, but still it has a dog.  Who is much loved by not one but two people.  And how their desire to ensure the dog is happy helps them find happiness.  Sweet and fun, a book I am glad I picked up as it fit the bill for what I needed - a pleasant time filler.

A fabulous book. The actual mystery starts slowly, but in a good way, allowing you to fall just a teensy bit in love with both the characters.  By the end of the story you will want to hug Laurie even if he is a spoiled brat.  Nicola is everything you want to be when you grow up - sane and down to earth.  I am hoping more of these two will happen with her and a certain Nevada policeman having an adventure of their own.  Great plot, fun characters and some thing that is not the Devil wears Prada with a snarky old fashion diva and a young protege.

I cant explain it. The Nate Temple books are horrible. The Callie Penrose ones are wonderful.  This book is nonstop blasphemous fun.  Huge consequences for actions happen in whispers and Callie and Roland have to fight their way to both freedom and clearing their as well as some werewolves names to freedom. Nate pops in with his friend the day walking vampire but he is merely a sideline. Callie shows just how bas ass her fighting and sarcasm are in this hard to put down book.  I cant wait to see what happens next and with our giving spoilers lets just say the Vatican is one place which may never recover from her visit.
