I ordered the red kettle and loved it immediately.  I wondered why I hadn't gotten an electric kettle sooner.  It heats very quickly, automatically turns off when boiling has occurred (so you don't need to watch it!), and pours nicely.

A few quibbles:  It is a bit loud when heating.  I have to fill it through the spout rather than the top because the lid doesn't open far enough.  And the pot isn't insulated, so the water doesn't retain its heat for long once the unit turns itself off.  Funny though, despite these drawbacks, I still love this kettle and would purchase it again.

And it's a pretty spot of warm color on my counter!

This is an excellent book, both for newer and more experienced cooks.  The recipes all range from easy to fairly easy.  The ingredients can be found in any regular grocery store.  This is the book I reach for on a regular basis when wanting to make a quick-ish weeknight meal.  I've made about 10 or so of the recipes, and have been happy with each one.

Only two quibbles.  First, sometimes the directions lack specificity.  Be sure to read a recipe all the way through before you start, making sure that you understand what needs to be done, because you might need to improvise a little or add a step here and there.  Second, the photos of the food don't necessarily match the food exactly.  For instance, for one vegetarian noodle recipe, the photo clearly showed shrimp.  Another example- the cover photo shows fried slices of potato, but the recipe actually calls for sauteed cubed potatoes.  But these are only minor quibbles.  I would still recommend this book highly.

Love this cookbook! I've made about 15 of the recipes, and they've all been excellent. While a knowledge of basic cooking is essential (of course), few of the recipes are particularly time or labor intensive, and some are downright easy. And the ingredients can be found at any local grocery. And yet, given the ease of cooking and the standard ingredients, Clark's recipes are delicious. She is an artist, excelling at combining flavors and textures, so that each dish is far more than the sum of its parts. I highly recommend this book!

I would point out one thing. This isn't a criticism of the book, but simply a caution. It seems these days that people want a cookbook with a specific eating theme- vegetarian, gluten-free, paleo, low-carb, low-fat, vegan, comfort food, BBQ, desserts, etc. This book doesn't fall into any category. It contains a wide range of recipe types, something for everyone, but not a lot of any one kind. I love that about the book. Something to fit my every taste and mood.

This is not only my favorite gluten-free cookbook, it is one of my very favorite cookbooks of any kind. I don't eat gluten-free in general, but the desserts in this book are so delicious, that I prefer them to the traditional wheat flour kind.

In general, too many gluten-free dessert recipes simply take a traditional wheat flour-based dessert and convert it to gluten-free using a combination of other types of flours. The results are almost never as good as the original. This book, however, doesn't take that approach. These recipes were created from the ground up using gluten-free ingredients. They are unique unto themselves. Every recipe I've tried has been lusciously good. If you try only one recipe in the entire book, try the coconut cake recipe. Best coconut cake I've ever had. A revelation. I have naughty dreams about it :-) And it is ridiculously easy to make. Whirl all ingredients together in a food processor, and bake.

No flour blends are used. No 1/3 cup of this, plus 1/4 cup of that, plus 1/2 cup of something else. Almost any given recipe uses only one flour-like ingredient (cornstarch, almond flour, etc). And none of the more exotic flours that can be difficult for some people to find (eg. teff, kaniwa, etc.).

One caveat. If you don't like almond flour/meal, then this probably isn't the cookbook for you. Many of the recipes use it. If, however, you love almond meal as much as I do, you will dance around your kitchen in delight when making these recipes.

Apparently I'm not as enamored of this book as most people seem to be.  It isn't bad, hence the 3 stars.  But it isn't particularly good.  I've made about 15 of the recipes, and they were all fine, but none of them were delicious.  None were the type that I would want to serve to anyone outside my family.  And, really, I serve them to my family only when I need something both very quick and healthful.  I have so many other vegan recipes that are truly delicious.  This book has retreated to fallback position.

I still make recipes from the book, for this one reason.  I like having something healthful in the fridge, so that if I want lunch or a snack, there is something already prepared, thereby preventing unhealthful grazing.  I would recommend this book if you are looking to fill that niche.  And most of the recipes use ingredients that are already in a decently stocked kitchen, so you won't have to run to the store for something unusual.

One aspect of the book that is a tad bit off-putting.  Nixon changes, sometimes significantly, traditional recipes from many cultures, making them both vegan and easy to prepare from standard U.S. ingredients.  That's fine.  But she still calls her recipes by the traditional recipe names.  It seems a bit presumptuous, in a steam-rolling western kind of way, to usurp something from another culture, change it significantly, but still call it by its traditional name.  (Certainly use traditional recipes for inspiration, but call them something different.)  I'll likely get lots of Not Helpful votes for daring to say that.  But, really, think about it.  Isn't that kind of rude?

This book was clearly written with good intentions, but falls short of the mark compared with other similar volumes.  The first half or so of the book discusses why a vegan diet is beneficial both to the person and to the planet.  Not bad information, but it has been presented far better in other books, such as Thrive Foods.  The Kind Diet provides the wikipedia short version, easily digestible but without much depth.

As a recipe book, it also lacks depth, there being very little variety in the type of recipes presented.  They all seem very similar.  For instance, almost every recipe uses shoyu (soy sauce) and some form of umeboshi plum.  These may be Alicia's favorite recipes.  That is fine.  But if a person is going to create a recipe book for sale, he/she should include many different types of recipes with different flavors.  Her recipes also tend to be bland.  She believes that spices aren't calming, and shouldn't be used much.  This view makes little sense.  Numerous spices have been shown to have enormous health benefits, and none of them have been shown to cause any sort of systemic inflammation.  And, so importantly, spices add to the sensations of fullness and satisfaction, so a person tends to eat less of flavorful food than of bland, thereby preventing overeating.

In sum, no one other than a somewhat famous celebrity would have been allowed to publish this book.  It trades on name recognition rather than on excellent content.

First, I will say that Gillian Flynn is a good writer in some ways.  Meaning, first, that she knows how to create characters and portray them convincingly and in depth.  And second, that her descriptions, specific scenes, character interactions, etc. are all well done.  The problem?  She lacks (in this book, at least) the ability to create an interesting story that seizes a reader's attention, draws him in, and won't let go until the last word has been read.  At many points in the book, the story just dragged, and in some places was just downright boring.  Enough exposition, enough with characters simply just thinking and thinking.  At some point, in a decent mystery, something needs to actually happen.  The unanswered question of who killed Libby's family just wasn't enough, on its own, to drag a reader through the entire story.

Another problem: the main character Libby.  One rule of writing: a character doesn't need to be likeable, but she does need to be interesting.  Libby wasn't interesting.  After the initial novelty of having an unpleasant, screwed-up main character, possessed of essentially no redeeming quality, wore off, Libby was just downright repulsive.  Yes, Flynn tried to create the character who might really have resulted from the poor upbringing and the terrible experience of the murders.  But that resulting person doesn't make a good, interesting, readable character.  As for the other characters, they weren't interesting either.  Seldom have I read a book with such an unpleasant group of people.

As for the ending, I won't say what happened, but I will say this.  The mystery is resolved in two pieces.  The first aspect is decent, and is consistent with the entire story that a reader has been wading through.  The story does indeed plausibly lead to that point.  The second aspect, however, comes pretty much out of left field.  (It is foreshadowed a tiny bit, but that foreshadowing, in retrospect, seems clunky and stuck on.)  And it is so unlikely, and inconsistent with the rest of the book, that it seems like a complete cop-out on the part of the author.  Causes a reader to audibly groan.

A contrast?  Flynn's Gone Girl.  Terrible ending aside, that book was much better written.  Things happened.  The story progressed.  And the main characters, while not likeable, were interesting enough to hold a reader's attention.  If you wish to read a book by Flynn, try Gone Girl (but do brace yourself for a ridiculous ending).

Lovely coloring book. The designs are beautifully wrought. The paper is high-quality. Don't know that this book induces meditation more than any other :-) but it is great fun. The price, though higher than most other "adult" coloring books, is well worth it, not only for the quality but also for the varied selection. 90 mandalas in all, while those other coloring books tend to offer only 30 or so. If you're looking for a coloring book, I highly recommend this one. My favorite. The only caveat? Some of the mandalas have fine detail, so you'll need a good eye and a sharp point.

This book has some positive aspects, no doubt about it.  It is a good, fast ride.  There is little in it that is superfluous (unlike so many bloated books).  It is a tight, well-paced story.  And I liked Kick herself.  As a character, she certainly has potential.  I was going to give the book 4 stars, but the more I thought about it, the more the negative aspects bothered me, as follows.  (Some spoilers below!)

1) Cain makes a big, very specific point of having Kick remark, near the beginning, that it is impossible to tell a loaded pistol from an unloaded one simply by picking it up.  Ummmm.... SO NOT TRUE. Ammunition is made of metal. It is heavy. A pistol with a fully-loaded magazine feels far heavier than one with an empty magazine. And not only is the weight difference noticeable, but the weight distribution of the pistol is different (more top heavy than stock heavy when unloaded).  Why is this error so annoying?  Because both Cain and Kick lose all credibility at that point in terms of knowing their subject matter. I didn't really trust any other "facts" subsequently mentioned.

2) Kick is supposed to be a highly-trained, kick-ass kind of gal.  I believed that in the beginning.  But other than two (if I remember correctly) brief examples, she doesn't seem capable of taking care of herself in actuality.  And she seems incapable sometimes of thinking through a problem logically (such as scaling the side of a building without first checking to see if the front door is unlocked).

3) The extreme manner in which Bishop first approaches Kick is absurd.  No reason for it whatsoever.

4) Bishop himself is a character we've seen many times before in books by other authors.  Mysterious, dark past, violent but only in service of a good cause, sexy, living in a fantastic house and driving cool cars.  You get the idea.

5) I know why, as a plot point, Kick's abuser must live, but the manner in which his life is saved is truly absurd.

6) There is no legitimate reason for Bishop to approach Kick to begin with.  She does help him with information a few times later in the story, but at the beginning, he doesn't know that these future situations will develop.

7) I like the fact that Kick's mother is narcissistic, exploiting her daughter's abduction for her own gain, but given that fact, it seems highly unlikely that Kick would have anything whatsoever to do with her mother by the time the book takes place.

8) Even though we are told that Kick's kidnapper abused her terribly, we aren't ever shown that in any way.  (I don't want much of a description of that horror, but just some solid indication here and there.)  In fact, essentially the only flashbacks we are shown are those in which the abuser is being nice, even fatherly, towards Kick.  This imbalance skews a reader's perception of him.  He is an evil monster, but we don't really receive that impression viscerally.

Wish I'd read this book years ago, when I first started studying Buddhism.  Howley strips away the various cultural accretions that make most strains of Buddhism confusing/contradictory to a novice, thereby laying bare the essence of true and original Buddhism.  This review is very short, but all you need to know is this.  If you want a simple (not simplistic) explanation of Buddhism, then this is the volume for you.

I adore this book.  I am thrilled that such a thing was written.  But I want to make very clear at the beginning here, that I don't actually cook from it much.  The recipes aren't the kind that I usually would make.  (I prefer vegan food from varying cultures.)  However!!!  Perhaps because I love social history, for me this book provides a wonderful and unprecedented review of middle-American food from across the country.  And not just of the food, but of the people themselves.

Clayton and his wife spent several years driving around the country, stopping in small towns, inquiring about the best traditional cooks in the area, and then interviewing them and obtaining their recipes.  The resulting recipes are great fun to read.  Many of them are clearly regional.  And many of them are also "ethnic" recipes that the cooks' antecedents brought with them to American from many different parts of the world.  Those recipes, along with the accompanying interviews, are a true treasure trove.  There is no other book like this.

The book was written in the early 1990's, and so now, 20+ years later, it is moving into the realm of (recent) history.  I wouldn't be surprised if, centuries from now, this book will provide a unique glimpse into real home cooking in 20th century America.  Fantastic!!

This is the best book, of any kind, that I've read in a very long time. It's an excellent example of simplicity, clarity, and ease of expression combined with complex and unique analysis. Meaning, it's a scholarly book that anyone can easily enjoy.

I love history, and I love good literature. This book blends the two to elucidate something stunning about this country's past, as well as its present, and even its future. How unusual it is to find a book that actually expresses something new, old tropes that have been considered in a new and unique way. And, as with all great thinking, once it has been explained, it seems so very obvious and true, making a person wonder why no one thought of it earlier.

If you are deeply interested in this country, in its past, present, and future, if you are looking to grasp some heretofore undiscovered wisdom to explain it a little better, then you must, must, must read this book.

Andrew Levy, you are my new hero!

I have been a huge Dexter fan since the first season.  Loved this show, and couldn't wait for each successive new season to come out on DVD.  But this season?  So boring.  Oh, wait.  Not boring.  BORING!!!

First and foremost, the killing duo of Edward James Olmos and Colin Hanks absolutely put me to sleep.  The dullest murderous duo ever.  For a show that has created some of the most fascinating psychopaths in the history of television/movies, this pairing, and the accompanying writing, were shockingly bad.  Neither of the actors scared me in the least.  Not for one moment did either of them seem believable as a killer.  Colin Hanks in particular.  It was embarrassing to watch him try so hard and so unsuccessfully to be a convincing bad guy.  He simply pouted a lot, like a petulant little boy.  Who on earth was responsible for that casting?  And there was no consistency to his character.  He was ridiculously wishy-washy.  And even after the "twist" was revealed, and the wishy-washiness made at least a small bit of sense, that didn't change the fact that all of the preceding episodes were deadly dull.

The whole over-arching religion theme of the season was incredibly heavy-handed, ridiculously smack-you-in-the-face.  A theme should play out naturally and subtlely in a story.  It shouldn't be clunkily imposed on every last facet.

I understand that a show must keep changing (and hopefully evolving), but the whole (SPOILER ALERT!!!) Debra in love with Dexter idea was ridiculous.  That is the sort of idea that a dying show uses (unsuccessfully) to create shock and drama.

I also agree with numerous other reviewers about the ads for other shows, as well as for the next season of Dexter, that you can't forward past.  And yes, especially the fact that the very last (shocking?) seconds of Season 6 are shown in a preview for Season 7.  Truly unbelievable.

I will start by saying that this book isn't for everyone (as you can see by the star review distribution).  There is an aspect to the story, regarding Rose's brother, that is odd.  I'm not even sure why it was there, or what it added to the story.  But I didn't mind it like some people do.  But if you don't like unexplained oddness, you might want to try another book.

That being said, I liked this book considerably.  Bender is an excellent writer.  She takes a rather pedestrian subject (a regular ol' family), adds a little twist (Rose can taste emotions, thoughts, etc in food), and turns it into a highly readable story.  Nothing particularly dramatic happens (for the most part), there are no extreme characters, and yet the story draws a reader in, effortlessly.  It is simply fun and engaging.

My only quibble is that the book is a little too long, given the subject matter.  It might have been better if it had been shorter, maybe by about 50 pages or so.  There was one section, maybe about 60% of the way in, that dragged a little.  But that is only a minor quibble.  I would still recommend this book to anyone who wants a light and unusual read.

This is McHugh's first novel.  She does have talent.  She writes scenes in a way that made me truly believe the people and the action.  In that regard it was an effortless read.  I enjoyed the setting, the characters, and the story.

My quibble with the book is this.  McHugh has yet to develop a feel for dramatic pacing.  The book moved along at one speed at all times.  That is, the pacing was very even.  What should have been the more tense, dramatic, and/or climactic scenes didn't feel any different from any other scene.  Even the denouement, when the bad guy gets his due, didn't feel much different from a baby shower that was depicted.  For this reason, at the end, nothing of particular consequence seems to have happened.  There is no sense of reader catharsis whatsoever.

Now that I think about it, I'll add one more (slight) negative.  The story was structured as two parallel stories, one following Lila as a young woman and the other following Lila's daughter Lucy as a young woman.  Parallel structure is fine, in story, theme, etc.  But in this book the parallels became too obvious and heavy-handed.  In fact, in Lucy's story, a potential love interest, Daniel, appears, but serves no real purpose other than as a parallel to Lucy's father Carl.  If Daniel didn't exist, the story wouldn't really have progressed any differently.  And that is just one example.

I enjoyed the book to some degree, but I can't quite say that I would recommend it to others. There are other novels of mystery and/or suspense that are far more well-paced and suspenseful.  But I will read McHugh's next book, to see if she has matured as a writer.

My first experience with 3D printing was almost 20 years ago when my dad showed me a small form he made on this huge machine from a CAD drawing.  The technology was new, but I was so intrigued!  Fast forward to 2013 and I finally bought my own 3D printer from a Kickstarter campaign.

I am so glad I found this book.  It an excellent read filled with both great ideas to help monetize your new 3D printer and also detailed information about advancements in the technology that give you a nice idea of what to expect over the next few years of this exciting technology.  I would highly recommend this book to 3D printing enthusiasts or just anyone who is interested in discovering an alternative revenue stream that doesn't require a huge investment.  A++

What a fantastic book. Stan I.S. Law is easily one of the most prolific writers of this generation.  Enigma of the Second Coming is the story of John Hydon, a brilliant scientist, and his family.  They live in a sanctuary deep in the Yukon where they study the planets, the universe, and more. I found the book to be deeply engrossing and a certifiable page turner.  The book is quite complex and really conducive to deep introspection.  All the while, its really an entertaining book!  You can't go wrong with this one.

Prior to reading this book I had never heard of the Ninth Legion, but after reading this book I was quite intrigued! The book is very informative while at the same time offering an excellent fictional narrative. The plot is well developed, the characters well written, and overall this is a very fun read. I highly recommend this book to lovers of fiction or anyone interested in reading about the NInth Legion. You will not be disappointed!

I found the dependence ink easy and fast. It wouldn't be good to hold down the pen and leave it in one spot unless you want a large round circle on your image.

I got these stamps to add a little pizzazz to my cards. So glad I did. They're perfect and exactly what I was hoping for. They are all small and several are tiny. I used some as an accent in a larger stamped snowflakes and others with a smaller size stamped snowflakes that fit perfectly; leaving the background as an accent color. As other reviewers mentioned they peel off great without any breaking. I use my x-acto knife to pick them off and place them. It's really that easy!

It's just the perfect size for a carry on or for the gym. I use it when I travel and just love how durable it is. The straps are comfortable enough to hold by hand or around your shoulder. The lining is perfect; it's easy to clean and wipe away any spills or mess.

For the price I paid for these pens I'd say I hit the jackpot. They glide smoothly on the paper. I'm in love with the glitter pens, they're so cute! Well all of the pens in this set are awesome. You get a good verity of all colors. I'm very happy with this set.

This is just OK. It's made in china. You can tell it's cheaply made. The first one I received was all scratched up. Amazon sent a replacement right away. The funnel is great to get my booze in. :)

Tsukineko make good quality inkpads. I love the rich colors and how they don't smudge once you've used it.

Keep in mind this is NOT water resistant do you don't want to use these with your watercolor crafts.

users.query: It's well constructed and the coating is a nice finish. I would recommend if you're looking for chocolate brown decor in your bath.

cands.text: Held out a long long time before finally buying this. Glad it's finally mine. Quality built. Has rollers. Drawers slide smoothly. Took off a star off because I was expecting it to be darker like the picture, but it's a light charcoal.
Looks great, I really like it. It's solid and heavier than expected and is a nice addition to my new home. Thank you!

My first doormat for my first home. Appears to be nice quality. Comes nicely packaged. We'll see how it holds up!

UPDATE: Over a year later. Color has faded tremendously. Looks like it's 20 years old and it's not like I have a lot of traffic with just me and my dog with occasional guests. Can't recommend.

I like it. Comes in a lot of pieces to be assembled which was expected. Instructions were straight forward and easy to follow.

The color matched well with my decor. Taller than I expect which was a bonus for me since I'm tall and hate bending over.

I would recommend. Can't beat the price.

Wonderful product. It's big. It's heavy. It's colorful. It's quality made and looks just like the picture. Couldn't ask for better! The bottom also has tiny cork pegs so it doesn't slide around and sits comfortably wherever you lay it down.

Wonderful product. It's big. It's heavy. It's colorful. It's quality made and looks just like the picture. Couldn't ask for better! The bottom also has tiny cork pegs so it doesn't slide around and sits comfortably wherever you lay it down.

First off, it's huge and nice. I bought this for my sister's 25th birthday. I filled it up with birthday confetti and other, smaller, wrapped gifts inside of it that were hidden so when she opened it she could dig through it for other birthday gifts. It was a hit and she seemed to really like it.
Appears to me nice quality. Feels nice and comfy on the feet. I wish they came longer as I have a long bathroom. I bought the 40" ivory color.

I like it a lot. It's "almost" identical and reminds me of the one my folks had when I was growing up that has since been lost to who knows where. Fairly straightforward on piecing together. Nice quality. Definitely a nice additional near the front door to throw the hat and coat on.

Don't fall for the other reviews. It's a trap. I waited for this vase with excitement only to be completely let down.

Not only did it take forever to get here, but it arrived in pieces. Three to be exact.

The packaging was horrible. Loose, inadequate and unacceptable for ceramic traveling hundreds of miles. You need more than just top and bottom styrofoam inserts with the vase wrapped in a thin piece of plastic sitting inside a box marked "fragile" within another "Amazon Prime" box that has NO visible marking of "fragile" anywhere on it -- makes sense.

The ceramic itself is thin and cheaply made. Another reason why it arrived broken. For it's size, it's very light and that should give you some indication of what you're receiving. Not quality.

The colors that everyone else "raves" about aren't anything to rave about it. So personally, I don't get it. Perhaps folks need to get out more? They're dull and don't "pop". They're nothing to take a second glance at if you had friends or family over. I can already feel if I had it setup some place I would probably get sick of looking at it because it would make me very depressed, rather than happy or proud to have it in my home. That's how bad the design and colors are.

At any rate, you've been warned. If you like nice stuff in your home, move away from this item. However, if you're the type who believes, "one man's trash is another's...", then by all means, waste your money.
Cheap. Nothing "high quality" about it. 100% cotton on another planet maybe. Material is ULTRA thin, almost see through. Wait, it is.. Don't recommend.

Been decorating my kitchen with these little guys over the past few weeks. This one seems heavier than the others. It's nice quality and a nice addiction above my kitchen cabinets!

Yes, I would recommend if you like the Fat Bistro theme.
Love'em. Fantastic bowls MADE IN USA! Solid construction. Perfect for my Boxer. No more squeezing her little nose in a tiny dog dish.

Look great in my office. Assembly was slightly cumbersome, but perhaps I'm just getting cranky in my old age now. :)

I opted for the glass doors and it looks sharp. Dark walnut looks terrific for me. I'd recommend if you're looking for a sleek and simple cabinet.

Beautiful, elegant, functional, and actually works.

Just replaced my entire kitchen counter-tops, sink, disposal, faucet, and of course soap dispenser. I replaced all the sink items with Moen products and couldn't be more satisfied. I had an old in the sink soap dispenser purchased from Home Depot that came with a stainless steel sink bought last year that barely functioned after a month and just felt cheap. It was horrible to use. But, this Moen soap dispenser is solid and built well.

It doesn't leak or spill any additional soap after using it either. It seems to have some sort of suction capability after you depress the push-button . I haven't seen one drop leak yet. When you do push on it to dispense soap you don't need to aggressively man-handle it either. Just a light push on it and enough soap comes out for your needs.

Installation took less than 5 minutes. Highly recommend if you're doing a remodel and this is the style you're going for.

It matches well with my dark furniture and I needed something to put above my fireplace for decoration since it just looked too bare. This worked out well. One tip on hanging it up with the wooden blocks included because it's a decent idea but poor execution in design. You'll need to put something small (I used some cardboard laying around) behind them. If you don't, and just tighten the blocks up against the wall as is there won't be enough clearance for the shelf to hang and fit securely in the blocks properly. Just a word of advice.

I'm not sure if I would recommend this product to anyone because I don't feel for the money plus shipping it's worth a recommendation. Could be and should be cheaper for what it actually is.

Very well made flange. Quality material. I can't believe how much research I did on "flanges" before moving forward on this one because I didn't want to eventually have one that started to look nasty or rusted after just a few weeks of use. Nope!

This one still looks as sharp as the day it was installed. Matches all my other fixtures around the sink area.
Looks great. Arrived in perfect condition. Well packaged (thankfully). More detail than I was expecting.

Exceptional. The one picture doesn't do them any justice. Sturdy steak knives that are sure to last in my opinion (I mean, I hope they last!). The handles are nice and thick, shiny and well constructed so you have something to hold onto finally! Cut's well.

The etching says made in 'Brazil' and I'm happy to offer these to guests or family anytime we're being the carnivores we're meant to be.

Installation: B+
Appearance: A
Quality: A-

Overall, I'm satisfied with the product and like how it looks. Installation took some time to line and level everything up precisely. I hung mine above my fireplace and it looks good. Nice and colorful.

The product itself is great. Five stars.

Only reason I gave it three is because I'm not sure who's doing the shipping and packaging, but they need to be fired. This was placed inside a large box with other items from Amazon and oil was on everything. Luckily, the other items were in boxes too. But, just how unintelligent do you have to be in life to realize that you're throwing OIL inside with other items and don't even bother to wrap it up within a bag or container of some kind as not to leak during shipping? Common sense - not too common anymore folks.

These water jugs are great. I'm surprised at how strong the little handle is. I keep expecting it to snap off when carrying it around, but it hasn't..yet.. I bought two. One for water and one for all my juiciing (fruits/veggies). Well made.

I officially feel like my Grandmother now. Reminded of all the mornings she would boil water on the stove and the whistling sound her kettle made.

This is a nice kettle. Not sure what else there is to say about it. You remove the lid, pour water into it, put the lid back on, place it on the stove, and boil the water inside until you hear it whistle.

I did do what I felt was a little too much research on an item this basic before going with this one. We'll see how long it lasts!

These cables are top notch. I've purchased five of the 15 ft versions and they've worked flawlessly so far.

If I could make a recommendation to anyone running Windows and looking to purchase USB extension cables such as these is to make sure you've gone into your power settings via the control panel and make sure your USB isn't set to power saver mode. Change it to always on, otherwise you'll run into problems.

Highly recommend as a powered USB extender cable.
Works surprisingly well for small projects. However, NOTE.. it will only push 18V phantom power to a condencer mic. Not 48V. That's all its capable of.

users.query: I fell in love with the Hollows series while reading through the shelves of my local library. Now that I have a Kindle I can afford to buy books for myself, so I'm trying to collect the series.

I fell in love with the Hollows series while reading through the shelves of my local library. Now that I have a Kindle I can afford to buy books for myself, so I'm trying to collect the series.
This series of books are light and easy to read, yet the anticipation keeps the books interesting. I'm looking forward to reading more of the series!

This is one of the best series I have ever read. I have most of the books in hardback paper edition and now want to get them in electronic format. I'm looking forward to finding time to read the series again and get the latest book.
Grandson loves the series! To keep him reading, I preorder these books and when they arrive in the mail he reads them.
This is a cute series to read. I'm hoping to get the rest of the books soon to continue the fun!

Light and fun series with fun characters and fun plots. I want to read the entire series but haven't gotten all the books yet. There's always something lurking around the corner to keep the reader guessing.
Cute story! I'm getting other books in this series. It's light and fun.
This was an interesting book that kept me guessing. The characters were quirky and unique. I'm looking forward to reading further installments of this series.

This is a fantastic series of books and I highly recommend them all! So maybe the series is light and not really deep and brain-pounding, but I love the way the author writes, I love the characters, I love the realness of the stories. I need time after reading these books to come out of the story. In other words, I get so caught up I tend to believe I'm there so need a reality check after reading! I could hang with this crowd all the time. I want them for my besties! This particular book takes place in the new venue but it is every bit as alive and fun as the first few in the series. Characters are well rounded, plot is believable, and the comedic antics of some characters makes the book entertaining.
This was an enjoyable book! I am definitely looking forward to finding more in the series. The characters are lovable and you want to root for them from the first sentence.

This is an interesting way to continue a series. Not quite sure if I like it or not. I love the Jack Noble books, and I enjoyed these installments. The episodes end abruptly then pick up immediately, but there's no closure. I'll be getting the next "season" to see where it goes but I would rather be spending time reading a good quality book rather than reading a TV series, because that's more what these episodes feel like.
Fun book! I'm looking forward to more of the series.

I didn't realize when I purchased this set that I already had book 4. So I sort of over purchased here... But the Sloane Monroe series as a whole are great books! Fun to read, keep-you-guessing books.

Fast paced and exciting. I love the series. I haven't been able to read the series in order but the books are good enough that I can catch up with the back story in books that I read ahead, and still enjoy the books I read that came before newer books. The spin-off books are great, too! Toby Neal is a great author.
Christmas gift for grandson. He absolutely loves this book series!
Christmas gift for grandson. He absolutely loves this book series!
I really enjoyed this book. I love the combination of animals and ghosts. There was some drama, and some comedy. Overall a fun book and I will seek out more books in the series.
Fun book. Recommend for light reading. Hope to read more of the series.
This is a great book series. The characters are great! I love the interplay with the ghosts.
This was a fun ghost hunter book. I instantly fell in love with the main characters. The plot twists kept the book moving and fun. The added bonus of the pets was great.
Took longer than anticipated to put together but went together easily. Thought it would radiate heat further out than it does. For what I have planned I'm sure it will work well.
Bought for my grandson. He loves this series! I've preordered most of them for him. I really should read them sometime when I'm visiting.

These are as described by the seller. Cute, small, little light up 3 inch ice cubes. I originally purchased these for a Christmas gift, then changed my mind on giving them to the intended recipient. Now I have 2 sets, and don't know what to do with them! I live in a 2nd story condo, so I don't have a path that needs lit. I'm torn between sending them back (they are still in the box they arrived in nearly a month ago), or finding something to do with them!

The story is good but -- This is a short - very short - story. I was disappointed because no where in the description stated this. I assumed it was a new novel in the series. This was about as long as a chapter (and would make a good first chapter of a book) but then the first book of the series (Solomon vs. Lord) followed. I got this book free. Had I paid money for it I would have returned it.

Had I known it was a short story before acquiring it I would feel different as I would have been expecting a short story not a novel.

users.query: I purchased this as the basis for a Halloween costume and it worked well for what I needed. The material doesn't breathe at all, so I would be hesitant to wear this in any kind of heat or humidity. I am a 14/16 pear shape and it is pretty flattering.

cands.text: I bought this as the basis for a Little John tunic for a Halloween costume.  It worked out really well. It's a really well made, high quality sweatshirt. The material is very soft and thick. My husband stayed very warm on a cold Halloween night!

I purchased this to store old bridesmaid dresses in in our basement. It is a nice size. The downside is the smell. We had to air it out for weeks. When I did put clothes in it the clothes smelled like chemicals and plastic after only one day.
These were really soft, not see through, and warm, but they were really uncomfortable. Im a 14/16 pear shape and the L-XXL was uncomfortably snug. They also weren't as high waisted as I had hoped.

I'm a 14/16 pear shape and have always shied away from skinny jeans, but these are fantastic! The are stretchy, but not too tight. They hold their shape and don't get baggy after a long day of wear. They Have a higher rise so they help hide the post baby tummy. I'm very happy with them!

I am a size XL 14/16 and the XL fit great. The arms are a bit snug, but it's fine across the bust, shoulders, and stomach. I'm 5'9" and its a little shorter than I would prefer. All in all, it's a good costume for the price.

My husband doesnt wear dress shirts often and needs one crisp white shirt on standby for when he does. Hes worn this shirt about a dozen times in the last year and it has been great. It hasn't lost its bright white color, the starched collar and cuffs are still crisp, it was very cost effective, and he says its really comfortable. It is easy to iron and its seems to be a good fabric weight, not too thin. We will be repurchasing this shirt when it needs replacing.

We purchased these for a Flynn Rider costume this Halloween and they were perfect! My husband is 6'3" and they hit right below his knee. They were roomy enough to accommodate his khakis being tucked in and his black dress shoes. He received a ton of compliments on them.

I am a size 14, pear-shaped mom and I have the hardest time finding jeans that fit and don't look like the dreaded "mom jeans." I tried these on a whim and they fit like a dream! I wore them twice all day (6am-10pm) and they held their shape throughout the day and didn't stretch or get a saggy bottom. They fit my waist, hips, and thighs and don't gap at the waistline. There is some flashy embellishment on the pockets, which I don't tend to like, but I've received compliments each time I've worn them.
They are extremely comfortable, but the size 10 is right at the cusp of being too small. I would have sized up to a 10.5 if it was available.

This is a quality American flag. We've had it flying daily for three months in the Midwest heat, humidity, winds, and storms and it still looks brand new. We've had no fading, ripping, or loose threads. I'll definitely buy again when we need to replace our current flag.

We received Dinosaurs Love Underpants for my daughters birthday and she loved that so much we bought Pirates Love Underpants. It didn't disappoint, my daughter loves this as well and it's become one of our staples during reading time. Plus, Ben Cort's illustrations are so vivid and fun.
It fits well and looks good! My husband has been wearing it for about two months and it hasn't faded or stretched out (as some graphic tees will). Highly recommend for any TMNT fan!
This is super cute, but it was way longer than expected. I'm 5'9" and it came down to my knees. As cute as it was, I had to return because it felt like I was wearing a robe.

I ordered a size 14 and these were very tight. I have other Lee jeans and a 14 fits perfectly in other styles. These were tight, short, and very stretchy. I did give 3 stars because I liked the stitching on the back pockets.

This is my new favorite fabric. It's much thicker than regular cotton and would not work well for quilts. I used it for curtains in my daughter's room. I initially was going to line them with a blackout curtain liner, but due to the thickness of the fabric it was unnecessary. The color is a pretty minty green and is true to the picture.
As always, my daughter's Stride Rites are adorable, fit perfectly, and have held up to her high energy antics. She loves her minnie shoes and they look just like the picture.

We just went camping with this lantern and loved it. The dimmer setting was great, it's really bright, very durable, the handle is a good length, and it held up well with a campsite full of excited kids. It wiped clean and didn't acquite any sctapes or scratches.  Although this is simply aesthetics, I loved that it looks like the old propane lanterns. It makes me nostalgic for camping trips from my childhood. I would definitely recommend it.
These are for a jungle themed birthday party. They're cute and will serve their purpose, but began to deflate after a few hours.

I am a size 16 pear shape and was looking for a good pair of high rise compression leggings for jogging. These had a great amount of compression, but they were not a high rise on me. I had to return for a different pair.

I am a size 16 pear shape and was looking for a good pair of high rise compression leggings for jogging. These had a great amount of compression, but they were not a high rise on me. I had to return for a different pair.

I made a small floor pouf (17 inches across and 12 inches tall) for my daughter's room and used this as the filler. It worked great! It's lightweight and has held up to a toddler stepping on it multiple times a day getting in and out of bed. We had more than enough for the pouf and we were able to refill a full sized bean bag chair we have. The beans are made of styrofoam and get everywhere when you're filling. We found that using a peice of paper as a funnel and a paper bowl as a scooper worked the best and prevented the most cling from the beans.

I was looking for a solution to prevent my 2 year old from turning on our gas fireplace. I was looking to replace the switch with a sensor that could only be activated by remote, but wanted to try a cheaper option first. It's been three weeks since installing the cover and it has worked so far! It is easy for adults to maneuver the tab and flip the switch, but it is completely toddler proof! I'm very happy with this switchplate cover.
These were very good looking shoes, but they were huge! I had to return for a smaller size.

This was a gift for my 7 year old nephew and he loves it!

Also, there's a copy if this at the children's reading nook at a local museum and it's the book all the kids wait for and love to read. Big kids read it out loud to the younger kids and there are many smiles, giggles, and rolling-on-the-floor-belly-laughs.
