users.query: Actually, I purchased these to weigh down my pool skimmer basket. Two of them did the trick, and for much less money than the weights marketed for pool skimmers.

cands.text: Considering the price, I was worried about the quality of these. They work great, hold securely, and look good, too.

If I could give zero stars, I would. These worked great up until about a couple of weeks ago, but now both of them have quit working properly -- and they're only 10 months old. They're supposed to flip-flop such that they squeegee rain in both directions. Now they're flipped, but don't flop, so they only squeegee in one direction; in the other direction they scrape or "shovel" resulting in chatter and not cleanly wiping the windshield. I have had Bosch ICON blades in the past that have lasted for years. Needless to say, these will be the last ones I purchase.
Worked great with the Bora 2.25-in Clamp (from Lowes). A little bit of a hassle to assemble (not great instructions), but that's a one-time proposition.
Product was far too short for the deep drawers where I wanted to used them. I sent them back.
My Reef flip-flops are started to get long in the tooth. I tried on a friend's Crocs (just my size) and loved them. These immediately went onto my Christmas list, and I love them.
The reason for four stars is because the description implies that it is a Hayward-branded product. It isn't, but it works just as described and is much cheaper than the Hayward product.

This is a well made product, but unfortunately it did not work for me. The mounting brackets are tall and, with 8' ceilings, 4" crown molding, and 3" door trim, they simply would not fit. I worked with the seller trying alternative mounting solutions, but none would work. The seller was very cooperative in allowing me to return the item for full refund. I would like to emphasize that, given the correct circumstances (e.g., 9' ceilings or no crown molding), this would be an excellent product and I regret that it did not work in my situation. Also, to the seller's credit, since my purchase the description of the door on Amazon has now been greatly enhanced to reflect the door's dimensions, specifications, and limitations.
Perfect fit for my Stihl BR380 backpack blower. Good price, too.

Great value and quick delivery. Can't give 5 stars because I have no idea if they really work: like trying to prove a negative, I guess I will only be able to tell if they do NOT work, which I hope never happens.
Needed a replacement for an old one that broke, and this did the trick.
Needed an inexpensive gym bag (not an overnight bag; not a backpack). Nothing fancy, but it's just what I wanted. Great price, too.

This product is worthless. I have tried, twice, to use it to jump start my motorcycle and it failed both times (I ended up having to use conventional jumper cables to start it with my car, whereby it fired right up). This is not a large bike (750cc) and the battery was not completely dead, just weak (the Weego, conversely, had a full charge). Unfortunately, this is the type of product that you use when needed; and when I needed it, it was beyond the date when I could return for a refund. What good is it if it cannot be trusted in a time of need? Since I am stuck with it, maybe I can use it to power/charge my cell phone.

Because of its size it has its limitations. But for its intended purpose it is a great tool, and its smaller size is also precisely why I wanted it (why drag out a full size radial saw when this light weight beast will accomplish the task). I wish I had bought one sooner.
Worked great. Price not great, but competitive with big-box stores (Lutron must control the pricing).

The clamping part is OK, but difficult to adjust and hardly "quick release." It needs to be unscrewed (many, many rotations) to open the jaws enough to fit around the bar, then screwed back in (again, many times) to tighten the jaws loosley. Then, and only then, the clamp tightens firmly; unfortunately, this pretty much relegates it to a permanent mount, and certainly not a quick release (about the only "quick" thing is that no tools are required). Nonetheless, once secured it has the potential for being a nice mount. However, the camera-style tripod mount would not tighten enough to keep the camera from moving (pivoting) slightly; the knurled disk adjustment knob (standard on camera tripod mounts) should screw up to the bottom of the camera to prevent it from turning, but even when it was screwed as far as it would go there was a slight gap between it and the camera body. All in all, it makes a good clamp for stationary use (thus 3 stars instead of 2), but not enough stability for a moving vehicle.

The strap itself works GREAT. Unfortunately, there is no way to pivot the mount. If your handlebars are perpendicular to the line of sight you're recording, then it's fantastic. Otherwise, you'll need to get a ball mount or swivel to augment it.
I have several of these with the shorter shank, and they have all performed well. This one, so far, works equally as well.
Works great for when I need to stream a lot of data.
Excellent product, and inexpensive, too. Sometimes you don't need to use a full size pan, and this does the trick.
Works well; fits well; easy installation; good price; quick delivery.
This is my third pair of Rocket Dogs and I love them. They're comfortable, stylish and fit great.
This is exactly the same model as my existing thermostat which quit working. This one replaced it perfectly, and was considerably cheaper than anywhere else I found.
Read three of the four; so far, so good. Not Raymond Chandler, but who is?

users.query: Jake Grafton and Tommy Carminelli lead the fight against Chinese espionage. The story's introduction moves slowly but after several chapters, murder and mayhem dominate. Our bloated bureaucracy blocks effective anti-terrorist activities and frustrates the reader, but current world events make good reading.

cands.text: I have read all of Coonts' stories in the Jake Grafton series, so I can rate his efforts. Tommy Carmellini provides humor to a very serious plot, a president's attempted take-over of the United States. From the outset, we read of ISIS atrocities and conclude with more murder and mayhem. With the character of Jake Grafton & other patriots, Coonts wants to inspire readers to prevent the horror he describes.

Book #2 in Jake Adams series has some humor & some mystery as the hero, a former CIA operative, in his new PI role fights terrorists in Ukraine and Kurdestan. Mystery centers on who the terrorists are and what the new toxic weapon is.

Beijing Red is an interesting and entertaining account of a former SEAL's attempt to donate his time and efforts in China. Nick Foley becomes immersed in a Russian attempt to buy a super weapon from a renegade Chinese scientist. Alex Ryan writes well enough for me to try another of his books, but I wasn't thrilled with the evil he depicted in Beijing Red.

Scott McEwen shows clearly the political corruption and societal chaos of 21st century Mexico while continuing his detailing of CIA black ops. Also part of the plot is the tale of veterans of the Iraq & Afghanistan wars. Aside from vulgar language and lots of violence, readers learn a lot while being entertained by non-stop action.

Jake Adams teams up with CIA girl friend, Toni Contari to protect scientists who have discovered new elixir to prevent heart attacks. As usual Trevor Scott centers most of the action away from the US; this time Jake fights evil and greed in the Austrian and Italian Alps.

Jake Adams continues free lancing efforts to stop international espionage in Russia, China, and Korea. Even though Jake is an action hero, he always shows his scientific prowess; Vital Force highlights world powers' efforts to lead in  advanced laser technology

"Fatal Network" is the best of the six books in the series I've read because it seems more believable. Jake Adams, a former AF intelligence officer and CIA operative, is a PI commissioned by an Oregon computer company to investigate internal security problems in Germany. Former lover and CIA operative, Toni Contardi, appears and works capably with Jake.
John Clark, Ryan Jr, and the Office fend off various terrorist plots while hampered by a feckless POTUS and his administration.. You learn how patient and innovative jihadists can be.

Marc Cameron's research into Chinese political structure, his investigation of human trafficking, and his knowledge of places like Buenos Aires make his edition of Tom Clancy's Power & Empire top notch. Cameron kept President Jack Ryan's character in tact as well as the personality of Jack, Jr, John Clark, et al. Most importantly, Marc Cameron wove a suspenseful tale combining Chinese perfidy and the ugly issue of human trafficking.

In this Jake Mahegan novel, the hero responds to a request from one of his former military buddies and becomes embroiled in an attack on a school and kidnapping. As has been the case in A.J. Tata's previous six novels, the protagonist is accompanied by strong women. In Besieged, Jake has help from a nurse who is also a surfer. However, the exciting plot centers on autonomous cars which are coordinated with autonomous "planes." Iranian terrorists provide non-stop dramatic tension which includes a youthful autistic savant.
Coonts provides perspective into Naval air efforts in Vietnam War. Good history and drama come through eyes of Lt. Jake Grafton.
Coonts dramatizes the bumbling efforts of U.S. as Soviet spies and treasonous Americans work to steal secrets. Coonts presents a believable account of burocratic ineptitude.

With each successive novel, Nathan Goodman becomes a better writer. His dialog contains more humor which relieves the tension of the plot dealing with a huge terrorist event. Jana and her two male friends are challenged by a complex series of domestic and foreign agents.  Both the  FBI and NSA try valiantly to stop the jihadis' plan to set off a nuclear device.

Mark Greaney captures 2016 headlines with his fictional account of a foreign hacker's and ISIS's damage to US government workers. Greaney bases the plot on the actual hacking of government workers' personnel files. President Jack Ryan as well as agent Jack Ryan, Jr. and his team work to discover the foreign hacker's identity and stop horrific ISIS assassinations. Greaney has created one of the best Clancy-sequels ever.

As Nathan Goodman introduces his protagonist, readers become interested in the business whiz, Jana Baker, who becomes an undercover help for the FBI. She risks her life in the effort to stop an immigrant family from a world-wide terrorist event. Goodman presents his heroine as a normal middle-class 23 year old who energetically pursues a business or an investigative goal. I decided to order the entire series.

In this 5th book in the Tracie Tanner series, she infiltrates the USSR to uncover the plot behind Polonium-250 used to cruelly kill CIA agents. Tanner must uncover the KGB agents and scientist involved as well as eradicate them. Tracie confronts both physical and psychological burn-out by the end of this assignment, both of which help readers understand the challenges of those who protect their nations from foreign intrigue.

With House of Spies, Daniel Silva continues his Gabriel Allon series, but readers do not have to have read any of the previous books to enjoy Silva's research and writing skills. The author asserts that all characters and events are fictitious, but informed readers would recognize terrorist attacks in England as similar to what Silva portrays. Since I devour novels about our military heroes and terrorism, I can compare/ contrast House of Spies with others in the genre. Silva provides great in depth information about MI6, the CIA, and Israel's Office which Gabriel Allon now heads, so readers learn intricate details about anti-terrorist activities.  Silva also combines dramatic tension with humor, so his books are a fun read!

Even though Three Minutes to Midnight is the second in the Jake  Mahegan series, readers are skillfully woven into the hero's backhtound. A.J. Tata presents a frightening scenario where Jake Mahegan's assignment in to find a missing geology professor/army captain who has just returned from a year in Afghanistan. As with the other 5 Tata novels I have read, the plot is full of surprises. The author develops his characters well and at the end of a book, I order a sequel because the family or character is a friend. A.J. Tata, a retired general, also impresses me with his portrayal of female characters who are realistic and modern.

Dewey Andreason heads a team to stop a war between India and Pakistan. Ben Coes knows international intrigue and his protagonist becomes an even more appealing hero as he leaves his self-imposed exile down-under to help put out fire in Middle East.

Coes knows government and current events. He also spotlights his writing skills as his protagonist experiences yet another heart-breaking loss. This novel, like the previous three Andreas books, informs the reader; this time we go inside China and see this nation's tentacles reaching around the world.

I am now reading Clean Kill, the sequel to Dead Shot, because I loved it. I especially appreciate Coughlin's knowledge of being a sniper. He portrays the lonely existence  and anguish of the trade. I respect the writing of Sgt Jack Coughlin and his co-author, their use of metaphor, simile, etc. Dead Shot allowed me to get into the head of an Englishman who turned against western society and its values because of his ethnic and religious background. Another facet of the Kyle Swanson series that I, a woman, value is the strong women who work with the hero or are his friend or beloved. Jack Coughlin and his co-writer are adept at portraying strong female characters.

Dr. Carson presents a different perspective on people's personal problems and their solutions as well as national issues in order to help our country. He also tells about his childhood and how his single mother convinced his brother and him to strive for an education to improve themselves. Both autobiographical facts and philosophical information are readable and useful.

Sam and Remi Fargo fight evil (corporate as usual) as they explore historical sites. Cussler provides non-stop action as well as historical and geographical information. I am a Clive Cussler devotee and recommend any of his well-written books.
Lilting poetry and lovely illustrations add to the objective presentation of America's presidents from Washington through Obama.

Ben Coes sets this Dewey Andreas thriller in both Syria and the US. Coes allows readers to see the sick mind of  an ISIS leader. The action is not just gripping but realistic and the plot is contemporary.

users.query: They are exactly what we wanted.  Can see better at night.  Not to difficult to install.

cands.text: I absolutely loved how this series played out.  The dynamic of these 4 people is great.  It has some totally hot games played.  I could read this over again and not be bored.  Definitely worth buying the bundle.

Cute!  Spencer and Charlotte are super hot!  They really do burn up the pages.  It was also great to see that the woman straight up told him what she wanted.  And the drama at the end was not what I was expecting it to be.  I was quite happy with how the story ended.  I love how Spencer would remember all these little things about Charlotte and things that she liked, but he didn't think much about it.  I am super glad that he was not too stubborn to admit his feelings.

This is a whole new take on the series.  Now you get the POV from Connor and Rose.  They are quite the interesting couple.  You finally get to see into their mind after hearing Lily and Los thoughts about them.  The whole clan is now in a reality show.  They are followed around by cameras for 6 months and Daisy and Ryke also end up moving in with them.  The producer also moves in with them and makes everyone think that he was Roses ex-boyfriend.  He was in it to cause as much drama as possible.  Lily and Lo are supposed to get married, but the fact that it is being forced on her is making Lilys anxiety through the roof.  Rose is working on getting her fashion line back on track, a few scandals have cause the line some issues.  She is also dealing with planning Lilys wedding, working on the reality show, and working through her own anxiety regarding her relationship with Connor.  She was too independent and had to work on letting another person in, relinquishing control.  And Connor is a control freak!  Genius, controlling, and arrogant.  They have these arguments that are hilarious.  Things most people would never even thing about.

I still love these characters and am totally loving that the series keeps going.  So I will continue on to the next one

So great that my eyes are killing me!  My only complaint was that it seemed to drag on in some parts.  But as with any good book, it ignited very strong emotion in my. I cried in some places and got very angry....  Some may think that there was too much back and forth with Nicholas and his feelings.  But in reality men were that stubborn, so it was fairly realistic
I just love this series.  It's always something with these old Anderson men.  But seriously... Where can I find a job with all the benefits they offer???

Since I had already read the first 2 books in the series I already knew this was going to be an emotional book.  Right from the beginning it was bringing tears to my eyes talking about Janie's attack.  But I loved the story of 2 broken people working to heal each other.  And really.... could Cullen get any hotter???  His fears on hurting Janie is just about the sweetest.  I feel like the pie to the face was a masterful touch to the story.  But the question that I still have is did they move in together???
Still another great story in the Girl Series......

I can honestly say that I love these books.  I have become so in love with these characters that I can wait to read the next books.  I love that its not a happily ever after, but more like a work in progress.  I think that Lily and Lo are so realistic that they really could be any one of us.  And they are working to make it work because they love each other.  I know some people just want the romance and fairy tale endings... I like happy ending books too... but these can give hope to people who have any kind of issues that they are working through to make their happy ending. Now I am excited to go on and read about Conner and Ryke.... I love how they just inserted themselves into Lily and Lo's lives.  It continues to be a series that I enjoy.  The emotions that come from their lives, their problems are real for me.  I have found myself crying at their sadness, their happiness, their triumphs and their failures.  I am constantly cheering them on and I will continue to do so as long as the series goes

Borrowed this from the library... I read the French Quarter about a year ago.... loved it.  Thought I needed to read this one too.... I am currently on Key West.  These are some of the hottest books ever!  Im not at all into some of the things that are played out in the scenes, but they still seem so hot!  Lets just day that my husband is usually quite happy after I have been reading Lacey's books!

.....that I have to wait nearly 6 months to see how it turns out!!!

After one review I read I was concerned that I was going to end up not liking it. I should have known better.

Yes, Donovan's hot and cold got frustrating. Sabrina's back and forth got annoying. But that is what makes it a story. Not everyone had an easy path to love...and we sure wouldn't be buying books with such an easy story.

I think it was another fantastic example of the great writing and story telling Laurelin Paige has been giving us and I am eagerly awaiting September when I can get back to their story!!!

I enjoyed this series.  I would have to say that the first one was my actual favorite.  I kinda liked the back and forth between Nate and Erin.  Sometimes, though, I felt like the writer was trying to hard to make it seem more like the men were talking like "men" with each other.  I know that they usually speak to other men different than when a female is around, but I really don't think it goes as far as it was portrayed in these books.  Other than that I enjoyed reading the series, and my heart broke in Ring of Fire like Im sure many others did.  I would buy other books from this author.  Although I will probably wait to make sure that there isn't going to be a box set with another story that cant be purchased  alone.

Wow!  Callie and Reid are super hot!  Hooking up with someone you work with is always a risky move.  Especially when the object of you lust has the managerial job you want!  But that sure doesn't stop Reid from getting together with Callie.  That is, until he finds out that he has a shot at taking that managerial job from her.  I won't get into all the details, because that would take away from your enjoyment of the book.  Its an enemies-to-lovers story.... then they go back to enemies.  Reid screws up really bad, but Callie was still willing to put herself out there to get the guy back.... but he just got himself in deeper and deeper.  These 2 really frustrated me!  But the effort that Reid finally puts into trying to win her back is just the sweetest!   I really did love this story.  It was a great read with some hot spots and not too much angst issues involved.... I really loved Callie and Reid!  I was sad to see their story end.

Absolutely wonderful!!!  The return of Hudson and Alayna was everything I hoped it would be!  I always wonder what "happily ever after" looks like for some of my favorite couples.  We have gotten to see little pieces of theirs in the other books from the Fixed universe.  Getting another full length book on them was fantastic.  It was a reminder that even "happily ever after" requires work and compromise.  This was a very suspenseful book that constantly had me thinking.  Hudson was receiving threats against his family, and he did the typical Hudson things.  He should know that trying to keep things from Alayna doesn't work... she snoops into everything!  Hudson starts digging into his past so that he can try to figure out who is sending these threats.  The story sends you into different directions of who you may think that it is.... and when I found out who it was I was SHOCKED!
This book didn't break my heart into a million pieces like the other "Fixed" books.  This does not mean that it did not elicit feeling from me.  I was so happy reading about the life they were building.  I was SO proud of how Alayna was handling the task of getting into Hudson's past.  At one point there is a conversation when Hudson is telling Alayna that he had a snapshot kind of dream of what their future was.... as he was describing the future he saw them having I was smiling  like a total goober with some seriously happy tears trying not to fall from my eyes.  It showed how far Hudson had come from the man that did not believe in love!
Another spectacular Fixed book that everyone who loves Hudson and Alayna need to read!  You will not be disappointed!!!

This book was super hyped up with in reader groups on Facebook.  So I decided I needed to see what the fuss was about.  I was not disappointed!

This is a story of 2 people, Ana and Kevin, as they struggle to deal with their sexual preferences.  They are neighbors.  They find, as friends (both 16), that they see something in each other and become best friends because they can completely be themselves.  Eventually it progresses into experimenting with each other.  After some time they ended up having a falling out and went their separate ways.  She comes back home toward the end of college and they end up being best friends again and then again progress to lovers.

This book has so much more than just a lot of hot sex.  They have a real friendship.  They have relationships with other people.  They have other real life problems. And along with it all is the constant fear that some one will find out what kind of kinky things they are up to in the bedroom.  I loved that they took turns feeling the severe insecurity of it all.  I love that no matter how much Ana runs from him, Kevin is always there for her.  I cried so many times.  My stomach was constantly in knots.  I laughed at their banter. At times my heart was racing, and stayed that way for 15-20 minutes after I put the book down!  And I did not want to put it down.  I was sad to see it end because I would loved to have spent more time with Kevin and Ana!

There was most definitely a lot to the story of Lincoln and Quinn.  I felt like she had been through so much.  The secrets that were between them were all HUGE!  And it is totally understandable why they kept these things to themselves.  Had they not kept these secrets then they may not have broken up for that 7 years.  (but then that wouldn't have made a very good story).  I totally hated Kellen and was not at all sad to see him get what he deserved (especially with the things he was saying to Lincoln about Quinn).  I think that Quinn had to have been a very strong woman to have dealt with Kellen the way that she was.  I really enjoyed this books.  I loved the story line and loved the characters (for the most part).  I would even read it again.

I thought this was a pretty good story.  I fell in love with the characters right from the beginning.  I wasn't expecting for Ty to be the one to fall so easily.  I thought Kendall was a pretty well written character.  Personally I love that she had ambition and was conflicted about "sacrificing" her dream because she had fallen in love.  Dreams can always change.  Plus the idea of sticking it to the mean girls from school days is always fun to think about.  Overall I felt like it was a good story with a great ending.

I love Spencer.  I love Brandon.  I love that these books are from both points of view, but separately so it wasn't confusing.  I will not ever be able to hear those songs again without imagining the couple how I see them in my mind.  I will totally stick with this author.

Getting into this book was a little slow for me, mostly because I am really not into fighting all that much.  But just like Hazel I was pulled in by Knox's eyes (or at least the description of them).  The connection between these 2 was so intense that I could feel it!
Hazel doesn't let too many people get close to her.  She has dealt with a lot of loss and tries to avoid making connections as much as possible.  Then came Knox.  He pulled her in with his charm and cockiness.  Once he had her, he was not letting her push him away.  Hazel feels like their connection gets too strong too fast, so Knox agrees to slow it down.  Since she was traveling they texted, talked on the phone and did Face time.  But when she needed him, he dropped everything  to be by her side.  There are some sad moments.  There are some funny moments.  There are absolutely some hot moments.  There are some suspenseful moments.  I went through all kinds of feelings while reading this book, but boredom was NOT one of them!

I normally don't get into the paranormal romances.  But this one was pretty good.  Very HOTT!  Kinda made me want a Fire witch of my own.  And I have to say that I was NOT suprised by the mole in the story, I was just shocked that someone else wasn't in on it with her.  At first the story seems to move kind of slow, but when it picked up I couldn't put it down!

It was dark and depressing.  It made me cry like crazy.  I had a hard time keeping myself reading it, but then I also didn't want to put it down.  Mira is a VERY troubled young lady.  I really feel like Six was pretty good for her in the beginning.  There were many things that he did and said that I really thought were not very helpful to their situation.  But then he would be so sweet and caring.  He is really hard to get a read on. Especially since you are getting everything from Mira's POV which is slightly off due to her mental illness.  I love these characters and the worst part of this story is reading about all the struggles they face.  The thoughts that go through her head when she is feeling her worst!  Its all very heart breaking!  I want to say that I loved this book, but I really cant "love" anything that dark and depressing.  So I will honestly say that it is a great story.  Absolutely one worth reading!  I am very much looking forward to the conclusion of Mira's story.

Lily and Loren are both addicts.  Lily is addicted to sex, Loren to alcohol.  They depend on each other to enable their behaviors.  For years they keep to themselves so that they hide these addictions from their family.  They start to allow people into their lives, becoming friends with them.  Thats when it all starts to come out.  Lo doesnt do too good of a job hiding his drinking from their new friends.  Lo finds out some other things about his life that he had no clue about.  The story ends on a cliffhanger with Lo leaving Lily behind to battle her own addiction while he goes off to rehab.
This is the first book in a multiple book series.  It is a great introduction to the main characters that you will hear so much more about over the next many books.  I fell in love with them all and love to read about them over and over again.  I have now even listed to the audio, and it is fantastic!

I really don't think that I could have loved this book any more!  Evie is a goddess!  Abel is a tortured, yet totally lovable, soul.  I love the time span of this book.  Since it starts out when they are so young, I was really reminded of how potent young love can be.  The things that you do with your love when sex is not yet something you are ready for.  I would image, as a writer, that is a difficult thing to toe the line of without making some people angry.  (Saffron does a fantastic job of this!!!)  There were more than one occasion that I found myself tearing up or just out right crying!  I love how Evie sees in Abel what everyone else refuses to acknowledge.  Their love is absolutely the stuff of legends!  They both love with their whole heart.  Despite what they are facing, they don't seem to lose faith in each other. Even when it seems like they may be losing faith in them self!
5 stars is not enough to rate this story and all of the emotions it pulled out of me.  I felt joy, sadness, anger, confusion, and of coarse I was turned on!  Saffron knows just how much angst to put in there without it becoming too much! I was on the edge of my seat through the whole story just waiting to see what would try to pull them apart!  I only wish that I could have spent more time in Evie and Abel's world.  I really did not want to stop reading about them.

I was not the hugest fan of this book.  I thought that the idea was great but I kind of feel like there was too much going on.  Finley was a student who thought a guy was attractive.  Turned out that he was her teacher, Cabel Jones.  They end up running off together to get away from some people that are after them.  But then it turns out that they are really just after him.  Then while they are staying together she gets hurt, she is a bit whiny and doesn't listen to what she is told at all!  In a life threatening situation you would think that after the first 2 times she messed up while not doing as she was told would have taught her to listen.  But really there was just too much going on and went through it really quickly.  I don't know what the second book is about, but I kind of feel like this one on its own could have been made into 2 books with how much drama/action there was.  It was not a terrible book.  But for me it felt like there was too much and it was being rushed through.

Elle meets Sinclair on the plane to Mexico.  There was instant flames!  They start a super hot holiday affair.  It was a great story of their time together.  I fell in love with this couple that was not supposed to fall in love with each other.  I am so excited to get into The Secret to see what happens with them!!!

Where we left off, Diana was determined to get Adam to love her again.  He can't love her if she is a sub, but she can't love him unless he is dominant.  Now I am not sure why they couldn't figure out how to make this work earlier.  (besides the fact that the book would be significantly shorter)  So basically they have to work their way to the happy medium... compromise and honesty are key to a great marriage.  I really kept thinking that the book was not going to turn out with the ending that I wanted.  I thought that there was something that was going to happen to piss me off..... But I can honestly say that I loved this book.... everything went exactly the way that it should.  This was the first time I read C.D. Reiss (the duet was my first by her).  I will definitely read her work again.

users.query:
The Conventions and Craft: Grade 4 Teachers Kit by Scholastic is a good structured plan for Grammer, Sentence Structure, and Word Study for Fourth Graders.  The set comes with five books, one collection of magazine articles for kids to read, and a teachers guide.  The guide has a year long lesson plan based around a ten month school enrollment period and is broken down into five main categories with multiple subcategories of lessons within those five main lessons.  Within each sublesson, the teaching material is broken down into five days of instruction.  Day one focuses on studying the mentor text (the books listed), day two is modeling the target understanding, day three is analyzing the student's writings,  day four is inviting application, and day five focuses on review of the subject matter.  There are many examples on how to introduce the works to the kids, how to encourage the kids to talk about what they learned and how it applies to what they read, and how to utilize what they learned in writing of their own.  The subject matter is broken down as listed below:

Power Up Grammer
1. Lift Descriptions with Adjective and Adverbs
2.  Control Verb Tenses
3.  Spark wonder with Abstract Nouns
4.  Connect Pronouns with Antecedents
5.  Maintain Subject-Verb Agreement

Build Strong Sentences
1.  Create Simple Sentences
2.  Distinguish Complete Sentences & Fragments
3.  Create Compound Sentences
4.  Create Complex Sentences: Introductory Element
5.  Insert Appositives to Rename or Explain
6.  Insert Closers to Add Information
7.  Enhance Imagery with -ing Words
8.  Consider Prepositions as Sentence Openers
9.  Consider Adverbs as Setence Openers
10.  Speak to Readers with Imperatives and "You"
11.  Create Flow with Linking Words and Phrases
12.  Vary Sentence Beginnings
13.  Craft Strong Leads
14.  Group Ideas into Paragraphs
15.  Craft Strong Concluding Statements

Expand Word Knowledge
1.  Select Precise Words and Phrases
2.  Choose Words and Phrases for Effect
3.  Integrate Compound Descriptors
4.  Reach for Persuasive Language
5.  Indentify Commonly Confused Words
6.  Evoke Imagery with Words and Phrases
7.  Create Images with Similies and Metaphors
8.  Understand Root Words and Affixes
9.  Select Powerful Verbs
10.  Choose Just-Right Synonyms and Antonyms

Master Punctuation and Capitalization
1.  Punctuate for Effect
2.  Use Commas: Phrases in a Series
3.  Use Commas: Clauses and Linking Words
4.  Create Contradictions and Possessives

Edit Like an Expert
1.  Reread to Clarify and Edit
2.  Practice Spelling Conciousness
3.  Use Layout and Spacing in Interesting Ways
4.  Using and Editing Checklist

This book also includes and appendix that feature support pages for the learning material such as a page listing all of the conjunctions (for and nor but or yet so), commonly confused words (are our hour, by bye, buy, etc), assessment tools such as editing checklists and self assessments, as well as record keeping tools for teachers on how well the students are progressing.  For those who are looking for a teaching guide that includes printable worksheets or a variety of activities to teach the material, this set does not come with those materials.  The model for learning with this set revolves a lot around having the students working together to identify the issues with the sample writings, and with teachers reviewing the students free writing.  Overall, I found this set to be good for both homeschooling and classroom teaching environments, but found the material to be a bit too redundant in teaching style and a bit too structured.  With books this short in length and limited to the six books and fourteen 1-2 page magazine articles, I would imagine the kids would get bored quickly unless you supplement with other reading and teaching materials.  Overall, this is a good basis for teaching grammar, sentence structure, and writing, but I would definitely supplement with other resources as well to keep things interesting.
