The Conventions and Craft: Grade 1 Teachers Kit by Scholastic is a good structured plan for Grammer, Sentence Structure, and Word Study for First Graders. The set comes with six paperback book, one collection of magazine articles for kids to read, and a teachers guide. The guide has a year long lesson plan based around a ten month school enrollment period and is broken down into five main categories with multiple subcategories of lessons within those five main lessons. Within each sublesson, the teaching material is broken down into five days of instruction. Day one focuses on studying the mentor text (the books listed), day two is modeling the target understanding, day three is analyzing the student's writings, day four is inviting application, and day five focuses on review of the subject matter. There are many examples on how to introduce the works to the kids, how to encourage the kids to talk about what they learned and how it applies to what they read, and how to utilize what they learned in writing of their own. The subject matter is listed down below:

Getting Started
1.  Say the Message, Write the Message
2.  Visualize and Draw before Writing
3.  Spell Phonetically
4.  Include All the Words in a Message
5.  Watch Word Spacing
6.  Use the Entire Page

Build Strong Sentences
1. Write Complete Sentences
2.  Expand Short Sentences
3.  Create Compound Sentences
4.  Capture Attention with Exclamatory Sentences
5.  Vary Sentence Beginnings
6.  Vary Sentence Lengths
7.  Craft Strong Leads
8.  Craft Strong Conclusions.

Power Up Grammar and Word Knowledge
1.  Use Adjectives to Add Details
2.  Create Action with Powerful Verbs
3.  Convey Shades of Meaning
4.  Create Voice with Onomatopoeia
5.  Show Order with Temporal Words
6.  Use Comparatives
7.  Build Connections with Prepositions
8.  Form Plural Nowns
9.  Show Ownership with Possessive Pronouns
10.  Maintain Subject Verb Agreement
11.  Control Verb Tenses
12.  Understand Personal Pronouns
13.  Follow Pronoun Order
14.  Include Demonstratives
15.  Understand Compound Words and Words with Affixes
16.  Identify Root Words and Endings

Master Punctuation and Capitalization
1.  Use Question Marks in Interrogative Sentences
2.  Capitalize Proper Nouns
3.  Use Commas in a Series
4.  Use Apostrophes to Create Possessive Nouns

Edit Like an Expert
1.  Use Layout and Spacing in Interesting Ways
2.  Reread for Each Editing Point
3.  Use Syllabication for Spelling
4.  Take Advantage of Resources

This book also includes and appendix that feature support pages for the learning material such as a page listing all of the conjunctions (for and nor but or yet so), commonly confused words (are our hour, by bye, buy, etc), assessment tools such as editing checklists and self assessments, as well as record keeping tools for teachers on how well the students are progressing. For those who are looking for a teaching guide that includes printable worksheets or a variety of activities to teach the material, this set does not come with those materials. The model for learning with this set revolves a lot around having the students working together to identify the issues with the sample writings, and with teachers reviewing the students free writing. Overall, I found this set to be good for both homeschooling and classroom teaching environments, but found the material to be a bit too redundant in teaching style and a bit too structured. With books this short in length and limited to the six books and fourteen 1-2 page magazine articles, I would imagine the kids would get bored quickly unless you supplement with other reading and teaching materials. Overall, this is a good basis for teaching grammar, sentence structure, and writing, but I would definitely supplement with other resources as well to keep things interesting.

We purchased the Scholastic 3rd Grade Workbook from our local warehouse store.  So far, I've found the Scholastic 3rd Grade workbook to be a good resource in getting your child prepared academically for the next grade, or to supplement the work they are currently doing in 3rd grade.  Unlike other "grade level" workbooks, this workbook is completely divided by subject.  Activities are not spread out, there is no determined starting page (you can start on the Grammar Section which starts on page 164 vs at the beginning of of the book which focuses on Reading Comprehension).  Each lesson is clearly labeled at the top corner of the page, are brightly illustrated, and fairly well through out.  The workbook covers multiple subjects, and even features a full section of Contemporary Cursive, something some schools are not teaching.

For the curious, this workbook goes over Reading Comprehension, Tests on Reading, Contemporary Cursive, Grammar, Writing, Maps, Addition and Subtraction, and Math.  I've included photos of the table of contents in my review so you can see the individual topics covered under these headers.

I liked how this workbook has a variety of activities in it, and how the activity pages were not just filled with extraneous pictures and glaring blank spots.  The Reading Comprehension pages required the kids to actually read full pages before answering questions, and the mathematics pages had a good amount of math problems to solve, but were not "drilling" type pages.  Each page is easy to tear out, should you want to make smaller packets for your kids to do by themselves, and if your kid is the type who needs encouragement, there are stickers at the end of the book for you to give out.  Note - unlike the lower level workbooks, there is NO certificate to give your kid at the end to celebrate completing this book.  I'm not sure if your kid needs the certificate, but if you do, you will need to print your own certificate out yourself.

No kid enjoys workbooks, but the Spectrum Critical Thinking for Math Workbook will help said kid reinforce their math skill for 6th grade.  If your kid is having difficulty with 6th grade made, is looking forward to what is going to be learned in 6th grade, or needs a summer bridge book from 6th to 7th grade, this book will help address those issues.  The workbook is broken up into seven main chapters:

1. Number Systems and Operations
2. Multiplying and Dividing Fractions
3. Ratios, Rates, and Percents
4. Integer Concepts
5. Expressions and Equations
6. Geometry
7. Probability and Statistics

The problems are well laid out, and each sub-lesson includes an example of a completed problem at the top of the page with some explanation.  There is plenty of space for problems to be worked out without sacrificing the number of problems per page, and the solutions at the end of the book include the solving steps, so your kid can check their answers themselves - or if you're a parent who forgot how to work out these problems, you got help, too!  Overall, this is a very useful tool in helping your kid better understand mathematics in 6th grade.

I purchased the Scholastic 2nd Grade Workbook from our local warehouse store before summer began.  I picked up a 1st Grade workbook along with this book for my younger kid.  Sadly to say, this book fell really short of my expectations.  The biggest problem I had with this book is that there were multiple pages throughout this book that were exactly the same as the 1st Grade book.  We're talking the exact same page - just in different locations throughout the book.  To add insult to injury, our warehouse store had packaged this book along with a Scholastic Summer Bridge 1st-2nd Grade book, which again featured the SAME PAGES in the Summer Bridge book.  Really, Scholastic?  That's lazy on so many levels.

At the end of the day, if you get this book as a stand alone book, you'll be pleased with it.  The 2nd Grade book covers a large variety of topics, penmanship, grammar, reading comprehension, and mathematics.  The activities are age appropriate, well detailed, and the printing/illustrations are appealing.  The workbook comes with reward stickers, should your kid want them, but does not come with a reward certificate at the end , so if your kid wants the cert, you'll have to make one yourself.  Personally, I would not suggest getting this book along with a Summer Bridge 1st-2nd Grade nor would I purchase the 1st Grade Book since many of the activities are essentially the same.

As a fan of workbooks for the kids over the summer, I was interested in introducing the 5th Grade Math Common Core Workbook to my kid.  Unfortunately, as a stand alone workbook for Grade 5 Math, this book fell woefully short.  First off, because I did not get the "Free Response" workbook, I can't review on how effective this book would be with the accompanying book.  Each page consists of 4-6 math problems.  Each problem is separated into it's own box, and each box is multiple choice.  There is little to no space for kids to work out the problems, no explanation or examples on how to solve each problem, and while there are QR codes to view a teacher teaching the weekly set of problems, the guidance and teaching wasn't all that great.  While I was able to explain to my kid on how to do these problems, as well as supplemented him with a notebook to work out the problems in, I would've liked to offer him something he could've worked on by himself that is self contained in one workbook.

Overall, this wouldn't be my first choice in mathematics workbooks for kids.  The format is lacking, the multiple choice answering was unnecessary, and there really needs to be more space for problems to be solved in.

First off, Kumon should have just combined the "Are You Ready series" cutting and pasting skills into one book. I bought the Pasting Skills and Scissors Skills workbooks in a two pack from Costco. While the scissor skills book is pretty good because many of the activities can be done by the child alone, the Pasting Skills missed the mark because half of the project must be completed by the parent (unless your kid is really good with scissors, that is). Unlike the other cutting skills book, the lines that are around the shapes are very, very thin. Unless your kid is very proficient at using scissors, many will not be able to cut out these shapes easily. Kumon really wants the kids to focus on one thing...pasting and ONLY pasting. My 4 year old son, whom has no problems cutting out shapes from the other Kumon series books, had a much harder time trying to cut out these pencil thin lines. This is not a bad thing to give something more challenging to your child, but for my daughter who is not as proficient with scissors, it was downright frustrating for her. She hated having to wait for me to cut everything out, and got upset when she tried to cut these thin lines and ended up butchering the tiny shapes. A better pasting book is the Play and Grow: Cutting and Pasting Paper (Play & Grow Workbook). With that workbook, you get things for your child to cut out, then paste into the book. There is also a story included with each project. One thing my kids did like about this book was that there were puzzles to glue together. Again, you will have to cut it out, otherwise the puzzle will not look that great. The paper stock for this workbook is thin and shiny, which makes it okay to paste, but definitely something you will need to cut out. All in all, there are better activity books available from Kumon...I would pass on this until your child is older and highly proficient with scissors.

I really can't praise Kumon enough - the simple progression these workbooks go through really help child garner the skills they need while still making it fun.  The first few projects were really simple - just cutting straight lines from the top of the page to the bottom.  Zig Zag lines were introduced next, then simple shapes, then curved lines.  The lines get thinner and thinner, although when looking at them, it didn't seem like they were at first.  My son is halfway through the book and always looks forward to do his "cutting project" each day.  There are 40 pages to cut in the book.  I will definitely buy this for my daughter later - it's amazing to see how well my son can use scissors now...and how proud he is to finish each project!  Highly recommended!!!

The alliterations serve as the 5 leadership principles that hold the book together. The leadership mosaic the author proposes consists of five characteristics - conviction, creativity courage, collaboration, and contemplation. The chapter titles are clever, yet too gimmicky to form a strong framework and basis for a book. The author includes many quotes from leaders. Some of those quotes were very poignant and insightful. He also touches upon many current buzzwords, phrases and acronyms like VUCA (Volatile, Uncertain Complex and Ambiguous). In the end, the book lacks inspiration, flow, and a solid framework because its structure is based on gimmicky alliterations and reads like a theological tome without strong voice.

My eight year old son has been performing magic for about two years now and is a regular attender of several magic clubs and conventions.  While he's learning a lot from other magicians, we really wanted him to encourage him to start learning by himself.  The Practical Encyclopedia of Magic is a great fundamentals book for magicians.  There is a good variety of tricks in here including tricks that are sold as singular boxed tricks in magic shops but performed with everyday items (example - "Hot Rod" using a butter knife and a paddle move), easy tricks for kids (such as linking two paper clips using a dollar), and tricks that even seasoned professionals utilize (double lifts, biddle lifts, palming coins, etc).  There's a good variety of tricks in here for magicians of all levels.

Asides from magic tricks, this book also includes a small section on the history of magic, information regarding misdirection, practice, patter and style, and explanations about the difference between comedy, close up, television, and stage magicians.  The book is separated into these main categories of magic:

Card Magic - This takes up a majority of the book.
Dinner Table Magic - Tricks you can do with everyday items found on a dinner table.
Match Magic - Tricks involving matches and match books.
String Cord and Rope Magic - Tricks including rubber bands ropes and cords.
Mind Magic - Not so much mentalism as it is predictions.
Silk, Thimble, and Paper magic - Even includes a version of a snowstorm!
Money Magic - This includes tricks like linking paper clips and lots of coin magic including French drops, coin rolling, etc.

The quality of the effects are great, the illustrations and explanations of the tricks are clear and easy to follow, and all of the tricks can be performed with items found around the house - no having to buy gimmicked props....you get to make your own!  The explanations also give simple routine ideas.  Again, many of these tricks, particularly the coin and card magic tricks are performed by seasoned professionals.  If you have a magic club in your city, it would really benefit to get feedback and advice on how to improve the techniques taught in this book.  Overall, this is a really fantastic comprehensive guide to magic.  This would be a great gift for magicians of all ages.

I have two preschoolers, and I can't be more pleased with the way Two Plus Two is not Five introduces math to them.  Similar to Kumon (and quite possibly better than), Two Plus Two works in progressions and slowly gets harder as a new concept is introduced.  The pages can be torn out to be written on, or you can photocopy the pages to keep the book intact.  One thing I really like about the Two Plus Two workbook as opposed to the Kumon workbooks is that there are no "unnecessary pages". Kumon beginning adding books seem to all start with writing out your number pages, number connect the dot pages, and the like.  While this workbook is more bland looking (there are no cut images of animals or boats or the like), the concepts are spot on and direct.  For younger kids, this may be something of a turn off, however, you could always break a page down into two projects for the kids, or have them do only a few problems at a time until they can complete a page.

There is no adding or subtracting of two double digit numbers (10+25 or 20-12 equations), but there are plenty of adding and subtracting of double digit numbers with single digit numbers.  There are also a lot of tricks to adding and subtracting, many of which I never learned and found were really helpful!  This is a wonderful book for any kid who needs a little more help on math at school, or for home schooling kids.  Highly recommended.

My kids usually like the Kumon series of books.  However, their math series was not one of them.  The book is simply too much repetition for young kids and too slow.  The first few pages were "connect the dots" and number tracing.  This took out about a 1/3 of the book for my kids as they already know how to count and the connect the dots was too simple.  By the time it got to actual addition, it went so slowly adding +1, then +2, then +3...they got so frustrated for variety that I ended up printing some worksheets online.  For younger kids, I could see this book causing problems because it's really just problem after problem...nothing that a new young learner would most likely enjoy.

This book may work for some, and yes, it probably will help speed up addition by a few seconds, but if you're looking to solidify concepts and get better tricks for learning how to add, you may want to consider a different book such as "Two plus Two is Not Five" by Susan Greenwald.  That book covers more concepts, and is more relevant if you're looking for an overall teaching addition book.

My kids love a good challenge.  Recently, I've been giving my 4 and 5 year old workbooks to learn how to add, subtract, and to figure out simple geography.  After using the Kumon Simple addition and seeing how quickly they figured out counting number and addition, I thought I would give them the subtraction book to work on.  I was a little disappointed to see much simple this book really was.  The first few pages are number pages.  These pages feature the numbers, but instead of having them count up, the kids had to trace them counting down.  We skipped all those pages because my kids know their numbers and really didn't want to bother tracing anything.

The next pages are just pages and pages of equations.  My kids don't mind this format, but they ended up getting bored because it's just page after page of 5-1.  6-1.  10-1.  It takes a while for it to get to the -3 point of subtraction.  This same problem happened when they were working on the addition book - because the progressions are so slow, this book really isn't for all kids.  If you have a kid who is just learning numbers, or who is really struggling with subtraction and needs repetition, this would be an okay book to go with.  Unfortunately, this book just wasn't for us.  We ended up going to havefunteaching.com to print out slightly more difficult subtraction sheets for my son and subtraction sheets featuring pictures for my daughter.

I recently purchased this activity book for my kids to use on our 6 hour long drive to Los Angeles.  This book is a boon to any parent - there are plenty of activities in this book that both my 6 and 7 year old to do from mazes, to work puzzles, to coloring activities...it kept both kids very busy on the ride down, and is even keeping them busy when we're not in the car.  The activities are entertaining, and for $5, this is a good way to keep the kids busy (and quiet!) on the drive.  Just a note - your kid should be able to read simple instructions to really enjoy this book.

I purchased the Kumon Kindergarten Series workbooks from Costco in a two pack, and I have to say that I'm not super impressed with the "Are you Ready" series. The set I got was the "Scissor Skills" and "Pasting Skills" workbooks. Why these two workbooks were not combined into one book, I don't know, but they should have just combined them as they did with the Play and Grow: Cutting and Pasting Paper (Play & Grow Workbook). The Scissor skills book is in the middle in terms of difficulty between the My First Book of Cutting (Kumon Workbooks, Commonwealth Edition) and the Play and Grow: Cutting and Pasting Paper (Play & Grow Workbook). It has some of the simpler activities such as cutting just lines from the My First Cutting workbook, but also included some of the harder shapes to cut out from the Play and Grow Workbook. One thing I did not like about this particular workbook is that the paper is much thinner stock than the other two workbooks. The kids had a slightly harder time cutting the paper because it kept flopping around. That, along with the shiny paper stock, made some shapes really difficult for my daughter who is new at cutting out shapes. This won't be a big issue for kids who have been practicing cutting for a while. There are about 30 cutting projects total, and some folding and pasting projects are included by the end of the book. My kids liked this book alright, but definitely liked the Play and Grow: Cutting and Pasting Paper (Play & Grow Workbook) much better. Recommended.

As a parent helper at my kid's school, I go through a LOT of papers.  I sort through class papers, projects, announcements - you name it, I've had to get it prepped.  Lee Sortkwik really helps get through papers quickly.  I can moisten my fingers without having to lick them (gross!), use a damp sponge, or wear those weird rubber fingertip things.  Papers are easily grasped and not marked by the Sortkwik material in any way.  The Sortkwik is also much cheaper to buy via Amazon - I went to the local big box office supply store, and one container of this costs as much as two on Amazon!  I won't have to buy it for a while though - one container of this stuff lasts a long time!  Overall, very pleased with this product - this would be a great addition to a "back to school" teacher basket!

Reading books to my kids is fun, however sometimes get gets boring since most kids books are designed to entertain kids - and only kids.  Having read another book full of sing song rhyming prose, I was ready for something good and funny to mix things up.  Duck in the Fridge is a fantastically funny about the power of reading.  Full of silly puns, great illustrations, and hilarious demands for pizza (and lots of it!) this book was both fun for my kids to hear and for me to read!  The illustrations are bright and cheerful, the story is engaging, and the puns - while appropriately terrible - were hilarious for the kids to hear.  This is a great "good night book" that I will be getting for all my friends when they too have kids!

The Common Core Math Workbook: Free Response by Argo Brothers by itself is a fair workbook of additional math practice for your kid.  This is definitely not a drilling type workbook. nor is any explanations/examples are provided to learn new material.  This book is designed to be more a reinforcement tool of concepts your child should learn from class or from the provided videos.  The book is set up so kids can do a single page of math (single side constitutes as a page) per day per week (week is considered 5 days only).  Each page features 4-6 problems in word problem form.  The workbook is printed out on quality paper, is well binded together, but do not have perforated pages to easily pull out.  There generally is enough space for students to work out the problems as well as provide an answer, although some could use a little more space.

While the book itself isn't all that bad, the video explanations were not all that great.  Having used sites such as Khan Academy, the kids felt that the video explanations for Argo were too quickly glossed over and were poorly explained.  Using Week 1 Day 1 as an example, in the second question stated as such:
"Annie had $700 that was in $100 bills.  How many $100 bills did Annie have?"
The explanation was:
"Well, think about, right?  If she has a $100 note, right, and she has $700 all in total, well that means she has 7 of these $100 bills!  So she has 7 $100 bills.  Or you can write 7 hundred dollar bills."

Now, seeing how my kids have no problems with multiplication or division, explanations like this was not a problem for them.  HOWEVER, for kids who don't get or are struggling with this concept, this is an unacceptable explanation.  At no point did the teacher note that this was a division problem, and the "show your work" portion that he drew out was simply laughable.  For students who are required to actually write out how they came to the solution, explanations such as this would not pass.  I looked at later explanations and found the explanations were just as bad.  In Week 13 Day 3, the teacher explained how to find the perimeter of a rectangle with an area of 48 sq. meters and one side noted as being 12 meters long.  He breezed through the explanation noting that "well, 12 x 4 = 48, so this other side should be 4.  Then you add up the sides so 12+12 is 24 + 4 is 28 + another 4 is 32.  The answer is 32 sq. meters.  I'm so glad he caught his error because only an area is measured in square meters.  That said, errors like this shouldn't have even been included in another of the explanations.  If you want to get an idea of how the video explanations are, you can access all the workpages and videos without having to buy the actual workbook.

Overall, the workbook isn't bad if your'e looking to add just a tiny bit extra work to help reinforce concepts for kids.  However, the video explanations are poorly done and are geared towards kids who already know the progressions very well.

The Common Core Math Workbook: Free Response by Argo Brothers by itself is a fair workbook of additional math practice for your kid.  This is definitely not a drilling type workbook. nor is any explanations/examples are provided to learn new material.  This book is designed to be more a reinforcement tool of concepts your child should learn from class or from the provided videos.  The book is set up so kids can do a single page of math (single side constitutes as a page) per day per week (week is considered 5 days only).  Each page features 4-6 problems in word problem form.  The workbook is printed out on quality paper, is well binded together, but do not have perforated pages to easily pull out.  There generally is enough space for students to work out the problems as well as provide an answer, although some could use a little more space.

The video explanations for the Grade 3 book is much more comprehensive than the Grade 4 video explanations.  The teacher in the video goes through at a much slower pace, and for the most part explains all of the steps that are taken to reach the answer.  Each problem is carefully explained, neatly written, and in some cases, the teacher even goes back and shows examples on how to "check your answers".  If your child hasn't learned the concepts presented in this book, the video explanations actually help quite a bit.  There are some minor issues we did have with some of the problems though - in Week 3 Day 3, the visual representation of the fruit in the problem was presented with four whole circles and three quarter circles.  This confused my kid as she asked "is this asking me to multiply by 3/4s?"  Problems like this are few in this book, and again, the explanations are really quite concise.  Overall, good math supplementation for third graders.

The Smithsonian Maker Lab: Outdoors book is a great afternoon project book to work on with the kids.  The book includes instructions and explanations for 25 different projects including:

1. Periscope - A working periscope/how bouncing light works with mirrors.
2. Butterfly Feeder - A plastic cup butterfly feeder/how butterflies feed.
3. Wormery - A see through worm farm (similar to an ant farm)/vermiculture composting.
4. Erosion Bottles - A demonstration how plant growth effects soil erosion.
5. Soil Free Planter - Growing beans in water/Introduction to aquaponics/hydroponics.
6. Seedling Pots - Making compostable pots for seedlings/paper recycling.
7. Mycelium - Growing your own <nonedible> mushrooms/How mushrooms grow.
8. Barometer - Building a working barometer/Isobars and atmospheric pressure.
9. Rain Gauge - Building a measurement for rain/discussion on weather tracking.
10. Thermometer - Building a working thermometer/discussion on body temperature.
11. Anemometer - Building a working wind speed gauge/discussion on how scientists measure wind speed.
12. Cracking Rocks - A demonstration on freeze-thaw action works in water/air using balloons in plaster of paris/how rocks are cracked in real life.
13. Giant Bubbles - Creating huge bubbles using homemade bubble solution/discussion how snails blow bubbles.
14. Spinning Whirlpool - Creating "whirlpools" in bottles/how tornados work.
15. Watertight Water - Poking pencils into a water filled bag (with no leaks!)/discussion how water pressure.
16. Saltwater Jars - Creating multicolored bottles of water/explanation of water densities
17. Pin Bottle - Poking holes in water bottle/further discussion of water pressure.
18. Ice Cream - Making ice cream in a bag/states of freezing of cream and type of colloids.
19. Marbled Pebbles - Coloring rocks with nail polish in water/effects of oil spills.
20. Twirling Helicopter - Making straw helicopters/how helicopters and drones work.
21. Diamond Kite - Making a kite/how kites work and how kite surfing works.
22. Water Rocket - Making a water rocket that flies up/how real rockets work.
23. Air Cannon - Making a working air cannon/discussion on how air cannons work and how vortex rings are created in nature.
24. Compass - Making a compass with a pin/how compasses work and how some animals have organic compasses.
25. Geodes - Making a geode out of an eggshell and alum/how alum creates crystals and explanation of rock geodes.

The explanations are very brief, but a good intro for most elementary school audiences.  Most of the experiments can be created in an afternoon or less with basic household items.  The photographs are bright and well done, and the instructions are easy enough for most kids to follow without too much help from adults.  Our family found this book both fun and educational, and it is a great addition to our "we're bored and want to do something" library.  Overall, this is a good book if you're looking for an educational project to do with the kids.

The Charlie Brown Dictionary is based on the Rainbow Dictionary by Wendell Wright.  It uses several methods to help kids understand what exactly a word means.  The five main principles include:

1)  A picture with its caption-delineating an object, illustrating an action, or illuminating an idea.  Such as "full" - Lucy's basket is full. There is no more room in it for anything more.

2)  The simple explanation of the meaning of the word.  Such as "finish" - We will finish our work very soon.  We will come to the end of our work very soon.

3)  The use of the word in a sentence with additional facts to help clarify meaning.  Such as "face" - The front part of your head is your face.  Your eyes, nose, etc are on your face.

4)  The use of the word and a synonymous word or phrase.  Such as "leave" - Sally watches Charlie Brown leave the house.  Sally watches Charlie Brown go away from the house.

5)  The use of the word with its antonym.  Such as "dirty" - Pig Pen's hands are dirty.  Pig Pen is not clean.

Each page defines anywhere between 2-9 words, and are feature full color illustrations and single comic panels from the Peanuts line.  Our kids love Snoopy so much that occasionally I've seen them literally reading the dictionary.  This is a great book for early learners/readers.  Highly recommended!

A wonderful book on business and how to apply Marine Corps principles from the "battlefield to the boardroom". Plenty of the chapter titles are platitudes and common sense, but what I especially enjoyed were some of the business case studies he discusses on the failure of Friendster, deals gone awry with BMW, VW Bentley and Rolls Royce. Mr Marlin  also discusses some of the biggest valuation blunders of the the internet. He also discuss several wars and how attention to small things make a great difference in the long run.

If you transitioning from the military to the business world or in the business world or consider hiring a veteran I'd highly recommend this book. Also, in one of the chapters he retells a long ordeal with doing business in Japan. That story is highly recommended if you decide you want do to a M&A or business in Japan. You'll learn from his mistakes and save 18 months of what could be wasted time and also gain understanding of how Japanese do business.

When it all boils down, the big difference between dieting and making a lifestyle change is a matter of achievable discipline.  Dieting is often associated as a more temporary change marked by eating less, exercising more, and depriving oneself of food items like sweets, fats, carbs, sugars, meats, dairy, etc.  Lifestyle changes have elements of dieting in it, but emphasizes that you're changing habits in a slow and achievable way.  Lean for Life emphasizes on a healthy lifestyle over "quick fix dieting".  While exercising for hours daily and restricting calories to lose weight fast seems like a good idea, ultimately you're setting yourself up to fail when you stop exercising a lot and eating a normal diet.  The Louise Parker method circulates around four concepts - Thinking Positively, Living Well, Eating Beautifully, and Working out Intelligently.  These four core concepts changes habits, and hopefully you'll lose weight along the way.  There are no calorie counting, nutritional info, and rigid plans to follow.  Also, Parker emphasizes that "theres a huge difference between clean eating and lean eating. Just because a food is whole, raw or organic doesnt mean its a free-for-all. A wheat-free, gluten-free chocolate cake is still a cake."  With that in mind, this lifestyle change does allow for you to eat foods you love, such as dessert at a restaurant, but encourages you to eat healthy a majority of the time.

The first thirty pages are focused on her four core concepts:
Thinking Positively - Adopting a positive attitude, visualizing goals, keeping good company/people to encourage you
Living Well - Getting good sleep, decluttering, enjoying daily pleasures
Eating Beautifully - Balanced meals, staying hydrated, eating three meals and snacks
Working out Intelligently - Getting a minimum of 10,000 Steps daily, 15 minute workouts daily

The remainder of the book is based around relatively simple to follow recipes.  The recipes themselves are tasty, although some of the ingredients are not common in most kitchens such as groundnut oil,  haloumi cheese (grilling cheese), tomato passata, or pancetta lardon.  Because Parker is from the UK, other items are commonly found in the US, but are simply named differently such as aubergines and courgettes (eggplant and summer squash/zucchini).  She does encourage that you substitute out and alter recipes once you get a good handle of them, which was nice, but for novice cooks, it would be helpful to give more examples of how to sub out.  I did like how she gave a framework of recipes as a whole in the beginning of each chapter though - as an example her structure of a soup consists of a protein, sauteing bases (main ingredients), stocking up on flavor (stock, wine, seasonings), additional veggies, and sprinkles of items to add crunch, richness, and flavor.  For seasoned cooks, this definitely helped get some creative juice flowing.  One more important thing to note about her recipes: the measurements are in metric.  There are parenthesis that give measurements in cups, but for some items such as kale, you will need a scale.  This is a purchase I recommend simply because - unrelated! - it makes baking cakes and bread more accurate anyways.  It also opens the door to really good recipes off of international websites as well.

Overall, I did enjoy this book, and really loved her whole body and building habits approach to living healthy vs dieting.  The only thing I would really ding the book on is the fact that you will likely need to buy her book "Lean for Life" to really get the full benefits of her eating/exercise plan.  Because Parker "loathes to count calories", she doesn't really go into portion size nor how to completely balance out of a plate.  For complete novices, it would be nice to have some more guidance on this, which I'm sure if in her other book.  That aside, the recipes are quite good, and the family did enjoy the new variety of dishes appearing on our dinner table.

The 100% Natural Beef Tripe Sticks by Best Bully Sticks were a hit in our house.  My 15 lb Papillon really enjoyed the tripe sticks and was able to chew through them without issues.  The sticks are easy to digest and because they are single ingredient, he didn't have any stomach issues with these.  The sticks are easy to chew through than bully sticks, but harder than pig ears.  Each stick is rolled, compressed a bit, then dried, so it does offer a better chewing challenge for your dog vs pig ears.

The pieces vary greatly in size - some are thicker than others, and the sticks range anywhere between 4.5-6" in length.  In the bag I received, the majority of the bag was in the 6" length.  These do have some scent to them, but I usually store treats like these in the freezer, so smell isn't an issue for us.  An added bonus for freezing - the treats get a little harder so your dog will need to work a little more to chew the treat, which is something my dog loves!

Overall, these are great treats to get your dog.  If you have an aggressive chewer, s/he may probably plow through these pretty quickly - but if you have a moderate chewer like our dog, these chews work well and take a little time to go through.  They're much healthier than processed chew toys like those green toothbrush chews, easily digested, and are fun for dogs to chew on.  I would definitely purchase these in the future.

FYI - I was selected for this opportunity to review this item free of charge. The content and opinions expressed here are all my own.

IDW does it again with the Krang War!  Ben Bates is the comic artist this time around, and his artwork is great.  The characters are a lot less blocky than Andy Kuhn's rendition (see IDW TMNT Volume 4) and the there's a lot of great little details that he puts into the artwork.  Without giving away any major spoilers, the storyline is fast paced, there's humorous little bits placed here and there, each turtle is given the chance to do what he does best (and wants to do for a change), and the 80's cartoon is given a nod with a definitive use of three characters I would've liked to have seen more - Zak, Dask, and Kala.

It's great that IDW is bringing back the turtles - the artwork is great and the storyline is fun to follow.  Can't wait til Volume 6 is released:  Cityfall!  Highly recommended.

I have been a fan of Sam Talbot's since seeing him compete on the second season of Top Chef.  I own Sam's first book, "The Sweet Life," and was excited to see his newest book, "100% Real." Sam provides a lot of information in an approachable/conversational tone. He shares his passion for healthy eating and 'finding the comfortable place of eating what you know is good for you and enjoying what you eat.'  He provides helpful suggestions of what to keep in your fridge, as well as, multiple options when making substitutions to "traditional" choices in flours, sweeteners, oils and milk.

All of his recipes are noted to be either vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free or dairy-free.  He also lists hands on time and total time which helps when trying to plan out what you can make during a busy work week. Instructions for all recipes are clear and easy to follow.  Each recipe is accompanied by a picture and makes you want to try making each recipe. I found that I had most of the ingredients in my pantry but the ingredients I did not have can easily be found at the local supermarket. I really liked the fact that the recipes span across different seasons so I have something to look forward to.

I myself have made two recipes thus far - the Cinnamon and Coconut Chickpeas and Iron Skillet Shrimp with Grapefruit. I liked the chickpeas and now have a healthy snack I can keep on hand.  I loved the Shrimp recipe and know I will be making the dish on a regular basis. I can even use the shrimp and seasonings and use it as the base for some tasty shrimp tacos.  I will say that the hands on time for me was a little bit longer than what Sam had written but nothing absurd. I found the recipes filling but not heavy. It's a great feeling knowing I am eating healthy but doesn't feel like I am being restricted.  Overall, this is a great healthy cooking cookbook to get for yourself or a friend.

users.query: I like Patricia Briggs' modern werewolf series, but had not read any of her earlier books.  The first of the 2 books in this volume is good, but not as well done as the second.  These books are not as good as the later series, author has improved with experience.  Nevertheless, this volume is worth reading:  a good story line and good characters.

cands.text: I am intrigued with the concept of werewolfs interacting as normal members of society, but not so intrigued with over a third of the book being sexual attraction and romance.  I'm not a prude and don't mind sex, but I find written descriptions generally boring.  More story - less romance.

I enjoyed this new series by Charlene Harris.  This first book was primarily an introduction of characters and plot establishment.  I have read the second book in the series and hope for more plot lines in the future.

I have enjoyed all the books in this series.  Grand conspiracies with supernatural folks get a bit tiresome, but the characters are good and the interactions with the non-magical world are interesting.
This book is worth a read, but I had no desire to read the next ones in the series.  The plot is a bit contrived and although I liked the characters at first, I soon got tired of them.
I like all the books in this series, but by the sixth book it has gotten a bit stale.  Be warned, if you have not read others in the series, these books are extremely violent and amoral.

I enjoyed this enough to order the second book.  I especially enjoyed the chapter headings.  The series is part romance, part adventure.  It's nothing to take seriously, but the story line is intriguing.

I enjoyed this book although it is not a literary masterpiece.  The author did not make the common mistake of introducing too many characters to develop properly.  I read mysteries for the characters, but the who done it part was also intriguing.  I would buy others in the series.

I like this author very much and have read all the others in this universe.  This book ties up a lot of loose ends from previous books, but I would not recommend it to someone unfamiliar with the series.

I like this series enough to buy this book and others.  It probably wouldn't appeal to everyone, however.  Each book consists of a series of fairly brief action-adventures with a theme tying all together.  I like the characters and their actions with one another.

I like everything Patricia Briggs writes.  Her characters are very good and although she writes in a fantasy world she doesn't get too carried away with super villains and underdog heroes.  This book of short novellas adds dimension to her other books, but can be read as a stand alone.
I was looking for a new series to read and this one was OK.  I probably won't read any others in the series, but this book passed the time admirably.

This whole series is fun.  The characters are great with quirks and personalities.  The plots are always well developed.  These are the kind of stories that can be read and re-read just for enjoyment.

Dickson was one of my early favorite authors so I was looking forward to enjoying this book.  It turned out to be a textbook on wolf behavior.  The story, once the plot was established, was non-existent.  I finished it by shear will power.

I enjoyed the premise and the characters.  I haven't decided to get other books in the series, but this book is a good example of urban fantasy.  Good but not great.  Worth the read if you don't have to get it in hardback.

I enjoyed the premise and the characters.  I haven't decided to get other books in the series, but this book is a good example of urban fantasy.  Good but not great.  Worth the read if you don't have to get it in hardback.

I enjoyed this series, but was a bit bored with it by the end.  The inventions and adventures were fun at first, but got old with repetition.  The characters were good and their quirks made them interesting.  These books are worth a read, but not a reread.

I enjoyed this book enough to read the second one in the series and plan to order more after a break.  I liked the fact that the various actions took place quickly with no dragged out planning.  One action and then on to the next.  I also liked the characters although many people might consider them cartoonish.

This is a great series.  It has good characters, and interesting plot and well scripted battle scenes.  I'm not big on battles, but Weber does them well.  My interest is in the characters and the plots.  I have read all the books in the series and all are good, but some drag a bit.

I like this series, but it takes a while to get on with the plot.  The author does great characters, but unfortunately or fortunately, depending on your interests, spends a great deal of time talking about battles, strategies and innovations.  I am looking forward to the climax. I hope it will be the next book.

I like this series, but it takes a while to get on with the plot.  The author does great characters, but unfortunately or fortunately, depending on your interests, spends a great deal of time talking about battles, strategies and innovations.  I am looking forward to the climax. I hope it will be the next book.
I was intrigued by the plot.  The characters were interesting, but could have had more depth. A fantasy without a super villain.
I didn't finish this book.  It was a collections of short stories, but 2/3's of the way through the book I still had not found one that I liked or that made sense.

I really like the voice command feature of this GPS.  It also works far better than the built-in navigation system in my Cadillac!  This one gets me to the driveway - GM's dumps me at the end of the street and says my destination is in sight - not on the left or right as the Garmin does.
This book was worth the $1.99 I paid for it, but is nothing special.  The book got better as I got further into the story, but I will not add the author to my list of favorites.

The premise of salvation and choice was interesting.  However, the difficulties involved in colonizing a new planet were largely ignored in favor of a plot to put dictators in charge.

I did not order the next book in the series

users.query: A Salty Piece of Land by Jimmy Buffet is a tale about a cowboy named Tully Mars who leaves Wyoming, with police and bounty hunters on his trail, and sails off to the Caribbean to hide at the Yucatan Peninsula. This book chronicles the people he meets, their lives, their tales and how it all weaves into Tully's life which is interesting although not particularly focused. Tully becomes a fly fisherman, guide and then takes on the task of restoring a beautiful Bahamian lighthouse on a fictitious island. During that journey he meets a 103 year old Sea Captain named Cleopatra, as well as many Islanders, some pirates, drug dealers, and friends. The book meanders through his travels while on his way to his destiny, however this leads to many side stories and lateral prose that does not lend to a focused story. However, you are definitely made to feel as if you are in the Caribbean, feeling the sun, salt, insects, tropical rain, eating fresh fish and drinking decent liquor. Also, if you are a true Buffet fan you will recognize his lyrics sprinkled throughout the prose of this book. If you enjoy fishing and hearing tales about various boats, islands and the Caribbean you may enjoy this experience of being transported to the Islands for a vicarious read.

cands.text: Assassin's Shadow written by Randy Wayne White as Randy Striker was a great fast read about an ex-SEAL by the name of Dusky MacMorgan. Retired and secluded off a private island near Key West, he is content with the isolation of the sea, until he received a visit from one of his former commanding officers. He was given a mission to assassinate another assassin who works for FEAT. Freelance Extortion and Terrorism. The assassination is to take place at St. Carib, an exclusive island near Key West where the very rich and famous go for physical recreation. Dusky needs to complete his mission before his target completes theirs only his mission becomes complicated by two beautiful women. Dusky doesn't know who to trust or who to love and then he becomes the hunted! The backdrop of Key West, the sea and other islands just makes the story that much better. More like a novella than a novel, but a great read.

Wonderful guide - about defining and setting goals and going for them! Very philosophical. Define what you'd like to DO and allow yourself permission to do it! Very inspirational -  explore the reasons for being on this earth. Great trilogy of light spritual reading.

A great story about a short-order cook who is able to communicate with the dead. They offer information for many different reasons. In this book, a recurring tragic nightmare is about to come true and Odd goes to the mat trying to prevent a horrible wrong from occurring in his town of Pico Mundo. In the process he receives help from girlfriend Stormy, a few dead souls and the local police chief. I haven't read a Dean Koontz book in a long time and have forgotten how much I love his style of writing. He is truly capable of writing a light hearted horror story. Great, quick paced read.

A great inspirational and philosophical book when you reach that point in your life that you say "Is this all there is?" A way to look beyond your daily grind and decide what you were really meant for. Uplifting, offers encouragement and hope in a light hearted soft manner. There is a great deal more that life can offer!
A great cozy mystery about a woman who inherits a seaside inn from her Aunt and Uncle. Mystery abounds when a dead body is found on the property. Great characters - good read.
Very nice cozy about Pecan Farmers who deal with murder, sabotage and vandalism. By the end of the story I was hungry for Pecan Pie!

An enchanting tale of young Rose Martin who marries a 19th century lighthouse keeper and moves from Virginia to their new world  a rocky island lighthouse one mile off the Massachusetts coast. She starts her diary detailing her life on Jan 1, 1900. At first, she details her love and the wonderful new experience of living near the sea.  Slowly, strange things start to happen. A phantom fragrance, messages, sightings and items found all within the 102 step light tower. She soon realizes there is a horrible secret surrounding the lighthouse. Nearby villagers refuse to discuss it.  Rose then discovers more information in the village church cemetery and realizes there is a gentle haunting going on  A wonderful, fast paced read by Kathryn Louise Wood for those who cherish love and lost souls.

I finally finished this book, but it was a little difficult for me. I wanted to see how the mystery and plot worked out and so I did. I had trouble in two areas. The first was that I kept waiting for that place in the book where you are finally so grabbed by the plot that you are compelled to finish as soon as possible. Sadly, I never found that. Secondly, I was a put off by a number of ethnic and sexual slurs that would not be acceptable if published today. The book was written over 20 years ago. The murder concept was intriguing, but you have to work to get through this one.

I have always enjoyed James Patterson. His new Private series does not disappoint. Of the 5 books I am aware of, he uses 3 different co-authors and the small differences in the writing are apparent. Otherwise, the series is about Jack Morgan, ex-military man who inherits his father's business of providing for the priviledged in the world. He has many of his own enemies and the bulk of this book is about him fending off his own troubles. Overall, another successful Patterson series.

Wonderful story about a girl named Kristina who travels to Bernovem with her pet rat, Raymond in order to save the kindgdom with a magical stone called The Warble. Enjoyable, fast read, sure to be enjoyed by all.

Eco-thriller based upon dangerous, deadly bacteria being released on the beaches around the world.
The book focuses mainly upon the response of the medical community and is a bit clinical. It has a
lot of characters and a lot of victims but doesn't dwell on victims stories. Character development is
focused on a few main protagonists and is not deeply pursued. Probably not a good book to read during
your beach vacation.

The Talisman was fascinating to me - imagine, Jack Sawyer, barely a teenager trekking across the country to obtain the one thing that will save his mother's life. Your son is your son. I can't imagine my son trekking across the country at that age in the modern world without me putting out some sort of alert, and even more so when everything he meets and encounters is horribly dark, twisted or evil.  I love Stephen King. Peter Straub is not as familiar to me, but I loved the whole concept of this book. Slipping back and forth between worlds was kind of neat except for the evil that lurks within. This book was written twenty years ago. Had it been written now, I think they could have gotten the point across with a shorter version, but overall I loved the book. At the end, he is crying as his mother receives the Talisman. It was very touching. However, the one line that states Jack's ordinary life "was back" is probably most debatable.

Alison owns a Shore Town Inn that's inhabited by two ghosts, Paul and Maxie. Alison sees dead people and one asks her
to help solve his murder with the help of her ghost friends. Close by, her very alive widowed mother is still dating her deceased dad. A great read - nice light hearted paranormal mystery book. In E.J. Copperman's Chance of a Ghost, Alison Kerby's Harbor Haven guesthouse hosts two live guests as well as two resident ghosts and many other visitors. While trying to avoid a raging snowstorm that's threatening to hit the Jersey Shore, she is pulled into solving the murder of one of her mom's ghostly friends. The catch is that if she solves the murder of Lawrence Laurentz, she may gain the opportunity to see her dad again (who died five years prior.) This is the fourth book in the Haunted Guesthouse Mystery series by E. J. Copperman who is also the National Bestselling Author of Old Haunts. If you enjoy a light hearted paranormal mystery full of zany characters, then give Chance of a Ghost a try.

A great part of the trilogy - have faith that you can achieve more. Don't be afraid to explore your meaning in life or look beyond your daily grind. Cast your fear away - great trilogy of books for philosophical folks.

Taming of The Bastard is a fun filled novel that fans of Chick Lit are sure to love.
Millie works in a pub and falls for the man of her dreams. Sam,a handsome rugby player,
falls for Millie. The novel tells the tale of two single people, who risk their independence,
to try to find love and trust in a relationship, while associating with wild friends and colleagues.
Some of the language is a bit different for Americans, as the novel takes place in Australia, but
easily understood and a fun romp, especially for Chick Lit Lovers.

Linda Rawlins Loved, Loved this book - I've always loved Jesse Stone novels by Robert Parkers but the new Jesse Stone by Reed Farrel Coleman, writing for Robert Parker's estate is even better. He seems more human to me and I enjoy his character very much. This novel is about a cold case, meshed with a new case that leads to old secrets, old murders, old alibis and relationships in a small town. Great book!

We return to Bernovem in The Shard - Book 2 of The Bernovem Chronicles. Kristina finds herself back in the magical land, along with her not so good friends, Davinia and Hester. Once again, she meets up with her beautiful prince Werrien and both have matured into lovely teenagers. Together, they traverse the waters in the ship Kristina to see another favorite land, but danger is lurking around every corner. Once there, they encounter faeries, gnomes, and dwarves as well as evil. Kristina must fight to save her beloved Werrien, despite knowing she may have to leave the land to survive. An enticing fantasy series that will be enjoyed by all.

Tripwire is the 3rd book in the Jack Reacher Series. Jack is found in Key West, FL digging swimming pools for cash. He's happy as a bouncer at night until someone comes looking for him. Reacher avoids being found and within a short time, the stranger is dead. Two other men come looking for Reacher and now he wants to know why. He flies home to find a link to his Commanding Officer, Leon Garber, who has just died. Reacher meets up with Leon's daughter Jodie, a young woman to whom he was attracted when she was a teenager, and is now grown up and available. Reacher and Jodie partner to find out why her father wanted him and what the connection to the murder is. In the meantime, they are working against time to prevent more mutilation and killing.
I enjoyed the first two Jack Reacher novels and have heard the series is great. However, this novel was not as good as the first two. Reacher's character seemed off, having no sense of civility, being off base regarding his hunches, and suffering from anxiety at times. Not quite what I expected from the lead character. The novel also included long descriptions of scenes that could easily be cut without changing the story or content. The denouement was good and the expected pace and activity returned. I will continue reading the Reacher series, however this one novel is a bit off.

I was given an ARC of Stories from the Stoop and must say I found it intriguing. Steve Bernstein takes us through his life with a series of stories from childhood through current day. He tells of childhood bravado, insecurity, adventure, love gained, love lost and eternal friendship. Well worth the read and opportunity to examine the things that have made the biggest difference in his and perhaps our own lives.

Well written cozy mystery about the Gray Whale Inn - bed and breakfast on Cranberry Island, near Boston. In this second book of the Gray Whale Inn mystery series, innkeeper Natalie Barnes has her hands full while once again finding dead bodies and solving murders. After her employee doesn't show up for work, Natalie goes searching and finds her body in one of the bogs. Natalie tries to solve the murder on her own after the police want to quickly label the case a suicide. As Natalie searches, evidence and bodies start to pile up. While handling the investigation, she hosts annoying guests at her inn, has a falling out with her best friend over the attractive Reverend Richard McLaughlin, and searches for clues about the rumored ghost of a cook that was murdered at the Gray Whale years ago. Quick paced mystery, fun and intriguing. Some of the subplots were a little convenient for me but all considered, a good read.

The chef of a local soup shop is arrested in Snowflake, VT.  The soup shop owner does all she can
to clear his name as she needs him back at work.  Lovers of ski resorts will enjoy. Main character
is persistent but not always likeable.

In Shadow Play, by Iris Johansen, Eve Duncan is contacted by a sheriff from California to ask for help. He wants her to reconstruct the skull of a child found buried in the forest. Both the sheriff and Eve take an unusual interest in an intense case. The killer is still watching the grave of the child he buried and begins to kill all who venture near. Eve, not trusting the sheriff, counts on her SEAL husband, Joe Quinn, for help as well as some of her friends with special talents. Eve then finds out another child is destined to be murdered, but not if Eve can find and rescue her in time. It's been a few years since I've read a book by Johansen but I enjoyed this book thoroughly. Fast paced, captivating, fresh content and full of a few good twists and turns. Enjoy!

John Sandford - Deadline is about Virgil Flowers, an agent with the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension who is called by a friend to help him solve a series of dognapping cases in which dogs are taken and sent to medical labs. The case quickly changes as a local reporter is murdered and then the school set on fire. There are more sinister things happening in Minnesota and they do not involve dogs. Virgil quickly goes about investigating the underbelly of a small town and finds more bodies and corruption than he cares for. Quick reading but involved plot - You'll love Virgil Flowers.

The Ghost and the Dead Deb (Haunted Bookshop Mystery)Enjoyed this book. I enjoy the writing of Alice Kimberly(pseudonym) and Cleo Coyle (her other pseudonym) I like the characters and the relationship between the dead gumshoe Jack Shepard and his investigative partner Mrs. McClure. As far as the mystery goes, you need to pay attention to details while reading, so it's not as quick a read as other cozy mysteries but entertaining non the less.

users.query: I bought this siphon thinking that it would utilize the carbon dioxide cartridges better.  Not so.  You need two cartridges to charge this siphon adequately.  The lever and nozzle is not angled as pictured; rather, it  is horizontal, which is awkward, particularly combined with the size of this product.  It seems a bit flimsy compared to the iSi.  It won't fit in my refrigerator without making more accomodations than would be convenient.  Perhaps I can use it for parties, icing it in a cooler of ice with the bottled drinks.  For most needs, 2 1-quart iSi siphons will work better.

cands.text:
This thing is heavy, and the rubber bottoms are loose.  And the added capacity results in slightly diluted carbonation, compared to the smaller metal iSi seltzer bottles.  On the other hand, capacity is greater, and the fill level is visible.  The mesh appears very sturdy, much thicker than I imagined.  Screwing on the top to achieve a seal is much easier than the iSi.
SUPPLEMENT:  Pressure becomes very weak before the bottle is emptied.  So it takes much longer to fill that second glass and even longer for the third glass.  Also, the fill mechanism is much simpler than iSi, so that you get a lot of blowback when filling unless your technique is good.  I eventually gave up and went back to the iSi bottles, which hold just over 3/4 quart or 700 ml.

Two posters/commenters have noted that a spacer needs to be added to the end of the cartridge, one used a penny, another a paper wad (my favorite).  The cartridges do seem to be slightly smaller than the iSi cartridges, so some compensation is needed.  Before I read the spacer solution, I was simply rushing the closure of a new cartridge into place.  I will try using a spacer next.

At 45 each, these soda chargers are a good, economical alternative to the iSi branded chargers that I have been buying at about $1.20 apiece, when I could find them.  One proviso:  These chargers seem to be slightly smaller than the iSi chargers, potentially resulting in leakage during installation.  My workaround is to screw the housing just to the point that the cap of the new charger meets resistance; then I twist the housing quickly all the way into place.  I hear some gas seepage, but there is not much loss.  The seltzer seems to contain plenty of CO2.  I imagine I'll be buying these in the future.

Revised and improved special info for the Brother MFC 9560 CDW TN 310/315 refill:  For an initial refill of the toner cartridges that come with the printer i.e., without the "flag gear" or "reset gear" on each of the toner cartridges, there are barely adequate instructions on YouTube, inadequate instructions in the kit.

First, review one or more of the YouTube videos so that you have a general idea of what you are looking at.  The process id straightforward, but filling the cartridge can be MESSY.  Assemble plenty of newspaper sheets, an apron, phillips and flathead screwdriver, one rag per cartridge, a box cutter or sharp knife. Spread out newspapers and wear an apron.  Having at hand a vacuum cleaner with small attachments is a good idea.

Use a pen knife or screwdriver or similar object to SLOWLY AND PATIENTLY pry off the toner plug.  It is hard to remove due to its redundant rims.  (Which prevent the escape to toner.)  Slip the toner cartridge into a plastic bag, toner opening down.  Rap the cartridge and empty out all toner that you can.  Remove the cartridge and vacuum and wipe the exterior of the cartridge.  If you have small vacuum fittings, try to get a bit more toner out.  Lightly replace the plug; don't push it in far, because you will remove it again later.  End of one messy part of the process.

Next, flip the cartridge over to the other end.  Resetting or installing the flag gear entails removing the three screws, carefully removing the plastic gear cover, placing (or resetting) the flag gear and its spring as shown in the videos, and closing up.  Keep the gearbox end upright so gears don't fall out.  (They only go back one way, so it's not a disaster.  Same with setting the flag gear.  Generally, if everything fits, you've done it right.)  If the flag gears are already there, you presumably know how to reset them, since you presumably installed them yourself.

Next, cut off 1/3 to 1/2 of the the conical tip of the screw-on filler cap spout so that there is a fairly large opening, to ensure the smooth flow of toner.  Shake the toner container, then remove the toner cap and peel off the seal.  Screw on the filler cap.  Remove the plug from the toner cartridge again.  Carefully pour the toner into the cartridge, tapping the toner container as needed to promote flow until the toner container is empty.  Block the toner cartridge opening with the filler cap at all times.  Recanting my previous advice, I no longer recommend punching a hole in the bottom of the toner container; that introduces several ways to induce MESS.  Place the empty toner container into the plastic bag.  Clean and wipe down the toner cartridge again.

Reinstall the toner cartridge into the tray, the tray into the printer, and close the cover.  You're good to go, they say.  And you might be.

BUT IF YOU GET A "REPLACE TONER" MESSAGE AT THIS POINT (like I do), HERE'S A SECRET FOR THE Brother 9560:  Open the front cover (toner bay). Press the "Clear" button.  A SECRET MENU will appear from which you can reset any toner cartridge.  I reset the standard choice for each color.  K is black.  Voila!

I wanted something larger than the Prepworks spinner by Progressive.  The capacity is larger, but the ease of use is less.  I cannot hold the handle and spin; the top comes right off.  I wedge the device into a corner of the sink, press down firmly between the spinner and the spout, and spin.  Each time I pour off the water, I shake the spinner to ease the next spin.  I may to back to the Prepworks spinner by Progressive, which is well designed in every respect, and the small size of that device may be no accident.

This is a very handy tool.  I use it a lot for cutting trimmings down for the recycling bin as well as pruning and trimming.  It has outstanding leverage and is very lightweight and maneuverable.  This can lead to overoptimistic demands, and breakage.  The Fiskars lopper and trimmer I mostly use rely on clever design rather than sturdy materials, so you have to use a little sense about how much pressure to exert.  I learned my (devastating) lesson after breaking my first one and like its replacement a lot.

This is a handy little salad spinner.  The mechanism is simple and doesn't fail like my last two spinners.  The grip and spinning handle work easily together,  and the spouts (one on each side, to accommodate southpaws) speed up drainage.  It is small, but is so handy to use that I would rather do a couple of loads in this spinner rather than make room on my counter, in my drainer and in my cupboard for a larger one.

5 year update -- I now conclude that this is the best designed spinner I have seen.  It addressed every problem well, and the smaller size is no accident.  It's even ambidextrous for the lefties in the crowd.  I previously detracted a star for its smaller capacity, but having struggled with a larger spinner of similar design, I now understand the size limitation.

With modest handyman skills, I had no difficulty installing this replacement igniter, and it works flawlessly.  In the process I learned a little about how simple a BBQ grill is.  If you own a few hand tools and use them occasionally, you will have no trouble with this.
This is for travel.  On its first field trip, it was a slow charger for iPhones.  So it's a mediocre solution.

This is a fast, high quality, printer, scanner, fax, copier.  This machine supports my Mac well, handles heavy workloads, plays well with various software, etc.  I added a second paper tray ($200) so that I could print on copy paper or bond without messing with the trays, maxed out the RAM ($40) to speed things up and improve the multiple copies function of the copier, and selected "Print as Image" in the advanced printing options, which finesses Acrobat issues.  This is the peripheral for you (although you'll still want an inkjet printer to print photos).  The printer seems slightly slower in Word than the HL-1470M printer it replaced, which is pretty fast.  It prints Acrobat documents very fast with the added RAM.  The manual printer feeder handles envelopes, thick paper, whatever.  The copier is very fast and tends to correct exposure problems on its own.  The scanner is very fast.  The fax machine works very well.  The feeder for the copier, scanner and fax works well.  At a street price of less than $400, this is an outstanding value!

This is my third Brother laser printer.  I have appreciated Brother printers over the years because they have been durable and trouble-free.  My black and white HL1470N must have been purchased @ 14 years ago and continues to work flawlessly without problems, although the supplemental paper tray seems to be no longer supported.  My MFC8440 was acquired 8-10 years ago for scanning and fax, and has been very satisfactory except for the annoying paper curl; again, the supplemental paper tray can no longer be separately managed.  My recently acquired MFC9560 does it all, including no paper curl.  Perhaps best of all, it seemed to install itself into our WiFi network.  Having read some of the reviews--thank you one and all for generously sharing your painfully acquired knowledge--I got a filler kit for @ $85 that includes replacement caps,  springs, etc. that seem to make ownership of this device a happy and frugal experience.  If I have buyer's remorse later, I'll revisit this review.
