This is a simple and effective device for dorm use or sub-four-star travel that simply keeps the watery soap goo contained.  It works much better than those hinged models that are much more common.
When you're on the road with family, this provides a lot of usable plugs.  Hotels are getting better, but bring an extension cord.

I paid $5.59 for this product; shipping was free.  The bowl is reasonably large and holds a fair amount of sweetener, which seemed to be an issue with many sugar bowls available.  The mouth is wide enough to accommodate a small scoop, so that filling with granular sweetener is convenient.  Removing and replacing the lid is easy and the spoon cutout accommodates sizes from demitasse to teaspoon.  I would have preferred a non-reflective finish, but function was paramount.  The shape is pleasing enough.  The metal is thin, but that is generally true these days.  At $5.59, this appeared to be the best value available, and is entirely satisfactory.

What could possibly make a litter scoop superior?  I broke my cheap scoop dealing with the wheat-based litter I use, which is a bit crumbly when wetted.  This scoop scrapes the bottom of the litter box well and takes pressure without breaking.  This is a better litter scoop.

This is a grown-up faucet for a large sink.  It replaced a cheaper, smaller horizontal pull-put Moen faucet that was having difficulties, and the improvement was dramatic in our large sink.  The stream hits further out in the center of the sink, so I use the pull-put feature much less often.  When you shut the water off, the full/spray setting remains as it was.  You can have a very low spray volume without reverting to a full spray.  The vertical pull-down is much handier than its predecessor's horizontal pull-put.  The substantial weight on the tubing and the magnetic homing feature in the faucet makes returning the pull-out easy and reliable.
As a student, I was a dishwasher in a commercial kitchen for an evening or two.  I don't recall what chain of events placed me there, but I recall the efficiency of the overhead pull-down faucet.  There were hundreds, if not thousands, of assorted dishes and silverware arrayed chaotically in a stainless steel trough, presenting a seemingly Sysiphean task to my unpracticed eye.  Astonishingly, I was done in less than an hour thanks to the pull-down faucet and the large sink-like working space.  When I recently saw this design now available for residential kitchens, my memory was triggered and I was intrigued.  When my previous faucet started to fail, I could not resist the temptation.  I'm glad I moved up.
(Incidentally, Moen offered to replace my faucet free of charge.  They also replaced my cartridge free of charge.  Moen is a good company.  Why switch to Delta?  The magna-tite return system seems bulletproof, and the Moen Return system was always weak.)
Delta recommends that you twist the pull-out  rather than pulling it directly down.  That makes removal very smooth.  I suspect that the magnets become ineffective over time if you just pull it down without twisting.
A home handyman with little experience can install this device.  Access for everything is easy except for tightening the faucet housing to the basin.  Although Delta provides a wrench for installation, there was not enough clearance in my case.  A deeper nut would solve this problem.  I had to resort to a Basin Wrench (Google it) and I don't know what else would have worked.
Delta could improve this faucet by redesigning the housing for the washer at the base of the faucet housing so that one person can tighten the faucet down.  Mine is slightly off as a result.  A deeper washer and channel would do the trick.
Because of the height of the faucet, I get a lot more splash.  In response, I reduce the flow, or pull down the pull-down, or sponge around the edge of the sink afterwards.  It's not a big deal for me.

These are pretty cool and well-designed.  i will expand the apertures with an ice pick to get the right squeeze resistance, but they are appropriately on the tight side to start with.  The correct aperture will vary with the viscosity of the contents, i.e., lemon juice v. mayonnaise.  You could use these to store solid foods as well.

Solomon understands the human foot and convenience better than perhaps any shoemaker.  The support is very comfortable, and the lacing system provides near-slip-on convenience with shoelace support.  This is the ventilated model.
This is a good blade, but the handle needs more mass.  The blade will cut what you want, but you get little purchase from the very narrow handle.

This is a solid, simple radio.  Tuning and sound are better than expected.  Reception is good.  Separating the power switch from the volume wheel is a surprisingly nice feature.  I use mine when I'm doing a chore outside the house or in a part of the house that doesn't have a radio or TV.

They got this jacket right.  It is very light and comfortable, has sturdy zippers.  It provides adequate temperature control for temperatures that pass for cold in the San Francisco Bay Area.  For colder temps, layering would be quite comfortable.

4.5 stars.  This group combines solid beat, harmony, and melody with extraordinary lead vocals and innovative sound throughout.  Every song on the album is pleasing and stimulating.  And the whole is greater than the sum of its parts.  Collections like this are why people bought albums in the 60s.

I use this product as a visual aid to stimulate visual purple in my retinas.  It seems to be effective, but must be held close to the face to achieve adequate brightness.  I adapted this usage from a years-ago Bates practitioner who achieved the result with a light bulb and an electric fan that had been slowed down by removing some of its windings.  This is a lot easier.

users.query:
Ive read more than a few books on presentations and I believe this is one of the best I have found, with real examples and great tips. Working all the way from finding the idea to creating the speech and tips for delivery this book won't let you down.
Do you want to make your presentation memorable and credible? This book not only focuses on the speech but also provides tips for your presentation. Well worth it.

cands.text:
If you have to speak in public you need to read this book. Even if you don't think you have problem with public speaking, this book can still help your skills improve.

I have found in the past that I was nervous about it and if youve ever experienced that feeling in your stomach, you should take a look at what the author recommends. This is a great book with some nice tips to make you more successful. I also liked how it was set up in easy-to-consume sections, making it easy to follow and implement. Highly recommended.

This book is a real gem regarding the key elements of communication. Its full of examples that help with improving communication skills. The author has done a great job giving practical advice along with constructive ways of looking at life and our attitudes towards other people.
Overall its easy to read and concise- and its also thorough when it comes to topics of communication.
So many people have the desire to be a good communicator but it often feels like something is missing. This book gives practical and simple recipes to talk with other people. Such a great book deserves 5 stars!
I found this book to be full of interesting tidbits. Its not about overpowering others but by treating others with respect and having confidence in yourself. Definitely worth a read.

This book is easy to read and filled with great information about George Washington and the great impact he had on the creation of the United States. I recommend this book- it was well written and gave a pretty complete picture of the individual and his outstanding talents.

This book definitely does what it intends! There are memory methods in this book that can serve you well in not only in college courses but in the working world. The book is not just about reading; you have to put some work in as well. But don't be put off- as long as you are willing to put in the time, youll reap the benefits. If you like learning new things, especially when it comes to memorization, this is the book you want! Definitely worth your time to read it and do the exercises - you'll be pleasantly surprised. I certainly was.

Before I got this book I didn't know that essential oils were one of the oldest and most effective treatments for improved health and well-being. I really like how simple yet informative the book is. It presents the benefits of essential oils and the directions are really easy to follow. I am definitely looking forward to trying essential oils and this book looks like a great start!

This is a very informative book for first time parents. It has a lot of great information available for quick reference. What I most enjoyed was the practical and down to earth style that will set a new parent at ease and serve as a good resource after baby's arrival.
I highly suggest this book to new parents, especially first time parents!

This is an excellent short book for those interested in mindfulness and starting out in the practice. It is written in clear direct language and provides some of simple examples to incorporate mindfulness into your every day practice.

This is a brief but interesting book on Abraham Lincoln. I've not read many books on Lincoln, but this really helped introduce me to him.
I also got a sense of Lincoln's historical context as well. There are some interesting personal details that helped add a lot of color to my understanding of the man. I would recommend this to anyone as the first book to read on Lincoln.

Parenting does not come naturally to many people and it can be a struggle to raise kids to become strong, confident adults. This book was easy to read and understand. The concepts are simple and I felt they were all the things I already knew but needed help and reminders as to how to implement these ideas into our daily, chaotic life.

As I read through the book I found myself feeling calmer! Instead of trying to control or manage our kids the author teaches us to understand their side, why they do what they do and how to respond to what they do and say. It then goes on to show us how to connect with them and develop a strong attachment so that they naturally want to cooperate with us.

This book is so much more than I thought it would be, and it's worth every penny.

This book has a wealth of information to get ready for any sort of natural disaster or problem.
I was really impressed after reading this book and now feel like I know a whole lot about the various methods of canning and making sure food doesnt go bad. This book delivers a lot of detail  in each chapter on how to manage what you would require if something were to happen that would disrupt your normal routine. Good book, highly recommended.

This book has a wealth of information to get ready for any sort of natural disaster or problem.
I was really impressed after reading this book and now feel like I know a whole lot about the various methods of canning and making sure food doesnt go bad. This book delivers a lot of detail  in each chapter on how to manage what you would require if something were to happen that would disrupt your normal routine. Good book, highly recommended.

This book was a good read and it kept me engaged the entire way through. Thinking about and doing some of the techniques proved very relaxing. Just thinking about the factors in my life caused me to assess my stress level and whats healthy for my lifestyle.
The chapters were short and concise without any extra filler. Highly recommended!

This is a great book because it gets straight to the point. If you don't want to pick up a 300 page book telling you hundreds of reasons why should be happy, then get this book. This is a book that you can consume quickly.

The chapters all deal with meaningful things, so it's definitely a book you'd want to re-read because they can apply depending on what you are feeling. It helps by giving you some specific tools and tasks to help you focus your energy in a positive way.

There are so many distractions around that prevent you from being as productive as you could be. I can only speak for myself but I could easily be distracted by my smartphone, TV or internet.

That's why I was so keen to get this book. It offers practical advice about being more productive both at work and at home. There are some real ways for people to become more productive including how to manage email! And its a good reminder for me to start cultivating good habits.

I'd definitely recommend this for anyone who needs help being more productive!

This book offers a practical, real world guide for being successful. As a business owner, stress comes at me everyday, all day! What I love about this short book is that there are practical guides, real world action steps, for handling life.
Since being introduced to the concept there have been several occasions when I have been faced with a difficult situation and have referred back to this book. It helps to reinforce the concepts surrounding self confidence and self esteem.

This is a great guide that contains a lot of tips and insights on how to interpret women. I really liked the logical way in which the book is broken down and particularly liked Chapter 5 "Make it safe for her to be vulnerable" because it's helped me gain better insight into how women process information. It also shows how our actions (which sometimes seem like deal breakers to us!) are perhaps not such a big deal in the overall context of a relationship. It helps to show what the real priorities are and how what men see can be completely different than what women see in the same situation. Good advice that can be used over and over again.

This is a great book and I wish I had it years ago. I am excited to have it now because I want to make sure we have the time to make (and enjoy) them this season. I really like the fact that the crafts are not too complicated and can be adapted easily based on your child's age. Theres still time to enjoy making these crafts with your family before the big day. Pick it up now and have a great Christmas.

This book is well organized, and it would be a great tool for anyone battling an overload of stuff. The chapters are straight forward in helping the reader break down both physical and mental challenges in their life. Dont believe me? Well I could be accused of an attachment to items that I just don't need - but really like. Things that sit unused in the closet that I am saving for a rainy spring day that I need to get rid of.
The no-nonsense approaches outlined in the book are still quite gentle, and actually makes the sometimes tedious task of clearing out living space less of a chore. Well organized and helpful - I highly recommend this book.

If you are considering a kitchen renovation, then you should buy this book. It is well organized, clearly laid out and full of practical advice. I also enjoyed the writing style, which is straightforward and direct. The book will guide you step-by-step through the planning of your renovation and help you avoid costly mistakes.
I also heartily agree with enlisting a professional especially if you are contemplating anything complex. Even though you may be able to handle the planning, during construction they will be able to help guide you through the stress and mess of that process.

Every day we hear about the dangers of eating this or that. Finally sugar consumption is starting to get the recognition even though its pervasive in almost every packaged food!
People are starting to see the devastating effects of sugar in things like obesity, diabetes and other related health problems.
This concise book gives you tips and strategies to remove sugar from your diet. There is even a good quiz to determine what level of sugar addiction you have.
If you have diabetes or if you trying to lose weight, or are just trying to get healthier, the author suggests a sugar detox.

I have used Evernote for almost as long as it has been out. I love the fact that I can put almost anything in it and I can find it later. First I used it for research, then I sent emails to it (that I want to be able to find later) and I also clip web pages.

Im now a premium subscriber and just by reading this book I learned something! Make that I learned A LOT.

Love the web clipper Ive been using it a lot lately but then I found out you can highlight it right before you clip the webpage. Now I don't have to remember why I clipped the article!

The images in this book are great for showing what to do and the features of the different applications.

Now I am looking forward to using the features even more.

users.query: There's a seam right on the heel and it rubs terrible. I had to throw them away after 2 days.

cands.text: The elastic straps are SO uncomfortable. The elastic is stiff and rigid. If I hadn't already washed them, I would have returned them.
Daughter complained it hurt under her knees. Cute but not comfortable.
Very comfortable! I have wide feet anyways but also 3rd trimester pregnant and these are great. The fit, the style, the quality.
I bought these for my daughter because boys undies have better coverage and are more durable.  The patterns, color and fit are great. Washing has made them softer. We'd definitely buy them again.

Nice but the lace section is tighter. I have the regular (no lace) and the laced version of these and unfortunately the lace doesn't stretch, so it feels tighter and it's noticeable when wearing it. Hindsight, I would have stuck with the plain Jane version (no lace)
Too thick for us. They're decent socks but I was hoping for a thinner sock. They'll do fine for winter boots or rubber boots. They're too thick for regular shoes and run a bit large.
Really cute but really tight. These fit my 5yo fine but I won't be wearing them.
Squishy soft.  Overall they don't seem like they'll last a long time but you get what you pay for right. For the price they're okay but don't expect high quality.
Soft. Fit good. Durable. Cute!  Everything I expected from naartjie brand.

Great socks!  Very cute, well made. We have used these for 6m now and they hold up nicely with wear, great colors but they do fade a bit with washing (as expected). The size was right on for us. I think we selected the 3-5t and our daughter is wearing an 11-13 shoe. We'll definitely be purchasing the next size up when she outgrows these.

Why did I think this was a softer material (like cotton)? This is a slick material, easily washable and easy to clean. It fit the bumbo well.  I purchased the one on sale, about ten dollars, which was a fair price (I wouldn't have paid more).

Good quality and I love that the cape snapped on instead of Velcro. This sizing was spot on for us.

The only negative is that it did fade pretty fast. We've washed this 4 times (maybe 5) and the buckle has faded from black to grey. I put something black next to it so you could see the fading.

Even with the fading we would but it again. The fabric and fit was great.

Amazing!  One clove at a time and it works beautifully!  Seriously, don't waste another minute tediously peeling the skin off of cloves.  This works!  Just cut the end off of the clove, pop it in the sleeve, wiggle wiggle and you'll feel and hear the skin come off the clove. So. Darn. Easy.

After washing these, the blankets fluffed up nicely. Overall I like how breathable they are, the size and the colors. I'm unsure of the long term durability but time will tell. I'm posting a picture showing the ZigZag brand with polka dots vs the Anis Anis brand with elephants. You can see that the ZigZag is more losely knit which is nice for hot climates but makes me question its durability. I'll update in 6mo or so with the durability review.

Once it arrived we were happy with the swimsuit. It's hard to find these that cover in a modest way and protect from the sun. We bought a size up so it wouldn't be too tight. The quality and fit was fine. The shipping took a long time.
These are incredibly helpful but not the best quality. Some came with the ink smudged or scratched off and the edges have lifted on a few of these stickers. Overall I'm happy with the purchase.

Super cute blanket. The price matches the quality ($20 ish). The tail portion is not sewn up, there is a round opening with enough room to stick both feet through (if you wish). The back, where your rear end and back are, is open... it's not a sack, it opens up from about the knees up, it v's out. The tail doesn't fan out on its own, no supports in the blanket to lay out but it's cute when you fan it out while laying in it.  My daughter, nieces and sister love them. I'd definitely buy more for gifts at this price.
Shrunk way too much with first wash.  The 6-9m size barely fits my 3m old. The cotton is thin and scratchy, reminds me of cheesecloth. We are returning ours.

The plastic is all scuffed up, long swipe scratches across the front of it (similar to hair brush strokes). It was wrapped in a plastic covering so I'm not sure if this was a returned item or damaged through the covering. Really disappointed.
Whole, dried, quality meal worms. Bought these for outdoor bird food and just waiting for the birds to take notice.
These are far from deluxe but for the price they're fair. I would compare them to something you'd get at the dollar store.
It states it works down to -2 F... it does not. We're currently at 15 F and it is not working. In the 20's it works fine but once it hits the teens, it's hit or miss. Disappointed.

users.query:
This stuff got rid of the crickets! Before turning to pesticides I had tried orange oil, horticulture vinegar, and cedarwood oil with no success. Then someone at the home improvement store recommended Triazicide, but that didn't work either.

I then tried the niban and it worked. After about 4-5 days, no more crickets.

The bottle says not to apply other pesticides along with it because the insects might not take the bait. For me it was too late as I had already applied the Triazicide. Maybe that's why it took a few days for the niban to work.

It comes in a big gallon (?) size bottle and I probably only used about a cup of it, if that. I wish I had bought a much smaller size (if available?).The directions say to put it out in a 2-foot wide swath, but I wanted to apply it in a much smaller strip around the foundation of the house. It has a shaker top and it was hard to apply in the smaller area that I wanted. It would be no problem to apply it in the 2-foot area they recommend. One of the areas I applied it was on a patio and I could see where it blew around and accumulated in places I didn't spread it (along the edges of the door mat, feet of the patio furniture, etc.) So be careful with pets and children and tracking it into the house if applying on hard surfaces.

cands.text:
I bought this as an alternative weed killer. Works great on weeds in one application.

It works on bermuda grass, too, with multiple applications. The trick is to apply as close as possible to the roots. Otherwise it just burns the tops, leaving the roots intact.

Don't use this in areas where you want grass. It will burn or kill the grass.

For years I've purchased Wedderspoon Raw Manuka Honey Active 16+, 17.6-Ounce Jar. However, after reading a review where the labeling has changed (no longer saying it's organic certification by Ecosert SA, instead of saying no chemicals or pesticides, it now reads "no added "harmful" chemicals and pesticides.") So, I ordered this version of Wedderspoon's Manuka honey. This honey doesn't really taste like the other Manuka honey. It's got a rather bland taste. I agree with the other reviewer that the jar for this honey is surprising small. But I am happy that this honey does come in a glass jar, albeit a clear glass jar. (I think the jar should be dark to protect the honey.) For those keeping track.. the jar label on this product does have the OMA and EcoCert symbols on it. There is a batch number printed on it. Ingredients: 100% raw manuka honey. We guarantee: Honey that is free from Chemicals & Pesticides; Antibiotic and GMO free honey; Hives are made from environmentally friendly materials; and, Our honeys have been harvested following strict Organic New Zealand guidelines. I prefer the taste of the other honey. But I do appreciate the labeling on this honey as well as the glass jar.

This worked for at keeping the birds away for 1/2 a day and then they were all over the lawn eating the new grass seed. The reflecting light gave me a terrible headache, but didn't slow down the birds.

I am doing a backyard project that involves blowing gravel and other debris and it's kicking up a lot of dust and dirt. The first day I worked for a couple of hours and wore just a plain surgical mask, but dirt/dust was getting through and into my nose and mouth. The next day I worked for another couple of hours and wore a bandanna around my nose and mouth (like many landscapers do in my area) and dirt and dust was still getting through. After the second day, I woke up with nasal and chest congestion and irritation. Not good. So I purchased the 3M 8120 Particulate Respirator. They really work. I have not had any dirt or dust get into my nose or mouth while wearing this product, and no nasal or chest congestion or irritation.

On me they fit very tight around my mouth,nose, and head, which was at first was uncomfortable and took a little getting used to. But now after a couple of minutes I don't noticed it. Also, there is a metal nose clip that you should spend time adjusting for the best fit. After working for a while I can feel sweat accumulate above my upper lip while wearing these masks, but it's a small price to pay for the protection these masks offer.

I have not noticed any dust/dirt in my nose or mouth since wearing these. Also, I didn't realize it before, but before wearing these my breathing was pretty heavy, and I thought it was just from the exertion of working. But I think it was actually because I was breathing in dust and dirt. Since wearing these masks my breathing has been normal.

I would definitely buy these again.

I bought this food mill for deseeding blackberries to make jam. I've never deseeded blackberries before and have never owned or used a food mill before purchasing this.

All in all it does a good job. I highly recommend you test milling berries using the different screens before you start. Here's my experience.

I tested milling a 1/2 pint of berries using the finest disc that comes with the mill. When I used it, all I got was juice. Not a single seed made it through. So you can make great berry juice using the fine disc. But there was no pulp and you want a little when you're making jam. So then I tried milling a 1/2 pint of berries using the medium disc and the result was a thicker juice. I think this would be fine for making jam, although I wish there was more pulp. A few seeds made it through the medium disc, and I strained the juice to remove them. So if you were making jam, it would be a little time-intensive to get all the seeds out.

So I highly recommend you test milling the berries before you start. I would have been really disappointed if I had run all my berries through the fine disc only to find I had juice. In addition, I think the size of the berries might impact the disc to use.

Happy jam making!
This really enables you to apply powders effectively. It's made of very sturdy and hefty materials.
This works very well. There is a bit of an odor so you probably want to work in a ventilated area.

We bought this to protect the yard from birds after seeding for grass. It's impossible to use. It doesn't hold it's shape after stretching out and shrinks back up. You would need to make a frame out of wood or PVC pipe and somehow attach it to get it to stay stretched out flat. You need two people to use it.
I bought this so I can take creamer with me when I travel. I don't think I could use all of this in my lifetime, though. I've since learned smaller packages are available.

There's a lot of good info in this book, but you have to wade through a lot of wordiness to get to it. I would have preferred maybe just a list in the first chapter of all the natural cures and then have subsequent chapters provide more detail if people want to read it.

I've been watching the Deadliest Catch now for three seasons. And since the last season ended (what, maybe 2 weeks ago?) I've been going through Deadliest Catch withdrawl. I went to order the seasons on DVD and saw this book. The Time Bandit is one of my favorite boats to follow on the program, so I decided to order the book and was really looking forward to reading it.

It arrived today and I have to admit that I started thumbing through the photos in the middle of the book first. There are some great photos of the captains as boys, with their father, with their other fishing brother Neal, their grandma, their mom, their children, cute puppies, etc. And then I think it is the last photo is a rather sophmoric sketch of a naked lady drawn on the side of a truck?? What were they thinking? What was their publisher/editor thinking when they were deciding on photos to include?? It's really tacky and tasteless.

I think they have to remember that they have a huge female following. And the ladies aren't going to like it.

Again, what were they thinking?

Sorry to be so rough on these guys, but the book is going back. I don't even want to read it now.
Leaves bubbles between the protector and device that you can't smooth out. Also, there is a lot of sticker residue on the protector that won't come off.

FYI that this item is not returnable.

I bought three bottles of it and learned I did not need it. When I attempted to initiate a return, a message appeared that it isn't eligible for return because it needs special handling.

This book provides a lot of patterns based on different Native American tribal designs. I also like that they suggest bead colors as I am a beginner and a little color challenged. The book discusses bead weaving (using a loom) and applique beading (on fabric), but if you're a beginner you'll probably have to look on YouTube for more info. I think this is more of a pattern/design book than a how-to bead book. I am actually to try to use these patterns for embroidery, which I think is also doable. The first part of the book presents designs for bead weaving and the second part presents designs for applique beading. The bead weaving patterns are smaller than those in the author's book North American Indian Beadwork Patterns North American Indian Beadwork Patterns and in this book there are frequently multiple patterns per page. The applique beading patters are pretty much the same size as in that book. There is no table of contents or index, so if you're looking for designs from or inspired by a particular tribe you have to page through the book. Here's a list of tribes covered. I've tried to be as accurate as possible but provide no guarantee to accuracy. The tribe names are those as printed in the book. Note that the designs for a specific tribe aren't covered in consecutive pages, and for example you may find Sioux designs on pages 4, 8, 11, 30, etc. The number in parentheses indicates the number of patterns/designs. The best thing about the package is the DVD. There are several workouts on it that make it worth the price of the ball. On the down side, the ball is difficult to inflate with the pump that's included. I bought a separate pump that was even worse than the one that was included in the package, but between the two I got it inflated. The inflation instructions that come with the ball are sparse. I found some good info on the internet that helped me a lot. Use the following as a guideline to know that the ball is properly inflated:

  * 55cm - 69 inches in circumference
  * 65cm - 81 inches in circumference
  * 75cm - 93 inches in circumference

Also, inflate the ball approximate 3/4 and let it sit 24 hours. Then inflate it to the proper size. This gives the ball material time to adjust having air and makes it easier to inflate it to the proper size.
Good product. I didn't read the description very carefully, so was surprised at the small package/quantity received. Still, very tasty, but a little expensive for size of package.

I had been buying the Wedderspoon manuka honey but then learned that honey isn't UMF certified. I bought the Happy Valley UMF-certified honey and can really tell and taste the different. This honey is more expensive than other Manuka honey, but you can really tell the difference and you can use less of it. I will be buying this honey from now on.

This tea is really delicious! This is my first time trying pu-erh tea. I'm happy I discovered it. By the way, I drink it straight up (no milk, sugar or honey - and drink all my teas that way.) Very nice!

This item is okay. The only thing is that the entire vegetable can't be spiraled, and you're left with about 1 1/2 to 2 inches of vegetable. I made the mistake of cutting a zucchini in half to make noodles, and I could only spiral 1/2 of that.  I spiraled the other half and ended up with two 2-inch pieces left over, which was basically half of the zucchini.  So I suggest spiraling whole vegetables and refrigerating what you don't need.

Also, the two different ends are supposed to be different sizes, but I could tell only a slight difference. So one side is not a whole lot larger or smaller than the other. I am keeping this due to the size, as it is compact and is easy to store. If I get more serious with spiraling veggies, I will probably buy a larger one that spirals the entire veggie.
These are shorter than I thought and I little flimsy. I ended up getting others for my project, but I'm sure these will be handy one day. Measure before you buy.

I bought this to test test different areas in my home. Overall, my ambient reading is well within the normal range. But I was surprised to see how high the readings were:

* Near the stove top of my electric range.
* Near the earpiece of my cordless landline phone (this reading rivals my cell phone). (Interestingly, we have an old convention push button princess phone and and the meter stayed at the ambient reading when I made a call. I think I'm going back to the old school phones if I can find them in the stores anymore.)
* Near the clock radios on the nightstands in the bedrooms.

I also got very high readings right at the surface of my laptop keyboard, but they plummet when you move it just inches off the keyboard.

I wasn't surprised to see reading through the roof when I turned on the microwave and near my cell phone. I also turned on the TVs in the house and the readings were normal where everyone usually sits to watch.
This fit my kenmore upright vacuum and works great. It was easy to install and it's nice to have a few extra on hand.

You can probably find everything that this books contains by searching "5:2 diet" on the internet. I really didn't discover anything new that I hadn't already read by searching the internet about this diet. But for people who want it all the info consolidated, this is for you.

This rack is smaller than I thought it would be If you're thinking about buying it you might want to take a ruler and measure out its dimensions. Also, it's sturdier than some, but it's definitely not commercial/professional grade. Contrary to the product description I don't think a master chef would use this. Like someone else said, the grid design could make this hard to clean. I'd return it but it's not worth taking the hit on the returning shipping charges.

users.query:
This CD/DVD package is a recording of Evanescence's live performance in Paris during their 2004 world tour. Let me start off by saying I love the band's major-label debut, "Fallen", but this is really for the die-hard Evanescence fans. I did enjoy this package very much, but there were a few things that disappointed me. Here's the rundown...

CD: The band sounded excellent when I saw them in concert during the U.S. leg of this tour. Although they perform well, I don't think they sound as good live as they do on the album, unless you're actually at the concert. Don't get me wrong, the band is VERY talented and Amy Lee is an amazing vocalist, but there are several times during the show when she is struggling to hit notes. I don't think she used "studio-magic" when making "Fallen" because during the back-stage segement of the DVD, she is singing beautifully. I just think that when she runs around on stage and gets out of breath, it gets hard for her to sing as well. As for the band, they sound fine, with the exception of the guitarist still trying to keep up with the solo's Ben Moody wrote before leaving the group. Ben was an amazing guitar player...the other guys are good to but during "Going Under" the solo is a little loose and is only about a quarter of the length as it is on the album. Aside from those things, the disc is really good. The guitars and drums sound very heavy, especially on the opening song "Haunted". For this show, the band performed 10 out of the 11 songs from their "Fallen" album, as well as 2 b-sides ("Farther Away" and "Breathe No More") and even a beautiful cover of Korn's "Thoughtless". I think these songs alone are worth buying this package for. Finally, the CD ends with a previously unreleased studio track called "Missing". It's a very nice song but I wouldn't say it's one of their best ever. Pretty good overall.

DVD: This is the same performance as the one on the CD. Rather than just filming the concert with multiple cameras, lots of effects (such as slow-motion, repeating frames, blurred images) were added to make the performance more dramatic. This could be good or bad, depending on your outlook. I think it's good because it makes the performance more interesting to watch...but it could also be bad because it feels like your watching more of a music video rather than a concert. The backstage footage is pretty interesting, there's no interviews, it's just the band goofing off left and right, but it's pretty funny. You'll see brief cameos from the guys in Seether, Breaking Benjamin and Three Days Grace. Also included on this disc are the band's 4 music videos: "Bring Me To Life" / "Going Under" / "My Immortal" / "Everybody's Fool". The videos are good and it's nice to be able to watch them whenever I want.

cands.text: I know these guys still have quite a ways to go, but I have a feeling they are gonna be the next big thing, probably by the time they put out a second album. This CD however, is awesome, and everyone I've talked to that's heard it seems to agree.  The big radio songs like "Wasting My Time", "Deny", "Live A Lie" and "Sick & Tired" are great songs, but they don't justify the variety of style on the album.  You also need to check out songs like "Slow Me Down", "One Late Night" and "Somewhere" to get a better idea of the whole album.  Apparently, these guys received a record deal after being taken under the wing of Nickelback, and it kinda shows, because some of the album's guitar riffs have a similar sound.  While slightly using the sound of Nickelback, you'll also hear similarities to bands like 3 Doors Down, Creed, Tonic, Goo Goo Dolls and Fuel. You can't like just 1 or 2 songs off this album, if you like one, you're gonna like 'em all. Do yourself a favor and buy it!

Stone Temple Pilots had some really great albums (Core, Purple, No. 4) and some really mediocre albums (Tiny Music, Shangri-La).  Unfortunately, this album leans towards the latter.  While the band attempts to stay fresh and do something a bit new, it's very easy to imagine this album coming out after 2001's Shangri-La Dee Da.  The group pretty much abandons the style heard in songs like Sex Type Thing, Interstate Love Song, and Down.  Instead you'll find more similarities to songs like Lady Picture Show and Days of The Week.  I have to admit, on my first 2 listens of this album I was not very impressed.  But since nothing else had come out recently, I continued to listen to it in my car until the songs started to grow on me and get stuck in my head at work.  My favorite song on the album is Cinnamon, a fun, sweet lullaby but with a fast tempo that is undeniably catchy.  Between The Lines was probably chosen as the first single since it'll sound the most familiar to STP fans.  At first I was annoyed by Scott's attempt at singing like Bob Dylan, but now it doesn't bother me so much.  The new single is Take A Load Off and it sounds like it's straight off Tiny Music.  It's a good tune but I don't think it's memorable enough to be a single.  Bagman has some very Beatles-esque harmonies, which is funny since the title sounds like Taxman.  Hickory Dichotomy has both a title and a sound that is a bit strange, but you'll find yourself humming it soon enough.  Fast As I Can is another one of my favorites on here, it kind of reminds me of Tumble In The Rough from Tiny Music.  I also like Hazy Daze, and Huckleberry Crumble has a very 70's rock sound to it.  First Kiss On Mars has some David Bowie style vocals and a chorus that's fun to sing to.  Most of the other songs were pretty forgettable though.

So what we have here is a decent album, but lacks the strength that we know the band is capable of.  Is it better than Talk Show? Yes.  Is it better than Army Of Anyone? Yes.  Is it better than Scott's solo albums? Yes.  Is it better than Velvet Revolver? No.  As far as holding up with other STP albums, this is dead even with Shangri-La Dee Da, my least favorite of their's despite a few good songs.  Welcome back STP, but let's step it up a notch on the next album.

I really didn't expect that I would give this CD 5 stars. I only gave 4 stars to the band's last album, "Comalies". But what can I say, I have no complaints about this new album.

It's been 4 years since Lacuna Coil released "Comalies", although it didn't really start to gain a lot of success until 2 years ago. I was anxious to see what growth the band would go through on the next album, but I kinda expected more of the same. However, when I first popped "Karmacode" into my car stereo and heard the pounding rhythm guitar with Christina's wailing vocals on the opening song ("Fragile"), I knew this album would be new and fresh. That feeling grew with each song that I heard. On "To The Edge", there's some really interesting sounds going on that the band has never used before, yet it sounds like what Lacuna Coil should sound like. The album's first single, "Our Truth" didn't really grab me at first, but when you turn up the volume on a good sound system it really is one of the best tracks on here. I love Christina's voice in this song. On "Within Me" the group slows down a bit for something slightly more melodic, but they quickly break back into their energetic rhythms on "Devoted". On "You Create", it begins with Christina singing a beautiful melody and then the instruments come in. However, this song is merely an intro for the next track..."What I See" is my favorite song on the album. Musically, it's perhaps the band's heaviest song, and the guitar could pass for Korn in some places. It's just an incredibly catchy and heavy song and the vocals are terriffic. "Closer" is a song that I thought sounded a bit odd at first, but the very catchy chorus lets you sink right into the song. Finally, the album ends with a cover of Depeche Mode's "Enjoy The Silence". I've been waiting years for someone to cover this song, and this was by no means a disappoitment. The band keeps all the beauty of the original version, but also makes it more aggressive.

Even though I consider myself a pretty big Lacuna Coil fan, I didn't expect to like this album so much. I liked "Comalies" but I knew there was room for improvement. On that album, it seemed like the instrumentation was kinda simple, and was mostly built up around enhancing Christina's voice. This time around though, the music is much more interesting with fancier guitar work and better sounds. Also, when it comes to singing, the last album featured a lot of trading off between Christina and the male singer...but this time they do a lot more singing at the same time. Yep, the band definitely made any and all improvements that they needed to. This is going to be the album that puts them on the map.

Let me just start by saying that I absolutely loved every second of 10 Years' debut album, "The Autumn Effect." Although they came off as an obvious Tool/Perfect Circle wanna-be, they pulled it off nicely. Their ability to write creative hooks with beautiful melodies, and also rock out here and there, made them one of my favorite new bands.

After a long wait, we finally have the band's sophomore album, "Division." I wasn't really sure what direction the band would go in order to step up their game, especially since "Autumn Effect" sounded more like a 2nd or 3rd album anyway. For the most part, it seems the band has maintained their previous style, but with a few twists here and there. Songs like "Beautiful," "11:00am," "Russian Roulette," and "Picture Perfect" easily sound like they could've been on the first album. Then there are songs that are similar, but take on a more typical radio rock sound like "Actions & Motives" and "Just Can't Win." Then we have a couple songs that sound completely different like "Focus" and "Proud Of You," which are definitely more on the experimental side. On my first 2 listens, I enjoyed the album, but felt that it failed to achieve the same magic as The Autumn Effect.  I kinda felt like they had taken a step towards sounding like everyone else in their genre. But after a couple more listens, you begin to really love all the songs. "Actions & Motives" is a good example, I thought it was mediocre at first but now I love it. This has become one of my favorite albums of 2008, but I still don't think it's quite as good as The Autumn Effect. But if you really loved that album, then I think you'll enjoy this one to.
