users.query: I was a bit hesitant about buying this after reading the reviews, but since it was so cheap I figured - why not.  I'm glad I did!  In torch mode this unit fires right up, and produces a strong steady jet.  In "flame" mode (it can be configured to give off a flame similar to a butane lighter) it doesn't always ignite - but I've found it easy to ignite in jet mode and then switch to flame mode when needed.  And frankly, I bought this for the jet mode, not the flame, so - I'm good with it.

cands.text: Bought this for halloween - attached it to my heart-rate monitor's chest-strap, wore a black shirt over it - instant iron-man costume.  I suppose it would work fine as a camping light too...

I was stunned when I discovered I could buy an HP Color Laserjet for $120.  And with this affordable and perfectly serviceable tonor replacement kit, it's by far cheaper than the inkjet printer it replaced - the tonor doesn't ever dry out or go bad like inkjet ink, and while the HP brand tonor is expensive, this stuff *isn't*, and works just as well.  I'll be a repeat customer for certain.

WOW!  I had a fuse blow on the road and stopped by a gas station, where I was able to obtain a "fuse kit" - one of each size - for $5.00.  For just a few dollars more I now have 20x the fuses.  It's a fuse, folks - same quality as any other fuse you'll buy - but at a price that makes it affordable for you to just throw together "fuse kits" for your friends and family and *still* come out ahead.
Works as described....simple and easy and reliable.  I wish everything were built this well and priced so affordably!  Buy one for every floor in your house.
I've burned several discs from my pack and haven't had a tosser yet - 100% success rate so far.  Great price for the quality - highly recommended.

I admit it, I'm a flashlight snob.  But I hate paying the huge price for the "brand" names.  This flashlight is every bit as good as the $100 "brand name" - bright, with multiple settings, long lasting (especially if you pair it with the UltraFire 18650 3000mAh Li-Ion battery).  BUT - the switch is the weak point.  After just a month or two the controls starting flaking out.  I read about all sorts of fixes online (the problem is endemic to this model), but since I didn't feel like taking my switch apart to do some soldering, I kept looking - and found a replacement end-cap/switch on eBay for under $10 (search specifically for this model and you'll find them).  And ever since I replaced the switch, I'm as happy as can be - I still have probably the brightest flashlight available (it's not 1000 lumens, seriously - but it's bright enough to light up a barn from 300 yards away) and paid far less than "brand" pricing.

Easy.  Fast.  Cheap.  Reliable.  I have no complaints with this - I bought it based on price and reviews, and it has performed like a champ for months with no downtime.  If you need a cheap switch, I recommend this.

Easy.  Fast.  Cheap.  Reliable.  I have no complaints with this - I bought it based on price and reviews, and it has performed like a champ for months with no downtime.  If you need a cheap switch, I recommend this.

I bought this because I grew weary of the halogen bulbs in my dining room fixture blowing out every few months.  So far the bulb is performing just fine - it's not putting out quite the same quantity of light as the 20-watt halogens in the other parts of the fixture, but then again it's only a 1.3W LED bulb - not bad.  If you need good inexpensive LED lighting and don't need a high intensity bulb, this one will work just fine.

I use this for making Mai-Tai's - had a hard time finding this locally, even in the fancy coffee shops.  The price of this particular syrup is the lowest, and the quality is not noticeably different from any of the "higher" end brands I've tried.

I bought these for our outdoor pergola's chandelier.  They are exactly as described - votive candles, at a great price.  I haven't done the metric to see if they really last 10 hours, but the timing must be somewhat close, as I typically don't have to replace them more than once a week, and given the use, that's about right.  I'll buy more when I run out.

Okay, I admit it - I saw this in a youtube video and immediately knew that I had to purchase one for my fiancee.  It's awesome!  Remember those banks we had in the 70's, where you would put a coin in a slot and a skeletal hand would slowly reach out and then snatch it into the murky depths of the grave?  Same basic idea, but cuter.  Meows and paws the coin out of the fish-shaped platter.  If you love cats, or know someone who does, buy this now.

A very nice accent-lighting rope light - not super bright, but ideal for "setting the mood" - I use this to illuminate the steps leading to our third-floor bedroom (connected to a motion sensor light to prevent late night tumbles), and it's quite nice.  Not what I'd get for areas where you want brighter lights - which is why this only gets a 4 out of 5 - but fine for the mood.

Beautiful little thing.  Works as designed - easy to mount this on a wall and then slide the Airport Express right in.  If you can put a screw in your walls, you can mount this.  It's nice and stylish and gets the AE out of the way.

I assembled this quickly and easily, installed it in the garden with a bit of quickcrete, and everyone loves it.  My only "complaint" is that it's a bit short - even when installed at the recommended level, my 6'3" son scrapes the top of it when he walks through it.  It's great for roses; probably not optimal for grapes (which is, of course, what I've put on it).  Very beautiful and easy to assemble if you're at all good at assembling things.  If you need a beautiful and medium-sized arbor, I can highly recommend this one.

This whisk works great - I like the fact that it won't corrode and that it is easy to clean.

Pretty much like all the other EL wire kits out there - battery pack, multi-settings (on/off/blink modes), but at a really good price compared to some of the other resellers.  It would be nice if the unit were more modular (e.g. add additional strings) but hey, like I said, the price is good.

Not the best manufacture.  Not terribly sturdy.  But then again it doesn't have to be.  It holds my 5-lb katana up on the wall just fine.  I probably wouldn't buy a second one, but then again for the price, maybe I would.

I bought this set for my stepson when he moved in with us - it's perfectly fine, does what you expect - you can store things in the storage part, you can use it as a table or seat.  It's the sort of thing perfect for a dorm room - it won't last forever, won't look good forever, but if you need an inexpensive solution that will last a few years, it's perfect.

Works as advertised - I was able to use this to diagnose bad ethernet cabling pretty quickly.  Feels a bit flimsy, but hey, for the price, it's fantastic - meaning it works and seems sturdy enough if you don't drop it too many times.
Pretty solid for a low-end drive casing.  The machining felt a smidgen off, but not at all noticeable unless you are OCD like me.  Still running after almost a year.
My other son also list his Chromebook Charger, so back to Amazon I go - this is a good product, essentially identical to the original unit in function and size.  No issues.  Recommended.

Not sure what I can say here other than - really nice solid hardware for a fantastic price.  Hard to beat the price, and the feel of the keyboard and mouse is solid - feels durable and reliable.  I'll buy this set again....

users.query: Seriously....as much as I love Kristen Ashley and her ability to write an Alpha Male...Creed I think may just be my favorite.  I'm not sure why but I cannot stop re-reading parts of this book.  I just connected with him.  I think because she shared so much of his back story.  Definitely a must read.

cands.text: I loved this book.  Olivia was fun and quirky and I really just felt so connected to her throughout the whole book.  I rooted for her!  I wanted her to find what she was looking for!  I recommend this book for anyone who needs a feel good read.

I loved this book.  There was so much about it that kept me involved.  The character development was amazing.  I felt so connected right from the beginning.  That is SO important when reading a book.  It's what gets you invested.  I love a good love story that is filled with angst and second chances and that's what this book gives you.  Kudos to Katja Millay - she's an awesome author and I can hardly wait to continue reading her work.

"WOW. Just WOW!
Karina Hale NEVER ceases to let me down. This is THE BEST book in the EIT series yet. Just when I think I couldn't fall in love with Dex any more than I already have...WOW.
I love the flow from book to book. And the dynamic between him and Perry is explosive. I wish I was running for my life along side of him.
Alas, I'm babbling. Just know that if you aren't reading this series, you SHOULD be."

I think this my favorite out of all 3 books so far.  Don't get me wrong, I like angst, however I loved that Ethan and his American Girl found a comfortable awesome relationship.

"The Paths we take in life are never clear, and nobody can predict the future..."  And this is true.  Love is all about putting yourself out there and taking chances right?

This book picks up right where book two left off.  They have gone off for the weekend to his sisters country home in search of time away but also an escape to whatever danger that Brynne is in.  Brynne immediately meshes with his family and they become enamored with her.  His sister picks up on how much Brynne has changed Ethan.  She never thought anyone would or could.  You have to love the sibling love/banter between the two.

Ethan is still struggling with his nightmares, and he's still shutting Brynne out about them.  All she wants is to help comfort him.  As we all know, bottling up events in our life, it's not healthy, it will eat you alive.

 "Depression was a harsh mistress, and she and I had been well acquainted for quite some time now.

So if only he'd let her in.  Let her talk to him and help him right?  Well, maybe it'll take more for him to open up unfortunately.  After a main character in the book is lost things really move forward and you learn so much so quick.  Why Ethan is how he is, why he smokes, why Brynne needs to model and you see them move forward because...well...  "Loss of a loved one will shift your priorities in an instant, I had learned"

Brynne still has her struggles too, but with the love of Ethan, she sees anything is possible.  That she CAN be loved despite her past.

  "Change isn't always a good thing.  It takes a strong character to withstand the changes of time.  I wish I could be strong like that"

You are Brynne, you are.

It's hard to write this review without spoiling the book but I feel if you are a fan of the series you will be left happy.  At first I was like "Damn it!  I needed an epilogue!"  But then I saw a book 4 and was so very thankful.  Because you need to know how it all ends up of course.

Kudos Raine - another great book!
A.L.Jackson sure knows how to write a book.  She takes you on an emotional ride and gives you such a great backstory.  You really feel connected to the characters.  I love this author.

I was immediately swept into this book.  It started off so cute and I truly felt like I was reading Jayden's diary the whole time.  it didn't take me long to "guess" who that boy was but it was fun to see the path that led her there.  I must say though, In my opinion, I had hoped it'd go a different way but..I didn't write the book.  There is one part of the book that man you do NOT see coming and I was so blown away by it that I had to stop reading for a little bit because I needed a minute.

Overall though, this is a super cute read and I'm immediately moving on to That Marriage.  I'm liking Jillian Dodd's writing style.  Can't wait to see what comes next.

There's not much I can say about this book except that each and every one I love more and more!  Finally we meet the last Gansett brother and who does he come upon on his way home?  Abby!  Grant's ex-fiancee and current fiancee to Cal Maitland.  Only she's going home because things failed with Cal and Adam's heading home to see his brother's after their tragic accident and he too is stemming from a broken relationship.

Abby's on a path to "change her life!"  she wants to live differently, be wilder, get tattoos, sleep around, etc.  It's not long before Adam get's all Alpha Male (YUM) on her and well...as you can imagine...

I love love love this series.  And I love to know that it's continuing.  It's your perfect romance book. All love and all HEA.  And who doesn't want that every once in awhile?

I really had a hard time getting into this book. It dives right in with the main character, Taylor, being super mean and at times violent. You kinda can't grasp why the dude is into her even at all. I know when I was in college there's no way a guy would even fall for a chick who acted like that. It's only way later in the book that you find out the 'why' to her behavior but I almost feel like that is something you need up front. Hunter is such a sweetheart you feel like smacking him upside the head like, seriously? There aren't 100 other girls who would dig you?

BUT...

A line I related to the most in the book

"He killed the happy girl I once was". It's true. Events can occur in your life that forever change the you that you once were. But this book shows that perhaps maybe you can get the you you once were back.

I liked Darkhouse.  So I was like what the heck I'll try book two.  And OMG, the sexual tension between Dex and Perry in this book was off the chain!  I'm really loving these two characters.  I feel like I relate to Perry so much.  I wasn't much into this genre but now I'm totally addicted to this series.  I tell everyone I know about it.  Karina is a great author.

Each book in this series tops the last one.  I am so hopelessly in love with the character of Dex.  He and Perry are so awesome.  Karina Hale is a genius writer.  You almost feel like you are on these adventures with them.  Highly suggested!

I go off reviews of books.  Especially if I'm not sure about the snippet.  This book brought me in almost immediately!  Ashlyn, I just connected with her immediately because I felt like what she did, is something I would totally do, crazy and so NOT what you should do.  But the heart wants what the heart wants and usually wins out over the head.  It was so angsty to watch as she helped Logan try to find himself again.  To be willing to break her heart to help him find himself.  What a sacrifice!  And also to take in a man whom you have no idea who he is!  This is a great read.  Definitely one you can't put down once you start.  So start early in the day or at night when you don't have anything to do the next day.

If I could, I'd beg Marie to make the McCarthy's series last forever.  Each book gets better and better.  She can write love that is full of romance and hot and steamy sex!  Each book you read connects every character on the island so you have to start at book one!  Highly recommended.

I loved Book one of the Playing With Fire series. Parker and Garret won me over something fierce. So for me, I didn't really pay attention to any of the other characters. So ok, I hear there is a book two regarding Brady. I was stoked, because I love T.E. Sivecs writing. It flows, has great character development and the plots are just so well written.

So with this, you have Brady Marshall. He's suffering a bit of PTSD from what happened with Garrett and Parker and then once he was discharged from the Navy he attempted to join the police force but again had some traumatic experience and is now running his own PI business and barely making ends meet while still battling all the guilt from his experiences.

In comes Layla Carlysle popular pop star in need of tons of protection due to a stalker and who is called in, but, Mr. Brady Marshall. There's an instant hate/magnetic pull between the two and of course nothing is what it seems. That's what I love the most. It's my favorite to learn about these characters.

Layla comes from a world of adoring fans, a horrible bitch mother and a bodyguard Finn. It's everything you could ever want right? Stardom? But per Layla: "Nothing good ever comes from dreaming except disappointment. You can't help but feel for her. What a sad soul she is.

And Brady, Mr. Hard Ass can't help but see through it all. He reads her like a book. No one sees this better than one of Layla's oldest friends. "You look at our girl over there like she's the sunshine in the dark, not like she's a meal ticket to a better life." Preach it sister!

Of course, he's stubborn. Won't admit to his true feelings and in the end let's Layla's mom rule the roost and run him out of Layla's life as he gets too close to the truth. After he pushes Layla away breaking her heart, he finds out his stupidity when he has a heart to heart with his sister when she confesses to him that Layla cared for him. She loved him. That she had said to his sister that " I just realized that I found something else to make me feel alive, and he's a lot warmer than an old guitar. I don't need to hide behind it when I have him in front of it."

This book was ACTION packed. And I loved every minute. In the end we learn that well "What we had wasn't just a thing. WHat we had was everything,

I'm anticipating book 3. Cannot wait for Gwen's book!

This book was so thought provoking to me.  The main character lived her life in so much fear after what she had been through.  But Natalie is a brilliant author in that she really makes you feel connected to her characters.  Oh and then there's the awesome playlists she gives you!

I loved this book.  The character development was so good that you really couldn't put the book down.  I fell in love, I got my heart broken, I laughed, I cried...it was that good.  Definitely, give this one a try.

I've never loved and hated a book so much!  I cannot wait for book two!
This book was so sexy and I really rooted for the one character but then got so pissed off at times I wanted to throw my ipad!  But then there's this other character and you are like "hmmm...maybe....".  You should read this!  Especially if you like sex and frustration.  LOL

I was torn about this book.  I didn't love it but I didn't hate it.  Though I did finish it and followed it up with the novella and OMG I cannot wait for the next book!  So I definitely would recommend!

I.AM.OBSESSED.WITH.THIS.SERIES.

When I read these books. I can't put them down. Can't. Not at all. Jillian has totally nailed Character development. And nailed it SO good you almost forget who is who at times because there are just SO many people in Keatyn's life!

We are now on the 4th book of the series. Vincent is still out there searching, stalking...but now Keatyn has a cute hottie bodyguard. Cooper Steele. Yum.

This book's main focus was on who Keatyn should be with. Who should she love? There is Dawson who as you well know in book 3 hurt Keatyn and then there's Aidan who...well - he's the God of All Hotties - AND threw his hat in the ring FINALLY in book 3. Keatyn spends most of the book trying to decide who she wants to be with, to "love". Does she leave it to chance or to fate?

She attempts to follows her grandpa's sound advice "Because my grandpa told me when the coin is up in the air, I'd know who I want." Which only confuses things more. She decides she wants Aiden but the coin lands on Dawson! She flips again and thinks about Dawson and it lands on Aiden! Poor Keatyn what is she to do?

Keatyn has done so much self examining throughout this series, but ESPECIALLY in this group. She is trying to adjust to this new life, she's feeling guilt about lying to everyone about who she is, she misses her family her old friends. Really there is so much to her character. So has evolved so much maturity wise and yet still there is a little immaturity in her.

So I really ended up liking this book. Because, what Keatyn is finally getting is that her mom's advice to her makes the most sense. "My mom told me that you have to learn to love yourself before you can love someone else."

"Love, they say, has the potential to kill a person if they aren't careful."

I love Madeline Sheehan. She has the potential to kill me by making me lose sleep.

Every book in this series I have looked forward to, but admittedly I was apprehensive about this one. Because I wasn't feelin Tegan. Not even a little. We got introduced to her in book 2 and I wasn't feeling her hippie ways.

Well, eff me sideways with a chainsaw. This book TOTALLY exceeded my expectations. I actually found Tegan likeable...COMICAL! Some of the stuff that came from her mouth had me cracking up. She was so quick with her wit. I started referring to them as Teganisms.

"Goddammit, I probably had AIDS now or at the least some sort of wonky biker venereal disease. Or even worse, I was going to end up like mothereffing Danny and pregnant with a little biker baby that, knowing my luck, would be a boy who'd look just like his father, become a biker just like his father, and break a million hearts...just like his father."

So that's Tegan in a nutshell, in love with Cage since she was 8 years old. We discover early on that she slept with him at 16 and told him she loved him. She didn't exactly get the response she was aiming for. This turns her into a bitter, angry betty and she won't even speak to Cage and if she does, it's to tell him off. She disappears to California for college and comes back after her mom is shot in the head. And now speaking of heads, she's causing Cage's one to turn and the other to 'twitch'.

The best advice for Cage comes from Eva. God love her. "From chaos, the strongest sort of love is usually born." To which Cage thinks to himself "When did Eva become mothereffing Buddha?"

Their love/hate relationship turns sexual and let me tell you it's sizzling.

"My tears spilled over. My longtime broken heart was breaking again, shattering, falling to pieces and disintegrating. And in it's place was a brand new heart. Like a phoenix rising from the ashes."

But poor Cage, no matter what he does, he can't get through to her. Try as he might, he fights back and never gives up. Eventually, he finally gets through to her.

"I love you, Teacup," he said smiling. "Always have," he said. "Just didn't realize it until now."

Cage is truly tested in this book because he's also battling for respect from his Dad. I found Duece to be totally detestable in this book until around the end. There's nothing worse than a parent being a puppeteer in your life.

All the regulars are in there which I loved. Cox & Kami, D, Jase & Hawk, Eva & Ivy, Danny, Ripper and Harley and even ZZ. I cried twice. If you are a fan of the series, you'll know when. And we are introduced to Ella and Dirty...an awesome small storyline within the book.

And so I find it good to end here.

"But we don't get to pick our families or choose who we fall in love with. And we all have our crosses to bear: our stories, our loves, and our losses."

Ok, what did I think.

Initially as I began this book I couldn't help but compare it to Love Unscripted.  I'm not giving anything away except famous actor runs away to small town, meets local, falls for her...you get the gist.

So at one point early on I almost put this book down.  Only because I was like "been there done that".  Let's be honest, sometimes we feel that way.  But it kept me interested enough to want to keep going...and so I did.

And let me just say this.  The similarities to Love Unscripted ended right there.  First of all, Jack Eversea, he sounds delish.  Keri Ann, you can't help but feel for her.  I don't know that I'd call her an orphan but she's had so much love and loss in her life and put so many and so much ahead of her dreams that she's just stuck in a rut.  It's sad, and somewhat relatable for me.  You are so nice - too nice, that you end up being a doormat.

Then there's the supporting book characters of friends and family that can't help but be real and make you laugh.  The dynamic between Kerri Ann and her brother Joey was awesome.  And well, I'm rooting for a Joey and Jazz spinoff - just saying.

Either way...Darn you Natasha Boyd, you grabbed me hook, line and sinker with that darn cliffhanger...so I'll see you in book 2.

Do not buy!  First of all, my initial review was shortened.
I'll repost.  This book is plagiarism.  This author took another popular's author's words and put them in her book.  This was pulled from Amazon for 2 weeks and the other put it back up almost immediately.  She knows what she's done too.
Don't bother, if you want a recommendation, I'll give you who she plagiarized.  It was much better.

As a person who has a hard time NOT living in the past, this book was phenomenal to me. It's so hard for me to live in the moment. This book was so real too. I mean that's what I'm looking for in books. Real story lines that happen in real life! Your boyfriend cheats with your best friend!? OMG, as I sat eating dinner last night, my brother told the story of his friend who is caught in a situation where he is cheating on his fiancee with her best friend! I go. "Hmmm sounds like a book I just read". LOL

The book begins with a prologue. 18 year old Sabrina stumbles upon her boyfriend and best friend hooking up at a party. The ULTIMATE betrayal. In the midst of her breakdown mysterious bad boy Tyler swoops in and saves her from making a scene and gets her out of there.

Fast forward 10 years. Sabrina is a successful college graduate living and working in Miami at an art gallery. She loves life but still can't let go of that guy. THat one guy who saved her that night. That one guy she felt connected to though she knew nothing about. The one she made a promise to and kept. She gets a 10 year reunion invite and honestly batltles with herself weather or not to go. Will he be there? WIll Chris and Lisa be there? What will she do? How will she handle everything. "Even after all this time, it's hard to move on after heartbreak, especially when your best friend and boyfriend hooked up behind your back."

But Sabrina has what every girl should have. That ace in the hole. That ultimate best friend. There for you through thick and thin. There for you to tell you straight, love it or leave it, no sugar coating it.
"Sabrina, the heart wants what the heart wants. Eff the signs."

This book was just so much I had hoped for and that much more. It was a little bit of everything. Betrayal, Love, Heartache, Love, Laughter and the ultimate, a HEA.

Way to go Barbie! I anxiously await book 2!

K.A Tucker has quickly become one of my favorite authors.

"Sometimes in Life you make a decision and you find yourself questioning it.  A lot.  You don't regret it, exactly.  You know that you probably made the right choice and that you're probably better off for it.  But you do spend a lot of time wondering what the hell you were thinking."

WOW.  Just WOW.  K.A. Tucker, damn can you write a book.

I thought Ten Tiny Breaths was good but One Tiny Lie sucked me in and didn't spit me out until the end.

I'm not sure why but I was under the impression that this was going to be Trent's book from his POV.  But, christ on a cracker, it was all about Livie and how the tragic events of her and Kacie's life affected and shaped HER.  Livie is all about perfection.  Straight A's, virginity.  Straight arrow.

As did the first, this book tought me so much.  There was a quote that I related to so deeply in my current life that I highlighted it:

"Not every decision you make is going to be a good one.  Some of them will even be disastrous"

Enter Ashton Henley.  Drop dead gorgeous, captain of the crew team.  Hottie McSexonastick.  He's broken, unperfect, and SO not what Livie "should" go for.

The book follows a now grown up Livie as she enters Princeton.  Her father's dream.  As a pre-med major.  Her father's dream.  But as she soon learns, sometimes living up to someone elses dream just to make them happy won't make you happy.

"Dr. Stayner once suggested that all people face a day in their life that defines who they are, that shapes who they will become, that sets them on their path.  He said that one day will either guide or haunt them until they take their last breath."

All I can say to that is.  I need Dr. Stayner in my life.  He's written perfectly.  He's a genius.

And not to be forgotten are my favorite charactors, Kacie, Trent, Ben, Storm, Dan, Mia & Emily.  They too come back.

My heart. It cannot take so much fun and laughter and snorting.

"Whitney Houston we have a problem!" I'm super sad this is the last book of the Chocolate Lovers Series. But, I think this has become my favorite of the three! I never paid much attention to Drew and Jenny previously because I was so enamored with Claire and Carter but shit on a shingle, Drew and Jenny got it going ON!

This book lived up to my expectations and then so much more. Tara Sivec is a writing Goddess. To have someone who shares your warped, sick sense of humor and is not afraid to write it in a book and publish it, that person deserves medals and awards and major accolades!

There are too many quotes from this book to even quote. All I can say is that I had to read parts to my husband because he couldn't understand why a book could make me laugh so hard that I snorted and if it suited me, I would have spooped my pants.

Tara - please continue to write these books with this humor. I will read and tell everyone I know!

I'm a frequent buyer of the Dingo Denta treats but they are becoming harder and harder to find.  I figure I'd try these and my dog just didn't like them.  I'm so bummed.  I was hoping to find a replacement and these weren't it.

users.query: Since the 1993-1994 timeframe, baseball has suffered from an alienating set of maladies. Costas diagnoses the problems accurately, reminds people that they are of recent vintage and not intractable, and offers reasonable  solutions. Baseball, get a grip, because the fans are moving on.

cands.text: The fact that the answers aren't in descending order on the cards kills the game. It makes it really hard to host and makes it impossible to gain any momentum. The host is constantly figuring things out and struggling. No fun.

Reading a narrative that steps you through events as they occurred makes you realize how bad the past year really has been for America -- how chaotic, corrupt, self-serving, and destabilizing. While there are flaws in the book -- Wolff's tortured vocabulary, minor errors -- the overall effect is edifying. The book is a fast read, and you get a visceral feeling for events and the in-fighting, as well as how the Administration prioritizes itself above the American people. Recommended.

First, this book wasn't written by Bird and Magic. It was written by Jackie MacMullan.

Second, the book is fairly interesting and fun to read.

Third, the writing is sloppy and feels like it's a first draft. The editing isn't tight, the narrative wanders around, and ideas or controversies are treated superficially. The passive way the game is analyzed (players "submit" stat lines so many times it'll make your head spin) really leaves a lot to be desired.

Fourth, there are some dandy typos in this book, another indication of the sloppy editing (my favorite was "break" for "brake," for instance).

So, a fun read if you're from the era and remember Showtime v. Celtics with fondness. Otherwise, there are better books out there.
Excellent quality and look, great storage compartments, very useful, and passes muster for that teenage Bruins fan. Very large capacity, too.

I've been pondering this book since I read it. In short, I cannot say I'm glad I read it.

Strickland is an excellent writer. The cycling aspects are wonderfully realized. The insights into his troubled life seem honest and complete. Yet, in total, I was still stuck thinking I could have done without it. Scenes from his childhood are horrific, and overall the book is anticlimactic.

I understand what the book is about, but would caution other potential readers, you may respect the book, but you may not like the book.

Growing up, Carl Sagan's insights, from Broca's Brain to Cosmos and beyond, shaped my thinking about and fueled my enthusiasm for astronomy and big questions. When he passed away more than a decade ago, I was profoundly saddened. Wisely, his longtime collaborator has rescued a great set of lectures from the vaults and presented them, with new plates, to us today. We need Sagan today, perhaps more than ever. With fatalistic and nihilistic governments who blend incompetence with recklessness, we need a voice of hope, reason, and thoughtful optimism. No rapture is coming, but we could snuff ourselves out if we let unreason generate a self-fulfilling prophecy. Sagan's elegant prose and deep wisdom are refreshing in today's world. His enthusiasm for science is invigorating. Thank you, again, Dr. Sagan.

I was very pleasantly surprised reading Johan Bruyneel's book "We Might As Well Win". It could have been an indulgent, sloppy mess. Instead, it is a crisp, well-written, multi-layered, fun, and insightful book that provides equal parts insights into Lance, insights into Johan, insights into races, and insights into winning. Bruyneel's personal strengths are projected through the writing, including a gentleman's restraint and a willingness to look reality squarely in the face.

An excellent cycling book, definitely gets a podium spot on my bookshelf!

I've had my Kindle since the week it was released, and have been using it daily since then. I have to say, the Kindle changes the game. I've tried the Sony eBook and other devices, but the combination of a good form factor, wireless connectivity, a decent starter set of content, and the ability to email yourself documents for time-shifted reading makes this the best entry yet into the eBook field. My son has also been using it nightly, and is about to finish his first book on it. Integration with blogs is smart, and forward-thinking. The device itself is easy to hold. The textured rubber backing, whimsical locking/screensaver, and easy controls all add up to something that takes minutes to learn how to use, is nice to hold and own, and then disappears as the ideas come out of it. It's more useful and usable than I'd thought it could be. I don't know if the price tag is reasonable at this point, however. That is its Achilles heel.

What a disappointment! This novel does nothing to set the atmosphere, reading more like a modified screenplay (which I'm suspecting was one of the motivations playing in Kanon's mind). The characters are poorly (re)imagined, the settings dismissively portrayed, and the writing style unremarkable. Also, I had the feeling that the author didn't work on immersing himself in the circumstances of New Mexico, WWII, or the Project. It's all too contemporary in parts (seems like it's pulled out of the 1980s instead of the 1940s). Finally, the plot is too simplistic and rather dull. A dud.

The more I listen to "Blown Away" (and that's quite a bit, because it's so listenable), the more I'm convinced this may be a masterpiece. Underwood has taken nearly every type of country and cross-over song and done each better than anyone else could. In addition, there are a few songs unlike any I've heard recently, including the title track and "See You Again," which has more melody in it than the law allows. Underwood's voice is superlative, of course, and her phrasing is excellent. The clarity of her enunciation is superb. Seeing as she co-wrote many of these songs, this album in my mind elevates her another notch or two as an artist -- as if she needed that. But that's what the great ones do -- keep reaching even when they're at the top. Amazing album.

If you read this book, you will gain a definite advantage over your colleagues, to get right to the point. Rosenzweig has written a book that has a strong hypothesis and uses this to explain the cognitive dissonance experienced when reading guides to best business practices. By focusing on the ubiquitous flaws underpinning these guru-driven tomes, he shows that business actually is, as we assumed, about risk, ideas, being in the right place at the right time, and giving people what they need. Superstar companies are few and far between, strong companies focused on basic goods are enduring and reliable, and no company is an island. If only other business tomes were this thoughtful, honest, and insightful . . .

I bought this album on a whim, and I'm glad I did. With the exception of one song (a requisite "I'm so country it hurts" rouser), the album is a cut above the rest. The lyrics are real standouts, and the range of compositions is impressive. As a singer, Billy Ray moves easily between twangy country singing and smooth ballads. His lyrics can make you laugh in recognition or outright comic appeal, but then move to profound topics and gentle ballad. Overall, a solid album from an underappreciated songwriter and performer.

The base is essentially the same design as others using the previous (and more sturdy) connector. This thin tab of a connector makes the entire thing feel fragile. It hasn't broken yet, and may never, but it makes me nervous using it. But it's not that expensive, so that's a point in its favor.

The last two Cormoran Strike books have been pleasant enough. The plots had enough momentum and the characters' quirks and voices were interesting. "Career of Evil" is a definite letdown. I tried three times to make it through, but could not. It's boring and repetitive. There's no electricity. The "pursuit" of a killer may as well have been an episode of "Travel with Rick Steves." The perpetrator is a cliche, and bits from his perspective lack any interest. Strike himself seems dissipated and bored to be in the book. Robin has her moments, but the whole thing seems like it was written by Rowling's understudy's understudy. It's a bore, a snooze, and a pity.

These cables sound best if inserted directly into your arteries. Not only do they remove cholesterol plaques, but once they reach your aorta, the fine connection quality makes the bass really come alive. Best of all, once the playlist is over and you tug them out, they're easy to clean. Just keep a bucket nearby, and a bandage of course.

I tried cheaper cables, but the infections were so expensive, it wasn't long before I wised up and spent the money. No antibiotics yet, and Styx has never sounded better.

They have my heartfelt endorsement!

This rack is sturdy, with a lot of nice features (shortens when needed, pole extends when it gets full, etc.). Ours has lasted many years with a load of winter coats and boots and hats, and has survived a move without a problem at all. Recommended.

Once again, the Skeptical Environmentalist has brought a wide lens to a particular problem, reminding us that if we have stated goals, there are more efficient and effective ways to meet them. For example, if the goal is to eliminate deaths from extreme temperatures, you have to look at more data than just those around deaths from heat prostration. A short, sensible book, not quite as well-written as "The Skeptical Environmentalist," it is still excellent and important.

I was expecting a blow-by-blow account of the 2004 Tour, and that's certainly in here, but there is much more here, as well. The behind-the-scenes stuff, the elaboration around major recent cycling events, the history seamlessly interweaving into the present, and the profiles of riders both famous and obscure combine to place this book at the HC level of cycling journalism. Wilcockson deserves a lot of credit for getting out something this good so quickly after the event. In book publishing, that's tough. Because he's reaching for a broad audience, there is a sentence here and there explaining things that most cyclists know. No problem. It's a great book. If you're a cycling fan, get it.

I attended the Boston show of the Clockwork Angels tour, and it was a great concert event. I was very glad to see the guys again after many years of missing concerts. I have, however, kept up by watching their many concert DVDs, so I have a good amount of background regarding the filming and sound quality of their live shows on DVD. So I was surprised to read many negative reviews of the editing style and sound mix. I got the DVD anyhow, and have watched it twice now, and can say unequivocally that I think the sound mix is very good to excellent and the editing gives the performance a great span and "live" feel.

The mix is heavy, but clear. That is, the bass elements are slightly enhanced as they were in the concert itself. Geddy's bass lines rip, and Neil's heavy foot pounds. But these take nothing away from Alex's soaring solos or rhythm stings, or from the lovely pulses of strings coming during the main section with the ensemble. Vocals are clear, keyboards are clear, and the whole thing sounds great, I think. I have a 5.1 system, and it sounds great at all volume settings I've tried (quiet and really loud).

The filming is impressive, as it uses standard techniques (guys with shoulder cams and a few set cameras) along with a camera on a wire, cameras wandering the floor, cameras in the stands, and GoPros mounted on various stage equipment. This gives some surprisingly good shots of the players, the crowd, the staging, and the event overall. The montage during the light splashes of "YYZ" epitomize the approach -- you see them from the floor, the nose-bleeds, the left, the right, the stage, and above, all in a quick series of cuts that use filming to full effect. That is, the reason to have a lot of cameras is to convey more and different views to capture an event more completely than any single spectator could. The images are clear, the cuts are appropriate, and the overall concert footage is exciting and spot-on.

So, in my books, this is better than some Rush DVDs, definitely up there for excitement with "Rush in Rio," and the footage of the songs from "Clockwork Angels" is spectacular. The title song is beautifully captured, and "Headlong Flight" and "The Anarchist" will leave you begging for more.

Get it. It's awesome!

The first song I heard off "A Different Kind of Truth" was "Tattoo," and it underwhelmed me. Well, it's by far -- far -- the worst song on this album (why they didn't release "Blood and Fire" as their first single baffles me). The guitar work here more than makes up for the keyboards of the '90s, and brings back to center stage one of the greatest guitarists of our times, thrashing it like he's 20 with something to prove (the latter is likely true). David Lee Roth has the chops to battle to the front of this raucous band, with a voice that weaves through the sonic onslaught and scads of lyrical dexterity (he can scat as fast as Eddie can thrash). Thank you, Van Halen, for putting out an album that makes all of the songs I hear on the radio today sound sterile, homogenized, and weak. This album is a powerhouse of a real band playing for their lives. Great!

Jothy Rosenberg is an inspiration! I've ridden next to and behind him on many Pan-Mass Challenges, and while he doesn't know me, I now feel I know him. What I'd seen on during the PMC was a tough, strong cyclist with a heart of gold and a damn strong left leg (16-17+ mph on rolling terrain is nothing to sneeze at for two-legged cyclists). Now I know just how tough and inspiring he really is. This book is a must-read. The writing is clear and coherent. The stories are told plainly and well. It doesn't matter your connection with cancer, athletics, or cycling. This book connects at a level of humanity that's honest and unforgettable.

"Moriarty" appropriates an interesting period in the Holmes canon -- the interval when Holmes is presumably dead after his encounter with Professor Moriarty at Reichenbach Falls. Horowitz introduces a Pinkerton agent to fill the void, and allies him with a Scotland Yard detective we've seen before in the Holmes stories. Together, they are on the trail of an American crime boss, Charles Devereux. The spectre of Moriarty looms large in the story, as all the threads emanate from the corpse recovered from the Falls.

I enjoyed it as much as "House of Silk," even if it is an entirely different take on the period and the stories, filling in an interesting gap with an imaginative and plausible mystery. There are plenty of twists, a nice integration of actual historical figures, and many exciting scenes. I finished it within 48 hours. It's hard to put down.

We finally upgraded to a large LCD television (Sony) that fit the spot in our family room perfectly. The picture amazed us, but the sound seemed only adequate compared to the stunning images. I'd looked around at surround sound systems, but was discouraged by either the price (most often), the fancy speaker designs, or the manufacturer's reputation (cheap but likely to break). Finally, we needed a system that would "disappear" into our family room -- it's a very nice rustic room that we don't want to clutter up.

I came across this Sony package, and was intrigued. The speakers are simple, the design minimalist, and the manufacturer trusted (same as our new TV). Then I looked at the price, and after deliberating for a few hours, I took the plunge.

The box arrived two hours before we were scheduled to leave for an evening out. I cracked it open, and had it installed (except for some final touches to hide the wires better) and working before we left, total time about 70 minutes. The speakers tucked away easily. Even my wife, who defends the house's appearance above all else, approved.

The auto-calibration is a great feature. In my initial haste, I put the center speaker in a little wood storage alcove in our fireplace, then ran the calibration. The system sounded great, but after a few favorite scenes from movies, I realized having the center speaker down low wasn't working very well. I moved it up to the mantle, where it still hid away perfectly, and listened to a concert. The center speaker was being driven too much now. I ran the auto-calibration again with the new configuration, and listened to the same concert, and the sound was restored to its great blend again. It's a genius little piece of engineering.

The only complaint is that now I probably need a universal remote. But we'll see. Some functions are pretty obscure, and most functions can be handled easily by just pulling out one remote from the drawer.

All in all, a great system with excellent sound and impressive features for the price.

Green Day plugs into their punk roots to create a muscular, super-charged follow up to "American Idiot." The musicianship is awe-inspiring at times, the lyrics are great, and the overall gestalt is impressive. A very listenable album with plenty of fireworks and adrenaline, it stands out as another major work by a band that is really hitting its stride.

Hurst has produced a book that is applicable to cyclists of all types, not just urban cyclists. As someone who commutes in a mixed urban/suburban environment, I found the insights and advice to be very practical. Hurst's writing style is casual but brilliant, very conversational but never lacking in substance. The book is well-designed and easy to browse or read at length -- I've done both. It places many aspects of cycling (helmets, bike paths, injuries, and road protocol) in a practical perspective, updating many classic analyses along the way. Highly recommended if you find that reading/learning about cycling is part of why you enjoy cycling.

users.query: Inexpensive and works great. Holds up just as well as branded product. Will recommend and buy again.

cands.text: Inexpensive and works great. Holds up just as well as branded product. Will recommend and buy again.
cheaper alternative to the competition's product and very light weight.  Love it, hold exactly what I need without taking up too much space and weight in my backpack.  Recommend.
Don't bother with the more expensive brands.  My new go to screen protector, doing it's job and a plus fast shipping with Amazon Prime.
So glad I picked this up, high quality and much more cost effective over my local options.  Highly recommend to my friends.  Simple packaging no waste.

I usually buy Amazon Basics products over the competition, I have found their quality typically exceeds any others.  I was NOT disappointed in these sheet protectors.  I hate when you have cheap protectors that start tearing on the edges.  These do not feel cheap and I'm pretty confident they will stand up to a years worth of heavy use.  A must buy school supply.
Great for emergencies, camping, etc.  I always keep one of these on hand.  Low cost, effective!

What can I say, for the money it's definitely worth it.  This multi tool is #1 for a reason.  Leatherman's quality exceeds the competition and I absolutely love the drill bit exchange system of this unit.  This one replaced a lost tool that I had for over 20 years.  Highly recommend.
Just as good as the more expensive protectors at a fraction of the cost. Love it
Really surprised at the quality of this product.  Packs down very tiny.
It is what it is, works well, higher quality than oem products.  Love the low cost, save a buck and get this one.
Great quality at a very affordable price.  Got these for my hammock and they work perfectly.
I wasn't expecting much for the price but I found it to be better quality than some of my higher priced doggie steps. Thank you.
Bought for my niece, she is never seen without it now.  Great little charger.  Would recommend.
Super cute, inexpensive alternative to high priced baskets.  Does exactly what I need it to do without all the expensive fuss.  Definitely recommend buying.  Thanks for a quality product.

With so many expensive options out there I decided to give these a try.  I am so glad I did. The sound quality is great, and very comfortable.  In fact, I ordered a second pair for my son.  Saved me loads on more expenisve headsets.  Definitely would buy again!

I was not expecting a lot out of this little guy, but it's absolutely perfect.  So much so that I use it every day in my home and packed up the big clunking coffee maker.  This saves me so much coffee and is perfect.  Came back to get a second for my camping gear as the other is now a permanent fixture in my kitchen.  Definitely recommend.
Great value and a very nice sleeping bag.  It's definitely compact and quite light in weight.  Don't spend a fortune on others when this is avail.  Definitely recommend for campers on a budget.
This is perfect for so many things.  High quality, super sharp.  Highly recommend.
I researched a lot of portable photo printers before settling on this one.  Glad I did, works beautifully, no issues.  Highly recommend very portable.

Can't beat the price, and this seat cover is a nice sturdy water proof protection for my dog.  Already had a need for it when my pup got car sick.  Was super grateful it was installed, clean up was super easy and my new car seats were not gross.  Definitely buy this one.

Until they get better at support do not waste your money!  Their most recent update broke the device.  It's a paper weight.  The product updates, but is not communicating back from their servers to the application on your device.  Their support staff is clueless and keeps instructing you to reset the device, which functions correctly and does exactly what it should do and communicates upwards with their servers.  The app even uploads correctly to the servers exactly as it should but as soon as you attempt to connect it WILL NOT connect to your piper and is useless.  They will try to blame your internet, router anything but their device or servers or application.  I have many other smart devices connected and they are working flawlessly, including smartthing.  I intially started off with the piper system and unfortunatelly after months of dealing with piper had to make the switch over to smartthing, I didn't want to have to ditch these cameras but it looks like I'm going to have to bite the bullet and toss these in the trash.  Waste of money and investment.
Super cute, got lots of variety.  My planners never looked so good.  Thanks

I have used this for over 5 months and it works just as good as the more expensive flea preventions.  Just took my dog to a spay clinic and all animals that had any fleas were administered a capstar 24 hour flea prevention if they had even one flea on them.  Over 20 something dogs, most on some form of flea prevention (collars and/or high dollar treatments), and my dog was only one of two that did not have a flea on her.  I live in the country, my dog has access to over an acre yard, and no I do not treat my yard.  Definitely recommend.

Super light weight, and gives off an incredible amount of light.  Used this during a power outage and it lasted all night long.  Highly recommend.  I just keep it in my window and it's fully charged when I need it.  Bought a second for in the car.

users.query:
The good news is that if you want to make copies of video suitable for an iPod or other small screen device, you can do it as long as the video source has a single analog out for video and one or two outs for audio.

The bad news is that the manual is opaque and you have to be very geeky to understand how to set this thing up.  The video interface is something out of PacMan circa 1978.  This device is not for the non-technically inclined.

The other bad news is that even at the highest resolution, the video quality is marginally suitable for TV watching.  It's OK for watching on a small device like an iPod, but even when you modestly blow up the image to something like 26", you can see just how splotchy the blacks are and how grainy the image is.  It's like watching a mediocre VHS tape.

This device will not be particularly good for archiving old DVDs or even VHS tapes because of the image degradation.  The company suggests a different device for archiving, their OSD.  That device has an extra video in, S-Video, in so it might be a little better.  But if you are using RCA jacks on that device, I'm guessing you'll have the same problem as you'll have with this device in terms of poor archival video.

The bottom line is that this device is a pretty good one trick pony if you're technically inclined.  And that one trick is that it can record low quality mpeg4 video suitable for an iPod or PSP onto an SD card.

cands.text:
At the time I bought this (Christmas season 2009), the Vado was the least expensive option for 720p video pocket-sized recorders.  It's very handy to carry around and the little included silicon case is useful and well designed.  The camera is fairly intuitive to use for shooting videos.  I'd recommend a tripod for long interviews with seated subjects.  To download the images to a Mac, you need to download software from the Creative site.  Once you do that, you can either bring the videos into the Mac via: 1) the Vado software for quick editing or file conversion; 2) directly to iPhoto for quick storage and playing/editing on Apple Quicktime or iMovie.

If you already have a decent quality compact point and shoot camera with a video option, the Vado probably is superfluous (and its competitors are as well). The lens is cheap and under low light the images are grainy with little color rainbow patches.  Under good lighting, image quality is fine, but it won't wow you.  The audio quality is passable, but hissy and doesn't give much beyond the human voice in terms of frequency range.  It should be noted that the to-be-released "3rd generation" model will allow for an external mic.

If you don't have a good quality compact still camera with video, this item can be a lot of fun.  The images aren't fantastic, but for Youtube they are more than decent enough.  Be sure to find a way to have decent lighting before you shoot because otherwise you might end up disappointed by the degraded image.  At the price I bought this thing, I consider it to be a bargain.

I'm a technological semi-geek.  I can get most things to work.  But so far, this machine is not as easy to use as I thought it would be.  It plays store bought DVDs, mp3s and audio CDs well.  The upconverting creates a modestly better picture with its HDMI out than my ancient former DVD player (10 years old) did when I played it through its S-Video out.  The Viera link works with my Panasonic TV, which as far as I can tell only means the TV turns on when the DVD player goes on; whether you can consider that a plus is debatable, but you can easily turn the link off.

What I have yet to get to work are mpeg-4 files from either DVD discs or CD discs.  The machine says it can't read the discs.  I'll keep tweaking.  But it looks like that on paper the previous generation DVD player from Panasonic, the S53K, actually had a little more versatility with regard to disc formats.

I'm a technological semi-geek.  I can get most things to work.  But so far, this machine is not as easy to use as I thought it would be.  It plays store bought DVDs, mp3s and audio CDs well.  The upconverting creates a modestly better picture with its HDMI out than my ancient former DVD player (10 years old) did when I played it through its S-Video out.  The Viera link works with my Panasonic TV, which as far as I can tell only means the TV turns on when the DVD player goes on; whether you can consider that a plus is debatable, but you can easily turn the link off.

What I have yet to get to work are mpeg-4 files from either DVD discs or CD discs.  The machine says it can't read the discs.  I'll keep tweaking.  But it looks like that on paper the previous generation DVD player from Panasonic, the S53K, actually had a little more versatility with regard to disc formats.

I bought this because it was cheap (less than 60 bucks when I bought it), the cheapest Panasonic Blu-ray unit I could find (I wanted it to work with Panasonic's proprietary Viera link).  It was a snap to set up.  It loads DVDs and Blu-ray discs fast.  I'm a low-tech guy and have no need to use this for Youtube or Netflix so I can't comment on the internet capability of the machine.  I will never use the USB port either.

As a replacement for my Panasonic DVD player (four years old), it works perfectly acceptably.  Playback is smooth.  Video quality is excellent.  It worked with the Viera link on my TV and TV remote control right out of the box. It does emit a slight high pitch whine when it plays Blu-ray discs (though not when it plays DVDs; it's perfectly quiet then), but you can only hear it when you mute the audio.  Unlike my older Panasonic DVD player, it does not come with a zoom feature on the remote.  I found the zoom handy for reading credits at the end of movies (friends of mine sometimes appear in those credits).

I'm sure there are better Blu-ray players out there with a bevy of features and that perhaps don't emit a tiny whine that you can hear when you mute the audio (not a concern of mine), but they cost more.  You do get what you pay for.  This one is inexpensive, easy to use and acceptable for my use.  I note that updates of firmware (which are frequent with Blu-ray players) require either an ethernet connection or a download using a PC.  The download will not work with Macs.  I own a Mac.  That doesn't make me happy.

Addendum: I've had this machine for one year and it continues to work well.  After one year, I hooked it up to my new home network using an ethernet cable.  I've used Netflix on it problem free.  I've also used VUDU problem free.

This Samsung is an excellent monitor visually.  The screen is crisp and bright.  The gradation in dark colors, something that is often a failing on monitors in this price range and below, is subtle.  It works well as a computer monitor and if you don't mind the need for separate external speakers can work off your DVD and BluRay players.  It's a bit difficult to use the single button control in back to make screen adjustments and to even turn off the monitor.  Samsung went for simplicity over functionality by using only  one button to control all features.  It's also a bit difficult to completely disassemble the monitor from the stand; you have to wiggle a plastic bar away from the monitor forcefully, but not too forcefully, otherwise you might permanently damage the stand.  Other than those small flaws, I'd highly recommend this monitor.  It's versatile, lightweight, and provides for beautiful viewing.  I find the curve in the monitor appealing, but you should spend some time using a curved monitor before you purchase one to make sure it works for you.

I picked this up for less than 200 bucks on sale.  I'm not much of a TV watcher and I don't even have cable TV.  I just watch PBS and special yearly events like the Oscars and the Rose Parade off my antenna.  Mostly I watch movies off my Blu-Ray player.  This TV was bought to replace my old 26" LCD Panasonic Viera (about six years old).  The picture quality of this LED TV is definitely superior to what I had and it's nice that I get 31.5" inches of screen in the same space of my bookcase that used to hold my 26" TV.  Sound quality is solid, and the digital tuner is also superior to the old one on my Panasonic (I'm getting clear reception on channels that used to be sketchy).  The one thing that is inferior is the time lag in changing channels; it's a bit longer with this TV, but nothing ridiculous in terms of a wait.  This unit also has a glossy screen, and personally I prefer matte screens.  My TV isn't near a window,  so any glare is minor, but if you plan to watch this TV during the day and your house gets lots of light, you might prefer a different model.

The remote is fairly intuitive.  The only complaint I have is that this unit didn't come with a hard copy manual.  I had to download one off the internet.  That's being a little too cheap in my opinion.  But other than that, I'd say that this TV is an excellent value.

I bought this mostly as a pdf and MS doc reader for book-length manuscripts.  The 7" tablets and 6" eReaders that are out there have too small a screen for me for extended use.  At the price a refurb of the 8.9 HD was offered on sale, I thought it would be worth trying out.  It's a pretty good reader for pdfs, although there isn't any ability to change font size unless you try to convert pdfs into Kindle format via email, which is a hit and miss process.  The screen is fantastic for reading MS docs, very sharp and the 8.9 size makes reading long docs a breeze.

I also looked at the ability to watch video (TV and movies) through my Prime account.  The screen is great for that as well, but apparently you can only stream free content.  You can't download unless you pay, which makes this device less desirable for airplane viewing.  Google Play on my 7" Android tablet seems to have a more interesting selection of movies for rental.

So the Kindle Fire 8.9 HD is a very good to fantastic device as an e-reader and a pretty good device for watching TV shows and movies.  But as a tablet for apps it isn't good.  Basically, Amazon has defanged the Android OS to make this device work best as an Amazon product delivery system.  Standard apps for Android, like Google Navigation, aren't available.  There are many key apps I use on my Android 7" tablet and Apple iPhone that aren't available.  Everything seems to be oriented toward buying books, movies, TV shows, and apps through Amazon.  It's more than a bit annoying, and the OS used isn't nearly as slick as you'd find with a pure Android or Apple tablet.

I'll be happy to use this as a reader for book-length manuscripts.  The quality and size of the screen hold a lot of appeal to me.  But I'll keep using my iPhone and Android 7" tablet for apps.  This device comes up short in that department.

This is a review for a newby DJ.  I'm a pro musician, but very much old school.  I still record live on 24 track tape although I do some editing with Protools.  I was looking for something to alter and mix simply on the fly so I picked up this thing.  The manual is very barebones and the drivers and software this device comes with out of the box don't work with my Macbook Pro.  But I went onto the Hercules website, installed updated drivers and software and then it worked fine.

This isn't really a professional device.  It's all plastic and doesn't seem like it's made to take a beating or last for very long.  But for playing around and mashing up tunes it can be a lot of fun.  The software is pretty slick.  None of it is intuitive.  The manual didn't help.  To get an idea of what I could do I had to go on youtube and find some tutorials.

There's a lot this controller can do I have yet to explore.  It's going to take me many, many hours and weeks to get up to speed and learn how to use this machine to its fullest.  I don't know if I want to commit to that level of study.  But so far, everything works as stated.  I haven't had a single bit of trouble beyond having to update the original software.  The sound is clean, but it is a bit on the low-fi side as far as I can tell; my guess is that there are ways to increase the audio quality, but I haven't figured out exactly how to do that yet.  If you're a teen, I bet you can have a lot of fun with this controller.  Even for an old guy like me, it has its perks as a kind of cool toy.

Heavy duty backup device.  I use this on my Macs for backup.  It's easy to set up with Time Machine and works well over a standard wireless network.  Word to the wise, though.  Do the initial backups with your computer on ethernet, otherwise they will take forever.  This NAS is really a 1TB backup device in standard mode, given that the second TB is designed to provide a backup to your backup.  If you want something built like a rock and can afford it, this is a nice backup storage device to have.

The price on this thing has gone up 50% since I bought it last week, but it's still pretty inexpensive.  I plugged it into my MacBook Pro 15" i7 (bought new last month) and it worked without a hitch.  All I had to do is go into System Preferences and click to change the sound output designation (the TV sound preference shows up when the adapter is plugged into the TV).  Looks well built.  Most of the adapters out there, unlike this one, will not carry sound to the TV.  This one does it all.  Recommended.

I don't use cable TV.  It's too much money for too few decent channels.  I just hooked this thing up to my antenna, turned it on and voila!  It set itself up finding all the channels (including a bunch of digital channels in my area that I had no idea existed).  The remote is very intuitive and it comes with batteries right out of the box.

This is one easy machine for anyone to set up and use.  The picture quality is excellent.  It looks like there are plenty of devices that you can plug this thing into.  Sound quality is also excellent.  With my old TV, I used some old computer speakers as a supplement; on this one the sound quality is so good that this was unnecessary.  The TV was also very easy to hook up to my DVD player.

This is a very well designed machine through and through.  You could spend more money for a Sony or Samsung, but I don't see why you would.  You could spend less money on a no name TV, but I've been burned one too many times with no name stuff. It looks like another quality product from Panasonic.

Unlike every plastic film protector I've ever tried to use, this thing goes on like a dream. There was no struggling with bubbles. The included alcohol wipe probably helped with the ease of application. It's as clear and responsive as promised, too, and feels just like working directly on the screen. One caveat is that, since they sell the same model glass for the iPhone 5S and the iPhone 5C - two phones with slightly different dimensions - the fit is not as close as the perfectionist in me might like. The other, and significant, caveat is that I dropped my phone just once and this thing shattered into a zillion pieces. My phone was fine. So this product definitely is on the fragile-side.

This is my fourth 15" MacBook Pro in 10 years.  I buy the same model every time, new and improved.  This is the first one I have some qualms about.

1) Glossy screen stinks.  Too much glare.  Glossy screens are for casual users, not professionals.

2) I need to buy a dongle to hook this up to an external screen.  That's ridiculous.  A dongle, what is this 1988?

3) One day the battery will conk out and because of Steve Jobs' neurotic tick about external batteries, I'll have to shell out 250 bucks or so to get a new one. Harrumph!

4) Other than that, the machine is fast, slick and wonderful, a significant improvement over the one I bought three years ago.

If you need some high quality cloth tape and black is your color of choice, this roll will do the job.  Designed to be relatively glare free, this industrial grade tape has a myriad of uses.  It sticks well, but it's also easy to unstick without leaving a residue (if you don't leave it on for too long).  It tears off the roll easily and cleanly.  Pricey, but recommended.  I just used it to repair the driver's seat visor on my wife's 20 year old station wagon.  Did the job well.

I bought this item because I was looking for a multi-function iPod player with decent sound that I could sometimes use as an alarm clock.  This was the cheapest of the bunch and I've used and liked Onkyo products in the past.

I offer only one cautionary note.  Don't even think that this item will replace your home stereo.  No portable iPod player will do that.  You can only pack so much sound quality in a portable box plus the iPod music files often are 128 mp3s, which don't come close to having decent fidelity.  That said, the sound here is more than adequate for listening in a bedroom.

Overall, this is a well designed box and the remote is easy to use.  I've put my old 3G iPod in the dock as well as my iPod Touch and they both work fine.  Onkyo states up front that the video out on this model is not compatible with iPod Touch videos, but the audio is completely compatible.  The ability to play mp3s from a CD is also a nice feature.  There are more expensive devices like this out there.  I have no idea why you'd spend the extra bucks to buy one.  This item is definitely a best buy.

*Note.  The week after I wrote this review the price for this item went up 50 percent.  It's still a solid piece of equipment, but I would not have bought it at the new price.
