Hey, you!  Yea, you!  Are you one of those people that seen the previews of "Aeon Flux" and thinking, "Woah!  This movie's so gonna suck; I mean, "Catwoman" suck"?  Well, my unseen random consumer...I cannot blame you: the concept looks awkward, the stunts are glorified, and Theron's costume screams out "blech!".  My thoughts haven't changed, but within 700 words, my thoughts will render how this 1-star predicted disaster convert into a shocking 3-star entertaining romp.

With 1-star on my mind, I have to grasp into the story, which is about as comprehensible as Dubya Bush making his speech.  In about 7 years from now, 99% of the Earth's pop is dead from a virus...possibly from the avian flu.  Those that survived are on scientific notice, and one Trevor Goodchild conducted a cure that will purity the remains...sort of.  All I know is that 400 years into the future, one 'psychedechnical' (Psychedelic meets Technical) city holds the survivors under control of the Goodchild regime, runned by the same guy who cured them 400 years ago (???).  But the rebels against the regime's reign continues to weaking his power, though the territorial rebels are destroying for the good, as the regime are really hostile that often kills certain civilians that might corrupt the nation's premise.  In other words: Government = bad; "bad guys" = good.  Only one Aeon Flux (Charlize Theron), a high-ranked fighter of the rebels, has the strength to take down something as confusing as the regime.

So, Ms. Theron here fights the government wearing clothes that ranges from "Awful" to "Not awful like the last one", although I doubt Theron would degrade herself to wear the old revealing get-up the original femme fatale wore on the animated show.

Anyway, the "future" remains uncertain, and by uncertain, I mean I have no idea how anything I see in this film work.  How did Aeon's weapons work, how do the futuristic security system function, how is swallowing some pill got Aeon get in touch with the leader of the rebels from her mind, and what are the foods these people are eating?  It seems as though the movie just goes into the future setting without any hint of social explanation.  At least the producers kept the atmosphere in spirit of the original series, along with its intended characters and premise.  And as long as you can tolerate some of the actors goofy one-liners, the characters act well, and Theron is a good Aeon, which is why the star went up a pound.

Another pick-er-upper is the fact that the movie has layers, albeit layers done very sloppy.  As Aeon confrots Trevor to assassinate in a vengeful manner, as she should, a revelation occurs when love and secluded past memories affected her way of thinking.  Neither had killed each other, which resulted in a backlash between the regime and rebels.  That's when the good part sets in, as many mysteries of the film (but not all) have been revealved that deals with the past, the search for a cure, and cloning.  Now, she and Trevor alone are on their own mission to find a solution to the nation's problem, while getting away from the regime who not only considered them as fugitives, but so has the rebels who now wants to kill Aeon.

"Aeon Flux" is not so bad, I was really surprised.  The abrupt and incohesive premise should've been dealt with more "flux"-iblilty, but the fact remains: it's not boring, it had some cool action scenes, and it had a solid story as it progresses.  As long as you don't think of this as Theron's big hit like "Monster" or "North Country", this film will give you a decent time.

This is Del Keyes, saying "At least it's better than that Tomb Raider film."

Well, after my "Country Bears" review, it was only a matter of time before I come across a monkey movie. And yet miraculously, this is the better film. "Monkeybone" can give most children nightmares, pretty much what "Cool World" did for me. But unlike Ralph Bakshi's unmerited trash, I sorta enjoyed this movie as well as admit to its disturbing atmosphere. Director Henry Selick has always been the go-to guy for scary designs based on a couple of films he made, which is why he's Tim Burton's no. 2 on his buddy list. His stop-motion works always appear so grim and yet so fascinating, filled with creative nuances in how the set pieces move. Therefore, I really like the visual treatment this live-action/stop-motion combo is going for. It's about a cartoonist named Stu (Brendon Fraser) who successfully pitched a cartoon series based on his creation, Monkeybone. He was about to pitch to his scientific girlfriend (Bridget Fonda), until he somehow got into a coma from an inflatable animal-related car accident. His soul went into a purgatory-like place, Downtown. It's a vulgar, perverse surreal world he's in, and many frightening stop-motion animations cross his path; on the upside, it had Rose McGowan as cleavage-tastic catgirl. He meets his cancerous, unlikable imaginary simian, Monkeybone, and the two tried to escape from this world, but it was trick by Monkeybone who instead stole his body. Stu has to rely on the unlike force of Whoopi Goldberg as Death to get his body back and to stop a sinster plot to produce more nightmares from the living, because his girlfriend happened to make chemical compound called 'nightmare fuel' (which acts more like the toxin The Scarecrow used). As interesting as the story is, it's not much to rave about. The director seems to be weak in the real world scenes, because they're not as fun as Downtown and the Monkeybone-possessed Stu's antics are more primal than clever. If there's one scene in the real world that I enjoyed, it's the part where Stu possessed a dead gymnast (Chris Kattan) and is being chased by doctors wanting his organs, probably because Bob Odenkirk was one of the doctors; normally, I would get annoyed wondering why the doctors are chasing a corpse without wondering why it's even alive, but since Bob and Chris delivered a good set of laughs, I let it slide. "Monkeybone" was fun by its artistic merits, because it sure isn't for Brendan's dull attempt at playing two characters, the title character's wisecracks, and people simply monkeying around.

Kristanna Loken tried her hardest, but she couldn't escape from her Terminatrix past. While she does look the part as Rayne, she didn't convey the part in the movie; I never played any of the "Bloodrayne" games, but I know the lead character wasn't boring. The actress didn't bother to emote whenever she speaks, whenever she performs, or whenever she stands perfectly still with her cleavage hang out. It's rather difficult to get involved with her plight since she simply walks across straight lines while reading them, and she's not the only performer at fault. The other actors are blisslessly underperformed; I expected such quality in Michael Madson, who's an incongruous addition among the cast alongside Michelle Rodriguez, but not even Ben Kingsley gave it his best as the antagonist named Kagan. Such light-handedness could be blamed by the poor script, which has characters deliver corny or awkward lines like, 'Kill her; let find the Eye or let her try, then kill her'. Thanks, Boll. "Bloodrayne" is a dull movie to sit through. It holds nothing back on the extreme gore and nudity, and it does have pretty nice locations, but this is a lifeless movie. None of the characters have any depth to them and they don't really matter in the long run, and some of the plotlines that occur are irrelevant; plus, it had a pointless montage at the end of the movie. It's hard to really hate this movie like I should in a Boll movie, but in this case, nothing about this movie really matters. At least the game that comes with the package was a decent extra.

Ben Stein needs to learn that most of his audience aren't as smart as him, so he needs to reach out to them in a manner they could understand.  The thing about documentaries is that no matter how uninteresting or compelling they are, they usually have a theme to comprehend the viewers. For "An Inconvenient Truth", it's about the dangers of global warning; for "Religuious", it's about the falsehood of religion; for "Sicko", it's about the lack of universal health care. When it comes to "Expelled", I presume it's about blanketing Intelligence Design.

Here's the thing: what IS Intelligence Design? The movie doesn't explain what it's about, or show examples as to how it works; the movie could've show a chalkboard of numbers, at least that wouldn've been an explanation.  It took me a while after seeing the film to vaguely grasp that it might be a study or proof that some superior being created life on earth, and even then, it's a very undefined subject.  What I do understand about "Expelled" is that it's another religion vs. science debate.  For most of the film, it's about scientists and esteemed authors throwing around arguments about Darwinism and Creationism, how the higher-ups are trying to diminish those who try to prove evolution wrong, and at one point the film even went as far as comparing Darwinism to Nazism and how that's the future of humanity.  Wow, I really doubt the majority of the world would lead to something that extreme.

What "Expelled" really is is just people throwing big words at each other, without making soluble proof to support their sophisticated beliefs.  And that's the problem with this documentary: it's too high-brow for its own good.  It's also incredibly dry, and when it's advertised as a comedy of sorts, I expected some perks to keep it lively; with Ben Stein, I can't tell if he's trying to be witty or not.  He tried by adding 'funny' clips and wacky skits during his narration, but they're just there, and I don't see how most of them illustrate his overall views.  As a documentary of entertainment value, it's lacking; Michael Moore, he is not.  Moore may be exaggerating a lot of facts in his films, but he was to-the-point in what he's trying to say, and his films can be both informative AND entertaining. With this film, I felt neither enlightened or immersed by the content, just exhausted.

I have no real opinion on the movie's subject, the convoluted nature of it made it sorta difficult to form one.  But I do believe in freedom of speech.  IF there really is a force to restrict people to talk about I.D., then I don't approve of it.  People should have to express what they like to say; even if they make absurd, uncanny, and incredibly farfetched statements, they have the right to make absurd, uncanny, and incredibly farfecthed statements. If Ben Stein wanted to make a documentary about this subject, then he has the right as well.  But he should at least make it exciting.  The most important factor about a documentary movie is that it invokes awareness and understanding, and "Expelled" did neither for me.

Trying to complain about Disney's obsession with movies about talking animals is self-defeating. Like taxes, they will never go away, and we'll see more them in the future. As long as kids eat this stuff up, there's an audience for this cheap marketing scheme. This might sound like I'm already hating "Beverly Hills Chihuahua", but I can't for the life of me say it's awful. It's just another silly talking animals movie, but at least no one's singing for its own sake or people throwing arms at verbally-understood creatures like hypnotized drones since the dogs and humans are in their own communicative world. Already, the movie's a step up from "The Country Bears". Chloe is a selfish, materialistic spoiled chihuahua raised by a rich Jamie Lee Curtis. While the dog's under the care of a babysitter (the barkeep/diver from "Coyote Cave"), the neglectful babysitter and her friends go off to Mexico, where Chloe will eventually be dognapped by a crime lord who controls the dog fights. She escaped with her allies, and while she tried to head home, she learned about the flaws of her character, realized what's important and all that typical Disney schlock. Even she eventually gets better, I just can't stand this dog: not because of how self-absorbed and demeaning she is, but how obnoxiously chatty she is. Always has to worry about what she wears, often making sly comebacks, and frequently pointing out the needs of her rich style. She's the benefactor of my disdain for animal chatter. Delgado, on the other hand, is an upside to the verbal animals concept; he's the main protector Chloe met before she escaped with him from the villain's hideout. Cool name aside, he's not much of a chatterbox, can't tolerate Chloe's high-strung behavior, reliable, and takes a direct approach to everything. I actually like tha dog, since I can sorta identify with him in a non-species manner. Too bad, much like every other combative stray in many romantic films, he has to grow all caring about Chloe even though he shouldn't; at least he didn't fall for her, but he still worries for her. As you can see, talking animals has never been annoying because of the concept of talking; it's how much they talk and the attitude they have when they speak that can be damaging. For Delgado, he's a tolerate exception. The movie was fine enough with just dogs with obvious CGI lip-synching, then it had to bring in the rat and iguana. I never liked them, because they represent they are bad habit of Disney. Because it's a requirement for Disney movies to have a comic relief (and the George Lopez-voiced Chihuahua doesn't seem to be good enough, apparently), there has to be two bumbling thieves to crack jokes and cause chaos. That's just peachy, an obviously CGI rat and reptile doing forced laughs to bug me. But the movie does have other interesting characters. It does surprise me that the main human antagonist, in a movie about dogs talking in puns and accents, actually appears threatening and not a corny villain desperate for laughs (I'm looking at you, clown from "Air Bud"), and the nefarious doberman named El Diablo ain't that corny either (though I wonder why dobermans always have to be bad guys). What else can I say? It is what it is, nothing to get enraged about. "Beverly Hills Chihuahua" has a story that plays it straight: it's a dog who lost his way, facing challenges and peril in an exotic scenery. Is it really best Chihuahua movie ever made? Close, but it sure didn't beat "Oliver and Company"; sure, that movie is about a cat, but it does have a chihuahua playing a racist stereotype.

- MY RANT

I LOVE Zero 7's debut album, "Simple Things."  It's hard to conject the posititve aspects of this LP, because it's SO multi-layered.  This album makes me dream, think, love, and explore many things about myself.  There is absolutely no bad tracks in this LP, and even a weak song like "Salt Water Sound" is still good.  Songs like the "Destiny", "This World", and "Spining" are all amazingly produced with vocals that match each track's sound perfectly.  The instrumentals themselves are just as great, with my favorite being the poignant "Take it Away."

"Simple Things" is different than what I normally hear.  It's soothing, yet it throbbs me.  I can't help but recommend this album, though if the album samples bores you, don't bother with the LP.  Leave others like me to enjoy the sounds of nature and culture.

"Kangaroo Jack" is similar to "Boat Trip" in that its whole attention is based on false advertising.  TV ads, posters, and the DVD cover art picture this attempt at a marketable mascot as Mr. Cool: talking slick, doing dance moves, and singing old songs that are glorified puns of his being; he's suppose to be the next Mc Skat Cat.  The thought of all that cringed me, but it turned out that the marsupial's wayward coolness only occurred in a two-minute dream sequence, as well as the end 'outtakes'.  I was relieved, but then I had to face an even more cringing aspect: Anthony Anderson cracking jokes and getting Jerry O'Connell into trouble.

The real story of "Kangaroo Jack" is about a hairdresser (O'Connell) and his buddy con-man (Anderson), although they seems to be friends out of obligation since the con-man rescued the hairdresser's life long ago and neither of them can't stand each other.  They both work for the mob boss (played by an underused Christopher Walken), and after a reckless chase of a heist went horrible wrong by those two, they were sent to Australia to deliver a special package to a Mr. Smith; neither of them knew they were being sent to be executed.  On the way down the desert road, the two found an apparently dead kangaroo they named Jackie Legs; they stupidly made him wear a jacket with the special package inside, but the kangaroo was actually alive and escaped.  Realizing what they lost, they're off on a chase across the outback, while Mr. Smith and the button men eventually chase them with guns blazing.

I'm getting a little bored with the comedy yells.  Jerry and Anthony yell when they're pedaling across a busy traffic to avoid the cops, they yell when they drove their jeep through rocks, they yell when their fighter plane is out of control by their stupid antics, and they yell when bugs are crawling on them.  They're about as predictable as the love-interest in this movie, an animal-caregiver whom she first met them on the plane and eventually falls for the hairdresser, because what girl wouldn't fall for Jerry O'Connell?  Jackie Legs got on my nerves, mainly due to how he was shot; the kangaroo is almost always in a close-up face-shot when he does something humor, like the movie was forcing to kids to say, "hey, this kangaroo made a funny face.  LAUGH, KIDS, LAUGH!"  Even more astounding is a couple of film goofs I noticed: the mobs were calling Mr. Smith in daylight on both locations, even though due to time difference, it should've been nightime in Australia; and most notably, the scene where the plane destroyed its left wing, but on the next scene the left wing is still in place.

"Kangaroo Jack" is not only irritating to watch, it's also kinda unfriendly for kids.  Besides the typical misunderstood gag about poo and one's orientation, there's a lot intense violence regarding guns, Jerry copped a feel, and the animal-caregiver took a waterfall bath in a provocative manner (though she's wearing clothes).  I'm beginning to think this movie is suppose to be a PG-13 action-comedy not unlike "Rush Hour", but the studio decided to add a wacky marsupial and targeted this movie for a younger demographic; that was a bad idea.  Although, the cinematography looks nice, but then, Australia is always nice to look at.

The MC books I usually read are all about the club being into drugs and sex etc. But this MC book is about something different. Its like this MC book is about family. And love and the MC club really cares about the people who are in the club not just as they are a member by that they are family and the care deeply for one another. They all want a family and a life outside of the club too. But, when Brice meets a woman he never thought he would meet she is hiding something from him. And he needs to break through her barriers so that he can begin to help her break away from her past and begin her future possibly with him. They both have secrets. Can they both share their secrets? Or will their secrets destroy any chance they have of being together? Well, I will let you read the book to learn all this and more. I can't wait to find out if this author has more books coming our way. As I have now found a new author to follow and read what she writes in the future.

I was given a copy if this book in exchange for a fair and honest review.  Lane and Mallory have meet under some circumstances that mean they really could never have a relationship but something about this girl pulls Lane in. He knows having anything to do with her is wrong and she knows it too. Mallory has a past that has made her very fearful of getting close to people. She has a wall put up but when she meets Mr. Stone something draws her closer to him each day. Is there anyway these two can find a way to meet in middle and have any kind of a relationship or is it just too much to handle. Mallory doesn't know how to trust anyone or open up to anyone and well Lane is just a typical man who doesn't know what he wants with a woman. Does he want one to marry, just one to have when he wants her etc? Mallory needs to move on because she knows what she feel is impossible to act on. And Lane nows it more than Mallory does. Sometimes this book made me cry, it made me scream, it made me laugh and it made me want to reach in and choke Lane for not waking up at times and realizing what's right in front of him. There are things though that Mallory is hiding from Lane and the same for Lane hiding from Mallory and well when the truth comes out who is going to get hurt the worst? I can only say that I was amazed by the characters and they way they were written about in this book. I was amazed with the storyline in this book. This book took hold and would not let me stop until I had finished the entire book. I will not tell you the ins and outs from here because I don't want to give anything away but for me this is a book that I recommend as a read to anyone looking for a love story where two people don't even know love for themselves.

I was given a copy of this book in exchange for a fair and honest review. What a brilliant love story!!!!  This book was truly amazing. At every page turn you where wondering if things were going to work out for Anne and Blake. I mean come on they have such different backgrounds can it really work? But I  will let you read the book for that answer. Anne and Blake are both chasing the freedom to live and love without barriers that some people seem to think they have. There are obstacles that get in their way and well quite frankly can they overcome them? Will they get their happily ever after? Well I won't tell you that I will tell you that I can't wait for what's coming next. This book is great and i highly recommend it to all readers. It just warms your heart the way this book is written with love and understanding. So go now and one click this book or add it on you TBR list on goodreads.

This book has a very interesting storyline. Sylvia needs her fantasy fulfilled and her friends know just what to do. So they call a service and plan to have her most secret of fantasy come true. But can Sylvia keep it professional or will feelings get involved. Slade is one of the men there to help fulfill her fantasy but there is something more to him that meets the eye. And Sylvia doesn't know if she can get past the way he looks at her.  Or the way her body responds to him. I liked this book. I do need to read more so that I can find out what happens between the two of them. Great book.

I was given a copy of this book in exchange for a fair and honest review. Honestly I had only read one other book by author A.M. Willard but I loved that one so I said I had to read this one since its the first in this series of books. Morgan thinks she is marrying the man of her dreams but is she. Morgan has her own bake shop that people stand in line at to get her amazing treats. But does her fiancee really love her for her or is he just up to something else. Simon just maybe isn't the man that Morgan thinks he is. Morgan does however meet Brody but what is a woman to do? She was just engaged to Simon who well I can't tell you. I just can't give that away to potential readers. This book is a lovely journey of finding,losing, and finding potential love again. Morgan loves to bake and whats one way to a man's heart is through his stomach right? Well you have to read this book to find out all the details but I can tell you that Simon may not have been the only man with his eyes on Morgan. I love the sweetness of this book and how Morgan would do anything for anyone if they needed it. This book is the girl next store love story that makes you wish that Morgan could see what she has to offer any man. In this story you also get the story of some of Morgans friends these are very easily brought into the story.
Another great book by author Emily Jane Trent, I fell in love with Stefano and Kyra and the more I read the more secrets are revealed. I can't wait to see where this series takes me.

Reclaim Me is the second book in the Jaded Series by Alex Grayson it brings us the story of life long friends/enemies Mia and Mac, Once thought to be the forever sweethearts a series of events have taken them to separate places. All these lost years with no reason why Mia feels she at least should hear what Mac has to say knowing she will never be able to forgive him. But when Mac wants to let Mia know all the secrets of the past will Mia be able to forgive or will the hatred be too much to handle and will Mia need to run. This book was one that I feel into and couldn't put it down. This books takes you to places that you only hear about most times and when you read this book you are going to have feelings some undeniable feelings. This book not only breaks your heart but it will be able to mend that broken heart back together again if these characters aren't too stubborn to finally listen to one another. But has to many years passed for closure. Or will they be able to finally be around each other as friends when the truth comes out. Love this story.

This is the second book in the Straight from the Heart series and this time we learn more about Cale and Bryn. We also get more information about their budding relationship, However how are keeping secrets from one another. Cale has demons he doesn't want Bryn to find out and Bryn has things from her past that make her kind of closed off to relationships. Both love their band and really deep down they love each other however until they both open up about things they will always be too afraid to really show that love to each other. This book also takes up deeper into some troubling things. This book is suspenseful, romantic and just really good. Can't wait to read whats to come next. great book.

This book is a beautifully written story of first love. When Chris meets Claire he can't believe she has survived the life that she has been living. Claire had been living on the streets and wasn't very excited about another foster family. However when Chris welcomed her into his home with his mother she felt that maybe things could be different. Christ liked music and was beginning to prepare for a possible music career. Claire just wanted to be loved and cared for. Do Chris and Claire get their fairy tale happier ever after or is Claire too afraid of what might come if she falls hard for Chris. I won't give any more of the story away you need to read this book to find out the rest. I can say that this book will make you cry, and it will make you frustrated and it will make you happy all at the same time. I have completely finished the series and will post the reviews to the other books as well but if you love basic love stories then this is a must read. This book offers some twists and turns that you don't see coming as well. Very well written.

Loved this book. Love this series. Cassia Leo really has a way of breaking into your heart and not letting go. Chris has never gotten over his first love. And Claire even though she thinks she has moved on truly she hasn't. Can they find their way back to each other and survive the many secrets they each have? Or will it be too late for them to make a difference. As with all Cassia's book this one too ripped right through me. I had tears and laughs all the way through with then again just wanting to reach inside and shake these two to make them wake up and see what they have together.

First off let me begin by saying I love Christa Lynn's work. But something about this book just took a hold and really held on till the end. First you have Ally and she has something inside that scares her in a way that makes her at one point maybe just want to runaway from it all and never look back. Then you have Jackson who has things to hide himself and when you put them both together you get this wonderful story Running From Destiny. Are they both running from their destiny with each other? Or are they running from their separate destinys. Well that you have to read for yourself. I spent a few nights staying up way to late since I couldn't put the book down and just had to know what was coming next and where do Jackson and Ally end up. But I can say I laughed and cried a little and then wanted  to reach  in and slap the crap out of them at a couple of points in the book. I will continue to search for book by this author Christa Lynn because this book alone makes you know she has so much more to give her readers. Can't wait to see what she has coming next. I recommend this book to everyone and you need to get this book now. Great job author Christa Lynn.

One of the best MC reads I have every had the opportunity to read. This book came to me through NetGalley and I am so happy it did. Ghost is a story of family, love, and helping one another to be better than the day before. But it also has so much suspense that it keeps you on the edge of your seat the entire time you are reading. I couldn't put this book down reading it from start to finish in a matter of hours. This MC series has made me a fan of this author from this day forward and I can't wait to see what she has coming next. Excellent read.

This is my first book by author Amo Jones and my goodness she did not disappoint me at all. Phoebe Rendon has a family unlike most of us. They are in the Sinful Souls MC club. And her brother loves her without a doubt and wants to protect her with his life. But he can also maybe be a little over protective. Phoebe loves all things fast and she wants nothing more than to live her life driving fast cars but that takes money so she takes a job that she really doesn't like too much in order to fulfill her life long dream of owning her own track. So she works as a fashion consultant and needs to go on the road for one last job to get the money she needs to make all this work. Never did she expect to find him again, the man that she once thought she loved. Until the day he left her. Can she continue with this job that she needs to finish out her dreams? Or will she lose it because of him, the rocker that she once thought loved her too, Ryder Oakley, in all of his glorious hotness that she once thought she loved. And who she thought once loved her. But something has changed he is no longer the nice man that she thought she loved but he is cold hearted to her. But what did she do? Does he really hate her that much? Also you have his twin brother that looks just like him. Can she get the answers she desperately needs to know? Why did he leave her so long ago? Why couldn't he just talk to her? Is there a chance that things can be different with them or will she lose herself in the process? This book is a romantic, suspenseful, rocker book with some MC thrown in too. At times I cried and laughed all the while wanting at times to reach into the pages of this book and strangle the men all at one time. Amo Jones is a wonderful author who really has a winner in this book. Everyone should one click this book and or put it on your TBR list on Goodreads as soon as possible.

A lover's Lament the story of Devin and Katie is an amazing story of love with trials and tribulations taking them on a path neither of them knew was coming. The time they have together is some of the most amazing love that one person can have. I read a small description of this book and saw the large number of reviews and said I have to have this book. And wow I am so glad I did I read it on two days and that's all with watching my kids etc. This is a book that you just can't stop reading until the end. Now I have added another author to my list of forever authors ones that I will forever one click their books as well as follow them anywhere available so that I don't miss another book they have available. Don't miss out like I almost did go grab this book now. It will have you laughing, crying and totally losing yourself the entire time you are reading it.

Claire has a secret and she doesn't want Chris to find out. In the book before this she had made a decision about her and Chris that she would maybe regret but felt like it was all she could do. Then a few years later things just come crashing down on her. She loves Chris and although she chose to let him go she never stopped loving him. But can she tell him he secret. Can they try and heal both their broken hearts? Claire has not felt the love of a family for so long she's afraid to let anyone in. But can she continue to let Chris back in or does she run. Maybe she can maybe she can't thats for you to read and find out. Will there love survive the secret? That too you will have to read and find out. I loved this book and this is one that I will read again and again. At some points making me cry, laugh and want to reach in and just strangle people.

Yet another excellent heartwarming romance novel by the amazing Debbie Macomber. I was thrilled when I got approved from Netgalley to read the second book I have ever read by this author but it sure won't be the last. Keep them coming please.

Well I didn't think it was possible for the author to take me on an even better journey than her first book in this series but boy was I wrong. Once again Valerie and Flynn are able to break my heart open wide and slowly start to put it back together again. I will say there were times I wanted to reach into the book and strangle some of the characters but I had to give it time to see where they ended up at. Once again I had some tears, heartache and the desire to shake some sense into these characters at time but once again KL Shandwick was able to give me the story that I loved so much the first time around. I loved this story and can't wait for part three to be released to see exactly where Flynn and Valerie end up.

Never Tap Out my first book by Author Victoria Prince but most certainly not my last. When I came across this book listed as an ARC I was very intrigued. So I contacted this author and was given the book in exchange for an honest and fair review. So to begin you have Katherine who has been in a real life rut the past couple of years. She doesn't feel she has any real family left and often times wonders what it is she has been put here on this earth to do. Katherine's mother was a very well know wrestler who Kate admired every day and often wondered if she could be remotely as good as her mother was. So Katherine decides to give it a try and well to say the least at times just the training alone kicks her ass. Can Katherine even get remotely close to the caliber her mother was in this sport? And along the way the people that Katherine meets out of all of them one person James has literally lit a fire inside her that she herself may not be able to extinguish but does Katherine even want to extinguish this fire. There are things that even Katherine is afraid of that haunt her dreams every night. I cannot tell you though since you will learn all this when you read the book. I can say that I was very surprised about the things that happened in this book and how loverly the story was written. Never Tap Out = Never give up in more ways than one.

Emma is a housewife that is beginning to write a book and needs some research. But her husband Daniel just may not feel the same way she does about her research and if he was to find out what would be do? Then you add Markus into the mix and well you have a wonderful love triangle. Emma needs to get information for the book she is writing pertaining to the BDSM world so whats the best way to get it but go to the source. Emma finds herself in a twisted life of lies and deceit. Does she still love her husband? Or does she want more? This book will take you on a ride and not even you can figure out where it is going with the next page turn. I would recommend this book to anyone who wants a little twist to your love stories. And a little crazy with them as well because at times Emma thinks thats exactly where she is going is Crazy.

This will have been the first book I have read by this author but it won't be my last. Cory and Lacey meet under some usually circumstances but for some reaso Cory feels he needs to protect Lacey at all costs. Lacey thinks he is being over protective until little things start happening and in the back of her mind she is concerned. Buy should she tell Cory she feels something is happening and she might be in trouble. Maybe Cory will think she is crazy. Cory knows more than he is letting in as well but he doesn't want to scare Lacey away. Cory seems to really care for her. But when things finally come to light what's going to happen. Laceys scared, Cory needs to protect her at all costs. Can Cory protect her? Or is it too late!, A must read book of 2016.

I was provided a copy of this book in exchange for a fair and honest review which I am providing below. Wow Defy takes us on the journey of high school teacher Melody Greene and high student and football player/ hot head Jamie. Jamie is a High school senior and a member of the Hotholes a group of high school kids mostly up to no good. They also pretty much have the run of their town. Melody Greene is the lit teacher and once was a ballet dancer with high hopes of remaining in Julliard and being a professional dancer. However she had that taken away from her suddenly and now had teaching which she hated. One day while working she was having a bad day and lets just say she crosses paths with her student Jamie. Jamie has had sights on her for a long time. Melody finds herself drawn to Jamie and well lets just say things get hot. Melody however has constant fears someone will find out. Jamie just doesn't care. Can teacher and student continue their affair? Is it really an affair or just an easy way for Jamie to get what he wants? This book has excitement at the turn of every page. Can't wait to read what this author has next.

I could have sworn this review was already posted but well maybe it was my error. But Pepper Winters and this dollar series has been my most beloved series of all times and I just fell in love with these characters. I couldn't wait to get more and more of these books. It almost killed me to have to wait for millions not knowing what was going on while also being hard knowing it was the last in the series. Pepper I have devoured each and every one of your books and can't wait for whats to come.
My son loves this brand of wrestling shoes they are very comfortable and are very soft. Fit very well and true to normal shoe size.

I was given a copy of this book for review. OMG Amo Jones I am so thrilled to have found you and your books. I try new books all the time but yours have just grabbed a hold of something inside me and won't let go, to the point I stalk you to see what you have coming in the future. One Hundred & Thirty Six Scars is an amazing read that takes you on a journey of someone who thinks they are not worthy of love and feelings. Someone so hurt that they don't believe anyone can love them. But then he meets her, Meadow, and then he began to feel things he never knew would exist for him. OMG this book took me to places that I didn't know I could go while reading a book. If you like books that are full of excitement and thrills all while creating a wonderful backdrop for more then this is your book. When you have had nothing but hurt and pain in your life you just don't expect that to change until the right one walks in. Especially when you least expect it. Beast and Meadow have several obstacles thrown their way and well let's just say that with a name like Beast you can only imagine what he could do or be like. Amo Jones has quickly become one of my most favorite authors and I will continue to wait not so patiently for what she has to come in the future.

I have been a fan Hannah Ford's for the last year or so always waiting patiently for the next book in her series to become available. The What He Wants series is a series that I can never put down and I beg for the next one to become available. Sometimes you wonder if you are ever going to be able to find your man. Noah is a man who seems to have it all. But does he really. He then meets Charlotte and she dreams of a day when Noah will notice her for the sexy woman she is. However, when Noah starts to really notice her does she know what she is getting herself into. Noah likes his control and she has feelings for him. Noah is a demanding man who always gets what he wants but can she give him what he needs. This book and this series is one that will keep you on your toes wanting to read whats coming next. I went through this series in a matter of less than a week and still am begging for more. Hannah Ford is an amazing author and can deliver a story to you that you will be demanding more of as well. Grab your copy of this series as soon as possible and add it to your TBR Good reads list as well. Hannah Ford you are amazing and I cannot wait for what you have coming for all of us in the future.

I replaced my sink, disposal and faucet all at the same time.  I swapped out an old ceramic sink with a stainless steel and my badger 1 disposal with this one.  Even with sink types considered, since ceramic sinks usually dampen sound better than SS, this disposal is quiter than the old junky, defective badger 1.  I've had no problem with jams, or power of this disposal.  It's handled everything we've dumped in it without issue.  The EZ Mount system is very easy to install and since I put this on a stainless steel sink I didn't need plumber's putty.  The rubber gasket was all that was needed.

The one thing I do want to mention is that this disposal does come with a 3 prong plug, so if your previous disposal is direct wired, you will either need to wire this up to the existing wire by removing the plug or by dropping an outlet in the wall under the sink.  I opted to install an outlet.  I cut the hole, installed a post work wire box and wired a ground circuit outlet in.  Not that any of that has anything to do with the review, just gloating I guess.  Anyway, fantasitc product, and hoping it will stand the test of time as others are saying it does.

Purchased the Stainless steel version of this faucet for a decent price.  Our first impression of the faucet was that it was a pretty decent deal and looked good on the surface.  My initial concerns were that the inner connectors are all cheap plastic, the neck dribbles water for a few seconds after being turned off and approximately 1 in 3 uses of the faucet we will hear a loud popping when the water is turned on.  Seems that something is wrong with the water diverter / sprayer or something of that nature.  I checked all over for leaks that may be causing the water to dribble and found nothing.  Additionally, the base of the neck that you must turn to tighten the neck to the facet base constantly turns and loosens as you move the neck back and forth from one side of the sink to the other.  This quickly becomes annoying due to the need to constantly retighten the neck base so that the neck doesn't fall off.

After a few months of using this faucet and needing to tighten the base of the neck to the base of the faucet, my wife noticed water pouring from the base onto the counter and into the sink when the faucet was turned on.  I unscrewed the neck and immediately noticed that one of the rubber water sealing rings on the base of the neck had broken.  I went to Walmart and picked up the Peerless brand spare parts pack they had there, which included all of the various rings and such for Peerless brand faucets.  I installed one of the spare rings and screwed the neck back into the base.  While doing so I heard a loud pop and once again removed the base to find that the plastic portion of the facet base had cracked.  Apparently the Peerless spare parts rings are slightly larger than the rings initially installed on this Peerless faucet.  The pressure from the miniscule size difference cracked the cheap plastic in the base.

I emailed Peerless support and they quickly got back to me and said they were sending out the replacement part.  I received the package a few days later and immediately realized they had completely failed to send me anything that I needed, including parts for the wrong finish of my faucet.  So I emailed them again, waited a few days and received a reply stating that they were again sending out he replacement parts.  After a few more days I received the package...they had sent a whole new faucet.  I installed the new faucet and everything was back to the way it was.  The neck dribbled, the neck base loosened over time, and all of the parts were still cheap plastic, but at least the faucet was working.

A few more months went by and now our faucet sometimes doesn't leak after being turned off.  No rhyme or reason as to why this happens.  The hot water handle also has a very loud and annoying squeal when turned on and off now.  Like wet rubber rubbing against itself or something.  No idea what the problem is and figure we can live with it so long as the faucet just works.

I'm fairly disappointed in this purchase.  I really do wish I would have spent a little more on a good faucet and not tried to save a few bucks.  As a point of interest, Peerless is, apparently, Delta's cheapo brand as that appears to be where my replacement parts came from.

and the bit still looks fantastic.  Had to drill a hole in my SS sink for a sprayer.  Used tap magic cutting fluid and a high speed drill and the bit still looks brand new.  The bit feels heavy and well built, and was able to cut through my new sink like butter.  I'm sure I even used too high of an RPM on the drill to do this, and the bit came out just fine after all was said and done.  Best few bucks I've spent on a drill bit in a while.

I was a bit apprehensive about doing this install, even though my technical and mechanical skills are very high, mostly because I lack patience for small, meticulous work like this.  But I manned up and jumped right in last night.  After quickly skimming a YouTube video for items in the device to watch out for during replacement, I began.  I'm not going to go over the technical aspects so much as there are literally dozens of awesome tutorials out there.

My digitizer was very shattered...on a scale of 1 - 10 (1 being a crack and 10 being completely blown out all over the place) mine was about a 7.  Many tutorials are going to tell you to take your time, be patient and carefully pull your broken screen off with a bunch of tools...this is good advice.  I got a small flat head and a hairdryer and carefully, but quickly chiseled out the screen.  I probably wasn't nearly as careful as they tell you to be because I broke a lot of glass and created many new shards, but was careful to brush them aside while working.  These glass shards are VERY small and sharp.  Please be careful not to lose any otherwise you may find them in your hands and/or feet later on down the road.  After about an hour of pulling the border glass off in various sized chunks, I was able to pull the remaining portion of the screen off with ease.

Once the old screen was off I cleaned out the remaining shards and glue and place the new ditizer back in.  I then checked the functionality of the new digitizer, the wifi, the volume, the lock and the power buttons before putting everything back together.  This is my biggest recommendation... CHECK ALL BUTTON AND DEVICE FUNCTIONALITY BEFORE SCREWING THE LCD BACK IN AND GLUING / STICKING THE NEW DIGITIZER IN PLACE!  If you get everything back in place and then find out you did break you volume buttons, or put the digitizer cables in upside-down, you're going to be hating life when you realize you have to do everything all over again.  But this time you have to do it without breaking the digitizer.

Moral of the story, my device is working perfectly.  The digitizer I got was excellent quality, no dead spots found, it's the correct size, crystal clear, looks and feels like the original and for a fraction of the cost of the OEM digitizer replacement.  I really have no idea why anyone would complain about this product...unless they worked on the Apple "genius" bar and are losing massive amounts of money because people are realizing they don't need to pay astronomical amounts of money for repairs to their locked down / proprietary / non universal products that break when a butterfly touches them.  Noooooooooo, that couldn't be the case.

Update: It's been a year and a half since I did this replacement.  The replacement screen and digitizer is still working strong even after a few more drops and two and three year olds playing with it.  Don't know if the screens going out now are the same as I received, but the one I got was cheap and very durable.

If only I'd purchased this years ago.  I have an A/C unit drain on the floor in my basement, so I can use the constant drain feature instead of needing to empty the bucket.  I can't get the separate hose that I purchased with this thing completely flat on the ground, not that that causes any issues.  Just for kicks, occasionally I'll go down and step on the hose to flatten in out and will hear a big dump of water go down the drain...so I know for sure this thing is definitely working.

The unit is pretty light, much more so than I anticipated.  The power cord is fairly long as well, which is good because the instructions apparently say not to use an extension cord for some reason.  The features are great.  It has a fan speed and humidity control options which both seem to function well.  I pretty much run mine on constant though and have not used the humidity control very much aside from just testing it out.

The noise could be an issue if you have this in a more family room setting.  It's nothing out of the ordinary though.  It's way quieter than an normal box fan on a 2 or 3 setting, and I've only operated this thing on high fan speed.  If you were trying to have a quiet conversation with someone and this thing was sitting next to you, then yeah, it would probably cause some issues on high speed.  Aside from that, I don't get the noise complaints.  It has a fan to pull the air through, it's going to make noise.

All in all, this was a good price and has great features.  It's also about $20 cheaper on Amazon versus the big box hardware stores at the time of writing.  Just a heads up.  And remember to get the drain hose if you plan to use the constant drain feature, this does not come with a hose.  I think it uses a 3/4 hose attachment if you plan to do something else like fix PVC piping to it for a permanent placement.

but was pleasantly surprised by how enjoyable it actually was.  I had heard that it received bad reviews after purchasing it for a trip I was going on.  I ended up playing it and found it difficult to put down.  Game play is fairly straight forward.  Equip yourself with the proper equipment, select the mission then go kill everything you see.  Pros and Cons:

Pros:
1.  Has a fairly decent selection of character parts to customize your character to your wants.
2.  Weaponry customization and upgrading is surprisingly vast.  I had no idea so many weapons were going to be available.
3.  Mission availability is very nice.
4.  Graphics are pretty unbelievable for the PSP.
5.  Items are everywhere.  And harvesting kills is a cool feature.

Cons:
1.  Controls are kind of unintuitive.
2.  Targeting system is nonexistent
3.  Stats and mission requirements are fairly difficult to understand.  Lots of reading required in order to understand what it is you are supposed to do.

All in all this game is very worthwhile.  I'm going to purchase part 2 now simply because this one was that much fun.

I've used this attachment with my dremel for at least 5 hours total time now, with various bits attached, and it has worked like a charm.  I followed all of the initial setup intructions for it, and off I when.  I've had no issues so far, and the attachment to my dremel was super easy.  I would recommend this purchase to anyone that uses their dremel a lot and wants better precision on their projects.  It's much easier to hold this and get precision work done than the dremel itself.

only 2 stars because the drainage design on this unit is horrible and can be very dangerous as water and electricity do not mix very well.  The condensers get really dusty, sometimes that dust mixes with the water that is supposed to drain to the bottom container to evaporate.  Very often with this unit, the water mixes with the dust and clogs some of the upper drains and the water overflows out of the unit and all over the floor.  Take off the right panel, about half way up there is a small yellow tray under the top condenser.  There is a small hole in that tray that is probably clogged, if you're having trouble with the water pouring out on to your floor.  Use a paper clip and carefully stir it around in that drain hole and pull out all of the junk that builds up in there.  That should fix the problem with water overflows.

However, this unit does cool very well.  It bottoms out at 64 degrees F for cooling, which is more than enough for most rooms.  If you want to try and stop the water from coming out of this thing, try to drain it every week or so if you live in a very humid environment.  If you live in a dryer climate you may never have to drain it as the unit should evaporate the water in the basin and blow it out of the back exhaust.  But that's what it is supposed to do, that doesn't mean it's always going to do it, hence the 2 star rating.  The drain plug is in the bottom of the back of the unit.
