The Chief Justice of the California Supreme Court, Fritz Rayburn is murdered and his sixteen year-old stepgranddaughter Hannah Sheraton is arrested. Her mother, Linda turns to her old college roommate Josie Baylor-Bates for help. At one time, Josie was a "hotshot" criminal defense attorney, but she has left that life behind her and settled into a small practice in Hermosa Beach, California. When Hannah is charged as an adult, Josie decides to help her...

Josie is haunted by memories of something that happened to her mother  and an old case where she defended a woman named Kristin Davis  it was her last case as before she left the "fast track" behind. After that case, Josie "realized she no longer had the stomach for defending those who should have been indefensible" ...

I was engrossed in this book from page one and I did not put it down until I reached the very last sentence. The characters are richly drawn, you can visualise each of them in great detail  all the way to seeing Hannah's cuts and her frightened eyes. You feel like a spectator as you watch the courtroom drama unfold. It is fascinating to follow the clues and evidence and try to figure out the whodunnit. I thought I knew early on who murdered Fritz Rayburn and why, but I was wrong. The real culprit was a bit of a surprise to me...

This book has all of the ingredients necessary for a great legal thriller: secrets in a wealthy family and the lengths they will go to to keep those secrets from being exposed; a tenacious defense attorney ready to put it all on the line for a mentally traumatised young girl she believes is innocent; excitement as the courtroom drama plays out  and the desire to find out the truth no matter what...

I was very impressed with the details of Hannah's mental disorder that were included in the book  it is very clear to me that the author cared enough to take the time to do the research...

I am a new Rebecca Forster fan and I will definitely be reading the rest of The Witness Series!

This series was recommended to me by Amazon based on my books I have read and enjoyed. That series was recommended after I read THE RIVERDALE PONY STORIES.

In thirteen year-old Emily Dickenson's house, there were some things she was not allowed to talk about. Horses were one of them and her dead sister was the other. She had been only five years-old and she had idolised her big sister  then the accident happened...

Emily loves horses and wants to ride them. For the past year, she has been secretly working at Sand Hill Stables to pay for riding lessons. Her best friend and "partner in crime" Mickey is the only person who knows this secret. Emily has told her mother that she has joined the choir...

Then Emily gets a chance to prove herself in the Fox Run Farm show. Will she be able to keep this secret from her mother? More than anything, Emily dreams of owning her own horse and winning competitions...

Claire Svendsen is the author of this delightful series of books and you can tell that she loves horses. The book series SHOW JUMPING DREAMS will appeal to young ladies and can be equally enjoyed by any horse lover...

Kindle Unlimited Member

Cara Laursen calls criminal investigator Larry Macklin. He is surprised to hear from her since she told him she was not comfortable dating a deputy. Cara asks Larry to come to her house because she needs help. When he asks her what was wrong, she does not want to talk on the telephone. When Larry arrives fifteen minutes later, he finds the chief suspect in his latest murder case sitting in her living room  her father, Henry...

Henry tells Larry that he is innocent and someone is trying to frame him, but the evidence points to his guilt. When a second murder is committed, there are links to Henry and Larry cant stop him from being taken into custody. How far is he willing to go to help prove Henry's innocence?

Eddie, Larry's first official confidential informant (who saved Larry's life in November's Past) makes an appearance in one of the subplots. Is there a bad apple in the sheriff's department?

This book opens with a murder scene and it gets better from there! My attention was captured immediately and I was lost in the book until the end. There were twists and turns to keep me guessing and plenty of clues to follow. The characters were interesting and storyline was believable. This was a true mystery for me -- I did not guess who was guilty before it was revealed although I did figure out why the murders took place.

I first bought six of the Vigilante series in 2012 and the last six were purchased earlier this year. For the first time, I am reading the entire series from beginning to end. I did not remember any of the storyline, it was like I was reading the book for the first time. I became a Claude Bouchard fan when I read "ASYLUM", a psychological thriller (with an AWESOME ending, in my opinion).

It is the summer of '96 and a vigilante is at work in Montreal. He is hunting down and executing people who have made others suffer. The newspapers have dubbed the unknown man the "Vigilante" and the police cannot find him. Most people would not care as he's ridding Montreal of some of the worst kind of people: drug dealers, pimps, gang-bangers, murderers, and the like. There have already been sixteen murders in six months and they are no closer to identifying the man behind the murders.

Claude Bouchard grabs your attention at the prologue and keeps you glued to the book until the end -- I read this through in one sitting. The people are interesting and you want to follow the storyline just to see what happens next. You want to see the mystery solved so you know who the vigilante is, but you secretly hope he keeps on executing evil people who have done very evil things. There are many twists & turns along the way in this thriller that you will change your "suspect" several times before you get the the end of the book (the last vigilante action in the book is my favourite).

Some people were upset with the ending because it left some questions unanswered. I'm under the impression that series writers will leave a "cliffhanger" to keep you interested in the series and to make you want to read the next book (much like a prime-time television shows do at the end of each season to get you want to watch next season). It's okay if you don't get all of the answers (or you might not feel like you got only part of the story), read the books in order & you will most likely "get it".

Having had been a victim of a violent, horrifying crime (a case remains open, with no leads or suspects, to this day), I can understand how someone might be inclined to become judge, jury & executioner -- especially when police cannot get enough evidence to solve case(s), prosecutors that do not want to try a case they might not win and/or the justice system fails to properly punish the evil in this world. Anyone who has suffered at the hands of another, who remains free to prey upon others has probably felt the same way at one time or another...

Thank you, Mr. Bouchard for this great series -- I'm already reading book two: "THE CONSULTANT"!

In Boston for a conference where Dr. Greta Allstrom delivered a paper on Theoretical Implications of Anti-Dementia Drug Delivery Through Nano-Robotic Means." Afterwards, Dexter Corgan and three three nameless "would-be investors" take her to a "meeting" in a a Boston pub.

She "kept her hands in her lap to hide their trembling" as she meets with  Dexter Corgan and the men. She needs the $80 million she knows the they are offering. She knows the nano-robotic delivery would work. It would change lives around the world -- And she can help save lives...

Dexter tells her that any financial arrangements will be handled through the three men from this point on. It has been his job to been to attend the conference, evaluate presentations and bring them the best. If they hire her, they will pay him a finder's fee. She obviously is "the best" to someone because she is now meeting with them. As she had feared, the strings attached to the offer were unbreakable...

When Doug Winn sees his doctor in Portland. The news is not good. The last round of chemotherapy did not work as well as they had hoped. He cannot be put on the transplant because the tumour is too big. The doctor asks Mr. Winn if he has located his son, a possible liver donor. He says no, but as soon as he leaves, he places a call to the mysterious Stevey Tran and tells him that he needs to find his son. He explains that he needs a live liver donor that will match his...

In Pittsburg, Connelly brings the twins to Sasha's office so she can nurse the babies. Sasha feeds one while Connolly  diapered the other, then they swap. Connelly is still employed by Hank Richardson, but Hank only calls if he needs a "the highly trained federal agent with the top-secret clearances and sniper-level marksmanship skills." Instead, he spends his days going to "pediatrician appointments, feeding the cat, walking the dog, and whipping up elaborate meals from scratch." And he seemed to love it! He is enjoying his time with Sasha and the twins Finn and Fiona...

Connelly is back at home with the twins sleeping, when his doorbell rings. As he goes to the door, he hopes to get to it before the person rang the doorbell before they do it again and wake the babies. Standing there is an Asian man with a message. The stranger at the door told him that a man in Maine knows his father and he would put him in contact with the man. He hands Connelly an unmarked envelope and takes off...

Sasha and Connelly have been married for almost two years. Finn and Fiona are happy, healthy babies. Mocha and Java round out this little family.

Leo is actively trying to find his Vietnamese father...

Sasha takes a case from Golden Village on behalf residents who may have been unwilling subjects of medical research...

Yet another great book from Melissa F. Miller. I love this series, the author outdoes herself with each new book. They just keep getting better! Ms. Miller knows how to tell a story that will keep the reader turning the pages to get to the "next best part" of the story. I am interested in the characters (Sasha, Connelly, Naya, Hank et alii) and I want to know more about their lives and how they are going to prevail the next time they tangle up with the "bad guys."

Another 5-star review from this fan!

Up Next: International Incident

users.query: A lively tale of an extraordinary career. Mr Lear's credits set a standard that it is hard to imagine will ever be matched must less surpassed. Mr. Lear's career spans a time of change and transformation in entertainment that presented unusual challenges. While other writers, producers, and directors tried, no one succeeded at the level of Norman Lear. Anyone interested in the challenges of creativity will find endless food for thought in this tale. It all seems normal and familiar to anyone familiar with Mr. Lear's work until you realize he is not an institution, he is one man with a combination of talents that deserves the definition of unique.

cands.text: There is only one Bill Moyers. The arch of his career, the perspective and insights he has brought to the events in and of his life qualify as unique.
If you like genre of British mystery, the pace of this one will entertain you. David Tennant leads the usual company of brilliant ensemble players.

Well told tale of the birth of HP. The classic garage story. The insights into the characters of these early entrepreneurs in the IT world are particularly instructive. A good psychological and business perspective well mixed and well written.

A young ambitious, arrogant, driven Churchill pushes and stumbles himself into an adventure that had it gone wrong would have left him in the dust of history. But Churchill being Churchill his chutzpah works for him early in his career as it did later on. This is an adventure tale and written as such, a quick trip that is revealing not only of the young Churchill but the South Africa of the turn of the century; any number of reasons to enjoy this tale.

Full disclosure: I am a Raymond Chandler fan. Once I discovered him, I devoured his work and then have chaffed under his slight output ever since. I was familiar with Mr. King by reputation and his worldwide success, but not tempted by his previous novels. I expect I am the unusual example of who comes to Stephen King for the first time in his apparent shared enjoyment of the Chandler style. Hurrah. The result is delightful. Mr. King's skill as a writer is a foundation for flexing his muscles into a variation of style that he pulls off with what seems like ease but I expect took the grinding work this level of writing demands. If you are a Chandler fan you are in for a treat. If not you are still in for a treat.

The biography of a performer with well researched and throught through analysis of what experiences created the David Letterman many thought they knew from his nightly visits into so many homes. A notoriously private man in a public role with all the attendant contradictions intelligently explored. The detail is of a great value for anyone who wonders how this era of comedy, standup as well as late night evolved and works.

If a computer did not write this book then E.K. Blair wasted a lot of time. Ms Blair is not a writer. She takes one sentiment, one feeling, and masticates it like a cow until it is chewed over so often you cannot recognize the result. The book is advertised as a "true story". I know better than to question the reality of Anonymous, but even if she is a true character, mores the pity. Yes the sex scenes are frequent and graphic, so much so that they dull the imagination into more technical repetitiveness. Be my guest but if graphic sex is your thing, there are a long list of writers who have taken the voyage from passionate to kinky sex and back again with art and feeling. This trip is more like a bad sex toy.
Ms. Blair claims to be a "romance writer" in interviews. Pity the reader who interprets this drivel as "romance". But full disclosure: the book is a hit, best-seller popular. The only conclusion I can draw is that there are a lot of readers who need help.

Another of the tight productions that characterizes the BBC style. A compelling even riveting story with the tension of abducted children carrying the viewer from episode to episode. Full developed and meaningful characters, superb acting. Unless you are made of stone you care about the families involved.

Another of the tight productions that characterizes the BBC style. A compelling even riveting story with the tension of abducted children carrying the viewer from episode to episode. Full developed and meaningful characters, superb acting. Unless you are made of stone you care about the families involved.

The series has reached maturity and the characters are even more fully developed. If you have been along for the ride you are a family member by now and involved with the principals as they go through their development and changes. The high quality of acting, script, direction, cinematogrphy and editing are a norm in this and other UK series. There is a genre at work. If you enjoy it, this is one of the most enjoyable iterations of the genre.

Effective use of research and great sources many not before available. Mr. tye experienced hand at biography shows to good effect in dealing with a man of many contradictions. The evolution of a Kennedy life, particularly in Bobby's case is a challenging trip that Mr. Tye accomplishes convincingly. The author has the sense and confidence to leave unanswerable questions to the reader.

There is no story here. Fine for those who are not oriented to story. There are broken chains of life and love and relationships that meander. The best of the lot is a tale told early on from the point of view of a young poor villager who becomes the major domo for a wealthy boss. The man marries in a loveless union. The whys and hows are a novella unto themselves. Had that been the book it would have been five stars. The rest I found aimless with characters I could not care about. The author flits from place to place and jumps back and forth in time in an effort to string emotions and people together. He lost this reader in the process. I am left to wonder if Mr. Hosseini did not come to this novel with such a large reputation, would it be widely read or favorably reviewed.
A piece of nostalgia for those who enjoy his humor and persona. Not a revealing autobigraphy but a fun anecdotal trip through his life. Breezy.

A prodigious biography, but caution, its front-loaded with nerdiness. Stephen Manes has what many consider the best biography of Bill Gates. Mr. Manes research is at a level that few biographers attain, particularly as he deals with the complexity of the birth of an industry. The result is often overwhelming with numbers and names of the early proliferation of computer languages and stages of software development. To anyone who lived the era this is fascinating and memorable stuff . Just about the time you hope to get to the character of Bill Gates the author is there with insights, anecdotes and the maturity of a biographer who has come to know his subject well. This is a large work. Not airplane reading, and not light reading. But the reward is in a deeper understanding of one of the most interesting men of the last two centuries. The new edition helps. The original was written in 1994  and much has happened since. But the fact that the original is now more than 20 years old gives a perspective not cluttered with recent events and yet helps this reader understand better the transitions that the Gates' have made.

Here we go again, this time courtesy of ITV in a sweeping tale that is as elegant a soap opera as you can find. The Brits should take a patent on their period costume dramas. The beauty of these productions is the fact that the company of actors that make up the British theatre establishment as time to inhabit their characters and bring us the viewers along as family. I expect the actors themselves are cheerfully done with their alter egos, all the more the play at the heights of their acting powers. To those who have seen THE PALACE the derivative nature of the birth and growth a great department store is a vehicle that works well surrounded by the human and political intrigue.  Jeremy Piven shows again how much better the Brits are at playing Americans than vice-versa, and not just the accent, but the character. Frances O'Connor as Mrs. Selfridge commands many of the episodes as her character evolves. A great occasion for the total immersion of binging or stretching out the episodes with always something to look forward to.

If you have seen Lippizaner perform, if you just like horse stories, this is quite a ride. The balance of history is not at issue here but the survival of a remarkable breed and the tradition of its riders and trainers is the core of the story in the midst of WW II. The heroes in this case are the men who cared enough to commit to the horses.

The title is literal. The subject is huge, but the source of most of the information is from a single event that is the centerpiece of the book., Its a good quick read, but not a comprehensive piece of journalism.

As time passes this President as others before him grows in stature and understanding. The strength of Mr. McCullough's biographies is the depth and breadth of his research that expands the understanding of his subjects. If you think you know Truman, you will learn much more than you imagine. If you are unfamiliar with the Truman Presidency, this is a revealing trip like no other.

Mr. Mudd was one of the better intellects in the CBS News pantheon of correspondence in the network's hey day. The book is anecdotal trip through Mr. Mudd's career with his considerable accomplishments. What is missing is what he is capable of, perspective and insights into his time, the culture of TV News and how it helped shape an era when there were few choices for news.

And I am not an economist. Much of Mr. Piketty's writing is accessible, but a good deal of it is written with an eye for his colleagues in the dismal world of economic theory. The publicity surrounding Mr. Piketty's was barely short of the kind of marketing and fuss reserved for things like a new IPhone or the Segue if anyone remembers. I read the book in the hope of cutting through the fog of sound bites that do not apply to this or any serious economist's work. The rewards are there for the reader with time and patience, but have one or more colleagues or friends handy who are interested and willing to discuss the theses Mr. Piketty puts forward and the knotty problem that bedevils all economies in today's world. The gap between those who have and those who so much more, and the wider gap to those of have very little or nothing.
They're fine though each piece is relatively short. You are likely better off with a long strip that you can cut to the lengths you need.
Does the job which is all I was looking for. If you want elegance or beauty look elsewhere, and pay much more.

Friends swear by skim milk as the best frother. I find whole milk is better and in France the whole milk produces even greater froth than in the USA. Difference in butterfat content? The key is it works, and works well.

Assuming you are interested in fashion photography, this is a trip unlike any other i am aware of. The small coterie of star-photographers who have moved through the fashion world's evolutions are an evolving generation upon generation of survivors in an irrational world of personalities and values that shift with the changing cast of magazine editors who make and break photographic careers. Small wonder, the photographers themselves have  limited lifespans for the most part, though a few bridge generations and become icons. The insecurity that is matched only by the even shorter lifespan for models and even designers creates a backdrop of drugs and dissolution. This is not a happy volume, but the intensity of competitiveness and the cost of trying for the golden rings of success make for a powerful tale of human frailty and power. The book could easily be fiction, but what appears to be dig-deep research produces one powerful portrait after another. Whatever your image of a big time fashion photographer, this is the reality and it is not pretty.

I read the two Heileman volumes backwards. DOUBLE DOWN, the Obama-Romney race was first and is a brilliant piece of work that benefits from what the authors learned writing this first book. For anyone with an interest in politics this is catnip, and a juicy steak or anything else your palate desires. The book occasionally suffers from bouncing back and forth in time and gives short shrift to events that are waiting to be fleshed out. That is the nature of this kind of high speed effort, particularly the first time around. There are first time insights into the characters of the candidates and their handlers that anyone who lived through the campaigns and read the daily press would never have known. The intensity and value of the interviews that make up the backbone of this book's narrative is impressive work. The authors have created a model of political reporting

users.query:
I always take a chance when ordering shoes without trying them on, as my feet are ultra sensitive.  The women's sport sandals in this style have intrigued me, as they offer support, toe protection, flexibility in fit when your feet get hot, and in many cases can be worn in wet conditions.  When these Nevados were offered at about half the price as other brands, I decided to give them a try.

I was very pleased with the fit, the comfort, and the not-too-clunky style.

However, I would caution prospective buyers, that if you expect the specific color that is pictured, you may receive a slightly different combination.  The sandals I received were indeed grey/light blue, however, the webbing is the light blue, and the lining parts are the grey; just the reverse of the photo, and the written label.  For me, this was not a problem, as I have many summer clothing items in denim blue tones and khaki, and maybe it will work just fine for you as well.

cands.text: The leather is supple. The color was just what I wanted. The foot length was perfect and the insole was comfortably cushioned.  The quality and comfort are what I have come to expect from the Naturalizer brand. I ended up returning the sandals however, because the strap positioning at the back slipped off my heels. It is an unusual two strap arrangement that crosses loosely over the heel rather than being attached to the upper front assembly.  Perhaps it would fit another foot/ankle profile, but did not work out for me.

Perfect color. Perfect weight. Perfect loose and comfy fit. Very nice construction. Glad I spent a little extra on these bamboo knit pajamas. I could wear them all day, and night. I am not a fan of pockets on the pants, but if you are, these would please you. Looking at other colors for a second purchase.

I am happy with my purchase of these rayon "harem" pants. It was hard to decide which color, since there were many attractive designs. I love rayon for summer. I also prefer to cover my legs to avoid too much sun. The fabric is very lightweight and breezy. There are also many waistband styles from this company, with just a "one size" option. For flexibility, I chose the drawstring waist. It also has an elastic band sewn along with the drawstring, which may or may not be comfortable for all sizes. The package is very compact for the full size pants inside, which I think would be better used for crinkled cottons and gauzes, as the rayon came out very wrinkled, and will need thorough pressing before the first wearing. Overall, a fun and comfortable pant, at a reasonable price.

I am a slipper lover and This brand has my loyalty. I have a wide variety of colors and styles of slippers, you might say that Now that I am retired I live in them, and almost every day this is the one I reach for. There is plenty of room for my toes to breathe, yet the fleece lining is cozy. I wear this pair year round, barefoot. Some of my floors are not carpeted, and I wanted a sole that was quiet, so I took a chance, even though it was described as "outdoor ", and was pleasantly surprised. I guess this is a softer type of rubber. Cute embroidered motifs, boiled wool and suede and a Sherpa-like lining. Easy access without being completely open in the back, and very nice cushioning and a bit of arch support. Since I wear them every day, they are well worth the price.

I first discovered these great socks while visiting a boutique in a beach town in Oregon. This order is my second pair. I prefer cotton for warmth and cushioning and absorbancy. These are a combination of 80% cotton, 19% nylon, 1% lycra. Throughout the day when I am wearing them, it makes me smile to imagine I have the colors of bright crayons inside my shoes! I wear a size 8 1/2 women's shoe and the Medium is a good fit for me inside clogs or boots.

These are my three-season, go to pants for almost all my everyday events. House chores, errand running, gardening, and casual meet with friends gear. I saw the nurses wearing them, during recent hospital visitations, and they looked like a perfect cross between sweats and cargos, with the added bonus of no protruding jean button, or dangling drawstring. Just pull on and go. I am giving four stars because they(I have black ones) are real lint and pet hair magnets. I wear a 12 in Lee classic fit jeans, and the Medium fit well, though a tad long. I usually wear flat slip on shoes, so I expect to have to hem any pants. Another color is on its way, as I write this. What a fun find!

There is so much to like about these slippers, from the combination of suede and boucle materials, to the comfy lining, to the sturdy outsole. They are easy to slip on and off. However, when trying them on for the first time, I felt a sharp edge tearing into the top of my foot. Inside the tops is where the size and ID tag has been sewn, with a lip of raw material around the edge. It is positioned in such a way, to remove it would probably damage the lining of the slipper. I love to slip bare feet into cozy slippers, but am unable to do so with this model, so will be returning them.

I ordered this assortment to coordinate with a kantha stitch coverlet, with the grey background. All the covers have the same print, with a variety of colors to set off the floral motifs. My package had red, hot pink, black, orange, and turquoise. The size is a bit misleading. A full 18 x18 pillow form is too big, especially given that the back side has a skimpy overlap closure. And the 16 x 16's I used didn't quite fill to the corners. Unlike the coverlet( in another order/ review) these had no processing smell, so I began using them right away. It's possible since they are cotton, there will be some shrinkage after washing, and the 16 inch pillow forms will be just fine. Colorful casual spots of color for that bohemian look and feeling.

Bought these as a gift for a tall, lanky man, and the medium fit just fine, with scant shrinkage, even after repeated washing. He likes the open leg bottom rather than the elastic casing that comes in some sweat pants. The fabric has not pilled, and is a comfortable medium weight, for three season wear. They are a little more "presentable" with the cargo pocket, than generic athletic fleece pants. Good value for the cost.

This is a great addition to my summer wardrobe. I love the loose, but not sloppy fit, the poncho like styling and the breezy COTTON fabric. In my comparison shopping, I have found more fitting success with items imported from India which this brand is, or Thailand, rather than China or Korea. This particular top has a multilayered image, with stamping and dying techniques used. There are subtle touches of machine embroidery, and a few purple sequins. Even with the 70's  tie dye effect, it still feels very versatile to dress up or down;, going with skinny ankle pants, or shorts, or flowing palazzo pants. My favorite top this Summer.

I was looking forward to assembling and using this rack in my small closet. It was perfect size to fill a back corner. So, I was very disappointed upon opening to see that the color was clearly different from what was depicted. I ordered the beige/natural, with chocolate brown trim which would match other organizing containers I already had. This item was a definite yellow color, and not beige. I have returned the package.

I am new to computer games, and have tried out several styles on the free online sites. The "match 3" type seems to be the most interesting to me, in figuring out the strategies, testing my reaction speed, and my patience. I ordered Amazonia, based on other reviewers responses, and have enjoyed playing it over and over again. It is slightly different visually as the blocks are hexagon shape, resulting in more angles to shift around.  As one reviewer commented, there is a stage at which it can get sluggish, with only one piece moving at a time, but I have figured out a way to get around that. It is bright, colorful, tells a basic story, gives rewards, and keeps this Granny's mind active. For a small investment, I have enjoyed hours of entertainment.

I stumbled upon this book, at a fabric store which caters to quiltmakers. It stood out for me because of the focus on solid colors, primarily white, which makes a bold, and sometimes subtle graphic statement. The traditional use of commercial printed fabrics is practically non-existent. I love the emphasis on line, as with stitched line that creates texture and depth, and with the spare placement of colored blocks amid the fields of white.  It is easy to see the Amish influence that the author mentions, in her designs, yet with a very clean, modern approach.

I noticed the blurred focus in the photos, that others mentioned, and accepted it as yet another element of the overall modern style of the book and its designs.

It was confusing to me, however, after reading about the philosophy and journey of discovery of the designer, and touring her "gallery", to have the remaining two thirds of the book contain detailed instructions of each of the thirty quilted projects.  Is this a reference book on the concepts of abstract design, or is it a how-to book to duplicate the author's work?

I have found that many of the design concepts can be applied to working abstractly in other art mediums,such as collage and mixed media painting, making this a valuable resource to include on my bookshelf.

These cotton knit pjs are just right for cooler nights in Oregon. The fabric is soft against your skin  and has a pretty bird vine and flower print in charcoal on white. Be aware, however, that there is shrinkage even when washing in cold water. Though the cut is roomy enough, a couple of inches were lost in length, top and bottom, thus my "too small" fit assessment. I ordered Large, based on others reviews, and these still seem skimpy to me. Perhaps the woven cotton ones would not shrink as much.

I love the feel and the breathability of all cotton for my bedding, and for my pjs. Very happy to find these in so many fun and traditional prints and solids. Since I used to have a tailoring business, I always check the workmanship, and almost every detail is perfect. I do however, agree with another reviewer who cut away the brand labels from the inside of the neckline. Can these be sewn on the Outside? Also, after washing and drying, there was little or no shrinking, but, the the front facings on the top were twisted, and did not lie flat. For a smoother look, I hand sewed them down. Yes, the sizing is generous. I usually fall between 12 and 14, so I sized up for roominess, and for possible shrinkage, and still have to roll up the pants twice. I am ordering another set in a Large, for comparison . Stay tuned...

I want these scrubs to work, mainly because this is one of the few companies who offer the olive color. I ordered Large, because I carry my weight in my tummy, and I need the extra length in the rise area. So, even though these fit around my middle, there are handfuls of crisp fabric everywhere else. If I go to a medium, my concern is that the rise will be too low. Right now, my plan is to wash them and see what, if any, kind of shrinkage there is. I love the idea of a cross between cargos and sweats for my casual, retired life style. I am a persistent shopper, and will keep trying until I hit the right combination. Thanks Prime, for free returns!

An alternate title might have been, "Surface Design Techniques in a Nutshell".

This is another book from Chris Cozen chock full of techniques using Golden Acrylic Colors and other Golden products, this time showing how these materials can be used to apply color to fabric. The author assumes that we will have read her prior two books, published by Design Originals in order to grasp the "basics", and therefore presents the demos and instructions in ways I found sketchy and incomplete.  The finished examples are often not the ones with explainations, and somehow I kept turning the page expecting more, only to be presented with the next technique.

I like the breadth of techniques, but was overwhelmed by the aspect of having to purchase several specific Golden products in order to experiment with the illustrated projects. And for me, the size and number of the color photos seemed out of scale to the placement and smaller font size of the written copy.

If you are an artist who is confident using acrylics and wish to expand into fabric and textile, this book may be just what you're looking for.

I was pleasantly surprised to find that this flannel duvet cover was reversible, so that the print shows on both sides, rather than having a contrasting lining. This is a subtle color, more like a dusty plum in my opinion rather than classic lavender, and goes very well with the dark espresso stain of my platform bed, and white sheets. Just the little pick me up I needed to get through these final weeks of chilly weather, without busting my budget.  Be aware, though, that this is the D C only, so you won't be disappointed if you were expecting matching shams.
Even though the fabric stretches, this is too narrow a cut for those of us with a generous bust and hips. Nice colors, and nice walking slit, but overall too clingy for my taste.

When my doctor ordered a cardiac event monitor for me, I began looking for a sports/ leisure bra that didn't pull over my head, and get tangled in the wires, and something that fastened in the front. This bra comes in cotton, as well as a nylon and spandex blend, which is what I got. I was curious about the multiple sizing; you choose your band size, 38 say, and then the cup stretching accommodates B, C, or D. It is perfect for me as I am a between cup size. I like the shimmering fabric that has a knitted in pattern. I like the plush backing on the elastic. I like the design touch of lace which covers the hook and eye closure, however, it took me some practice to locate the position of the top and bottom hooks nestled behind the lace. One small complaint, not limited to this brand, is that I wish the mfg. would position the fabric content label on the outside of the bra, and/ or, make that tag from a soft fabric. After wearing my bra just a short time, I developed skin abrasion from the tag. I will cut it off before next wearing, but now have to figure out a way to save the information. Nice solution during my device wearing period, and beyond.

Fom the title and the introduction and the notes on the book liner, I expected this to be a memoir style personal story about someone with no prior sewing/quilting experience who falls headlong in love with the world of quiltmaking,and how this journey has impacted her life. And the book started out in that way. It soon became, however, more of a collection of essays and interviews about the social culture and big business of quilt festivals and competitions. In some places I got the feeling that the whole book was a promo piece for Texas tourism, as the "capital" or birthplace of the International Quilt Festival, which has been held in Houston for many years. Using black and white photographs did not do the work justice, nor did the quality or size of the photos in color. This book seems as if it may have been a proposal for Gillespie's book in 2009, QUILTING ART: INSPIRATION, IDEAS and INNOVATIVE WORKS FROM 20 CONTEMPORARY QUILTERS, which I had read prior to this, and which was a tribute to those who work in the area of fiber art.

If you want a basket set that fits into the 14-15" wide bookshelf, this one works. It is stained a nice rich walnut color and has two grab openings. However, and this is a BIG However, these are made of rough material, like stiffened twigs with little prickly hairs, and they are very rough and abrasive on everything. Because they are the size and color I wanted, I will keep them and adhere a protective layer on the bottom to insure they don't scratch the finish on my shelves. I like the convenience of online ordering, but in this case, I wish I had been able to feel the texture first.

It is always a gamble when choosing bedding from online descriptions, photos and reviews. I continue to shop this way, however, for the convenience; shopping from my computer in the privacy of my cozy corner is an Introvert's idea of paradise. I will say that I am choosy, and have returned as many, or more duvet covers, quilts, and sheet sets as I have kept.

This set however, was a delight from the moment I opened the zipper case. The microfiber fabric is soft to the touch, the size (Full-Queen) was generous for my Full mattress and bed frame, and the three accessory pillows are uniquely designed. Since there was no zoom in feature on this product, I had to guess at the scale of the loose paisley images, and based on the soft blue and white decorator touches, I was expecting something in the range of blue tones, on an off white ground, with earth neutrals.

It is much more vivid in hue, with the predominate "blue" being closer to a true Teal, with pale aqua and splashes of lime green accents. The overall effect is soft, because it is printed with a "watercolor effect". The 1/2 inch binding is the solid teal, and the back is the solid soft aqua. It is perfect in my bedroom which has off white plastered walls and espresso brown furniture.

I was also pleased with the reasonable price, as I enjoy changing the mood in my rooms every few seasons.

If I had one suggestion, it would be that the manufacturers create some way to keep the shams closed, like velcro, at the back envelope opening.

This is my first try at Hidden Object games, and it is just challenging enough to keep this 70-something brain busy. I like the idea of different room settings, and the visual style of the Victorian mansion. There is just enough similar but different, and new objects showing up later in the game, to keep me thinking. Some things have "British" names which could be a stumbling block for people. There is the variety of puzzle pages to assemble, and also spot the differences panels, along with the hidden object pages. It moves at an easy pace, six rooms to a round, with new clues to keep the story moving. The one glitch I found was that in the Freeplay mode, you can only improve your score so far, even though it lets you replay rooms as often as you wish.

What a clever invention this organizer rack is! I found it among the listings for bookcases and shelves, as I was browsing for ideas for storage in my studio. I wanted something that could hold my packets of collage materials upright, visible and within easy reach.  This small stand is just perfect for that use, and takes up little floor space. The birch side panels and the natural canvas pockets compliment my other wood furniture, and the work-in-progress mood of my room.

I usually defer to my on site handy person when it comes to RTA, but this project renewed my confidence in my own assembly abilities.  All the parts were numbered with removable stickers which related to clear instructions and diagrams. And the packaging was snug enough to avoid scratches. The screws were easy to turn with the provided tool, and the dowels were an exact fit for the corresponding inset holes.  Much attention to detail, like the tops of the screws being painted to match the wood.

My only small observation is that the canvas piece could have been more carefully packaged, rolled perhaps, as it needed serious pressing before the wrinkles came out, which needs to be done before any assembly. Overall I am totally pleased with this purchase, and I'm sure it could fit many other needs.

users.query: I purchased these for my mother, who does Zentangles.  She loves them!

cands.text: I purchased these for my mother, who does Zentangles.  She loves them!

These are small and simple, but absolutely perfect.  From a distance, they are hardly noticeable - understated (in a good way).  But as you look closer, they have a beautifully detailed holly pattern.  Very easy to attach to a mantel, and very sturdy.  I look forward to getting many good years of use out of these classy stocking holders!

I *really* wanted to like these.  I think it all depends on how you intend to use them.  The brush tips apply REALLY thick and the ink/dye bleeds like crazy.  The colors are very vibrant, but using relatively thick paper, I can see the colors almost mirror imaged perfectly on the opposite side of the paper, they bled through to the next page, and even a little to the page after that.  If you're looking for really dark, vibrant colors and you're using a really thick surface with protective covering beneath it, this will work great for you.  If you're looking for beautiful (but slightly less saturated) colors that are a lot less likely to bleed, I recommend Tombow dual tip brush pens/markers.
I didn't love these.  They are a little too low-rise (in my opinion) to be effectively worn as yoga shorts, and the fit is somewhat small.
These colors are extremely vibrant!  Perfect for my kids' craft projects!  We enjoyed using them and will look for more ways to incorporate them into our artwork.
My kids LOVE these!  It's a great treat for them when we're on the go.

I am not terribly proficient in yoga, but I purchased these for use in the YogaX workout from P90X after going through the first couple of weeks without them.  These made the practice of yoga MUCH more natural and efffective - made me wish I had purchased them sooner!  The density/firmness is perfect.  I am very satisfied with this product.  Thank you!

I love these.  The colors are fantastic and the styles are versatile.  It's a perfect way to disguise a "bad hair day" when you don't have time to wash and dry, or a cute accessory as an accent to many kinds of outfits.  The fabric is thin, but I prefer this in the summer.

After buying a set of these in more "girly" colors, my boys wanted some for themselves.  I found the set with the flames and the American flag to be one they could agree on, and they are very happy I bought them.  They wear them almost daily!  Their friends were getting a little jealous, and the bandanas are so well priced, I gave some away to a group of their very happy friends.  I'm sure I'll be ordering more.

I teach a couple of theory and ear training classes at a university, and this tool was exactly what I needed.  It works great, is easy to use, and saves a lot of time that I was wasting while trying (and failing miserably) to draw straight staff lines on the board freehand.  The price was extremely reasonable.  I'm really glad I bought it!
I like this - it works well and my kids love it.  In my opinion, it's a little too rich/sweet.  But many people prefer this kind of finished product, and I never get complaints when I make these!
My husband bought these for me for a Christmas present.  I love them.  They are beautiful, classy, and versatile enough to go with dressy or casual.

These are the BEST leggings I've ever owned!  They are soft and cottony, but also thick enough to not be see through (or even worry about panty lines).  As soon as they arrived, I tried them on and loved them so much, I immediately went to my computer and ordered a pair in black.  You can sleep in them, work out in them, run errands in them...  They are just perfect!

I recently published a YouTube video called The Ultimate Bullet Journal Paper Test in which I compared Dingbats with Moleskine, Bondibook, Leuchtturm, Rhodia, and Lemome journals. In my opinion, Dingbats won in almost every area. Tombow monotwin pens bled through a little, as did a couple of my wettest brush markers, but Dingbats was the only journal to appropriately handle my wettest fountain pen inks (such as Noodlers Apache Sunset) without ghosting, bleeding, or feathering, while maintaining color vibrancy. Ill be purchasing Dingbats journals from now on. The quality is undeniable.
Ive had my set for two years. Lots of use and abuse, as I travel frequently. These have held up perfectly. I couldn't be happier!
I bought these on a lightening deal for less than 5 bucks, and now that I've received them, I definitely feel they are worth FAR more!  These look great and are comfortable to wear.

This is lovely, but (as others have said) a little small.  When I first put them in my ears, they pinched and were uncomfortable for a while.  I found it very easy to bend the metal to make the grip a little looser, and after that they were far more comfortable.

We got these for my son as a reward for finishing his (homeschooling) 1st grade curriculum for the year.  He LOVES them!  He is glued to them at every opportunity, and it provides another outlet for his Minecraft obsession when he has already used up his allotted screen time for the day.  I highly recommend these books!
Bought these for my 5 year old son's "Paw Patrol" themed birthday party.  They were a hit!

My children LOVE their LeapBands!  It's a great way to get them moving - particularly on those less-than-perfect weather days.  It's easy to set them up on line, and allows the children extra motivation to unlock characters and earn points.  You can also set up "quiet hours" so they aren't playing with their LeapBands when they should be doing schoolwork or sleeping.  It's like a MUCH less expensive, more entertaining FitBit... for kids!

I realize I'm probably in the minority saying this book is only "okay" as many of my friends have raved about it.  I didn't find it to be particularly well written (language barrier issues) and some of the advice is just plain weird (I have no intention of thanking my jacket at the end of the day for doing its job).  There is also a lengthy section addressing Japanese religious items that is not necessarily applicable for most Americans.  That said, the book has a lot of good ideas, and I look forward to passing it on to another person who could use the inspiration.

It's a much smaller fit than what is demonstrated in the picture. You'd have to be a size 4 and SHORT (petite) in order for the shirt to wear like it does on the model. Does it fit a size medium/large?  Yes, but it won't drape down like the picture.

I think the style of the shirt is quite lovely.  The white is very slightly see-through, but mostly okay.  But these are styled VERY narrow in the waist.  I could wear it as is, but I'm looking for something a little more appropriate for professional wear, and if I had known that the fit would be so "skin-tight" I would have ordered a size larger.

My boys LOVED these shoes, but after about two months, the heels were completely worn. I'm so disappointed in the lack of durability. They will be very disappointed to find these in the trash after such a brief time wearing them.

I'm a beginning hand letterer and I think this book is my favorite. A few things you'll find in this book:

Step by step, clear instructions on how to begin exploring this art form
ENCOURAGEMENT- information is presented in a positive, encouraging tone
VARIETY - at least 10 examples of differing styles of letters (full alphabets) and numbers
Inspiration- some great suggestions of ways to using lettering (different kinds of projects)

I also own Peggy's Botanical Line Drawing book, and it is a winner. If you are not already, check out her resources on skillshare, Instagram posts, Facebook, her blog, etc. She's just a great teacher and a good person to follow in the lettering community.

users.query: I use this on my Beretta PX4 Storm--just a drop on the rails and the rotating lug.  Works great!!!

cands.text: I use this on my Beretta PX4 Storm--just a drop on the rails and the rotating lug.  Works great!!!
This is simple to apply and easily recognizable by other Beretta shooters.  It seems very durable and is a bright white color.
This is the perfect pistol case for my full-size PX-4.  At first I bought the 8-inch but is was too small for my full-size pistol.  It was difficult getting info on what size fits what pistols.
For me, they don't work very well.  I'm not sure if it is the fit or what but muffs are a much better solution for me when shotgun shooting.  Sorry I wasted my time and money on these...

I used this to cover a capscrew on a anchor shackle.  I applied two layers, one after the other.  When applying the second layer, I may have used too much heat from my heat gun and the tube split wide open longitudinally.  Be careful!

After comparing the Lasermax Micro and this Crimson Trace sight, I chose the Crismson Trace Rail Master and some of my reasoning was based on the number of reviewers of the Lasermax unit that complained about the sight coming loose during shooting.  I haven't had this problem with the Crimson Trace unit!  Some reviewers complained about the 5-minute turn off on this unit--I think this is an advantage rather than a disadvantage because it saves my battery.

This unit was very easy to sight in--just matched it up to the iron sights and then at the range it was right on.  At the range I did try to make a minor adjustment and turned the elevation screw about 1 full turn--this moved the sight about 1 foot at 25 yards!  The adjustment screws are very sensitive!

This sight improved my shooting significantly at 25 feet--maybe 1 inch smaller groups!  I highly recommend this unit!  I am using it on a Beretta PX4 Inox 9mm.

I replaced a one-year old furl tank sender that was supplied by the tank manufacturer after it failed.  The new Moeller fuel sender worked perfectly.  I didn't need the extension--so I removed it an applied the float directly to the main arm.  The unit comes with a new gasket and all the fasteners--everything you need for installation!  The unit seems to be well made and the materials seem top notch!

It is amazing how much these fins increase the performance of an outboard motor!  I have installed these on my 6 HP Yamaha outboard used on my APEX 10 Lite RIB and can plane with just me aboard.  Great product!
Very well designed product!  We applied this to our outboard engine (with other decals) to reduce the potential for theft of our outboard motor.
Excellent tips for cruising the ICW!  We are in the midst of the ICW now and these tips have been invaluable!
This is the only cap that is worthwhile on your Nikon camera!  It is always a good idea to have a couple spares though.

I use this size for both my 50/1.4 and 85/1.4 lenses and while it has more space than needed for both, it protects them very well.  (I used to use socks to protect my lenses individually when I packed them--this is a lot better!)

I used this product in my boat's transmission to try and stop (or slow down) a leak.  Instead of helping, the leak got worse.  While I can't say this product made things worse, I can say it did nothing to help.  My transmission is now being repaired.  So, my advice about this product based on my experience is don't expect an improvement--bite the bullet and get your transmission fixed right!

I like the separate panning capability with the lock that other relatively small heads don't seem to have.  Also, this is surprisingly strong for such a small size.  Bought this for my monopod but may also use it on my tripod.  (This head is an overkill for the gorilla pod, which is being marketed as a companion offering here on amazon.com.)
My wife uses this for her Nikon D200 and Nikon 16-85 VR lens and it works perfectly for that!  Great quality and appearance!

I bought this adaptor ring for my new (used) Nikon 20mm f2.8 lens so that I could use my 77mm filters from my other lenses.  It works great and doesn't look bulky like I expected it to look.  This turned out to be a nice inexpensive solution for me...
I have switched all my lens caps to this design and it works great.  Still, sometimes, I lose one and have to replace it but they can be delivered quickly and inexpensively by Amazon.
These drill guides are very well made and very useful, particularly on a sailboat when trying to drill holes in one-inch diameter stainless steel tubing!
While this would probably work in terms of size, I didn't like the need to stack lenses vertically.  Otherwise, good quality and attractive appearance!
I have switched all my lens caps to this style...they work great!  Still, I don't know how I lose one every once in a while but replacements are easy to get here at Amazon...

I really like this knife's design and the quality seems good too.  When I received it I was surprised that it said "Made in China" on the base of the blade.  For some reason, this immediately lowered its value to me...
Great jeans!  I bought these jeans in three different colors since I like the fit so much.

users.query: My Daughter loves this 4 wheeler, it is well made and is easy to put together, highly recommended for anyone that wants a vehicle that will last with even harsh treatment by your little one

cands.text: This is a great scooter for my little girl, she loves the fact that the basket is able to hold her stuffed animal while she rides the scooter.
Bought this dollhouse for my 3 year old Daughter she absolutely loves it. It is sturdy and well made and very easy to put together.

Bought this dollhouse for our daughter for Christmas, it was easy to set up and assemble, I know that some of the reviews stated that they had trouble in assembly but I found this one very easy to assemble if you took your time, followed the instructions and didn't try to force things to fit. Our daughter had just turned three a few days before Christmas and she loves this dollhouse.

I was a little concerned when I read all of the problems that some had with assembly but this was a very easy to assemble and a very sturdy BBQ. I could not be more pleased with this unit. It makes great food and holds heat very well. If you buy this unit I am sure you will be happy.

Great product, I opened the package and was frankly I was surprised with how well this motor was made and the finish work was excellent. I filled the unit with oil and gas, check for leaks and pulled the starter rope 2 times and it fired right up. I have only had to pull the rope starter one time each time after this to fire the motor up. It runs well, is not noisy, shifts without problems and idles smoothly. What more can you ask for from a small motor. I recommend this motor to anyone that is in the market for a trolling motor or a motor for a small boat, I put this on my SunDolphin Sportsman bass boat and it is just want I needed and wanted. I had ordered one of the cheap motors that are sold here on Amazon, you will know what I am talking about, the 298.00 Cheap Chinese motors and when I opened the box I didn't even bother firing up the motor it was so poorly made. The Coleman 2.6 is made in China too but it is obviously built to different standards then the 3.5 HP 2 stroke motors. Please buy the Coleman motor you will not be disappointed.

Great smoker, well built and very easy to use. I have a Bradley smoker for my home but bought this one for my motorhome for when we are camping. I have used the Bradley for over 8 years but I think that this smoker is even better and more user friendly with the exception of having to load chips about every hour for the first few hours. Great food, highly recommend this smoker to anyone interested.

Great smoker, well built and very easy to use. I have a Bradley smoker for my home but bought this one for my motorhome for when we are camping. I have used the Bradley for over 8 years but I think that this smoker is even better and more user friendly with the exception of having to load chips about every hour for the first few hours. Great food, highly recommend this smoker to anyone interested.

Actually bought this to mount on the back of my Jayco Fifth Wheel Trailer to bring my Champion Generator on our camping trips where we are cold camping with no power at the camp sites. This folding rear platform makes it very easy to load my generator with the ramp down and then folds up very easily for transit to and from the campsites.
Well made and complete aquarium with the exception of the air pump which you have to order, but if you want a great setup this is it.

I bought this for my daughter, she loves to kick, thrown and play with any type of ball from a basketball to a football, but she really loves this and it is a great tool for teaching hand and eye coordination. I strongly recommend this basketball set for your toddler.

I bought this for my daughter, she loves to kick, thrown and play with any type of ball from a basketball to a football, but she really loves this and it is a great tool for teaching hand and eye coordination. I strongly recommend this basketball set for your toddler.
I bought this for my Jeep Liberty, was very easy to install, from start to finish it only took me two hours to install. It doesn't get any easier.
I use this for braking my towed Jeep behind my Motorhome and it works great, reliable and effective. Highly recommend for anyone that is flat towing a vehicle.

We bought this for our daughter, she is 23 months old, we like to purchase learning toys for our daughter. She likes the lights and this enables our daughter to use her memory to play the game, it took a few times for her to figure out that she needed to follow the lights and repeat the sequence after that it was amazing to she her progress from one light to now she can follow four or more. Some people have told us that 23 months is too early but I think it is never too early to start learning to remember. Our daughter loves this game and so do we.

Great generator, out of the box to running in about 10 minutes. Shipped and delivered 4 days quicker then originally estimated. Delivery was to our door and couldn't be happier. No shipping damage and everything was in great shape when I took it out of the box. Started and broke in on LPG. Runs great, not as loud as I thought it would be after reading some of the reviews I thought that it was going to be very loud but it was definitely not. The generator was purchased for power when we cold camp with our fifth wheel trailer or emergencies at our home. So far I am very impressed and strongly recommend this generator if you are in the market. I have owned several generators in the past, some for business use for construction sites and others for my cabin that is off the grid and so far this is the best generator that I have found for the money.
Small but very strong and easy to use as well as install.

I love this trolling motor for my Sun Dolphin Sportsman Bass Boat. I mounted this on the front of my boat, I did have to reverse the handle by removing the set screw and rotating the handle for bow mounted operation but that took all of 5 minutes and allows me to have the trolling motor up front and my gas motor mounted on the back of the boat. This motor, is strong, light and works great, has 5 speeds forward and 3 in reverse so you do not have to rotate the motor 360 degrees to operate it. in reverse. The battery indicator light on the top works great and for the money is one of the best motors that I can recommend for a small boat. The motor operates quiet and does not vibrate when in operation.
Great stand, was very easy to put together and very sturdy. I strongly recommend this stand for anyone wanting a strong, sturdy and easy to put together aquarium stand.

This cord is made from good materials with the exception of the male end that goes into the female receptacle that is mounted on the towed vehicle. The location of the terminals are not mounted properly on the cord to allow it to be incerted without a great deal of force and fighting with it. Other than this everything else is well made.

I was worried when I read some of the reviews, but I have to say that I am very pleased with this TV. It was well packed, worked extremely well and does everything that you could ask for in a TV/DVD combination. I bought this for my motorhome, when I installed it I found that the sound is more than adequate, when you read some of the reviews you will see that some say that you cannot hear the tv, I cannot say if they have improved the speakers but on my tv the sound is more than loud enough. I will hook up external speakers for a better bass but that is a personal choice on my part nothing wrong with this tv. As to the comments by some that they have a problem with ejecting a DVD, it is not in the instructions, but on the remote control you push the red button and the dvd will eject. I just pushed every button until I found the right one. Not the best instruction manual but if you spend a little time you will be able to figure out how everything works.

When accuracy is your goal then you really need the overall length gauge. I shoot a Springfield M1A Super Match and although this rifle is capable of amazing groups with the use of this tool and using the information that I gathered by checking this rifle I was able to see my groups shrink by over 1/4"at 100 yards I now see three round groups that are touching one another and at 500 yards by over 2" by properly sizing my rounds to the rifle. This may not sound like much but in a competition it can mean quite a few more X ring shots. In hunting it can mean the difference in a wounded animal and a clean one shot kill. I highly recommend using the Hornady Lock N Load Overall Length Gauge if you reload. By the way I now use this tool with my hunting rifles and have seen my groups decrease in size with these weapons too.

My 5th wheel was prewired for a rear observation and backup system. I installed this camera in about 45 minutes, checked it out the monitor mounted in my Truck and I have a clear view of what is behind my RV when we are on the road. Day or Night I have a clear image. The night time IR Camera works great when backing into sites when camping. I have no reception problems at any speed and this unit can be used as a security monitor at night when at the campsite. We had to wire in a separate power feed for this option but it was very easy.
We gave this to our daughter for Christmas she is so happy and we are truly impressed with the sound as well as the quality of this Karaoke equipment.
My wife loves this watch, it was a Christmas gift that she wears everyday with pride.

users.query: Very realistic.  Lite enough to carry around but durable enough to handle crowds and occassional sword fights.

cands.text: Sturdy and great sound.  I bought for my daughter and she loves them.  I can't hear her music while I'm driving, so that's a big plus!

Comfortable in hand, easy to use.

no safety, so be careful when cutting their nails
