users.query: The case is robust and I used two of them without issue.  The most important two features are that you can lock the lid down with a secure clip on both sides of the tops of these and that there is an adjustable divider to adapt to different group batteries.  I am pleased with them and have no reservation with the value of my purchase.  They are exactly as advertised.

cands.text: This the third Tripp Lite I have purchased and since I use this brand, have had no issues.  I live where the power regularly goes on and off and pulses are common too.  No more toasted devices.  The case is tough steel and the construction adds to the ability to function.  Read up on your topic people!  A plastic power strip is not enough!  Do you want to be without your tv for even one night??  Tripp Lite should make BC products.
This is the one.  Metal case, very sturdy, and correct lights to monitor.  I have used Tripp Lite models for years to safeguard some high end audio equipment and am glad of it.  Very good value.
The battery looks well constructed as compared with the Canon original which was replaced and thus far has performed flawlessly.  Would buy again without reservation.

These are not robust in the least, and I guess at their price point that is okay, but . . . . .

They did last a few days and shown brightly, but now have gone dead.  The solar cell may have died, or the battery is kaput, but either way, there is no way to guide the Great Pumpkin, and that isn't right.

Either find a pricier model or just give up.

Oh, it's only electricity, so close enough is fine.  Ummm, not for me.  This instrument follows the line of Fluke products and that means it is great.  Repeatability says much about a measuring device and this has a nice consistent nature.  It is well sized, the leads are great, the case is pro, and you need to be good to yourself and get this.  Please check all circuits before you touch.  Shutting off the breaker is not enough.

Having once had the good fortune to be in the factory, and to meet the patriarch of this brand, I have always been a fan of their products.  I have a car charger from the 1970s and it is still in use regularly without failure and even looks new.

This new mini charger is what I use to keep my ATV ready.  The utility connections are excellent and they include all the plug choices to fit your needs.  I put the connection on with the two plugs and it is a snap to re-hook the charger for storage when I return the ATV to the garage.  Very nice.  The status lights are logical, the charger itself is quiet and is quite small to not take up space in the garage.  Very small, in fact.  These people are good folks and the products they make are high quality: buy this charger and forget about it.

The clip is strong as is the webbing of the strap itself.  It adjusts easily and keeps the adjustment without slipping.

 I used these to fashion a raccoon proof garbage can lid.  So far so good, and that means these babies must be tough.  I suppose you could use them for luggage as stated in the product heading from the manufacturer, but that is not as much fun as tussling with the local wildlife.  Good quality, I'd buy them again.

The double hinged part of the device makes it difficult to use, in my experience.  Look for one with a single piece, not articulated as in this one.  These style of leverage corkscrews are the best in my view, but look beyond this design.  Having said that, the construction quality of this offering is well made, thus two stars.

This lock is secure, of course, and has materials of construction that should last a long time in weather.  The mechanism is smooth, and any thief activities are likely to be channeled to the chain or hasp since the lock will take a very concerted effort to defeat.  The use of the shrouded top concealing the shackle makes it nearly impossible to get a bolt cutter onto the part needing to be cut.  Very fine lock and worth the Amzn cost.
Strong elastomer, and the snaps are of a nice strong grade, too.  Good item to use with divers and the value of this snubber is right on the button.

The box is heavily constructed and the cover plate actually fits on the box!  The screws are not of the usual low quality such as I often find on load centers, regardless of brand.  The knockouts are a bit tough to remove but I guess that is due to the metal gauge.  Very nice box and very reasonable in cost.  Be aware it does not offer a knockout in the back if you intended that to be so.

Excellent choice for me.  I took both still shots and movies, and the image quality is quite good.  I am always pleased with the Canon brand and this one does not disappoint.  It is very thin and can easily be kept in a pocket, and I find it less intrusive than my cell phone by relative size.
While not the factory unit, it fits well and I could not distinguish a difference in quality.

I have a Cannon down rigger and the stock plastic holders are not able to be kept in the proper orientation very easily and they are not for adjustment; the process is time consuming and requires two wrenches.

I added these rod holders to allow use of dipsy divers and a side planer on the side opposite to my single downrigger.  They work great as long as you can mount them to a spot strong enough to hold.  As another reviewer said they also store rods upright easily.  When traveling, they store in a down position parallel to the deck, so they fit under the boat cover.  All good.

These rod holders are fantastic for adding two rods to you salmon smashing arsenal.  The two axis control is worth it over single and I am very, very pleased with them.  They connect well to the mounting track also sold by Cannon.  I used an aluminum backing plate with 1/4 x 20 x 1.5" ss bolts to secure to a metal portion of the track to the deck, instead of wood screws supplied, and the rod holders are rock solid in their placement.  Excellent purchase and the price is right, even with Prime shipping.

Will you miss the sound of cymbals crashing every time you wish to cover a pot of boiling water and reach into a crowded cabinet of scattered lids?  Hard to say, but this organizer does what it is purported to do and does it well.  It is of a nice construction and should last longer than I do.  It really does the trick of standing up the lids for my newly acquired Cuisinart pots and pans, while taking up the least amount of space.  It flexes to fit the space in your cabinet and I will bequeath it to my progeny in my will as I intend to never give it up.

Well constructed container and the more narrow dimension allows storage without monopolizing the refrigerator rack.  Lids are both secure, and you may wash it thoroughly as there are no impossible to clean nooks.  Exceeds my expectations.

These are of a sturdy construction and are the right capacity for me for leftovers and holding guacamole and similar dishes.  The lid fits very well and they stack nicely.  Best of all, I don't fear them crashing when I put them away in the cupboard.  Good value.

I have now purchased five of these, one to replace the light I dropped from about 20 feet.  Four have made it into service.  I have used one pair for about three years with no issue, although I don't use them much.  As a portion of my review, they do bounce well, but the glass bits just don't seem to handle it.

I have not had an issue changing a bulb, but I think the glass cover plate could get tight if it sees some weather (?)  It rests on a rubber gasket and just needs a turn to release it.

So, they are fairly bright, but if you want more wattage for the cottage you should be thinking a different version, or LEDs if you leave them on much.  I do like the ability to point the beams and the shade does work well to prevent light pollution of your neighbors.  They are easy to assemble with the very necessary cross bar to attach the fixture to a receptacle.  Wire caps are likewise included, but I prefer to use my own from stock.  There is even a little rubber plug to seal the screw port from which the fixture is hung which is kinda nice.
Plugs come with an accurate and consistent gap and the brand is known to me in several applications and I am never disappointed with the brand.

Now, I love Coleman but these have a lid that will not stay open on its own.  The lid closes very securely to the body of the cooler, and as others have noted, the prevention of air intrusion is a key to good insulation.  Thus, while the lid is a good seal, it will not stay up when opened and this bugs me.  The handles are about average and may have gone downhill somewhat since the last time I bought a 48 Coleman.  I've always loved the brand since we had the old metal units, but next time I will do a better job of cross shopping.  Relative to value, I found them at a much lower cost after I bought 3 on Amzn.  I've a bit of buyers regret.

I did not include a review of overall insulation, but have noted no difference in previous models I have owned, no neither a plus nor a minus.
You should shop better than I did

I guess they do not as the filter fits a variety of smaller engines each with their own o-ring or gasket, but I would like the option.  Hey, I'm a needy person.

I'm not certain what it is about the belt, but it looks cheesy.  The leather looks as though it is pressed cardboard and simply too shiny.  Also it is a tiny bit too wide for my taste.  I will keep it as a stocking stuffer, but am getting another one of different brand to see if I can upgrade.  On the plus side, the reversible function is perfect.  So, I think as a matter of form, I don't like it at all, but for function it is 5 stars.

cands.text: This novel makes such a strong statement about the destruction of a culture and its environment through the use of mystery, suspense and well-drawn characters.  It also questions conventional perceptions of heroes and villains and thus revises the myths that the author is drawing on.  That's what makes it so brilliant.  She Walks These Hills in the best book I've ever seen from Sharyn McCrumb.  I am in awe of her achievement.

Even though the tribe was invented and the background was a composite, I liked the feel and the ambiance of the reservation portrayed.  The author dealt with some real problems of actual tribes.  The characters were well developed.  I liked the process of change that the hero and heroine both went through.  I also liked this book's use of myth.

I rarely review paranormal romances. Yet authors that are new to me who are doing unusual twists on a familiar theme can attract my interest. I received a digital ARC from the author in return for this review.

I appreciate that Borgne invented a Native American people called the Mahasi who are enemies of the neighboring Iroquois. This implies that they are a Northeast Woodland people. My favorite fantasy author Charles De Lint has also created a fictional Native people in order to avoid writing inauthentically about a particular real Native American culture.

I feel that this book is potentially alternate history because if you project the impact of the spread of Native shifters, this factor alone could have radically changed North American history.

This novel lays bare a darkness at the heart of early American society.  The history books do mention the prevalence of indenture, but we don't hear the voices of indentured wives in their pages, so it is left for novelists like Margaret Lawrence to remember their sorrows.

I loved the heroine Tamara Swift.  Her brother isn't that strong a character, but I love him when he stands up for her and acknowledges her gifts.  The best ghost is Bodicia. This novel's Byron is fun at times, but a complete travesty of the historical Byron.  This is the first time I have ever seen Byron portrayed as effete.  He was actually a rather macho athletic type who died while on a military campaign. I think the authors have him confused with Oscar Wilde.

The plot improved in the last third of the book, but not tremendously.  A flashback for the villain would have given the book a great deal more power.

I would have read Original Death by Eliot Pattison eventually because I am a fan of his Colonial American mystery series to which this book belongs.  I am glad to have had the opportunity to read it a good deal sooner since I was provided with an advance copy in return for a review.

The best reason to like a mystery is a plot with unexpected twists.  Original Death definitely delivers plot twists. When the revelation of whodunit finally came, I could honestly say that I didn't expect it.

The characterization was excellent. The anguish of Duncan's Native American companion Conawago over the village massacre that he and Duncan encounter was quite moving as was Duncan's inner conflict precipitated by this mystery. There were also some wonderful side characters such as Hetty the Irish seer, Kassawaya the Oneida warrior woman and the real historical personage, Colonel William Johnson.
I can recommend this novel to fans of historical mysteries and of the Sara Donati novels that take place in the same period and were also inspired by the Leatherstocking Tales.

The cover shows us the three central characters on which the novel will focus.  In the beginning of my reading process, I referred back to the cover because the artists conception of these characters helped to anchor them in my mind.

Eventually, all three of the protagonists made a powerful impression on me.  I asked myself why I felt one character relationship was the emotional heart of the novel.  Since the characters were both white, I wondered if I was being racist.  I decided that I felt that way because of the barriers between the two characters.  Kollenborn shows us that there could be huge differences between white people in South Africa.  There were white opponents of apartheid.  I did think that the central relationship of the novel was intended to be the friendship that developed between the two female protagonists, but it wasn't freighted with the dramatic intensity that would have made it feel more significant.

 I also would have preferred fewer information dumps. I admit that some information was definitely necessary to the plot.  I discovered that necklacing was far more horrific than I had previously imagined.

There was a handful of typographical errors, but several of them were noticeable because they occurred within a page of each other.  Yet few books are completely error free.

The study guide for book clubs asked questions that were thought provoking, but there was no question about the Truth and Reconciliation process.  The character Joanne wondered if this process really could heal South Africa.  I think that book groups will want to discuss how the book depicts Truth and Reconciliation, and whether its an effective policy for South Africa.

How The Water Falls by K.P. Kollenborn testifies to the capacity of individuals to bring about social change. The protagonists are only a small sample of the type of courage and commitment that was shown by a great many individuals in South Africa during the period that brought about the end of apartheid.  Without them no change would have happened.  The stories of Kollenborns fictional exemplars are inspirational.

This is a well-written novel dealing with the residents of a small Florida town before, during and after World War I.  It's a moving portrayal of the period with enough detail to convey authenticity.  It focuses on important themes such as prejudice, the realities of war and the cultural beliefs surrounding it.  The characters are well-drawn.  Even the villain has dimension since we learn something of his background.  David Cooper, the central character, is well-intentioned and heroic. He isn't perfect by any means. He makes mistakes due to misperceptions, but he is faithful to his principles and values. I was impressed when he taught his wife, Sara, to drive a truck. There can't have been too many American women driving trucks in 1917. In fact, I discovered in an online search that the first American woman to receive a commercial license to drive a truck was Lillie Elizabeth McGee Drennan in 1929. David's willingness to instruct Sara, so that she wouldn't be isolated on their farm while he was "Over There" in Europe, speaks well for their relationship. I enjoyed Sara's gumption.  Sara's father, David and Sara's African-American neighbors and David's German immigrant employer are all notable and sympathetic characters.  The plot was dramatic, moving and suspenseful--particularly toward the end.  I would recommend Fire Angels as a book club selection because it provides a number of substantial topics for discussion.

I have been a fan of Susan Krinard.  She's an original writer who has expanded the limits of romance, but this book was seriously problematic for me.

The success of a romance depends on the reader believing that the primary couple are experiencing true love.  When the primary couple are therapist and patient, it could be that what is happening is a phenomenon called transference.  This is why it's considered unethical for therapists to become romantically involved with their patients.  It bothers me that Susan Krinard doesn't even mention the issue of transference in her author's notes where she does go into the controversy over recovered memories.  Yet the problem of transference is central to the novel.  This is an ill-chosen concept for a romance. It makes me uncomfortable.

This is the third in Frederik Nath's trilogy of novels taking place in France during World War II.  I recently read the previous volume, Farewell Bergerac and liked it very much.  I also liked Francesca Pascal,  but I have to say that I didn't find it quite as satisfying a read as I'd hoped.

In  Nath's author's note that is appended to this novel, he wonders if he's portrayed Francesca Pascal believably since he's never previously written from a woman's perspective.  He has no need to worry on that score.  She was both credible and appealing as a mother, an independent woman and an artist.  I admired her courage.  Participation in combat is not the only mark of courage.  Sometimes courage is the ability to endure. Endurance involves always remembering who you are. Francesca Pascal maintained her sense of identity in the forefront of her mind no matter what happened.

Although I believed in Francesca as an artist, her obsession with the painting "Paysage Le Mur Rose" by Matisse is a total mystery to me.  I thought I might get a handle on her conviction that it represents France if I looked at it online, but I still have no clue.  Such ideas are very subjective, of course.  I personally find certain paintings of the French countryside by Van Gogh more emblematic.  I wish that Nath could have expanded on exactly what it was about "Paysage Le Mur Rose" that meant so much to Francesca.  It would have given me more insight into her character.

 The portrayal of Francesca's gay friend, Charles, was a disappointment to me.  He seemed to have so much potential at the beginning of the book, but over the course of the narrative he disintegrated into stereotype.  Stereotypes have a basis.  People do behave stereotypically in real life, but in fiction stereotypes aren't very interesting to me because they are a predictable element. I imagine that the reason for taking the character of Charles in such an obvious direction was to provide Francesca with a dramatic inner conflict.  Yet I think that Nath had an opportunity to do something innovative with Charles, and he threw that chance away.  If Nath had chosen to develop Charles differently, he could have had his own storyline focused on his perspective. I realize that this would have required a completely different structure for this book, but I think it would have been more memorable.

I was amazed at how moving and appealing I found the hero, Diego, who was a traditional healer known as a curandero.  I was also impressed with the love and respect with which the author wrote about Latino traditions.  I was pleased with Harlequin for publishing such a book. This is the first novel that I've read by this author. I am voluntarily reviewing it.

First, I'd like to call attention to the cover which made me want to read Starswept when I first saw it on Mary Fan's website. It's not only beautiful, but it said to me that it's a science fiction novel about a musician. There aren't very many of those.

I thought that the name Iris was very appropriate. In Greek mythology, Iris is the goddess of the rainbow which represents diversity in the current American cultural context. In a biblical context, the rainbow represents a promise that the biblical deity will not destroy the world by flood. So the rainbow is a hopeful symbol in the dark times that both we and Iris are experiencing.

Mary Fan's "if this goes on" premise asks what would happen if there was an attempt to control or even erase the uniqueness of each artist for corporate purposes. What if the one of a kind experience of a performance didn't matter so much to an audience of aliens who don't value individuality? What would music and musicians become in such a setting? Mary Fan shows us dramatically how artists can be crushed through the eyes of Iris who is determined to escape such a fate.

Fortunately, Iris isn't the only one who struggles against the system in which she is caught. Iris finds her romantic counterpart from among this underground group of rebels. I was rooting for their relationship even though it seemed impossible. Since this is the first book in a series, we don't know whether their cause will succeed. The struggle continues, but the rainbow exemplified by Iris appears as a sign of hope in the sky. For me, Starswept is a strong candidate for best YA novel of 2017.

I actually preferred this over Frances Sherwood's novel about Mary Wollstonecraft.  Whether you believe that Wollstonecraft had an affair with the painter Fuseli makes a big difference in how you perceive her.  It makes her seem like a perpetual victim who was always making mistakes about men. This discredits Wollstonecraft as a pioneer of feminism.  Lyndall Gordon rightly points out that there is no evidence that Wollstonecraft was involved with the married Fuseli and calls it "the Fuseli slander".

On the other hand, Gordon does engage in speculation herself.  They are mostly educated speculations  and there is a good chance of them being true. I thought that the speculation that Wollstonecraft's lover Imlay  was a spy had the least credibility because there are other explanations for his behavior that seem more likely to me.

I was glad that Lyndall Gordon included such tantalizing bits about Shelley's first wife, Harriet Westbrook and Clare Claremont, the daughter of William Godwin's second wife.  The little she has to say about them makes me think that they were extraordinary women and I'd love to know more.

This is the first book I've read by Ken Bruen, and it will probably be my last.  He certainly has a way with words, but his protagonist's angst is laid down with a trowel.  I also found the character repellent.  I normally like literate heroes who can wield allusions well, but this guy's no Spenser.

What bothered me most is that the case that was supposed to be under investigation was submerged under the weight of the main character's misery.  It's as if the author only occasionally remembered what the book was about. That's a shame because my primary motivation for reading it, is because it deals with the notorious Magdalen Laundry.  I don't think this theme was prominent enough to be mentioned in the title.  This book should be called An Addict's Ruminations.

I have a tendency to read books in a series out of order if I am drawn to the description of a later book. The author generously provided me with an ARC when I expressed interest in reviewing this book. Although this is the second book in The Healer's Shadow series, I didn't hesitate to plunge into it without any previous acquaintance with the work of Zoe Brooks. I always expect that an author will want to make sure that readers like me aren't too much out of the loop. I am happy to report that Love of Shadows, the sequel to Girl In The Glass stands on its own. Reviews of the first book categorize it as magical realism. Based on this second novel, I actually thought this series is more similar to Ursula Le Guin's books set in the fictional country of Orsinia. Like Malafrena and Orsinian Tales: Stories, Zoe Brooks deals with a real world type of setting with realistic characters and problems. Her fictional country could be any second or third world country where old traditions have been condemned by rulers who are certain that modern Western ideas are superior. The mysterious Shadows could be any despised minority who are viewed as less than human by minds darkened with fear of difference. Judith, the traditional healer protagonist, has no paranormal powers. She has learned how to recognize and utilize the plants that have been used in healing for many centuries. Herbalism is often viewed as primitive superstition because modern people have forgotten that many drugs prescribed by doctors are synthetic forms of the plant medicines in the herbalist's pharmacopeia. Zoe Brooks also illustrates how this issue is also an economic one. When the herbalists that served village communities are banned, it is the health of those who can't afford doctors that suffers most. This is shown without preaching through allowing us to experience the events of a well-devised plot. Love of Shadows is the work of an accomplished writer who is hitting her stride. Zoe Brooks writes about issues that she cares about, and teaches her readers to care about them by creating characters that get under our skins and into our hearts.

The first book I read by Mary D. Brooks was Awakenings, the fourth volume in the Intertwined Souls series.  The reason why I went back to the second book afterward is because I read spoilers in Awakenings that revealed the entire plot of the first novel in the series, Blood of the Greeks.  This is one of the perils of reading out of order in a series.  Where Shadows Linger takes place in Australia.  The Sydney Harbour Bridge illustration on the cover is a nice reminder of the books location.  Awakenings didn't really deal with the lives of the protagonists in Australia.  I also had never read a book set in post-WWII Australia, so I thought I would learn about the historical context from this novel.

Both Eva and Zoe encountered prejudice in Australia.  It is a sad paradox that nations which have a policy of welcoming immigrants often have tendencies toward ethnocentrism.  I admired Zoes insistence that Eva deserved better work conditions and employment, and Evas determination that Zoe shouldnt ever abandon her dreams.  These women are always standard bearers for the ideal of true love.
When Evas past in Nazi Germany catches up with her in Australia, Zoe is loyal, courageous and protective.  This series is definitely for readers who want to see lesbian lovers being heroic, and triumphing over adversity.

My favorite part of this book was the association of some of the characters with motorcycles.  Ive always enjoyed the sight of female motorcycle riders, but the image of Father Haralambos, a Greek Orthodox priest, on a motorcycle is also entertaining because it seems so unlikely.

Unfortunately, this book did have a noticeable flaw.  There were no typographical errors, but I found some continuity errors.  Most of them were minor.  A continuity error happens when the writer doesnt keep track of what she has already written or what she hasn't written yet.  An example of the second type of continuity error happens at 19% in the Kindle edition when the cat Ourania is mysteriously mentioned before Zoes first encounter with her at 23%.  There were more serious violations of continuity in an action scene involving numerous characters in which the author repeatedly loses track of where the characters are in relation to each other. Admittedly, its tricky to visualize a scene that is so complex, but I have to say that the narration of that entire sequence is contradictory and confusing.

 I also noticed a scientific improbability in the same action scene.  A heavy projectile has increased gravitational pull when its hurled.  This means that it will land with a great deal of force and would be likely to cause damage.  You cant just casually throw it across a room.

Mary D. Brooks is an author who deals with compelling characters and themes, but When Shadows Linger needed the sort of editor who pays attention to details.  Continuity should be a special concern because readers who are confused may give up on a book or an entire series.

I received a free copy of this book in return for an honest review.

I tend to prefer novels that demonstrate their themes through the events of the plot rather than bringing the plot to a halt while the characters discuss ideas.  So I thought that the didacticism in this novel did become too overt at times.  Yet I did consider the resolution of the plot  an eloquent statement about the value of sacred cycles in any culture.

I enjoyed some of the character background.  I think I would have loved to have been a child with a puppeteer as a parent like central character Lydia Rosenstrom. The bond that resulted from Lydia's shared experience with her niece Ivey made their relationship seem more intense.  I also thought that the background of computer genius Claude Vandermeer made him more sympathetic to me.

There were aspects of the characterization that I didn't care for.  Although Mayan Interface is not New Age oriented as a whole, Lydia exhibited certain New Age attitudes that I occasionally found bothersome.  I also didn't like the fact that the Maya holy man was called  "Nacho".  It seemed to me that naming him after a snack trivializes him.  It's hard to take a character with such a name seriously.  On the other hand, I wondered if the historical personage who became the VR persona of one of the characters was too imposing for him.  Perhaps the authors were attempting to show that he had large aspirations.

The novel itself had large aspirations  that I rather admired .  I liked the main thematic thrust of this novel.  The idea that time doesn't exist on the plane that is accessed by mystics, mediums and shamans is common to a number of spiritual traditions.

The idea that virtual reality  might have unpredictable impact on people is an important observation that we need to heed.  We have already seen that our entertainment technology can have negative effects on some individuals in the case of 3D movies.  Perhaps one of the lessons of this novel is that we should be more cautious about technological innovations.

I did like Patrick, the hero of this historical paranormal romance, very much.  He is strong yet vulnerable.  I was interested in the concept, and the situation of the O'Malley clan was compelling.  I admit that I preferred the heroine's cousin, Kyra, over the heroine, Darina.  This bodes well for the sequel which focuses on Kyra.

On the other hand, I disliked the stereotypical villain and the cliffhanger ending.  I was already prepared to purchase the sequel.  The emotional manipulation of a cliffhanger was unnecessary.

There were a couple of minor historical errors that I could forgive because they had no impact on the plot.  My qualms about the scheduling of the wedding because of the symbolism of that date in the ancient Celtic religion seemed to be a more serious issue, but I learned during a web search that it was actually a traditional time for weddings among the ancient Celts.  I found that there is pro and con discussion among current Pagan practitioners about the desirability of a wedding on that date.  So I no longer have so much difficulty with when the O'Malley clan planned to celebrate Patrick and Darina's marriage.

Despite the drawbacks of this particular outing, I hope to return to the world of the medieval O'Malleys of Ireland soon.

I received this book for free in return for an honest review.

I decided to read the indie spy thriller novel And The Wolf Shall Dwell by Joni Dee because I was interested in the perspective of this new Israeli-Canadian author. I received a free copy and am reviewing it voluntarily.

Like most spy thrillers, And The Wolf Shall Dwell is plot driven. So it will fulfill the expectations of thriller fans who expect a fast paced plot with a great deal of action. The events are credible enough so that they could have happened in those particular circumstances. It is a competently written novel with a suspenseful narrative.

When I agreed to review Point of No Return by Martha Gellhorn for the publisher of the new digital edition, I knew nothing of the author. The name was familiar, but I should have known more of her. She led an extraordinary life as a war journalist, novelist and the third wife of Ernest Hemingway. Without this background, I began reading my ARC from Open Road Media via Net Galley without any expectations or preconceptions.

Gellhorn wrote Point of No Return soon after WWII. It was first published in 1948. According to her Afterword that appears at the end of the book, she had been a witness to events in this war as a journalist who traveled with British troops. Although I have read quite a number of WWII novels, I hadn't read any that were written by a woman author who had experienced the war first hand.

The resolution of Point of No Return is extremely powerful. Gellhorn tells us in the Afterword that the reason she wrote the book was to exorcise what she saw at the concentration camp in Dachau soon after its liberation. When she wrote the book so soon after that event, it must have felt like a raw wound. Seeing a concentration camp after it had ceased operations can never be equivalent to the trauma of a survivor of the camp, but I imagine that it would still leave a mark on someone's soul. She wanted Jacob Levy to be the keeper of that memory.

I liked this book despite the fact that I considered it structurally flawed.  I was won over by the loveable Grandpa Fentress, who turned out to be more than a bit of a scamp, and some remarkably entertaining twists in the narrative.

Yet I would be remiss if I didn't point out that very few events in Jacob's Cellar were shown as happening to the characters in real time.  More than ninety percent of the novel is conveyed through exposition, dialogue about events that had already happened, and letters.  It seems to me that this is not the most effective way to construct a narrative.  It lessens the impact of the novel.  I often felt distanced from the characters, particularly at the outset. I had a hard time identifying who all these people were, and how they were related to each other. I wished that I had a chart of the Ebhart family for reference.  I might have had an easier time if there had been some flashbacks so that I could have had more direct contact with the more historically distant characters.  They would have been better fleshed out, and therefore more memorable.

The expository passages sometimes felt long and tedious.  This was especially true of the narration about the Civil War.  The author was showing off the extent of his research, but not contributing very much in the way of excitement.

I honestly feel that Jacob's Cellar was meant to be three books.  The first would be about the earliest generation of the Ebharts in America.  Since the 18th century is my favorite period in American history, I would definitely have loved a firsthand account of the Regulator Revolt and the Battle of the Alamance.  The second would deal with the life and death of the mysterious Jacob, and the third with his son Jake's experiences in the Mexican War and the Civil War.  The drama of Jake's war experiences could have been brought to life more successfully by showing them as they happened through the eyes of both Jake and Adelita.

The YA novel Stalking Los Angeles by Tom Berquist alternates between the viewpoint of Reggie Youngblood, a Native American youth, and a mountain lion growing up in the hills around Santa Monica.  Tom Berquists perspective as a wildlife advocate informs the narrative.  It was fascinating to see the human boy and the young lion pass through similar stages of development.

Another significant theme in this book is Native American identity.  Reggie attempts to follow a Native spiritual practice on his own in absence of a community.  His father had decided in favor of integration with Euro-American society.  While a vision quest has traditionally involved isolation, it was normally interpreted with the guidance of an elder.  Reggie had no Native elder to assist him.  This aspect of the novel demonstrates that a successful adolescent rite of passage may require some direction from an adult.

Wildlife expert Joe Sartor does provide Reggie with a professional role model.  Reggies bond with Joe is a positive influence on his life especially as compared to his ambivalent relationship with his PTSD and alcohol ravaged father.  Berquist realistically shows that recovery from PTSD is a long process that can involve setbacks.

I thought that the cover design could be more effective.  I would have chosen to place the title and author below the illustration rather than superimposing the title over the shadowy head of the lion within the clouds.  I had to enlarge the cover image in order to see that lion head.

There was a handful of typographical errors, but these weren't very notable since the novel as a whole was so well-written.

I was heartened by this books resolution.  Since the preservation of endangered species like the California mountain lion is important to me, I was glad to see Joe Sartor and Reggie Youngblood involved in this cause.  Despite human encroachment on the mountain lions habitat, Stalking Los Angeles offered some hope that humans and lions might be able to co-exist.

The stream of consciousness technique used in the first story, "Shades of Grey", is highly effective for showing us the experience of a captured UK black ops agent.  He's not a very sympathetic character, but neither is anyone else described in the story.  That's very much the point of it.  He's what passes for ethical in the context of black ops which requires people who are willing to do whatever it takes to complete an assignment.  He's very critical of other black ops agents for enjoying violence too much, but he's no paragon of virtue himself.  I wondered about the location of this story's events.  It could have been in Ireland or somewhere in the UK itself.  The protagonist mentions at least one mission within the UK.  I remember thinking while I was reading this story that the protagonist could just as easily have been a mercenary.  Mercenaries seem very similar to black ops agents.

The second tale in this anthology, "There and Back Again" takes place during WWII.  The central character, James, was rather bland compared to other characters in this anthology.  James' war experience causes him to think differently about courage and cowardice.  His fellow combatant, David, is much more complex.  David is along the lines of the black ops agents in "Shades of Grey", but he has survived a difficult past which makes him somewhat more sympathetic.

I would categorize the last of these stories, "Down The Rabbit Hole" as a horror tale.  I don't think it's about domestic abuse as other reviews have said.  The horror element surfaces much earlier in the story.  I've seen other similar situations in the horror genre.  Like the previous two stories in the anthology, it deals with crossing the line ethically.  Where should that line be drawn?  What happens when the person deciding whether the line has been crossed is a child?  I think that another theme that this story shares with the others is that violence begets more violence.  If countries have black ops teams, their antagonists escalate in response.  The same thing certainly happens in war.  In "Down The Rabbit Hole" the violence that begets more violence is incubated within a family.  When the violence escalates, no one can predict what the consequences will be.  It's hard enough for an adult to be faced with such a situation.  The responsibility would have to be staggering for a child who must figure out how to deal with what seems to be like a juggernaut that he is helpless to control.  Fortunately, this is a remarkably tough child.  I would agree with the reviewers of this anthology who consider "Down The Rabbit Hole" the best of the lot.  This story's placement provides Shades of Grey with a strong finish.

I really like the variable lighting and the haptic pressure page turns.  I don't like the re-set button on the back.  I expected it to be on the bottom.  When I looked for help specifically for my Voyage Kindle, Amazon's instructions showed the reset button on the bottom.  I did finally notice the reset button when I turned it over.  Unfortunately, I get accidental page turns and accidental resets when the Kindle is traveling with me in a bag on a bumpy road with bad potholes which happens almost every trip I make.  I wish this model wasn't so sensitive to being jostled in transit.

This book offers up a rich variety of soups, salads, vegetarian, meat and fish dishes. The dishes can be cooked ahead of time and/or in larger amounts that can then be kept in the fridge or freezer for consumption later, which will save both time and money.

One of my favorite dishes is Chicken a la Plum, which offers a savory and sweet taste sensation.

cands.text:
So many choices with different taste sensations. The author truly takes you around the world with his international recipes. With so much content, you can plan several weeks of meals with this one book.

Here's a meal plan I made:

Breakfast - Cuban Spinach & Avocado Omelet
Lunch - Morocco Chicken & Sweet Potato Stew
Snack - Mexican Meatballs with Tomato Sauce
Salad - Fresh Berry Salad with Strawberry Vinaigrette
Dinner - Spiced Roast Beef
Dessert - Southern Pecan Pie with Date Crust

I love my slow cooker and having a wide selection of recipes to choose from really helps.

This recipe book covers a wide gamut of different dishes so there's sure to be something to please everyone.

My favorite so far is the chicken cacciatore. Can't wait to try the others.

I'm a big fan of slow cooker recipes so when I found this book for a gluten free diet, I couldn't resist. The variety of ideas makes planning for meals during the week a snap. The book includes a few vegetarian dishes and desserts.

The family really enjoyed the chicken taco recipe and I'm looking forward to trying out more this week.

I just love this book. With a huge variety of quick and healthy recipes, it was easy to plan a full meal. There are recipes for each of the following categories: soups, salads, dressings and sauces, appetizers, main dishes, side dishes and desserts.

Here is a meal plan I put together for the family:

Appetizer - Oriental Smoked Salmon Roll Ups
Soup - Fresh Leek & Potato Soup
Salad - Mediterranean Pasta Salad
Main - Roasted Chicken with Tomato & Artichoke
Side - Roasted Root Vegetables
Dessert - Peachy Upside Down Cake

There will be many more days like this.

I love my slow-cooker and any good recipes are a welcome addition to my dinner table.

Not only does this book give you 15 slow-cooking recipes, but it also includes a few tips to ensure your final dish is cooked to perfection.

My favorite so far has been the Asian Beef and the Greek Stuffed Chicken.

I have always loved Japanese and Asian food but I never really believed that I could cook this exotic food at home until I saw this book.  I like the one dish meals which I found were fast and easy to make. My husband and I just loved the Japanese Teriyaki Chicken.  I was impressed with the variety of both vegetarian and meat selections. Delicious Japanese food with a modern twist!

Instead of buying processed frozen dinners from the grocery store, this book provides a viable alternative.  The idea of batching your cooking and freezing it for convenient access later is a tremendous time saver.  The book also provides many examples of food that I haven't considered freezing like burritos and baked potato.

If you love meat, you'll love this book on how to prepare your meal for the grill.

The book is divided into the major meat categories for easy reference such as chicken, beef, pork, lamb and turkey.

There are still a few weeks left for outdoor BBQ'ing. My favorites so far are the Chili BBQ Chicken with its homemade BBQ sauce and the Pineapple Marinated Steak.

I found this book nicely laid out with useful information such as prep time and cooking time.  The suggestions at the beginning on how to use book was also helpful.  The recipe I tried was the "Garlic & Barley Chicken Stew" and it was delicious.

This cookbook is suitable for anyone with a busy schedule. Who wouldn't want to spend less time in the kitchen if you always have things on the go. But how else can you get a decent home cooked meal?

The recipes instructions are easy to follow and they taste delicious. My favorite so far is the Chicken Alfredo but there are many others in this book that come close to second.

This book contains recipes for every meal of the day so there is no shortage of ideas.

Interesting fact:
Although rice and potatoes are normally known to consist mainly of carbohydrates, the book does remind us that they also contain some protein.

Here is a delicious meal plan that I was able to prepare from the book:
Breakfast - Apple Pancakes
Lunch - Sweet Potato Burgers
Appetizer - Garlic Lemon Mushrooms
Dinner - Eggplant Lasagna
Side dish - Brussels Sprouts
Soup - Butternut Squash Soup
Dessert - Strawberry Cobbler

With so many other recipes available, I'll be able to design many more meal plans.

I love my slow cooker and when I found this cookbook, I couldn't resist trying out these recipes.  I am a big fan of lamb so the leg of lamb recipe won't disappoint.  The Party Menu and Shopping List at the end of the book is also a big help when going grocery shopping for the menu.

The problem most people have when going on a diet is giving up their favorite foods.  With cookbooks like "International Paleo Recipes For Two", there is no need to give up what you love if there is a satisfactory alternative.  I am a fan of ice cream so when I found the tropical ice cream recipe, I knew I found that alternative.  Another favorite is the Grilled Tuna Steaks.  This book offers enough variety to plan weeks of paleo meals without getting tired of the menu.

I didn't realize there was a name for it but I've been doing "clean eating" for a while. That is to say that I've been avoiding processed foods and have been eating fresh and natural foods.

With over 60 recipes to choose from, it is quite easy to plan your week and make up your own meal plans. Here one I made today: Hearty Vegetarian Soup, Greek Isles Salad, Orietal Spring Rolls, Penne Pasta with Chicken, Golden Brussels Sprouts and Strawberry Crumble. Yum.

I found this book well organized. There are five categories of sauces: meat, BBQ, tomato, mayonnaise and fruit. I would rather make my own sauces over using the ones available commercially. This way, you can control what goes into it.

With 30 different recipes to choose from, most of these will cover the majority of our meals.

This book is a useful resource for freezing foods that will help reduce your food bill due to less wastage.

Something that I never thought about freezing is cooked rice.

The Refrigeration Guidelines for different types of food and Freezing Time Guidelines will be very useful for those times when cooking big meals.

There is also a good summary of what not to freeze.

For those who suffer from inflammation of sorts, it may be food related. If so, then by avoiding those types of food can help reduce that ailment.

This book offers 25 anti-inflammatory food recipes and is organized into the categories of breakfast, soup, salad and other dishes.

Of course, reducing the incidence of inflammation through diet is not a substitution for medical treatment where warranted.

There are 30 recipes that I can use to prepare slow cooker meals for the family. Each recipe also includes nutritional information which I find very helpful.

The ingredients are easy to obtain and the directions are simple to follow.

I love my morning smoothies and this book doesn't disappoint.

If you want a change from bacon and eggs or a breakfast sandwich, try something healthy. You can't go wrong with fresh fruits and vegetables.

I especially liked the Wednesday Smoothie - Tangerine. But all of them are healthy for you and taste great.

This is my first book on African recipes and I've always wanted to try preparing them myself.

My favorite dish so far has been the Baba Ghanoush.

This is a story of loss and new found love.

Cody made the biggest mistake of his life when he enlisted in the army and drove his love away forever.

After returning from his duties in the army, his parents were no where to be found and the family farm was repossessed by the bank and sold off. Even worse, the love of his life had disappeared.

What Cody found afterwards was totally unexpected.

Losing weight is never as simple as eating less. This book helps focus on the core issue using key questions. These questions address your reason for wanting to lose weight, your motivation to move forward, your willingness to stick to it and your willingness to change your identity.

Identifying and understanding triggers that encourage bad habits will help in your plan to avoid those triggers. Replacing the bad habits with good habits will reinforce the change.

Part of a successful program is keeping track of your progress. The book includes a free measurement tracker that offers feedback on your weight loss program.
Not only is this a good book on training a puppy, it is a great book on teaching young children responsibility.  Children learn best when they are actively engaged and this book fits the bill.

This book is well written with a pace that is quick when it starts off. Each escape scene kept me on the edge of my seat... I couldn't put the book down. The point of view is given in the first person by protagonist, Kevin Turner. The story revolves around his personal account as a newspaper reporter of events that transpire over the course of doing his job.

I can see that this story would be good movie material. For people who love a good zombie story, this book delivers on that promise.

Nothing beats a BBQ in the summer. The timing of this book can't get any better.

There are many ways to prepare a BBQ meal and this book doesn't disappoint. Some of these recipes can be prepared indoors, a perfect alternative if the weather decides to be uncooperative.

The triple free bonuses are a pleasant surprise and offer great value.

My HP Dv7 series laptop needed a new drive at last, especially after upgrading to Win10, and I knew I was going to get a SSD style but was not certain of which brand.  I have had very good luck with SanDisk products before so went with their 128 gb SSD drive.  Since I only put the OS on the main drive and store everything on the secondary, I did not need more space.

Basically, this is plug and play.  I replaced the drive in very short order, inserted my OS disc and the speed at which everything loaded was impressive.  I had no issues at all with either installation or performance and I am very pleased.  As a bonus, my computer and the power adapter run much cooler as well.  I would definitely recommend this brand for anyone needing a SSD.

cands.text: I bought two of these for my older laptop.  I really have no need for drive space more than 500 gb anyway since my laptop has room for two.  This drive improved my disc performance dramatically and I have had no problems with them.  I have always had good luck with Western Digital drives.  I highly recommend this drive.

I have had WD internal drives before and had pretty good luck with them and I needed an external drive and decided to give this one a go.  I got the 1 TB version and am fairly pleased with it.  The transfer rate is definitely fast and I like that it is powered by the USB port rather than needing a separate power adapter.  The security features I do not use so I cannot speak of them.  I marked it down simply because I somehow believed that this was a solid state drive when in fact it is not and I think that should be made clearer in the product description as that is what I really wanted.  But, I will keep this one as it is pretty good for the price.

I recently got my Mom's HP DV7-6000 series computer because she wanted a new one and hers was not working.  Turned out to be a bad hard drive.  When I took the bottom off to replace it, I found space for a secondary drive, but no cable to connect it.  After coming to Amazon to find one, I chose this product.  The real cool thing is that it comes with 4 screws to mount the HDD to the holder.  The connector easily installed and has worked perfectly.  I would recommend this product.

This burner seems to work fairly well.  It burns almost as fast as my internal drive.  The one thing that was quite irritating was that not only my laptop, but my sister's surface would not recognise the drive when attempting to create a backup disc for windows.  But it does work for everything else I need.  Overall, I would say it is a good buy.

I am very pleased with this BB pistol.  It has more power than I thought it would have, it feels solid and it is easy to load and operate.  As a bonus, everything you need to get started comes in the package.

This programme has worked fairly well on my PC.  The one thing I have noticed is that it does not always sync with the last page read from my Kindle, so I have to do it manually.  Other than that, I like having it on my PC.

I have this on vinyl and wanted to get this remastered CD in order to preserve it.  I am not disappointed.  The audio quality to me is excellent.  This album is truly original and is an absolute must have for any collection.  The one thing I did not like was the bonus tracks.  They are good, but I would have preferred if they had put them on a second CD so I could hear the original album without it going into the other tracks.  To me, it takes away from the original release to have it on the same CD.  But other than that, I love it.

I loved the Hellraiser movies and the creepy macabre music in them.  This double disc set is perfect for those times I want to relax to something less ordinary.  I would recommend this to any Hellraiser fan.

When I first got this (I had to buy it again because it disappeared) I have to say I did not like it very much.  But upon further listening, I realised I actually liked it better than Sixteen Stone, so it sort of grew on me as the saying goes.  This CD is more stark and a bit darker than their debut, but it is an excellent album.

Most of the other reviewers have said what I would have so all I can say is that this, to me, is one of the great one-off albums of the 90's.  Kind of like Mad Season's Above.  Every song is spot on.  It just does not get much better.

This has to be my favourite DS album.  I cannot understand why it was so underrated when it came out.  They recorded it in the Bahamas and the musical influences are evident, especially in the first track.  This album has a terrific flow to it and not one song is out of place.  To me, this CD is a must have for my collection.

I bought this CD mainly for the song The Rose which I always thought was Bette at her best.  Overall, I like the entire CD but sometimes with some songs, I found her voice a bit grating or not well suited for the song.  That being said, she made a great effort in the movie and made the character musically believable.  And for 3.99, it was worth it for me to have the CD.

I find it a bit difficult to rate this book.  In some places I would give it 5 stars and in others a 1.  It feels uneven and sometimes just drags, while at other times it has  you wanting to read faster to know what is going to happen.  The topic is controversial but that does not have any effect on my rating.  It is hard for me to recommend this book due to its unevenness.

This stylus has proved to be an excellent replacement for what was the D5100SKII from Stanton.  The differences are that this stylus is elliptical and the Stanton brand is conical, so this one tracks better.  It is less money but it actually sounds better than the Stanton stylus.  It is also made in Switzerland, much to my relief and not from China.  I use 1.75 gram tracking force with this one and have had no problems.  I will buy this one again.

I really like this album, though not quite as much as Ten.  I have always been a PJ fan, and this album has some great music on it, but it also seems a little uneven from one song to the next.  I had to buy it again as my other copy was permanently borrowed and it is a CD I will always want to have.  But it is not in my list of favourites, mostly due to its unevenness.
It was great to have all 7 books on my Kindle at once rather than having to buy them separately. A truly great story.
It was great to have all 7 books on my Kindle at once rather than having to buy them separately. A truly great story.
It was great to have all 7 books on my Kindle at once rather than having to buy them separately. A truly great story.

Not the best of the Hellraiser series but for any fan of the Hellraiser mythos this, like the others that follow down the line, is required to make the collection complete.  I got the DVD version so I cannot attest to the quality of the Blu-ray disc.  I would have hoped for some extras even on the DVD release but that hope was in vain.

This is my all-time favourite EJ album.  I bought this to replace a double CD set of the same title I bought in the late 80's.  The job they did remastering this disc is outstanding and it is all on one disc this time, too.  I couldn't be happier.

Mark's books can tend to be uneven from book to book.  Some I really like, some I don't so much.  This, to me, is one of his best.  It is about a boy named Elijah and how his faith is tested when he comes to the realisation he is gay.  His church is against gays, but he finds solace in his friends and in when a serious health issue arises he ultimately rises to the occasion.  This was a book I could not put down.

When I was a kid in the early 80's, my dad had a watch nearly identical to this one (I still have it, it still works but I do not wear it anymore) and when I saw this one, I had to have it.  It is very simple to use, no fancy functions that I will never use and its setup is the exact same as my dad's old watch.  I am very happy that they still make this model.  You really cannot go wrong with this watch.

As I have said in other reviews on the Rush vinyl reissues, the quality is superb.  This is no exception.  And this reissue sold by Amazon is the hologram edition and I have to say it looks pretty cool.  You do need to use a focussed LED light for best results, though, for the clearest image and colour rendition of the hologram.  Also, as the hologram is on the second side, there is no groove run out to the label after Something For Nothing.  This is to make the hologram possible.  So those with semi-automatic turntables will have to manually return their tone arm at the end of the second side.

This is another of those greatest hits collections that actually hits the mark.  To get a feel for their music you do need to listen to their albums, but for jumping in for the first time, this is an excellent place to start.

More letters from kids, which can be quite entertaining at times, but again as I said with the first book...if you get it on a Kindle many of the pages are unreadable.  This makes it a disappointing reading experience overall.

users.query:
This light does everything it claims to do. It is simple to setup, efficient energy user, and gives plenty of light for growing plants. My orchids love it because of the bright light it gives without extra heat.

Highly recommended!

cands.text: It was everything I expected. I wanted a daylight LED that fit a piano lamp. It fit, it's a very even daylight color, and it's bright enough. OK, it's not flood light bright, but I didn't expect it to be. I estimate it's equivalent to a 60W bulb. The swivel feature is nice in a piano lamp to make sure it's pointed in the right way.

We do cabin camping and need that evening and night light at the table and in the cabin. This has a very nice light that is very even. It's also easy on the eyes, but bright for an area. It works well for reading by too.

The annoying thing is getting it working right from the beginning. It comes in the 10 second demo mode. However, the instructions say nothing about how to get it out of the demo mode. I searched online too and found nothing. I had to call Energizer to find out how. You have to take all the batteries out for about 30 seconds and then put them back in. Then it will work normally.

The other mildly annoying thing is that you can't just turn it off. You have to hold the button until it dims down then up again. Then release and press the button again to turn it off. This is workable, but seems like bad design.

Otherwise, it's a nice camp light.

It does everything it says without any problems. It has a brief learning curve, but not too complicated - if you've ever done anything like it. The slow wind up of the alarms is a very nice feature. The fully adjustable light is also very nice.

Recommended.

Recommended.
It's simple and effective. It does what it's suppose to do without any trouble. Highly recommended!

It works, works well, and easy to use. I mostly use it for soapmaking and haven't had any trouble with it. It is very fast for soapmaking.

Highly recommended.
I use this to blast hot air from a 1800W hot air gun to finish my encaustic paintings. It absolutely keep the heat away from anything around.
This probably isn't fair, but I use it only for encaustic painting. I melt the wax/resin colors on it to "paint" with. It's accurate in temp control and very steady. Highly recommended!

This is very complete with lots of scientific backup for a complete Paleo/Low Carb lifestyle. Yes, it's more Paleo than Low Carb, but explains very well.

It isn't just about what you eat though. It scientifically goes into vitamins, exercise, sleeping, and others to make a complete package. I can't say I've tried everything, but the changes I've made from a strict low carb diet have been beneficial.

Highly recommended.

This works great with no trouble. It's easy to use and seems very accurate. It has easy settings for different meats and how well done you want it. Sometimes I'd like to set the alarm at an in-between temp, but it really isn't a problem. I've had no problems for the past couple of years.

Highly recommended!

I haven't used it as much as I thought I would - the story of my life with tools. It seems durable and more than up to my light to medium tasks. The fixes speeds aren't as much a limitation as I thought they might be. I'm very happy with it!

It's small, light, and starts up fast. We are already embedded in using Google products. So, this is great for all those Google products. The key thing is the keyboard. Unlike a tablet, you can use this keyboard like a completely normal one. It is completely productive.

We have had no problem with speed. It has kept up on everything we've tried. Well, when I've played music from Google Play it plays very well. However, it really hurt the multitasking. The speakers are pretty good for a computer this small, but they certainly aren't great for listening to good music. So, the playing from Google Play really isn't an issue.

This is almost a fully functional small computer. However, you have to be able to work in a completely Web based world. If that world is Google oriented, so much the better. Still, if you can get to it and run it in Chrome, you can run it. It isn't limited to just Google products.

We love it!

Highly recommended.
A great little book for artists to read on occasion to remind about how and where to get and create your art.

OK, I don't really need this kind of speed very often, but it's very nice to have on occasion.

Highly recommended.

I heard about this from Good Eats years ago, but never got around to getting it. Now that I finally have, I'm very happy. It works great with tough meats, particularly if braising is the method of cooking.

It won't completely cut down the long stringy fibers in some cuts of meat, but it helps. Of course, cutting those meats smaller across the grain is very good too.

In short, this is the very best tool I've found for dealing with tough meats. It cuts a lot of that connective tissue that long, slow cooking will finish off into nice tender meat. It also helps meats that are going to be cooked faster too, like grilling or frying.

Highly recommend!

I read a lot of reviews before buying this. A lot of them thought it was very complicated to setup. I didn't find that to be the case. It took a little time, but wasn't hard.

I have mine set for some warnings only; no watches. I haven't had that many yet, but it does work. I am comforted by that.

At first I thought that the display was too flat for a bedside clock radio. Now I think it works. I can look at the time only when I want to. With the flat display, the light doesn't bother me until I do look. OK, my eyesight is such that I have to get that close to it anyway.

The only minor annoyance is the message if it hasn't received anything within 10 days. It's easy to make go away, but it is a minor issue.

I highly recommend this weather radio. You can make it tell you just what you want weatherwise. You can trust it too.
For a small camera, it's a little big and top heavy. However, the "big" gives a smoother light. The color is good and the light is even. I'm very happy with it.

We haven't used this as much as we thought we might have, but it is a joy to use. It is smooth, easy to line up, cuts like a hot knife in butter, and will shave off as much or as little as we like. This is one of the best trimmers I've ever used. It is fun to use and feels very satisfying to get flawless cuts every time.

One tiny note: my wife sometimes would like an arm to set a length for batches of cuts at one length. This does not have that. If that is a big requirement for you, look elsewhere. It is only an occasional need for us and workable enough.

Highly recommended.

It really has pulled stubborn odors out of our apartment over a few months. We moved into an new apartment that had a number of funky odors. Other methods didn't work so well. It took a couple of months, but this really has filtered out those smells. Highly recommended.

This camera's features, flexibility, and quality output were more than I expected. It's easy to use in all modes. It is small and light making it very easy to carry in different ways. (It's not small enough for most pockets, but that fine for my style.) I love the fast f1.4 lens for very good low light shooting. I also love the 24mm wide angle. It doesn't go out very far on the tele side, but that's fine for what I shoot. The sensor is large enough and good enough that I don't do any post processing noise reduction!

Highly recommended.
I thought I might like it, but it was better than I expected. It's a great story told very well.

I don't know how much of this is really like doing a start-up in Silicone Valley, but it was an interesting read. I certainly got the impression that it was very much like the real thing though. Actually it felt so real that it was scary. I guess I'm not cutout for that world.

If you every thought you might want to do a Tech startup, read this book first.
I'm using this to connect my computer to my TV. It's working just fine. No reason to spend any more.

I enjoy all my Mogwai music. The variation and ever changing melodies of their creations is always refreshing and worth buy the new release without a second thought. This particular AmazonMP3 download was a refreshing change of pace. It was slower and more mellow than their regular tempo and tone. I like it very much and highly recommend it getting it.
For really cooked on stuff, this isn't very good at scraping out the gunk. For just cleaning out lightly cooked stuff, it's OK. I cook my stuff enough that I rarely find this useful.

users.query:
My girlfriend has a gorgeous room for makeup and fashion, so I recommended that she use a small surge protector for the Hollywood-style vanity (it has about 14 expensive bulbs). This was the smallest surge protector that provided decent protection.

It does the job -- haven't had a surge yet to test it, but their hefty guarantee helps the confidence. My only criticism is that the large Tripp-Lite logo is unsightly (who wants to see that?) and the actual design of the protector partially obscures one outlet in a double. It could have easily been shifted slightly to keep that second outlet free.

For the price, it's great, but it may not be the best fit for everyone.

cands.text:
I have a Braun Series 7 electric razor that I've had for about 5 years, and nothing comes close to being as useful with it as Lectric Shave.

This is one of those products that has been around forever for a reason. It's simple and effective. I put it on my face, wait about 30 seconds, and then use the razor. It gets much closer than the razor alone or any other product that I've tried.

It might seem expensive at $7 or so for a bottle, but that bottle lasts a long time.

Lectric Shave is like WD-40 or Ballistol for your face. Ancient technology, but I don't see a better product coming along ever.

I got this when it was on sale for about $29, which was a fantastic price. My desk is tempered glass with black trim so it's a perfect aesthetic fit.

I had a laptop stand with several USB connections -- it was good, but it was white and a gaudy neon green. It served its purpose but looked a little odd.

This one is simple and attractive, and honestly, I don't miss the USB connections. I never used them all that much.

The stand gives me all the space under a 24" monitor with no hassle and a chic design. I'm not sure I'd be excited at $50, but I was pleased at around half that.

I'm far less concerned with kitchen and dining room style than my girlfriend is, so she picked out this napkin holder. I was about to stack the napkins in the center of the table for free, so dropping $10 on a holder seemed... egregious.

But now I'm a fan. It's simple, chic, and well-made. The holder is heavy and solid -- I'm happy to have purchased it. It's clean and attractive on our table, and it certainly does the job.

I can't imagine paying too much less and getting a napkin holder of this quality, so I recommend the Spectrum Euro holder highly.

I really like Rolodex's Mesh office products. They're simple, look decent and very cheap. I have several including the business card holder, pen cup and phone stand. All were a few bucks and look exactly the same as when I took the packaging off.

I needed a wastebasket under my desk at home, so I immediately checked this one out. $10? I'll take it.

Another solid product from Rolodex. Really, really pleased.

I've consistently been happy with Amazon Basics products, so when I needed several Lightning to USB cables for the office, I went with Amazon Basics models.

It was a great decision. The build quality is solid, which is something that I've had trouble with on some MiFi and even Apple cables. The Amazon cable is thicker and the connection between the cord and the Lightning/USB ends has held up much better than other cords.

In short, it's perfect, it's lasted a year with no problems, and it's cheaper. I'll be picking up a few more of these for the home and car.

I have a Husqvarna 223R gas brushcutter and I needed a full face shield to accompany it. I've used Husqvarna's forestry helmet before and liked it a lot, but I wanted something a bit lighter that would be easier to wear for long outdoor sessions.

This face visor absolutely delivers. It's comfortable to wear, keeps everything from hitting my face (including covering my throat area, which is AWESOME) and doesn't get hot. It also doesn't fog up, which lots of plexiglas products do for me.

Perhaps the most impressive aspect is the noise reduction. I really wasn't concerned with noise, so the visor aspect was my main concern, but it reduces noise by a tremendous amount.

As with pretty much every Husqvarna product, the assembly instructions are AWFUL. Imagine Ikea-style directions with no text and pictures that don't quite fit your item. It was frustrating and took me 15 minutes to figure out, but you can do it with some time and patience if you look at the item picture here on Amazon and try to recreate it (there aren't THAT many pieces).

Still, this thing is worth its weight in gold. I'd go with a real forestry helmet for anything involving a chainsaw, but everything else, including brushcutters? This face shield is the way to go.

These little things are handy. I have a TV in my office, one on my home office desk and a new 55" Samsung curved TV, so the three pack allowed me to plug the HDMI cable vertically to ease tension on the HDMI port.

For a couple dollars, these are a nice solution to help protect your HDMI port. I don't want to have to send a TV away for repair, so if I can get something that solves a potential problem before it happens -- and cheaply! -- I'm happy.

I recently outfitted the entire house in LED bulbs, mostly in 5000k daylight (which I prefer). However... a few parts of the house just don't work well with that color temperature (like the dining room), so I picked up these LENMAR dimmables.

They do the job properly and give off a gently-glowing soft white light. I haven't had any issue with dimming/flickering or with the bulbs not working (my failure rate on LED bulbs has been about 10%, so we'll see).

I received this item at a discount for an honest, unbiased review, which I've tried to provide here. I depend on honest reviews myself to make purchases on Amazon, so it's important to me that I do the same for other people.

I wish I could speak to the longevity of these, but I'll really only be able to do that after quite some time... and hopefully at least as long as the bulbs claim to last.

I was a pretty big fan of Cree bulbs based on price and performance, and then I had a few issues (to be fair, they replaced those problem bulbs immediately and with no hassle). It's looking like LENMAR will turn out to be comparable on quality and value.

I needed a respirator for a lead paint refinish job and I wanted a relatively inexpensive low-profile unit that was comfortable -- and wow, did this do the trick.

I really can't believe how comfortable it is. After just a few minutes, I didn't even know I was wearing it. I worked for nearly 8 hours without needing to stop and take a break because the respirator had too much breath condensation or I needed it off my face. The adjustments are easy and actually result in a tight fit that's still easy to wear.

I'd recommend getting a set or two of replacement cartridges right when you order the unit. You're going to need them, so why wait?

Our office is great, but it doesn't have any windows. We thought getting a Miracle-Gro AeroGarden with LEDs would perk up the room.

We have two desks facing each other and we put the AeroGarden in between them. Within a week all but chives had germinated. A few days later and we had basil and dill to harvest.

Chives took a while, but now it's developed well and we have more herbs than we can handle. We love the 'Office Farm' and produce more dill that we're even able to consume (and we love dill). All the plants are producing well and it looks pretty awesome, too.

In terms of maintenance, we rarely have to pour in nutrients and we add about a liter of water every 4 or 5 days. It's INCREDIBLY low maintenance.

We love the AeroGarden and it keeps producing non-stop. It's added a cool dimension to our office, is easy to maintain, and the herbs taste great.

I tried to save a buck with a spatula set from Ikea. Dumb move. It was heat-resistant, but only up to 225F. Those spatulas didn't last long.

The di Oro spatula being safe up to 600F is great, and it's a nice blend of pliable/flexible and stiff, which means I can still use it to break up ground beef or turkey in the pan.

The handle is covered in silicon, too, which is an upgrade over the polymer spatulas I had. They'd get a little slippery from steam condensation.

I received this product at a discount in exchange for an honest, unbiased review, which I've tried to provide here. I've purchased about 4 di Oro products and have been impressed with their quality (and for the ones I've had a while, their longevity). Their kitchen products are well-made, and this turner spatula is no exception. Really good stuff.

I had my Garmin mounted with the adhesive circle on my dash, and after about two years it fell off on a hot day. I decided to go with a friction mount as a replacement because there wouldn't be any more problems.

I drive a Honda Civic, so there's not a ton of dash space -- pretty standard. This doesn't slide around and isn't so big that it's obnoxious. When I do need to renew the suction cup, it's much easier than the dash-mounted adhesive.

And with all AmazonBasics products I've ordered (iPhone cables, camera bags, etc.) this is well-made and at a great price. Highly recommend!

This really is a 5-star product -- it's a good price, it's high-quality and simple to use. The results are excellent for amateur to semi-professional product/tabletop studio photography.

I really liked the instructional/assembly videos and the tutorials from the company. They very much want us to succeed with their product. It's a great sign when a company doesn't strand you after you've opened the box.

Within 15 minutes of opening the box, I'd assembled the studio and had it ready to go on my desk. Amazing! I've taken ~30 product pictures with it so far and I'm very, very pleased.
