Great planner. Starts from June 28, 2015 and goes to July 2, 2016.

Each month starts with a monthly calendar, and then afterwards a spread of weekly calendars with lines for notes for that month. The paper is a little thin, but it isn't cheapy. The plastic (or plastic-like) tabs for the months will come in handy when needing to jump back or forward to a date.

The cover is sturdy, like plastic also, and has a seamed/finished/crimped edge (not sure how to describe it) to keep it from fraying.

My only issue is that the weekly calendar goes from Monday-Sunday. I would prefer a Sunday-Saturday version, but I suppose most calendars designed to be academic do it this way. It just isn't intuitive to start on a Monday. The monthly calendar, however, does show standard Sunday-Saturday on a row.

The front of the planner has a page of calendar years at a glance, from 2014-2016. At the back are a couple of pages where you can write down contacts, a page called "Event Calendar" for you to write down important events, and a holiday list showing the holidays with dates from 2015-2018.

The pages themselves are 8.5" x 11", so with the tabs and the spiral, it will be a bit wider than your average piece of paper.

This is a great autumn hoodie. Not too thick or bulky, and not too thin. Most importantly, the fleece is super soft and comfy, made of a 60/40 cotton/poly blend (I'm reviewing the granite heather color -- other colors may have different fabric composition).

The cut is pretty slim, especially in the sleeves, so you may want to order a size up if you plan to layer with a long sleeve shirt underneath.

I've washed it once and put it through the dryer with no problem. We'll see how it manages several washes. Haven't had much opportunity to wear it yet with summer weather continuing into October. Looking forward to it for morning work-outs, or lounging at home once the weather cools down. Will update this review once I've had more opportunity to break it in.

I really wanted to like this water bottle. Seems simple enough -- glass, no BPA and other gnarly plastic stuff, lead free. And bonus that it is borosilicate, the stuff the old-school Pyrex (that doesn't explode) was made of. Sadly, the bottle has been one problem after another. Gave it several chances, but sadly, it did not pass.

Upon unpackaging, unscrewed the lid and put finger inside bottle just to lift it. Good thing I did that. Noticed a rough surface at the inside top where it slopes into the neck. Scraped a little and found that small pieces of what I assume is borosilicate (?) stuck all round that surface. They came off when scraped, so that would have ended up being ingested. Gross. Are there some at the bottom? No idea. The opening is rather small (~1 1/8") so getting a brush in there is difficult and there is no way to really tell if it is clean.

Also upon opening, the "washer" or O-ring seal fell out from the lid. Took the back of a fork and pushed it back in -- that seemed to fit it in snugly, for now. This part of the story continues below.

Washed the bottle as best as I could, and let everything air out for a couple of days. Then excitedly filled it up with regular room temp water to take it for a spin. After about an hour, unscrewed the lid to take a swig. YUCK. A very strong chemical smell (kind of like epoxy or along those lines) came from the bottle. UNdrinkable.

Wondered if the O-ring was the smelly culprit. Nothing on the bottle smelled after the initial wash and airing out so started with this as process of elimination. Had to use a toothpick to pry it from the lid. No biggie, but then realized that that was a good place for mold to grow if not removed for every wash.

Washed bottle again, and refilled with room temp water. Screwed on lid without the O-ring and let sit for an hour. When going to take a drink, was pleasantly surprised the odor was gone. Left bottle overnight and the next day, unscrewed to take a whiff, and detected the chemical smell again. Not as strongly as with the O-ring, but still did not make me want to drink that water. (On the plus side, even without the O-ring, the cover seemed to seal the bottle well and not cause leaking even when shook or held upside down for a short time.)

Wondered if the smell is the silicone sleeve, but it doesn't smell at all. The odor only happens when the bottle has been sealed for a while, and is opened. Is it the lid itself? The way the metal was adhered to the plastic lining? Possibly. But that renders this product useless. And what is THAT plastic made of?

The small shards loose inside and noxious odors emanating from it alone are enough to say stay away from this bottle. But even if those weren't factors, the bottle would get 3 stars. Unfortunate. I guess public drinking fountains aren't so bad after all.

Lovely ring. Very classic, strong look. Best of all, it is comfort fit so no cutting feeling on your finger, and easy to put on and take off. The titanium silver-colored ridge isn't as white as in the product photo -- it is a little more "tinted" in person, as most titanium is, which I don't mind at all.

Comfortable and beautiful.

These little snacks are like mini skinny Pop Tarts. You get two crisps to a pack, 8 to a box. The snack is very crispy, like a cracker, with a thin layer of apple cinnamon filling in the middle. Maybe I was expecting a Pop Tart or a McDonald's apple pie, or maybe even a Fig Newton. I found none of the above. I'm a pretty texture-conscious snacker, and I found that the cookie portion of this snack was too crispy to match with the too-thin/too-sticky filling inside.

Taste-wise, it's fine. It's just the texture combination that I didn't like. Maybe it was the only way 100 calories could fit into each pack (it's great that each crisp is only 50 calories), but I'd rather have a couple of fig newtons to feed my snack-time hunger.

This pen gets 3 stars from lefties (like me) and 5 from a right-handed person (my husband). Therefore, averaged to 4 stars. It has good ink flow, nice feel holding it with the full-barrel grip, but it just doesn't offer a "smooth" write for the left-hander. You know that foley sound made in TV shows and movies when someone is frantically scribbling something on a piece of paper? That's the sound it makes when I write with it. My theory: The same problem doesn't exist for right-handers because they pull the pen along a line of writing, while lefties are pushing it -- if that makes sense. (I still don't quite understand this since the pen is inherently ambidextrous since it's all symmetrical and the ball is round...) I tried writing with my right hand, and yes, it was useless scribbles, but the pen did feel much smoother and the ink flow more even. I guess I can always try the Maped Visio Left-Handed Ball-Point Pen, 2 Pack, Black and Blue (224327) O_o

I'm a big fan of Kipling bags -- the Lancelot is the latest I've added to my collection. It's main purpose for me is to hold my Motorola Xoom and also function as a purse. I love it because it's compact, and the separate zippered pocket in the bag is roomy enough to hold my Xoom with space to spare. I've actually toted my Xoom and an iPad 1 at the same time with no problem.

All my regular purse contents are in the front zippered area, which has tons of pockets inside to help you keep your things organized.

This bag has a wider strap than other Kipling bags I have. At 1 1/2", it doesn't cut into my shoulder even with two tablets weighing it down. With the strap at its shortest, it feels snug over my shoulder and doesn't bounce around my side when walking. With the strap extended to be a cross-body bag, it also feels comfortable while walking.

The best part about it is that it's not a giant laptop bag and is much more stylish and functional than one. Even when you stuff it full, it looks compact and neat and everything is easy to access.

And, its water resistance and secure zippers along with the fastened flap give you peace of mind that everything is secure.

Side note: If you're looking at the dark blue one, you should know that there is a version of it without the contrast stitching, which you can find here if you search for "Kipling Lancelot" because it's not available from this particular link (as of the time I am writing this review).

I am an AFOL (adult fan of LEGO) who collects their limited-edition minifigures and this was my first minifigure book. I LOVE IT!! Not only does it include an exclusive toy soldier minifig (see lower right of book cover), but it is like nerd heaven on every page! You find out the character traits and more of every minifigure from series 1-10, but what I love the most are the little factoids included. Some historical, some design-based. For instance, did you know the mime from Series 2 (LEGO Minifigures Series 2 MIME was the first minifig to be completely black and white? (That was one of my first minifigs so I have a soft spot for the little guy.) This is a must-have for every minifigure collector, no matter what age. I find myself re-examining pages over and over because it is so fun to look at. There is a whole series of these books, if you are new to them. A great gift for the LEGO lover on your gift list!

Fun cat tree with lots of levels which is great for multiple cats!

The tree is delivered in pieces, but assembly isn't too difficult if you have a second person and some patience. The included black-and-white instructions, while helpful, are not super easy to understand. I had to check online photos to see the suggested assembly color-wise. And the included screws were not well-labeled so it was a bit of a guessing game to pick the right one for the right spot. Nothing too complicated.

Also included is an Allen key to tighten (or loosen if mis-assembled) parts.

Material-wise, this is the "newer class" of cat trees which uses a thin, micro-plush material rather than the old-school carpet. The sisal rope on the columns is a nice touch. The round "beds" are soft and cushy, though the cushion part is not removable.

At about 59" tall, it is a little shorter than my cats like, but it is a good-sized tree. Make sure you check the measurements for where you'd like to put it. It is sort of a corner piece, but the round "beds" won't let it sit flush in a corner. The bottom edges will be about 3-4" from the wall.

This was my first Kubros figure -- and as a Trekkie (not quite a bonafide Trekker, I must admit), it was the perfect one to delve into.

It is the perfect gift for your favorite Trek fan. Not only is the 8-bit look retro cool, the whole product from start to finish is fantastic. First off, the PACKAGING ROCKS. The box is highly collectible, with one side panel a photo of Leonard Nimoy as Spock, but every step of opening it is a designer's delight. The top opens kind of like a snack box, with a pull-away strip that exposes a tab so you can close the box. Open the flaps and the side flaps are Mega Bloks Spock's eyes/face in glossy print. A delightful detail! The inner flaps and entire inner box is printed with all the various Kubros figures as line art. AND, each plastic bag inside containing the bricks and pieces are all printed with the same art. Love it.

Now, for the figure itself. With 133 pieces, and it standing 5" tops, this is a fairly quick build, with a couple of exceptions. Following the instructions, you build the head first, then the body, then legs and arms/hands. My biggest qualm is building the head, early on in the instructions. There is a point in Step 2 of building the head where the only connection point of two constructed parts is a single 1x1 flat segment. This makes building onto what you have so far very difficult as the connection keeps disconnecting, causing parts to fly. (Pro tip: look for the neck piece and go ahead and snap that in -- it will stabilize as you build.) Other than that, building is easy to follow and quick.

Finished, he looks fantastic. Though the arms are poseable at the shoulders, this construct isn't meant for much play. Pose-and-go is more the thing. Moving the arms too much will make them fall apart. The head can also turn, so you can get the Vulcan sign higher up if you'd like.

Overall, a great collectible Kubros to celebrate Star Trek's 50th anniversary! Very pleased with the entire presentation.

"A Pearl in the Storm" begins as a book about a woman who decides to row solo across the Atlantic. Tori Murden Mcclure starts out with an ego so seemingly inflated that she may have been better-suited ballooning across the ocean. However, her arrogance comes head-to-head with the sheer strength of Mother Nature herself, and thus ensues a gripping adventure of a woman battling not only the sea, but her own humanity.

I didn't like this book in the beginning. Mcclure came off as too arrogant and confident to make me want to read much further. It's hard to root for someone who is already so full of themselves that there is no room to feel any sincerity for them. But as the story progresses and Mcclure faces life-and-death challenges on her sea-faring journey, the book got harder and harder to put down.

She breaks away throughout the book into interludes about her past. Stories about her childhood, her college education... although these vignettes were insightful and informative, I felt that they were a little too long. They distracted me from the main story, as if to dilute the rawness of her experiences on the Atlantic. Despite these disruptions, I now appreciate the candidness of Mcclure's descriptions about her feelings and the events of her journey. The significance of her personal transformation would not have resonated sans the egotistical tone that saturated the early chapters of the book.

If you're looking to merely read about a daring outdoor adventure, this book probably isn't the right book for you. There's so much more to it. I cracked open "A Pearl in the Storm" not expecting much, but was rewarded in the end. There's extreme adventure, a little humor, and a sprinkling of romance all rolled into one.

The Riddler Chase is an excellent LEGO set for all ages (as are all LEGO, for that matter).

This set is fantastic because it is not only mid-range in price, but it comes with TWO vehicles, and THREE minifigs! A great value. This is the first set with The Flash, which in itself makes it worth the price. If you check resellers for just that minifig, you will soon realize that getting this set is a much better purchase.

I am not a huge fan of the Riddler's hot rod, because the front half is rather plain even with the Riddler decal, but Batman's ride is awesome! And it shoots little missiles!

The orange-tinted driver canopy is awesome, and Batman fits nicely inside, even with his cape.

Just be a little wary of loose pieces, aka, the cash in the back of the Riddler's car. They will fall out easily and get lost. Only a problem if you have little ones (human or furry ones) that may find them for snacking. They are 2x1 tiles, so I'd say your bare feet will be relatively safe.

Highly recommend.

p.s. If you decide to hold out on this one and are a fan of The Flash, there is another set slated to come out next year (2015) with several minifigures including The Flash, and Gorilla Grodd! AND, Wonder Woman's invisible plane. It will cost more, but sounds like it will be cool if you want to wait.

Remembering Smell is one of those books that sheds light on something you'd probably never think about -- something you take for granted every day -- your sense of smell.

A fascinating read about an unusual medical condition and how Bonnie Blodgett, a professional garden writer, succumbed to the depths of depression before empowering herself with science and strength to tackle her (thankfully temporary) condition. Blodgett artfully demonstrates how the loss of a basic sense affects a person and how something so often taken for granted can affect one's ability to simply be.

A very unique book that crosses memoir/science/psychology lines artfully and entertainingly.

Should you decide to skip on this title, at least take heed: STAY AWAY FROM ZICAM! That is what caused Blodgett and many others to lose their sense of smell. Lots of information on the 'net about it.

I consider myself a "point-and-shoot graduate" in that although I still keep my trusty little camera around for capturing everyday happenings, I'd like to get to know more about DSLRs and actually use the one I have access to effectively.

This book, "The DSLR Field Guide" is a great bridge from point-and-shoot to DSLR. Michael Freeman explains the camera by parts -- sensor types, how image processors work, lenses, etc. -- and explains how those parts work with a DSLR. Then you learn about camera menus, image resolution, and more. I appreciate that he writes the book in general terms so whether you have a Nikon, Canon or whatever, his descriptions can apply to your brand of camera.

The book is divided into two main sections:
1. The Digital Environment which covers what I mentioned above, and;
2. Image editing -- details about common lighting scenarios, monitor color calibration, downloading and processing raw photos, basic photo adjustments, etc.

Overall a very comprehensive book capturing more than enough details for what you need to advance your photography into the DSLR world. Definitely not something you'd buy for your professional photographer friend, but the perfect gift for your shutterbug friend who wants to dive into more advanced photography. If you're still a point-and-shoot loyalist, this is still a great title to get a good foundation of basic digital photography knowhow. The whole section on image editing is filled with useful info.

The compact size of the book is also a plus. At ~4.5"x6.0"x0.75", it can easily fit into a large camera bag or a purse. It's not really an on-scene reference guide because it doesn't lend itself to quick lookups (which I don't think was the point of the book anyway), but it's nice to keep near the camera especially when you're exploring DSLRs for the first time.

So Lego has been releasing series of limited-edition collectible minifigures every few months for a few years now. They are currently (as of Jan 2013) on series 9. This guy, the mime, is from series 2, so the only way you can get it is from resellers.

He is one of my favorites of the entire collection thus far. The black-and-white theme is ingenious, and the three different heads make for a unique presentation.

As always, fantastic Lego quality.

For the newbies, he is a standard Lego minifigure, so the parts are all interchangeable with other minifigure parts.

I did a ton of research before deciding on the BlueAir. You'll find that the Blueair, although maybe making a bigger dent in your pocketbook than other big-name air cleaners, is your best bet for a quiet room with clean air. I've tried many other brands who claimed to be "whisper-quiet" and the like, and so far, only the Blueair has lived up to its claim.

If you put it on the HEPAsilent mode, you'll have to look twice to even see if it's on. And that's not an exaggeration! Even in this mode, you can see particles going into the intake, so it's still effectively cleaning the room. It also takes very little electricity, so it's no strain on your utility bill to leave it on all the time to maximize room air quality.

The unit is rather large, as other reviewers have mentioned, but once you get it against a wall, or under a console table, you're good to go. The only other potential issue you may have is the blue LED which tells you the unit is on. I'm a light sleeper (hence requiring a very quiet air cleaner) and the LED was so bright that I had to cover it so I could sleep. A very minor issue which will only bother the most sensitive sleeper.

The filters are very easy to change, and are also conveniently available on Amazon! They require a switch-out every 6 months, in addition to a quick vacuum of the ionizing brushes inside the machine. If you deal with odors, then try the SmokeStop filter. It's quite a bit more expensive, but it works wonders. My neighborhood had a methane gas leak, and the SmokeStop filter took all the odor and toxins out of the air. The room with the BlueAir was the only "safe" room I could be in. So I'm sure it handles cigarette smoke with ease.

You won't go wrong if you invest in one of these. Oh, and a sidenote, I have 2 cats, and a cat allergy (as well as a myriad of other allergies), and the Blueair allows me to keep my kitties close, and get a good night's sleep!

As a woman who prefers to wear men's watches because their faces are just bigger and easier to read, I was happy to see this Timex watch with actual numbers that were more than 6-point font size. It is also has a very classic look which is great for going with many different outfits.

Upon receipt of the watch, I was very disappointed that the battery was dead. I thought Timex was supposed to keep on ticking?! Maybe it didn't get a licking... ;)

So, had the battery replaced, and was very pleasantly surprised to find that it has an Indiglo light! I guess I didn't expect that from a watch that looks "old-school" but it indeed has the light. Super handy in the movie theater when you don't want to get blinded by your cell phone to check the time and annoy fellow theater goers.

BUT. The thing that made it lose 2 stars -- it TICKS SO LOUD. Even when I'm driving in trafic, I can hear it ticking away. That's the last sound I want to hear when stuck in traffic. I have found myself getting distracted in other situations too. It is like a dripping faucet. AAGGHH!!

Overall, it is a very nice watch. The leather band is nice and there is a good stretch of holes along it for wrists of every size.

Just... TICK TICK TICK TICK TICK...

Was skeptical about this keyboard because I am pretty picky about the tactile response of keyboards in general. However, I was pleasantly surprised! This keyboard feels great. The keys aren't very loud and have soft typing action, but they feel good, like you know you are pressing a key. It can be equated to the feel of the newer Apple keyboards. As a piece of hardware, it's lightweight, yet sturdy.

Although it's designed for iPads and iPhones because of the command/option/control keys that differ from a Windows keyboard, it can still be used by Android and WIndows products. It easily connected to a Motorola Xoom with no problems and worked like a charm. It has so far worked for me with the Xoom, an iPad2, and a MacBook Pro.

It requires 2 AAA batteries (included!) and has an on-off switch in the back so you won't drain batteries when it's not in use. (Thanks to gtcaz for pointing out my misID of battery size.)

To connect, switch on the keyboard's power, and a little blue LED will flash on the keyboard. Enable Bluetooth on your device, and scan for new Bluetooth devices. The keyboard will come up, and you may be asked to enter a numeric code on the keyboard and hit return. Voila! Connected! If you switch between devices, you have to do this each time, but it's very simple, so I don't find it to be a problem.

Also a plus is that it comes in Amazon's frustration-free packaging. I know that only counts for when you first get it, but it makes for a positive way to kick things off.

users.query: Best catnip toy? Yes! Durable? No! I introduced this to an older cat who in her entire life never responded to catnip... she loved this! However, my cats will tear into these and by the end of the day... shredded. $8 for less than 24 hours of play. I wish they were made more durable. They make my cats so crazy!

cands.text: Best catnip toy? Yes! Durable? No! I introduced this to an older cat who in her entire life never responded to catnip... she loved this! However, my cats will tear into these and by the end of the day... shredded. $8 for less than 24 hours of play. I wish they were made more durable. They make my cats so crazy!

My cats love these, but they don't last long. I wish the material was stronger, because they shred these to bits in less than 24 hours! Not made tough enough for my cats! I even introduced one of these to a cat who never in her entire 14 years would go near catnip and she loved it! Now that is a true two paws up for this product!

Cheapest, best cat toys ever! I have several cats that love these and one cat that adores these! Probably the cheapest cat toys you'll find that they can't get enough of w/o catnip! The last pack I got, one of them was missing a bell, but I tossed it to my cat and he went after it anyway. They get lost easily, but my cats have a blast... at 3 a.m. usually. They can pick them up with their teeth due to the slats and it's looks pretty darn funny.

My cats love these! One in particular is quite fond of this type of scratcher, either for scratcher or simply sleeping in the "wave" or draped over the "wave" or any other weird position cats can get into. The toy is never touched, or if it is, not when I'm around. My old one was well used and well loved to the point I finally had to toss it. This is the replacement. It also looks great in your house/apartment/studio and it's not too large and is stylish.

Cat approved. Several cats in my life have loved these mice. I have tried others, but these are the ones they like. They'be been tossed high in the air (by the cat), batted, dunked in water bowls, tails torn off, and hidden underneath furniture for months. Simple, cheap cat toy that last and make my cats very happy!

Very small, and I bought them because I thought they glowed in the dark (another customer commented that they do not). When I first read the description in 11/14, I was sure it said they did, but perhaps I misread. Catnip isn't very potent, although my cats will sometimes be "attracted" to them and have a short catnip fit and then ignore them. They never actually play with them - I'm a night owl.

My large version of this box cracked w/in a month. Since it was still more or less functioning, I put off buying a new one until the only thing left was the jumbo. I'm actually glad! While I use more litter, my cats are happier! I have two males, about 13 lbs each, so not small boys. The large box they would sometimes poop outside through the swinging door, but not with this jumbo box! The largest of the two cats, who is built like a line backer, but it's probably an optical illusion as he is all fur, fits in there with ease and I no longer see little faces or bums smushed up against the door. They just disappear. It has also cut down on tracking litter and smell. Would purchase again!

I have tried liners, several kinds, but no longer recommend liners for this box. Even double bagged they shred both in 24 hours and you use three times more litter, because the bags create air pockets. Then once the holes start, all your litter gets trapped underneath and is completely wasted. I wasted a lot of money on liners and litter trying this out.

While they look nice and wash great, my cats ran away when I removed them from the box and are scared of them. It's been three weeks now and except for peeing on one, no doubt to show their displeasure, they haven't set paw in them. I've put worn shirts in them so my scent would be on them to no avail. I've placed them in the beds and they fight me, meow, and run away.

UPDATE: After 6 weeks the cats finally started sleeping in the beds and now love them. They still occasionally pee in them, they're cats, they do odd things we can't explain, but the beds wash and dry wonderfully. The one bed did develop a small hole and like many other reviews all I see is regular stuffing, no actual "thermal" stuff. I don't really care for the price and they're happy, but if they are in fact just plain stuffing, why false advertising?

Cats love it! Two paws up from - most - of my cats. Hey, cats are picky, not every cat will love it, but the majority of mine do. I have a ginger (like in the picture) who adores it, he sits on it constantly, curls up in it and sleeps. It gets used a lot. I have others who rarely touch it, but they do on occasion. I don't have any who "hate" it. You just have to figure out if you have a cat who prefers tall, vertical stretching/scratching or lower, horizontal scratching. So they mostly scratch furniture, this will probably work, do they like to really climb? You might want a taller one. Either way, I like the fun and funky design of this one and for some reason, several of them like to curl up on the "wave" and just sleep. It's made very well, it came a little lose, but I just turned the pole and it tightened right up. Yes, it comes just as you see it, no putting it together! My cats prefer this material over carpet and they tend to ingest cardboard.

This is my 2nd cat DVD, the last one (a different company) I have 4 starts to and 6 out of 8 gave it only one paw up... this "mewvie" gets four paws up! It's really more like 6 1/2 cats, as one is pretending not to like it, but I do catch him watching it, although not yet fully addicted like the other six. As I type this, one of them is staring at a blank TV screen right now, hoping I'll turn it on. As soon as they hear the TV come on, they come running. They paw it, bat it, bite it, look behind it, beside it, on top of it and everywhere else to see where that pesky squirrel could have gone, that bird flew to, or the chinchilla jumped to. They look at me with incredibly sad little faces when I turn it off, even if none of them are actually watching it! Watching them watch it is hysterical and makes me wonder about my sanity and the lack of having an actual life. If you read my review on the other DVD I bought for cats, you'll know why I start this TV for cat obsession in the first place, but I don't feel like repeating the entire long story here, suffice to say, the cat we intended it for, shows very little interest, but he is the one that I have caught watching it on the sly. Maybe I'll get him yet. Long story short, it's to try and keep him entertained more inside, so he'll stop attempting to get outside.

Pros: Cats LOVE it. I have 6 little TV junkies now! The video loops over and over from bird to animal and back again. You can select where you want to start the video, on a bird, on an animal, your choice. NO FISH! The other video had fish and they yawned at the prospect of the fish and it had way too much of the fish. Thank you for NO FISH!

Cons: The background noise is birds, always birds, there may be crickets on the screen or mice, but you still hear birds. Maybe this is to attract the cats to the TV, I have no idea, but I can mute it and they still like it. The bird sounds seem to be repetitive and get annoying after awhile and I love birds. However, the same ole same ole over and over and over... yeah, not so much.

I've tried three cat videos so far, Happy Cat TV, this one and Mewvie Episode 2. I thought they would prefer Episode 2, because in my Happy Cat TV they loved the birds. Mewvie Episode 2 is all birds. The birds however are not very "active", they don't fly around enough as in the Happy Cat TV. I cannot return it as it's opened, so I may try and see if they will get interested in it yet, but so far the second one just hasn't been as interesting to them. If you can't decide which one to buy from this collection, I recommend Mewvie Episode 1 (this one) over Mewvie Episode 2.

This carrier is great! I got it for a long trip and am currently trying to associate the carrier with good things and not bad things (aka no vets!) and taking my cat for car rides in it and back home and he's starting to settle down and get used to it. He's a larger cat, Siamese Cross/Ragdoll and he fits in it comfortably. I love the front entrance, the door is very secure! My old carrier the door fell off when I first got him and he got loose and thankfully I caught him, but wow did that  scare me! This door, I make sure is secure before picking up, but the top and bottom plastic really does keep it from falling forward! I didn't think the door swinging both ways would matter, but I had it up against a couch and that came in handy. I didn't have to turn it around to open the door, one way it would bounce shut, the other way it would simply lie flat against the couch, genius! The top entry is purr-fection! No more hassle fighting with a cat who doesn't want to get in a carrier (although he's getting used it it now), just plop them feet first down in and hold them in while putting the lid down and secure it! I "think" they appreciate the fact they can see out, but it's tinted, so sunlight, etc. isn't blaring in their eyes. The ventilation is nice for trips, plenty of it and a small, rectangular cat bed fits in the bottom nicely for comfort. My cat can stand up and turn around, stretch out some and seems comfortable. He's complaining less and less. I keep it on the floor with the front door completely off when not "in use" as a little house, although he's not having any part of it, the rest of the cats think it's great! Very well made, very secure side clips, unlike a lot of plastic carriers where you fight with those plastic clips, this is a top of the line plastic carrier and well worth the money! Handle is comfortable to grip too, but because of the width it's a little awkward, but find a carrier that isn't. There are clips in the front and back if you can find a strap (not included) to put through there as a shoulder strap. Area in the top for seat belt that secures it very nicely. If you're going to be carrying it for long periods, you might want to consider padding the handle a bit, as it has grooves. Highly recommend!

I really like this litter box and so do my cats. The rounded edges make it easy to clean. I don't think that charcoal thingy at the top does anything, honestly, but it keeps there from being a hole in the top, so I leave it. My only complaint, less than 30 days of owning it, the bottom cracked and became warped. I'm trying to figure out who to contact to get a replacement while I'm still using the cracked bottom. It's on the side and up far enough that it's not causing a major problem, but one month? Warped on the bottom? Do yourself a favor and buy a nice, big, metal scooper. The plastic one is useless.

First, product quality. Cheap plastic. It took me quite awhile to get the top "locked" into place, because everything was crooked. The plastic was cheap and flimsy. Once it was in place, albeit crooked, it did work. I filled it with Precious Cat litter to start (when I ran out I switched to Tidy Cat Instant Action and both worked great) and waited for my cat to use it. I didn't have a large area to roll it, so I had to roll, drag, and complete the roll onto it's top and then roll back. The clumps all went in the little scoop as promised. Perfect! This worked quite well for the first few two weeks (as well as the Cat Genie to put them in) and then the scoop started to not only fill with clumps, but whatever space was left, with litter. A lot of litter got wasted, because there was no way I was going to try and "filter" it. I bought so I wouldn't have to scoop it like a regular cat box and touch anything, hence I also bought the Cat Genie!  I never had a problem with the inside/walls getting dirty, but I only had one cat and he tended to go in the same spot and I cleaned it daily and never let it go more than two days. After a few weeks I did notice small clumps of waste in the litter itself that would go into the sifter and then come back out, at this point it was probably time to dump the litter and put in fresh entirely, but as I was away from home on business for two months, this wasn't really an option for me. I was lucky to find a place I could even take/keep my cat! There was absolutely no lingering smell (except directly after his highness would have a blowout) from the litter box, even if I let it go 48 hours. Beware, they will kick litter out of that open door everywhere! Keep a broom handy, you will need it. By the end of the two months I could see this litter box was wearing out and decided to just donate it to a local shelter than trying to ship it home. They can use it as it is, as a regular box, or simply recycle the plastic. If you need a quick, cheap solution for a few months, buy it, otherwise, don't expect to use it long term. Especially if you have a single cat that poops as much as mine does!

I have the Catit Jumbo Litter box and after trying the Jonny Cat liners and having to strain to get them to fit, trapped air, and other issues, I gave up. I saw these were larger and bought them. Wow! What a relief! They fit! I tape them all around so they are a tight fit, put in the kitty litter so it's a good two inches deep and no trapped air! I do have to use two bags (double bag), because cat claws will shred these suckers in less than 24 hours (as they will with anything 2 ml). Someone needs to make a jumbo that's about as tough as a spaceship and then maybe cat claws wouldn't shred them. While I hate losing all that litter down the huge hole, I now have a general idea of where the hole always is and plan to put duct tape over that area next time and see if that helps. Note to self, buy duct tape. My cats really like the larger box, as do I, it cuts down on smell (I have no idea why, but it does!) and accidents (pooping out the door), but finding a liner was a hassle! At least the hole generally does not go through to the second bag or only minuscule holes, and thus just "litter dust" has to be shaken out of the pan after I take the bags out, dump them in the trash, and replace them. Great for living in an apartment, cold winters, and my back! Worth the extra money than having to wash it out every 3 weeks. Maybe if I owned my own house, with a hose, etc., but I don't. Can't say it's "quick", because you have to tape the bags down, but at least they fit! Highly recommend for odd shaped, high backed, jumbo boxes, but double bag, because they will be shredded!

UPDATE: Shredded through two bags (double lined) in less than two weeks. So much for easy clean up. I give up on liners. Two stars because it actually fit the box.

I bought this to take on a SW fight after reading they are lenient. My cat is about a foot high and nearly 20" long (laying) and around 10 lbs. I got him in it and he could not move! His head to tail was touching the front/back of the carrier, his head had to be turned, he could not stand up, and was quite freaked out! He tried to immediately tear at the mesh and I got him out before damage could be done. How any cat can be comfortable in this carrier stuffed under a seat is beyond me. The carrier was bulging! He is a great traveler and fine with hard carriers, which are larger, but this is far too small and inhumane to put a cat in, then under a seat for a flight! Measure your cat!

Note: My cat is a Siamese/Ragdoll Mix, so he's not a small cat, wide girth and it fits perfectly!

I love it, cat's not too fond of it... yet. My late cat loved to go outside on a harness and leash. I used a dog harness on her, but they never quite fit right. When I saw an actual cat harness, I was thrilled! I'm taking my cat on a plane and I wanted him in a harness for better security. I wanted to get this good and early so I can get him used to it. I had hoped that like my late girl, he would take to it like a duck to water, but no such luck. He's about 10 pounds and is a stocky built cat and this fits great once I let the strap all the way out (quite a girth on my Siamese Cross - DLH). If he's not relaxed, it does go over the shoulder blades, but I've put my fingers under there and they are not pulling/cutting his body and he doesn't act uncomfortable, I just get a look of... "you have shamed me..." So, starts the harness + treats + small leash to try and accommodate him well in advance! Knock on wood, he has stopped rolling around trying to get it off - how he thinks that is going to work I'm not sure, but... I've never tried to understand a cat's logic!

Update: This is coming a bit late, but my cat wore this like a trooper through airport security w/leash and it did NOT set off the metal detector. He was fine in it for the entire trip (cross country), albeit happy to get out of it, of course, and not too happy about putting it back on for the trip home. I'm now relocating cross country and he will have to wear this again (poor guy) and I'm buying another one for my second kitty who is also moving with me, but I haven't told him yet he has to wear a harness. Uh oh.

Looks adorable over my door, but doesn't hold much! Don't put a lot of weight on kitties paws, either the cat will tilt or the item will just slip off. I have a bathrobe on each one and that was iffy at first until I balanced them just right. Still, wouldn't send it back, but wouldn't get it for hanging, say, jackets on.

I bought this for classes (college), because I wanted something that didn't look like everyone else's... and I'm a crazy cat lady. I've had no problems with it thus far and I've used it for several classes, although I do e-mail myself any work we do in class as a backup always. I love the look, it came in a cute little tin, which I can easily use to wrap up a small gift or gift card in the future. It was a decent price and it's a adorable! I love that there is a place to put the "paw" when you are using the thumb drive so you don't lose it. I have a very narrow area to fit flash drives on my computer and this isn't too thick, some novelty drives are too large. Really enjoy having something "different" than the standard, plain ole thumb drive!

After trying a stainless steel bowl that one of my cats loathed (he would take it apart at night and flood the floor), I decided, time for something new! 1. Something he can't take apart and 2. Something that mimics the sink faucet. I came across this, and while I prefer stainless steel, porcelain is better than plastic! My two cats love this (should that be eight paws up?)! They drink a lot more water now, in fact I have to top it off everyday and I fill it as full as you're allowed! The motor is quiet, I cannot hear it at all, unlike my last one, just the relaxing sound of mini waterfalls in my apartment. No sarcasm, it is relaxing, unless you really have to pee! Very easy to clean, again, unlike my last one, and I'm glad this one has a filter that goes around the motor. That helps a lot, I highly recommend you continue to buy and use those. Having had fountains without them, your motor will start to grow things that even you can't determine, get insanely clogged with fur, and be a nightmare to clean. No more! My only problem is that I have hard, well water (I rent so I have no control) to wash with, which leaves hard water stains and residue. I use purified water only for their drinking supply. Highly recommend for your pets health. I was surprised by how much more water they drink with this fountain! Worth the big bucks!

What can I say, a favorite as a child, a favorite as an adult. I had to have it on Blu-Ray when I saw the great reviews. Nature just pops! In my opinion, you can't outgrow Milo and Otis, any age can enjoy it if you love animals and nature. I have never believed all the hype that animals got hurt as it was never proven. I will continue to believe that and enjoy the movie as I always did.

I love Brian Froud... I have all his Lady Cottington books (aside from the smells one - it seemed a tad too gross for me) and I have his other Fairie books. I was excited when I saw this because it was Brian Froud and it had little pop-ups, doors, etc., hey, I'm a kid at heart! I like those kind of things! Based on several reviews it sounded wonderful. I bought it, I returned it. The pictures seemed to be a bit repeated from his previous work, the doors, pop-ups, etc. were mediocre compared to other books of it's kind (I like elaborate pop up books) and the story... snooze fest. It's done in riddles and rhyme with one fairy talking to another who are talking you and well, it just feels flat.  On top of that, Amazon said this was a "brand new" book, but it came with a remainder mark (black ink across the top or bottom of the pages which indicated it was either used or overstock from a bargain book warehouse) and it looked used. I exchanged it immediately w/o reading it and the second one came, I read it and realized it too had a remainder mark, but on the top, not the bottom and the black ink had bled onto the pages. If you are selling a brand new book, there shouldn't be any black lines on them, it's a dead giveaway you are being supplied by a whole seller/overstock company who gets slightly damaged books in general. I've bought from them before! Very disappointed in Amazon for the first time and with the book. I don't recommend, except maybe for a child and even then, eh. I gave it two stars for Brian Froud's art work, but 1 1/2 would have been better.

I was looking for an 8 GB thumb drive by a trusted name when I found this... 16 GB for the same price as the 2 GB I bought my mother?! Wow! Great deal, great drive, and no losing those pesky tops. Highly recommend!

Doo wop is still alive and well in the new millinium and these boys are the best. I had the pleasure of seeing them in their first USA promo and meet each and every one and they are wonderful, down to earth, sweet guys, who can really sing. They sang two songs acapella and my mum, who was with me, didn't even realize they did not have music. These guys have it all, talent, looks, and personality. This CD is packed full of old favorties, classic rock, and new songs by them. Gambling Man, their newest song is amazing. If you pick up this CD, be sure to check their video's out on YouTube. You won't be sorry you purchased this album.

Disc 1 is like the original album, which I also own.  1 major flaw is that "Love Is A Many Splendored Thing" cuts off at the very end of it!  I was upset by this, hence the 3 stars instead of 4.  Disc 2 is a lot of fun w/some remixes and sing-a-longs, all in all, I'm pretty happy with it being that I'm a HUGE Grease fan.  If you like Grease, you'll love this, it's fun.  Too bad when they "remastered" it, they didn't catch there 1 mistake.  Oh well, at least I have it on another album.

I purchased this several years ago and I just installed it to play again. Yes, it works on Windows 7. My only disappointment, they didn't release a sequel!

This game is wonderful. I am an adult player and this game really keeps my attention.

Pros:
1. Graphics are beautiful!
2. You can create your horse, although limited, still fun.
3. You can create yourself, also limited, but still fun.
4. Taking care of your horse does not take long if you do it after every training or tournament.
5. You train in 2 star, 3 star, and 4 star jumps, dressage, and cross country. Each one has slightly different scenery.
6. You compete in 4 locations, each in 2 star, 3 star, and 4 star with three events in each competition, dressage, cross country, and jumping.
7. The four locales are very different and different scenery.
8. The game gets increasingly more challenging and it's not easy to start off with!
9. 2 star locations have relatively short challenges, then 3 star gets longer, and 4 star takes about 3 - 4 minutes for dressage, up to 10 minutes for cross country, and 3 - 4 minutes for jumping. That's in REAL TIME.
10. You level up your horse on your own terms as you earn points, so it's up to you where to place you points on stamina, trust, speed, jumping, and agility. These are key to getting good times and winning. Eventually, by the time you finish 4 star events, you can max your horse out to 100. That doesn't mean you'll still get a perfect score or make every jump though. If you come into a jump to fast or at a weird angle, the horse still may refuse you.
11. You can play back video of your rides.

Cons:
1. There isn't even more to this game!
2. The dressage can get really boring after the first few times and w/the sounds it makes and the constant beat, I usually get quite sleepy doing dressage which is done simply by pressing the correct arrow key at the correct time, however, you can watch the horse do actual movements which are extremely realistic.

If you're wondering how the horse is controlled, you use the W and S key to go fast/slow and the A and D key to move side to side. Spacebar jumps and the Shift key makes the horse gallop. Arrow keys are used only for dressage.

If you can find this game for a decent price (don't spend $100 like some people want), buy it! You will NOT regret it, but it may spoil you for other horse games, I know it did me!

I may try and edit my review later and add a video.

users.query: Aspects of the film show skill and craft, but the cultural insanity of the KSA reality versus the surreal dream sequences was an un-compelling mix for me. I did not care about a single character and am not curious how it ended. Probably cute for someone who has worked in Saudi as a Westerner.

cands.text: It's very, very good. But not perfect, certainly. And not brilliantly paced. The last episode could have been a half hour longer to wrap up the story more smoothly. It winds up a little quickly for my tastes and doesn't give you a lot of development time for tension. Characters do things for inexplicable reasons. Bad guys are a little more clever and successful than any reason has been given. Enjoyable, but messy.
It seemed slow and to have very little story. To me, it played more like "the confessions of a paranoid drug addict". But I admit i wanted to see how they would end it.

Nothing especially wrong with the story...it's a frame-up in a style most modern film viewers could enjoy, but it's so over-the-top with melodrama and see-it-coming scene pacing that what could have been a whiz-bang of a drama ends up being a plod through a get-to-the-point sea of procedural scandal and hassle. If you don't want a rundown of the plot, you can stop reading here. The set-up involves Alan Ladd as an artist...a painter. Not shockingly, he plays a man of few words with a flat affect. He's shown as friendly with a particular set of kids (as portrayed in the film, it would be regarded with open suspicion in today's climate... and by the way none of the kids speaks clearly so you can't understand about 70% of what they say.) But he's a hard-working artist who happens to paint in every known style... and prolifically with what appears to be about 50-75 complete canvasses scattered about the house and barn. Immediately and very negatively, it is established that he is not liked in the community and that his nut-case secret-drunk wife is, conversely, very popular.
Yeah, so it's tough to watch a nasty drunk woman make a fool of herself and her husband, but when she turns up missing and is presumed, then confirmed murdered, you've got to go through the whole hick-town witch-hunt routine. The troop of kids he's buddy-buddy with that you can't understand, all help him to save his bacon. Worth watching if you have an Alan Ladd jones, and if you're looking for a good script to do a remake. As a form of entertainment, I'd say you can do better.

The cinematography/lighting are the real star of this picture. John Cusack did a very good job in this film, but I simply don't buy him as a 1940's character. The Chinese actors were all fantastic and the love interest chick is crazy beautiful and I liked her accent when spoke English. The script could have used some help. It's trying to be a kind of Casablanca type of deal. Which worked about as well as imitation chocolate. Worth watching if you like the era.

There's no question that the intention behind this piece was honorable and approached with the spirit of love for magic as an art form. However it falls short of telling an organized story or communicating a focused point of view. Beautifully photographed and with interesting magicians who are certainly qualified to comment on the skills being discussed, it fails to make clear connection for non-magicians about (most critically) the history of magic tricks *with examples and clear explanations*. I emphasize I was not expecting a bunch of trick reveals. I was expecting a beginning, middle, end structure that left me with a feeling I'd learned something. I never got it. A great deal is alluded to or implied. I wished I could go back and re-edit the whole movie so that I personally could understand what I was supposed to take away. It seemed a long argument on the ineffable nature of magic performance and why it entertains. The good thing about it is that non-magicians can become familiar with a few important magicians they've not heard of and tantalizing glimpses of magic apparatus and 19th-century conjurers who still influence the art can be gleaned.

I bought this because Michael Kitchen is prominently promoted in it, but he's not in it near enough to justify using him to promote the film. To boot, it's a depressing and repetitive production with scene after scene of pleading, crying, and threatening. The characters are mostly stupid and irresponsible, which makes me not give a damn what happens to them. I wouldn't have paid good money for this had I realized how meatless of a role Kitchen's character is. His performance does not suffer. But the whole foolishness of the story is not worth viewing.

This second story has less direct interaction between the two main characters and suffers a little from that. But it contains all of the answers as to why Lisbeth is so fierce about not being victimized by anyone. The actress is dressed in a softened and more mature look than the first film. Great acting and character development.

For adults who are indifferent to trendy books and movies - I write this review to let you know this is a decent film. The violence is  intentional and serves the plot. The themes are akin to the anti-Totalitarian tales you read in high school with some Dungeons & Dragons/reality show connventions exploited to give the fight against opression a modern twist. Watchable, but not life-changingly powerful.

Deceptively cute, it seems like this little film wouldn't hurt a fly, but as a technical piece - it's ass-kicking. Part editing workshop, a master class in acting, and a scriptwriter's biggest challenge a lot of skill went into telling this story charmingly and tight. Each scene has to economically convey a funny AND poignant truth about relationships, incorporate all of the main characters, ( I had to watch it twice to realize his office friends are the other characters. Doh!) and find a creative and plausible way to make the scenario dissastisfying to the Elliot character. Fraser's performances are humorous and his characterization of the "dork" Elliot is terrifyingly real. The makeup and hair perfect each clever portrayal of the powerful, dumb, smart, sensitive roles he plays in trying to get "the girl" Costuming for Hurley was mad-crazy-good and she her Devilish attitude struck a surprisingly convincing note. The whole thing is funny and fun, but there is serious talent here.

Great movie based on a variety of true incidents and characters from WWII. I love the actors performances and the leads all gave great chemistry. Some points in the film are not clear at the end, but it doesn't matter all that much. Warning about Paul Verhoeven (the director) commentary track. He is not accurate on several political points he states as fact, which should handily offend every possible side a viewer could be on politically. Something for everybody, believe me.

Scarecrow & Mrs King had a fantastic First Season because the characters had places to grow, plus they had great dialogue. It's hard to keep that energy going, although it helps that the electricity between Kate Jackson and Bruce Boxleitner could power a Cuisinart. Once you "consummate" a screen romance with mutual I-love-yous, it's hard to stuff that genie back in the bottle...which is essentially how S3 ends. In Season 4, the cute dialogue comes back stronger and the writers find a way of extending the romantic tension between Lee and Amanda - by giving them a new secret. Sadly, as Kate Jackson had to take care of some medical challenges in real life, the show producers either for contractual reasons, or another, chose to stick to schedule and write around Ms. Jackson's absence by giving her single scenes - and eliminating the Amanda character in almost any of the plot. Her absence quickly reveals how critical Kate's energy is to making the show compelling.

There is very little story or depth of character to this brief dramatic interlude. For a long time, people have been falling in love and getting themselves into emotional entanglements. So the audience should understand pretty intuitively and without a lot of played-up revelatations what's going on in this on-the-rocks romance. Yet, the film takes 90 minutes to drag out a conceptually simple farewell scene. Sure, Montgomery Clift looks great and the key lighting on everyone's eyes ratchets up the intensity. But this movie pales in comparison to gems such as Place in the Sun, or I Confess. The latter of which is a don't-miss, this one not so much. Any appearance of great actors in old movies is worth watching for fans of the genre, but I would not hold this up as the epitome of the art form.

Gorgeous lighting, vintage cars, unusual locations and fun WWII research - not to mention the exciting performance of Michael Kitchen as Foyle make this a must for Brit Dectective fans. Some of the secondary characters don't excite me, but then there are some great secondary characters later. There ARE subtitles! Not sure why someone wrote there are none. You need them occasionally to pick up muffled ddialog. Love owning DVDs so I can have extras and watch anytime no wifi.

Hardly a light-hearted film, this takes a sober look at one woman's choice to share her life with an alcoholic. The consequences of his drinking exact prices small and large for the family, yet - she still has a life of her own as do her children. I personally enjoyed it and did not find it depressing, even though the scenes are not always pleasant. Perhaps there is a message in the film about choosing what to focus on and remember in life.

This is not a lighthearted movie. It's akin to watching a quick revolution in a marriage rather than a "once upon a time" tale. The action is uneven with the first 20 minutes being too slow, and the last 5 minutes being a quickie resolution like a Disney sitcom wrap-up. I am willing to declare the idea of this film "brilliant", but it cannot be "classic" with this pacing, I'm sorry. Also, please know that I am *crazy* about George Sanders, and I would pay to watch a movie of him brushing his teeth...but I cannot claim this is an endearing role. The role and the lighting in this film are unromantic, though. The instant-watch version here on A-zon is a terrible print with apalling audio. For further investigation if you liked, or disliked this film, but want a great story about a married couple that is a helpful comparison to this film and maybe a bit more "accessible", I heartily recommend The Painted Veil. For the benefit of those who want to watch the tatty online version, there is a section where a hand-written letter is being read but the dirty scratched print and missing footage renders this nearly impossible to comprehend. HERE IS WHAT IT SAYS: (stop to avoid mild spoiler) "I'm going to Capri to have a little fun, as you said. Museums bore me! You'll have more time for your pilgrimages this way."

This film is how films should be made. ..but this isn't made as perfectly as it could have been. Mel Gibson is an underrated actor, except in this film where he's phoning it in...or being given too soft of a time by the powers over the film. Loved having Lucy Liu in it. Slightly silly. But enjoyable silly.

I watched this series as a young teenager with my mom and we both really escaped into it. It's actually an interesting experience to see what I loved as a kid and realize the quality was really there. There are very small details in dialog in Season 1 that get unexpectedly added by the characters - perhaps even are ad-libbed by the actors themselves. Very quick rejoinders that you don't expect enhance the dimension of the characters and the humor. The pacing of the romantic tension between the lead characters is excellent in season 1, given the fact that you'd never know whether or not you were going to be renewed when you start shooting. (Nowadays, you don't even know you're renewed after finishing the season...) SC&MRS.K still holds up very well. Costuming has a few small "whoa is THAT out of fashion" moments, but otherwise all elements, including the editing look current enough to avoid distraction a generation past it's shelf life. Fun show!

Plot summary: Story within a story. Author writes about a jumped up country girl who wants the glamourous life and an ambitious husband. Is criticized for his portrayal of such a girl by his contempories for bringing France into disrepute. Excellent production! Leans a little bit feminine, but also highlights the challenges of men meeting expectations. Gorgeous lighting, costuming, and convincingly acted. Interesting to see Louie Jordan as a puppy and Harry Morgan with hair. SPECIAL FEATURES: Cartoon- 'Out-Foxed' featuring Droopy (fox is voiced in a send-up of Mason); a mildly humorous satire called "The Good Old Days" where the hassle of yesteryear is played up over the romance; subtitles in English or Portuguese.

I was a late-to-the-party Star Wars fan as a kid. Jaws was hugely hyped and it wasn't amazing, so I ignored this film for months and then fell hard. But I was a Han Solo girl, not interested in some Princess, although I enjoyed her performance just fine. But then as I got older, and lived not terribly far from the Princess General, I realized how much more interesting I found her. I have been surprised how much I miss her voice. As for this book, I am glad she told of her Big Secret Romance with her co-star and that it wasn't a classless bodice-ripper re-telling of this circumstance. It's extremely contemporary to this past 24 months for a work that looks back 40-odd years. A must for any female fans who saw the film first-run.

It's not a big-budget film, but it's got a lot to offer content-wise. Kinda-sorta it's romantic comedy, but Carolla's artistic style seems to emphasize the process of achievement as an underdog, such that the "coming out a winner" is the "getting the girl" rather than actual winning the heart of a woman. This style element didn't harm my ability to enjoy the film since the romance is symbolic more than a driver of plot. Carolla is rightly celebrated for his rags-to-riches fame in his personal life, so it suits him to make stories surrounding the kinds of trials that have carried him to the success everyone wants. As a native of the area where this film is shot, I appreciated the Hollywood/Glendale locations. It established an important feel to the film, and cements Carolla's brand. The Oswoldo character is of tremendous value comedically, and functions not unlike Pedro in Napoleon Dynamite. However, his overly thick accent may frustrate some viewers. It's intentional, of course, to have Oswoldo barely able to communicate in English à la Manuel in Fawlty Towers. Since there was likely no budget for dialogue replacement, the ideal level of unintelligibility may not have been achieved. Watch Road Hard if you enjoyed this. Familiar themes for Carolla fans and just the thing to watch on a plane.

These have a slimming effect and look dressy for jobs or travel that requires boots, but could use a little class. If you know you have a particularly thick foot, you may not be able to get away with the fit of these. Plenty of room in the ankle.

In my opinion, these are not worth having unless you want them for a serving spoon at a party or to amuse kids who won't care about the quality. I bought one of these for $8 and change. It came packed really well and with a nice card it was mounted on. The finish was beautiful and the guy I gave it to was stunned at how cool it was. I didn't find out until too late these were coming from China. They have taken several weeks. Are a knock-off of what I bought, not the same thing. They are scratched on the plating upon arrival and badly turned at the edges. don't even waste your time. Get the original. I'm just going to sell these at a garage sale or give them away to someone I don't care for. Not even worth returning it.

This is an adequate value, but it's not as amazing as some of the reviewers are saying. The visual effect is DEFINITELY worth the price. But up close, you're better off shopping for vintage and getting your money's worth. Positives that people have not mentioned in other reviews: it comes with a weird keychain/clip in a metal color which matches the metal on the purse. I believe it is also a bottle opener. Not something I usually need for a night out...YMMV. It comes in a plastic pouch to protect the product in shipping, which you can use to store it. AND it comes with a sateen bag which you can use to pack it when you travel to a special event. VERY helpful.
It is not especially durable seeming. But I love the thoughtful detail of the beads on the bottom to kind of keep dirt off or the lightest splash of water from soaking through the bottom immediately. I would have shopped for a lower price myself. I'd expect to pay $18 - $25 for it. Not $30. Not mad about it. Still a pretty purse that I'll get plenty of use out of.

It's interesting to read all of the wide-ranging experiences with this product! I have a biggish foot and consider my "real" size to be 10.5, but sizes vary from manufacturers so I tend to use a 10-11 range. My foot is not thick or boxy, like man feet. These fit a little loose for me in the wide size, but mostly loose in the heel. My foot is not especially wide, but a pointy toe box is not workable for my feet so I can see why people with actual wide feet would not find this wide enough since it fits me only very, very slightly roomy in the vamp. These have a European kind of casual look without swerving into hippy-wear. I wish I had bought the black ones when I had the chance. Anyone unhappy with your shoes in 10 C/D, return them so I can buy them! I bought Olive and even get compliments on them from men!

The fabric is fine. The color is good, there are no grommets and I do not believe the holes are very secure to hold the fabric. I believe it will tear and wear out quickly and does not hang beautifully like grommets do. It is WAY over priced without grommets. This item is worth less than $5. Do NOT PAY $12 for this.

users.query:
This was purchased following what ended up being my dog-boy's allergic reaction to a chunky turkey kibble (with grain).

There is almost nothing he hates more than getting wet, whether it's rain, the spray-bottle I use to train all my beasts to stay out of the kitchen during food prep (theirs or mine), and BATHS!  A tease will get me ears up when I ask, "You wanna?" until I get to the end of the question with "bath?"

It had to be done.  At first, I wasn't sure about the reason for the rashes and even more damaging scratching he was doing, and he had started to really smell bad.  He hated every minute of it - and so did I.  The instructions say to "allow" it to remain on the beast for 10-15 minutes after lathering, but *insisting* would have been more accurate.  I had to bathe him twice within 2 weeks because the other things I was doing were not effective fast enough.  I got smarter about protecting surfaces from frequent shake-offs in my one and only bathroom tub, and he didn't seem to mind as much the second time.  He actually may have appreciated how good his skin felt afterwards.  He acted like he did.

Once calm had been restored each time, the stink was gone, the gunk from a couple different medications was gone, and his fur was fluffy and soft - even the coarse guard hairs to some degree. As everything in my yard was suffering from some kind of mildew and/or fungus last summer, and while there probably aren't any fungi that are transferable to animals, it became my final choice based upon the description and the reviews.  It certainly didn't harm him in any way, and now I'm prepared for any future fungal or bacterial infections.

cands.text:
Dog-boy loves this kibble!  Had to go on a trial and error search for a new product after he wound up with a nasty yeast infection in his ears and was scratching himself all over. Hours of research and reading reviews led me to this variety of the TOTW products.  For him, unlike a lot of other dogs, potatoes are the culprit - doesn't matter if they are white or sweet or how low on the list of ingredients it is.  This has neither potatoes nor grains.  I was unable to find any other reasonably affordable product that excluded both.  In combination with some topical products and benadryl, we got the ears back to peachy, and his smile came back once all the itching went away.  His coat and his eyes look great.  He's back to being the goofy devil dog he is.

Now I am talking about pencil eraser sized kibble and a 45# dog.  Doesn't matter.  It's tiny and I wet it well so that it actually slows him down a bit as he normally inhales whatever is put in front of him.  It tastes so good, he goes back to lick the empty bowl hours later.  Planning to buy it exclusively.

Planning to buy it exclusively.

This brand was mentioned in several of the thousands of reviews, or was it hundreds of thousands, I read when deciding what grain-free kibble to switch my adopted dog-boy to.  When I got him from the local Humane Society, they said to feed him grain free food.  The prices of grain-free products are ludicrous, and I've never had a dog that required grain-free before, so I ignored that advice.  He developed a very small hot-spot under one front leg maybe a year after I brought him home with me, but I was able to keep it in check and I never made the connection, so, no problem.  Then I picked up a sack of turkey chunk kibble and everything went to hell.  He broke out in rashes in all sorts of places and scratched everywhere around the clock.  You'll find my other reviews in Curoseb, SynergyLabs Veterinary Formula Clinical Care shampoo, Sulfodene Wound Care related to that ordeal (with props to Desitin and Benadryl).

The Merrick Lamb & Sweet Potato kibble is apparently yummy.  He'll finish his serving and lick the bowl for a very long time after it's gone. The feeding instructions for his weight seem a little high, since it sure looks like he's put on some weight at just a little under the recommended daily rate.  I can't be sure yet, but it appears that this 25# bag will hold him for a month. He's been eating it for 9 days, and, with all the shampooing, topicals, underdoses of Benadryl, and this food, his allergic reaction seems to be almost completely gone.  The ingredient list and manufacturing process both sound pretty fantastic, so despite the expense, I am delighted.  I will likely make more purchases, maybe the buffalo and/or salmon, too.  (Anyone know where a retired old girl can get a job and pick up some cash? lol)

Destruct-o-dog is only slightly larger than Jumbo Lamb Chop which is probably why it is still in one piece after slightly more than 2 months. He has plenty of plush fabric to bite into and hasn't been able to wrangle enough of it between his hind legs to be able to tear off the tail, ears, feet or any other parts. I can tell he's a little frustrated by the internal squeaky moving around in a belly cavity, but it does keep him busy. It has not yet been washed, although it is overdue.  Judging by how well it has held up to all the dog spit it has been subjected to, I am confident that it will come through unscathed - I believe it is to be cool air tumbled.

Dog-boy loves it.  He has given me bruises as he shakes it in front of me to get my attention and involvement, but no reason to take away any stars.  If I don't keep an eye on him, he will quietly worry the rope fabric in order to destroy and consume it, but again, no reason to take away any stars.  The minty smell really only lasts a week or two, but hardly a deal-breaker.

Had I scanned through them before I made my selection, I probably wouldn't have purchased this item.

My lazy cats, generally disinterested in almost any cat toy, went wild.  The formerly feral female runs this house and muscled out her bigger, tamer, formerly male companion.  Her only real competition was the dog who was equally attracted to it.  I will have to find a way to give them individualized playtime, well, except for the dog whose job it is involves continuing focus on terrifying squirrels that dare enter my yard.  They chased, leaped, captured and eventually released the feathered teaser without damaging it.  There were even vocalizations.

It was loosely packaged with a 32oz bottled product and had plenty of opportunity to become damaged in transit, but held up well then, too.  It has a foam(ish?) kind of cover on the handle, and the poles have enough flex not to break.  Feathers are attached to what appears to be fishing line.

In spite of my bad attitude toward reviewers who receive products in advance of their glowing texts, I must agree with their feedback.  It is a very reasonably priced, and highly effective, cat toy.

This was a For No Reason gift from my far-away son so you won't see Verified Purchase on my review.  Ran across it as a suggestion on a different page.  Because I also have a med-large dog with a penchant for slaying rodents he runs across in the yard, I left the little critters attached to the cardboard as is.  The smell is intensified, the multiple little spiky tails are very attractive and easy to grasp by mouth or by claw, and they haven't been lost under or behind anything!  The two cats are very happy with the 3-some toy and the dog has accepted that it's a "kitty toy."  We're all very pleased, and it seems to be very durable and reasonably priced.

Medium size (~50#) Destruct-O-Boy may have met his match.  Two year old rescue dog has chewed the eyes out of a leftover child's super safe stuffed animal, accumulated several now denuded tennis balls, and has punctured the 26th, 27th, and 28th soccer balls to have come over the fence. I haven't been returning them since 3 years ago anyway, so the neighbors' training has been terminated.  He is slowly working the laces out of a child's football - yes, from over the fence last year or the year before - and it seems to be his favorite, which is what lead to this purchase.

The rubber material and shape seem to be too slippery to allow him to satisfy his goal of puncturing it. He remains mystified in my ability to make it squeak, but still engaged in the competition to squeak it himself, with an occasional success to his credit. The boy has an amazing capacity to expand his jaw in much the same way as a snake might. He is cognizant of his canines and how to use them effectively in destructive pursuits. If you have a larger dog, your mileage may vary.

This was purchased for a cat that totally stopped drinking bowl water after he learned to drink from the bathtub faucet.  He and his once feral step-sister took about a week getting used to the sound and the peculiarity (to them) of its design.  Bob still prefers the narrower stream coming from a greater height to what the fountain provides, but he does drink from it. Izzie is fascinated with it and puts things in solely to fish them out. I believe she actually drinks from it, as well.

The stream is a little strong, according to Bob, even on the lowest setting.  Cleaning is simple enough. It has a good weight, with rubber tabs on the bottom, so I don't have to keep putting it back where I want it, as I often did with their bowl.

They've had it about a month now, and the only problem was one occasion when I allowed the water level to get too low, resulting in a hideous sound.  My bad.

These have to be the greatest rawhide product ever!

There was a recall of certain brands of rawhide chips, including Companion, which were previously stocked by my grocery store, but then were no longer available.  Everything else available fell into the small dog category or was just junk-food for dogs. Dog-boy loved them, so finding a replacement became a priority. Hours were spent looking at Azn reviews and researching each of those. Ugh.

These are uniform in size and don't have any thin, sharp edges, as the chips so often did. He can consume one, with the dedication he puts into it, within only 10-20 minutes, but there's really no need for a doggie bag here.  They do serve to keep the tartar on his teeth to a minimum.  There has been no splintering and no choking, no digestive problems.  And he loves them!

4/3 update:  Dog-boy still loves these, and his teeth (for which he also gets a denta-treat) are looking good.  I did some research and learned that each of these is *about* 100 calories each, so you may want to adjust your pooch's daily intake.

My boy will eat literally anything with gusto ... including orange peels ... that he believes I eat, so it's difficult to rate based on his enjoyment.  They smelled delicious to me (any wonder that Reese's PB Cups are one of my favorites?).  I do not have the skills or the equipment to do a nutritional analysis, so I have to take the producer's word for their value.  He's still rather young and very active, so the benefits of the glucosamine and chondroitin additives are not obvious.  I do dispute that the product is not a soft treat.  They felt flexible coming out of the bag, and there's no crunch whatsoever.  My 43# dog-boy devoured each within two minutes or less of receiving one.  My biggest issue is that, while he had been receiving kibble and treats containing grains, he developed a severe reaction to an unrelated product with grains - and other stuff.  (I had been advised by the Humane Society location where he was adopted to go with grain-free, but they couldn't or wouldn't give me any kind of history on him.)  His sensitivity may abate after *not* receiving food or treats with grain for awhile, but can't take the chance just yet.
