The story that unfolded was gripping and you find yourself rooting for the heroine, and the ending she so desperately deserves. I look forward to reading more books by this author. :)

From start to finish this book kept me completely hooked and unable to put it down. I love the Dulcie series, and I have been a fan from the very beginning. I was very sad to hear that this was the last book, and I hope that somewhere down the line, Dulcie gets to live on with more adventures. Wherever there is Dulcie, there will always be a story to be told. :)

This book was definitely a true gem that I am so glad I found. This was the first book I have read by this author and i can tell you that it won't be the last. She has a way of pulling you into the story and you feel like you are a part of it. I rarely find myself so emotionally into the characters when i read, that I actually feel their pain or joy and can be brought to tears. I definitely recommend this book and look forward to reading more of her work. :)

This book starts out slow, but it really picks up. I enjoyed the way the writer allowed the characters to provide their own point of view of the story as it unfolded. It allowed you to get a better understanding of the story and how it affected everyone involved. I am getting ready to start the next book in the series, and I can't wait to see how the story unfolds.

From start to finish I LOVED this book. The story that unfolded was definitely one that kept you pulled in. I found myself unable to put it down, and rooting for the characters throughout the story. I am so glad I took a chance on this one, because it definitely paid off. I can't wait to read more work from this author.

I just got done reading this and I really enjoyed it. The short stories were great and I loved getting to know more behind the scenes stories involving the characters. It definitely shed more light on the things that occurred in between the books, and with the series in general.

My favorite part of the book was the short story "Son of Magic" by Rick's 16 year old son Haley. This story was beyond anything I would expect from someone as young as Haley, but it is obvious that he has pure talent. I would definitely add him to your list of authors to look out for, cause he is destined for great things.

Thanks Rick for bringing us another great adventure in the Heroes of Olympus and I am counting down to "The Mark of Athena".

This was the first book I read by this author and I normally don't read books like this. After finishing the book I'm really glad I took a chance. The story that unfolded was very believable and I really enjoyed the character of Trevor. His story is one that needed to be told and I'm very glad I read it.

I don't know if words can describe just how much I enjoyed this book. From the beginning all the way until the end, I was absolutely captivated. Claudy is such an amazing writer, that you find yourself so easily pulled into the story, unable to leave. I swear if it were possible to move to Tir, I would buy the first ticket!!

I loved to see the progression of the storyline and the characters. Just when you think you have a favorite character, you get introduced to more that you find yourself loving, just as much, if not more. I've already purchased the next book "Catch & Hold - Legend" and I'm so excited to see where the story takes me.

This is definitely a series that I will re-read over and over again. Thank you Claudy for another amazing book!!

In true Claudy Conn fashion this historical romance did not disappoint and kept me thoroughly entertained. I really enjoyed getting to see Sir Edward come into his own and see another side of his story which was initially told in Wildfire Kiss, book one in this series.

If you love historical romances you will absolutely love this book and the story that unfolds will keep you wanting more. :)

Thank you Amanda for another Great Book!!! This story was even better than the last one and I didn't think that was possible. I really love the world and characters that you have created in this series. You can't help but fall in love with all of them. I look forward to reading the next book in the series. :)

From start to finish this book was perfection. I have loved Greek Mythology since I was a kid and I'm so glad I found this series. Tina Folsom has a way of pulling you into the story and bringing all of the Gods and Goddesses to life. I am so excited to see this series is continuing and I can't wait to read the next book about Eros. If you haven't started this series yet you really need to. :)

This is the first book that I have read by this author, but it will definitely not be my last. I absolutely LOVED this story from start to finish and found it impossible to put down. The story that unfolds is one that is very well written. You can't help but fall into the story and fall in love with the characters. This is one hot read, and one that I am so grateful that I read. :)

users.query: I use one of these units to store my cone threads, another for fabric and two in the closet with a shelf across the top to connect the two of them for my work tools. Downstairs in the kitchen, I have another one on the side counter to hold plastic wrap and aluminum foil. They work well in lots of spaces.

cands.text: I use this in Moms' room to hold all her medical supplies and it works very well. in fact, I was able to get rid of a table that was using a lot of space in her room. So now, I have more room and rolling storage so her supplies can be reached from the bed and then rolled into a corner when not needed.

Purchased for hanging fabric strips while quilting. I precut all my strips when sewing and always had to place the strips on clothes hangers, over the door, in boxes, etc. Hanging the fabric strips on the slats of the rack, I am now able to keep all the strips together for the whole quilt. I chose no to use the 2nd from the top shelf, so the strips will hang straight down without wrinkling the fabric. I do have to fold the strip once if the strip is cut width of fabric. It is very sturdy and looks great in my sewing room.
I can store the rack under the sewing table after trimming about an inch off the bottom feet
The unused shelf is stored on the rack by simply placing it on top of another shelf.

I have to admit, I did not purchase to use for my jewelry. I use this to hold my sewing machine presser feet. Much nicer to look at than a plastic box, keeps the feet separate and easy to find the one I need. The box is well made and very pretty too.
Essential tool for sewing room. Great deal on these clips.

First time buyer of this thread. So far, I have used it for piecing, and all my vintage sewing machines love this thread. A friend of mine brought some over a while back and we tried it on the long arm and it works beautifully there too.
I have loved to sew all my life and the thread of choice was Coats and Clarks. Love their poly wrapped cotton thread. Then all at once all you could find was 100% polyester thread in the local stores. OK, so learned to like it too. I could buy 500 yd spools for around $1.50 to 1.75. Then C&C went up a lot in price, ($3.50 per spool ) and reduced the number of yards on the spool to such a small amount, (i could only wind 3.5 bobbins and the spool was empty) that I started looking elsewhere for a good reasonable priced thread with enough on the spool to last through the piecing of at least on quilt. And the C&C thread was really linty, always had been, but it was all I knew.
Aurifil is still a bit more twisty as it comes off the spool,and I can live with that. It doesn't break, gives a good strong seam, and it is thinner
that the C&C thread that I was used to sewing with. The price per yard is very good too.

8-18-2016  Revision to my review: Halfway through the spool, the thread became very weak, unable to use the rest of thread on the spool.
Purchased this to use by the longarm machine while quilting. Holds all my tools and rolls easily. Wish it did not have locks on two of the wheels as I don't need locks.

I needed a light that was tall enough and had moving joints so it could be positioned behind the sewing machine or pulled forward to spotlight the needle when necessary. This fits the bill. I use my own bulb in light, joints can be tightened if needed so it should not be hard to keep it in position I place it in.

I have used the regular hem gauge for clothing for years and love it. When I saw this one, I knew I had to have it for doing curtains and such. It is plenty long enough and wide enough to press hems into large sections at a time. Be careful when storing as it will bend easily, being thin metal. Also, be careful when pressing as it gets hot .

Larger than I expected, This will certainly hold a lot of flour or sugar. I had planned to replace all my old canisters with glass ones. Think I will have to order the one gal size because this one is really big and all I need are ones that would hold 5 lbs at a time. The lid is easy to place on and take off with a plastic seal that should be sufficient to keep 5 lbs of flour fresh.
holds my nexstep bowl swab securely and no leaks because there are no holes in the bottom

I have several of these to wear around the house. Pockets are large enough to carry a lot of items including a cell phone. It fits well, being a little loose, which is what I need when cleaning house or working in the yard.
Did not actually have to use this yet, but it will certainly be handy when needed.

I bought this to use under a rotary cutting mat for my sewing room. It works great. Turns pretty easily, just a little noisy when being turned. I expect that to improve with use. The first turntable purchased was more expensive, and made just for the purpose for rotary cutting. However, in use and cutting nearing the edge of the board, it would "dip" down as I  cut. This one does not do that. It remains steady and I  can put up with a squeak during turning for the amount of money I have saved by using this one, instead of the one designed for quilters.

This is the bees' knees for marking cutting lines on my rotary rulers. Cannot live without. Also use it to mark seam lines on my sewing machine. Has just a little bit of sticky on the back to hold it in place. Easy to remove when finished.

This is the bees' knees for marking cutting lines on my rotary rulers. Cannot live without. Also use it to mark seam lines on my sewing machine. Has just a little bit of sticky on the back to hold it in place. Easy to remove when finished.
Easy to assemble, and is very sturdy. Doesn't wobble or bend. Holds lots of clothes easily.  I would love a smaller version for a small room downstairs that does not have a closet.

Purchased these to mark my fabric cutting boards, they work great! Seller shipped really fast and the price was good too!
I will certainly buy these again when I need more.

Great tool  for quick bike repairs
Made to fit the nuts on your bike and easy to store
I've used this for years and would not be without it. Renews dry threads and helps to stop it from sticking to itself under high speed sewing, or easlly slip through fabrics for hand sewing.
I've used this for years and would not be without it. Renews dry threads and helps to stop it from sticking to itself under high speed sewing, or easlly slip through fabrics for hand sewing.

Excellent for outside grill. Still very large for using on stovetop with average size pans. I did try it inside, and discovered that meats, such as sausage patties or hamburger, need to be turned at least once, or uncooked meat sticks to the ridges and then you are trying to remove it from a hot metal so you don't place uncooked meat on top of cooked meat....not good. We will use it outside only and I'll keep looking for a smaller one for inside that is smooth on the bottom.
Purchased as a gift and have not heard any complaints so I expect they are happy enough with the hammer. Intended for use to do odd jobs around the house, not build the house!

My treadmill was delivered in 3 days. Thank you Amazon Prime! UPS helped me to carry it inside and place in foyer. Thanks UPS!

Unpacking was not that hard. Instructions right on top, so easy to take out and read first. Only 6 bolts and nuts on the front bottom and 4 on the top for the arms. However, nowhere in my instructions does it say, start the bolts then wait to tighten all of them at the same time. Had a dickens of a time getting those bolts and washers in. They will not line up if any of them are too tight!
Next, the picture of where and how to apply the lubricant is fuzzy, Had to go to you tube to find out how this is done. Still, don't know how much of the lubricant to use, but will use a thin line to judge how much it spreads. Haven't turned it on at this point, but working on it. Will revise review later.
Revision: Lubrication completed, used about 1/2 bottle sent with treadle. Hardest part was application of the lubricant because the belt had to be loosened. Getting it reset was the worst part of the entire procedure.
The motor is exceptionally quiet! Only thing I could hear was my feet striking the treadle. I hope that it continues to work as expected and will update this in 6 months.

This ruler only measures up to 12 inches. The fabric has to be under 6 inches wide. the 3/4 inch marks are the shortest cut. I needed this to cut presewn strips into 1 3/4 inches. The straight line marks are too far apart to allow you to line the strip up and still cut 1 3/4 inch wide strips. I had to fold my strip to fit into the 6 inch height of the ruler. So, Just be aware that if you want to cut 1 3/4 inch strips, then they have to be under 6 inches wide and you will need a smaller rotary cutter - the 45 mm is too large to cut on the 3/4 inch marks.

users.query: My wife LOVES green & polka dots, so this was perfect. She's doing preschool curriculum at home with our 4 year old son. She laminated it, so it would last longer, and we haven't had any trouble with it coming off the wall. It's also at the top of the wall, and the letters are big enough to be seen from that height.

cands.text: Laminated it to last. It's really helped our 4 year old with his counting. Flash cards only go up so high for preschoolers. We have him counting the days he's been in preschool. The repetition, and visuals are great!

I feel like we got a great deal on this at $11. We use it at home for preschool. I spent hours laminating each little piece so it would last longer (we also have a toddler running around who LOVES to make messes). I use a door hanging shoe organizer to keep it organized. The only drawback is I was hoping to be able to use wet erase markers on it after it was laminated, and no markers work on it at all; that's probably just the laminate quality and has nothing to do with this great learning tool.
Beautiful and sturdy. If you have coloring crazy kids (like we do) they wash easily enough with crayon.
This is cute, and exactly what I want to get my daughter for her birthday. This costs less than $10 at another retailer. Shop around. Don't spend $25 on this!

My children needed something to play with their magnets on. We have only a mini fridge living in an 800 sq. ft. space. We had a hand-me-down board I tried to magnetize with paint. A BAD investment. It didn't work at all even with following all instructions, and applying several coats. This was a GOOD investment ($142 for a 3x4 board). It's much heavier than a nonmagnetic board, so plan to do some serious wall mounting into studs and all that. It has all the hardware. It has a chalk tray. Magnets have no problem sticking to this. We're happy with it, and most IMPORTANTLY the kids are happy with it.
They don't bend like other cardboard puzzles. They are bright & colorful, so my kids LOVE them. Melissa & Doug are a great brand!

It's a lovely piece. It's a little wobbly though, and you need to make sure you even out the weight when hanging coats so it doesn't tip over. Hard to do when BIG and small live in the house. We don't have ANY wall space for mounting hooks for coats which is my preference next to hanging them in a closet, but we don't have any closet space either, so this has to work for us. This option was just shockingly more expensive than we thought it would be.
Our kids have so much fun with these! We have a hard time not playing with them ourselves. Quite happy with them. We can get a good deal on them when they are on sale or an "ad on."
Our kids have so much fun with these! We have a hard time not playing with them ourselves. Quite happy with them. We can get a good deal on them when they are on sale or an "ad on."

We bought this for our just turned 2 year old. She is too small & uncoordinated for the hopper ball our son has, and this was just right for her. It's short enough for her to sit on, and she can bounce around with everyone else. The disclaimer says it's best for 3+ (I think that's due to a possible choking hazard with the pin that blocks air from escaping. It's small, and could fit in the mouth. Not a problem for us, as it doesn't fall out easily, nor does it pry out easily, and our daughter is past the putting everything in her mouth stage). I should also mention our daughter is tall for her age at 3 ft., so please consider that before taking my advice and buying it for your 2 year old. In my personal opinion though, a person a few inches shorter than 3 ft. could also sit on this.

I have a  four year old and a 2 year old who LOVE these. The four year old is getting ready for kindergarten, and the 2 year old is picking up everything the four year old is learning! This was an excellent deal too. Other 3 pack videos in the Preschool Prep Series were about $35, but this 10 Pack was about $40 when we bought it, and included all the other 3 video series. So we got more bang for our $buck$.

For $10 this is a nice, big, rigid board. I needed one for my son's play dough. For that use I'd give it 5 stars. I'd totally use this in the kitchen too. Would prefer a board with a spill catch in the kitchen though, so that's why it only gets 4 stars.
This two piece set was cheaper at $3 than buying the turtle on it's own. Totally happy with it!
Our 3 year old son's FAVORITE Christmas book two years in a row. We even bought an advent calendar, so he can count like they do in the book.

Very happy with these! To start, the colors just make me happy. I do a lot of shopping around for deals, and I can't find anything like this (a 3 pack for around $25!). When I saw them I immediately bought 2 sets.. They aren't so huge that they take up a bunch of space (we live in an 800 sq. ft. home), but they'll fit a lot. We're going to use them inside for storing animal food, kitty litter, and all our recycling! We have to take our own recycling to the recycle center, so these will make storage and transport so much easier! The description is completely accurate: the lids stay closed, and they also stay open when you need them to. They stack on top of each other, AND inside each other in case you need to put them away somewhere. I would totally buy these again at this price!
Bought this for my wife at Christmas. She LOVED it! She's not a big knick knack collector, but these Willow Tree things she loves.

I bought these because my son is starting to read. I underestimated him though, and he had them all memorized within a day of me reading them to him, so his reading wasn't really being challenged. Have your kids sound out/read these themselves, and I'm sure they will be a good learning tool.
These things are strong! I even hang wet towels on the sides our old metal cabinets with them. That may cause them to rust later, but it hasn't happened yet. Will babying more in the future!
Our son spray painted the side of our car. Had to use a bit of elbow grease & a lot of buffing, but with this it all came out.

This lacks a bit of something. It's heavy, and seems rickety when you first put it together, but stabilizes as you continue to assemble it. The 72" height comes from 2 separate poles that don't come together securely enough in my opinion. The shelves are particle board (as I expected), but are only 3/8" thick. The box says the weight capacity for storage is 4,000 lbs (800 lbs per shelf), but I wouldn't put more than 200 or 300 lbs per shelf. It fits our needs & was a good price (under $60). Despite some misgivings, and hoping I get the parts that came broken replaced quickly, I'd buy it again.

We bought this "Used - like new" for half the cost of a new one. Hooked it up, and had no problems. We like the White Rogers thermostat because it has a cover for most of the buttons, and our children can't push them. A feature most other thermostats didn't have.

Have had these for 2 years. They're just now starting to wear out on the inside and sole. I've never had a work shoe or boot last this long! Bought 2 pairs to alternate each day, and allow the other pair to thoroughly dry. Each pair took about 2 weeks to break in. Wear thick socks for best comfort. Recommend treating the leather to protect it as they scratch up in a harsh work environment. I use Kiwi conditioning oil. I work in a warehouse 10-11 hours a day and gouged one pretty good before treating the leather. I prefer an American made shoe, but sometimes that's just not in the budget. These fit my needs without sacrificing quality at half the cost.

Had a root problem the day after we moved into our old "new" home in May 2016. It had 2 large sugar maple trees out front. We had a bit of cleaning up to do. It could've been worse though. The plumber came out and used this stuff, and it cleared right out. Cost us $120. Our water lines are about 75 feet to the main line on the street. He used 4 lbs. and had us wait a full 24 hours (not just 8 hours) before we started using our water lines again.  No problems with blockages this year, but we used 2 lbs. for annual maintenance. We saved $72!!! Even if we had used as much as the plumber did last year we would have saved $50. We're all about DIY maintenance, and not waiting until there is a problem to do something about it. The pictures shown are when we discovered the problem back in 2016. We haven't had any plumbing backups since using 4 lbs. of this stuff.

We'll report back if there are any problems within 12 mos. of the current May 2017 application.
Buying this kind of candy is not cheap! Some places I looked sold it for $8 p/lb!!! This was the least expensive of all options, and it's what we needed.

Bought these to keep a light pair of shoes in our hiking pack. They were 75% off so they were the right price. They're not cushy, but the Vibram gives you a good grip on whatever you're walking/running on. There's a warning on the label when you get them NOT to wear them for very long, because they offer zero support. This is true, and with my high arches I have to remove them after an hour or so. They're exactly what we needed though, so no complaints here.

users.query: My 2nd Sam Archer novel and I liked it. This time the story was all about Sam, as opposed to the 1st book in the series (Nine Lives (Sam Archer Book 1)) which featured Sam's team, and he had a middle size part in the story. This one started slow but then got going in high gear with the action department. I will read the 3rd book in this series real soon (Blackout (Sam Archer Book 3)) especially since I found out it is available as a Kindle Unlimited book. If you like police action thrillers you will like this one. I would suggest starting off with the first book so you can get to know Sam and his team. Bad action movie plot? Nah, but it would be a fun action movie for sure.

cands.text: Let me tell you, if this had been the 1st Chandler story published, I probably would not have read the others. I enjoy this series very much, from the first novella actually released Exposed - A Thriller (Chandler Series) (but 2nd overall in order of the stories) to the 2nd full length novel (but 5th overall): Spree (Chandler Series). I have also read Flee (Chandler Series) (which is the 1st novel published, but the 4th Chandler story overall, but I believe it was the 1st Chandler story published) and I have Three (Chandler Series) (3rd novel, but 6th overall Chandler story) on my Kindle ready to be read. Yes, this book does have some action, but not until the 78% mark or so. With "Exposed" and "Flee" the author got to the action and mayhem right off the bat. The 75% or so was a lot of flirting, some sex, but almost no action. Just not what I was used to with this series. Thank goodness I used my November KOLL to read this story. But it might be a while before I decide to take on "Three" or Naughty - A Thriller (Chandler Series) (Codename: Chandler) (3rd novella and 3rd Chandler thriller overall). Ann Voss Peterson's influence? Who knows?

This title was my first exposure to "The PROJECT". I did enjoy the story and the characters. I plan to read the other titles in this series (I already have Black Harvest (The PROJECT) on my Kindle). I just found this story not as complex or detailed as a typical James Rollins tale, such as: Map of Bones: A Sigma Force Novel or a Clive Clusser tale like: The Mediterranean Caper (Dirk Pitt Adventure). I would say a typical Rollins book is like a big buget movie, but a PROJECT book is more like a Made for TV movie. A good movie, but with a lower budget to spend on bells and whistles. Very much like comparing Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom (Special Edition) to the TV movie Librarian : The Curse Of The Judas Chalice. I love them both. The Lance is light thriller reading, and like I said, I will try other PROJECT titles and see if the author progresses as he adds more titles to this series.

I finished this exciting thriller just last night. Wow! I had first read Stephen Knight almost 2 years ago and loved his stuff. This book continues the story that began in The Gathering Dead (A Zombie Apocalypse Novel) &Left With The Dead (A "Gathering Dead" Novella). After reading a couple 1 and 2 star so-called action thrillers lately, it feels good to read a well crafted story again. Yes it is about zombies, but Stephen can write. He draws you in with his great cast of characters, he pays attention to the plot details & his writing describes the mad world of zombies, but from a human point of view. Bottom Line: this is a very good book, just happens to deal with zombies. A lot of heavy issues involved and Stephen does not gloss over them. I waited well over a year from reading "Left with the Dead" to this thriller. I will not wait long before I get part 2: The Rising Horde, Volume Two (Sequel to "The Gathering Dead"). There are some books that are so good, you know that if someone leaves a review, it has be a 4 or a 5 star review. I feel that way about The Rising Horde, Vol I. Assuming the reader knew this was a zombie thriller (and heck, even if they didn't), I could find no fault with the book. I was just so happy to be reading a book by a writer who cares for his readers and published a well written story. Before I even checked this morning, I just KNEW there could NOT be any 1 or 2 star reviews. What would be their basis for such a review? I am a little surprised at the four 3-star reviews, but then again, some readers have a tough grading scale. I like to think I have a tough but honest grading scale as well (just check out my past reviews), and if I really ENJOY reading a book (as I do this one), then I like to tell the world.

Wow! I just read my 2nd book by Shane Brown and I loved it! Shane Brown is 2 for 2 in the action-thriller department as far as I am concerned. I loved FAST, and I loved Plaza just as much. The action for FAST was fantastic and it fit that type of book. FAST was a military action thriller all the way.......While Plaza is an exciting combination of archaeology and all-out action. And of course, once again, Shane tossed in some strange monsters/creatures and the story took place in an isolated location. A different kind of action then what was featured in FAST. PLAZA is more along the lines of Amazonia, with maybe a tad more action. I loved Amazonia as well, and consider it one of my favorite James Rollins books. I think FAST will be favorably compared to books like Matthew Reilly's Ice Station, while PLAZA will be compared to Amazonia and another Reilly thriller: Temple. I normally do not read two books by the same author so close together as I did FAST and PLAZA, but I could not wait once I found out Shane Brown had a 2nd book avaiable. And what a good deal on his prices, both books selling for only $2.99 and I think they are available on Amazon Prime to borrow for free (one book per month). Now I must pay the price for reading both of his books so close together.......I have to wait UNTIL his next thriller comes out (FAST II?).

Last night I finished CORRECTION: A Gerald Ruhming Tale of Terror (SIMON VECTOR) by JAK HOLDING. As the title indicates, this novella is a tie-in to SIMON VECTOR. I was all set to read SIMON VECTOR when I ran across CORRECTION. Turns out the two books can be read in any order, but I figured I would start with the novella first. The "Mad Doctor of Mars" (Gerald Ruhming) is truly a major sick puppy. Can't wait to see how the story unfolds in SIMON VECTOR. I checked the authors (John And Ken ~ JAK) website and discovered that there will be 4 entry point novellas to the world of SIMON VECTOR, and CORRECTION was just the first. The remaining 3 will be published in the next couple of months. Based on what I have read so far (especially the subplot dealing with the "former" marshall) I will probably end up getting those entry point stories as well. I am hoping that SIMON VECTOR lives up to the hype I have been reading.

I finally got around to reading this story, and I am glad I did. One reviewer commented the story was too violent- - - It's a zombie book set in the ole west, what else would you expect to read? Dawn of the Dead - Unrated Director's Cut [HD] meets A Fistful of Dollars [HD]. Gruesome? You bet! This is a short read, but I thought the author did a good job of setting the characters up, with the two main characters being an outlaw on the run and a intelligent hooker with a heart of gold. Loved the ending........I could just see their eyes rolling....here we go again....Which leads into the 2nd of 3 books in this series: Tartarus (West of Hell #2).

Let's face it, if you have already read the first two Joe Ledger novels: Patient Zero: A Joe Ledger Novel and The Dragon Factory then by now you should be hooked on the series and will pick up The King of Plagues. I love all 3 of these great action thrillers. But, Patient Zero is my all-time favorite Jonathan Maberry novel. From there I spread out to include all 3 books in the Ghost Road Blues series. But back to The King of Plagues. It might not feature as much as action as the first two, but it gets into the character and world of Joe Ledger a little more. I give it a solid 4 stars. Can't wait for the next one. I am picking up the Joe Ledger short stories where ever I can: Material Witness: A Joe Ledger Bonus Story and Countdown: A Joe Ledger Short Prequel Short Story to Patient Zero so far. Joe Ledger gives me my Jack Bauer fix now that "24" is off the air. While I have all 3 Joe Ledger books in paperback, The King of Plagues is my first in the Kindle format (and I do not double dip alot).

Okay, I consider myself a Jonathan Maberry fan. I got hooked on Patient Zero: A Joe Ledger Novel a couple of years ago and bought the trade paperback size book as soon as it came out. I now have paper copies of the 3 Joe Ledger books, and Kindle versions of Patient Zero and The King of Plagues: A Joe Ledger Novel (Joe Ledger Novels). Patient Zero in turn led me to the 3 Pine Deep books which I just love, and want more of. Anyways, Dead of Night came out back in October or so, but it was not until Feb that I actually ordered it. My mistake in waiting so long! I loved this zombie thriller. As others have noted, this book screams to be made into a movie! A well written zombie thriller is a feast to behold and Dead of Night delivers. Jonathan writes a very beliveable version of how this zombie epidemic could develop and fester so quickly. I loved all the characters and got hooked on this book right off the bat. I agree with all the good reviews and will not hesitate the next time a Maberry adult oriented book comes out (like in April when the next Joe Ledger novel hits the street).

Another Beta tester here: I was somewhat disappointed in To Faithfully Execute. I loved the first two books in this series: State of Rebellion (A Pug Connor Novel) and Uncivil Liberties (A Pug Connor Novel #2), giving them 4 star reviews. I was really getting into To Faithfully Execute for most of the book, but the ending seemed to disappoint me. I guess it was Pug Conner constantly changing jobs/gears in the same book. He starts off as a Marine General as part of a goverment team assigned to handle secret missions involving terrorists. I enjoyed the Rainbox Six aspect of this part that involved Pug and Carlos taking out bad guys anywhere in the world. Very well handled. Then Pug gets invited into a secret global civilian organization bascially doing the same thing, but without goverment ties. This forces Pug to resign, for the good of the service and so on. But then Pug took over the private securtiy firm that was causing most of the trouble in the 2nd book (Hoover Dam anyone?) and in the beginning of the 3rd book. We really didn't get to see Pug do more than set things up before he switched gears again and accepted a job with the Republic of Western America as a Marine General. But how can that be? He was a General in the United States of America's service, not the Western Republic. I got lost figuring out who Pug was suppose to be and whose side he was on at the moment. We really did not see much of Carlos in the latter third of the book. And President Snow came off the worse for the wear in this one, as compared to the great job he did in Uncivil Liberties. He kept making empty threats he could not or would not back up. Kinda wasted his role in this one. Oh well, "In for a penny, In for a pound" as they say. I will give the next book a try, to see where Gordon takes this series. But IMHO this was the weakest of the series, and Uncivil Liberties was the best (tough to beat out the beginning and ending of that one), just edging out State.

How refreshing to read a Young Adult thriller set in a dark future, that does NOT remind me of The Hunger Games (unlike the Z 2134 (Z 2134 Series Book 1) series (along with Z2135 and Z2136)). I enjoyed Defect #1: Legacy Code Prequel Series (Fractured Era Series) and liked Part Two even more. Certainly enough to go on to Parts 3 and 4. I have Autumn's Legacy Code (Fractured Era: Legacy Code Book 1)] on my Kindle already (the Defect novellas are a prequel series to Legacy Code, they sort of set a foundation for that story). The story is set in a dark future with tones of X-Files thrown in. We learn a little more in each novella...can't wait to see where this goes. I will hold off on Legacy Code until I am thru with the Defect novellas.

Let me tell you off the top of my head, I love reading Matt Reilly books. One of my All time favorite action novels is Ice Station. I remember when I first read Ice Station and said to myself I would take a break once the action slowed down and it started getting all techie or lovey dovey or such. Well, that never happened and wham! I was hooked. The books featuring Scarecrow seem to be written for guys and gals like me who crave action, on an adult level. My favorite movie is Die Hard. The action in Ice Station and other Scarecrow books is constant and a little over the top, but brutal kick butt action none-the-less. To me it just seems as if the Jack West Jr. stories are written for a younger audience. Maybe PG-13 whereas the Scarecrow books are more "R" rated. I guess that is why I waited years to finish off the Jack West trilogy and bought the book at a close-out sale. I could not see spending a lot of money on basically a kiddie book. Now on the other hand, a couple of years ago I spent $26 to get a hardback copy of Scarecrow delivered to me before the book came out in the U.S. And I plan to buy the latest Scarecrow novel Scarecrow Returns for my Kindle. I am willing to pay over $10 ($11.99 in this case) to read this story NOW instead of waiting for the paperback to come out and thus get a lower price for it on my Kindle. I liked 5 Greatest Warriors, but 3 stars is more than fitting for an adult reader, maybe 4 stars if you are in your teens.

Darkness on the Edge of Town was a free book on my Kindle. I am glad I decided to give it a try. I enjoyed the book very much and plan to buy several more novels by this author. I just need to decide which Brian Keene novel to BUY first: A Gathering of Crows or The Rising. I'll end up buying both, but which one to read first? I have read Under the Dome: A Novel and rented the Blu-ray vesion of The Mist (Two-Disc Collector's Edition) [Blu-ray]. This story is closely related to those two, but it can certainly stand on its own very well. Brian develeped his characters nicely and kept the story focused on a small set of people. Creepy, very creepy. Amazon had a good plan here: give away Darkness on the Edge of Town and then the readers will want more of Brian Keene. It worked for me. Thanks again to Amazon and Kindle for introducing me to two new authors: Jack Kilborn (Afraid) and Brian Keene.

This book lived up to what I was expecting. Similar in parts to James Rollins Amazonia, but different enough to let me like it on it's own. I love these thrillers set in the deep jungle. Brings back a feeling of watching the Johnny Quest (Jonny Quest - The Complete First Season) cartoons back in the 60's. Plenty of action in this story. The mystery behind the story played a big part and it was fun finding things out along with the cast of characters. I will for sure check out other books by Brown like: Black Sun: A Thriller

A very short thriller featuring my new favorite action character Will Robie (from The Innocentand The Hit) together with characters such as Oliver Stone from the Camel Club series of books such as: The Camel Club. Just enough of a story to tease us fans until the next Will Robie story comes out in April: The Target. I love team-up stories like Bullseye, where an author will team up two or more of his most famous characters in one story (like David Morrell did in The League of Night and Fog: A Novel (Mortalis). Looks like I will be branching out soon to other David Baldacci books.

I have been a Jon Land fan for over 20 years. I got hooked on his writing way back with The Eighth Trumpet: A Jared Kimberlain Novel (Book One) and The Gamma Option: A Blaine McCracken Novel. Jon always writes exciting thrillers and his characters are tough, but honest deep down. As was the case with Jared or Blaine, Jon once again comes thru with strong central characters such as Ranger Caitlin Strong and Cort Masters. Each character has a history and secerts. Masters role is like a side-kick to Caitlin and provides a love interest. I enjoy reading how these two characters work so well together, similiar to the two main characters in series that featured Ben Kamal and Dainielle Barnea, such as Blood Diamonds (Ben Kamal and Danielle Barnea Novels). Jon's stories are full of suspense, action, intrigue, and many sub-plots. I am looking forward to the 3rd Caitlin Strong novel and many more after that.

I love this sci-fi YA super villain series. This is my 2nd Reckoners read and I love them both. I am also next in line at my digital library to read the novella that bridged the gap between the first two books: Mitosis: A Reckoners Story. Brandon is 2 for 2 as far as I am concerned and I will be first in line next year when the 3rd novel comes out. The characters are well set up and the story has several mystery angles to the plot. Not a cliff-hanger ending....but ooohh, it is setup for a 3rd exciting chapter. Can't wait.

After reading Stephen Knight's The Gathering Dead and enjoying it very much, I thought I would give Hackett's War a shot. It was well worth it. This is a short action story and somehow it reminded me of The Expendables (Three-Disc Blu-ray/DVD Combo + Digital Copy) (in a good way, as I loved that movie). I will certainly buy any future stories featuring Hackett and his crew of warriors. Very well written, as was The Gathering Dead.

I re-read this great action thriller recently on my Kindle. I first read this thriller back in 99 or so. I loved it then and I still love it! From Hunter I branched out to all of his other thrillers like: Cain,Leviathan, and another of Huggins's thrillers I picked up a week ago: Reckoning. I have all these thrillers in trade paperback format, except for Hunter wouldn't you know. I plan to re-read The Reckoning one of these days (another Huggins book on my Profile Shelf). I think I like this book because it has several elements of Predator in it: a hunt for a killer beast/monster, an elite military hand-picked squad, and the cold thick Alaskan forest instead of a hot steamy jungle. And then of course the cool character of Nathaniel Hunter himself and his companion "Ghost" (a rather large powerful wolf). A bit macho at times. but I don't care. Hunter comes across as a no-nonsense type of guy. Reading the book you come to believe he COULD track this creature and he COULD fight it, and he COULD win! I love the cast of supporting characters as well: Bobbi Jo, a tough as nails female sniper, Taylor, the big weapons expert, and Takakura, a Japanese soldier as good with a katana as he is with modern weapons(yeah, the whole honor thing, but it works here), and a couple of kick butt Marshalls who show up at the end and join in the fighting. This book is ACTION, ACTION, and more ACTION! Reading it for the 2nd time was just as fun/exciting as the first time. I am looking forward to re-reading The Reckoning.

I just finished No Other Option by Marcus Wynne. What a great action thriller! This is the 2nd book by Marcus I bought for my Kindle (with the other being With A Vengeance). I have a third already on my Kindle (Johnny Wylde), and I plan to pick up at least two others by him (Warrior in the Shadows and Brothers in Arms). No Other Option is an action story about a rogue special Ops soldier that goes a killing/rape rampage and has to be brought in or taken out by one of his own. Kind of a cross between First Blood by David Morrell and the movie The Hunted (Widescreen Edition), starring Tommy Lee Jones. Marcus's writing compares very well with authors such as David Morrell, Robert Ludlum, or Brad Thor any day of the week (and I love all 3 of those authors). This story features well written characters (police, marshalls, & special ops) and a suspenseful plot.

What a super good deal you are getting with this $0.99 special book. Action, suspense, & spy tradecraft in a book that rivals stories by David Morrell and I love his stories as well. I read No Other Option by Marcus Wynne years ago and I always meant to read more of his books. When I saw this low cost thriller I jumped on it and I am glad I did. I certainly plan to pick up his other books that are available on the Kindle: Warrior in the Shadows &Brothers in Arms. These both go for about $7-$8. I picked up another $0.99 sale by Wynne called Johnny Wylde. If that story is even HALF as good as With A Vengeance I will be very happy. With a Vengeance is heavy into knife fighting, much like David Morrell's The Naked Edge (which I feel is very good as well). I hope Marcus is on the mend and I will be looking forward to many more books from him. If you like action books even a little, then I say go for this thriller. Of course you may never want to fly again after reading it, but you will be entertained.

After spending most of August looking over books, I choose Afraid to be the first book I downloaded & paid for to read on my new Kindle 3.  The reviews were dead on (so to speak).  This is just the first of many Jack Kilborn & JA Konrath novels I plan on buying and reading (I already have Serial: Uncut on my Kindle).  The Red Ops "bad guys" in Afraid are pretty sick puppies.  Afraid is an exciting suspenseful thriller!  Just when you think things are bad enough and they couldn't get any worse: they do!  Can't wait for this to be turned into a movie!  Plenty of gore and blood, but a good solid story as well.  I enjoyed reading about the characters, both good and bad.  I read alot and I am surprised that I have NOT heard about Konrath (or Kilborn) before.  I am hooked now.

P.S.  Would love to read a spin-off book from Afraid ~ about a mission or two with the "Red Ops" sick puppies.

I'm pretty new to the Kindle Fire (4 weeks now), but I am catching up.  I am up to 10 videos on my Fire.  I just watched The Dark Knight once again, but this time on my Kindle Fire.  Whoa!  It brought back some good memories.  What a great movie and what great acting from all involved.  I saw The Dark Knight Rising on the opening midnight show (in Oklahoma) and I am planning on seeing it again tonight.  I am now even more in the mood.  The Kindle Fire is perfect for watching videos.  I picked up the Dark Knight when it came on sale for only $4.99.  I can't remember if Batman Begains was on sale at the time or not.  If so, I should have picked it up as well.  I even took my Fire to work and watched about 45 minutes of The Dark Knight during my lunch hour.  I hooked my work PC's speakers to the Fire and rocked out to Batman, Two-Face, and the Joker.  Still using the Volume+ app to boast the sound on the Fire.  If you have a Fire, this would be a good selection to have on-hand.  I watched it once and it is back on the Cloud once again.  Ready for my next viewing!

Part of me wants to call this book an action thriller, but that does not do justice to this book. Yes it has action, and I am very much an action junkie along the lines of Die Hard Collection (Die Hard / Die Hard 2: Die Harder / Die Hard with a Vengeance / Live Free or Die Hard) [Blu-ray] and the recent The Expendables (Extended Director's Cut) [Blu-ray]. Or, in the case of books: Scarecrow Returns by Matt Reilly or one of my new favorite action authors Michael Stephen Fuchs, author of D-Boys. These two books are almost pure action/hi-tech. I love them, but a Spider Shepherd thriller has more than just exciting action. Stephen Leather writes a very well crafted thriller. His characters are very human, well developed plot lines, and enough detail to let you know that Stephen knows his material. This is my 2nd Spider Shepherd book that I have read and I enjoyed them both. I have another two in paperback, but I might hold off reading them until I can get a Kindle version of them. In an earlier review I called Spider a "British Chuck Norris", and I meant that in a very good way. In America, Chuck mostly played characters that you knew you could depend on, he would get the job done, is very loyal to his family, co-workers, and friends. A no-nonsense All-American type of guy. Spider is the same (except British). He is not Superman, but he is very professional and well trained. Sounds clich, but I would love to see a movie version of almost any Spider novel. Another franchise for Jason Statham?

This is a fun little action story. Took a while to warm up to the lead character (Dillion), as he came across kinda selfish at first. But, it was an origin story and it takes time to set things up. One reviewer suggest that the 7 ft suit reminded him of Iron Man, but I feel it is more like X-O Manowar (where an alien suit bonds to Aric of Dacia, a warrior from 2,000 years ago) published by Valiant Comics and featured in X-O Manowar: Centurion (Kindle Worlds Novella). It it will be interresting to see where Victor takes the Black Onyx next.
This is a great series and this collection is a great way to read this series.  This is not the end....more Lazarus coming soon!

users.query: Fantastic book for exploring your personality and that of others. The 9 types of the Enneagram are also related to the 16 MBTI types. Excellent book for use in business and writing. Each of the 9 types has bountiful examples of behavior in all aspect of life, such as career, relationships, as a child, or as  parent. Highly recommended!

cands.text:
Ben Bova has amazing credentials, and  really delivers with this book. His advice is eminently practical and easy to understand. Bova gives detailed advice, then illustrates it via a short story, which is then further analysed to ensure comprehension.

Fantastic resource!

I was very disappointed with this book. First of all, I've never seen a book typeset with type so small, It might be 8pt, most books are 12pt or thereabouts. I'm a young man with decent vision and I had trouble reading it.

Secondly, like most of Writer's Digest books - it's hit or miss on quality. They've published some great books, but they've also published an equal number of duds. Quality, NOT quantity folks!

Thirdly, the book is a collection of essays, not a cohesive guide to writing horror. I wanted a book where I could examine the mechanics of creating good horror; this was a series of opinions on various aspects, but was not well unified at all.

There may be a few nuggets in there, so I'll give it three stars, but have a good look at any Writer's Digest book before you buy - they seem to be interested more in  making money than serving to educate bourgeoning writers.

This is one of the very first books I bought on Asatru, and I have since ready pretty much read everything out there - this is still my favorite book on the subject.

Greg introduces Asatru in an unbiased and straight forward manner. There are lots of books out there rife with extra detail that might overwhelm a person interested in exploring Asatru - this is not one of them. Living Asatru achieves a perfect balance of depth and breadth.

I wish there were such excellent introductions to other faiths for people; Greg's work is an in valuable contribution to the community.

Eoghan Odinsson, Award Winning Author of  "Northern Lore: A Field Guide To The Northern Mind, Body & Spirit"

Dan Abnett is really a great writer, and this book is well written. I just found it a bit too quirky and strange for my tastes. He pushes the envelop in describing a weird and highly commercial future, which will be welcome to some, but was too odd for me to enjoy.

Great Book, just not my cup of tea.

I must say that Schmidt's approach to archetypes using the Greek Gods & Goddesses to illustrate them was fascinating. There are some  nuggets in the book, but I didn't feel the archetypes were that useful. I found the major male and female types too severe. I couldn't find one that I could use for my protagonist.

Overall, it wasn't what I expected.
Great little book. Just enough detail, presented clearly and explained cogently. I'm very glad I purchased this book. Go buy one!

I read a lot of books in a year - 106 in 2014 to be exact. This is one of the best I've read in many years, and reminds me of why I love Science Fiction, and Space Opera specifically; big Ideas, sweeping storylines, cool tech, vividly drawn characters, action, and romance. Fluency has it all. It's an intelligent and gripping novel that kept me up till it was done. I especially liked a female protagonist. Us guys get most of the page time in SF, so it's refreshing to embrace a woman's perspective. Well done Ms. Wells! Book 2 please!

I read a lot of books in a year - 106 in 2014 to be exact. This is one of the best I've read in many years, and reminds me of why I love Science Fiction, and Space Opera specifically; big Ideas, sweeping storylines, cool tech, vividly drawn characters, action, and romance. Fluency has it all. It's an intelligent and gripping novel that kept me up till it was done. I especially liked a female protagonist. Us guys get most of the page time in SF, so it's refreshing to embrace a woman's perspective. Well done Ms. Wells! Book 2 please!

Given my love of books and writing, I suppose it's not a huge surprise that I love Typography and Fonts (or more properly, typefaces). I just purchased this really cool book that any lover of fonts should read.

It's highly entertaining, and has examples of how different fonts originated (Comic Sans MS anyone?) as well as all kinds of other cool Font-lover trivia.

I really enjoyed the history and usage of the fonts listed, as well as some info on the general terms and language of typography.

Most of all this book is fun! The first few pages have some amazing examples of typography in action, such as in Newspaper classifieds and street signs.

This is a book I'll read again and again and will keep my well read copy of Walden company!

Excellent first book from Philip Chen. Part Tom Clancy thriller, part sci-fi, Chen does a great job creating a compelling page turner, packed with technical detail, pervasive mystery and culminating in a heart stopping cliff hanger. Looking forward to the next installment!

Eoghan Odinsson, Award Winning Author of "Northern Lore: A Field Guide To The Northern Mind, Body & Spirit"

Very good book, cool concepts, lots of action, and a promise for things to come.

Good vacation or weekend read.

This is a lighthearted, yet useful little book. It has plenty of very useful suggestions and tips on improving your writing, as well as manifold examples and exercise.

Definitely worth picking up a copy.

This is a lighthearted, yet useful little book. It has plenty of very useful suggestions and tips on improving your writing, as well as manifold examples and exercise.

Definitely worth picking up a copy.

Sometimes in life you get much more than you were expecting, rarely, but this book is a good example. I'll let others reviewers cover specific content, let me tell you how this book made me feel.

I was looking forward to it after having some interaction with Mony & Alberto, and thought I would be reading a book about a pilgrimage, and I expected a sort of travel guide. Sounded great!

But what I got was so much more. This is a true story and has everything you would expect in a Hollywood blockbuster. It's a book about rebellion, a book about noble pursuits, it has sadness, happiness, delight, death, romance and adventure.

There is insight and depth in this book that touched me very deeply, and at times had me choking back a tear; not for sadness, but for the beauty of an experience and insight that was shared with me and resonated on a level I rarely feel.

If you're looking for a book that's about a pilgrimage, then here it is. If you're looking for a book about self-discovery, love, anger, compassion, peace and conflict, then look no further.

This book is an incredibly broad sampling of the human experience, and yet still manages to cut deeply into your soul while reading it.

Eoghan Odinsson, Award Winning Author of "Northern Wisdom: The Havamal, Tao of the Vikings"

Fascinating book! This covers so many structural elements of a story that I had never considered. I'm a planner and a plotter, so this book is like candy to me.  If you're a serious writer, grab a copy.

I didn't know when I bought this book that the author created Rambo. That was very valuable. That experience gave Morrell a perspective on writing, few have. The book is chock full of practical advice, as well as information on the entire commercial process, as he experienced it.

All in all, one of the better writing books.

I didn't know when I bought this book that the author created Rambo. That was very valuable. That experience gave Morrell a perspective on writing, few have. The book is chock full of practical advice, as well as information on the entire commercial process, as he experienced it.

All in all, one of the better writing books.

While I wouldn't judge this the ultimate thesaurus, it's a fantastic little tome.

Innovative, concise and eminently useful.

I just purchased the companion as well.

Highly recommended.

Another great book my James Scott Bell. Bell gives us a broad set of tools to re-evaluate an existing novel, or to plan a new novel with an eye to creating conflict and suspense. I was impressed with all the techniques to create conflict - such as asymmetric dialogue: not answering a question directly, but saying something else. The book is chock full of such clever tips.

To echo R.A. Meeks sentiment, I too wish I had this book years ago. Lale does an excellent job of navigating the complex developments and many facets of modern Asatru.

Lale presents the lessons in this book like a patient mentor, carefully teaching us many of the basic and very important aspects of the path. She also adroitly handles a few of the more sensitive aspects of Asatru, such as universalism and folkishness.

This is a "must read" for every person new to Asatru, or just curious about the path.

I look forward to more of Ms. Lales work.

Eoghan Odinsson, author of "Northern Lore: A Field Guide To The Northern Mind, Body & Spirit"

This is an absolutely incredible headset! I've tried several Bluetooth headsets for my phone and music, and found most to be quite uncomfortable.

There may be headsets on the market with better overall audio quality, but the quality for the 855 is very good, and the other benefits such as low weight, comfort, noise suppression due to earplug design, far out weigh any marginal increase in audio quality. Price is also great! I got mine here on Amazon for less than $70.

I use mine in my Jeep and on my motorcycle, and the design blocks all external noise, giving me a nice quiet ride - even without the music playing.

I believe this is the most versatile bluetooth headset on the market, and one of the best all round values.

Well done Plantronics!!

This was my first Ringo book, and it won't be my last. While there is some action, the bulk of the book is a fascinating tale of one man building an economic empire, and at the same time saving Earth. The technology and science described in the book are really engaging. I'm well into book 2!

This is one of the coolest books I've read in ages. The first thing that hooked me was how well Clines developed the characters. Im normally a plot person, but each of the characters living in this building was so intriguing.

As for the plot, well I cant say too much without spoilers. It is very much like a LOST type of story, with very unexpected happenings, but unlike LOST this book has an awesome ending!

So in summary: Fantastic Characters, Mind Blowing Plot, and perfect Pace. Best book I've read in 2012.

Hugh B. Long, Award Winning author of The Yggdrasil Codex

This is the best book I've read in ages. The characterization of Harper is so engaging, and the mystery.... well, no spoilers, but "Holy fishhooks, Batman!" Riddle had me sucked in from page 1, and reeled me in through a sleepless night to finish the book!

This book, to me, is like Dan Brown meets Michael Crichton, in the best possible ways.

This is the first of his books I've read, and I'm already on to his Atlantis Trilogy.

600 Push-ups 30 Variations is a handy little book, jam-packed with information. As a Black Belt and someone who travels frequently, I'm always on the lookout for ways to exercise, and often I don't have the to go to the gym. Bob's book offers a huge variety of exercises that require no equipment, no gym, and very little time.

600 Push-ups 30 Variations is also very well illustrated, with clear and detailed pictures of Bob demonstrating each of the exercises.

There are also excellent routines included - I especially enjoyed the 600 pushups incorporated into a 60 min run.

Like many things in life, it's the basics that you can fall back on and build upon, and this is exactly what Bob's book does.

Eoghan Odinsson, Black Belt & Award Winning Author of "Northern Lore: A Field Guide To The Northern Mind, Body & Spirit"

users.query: I am totally caught up in this series. While I normally look for more paranormal adventures, the exploration of tech and galaxies is taking me on a wonderful ride. I am so happy that book four comes out in 5 days. The characters are engaging and the plot is intriguing. Well done for this genre. I am a fan.

cands.text: I am having a blast with this series. The editing is getting better but still needs help. But none of that takes away from the twists the action and the characters in this far out sci fi trip! Love the connections all the players have found and the development of the plot. Fangtastic!!!!! Fun and sooooo addictive. I am a forever fan!

Fantastic dimensional experience. Real magickal characters. Ever changing complex scenarios. Love the imaginative science and world building. Always full of inter relationship challenges and resolutions. Lots of love laughs and overcoming tragedy. This series has it all and I am an addicted fan. Cannot wait for the next book!!!!!

I have been enjoying this series. A bit serious but well written with great characters and world building. I like the alien aspect. Not quite enough humor and edgy modern affectation but still enjoyable! Doesn't beat the BDB however. I apologize but I found that series first and nothing beats that one!!!! Again sorry. That will not keep me from continuing to read this one though!  Looks like you two have been competing for a long time! The more the merrier! And Dragons are still my all time favorite! Anyway I'm on to book 6 regardless of negative reviews. I am a loyal fan.

Please just don't stop writing! Each book in this series builds upon the last. The characters grow and the world expands with non stop action and plot development. I especially like that previous characters are not forgotten in each new journey and play appropriate roles in resolving issues. A very addicted fan!

So glad to know that the series will continue with Sloan!  While the style lacks a certain " epic" dimension I have never laughed out loud so many times in so many books. The characters are just so witty and fun. Of course there are all the steamy romance and paranormal elements to keep the reader interested. Keep this series going! Well worth the ride!

I love this series. Although I look forward to more interesting info on the portals, other worlds and other supernaturals beyond the deadheads. Next Gen carries on the proud tradition of KBS and I remain an addicted fan!
I am following this series with interest. Imaginative and fast paced. Characters that grow and stay with you. Great world building. Keep em coming!

I am in it for the long haul. Thank you so much for the free book one. I am easily addicted but this will be one of my top favorite series, I can tell already. Well written and wonderful world building. Deserves all the accolades it has already received. I might be late to the party but will one of the most appreciative fans! A great beginning!!!

I have LIVED this series from book one to 10. What a wild ride! Sorry to see its over but I am completely satisfied and elated with each twist of Rylee's adventure!!! Every character has left an indelible mark on my psyche. I look forward to ANY continuing effort on her journey with the supernaturals the veil and the rim. NEVER A DULL MOMENT!!!!!

I just love this author and this series. Always creates an ongoing addicting tale that I cannot refuse. Will be following Leonides and Alisha throughout their journey in space and myriad cultures. Great world building action and characters. Keep me apprised. I am already anticipating the next edition! Woohoo!

I am easily hooked. I wish I could give this series 5 stars. It's pretty well written. But a bit too much obsession with car and guns and architecture. Don't care for the stereotypical depiction of what kills vamps etc. I continue to read because the characters are growing on me. And the adventures tho a bit predictable keep my interest. Needs more in the relationship department and needs to expand the magic/preternatural realms to add excitement. Reminds me of a Vin Diesel movie with too many car chase scenes. I like Vin by the way. Still I keep reading.
this trilogy is a wild ride. Couldn't put one book down without starting the next. Great read. Thrilling and frightening at the same time. And a very interesting point of view re genetic engineering.

I read Blood on the Stars first. That was interesting and exciting. This series is very serious and pretty wordy.
MARINES. While I appreciate the forewarning re the first person and I found these 12 chapters satisfying as far as information, it was a real SLOG getting thru it. I couldn't wait to get to book 2 for some action.
COST OF VICTORY. At least the story and characters started to move along. I love the main characters of course. Cain Holm Garret Sarah and all the marines. I was truly depressed with the the malicious Stark Alex and Cooper and the vile goals of the power monsters. I found myself flipping thru pages of redundant histories however. I want complete back stories of course. But so much repetition with no interesting aliens to break the war atmosphere was hard.
A LITTLE REBELLION. Finally! I found myself asking why doesn't anyone EXPOSE that damned Stark! Or even at times wondering at a missed tactical choice. However this episode was satisfying in its outcome even though the journey lacked any humor or bodacious personalities. I will follow. I am easily addicted to a tale.

I have enjoyed this entire series. all the characters and world building keep me interested and wanting more. I hope to see more from Ankari Victor Lauren Sergei Jamie Tick and of course Striker. Can't wait to meet the woman who revels in his comics. Sorry I haven't reviewed the first four books. Just on a roll reading. I am a fan!

5 stars because I am a everlasting fan. Thank you for starting out with the cast of characters. I love the way you brought each and every individual into play in this "new season" with reminders of past experiences. This book is a great prelude to the future downfall of the consortium.  I truly look forward to more adventures and more exciting interactions. I did feel that the painting of utopia was timely and picturesque but it felt a bit overdone. Most all of the characters have found their home/peace with family and love, and that is a great thing but some of the sweetness was redundant. I sincerely hope that there will be a continuation of the psy/changeling world and I will be back to buy. Please don't make us wait for an entire year!!!!!!!!!

Love the multiverse. And all the varied worlds and well developed characters in each of these worlds. I am really enjoying this series and following Ada and Kay on their expanding journey both physical and romantic. Good one!

Everything comes back so clear and experiential. Even after so many other books I knew the world and the characters right away. I am looking forward to Del's journey as phantom seeker and lover of roarke!  Love that dragon too! I am addicted and a big fan!

Enjoyed this little reminiscence. But really want a full blown "next book"! I keep hoping. The characters are like brothers and sisters to me. The scenes replay in my mind without searching for them. Great writing. More! I want more.

I want to know more about the tech from pre CA! I look forward to Barron Andi the Dauntless all the fighters the Marines and the Intrepid in their search of the Badlands. I know I am writing the next book in my head but come on! Love the interactions and the plots. I couldn't put this one down in anticipation of the big discovery. Was somewhat disappointed with the ending but understandable knowing the cruelty of the Union. I am a fan and I will follow!

Very good sci fi and intriguing aliens. Of course I am rooting for the human race and the freedom of the seven others under vilarasi control. Now Procter just has to use Granger to produce an antidote and move on to victory!!! I'm a fan.

Enjoyed this world and need book 2 to continue the life of Tate! Want to know all about her past and the larger implications of the AI, Ryu and Jax!!!!! When will a sequel be released???? I am looking forward to it.

Great combination of characters and sci fi world building. Wish I didn't have to wait so long to find out what happens to Pike, Walker Nhean and hopefully what's left of Dawn. A saga just waiting to expand into an epic! Smile.

A great continuation of the Midnight Breed. Wonderful characters and world building. Thank you for all the quick references to the past n the beginning of the book. It helps so much to have the whole picture filled in. With so many series favorites out there this helps immensely. This is one of my top ten favorite fantasies so I have enjoyed this one that much more!!! Always a fan!!!!

after living away for a long time. Of course I have enjoyed wheelers story. While I have awaited this book with great anticipation I felt that it didn't have the same excitement and emotional attachment as the story of Lexi and ivy. Can't put my finger on why. Naya and wheeler are great characters. Maybe the depiction of the villains and their actions were too much "understood" since it was expected that the reader knew the scenario. And I felt that references to Lexi were too uninvolved. Again. Can't put my finger on it. Still I am a huge fan! And I want more of both the seven series AND Mageri!!!!! Wish I could give this five stars. But look forward to all of Danika 's work!!!!!

Another addiction to add to my list ... Well written sultry detective ... My mother turned me on to this series. I have a lot of catching up to do. I am on book three now. Will keep coming back to Jd Robb ... Love the characters.

users.query:
This book wasn't what I was expecting (I was expecting it to be darker or more twisted), but that's on me. The book was a little slow to start, but overall it was good, and really I can't say anything bad about it. It was mysterious, but in the end it was all explained and made sense, so you don't have to worry about it being confusing or about not getting answers. I think I recall seeing some reviews that mentioned it being shocking or mindscrew-y, but I didn't think it was, although that could be because I figured out the general gist of what was going on around the 43% mark and then pretty much figured out the rest also before it was revealed. [Hidden spoiler about whether the book had a happy ending or not can be found in my review on my blog or Goodreads.] And getting to understand Raleigh and why he did the things he did gave me new insight into someone I might've judged in real life if I didn't know his story. So overall, it wasn't quite what I wanted but was still enjoyable.

Rating: 4 Stars

Original Review @ Metaphors and Moonlight (link in profile)

cands.text:
3 Stars

*I received a free ecopy of this book via Netgalley in exchange for an honest review.*

I don't think there was anything particularly wrong with this book, and other people may enjoy it, but I just couldn't really get into it.

There were still some things I liked though. I was really excited for this book because I always get excited when I find sci-fi/fantasy about characters with disabilities or chronic illnesses, and this protagonist had one of his legs amputated. The thing I loved about this book was the uniqueness and poignancy of it. It was also thought-provoking, moving, creative, interesting, horrifying, amusing, and compelling. Maybe if I just keep tossing out adjectives, I'll eventually feel like I'm accurately describing the feeling this book gave me throughout the first half.

When R was explaining and showing what life was like for the zombies, how simple yet kind of sad and meaningless their lives were, those were the parts that were moving and thought-provoking.

Getting to see things from a zombie POV, especially Isaac Marion's version with the whole little zombie society they had and the way these zombies worked, that was the creative and interesting part.

I would be laughing one moment at the absurdity of something, like R's zombie wife leaving him for another man while he was taking care of their adopted zombie kids, then I'd suddenly be frowning and sad a moment later.

Other times I'd be both amused by the creativity but also completely horrified all at once, like when R took his kids to the zombie school---an enclosed space where they trapped live people so they could teach the zombie kids how to attack and eat them.

I haven't seen the movie for this book, but I can't imagine it would even remotely compare because the beauty of this book was in R's emotions and thoughts and perceptions, the sadness and the void in him as a zombie, and what it was like for him to be living in a way but still dead.

Also, I was worried that it wouldn't make sense how Julie could be interested in the guy who killed her boyfriend and that the only reason R would be interested in Julie was because of Perry's memories, but those things actually worked out in a believable enough way.

All that being said, the one major complaint I have is that the book was slow and easy to put down. I never had this, "I have to know what happens next!" feeling.

My second biggest complaint is that the paranormal aspects (like how R was changing, the way Perry somehow communicated with R, and what happened to the Boneys) felt kind of random and deus ex machina.

Oh, and while I'm on the topic of paranormal, I felt like this was a more fantasy than sci-fi take on zombies. I'd consider it sci-fi because it was still post-apocalyptic, but I'd also consider it paranormal/urban fantasy and even metaphysical & visionary because of how it delved into human consciousness and potentially spiritual stuff.

I was also bothered by the invasion of privacy every time R experienced one of Perry's memories. Not only was it an invasion of Perry's privacy, it was an invasion of Julie's too since he experienced memories of intimate moments (I think even sex, but that wasn't shown in the book) between Perry and Julie. I know that was the premise, and it was a cool concept, and I didn't blame R for eating the brains since they gave him life in his otherwise dead world, but the fact that R then went on to be friends with Julie after seeing her in moments when he wasn't supposed to was still unsettling for me.

But overall, as I said, though I found the book slow and had a couple issues, I also found it creative, compelling, and poignant at times and am glad I finally read it.

It turned out, however, that I had the complete wrong idea about this book; I thought it would be a dark slave/master romance/erotica---which, aside from the dark part, I don't even usually like, so why exactly did I think this would be my kind of book?---but that wasn't what it was like at all.

The series did have a romance that started out as slave/master, but it wasn't some immediate jump from one to the other in a Stockholm Syndrome sort of way. In fact, there was zero romance in Book 1 and only a kind of potential romance in Book 2 (even though you know what's going to happen from the start). Plus, the slave thing was terrible but in a believable sort of way rather than being ridiculously extreme the way I was expecting it to be considering books tend to err on the extreme side of things and considering I have read so much worse in other books [hidden spoiler can be found in my review on my blog or Goodreads].

Ok, yes, the general debauchery and sexual abuse in the palace was excessive (so don't go into this book expecting something clean), but even that was written in a way that kind of didn't seem overdone? I guess I was able to believe that the nation of Vere, or at least those living in the palace, were just like that and that it was all normal to them. I mean, all the nations had sex slaves or pets, so if I could believe that, it wasn't much more of a stretch to believe they treated them horribly and made them "perform" in arenas and whatnot in Vere.

As for the things I liked about the book (since everything I've said so far was kind of just explanation)...

I loved the writing. It was so eloquent. I learned a lot of new words, but it never felt like the author went crazy with a thesaurus. The writing matched the story and Damen's character perfectly and was just a pleasure to read.

And speaking of Damen, he was another thing I loved. He was actually smart, did what he needed to, kept quiet sometimes even when people were goading him, didn't get bent out of shape over comparatively little things, etc. He kept his eyes on the goal, which was to escape and get back to his nation. And it was actually understandable the few times when he did mouth off or object or stop cooperating. I couldn't blame him because I probably would've done the same. I was also really glad that he didn't excuse Laurent's cruelty just because Laurent sometimes did something nice. He knew that Laurent was manipulative and only did things when he had something to gain from it. He didn't let himself be drawn in by Laurent's charms. I told you, no Stockholm Syndrome here.

Laurent was a well-written character too. Not a likeable person (well, I loved him by the end of the series, but that's not what this review is about), but good as a character. Cold and cruel and manipulative and ridiculously smart.

So overall, I was really surprised by this book and didn't want to put it down once I started. I was completely drawn in by the eloquent writing and the complex characters!
