I Put one in a Mac Book Pro, it boots up in 7 seconds now.

Liked it so much I tossed one in my laptop too.

The transfer speeds are snappy even compared to the MX100 I used to run.

The reliability is supposed to be great increased over the previous generation as well.

cands.text:
I'm sure this laptop is now dated.
I've owned it for months and its performed well enough.
The touchpad is garbage though.
ASUS thought they would be clever and jump on the "gesture" bandwagon, all they produced was a annoying pad.

I went to install 8.1 on this system, everything worked great, except there are no 8 or 8.1 drivers for the terrible touchpad.

So with that in mind, this is actually a terrible machine.  Over engineered and under thought.

Good weight and comfortable ergonomics.
My thumb does accidentally find the speed adjustment keys frequently.  So that equals fragged.

I will replace this shortly with something else, but it's always good to try new gear.
Someone with short fingers may find this to be their favorite mouse ever.

Aside from the speed adjust key location, this is a pretty good mouse.
Way better than anything Razer is dishing out these days.
And this is great comparatively beaus you don't need to sign up online for a cloud profile just to install drivers.

Ive had this for about 6 months. Initial setup is simple enough. But thats right about where the good times end.

The movement detection is clumsy and full of False Positives and False Negatives. Meaning it never reliably records. You must pay a subscription fee to properly use this device, but actual useful updates are up sold as Premium access. The audacity of these people.

I recently changed my WiFi password and I can no longer connect to the camera via Bluetooth to update the settings. Ive tried different phones and gone over the procedure a dozen times.

I emailed customer service 5 days ago and have received no response. Well other than the SPAM they will email you.

This security camera was costly and a total joke.
I suggest anyone shopping for one consider something else. The Kuna is your next headache.

Great CPU.  This with my 970GTX allows me to lay waste to all my online adversaries.

Make sure you read current trends in the market before buying this.
The latest isn't always the greatest, but do your homework to be sure.

Surprisingly simple install.
M$ doesn't usually like their customers and you can tell by their service.

With this you will have to create a MS account and use that to download the software.
I didn't have any issues.

For anyone who has used a real gamer keyboard, you don't want this.
Its cheap, the keys stick up, so basically I find myself having to press A,S,D,W or X 2 times to get the input recognized.
A majority of that time results in me being fragged.

If you're just a poser who likes lights and don't play to win, this is your keyboard.
For the money you can get a basic Logitech Keyboard that will prove to be much more reliable.

Good weight, nice tracking.
I've abandoned Razer products since their new Driver Cloud system.
And man I am glad I did.  This thing works better than the last 3 razers I've had, and it's a third of the price.

High quality flashlight that has the convienance of charging on the go. On Turbo mode it will run 1.5 hours.
Which is to be expected. Anyone claiming a life longer than that has put a larger battery in or is defying the laws of physics.

Pretty good little device.
Offers every method of storage and security triggering you would want.

DO CHANGE THE DEFAULT LOGIN INFO AND PASSWORD.
Otherwise you're hosting your own Truman show for the world to see.

Got this today, unpackaged it, popped it into my truck and plugged in my iPhone.

The sound quality was awful. Not even remotely close to being a functional item. Bad unit?  Probably. But I'm returning this to try another brand.

Broke after 3 days of use.
It just started toggling on and off by itself with a full charge. Kept t plugged in to see if that was an issue, it continued to power cycle itself.

SENWOW did reach out to me and sent me a replacement.  So their Customer Service is really good.
I've only been running the replacement for a few days, but will update my review if it holds out or fails.

So the replacement unit has been working OK.
I decided to pull apart the failed unit for some Failure Analysis.

Found the leads to the speaker charred and the chip on U8 blown.

Great value.
The build quality is top notch, I'm impressed.

Update:
Wearing them the fifth time just around town and they broke. An eye tore right off when lacing it up. For $120 Id expect a little.

These boots are terrific.
They broke in quickly and I've seen no quality issues with them.

They're the most comfy boots I've ever worn.

Old school and reliable.
Incredibly industrial build quality.
I expect these to last for years and years.

Got this to keep in a rental car, after about 3 hours into my initial 4 hour drive this thing was dead.
My backup charger worked fine on the same port.

Got this to keep in a rental car, after about 3 hours into my initial 4 hour drive this thing was dead.
My backup charger worked fine on the same port.

Cheap and they work.
On a 1-10 I give the sound quality a 5.
These are easily blown away by even OEM Mac earbuds.
But if you just simply need some cheap earbuds that will work, these are a potential candidate.

Amazing!  I should have bought this years ago.
It just works straight out of the box!

The mouse tracking is decent BUT the dang mat slides all over my desk.
I've never had that issue before with any other mats.

Just as good as the $50 UTG, but fewer features.
This is a budget line that I'm surprised to find Bushnells logo on.

This grip is 11/10.

Installation was easy, it includes everything but a hair dryer.

The heated it up 3 times and massaged it into every crevice.
Don't heat it up too much though, the lower is plastic and can become malleable and deform.

I took my time on it and it looks like it came from the factory with this on.

No Glock is complete without these grips.
With more practice I shall eventually gain control over all matter and time.

I normally wear a size 10, ordered these in a size 10 and they fit fine.

The initial quality and comfort is good.
They're actually nearly as comfortable as Burkenstocks.

The coloring is low on the soles, so you don't actually see it much.
If someone you know wants some sandals for kicking around in this summer, these are a safe purchase.

Dorcy flashlights seem to be the best of the budget flashlights.  They're rugged, bright and reliable.

However one of my recent orders arrived missing a battery.  The packaging was intact, so its a mystery.
Its definitely not ftf.  But is a good emergency tool for the glove box.

users.query: Rather enjoyable to watch.  Cusack is terrific.  This movie is a full-blown "Twilight Zone" on steroids.  I wish the ending would have been more shocking though ... a little disappointing on that front.  (Spoiler alert:) I wish that the hotel manager would have been some sort of behind-the-scenes string puller or the one who benefited from the evil hotel room.  But, that is my only complaint.  Other than the lackluster ending, the movie is a nice mind thriller.

cands.text: This might have been a good movie but the quality and sound are so bad that I turned it off.  The plot was kind of intriguing so I was disappointed to have to nix it due to the poor quality of the film.  Nobody's fault - it's just an old neglected movie.
I love this movie so much.  The acting is terrific and the plot is wonderful.  A great way to spend a rainy afternoon!!!!

This is a VERY low budget film but surprisingly well done.  The only thing that distinguishes this from a high-dollar production is the low budget they had to work with - other than that, the acting is excellent - perhaps even better than professional big-name actors and actresses who "try too hard."  The woman who plays the psycho is so realistic that I have to wonder if she's not nuts and creepy in real life!  If she's a sweetheart in real life, then she deserves an academy award.  It's the humdrum neighborhood and typical mundane setting that makes this movie very interesting - everyone will recognize it from real life.  The rest of the cast is very good too.  The plot is decent ... the doll is out of the Seinfeld episode, so that actually gives the movie an added amusement factor, and there can't be anything wrong with that!  Only watch it if you have nothing else to do though, obviously.

Sheer delight.  Yes, it's a soap opera, but a classy one set in the days when department store customers were treated like royalty, and department stores were BEAUTIFUL.  The background music really sets off the rather light, whimsical plot incredibly well, and the actors really are consummate professionals - engaging and over-the-top (but not too) pure Broadway types.  The plot is really cute: It's like Peyton Place meets a turn-of-the(last)-century London fancy department store - in a GOOD WAY.  Beware though - once you watch this, you will really NOT want to step foot in one of those drab, warehouse box stores ever again and you will find yourself yearning for the days when those who designed department stores had (sorry to say) MUCH more cultivated tastes.  You won't ever go back to  a dreaded/drab Wal-Mart at the very least.  The actor who plays Mr. Selfridge has an incredible grasp of the character and really should be commended.
Terrifically witty and excruciatingly entertaining.  I am hooked, hooked, hooked and "miss" the characters when I'm not watching!  Pure genius.

The acting is fabulous; plots are thought-provoking and exciting (although in season one, the writer's do not yet have their "sea legs," but is forgivable due to FANTASTIC ACTING as well as the fact that the plots get exponentially better and better as the season progresses.  The entire cast is a treasure.
This ranks right up there with Hocus Pocus without the big-name cast.  Very enjoyable and is a MUST for Halloween spooky movie watching.  Just loved it.  Well done.

George Romero's Season of the Witch is a cult classic and a little psychological dark gem.  Well done, quirky and weird.  Romero deserves to be in the same category as Roman Polanski (without the big budget!)

Well done and entertaining (enough.)  I didn't expect anything stellar, but I doubt the creators of this Lifetime channel type show were out to set the world on fire here.  It's a typical "rainy Sunday afternoon" time-passer show.  With that said, it is entertaining in a blase sort of way. Hamlin is excellent as usual and does a great job portraying a psychopath, which is always fun to see (juxtaposed against his L.A. Law character, especially.)  If you have not got a whole heck of a lot to do and want to be mildly but pleasantly entertained, this is pretty good.  The cast is A list, so the acting does not disappoint.

I was considering getting this book (I am a huge Martha Stewart and Barefoot Contessa fan!!!)  So, I read many of the reviews on Amazon, and it seems that a lot of people stated that the bad reviews were due to "sour grapes" and "jealousy."  But when her publisher recently dropped her, that is when I decided not to buy this book.  No sour grapes here, and I could care less about whom she is or is not related to.  I just don't want to waste my money on a book by someone who was immediately dropped by their publisher ....  She obviously is not that talented.  Sorry.

Donald Bain's impeccable writing once again shines.  The book as a great plot, but more than that - the book is just plain old fun to read.  Excellent read for a stormy night under the covers or for on the beach.  For this particular genre, it doesn't get any better than this.  Donald Bain's writing is very sophisticated, and I APPRECIATE THAT.  Not many writers in this genre can compete with Bain.  And what could be better than Bain (real person) mixed with Jessica Fletcher (fictitious character)?  It's a winner.  As usual.  I LOVE the Murder She Wrote books (and TV show!)  Timeless fun.
It is as good as it gets and proves that the mundane is the most fun subject of all!  Larry David is uniquely hilarious as usual with his stellar supporting cast.  Bravo.

This is an especially good season.  The show is its usual witty and hilarious self, but it's a bit more emotionally complex, sophisticated and much more poignant than one would expect.  Larry David is sentimental and sweet in this season in particular.  He shows a side of himself that is endearing and quite touching.  The comedy is over-the-top and unique as usual.  LOVE THIS SHOW.

This is an especially good season.  The show is its usual witty and hilarious self, but it's a bit more emotionally complex, sophisticated and much more poignant than one would expect.  Larry David is sentimental and sweet in this season in particular.  He shows a side of himself that is endearing and quite touching.  The comedy is over-the-top and unique as usual.  LOVE THIS SHOW.

If anyone wants to know the dark truth about how the world really works (and a VERY small minority on the planet has always been destined to find this stuff out and will not be denied) this book is a MUST. The author does an excellent job of pointing out the disturbing similarities between what is taking place in America today with the evils of the Third Reich and the very dark Soviet Empire. Most people don't have the intellectual caliber required to understand this book, however, that is to be expected and there is NO surprise there. The author shines the light of truth upon the dark cabal which (thinks it) runs the planet, and I appreciate this very much. Hats off to the author.

Spencer Tracy and Gene Kelly are about as wonderful as it gets in this movie about the bible thumpers who tried to make it illegal for teachers to teach anything other than Creationism/Religionism regarding the origin of man.  But, this movie is REALLY about how the bible beaters' MAIN GOAL WAS TO GET ATTENTION.  They loved the circus-like atmosphere and the national press attention given to their town.  Their immaturity is on full display here.  But, again, Tracy and Kelly's acting is WONDERFUL and make this movie more than worth watching.
Perfect show.  Dern and cast are marvelous.  Mike White is to be commended for a stellar performance and for his deep, insightful writing.  Want to see these characters do more.

I have watched 3 episodes and am extremely impressed.  For real astrologers (and not pseudo wannabes) this show is an excellent study of the Piscean vibration.  She is confused to the extreme - Laura Dern is absolutely brilliant in her portrayal of a confused woman.  Very fascinating show.

I am a huge Murder She Wrote fan - both the television show and the books by Donald Bain.  Basically, these beautifully written and delightful books are sophisticated "Nancy Drew books" for adults, and that is just about the highest compliment I can give!!!!  Love the characters, settings and plots.  Nothing could be better for curling up and reading when you're at home sick in bed!!

You watch and buy the "SoulfulT brand," (whether via her Youtube shows or her book) in order to bask in the sunshine of this beautiful soul.  End of story.  She is about as real and as endearing as it GETS.  If there were more people like her in the world, the world would be a much better place.  She is smart and lively.  It's not so much about the cooking per se (although she's a natural home cook and is informative and entertaining to the extreme,) it's about HER.  She is WONDERFUL.

Although I usually cook in multi-clad stainless steel, sometimes I want to "go old-fashioned" and use cast iron since it is unmatched for its cooking powers.  For some reason, food cooked in cast iron has a much more appetizing aroma (no clue why.)  I am not interested in seasoning plain cast iron, so I prefer the enamel-coated cast iron.  This pan fits the bill and is a really nice pan.  Fried in in last night, and the food came out perfectly - the house smelled heavenly, which is something that doesn't happen with my stainless steel (which I love too.)  Clean up is a total breeze.  Another fabulous Cuisinart product.  Highly recommend.  By the way - for shallow frying, do not fill the pan with too much oil because the food displaces the oil, and you don't want the oil to slosh out.  The pan is deep enough, but you still have to be very careful.

Wonderful book.  Sara is one of my very favorite television cooks.  She is SO PERSONABLE and intelligent!!!  Wish Amazon would carry her tv shows.  This cookbook is quite different .. lots of ethic flair but very simple and well organized.

These are so useful.  I buttered one, cracked an egg in it, mixed in a little heavy cream, salt and pepper and microwaved the thing for a minute or two, give or take.  And voila.  Out came a luscious little scrambled egg.  I can't wait to use them for chicken pot pie and mini puddings and souffles.  They are also gorgeous.  They stack well.  I have two sets.

Excellent inside story about the 2016 election.  Roger Stone has many years of insider political experience and is also a first-rate writer.  Enjoyed the book very much and finished it in 3 days.  It's very interesting - a page turner.  Could open some eyes.  Might be more Roger Stone books.

Fabulous book written in a easy-to-read, semi-humorous style.  The author brilliantly blows the lid off the allopathic medical industry profit scam.  Highly recommend!!!!!  Make sure to read Confessions of a Medical Heretic by Dr. Robert Mendelson as well.

users.query:
This is the first book that I've read by Jessica Ingro and I can tell you right now, it won't be the last!

Shane Mack MacAllisterholy hell, he is hot a sin! I loved the banter between Mack and Megan (they are absolutely one of my favorite couples), and to be honest, I felt like it only intensified their undeniable attraction to one another. Now the sex scenes *fan self* are not for the faint of heart. They are H-O-T! But this story is so much more than a no strings attached, sexual relationship. They are both still coping with the loss of loved ones, and while they try to keep each other at arms length, there's no denying the magnetic pull to one another. Sometimes the heart knows what it wants, and there's just no use in fighting it.

Sex, drama, suspenseyou can't go wrong with this book! It can be read as a standalone, but I'm going to one-click the first two books right now! Can't get enough of these characters!

cands.text:
Loved this book so much! This is the first book I've read by Jessica Hawkins, and I am beyond impressed with her writing. The characters and their emotions were so well portrayed, I felt as if I was in the room experiencing them alongside Sadie, Nathan, and Finn. Now, I don't condone cheating by any means, but the chemistry and angst between Sadie and Finn was undeniable. I was torn between wanting them to be together and wanting Sadie and Nathan to work things out, but at times Nathan seemed so cold and distant, I couldn't really blame Sadie for straying and looking for affection elsewhere. But as with any relationship, the underlying problems aren't always visible until you're on the outside looking in.

This book had all the best components of a romance novel...drama, angst, heartache, and a modern love that I think most readers can relate too. I enjoyed this book so much, I'm going to one-click the rest of Jessica Hawkins works!

I was pleasantly surprised by this debut novel from author V. Murphy, and I was immediately sucked in from the very beginning.

Things between Harper and Ryder started out rocky. They both have painful pasts and secrets continued to cause strain on their relationship. But sometimes two people are thrown together when least expected, and what lies beneath all of the secrets can bring them even closer together.

I'm really looking forward to the sequel!

4.5 Stars!

This is the first book I've read by Staci Hart, and it definitely won't be the last. The cover and blurb immediately drew me in, and from page one I was hooked. Ms. Hart really knows how to start off with a bang!

Now, I've read my fair share of friends-to-lovers books, and this one is something special. I mean this book has everythinga tight knit group of friends who always have each others' backs, steamy sex scenes that will have you squirming in your seat, enough drama to get your blood boiling, and witty humor that even had me laughing out loud along with the characters.

I don't want to give away the story, but I will say this: Lily and West spent so much time fighting off what they both knew was there all along, but the heart wants what it wants. Sometimes it's better to take a risk than leave yourself forever wondering "what if".

Overall, I loved the story and this author's style of writing. The characters were definitely relatable. I couldn't help but love Lily's humorous personality, and West was the perfect balance for her. The story flowed well and kept me wanting more. I could definitely see some of the supporting characters getting their own books too. Can't wait to read more from Staci Hart!

Loved it! By far Erika's best book yet!

This was a beautifully written story of two people running from their pasts and brought together when they were least expecting to find love. But no love story is without obstacles, and while they're living their lives trying to please everyone else, they overlook that maybe they are the ones needing to be saved themselves. The love Dani and Holden share is undeniable, but is that enough to keep them together or will they continue to let others dictate the paths their lives will take?

Definitely a must read! You won't be disappointed!

LOVED this book! So different from the other Motorcycle Club romance books I've read, which I found to be extremely refreshing!

Jasper (aka Angel) and Eden are the perfect couple, and even time and distance couldn't keep them apart. When Eden comes back into town she looks to the Angel Warriors MC for protection for her and her sister, but the last person she expected to come across was her former boyfriend, Jasper. Worlds collide and emotions run high, but will the lies they are hiding from one another tear them apart, or can they push through their past indiscretions and find a future together?

This book really was fantastic and the character development was simply perfection. I could feel the love, tension, and fear surrounding all of them, and it only drew me in even more. And the endlet me just say I need to next book NOW! A wonderful, suspenseful MC romance that will have you crawling back for more. I highly recommend it!

It's not easy to top the first book in a series, but Tarryn nailed it! Thief threw me through an emotional whirlwind right up until the very end. Thank you for showing us that relationships aren't perfect, love isn't perfect...but even through all of the pain and heartache, if it's meant to be, love will find a way to bring you back to the one that never should have gotten away.

This book has everything a romance reader could ask for...sexy characters, steamy scenes, secrets and deception,  plus a whole lot of drama. Emotions will run wild as you read this standalone novel, but it is so worth it by the end. Dawn's character development is something that has always drawn me into her books, and Twisted Up In You confirms that this is definitely one of her strengths. Plus, the Angel Warriors MC is referenced throughout this book, so if you loved her MC series, this is right up your alley!

I really enjoyed this book! Now let me start off by saying that I haven't read the first two books in the series; luckily this story can be read as a stand-alone (but I REALLY want to read the first two now).

Ryan is pretty awesome and not like a lot of the lead males in romance books these days. I feel like a lot of authors portray male characters as these sexy alpha a**holes, but Ryan is sexy and sweet without even trying. I can see why Sofia was apprehensive about starting anything with him because of his job and the image he has to portray for customers, but hes just your average guy looking for love. Thank god for Grant urging Sofia to give Ryan a chance because they really are perfect for one another. And did I mention how much I loved Grant?! I think he was my favorite character. The banter between him and Ryan was hilarious and flowed so well.

Some parts of the book did move a little slower than I wouldve liked, especially since it took so long for Ryan and Sofia to finally get together. And once that happened the story progressed rather quickly. But other than the pacing, I thought it was great and highly recommend it.
I was hooked from the very first page! An enticing storyline with painful pasts, uncertain futures, and loveable characters I just couldn't get enough of...this book had it all! Highly recommend!

4.5 Stars!

Loved it! I feel like this book cleared up a lot of pivotal moments that took place in Sharing Harper. Harper and Ryder are still battling issues from their past, and when Ryder and his ex-wife, Kylie, are invited to a wedding in Texas, it causes Harper to doubt how genuine his feelings really are for her. Ryder will always have a connection to Kylie, being that she is the mother of his child, but Kylie threatens to move to Texas with Evelyn, and Ryder is faced with having to choose between the woman he loves and being closer to his daughter. Things only get worse when Harper shows up in Texas and has to face seeing Ryder in the arms of his ex-wife. Is their relationship strong enough to get past the issues that continue to haunt them, or is their relationship bound to crash and burn?

And FYI...the epilogue...holy crap I need the next book now!

This was a fantastic debut novel from Ashley Erin! The way she brought the story to life, from the character development to setting the scene, was simply perfect. Her style of writing kept me captivated from the first page to the last, and by the time I reached the end I was dying for more. I think what I loved most was that these characters weren't glamorized. No millionaire playboys or rockstars or athletesjust normal, every day people living through experiences anyone might possibly encounter. Emma was definitely relatable and I could empathize with what she was going through. Thankfully her childhood friends were there to help her pick up the pieces after she had lost so much. The way Dane gingerly broke down her walls and swept her off her feet had me swooning hard for him. But at times, I did feel that their reunion as friends and their progression into something more was a bit rushed. I often found myself questioning what exactly it was attracting them to one another, but I think the underlying mutual feelings had always remained, even as kids. The supporting characters were just as well written and I'm really looking forward to reading the next book in the series, All About Hope!

This is the first book I've read in the series, and I simply loved it! I'm a sucker for books pumped full of heart racing angst, and Emeralds did not disappoint! Now, I will say that once I read through the first half of the book, I wasn't sure how I felt about Trihn and Preston's budding relationship. The physical chemistry was there for sureK.A. Linde is a seasoned veteran in that department. However, I didn't feel the emotional connection between them. It was frustrating in the beginning, and I found myself questioning why they were together (other than for steamy, panty-melting sex). But once the plot thickens and drama ensues Oh lawd! I couldn't stop reading! I ate the pages up so quickly, my head was spinning by the time I had finished it. I don't want to spoil anything, but this book is so worth reading! Another gem from K.A. Linde!
Another amazing book from Ms. Molly! And I have a confessionI loved Trent! Seriously, how do you make someone's captor so damn sweet and sexy?!

I read this a few months ago and absolutely loved it! I loved all of the characters (<3 Chase!) and thought Molly presented them very well. This book really broke my heart though...I've never had a book affect me so much. As much as I hated the one bad scene, the way everything came together in the end was perfect!

In response to one of the reviews that said the story was not realistic or believable...it's just a story. It doesn't have to be 100% believable. That's what make it so enjoyable!

Oh.my.goodness! Absofreakinlutely LOVED this book! I've been team Aiden since the beginning and this book just proved why! I'm so hooked on this series...and with an ending like that, I'm dying for more! Can't wait for Love Me!

4.5 Stars!

Let me start out by asking...where is my invitation?! But seriously, this book was hot as hell! The perfect combination of sweet and sexy, with a hint of forbidden romance.

Booker and Peyton are both lawyers, and it's clear they are passionate about their jobs. But when a case brings Peyton to Sensation, an exclusive sex club where her client is a member, she discovers that Booker isn't just a beast in the courtroom. Things begin to heat up between them as they take on the risk of seeing one another, but is it really worth it to put their careers on the line?

This book had the perfect amount of sexy scenes, with
some light BDSM and a whole lot of passion. Overall it was a great read!

What happens when you cross a professional cuddler with an MMA fighter? A blazing inferno of sexual chemistry neither one of them can deny.

I have to say it is quite refreshing to read such a unique and well written book, especially one touching on a profession that not many know really exists. Professional cuddler? Yup, you read that right. But there is so much more to Jade's story than just giving people a bit of affection in return for money. With Ryland being to ultimate alpha male that he is, I knew right off the bat that cuddling wouldn't be enough to tame the savage within him. When he hires Jade to go on tour with him, the heat bubbling between them only intensifies, and while Jade tries to fight to keep their relationship professional, she isn't entirely immune to the sexy fighter's advances. As with any relationship, the pasts never truly stays in the past, and Jade is once again thrown through a loopthis time with Ryland along for the ride.

If you've never read any of Emma Rider's books, I highly recommend them! She has such a way with words that you can't help but be drawn into her books. Grab your copy of WANT because this is one story you won't want to miss out on!

Love's Suicide was one of my favorite books in 2014, and I think Love Survives very well may be my favorite in 2015!

Going into this book, I was worried that it might be the same exact story spewed out from Brooks' POV, but I was pleasantly surprised that it was so much more! Watching Brooks internal struggle, as his brother Branch kept him and the girl he'd loved since he was a child apart, was heart-wrenching and downright frustrating. But one night, one life altering mistake, sent Brooks', Branch's, and Kat's lives in opposite directions.

Brooks thought by enlisting in the military he'd save himself the pain of having to endure watching Branch and Kat together, but in reality, what he saw and experienced overseas weighed even more heavily on him. My heart broke reading through those chapters, and I went through quite a few tissues before reaching the end of this book.

Kat continued to struggle as well, and seeing it through Brooks' eyes nearly destroyed me. They had both been through so much apart, I wasn't sure if they'd ever find their way back to one another.

If you've never read any of Jennifer Foor's books, I highly recommend Love Survives. It's well worth the emotional turmoil she'll put you through!

I was honored to read an ARC of Teach Me Love and enjoyed every second of it!

Let me just start off by saying, there is nothing sexier than a man who loves kids. That alone had me swooning so hard for Jacob Greene. The chemistry between Jacob and Abigail is undeniable, and it doesn't take long for them to realize that they might just be the ones to help each other heal and move on.

This breathtaking story tugged at my heart from the first page to the last, but S. Moose found a way to mend it whole again. With characters you cannot help but fall in love with, Teach Me Love will put your emotions to the test and make you question whether love really can overcome the ghosts of your past.

I highly recommend this book! You won't be able to put it down!

One of the best books I've read this year!

I love Jennifer Foor's style of writing and how easily I fall in love with her characters. This book is right up there with the entire Mitchell Family Series (which just so happens to be one of my favorites). I think Colt and Tyler have some competition now because Brooks Valentine simply stole my heart!

LOVED this book! I was able to connect with the characters instantly, and the emotions they evoked in me were all over the place! Their pain, sadness, heartache...I felt it all! And at times I wanted to shake Briar and Arrow and make them open their eyes and see what they had right in front of them! But I will say, I was very happy with the way this book ended, and I can't wait to read more from Bayli Lane. She's a wonderful writer and always has a way of drawing me in with her words.

Loved this book so much! Dawn and Chantal did an amazing job! I fell in love with Kade when he was first introduced in Chase, but now I love him even more!

Kade's playful cockiness immediately drew me in, but soon you find that he has a huge heart as well. Unfortunately that gets him into trouble when Nikki and Ashley butt heads, and he is forced to choose between the woman he loves and the friend he promised to always protect.

Highly recommend this book and I looked forward to reading Ryder's story!

Silla Webb is one of those up and coming authors who shines through everything she writesand Lies Beneath the Surface is no different! Simply put, I loved this book. I really liked that the story began in the past from Colton's POV, and then rolled right into where book 1 left off when Carly Jo found out she was pregnant. Colton is immediately flooded with similar feelings he had when his daughter Heidi Jo was born, but little does he know, this time he might not be the father. Throughout the book I tried to guess who it was and to be honest, I wasn't sure who I wanted to be the father. I loved both Colton an Luke and knew either one would stick by Carly Jo no matter what.

I also really liked that Carly Jo's sister, Savannah, was a much more prominent character in this book. My heart ached for her, and I just wanted to wrap her up in my arms and tell her everything was going to be alright, but at the same time I wanted to shake some sense into her and tell her to open up her eyes to the lies surrounding her.

If you thought Covered in Coal was full of secrets and suspense, just wait until you read this book! You won't want to miss out once they're revealed!

users.query: I can't get enoughoff this instamental. I heard it on an episode of the leftovers and have had it on a playlist ever since.

cands.text: This is a rare find, and it's like fresh air, hearing a song that is about being content.

This is a great song, the content and sound make this one a BUY! BUY! BUY! (*thanks Jim Cramer). I would think that some think this song sounds like a "more holier than thou" theme, but I don't see it like that. I see it as looking more at one's self and trying to overcome pride in how you may feel people should treat you.
I could not pass up the $.25 price tag on this song. I probably would not have bought it otherwise. it may come in handy.
This song gets the blood flowin' I always have this on my workout playlists because it's just got that tone to it. Oldie but a goodie.
I like when this song comes on my playlist. I was at the Hard Rock Cafe a little while ago and it was playing in there... So it must be cool.
I like when this song comes on my playlist. I was at the Hard Rock Cafe a little while ago and it was playing in there... So it must be cool.

This song is awesome! I heard it on the radio and downloaded it instantly so I could listen to it again. The drums in this song really get me going, it's a rush of energy for me. It's kind of rocky/metal with a slight hint of some funk maybe. I listened to the album after I got this song, nothing really jumped to me like this song, so this is the only song I own from this album and group. I'm not sure what it is but the songs seems different to me than the other stuff I listen to, it's a nice change.

After playing guitar hero world tour, I put this song on my list. I've heard this song so many times and I still like it. I like the songs that you don't really get sick of hearing. This is one of them for me.

I waited a long time for this song to make it to Amazon mp3. I'm glad it's here, I think this song came out after DMX fame started dwindling. His music confuses, one song is a prayer the next is a murder. When it comes down to it, the song sounds good. I guess that's why we listen to it.

I had already bought the Adorn single, but once the album came out, I listened to all songs on here, then I listened to the full versions on youtube. After hearing the songs I wound up buying the album. I don't think there is one song that I skip over on this album when listening to it. He's got a unique sound.

As I am writing this, the machine is downloading it's latest firmware update. I recall some people complained of long download times. Please make sure that the Ethernet settings are appropriate for your home network, as the default connection speed is only 56k. I have mine set to 768k (sounds right) and the downloading process took only 20 minutes, approximately.

*cracks a can of Red Bull*

ahh, where was I...

Oh yes. To connect to your home network router, first connect a suitable ethernet (cat5) cable to the A35 and the router. For me, the router is two rooms away and I didn't want to be bothered with going out and buying a wireless modem for the dvd player before I know it will be worthwhile, so I retrieved my 75 foot long cat5 cable and ran it from the router to the player up above the TV. This was necessary, as I do not have an appropriate video-in on the computers to view the setup screens. I realize not just anyone has a 50+ foot long cat5 cable laying around, so you will need to do the needful so that you can be connected to your router and have access to a television.

Now, power up the A35 and go into Ethernet. The user's guide is very clear on how to do this, and worked for me just fine. Set DCHP to on and DNS to on (DNS is obtained via DCHP). Press confirm and wait a few seconds. If your IP address changes to one that seems correct (such as 192.168.1.102 or similar), then press OK to accept the changes. It is OK if your gateway is 0.0.0.0, at least it was for me.

Power off the machine. Wait a few seconds. Power it back on.

Now choose General->Maintenance->Update and run through the OK screens (license agreement or w/e that is). The player should now see the update server and will display a message that it is updating and to not power it off. Sound advice.

With a decent cable connection, you should be done in half an hour. The player will power itself off when the update is complete.

Turn it back on. Do not worry about setting the time (again). There is a setting in the menu to have the player obtain time/date settings automatically via the network. Since turning that feature on, it has stopped nagging me with the set date screen on boot up.

Unfortunately, I am still waiting on my Samsung LNT4069FX to arrive, so I cannot comment yet on upscaling. However, I just put in my widescreen version of Conan The Barbarian (a never-endingly great classic) and it works and looks just fine.

Boot time is about 30-35 seconds, well within reason. You're only going to notice it if you forget to power on the player until the last moment. Make sure it's the first thing you do before pulling the film, grabbing drinks, getting comfy, etc.

The remote seems well-made and is very functional. There is a dedicated slow-motion button that shifts between 1/2, 1/4, and 1/8th speed frame rates. There is also a dedicated frame-forward button when paused. It has a very robust repeat system, which can repeat All, Title, Chapter, or point A-B.

The inclusion of TV controls (channel, vol, source, mute, power) on the remote is very nice and putting in the code is a cinch with a dedicated TV CODE button.

The user guide is very clear and informative, although I do not see anything regarding the persistent storage (128MB). It seems to be used for storing content downloaded from the internet that pertains to your movies, or for future feature upgrades to the player itself (from the A2 product description).

Allegedly, the resume function only works on standard DVD and only if you keep the disc in the player. It clears the memory if you open the tray. Since all the HD-DVDs I have are going to be used as presents, I'm hesitant to open one for testing. I will take their word for it, though, as I've seen other users complain of resume not working.

I wish the USB port was functional already for playing images or video (divx, h. 264), but that's a minor point, as I'm going to be connecting one of our computers to the LCD tv when it arrives via an extended S-VGA patch cable.

Overall, this thing seems to be working fine. I will give an update once the Samsung arrives and I have had a chance to test it out.

Oh, and don't support Sony's proprietary Blu-ray format - they are already controlling too much of the entertainment industry as it is. The PS3 is a trojan horse attempt to establish a blu-ray infrastructure so that everyone who owns one will be coerced into buying Sony blu-ray discs by default. Very, very clever marketing strategy. I like Sony, but I don't approve of the way they are trying to manipulate and control all sides of the industry, from production, to the disc format, to the players themselves. They are going for it all, perhaps, partially as vengeance for their failed BETAMAX format. I like the idea of the hard coating (not the extremely thin layer of plastic), but I just don't think it's a good idea letting Sony rule all aspects of the film/entertainment industry, a monopoly in their own right. HD-DVD, with more layers, has a potential of around 140GB, which is more than enough for anything in the near future. Also, there is the new holographic technology coming out. So stop thinking size is all that matters between formats, because it's not; keeping Sony contained, so that prices are more competitive, is what matters.

I hate to title my review after others, but that's just what this little guy is. Our house has anywhere from 2-4 computers (including the laptop) connected to the network, and it's not so much the number of computers that's any problem - it's the question of how to access the music stored on those computers easily to get it playing over the central entertainment system. Well, the quest hasn't been an easy one... it started with a, dun dun dun! Linksys Wireless-G Music Bridge. Probably the most useless and "fail" product ever. Trying to configure it properly was a disaster.  All of the settings would look right, but the thing just wouldn't connect! Sometimes, magically, I was able to get it working, but not for long. I'd try to use it again the next day and it would be unresponsive. Finally I junked it and decided to try an Apple Airport Express. Similar experience, with tedious and iffy configuration. I got it working, but it just didn't seem all that great, and it would fall offline sometimes, like the Linksys. So I took the Airport back to the store and looked around some more. It was then that I spotted the Roku. More expensive but, hey, it looked well made and actually had a text screen, and so, desperate and intrigued, I took home the Roku with my breath held.

Plugged it in, the screen came up, and it found my wireless router in a few seconds. Gave it the encryption key, crossed my fingers, and hit OK. After a moment or two... TADAA! It was connected and I was amazed! Two minutes of button pushing on the Roku remote and I was done. I never even had to visit the computer. Mental kudos to the Roku designers from me!

From there I just had to make sure the computers were set to share their music libraries over the network (Vista) so that the Roku could see them and access the music. Once that was done they popped right up on the Roku's screen and I was able to select one and browse it however I liked (playlists, server containers/folders, etc.). The music quality, as others have stated, is rather excellent. The specs say the following:

400MHz processor
16MB RAM
20-bit D/A Converter
~96dB Signal to Noise
90dB dynamic range adjustment
20Hz - 20kHz frequency handling
up to 48kHz sample rate
up to 16 bit stereo

So with these specs you get great audio performance. I don't think I've ever had a song sound "wrong" through the Roku, which is a good thing.

You also have access to a great number of internet radio stations with the Roku's built-in browser, which was a nice surprise to me and a great little bonus! You can search by favorites, genres, names, or keyword.

So to conclude, if you have a large mp3 collection that you would really like to hear over your home stereo system and a wireless network, this product is one of the best and easiest ways to make it happen.

Since moving into our current house and with the establishment of our wireless network, I've gone through some grief trying to connect the family computers' music collection to the central sound system in the main family room / den. Our setup consists of a Motorola broadband modem wired to a Linksys Wireless-G router wired to the two computers in the study. There is one wireless access point in the den, as well as a new, third computer, which connects to the wireless network via a Linksys WMB54G Music Bridge (I'll explain).

Last Christmas, I bought the Linksys Music Bridge for my parents, with the idea of broadcasting music to it from the computers located in the den. I had read about the problems encountered with trying to make it work, but I saw it as my only real option at the time and decided to risk it. Following some of the user-created tutorials here and elsewhere on the net, I managed to get it working for periods at a time. I say periods at a time, because inevitably, it would lose connectivity and the bridge software would not be able to pick it up, requiring me to tinker with it to try and reestablish a connection. Recently, it seemed to stop connecting altogether.

I read about the Apple Airport Express, so I picked one of those up. I brought it home from Best Buy and plugged it into a socket just behind the main entertainment system's cabinet. It has one light that blinks amber if there is a connection issue or solid green for an established connection with the network. Going through the configuration routine a couple times, I was able to get it to connect to our wireless network without nearly as much trouble as I had 8 months prior with the WMB54G. The only drawback to the Airport Express is that you can only access it with iTunes, which, when an external speaker connection is detected, creates a dropdown box in the lower area of the main window that lets you select which external speakers or Airport you would like to output to. To me, this felt a bit limiting, but I would probably have lived with it, had I not encountered an anomaly:

Now, I was planning to junk the WMB54G, but we had just bought a third computer (den), which of course needed a way to connect with the network. On a whim, I plugged it into the Linksys Music Bridge. Lo, and behold, it was able to use the Music Bridge like a wireless modem! (so it wasn't a total loss, after all). However, opening iTunes, it was somehow unable to see the Airport Express, and despite my efforts, I never could get the dropdown box to appear. I wasn't about to have a 2/3 solution, so back the Airport Express went. I scanned the isle, and there was the Roku M1000. It looked promising and well-made, so I bought it.

I cannot describe how cool this thing is! Setup of the Roku M1000 to the network was a real pleasure, for a change! In the first place, all setup configuration is performed at the Roku itself, using the remote and the display, which sure beats the heck out of going through a setup routine at every computer on the network! The Roku is an electronic Einstein compared to the others. It found and displayed the network name on the screen. I told it to connect. It immediately acquired all the right IP/gateway information without me having to baby it. Awesome!

Second, the Roku is smart enough to be able to scan for and find music sharing servers on the network by itself, without any additional software installed on each computer. I have not tried WMP specifically yet, but so far, whenever I have had one or all of the computers running iTunes with sharing enabled, the Roku would always find and display their library names on the screen. Sweet! Then it's just a matter of choosing one, and deciding which browsing method to use. That simple! It also will connect to hundreds of internet radio stations, right out of the box! So, even if you have not set up a music collection on your PC, you can still use it. It also shouldn't be overlooked that, unlike other devices, you don't have to go to the computer to play music from it. Since the Roku has its own display, you can browse and change the music right there, using the remote.

When I contrast my experiences regarding other devices, such as the Linksys Music Bridge and Apple Airport Express, both of which are more limiting and more prone to setup issues, with the Roku M1000, I feel that everyone wanting to get music from their PCs to their home stereo system should be made aware of this little guy, as it is by far the easiest and most versatile solution out there.

I've owned one of these guys for about 8 months now, and it has never worked consistently. Following some of the helpful online tutorials, I was able to get it working - for a while. Like many others say, you are potentially bound for hours of headaches with this thing.

If you are interested in a wireless music solution for getting music off your PC to a home stereo system, let me do you a big favor and steer you toward one of the devices made by Roku, such as the M1000.

Seriously, avoid this. Get an M1000 or better. I did, and it solved my entire problem and then some.

This receiver was much deeper than the old Technics it replaced, so I had to relocate it to the center cabinet, on the top shelf above our very nice Samsung lcd TV (<3 Samsung). Running the wires was, by far, the hardest part with the setup at my parent's house, because they have this big, fancy, wooden set of entertainment cabinets pressed within 8 inches of the back wall, so it is tricky moving a lot of cables around back there.

Well, we have just gone from 5.1 surround to 9.1 surround with this sucker, (if you count the Presence speakers). Two Bose 301 Series bookshelf speakers  serve as the front mains, then there are 7 Klipsch speakers - 4 in the upper corners of the room (presence and rear surround) and two more, placed halfway back, along the sides of the room (known simply as the surround speakers). I haven't really tested whether the presence speakers do much yet (depending on the DVD, of course), but the side surrounds really add to the experience and allow effects from the DVD to be placed more accurately around you.

I believe that Yamaha is known for the quality of their Receiver/Amplifiers and so far I don't have any doubts. The auto-setup works well as a starting point and seems to be very perceptive (accurate) in measuring the speaker distances. It also checks the speakers against cross-wiring, which is a nice touch... I did not even know it, but the rear left surround had been crossed since forever, and this little, I mean big, guy brought it to my attention! I really like the feature set this thing has. You can set the initial volume when it is powered up, as well as set the maximum volume allowed, so it will never be possible to accidentally crank the volume too high and blow your ears or a speaker out. I did have an issue with the pre-out for the sub... it didn't seem to always be "on", with certain sound programs (8 channel enhanced audio), so I also wired the sub from the front speaker leads and this lets it work consistently, regardless, and therefore sound better. I will have to look into that again, as to why the .1 was not utilized, or did not seem to be working, for the 8 channel enhanced audio program.

I may write more later, but overall I am pleased and impressed and it is what I expected from Yamaha. I probably wouldn't trust another brand.

So I've been house-sitting for my parents while they are on vacation and decided now was the time to force-upgrade the bedroom and guest bedroom TVs, taking away the terrible little (if at least functional) Dynex sets. I scoured the internet for info on all current 32" TVs. The next step up, at 40", was too big for the locations.

At first I stuck to my guns and went with good ol' Samsung. That TV was edge lit and had a too-noticeable bleed spot in the upper-right part of the screen. I took it back, went home and debated. I decided that I really did not like Samsung's mono stands, and their 'V' stands seemed very flimsy. This was while considering their premium 32" version J6300. In desperation, I decided to look at Vizio TVs and, as BB had closed for the night, I went to WM. I bought the only set they had, which was the D32x-D1.

I took it home and set it up. The picture, I noticed, was pretty good right out of the box! After some minor tweaks, which I'll mention here --

backlight to 64
brightness to 32
contrast to 64
color to 50
tint left at 0
sharpness to 64
color temp normal
black detail off
backlight control on
reduce noise left at low/low
game latency off
film mode auto
gamma left at 2.2

-- I was actually very pleased with the image. Using my Galaxy S6 Edge as a reference, I had compared skin tone, colors, and contrast (including black levels) while making the above adjustments.

The results were very comparable, although I did stop down the color on the TV to 50, as phone screens tend to be saturation-heavy.

In my estimation, Vizio's direct lit full-array screen is superior to the edge lit Sammy, in terms of consistency. The built-in grey tests were nice and flat with no bleeding or leaking at all. Black levels on the Vizio are also very good -- appearing to me to be essentially as deep as on my phone.

The bevel is nice and thin and the overall appearance of the set is appealing. I bought a Chromecast for each in order to bypass relying on the Vizio apps, which I think everyone ought to do. You can throw any content, be it music, photo, or video, from a phone or laptop (or macbook) to a Chromecast enabled TV with just a couple taps/clicks. The Chromecast is also useful in showing the time and temperature, while the display is idle.

But enough about my discovery of Chromecast. I'm here to talk about this TV.

This particular model (D32x-D1) comes with a fantastic remote with quality buttons (most are rubberized) that have a satisfying 'click' to them. One of my three wishes would be that all remotes felt this way. I love the Samsung remotes, but I am loving this one just as much, if not more! To be clear, this is the full size remote with the quick buttons for Xumo, Netflix, and iHeart along the top. An important detail, as I had mistakenly bought an E-series 32" Vizio for the second screen and found it comes with a very basic and unattractive remote, because that TV expects you to make most of your settings changes, including setup, with your smartphone or tablet. I found that an awful pain (some of the settings in the app seemed to not even work). Immediately took that one back and made sure to get another D32x-D1. I absolutely wanted the full and proper remote.

As an aside, I also found the colors on the E series set to be inferior (or at least harder to get looking right). Surprising, as I assumed the E series was supposed to be a step up from the D series, but found this not to be the case! At least in terms of this budget set. Picture brightness and color depth seemed similar.

The on-board speakers in the Vizio are far better than the ones in the Samsung, as they are both louder and clearer. Despite that, I broke down and bought a Sonos Playbar during my first trip to BB, which turned out to be another surprise, if a much more expensive one. (The store demo does NOT give you a true sense of what it can sound like when it has walls and ceilings). This TV plus the Playbar are a Heavenly match for casual bedroom watching. I'll likely feel compelled to get another Playbar to go with the other set (so I do hope these will hold up).

Compared to the slightly more expensive Samsung, I find the Vizio menus a breeze to navigate (I was afraid they would be inferior), and there are options to customize just about anything, including a sleep timer for music-only playing (Chromecast may interfere with this), the normal idle sleep timer (important for dozing off to something), a color tuner (for very fine adjustments), as well as some intelligent designs: On the Samsung, there's an option to disable 'volume disabled' screen reminders when you have the internal speakers off and you're adjusting volume for the Playbar. The Vizio does not have this option, BUT, it intelligently turns off the reminder after the first instance, for the duration of the current session, as far as I can tell. Now that's what I call a smart TV!

In summary, I feel like the D32x-D1 is among the best 32" TVs out there. Unless you really want to use your phone (or tablet), make sure when buying that you are getting this model, or that it at least includes the full size remote.

BUYER BEWARE

I bought three of these initially -- one for a DVR expanded storage, one for my parents win10, and one for my work imac.

All three stay on 24/7.

So far, two have died within a few months of purchase, in roughly the same fashion -- I start seeing drive disconnection warnings, and then some weeks later the drives no longer recognize in the OS, even after disconnecting the Duet from power for 5 minutes and then reconnecting and turning back on -- the blue LED lights will no longer light up and it seems that something in the Duet relating to the disk interface is prone to premature failure. The unit on the DVR and on the win10 machine have not suffered this yet, so I'm guessing it's some randomness combined with either quality control issues or else a design or component flaw.

This is extremely frustrating! As the one at work is critical for accessing production data! Luckily, I did invest in a TS-459 Pro+ a few years back, so that has been serving as a slower yet perfectly reliable storage method, while I deal with the failing Duet.

Luckily I found one of the receipts and was able to successfully RMA one of the Duets for a replacement.

KEEP YOUR RECEIPTS.

Should you buy these from B&M stores like BB or F's. With Amazon, at least, you always have proof of purchase in your account, which is how I SHOULD have bought them.

I would advise you to avoid the BlacX Duet (and the single version) at all costs. Maybe try the Cable Matters version, like I'm doing.

I haven't toyed very much with it yet, but I intend to expand this review as I do so. I only have the two front channels + center connected at the moment, but I do plan to wire up an additional 2 to 4 surround speakers plus a DefTech Pro 1000 sub and give it a thorough audio test. I'm sure the neighbors will love me when that time comes.

I also will soon test the front USB port for controlling an iPod and see how well that works.

One of the principal reasons that I bought this is that I've hated how most every receiver out there is HUGE in size. I always wished for something a bit more elegant. I discovered that Marantz would be releasing this slimline model purely by chance! Now it is mine at last... and it's definitely the most stealthy receiver I've ever seen! The front panel can be made to auto-off so, right now, it looks like the unit is completely powerless when it is exactly the opposite.

As far as heat is concerned, though I'm hardly cranking it, the large area of top venting seems to dissipate the heat efficiently before it has a chance to build up inside the unit. This is a good thing, since the other major reason for buying it was to fit within the confines of my TV stand's built-in component shelf, which is barely 5 1/2" high. It seems to have ample breathing room, more than I originally estimated, which is really impressive!

I feel like I owe Marantz a big thanks.

The G35 allows modification of Bass and Treble levels, so I boosted them as follows: bass: +9 treble: +9.

The G35 was tested in stereo mode (surround virtualization off). Now let's begin...

G35: 4 koss: 4.5 shure: 3.5

G35: 4 koss: 3.5 shure: 4.5
Brightness:
G35: 4 koss: 3 shure: 4.5
Comfort:
G35: 2.5 koss 4.5 shure 4.5
Construction:
G35: 4.5 koss: 3 shure: 4.5

Now let's run the numbers...

Value:
Logitech G35 - 19
Koss UR40 - 18.5
Shure SR240 - 21.5

With bass and treble maxed out, the G35 has enough bass to satisfy and is tighter sounding than the UR40. The cord is thick, surrounded by a woven material, and feels like it would be very difficult to damage accidentally (short of yanking on it or kicking the USB plug). The headphones themselves seem very sturdy and the adjustment band is metal. With the phones against your head, they seem to hold fast and do not feel like they might slip down. The faux leather pads are cushy but lack the width and pressure distribution of the UR40 and SRH240. Considering that the G35 applies the most pressure around the ears, this can cause comfort issues with prolonged wear. I was able to minimize the discomfort by adjusting the phones downward so that they were pressing against the ears as little as possible. As long as your ears are not terribly large, you should be able to find a reasonably comfortable position. Make sure that if you play with the Voice Morphing Preview option found in the utility program, that you disable it when done, as left on it can cause a slight humming noise. The microphone has a flexible rubber arm that folds conveniently out of the way when not needed and I found the pickup quality to be fine. The voice morph is a gimmick more than useful, unless they decide to add better morphs in an update.

The UR40 seems inherently biased toward the low end and gives the most impressive bass without modifications. Without comparing to other headphones, the sound is very acceptable. However, after listening to the G35 and SRH240, the UR40 sounds muddy in the highs and mids by comparison. I still like the sound, despite that, and it does have exceptional bass response. The deal breaker for me is the flimsy construction quality, despite a lifetime warranty. The entire thing is plastic and the joints that attach the phones to the adjustment bands look unnecessarily fragile. The cord is also on the short side and very thin. Despite appearing closed, the UR40 is vented and quite open to environmental sounds, which can be good or bad depending on what you want. The comfort mesh around the top is notorious for coming loose, thanks to being attached by flimsy little black rubber bands. If you don't mind being prepared to replace them sooner than other headphones, or plan on being careful, these deliver great lows and adequate overall sound for the price.

If you are looking for a clear, bright sound with complimentary lows, the SRH240 delivers just that. The comfort level is on par with the UR40 but the build quality far surpasses it and feels very sturdy. Unlike the G35, it is less physically oppressive and does not apply as much pressure around the ears, which I appreciate. While not as heavy as the UR40, the bass is plentiful and compliments the overall sound very well. It is also a closed back design for good isolation.

If you have access to an equalizer, such as the one found in iTunes, you can compensate for the weaknesses and enhance the strengths of each of these sets to get a great sound, as I am currently proving to myself. I could honestly pick any of these and be happy with the sound, so it's almost more a case of priorities.

I own the AT version of this, but other than that it's the same thing. I have used it so far for...

...an external sound processor for my computer, using a set of DT770 headphones.
...running a record player through a pre-amp, then to the RCA inputs on channel 5/6 of the PV10AT, recording to Garage Band on a Mac Mini via the USB-B connection.
...recording vocals with a shotgun condenser mic, through the mixer channel 1, playing with things like AutoTune (remember, this BT model does not have AutoTune) and effects, which are mostly delays and reverb type effects. There's also a compressor knob for the first 2 channels.

The construction is top notch. The metal chassis feels very solid and like something meant for the road. The only weakness would be the good quality plastic control knobs, which since they are plastic and not super heavy duty, means they are the weakest point of failure that I see. It would have been great if the sticks underneath the knobs were metal, but oh well. Can't have everything for this price.

All controls are smooth and work great. The unit is metal and so should be less noisy than any mixing deck with a plastic housing due to the natural RF rejection of metal. I recorded one LP track for my dad into Garage Band, as a test, and the result sounds great.

This thing has a lot of functionality, which I may or may not ever use, but I prefer to have too much than too little, particularly when much simpler and smaller devices (Novation AudioHub, Scarlet 2i2, etc.) cost about as much as this beast. So, unless you're really needing to save desk space, or just want to use it as a headphone amp for your computer, you will be fine with something like a Scarlet 2i2, which sounds great and takes up a fraction of the desk space.

However, if you want to have more options "just in case" and have the desk or shelf space to spare, or need good RCA recording, this thing does all that.

You get a lot for your money in the PV10BT or PV10AT. I was considering the Novation AudioHub, and while I'm sure it's well built and has high quality audio processing, and with the RCA inputs, can probably record from Analog sources like Record Players (Turntables, whatev') just as well, you get a lot more for your money with the Peavy, like EQ options, effects, auxiliary, not to mention a ton more inputs, including Bluetooth Input.

Overall, this thing is bad ass and I'm very satisfied with what I got for my money.

As the title states, I feel this is about the best you can expect from a consumer level camera on the market today.

I have been experimenting and putting it through it's paces for a month now, and am pretty familiar with it's capabilities and quality. I am currently on my family's second vacation trip of the year and and have taken some footage ranging from indoor/outdoor pet shots, the mountains and waterfalls of western Colorado, night-time 4th of July fireworks, indoor, well-lit cousin/family members and an indoor shot of mom covering a chocolate cake with meringue icing. Lots of good, typical, casual-user type footage.

With the recent purchase of a mini HDMI to standard HDMI cable, I was finally able to view all of this footage on a 45" Sony BRAVIA LCD TV in all of it's HD glory. Before, I had been getting by with the AV/Component cables and there is a night and day difference between those and the digital signal of HDMI.

A good part of my footage was shot in the lowest quality possible. I also shot a substantial bit in full HD. Honestly, the low quality looks darn near as good as the full quality, so for those who somehow shoot hours of footage on end without access to their computer to dump the material to, you can vastly extend your shooting time if necessary with minimal compromise. Besides, even at full quality HD, a 60 GB hard drive is like having a camera with SEVEN 60 minute tapes spooled end to end. At the lowest quality (HD) recording time is just under 23 hours. There's really no reason to upgrade to the SR12 unless you are some kind of shoot-a-holic, but shooting 120 GB of footage would be an editing nightmare anyway.

Viewing the full HD footage on the BRAVIA TV via HDMI, it looks about as sharp and clean as you could possibly ask for. You can pick out the individual strands of fur on animals cleanly.

I cannot comment on 5.1 surround sound, as I am not yet home from this trip, but as soon as we return (tomorrow) I will definitely test it out.

I recently handled the Canon HV30 in CC and was not very impressed with the build quality or the viewfinder - poor refresh rate and everything plastic. The Sony SR11 gives you a hefty chrome metal push-dial for adjusting focus/white balance shift and aperture. It's very effective for controlling focus when in low-light/indoor situations or the aperture. I find that the camera DOES lean toward cool colors by default, so I have the White Balance Shift set to maximum (+4) to bring a warmer, more natural tone to things. You may find that you need to do the same. Thankfully, when adjusting parameters manually, they are retained, meaning you can set White Balance Shift, Focus, AND Aperture all at the same time. It's about as good as it gets without jumping into the $3000 dollar camera range.

The x.v. color is a new, wider color gamut that is supposed to give more life-like coloration to subjects. If you shoot in this mode, you will only see the difference when played back on an x.v color compliant product (new Sony BRAVIA TV sets). Otherwise, from what I can tell, it seems to produce a somewhat less saturated image. I am still trying to decide which look I prefer. I feel the normal colors look pretty accurate under most conditions. Occasionally, greens seem a little too bright (trees, grass), but overall, color reproduction is very good.

One thing I love about Sony video cameras is their smooth operation. The zoom is smooth but agile if you need to punch it in our out fast. The viewfinders are also very smooth, unlike many other video cameras. (I say 'video camera' because 'camcorder' just sounds too consumerish and cheap for my taste).

The build quality feels very solid, has substantial weight, and feels very secure in the hand, thanks to being able to get a grip on the top of the camera. I think people who lament over the weight of the camera and wish for something lighter are foolish. The WEIGHT adds INERTIA which means more RESISTANCE to SHAKING of the hand. This is a vital fact that most consumers seem ignorant of, and trust me, watching footage on a big screen, you better pray that your footage is as close to tripod-steady as possible.

This camera comes with a fun and cute DVD that goes through some of the basic filming techniques. Several of these concepts are taught in a typical introductory Film & Video class, so it is actually quite a useful video, and it is amusing (to me at least).

I think I could not have bought a better camera for what I desired in a camera, the price point, and what is currently available. I would have PREFERRED to save up and purchase a Canon XHA1 for the pristine optics, better manual controls, and extremely good light gathering (very low low noise even in challenging lighting situations), but I do not want to mess with tapes and the 1:1 tape transfer process again. Hard disk recording with a 3k HDV video camera is possible but expensive. This camera and it's accessories/cables fits perfectly in the very nice leather bag I already own, and is very well protected therein, so for me it was nice to not need to buy a new carrying case.

If you need to see some online footage of this camera in action, check out Vimeo and search 'sr11':

[...]

Further comments/notes pending...

The premise of all Monster cable products is based on the well-known axiom that there is a sucker born every minute. Or at least, that's how I see it, since Monster could not possibly charge the prices they do and stay in business if it were not for the existence of gullible people with lots of money  who willingly buy into the hype without doing so much as basic research.

I bought a generic 10FT HDMI cable to run from an OPPO DV-983H to a Samsung LNT4069FX 40". It works flawlessly, cost me about twenty dollars and supports the 1.3a standard. Need I say more?

My parent's receiver doesn't have a proper RCA phono input and my dad thought his old Dual record player was broken. That is, until we turned it up really loud and could barely hear the audio. So we knew it wasn't being amplified properly.

I researched and came down with this Cambridge Azur 651P (black model) as something with a good balance between quality sound and price.

Tested with my dad's Dual, as well as my own Technics LP1240 series TT.

The Dual does not utilize a grounding wire and honestly does not need it. Sound is well amplified, crisp, and warm.

Same with the Technics, except there was an audible 60hz hum until I screwed in the dedicated ground wire from the Technics to the Cambridge (in the back there is a ground wire screw). Then all was good.

It takes about 12-15 seconds for this pre-amp to warm up and start delivering sound, which is no issue to me.

Heat generation seems minimal. It has been used several times and left on at length, and no issues.

Overall, for the price, size and sound quality, we are very satisfied.

I have owned this Samsung for several months now and I think I can write a fairly accurate review based on my experiences.

First of all, my set has been working fine without any issues since I've had it. Over the last few years I have been won over by Samsung for their generally no-nonsense styling, vivid images, and competitive pricing.

As others say, this is a great set at a great price and though there are a couple drawbacks to DLP, to get an absolutely perfect picture at this size would require you to spend double the money, money I would much rather put toward movies and shows to watch.

The only significant drawback that I have found, due to the technology of HD rear-projection screens, it that it has a limited viewing angle compared to LCD or Plasma. If you sit high or low, you may notice the screen is not quite uniform in brightness. Also, the further from the center of the screen you sit, the more brightness and contrast you lose. In certain cases I can see this being a real nuisance, but as long as the screen is viewed at a good 12~15 feet, and no further to the side than what you'd get by sticking two couches together, then I think you'll be quite content.

I'll often run a movie or show while I'm at the computer, which puts me at a viewing angle of nearly 145 degrees off-center. The picture loses roughly 60-80% of it's optimal brightness and contrast at this angle, but I find it adequate to glance at and see what's going on.

Watching Planet Earth HD on this screen, my parents were amazed at the size and clarity. I watch mostly standard definition DVDs on a Toshiba A35 HD player and even the original Star Trek episodes look great. I also have the set hooked up via HDMI to my PC and that works really well, though I seemed to have some fitting issues initially, but maybe that was due to my using a dual-display setup. Either way, I can play computer games on it and it's like having a 61" computer screen.

There are many options for customizing the picture quality - everything from color control, black level adjustment, LCD brightness, to sleep timer and what-not. I'm not at home right now so I can't rattle them all off, but there is NO 120hz refresh rate like on certain LCD sets, in case anyone does not know. The 120hz is cool and can enhance your experience, especially when watching high speed sports! But with movies it can be a distraction to itself, since movies take on a very un-film-like smoothness. Some may care, but it really shouldn't be a major buying decision. Also, I've never noticed any ghosting or artifacts with this set.

I'm very happy and if I were dropped back in time with the same decision to make, I'd probably buy this again. Once more, the bang for buck on this is hard to beat.

I suppose the bottom like might be that if you want a 60+ inch HD screen and don't want to spend the money for a Plasma or LCD, then this is the next best thing.

When she came up behind him and tossed a penny in the pond and asked, "A penny for your thoughts?" he should have replied, "Sorry, mine cost a dollar."

Feeling like a drawn out Twilight Zone episode, as others have indicated, it probably would have worked better as one. There's really not all that much going on, with a plot that could easily condense to 45 minutes. Normally, I don't mind slow pacing, but the characters aren't all that interesting, and the plot twist is all but wasted. I mean, he gets to the mirror earth, finds out what happened, and then dies. The end! I can't imagine what Planet of the Apes would have been like if it had played out similarly and you only saw about 15 minutes of the new world before the main character died and the movie ended.

Having the twist be a mirrored, yet identical, world is clever, because all that is required is to flip the film horizontally and voila! you're on the mirror Earth! No extra props or actors required. Kinda cheap when you think about it. Cheap enough for a TV show, hmm. However, this film is worth a look for its superb model effects and interesting concept, but very little else. If only there were just a little something more to it, it could have earned a spot on my shelf.
