It's not exactly thrilling to learn that another of one's favorite directors has jumped on the CG bandwagon with their latest production. I mean, is it really necessary to spell out Star Wars I, II, III and George Lucas? Due to this, I haven't bothered to even consider seeing this until recently.

Now, since I have waited so long, I've missed the chance to see it rendered in full 3D in the theatre. I am, at least, familiar with the 3D experience, though, so I can imagine pretty well what it was like.

Sound production is rather excellent and immersive on the 7.1 setup (actually 7.0 since I stole the sub).

The CG blending on the characters when in their avatar form was done remarkably well. The lush environments of the planet, Pandora, were also exceedingly detailed. The only issues I noticed were with some of the creature animations, the 'Nantang' in particular.

The dialogue, as a whole, came off pretty well, though there were at least a couple points where I felt it was a bit lacking -- the whole, "at first it was just orders, but then everything changed, I fell in love, etc. etc.." is by now such trite dialogue, was it really necessary to have it in a movie which was made to push cinematic boundaries? It just felt slightly George Lucas of James Cameron and I wish he had handled that scene with a little more originality.

I just couldn't bring myself to give it an A rating, as much as I wouldn't mind. Even with considering the huge budget and the amount of effort that went into its creation, it's more a landmark in computer graphics than in film, at least from my perspective. I couldn't stop comparing a lot of the visuals to Crysis. They are breathtakingly beautiful, but they are still clearly CG and, in my book, it's not the effects that make a movie good.

--update--

So, it's the next day and I still have a lot of mixed feeling. Avatar is definitely a good movie with unquestionable production values. The question on my mind is, rather, how to judge the film in terms of story vs. characters vs. production. I think it would be something like the following, listed in order of personal importance:

Characters, B+
Story, B+
Production, A+

The characterization might have deserved higher, if Sigourney Weaver's character hadn't felt sometimes a little forced when trying to play the part of the hard-ass lead scientist. This leaves me with production as clearly the strongest aspect of the film and 3rd in personal importance. Therefore, I feel that my 'B++' rating is about right.

These are the best and brightest hands-free units that I know of.

With 4 levels of output (low, med, med-high, high -- not sure about the claim of 5 levels), a compact 'army' style form-factor, quality headband, all metal construction with rubber gaskets, and somewhere between 1000-1200lm of output, what more could you want in a flashlight.

I simply don't buy any other kind -- mounting it on your head is, hands down, the best way.

Throw it on, click it on, go about your tasks.

No worry about where to set it -- it's on your head, so it points wherever you are looking.

Sometimes, you need to tweak it up or down in the rubber holder, but that's all.

Great for having in your bug-out bag, or just in your car for at night -- changing a flat tire, examining the engine bay, searching your car's interior.

At around $C dollars a-piece, they aren't exactly cheap, but neither are they super expensive. For the construction quality and size, they are well worth it.

users.query:
Relatively easy to assemble. My wife and I had it up in about 30 minutes. Throwing in a couple cheap Ikea-like wrenches would have been nice (some tools requires).

Pretty stable. We have 2 heavier kayaks (75lbs and 65lbs) as well as a lighter cheap-o sit in and the unit is solid.

To make 3 fit in our garage around the garage door bracket we need to leave one flat on the bottom. However, we could adjust the arms to they all sit on their sides if it weren't for our harage door bracket.

So far so good.

cands.text: Easy to install. Easy to use. Convenient fold out of the way design. A bit of highway wind noise but that's to be expected (not bad enough for me to remove them). I'll be getting another pair.
Easy to install and it's comfy. For the price, it can't be beat!
Easy to install. Cheaper than dealership. Still overpriced but what are you gonna do? It's nice that it matches the rear cargo tray that came with my 2016 Forrester XT Touring. Good fit.
Not bad. Not great. Always stuck together. No real complaints. Packaging is always fine but product still is stuck together and sticky. Messy compared to other snack options.

A little odd that this "item" and its reviews are exactually several very different items. My review is for the 36W 4ft light system with stand.

Easy to assemble and much more durable than I expected. I hooked it up to a timer switch we had lying around and our seedlings couldn't be happier. Pictures shown are initial setup and then 1 week later.

The adjustment string is a pretty neat idea and has allowed is to adjust the light for taller and shorter plants.

We've had it only a week and are very happy. I wish I did a control grow without the light to show the difference but I didn't. So oh well. I will try to remember to update in a few weeks.
I haven't used a new thumb drive in quite some time. This easily transfers 50GB of data in minute or two when using USB 3.0 (on a MAC). It took about 20 minutes using 2.0 on Windows.
I was skeptical of the price but tried anyway based in good reviews. They were right! High quality materials relative to cost. Functional and sturdy. What more do you want?
Wife loves it. Looks nice. Bottom shelf is bonus storage. Doesn't make our shower look like an old folks home, so that's nice. Holes on top allow for water drainage.

Great camera with awesome photos. My pictures came out just as good from a recent trip to Alaska as the folks carrying around the huge DSLR, etc. Takes a little trial and error getting the right settings for scenery versus close-ups but it's pretty easy to figure out. Just point and shoot!

We packed these full and checked them on a direct flight. 1 bag was full of mostly clothes, hangers, and a couple books. It weighed 49 pounds. The other bag had a 22" computer monitor (wrapped in pillows), a laptop, clothes, boots, shoes, and a couple books. It weighed in at 40 pounds. Both bags made it without any issue. I would probably zip-tie the zippers together if I were to check them again just to be safe. Highly recommend if you're looking for a short-term checked bag under twenty bucks.

Nice idea but it's garbage.

First, it's plastic. Seems heavy duty enough but description references aluminum and steel. It's not.

Second, it protruded from the bar a couple inches (see pic) not a flush mount as the item's diagram shows.

Lastly and most important, it doesn't work. I tightened as hard as I could and I was still able to rotate and remove without any effort at all - I can't imagine how this wouldn't pop right off on an actual ride.

Very cheap. Looks good in the photo, but in person, the edges are rough - on the white iPhone, you notice dozens of imperfections along the ridge. Would be a great bumper if not for so many imperfections.
No handle. Only the base. Useless. To top it off, each head arrived in a HUGE box that could hold 10 or more. Don't waste your time or money.

For ten bucks +/- you can't beat it. Works well right out of the box. Stayed secure to counter, peeled properly, no issues with apples breaking, etc. I've peeled literally thousands and thousands of apples from years of working an Apple Crisp concession stand. This unit holds up great for occasional home use.

Easy to read and a good "first dashboard design" book. Nothing new or all that creative if you understand the basics of design already. Big font, lots of pictures, etc so I will pass it along to the new analysts for homework.
Meh. Not great. Not bad. I wouldn't order again. I see them all the time at airports - might be an option there in a pinch.
Good for the price but it it pretty thin plastic. Works for my needs but not the most rugged.
Awesome awesome awesome. Very high quality. We will use for years to come.

By far, the best iPad accessory I have purchased! After being fully let down by the Apple branded products, I tried a few third-party items. This is the first that I am truly impressed with. The keyboard works great and the case itself is durable and not bad looking. It makes for a great travel companion to the iPad. I will be keeping it in this case all the time.

I agree that the soft keys take time getting used to, but the single silicone design does make it easy to clean and prevents potential liquid damage or stuff getting under the keys.

So far, no problems with the charging port (same mini-USB as Blackberry Bold, etc) as other have reported. I wish I had purchased this case first and not wasted money on the other junk! Live and learn...

My only main problem is the difficulty to find a better angle - the mount only moves so many ways.

I too had the night time problem many are complaining about. At first, the camera seemed to work fine at night then it started showing all dark. I called DLink and they had me perform a factory reset. They said it was a common problem and the factory reset seems to fix the problem.

I will update should the camera stop working again.

The SD card is very convenient - allowing me to connect 4 cameras to the DLink recorder and using the SD card for this camera. Picture quality is more than acceptable for the price range and the HD quality provides a clear crisp image.

The entire office goes crazy for these things. They arrive in great condition and are addicting as they get. I wish they made a version without nuts on the outside, but I don't notice them that much and other people seem to love that.

Neat idea. Easy instructions. Doesn't work with any remote we own. We tried Samsung TV, Samsung Speakers, Xfinity cable box, and Visio TV. The wand would not program to ANY of them. Huge disappointment. 2 stars for idea and easy instructions but this guy is going back.
This tea tastes like I took a pile of lawn mower clippings and soaked them in water. Absolutely horrid. Try the actual berries, which are quite nice.
We have a couple of these. We have used to spray insecticides, fungicides, and fertilizer. Works like a charm every time on our garden, fruit trees, berries, etc.

Awesome blender and worth every penny if you use it on a daily basis. I purchased mine directly from Vitamix (refurrbished models are cheaper and still have 5 year warranty).

Great for making smoothies - green or traditional. Also makes an awesome milkshake.

Haven't tried the other recipes yet (soups, etc) but I look forward to soon!

users.query:
Tom Bird really knows how to reach inside the heart of a budding writing and draw out the Divine Author Within. His extensive personal research on the craft of writing is fused with a deeply thoughtful approach to awaken the inner muse and keep the ideas flowing. He proves that setting time limits and expectations for writing, then taking time to clear your mind and open yourself to rapid inspiration is the best way to give birth to a novel. Get the ideas out there. Get the words on paper so they can be real.

Tom teaches techniques for letting go of the critical logical mind and giving the CREATIVE mind permission to be free. He shows how to live up to your highest potential, not just in writing, but to use these simple guidelines to bring out the best in all aspects of your life. Written with tons of quotes from famous authors, leaders, and creative minds that show that his way of thinking has been implemented by successful people for a long time. Creativity needs to flow. Stop thinking, and LET IT GO.

I did not purchase the additional audio CD that goes with this book, but wish I had it for my own writing. On it, Tom describes that the CD helps relax the mind, center your thoughts, then provides a soothing background to listen to as your writing. I would love to try it. Tom also offers retreats where participants go to ACTUALLY write their book in a weekend. It sounded fantastic!

A must read for all aspiring writers. I highly recommend absorbing the knowledge and wisdom that Tom Bird has given in this book and applying it to your own creative endeavors.

cands.text: Advice and daily habits from a variety of successful authors, but many of the things people advised were the same. Good to read once and adapt what you find to fit your own promotional and writing needs.

This book really helped me as an editor to improve my skills. The advice and instructions are easy to understand and have made a big difference to my clients. I refer back to it all the time. It is also good for authors who self-edit their books.

Thought provoking with lots of insight into listening to your "best self" and the voice of truth inside. Author Molly Carroll uses numerous examples of real life situations where using intuition brought people better results in life. Definitely worth reading!

A must-read for authors who want to make their writing stand out. Jodie Renner knows the literary world well and gives helpful advice that writers should know. Great for editors too! If everyone writing or editing a manuscript would take the time to read this book, I believe the literary world would vastly improve. :-)

Katherine Owen is my new favorite author! I am hooked on her style of writing. From the very first page of "Tell Me Something True" she takes the reader on an emotional journey of heartache and pain, love and loss, courage and determination from Tally and Linc. In this second book, the level of emotions is just as intense. Katherine captures your heart and doesn't let go.

Open that wine bottle and settle in for a long night of reading. Once you start these books, you won't be able to stop. I read the first and second books in one weekend. Now I'm on the third book. Bravo, Katherine. Don't ever stop writing. You have a talent that shines!

Highly recommend this series!
I read this in one day. Once I started that first chapter my heart was hooked. A story proving how precious love and life is.
I read this in one day. Once I started that first chapter my heart was hooked. A story proving how precious love and life is.

I really got caught up in these books. Perception draws you in and the author kept my attention all the way through the final page of Contrition. Noah Brody and Zoe Vanderveen are well-rounded characters, full of emotional depth and the author does a fantastic job of letting you inside the heart and mind of both main characters. I read Ambition last (out of order) and had to smile at how well it kicks off the series. DEFINITELY RECOMMEND

As an author and editor I agreed with much of Mr Berhardt's writing advice, but felt he spent a great deal of every chapter promoting his own fiction novels as examples of excellence. Perhaps a quote now and then would have felt acceptable, but when comparing his own books with famous literary masterpieces, it felt vain.

However, most of his lessons would drastically improve an author's ability to write dynamic, engaging, memorable dialogue. I do recommend this book as a creative writing lesson.

Beautiful and thoughtfully written poems, sometimes wonderfully visual in word imagery, and in other poems the words just reached out and touched our heart! Modern thoughts by a romantic minded man. Author Michael Smith has a real talent for making his words draw real emotions to the surface. The flow of his writing is very professional.

It was nice to see that men have deep feelings to express, and even better to read those insights. It takes courage to share thoughts and feelings with others. Michael Smith does it with style.

This is my first book by L.A. Fiore and I loved it. Her writing style has fantastic flow, pulling you right through the pages. I read "Beautifully Damaged" in one day. Couldn't put it down. Trace is so much more than his dark past and Ember has the inner strength and heart to see the good in this damaged man. She describes herself as being plain, but that's just low self-confidence talking. Based on how other people react to her, she is obviously a beautiful woman, inside and out.

Love is never easy, sometimes it tears your world apart. Thats real, that's life. Trace may be rich, but who he is as a man isn't about money at all. The complex twists in this book are unexpected. It keeps you wondering about the past. Each of the supporting characters are unique, bringing depth to the story. Looking forward to "Beautifully Forgotten" and learning more about Lucian.

This new collection of poems by Michael Peter Smith is clever and honest, his simple words filled with insight and thoughtful emotion. It often feels like taking a quiet walk with the author, talking about moments that touch his heart, and hearing his advice when life goes wrong. It was wonderful to read. His work has variety. Some poems are honest observations about people and life. Other poems are so beautiful they could be songs, filled with lyrical imagery and gentle cadence that makes the phrases flow.

The poems are divided into sections that begin with Everyday Things and Lifes Lessons, flow through Friendship and Relationship Issues, and move forward into poems that play on your Heartstrings. There are Moments of Clarity and Wishful Thinking and many more areas of life that the author shares his feelings on. It ends with passion in Sexy Implications that spark a fire in the mind.

There were many beautifully written poems in MUSINGS, but I had a few favorites. One Heart, about dealing with a long distance love. All We Can Be is a heartfelt promise from the man who vows to love forever. I had to smile at the clever phrasing in A Brick is a Brick, about a beautiful girl and a great big wall; a symbolic play on words about giving your heart to someone, piece by piece. Heart and Soul is the happy realization of two lovers telling one another that this love will last.

Michael Peter Smith is so clever, even his About The Author notation is a whimsical poem about growing up with words in his heart, doubting his talent, and finally having the courage to share his romantic heart with the world.

I highly recommend MUSINGS OF A MODERN ROMANTIC. There is something within these pages for everyone.

I had this one for a while before I finally got around to reading it, but Author Barbara Freethy delivered! It was a great story about family and falling in love with plenty of suspense to keep the pages turning. Very touching. Forgiveness and understanding are difficult sometimes, but when hearts open and let go of hurt, love walks in.
I loved this book and wish Debra Webb would write another Jackie Mercer story. There was so much potential for another!

Inside of each of us is the potential for many different paths in life. But our choices move us in different directions. This is my favorite book. I have read it at least 5 times in the past few years. I am a huge Richard Bach fan and love his writing. One is a story, but It always give you a fresh perspective on life and makes you think about how small choices can have huge consequences.

I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS BOOK!!

I truly enjoyed Gaia's gift, a story of heartache and loss coupled with the beautiful hope of second chances at life. Rachel's journey is touching. Author Fran Orenstein takes the reader right inside the character's hearts, showing who they are on the inside; their hopes, their dreams, their fears. Skillfully written with unexpected twists that kept me riveted. I read this book in ONE DAY. I hoped for Rachel's happiness, I worried she would lose everything, and I cheered in the end!

I was impressed with the professional talent that went into creating Klarissa Dreams. The artwork is really special. Each picture tells a story all by itself. The poems and short story collection were so touching, funny sometimes, and always found a place in my heart. I particularly liked "Masking the Mask" by Michael H. Hanson and "An Answer within Me" by Riley Steel. Those poems really stuck a cord of truth within. The story excerpt "Birthright Bestowed" by Erika Szabo was extremely visual in language and brought a clear imagery of the girl and her dream as she discovers her gift of healing. I also enjoyed "Alone In My Thoughts" by John Manning. The poem had a feeling of offered friendship, of peace for the weary soul. Very well written!!

My favorite picture was "MASQUERADE" with a beautiful woman partly hiding behind a bronze mask. I also thought "EVE" was extremely creative with the apple and the snake. Her smile is just naughty enough to show the temptations running through her mind, much more realistic than the angelic pictures others have created. "BETH" was beautiful and went well with the poem "Goddess" by Riley Steel.

This book is a work of art on so many levels and has such a positive feeling since its intent is to benefit Lupus and Cancer research. A worth cause to support!! I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS BOOK.

WOW, I am hooked on this series. I really like that Mattie is "normal" a very flawed woman, with many obstacles to overcome, much to learn. Becoming the Hand of Fate doesn't make things better in her life, it only makes everything more complicated. I love the way author Sharon Joss writes. Her style keeps everything moving fast, with lots of quick wit comments.

At the time of writing this, I am on book Four in the series-- see, I am very hooked.

The action scenes, beautiful locations, and the emotional rollercoaster of this book will leave you aching for more. The ending was so unexpected and took the storyline in a new direction. Very well written!!

OMG this was the best Crossbreed Novel, yet!! Christian has FINALLY evolved from the smart-mouth loner into a complex man. As we see glimpses of his past, how he and Raven's lives are more than just "partners" their whole relationship takes on new meaning. As this is all slowly being unveiled, we also get to experience another wild case that takes them into a dangerous underworld.

Christian Poe has met his match!

This is our second Lupine Pet harness. We love these! They fit our two small dogs very well and hold up to use. We use them everyday for walks and riding in the car. The patterns are attractive. People are always asking where we got ours. Our female has a pink one with hearts. We've tried other brands, Gooby was okay, but rubbed under the arms regardless of how we adjusted it. The Lupine Pet design is perfect for smaller dogs.

Sweet shy Sabrina is assigned to write as Sex Advisor for the magazine that Travis manages (who is really his twin Trent!) Her inexperience in love and relationships cause many nervous bumbled situations and mishaps that had me laughing. Even her homemade beauty aid experiments go wrong.

It doesn't help that she is deeply attracted to her sexy boss, who suddenly seems much nicer than before. If only she knew his secret!

A fun story with likeable, realistic characters. There is lots of talk about sex and romance, but most of the scenes were steamy-sweet. Trent gets far more than he bargained for when Sabrina finds out the truth and gets her revenge. The end was fantastic!

Our two small (both under 18 lbs) dogs were so excited about getting a new Piggie, carrying it around all day. But by the second day poor Piggie's head was coming off, tearing away at the neck. It is just sewn on, not part of the braid. Too bad. Kong toys are usually our favorites, but this one needs some work.

Beautiful! I bought this as a gift for my daughter-in-law for her birthday. Although it is small, the details are stunning. As always, the Hamilton quality is reliable. The colors of this angel are serene and lovely. She loves it. Made a fantastic gift.

Becoming an adult is never easy, but for Maggie the physical and mental abuse she suffers from her mother is horrific. Yet she handles it with strength and courage, always looking toward the day that she can leave. She works hard at school, supporting her mother completely. Meeting Vincent tests her inner resolve. I was proud that she stayed determined to be friends. Other young women might have jumped at the chance to be with Vincent, to escape the abuse by turning to sex: but not Maggie. She keeps their attraction on the back burner for as long as possible, and is rewarded to discover that she and Vincent share the sweetest kind of love. They love from their hearts.

This was a realistic and touching story that makes you reconsider your outlook on life. The book is written in first person, so we see everything from Maggie's perspective. (And a few chapters from Vincent.) Magnolia Wilson is heroic inside. Her thoughts and feelings are mature beyond her age, yet remain typical of someone who had lost so much.

I look forward to the next book!! Maggie and Vincent deserve a happily ever after.

This book and series is one of my favorites. I absolutely love the authors writing style and imagination. She does a wonderful job telling the story and I cannot wait for more stories in this series. I just hope there will be more.

This series just keeps getting better and better. I really enjoyed reading this story. The author sure does know how to bring your imagination to life. I couldn't stop reading once I started this book. I received this book in exchange for an honest review.

This series is great. I love the way the author keeps you guessing and engaged in the story throughout it. This story is just a good as the rest of the series. If you have not read the series I would really recommend anything Carrie Ann Ryan writes. Everything I have read from her I have enjoyed.

I love how the author is able to take legends or myths and put her own spin on them. I loved this story. It is well written and thoroughly entertaining. I didn't want to put the book down once I started it. I cannot wait for the rest of the series to come out.

I voluntarily read and reviewed this advanced readers copy of this story. Jessie Donovan did a wonderful job with this story. It kept me captivated from start to finish. I love how her dragon world sucks you in and leaves you wanting more stories. I cannot wait until the next book in her series is released so I can devour that one too.

I love the way the author pulls you into the story and captivates your attention. I was not able to put the book down once I started it. The author sure knows how to write a story that will entertain you from start to finish. This box set also includes a story called Bear Cubs for Christmas. It was really well written and kept me enthralled throughout the story.  I wasn't able to stop read it once I started it.

Poor Jay Felix has no luck with women at all. His mail order bride is gone and he is beside himself. He cannot figure out why he cannot keep a woman. Until he sees an on line auction for a womans virginity. Does he win her in the auction? Or will something else happen? I had to find out. Took all day but I was able to find out what happens with Jay Felix now. And I have to say I was really entertained throughout the story. Now I just need to get the rest of the series to find out what else happens to Jay.

If you could sum up Stolen and Forgiven in three words, what would they be?
Captivating, Enthralling, and Exciting

What other book might you compare Stolen and Forgiven to and why?
This book is unique as the authors take you to a place where the shifters are out in the open and yet hidden from humans

What does Aiden Snow bring to the story that you wouldnt experience if you just read the book?
The story almost takes on a life of its own when you listen to the someone else reading the book.

Did you have an extreme reaction to this book? Did it make you laugh or cry?
This book has made me laugh so many times while I was driving my car that people must have thought I was crazy.

Any additional comments?
The only thing I would find fault with the narrator for is his pronunciation of the word heady. To me the word the way he said it was wrong.

This a great mnage story about 2 brothers and their mate. Hazel Gower was able to keep me captivated throughout the story. I didn't want to put the book down once I started it. The love scenes are well written and steamy. I cannot wait to dive into the next book.

users.query:
DNF at 17%

The love of Josie's life was her high school sweetheart, Liam.  Was.  Up until he left her at the altar to pursue his music career and left her behind.  A tragedy brings Liam back into town but can it bring back their love?

Ok, I'll admit.  I went on a hunt for this book because I saw the trailer for the movie release.  Conveniently releasing right around Valentine's Day, the trailer looked like it teeters on the edge of a great love story and a hokey attempt at romance.  The book falls over on the latter.  I tried a few chapters and once I audibly groaned "OH MY GODDDD!", it was over for me.  It tries to mix in grief, friendship, and the-one-that-got-away romance but it just wasn't blending well together.  It felt very contrived and rushed with the dialogue between characters unbelievably cheesy.  It felt more like a generic outline or brainstorm of a book rather than a well-developed plot.

cands.text:
I flew through this book, it was action-packed and pretty emotional.  There were happy points, low points, and very steamy points. Sometimes, with steamy reads, it's all about the action in the sheets versus any actual story line.  Fortunately, that was not the case with Stone Cold.  There's family love, friendship love, first loves, and new loves all within an action-packed story line that I was anxious about the ending. I highly recommend this book!

Please note: I was provided with a complimentary copy by the author (and very happy to have read it :) ).

I knew it was a short read when I started it, but the plot was spotty. The characters' love story was glazed over and, unfortunately,  I didn't feel anything when reading this book. It was bland, at best.

Although I do understand that this book is the second installment in a series, I simply cannot say that I would be interested in reading the first book. This tragically dramatic, immature romance was quite predictable and redundant. It becomes very clear from the beginning of the novel that there is a huge obstacle in the primarily primal sexual relationship between James and Quinn: insecurity. Every single chapter, regardless of whether it was through James' or Quinn's narration, repeatedly conveyed the insecurity of each of them in regards to their relationship. Could they make it? Does Quinn deserve better? Is Quinn holding James back from his creativity in his art? Is their love enough? Most of these mental dilemmas are only temporarily resolved through sex. Which is an additional issue because James is holding back his apparent primal instinct to tear Quinn apart in sex, which bothers Quinn. Furthermore, the readers are constantly reminded in each chapter that James is, in fact, a trust fund baby. He could just throw all of this struggle away and sail off in a yacht with a million dollars to blow just by making one phone call to his parents. I get the concept of having to prove yourself, which both characters do, and I get the concept of individuality, but the repetition and consistent insecurity felt like it was all to make the book longer. One last thing: I am convinced that Ava, James' art teacher/mentor, dressed like Cruella DeVille. Every time (and I do mean every time) she is introduced into a scene in the book, she is wearing red and black.

Please note: This book was generously provided to me for an honest review.

Just a few months ago, I was fortunate to have been able to read my first book by Sarah Morgan: Midnight At Tiffany's. I loved the book and the band of friends within the story.  I was delighted to find that it was actually the third book in the From Manhattan With Love series as it easily read as a standalone novel.  Immediately, I was on the search for the rest of the series.  Then I read the first book in the series , Sleepless In Manhattan, and fell in love with the characters all over again.  Now, having just finished the second book, Sunset In Central Park, it feels like a trifecta!

Frankie Cole has made it out of her hometown on Puffin Island to The Big Apple.  She made the move with her best friends and has never looked back.  Shamed by her parents' divorce and her mother's resulting promiscuity, Frankie has felt as though the entire island knew about it and judged her for it by association.  In New York City, with the support of her group of friends, she feels confident in her field of garden design and floral arrangements.

Matt Walker has known Frankie her whole life.  His sister is one of her closest friends and he likes to think he is a close friend too.  One encounter leaves him realizing he has only scratched the surface of Frankie's true personality.  What is she hiding under the persona that she wears every day?

I loved the slow unveiling of what Frankie has been hiding and I felt the mask was justified given the shame and guilt that she felt from her parents' divorce.  Furthermore, I enjoyed how patient Matt was with Frankie's insecurities, yet he was still able to push her to be stronger and face her fears.  Frankie has a great supporting group of friends that the reader is able to see their interactions as the narration switches between Frankie and Matt.  Lastly,  I loved that Frankie was the hero at the end of the day!

I will be reading more of Sarah Morgan's books and I would recommend this book for readers who enjoy reading romance.  Also, for readers who enjoy reading about New York City as the setting is described beautifully.  It makes me want to take another trip out there!

On the other hand, I would not recommend this book for readers who do not enjoy explicitly sexual scenarios, brief violence, or foul language (which was only a few times).

Sylvie and Dan have been together for so long that they can finish each other's sentences. One comment from their doctor at their annual visit that they'll likely have almost 70 more years of marriage throws them into an emotional tailspin. They vowed to be together forever so they decide to cope by surprising each other with random and fun ideas. However, the biggest surprise ends up unveiling a huge secret. Will they still be together forever?

Typical of a Sophie Kinsella book, Surprise Me had my cheeks either aching in pain from laughing so hard or burning from secondhand embarrassment from Sylvie's mishaps. Sophie Kinsella has also crafted a wonderful tale by portraying several of the different types of love through varying characters. Eros (sexual) love with Sylvie and Dan, Philia (friendship) love with her neighbor Tilda, Storge (familial/parental) love with their daughters, Agape (altruistic) love with their elderly neighbors on the other side, and Ludus (playful and/or flirting) with Robert. These many characters blend into a fun plotline that hit me with a MEGA surprise plot twist.

I highly recommend this book for any adult looking for a fun romance that balances the seriousness of the effects of grief and misunderstandings. My favorite characters were the elderly couple that lived next door and had such pure love and both came across as genuinely sweet.

I would not recommend this book for anyone who might be triggered or offended by the following: grief, parental death, sexually suggestive scenarios, and foul language.

Please note: an electronic ARC of this novel was generously provided through the publisher via Netgalley in exchange for an honest review.

Characters were annoying and unrealistic. The author's idea of seduction between the two love interests was to say their first and last name repeatedly.

This was such a cute, fun read.  It was very easy to understand what the main character is thinking and feeling, and there are several disasters that occur that are just hilarious!

Purchase-wise, this book was in perfect condition and shipped quickly!

"I fell in love with a boy thirteen years ago and he, along with my best friend, proceeded to smash my heart into a billion pieces".

The girl who fell in love with the boy is the loyal, trusting, and compassionate Rory. The boy she fell in love with is the strong, protective Houston, who happened to be the older brother of Rory's best friend Hallie.. Although some might consider this to be a love story about Rory and Houston, it ends up also being Hallie's story. This book was dark, deep, and yet romantic. It "hits you right in the feels" as they say and leaves an impression deep in the recesses of a reader's brain. Fans of John Green and Jessica Sorensen may very well note a similar reaction out of their story as there is not any feel-good fluff to pacify the grueling nature of true love. It is an intense story full of secrets that take their sweet time to be revealed

"Maybe Houston was right. Maybe we will always make it back together. Then we'll never stop hurting each other".

I thoroughly enjoyed this novel, despite being rather impatient with the timeliness of the revealed secrets. I loved how raw this book was with emotions and commend the author for digging deep into the true angst of secrets and romance. It was action-packed with well-developed characters that every reader hopes for and delivers gut-wrenching scenarios for every bleeding heart. I would say that this book was hard to put down but, in fact, there were quite a few scenes that I had to stop in order to even breathe. Just when I thought that I knew what the next secret was going to be, I was proven wrong.

A few words of caution: this book has a cliffhanger, profanity, sexual situations, and covers sensitive topics such as self-harm, abortion, and even suicide.

Please note: A copy of this book was generously provided through the publisher via NetGalley.

I absolutely loved this book, the storylines of each 3 women and the secrets that have caused chaos in their lives. It is about their strength, loyalty, and dignity. I keep saying the author teases the reader in the beginning by playing with the reader's assumptions on what the secrets may be and when the one major secret is revealed, it blew me away. A fantastic read, I have recommended it to every reader I know.  A must read!

Finally! A book that I could really get into, and did! Unfortunately, I had been on a bit of a reading hiatus as I had gone through a few books that were more irritating to me as a reader rather than entertaining.  Finally, a book that pulled me out of the hiatus.  Therefore, I would like to personally thank the author(s) for writing this fantastic book.  It has a little bit of everything in this book: transformation, loyalty, intimacy, misunderstanding, stereotyping, suspense, and family drama.  I have read books in the past where the amount of topics were overwhelming in one book, however, they blend beautifully in this one.  The main character, Barbara transformed from a practically invisible small-town nobody with an embarrassing drunk mother into a powerful, smart business woman (shout out to feminism-you go girl!) that is in town on business from New York City.  The love interest in the book, Ryder, has been a playboy since high school who originally overlooked Barbara in high school but is now taking a job renovating her house.  The very place that her drunk mother was let go from for her drunken episodes, Barbara has been sent to shut down. Something she has had to do in several towns as part of her job, but this time it gets personal.  Not just for Barbara, but for Ryder, and someone else who demands to cause damage.  In general, I don't particularly mind cursing.  But for those readers who do, you should know that the foul language is rather minimal, only a time or two. There is a lot of steamy scenes in which those readers who are not comfortable with adult situations may want to be wary. Without giving any more away, I'll just wrap this up with it's a great summer read.  There's romance, grilling out, suspense, a beach, and warm summer sun.  I loved this book and highly recommend it to any reader looking for a fun, sizzling, beach read!
Please note: an ARC was generously provided in exchange for an honest review.

This book is hilarious! The situations that arise are comical, could be relatable, and keeps you guessing. I borrowed this book from the library, but I loved it so much that I bought it on here to send to my sister! I had never read any of Sophie Kinsella's novels before, but this book showcased her fantastic writing ability. I have already read "Twenties Girl" and "Remember Me?", they are fantastic! A must read for anyone looking to indulge in some girly humor, it's definitely a feel good book!

This book is hilarious! The situations that arise are comical, could be relatable, and keeps you guessing. I borrowed this book from the library, but I loved it so much that I bought it on here to send to my sister! I had never read any of Sophie Kinsella's novels before, but this book showcased her fantastic writing ability. I have already read "Twenties Girl" and "Remember Me?", they are fantastic! A must read for anyone looking to indulge in some girly humor, it's definitely a feel good book!

Have you ever loved a book so much that every time you see the cover of it you just sigh happily? Perhaps even swoon? That is my current state with What to Say Next by the very talented Julie Buxbaum. She has a way of hitting a reader right in the feels. I laughed, I cried, I cheered, I felt a wide range of emotions. I had this similar reaction with her previous book Tell Me Three Things (which I also highly recommend). Also, there was a big plot twist that was unexpected and essentially had me locked into the book, racing along until the perfect ending.

This was a great book that dives into the tumultuous waters of high school drama and then the riptide of loneliness catches you and makes sure you stay. It made me feel the grief, loneliness, and hope that the main characters, Kit and David, felt. These two were opposites in many ways, yet each of them have their worlds flipped upside down, which brings them together. It is a fresh reminder of the discomfort of finding yourself at the brink of adulthood. It abuses the heart, really, as it is heart-wrenching at times, yet you feel your heart swelling at other times.  All in all, a must-read that is different from other YA romance novels in that it presents an exceptional approach of mixing humor with grief to the common struggle of finding yourself. 

I enjoyed that there were unique attributes about the characters that set them apart from the general population in the book, particularly David's Asperger Syndrome attributes. I cannot say whether or not these features were accurate, however, I do enjoy the respectful and charming way of which his character was developed. I would recommend this for any reader high school age and older who is a fan of innocent romance and deep situations. I would also recommend this book for readers who are fans of math and science as David's narrative is heavy in those fields. On the other hand, it was not so heavy that those who are not strong in the math and science fields (including yours truly) could not follow along.

For those who may be offended: there was foul language, brief violence, infidelity, bullying, alcohol use, brief mention of drug use, and an overarching theme of grief.

Jean Taylor's husband is gone, she saw him get struck by a bus with her own eyes.  Bella Elliot is gone, the small child was playing in the yard and then disappeared.  Kate Waters wants the story.  Bob Sparkes wants justice.

There have been several mentions that this book is the next Gone Girl and Girl On The Train.  The only connection I could make is the presence of the media and the layers of secrecy.  However, I found this book to have more flakes than full layers.  Small chunks of information flaking off of the storyline rather than full secrets and lies.  The ending was more of a presentation of the disintegration than a turbulent reveal.

The only reason why I finished this book in less than a week is because the review deadline is today for me on Netgalley.  Otherwise, I would have easily pushed off finishing the book, which is hardly ideal. The Widow is a multi-perspective mystery/thriller book about Jean Taylor (the actual widow) whose life has been flipped upside-down.  Just when she thought she was getting used to the upside down, it flipped on her again.  Truly, this woman has a lot of drama happen to her for the least dramatic character that I have ever encountered.  The narration is shared between her perspective, the perspective of reporter Kate Waters, and the perspective of Detective Inspector Bob Sparkes.  However, there is a brief narration change from Detective Inspector Bob Sparkes to a character named Mike Doonan, but for the most part the narration swaps between Taylor, Waters, and Sparkes.

I wanted to be enraptured by this book but I could not connect to any character or perspective.  The widow being the titular character was lacking, in my opinion. Jean Taylor is plain and simple. Literally, plain and simple. She does not speak up for herself.  She does not voice her opinion.  She does not complain.  She just exists, for the most part.  Stereotypically, hairstylists tend to be more vocal and inquisitive in personality.  However, she proves the stereotype wrong.  She goes along with anything her husband says, regardless of if it is the right thing to do or if it is hurtful.  She just leaves him alone if he is upset.  She leaves him alone when he's on the computer for hours.  She does not seem to be upset by lying for him and helping him commit bank fraud.  She hardly reacts when he is killed by a bus in front of her. She is just plain and simple.

For those of you who may be offended: there is foul language, themes of violence, kidnapping, murder, pornography (particularly child pornography), and sexual abuse of a child.

Please note: an advanced reader copy of this book was generously provided through the publisher via NetGalley.

Very rarely does a reader come across a book where their initial conceptions about the book and it's characters are actually reversed. Initially, I did not expect much from this book as the last couple of "mystery" genre books I have read have been disappointing. The first 20% of the book appeared to be on par for those disappointing tracks. However, time and time again, Tom Claver showed his writing strengths as more and more unexpected action sequences took place.

This book was full of surprises as it unveils a tragic story with the main character, Harry, tries to get his life and work back together. Harry starts off as an unsavory drunken character that has lost his wife, Bethany, and his father's pride due to his downward spiral and alcohol addiction. Until his friend, Ed, recommends his services to Angela. Angela is a mother to Peter, and abused wife of the wealthy Nick Linehan. Although Harry is hesitant at first, he agrees to take on the job of helping her escape. What she did next, no one anticipated.

I highly recommend this book for all adult readers who enjoy action and a bit of mystery. It should be noted, for those who may be offended, that there is foul language, violence, and suggestions of sexual assault.

It should also be noted that an advanced reader copy of this book was generously provided to me by the publisher via NetGalley.

To say that I loved this book is a severe understatement.  I loved the layers and layers of secrets in each character and how each chapter removed one layer.  It was a jigsaw puzzle until the very end and was absolutely thrilling.  I've recommended this book to all of my friends, and a few of them (the ones who listen :) ) were shocked by how incredibly well crafted this novel is written.  No one saw the ending between my friends and I, no one! I read her other book, The Husband's Secret, and raved about it.  Then I read Big Little Lies and loved this one even more.  Liane Moriarty is a thrilling author and I highly, HIGHLY, recommend Big Little Lies.

Brianna's world is over.  She lost her baby and her marriage.  She puts on weights and walks off a pier into the ocean wanting to end it all.  What she did not plan on was entering a whole other world underwater.  Merman Zantu finds her and breathes life back into her.  Shortly thereafter, they fall into lust and mate.  Brianna's life starts over in a new world with a new mate because when merman mate, they mate for life.

Zantu has a hard time selecting a mate because all mermaids are greedy, manipulative, and leave mermen and their merchildren behind.  Having recently witnessed this happen to his brother, he avoids mermaids even more, viewing them as predators.  While treasure hunting, he comes across a human who needs rescued and breathes into her allowing her to breathe underwater.  Saving her life forever changed his.

I tried to like this book but it was irritating at times.  Zantu calls Brianna "my little angelfish" redundantly and the sweeping concept that all mermaids are greedy and malicious did not add to the book.  Furthermore, it felt like they were having sex every five pages and then they were telling each other that they love each other after only a brief amount of time.  The final redundant part for me was how Zantu kept thinking about how females cannot be trusted because they will leave you.  Yet Zantu left Brianna behind on more than one occasion!

It was a novella and easy to read in one sitting.  It is difficult to tell if this book was originally written with the intention of shorter length because it felt like a lot was left out.  The plot holes seemed to be covered up by more sex scenes.  Furthermore, there were big transformations that happened but were not explained how.  It just did not feel like it flowed well, in my opinion.

I am adding the second star because there was a lot of detail regarding the marine world.  Not only with what it was supposed to physically look like, but how all of the marine creatures interacted.

I would not recommend this book for those who dare bothered by explicit sex scenes, suicide attempts, infidelity, abandonment (particularly maternal abandonment), depression, violence, and coercion.

Please note: an electronic copy of this book was generously provided by the publisher via Netgalley in exchange for an honest review.

Emma Donoghue stuns again! I had read Room in the past and made the mistake of thinking this book might be along the same lines.  It was not.  The only way that they compare is that the main character has had an adverse experience before the novel begins, the focus on the strength of a child, and an underlying theme on whether or not a certain set of parents "deserve" their children.

Lib is a nurse assigned to observe Anna, an eleven year old who is gaining notoriety for sustaining without food for months.  The last thing she ate was a communion host at church a few months ago and claims to have been living on "manna from heaven".  Lib is an English atheist without a family who now has to work for a very Catholic family and her colleague is a nun.  She is determined to have this assignment end early by finding the truth behind this obvious lie from a child.  As more and more shifts go by, she begins to wonder if the child is even lying at all.

Anna is a young child who is very strong in her faith (she prays the same prayer 33 times a day, along with the rosary at night) yet is losing strength in her body.  She does not complain, instead believes the fast from food is worth the struggle if it means her dear brother Pat can be saved from purgatory.  "Poor Pat" died quickly from a stomach illness months before the novel begins.  The illness was so swift that he was not able to confess his sins before his death and therefore believed to be stuck in purgatory until his family prays enough for him to be released into heaven.  Can Anna's love for her brother keep her strength going long enough for Pat's release?

Anna's parents, the O'Donnells, are grieving the loss of their son, yet trying their best to maintain their farm and handle Anna's new fame.  People from far distances stop by their humble home just to catch a glimpse of her.  Mrs. O'Donnell especially seems to enjoy the visitors and Mr. O'Donnell prefers to keep working rather than entertaining.  But when Lib insists that the visitors be turned away for the duration of this observation, Mrs. O'Donnell makes her disapproval very clear.

All of these factor into why I really enjoyed this novel.  The culmination was very effective, as was the character development of Lib in particular.  There were a few surprising pieces of the novel that add depth to the characters.  There were a few characters that did not turn out to be who I was expecting them to be.  Emma Donoghue has a way of describing day-to-day routines in a way that is unexpectedly intriguing.  Furthermore, the evolution of the daily routines disguise the change in path towards the uphill road leading to the conclusion.

Please note: a copy of this novel was generously provided via the publisher through NetGalley.

Thank you Pinterest! I was introduced to Anne Bogel's work by Pinterest years ago by a pin about books that stemmed from her blog Modern Mrs. Darcy. I highly recommend her blog as it is a great resource for book recommendations as well as other fun lifestyle information. I also recommend her podcast What Should I Read Next? for all of anyone's bookish needs :).

An in-depth yet easy to understand look into different personalities. It is also a look into the interactions of these distinct personalities and how conflict can be reduced by understanding how each person's personality affects how they communicate. I really enjoyed how she broke down each personality type, gave strengths and weaknesses of each, and referenced other resources so that the reader can investigate further.

The section that made the biggest impact on me was the section about Highly Sensitive People. I have quite a few people in my life who would fit into this personality type and it completely opened my mind on understanding them. Also, it helped me learn how to be helpful when they are stressed. For example: keeping the kitchen counters clean. I wouldnt have thought about the importance of it before reading this book.

I would recommend this book for fans of non-fiction and self-help. I would also recommend this book for those who are fascinated by different personality types and would like to know more.

Bonus: The audiobook is read by none other than the author Anne Bogel herself!

Please note: I received a hard copy of the book for free from the author in the encouragement of an honest review.
Cute, funny, and made for a great Christmas present for a friend.  Tempted to buy another one for a White Elephant gift exchange! Highly recommend!

I had a hard time getting the sprayer to work. After several pushes down it finally started to spray. The aerosol is overpowering and I definitely recommend using this in an open area. It worked well for a couple of hours, then made my hair look greasy.  But I have fine hair, so that probably didn't help.

Gwyn is a fiercely independent sibling of the large Campbell family that inconveniently ends up in the wrong place at the wrong time far too often.  Her older brother David rules the castle that was part of the marriage agreement to his English wife Isabelle.  A castle that the English king wants back.

Jack is an English Captain who was given the title when his father passed away.  His uncles have harbored jealousy and bitter rage at his sudden rank despite the obligation to care for Jack as a nephew.  On the brink of war, Jack sets off on his own to prove to his uncles that he is worthy of his title.  Instead, he ends up needing to prove his character worthy to a certain lady when he ends up caught in a trap.

I must admit: If this book had been on a shelf in a bookstore, I might not have even had the interest to pick it up.  Highlander romances are not books that I am very familiar with but I may be more optimistic in the future.  I really enjoyed the fast pace and character development.  I also enjoyed the family interactions on Gwyn's side and how it starkly contrasted with Jack's uncles.  Lastly, I appreciated that this book read as a standalone despite it being the third book in a series.

Points of concern: there was mild violence and sexually suggestive scenarios.

Please note: an electronic copy of this book was provided for free from Sourcebooks Casablanca via daily e-mails containing excerpts.

The Birches have much reason to celebrate this holiday season. Their daughter Olivia is coming home for Christmas, for once. Olivia is a doctor returning from a trip to Liberia where the Haag epidemic has been traumatizing and she is forced into quarantine for 7 days after her return. Joining her will be her mother, Emma, who is keeping a major secret so as not to ruin Christmas. Also present will be her father, Andrew, who writes a column reviewing restaurants and his secret from more than three decades ago will make an appearance. Then her sister, Phoebe, who demands the attention of everyone, still lives at home with her parents, and is planning her wedding during the quarantine. Can they get past the miscommunication and secrets to have a happy Christmas or will the secrets prepare for a battle of betrayal?

It took a long time to pick up speed. Little bread crumbs had been dropped along the way which did build up to the second half, however, the first half was so slow that I was tempted many times to move on to another book. Fortunately, I did make it through and it picked up very quickly after about 60% into the book. A great portion of it was predictable, yet the character development finally comes through and I could not put the book down.

I gave it three stars because I took one star away for how long it took for the story to pick up speed and therefore the amount of times that I was almost at the point of giving up. I took another star away because there were far too many coincidences with the characters and too many secrets that it became overwhelming at times. When Jesse met Emma, for example, and she reveals her secret to him, a stranger. Emma then went on to meet Sean, Olivias secret. Jesse also met George, Phoebes fiancee, randomly while on a walk and again randomly in a bar and discovered his secret.

I would (and have) recommended this book for those who have traveled to Africa and feel that the warfare and politics of Africa are far too easily ignored in the West. Additionally, for those who feel that the rest of the world groups Africa into one general concept rather than it being an entire continent. I would also recommend this book for readers who enjoy reading about family dynamics and secrets being revealed. Much like (one of my favorite authors) Liane Moriarty books, that are told in different perspectives and center around secrets.

I would not recommend this book for those who may be offended or triggered by: foul language, cancer, sibling rivalry, homophobia, infidelity, infectious diseases, and warfare in Liberia.

Please note: an advanced reader copy of this book was generously provided by the publisher via Netgalley in exchange for an honest review (thank you Berkley Publishing Group!)

users.query: This switch can be managed from a web browser, the disk that comes with it isn't really needed. It comes with the typical wall-wart power supply. The Netgear Prosafe line is nice heavy metal, comes with slots on the bottom so it can be wall mounted and comes with mounting screws and wall anchors. The switch does support port mirroring, LAG, VLANS, etc. I actually use mine when doing network traffic analysis with the port mirroring capability. It's a nice small switch to carry around in your briefcase (although if you don't need 8 ports, the 5 port version is a little more compact.)

cands.text: As someone in the IT industry, I needed something small I could carry with me. I always have one of these in my briefcase when visiting clients as you invariably need a few extra ports, or need to solve a connectivity issue "right now." Lifetime warrenty is awesome, but having deployed probably 30 of these in various sizes, I've never had a Prosafe go bad.

Works in Windows 7x64 and Linux - I got this for using with WireShark for network analysis and it works perfectly for that as I needed two ethernet links from my laptop when monitoring with a switch in port mirroring mode.

One star knocked off for not being able to find drivers on the web site, but the ones on the CD worked - I just know that drivers are updated frequently (or should be.)

Purchased this for a friend who is tech-challenged. Setup was easy. First thing I did was perform a firmware update (which everyone should always do.)

It's a basic wireless router, and does that function fine. Due to the lack of external antennas, it doesn't have the range of a dedicated high-end access point, but in a smaller house / apartment it should work great.

If you have needs beyond a simple SOHO router, you may want to consider the EdgeRouter Lite ERLite-3 with a dedicated Ubiquiti access point or two which would be MUCH more appropriate for a small business setting than a SOHO WiFi router.

It's a wired / wireless mouse, and can be operated either off the nano-wireless receiver or the USB charging cable. As the battery life is terrible, only about 6-10 hours (and that's in power saving mode,) you will find you need to keep it charged whenever not in use, keep spare rechargeable batteries around, or plug it in and use it that way. With the weight of the mouse, it SHOULD have used 2 AA rechargeable batteries instead of 1 to at least give you a full day of usage.

Unfortunately the Logitech charging cable is thick and very stiff, needlessly so. As an alternative, I just use a regular micro-USB cable which works fine. It doesn't have the strain-relief of the Logitech, but as it's rather thin it seems to be fine.

The software is horrible both from a design and coding viewpoint. For example, in the definable profiles, you can set the DPI and report rate. For some reason, it takes 4 seconds for it to respond to a click changing the report rate or DPI up and down arrows. I don't know how anyone could possibly code something to perform this poorly on a core i7-3930K,  but not only should they be fired, but they should be barred from ever working in the software industry again. From a design perspective, you can assign multi-key macros to the extra buttons. The UI is bizarre though, you can enter key strokes but in order to also include mouse events, you have to right click on the keystroke window and choose insert mouse event....  Very non-intuitive. At the very least there should be an on-screen note to right click to do other actions. Also, in a macro, there is no way to have the macro send one thing on button down, and another on button up (which would be VERY useful.)

All that said, as a mouse, it works very well. It tracks fast and accurately and despite the design flaws of the software, once you set it up you are good to go. Being able to change DPI on the fly is awesome, as is having multiple profiles. For this reason, I'm giving it 4 stars but can't give it 5 stars due to the flaws listed above. You would think after being in the mouse business for so long Logitech would be 5 stars every time, but this just isn't the case with this mouse.

Update1: The USB receiver failed and I had to work with support to get it replaced. Really - that's a part that should never fail.

Update2: The left mousebutton has gone bad and now doubleclicks all the time meaning I have to throw this thing out. Highly disappointing in a mouse this expensive.

The hardware is fine, but the Cyberlink software it comes with is several years old and barely works. If you resize the window while it's doing a capture, the capture stops for example. Basically you can't touch it and then you are OK for a capture.

The included editing software amounts to a very limited functionality old version of PowerDirector (version 10 is included while version 12 is current.) Every time I attempted to perform any editing task (such as trimming a video clip,) it popped up a message saying I needed to buy the full version. Gee - thanks for nothing. My system is a high end HP workstation with an 8 core xeon processor, 32G RAM, video card that cost more than what most people pay for an entire system and the software is so slow and chunky that it's unusable and can't even play a video clip without stuttering. The full version of PowerDirector costs several times what this device costs, so I guess it's no surprise that the included version is so limited, but the text description for the EZMaker 7 claims that you can do all sorts of editing and that is just a bald faced lie.

You will need other third party software if you want to do anything with the videos you capture with this device.

First thing you do is make sure you upgrade your firmware. You should do this for ANY computing device as there is usually a few revisions since the item was manufactured and you finally get your hands on it. The current firmware is easy to use and the most common configurations for home / small offices are trivial.

I much prefer a router separate from my access points - the built-in wireless on 95% of soho wifi-enabled routers is lacking. Pair this with a Ubiquiti access point or two and you have a very solid network.

This unit is the replacement after going through belkin, Netgear, and Linksys garbage that always locks up or just start behaving oddly. My network is rock solid now.
A solid basic wireless mouse. Feels good in the hand and doesn't stress you out after a day of work.

This is a Very inexpensive AP / firewall / router for small spaces, small needs. It's fine at the far end of a 5Ghz bridge to use as a 2.4Ghz gateway / AP for a small number of devices with modest bandwidth needs. Do your research, read the specs, use this device in the way it was intended and it's a great deal. It will fail miserably if you attempt to use it in a classroom with 20 people streaming HD Youtube videos. As with all UBNT devices, the firmware it comes with is ancient and you need to update before using.

The 5 star reviews are not honest. This device is based on OLD obsolete technology. Because it's Java, it's VERY hard to get working AT ALL with a modern system. Java in the browser has been a dead technology for nearly 10 years - the fact that they are still using it says volumes. The interface is also very flaky and slow requiring constant re-logins as it disconnects all the time. In order to use virtual media, you MUST use external power using a 2A USB phone charger and an old-style USB to USB-Mini cable or it will constantly powercycle. In fact, you really need external power anyway as the unit will powercycle when the computer it's hooked to reboots. The virtual media, when it works, is also INCREDIBLY slow. If you get 1MB / s you are lucky. The mouse sync is also awful in the Java interface, it's a challenge to use at all, so be prepared to use keyboard shortcuts wherever possible. That said, it does work most of the time, and can save you in a pinch. I would look elsewhere though for a better designed more current solution.

Awesome price for such a capable SBC. I purchased it to run the Asterisk VoIP phone system for a vacation home and it works perfectly for that with tons of capacity to spare for other things I want to do. I installed a 32G MicroSD card for the primary data, backing up to a 32G USB flash drive.

This is not a typical home wifi router - this is designed for business or Pro-Consumer. In fact, it's not a router at all, it's an access point which is exactly what you need if you already have a router and want to add WiFi to your network.

The version 3 software (in public beta) allows seamless handoff between AP's meaning you can use an app on a tablet, roam around the entire building or campus without the app skipping a beat as the AP's communicate with each other and hand-off the connections to the best AP. This is a VERY rare feature in wireless systems, most others require controllers costing thousands of dollars.

To setup these AP's, you install an app (java based) that will find and configure the AP's on your network, including setting up guest wireless access. The install wizard is incredibly simple and just works. Once I had the software installed on the server (which was a whole 3 minutes) it took about another 90 seconds to configure the AP. Yes, it's that easy.

The unit uses passive POE and comes with an injector. This is nice, as we can plug the power into the UPS near the switch / server, and run a long ethernet cable out to the AP, not needing a nearby power outlet. It can be wall or ceiling mounted, and comes with long screws and a backer plate to attach to ceiling tiles if you want that option. Regular screws with hollow wall anchors are also included. Ethernet cables are NOT included (which is fine as anything they included wouldn't be the right length.)

As noted, it uses passive POE so will NOT work with a regular POE switch. That said, there are third party active to passive POE adapters that you can use with this device on a POE switch available in the $25 range if needed.

Doesn't track well on all surfaces, but overall a very good Bluetooth travel mouse for my laptop. It will not track on glass for example, and not so great on plain paper or file folder. Most regular desk surfaces work fine, as well as on the back of a standard legal pad (the cardboard side.)

The buttons appear to be reliable as is the mouse wheel. It does Not have a "free wheeling" mode on the mouse wheel that some of the Logitech's have, but I don't use that feature all that much (although it's nice if you are scrolling though a very long document to just let it spin.) Build construction does NOT feel cheap like so many inexpensive mice.

It's a reasonably heavy mouse, feels good in the hand. Battery life is very good - I ensure I turn my mouse off when not in use and the same set of batteries has lasted nearly a year. This current purchase was because I lost my last one that I've had for 2 years (same model.)

The mouse uses two AA batteries (included) that load in the top. The power button is on the bottom of the mouse and the switch is easy to operate.

All in all, a very good bang for the buck - price point seems very good for a Bluetooth mouse. One star taken off due to the fact that it has trouble tracking on some surfaces.

It works well on both USB3 and USB2 ports. I wasn't able to get more than about 160M/s no matter what SSD I plugged in, SSD's that are rated for 550M/s. That said, the primary use I bought it for is to clone laptop drives to new SSDs, something I do frequently. For this case, the old laptop HDD will be the slowest component anyway so the performance of this adapter is moot.

Very powerful, great signal strength. Used as a repeater to get internet access to a remote location too far from the main AP. Update firmware before you use it as they all come with very old firmware. This is not a consumer class unit, you need to know what you are doing to configure it.

The included 3' long USB3 cable was too short for a computer to sit on the floor with the USB hub on a desk. Ditto for the wall wart power supply. I did have to order a longer replacement USB cable. I wish I knew that these cables were so short before I ordered or I would have ordered the extra cables at the same time. The power cable is also very short which worked in my situation but may be too short for others. Other than that it works great.

Works perfect with an old UPS that needs a serial connection on Win7 x64 and I don't have a legacy serial port on my desktop or laptop. I bought a second to use on the road to hook up to the serial console ports on routers and switches.

I had an old first generation Wii.. The thing that drove me nuts on the Wii with the very slow scene change times, game loading, and navigation of the system in general. Enter the Wii U - Great - this thing is loaded with high-end processors and graphics engine, tons of memory, lots of flash storage. It should be awesome! Um, not so much. The system in general is VERY VERY slow, MUCH slower than the old Wii just navigating system menus. It's 30 seconds to go from screen to screen. I'm sorry, in this era of computing, anything with delays like that is a total failure. The people responsible for a design this unresponsive should be fired and blacklisted from the industry - about all they are qualified for is driving a garbage truck.. Yes, it is THAT bad.

As another reviewer mentioned, the first thing the Wii U has to do is updates. Lots and lots of updates. And it fails over and over and over with random errors that even the support web site can't decipher. At one point it randomly decided to actually work and apply an update. Nintendo - you have 32G of flash storage and you can't load the system with error MESSAGES? You have to use code numbers?!!!!! Really?!!!!

So here we are, lots of flash storage, and the ability to hook up a dedicated hard disk for more. You would think that the system would cache your frequently used games in memory, right? Nope - that memory is ONLY for downloaded games. It runs the games off the slow DVD drive constantly banging on it, LONG pauses between scenes. Apparently there are people that put up with this! Nintendo NEEDS an update that totally revamps the main menu system so that it is INSTANT - going from menu to menu should happen NOW and not with a 30 second delay. They need to cache the DVD's in system flash - requiring the DVD to be loaded is OK, just don't grind the crap out of the DVD drive for hours on end.

After all the frustration of just getting the Wii to work, updated, configured, navigating the terrible menus, you FINALLY get into a game - and the games can be pretty good, which is the only reason I didn't review it with zero stars. But I'm not reviewing the games here - just the system itself. And the system itself needs a LOT of work.

Like most inexpensive appliances made in china, this is cheap junk. It leaks due to poor design, and doesn't hold up. And when I say leaks, due to the design defect, it can be anything from a few teaspoons to a few cups alllllll over the place. Some well positioned electrical tape helped a little, but here I am on Amazon writing this review while shopping for something better to warn people how bad this thing is. It's also nearly impossible to properly clean - about the only way of cleaning it is to replace it.

Works pretty well but has imprinted writing that gets in the way. 3M shouldn't have ANY imprinted writing on it at all, or very faint at least. This is "stamped" in. It would be nice if the side viewing was a little more obscured but it's much better than nothing.

cands.text: My cat hates everything I buy. She would rather play with trash than what we usually buy her but this thing rocks! She is obsessed with it and we find her playing with it even when it's off. So exciting to find something she likes!

This was a great fun thing to do with my dog! You get lots of neat information with a breakdown of every breed and its family tree. Only took about 2-3weeks.
