users.query: I have read other books by this author and not a bad one in the bunch.  For some reason this one stood out.  Cy, a good guy with bad luck.  A fickle girl friend.  A spoiled rich rancher's son.  A resentful group of town folks.  A school teacher and an old deputy who befriend Cy.  All woven into a bittersweet story.  A really good read.

cands.text: and there were a couple areas where a bit more research would give more credibility but over all the book did everything a thriller should and did it well.  The characters were well developed and there are many characters.  The author doesn't skimp on them, the good. the bad and the ugly.  The story is another tale of revenge from an incident in the middle east over collateral damage resulting in the death of a family member. It also deals with big time drug deals moving around in NY, London and Paris. There are some surprises that certainly add to the story making it an excellent read.  You won't be disappointed.

I liked the story but have to give the book as presented a low rate.  I like Zane Grey and even his son's work so it is hard for me to low rate the book.  The story is one of romance, tragedy and pretty typical of Grey's style of writing.  If you can get past the poor grammar, run on and broken words at the wrong places it is a good read but often frustrating to follow.  I recommend a paper copy.

This is a great read if you like historically based characters.  The story follows the main characters of the mountain man era and the interests in trapping, gold seeking and interaction of whites, Mexicans, indians and half breeds.  The bad guys are really bad guys dealing in theft, fraud slavery and fighting indians.  I have read better and worse but don't hesitate to recommend this book.

Not exceptional but a worthy read.  Luke, his life, his loves make an interesting read.  From Ozark farm boy to Confederate soldier entrusted with and looses the Confederate treasury thru traitorous companions steal the gold. Fellow soldiers who kill Luke's friends and leaves him for dead. Luke's shame and quest to do right  take him on an interesting path.

I like Zane Grey.  His stories are written in the language of time past.  His eloquence of prose is far above so many authors.  What I didn't like was the beginning of the book, not the actual story, where I considered it demeaning and unnecessary to expose the shortcomings of the author.
 As one reviewer said, it seems impossible that the heroine could be repeatedly captured by various thugs and still be virtuous but then there were motives. The hero and his friends are guys to admire for their faults but moral values when needed.  The book could have been shorter but then how often do we read a good book dreading the end.  Many today do not have a clue what the railroad contributed during its heyday and sad.  Grey has given detailed insight to what it took by thousands of people contributing their part to make this happen
It was a pleasant read, well laid out by events with an unassuming hero and his lady.  Enough action to be interesting but not overboard in any area.

I read and like Grisham and not to compare the works this author made a more exciting read.  Constitutional law professor  rides a Harley, wear jeans and  boots (after all, he is in Texas) and is extremely loyal  to his friends in need.  There are some surprises in this west TX setting and the characters.  Among the cast is an honest but skeptical sheriff and a student aide with issues adding to the story.  A former student is killed, is it murder?  Unraveling the mystery makes a very good read.

I like Zane Grey and have read many of his books and watched the movies made from his stories.  What I resented was the Forward which I felt was demeaning.  I suspect many authors have editors and others that clean up what may be conceived as lacking to the final manuscript.
Having said that, the book was full of great characters and railroad history.  It could have been shorter, then again, how often do we wish a story would not end quickly.  The story illustrates the changing of America and the extreme difficulty, the corruption, the life in work camps and the morals, or lack of in vivid detail.

I am partly at fault for choosing this book knowing I am not big for short stories.  If those are your forte it probably will satisfy you,  Even at that, there are some worth the read and others seemed rather mindless but that is to be expected when there are many included in one volume.

I am a fan of westerns and have read many of the premier authors, this book holds its own and more.  The day to day ranch operation in details most authors don't bother with.  The conflicts of doing necessary and what is right.  Chet is not complex but faces many complex problems.  There is a feud that seems to never end., a cattle drive, horse rustlers, unhappy marriages, family relationships, friendships, good horses all wrapped up to make a great read.  I just don't have the word power to do justice to this author and book.

I like westerns and it takes a lot for me to low rate one.  I came close to quitting but finally, the story leveled out more and actually got better BUT, I have read much better.  If you have read everything in your library at least once then this is for you.
Frankly I liked  book 2 in this series better.  This book lagged a bit for me in the beginning but picked up.  The story was a bit preposterous but did hold my interest.

I lived in the 4 Corners area for several years in addition to  vacations in the some areas mentioned in the book so I was comfortable to start.  I like the history involved.  The story has a well written plot, with efforts to save a museum and other land from a fraudulent land grabber.  We have a hero that is a really cool down to earth guy,  We have a few sub plots involving the bad guy, the good people, victims of his fraud.  There are several good twists and a few surprises.  A minimum of tasteful sex and kudos to the author for that. I am sure no moralist or prude, I just don't care for second hand sex in detail.  Spider isn't John Wayne but he is likeable and down to earth.  Horses, pickup trucks, the beautiful scenery and the customary courtesy of the west.  There is even police cooperation from different involved jurisdictions.

Zane Grey is prolific.  He has the ability to put you there with his vivid descriptions.  I have not been to the north rim of the Grand Canyon until I read this book.  The characters, mainly Mormons, who save the life of a young lunger.  The family also has a half Navajo woman they raised. a worthless son who goes against his family and and assortment of rustlers with a couple of these guys who still have some morals.  It is the usual story of greed.  There is a wild stallion, a part wolf dog and a droopy eared burro  who contribute to the story.. The Navajos are portrayed in a positive way and good since I have enjoyed interacting with them in the past.  Overall it is a good read.

The good is for anyone who lived in Hawaii or never did but wanted to at least visit.  The plots were okay and most of the characters were interesting  The bad is Lei from a police standpoint. She has a great dog.  She was abused as a child and carries too many scars.  She has more issues than Time magazine, needing to cut her wrists, pinch herself to induce pain and carrying a talisman.  She is still seeking revenge on her abuser with intent to kill, not the mentality sought by police forces..Not a trend setter for a police officer.  In one book the author refers to having all officers go after and armed guy with rubber bullets, never happen.  Rubber bullets for handguns are not a norm.  She talks about bean bag shotguns shells for rifles then confuses them.  They don't make bean bag rounds for rifles.  Lei is undisciplined, emotional and can't decide about falling in love so while in love with one guy she has an affair with another, not heart warming in terms of loyalty.  A total loose cannon with only a few redeeming values.  She has luck doing investigations so advances from patrol to detective then the FBI, pure literary liberty.  Having said the
negatives and accept the liberty of the author the books were entertaining from a pure fiction stand point.  She does mature a lot in 4 books and that are all I will read of her.

I am a fan of guns, esp from the old west period.  I never heard of an 1886 Winchesr so decided to read the book.  It is a rather typical western but more. Interesting characters.  Dedication to a cause.  Almost some romance that I was sorry did not develop.  Some reaqlly bad guys and some good guys.  A range of geography  from Texas and Indian Territory to S Dakota with apt description of the country.  If you like guns, cowboys, good guys,, bad guys and some just plain folks, read it.

This book has a lot going for it on one hand but it is not exceptional.  The characters were all well represented and defined. The plot  was mostly plausible but even tho serious there was an undercurrent of lightness.  I didn't find the story as intense as it might have been. I am of the age of The Big Sleep and Bogie so this probably earned the fourth star with all the references to the movie.  One problem I had as a retired police officer was the fact the guy wanting to be a private detective doesn't feel the need to be armed, even after attempts on his life.  That defies logic to me.

The book has an entertainment aspect tho a slim one for me.  I enjoyed the take off with the attack on the safe house and escape.  The book carried on okay for awhile then to my thinking deteriorated to impossible killings by a guy with phobias.  The worst was just when the book just ended with business unfinished so flatly.  I have read other series that made you want to read the next in the series but this book didn't affect me that way.  Frankly I was more than disappointed in the end.
I enjoyed reading about the way of life and culture of the period.  The transformation of a shipwrecked officer to a worthy vaquero with the elements of a good western about horse thieves and honor.

A highly unlikely story particularly with 2 wild stallions but relax and enjoy the trip.  The hero seems most unlikely as is much of the story but it is a great and interesting read.  Don't be petty, there is not perfection all the time.

I have seen the movie Darby's Rangers many times and I am always moved by the events that crippled the Rangers in Italy.  The lead actor and his top Sgt were the kind of people I would like to serve with. The descimation of the battalion and subsequent death of Col Darby makes him a larger than life person.  The Rangers, now a permanent part of the US Army continue to carry the spiirt of the Rangers.
Set in Alaska with some insights into the NA culture and the park service it was a good enough read.

I ordered 2 pair of these like the ones I used in the military and found them to be quite satisfactory.  They fit well and are convenient.  I gave the product a four for the picky fact that the small chain allowing attachment to bags or whatever was missing in one. A minor point but a quality issue.
Lots of research and imagination involved in these stories.  Fans of Indiana Jones should esp like the archeology interest.  Adventure lovers will like the cast of characters.

cands.text: One would think that finding a LED replacement for regular incandescent decorative globe Light Bulbs would be easy right? NO! - In my case it has been quite a challenge in the past! Here is why... Firstly, the bathroom fixture in my house uses 'candelabra E12' Base. OK not a big deal as you do have various candelabra base bulbs available in the market. But, secondly (Most importantly) the globe light bulbs needs to be very small to fit properly inside that bathroom light fixture.. That's the real issue I was facing. When the original Decorative Globe Light Bulbs (40W regular incandescent bulbs) burnt out I did some minor modifications to the light fixture by raising the overall height by 1/2 inch so that it can accommodate a 'Micro-mini' CFL bulbs so that I can cut down on the energy costs and at that time (about 10 years ago) the only company who offered those small size CFLs were Sylvania 26941 - CF13EL/MICRO/827/C/BL/2PK Twist Candelabra Screw Base Compact Fluorescent Light Bulb Granted those CFLs did their job in cutting the energy costs down but they kept on burning out every year or so and I got tired of buying them again and again. I had searched everywhere for more reliable LED replacement for the light fixture that I have in the bathroom and I had found a seller here on Amazon known as 'Triangle Bulbs' who offered bulbs that fits my needs perfectly. Those bulbs were about 2 inches wide and 3.7 inches tall. While these dimensions are still the smallest available these will tightly fit in those special light fixtures I am talking about. Also, Just like the LED bulbs from Triangle Bulbs I am pleased to say these TCP 40 Watt LED bulbs also fits perfectly in my bathroom light fixture. So how does this TCP 40 Watt Equivalent 2-pack, LED G16 Globe Light Bulbs, Candelabra Base stack up with Sylvania 26941 - CF13EL/MICRO-MINI Compact Fluorescent Light Bulb ?? or Triangle Bulbs T95051-3-VA, LED 40 Watt Equivalent Dimmable G16.5 Light Bulb, Candelabra Base, Warm White, 3 Pack- Comparatively speaking, I think these are pretty darn good. The warm white is the color I like and it consumes even less power than the previous CFLs that it replaced. The only minor quibble I have is that since the cover is clear it reflects light differently when compared to Sylvania 26941 - CF13EL/MICRO-MINI Compact Fluorescent Light Bulb. I hope and wish that LED Bulb manufacturers like TCP makes bulbs with frosted white cover to diffuse the light better. Bottom-line: I am rating this product with Four stars! Thanks for reading my review.

LED Technology has evolved over the years and now manufacturers can make cost effective perfect energy saving replacement for conventional incandescent or halogen replacement bulbs. The Verbatim BR30 is 'LED' driven low energy cost lamp which is a high-quality, energy efficient replacement for halogen flood lamps. This lamp provides warm white light in the 2700K spectrum consuming only 8W of electricity giving off bright light equivalent of '65W' of wide flood light of similar halogen lamp.

The bulb has brightness which is rated for '650' Lumens with an estimated energy cost of about 96 cents per year when compared to a halogen bulb would be about 4 dollars assuming that you run them for about 3 hours per day. The energy savings alone is not the only factor, This bulb is free from Contaminants like mercury like most CFLs do and is more environmental friendly. Also since LED bulbs lasts about 22 years so it is more economical in the long run.

The bulb looks good, made with Smooth, streamlined exterior just like a regular bulb - no visible heat sink fins. This one mimics traditional halogen downlights. This is perfect replacement bulb in your recessed lighting needs. Most incandescent bulbs in recessed lighting fixtures are hard to replace especially when they are perched high up in the ceiling and generally is a chore to get an electrician to come and have the bulbs replaced. Since this one will last 20+ years just fit once and forget it. Excellent halogen recessed bulb replacement product.

The Desk Lamp functions very well and the light is bright enough for most intricate works like soldering tiny electronics surface mount devices (SMD) or needle/craft work where you need both your hands free to do the work. It has a 12-watt fluorescent bulb which is efficient low power consumption device which does not get hot as you look down the magnifying glass, BTW, the fluorescent bulb is type T-4 fluorescent white lamp not the daylight color or the full spectrum bulb to radiate daylight.

Aesthetically the design is old school, The base is plastic and so is rest of the body, But is sturdy enough and does not topple or fall out. The base is just enough heavy to keep it steady. The lid does help to stop light and can be used as regular desk lamp when you are not using the magnifier glass. The Magnifier glass is not having super duper Spherical qualities it does have extreme aberrations but it does get the job done and has fairly large magnification albeit distortions too when viewed at extreme magnifications. If you keep your eyes close to the Magnifying glass and keep the objects close to the lamp you get good view of tiny objects - just enough to get the work done effectively.

Having said, This is not a lamp which you can show off to your wife or try to please her with the color or design nor it will be good looking on any sort of modern furniture for that matter. However, as stated before you can use this Desk lamp for fixing things for your wife and make her happy - I call this WIN WIN situation! - Wife happy means life is good. what more can you ask?

I have purchased LED bulbs before from these 'Triangle Bulbs' company in the past and I must admit that these these LED A21 bulbs are also nicely made. The size of 'A21' is slightly heftier than regular 'A19' size bulbs. The heftiness comes because of the solid base which also acts as adequate heat-sink to cool the power electronics that drive the LED's. The heat-sink does get hot to touch during operation and is considered normal. Having said, These Triangle Bulbs T95141, LED Dimmable 100 Watt Equivalent Soft White Light Bulbs, 4-PACK gives out very bright soft white light and comes on instantly. Since the color is 3000K 'warm white' and since the LED's put out very bright light it may appear to be 'too bright' white where the yellowness is on lesser side. I would have preferred this to give out 2700K to match an equivalent incandescent bulb that it replaced. But once your eyes get used to it you will find it okay and very close to warm white color that we all are used to. Side notes: Please be aware that the size is slightly bigger than 'A19' size bulbs so it may not fit in subcompact light fixtures that are designed to hold regular A19 bulbs exclusively. The regular incandescent bulb replacement in such cases would be an 'A19' size. An example for standard 'A19' size would be Triangle Bulbs T95133-6 A19 LED 60 Watt Equivalent Soft White (3000K) Light Bulb, 6 Pack which would be considered as a perfect replacement. These however are for specialized uses wherein you have a fixture that can accommodate it and it provides Luminous Flux value of 1600 (Double the equivalent regular 'A19' size) consuming merely 16 Watts giving out 100 Watts equivalent light output. EDIT: Aug 30 2017 -------------------------- I regularly revisit my reviews to let fellow Amazon shoppers about longevity issues if found in any products that I review. I am sorry to say that despite these bulbs receiving four stars in the past but nearly 1 year later two of the four bulbs have died thereby I am forced to downgrade my review to two stars. Bottom-line: While the initial build quality is very good but after about a years use they stop working and sometimes you will have to tap them vigorously to get them running again indicative of loose solder joints inside the bulb. revising my review from four stars to two stars!

Beware that it is all plastic construction but looks beautiful! The One Bright white LED is bright enough for me, Just enough to light up the driveway which is what I wanted.

All 10 of the solar lights came in good packaging and worked right out of the box and was installed by me in less than 15 mins!

Just a tip, as it is Solar powered please make sure that you have decent daylight falling on the panel for 3-4 hrs a day for regular charging of the batteries, According to my observations, The solar Panel looks well sealed from accidental water leaks from rain or water sprinklers. The battery however is exposed (See the pictures that I posted) but still inside the light cap which should give ample protection, Time only will tell how well it will hold up against rains and water sprinklers.

I will update my review after couple of months of use and report back with my findings.

For now my recommendation would be - It is well worth it!

This Sterling Silver cubic Zirconia based pendant necklace is a Beautiful piece of jewelry both suited for Casual or Formal Occasions. This could very well be a special gift for your loved one. Having said, One thing I noted is that the Silver portions is not very shiny right out of the box. It surely looked lightly tarnished, which is the same as saying that it forms a patina much sooner.

This is rated .925 sterling silver. There is a chemical reaction that naturally occurs when Sterling Silver mixes with the sulfides in the air. IMHO, The more humid a climate you live in the quicker this tarnishing occurs. This Leviton IPS02-1LW model (with white face plate) is very sensitive especially when installed in areas which receives more than average ambient light. It either switches ON the load whenever ambient light changes slightly or fails to work depending on how much light is falling on the sensor. I tried to minimize the light going into the sensor by taping it with white masking tape but made no much difference. Also, the use of Ground wire makes it impossible to install in old houses wherein ground wire is not available. Also, in my humble opinion, using the 'Ground wire' as potential source of power to drive the unit creates 'floating ground' situations in poorly earthed/grounded houses. This happens when a old defective equipment in the house puts out abnormally high voltage to the poorly maintained ground which in-turn false triggers or fails to trigger this unit either by random or by fault of poor ground circuit in older houses (Most common problem reported by other customers)

While I am no expert electrical engineer but I do understand electronics and how this switch works. In my humble opinion Leviton must release an updated model that uses 'neutral wire' in addition the required 'ground wire' and use 'relay based' isolated switching to turn on the load to eliminate poor ground circuits at the same time make these feature enhancements:

1. Reduce the sensitivity to ambient light
2. Provide an intermediate time selection between 30 secs to 5 mins 1-2 mins would be ideal

I had been debating for quite sometime now whether to buy a Mono-crystalline or Poly-crystalline based solar panel for a solar hobby project. To give you a background, I am an electronics hobbyist & understand these technologies quite well and while I do not call myself a 'SOLAR' expert (yet) I do know what to expect out of an 'ECO'-budget friendly all-in-one kit like this from RENOGY. After reading several reviews here on Amazon & elsewhere on the web it was clear and evident that RENOGY does make good quality products. They seem to have a positive presence in USA and motivated to provide good products at reasonable price. While the panel & controller are made in CHINA (BTW tell me which product is not?) the quality of the materials and workmanship seems pretty good. Here is a little more detailed review of items included. SOLAR PANEL (100W Poly-crystalline) - 4 stars! ------------------------------------- The 100W Poly-crystalline based solar panel included in this kit is very well built. It feels solid. It is enclosed in a sturdy Anodized aluminum alloy frame. The Junction box (IP65 rated) and MC4 cables and connectors attached to the Solar panel are strong and well built. The panel's speckled blue color may not be aesthetically pleasing to some people to look at when compared to other Mono-crystalline variants which has distinct uniformed look but the panel's output performance is not bad after-all. Renogy did manage to make this look nicer by adding some thin white separating lines in the tempered glass to have little bit more of the 'uniform' look. If you ask most solar experts in the industry they will suggest to pick solar panels that are reasonably priced per watt, As long as the solar panels are manufactured in strict quality control with good quality Grade 'A' cells, the perceived efficiency which is still a major selling point for Mono-crystalline variants is not really a factor anymore. Agreed the manufacturing process of Mono-crystalline is costly thereby the cells are costly to fabricate and overall price is higher. But now Manufacturers have managed to make equally performing Poly-crystalline modules with similar overall size with lower cost of ownership. This panel proves that. I tested both Optimum Operating Voltage (Vmp) & Optimum Operating Current (Imp) and they fall well within the category specifications for the panel by the book. Under normal mid-day sunlight in sunny San Jose the Short-Circuit Current (Isc) using an AMP meter showed little above 5 Amperes of current. While this Short-Circuit Current (Isc) is less than 5.92A specified for the product, I concluded that the conditions of sunlight shining on the panel was not really 100% STC Irradiance thereby having a little less AMP value. Overall the panel is seen to perform adequately. RENOGY 10A PWM Charge Controller - 3 stars! ----------------------------------- The included charge controller in this 'basic budget' kit is well.. 'basic' indeed. This controller while it is far better compared to Sunforce 7 Amp Charge Controller which I own and reviewed earlier here on Amazon. I still find this 'not ideal' if you want to expand your panel capacity later. It will work just fine with this 100w panel included in this kit, But if you add more panels to your project you are better off getting a MPPT charge controller matching the capacity of your panel's output which are far superior in performance and makes best use of the available sunlight to charge your batteries and provide better efficiency. The rule of thumb is never to max out. Ideally for safety reasons do not exceed 80% of charge controller current rating. This rating should be based on the total short-circuit (Isc) of the solar panel(s) attached to the charge controller. The LED indicators are basic: - Solar Panel Green LED 'ON' - Solar panel is receiving light (Duh!) - Green Solar Panel LED 'blinking' (The controller has detected over-voltage) - Battery LED - Green 'ON' means battery voltage level is right but the charger is charging the battery. - Battery LED - Green 'Blinking' means the Battery is Full - Battery LED - ORANGE means battery voltage is low The same 'bi-color' LED will display in 'RED' color when there a load 'cutoff' event occurred like fuse blown or battery is disconnected for example. The '2 digit' LED display is numeric in nature and is only for displaying work mode. 'Work mode' being for controlling the Lights on the load side indicated by the DC load bulb icon on the charge controller. You can use the 'SET' button and set different so called work modes. For example: 00- means keep the lights ON from 'dusk-to-dawn' 01- means turn the Lights ON after 1 hour after sun down etc; 16- This mode lets user to use the SET button to manually turn the load ON/OFF 17- This is for TEST mode. The charge controller is run by both battery power & Solar Power. The 'idle' power draw at night when it is displaying status LED is >= 10mA, When the 2 Digit LED display is working it consumes >=22mA. It might be of a concern to low AMP batteries as it can drain the batteries when left unattended. But for a CAR battery or larger capacity 10mA of phantom current drain is not a big issue but better to be aware of. The charge controllers screw type posts are not heavy duty and you may damage them if you force a 8AWG wire into them. I think it was meant for 14AWG wires. But if you solder your wire ends and carefully insert them and tighten them with screws the contraption will work just okay. The underside of the charge controller acts as a heat-sink. Plan on allowing some air flow to keep the charge controller cool in extreme loads and ambient temperatures. Included 10' extension solar PV cable - 3 stars! --------------------------------------- The Included 10 feet extension cable is actually '5 feet' of usable length as you need both the + & - leads to connect it to a charge controller. I do not understand why solar manufacturers tends to market them at the maximum length. Just creates confusions for the end users. Overall the cables are fairly thick 'Multi-stranded' and just OK. Meets the specifications. Not sure about the longevity as they have not been put to real world tests yet. Universal Z brackets - 5 stars! ---------------------- These Z brackets are needed to mount the solar panels on the flat surface. The screws included are meant to be used on metal surfaces. If you are planning to mount this on wooden roof surface you need to use wood screws. The materials used in this Universal Z brackets are excellent quality. No sharp edges. It is nicely made to mount the panel safely and securely. That pretty much sums up what this kit includes. I have yet to fully use this in my solar hobby project as it is currently an 'on-going' project which includes various other sub projects that I need to finish-up before I can fully utilize this kit. Overall nice kit which has a good value for money. EDIT Jan 17, 2014 (Product has changed ??) ------------------------------------------- It seems the product has changed as the pictures of the charge controller also seems different than mine when I purchased for $179.99 on September 2013. Looks that Renogy listened to users like me and is now giving a better offering. If it is not mislabeled by Amazon by mistake then you are getting a even better deal with Renogy 30 Amp PWM Charge Controller  and nice long QTY 2 20 feet Solar Extension Cables. Hope this proves useful to you. Cheers! Overall Full Four Stars from me. I hope this review proves useful to you.

I bought The Kite Runner for my daughter for her summer homework assignment going into sophomore year. According to her, It is a very well written book with a smooth flow that transfixes, keeping the reader in the complicated mind of the main character, Namely Amir. Here is her review of the book in her own words! I was supposed to analyze every chapter; unfortunately I kept missing the end of the chapters! The Kite Runner tells of two Muslim boys growing up in Afghanistan, one Amir who grows up in a well-to-do house, and one Hassan, a servant who grows up in a lowly hut. Amir and Hassan live almost like brothers. In an effort to gain approval from his remote father, Amir resolves to win a kite fighting tournament at all costs. But, are your honor and the life of a true friend a reasonable cost to gain a few days of a father's affection? In one instant, crouched in a dark alley and witnessing something no one ever should, Amir makes a decision that defies his conscience, the consequences of which will change both his life and that of Hassan. In a vivid land treasuring honor and dignity, where children with no fathers beg for baksheesh, in a time where the Taliban has utter control, Housseni writes a heart-wrenching story of a young boy who fights guilt and shame into manhood, finds love and courage in a foreign land, and returns to his home to fix a terrible mistake committed twenty-six years before. I found the flow of the book slightly broke nearing the end. I got confused with events, had to double-back, and rack my brains to figure out what sort of message Housseni was trying to pass on. [Sigh, homework so keeps you from enjoying a good book] Also, I personally like predictable, happy endings, but this one left you needing more. It does seem, nearing the end of the book, like you can predict what happens next. It's not a perfect ending, but there's hope for every type of reader. I still liked it anyway. This story comes full circle; you'll see why when you read it. Really. Read it. After reading this review, you know you have to buy one! - Go get one!

Well after reading the reviews here and comments on the discussion boards I finally bought one for myself just to see the charger in action. This is not the first NiMH battery charger that I have collected over the years, but honestly speaking this one surely stands out best and works better than any one that I have owned so far.

It is well worth the money spent! Especially the freebies that come with the charger, The Travel Bag, C Size D Size Battery adapters, 4 AAA and 4 AA NiMH batteries itself makes up for the shortfalls one might encounter with this product.

PROS

[+] Compact Size, Charges both AA and AAA NiCD and NiMH batteries
[+] LCD display to show each individual battery capacity and Voltage which takes the guess work out of the picture when Typical RED or GREEN LED's are involved.
[+] Programming is possible for each slot or you can press couple of buttons and get all the batteries charged/discharged or tested, you can read the current status of the charging or discharging of each battery at a glance nice!

CONS

[-] No Backlight for LCD, It is impossible to see this charger in action in a dark room!
[-] Buttons can be sticky at times - May be my unit is flakey
[-] Only two slots (Slot 1 and Slot 4) can be used to super charge with 1800ma current when this mode is enabled, the Slot 2 and Slot 3 gets disabled by the microprocessor.
[-] It is not a fast charger, Average time for 2700mAH AA Batteries can take up-to 3-4 hrs depending on what charge state the batteries were to begin with.
[-] The Separate Power Adapter is needed (Included in the package) to get the unit to function, Portability could have been greatly increased if they had Power Switching unit built right into the charger.
[-] Build quality is so and so... seeing those tiny SMD resistors taking all that discharge load of all four slots makes me wonder won't they just fall off from the board when they overheat? - May be I am just too paranoid!

Overall, this is a good product - Go buy it as soon as it becomes available on Amazon!

Firstly, to those who gave this film a 1 or 2-star rating: The seller got it wrong when he/she referred to it as a comedy. Its actually a drama with comedic aspects. Also, yesMany of the scenes are sad, even in the first 1/2 hour or 45 minutes. Inaptly named Grace has him jump out of the window. While they're at that rocky beach, Little Miss asked him if he wanted to hold her favorite glass/crystal horse & he accidentally dropped it, breaking it. Both girls were angry, and when Little Miss told him to get away from her & she hates him, you can already see that he has a number of slight expressions on his face because he turned & walked away with his head down & a remorseful expression on his face, until he noticed the driftwood from which he carved out an original horse for Little Missthe one she was holding when she died. Yes, the topic of mortality in this film can be a thing many people don't want to recognize, but the blame belongs with nature. I was unlucky enough to be born with one deadly disease that caused another deadly disease. Every beating heart ceases to beat at some inevitable point. The point is that he DIDNT want to be immortal, so considering Little Miss death & the answer Portia gave him regarding the fact everyone he loves will leave was why Andrew runs to Rupert, presenting his designs for prosthetic organs. Scientists are already testing actual prosthetic organs, and could you imagine how many lives could be saved since theres a shortage of organs? If enough were made, I could receive a transplant as soon as my MELD score jumps up a bit. These bionic/human creations could change the face of transplantation as we know it!
Then theres Andrew, himself, who, even with a positronic brain, is NOT a mistakehes just unique. He has real human emotions. For very sick folks such as myself, I lie here wishing I had my own Andrew, to be my caregiver, & that I would demand one such as Andrew because he has true sympathy (I mean cmon: Andrew felt badly for sperm)a wonderful thought for a transplant patient with no real caregiver. Id be so good to him, and Id teach him things which weren't programmed into him, just as did Richard.
Oh, Kendall Brian HunterId say Robin Williams thoughts on suicide are moot, since he committed suicide.
Perhaps it was corny in certain scenes, yet logic dictates Andrews sense of humor after Richard taught him about jokes. In no way, as well, did Williams supersede the other characters (the Martins were clearly fleshed out characters, and rightly so since Andrew had no true sense of time. The familys lineage was not gratuitous. In fact, it made the average film watcher understand the miracle of genetics, and beautifully so.

I love his dissonant notes in the Twin Peaks soundtracks, which create a moody, haunting atmosphere. In addition, Badalamenti and Lynch's song, "A Real Indication", debuted as Bobby and Laura resolve an argument at school and he walks away, the song's lyrics resonate with both characters in separate ways. The only song sung by Julee Cruise, the melancholy "Questions In a World of Blue", appears on this album, as well, as well as the Theme song from the film which plays during the opening credits. Various other instrumentals appear including a TP montage, which blend most of Badalamenti's instrumentals from both the show and the film.
One weird thing though, and this is not a complaint at all: the song "Sycamore Trees", which appears in the final episode of the 2nd season when Coop first enters the Black Lodge, sung by Jimmy Scott. After all, however, when was David Lynch ever known for NOT being weird?

I bought this cd haphazardly at Kim's Underground in NYC about 12 years ago at the recommendation of one of the employees, and it has been one of my all-time faves ever since.  Chan's voice may not be the most attractive, but it and her music convey an unconventionally sad and beautiful melodic portrait with raw intensity in this melancholic, and oftentimes emotionally fueled album.  My favorite tracks?  Well, "Bathysphere" is an angrily obvious ode to adolescent angst and delivers with satisfying intensity;  "King Rides By" is one of the most gorgeously humble and tragic love songs ever produced.  I highly recommend this album if you dig that sort of thing.

Not counting Cloris Leachman, who is hands-down one of the best elements of this film, the film itself isn't bad. In fact, it's kinda good. It takes place in the seventies, during the days of Charles Manson and his cult. The protagonist, a young boy visiting his grandparents for a spell as his parents work out their problems and interested in the Manson cases, is told from the beginning to stay out of the cornfield, but unable to not take a bite of this forbidden fruit he finds himself exploring its insides and makes a horrible discovery. Further disconcerting is when his grandfather takes him into town where the boy is approached by a strange young hippie woman who creeps him out by something she says to him. She seemed to be with a small group of hippies hanging around a van. Further disconcerting, and frightening, is a man that the young boy sees in places such as on the street and around his grandfolks' house. Is this mystery man merely a ghost, or even more horrifyingly, is he real?
Much of the tone of the film is one of tension:  hearing voices in the cornfield, hearing and seeing people outside of the house at night, ominous shots of the cornfield, the mystery man, and the suspicious nature of the hippie strangers.
If for anything, the performance of Mel Brooks' seasoned muse Cloris Leachman is a great reason to watch the film. She brings life to her character through curmudgeonly crassness, deadpan sarcasm, and her signature dry wit.

Firstly, Deb in MI, even though you wrote your review six years or so ago and if nobody's told you, Young Frankenstein was intentionally shot in black & white to capture the old-era feeling of the original Frankenstein and Bride of Frankenstein. It should and hopefully will never be available in color. The color that is referred to on the disc has to do with the special features, I'm sure.
To Alric the Red: Iwhile I do agree with you that the quality of the video should be much better, the close-ups you refer to that increase the "graininess were not a post-production issue since non-linear editing did not exist at the time. The " graininess you refer to are pixels, and the squiggles are not actual squiggles, but are actually the movement of the characters and the ever-changing image of the props and background as the camera moves. While I do believe the blu-Ray transfer of a DVD transfer (losing a great amount of quality), I don't believe that in post-production it was quality and shade-corrected with a simple photo editing software. I don't even believe Photoshop was utilized for that. I'm guessing it was either done in Final Cut Pro or Avid, and quite lazily, I might add if the original film print was available for transfer. However, it's possible that it may not have been available, for reasons such as, let's say, legal issues or something.
In regard to the film, itself, anyone who denies it's not a hilarious classic is kidding themselves. For those of you who haven't seen it yet, don't listen to the guy who actually has the wherewithal to compare its comedic genius to Scary Movie 3. At least he redeemed himself a bit by comparing it to Animal House, as well, but still. The film is unique in its execution and fresh comedy, For those of you who agree with the guy in the above paragraph, perhaps you'd fare better buying something like Ted or Bad Teacher.

David Lynch's most narratively straightforward and touching story of the real life John Merrick (formally Joseph Merrick) who suffered from a horrific case of elephantitis and was rescued by a kind doctor (the great Sir Anthony Hopkins of Silence of the Lambs fame, of course) from a cruel, sadistic opportunist of a freak show owner and provides him with much more than medical help, but also befriends him and introduces him to a number of equally kind people.
I've found this film to be one of the most moving I've ever seen. The ending made me cry like a little baby. I also found Laura Palmer in Twin Peaks: FWWM to be a very sympathetic character, as you feel both her deep sadness and terror, but being an emotional person, myself and embarrassingly admitting this, even Laura Palmer and her terrible plight wasn't even as utterly heartbreaking to me, partly because The Elephant Man was treated so horribly his entire life despite the fact that he was intelligent, kind, and polite man and also because it is a true story.

Despite its shortness I enjoyed the book for what it was worth. However, I found a couple of Burns' theories to be incorrect according to the series. For instance, he says he believes that Bob is the "Dweller on the threshold" when in the series, as Hawk explains the legend of the Black Lodge to Coop, he clearly states that the "Dweller on the threshold" is the Shadow Person of the person inside the Black Lodge who is either trying to pass through to the White Lodge or trying to get back to our world.
There was another inconsistency in one of his theories which I can't recall at the moment, but other than this it was an interesting, short (although I must confess I craved a bit more), concise read.

I do agree with other reviewers that it makes no sense to have a bake or broil when it has no temperature control. Broil cooks with heat from the top of the toaster or regular oven, yet the heat comes from the bottom for everything. You cant choose a temperature at which to bake something, so basically, anything you cook in it is being toasted & not baked, and because the rack is too close to the heater one has to make sure to turn over whatever one is trying to cook. It means you have to keep an eye on it to make sure the bottom doesnt get burnt. I tried making buttermilk biscuits in there, but since they're not supposed to be turned upside down the bottoms got burnt & was too hard on my teeth, and the tops of the biscuits were not done. I had to put them back in upside down & keep checking them, which is annoying & sometimes pains me since Im very sick. I was gonna use the toaster to bake polymer clay pieces for jewelry making and dollhouse accessories, but I realized I cant use this toaster for that because to bake Fimo I have to set a specific temperature. Also, polymer clay should be removed from the oven 15 minutes after baking, and even in 15 minutes (youre not supposed to turn the clay pieces upside down) the bottoms of the pieces will get burnt, and probably quite badly since the pieces I make are very small. It doesnt give me any grief as far as how long it takes to toast anythingIve made eggos several times in there and toasted a corn muffin which I usually always turn over after cutting it in half, & just made sure I flipped them after about 5-7 minutes & would continue toasting for three more minutes. They came out fine. Two stars for the toaster featureif I didn't have to keep an eye on this toasters pyromania. I now realize I need a different, better toaster for the polymer clay projects since I make beads & things for my jewelry business. Saw a Black & Decker one for cheaper & it has temp control, so I plan to order it on the third of April. Better brand, anyhow.

I have worn a Luminox Navy seal watch for over 20 years. Yes, the glow does eventually dim and it needs to be replaced. The two things that always bothered me about the Luminox.
1. Plastic case
2. No screw down crown (It never leaked however)
I decided to give this Smith & Wesson a try. I really like the Tritium watches because they are so good in the dark.

The two watches could be clones in size and shape, both come with a Velcro cloth band and the same features. Glow very bright on both.

 Pros for S&W
1. The S&W is cheaper
2. The S&W has all the letters marked on the rotating bezel, Luminox has ticks for the 5,15, 25, 35, 45 and 55 positions.
3. S&W has a screw down crown.

Pros for Luminox
1. The LumInox has a tritium tube marking the 12 o" clock on the rotating bezel the S&W has a regular light dependent glow phosphor.
2. The Luminox has a tritium tube on the second hand., S&W a phosphor.
3. Luminox movement made in Switzerland vs Taiwan for the S&W.
4. S&W is heavier since it has a steel case. (not sure if that's bad or not)

So far the S&W keeps perfect time and the metal case is more scratch resistant than the Luminox. The bands wear is similar to the Luminox and IME needs changing annually.

Very bright and as per my watt meter are actually 150 watts. Comparison to HID is difficult because one is single bulb and this is multibulb emitter.  This does burn cooler than HID. These are very good in vertical umbrella type fixtures. If you plan on using them horizontally I wouldn't recommend it because a lot of the light is reflected either to the ceiling or into the fixture and not down to the floor. Unless that's what you want. Not a detriment to the light itself, just not the best way to use them IMO.  The LEDS are very white (I'm think 5-6K) and could support horticulture. You may need an adapter to use a HID fixture that was previously connected to a ballast since this can run on 110 AC current.

For a second I thought I could make it work with my own hardware but I get tired of fixing other folks mistakes so I sent it back.

I really like the tritium watches for being easy to see at night. I have owned 2 Luminox and 1 Smith and Wesson with tritium. In the overall comparison, this watch is a little bigger than the other 2, is cheaper but glows just as brightly. Like the Smith and Wesson, the case is made out of metal, but unlike the S&W it doesn't have a screw in crown, but it does have a lighted second hand that the SW does not.. The Luminox is plastic and doesn't have a screw in crown either, plus it is the most expensive of the three watches. The band on this watch is a little short and kind of uncomfortable but I planned on changing it when I bought it, so no surprise there. They make one with a metal band that is more expensive, something to look into if you like metal bands. The watch seems to run fine and keeps accurate time. I gave it 4 stars because of the terrible band and absence of a screw in crown. It's a good cheap alternative to all the other tritium watches on the market. Update 08/2017: I dropped the watch, my fault . The hands a big and have some weight to them. They moved and now collide with each other. I have dropped watches before and this never happened. I went back to the S&W.

What an amazing follow up to Blood For Life!! I could not put this down! Yes I did catch the little extras Lorrox put in there for us to find,very clever!! Just for a minute let's talk about his writing, the kind the greats have, grabs ahold of you and leaves you begging for more!! I love being an AR reader for writers like this!! Now I want to be a Knight of the Vampires!! June captured my heart, and her relationship with Beatrice is amazing. Eddy and June will make an awesome couple . Skip is the most patient human and father ever, where most dads freak out over little things, he is taking the whole zombie/vampire thing very well! Will we be seeing Skip turn in a coming book ? I want a love like Charlie and Sadie! This book is a testament to the strength and loyalty of the family. Heart wrenching in a certain spot, will leave you with a tear or two! I got angry and sickened along with them. I am now part of the Costanza family!! Now onto the next one!! I hope they carve up Melengrad!!

Usually I'm not one to read Sci-Fi. Took me a while to get into this book. So now that I'm done,I'm eager to read the next one..With that being said, let me give my eye into it,not on how good the writer is,we all know he is excellent,to be able to go from one to another to another,and jump back and forth like the book does..That takes amazing talent. Now, when I read a book I look at the Title and its meaning..So I will start from there..I'm, taking it Mr. Sanders didn't go by Miriam Websters definition on his words, not after reading the book, Paralysis, disabling of the nerves, a Paradox takes us out of our way of thinking. Now I see why. I have read a book before about someone living with different lives all at one time,but never jumping from one to another. Have we all lived different lives? The book says it takes us through 4 different lives,I counted 5..Maybe someone will too. We started out with what could be a robot,from there it takes on a Quantum leap/Highlander/Space Odyssey feel to it..Then we are introduced to Charlie,era 1911, 3 days had passed since he remembers being there,but in this 1911 reality only a few seconds..What really happened?  Then boom asleep,and wake up as a Prince in 1168, remembering a skull he had been looking for that had something to do with this time period back in or was that into 1911? So, now we have Richard...We meet the love of his life,Yvette. And are introduced to the black sludge later on..I noticed this was first time something was said that caught this souls attention and made him start to pay attention to each life and try to remember...Next is Vicky, a 1996 spoiled,computer literate,teenager,with a horrible stepmother,Dr. for a "father",and money,she lives in the Soviet Union,surrounded by secrets,she was also my favorite and smartest character, she also notices this sludge and remembers it from Richards life. One thing I learned,is none of these lives,souls,programs can drink.they start spouting nonsense..As the story progresses,the lives start changing quicker and quicker,more and more people from each life are trying to tell them something,but it seems as if each time that happens..You hear this..STOP..RESET!!!! So, I will!! Hope you enjoy as much as I did.

A book of shorts. I must say,these were a first for me. From the very first one to the last. The imagination of the writer. Some laughs and some OMG moments. The Thumbalina story was too funny. The stories can be dark and scary. Some like when you face your abuser in prison,is right up my alley. In my way of thinking to be able to come up with this many different tales and put them all together in one place, takes talent. When I read up on the writer,he has had so many different adventures himself,I know where the settings for his stories come from. I must use a quote from one of his stories"You can't stop a madness whose hour has come." That line just seemed to fit in with today's world. Thank you for the laughs and the shake my head moments..I'm sure the other readers will enjoy this also.

I guess when you are used to running a fortune 500 company and retire,you write children's adventure books. Whodathunkit? Well,for one I sure am glad Art did. We are introduced in the 1st book of a series of 9,to two typical boys, Archibald and Jockabeb, and their many adventures. This first book takes us into the forest, wrought with tales of ghost,and evil that lurks at every turn..So, how many boys do you know that would stay out of there? I'm a girl,like their sister Tess,and I wouldn't stay out,especially when I was their age. So, off they go. What starts out as a jaunt into the woods,turns into an adventure of a lifetime,that teaches them about themselves,and most importantly teaches them what is important in life, family, honor,friendships. Can you imagine, a map?  A hidden cave,a cursed Dragon? How about half crow/wolf creatures? Would you run or go deeper?An Indian boy,centuries old,they help. that in turn helps them, a beautiful bay horse they name Uno,that is also intertwined with the Indian boy, who seems to be theirs and Tess' protector.  Mystical, magical places hide deep in this forest. A place hidden so deep time stands still. A story so wrapped in mystery and magic. I am eagerly awaiting the next adventures. really hoping the involve Tess more. For a childs adventures book, this kid at heart really enjoyed it.

I have just finished the Guardians of the Boundary. Last book of the series I thought until I opened my email two weeks ago and had the new Edge of Pathos waiting for me from Kristen herself. Thats how I got to read the 2nd and 3rd book also..And for that I say thank you thank you thank you..Valerie must make the decision to led..The fracture is stronger,the Conjurors are divided,Reaper is making a good argument, but for the Globe and Earth to survive they must fight to keep their magic and way of life safe..The Pillars of Light must stand strong together..Is that possible?Or will the prophecy come true? A truly magical tale,woven with beauty,wonder,and imagination..A great work of art. Kristen takes you on a journey in your mind,across the universe to a different world,she has a way to make you feel as if you are full of magic yourself. As Valerie says,"We all have a little bit of magic in us..I can't wait to read the new one.

Picked up excellently from book one..I really enjoyed how the twins are starting to learn about their new world and magic..But still need to learn who to trust..I did receive a big shocker though..I've got one more to read,until I can get my hands on the other books..For a self published book,she did well

What an amazing story..I couldn't wait to see what he did next..And I saw the imagery of the ISIS group led by a Muslim man angry at America named Barack. Maybe it's just me but seems familiar sorta..It's a very well written book and I'm anticipating what Drake and Mike do next..No matter what you try to do,you will always be a soldier..These guys better watch it, with the cliffhanger at the end of the book,it's gonna be a great new story next..Can't wait till its available as a read and review or free..

Anna survived a devastating betrayal by her friends, survived cancer and ended up fulfilling her dreams. All with the faith of a mustard seed. Always a pleasure to read these books!!

I was part of the chatterbox from houseparty. I was excited to review this book,as there is nothing like a good mystery. This is the first book I have read from this author, and I am not disappointed. I quiet garden setting,two sibblings just found each other,and disgruntled nephew and a fte coming up all in one. Sounds easy enough right? Well it would be if they didn't unearth a 1940 something German airplane with a not so German body in the same grave..You know its somewhere,says so in book. But you kinda get caught up in story,hoping for that one bit to reach out and pull you in..There it is..From there on it is a rollercoaster of emotions for the characters and you the reader..I think there was about 4 people I thought did it, on I didn't mention the other murder? That's the other great part..Just grab a copy and read..It will stump you to the very end..I will have to keep reading more of these..Loved it.

I don't know if I should look at this book as a BDSM book, or a Stockholm syndrome book. Either way, the man got changed. A little extremely if I do say so myself. I did find myself towards the end, though, not being able to put it down. The final change, when he was seeing all he had done wrong. How profoundly it affected him, to the point of almost death. Almost Biblical, when we accept a new way of life, the old us dies. Of course he was going to fall in love with her eventually. Of course he would loose his best friend. I was hoping, that, eventually the meditating would resonate with him. Not to be.. An extremely different way of writing and capturing your attention. The ending was a bit of a cliffhanger though. I may or may not read next one to see where it goes.

Took me a while to get into the book,as there is a lot of descriptions of each branch of foreign military and police. Takes a while to get into the guts of the book,which to me is the violence and action. The difficulty level of the different languages,took a lot of getting used to. That made me see the genius of the story. I know for one thing,Sarah is definitely one not to screw with. I fell in love like she did with Michael and the SAS.  Now to the part that I just really loved,the taking down of the drug cartel. Brought to light the horrible drug trade. Very detailed in how they work and take over one town or in this case Country at a time. The execution of the take down were,detailed,thought out and blood pumping. The last part of the book was my favorite,with a few exceptions of lives lost. The rating is for how long it took to get to the point or action of the book. Endure on and finish it,you will be glad you did.

Follow the unsettling life of a 15 year old boy David. After the sudden,but,not unexpected death of his young mother. His subsequent rejection by his worthless father. He is tossed  into the system. He lives by the pop ups of feelings,anger,fear,loss of reality. When they pop up he uses his fists to deal with them. Calls himself a trauma baby. I was so excited when I seen that the writer actually  incorporated the title into the story. How he,the writer,could have very well been taking us on his own personal journey through his teenage years,crossed my mind many times. David isn't really a bully,more of a kid that just goes along with the flow,until the flow gets interrupted. Doesn't really seem to grasp the concept of action and reaction too well. Just sees most of his actions as a means to an end. That is until he meets Lucy and Jacob. I believe those two people,have made the most impact, since loosing his mother,on his life. He starts trying to be different,he promised. So how did it all end up like it did?

I did not expect to be the first person to review this great product, but here goes.

The system shipped and arrived before the scheduled date. I used to to sharpen my 20 year old Benchmade Stryker Auto and was very impressed with the results. Called a friend and said, "Bring me some knives!" He showed up with a pile of +50 year old forged Bowie knives and other knives that were in very bad shape. He said he bought a box full of knives from some old guy for $20 and the guy said he had them for a long time. They all took a lot of work to bring them to a decent edge, but they all are now razor sharp. Since I recently moved, I had no knives, so I went to the store and bought a set of cheap non-serrated steak knives and got them cutting like scalpels. I also needed some kitchen knives, so a bought a few cheap ones. All are now sharp and usable without a lot of effort.

CONS: Is this device perfect? In a word, no. Let's talk about the faults for a moment.

1. The swivels tend to stick sometimes, but a little oil on them and they loosen right up. I can't complain about that. I can't expect the swivels to work without some lubrication.

2. The vice attaches to the stone base with two machine screws with grommets on the bottom of the base. This forces you to use stick-on rubber feet at the corners. These stick-on feet do not stick very well on the rough surface of the bottom of the stone. Had the bottom been polished like the top and sides, they might stick better. I would have preferred to see the holes for the screws countersunk so the screws sit flush with the bottom surface, and that would allow a full sheet of non-slip rubber (shelf liner) on the bottom of the base. I will probably make this modification myself, but it should have been right from the factory. This is minor and not worth taking away a star.

3. With the price of this unit, it should have come with the Low Angle Adapter. You cannot sharpen a knife with a small blade, such as a classic multi-blade pocket knife without this adapter. The adapter cost ~$70. Still, I knew this in advance and I will not remove a star for it.

PROS: They got a lot right. This is a well thought out machine. I believe this is the third generation.

1. Set the thing on the table, grab a chair and get to work. It takes some time to get the bevel right from the hilt to the tip of the blade, but it is not hard work. Once you get finished with the 100 grit, you will progress through the others in order very quickly.

2. There is a ruler that attaches to the dual pin alignment tool. Use this, so that you can record how each knife is setup. This will allow you to get repeatable results the next time you sharpen the same knife. This way, you won't have to start with the 100 grit. You will be able to just start with the higher grits and do a quick touch up. As a tip, each time I do an original sharpening on a knife, I set it in the vice with the ruler and take a good photo of it. I name the photo of the knife with the brand, model, where the tip measures on the ruler, whether I used the top or bottom hole, and what angle settings I used. I then organize these photos in a folder with the owner's name.

3. The stones that the device comes with will be all that the average person will need. I seem to be doing a bunch of heavy Bowie knives and they need a lot of metal removed, so I did order the 50/80 set of stones to hog off that metal a lot faster. BUT, these are all diamond impregnated steel and they cut very aggressively. They remove a lot of metal in a hurry. These are not your grand dad's whetrock. Unlike other devices that use stones that don't stay flat, these are metal and they will remain flat and function properly for a long long time. TIP: Wipe down the blade before switching to the next finer grit. This is very important.

4. Leather strops are available and I did purchase these and use them with diamond paste. For most knives, I don't need them. Only a few knives really need the show polished edge. Regular old butcher knife? No. Filet knife? Yes. Steak knives? No. Your everyday carry pocket knife? Yes. If you buy the strops, PLEASE store each one in a separate zip lock baggie. You do not want them to touch each other and contaminate the different micron diamond compounds. I cannot stress this enough. Wipe down the blade between each progression to a finer grit to keep from contaminating the compounds. The compounds imbed themselves into the leather of the strop, so if they get contaminated with a different grit, you will have to throw that strop away. These things are way too expensive to be tossing them in the trash because of user error.

DANGEROUS: Use extreme caution when sharpening knives.

1. If you have children, setup in an area where you can keep them out. The same goes for pets.

2. You are going to be working in a moving pattern just an inch or less from the edge of a sharp blade. Be careful. Be sober. Get "cut resistant gloves" and use them every time. Repeat, EVERY TIME! I recommend these. http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0119UBIYG?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_detailpage_o06_s00 They are soft, flexible, comfortable, washable, and there is no reason that you should ever sharpen knives without them.

3. Don't reach over the knife that you are working on. Setup your work area so that everything can be in easy reach without having to get close to the sharp blades. Your blades will be sharp enough to cut to the bone with little to no force.

4. Do not sharpen knives if you are taking medication that might make you drowsy. Do not sharpen knives if you are drinking alcohol. Do not sharpen knives if you are not in a good mood and able to completely focus on the task at hand. If you feel distracted, stop! It's just not worth the risk.

5. Setup your work area with good lighting from multiple directions. Get a big (5 inch) magnifying glass to inspect the edge as you work. I use one like this. http://www.amazon.com/Carson%C2%AE-SureGrip-Acrylic-Magnifier-SG-14/dp/B0013KMW8Y/ref=sr_1_6?ie=UTF8&qid=1452291708&sr=8-6&keywords=magnifying+glass

Would I buy this thing again? Absolutely! It was expensive and I had to really think about it before spending that much money, but after using it for several days and sharpening a bunch of knives of different quality, I feel like it was worth every penny. I am planning on doing some sharpening services, and also some knife restoration services, so this device will easily pay for itself. For the average person that only needs to sharpen their own knives, there are cheaper devices such as the Lansky that will fill the need. If you want to professionally sharpen blades for some extra money (like me) or as a full-time job, this is probably the best way to get consistent "knife show quality" results.

NOTE: If you are planing to setup a permanent work area, and you can mount the vice directly to the workbench, then you can get the unit without a base and save yourself some money. If not, this stone base is very heavy and makes this unit very stable.

This latest Jericho Quinn novel in the series just seemed to go over the top in believe-ability. I would have given it a higher rating just for the intense fast paced action novel it is, but the author should have made it more believable in content. I don't want to repeat the novel but it is impossible to believe that our government can corrupt so many people to kill on sight, a citizen of the US. The main character could have contacted any news outlet to post his story, or use of social media to get word out of wrongdoing by our government agencies or individuals. In addition many of the elected representatives could have launched investigations against the corruption the author described. I would like to think that Americans like to listen and make informed decisions for themselves.
