The main male protagonist is sad and unfortunate to have met and married an "unstable" woman. She stole another woman's baby, coerced her husband to remain quiet, and got insanely mad when he did the right thing to contact the real mother. The whole scene is just too "maniac" and I almost wanted to give up reading halfway.
I wish Ms Stedman well and good luck with her next novel.

cands.text: Despite the fact this novel is not as masterfully crafted as others, I had a hard time putting it down. The style is direct, succinct, and yet personal. The male protagonist, Pat, is adorable, full with contradiction, compassionate, simple and, simultaneously, complicated. He has no clue why the world is against him and still believes in silver linings. Tiffany, Pat's counterpart, is awkward, eccentric, loud, and yet fragile. Together they paint the most unbelievable vista of a love story. There were a few times I felt hard to swallow because of the heavy sensation in my throat. I wanted to cheer for Pat, and secretly hoped what he would reunite with his (ex)lover.

I love the "content" of the book. Very inspiring. Obviously the author has sacrificed a lot for the sake of the family. Who wouldn't? It is humourous and sad at the same time. Occasional run-on sentences are okay. When the whole page is full of run-ons and very long paragraphs, it becomes confusing. I some times find myself lost, both in a good way and bad way, in the book because it is both stunning and confusing.

The author is trying to relate to his younger brother but that doesn't mean he has to talk like a high school cheerleader. I love and dislike this book. I feel so conflicted.

Give it a try. You may like it. If you can look over those those extremely long paragraphs and pages filled with run-on sentences, you may appreciate what is truly underneath the sea of words - the invaluable brotherly love.

I would give it a four stars. I like the pseudo logics and the fairy tale part. The plot linking the two protagonists is intriguing. What really turns me off is the vulgar sex part. The author keeps saying it is nothing sexual except the act is undeniably sexual. I am not a closed minded person but one of them is a minor! I would be okay if the author is honest about the sex part. It leaves a bitter taste.

Like many people, I have also read The Giver and Gathering Blue. The Messenger is difinitely the shortest and easiest to read. Unlike the first two novels, the setting is not a dystopian society. The world is nice, people helping each other, no lies, no hostility. Then the world is slowly, subtly, being conrrupted by greed, power struggle and deceipt. No one notices the change until there is casuality. The theme mirrors the founding philosophily of USA, and, henceforth, the beauty. It made me think about the people around me and how we "trade" tangible physical attributes with inner beauty, and the ultimate "messenge" the messenger fights to convey.
I real like this book, more than Gathering Blue but not as much as the Giver.

I really want to love this book. First of all, it has more than a thousand reviews. It is definitely a sign of a good book. I guess I subconsciously compare Divergent to  the Hunger Game, and the Giver, and now I am too old to understand a teenager novel. I found it hard to imagine a society to split into 5 distinctive factions (or virtues), and they are mutually exclusive. Just only a small number of Divergent? I would imagine many "Polyvergent"s. Beatrice seemed very average and self-centered; however, such character is very common in young adult novels. Four, on the other hand, seems almost "bipolar"!
The chemistry between Four and Tris is almost like Edward and Bella in Twilight. It is not bad. It is just nothing new.
There are serious flaws in the story, which are easily spotted but not enough to discourage reading it.
I am glad I finished reading it. Now I can read something else.

I have watched the movie and I likes it so much that I bought the book. It is one of the few occasions I like the movie better. The movie is filmed from the point of view of the mother and the journalist, focusing on the love of the mother to her unknown son. One the other hand. the book is written mostly from the prospective of the son, who was dead, and, thus, the details are reconstructed from interviews, videos, and scant printed materials.
I like how the author tried to put himself in the shoes of Anthony Lee. What I found discomfiting is his assumption of gay culture. He uses words, such as "overt gayness", as if it is a real word with a derogatory notation. The way he describes the gay relationship as "soulful, tortured, beautiful" is just too hackneyed. I had to stop for a second before I could continue reading.
It would be nice if he would spend more time describing the mother. There was much potential (and it was carried out in the movie.)

This book is about the protagonist, Sammy, tired of life and looking for a change. Little does he know, his son, Jacob, is considering the same idea. When Sammy is fired and Jacob is kicked out of school, they bond over a series of unfortunate (and fortunate) events over a weekend.
I pretty much can tell this book is written by a dad. I am too old to be teenage but young enough to remember. When a teenage boy is about to break up with his girlfriend, the last thing he wants is his dad tagging along. It is completely a father's fantasy. Then the father cries and the son holds and rocks him back and forth on the street?
I am old enough to understand why a dad may write this. Many parents want their kids to treat them as equals when the parents never treat their kids as peers. It is a nice fantasy.
The part between Sammy and his dad, however, is more believable. Sammy and his dad are more forgiving as they age. Their edges become dull. Sammy's love for Jacob reminds Sammy of his father. When the grandfather is getting to know his grandson, Sammy realizes how much he doesn't know about his own dad. Therefore, Sammy makes an effort to get to know his father and discovers the unspoken love his father has for him.
This book is about changes, acceptance and redemption. It is quite delightful and makes me think about my own dad.

The novel is sure a pleasant surprise. First, I like how the author interlaces the novel between the perspective of the older and younger antagonists. Mr Jankowski is animated and adorable. I felt like I could really take a glimpse inside an old person's mild. He is a young guy trapped in an old man's body. Jacob is young and innocent, but not as memorable as his older self. The adventure he had is almost like Tom Sawyer and Huck Finn. Sure, there were times I was confused. It doesn't seem so believable to have a college graduate jumping from one railcar to another, and the sex scene is unnecessarily. (I guess female readers demand certain rewards with reading romance novels.) {Spoiler Alert} I still don't understand why Uncle Al needs August for the circus. It seems like Uncle Al could have just replaced August with Jacob and the novel will shortened by half.
I wish Ms Gruen all the best and am looking forward to her coming books.

The movies based on novels are not as good as the novels. This one, however, is an exception. I can see the author projects himself as George. However, George is not desperate. He is actually strong and ready to move on. He doesn't want to forget Jim. At the same time, George also mentions Jim is the Death and George wants to meet another Jim. At the end, George dies as a hopeful man.

I picked up this book because of the good reviews and the number of reviews. Gwen shows us how brave Homer is facing this world. He never gives up hope. I am so glad last time I check Homer is still well. I recommend this book to any pet lovers.

I am glad I finished the book. I was going to quit since I was tired of reading repetitions of ashes, ice, hunger, cold, and more ashes. It doesn't getting better until much later when it was obvious the father is dying. The love of a father and his willingness to sacrifice for his son are crafted beautifully between words. Amid despairs and sickness, the father put up a brave face for his son, shielding him from brutal reality. The hope of the father, "carrying the fire", is sophistically painted near the end of the book. The author is very skillful in using very simple and few words to illustrate such complex and rich human emotions.
I think I am going to read it again to learn how the author orchestras such magnificent plot, scenes and characters.

Very addictive. Incredible plot and memorable characters. Wait till sale.

Graphic is okay.

This book is not a self-help nor a child psychology textbook.
A lot of people criticize the author's method of rising her kids with such stringent and Manichean methods; however, she wrote this book as a memoir. She is pretty honest and often contradict herself (We are only human!) She mentions Chinese people don't praise their kids but she repeatedly reminds the reader how talented her kids are. She describes her elite scholastic linkage, which can be traced back all the way to ancient China. She is married to a "white guy" but she emphasizes she was the first Asian woman he has ever dated (Unlike some guys with yellow fever who date nondiscriminatorily.)
Between the lines, I can see a hard working mother trying her best to raise her kids, sacrificing her time and energy and putting herself at risk of being disliked by her daughters. The quarrels between the author and her daughters are amusing (to me.) Even I myself am a first generation Chinese, I don't have any desire to have children. I was born in Hong Kong and I didn't come to US penniless.
The book turns out to be more interesting than I have expected. Just remember don't take it as some kind of guide book. This book is meant to be a memoir of a competitive mother trying to raise her children.
I have hardly read 5 pages and I already have goosebumps. I think I am biased. This genre is definitely not my type.

I wasn't interested in the book at first. Maybe the title? Perhaps the color of the cover? "My Heartbeat" sounds so trite.
This book is one of the books one the top of the list. Moreover, it was available.
I was wrong. Never judge a book by its cover (or its title if it matters.)
The characters are so familiar and yet so foreign. Until later in the book I realized I was once like them but now I am an adult. I don't even remember some of the names of the people I treasured so much when I was Ellen's (one of the protagonists in the book) age.
My vision was blurry when I read the last chapter. Imagine a grown man with his eyes wet reading a book.
When we are young, we challenge the world around us. May they be our parents, school or taboos. As we get older, we give in and follow, and even become part of the unspoken social norms. Even we know some of the norms are wrong but we keep silent just for the sake of "peace."
I also used to think I wouldn't conform to those unspoken rules and now I am one of the enforcers.
We should all take time to recollect and remember the person inside of us. The ones who are young and free, not afraid to dream nor hesitate to fight for the ideals.
I am glad I have read this book and I've learned what "va te faire foutre means.

I am a biology/pharmacy major. I am reading this book because of my interest in maths. I enjoy reading it because it is easy to understand and there is a lot exercises for me to practice. Some people think this book is not hard enough but I think Dr Strang did a good job. The target readers are general students. I have also been reading David Lays' "Introduction to linear algebra and its applications" and I prefer Dr Strang.

I just read the book and I could not stop crying the last two hours. I myself have a 15 years old cat. I can't say I agree with the author 100% on how he raised his dog but I am sure he tried his best. It is definitely  a good book. I am just surprise how much I have cried the last two hours.

The Daud storyline seems to be better written than the original Corvo storyline. I also like the extra special powers. I wish there is a way they can incorporate those new powers into the original story.

As I was playing the game, I found myself drawn by the manuscript. It was very well written. I wish I could write like that. It is definitely a game in its own class.
As an action game, I found it boring.
As a suspense thriller game, I found it not scary enough. Silent Hill is way more scary.
However, the quality of the storyline is superber. The script is well written.
I can imagine myself reading a novel like that.

At first I had a hard time getting the milk frothy. It seems to work better now I use it almost everyday. Some milk protein must have stuck to the metal mesh and made it more "impermeable."
I wish I have bought more. It is very comfortable. They are more comfortable than the Hane's but they absorb moisture better.

Like some other reviewers have said, it is not a fancy dress shirt. It is more like a casual dress shirt. I wear it to work and I am a clinical healthcare worker. It is not as crisp as I like but no one really care how I dress at work.
I will buy it again if they have another color or pattern.

First I have to confess I am not a Star Wars fan. So I am writing this review strictly as a MMO player.
At first I was kind of interested. A lot of names were foreign to me since I don't speak "Star Wars." I did learn them quickly because a lot of people online have no problem helping and criticizing you.
I was not impressed with the character creation. You don't really have many options. As a result, many players can look very similar to each other. Bioware now let ppl to wear "party wear." I have not yet seen anyone wear them. "Party wear?" I want visibly customizable gears!
It really doesn't matter what gears you obtain before you reach lvl 50. Once you reach lvl 50, everyone expect you to wear War hero or Battlemaster gears for PvP and Columi and Rakata gears. The gears I crafted before lvl 50 suddenly became useless. If you like to play PvP, you may find yourself switching gears back and forth. I find it tedious after the fifth time switching gears.
The 1.3 patch fixed a lot of problem. I have to give kudos to Bioware for the group finder. It is not perfect but it is a big improvement.
Some people are grinders but I don't like grinding just to get gears. It gets old very quickly after grinding for about a month.
If you are a big Star Wars fan and you don't mind grinding, you should give it a try. For me, I am going to let my subscription expire.

users.query:
I am into daily Holosync meditation (for 8 years and counting), focusing on and expecting positive and good and reprograming my mind from past storage of garbage and sabotage thinking.  I began reading this book on October 4, 2011 and finished on November 19, 2011 at 1:40 AM.  I love this book and i love the author Dr. Frederick Bailes.  He wrote this book way before the popular Law of Attraction hit the public.  This book was written in 1957 and has been a powerful additional resource in that all my experiences are controlled by what's in my mind, what i put in my mind via focus and how i use my mind.

I adore the prayer treatments in this book.  My favorite is on page 63 called A Basic Prayer for Expectancy of the Good.  I not only read it for the required 7 days straight but i continue to read each and every morning.  I have also purchased Dr. Bailes books Your Mind Can Heal You (written 1941) and Basic Principles of the Science of Mind 12 lesson home study course (written 1951).  I read and work through both simultaneously.  All i can say is wow!  This man was on point a long, long time ago and completely understood that all things begin and end in our mind.  Defeat or success is determined first and foremost in our minds.  Health and sickness is determined first and foremost in our minds.

One of my favorite paragraghs:  "Nothing negative can find a foothold in me this day.  No doubt or fear can attach itself to me.  No accidents or mistakes can occur because i walk in a path of right action both when i am thinking of it and when i am not.  I release myself and all my affairs this day to the perfect working of that Perfect Law, which turns these thoughts into things."

This stuff is deep.  And if you're willing to approach it with an open mind, without question you will know it to be truth, go forth with it and flourish like we were meant to!

Be well, from NYC... WE ARE THE 99%!

cands.text: I have owned this book for a while, in book form, and on my Kindle.  It was on YouTube where Rev. Ike made mention of Emmet Fox's book The Mental Equivalent that caused me to re-read it with complete and total understanding.  This book is awesome and a must read... and a must put into practice daily.  As stated by Emmet Fox "The door of the soul opens inward."  Amen!

Still loving this book as I begin the New Year 2016.  I have owned and read this book daily since 2012. Love me some Ernest Holmes.  If you enjoy positive words and prayer to start and live your day I recommend this book.  Love and a HAPPY NEW YEAR to all.

I always enjoy Neville Goddard's books, lectures and recordings.  This book ranks at the top with my favorites.  I recommend as this is a quick and powerful read.  Stay strong and do it!

Blessings.

Absolutely amazing.  I finally get it completely.  I have part if not all of this book in audio spoken by Neville.  It's a recording of him live in the meeting teaching this....Live In The End.  Love it.  It's all true.  God creates through my imagination!

This little book is great.  I continue to study and practice the great teaching of Neville Goddard.  The knowing and correct teachings of the imaginative power that is in each of us has been held from millions of us through so many entities it's a crime in my opinion.  If I may say, take your power back, take control of your mind back!  Use your imagination, use your minds eye and see, have and be all that you desire.  I do and it works for me!  Try to prove the Bible (as it is really about) and Neville wrong. You won't be able to.  Peace and Love.

I love reading this book.  I carry it everywhere I go.  It is small, colorful and brings out the joy in my soul.  I have several books and audiobooks by Florence Shovel Shinn.  She was and still is an absolute gem in our lives!

I used to ignore my instincts and intuition and always regretted it.  Not any more.  I stopped doing that before I read this book but this book helped to confirm what I knew to be true.  If you doubt me, just watch what happens when you listen to your gut and when you don't!

God Bless Us Everyone!!

EXCELLENT!  I have another book of Neville's that says the words in this book.  However this book is very short and specific on knowing what we want and using God's great gift of IMAGINATION!  Think it! Imagine it! Do it! You will see it come to pass.  It happens every time!!  Blessings to you and all you love.

What can I say about Emmet Fox and his books that hasn't already been said.  He was a master of the spiritual mind.  I love him.  I have a number of his books and they are all excellent.  Just be careful that you don't buy duplicate writings.  But even so I consider him generous to do that, but just review the books and read the reviews, you could save yourself some money.

This book is a very nice collection of essay's.  I choose to read one or two or three :-) each day along with his Daily Readings book and my prayer treatments.

Hope it's helpful and joyful for you to read as it is for me.

Peace.

A book of wisdom and truth I have read and followed over and over.  Read and practice daily, you will not be disappointed.  Trust and have faith.  All good is within.  Believing in oneself is to believe and know I am one with God.  I am a winner... and so are YOU!!

A very informative and helpful book to move ones life in the direction of positivity and success.  With all the great info I have in my brain from other sources coupled with this awesome step by step book, I got this!!  Much happiness and success to all of us who are willing to do what it takes!!

I grew up in a Baptist church.  My father (bless u daddy) was a minister and my mother (bless u ma) was a lovely saved woman, yet I never knew the right way to pray.  Now I do!

Thank you ma, daddy, and Neville Goddard.  I am practicing prayer this way daily and the blessings flow.  How great is that!

A wonderful book on my Kindle to repeadly reference.

I love this little booklet.  I let my 24 year old son read it and he loves it also.  Since I have The Golden Key within my Emmet Fox book Power Through Constructive Thinking, I'm going to give my son this little pamphlet and purchase a few more for other people.

I grew up listening to Rev. Ike on the radio with my mother.  I now watch his video's, listen and following his wonderful teachings on YouTube.  His son runs the church now, but there was and is only one Rev. Ike !!  This Science of Living Study Guide is an awesome book !!  I have been faithful to reading, re-reading and studying one chapter each week or every two weeks.  Rev. Ike learned a lot from Neville Goddard and as he became more and more popular (and rich) many religious types tried to ruin his reputation, especially in the black community.  Rev. Ike's teachings are based on learning or relearning the fact that God is not a man in the sky, God is the real man in me !!!  God is within each and everyone of us NOT outside of us !!  God and I are one is not just words, IT'S FACT !!  Believing in ourselves is crucial to how our lives play out.  Whatever a man (and woman) believes about himself comes true.  I choose to think all good about myself.  That is something no one in my church, family or friends ever taught me or told me.  I love you Rev. Ike and I know what you taught all those years was golden !!  Money is not the root of evil.  Money is NICE !!  Money doesn't make people evil or do evil things... Those who do evil were that way all along... Money had nothing to do with it !!

Read.  Learn.  Study.  Trust.  Know.  This is how life works.  Neville taught it best.  That's where most if not all of the new-jacks got this stuff from.  Life is great within for me and mine.  Regardless of what's happening outside myself I know exactly who I Am and that has changed everything for me.  God In Me Is My Health.  God Creates Through My Imagination!!

I have always liked classical music but I'm very picky about it.  I love the piano, so when I found this Healing Piano Music classical style I was amazed.  I play it every night sometimes mixed with relaxing water ambience.  I find myself in a peaceful state and off into relax/sleep mode I go.  It's just lovely to listen to.

This great little book in combination with Neville's lessons I am participating in through the freeneville website has proven to be an incredible journey to a positive new way of life for me and my loved one's.

A must share with your young children!

Blessing!

I own this book in paperback first.  It's filled with yellow highlight marks.  I made it a habit to take it with me everywhere (especially to the local laundromat) until I finished it.

I was very happy to get it on my Kindle.  I transferred all the highlights I had in the book to the Kindle copy.  It took a while but was worth it.

I make regular reference to all highlights and re-read the book when possible.  I love Earnest Holmes.  He taught the masses the Science of Mind because he loved people and wanted to help us live the best life he knew God had in-store for us if we would just free our minds from negative thinking and believe that we are one with good.

Blessings to All.
Bleak House, I adore this series!!  Now own it and downloaded to my Kindle HDX!!  Great to watch in the waiting room during appointments.  A masterpiece!!

Indeed a thinkers movie.  I enjoyed Z for Zachariah.  I had never heard of it and didn't know what it was about until I read the synopsis.  I like movies that cause me to think which is why I called it a thinker's movie.  If you are only into action, crashes, shootings and the like... you probably will not care for this movie.  Z for Zachariah, a movie that caused me to think and say, "what?"

Oh yes I do!  My consciousness (God within) is all there is.  One power, my Father/God, is it.  Not my will, his will be done.  For when I do things and think in terms of my will it doesn't work out as I desire.  Oh my, oh my, most of us have things so twisted and messed up in our heads.  This great little book has made it abundantly clear, finally, for me.  Thank you Neville, you are the greatest!!

The Original Fit is cut to fit the body.  My son has a 28 inch waist.  I bought the 30 inch waist size and the pants were too snug for him.  I returned (thanks Amazon for free returns) and bought him the 32 inch waist.  Normally I buy him the loose fit Dickies.  I didn't know the style made such a difference but live and learn.

I've had my Thule 13" case for over two years and people are always asking where did I get it.  I stumbled onto this bag in 2011 on the Apple website during the holidays for $20 off.  Everything I use fits into this bag with my MacBook Pro 13".  The shoulder strap cushion is awesome.  No pressure on my shoulder at all.  Have never had a problem with my zipper, it moves smoothly around the bag to open and close.
For shame, for shame!  This item should be removed from Amazon website as it is a fraud!  All the previous one star negative reviews are absolutely correct!  Shame, shame, shame.... shame on you!

I love, love these headphones.  I also own the red color.  I just wrote a review for the red one's so forgive if I don't go into great detail here.  I don't think anyone can go wrong with these headphones and for the price they are a steal coupled with excellent quality.

I purchased three packs of these 4 pairs of socks for myself and my two adult son's.  They are thick and warm.  The hold up nicely.  I have not experienced any of the problems some people have stated.  I was them in hot water with regular white clothes load and I do not use chlorine bleach (ever).  I either dry them on low for a short period of time or I lay them on the radiators in my home.

I recommend that people do not dry these socks on medium or worse hot temperature.  If you do that enough times they will definitely shrink and/or thin out.

users.query: A detective and a seemingly emotionless killer. but only if logical outcome. Prepare to be surprised at the twists.

cands.text: good woman detective fighting the usual male bias with strenght and courage. Interesting case with not too obvious clues.  i like her/  Will get the next one shortly

Serial killer after prostitutes but the writing is neither colorful nor intriguing. The midwife/detective may be interesting but the writer doesn't show us her personality well. The Police chief is painted as bumbling but without character painting a good picture so we understand his point of view.  Stopped reading after a few chapters as it became boring.

the writing is OK but not exceptional. the story is easy to follow and best, perhaps, for lovers of traditional murder mysteries noir. Our protagonist is suspected but his good friend has done some suspect things so we don't know who is the killer yet. i'm only 1/4 in and will continue reading. Some interesting twists already.

the mystery is there, but bizarre; and the coroner has insights which you will find interesting.  It isn't a noir mystery but rather straightforward police procedural with some twists of the 80 year old mind tempered with experience. good character development and plenty of action.  The writing is quite nice too. controlled and spare.

good procedural mystery with the decent sheriff trying to solve the murder of his former girlfriend and her husband. The pompous mayor and by-the-book ambitious detective brought in over his head because of the personal connection are, as usual, merely in the way. You'll like the large dog which befriends the sheriff. A good read and good first effort for this new writer. Look forward to the next.

careful plotting
every twist adds to the almost unbelievable denouement and you won't guess the end but the clues are there
not a thriller nor a thinking mans mystery. just a plodder

A fine beginning to a wonderful series of mysteries.. Two bodies without apparent connections but suspicious people hover around the periphery of Inspector Sejers case until he finds the connection.  And his patient curiosity will find all the answers. There is a bit of going back in time to examine the early life of the victims but the writing is so rewarding and kept me involved.  This is the 4th of Fossums' books I've read and it's nice to find the first (of the Sejer series) is no disappointment.  HIghly recommended of the Scandinavian genre. It may keep you up late...

Fascinating murder mystery with colorful period details and flavor of political clergy relationships so essential to the orderly world of knights, serfs, church, and family. I can't help empathize with Owen and his slowly dawning detection skills. Well written and absorbing

Fascinating murder mystery with colorful period details and flavor of political clergy relationships so essential to the orderly world of knights, serfs, church, and family. I can't help empathize with Owen and his slowly dawning detection skills. Well written and absorbing
the events and characters are captivating. The mystery is solved slowly and logically and you can be almost as astute as Sherlock. Worth reading although all this authors' books are marvelous.
This lady knows how to construct a mystery and feed you the clues slowly so you are completely wrapped in the atmosphere. Danger is real and your heart will pump.

several parallel points of view eventually merge into blood, torture, a maze, young boy detectives over their heads. Far too many difficulties and paths in a deadly physical maze. Design and Construction would have been beyond even a professional builder without a genius architect. The villain is neither. He is a sadist.

This is the fifth of the series I have read and it doesn't disappoint.  The girl is found, dead with an apple in her hand and a serpent nearby. A scene from the Garden of
Eden gown awry. Every twist and turn points to a different killer but the end is always a bit of a surprise. Not at all easy to figure out.  Especially in a day with little communication but letters and speech.  Our hero's Ralph and Gervase are interestingly of diverse talents. Enjoy the glimpse into a medieval world

Well written and intriguing. I received a free copy for review but am happy to report this is a murder mystery with plenty of clues and a boatload of characters/suspects.  The Mayor is that one dimensional character from Jaws more concerned with the image of the town than a possible messy murder.
Sheriff is nice guy who loves to solve puzzles and his sidekick is a big shaggy dog. I enjoyed reading this well-written mystery and hope for more puzzles from the author in future.  . This writer is in a class with some of the better mystery writers, with the ability to paint pictures of the scenes and moods of weather as well as people.  Highly enjoyable.

Police procedural in a time before police. Our hero is a down on his heels nobleman brought low by plague and war. You will like him. As a 13th Century assistant coroner in England, he  has no way to communicate except by foot slogging door to door, asking questions. Slowly and painfully (the weather isn't good, the clothes leave much to be desired)small facts are collected. The villains are not always who you suspect.
good writing and the tale wthin the tale is fascinating. a double murder inside and outside the main story

Engaging plot but the characters don't feel comfortable on the page. Not quite a smooth read when the "hero" seems out of touch with the crime novel. I am sure it's meant to be humorus and almost succeeds but tries too hard. Can't recommend it.
unexpected plot involving a baby fortuitously escaping a murderer intent on killing the whole family. Toddling to a nearby cemetery, he is "adopted" but the ghosts of the departed.
Interesting and impressive beginning to a series. I like the policeman falling for the upper class spinster and the reverse as well
the 5 yr old couldn't figure out how to make it flip. It lacks instructions.  the 8 yr old got it immediately. It is unsteerable so he found it a bit boring. adults got bored within 1 minute
back wheels will not contunue, must be given a push. interesting action but gears appear not perfectly synced. Have  used other itwems by this manufacturere wit success

Suspend your disbelief and enjoy a journey into another realm of time or space...
Mr Brown will bring you home, smiling.
good device but my printer (Canon) does not want to recognize the switch every time

users.query: Pretty and nice once assembled. Assembly is a frustrating experience to get everything to fit together in a state of limbo before the surrounding Pieces can be screwed together and the trellis stabilized.  My first one has been in use for three years supporting a pine tree that lacks its own support strength and continues to be pretty and useful.

cands.text: Once assembled its decent but you need to be an engineer to put it together.  The feet are hard to push on and  I recommend a lubricant like a small bit of soap.  One screw stripped out of the wood and I needed to do some bending of metal parts to get it finally together.

Nice once assembled but assembly is a nightmare.  For example the wheels do not fit into the base without careful hammering.  The arms assembly requires a lot of tightening and untightening to get the screws to fit into the respective holes..  Once inserted the seat pole does not seem to want to come out.  After 18 months the pneumatics failed and the chair won't stay up
Hard to control in tight spaces but fun and impressive otherwise.  Took a bright 9 year old grandchild about 2 hrs to begin to get the hang of it.

Impressive.  The first snow was just one inch, light half on top, solid on bottom and the solid kept jamming the blower, but i was able to unjam by lifting the unit with the handle and letting it fall gently.  Then came the first real snow of 4-5 in of heavy wet snow.  The Snow Joe was amazing in clearing it and throwing the snow 6-8 feet.  Did not run out of charge.  Did not jam seriously.  Even cleared the sidewalk that had been walked on.  Then we had the Big blizzard of 2015.  This machine is not designed to deal with 20+ inches of snow. It could do it slowly and with more than one battery, needing more than one pass to deal,with so much depth.  For this snow though we hire a guy with the big gas blowers.  But I Still love this machine for the littler tasks and clean up after a few more inches come down after the big machine has finished.  Then the Feb. 2 storm dropped 12+ inches and the little devil cleared paths around the yard.  First pass is a bit slow then it's pretty easy to clear after that with passes that carve off about 6-8in and you don't have to stop much to back and go as you do with the first pass. And now let's get technical. So this snowblower has a front scoop area of 18" x 8" or 124 in..  By comparison a large gasoline powered snowblower could typically have front scoop dimensions of 30" x 21" or 630 in., roughly 5 times the area for scooping snow.  That sounds impressive but the snow scooped still has to fit through a small area of the exit shoot and on the large gas engine it is nowhere near five times the diameter found on this battery powered unit.  Even with the two-stage design of the gas unit all that extra snow still has to fit through a relatively small exit shoot.  What I'm saying is that small in terms of the scoop size on the battery unit is a significant advantage in efficiently removing snow.  Then let's compare the amount of snow removed by different units. A 120 V electric snowblower typically with 18 x 12" scoop dimensions is rated at, in one case, 700 pounds per minute of snow blown.  This unit is rated at nearly 500 pounds per minute.  The  120 V unit is rated at 15 Amps which means approximately 2.4 hp. Given the relative removal rate that would give this unit a rating of 1.7 hp.  I'm not sure that's accurate given that that would imply 32 A of maximum current out of the battery, but it makes this unit even more impressive in it's performance.
The connection between the base and the support shaft is poorly designed and allows the top to wobble.  Very insecure.

Great for plants or small speakers in a studio out of the way of traffic, not stage or studio speakers generally.  They are solid and well built but I need more security in a speaker stand like the ones that have means to secure a speaker, not just a platform where tripping over the cables is a way to pull the speaker off or just bumping the stand can send the speaker tumbling.  Even in studios there is traffic that can force the speakers off unless in a corner.  I use on stage stands of the more secure design for sound stages I have set up for folk musicians before.  Up to three stages at a time.  This would be great for the Bose Bluetooth speaker or the like with no cables.

I have felled 4-5 in hard wood trees with fair ease.  Avoid cuts where the saw will jam.  Batteries can be an issue.  Some can be defective.  Always have 2 - I have 4 just for safety.  And a backup big saw is useful too.  18 in electrics are great if like me you hate the mess and carburetor issues of gas saw engines.  And keep a pan under it when stored for the oil leaks, but you do that with any chain saw.
Got this to haul stuff around the outside/inside - e.g. snow melt bags, firewood, etc.  Its great.
Great in the snow to avoid slipping particularly if you have balance issues.  They are a bit tight and as provided seem to fit OK, but will not accommodate my inserts for arch support.

The latch on the four boxes I got are fairly sharp and so hard to open particularly on two of them that they could cut your fingers.  Children could never open some of them.  I had to break one box to get back into it.  Very poor quality.  Back they go, too expensive to just throw away.
Having spent a youth in the maritime arts, I look for reliable shackle screws that won't easily back out and these seem to meet that goal.  Otherwise a nice solid shackle.
Good for plants, not speakers securely with cords to trip on etc.  I have had these for years. when it comes to setting up a sound stage I Use the kind that fit or screw into a bottom hole.

I agree with all the good comments in the other reviews and in the introductory comments of the book itself.  One sense one gets from seeing or indeed visiting such ruins is a sense that for at least a brief moment the place is all yours.  There are no residents to disturb or to be shooing you away.  In many cases, though, of such places I know of, the owners may have abandoned the property only to build a new place a few hundred yards away.  The old place could not be brought up to modern standards and amenities at any reasonable cost.
One place to look for abandoned homes is in National Parks where in the park formation residents were forced off their land.  One such area I am familiar with is Shenandoah National Park.  The local communities nearby still have descendents of those owners exhibiting a bit of hostility to what happened.  In the author's state of residence,Maine, the National Park there, Acadia, on Mt Desert Island, was created instead by gifts from generous owners, the Rockefellers being one.
Another great book in the same genre just published by the University of Virginia is:
Lost Communities of Virginia
Also from Amazon
This continues the fine Bluegrass music tradition of the Rangers.  A lovely listenable experience.
Scary cute but it breaks easily.  Seems made of something like a brittle ceramic, not a resin ?
This is definitely bluegrass.  All the instruments you'd expect are there and share taking center stage.  It's got a fine warmth.
After years of use of standing outdoor lights that got progressively rusty and were hard to change bulbs we got these and could not be happier.

Comfortable and neat looking.  Best with bullets pointing in. I keep looking at it to see the time, a habit from decades of wearing a watch pre iPhone.  Ha Ha,  not a problem, in fact nice to keep seeing it that way.

I love this camera and with AA batteries there are always replacements close at hand, well usually.  The SD card is in the same compartment as the batteries and that compartment cover is a bit awkward to open and close so use the USB cabe to down load.  Focus at extreme telephoto can be an issue but try landscape setting in the menu for distant images or portrait if closer, eg ten feet.  Also to be kept in mind is that the zoom function zooms 30X of lens function then another 4X of image area, and resolution, reduction.  Auto Focus in the latter can be less effective.

If you have an iPad there are free download apps that can provide a more solid keystroke effect.
Not as many keys as this but the effect seems better if you are composing or just learning a tune.
This will not hold a Nikon D40x with a small 18-55mm zoom.  That is just to small to be useful.

The pictures are fantastic and the recipes are more than scrumptious.  Once you get the Betty Crocker basics there is no room for any other cookbook than this.  The recipes have a lot of ingredients but it is easy to make substitutions to suit individual tastes.  I just LOVE it.  I took it into the office to show my paralegals.
