Learn to play at this level (another whole, but do-able story) and you will entertain yourself and others with a lifetime of pleasure.

users.query:
I'm torn on this one honestly. I wanted to love it. I read Beautifully Damaged the Indie version months ago and fell in love with it. So when I found out that Lucien's story was coming out I was beyond excited because I really liked his character. Although, I do love Lucien now that I got to read his full story it's the delivery of the book I was a little disappointed with.

I know every author has their way of writing a book and in no way am I telling anyone how they should write but I am entitled to my opinion. For me, this book had too much going on. I mean Trace and Ember had their story told in Beautifully Damaged so I think this book should of just focused on Lucien and Darcy. The multiple POV's which were not in first person is a little hiccup for me. I'm not a fan of third person reads especially if there is going to more than one character to follow.

It's all connected, I know, it's what connects the characters and brings the story to life but it was a little much for me. I liked the book, yes, a lot (I know that probably doesn't make sense but I really did). After getting over my little pet peeves and quirks I loved Lucien and Darcy's journey. It was emotional, heartbreaking and the passion and chemistry between them was beautiful. It was such an emotional rollercoaster.

This book is filled with love, suspense, heartache, twists and turns you will not be expecting. What I really do love about this book is that L.A. Fiore was able to draw me in emotionally and that's a biggie for me when reading. I want to feel the emotions the characters are experiencing. When they are hurting, I want to feel their pain. When they are sad and heartbroken, I want to cry along with them. When they are happy and content, I want to be smiling too. And she totally did that. That's what got me, that pull you feel when reading is what made me look past the little stuff and really love this book.

Do I recommend reading this book? Yes, absolutely. It truly is a great read of raw emotion, heartache and second chances. I'm just a little picky especially considering the first book in the serious was absolutely amazing but this one was just written differently. However, I did enjoy the story line and fell more in love with Lucien. So yes, if you haven't read it add it to the list.

cands.text:
Again, I have mixed feelings for this book. The Epilogue from book one is not consistent with this book, so I was left somewhat confused. This book did grab my attention more than the first however I still struggled to get through it. The editing issues sooo bug me, so unfortunately that cant be overlooked and it does play a part in my rating.

Lizzie is still immature and insecure but yet she supposedly has grown. I didn't see it. She just seemed too needy and indecisive and shes still hung up on Teagan who royally screwed her over a year ago.

Were introduced to a new character, Nick. He is an absolute sweetheart and sexy. He becomes a good friend to Lizzie and loves her kid. Of course he wants more but shes still nurturing her broken heart over her baby daddy.

Im giving this book 4 Stars because there were some emotional moments and for that moment in the story I was able to have an emotional connection with Lizzie. However, the events that took place took me by total surprise and had me thinking Why? I mean what was the purpose of that happening. But nonetheless, it was a very emotional moment in the story.

I loved the friendship that Lizzie and Nick had. They seemed to be having fun while harboring feelings for each other until Lizzie was able to get her head out of her ass.

3.5 Stars

I have mixed feelings about this book. It was a good read but didn't quite grasp my attention throughout. There were also some editing issues and that is a big pet peeve of mine when reading. As much as I would like to, I just cant overlook it. It messes with the flow of reading.

I did like the story line and the drama flair that was brought into it. But there were instances where I was just like Really?! and wanting to slap Lizzie for being so damn dramatic or insanely stupid. And then wanting to beat the crap out of Teagan.

There were some funny parts to it that had me laughing. I mean who wouldnt laugh at a bunch of drunken idiots. I really wanted to love this story. There were some mixed reviews and so I was hoping for a five star read, however, it just didn't quite do it for me. There was just no emotion and I was so detached to the characters that I was like meh, get over it.

If you like sexy Irish men and summer flings then give it a try. Everyones opinion is different.

I started off with mixed feelings on this book. The beginning seemed to drag on just a smidge for me. I kept waiting for that 'Oh sh*t' moment. It took a while to get there but once it did, I was sitting on the edge of my seat anticipating the turn of each page.

Yes, this is a dark read. Yes, there are some scenes that are not for everyone. Yes, there is a cliffhanger. So now we have that out of the way. For an author's first book, this was pretty good. I love that this was told in dual POV. I always like to know both sides of the story and what both characters are feeling. So that was a huge plus for me.

I really liked Laila and Aiden's characters. Laila isn't the usual weak and needy heroine. She is fiesty, mouthy and damn determined to not let her spirits break at the situations she finds herself in.

Aiden is dominate, yet caring and gentle. A man on a mission and will not be deterred from his plans. Whether you alter them or not, he moves forward. He's also very sexy and the pull between him and Laila is captivating.

Another thing that I really enjoyed about Melissa's writing style is that she uses such great detail in telling the story. And she turned it down a notch at just the right moments. I enjoyed reading this, I recommend reading it and I can't wait to get my hands on book two and find out what unfolds next.

The beginning of the book was a little drawn out but once it got into the story line it held my attention the rest of the way. It really is a great story. These are issues that people face on a daily basis. Such a strong message that I hope people will actually take away from reading this story because bullying is NEVER okay. In this story not only will we follow the journey of love but also shows you how the effects of bullying can have on a person and those who love them.

Nathaniel Nate Morgan is very protective of his brother, Nicky. He has always been that way since they were just kids. He was always getting into fights and defending his brother at every turn.

"I got used to getting in fights protecting my brother and as the bullies got worse, the fights got worse too."

Nate spent his whole life trying to protect his brother from the daily bullying and harassing. He was always too busy with his brother for relationships, even choosing to attend college near home.

"Looking back, I think I didn't get too serious with a girl because I thought it would maybe confuse Nick or make him sad that he didn't have that."

Elizabeth Decker had a perfectly normal life until her mother passed away when she was only 11 yrs old. After the death of her mother life took a turn for the worse. Growing up in a military home where her father turned to alcohol and a very mean sister, left Elizabeth a loner. She turned to her books and studies because she was always made to feel that she was a freak. Elizabeth's sister, Audrey, has not made it very easy for her to have any type of a real relationship or wanting to for that matter.

"Books could take me to other worlds. Books allowed me to become someone else instead of Audrey's plain, quiet, older sister. Books allowed me to escape the pain of having a sister who hated me and treated me terribly."

When Nate and Elizabeth meet there is an instant attraction but they both try to deny what they are feeling. Once they give in and take a chance they are put through some tough situations at the hands of a loved one. The things these two go through are unspeakable. I was so pissed off reading the things that they had to endure because of anger, low self-esteem, and bullying. They both needed to face their own issues in order to see if it is possible for them to have any kind of future together. I loved Nate and Elizabeth. They are so genuine and deeply care for those that matter to them.
They had such sweet moments together.

"Nate, baby, you have wrecked me. I had accepted my life as the freaky sister who never finds love and lives in her sister's shadow with seven cats. But you came along and rescued me, stood up for me, helped me to see that I didn't have to stay in Audrey's shadow. You're teaching me that I'm beautiful and worth someone's love."

This story will definitely take you on an emotional rollercoaster. It's a sexy love story that deals with learning how to trust, second chances, dealing with emotional scars and overcoming some unexpected twist and turns.

"I'm yours, Libby. Lost in you. Ruined for anyone else. You are IT for me Libby-girl. I've never, in my whole life, felt even close to what I feel with you. At the risk of moving too quickly, I love you, Elizabeth Decker. I'm in love with you. I. Am. Yours."

This is the first book I'm reading from this author and I'm already itching to get my hands on another one. What a great introduction to a new author. M. Never did a great job with the delivery and flow of the story. I was sucked in from the very beginning.

That beginning was.... I have no words. A gut wrenching opener that's for sure. But it kept me wanting more. I needed to see this play out. And what a thrilling, suspenseful and exciting journey this was.

I loved that the female MC was a f****** badass but also had her soft side. Stevie and Baz were sizzling hot together. Ah! And Baz!!! Gah, I loved Baz!

This was a great read that had me sitting on the edge of my seat. Definitely a must read and I'll definitely be one clicking more from this author.

Wow!! This one was so much more emotional.

Charli and Adam are hopelessly in love but sometimes things don't always go as planned. Decisions need to be made and no matter what hearts are going to be broken.

I loved this book. The story line just keeps getting better and better. It totally consumes you. This is so beautifully written. It's full of laughs, cries, sadness, heartbreak, betrayal, love and magic.

It's nice to see how well the characters develop and grow from one book to the next. Some take more time than others but G.J. Walker-Smith conveys those growth and emotions from page to page so effortlessly. I felt the emotions Adam and Charli were going through.

We also get to see another side of some other characters, such as Nicole and more of Ryan. I absolutely could not believe what a horrible friend Nicole turned out to be. That was so unexpected. And Ryan.... wow! I liked him from when he first came into the picture but he keeps slipping his way into my heart. I love that although Charli and Ryan are always teasing and stirring each other up they have such a special bond. And Ryan is a really great support for her. He doesn't sugarcoat anything and that's exactly what Charli needs sometimes.

As I got closer and closer to the end, I knew that this book would definitely stay with me for a while and this series will be one of those MUST re-reads. I laughed, I cried and I fell more and more in love with Charli and Adam.

So let me start off by saying that I am not a fan of third person POVs. But Holy hell, this book was so good. It had just the perfect amount of drama, heartache and sexiness with two strong dominant men and a sassy submissive. Even in third person this book held my attention from start to finish. I was glued to this book and could not put it down until the very last page.

I love Shayla Black. Ive read her books before so I knew going in that I was in for a good time. Add two additional authors that I haven't read from yet and WOW! The way this book was written, the flow of the story and the characters were just fantastic. Shayla Black, Jenna Jacobs and Isabella LaPearl did an amazing job bringing this story to life and capturing these characters journey with such raw passion. The characters will lure you in and have you emotionally invested throughout. The sex scenes are extremely hot and oh so steamy. I absolutely loved it and cant wait to read the next book.

3.5 Stars! I thought this was a cute read. This is my first time reading from this author so I didn't know what to expect going in. The blurb certainly caught my attention so I dove in.

This was a good story line. Great set of characters. It just didn't touch me emotionally. I didn't get that all consuming love feels I was hoping to get from this second chance romance. Overall, I enjoyed Charlotte and Troy's journey.

I'm so glad I continued to read this. I enjoyed this book more than the first one. This book was definitely more emotional. There was better character development and I loved that we got some of Kieran's POV.

The angst and emotion in this story felt more real. As we get more background on Jared and Kieran in this book, it made me feel more of a connection to them. Their pasts certainly aren't all hearts and rainbows and I felt the tugging at my heart.

I did love all the information into the BDSM Dom/Sub/Daddy/Boy relationship in the book. It gives you more insight and helps differentiate the whole Daddy/Boy v. Dom/Sub. Even though there were times where it just all felt the same to me but at any rate it was well written. Still not as kinky for me and although this was more on the emotional side, it was still.....sweet. The sex scenes yet again were hot as hell. Not my favorite from this author but she still did a good job on delivering Jared and Kieran's conclusion.

Im not a big fan of third person so its really hard for me to really invest myself in the story whole heartedly. I also felt like I was missing something from the characters. I didn't really get that sense where I felt connected to them.

I do love a strong and independent lead female character, so I instantly liked Cali. As for Owen, I love a guy who is confident and protective. And yes, Owen was exactly that. Of course with almost every male character, they have their moments where they grate on your last nerves but then have you swooning the next. He definitely had a sweet side and I loved how he cared for Cali.

With that being said, overall this was a good read for a debut novel. Michelle Dare really put a lot of emotion into the story.  Cali and Owen definitely didn't have an easy journey. This story is filled with enough drama, suspense, angst and some HOTT scenes that will keep you entertained throughout.

OMG! This was seriously such a great read. I was so hooked from the very beginning. I was so looking forward to reading this book. The moment I started I was drawn in and could not put it down. I read this in one sitting. These characters have wicked chemistry and I couldn't get enough.

Helena Hunting did such a fantastic job mixing in the humor, sexy and the drama. This was just a perfect blend and I was so ecstatic reading it. The MCs were absolutely PERFECT!! And OMG I swooned so HARD for the hero in this story!!! He was just panty f***ing melting and absolutely perfect!!! I swear my heart just about melted for this damn man. He was EVERYTHING and I wanted to wave my magic wand and bring him to real life!!!! The perfect book boyfriend for realz!!! And I so adored Amalie. She had me laughing and crying for her.

GAH! Helena Hunting delivered an outstanding read that had me so captivated, swooning, laughing and smiling so damn hard. I loved EVERYTHING about this book. The perfect story line, pace and characters. My only complaint would be that it had to end. I wanted so much more. This is a definite MUST READ!!!

I read this author's collab work and fell in love with those books so I knew that I had to check out her individual work as well.  I can't tell you how much I loved this story and these characters. Just from the prologue I knew I was in for an amazing journey. I was sucked in from that very first page and devoured this book in one sitting. I just could not put it down.

I loved Jackson and Lucas. The chemistry between these two was undeniable. They were insanely hot together and this author does an amazing job delivering the emotion throughout the entirety of the story. These guys had me all up in my feels. There was not a moment throughout this story where I wasn't in my feelings. I felt their pain. Their heartbreak. Their inner turmoil. Their strength and determination.

My heart was full after reading this. This author managed to convey every emotion and bring this phenomenal story to life. This was beautifully written and had great character development. Brooke Blaine delivers such an amazing, sexy and heart warming story that had me so completely consumed. I didn't want it to end! Brooke will have you transfixed with the emotions, passion and chemistry dripping from page to page. This is a definite must read and I already can't wait for the next book.

I'm not sure how I feel about this book actually. I have mixed emotions about it. On one hand, I really enjoyed the whole sexual aspect of it because let's just face it this book was HOTT AS HELL! On the other hand, I was just really confused as to what I was actually reading. This is my first time reading from this author so I didn't know what to expect. This story is definitely intense and left my mind in a jumble of f***ed up chaos. However, it was a f***ed up chaos I enjoyed! LOL.

The author really does an amazing job keeping you mesmerized and glued to the pages. These characters and the delivery of the story had me so intrigued I couldn't get enough. I felt dirty and depraved for liking some of this sh*t and getting a little hot and bothered. But HOLY HOT DA*N Isabella Sterling!

Miles and Bebe are not your typical romance characters and I absolutely loved that. This book was so different, so unique and so utterly raunchy you'll be needing a cold shower afterwards.

There were some parts where I felt could have gone a little deeper and maybe give us some more in depth as far as dealing with getting over some of the fears and the issues Miles had to overcome. He certainly deals with some f***ed up issues and although I am no expert in the mental health field but I would assume it takes more than a pretty p**sy to throw caution to the wind and be miraculously cured in such a short time frame. I would've liked to get into his head and see him deal with his struggles in a bit more detail.

Overall, this was a good read. Definitely sexy, intense, dirty and raw. Isabella Starling delivers one panty dropping story that will have you sitting on the edge of your seat.

Whoa! This book was emotional and sexy and will definitely have you sitting at the edge of your seat. I read this in one sitting and it had my full attention. My eyes were glued to each page devouring every word.

The chemistry between Olivia and Liam was seriously scorching. Liam is all alpha but does have a soft side to him. There were moments where I wanted to junk punch him because he acted like a complete douche at times. Olivia is still dealing with the loss of her husband and the emotions just rolled right off the pages when she was hurting.

I laughed and cried and totally swooned. I also had the occasional *gasp* and Oh hell no and WTF moments that had me gripping my ipad with anticipation waiting to find out how it all ends. Hilary Storm delivered an amazing story and set of characters that definitely left me wanting more. The Bryant family is seriously bada*s and I cant wait to meet the other brothers.

I feel like its pretty much a guarantee that Im going to like whatever this author writes. Ive read every book to date and each book gets better and better. Each book gets funnier and funnier. Each book makes me smile more. This book had me grinning so hard my cheeks hurt.

This story is just so engaging. From the very beginning I didn't want to put it down. There was a lot of laughing out loud moments, and shaking my head and some serious cheesy grinning going on. This girl. Gosh, this girl. Jana Aston sure knows how to write some memorable characters thats for sure. Violet was just so awkwardly  perfect! And Jennings, dear lawdy, that man!!! Mmmmmmmmmmmmm! That man is definitely sexy and swoon worthy.

This story was absolutely hilarious, sexy and romantic all wrapped in one. I love Jana Astons writing style. Her stories are always unique and all consuming. Her heroines are always quirky and outlandish and the men are always ones you wish you could find for yourself. I adored this story. Absolutely loved it and a definite must read!

I was definitely intrigued by the story and I've been following this series so it was a must read for me. I've never read anything from this author before so I didn't know what to expect. This book didn't exactly follow the other stories in the series. It took me a while to get into it. I just couldn't figure out exactly what it was that I was reading. At first it felt like a jumble of thoughts thrown in with hot sex but as I got more into the story then it became a little more interesting.

This was a quick interesting read with scorching sex. And of course Reece Richards! I mean the man is just all sorts of yummy. The author did a good job showcasing the relationship between Emma and Reece. I think that the whole super hero could've played more of a role into the story and maybe some more background info. So although, I don't think this read really suited me it may be a great read for other readers.

Received an ARC and read in a day. The book itself is short and will definitely leave you wanting more. I love how this was written as only Grim's POV. He is the bad boy, tough, tattooed biker that has a heart and isn't afraid to share his feelings. When he meets Red it's an instant connection and the sex is HOTT! No doubt about that. I would've liked to give 5 stars however, there were some edit issues (I wish things like this didn't bother me but they do :{ ) and there were also timeline gaps that confused me a little. But other than that it was a great story with love and lost, joy and heartache and I can't wait to read the rest of Grim's story.

Ysa and Sebastians story continues and I still have mixed feelings. However, I will say that even though there were certain aspects of the story that had me rolling my eyes quite a bit and annoyed me; this story was filled with so much more emotion than the first book. And I love a book that makes you feel what the characters are going through and M. Robinson definitely did that in this book.

There was so much going on in this story that it kept my eyes glued to the pages and my a*s firmly planted on my couch until the very end. My heart was racing and at times my blood was boiling and my iPad made it through without any scratches, dents or shattered pieces.

A great read that had me consumed from beginning to end and will definitely have you sitting on the edge of your seat. Ill be looking forward to reading more from M. Robinson.

This gets better and better which each book!! And I fall harder and harder for Vaughn f*****g Asher <3

Wow! I don't even know how to express how much I loved this book. I was sitting at the edge of my seat throughout. My emotions were all over the place. My heart was pounding. My stomach was in knots. My head was spinning.

I was truly stunned. I was so caught off guard. My heart went out to Vaughn. You can sense the desperation from him.

Grace is absolutely insane and I just kept screaming in my head No. No. No. or What the f**k are you doing? and What is wrong with you?

And then..

What. The. F**k. Just. Happened.!!!!

What a f*****g cliffhanger!!

I want to hate cliffhangers but I love cliffhangers. I hate that I love cliffhangers. I hate that JA Huss left us with this cliffhanger. But I love JA Huss for leaving us this cliffhanger!!! UGH!! Job well done, Ms. Huss, you have successfully left me aching, craving and desperate for more!

This was such a great read. Sad and heart breaking at times but mostly I found it super sweet and funny. This was very well written; the story flowed perfectly and was very easy to follow. Vi Keeland and Dylan Cross did an amazing job capturing the emotions and pulling you in from the very beginning. I love reading dual POVs. It gives you insight on the emotions from both sides.

Zack and Nikki will have you crying, laughing and touching your heart. Zack is the sweetest guy and I'm so glad that he wasn't the usual player in most stories these days. He was the good guy. The guy who has a huge heart. The guy who makes the perfect boyfriend. And Nikki, who has been through so much but carries herself so well. So brave.

I also like that the secondary characters play a huge role in the story. They're a great support system for Zack and Nikki. Zack had Kellar, who is absolutely hysterical. He will make you laugh every time. And Nikki had Ashley, who says the funniest things that will have you laughing out loud.

A wonderful story about loss, love and fate.

3.5 Stars

I knew going in that this was NOT a romance and I was totally okay with that. I love a good suspense story and the blurb totally had me intrigued. The story started off fine and somewhere along I just kept struggling to stay focused on the story. It was slow paced obviously telling her story will take you down the path that is her life. It wasn't until more towards the ending where it started to pick up and I found myself more engaged in Helena Ross.

Ive read books by this author before that blew me away. Her writing is always unique as well as her characters. Helena Ross was not an easy character to connect with and/or even like with the way she treated people which is understandable, considering what she went through. The secondary characters were enjoyable and likeable from the start. The unwavering support from two people who Helena has not been so kind to was touching.

It was a well written book and very unique however, this one just didn't do it for me. I mean the ending just about did me in. Thats where all the emotion was and I was in tears. It was absolutely heartbreaking. I just wanted to be consumed and engaged throughout the story and not just half of it. Though this may not have been a wow read for me it may affect and take to other readers differently. Its definitely different and if you don't take a chance on it youll never know if its your cup of tea or not.

This author blew me away in book one and she completely took my breath away in Heal Me!! A truly touching emotional love story. Alexandra Page delivers a phenomenal conclusion to Ellie and Niks journey. This was EVERYTHING!! I was instantly captivated from the very beginning and I couldn't get enough of these two.

This author does such a great job conveying the emotions. This book definitely had my emotions all over the place. I was laughing, swooning, crying, oohing and awwing, I LOVED the raw, heartwrenching emotions this author was able to pull from me. Her ability to describe and make you feel the grief, depression, anxiety and turmoil these characters were going through is just pure talent. I was so mesmerized by these characters and this story.

Ellie and Nik were the perfect couple. This book picks up right where book one left off and they have so much to work out. They go through so many ups and downs but their love and devotion to each other get stronger and stronger. GAHHHHHHH!!!! I love everything about this story. Nik is just the absolute BEST!!!!

This is was just an epic conclusion to an emotional, steamy, sweet, romantic, and an overall pure delightful read that I highly recommend.

Oh my! What a total surprise! This book was nothing how I thought it would be. Ryan was so pleasantly unexpected and I fell in love with him even more. Ryan and Bente's journey was absolutely a pure and beautiful love story.

Bente and Ryan happen to stumble upon each other after five years and the chemistry and feelings that they used to feel are still there. Ryan is absolutely remarkable and has done some growing up and is ready to make a commitment. Although Bente still has her doubts because Ryan hurt her all those years ago, she just can't turn away.

But Ryan is ready and he knows without a doubt that he wants that with Bente. Despite claiming to be clueless on how to be a boyfriend and have a relationship, Ryan is exceptionally attentive and the way he loves Bente is effortless. These two were made for each other. Theyre both witty, hard workers and dedicated to making their relationship work.

An absolutely brilliant, funny, and remarkably endearing story line. The more you read, the more you want. G.J. Walker-Smith does an amazing job with these characters. Ryan's niece, Bridget, is a huge part of this story and because of her we get to see a whole different side of Ryan that will absolutely capture your heart. Bridget is so adorable and Ryan is so good with her.

Once again G.J. Walker-Smith brings another addition to this series that without a doubt mesmerizes and consumes you. Another beautiful story with the added touch of occasional family drama, love, and magic that make it all the more a spectacular read.

I absolutely LOVE this story!! Ive probably read it a thousand times and can re-tell the story word for word. Well, maybe not word for word but close enough. Kirsty Moseley made me an instant fan when I read this book. I loved everything about it.

The characters I absolutely adore! Riley and Clay are best friends and they know each other so well. Or so they thought

Clay has been harbouring his feeling for Riley for a long time. It took Riley a month long vacation away from her best friend to realize that she just might like him as more than a friend.

Blake comes in the picture and hes looking for revenge on Clay and sets his eyes on Riley. Thing starts to get a little crazy and Blake just won't stay away from her. Its a crazy obsession that goes terribly wrong.

I love love love this story! I love that Clays nickname for Riley is Riley Bear. Its super cute and he is super sweet. Riley is a tough nut and won't let anything come between her and Clay.

A great read with some unexpected turns of events. I highly recommend it. I loved it. This is my go-to re-read book. My top favourite book EVER!!! I just instantly fell in love with this book and these characters. I think Kirsty Moseley did an amazing job writing this story and drawing out the emotions. I laughed. I cried. And I fell in love with Riley and Clay!!!

4.5 Stars!
OMG! I was a lovesick fool from the beginning of this book. Kaylee Ryan delivers an emotional, sweet, sexy and romantic read. I absolutely loved this! These high school sweet hearts made my heart all warm and fuzzy.

From the very beginning, Dylan was the most sweetest and respectful guy towards Avery. He just kept making me love him more and more. His love, devotion and determination for Avery will sweep you off your feet. Kaylee Ryan writes a beautiful story of ones true love. Dylan was just absolutely swoon worthy. He will have your heart fluttering with the depth of his love and the lengths he goes through to prove where his heart has always belonged.

I was totally taken over by Dylan himself as you can see. I loved the story line and the character development. I loved that this author kept this light and refreshing. Its not full of overly drama and angst. Its a truly beautiful story of a second chance at love.

users.query:
Three girls grow up in a small town near the Lebanese border in Israel. We follow their lives just before they are called in to serve in the Israeli army, through a short while after.

The stories of each one jump around and it's like being allowed into a person's mind for snippets of what they go through. We're introduced to a young man who recently served in the army and can't deal with his experiences. He's found dead with a self inflicted gunshot wound to his head. We see friends who are assigned to watch the checkpoints having their throats cut by Arabs. We see a family in the neighborhood where the wife can't deal the constant shelling by the Arabs and leaves her husband one day with their kids. We see how the war affected these women who find it hard to fit into society once their service is over.

Constant fear of something that may happen can be more damaging to a soldier than certainty. It creates an always ready attitude that's hard to shake off once they're no longer serving in the army. The toughness that's believed is part of the Israeli makeup often hides a fragile and damaged soul.

Important to read.

cands.text:
-When I started reading this book I didn't know what to expect. I knew that in general it was the story of two young girls who were twins that went through the holocaust and that the story was told from the point of view of each. But its such a powerful story, even though its fiction, that its difficult to explain how impacting the story is in just a brief summary.
-The beginning of the story, when the two sisters were in Auschwitz, was hard to take. Because they were twins, they were selected by Joseph Mengele to be subjects in his experiments. His sadism and lack of respect for Jewish life were hard to read about, as he subjected so many of his Jewish prisoners to the most cruel of medical experiments. The fact that the stories are told through the experiences of these young girls, who were just entering their teenage years, gave a more subdued and innocent look at his actions, but that made us, as adults, more attuned to the horror behind their thoughts.
-Pearl and Stasha had a doctor as a father. One night, about a year earlier than their removal to Auschwitz, during the time when their family was herded into a ghetto, after curfew, he had to leave the house to attend to a young patient, even though it was risky for him to do so. He never returned and for almost a year, his wife and father in law remained in the house, until they were rounded up by the Nazis and taken to Auschwitz. Once there, the twin girls were among the many children selected by Mengele to perform experiments on. Several Jews had to assist, and their feeble attempts to give some level of comfort to those Jewish subjects is heartbreaking in itself. The girls are ultimately separated, and they are continually subjected to horrors that are difficult to read about. Each thinks the other to be dead.
-The story continues and Auschwitz is liberated, but the war makes survival a trial in itself, as in those last months of battle, both the Nazi forces and local populace who conspired with the Nazis, try to continue the killing of Jews. The attempts at survival by each of the girls, and their resilience is heart lifting, but those who, at one time were forced to assist Mengele but who now do all they can to keep the remaining surviving children from the camp alive, have attacks of their conscience at the deaths they had to watch and all those they couldn't save. And these brave souls who were forced to oversee the atrocities were young themselves, being only in their twenties while in the camps, and yet they carried such a horrible weight over their heads.
-The first part of the book is the most difficult to read, as they are stories of daily horrors that these children faced. One day becomes the next and as the horrors of one day end, the horrors of the next day begin. Its when you see the end of the war coming, that you start to feel hope for these girls and the other young and teen age children they are encamped with. You know that, somehow, because of how closely Pearl and Stasha are bound to each other as twins and even know whats in the others minds, that they will somehow find each other in the end. That keeps you hoping that they will survive, though the scarring that occurred to their psyches, which is more horrifying than the sadistic tortures they underwent to their physical bodies, will affect them forever.
-This is a must read novel, as is a sign of hope for the love that two children have for each other and the feeling that while evil exists in the world, it can never eliminate the resilience of the human spirit to overcome it.

This is a WWII story that strikes at a reader's heart. It focuses on a young girl who is sent to live with foster parents in Germany. The kindness of her foster father wins her over quickly and it is only after the passage of time that she sees her foster mother is his match. It's a story told by a most unusual third person, and is told with a calming type of voice, with the idea that death is just another part of life. You are a witness to the happiness, the sorrows, the fears, and the struggles of the characters in a way that makes you feel that you see through to their souls. You want to get to the end, yet, when you do, you feel you've lost a close friend.

-The Yemenite Jews lived in their land for over a thousand years and, as Jews all over the world, they took on the local customs and traditions of the local people as their own. In Yemen, it was a tradition for both Muslim as well as Jewish women to adorn their bodies with elaborate patterns using henna as a writing material. Women who were masters of the art could be Jews or Muslims and were in demand by females of both religions.
-The Jews of Yemen in the 1920's were living in a time where their former existence was coming to an end, and a new type of life would be thrust upon them. With this in mind, the author follows one such person, Adela Damari, as she grows from a young girl to womanhood, all the while experiencing sorrows brought on by being a Jew in a Muslim dominated country, as well as the sorrows that are common to many people in the world, of not recognizing a true love and then losing it.
-Adela is the youngest child in the family and assists her father who fashions shoes and belts of leather. From the time she is 5 years old we are introduced to the fear of the Jewish community from the Orphan Laws, where, if a Jewish father passed away, his young unmarried children are taken by the state to be converted to Islam and where they may be anything from slaves in a household to an adopted child. Adela's father has a seriously bad cough, and the agent of the government, the Confiscator, frequents the shop of Adela's father, hinting that he would adopt Adela upon her father's death.
-An uncle comes who is escaping another part of the Arab world, and his wife, Aunt Rahel, is a master at applying henna. Rahel's daughter Hani, who is a little older than Adela, takes an immediate interest in Adela and they become fast friends. Through both Hani and Rahel, Adela learns the art of henna and the secrets behind the patterns that are produced.
-Adela becomes promised to another cousin, Asaf, in marriage when she is 9 years old, but her uncle and his son, Asaf, leave on a business trip and seem to have disappeared. Adela is in constant danger because of her father's illness and we watch how the culture allows for marriages between older men and young teenage girls; we see the many marriages that are arranged with no love between the couples; and we see how the Jews of Yemen are in fear of their lives because of pogroms against them by the Arabs and the ploys that Jews undertake to protect their children.
-It's a captivating story that follows the life of Adela through womanhood as she tries to connect with what she believes is her love match, even while fighting against the traditions that are forced on her by community traditions. Her aunt Rahel's marriage is one based on love, and Rahel tries to help Adela find herself in a quiet but devoted way.
-It's a very touching story that is fictional and yet filled with deaths of loved ones through illness, and killings by the Arab populace. The story is mixed with the actual events of the establishment of the State of Israel, and the operation in which the Jews of Yemen were airlifted into Israel to escape the killings in their native country.
-Prior to reading this book, I was in Israel and went to the Israel Museum in Jersalem where one of the exhibits was of the bridal dresses and jewelry worn in different countries by Jews. One of those countries in the display was Yemen, and seeing the clothing and the jewelry so recently, made the descriptions in the book all the more vivid.
-Very touching coming of age and love story that could appeal to all, with the added plus of seeing a culture which has now vanished and which is now, at least, memorialized in the pages of this book.

-Surprisingly good romantic thriller taking place in Egypt in 1941. Though Egypt is a sovereign country, the British are controlling the King. At that time, Jews are not permitted entry in Palestine by the British, as the British can't control the Arab population who reject Jewish immigration.
-Many in the Jewish community in Egypt are doing well financially and have set up various organizations to assist other Jews. One group was trying to assist Jews in moving to Palestine, but the danger became acute and it was forced to disband, but there were still members that operated clandestinely.
-A family of European Jews is hiding out in the home of one of the families of the pro Zionist Jews. There was a young man, Erik Blumenthal, his sister, Maya, and their father. They were hoping to have papers forged, allowing them entry into Palestine.
-A German spy, Kesner, was also in Alexandria, Egypt. Because many Arabs hated the British, it was relatively easy for him to find natives who would assist him in extracting information that would assist the Germans in taking over Egypt and the Suez Canal. He spoke fluent Arabic and was able to easily mix within the population as a Polish officer.
-Kesner is told to look for a young German Jew who has entered Egypt with his sister and father. He is given their pictures and undertakes to locate them, in order to ingratiate himself with the German high command. It was not revealed to him at that time, but the German Jew was a brilliant physicist who wrote a paper on harnessing atomic power to create a bomb. The young man was Erik Blumenthal.
-An American reporter, Mickey Connely, is also in the city. He's looking to break into a story which would help leapfrog his journalism career. He also learns of the Jewish physicist and tries to track him down. He inadvertently meets Maya, and, without knowing who she is, the two of them are attracted to each other, but each can't reveal the full reason of why they're in Egypt. They become enmeshed in the hunt for Erik by both the Americans and the German high command, and are in repeated danger of being killed or tortured by the Germans.
-Very suspenseful and the dialogue is very good. Very surprising that this is a first effort by the writer as it's written extremely well.

-A very touching short novel that could make anyone emotional. Its mostly told in flashbacks by a young girl who is just barely holding on to her life by a thread. It presents these flashbacks in a very unusual way and presents the relationships within what is evidently the very loving family that she came from.
-Last names are ignored here, as their last names could just all be family. Mia is the young girl that is the focus of the story and her father was a former member of a punk band and her mother followed suit. Once Mia was born, her father transformed and went back to school to become a bow tie wearing school teacher. Her mother changed outwardly as well, but inside, they were still the same fun loving and easy going people they always were. Mia had a younger brother, Teddy, born 10 years after her, with whom she had a very close, but occasionally teasing relationship. Mia had a natural musical talent from her father, but rather than go for pop music, she gravitated to classical music and playing a cello.
-In Oregon, where they lived, there was a light amount of snow that had fallen, but that was enough to cause a closure of the schools. The family decides to turn this into a fun outing and they all go for a drive. One moment, Mias thoughts are in mundane issues in her life and the next, all is turmoil. She is standing outside of the car which is now in pieces, after being broadsided by a pickup truck. Her father and mother are both dead and she starts searching for her brother, only to find a body that shouldnt be there. Its hers. Its here that the thoughts of the spirit of Mia takes over as she follows the medics who rush her body for emergency surgery.
-Once there, different parts of her life are recalled, from the boyfriend that appears to be a soulmate, though their relationship has its ups and downs; to her parents, who gave her such love and in their own way were very wise as they guided her through life; to her best friend, Kim, with whom she began their relationship as harsh enemies; and to her fathers parents, who are so different from each other but are each so close to her in their own way.
-Those people as well, come visiting in the hospital, and the spirit that is Mia, thinks about what they all mean to her, but she also thinks of all that shes lost and she thinks to herself that to go on living will be really hard. It would be so much easier to accept death and be with her parents and brother. It wouldnt be a successful story if she didn't choose life, but how she gets there is very well done. Its difficult not to feel for her as the people around her pray for her to get better, and understand that, even in life, things will be difficult for her going forward.
-Very well written.
