But it's simple delicious.  I use a bit of honey in it, but that's just my taste desire.
Revolution is a superior brand of tea to others, I think.  The bags are not paper.  You can see the picture on the box.  Some finer restaurants carry Revolution tea.

These are great little cups (like melmac) (not glass)  They cannot be put in oven of course, but think they would be ok for microwave.  (short period)  I use them for dipping chicken sticks, carrot sticks, etc... Not quite as bit as regular pudding cups, but could be used for that.

This is not very hot at all, but flavor galore!  It comes in a great hard plastic container with sprinkle spout, so don't have to use a spoon unless you want to.  I'm loving it.  Will take me a long time to use it all, but can add it to so many things...
great little pan  However, it's not ceramic, so it will stick some.  But it is heavy enough stainless and very good little skillet
Nice, keeps paints separated.  It is rather small though, no bigger than about 6 inches or so.  Adequate & thick enough plastic to hold. Wells not very deep.

After owning a Fire 7, I bought this for hubby for his birthday.  He loves it.  It is a bit different than the Kindle Fire 7, icons and pull downs a bit different, but it is a great machine.  It's memory capacity is very large, and we love downloading a lot of music, and books.  Of course, with books, after you read them, you can delete them from the "device" and still have them in the "clouds" for re-read at later time.  Of course, books that you refer to often, or might want to read without "wifi", would need to stay downloaded "on device."  The speed is fast.  Of course, our wifi is fast, and that makes a difference too.  Screen is nice and big.  The only thing I can say negative is that the "cover/protector" we purchased- will not stand on its END (up & down) because this Kindle Fire 10 is so tall.  That is not a biggy at all, but was use to my Kindle Fire 7 propping up on stand either direction.  All in all, we are glad that we got the Fire HD 10, as it will supply all his needs for entertainment.

I love this book.  I've read it several times.  In book form and audio.  It's such a "feel good" book, showing ordinary lives in a happy light.  It has warmth and character, hard work and brings out what really matters in life. It's about two people forming a small catering company that met in cooking school.  They struggle against their spouse and (girlfriend) to make the new company work.  There is much humor and compassion in this book as two small children appear in the mix who are related to them, but neglected and need special love and attention.
Nice sturdy table.  Can be used for picnic table, dining table (if you use table cloth).  Good purchase

Sure, it's not teflon, but neither are you getting the toxic substance from cooking with it.  This pan cleans up nicely for it being stainless.  I have all sizes in this type pan.  Love them all.  This one is great for omelets and small stuff.  Each size has its own greatness.  I really love the round bottoms on the pans.  The stir fry pan is great too.  The handles don't get hot, and they all clean better than my old stainless ones did.  They cook very evenly too.  I'm sold!
My husband got this for holding shelves in place while he paints them.  He really likes it.  He didn't have any trouble figuring out how to use it.  He says it's exactly what its suppose to be.

this is not completely hull=less, but much less hulls than regular popcorn.  It's also non GMO.  And although it's a bit smaller than regular popcorn, it pops well in my hot air popcorn maker.  A few kernels blow out before popped, but that's to be expected with the hot air popper.  We love this corn and it will last us awhile, as it is a 6 lb bag!  yeah!  I suggest you keep in the freezer to keep fresh.  The pantry moths started making their way to it, and I caught it before they infested into it- and put the bag in freezer.  Pops up very well, doesn't burn in my hot air popper, and only just a couple/few don't pop.  It's GREAT!  And tasty- yummy!

October 2017  UPDATE:
There are about 10 kernels that blow out of the hot air popper.  Sometimes, I throw the first few back in (before they get too hot).  But most of them pop.  I pour several cups into a glass canister with tight lid. The rest I keep in the freezer until needed.  This keeps the 6 lb bag fresher.  It is definitely NOT hulless.  I don't notice it so much when i'm stuffing my mouth, but on that last bite- when I've had plenty, I find there is a lot of debris that I still have in my mouth- so it's swish swish in the bathroom.  Extremely good while eating though. And the hulls are not big like many brands,.  Love that it's non GMO!  I still give them a 5 star until I find something better.
I first experienced this at the salon & ordered a bottle of it.  But it is very sweet flowery and brings nice memories of wild flowers, but is strong.  So i find myself not using it often.

Simple little rather thin cotton toile valance, but looks very sweet in my kitchen window.  The colors are muted, not bright- pale. So don't expect bright blue & white.  The white could be considered an "off white".  It gathers nicely on the rod (not provided).  Although it says 15.5 inches, (which is is), when its on the rod and gathered up, it hangs more like 13-14- which was fine with me.  Just place your rod at a spot where it will hang about 14 inches- to the spot that is best for your window.  Again, it's not thick and will not keep out light.  I have it over some kitchen louver blinds, and needed a bit of color to match my blue willow & light blue kitchen- with white cabinets (and granite look- corian- off white countertops)  These don't POP out at you, but they are simple and sweet.  I gave 4 stars instead of 5 because of thinness of material & paleness of colors.  When sun shines through my kitchen window (morning time), you see through it like water and don't see much color.  But later, they show up better.

I got these to go with Voice Alert System-6 Home/driveway Alarm.  Gives extra notification with more than one sensor.  Be sure to program the inside of each sensor to be different than others.  for example; one may say 1, 1.  Put another at 2, 2, etc....If you don't, each sensor will say the same thing as the others.
Follow instructions to the letter.  Not hard.  Install under eave of house/porch, etc...to keep rain off....I haven't had mine long enough to know how long they will last. They pick up at least 30 feet away, I think even further than that!  And they have a broad view, not just a zeroed in type.  They are very similar to motion sensors on regular burglar alarms - which we also have (inside our house/garage, etc)

Although it's well written, I found the writings to lack plot enough to keep my interest.  Her philosophy seemed out if place to me in parts of the story.  She was no doubt a very wealthy, spoiled lady of leisure.  She had nothing to do but wonder around her yard while others worked.  But she still had a way of putting words together.  I lived her view of a peaceful garden and that, for me is the only saving grace if this book.  Too disjointed in all other thoughts she wrote.

users.query: Great reviews with photos included! This was a Valentine gift for my 10 year old granddaughter and absolutely adores the sparkles and motion . . . I added a shorter white gold chain of mine for a better fit!

cands.text:
I did read the reviews before deciding to order this 'cute' and 'functional' wallet purse. The images from other reviewers show a very different image than the item I received! The 'gold' lettering is illegible and the inside zipper isn't functional. This was intended for my 9 year old granddaughter and the only positive is that I did not send it to her as a gift. The design is as shown but the craftsmanship is beyond poor.

Of all the products I've ordered from Amazon, this is the most disappointing. I do not intend to return the item . . . it just might be a five star find for someone else!

With mixed reviews, I decided to take a chance . . . perfect choice for me! They are 'sterling silver' and the CZ reflects light and sparkles of color. Exceptional quality for a reasonable price . . . a good gift choice, too.
What would I have wanted to know? The posts have an indentation that help hold the earrings in place . . . similar to the diamond earrings I have in yellow gold. The sizes are listed . . . don't know the metric system? The pupil of the eye is an easy indicator . . . a fully dilated pupil is 9 mm. 'Pin point' is usually 3 mm. This is a simple way to judge the size so one isn't disappointed. The black box makes this a suitable  gift.

 I don't enjoy 'real' shopping so Amazon's format, including the easy question option, is more than just helpful for me. Thank you for the reviews!

hs

Impressive! Comfy and easy to adjust for a perfect fit. They are well made and the description is accurate. My 9 year old granddaughter wears her long hair loose. She loves that 'free feeling!' The reviews were encouraging for a way to keep her hair out of her face. She chose the brown because it matches her hair and I'm wearing the silver/white. I expected her to take it off as soon as I adjusted it for her . . . surprise! It stayed on all day. She seemed to forget she was even wearing a headband. Fun day with different activities . . . granny (72), too!

Terrific customer service . . . definitely recommended!

These throws are terrific! The colors are accurate but don't begin to show the lustrous fabric. Well made and oh so easy to machine wash and dry. My grandchildren love the cuddly warm fabric . . . perfect size for all three of us. The aubergine is a rich shade that is closer to purple than to the darker shades of eggplant. It became obvious that I needed to add another color when the grandchildren had a 'slumber party' with granny and cats. Yes, the two felines have their own throws (black and grey to match their fur). The boy child's choice is navy and the girl child's favorite color (this month) is purple. I ordered three about a year ago and after weekly washing/drying the fabric and color hasn't changed. The colors don't fade/bleed so they can be included with other laundry. Kitty fur? Just put them in the dryer (no heat) for 10 minutes before washing. Easy care plus!

Definitely recommended!

My grandchildren enjoyed 'The Swan Princess' so much that this seemed to be a fun next adventure. The same animated characters with another wicked sorcerer. 'Friendship' is an integral part of this second in the series of three. Definitely recommended for those who enjoyed the first in the series (offered with prime) and grandchild approved!

Purchased as an instant video and stored on Amazon . . . smooth streaming and crisp audio.

After reading other reviews, this purchase was a fun surprise. The plastic box keeps the studs neat and easy to find. The size is tiny and that's what I wanted. No problems with the posts and they are comfortable . . . this was a good choice for me because losing one isn't panic mode. Lost too many expensive gem stones because of the backs. Easy keep and easy store with lots of sparkle!

Tiny and fun . . . definitely not recommended for children! The price is certainly reasonable and the information and size are accurate.  If  you want a crescent moon and star that will fit inside the the curve of the upper ear, these are just the right size. This was a 'for fun' purchase . . . the posts haven't bent and I haven't lost them. Another plus is that they have remained the original color.  Fun!

These were a fun gift for my 9 year old granddaughter and she was absolutely delighted! She recently received an easel and I thought these would be a good introduction to a combination art medium. I drew a fairy water garden for her and the results were better than expected. No, they aren't professional quality but the pencils and case are well worth the price for the young aspiring artist. I found them easy to create multiple effects with and without a few drops of water. I would recommend them for ages 6 and older.

These hoops are just the right size for me. The quality and sparkle are more than I expected for this price. Comfortable with a secure lock. The description is accurate, too. I added these to the CZ stainless stud collection . . . smallest stud first, hoop in the middle and then another small stud.

Teen age to my 71 years . . . definitely recommended!

Grandchildren seem to be a part of so many of my reviews and for good reason! If it isn't what they can enjoy, they will willingly voice their opinion. These two critics are well behaved and affectionate . . . yes, I do enjoy their company and finding fun, healthy treats for us. 'Pop Secret' has become a favorite! Easy to prepare, no burned popcorn and great flavor adds up to a perfect combination. Just the right amount to share and even the box offers convenient storage options. Recommended and grandchild approved!
A lesson of friendship and how it came to be. Another adventure to share with these cuddly grandchildren. A way to encourage friendship and marvel at their response. A happy ending for all!

These studs are a much better quality than expected for the price! Comfortable, lock line safety backs and lots of sparkle . . . the description is accurate, too.

Great find for me and definitely recommended . . . for any age (I'm 71) except young children.

11/4/2016
I liked these so much that I ordered the square shape set. The packaging is simple if you realize that the studs are pressed into a thin
Styrofoam rectangle and the backs are in a very small cellophane bag that is sealed with clear tape. The zip top plastic bag is intended for easy shipping and not for storage. That bag with the earring backs is easy to miss/drop when opening the zip top envelope. It did give me an idea for storing the different sets . . . ordered the wrong hard case for a Kindle 7 and it's a perfect size and color for the earrings. It actually contained a Styrofoam shipping insert that keeps the earrings (attached the backs) in an easy find/store container.

All of the sets I have are comfortable and keep their sparkle . . . I even sleep/shower without removing them until I decide I want a different 'look!'  None of mine have had the stems bend or insecure backs. The stainless steel doesn't cause irritation or change color and the stones have retained their luster. Perhaps I'll add a colorful set just for fun!

This was a 'request' from my granddaughter! It's her current favorite and has become one of mine. This was an Amazon instant video purchase saved to Amazon. The quality for both visual and audio is excellent with smooth streaming. A definitely recommend!
Note other reviews for content.

Much better quality than expect and a fun way to add a touch of color and light. Really pleased with the LED function . . . as soon as the room starts to become dark the light shines through the mushrooms and flowers. The half shell base easily plugs into a wall socket. Not too bright . . . a soft glow that is just right. I like this fun night light and plan to order two more (different colors) for the bathrooms.

The images are accurate and so are the colors.

Recommended and a fun gift!

Much better quality than expect and a fun way to add a touch of color and light. Really pleased with the LED function . . . as soon as the room starts to become dark the light shines through the mushrooms and flowers. The half shell base easily plugs into a wall socket. Not too bright . . . a soft glow that is just right. I like this fun night light and plan to order two more (different colors) for the bathrooms.

The images are accurate and so are the colors.

Recommended and a fun gift!

What a fun colorful pattern! I wear solid color T type dressy tops and this is the perfect hairband for me. Just as comfy and easy fit as the other narrow  bands!

So pleased that I found the Hipsy brand . . . thank you for all the product reviews!

These studs are all about sparkle and comfort . . . great to keep or give as a pink boxed gift! They keep that sparkle thru showers and sleep time, too. Much better quality than expected for the price and I don't have to be concerned about losing expensive diamond earrings. The earring backs are small and fit the safety ring stems to keep them secure.

Definitely recommended!

This was ordered as a gift for an adult friend and she called to tell me how much she 'loved' it! There is nothing like a 'smile call' of appreacion. Her TV remote fits perfectly in the mouth and is just right for a neck and lower back rest. I know just what these 'toys' can do. Choose by color or favorite animal . . . our 'family' is complete. The last additions were orded via Amazon instead of the 'Stuffies' web site. Amazon prime means two day delivery rather than a week. Two grandchildren were more than delighted with their new 'pets' and I kept a few for their visits. Soft copy book about your 'pet' is included along with fun stickers.

Definitely recommended for all ages over the age of 1 year . . . comfortable, easy to wipe clean and well made. Even my cats enjoy a place to nap. Remember: "It's what's inside that counts!"

A favorite book of mine with a different ending for the movie . . . my granddaughter enjoyed 'The Secret Garden' and 'Finding Rin Tin Tin,' so I decided (with parental consent) that she might understand the real meaning of 'a princess.' There are so many 'princess characters' in videos that I didn't want her to misunderstand. She will soon be 7 years old and recognizes the difference between 'make believe' and 'reality.' To have an 'imagination' can be a wonderful gift that can help us to endure what might be the complexities of our reality . . . a way to grow emotionally and help one understand. Good choice for this genre!

This was a 'gift' for me. The flavor and texture is just about perfect for my taste and I would not hesitate to send this as a fun gift. That 'picante touch' makes these olives perfect additions to salads or enjoy them as a tasty treat. The packing and shipping were exceptionally well done and they arrived when expected!
Fun sequel to 'Romancing The Stone!' Kathleen Turner, Michael Douglas and Danny Devito together? A 'jewel' isn't always a gem? Smooth streaming, crisp audio and easy storage with Amazon!

Perhaps the best of the Vietnam War movies with excellent cinematography and acting. Even though I have the DVD, using Amazon instant video and cloud storage is so convenient . . . smooth streaming and crisp audio.
Definitely recommended!

Reasonable nutrition that's a quick fix. These meals are easy to store and prepare. The Salisbury steak is a classic favorite . . . the potatoes may not be the best but the meat is tender and flavoful. Just add a salad for an easy to prepare meal. For those of us who prefer to grocery shop on Amazon, this is a definite recommend.

Good choice if you need a single box . . . some of the pieces were slightly broken (as expected) so that just means I don't have to break them. Good flavor and crispy, chewy texture. I do as much shopping with Amazon as possible . . do not enjoy the 'real thing!' This was offered with prime so it was a great choice for me!

The final touch for the La Choy Chinese products! Adds that extra crunch . . . if you are counting calories (especially fat), try adding 1/8 cup or less as a topping. The flavor and texture can be improved by heating in a toaster oven (350 degrees) for 2 to 3 minutes.

Favorite quick fix: 1 egg scrambled, 1/2 cup brown rice (rice bowls available via Amazon), 1 cup any of the La Choy veggie combinations (Chop Suey, Chow Mein or Fancy mix).
Scramble egg in microwave safe container (I use a shallow/wide bowl), add cooked rice and microwave for 30 seconds. Stir from the outer edge to center and microwave 10 seconds or till firm. Top with veggies and heat 20 seconds or until hot. Add soy sauce to taste (low sodium available) and sprinkle with Mein Noodles (Crisp the noodles while preparing other ingredients).

 One bowl for cooking and serving so no messy cleanup . . . enjoy!

users.query:
If you need a quick escape from reality, this series is the one to escape to. It's got hot guys, hockey, romance, and some angst.

Patrick O'Doul is this gorgeous, Alpha Male type, but he hates to be touched, something that goes back to his childhood. Ari Bettini just broke up with her long-term boyfriend, and is wary of anything to do with relationships at this point.

I enjoyed this book, don't get me wrong, but the problem I think I had with the book is that the romance goes from 0 to 60. There is this attraction there, but they hold each other at arms length and then all of the sudden they are falling into bed with each other.

That being said, I still think it was a really good book. It had all the hallmarks of Bowen's previous books. There wasthe romance, some great hockey playing, some drama, and some love. All of my favorite things.

My rating: 4/5 stars
*I received an arc copy of this book via Netgalley from Berkley Publishing. Thank you!

cands.text: I found this book hard to get into. Unfortunately, nothing grabbed me about this book which made it hard to finish. The romance was not developed fully (though, since it is the first of a series, I'll give it leeway for that), and it just felt like an average read. To be honest, I skimmed through after the first few chapters. Not my favorite read this month. It was an interesting premise, I just wish the execution had been a bit more polished.
If you're looking for a quick, hot read, pick this book up. It was great to see their relationship develop as the story went on.

If you love romantic, upbeat, romantic books, you will love this book. It will have you at turns laughing and crying (sometimes at the same time).

We first meet Clemency rushing to catch her plane and almost missing it (been there, done that!), and sitting next to Sam, who ignores her at first been then theres this connection between them that is undeniable. However, he is married and talk is where they leave it. Three years later, they meet again when Clemencys stepsister, Belle, moves back with her new boyfriendnone other than Sam. Things become a bit complicated as there are still feelings between them. I knew from the description that there was going to be a love triangle (my most loathed trope), however, I thought it was very well handled and resolved.

What I loved about Jill Mansells writing is the focus on more than just Clemency and Sam and Belle. We got to know the rest of the characters that played a part in this story. I was drawn into this town, and into these characters lives. Mansell is a new favorite author, one whose writing I need to catch up on!

I don't have the words to adequately express how much I loved this book. It was a brilliant conclusion to this duology, and had such heart to it. I absolutely adore Alexandra Brackens writing! Some small part of me wants this series to continue, but maybe with side characters having their own stories. While my favorite people, Nicholas and Etta, spent much of the story apart, I spent much of the story anticipating when they would reunite, and it didn't disappoint. They spend much of the story fighting their way back to each other, encountering danger after danger, and taking the reader all of the world, and through all different time periods. I have to say my least favorite character was Sophia. She improves a bit towards the end of the story, and I like that she is this fierce character, but she was just not a likable character for me. My only complaint is with the epilogue. Im not sure what significance it has to the story. To me, it just confused things. If anyone can shed light on the epilogue, please do! And, like I mention in my review of Passenger, Bracken does a wonderful job researching the time periods mentioned in her story!
This book sucked me in! I started and finished it in one day, it was that engrossing! Sarah and Dante are one of my new favorite couples, especially alpha male Dante!

I loved this book. It was an honest look at love, heartbreak, and friendship. It is beautiful.

To be honest, the thing that drew me to this book was the cover. It is absolutely beautiful. I had cover lust when I first saw it, and wanted the book because of it alone. Justeverything about that cover. I bought this book because of the cover alone, and it was the best decision I made.

Im so much better with imaginary people and their imaginary lives. -pg. 79

The main character, Emi is in highschool, interning as a set designer that her on-again-off-again girlfriend, Morgan, got for her. After having been broken up with for the sixth time, she needs something to distract her from her heartache. When she and her best friend Charlotte attend the estate sale of the late Clyde Wilder, it leads them to Ava. She is unlike anyone that Emi has ever met, and soon, she finds herself with a crush on Ava.

Whats the use in waiting until the right moment if that moment never comes? I say. "What if the moment escapes you in a split second when your focus was elsewhere? -pg. 284

Besides the Emi's story, I learned more about the movie industry than I thought I would. It was a look into the magic that goes into the movie sets, and just how much work it is. I loved that. When books usually deal with the movie industry, it's with actors, actresses, producers, directors, etc. But this one was behind the scenes, and I loved that.

For all that I loved Emi and Ava, my favorite character was probably Charlotte. She was there for Emi through everything. She is the friend that I hope I am to my friends-someone who is there through thick and thin, and is the shoulder to lean on and the person to vent to. I just loved her.

I blew through this book. I was finally able to sit down with it last night, and once I did, I couldn't put it down. This is a great, light read, something that would be a good summer read. Nina LaCour's writing is beautiful. Definitely give this book a try!
If you love a good romance, you'll enjoy this book. It's a short read--only 175 pages--that flies by. I would recommend this for fans of Amanda Quick and Elizabeth Hoyt.

First of all, thank you Mark My Words Publicity for letting me read/review this book!

I throughly enjoyed this book. I had read the first book, Going Down in Flames, and I liked it. I thought it had been an enjoyable read-I liked the book and was interested to see where Chris Cannon went with it, so when I got the opportunity to review the second book, I took it. Im glad I did, because I enjoyed the second book more than the first.

Bryn has it rough in this book. From her relationship with Zavien-which, can I just say was a terrible mistake on her part; I mean, he is already promised to this other girl, and he makes vague promises of them running away together. Basically, he is an a**hole. He pissed me off, let me tell you. I believe some of my Goodreads updates were along the lines of Zavien is a jerk to Zavien is now upgraded to a**hole to So Bryn needs to just date Valmont because hes a hottie and cares for her, and ditch Zavien, who is an a**. I developed a bit of a loathing for Zavien, if you couldn't tell. But back to Bryn-her relationship with Zavien is a good part of the first half of the book. That, along with attacks on the school, we see how their relationship just down spirals, and becomes more friendly with Jaxon.

Her solace, however, is her knight, Valmont-the first knight in a century or so. He helps relax her, and let her know that he will be whatever she wants him to be-friend, boyfriend, lover, whatever. I just absolutely love him. I wish that they would hook up already! But there is the complication of her grandparents checking her lineage with Jaxons (read: marriage contract), so that puts a crimp in my plans for the two.

While a good focus of the book is on Bryns differing relationships with these three men, another aspect of the book is Bryn trying to fit into this archaic and controlling society that doesnt quite accept her because of her crossbreed heritage. While she tries to adapt to a certain extent, she still tries to be herself which is what I like about her most, I think. She tries to adapt mainly for the benefit of her grandparents, who she is trying to get on better terms with (their relationship is another interesting part of this book).

There was so much action and heartbreak in this book, that I just throughly enjoyed myself while reading it. It was hard to put down!

Would I recommend? YES. Though, read the Going Down in Flames first, otherwise you won't understand what is going on.

Justoh man. This book. I love this book so much, I cant even begin to tell you. Rainbow Rowell has definitely become one of my favorite writers, with her ability to create these characters that you can identify and fall in love with so easily. After reading Attachments, which I reviewed here, I knew that I had to eventually own the rest of Rowells books.

I adore Cath, and her shy, fanfiction loving nature . She is sweet, caring, messed up just a little (arent we all), and completely absorbed in her writing. She was such a well written character, she almost seemed alive. I loved that she wrote fanfiction, and was this big writer in that world, though she is shy by nature. Being a big fan of fanfiction, I loved this aspect of the book. I love how much of a fangirl she is of the Simon Snow series (which is a clear parody of Harry Potter). It reminded me of the times I stood in line with my friends at midnight waiting for the next book or movie to release. Those were amazing times.

Then there was Levi, who I wish was real so that I could date him. ::I really do though:: He was so sweet and concerned about Cath when she went out, and was always there for her if she needed a ride home to rescue her dad, or save her sister. There were times that you wanted to smack him upside the head and ask him just what the heck he was doing? Was he trying to ruin his chances with Cath? but those were few and far between. I will say that Caths twin sister, Wren, upset me for most of the book in her selfishness to not want to be roommates, to not want to really ever hang out with her, and many other things;even though that made me sad, I understood where it was coming from, and interesting to see how that relationship would play out. Caths dad I just love, and feel sorry for all at the same time. After his wife up and leaves the family when the girls are in third grade, the girls struggle through life together with their slightly fragile father, who sometimes breaks down. The other characters in the book were some of my favorites as well, namely Reagan. Boy, was she a hoot! Sarcastic, slightly mean, but still caring, she was the perfect roommate to bring Cath out of her shell.

I thought it was interesting that Rowell included paragraphs from Caths fanfiction, letting the reader get into her head a little bit through them. It was an aspect I found interesting, after I realized what they actually were. They threw me for a loop the first time I came across one at the end of the first chapter.

Theres not really anything negative I can say about this book. I throughly enjoyed the book and would recommended it to any person out there who is a fangirl or boy, who loves fanfiction, or who just loves to read a well written book full of characters that you can fall in love with.

I came across this book on Netgalley, and the first thing that caught my eye was the cover (I mean look at it, its GORGEOUS.) Then that blurb, well, obviously I had to request it to see if it was any good. And it was definitely was! Auroras home life is not the best; with an aunt and cousin who hate her, an uncle who basically ignores her existence, and being bullied at school, life isn't easy. And then she and her family go to this mansion where she is kidnapped and taken through this portal into a magical world, where the real story begins. It is in this world that we learn the truth about Auroras family and past, and that she is actually the Princess of Illiandra. It is also here where we meet Rafe (a sort of Robin Hood in that world if you will), who she becomes immediately enamored with (kind of predictable).

I liked Aurora, and for a good part of the book I felt sorry for her, and was rooting for her. But as the story went on, it seemed she was more focused on Rafe and does he like me or is he just saving me because he owed my father a debt than on the fact that her aunt, the cruel queen, wants to kill her. That began to irritate me.

How will you ever know the magnitude of courage you are capable of if you never experience the hopelessness of fear? -24%

Another thing that began to frustrate me was the fact that almost all the action seemed to happen because Aurora made stupid decisions to go investigate something or because her ego was hurt, and as a consequence she almost gets killed several times. I couldn't help but feel that she was very childish throughout the entirety of the book.

For the most part this book was predictable (even down to the real identity of RafeI called that halfway through), but I truly did enjoy this book and I am looking forward to the second book coming out because I do want to see where Auroras journey takes her.

You know what book you need to get right. now.? A Man Called Ove. Seriously. It is such a beautiful book, and will make you appreciate all the curmudgeons in your life.

Seriously, you need to read about Oves life. It will make you cry, laugh, sympathize and be mad with him. Fredrik Backman does an absolutely wonderful job of drawing the reader in and showing you not to judge a grumpy person at first meet.

People called him antisocial. Ove assumed this meant he wasn't overly keen on people. And in this instance, he could totally agree with them. More often than not people were out of their minds.
Fredrik Backman, A Man Called Ove (pg. 36)

Ove is a straight-forward, has staunch principles, strict routines, and a short fuse. When you first meet him, you wonder what this guys problem is. But as you read on, you learn about Oves story, and that he just doesnt talk all the time. Hes actually a quite a taciturn person. Ove wound his way into my heart.

I will warn you, there is a theme of suicide in the story. Oves wife died six months before the story takes place, and without here, his life seems empty and he just wants to join her.

People said Ove saw the world in black and white. But she was color. All the color he had.
 Fredrik Backman, A Man Called Ove (pg. 45)

She was his entire world, the one whom he fought with everything he had for. So when she is gone, he is lost. His world has no meaning without her. But then move in some neighbors who don't pay any attention to his grumblings, and make their way into his grumpy heart.

This story is beautiful, and had me crying at times, and laughing at others. I highly recommend it!

I absolutely loved this book! I could not put it down. Meira is a strong female character, who I really loved. There is a slightly love triangle, but honestly, it didn't bother me that much. I loved Sara Raasch's writing; it really drew me in and gave me all the feels. I am eagerly anticipating the second book, Ice Like Fire, since we were left with a cliffhanger that was just plain cruel.

Just... I need to process this book.

Ok.

It is really hard to put into words what this book did to me. After finishing it, it felt like my heart had been ripped out of my chest, brutally stomped on the floor, then lovingly put back in. The crazy thing is that I loved every minute of that book, even when I was yelling at Tate for her crazy decisions. I ugly cried through the last half of the book, feeling my heart hoping and breaking right alongside Tate's as she tried not to hope for more out of the relationship with Miles, and I loved and hated that at the same time.

Colleen Hoover has a unique, wonderful way of breaking your heart, and then mending it together again. I love it when I find an author who has the ability to mess with my emotions so much. It does not happen often, and when it does, it is a wonderful thing. As this was my first book of hers, I cannot wait to get my hands on other books of hers, especially Maybe Someday.

This is such an emotionally honest, dark book. It is told from four different points of view, and each one brings a different perspective of the shooting. Two of the characters are trapped in the auditorium with the shooter, one is in detention in the Principals office and is able to contact the police, and the last is outside on the track with her team when the shooting begins. Over the next 54 minutes, we learn about each of these characters connecting history.

This book broke my heart. It explores a variety of issuesrape, physical abuse, sexuality, diversity, and sibling relationshipsall in the span of 54 minutes. Books about school shootings are something that is never easy to read, but I thought Nijkamp handled the subject deftly.

There were so many things I loved about this bookthe writing, Claire and Chris, Toms, the diversity of charactersI would recommend this to everyone.

I was eagerly anticipating this follow-up to The Girls in the Water, a book that I was in love with. I was excited to see where the characters of Detectives King & Lane would be taken to, and I while I wasn't disappointed, I thought this was a bit weaker than the first book.

Like in book one, this book was told from multiple POVs, which can be a tricky thing for an author to handle. This time around, I had a harder time getting into the story because of the switching POVs. What I did enjoy about this book was the way Jenkins captured the grief that everyone felt, especially Kiera North's parents.

Overall, this was a fun thriller to escape to, one that will have you finishing the book in one sitting.

This was such a great book to pick upI mean: Christmas, Paris, bookshop, romance. All the best ingredients for a cute romance book. Sarah and Ridge were adorable, who truly loved each other but had some work some things out in their relationship. It was realistic, and had me daydreaming of Paris.

At first I thought a bit predictable, but after reading it for a bit longer, I realized that its not at all. This book is all about a couple who are already together and trying to make a long distance relationship work. They are both desperately in love with each other, but when Sarah is in Paris and only sees Ridge for one day out of 90 days, she starts to question whether their romance will survive the distance. This is all about making your relationship work and about communication. This was a realistic romance book, and I throughly enjoyed every moment of being in that Paris bookshop and wandering Parisian streets (and even going into the Louvre to see Van Goghs Starry Night!).

This is the second book in The Bookshop series by Rebecca Raisin (the first being where Sarah and Ridge first meet and fall in love). This was my first book of Rebeccas and I was not lost at all.

This book had a lots of potential, and to be honest, this was a cover buy. It was insightful and captivating, but at the same time there was an element to the story that left me bored, and I can't pinpoint exactly what that was.

I have mixed feeling about this book. While I thought the writing was good and I was sucked into the story, I was also bored throughout a good portion of the story. It felt like nothing was happening even when things were happening.

The Girls follows Evie Boyd (age 14) in the late 1960's during the time of Charles Manson and his "family". Knowing that it was vaguely inspired by the Manson family, I was expecting it to be a bit more of a thriller. Instead, we follow Evie around, seeing her growing into womanhood as she becomes captivated by Suzanne and drawn into the soon famous cult. She gets introduced to some of the harder drugs and sexual assault. During most of the times that Evie engages in some type of sex act at the ranch, it is not willingly done; most of the time she is being coaxed into it. The only time she is vaguely willing is when Suzanne is involved.

What I did like about the book was it's raw quality. I could imagine myself back in the '60s, having the freedom to go out whenever you wanted, leaving your doors unlocked. I also appreciated the fact that there wasn't too much details when the murders in the book did eventually take place.

This book is conflicting for me, because while I found it hard to put down, I found 200+ pages in that I was bored, and pinpointing what exactly I was bored with is hard. There was some element that I wish had been in the story. Overall, I do recommend this story. What I found conflicting, you might not.

I found the beginning to be a bit boring, and Agnieszka a bit irritating. But there is a point about 50 or so pages in, when she is fighting off the advances of the Prince, that things clicked for me and I started enjoying this book. Things do slow down a bit towards the middle bit, and you have to muddle through, but once you get past that, things pick up again. (I don't want to spoil the story for those who haven't read it yet, so I won't say anymore on that).

I thought the world building in this was excellently done. Information was presented a bit at time so as not to overwhelm.

Now, (SPOILER), the wizard known as the Dragon is not actually a dragon. Sad, I know. I was a bit disappointed, because I love stories with dragons. And to be honest, he a bit of a d*ck. That being said, Agnieszka begins to grow close to the Dragon, and learn what it is that happens to the girls he takes to his castle every ten years.

I think my favorite relationship in this book was the one between Agnieszka and her sister, Kasia. They are close to each other, and do anything to protect each other, going so far as to rush into the woods to rescue the other.

Overall, I gave it four stars because of the lulls this book has, which at times makes the book become a bit dull. Other than that, the storytelling is beautiful!

An epic fantasy filled with swashbuckling adventure, intrigue, and beautiful friendships! I fell in love with this book!
The best thing about this book are the friendships. Theres a lot more that is great about this book, but honestly, my favorite part was the close friendship that exists between Safi and Iseult (threadsisters), and Merik and Kullen (threadbrothers). If you are looking for a book with great friendships, read this one!

Another character that I really liked was Aeduen, a Bloodwitch who hunts them throughout the story. You never quite know whether he is good or bad (but I secretly think he is good). He is bent on revenge, bent on tracking the Truthwitch and the Threadwitch. But along the way, he develops a life-debt to Iseult and learns that these two girls might be the Cahr Awyn.

I also loved that romance was a minor aspect of the story. Yes, there was strong attraction between Safi and Merik, and I totally ship them together, but the friendships are what stood out to me in this book. Also, I am totally shipping Aeduen and Iseult together and nobody will change my mind on that one.

And I cant even talk about Kullen right now. I just cant I love him so much and Im heartbroken.

I do wish this world had been a little more fleshed out, which is why I gave this four stars instead of five. I didn't quite understand what was going on, why these other countriesCartorra, Nubrevna, Portollaintensely dislike the Marstok. What does help a little in understanding the background of this story is Susan Dennard explaining the world of the Witchlands basically being loosely based on Imperial Europe (video below). I just wish I understood more about the magic of this world, and why everyone wants Safi for her Truthwitchery.

I started this book on my way back home from Okinawa, and let me just say that this book was enthralling. It had me turning the pages to see what happened next.

This book has often been compared to The Girl on the Train, and I can definitely see the similaritiesboth have an unreliable narrator, both have drinking problems, among other things. Im not big into psychological thrillers, so it being compared to The Girl on the Train was a selling point for me as I loved that book.

There were many twists and turns in here, some I saw coming and some that surprised me. But what really surprised me was the endingI didn't see that coming! Ruth Ware did a good job of stringing me along, making me question Los sanity, whether she actually saw a woman being thrown overboard or if it was just an nightmare.

Another thing I liked about this book was her relationship with her boyfriend. They had departed on bad terms when she went on this assignment, but we see periodically throughout the story him becoming more frantic to find out what happened to her. It added a twist to the story that kept you on the edge of your seat.

Overall, this was an enjoyable psychological thriller, one I definitely recommend!

I set this book aside at 130 pages, so this review is based on what I read. I'll be honestthis was a bit of a disappointment for me. The best thing about this book (in my opinion) is the cover. I'm obsessed with that cover. What bothered me the most was the narrator's (Odelle's1967) voice in the first part; the character is speaking in her vernacular, but the execution of it feels clumsy and really hard to follow--the author often loses me at parts, yet in another sentence will speak in complete sentences. I wish that there had been consistency in her voice, one way or the other, that way I could have adjusted to her pattern of speech easier. She cleans up the speech for Olive (1936 timeline), but then we're thrown back to Odelle's timeline, and it's jarring. I wish I liked this story, I really do. But besides the narrator's voices bothering and losing me, I was bored throughout. It didn't seem like much happened (though take this with a grain of saltstuff probably happened halfway through the story, I just didn't get to it). Overall, I thought she was more successful in The Miniaturist: A Novel.

Ill be honestwesterns are not really my favorite genre. I don't hate them, but I don't exactly go out of my way to read or watch them. But Vengeance Road was an absolute delight to read. Its a fast-paced story of revenge, shoot-outs, and outlaws. Erin Bowman could definitely get me t
I loved Kate. She does what she must to avenge the murder of her father, disguising herself as a boy, tracking down the Rose gang, gaining stragglers, and discovering surprising twists along the way. Shes a badass, with a fiery personality.

Im not sure what I expected when I read this, as I really don't have much experience with westerns, but this one took me by surprise. And there were twists that I was not expecting! I also enjoyed the fact that the love story was secondary and not an integral part of the story (in my opinion).

I definitely recommend this book!

Escape for the weekend to the seaside of southern France in this romantic read! You might have guessed by now, but I love T.A. Williams' books; they are romantic, light, and addicting, something I tend to look for in romance books lately. After escaping an engagement, Natalie escapes to Southern France to stay with her grandmother (her last living relative), to figure out her life. What she doesn't expect is to become popular with the male population, and to meet the man of her dreams.

This was such a fun, summery book, filled with history and romance, I quickly fell in love with it! This is one book you should definitely add to your tbr pile!

This is the perfect book for people who love historical/regency romance! It was like reading a tale by Jane Austen or Charlotte Bronte.

M.C. Frank does a brilliant job of (reverse) retelling the story of Jane Eyre, with beautifully written characters! The story was much darker than I was expecting, but I liked the twist that Frank gave to the classic gothic romance.

The story follows the Duke of Ashton as he meets and hires the tiny, demure governess, Beatrice  and falls in love with her. But what he doesn't know is her dark past that follows her around where ever she goes. I loved how this story developed and I could quite easily pick this up again and read their story over and over.

My one complaint: I thought the Duke of Ashton was a bit to bipolar at first. He would seem to go from one extreme to the other in his dealings with Beatrice. I wish that had been toned down a bit.

users.query: This is one of my favorite series. I downloaded this book at 3 in the morning and could not put it down. I love the cowboys of Crawley Creek and Vin is no exception. After being abandoned by his mom at the age of 3 he became one of many foster children at the ranch. Lauren, another child who spent time at the ranch stole his heart when they were 18. Bad decisions on his part forced him to leave Crawley Creek and her behind. Two decades later they come face to face again. Can they put the past behind them and find the love they shared?

cands.text:
This is book 1 in the Crawley Creek series. Drannon is a cowboy running a ranch with his foster brothers. He was brought to the ranch as a foster child himself when his mother passed away from an overdose. After his foster parents both pass away, he now has taken over the ranch/dude ranch with his brothers.
Lacy recently lost her job in Chicago but since she had already booked this vacation to Crawley Creek, she decides to still go. Being raised by her father after her mom dies in childbirth, she didn't get to do most things kids do. She always wanted to learn to ride a horse and decided that this would be the perfect time. When their paths cross, it seems as two lost people may have just found what they both needed.

This is book 4 in the series, and perhaps, my favorite so far. Hawke grew up at the ranch as a foster child. With both foster parents now deceased, Hawke and his foster brothers now run the ranch. Jeanette has come to the ranch to work as a therapist for them. The ranch will be home to foster children as well as adults who suffer from PTSD. From the moment she arrived, Hawke has had his eye on Jeanette. Jeanette may be attracted to him but refuses to let herself fall for her boss, or anyone else for that matter. Can Hawke finally break down her walls and give them a life they both deserve? Can't wait to see what happens next at the Crawley Creek ranch.

This is Abraham and Seraphina's story and how Crawley Creek all began. Lori King is fast becoming one of my favorite authors. This whole series has sucked me in. There is so much depth to the characters and their stories. Can't wait for the next one.

This is book 4 in the Crawley Creek series and the continuation of Drannon and Lacy's story. Drannon, determined to give Lacy the wedding of her dreams, enlist the help of the Crawley Creek family to help make it special.

I loved getting to check-in with the characters that I love so much as well as getting to meet new ones. This is easily one of my top 3 favorite series ever.

There is so many twist turns and surprises in this book that I don't want to give anything away. So I'll just say this..... I love this series so much. This family has each other's backs completely. Even though they aren't all blood related they love stronger than any family I know.
Dean has turned into quite a fine young man. There's no one more perfect for each other than Dean and Megan.
Megan, the first and only girl Dean ever loved as a kid is back in his life and he doesn't plan on letting her go again.
If you have read the other books in the Senses series, I highly recommend it. Being such a tight knit family, the characters are always popping up in every book.

This is book 6 in the Crawley Creek series. What's hotter than a cowboy? A cowboy who happens to be a hot sexy sheriff.
Sheriff Brandon 'Bran' Bowers, has been trying to protect Destiny since the first day he met her, barely clinging to life. Destiny has been beaten, and violently abused at the hands of a sex trafficking ring leader. Staying at the Crawley Creek Ranch, she's finally starting to heal both physically and emotionally. Bran wants to help her heal her heart, but he didn't expect her to heal his too.

This is book 1 in the Bradens and Montgomery series and what a way to kick off a series.
Grace Montgomery and Reed Cross secretly dated in high school. Being from rival schools, they felt it best to keep their love affair under wraps. After high school Grace wanted to get out of their small town and took off to New York city.
Ten years later their paths cross when Grace is back home visiting her family. It soon becomes evident that neither one had gotten over the love they shared. But can they overcome the obstacles that stand in their way and rekindle their love?

I loved this series. Rebecca, a successful business woman in her mid 30's, has everything she could want in life. Everything that is but love. She had been in love with her best friend, Kade, in high school but never told him how she felt. Then he left without so much as a goodbye. 16 years later he comes back into her life. Then there's Jason, one of her employees, who is 12 years her junior. He makes it clear he wants a relationship with her but she's very hesitant because of those two things. She's torn between Jason and the image of Kade that she has in her head.

This is book 2 in this series. Adian has fallen head over heels for his stepsister, Kacey. But being hurt deeply by him she left her father's house and hasn't seen Adian for six months. That is until she sets off for college. The same college that he will be attending.
I absolutely love not only the main characters but their friends as well. I'm hoping that some of them will get their own story. Can't wait for book 3.

This is book 3 in the HIS Series. Jake and Emily's story. Emily has loved Jake since she was a child. When she turns 18, she gives herself to him, although he was too drunk to fully remember it. After being kicked out of the only family he had left, he leaves. When he is rescued and reunited with Emily and her brothers, so much has changed.
I've loved every book in this series, but this one is my favorite so far. I have a soft spot for Jake.

I have been waiting for Gage and Sally's story for years. Yes years. It was so worth waiting for. After losing her husband in a horrible skiing accident, Sally focuses on raising their teenage son. Gage and Sally are co-workers and soon become the best of friends. Gage has never met anyone that he wants more than Sally. Knowing that she needs time to mourn the loss of her husband, Gage is happy to wait in the friendship zone for her, but determined to one day make her his. After being best friends for years, one night in Vegas changes everything.

Can they finally be more, or will they lose the friendship they have created?

This is book 3 in the Bad Billionaires After Dark series and my favorite so far. It's a combination of friends to lovers and second chance romance. As with every Melissa Foster book I've read, I couldn't put it down and didn't want it to end in equal measure.

Carson and Tawny became friends and study buddies in college. Eventually they took their relationship to an intimate level, but only behind close doors. Not understanding her feelings and what they said about her, she broke things off. Now, years later, one thing is for sure. They aren't done with this relationship. Not even a little bit.
A super hot read that has me excited for Brett's story.

This is book 4 in the Jaded series. Nick was so in love, had a great life ahead of him, until she was gone. He thought his life died with her. His friends, who had become his family tried to be there for him. But, Chris, the one person who he felt a connection with kept trying to get to him. Can he ever let go of his past and truly love?

This is the fifth book in the HIS series. I've been waiting for Trent and Kelly's story and it was well worth the wait.
After nearly losing his life saving his niece, Trent left, left his brothers, his family, the HIS (Hamilton Investigation and Security team), everything that mattered. Kelly is pregnant and just lost her fiance in a hit and run accident. That may not have been an accident at all. When Trent learns that Kelly may be in danger, he comes back home to help protect her. Can two damaged souls help heal each other?
I loved this story. It's action packed and sexy. Can't wait to see what's next for HIS.

I have loved every book in this series but I think this may be my favorite so far. The love between Luke and Stuart is palpable. The support of everyone in this family of friends is so touching. Each character brings something different to this "family" that makes them more family than their own biological ever could.
Luke always puts everyone before himself. Stuart is the one person able to make him change that.

I absolutely love this book. When Kacey's mom gets a new job, she goes to live with the father she hasn't seen in years. She's suppose to be there for 6 months. From the first moment she lays eyes on her step-brother, Aidan, she feels things for him she shouldn't. Aidan feels them too but tries to distance himself from her and his growing desire for her.
I can't wait for the next book in this series.

This book had me holding my breath, waiting to see what happened next.
After ending a bad marriage and going through an even worse divorce, Molly is beaten down and just trying to survive. Her sister sets her with the very sexy, very stubborn attorney, Marco. If her life isn't complicated enough, she takes on a roommate to help pay the rent. A very handsome, sweet roommate named Drew. Both men want Molly, and Molly loves them both. Just in different ways. Who will Molly choose?
S. Donahue knocked this one out of the park. Can't wait for book 2.

This book started out slow and I didn't the I was gonna like it, but halfway through I couldn't put it down. The grammar needs a little work but that's not a deal breaker for me.
Ali, is in love with her neighbor, Kyle, who has been her best friend forever. It's sweet when they finally admit that have feelings for each other more than just friendship. Then it turns a little dark an I didn't see the end coming. Looking forward to book 2.
I was given a copy of this book for an honest review.

Clem Jamieson loved the rodeo circuit and women. He found a warm willing body in every city he stopped in. He would love them and leave them, usually with a daughter on the way. These are the stories of 6 of Clem's now grown daughters. I love these girls. Strong, sassy women, who while they share DNA thanks to their wild father, are extremely different.

I adore this book. I fell in love with Hailey and Chase from the very beginning. Hailey and Chase run into each other at a high school reunion. They haven't seen each other since high school. Back then Hailey had been over weight and bullied. Chase, was a very popular guy and one of the only people who stood up for Hailey. From the minute he sees her now, he knows he wants her. Now if he can only convince her of that.

I've been waiting for what seems like forever for Hunter and Jana's story. I wasn't disappointed. It was so worth the wait. Hunter is an artist that owns a metal sculpting business with his brother. Jana is a teacher at a dance studio, has a love for theater, and helps her brother out at his bar when needed. Neither believe in love, but a good romp in the sack never hurt anyone, right? Since they have the same circle of friends and spend plenty of time together, FWB's (Friends With Benefits) seems like a perfect fit for them. As long as they keep their feelings out of it.
Not only are Jana and Hunter's characters great, it was so nice to get to see the rest of the Seaside gang and see what's been going on in their lives.

I enjoyed this book. It was sweet and a really quick read.
Annie and 3 of her friends go in together to buy a local tree farm. When another friend of Annie's passes away, Ryder, the deceased friends brother, and Annie's childhood crush comes back to town after being gone for 15 years.

Wow. One of the most beautiful, heartfelt stories I've ever read. An emotional read.
3 years after Jaye's fiance died in a car wreck, she's still struggling to get back to some semblance of a normal life. Her mother's meddling ways and desire to get Jaye to date again doesn't help.
Archer, a military vet, who struggles with PTSD, and somehow the world seems to have forgotten is homeless and not sure life is worth living anymore. When Jaye sees the homeless man searching for food in her trashcan, she doesn't feel disgust, or outrage. Instead she feels something much deeper. Compassion.

I really enjoyed Loving Liberty. The characters Libby and Oliver really got to me. There was a lot of depth to the story and sometimes I felt like I was on an emotional roller coaster. Liberty comes from a well to do family where a lot is expected of her. When she meets Oliver, he seems to be just what she needs.
I received a copy of this book for an honest review.

There's no denying the chemistry between Bear and Crystal. They've been really good friends for a very long time. Bear wants it to be more and he's a very patient man. Crystal has issues from her past that she would prefer stayed there. I adored this storyline. I absolutely love Bear and his sexy biker self. The only thing I wasn't a fan of was how wishy washy Crystal was and how she treated Bear. But I will say by the end of the book I liked her a little better.

cands.text: Great little gel pad. Used as a leg pad in my car. Applied some 3M VHB black tape

These pads are great
-  for the people who give them less then 5 stars that's because you bought them for improper application.
The quality of the product should not reduced due to lack of understanding - Ratings should be revised.

Brake pads work off of friction. Performance pads require more heat to get up to proper performance levels.
This is mostly used under aggressive brake as a few laps or several hard stops and you're good to go.

These pads are not recommend for daily driving (ie going to work, buying weed and picking up pizza!)
 as you mostly will not get to the higher levels of heat to get them to start to bite which will lead you to think they suck ...
Also note you must bed these pads in, as most pads perform better when bedded in.

If you're looking for more of a daily driver pad I'd recommend the Yellow PC (ceramic) pads.

I would not recommend anyone feeding this or any other low grade cat food to their kitty. I thought I was making a good decision by choosing this for my cats until my 18 month old girl Cinderella developed bloody mucus filled stools and started dragging her bottom after using the litter box. After going to the vet it was discovered she had developed some bad food allergies to what she was being fed. The first 4 ingredients make up over 90% of what your kitty is eating so to remedy this I switched their food. If you look at the first four ingredients in Purina cat naturals they are chicken by product meal, corn gluten meal, soy flour and brewers rice. Cats are carnivores by nature and their bodies are not able to properly digest gluten and any grain in general. You wouldn't see a cat in the wild living off corn, soy, and rice so why would you feed your cats that in your home. Please make the change to a gluten and grain free cat food for the sake of your beloved kitty. Although they are a little more pricey they're worth every penny in my mind after seeing what this low quality food did to my kitty.

users.query:
I really liked the sound of this blurb and as a retired police officer it should have been right up my street. Unlike most of the reviewers so far I just didn't find it funny and maybe it plays better if you are from the US. It's certainly an original concept and I almost hesitate to say it but I can see it as a movie.

I received a free copy of The Senile Squad in return for an honest review and my thanks to NetGalley and Concierge Marketing Inc for that.

cands.text:
I always think that there is an authenticity to books written by police officers that research can't provide. They just 'feel' right and this book definitely does. I really liked the main character Charlie and it's great to see this is the first in a series. There was a good balance between the police investigation and procedural parts and the personal life of Charlie and now that we know her we are all set for book 2. The murders were described with enough detail that you know what happened but not too graphic and I didn't manage to work out the murderer prior to the reveal. I do like when an author ties up all the loose ends in the final chapter but there was a part that felt a bit too contrived and I would have rather left unresolved. Overall, I thought this was a great read and I'm looking forward to reading more of the series.

I received a free copy of Mummy's Favourite in return for an honest review and my thanks to NetGalley and the publisher Aria for that.

I thought this started a bit slow but when it got going it really had a lot thrown into it. There was a particular scene that had me shouting aloud at the Kindle and will stay in my head for a while yet.  Part of the plot really tested my credulity, but it is fiction after all.  I do like this series and I plan to read the rest of it.

What a cracker of a debut. I really enjoyed the style of the writing and the characters of Connie and Sadler the police officers were the standouts for me. This is a classy novel and I look forward to future works from Sarah Ward. Highly recommended.

t probably says a lot about me as a reader that it was the cover that attracted me to this book. I thought it was a really good read even though I did find it a bit confusing at times. If this had been highlighted as a spy thriller I probably wouldn't have chosen it and that would have been my loss but I do think that to find the right readers it is relevant to mention it.  It strikes me that this would transfer easily to tv or cinema. Recommended for those who enjoy a twisty thriller but even more so for those who like a bit of espionage.

I received a free copy of The Cleaner via NetGalley and my thanks to the publisher for that.

This is a fast paced crime thriller with a fabulous lead character in Danny Benedict. I suspect that in real life he might be insufferable but as a fictional character I loved him. I found myself a bit confused at the start as there are a lot of characters and various locations. With hindsight I would have faired better if I had written a crib sheet of who and where. I enjoyed this more the further I read and Ill definitely be watching out for the next in the series.

I really liked the writing style of this one and was pretty much hooked until the trial. That section went on for too long in my opinion. Having read some reviews I was expecting a dramatic ending but it didn't quite go that way.  As I was reading it I already knew that it was to be a BBC mini series and I think it would work really well in that format.

This review is for the audio book narrated by Jake Urry.

I am fairly new to audio books and this is the first psychological thriller I have tried in this format. At the start I thought I was going to be totally creeped out by the narration, maybe the early mention of the clown mask, but there is something about a Welsh accent that I find soothing and even the darkest parts of the book didn't really unsettle me.  Set in the late nineties it was definitely of its time with the police 'banter' and that certainly did ring true to life for me.  I think this may have had more impact on me if I had read it rather than listened and I think it would have been a page turner. I personally would have preferred a different ending but I'm sure lots of folk will love it.

I received a free copy of Portraits of the Dead via THE Book Club on Facebook and my thanks to the author John Nicholl for that.

I think this may be intended as a young adult book but I didn't realise that before I started to read it or chances are I wouldn't have bothered. It is not my usual genre and I was using it as a palate cleanser between gritty crime novels. All that said I enjoyed it and it made me nostalgic for a trip I took to Martha's Vineyard. It's tricky to add much more without spoilers.

From the blurb it was clear that this was not going to be a comfortable read but I don't think I was quite prepared for how some of the descriptions made me feel. I have listened to a Jake Urry narration before so I knew that I could happily listen to him for hours and it was a gripping story. I think what makes it so uncomfortable is that from recent high profile child abuse cases we know that it's probably very close to the truth. Dr David Galbraith is a horrible man and I spent the entire book hoping that he would get his comeuppance. You will of course need to listen to it or read it to find out whether he did.
The narration was worthy of 5 stars but overall it's a 4 star for me.
I received a free Audible copy of White is the Coldest Colour and my thanks to Jake Urry for that.

I do like a gritty crime book and this is a great example of that. The characters are very real and it was very easy to watch the story unfold in your mind's eye. I will be watching out for more from Nicky Black.

This is definitely a book that stands out from the crowd. The format was quite different to anything I have read before and I had to keep reminding myself that I was reading fiction. I have to agree with the reviews that say it's slow and at times boring but it fits perfectly with the telling of the story and anyone who has ever been involved in a trial knows how they drag on. I wondered whether this would be a 4 star review but the originality of it bumps it up to a 5.

Well that was short and sweet but maybe that was part of its charm. When I'm reading first person it's really important to me that the voice sounds right and this was spot on. No surprise I suppose given that I am an introvert and while I don't ever think about making people "red and open" I could definitely relate to the idea of being "only quiet with my words" and "usually loud in my mind".

I like a quirky or oddball character but jeez Louise, The Introvert is all that and then some more.

I received a free copy of The Introvert via TBConFB and my thanks to the author for that.

This is a pacy and tense courtroom thriller which made me feel like I was watching it in a movie. I liked the idea of Eddie Flynn as a con artist turned lawyer but I wasn't totally won over by him and even though I enjoyed this book I'm not sure whether I will read the next in the series.

I have read enough Andy Barrett books now to realise that none of the characters get an easy time, not even his protagonist, and this is again true here. This is absolutely packed full of action and has a bit of a cinematic feel. I was intrigued by the title and when you read far enough through the book you realise how perfect it is.

Ooh, I'm quite glad that this was a short book and I mean that as a compliment to the author as I found this quite disturbing. I read so much crime that I think I'm ready for whatever plot line is thrown at me but this one definitely unsettled me. I raced my way through it as I had to know what was going to happen and from part 2 onwards I couldn't have put it down.

I received a free copy of My Girl in return for an honest review and my thanks to NetGalley and the publishers JJP for that.

It is a perfect companion to the original book blending some laugh out loud moments into what could so easily have been a rather somber tale.  The narration by Celia Imrie was fabulous and seemed to fit the story perfectly. Definitely recommended for anyone who had read Harold Fry.

I just finished reading this and already I think I need to read it again. The author has a lovely style of writing and the stories from her personal life really add to the feeling that it's a friend talking to you. To use the author's phrases I am a 'cradle Catholic' and most definitely a 'work in progress'. While the author gives plenty to think about, she helpfully gives references for where to find more information. A well constructed and well written book.

I received a free copy of All In via NetGalley and my thanks to Ave Maria Press for that.

What a fabulous book. Its tricky to review without spoiling it for those yet to read it but I think it will be great for book club discussions. I was completely duped by the author and with the benefit of hindsight I don't know why I didn't figure it out sooner. Highly recommended.
My thanks to Michael Joseph for the copy of Exhibit Alexandra received via NetGalley.

I was definitely hooked in by the first chapter and thought I could predict where the story was headed but I was totally wrong. Nap was a very complex character who doesn't play by the rules and has major emotional baggage from the circumstances surrounding the death of his twin Leo 15 years previous. There was a fair bit of tension throughout this book but I felt the ending lacked tension and felt a bit flat. I'm also left with a few questions about events that weren't answered.

I received a copy of Don't Let Go via NetGalley and my thanks to Cornerstone for that.

I thought the concept was really original, a world divided not by class but by memory length of only one or two days. The use of the idiary to fill in the blanks in their memory should have felt very futuristic but actually felt just one step removed from where we are now with our extensive use of electronic data recording. While there was some intrigue over the murder, we did have a fairly limited list of suspects. I enjoyed the flashbacks via the diary entries and got caught up in that to the point where I almost forgot about the murder. I liked that the chapters from the detective point of view started with a countdown of the hours until the end of the day when his memory would reset. However as he was a DCI I found it jarring that he was actively investigating the murder, making house to house enquiries and interviewing suspects.
This book is unique enough to stand out from the crowd but I do wonder whether setting it a bit in the future might have broadened the appeal and given it more believability.

I received an ARC of Yesterday via NetGalley and my thanks to the publisher for that.

users.query: This was a present for my 9-year-old granddaughter.  I wasn't sure she would be able to control it, but it turns out she learned quickly. This is partly a result of it's slow flight, but also from it's ability to glide when the power is off.  The one shortcoming I would mention is that the charging arrangement, in which you stick the bird's belly on a small protrusion on the remote control, is difficult to master because the port in the bird (which also contains the on-off switch) doesn't "click" or snap firmly into the charger, but just rests on it.
