In spite of great difficulty in getting it to work, I rate this product 5 stars because it DOES work and it solves a problem.  I got it because the Amazon Echo now offers voice control over switches like this one which show up as devices connected to your home's wifi.  With the device I hoped to be able to turn a light in our living room on or off, making it easier for an elderly person to control it.

First problem:  I need the WeMo app.  Not available on the Belkin web site.  I suppose more experienced users would have gone to Google Play for the android app first, but it didn't occur to me for a while.

Second problem: The app on my Android phone said it was installed but it couldn't find the Belkin WeMo Insight Switch.  Lots of plugging and unplugging, uninstalling and reinstalling, and finally it found the switch.  The light that it controlled could be turned on and off by the manual button on the Insight Switch and by the app on my phone.

Third problem:  "Alexa," the Amazon Echo device, could not find the device when I said, "Alexa, discover my devices," as Amazon's instructions specified.  Again I tried unplugging, replugging, deleting the app, reinstalling the app, and finally, just when I was prepared to return the device, the Amazon Echo said it had found the device.  I'm not sure exactly what combination of bumbling finally worked, so I hope I won't have to do it again.

The Belkin web site was not particularly helpful for this problem, and I couldn't find anything on Amazon that was helpful.

But now it works.  We can turn a light in our living room on or off by voice.  I feel as if I have won a great victory.

Impressive climbing capability.  Rugged.  My 11-year-old granddaughter put it to the test and it passed with flying colors. I thought it would be slow in order to provide torque for rock climbing, but it is fairly quick.

It doesn't work.  It wouldn't charge (nothing lit up), though the car charger indicated it was receiving power.  And it wouldn't pair with my Bluetooth phone.  This device is similar in appearance to the Supertooth Buddy (http://www.amazon.com/SuperTooth-Buddy-Bluetooth-Visor-Speakerphone/dp/B0044DEAUA/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1415233093&sr=8-1&keywords=SuperTooth+Buddy+Bluetooth+Visor+Speakerphone+Car+kit+-+Black) that sells on Amazon for about $35 as of November 5, 2014.  That device has received better scores on Amazon.

It just works.  I suppose I shouldn't be amazed at that, but lately I've bought some electronic items that were disappointing, or that required a lot of effort to get them to work properly.  This gadget pulls the audio from an HDMI stream so that you can feed it to a home sound system.  I plugged it in, it worked, and it sounds good.  I'm happy.

I wanted lights that could be set to the off position in darkness, to be lit only when they detected people moving near them (PIR detection).  These lights can do that.  The switch is inside the battery compartment.  That is somewhat inconvenient if you need to change the setting frequently, but on the other hand it would slow down someone trying to defeat the lights quietly.  I've mounted the lights near external video cameras, in the hope that a useful image may be captured and perhaps the presence of the lights and the video cameras will frighten the bad guys away.

The lights are very bright.  The solar cells do a good job of keeping the lithium batteries up, which is not really very difficult since they would illuminate for only 30 seconds on the rare occasions when they are tripped.  The batteries are larger than the conventional AA size.  They operate in parallel, so theoretically you could run the lights on only one battery -- but you don't need to.  Each light comes with two batteries.

The only downside I can think of is that the lights are somewhat more expensive than others that appear similar.  But having ordered cheaper ones the first time, I have come to appreciate the size, brightness, and quality of these lights.

Construction seems solid.  The mounting hardware is adequate.  They provide a template for drilling holes to install mounting screws.

This review is by a genuine buyer -- no free samples, and no reward for a good review.

Update 02/26/15
One of the lights quit last week.  Good batteries, but no way to make it light up.  I contacted the seller and 3 days later received a free replacement that works perfectly.  I'm about to order two more lights to give my house increased coverage.
This was a gag gift for my grandson who just bought his first car.  It served it's purpose.

It works well but the setup was not easy.  I had 3 sets of instructions.  There was the instruction booklet that came with the device, there was an email from the seller with a different set of instructions, and there was a reviewer on this site (initials JC) who offered yet a third set.  I tried each one.  The instruction booklet was difficult to understand and I was unable to complete the setup.  The emailed instructions were better but the instructions were difficult to follow because the web site that it told me to access with my phone didn't correspond exactly to what the instructions said and because my phone is set to capitalize the first letter of the first word of a sentence, but the username, "admin" had to be all lower case (it took me a while to figure that out).  The reviewer's instructions were the ones that finally worked.  Then my primary router said that there was a "router behind the router" issue but fortunately it offered to resolve the problem and did so after I rebooted the extender.

This charger can handle a large assortment of batteries, even two different sizes at one time because it has independent circuits.  It also senses the kind of battery being charged, lithium, NiMH, or NiCad, and provides an appropriate voltage and current.  The construction seems solid.  The charge indicator is a bit crude -- three levels of flashing LED's, with full charge shown by all three levels lit -- but it serves the purpose.

Each charger comes with two "D" cell battery shells, so that the batteries can be installed in an application that would otherwise use "D" cells.  But I'm not aware of a lot of places where a 3.6- or 3.7-volt battery of the "D" configuration are in fact used outside utilities or the military.  You certainly couldn't just slide them into an old 2-"D"-cell flashlight with a tungsten-filament bulb that is expecting 3 volts (and in this case receiving 7.4 volts).

This review is by a genuine buyer, no free samples and no reward for a good review.

I never intentionally use the extra buttons they put on mice, though I do press them accidentally from time to time.  This one doesn't have them.  Left, right, and wheel.  Nice and simple.  Also, the mouse moves smoothly with little resistance on the mouse pad. One minor problem -- the AA battery has to be forced to get it into the battery compartment, the opening of which seems to be 0.1 mm too small.  It may prove difficult to remove when the time comes.  But that doesn't prevent it from earning 5 stars.  I am a real buyer and I do not accept free samples for any reason.

The LCD characters are highly legible and the design is innovative.  Unlike some other reviewers I found the setup to be reasonably simple.  It comes with instructions, but I didn't read them.

Update June 2013:  It still works, but I've noticed that it runs fast, about 2-3 minutes a month.  I've taken my review down from 5 stars to 3 for that reason.  Digital clocks should do better than that.

The idea of an emergency tool with the ability to break a car window and cut a seatbelt when necessary seems like a good idea.  But this device is quite bulky and after carrying it in my pocket for a week I gave up.  The "siren" mode is loud enough to be annoying but not loud enough to be useful.  The flashlight and red blinker can be turned on easily by accident -- it takes just the lightest touch on a button.  After the week it spent in my pocket the battery was dead.

I can't say whether the window tool works because it is one of those things that you really can't test.  The tempered glass in car side windows and the laminated glass in windshields are expensive and inconvenient to replace, and testing it on ordinary window glass wouldn't tell you how it would perform in a car.  I have not been able to test the air pressure guage because the battery went dead.  Similarly, I have not tried to cut a seatbelt.  But my rating of the product at two stars is not based on my inability to test these features.  It is based on it's bulk and the fact that I could not rely on the battery to be working when needed.
The photo in the description is small.  I didn't notice that there are no buttons to control the Dish Network DVR.  This controller is useless to me.
It is hard to beat Logitech when it comes to the mouse.  The wireless range is good, resolution is faultless, and the colorful design alleviates a little of the drudgery of some computer tasks.

The author takes you into the mind of a dog quite convincingly.  This is a police story, with suitable twists, all of which are quite readable.  But the personality of the dog comes alive.  I'm looking forward to reading more books in this line.
It seems very competent.  It handles whatever I give it with no fuss.  Quiet.  I like being able to shred optical disks and credit cards into tiny pieces.

This book is part of the "Phoenix" universe.  In the book the author raises interesting issues of just exactly what is consciousness (as opposed to sentience) and what goes into the make-up of an individual person.  The characters left me thinking about the choices they made for some time after reading the book.
The football appears to be of good quality, but I'm not an expert.  My grandson is.  He loves it.  He says the grip is just right.

My wife wanted an MP3 player to use when walking so that she could listen to podcasts of "Wait Wait Don't Tell Me," and other NPR programs.  We tried a 1-gig iPod Shuffle, but it refused to 'sync'  with the iTunes software, and wouldn't work at all even after 3 hours of trying updates and restarts.  I was also irritated that I had to read the instructions just to find the 'on-off' switch.  We returned it to Amazon and bought a Sansa 2-gig player, a red one, for the same price as the Shuffle.  We chose the Sansa because some of the reader comments about the Shuffle had mentioned it as a viable alternative.  It is not much bigger (it uses the extra space for a screen that helps you navigate to the files you want) and it has a clip like the Shuffle.  The big difference -- it worked right out of the box.  It takes no more skill to put MP3s on it than than the drag and drop function in Windows.  My wife is now using it with no problems.

I bought three of these black-encased NP-20 batteries as spares for my grandchildren's three Casio EX-S600 cameras.  Their electrical performance appears to be fine, but once inserted into the cameras they cannot be removed by ordinary means.  I had to use a knife and a pair of pliers to get them out.  The two OEM batteries and one different brand of aftermarket battery with a white cover and a blue band at the bottom just pop out.  The seller has offered to refund my purchase price but not the shipping charges -- so my refund would be less than the cost of sending them back.  Clever marketing, lousy product.

06-17-09 update.  Two months after the purchase I received an email from the company.  In what may be a change of policy, they offered to refund the original shipping charge as well as the purchase cost.  I informed them that I no longer have the batteries because they were of no use to me, so I can't return them.  They then offered to refund the shipping cost and have since done so.  If this is something all buyers can rely on, I would change my rating to 4 stars.  Still not 5 -- that would be reserved for getting it right the first time -- but a full refund for defective or mislabeled merchandise is a good policy.
She uses it to carry her ice skates to lessons each week.  There is ample room for both skates and a few other small items.

It works well, but it took a while to catch on to how to program it.  You have to press "yes" after each command in order for it to remember.  My old Honeywell thermostat was more intuitive.  But considering the price and the fact that it works perfectly, I gave it 5 stars.

users.query: It just works-- I've had no problem with this battery.

cands.text: Works fine.  Purchased to upgrade a new Dell notebook PC.
I needed a spare charger for my X100T so this fit the bill just nicely.  I've not given it a full test, but it charges my batteries just fine and having the spare batteries is a bonus

I have the same product for my iPhone 6S Plus.

It works as advertised.  Like other glass screen protectors I've used, it will exhibit small chips over time, but it's not an issue and you'll have piece of mind knowing you've got a back up.

One of the reasons why I live this product the most (other than its value prop), is the plastic protector has tabs at either end to help align the protector as you apply it to the phone.  This is much like Zagg's offering, for far less money.  As a suggestion to the manufacturer, I'd suggest tinting the color of that plastic to help with the visual alignment.

The best tips I can give anyone trying to apply this screen protector:
1) Make sure the screen is dust and smudge free.  Use the included wipes and dust free lens cloth if you have one.  A little canned air will help.
2) Take your time applying this screen protector-- it will ensure you're getting the best protection and overall experience.
Works as advertised, though I've deducted a star because of the price.

I bought this for a desktop PC whose NIC was showing signs of failure.  I'd considered a replacement card, but this cost just as much so I opted for a cleaner wireless solution.

Set up was pretty straight forward.  It includes clear directions and a driver CD to get you going in minutes.  Once set up, the little dongle found my ASUS RT-AC66U and I was good to go.

Something I did notice was the throughput speed is not as fast as my other connected devices.  I have a 50 down/5 Mbs up Internet service and would experience that with my iPhone for example but I'm seeing more along of line of 44Mbs-45Mbs down / 5Mbs up with this wireless adapter. I think that's a function of the smallish antennas and some possible interference.  Not a deal breaker, but something of note.
Memory upgrade for a Dell Optiplex 3020M.  Works as advertised and much cheaper than the Dell branded option.

I went with this bundle over the very popular FitBit Charge HR for the following reasons:

1) No charging necessary, long battery life due to coin cell battery
2) Time is always on, making it much easier to get at a glance times like a normal watch
3) WATERPROOF... no need to take it offer in the shower, pool, beach, etc.
4) The HRM chest strap gives a more accurate reading than the optical sensor found on the Charge HR (or Apple watch)
5) Priced better.  Not knowing how "committed" I was to the whole activity tracking thing, the price for this was low enough for me to jump in without feeling like I wasn't getting enough value from it.

All in all, this has been a good product.  I suspect the step counter isn't extremely accurate, but psychologically having this on keeps me in the mind set of moving.

I'm not a huge fan of the app for many of the same reasons other reviewers have stated.  I also find it a bit finicky when it comes to syncing my heart rate data after an activity...sometimes it will sync, other times nothing.  That's a bit annoying and I hope that a future software update addresses that.  It syncs up fine with my Withings scale and the MyFitnessPal app.

Having to strap on a HRM vs. an optical HRM is a bit of an annoyance since I can't get constant monitoring of my HR and there's just one more piece of equipment I have to worry about.

For the few trade offs I made going with the Garmin over the FitBit, I'm still pleased with this product.  It does the basics very well and I really enjoy the fact that I can just put it on and not having to worry about getting it wet or charging it.

I won't rattle on with what others have said about this notebook, but I will say this is one of the best notebooks you can buy today.  The only notebook that I would compare this to in terms of specs and design would be the Dell Precision M3800.

This replaced a Mid-2009 13" Macbook Pro and I was blown away with the retina display.  I'm an amateur photographer and I was amazed with how crisp and 3-dimensional photos look on this display compared to my old notebook and 24" Dell Ultrasharp monitor.

I opted for this model rather than the entry 15" because of the 16GB RAM standard and discrete graphics. I wanted to get the most machine I could afford since I plan on keeping this for several more years like my last machine.  I think after the launch of the Broadwell chipped Macs next year, the gap between integrated and discrete graphics will be so narrow to the point of being imperceptible in most applications.

** March 2016 Update **

The headphones are still going strong.  Battery life is excellent.  I use them for a couple hours every night and I don't worry about charging them for a few weeks at a time.  The battery life indicator on iOS 9 devices is a really nice feature to monitor that.

One of my original concerns was about the comfort.  I have a  7 1/4" hat size head and I found the fit to be a tad tight with the usual heat build up on the ears after a short time.  I'm happy to report that after a proper "break in" period, the fit a far more comfortable and I can keep these on my head for much longer with little to no discomfort.

At this point, the biggest knock against these for me is the lack of folding capability for better transport.  But at this price the sound quality, fit, and other stand-out features still make this a great buy.  I can easily recommend these to anyone looking for a relatively compact set of wireless headphones that doesn't try to call attention to itself.

*** Original Review ***

I'd originally considered the Bose Soundlink line, but that $250+ price gave me pause every time.  While doing some research online, the Move wireless kept coming up as highly recommended.  Anyone looking to spend under $100 for a pair of bluetooth wireless headphones should add the Jabra Move to their short list.

The sound quality of these headphones exceed their price point which was very surprising.  There are certainly better sounding headphones, but you'll probably be paying much more for it.  I listen to a lot of bass heavy music and I felt like the Jabra could keep up without sounding too muddy/sloppy and drowning out the mids (vocals) and highs.  I think Jabra did a great job of dialing in the sound signature of the headphones to cover a wide spectrum of music genres.

Fit is secure, though my ears felt somewhat sore after some time due to the pressure of the ear pads.  I "flexed" the headband out just a touch to relieve some of that pressure and that seemed to solve that issue.

Likes:
+ Lightweight, comfortable to wear for moderately long wear
+ Reasonable sound isolation
+ Solid bluetooth connection
+ Excellent sound (tight bass and nice highs without sacrificing mids)
+ Good battery life
+ Includes 3.5mm audio cable for wired use

No Likes:
- Don't fold up compact
- Included audio cable lacks mic/music controls
- no active noise cancellation
- no case included

I can't speak for the issues with the ear cup quality, but will update this review if I experience any issues.

Recently upgraded a 250GB notebook HDD with this.  I initially considered the very popular Samsung EVO line, but just happened to see a great review on CNET for this Transcend line.  Given the review and competitive price, I went for it.

I cloned a 250GB HDD onto this in about 16 minutes and then used a USB 3.0 stick to transfer the user files via Windows easy transfer program.  I haven't tested it yet, but I'd full expect the read write times to meet or exceed the advertised specs.

So far, the drive is rock solid and really given the notebook a wonderful performance boost.

The Fitbit Charge (HR) is probably the most popular and talked about wearable on the market at the moment with a great mobile app to boot (all of which are justified), however this was an activity tracker that I just didn't get excited about.  The battery life and to a lesser degree, lack of waterproofing had me looking elsewhere for a tracker.

I purchased the Garmin Vivofit 2 because it offered a lot of features for the money (comparable to Fitbit) along with a long lasting battery, waterproof, and compatible with ANT+ HRM chest strap but I just wasn't in love with it or found that it was really all that nice looking.

Ultimately, I sold it for the Activite Pop.  The Activite and Activite Pop are watches first with additional features for tracking basic activity.  For the type of lifestyle I lead, this really meets all my expectations.  I'm not a fitness fanatic, but I have become more aware of my daily activities and being able to track my progress through the Withings app is perfect for me.  I also have the Smart Body Analyzer which syncs flawlessly with the app to give me a pretty good overall basic picture of my health and a means of tracking my progress.

I would like to see more functionality built in via the app with future updates for further customizability and editing automatically detected activities.

At $149 list, there are plenty of activity trackers out there with far more features that this price band.  However, statistics have shown the level of activity for consumers of these wearables drops considerably (to non-existent) after about a couple months.  If I end up falling into this statistic, at least I'll have a decent looking water resistant watch with excellent battery life that I can wear without worrying about the other features I may or may not use again.

If you can find a gently used model, you can save yourself a bit more money which makes this watch an even better value.

/// July 2016 Update ///

So, I tried editing some photos in Adobe Lightroom only to discover that images were not rendering in the Develop mode.  When I plug the notebook directly into the monitor, I get no issues.  Clearly the driver issues haven't been worked out yet for MacOS.

I deducted 1 star for the issue and hope that it gets resolved ASAP.

/// June 2016 Update ///

The audio issue was fixed.  I needed to change the audio from computer to USB Audio in settings.  Now the sound plays through the speakers.

////  Original Review ///

Please make sure you have the latest DisplayLink drivers for MacOS.

I use this dock with a 2014 MacBook Pro 15-inch (running OS X El Capitan) and 2 - Dell U2515H monitors.  The monitors have a native resolution of 2560x1440 and the only way to make that work with this dock is using the DisplayPort along with one of the HDMI ports.  It will not support that resolution with both HDMI outs plugged in.

I've only had the dock a week, but have noticed some scaling issues when activating Mission Control.  The top menu (that displays the desktops) is slight clipped.  Not a deal breaker, but i hope this gets resolved with a future software update.

There is also a noticeable flickering that happens with certain video/animation playback.  Before I upgraded the drivers, YouTube was almost unwatchable, especially at full screen.  That's fixed (installed driver ver 2.5.1), however when I run the iOS simulator (building iOS apps), the simulator screen with flicker when I'm switching views on an app.  I may try to re-install the drivers to see if that resolved the issues I mentioned above.

Performance issues aside, the dock works for my needs.  I could go back to just plugging the notebook up directly to the monitors w/ the Thunderbolt 2 ports, but this dock will be used w/ a PC laptop so it will do double duty.

I will provide updates if more problems arise or the issues I have get resolved.

users.query:
Things are not what they appear.

This story is a perfect blend of mystery and paranormal. The setting was the perfect backdrop to this hauntingly beautiful story. I was drawn in to the story from the first page and was constantly surprised. Just as I thought I knew what or who was behind everything something happened to throw me off. The author did a great job of giving small hints and clues throughout the story without giving away the entire mystery.

The romance was sweet and not too overdone. There was just enough to keep me interested without completely taking over the story. I also liked how it gradually built throughout the story instead of just being thrown out there. The characters weren't instantly in love instead they slowly came to know one another and became friends. I can't wait to see how their relationship progresses in the rest of the series.

Chira is an outcast and is not used to hanging around anyone other than her best friend Tasha. That is until she strikes up a a small friendship with the new boy Ben. She is a smart, loyal, and brave young woman that I enjoyed getting to know. I also liked seeing the growth in her character throughout the book. She started out as a bit of a loner, throwing up guards to keep people out. However by the end she had finally ventured out and gained friendships that she had never thought would happen.

Ben is an unusual, but very intriguing boy who has a very kind heart. He is very sweet and a bit shy, but once you get to know him he can be very charming. I enjoyed the banter between him and Chira they really knew how to make each other smile even when they were teasing each other. Ben also has a dark secret one that he doesn't like to talk about, but even so he does his best to try to protect people. He is a bit misunderstood, but it was so easy to fall in love with his adorable self.

Matt is Ben's cousin and the last to join their little group. It was a bit tense with him and Chira at first, but with his carefree attitude and easy jokes it's hard not to smile around Matt. We don't get yo see as much about Matt In this book, but I do hope to see more about him in future ones.

This is an exciting start to a promising new series and I highly recommend it to fans of mystery, suspense, and the paranormal!

cands.text: Mixed with mystery, paranormal abilities, and some steamy romance Anchor is definitely a lovely read. Right from the start I was caught up in the mystery and suspense wondering who the wolf that she had to save was. The heroine had a rough life because of her ability. Even after all the trouble her ability causes she still tries to do all she can to help others using this ability. Will Angus be the one to finally except her for who she is and will she be able to help her new found friends find the unknown woman from her visions before she is killed? You will have to read it to find out.

A short, but very sweet I really enjoyed reading this book and the characters were really kind to each other. It was a nice change of pace from the usual heroines who are taken on a journey of some sorts that is filled with near deaths and terrifying encounters (not that I don't love those). Not to say that the characters didn't have any problems, but for the most they had a very romantic meeting with only a small obstacle that they have to take care of. All in all it was a nice read especially since it is free.

Who would have thought finding your soul mate would be the easy part.
This was a suspenseful new novel that will leave you hungry for more. The imagery was perfect and helped to set the mood for the entire story. It was a very easy story to get lost in and I can't wait to see the rest of the series.
It's tough going through high school and discovering who you are, but things get a lot worse when you are a newbie witch. I liked Emma as a character and really got attached to her by the end of the story. Even though she has powers some might envy she still deals with many of the same situations other teenagers do and learns from those experiences.
I highly recommend this spellbinding read fans of paranormal romance.

This is an amazing series that has a lot of depth and emotion both in the characters and the storyline. I was a bit unsure of this at first, but after the first chapter was quickly drawn in. The story is a bit slow at first, but has enough intrigue and action to keep me at the edge of my seat.

By far the best part of this series is the relationships between the three main characters Nakaba, Loki, and Caesar. They each have their own unique personality and many times they clash with each other, but little by little we see some of the softer sides of them and how even when they absolutely hate each other they are able to bring out the best of each other.

Nakaba is calm and generally level headed, but her fiery temper comes to the forefront whenever someone threatens Loki. Nakaba and Loki do not have a romantic relationship, but their love for one another clearly shows through. Loki would give his life for Nakaba and she in turn would do the same. Although I love these two I did like seeing them coming to trust others a little more as the series went on. It showed how much they had grown.

On a side note I am secretly hoping that maybe just maybe there will be something between Nakaba and Loki in the future, but so far no good.

Caesar definitely has one of the bigger personalities in the book. He is obnoxious, arrogant, rude, insensitive, and yet at the strangest moments a softer side of him is shown. I think out of all of the characters he has grown the most. Though it happens gradually he does seem to show more of his true self as the series progresses. I liked this character because of how interesting and unique he was. He may not be someone I would be friends with in real life, but he definitely brings makes things livelier wherever he goes.

I cannot wait to read more of this series and highly recommend this to all shojo fans!

The book is full of passion, anger, turmoil, and characters with real life problems. It is sure to have you thinking about the story and its characters long after you turn the last page. The story line was well thought out and beautifully executed with memorable imagery and characters. I couldn't put it down and I only wish that the story could have been longer.

Julianna was my favorite and I really liked how well defined all of the characters were. They were real and had problems that many of us can relate to. I also liked seeing the growth in these characters throughout the story.
This is a story about finding yourself and learning to love the real you. There isn't always a happy ending in real life, but you never know what you can accomplish until you try.

For an amazing story that will take you on a roller coaster ride of emotions check out Slum Roots!

This is a unique and spellbinding twist on a classic tale that romance lovers are sure to enjoy.
The setting was interesting and there was a lot of descriptive imagery. I liked how the setting helped the readers to get into the moods of the story.
Tara is a bright and kind woman who has a knack for weaving tales. I highly enjoyed reading about her and discovering more about her and the other characters as well.
Rolph is mysterious and a bit of a storyteller himself. I liked his character a lot and enjoyed seeing how his relationship with Tara developed throughout this novella.
I highly recommend this story to anyone who loves the tale of Beauty and the Beast!

Full of intrigue and tons of action this is an exciting story that will leave you wanting more. The author is very talented and keeps readers on their toes in this suspenseful thriller. The imagery was great and helped to make me feel like I was there. The characters had actual depth and seemed real. I highly recommend this to lovers of suspenseful thrillers!

A beautiful love story of passion and love, curses and family secrets.

With beautiful descriptions and exotic locations the author weaves a heart wrenching tale of love and revenge. The author does a wonderful job of setting the tone of the book and showing the growing love between the characters as well as the hurt and betrayal that is felt.

This story led me on an emotional roller coaster and I loved every minute of it. It was hard to put down as there was so much going on between all of the different characters I had to know what would happen next.

The romance was beautifully done and not over the top. The characters were real and had their own problems and failings that they had to deal with before they got their happy ending. I loved the build up to the romance and how the different feelings both good and bad were explored throughout the story.

Luz was a strong heroine who was used to taking care of herself, but she wasn't afraid of strong feelings. I loved her inquisitive nature and that she didn't let anyone stand in her way of finding out the truth. Her relationship with both Leandro and Andres was intense and full of twists and turns. It was easy to get involved with the mystery of these two men and see how Luz could be torn about the two.

This was an intense romance with a good dose of mystery that I would highly recommend.

This book was very well written and in my opinion explored some of the inner relationships we have with our family members, although in a more brutal atmosphere, especially Bryn's relationship with her adoptive father Callum. Despite this though or maybe because of this I would only give this book a 4 out of 5 rating. I really liked the main character bryn and even her best friend Devon (he was my favorite), but I really hated Callum. The way he treated Bryn really bugged me, but other than that it was a great story. Don't take my word for it though give it a try.

Two very different people with one dangerous goal.

The setting was exciting and mysterious starting out on the streets of a society filled with secrets, danger, and one cheeky girl who is navigating it all. This was a fast paced story filled with a whole lot of action and a good sprinkling of mystery to top it off.

Kyra is a no nonsense kind of girl. She grew up having to be tough and its taken its toll. She does what she has to in order to survive, but still helps those in need whenever possible. I liked her gutsy attitude and the her confidence in her abilities. Kyra was such a fun character to get to know and I didn't want her story to end.

Tristam was a mystery in the beginning, but the more we learned about him the more it was obvious that he and Kyra were very much alike. He was devious, but would do whatever it took to protect his friends. He was not very trustful, but getting to see these two learn to appreciate and trust one another was an adventure all in itself.

For those looking for a thrilling action packed story this is the story for you!

From suspect to lover these P.I.'s know how to crack a case!

A good dose of mystery and intrigue topped with a sweet romance, this book is a real treat! I really enjoyed the action and suspense in this story. I also liked being able to figure out the mystery right along with Val. We are given just enough information throughout the book to keep us interested, but without giving it all away at the beginning.

The romance was well done and nicely paced. These two were able to get to know each other and we were able to see the sparks fly even when they were fighting their attraction. The amount of chemistry these two have is amazing. I loved seeing them interact with one another and really believed that they were a good fit.

Val is a quirky ad determined intern who is very easy to get along with. She does have a stubborn side though, as Leroy comes to see. She was a fun character and I had a great time getting to know her.

Leroy is a great detective, but he does have a bit of a past. He is loyal and determined, especially when it comes to Val. He could be a bit gruff at times, but I loved his character all the same. Almost as much as Val.

For a fun romance mixed with a great mystery check out "Sleepless in Las Vegas"!

All she wanted was a normal life, but fate had other plans.
I love this series. The setting is beautiful and all of the characters so unique. None of them are perfect, but they do the best they can with what they've got. This story is just plain fun and addicting. The lead character isn't overly cheerful and in fact is pretty average if it wasn't for her unusual ability to see spirits. Misao is a girl who has always longed for a normal life with her loved ones, but she doesn't get depressed and weepy. Instead she does her best to bear it and tries to rely on her own ability to gain happiness. She does falter at times, but I love that she isn't perfect and can have a bit of a selfish side to her. It shows that she is human. I love the dynamic between her and Kyo they are so great together. Even though Misao can be a bit nave when it comes to Kyo she doesn't let him push her around.
Kyo is a sweet guy, but he does have a tendency to love to tease Misao. I find it nice that although he wants to protect her he doesn't treat her like she is a china doll that could easily break. He tells her straight out what's going on and allows her to make her own decisions.
Aside from all the seriousness the story is full of hilarious antics that the characters get into and had me cracking up a lot. It gave us a nice relief so it wasn't overly serious. I can't wait to see what else is in store for Misao and Kyo.

A beautiful coming of age story about a young witch who just wants to be normal. Like many of us at her age Sydlynn Hayle struggles with all the problems and drama that high school can bring. As well as dealing with her attraction to football hero Brad and mysterious Quaid.

I loved this book and thought that it brought a magical yet relatable tale to life that many people will enjoy. Sydlynn is a great character and I liked reading her story and loved her "voice". Her secondary characters were really well written too. As far as the boys go I have to say that I tended to lean more towards Quaid, but that is just my opinion. Decide for yourself and check out this great novel!

Love has never been more dangerous.

This is a thrilling new romance that will leave you breathless. The impeccable writing and unforgettable characters kept me hooked from page 1. I couldn't have asked for a better paranormal romance than this. The storyline is unique and was filled with plenty of twists and turns along the way that kept me on the edge of my seat.

I was so immersed in this story that I pulled an all nighter just to finish it. I had lots of fun figuring out the mystery of the flesh eaters along with Pheonix. There were plenty of times that had me really worried about Phoenix's fate as well as times where I was mentally kicking Phoenix for some of her decisions. All in all it was a roller coaster ride of emotions and I loved every minute of it.

I couldn't help, but love these characters. Phoenix was a brave and kindhearted girl who I could definitely see myself being best friends with.

Demitri was my personal favorite character. He was a bit gruff at first, but after getting to know more about him it was plain to see he had a kind heart. He was a compelling character that I loved getting to know.

Luka was the more flirtatious and playful type and definitely an interesting character. He was fun and I had a great time reading about his interactions with Pheonix.

This is a dark and compelling new romance that paranormal fans won't want to miss out on.

Family secrets can be deadly.

I loved the suspense and mystery packed into this story. There were a lot of twists and turns that kept me guessing. The romance was nice and set at a decent pace with no insta love. I really liked the different aspects of this story and the paranormal elements really made the story that much darker.

Eila was a strong heroine with attitude. I loved her sassy nature and that she didn't let others walk all over her. She really held her own even when things started to get messy. Her relationship with Raef was interesting, sweet, and at times funny. There interactions were never boring and I enjoyed seeing Raef getting under her skin even though he could be annoying.

Raef is very protective, strong, and determined. He has lots of secrets and at first is hard to understand, but he has a reason for everything he does. He is kind and loyal to those he loves. I can't wait to see where he and Eila go in the future.

This is one paranormal romance you won't want to miss!

Fantasy and romance collide in an epic new adventure.

I really liked the use of Celtic mythology in the story. Very well written and a good amount of mystery and romance together. The different creatures we met both dangerous and beautiful were intriguing. The book is a bit slow paced, but it uses a lot of the first half for world building and setting a foundation for the characters relationship.

The romance was believable and very sweet. There was a lot of build up for their relationship which was nice because they got to know one another and didn't jump into anything. There were a lot of issues that needed to be worked through by both parties and I enjoyed the character growth.

Meghan is a used to being different, but even she believed a world where she was being pursued by creatures such as goblins and gnomes was too much. She definitely had a lot of adjusting to do, but she took everything in stride. She tended to be a bit impulsive as a character. This got her into a ton of trouble. Luckily Cade was there to bail her out.

Cade is a strange man from another realm, come to warn Meghan about who she really is. He was extremely closed lipped about many things, but was really sweet and a noble character. Cade is definitely not one to break rules, but where Meghan is concerned things never go as planned. Cade was fun character to get to know and I can't wait to read more about him in later books.

For fans of mythology and romance this is the book for you!

An exciting adventure that you won't be able to put down! The story had me riveted from the very beginning with the beautiful imagery and charismatic characters. There was always a bit of mystery shrouding the characters in the beginning and I had a great time figuring everyone out. The mystery and action were well done and had me on the edge of my seat in anticipation of the next turn of the page.

Dawn is a strong and courageous girl who I really admired. She had some tough decision to deal with in the course of the book and even when she wasn't sure of herself she still kept on going, which took a lot of courage. I also really liked that no matter what bad things were thrown at her she never really lost her sweetness. She was still a kind and caring woman who would do anything to help those she loved.

I also liked how the villains of the story weren't just plain evil for no reason. They had depth to them and their actions weren't always strictly black and white. It mad the story that much more interesting.

Ryan is a sweet man and I adored him. He wasn't always sure of himself, but he did his best to be good and help Dawn.

The romance was sweet and not rushed at all. I really liked how the romance developed slowly and how these two characters interacted with one another. I hope to see more of them in future books.

For an exciting and romantic adventure check out Sunkissed by Carys Jones!

Out of this world romance!

The author really knows how to keep up the tension and suspense with this action packed romance. I loved the bit of sleuthing and slow build up of the mystery. There is a lot to learn about these characters and we are given just enough to wet our appetite without giving away too much all at once.

Sloane is now one of my favorite heroines. She his spunky, smart, and can take a hit and give it back twofold. I love tough heroines and she had the brains and beauty to go along with it. I also liked that she didn't take anything for granted and really dug into the mystery that was unfolding before her. She also didn't let anybody push her around nobody.

Hayden was a total hunk and even more he was a brainiac. Two of the best combinations smart and hot. He could be bit moody, but considering his situation it was understandable. I liked that he tried to do what was right even if it didn't always turn out exactly right.

The Romance was nicely paced and I always did like the enemies to lovers thing. These two definitely got on each others nerves, but the spark was also there.

So if you are looking for a tough heroine and a well done alien romance check out "Lost in Starlight". I highly recommend this action packed adventure!

This story is a provocative tearjerker that I couldn't put down
Alexis is forced to deal with losing her family at a young age and even worse she has to deal with a mystery that could get her killed. I liked how much this character grew in the story she was really brave and went through things that no one should ever have to experience, but she came out of it a better person.  There was so much emotion evoked from this book and I could really relate to the character's need for independence in the beginning. So when she found her family missing after so much time apart I almost began to cry myself. It is a horrible thing to lose one's family and this book really captures the heart of a family and how precious they are.
Gabriel was a solid character with a lot of depth to him. It was nice to learn about him along with Alexis and come to understand him and his situation a bit more. I was really angry with him toward the end, but overall he was a great character.
The story itself was beautiful and heart wrenching at times with somewhat of a bittersweet ending. There was some happiness for Alexis whom I was glad for and I believe the story really makes you stop and think about the ones you love and to maybe not take them for granted because one day they may not be there.

I highly recommend this  story to anyone who loves a great provocative story with a bit of romance and I also recommend keeping a box of tissues close by because this will definitely bring some tears.

The Prince of Wolves was a fantastic read filled with action and plenty of romance. Jacque's two friends Sally and Jen are the wackiest couple of best friends I have ever read about. Even in some of the more serious scenes of the book they manage to bring a smile to everyone's face. Fast paced this book never gets dull and the heroine Jacque is extremely entertaining. Her reaction to the unusual situation she finds herself is disbelief and a little denial at first, but she soon learns to cope if not entirely accept all the new changes in her life. She is a strong character though and didn't crawl in a corner and cry when something was too much (there were a couple of fits thrown though).  Our hero Fane was very supportive and really cared for Jacque, not to mention drop dead sexy and Romanian.  Their relationship was a little fast because of the situation, but sweet and romantic at the same time.
For a lovely read with plenty of action and romance check out Quinn Loftis' Prince of Wolves!

Goblins don't get any sexier than this!

I picked this book up because of my love of the old 80's movie "Labyrinth". The promise of a sexy Goblin King and an epic adventure in a magical land was just too good to resist.

Delving into the story itself there was most definitely an irresistible yet aggravating Goblin King. There was also a lost brother to save, however the similarities to the old film ended there. Chloe Jacobs has created a whole new world of creatures and with a whole new set of rules to live by. The world of Mylena is full of dangerous creatures and even the weather is trying to kill the residents of this crazy place. The world building was wonderful and descriptive. It was only too easy to get lost in this world.

The story was fast paced and dived right into the action from page one. This was one of my favorite aspects of this book. There was not time wasted getting right into the thick of things and not once did things drag on or slow down.

Greta was a great heroine. She is compassionate, brave, and confident in her abilities. My favorite part about her, though, was that she wasn't perfect and she acknowledged this. She wasn't always the selfless warrior and made a lot of mistakes, but she learned from them and in the end she took responsibility for her actions. Her loyalty to those she cared about was unbreakable even in the face of her own wants and needs.

Isaac was arrogant, stubborn, and loyal. Isaac has some serious secrets, but his loyalty to his people and especially to Greta knows no bounds. He knows Greta's secret, but will go to any lengths to keep her safe. Isaac is often very gruff and mysterious, but when he is with Greta he often lets his guard down and his devotion is quite obvious. He has his own people to worry about and responsibilities he must deal with. He is a true leader and does what is necessary to keep those in his charge happy and safe. He also loves to provoke Greta and the back and forth between these two was always amusing.

I only wish there was more time between Isaac and Greta and for their relationship to progress, but I cannot wait to see more of these two and the rest of Mylena in the next book.

Faeries and Gnomes and Goblins, Oh My!

Perilous Light is action packed and full of twists and turns that will rival the previous book. In this book we finally get to see more of my favorite couple Charlotte and Calvin, but we also find out that there are still a lot of surprises left for Charlotte and her brother on their journey. Charlotte has done a lot of growing up in the past year, but she faces even bigger trials that will test her abilities to the limit. I highly enjoyed seeing Kevin finally meet his match in the last book and was very curious to see how or if that relationship would develop any further and I was not disappointed. While there were plenty of humorous scenes with Kevin he was also put to the test when he is sent out to find help. We get to see how Kevin adapts to the world of Energo in this book as he tries to find his way in this strange world while coping with his feelings for Samantha. Calvin is without a doubt my absolute favorite character and I must admit to having a big crush on him. I liked that we got to see a lot more about him in this book. We got to see glimpses of his character before, but we get to see into his head a lot more in this one and he really is a sweet and noble man. I highly recommend this series to anyone looking for a unique new world with great characters and a bit of romance. For anyone who is already a fan of this series you are sure to love this newest installment!

Cursed in love!

Fast paced adventure and steamy romance make this a wonderful new addition to the Brides of Kindred series. Filled with non stop action and a thrilling mystery, you won't want to miss Stavros and Charlie's story. Finally a kindred with long hair and tattoos to drool over!

I was also really excited to see more of the girls lives and Kat especially. I hope to continue to learn more about Shadow and the twins in further books.

Charlie is a take no prisoners kinda gal and teaming up with her sworn enemy is probably one of the toughest jobs she has ever had to do. I really liked this girl and her attitude, although her stubbornness with Stavros can be a bit frustrating. She is a wonderfully kind and loyal woman, but because of her past has made Stavros and those like him her enemy. The goddess works in strange ways, however, and I had a great time watching her fall hopelessly for Stavros.

Stavros is cursed, but unlike most he does no let this stop him from living life. On the contrary this makes him more determined than ever to do what he can while he can. To make the world better for everyone and make the most of his life on earth is his ultimate goal. I really respected his bravery and determination. It takes a brave man to overcome their fear and push, especially with such a crippling ability. He was just as stubborn as Charlie in the romance department, but even he cannot deny the sparks flying between them.

The romance as always was one of the best yet and was nicely paced. I love the buildup between these two and it makes it that much better when they finally come together. I also love how the world building in this series become more and more complex and interesting. There is always something new to discover in the world of the Kindred.

How can love prevail when you life has been Cursed? Read the newest book in the Kindred series to find out!

"Die for Me" by Amy Plum is a thrilling new adventure with some of the unlikeliest of heroes.
The plot was well written and gave bits and pieces of information without giving away all of its secrets too soon. I enjoyed seeing how these characters lived and how the Revenants came into being. The relationship between Vincent and Kate was sweet and grew at a decent pace giving them time to become friends and then maybe something more.
I loved that the author was very descriptive about the different locations in Paris. The imagery was very beautiful and really captured the romance and majesty of Paris.
Kate was really easy to identify with. I actually shared many of the same interests that she did, although she was a lot braver than I am. I had fun time getting to know all of these quirky characters right along with Kate.
Vincent was humble and really fun to get to know. He wasn't brooding or unhappy all the time even though he did have a lot of hardships being a Revenant. Instead he was sweet and really seemed to enjoy life no matter how bad things got.
I can't wait to read "Until I Die" and become immersed in this beautiful story once again!

Goddess Test is a dark and alluring new tale full of danger and hope.

Kate is a relatable heroin with a big heart. I really enjoyed following her on her journey and found myself just as entranced by this new world as she was.

I really liked Henry's character because I got to explore a whole new side to the character of Hades. He was a great character and I enjoyed learning more about him as the story progressed. He is definitely one of the more interesting and my favorite character from the series.

This story was full of twists and turns that had me anxiously turning each page. I highly recommend this to anyone who loves mythology with an epic love story.

Using this as the final stage filter in our APEC ROES-50 reverse osmosis system. We used the RO system without the Watts filter for about 1 week. Believe it or not, after drinking our normal coffee brewed the same way, I experienced acid reflux out of the blue. Never had acid reflux before with our unfiltered water used to brew coffee. I knew that RO systems increase the acidity of the water, but I didn't think it would actually produce symptoms! So, we added the Watts filter in hopes of raising the pH of our filtered water. No more acid reflux after drinking coffee! Water tastes nice and neutral too, a very pure taste and great mouth feel. I also tested the water using an API dropper test kit.
