I read the reviews and bought two sets for my 2013 F150 - one set for the cargo light, one for the reverse lights.  I am really happy with the purchase, recommend these.  I hope they last because they are a lot more than the stock bulbs.

The light is a major improvement from stock, not even close.  Someone else reviewed that there was not much difference, but I disagree.  The photos below were from my install.  I needed a nut driver for the tail lamps, a phillips screwdriver for the cargo lamp and then then bulbs snapped into place in the twist lock sockets.  It took me about 20-minutes.

>LED bulbs are a little longer than stock, but there was plenty clearance (see comparison photo)
>Illumination is impressive, very bright (see photo)
>Compared to stock the light is white and very bright, really cannot look directly into the light (see comparison photo)
>I felt almost no heat from the LEDs compared to the stock
>At first, I was concerned the base was too fat, but they snapped into the socket tightly
You'll remember these from your parents dresser drawer 40-years ago.  They are such good markers, sharp color and sharp lines, may they be manufactured for another 40-years..
These bulbs fit only the high beams on my GMC and it wasn't clear in the description. I think the HB4 must mean HighBeam4, but it would have been helpful if that was clear in the description.

This laptop was a good purchase when it went one sale sub $200, but it cannot replace a regular business machine or student laptop.  The Google Apps suite has a lot of growing up to do before it is anywhere close to professional, so one is limited to use this as an after hours utility.  Overall, I am happy with my purchase but this is a tertiary machine for me - just using it for hobby and travel.  If I had a choice, I would like something not 11", and not 15" - how about 13", team?

Pro
-This machine excels at replacing a tablet for watching internet flicks, chatting/hangouts; keeping up with emails on the go; or tracking a hobby.
- It would be ideal for taking notes in a classroom and not worrying too much about someone stealing it.
- Battery gives me about 5-6 hours with the screen dimmed a little.  Again, for $200, it's more than I hoped for and I'll be on to my next machine before the battery fails.
- I use this to jot notes down in docs, stream/bluetooth to the TV, and to do some webpage research.
-This is the small machine you want to fly with - battery lasts cross country, and there is less of the T-Rex tiny arms-can't open the screen-all-the-way.
-There is really no startup/shut down - just open and close the lid and it's on or off.
-Comes with 1TB Google storage (free for now...I feel the hooks digging in)
-If you use Google Play, it's a great tie in for music, books, movies (streaming, not storing)

Con
For $200 I wasn't expecting much, but...
-The frame is flimsy and seems warped right out of the box.
-The keyboard is not backlit, and you need to learn a lot of keyboard shortcuts to make up for the missing function keys.
-Screen resolution, while decent, leaves the characters either a little too small, or too big and pixelated if you zoom to the next screen resolution.
-Bluetooth is a little funky - I don't have trouble with my other BT devices, but this seems to skip and stutter in transmission.
-While the internet font can be resized, there is no font control on the programs or file menus - which really limits this machine's use for someone with weak vision.  You can only zoom the screen resolution, which as I said earlier, doesn't have enough stops to pick a good fit.
-16GB storage is already crowded after a month and needs weekly pruning/ management.

Seems like these puppies burn out in about an hour.

Other than that - they are fine, no smoke or sparks, they float as advertised.

Who expects these junky things to last.  Not me, so the fact that some have makes me surprised.  The birthday party was made a lot of fun with these on the hands of 8-boys running around in the yard at night.
I had to apply 5-6 coats to get a decent nighttime glow out of this paint.  Would not recommend it or get it again, but I'm not sure what works better yet.
These pens just never grow old and they make markups and grading as fun as it can be.  Getting some purples next.
These pens just never grow old and they make markups and grading as fun as it can be.  Getting some purples next.

Not me, but the 13-yo loves it.  If there are any grandparents or parents who want to stun their kid with insiders knowledge on the most bombastic keyboard out there - this is your ticket.

The illuminated keyboard has me thinking there may be a need for this device in my office someday.

Note that the keys are chicklet (yes, like the gum squares), so it's perhaps not a keyboard for a writer or code-composition purist.
This feels and functions much better than the MS branded headset I just sent back.  The 10-year old end user gives it thumbs up, so that's what counts here.

These hooks should have been around a long time ago, maybe they were.  The double side means no more removing the liner to get the curtain off, and vice versa.  Also, there is no more snapping open closed rings. I think they look nice also.

The bearings are a little loud when sliding across the bar, but that's common to all of these roller rings.

If you haven't watched this or introduced the next generation to the story (or John Candy), then you should put this on the movie night queue.  Some bona fide hilarious antics, and pleasant island attitude was captured.

Funny, I never wanted these, but my kid does, and they look really nice and still smell the same as they used to (while they are new).  The Chucks are a little elongated in the toe, fit was a bit looser than most of her shoes she told me.

OK here's the sitch.  We would get 1bar 4G on our ATT iPhones at home.  I grew tired of dropped calls or stuttering, so I plunked down the dough hoping this would work, and I'm here to say it does.

1 bar increased to 5?  No, more like 1 bar up to 2 from my office 40-feet away from this antenna, but that seems to be all I need.  It will pump up to 3 or 4 bars if I take the phone within 5-feet.

I would have given it 5-stars, except that the original power adapter died after 8-months.  I knew it was not working because I started noticing my calls dropping again.  Found a spare 5V adapter and my calls are back loud and clear.

So if the oil change place wanted $45 to replace the cabin air filter and you wonder if you could change it yourself, I'd say probably so.  For our 2012 Ody, the hardest part was working the filter housing out of the back of the glove box.  The filter came with a YouYube link and very easy instructions to follow.  Once I opened up my filter I realized it really wasn't that bad, though.

Single moms, men with soft hands, and 16 year olds today have it made with these kind of YouTube instructions.  When I was a kid, I'd have to read my Chiltons guide to figure something like this out, then I'd have to walk up hill in the snow both ways.

users.query: This camera could really be used for more than just a Baby Cam. The only feature likely that is unique to a baby cam is the "soothing songs." Aside from that, it works like a typical Wi-Fi camera. I have a D-Link Internet Camera and this TRENDnet is fairly comparable in terms of features and quality. The installation was fairly easy.  The Night Vision is decent. The speaker feature is somewhat freaky for normal people - imagine a voice just coming out of nowhere.  I don't know how a baby would react to it though.

cands.text: The VTech Kidzoom is a toy.  It's quite burdensome to keep around, as there are too many accessories because you need a different accessory for a different activity (e.g., skateboarding, going under water, etc.).  You can buy a Micro SD card to capture a lot of pictures and videos, but the camera is low grade so you get mediocre pictures and videos.  If your kid is old enough to operate this, he or she may likely already have a cell phone and any modern cell phone now will have a camera that would beat this.  The only thing that a cell phone won't do is go underwater.  If that's your thing, then maybe this is the camera for you.  Of course, there are several fantastic waterproof cameras out there (e.g., Lumix).

The small size of the Nikon S7000 makes it ideal for traveling. You can put it in your pant pocket and bust it out when you need to take pictures.

The 16mp takes beautiful pictures especially when there is adequate light. The Night scene setting yields decent low light pictures. The Easy Panorama makes taking panoramic pictures a relative breeze. The relatively fast shutter speed and sports mode allows you to capture quick moves pretty easily. The quality of the pictures are pretty good and sharp.

The megazoom is definitely useful for taking pictures at a distance and it is relatively resistant to normal levels of shaking. Other cameras are typically make taking sharp pictures hard when you maximize the zoom.

One downside is that the battery life is pretty short. Maybe around 150 or so pictures will be enough to drain your battery. I wasn't sure how to read the battery meter on the screen and had to suffer from a dead battery the first time I used this camera. I will likely get an extra battery with an external charger to make sure this doesn't happen again.

I was able to get the WiFi to work with my iPhone but I prefer just copying over the pictures from the SD card to my computer. It's just a lot easier but the WiFi transferring appears to work for those of you that are into that.

I bought this for my kid when I game him my iPad mini. This is a soft padding that allows you to cover the edges and back. The camera and top-right button are concealed by a soft rubbery-type cover that you can flip open. This is generally how the other jacks at the bottom are also accessed. I definitely feel that the iPad is more secure and prevents it from getting scratched or dinged.

The front has a thin plastic film covering the screen, which protects the iPad mini screen from whatever your child does (e.g., drool, food marks, and other stuff). I haven't noticed any impact on the touch screen of this plastic cover, so looks like a winner for me.

The back has a stand that flips out. It's a little hard at first but with a little bit of breaking in the stand was not too difficult for my 6 year old to open by himself. The angle is perfect for watching videos while on a desk.

The H3 is an excellent camera for those that want a 10x zoom and excellent picture quality, but don't want to break the bank.  The main advantage over a comparable Canon model is the Lithium battery (although you have to take it out of the camera to charge it).  Don't let the size fool you - this camera is quite light.  This camera does not have an Electronic View Finder (EVF), which I don't really find too useful and never used in my old digital camera.  The LCD screen is sufficient under most lighting conditions.  I haven't gotten around to playing with most of its features, but for normal point and shoot operation -- this camera is pretty good.

This Linksys router looks like it is meant for more serious users, which may justify its price tag relative to much simpler routers that work fine for me.  I have experience using a number of routers and the most basic ones typically all work for me.  Don't get me wrong, this seems like a very good router except that I could do without all the extra bells and whistles.  The mobile app access seems nice, but I rarely (if ever) need to do anything with my WiFi router.  I rarely care about range as I don't need the WiFi to go far or through too many obstacles.  Maybe the "beam forming technology" is helpful, but that may just be psychological (i.e., I can't tell the difference).

This phone has all the basic features you would want in a phone system - it has handsets that work, a digital answering machine, and it is easy to install.  This system has several handsets so you have the added convenience of being able to place handsets in several rooms.  The design of the phones are nice and sleek, and the numbers are easy to read off the screen.  My old cordless phone only had 2 little lines with an orange back light, so the big screen and light blue back light of these handsets is a little refreshing and easy on the eyes.  Another neat thing is that you can check the messages on your answering machine from any of the handsets.

Unfortunately, this phone does not have keypad lighting, which makes it extremely difficult to use in the dark.  In addition, the ring volume at its maximum isn't as loud as I want it to be.
Pretty good kit that allows your kid to build things using their imagination. Great way to spark their creativity.

My 1.5 year old has been enjoying this toy.  He has a similar looking toy but without the "Bounce" part.  He seems to enjoy this one more, but that's maybe because this is a new toy.  When my kid bounces up and down, the toy makes a sound which he finds amusing.  This toy comes out of the box with everything it needs, and the installation was pretty simple.  The only thing that was a pain was putting on the wheels, which for some reason requires you to exert a decent amount of force.

The first impression you will get when you get this case is that it is cheap.  You feel like it may break easily, but so far it has lasted a couple of weeks of "normal" wear and tear from a 4 year old.  The roller feature is actually nice, because it helps your kid lug the case around.  The launcher is also interesting, but ours came with a missing (albeit non-essential) piece.

The worst part of the case is that we cannot use it for 100 cars.  First, half of the case is practically useless.  The top half of the case has some sort of cover that is meant to prevent the cars on that side to fall off when opening the case.  This does not work!  Every time I open the case, the cars on the top half would fall off.  Therefore, I find only the bottom half of the case is usable.  Second, depending on the type of Hot Wheels your kid has, one slot may not be sufficient for one vehicle.

At the end, this case is a good place to stow away a bunch of vehicles rather than having it laying around all over.

This GPS system is fairly cheap and does most of the things you would want a GPS unit to do - get you from point A to point B.  Basically, that's all I really wanted when I bought this unit and I am happy to say that it has been pretty successful in doing that.  I had a little trouble at the start because it wouldn't lock-in my route and always had "Proceed to Route" on the screen even though I was already on the road and moving to my destination.

Having said that, this machine has a few annoying issues.  First, it sometimes just restarts automatically and could leave you hanging if you have to turn or something.  Second, it gets lost when you are surrounded by tall buildings.  Hence, you have to be sure that you know the turn-by-turn directions prior to entering business districts, etc.  Finally, it's "shortest time" route may not be the optimal route every time.  I went on a trip to Milwaukee to Chicago and the GPS took me through rural Northwestern Illinois, which increased the travel time home from 2 hours to 3 hours.  I don't know what happened there, but be sure to check the route before you embark on a long trip (I learned this lesosn the hard way).

For city driving, I think this unit is fine.  It has gotten me to most places without any real issues.  It's also cheap, which is good for reluctant first-time buyers.  After you get a GPS unit though, you will surely ask yourself why you didn't get one any sooner.

You'll get a decent number of hours of fun with this BOOMco blaster.  My kids did.  The darts appear a little harder than the Nerf darts (i.e., may sting a little bit more when hit at close range), but they seem to be a more accurate shot. Aesthetically, the gun looks a little funky but the colors are refreshing.  As for durability, this blaster appears to be well-made.

If this is your kids' first Angry Birds game, you will likely have fun with it.  It is easy to setup and watching birds going all over the place kept my kids entertained for days.  Adults can also join the fun and will likely end up entertained as well.

However, there is nothing fundamentally different from this game compared to other Angry Birds games (except the the Star Wars one).  The thing you have to consider is which birds you want to be playing with because that would depend on the game you purchase.  Otherwise, the way things work is pretty much the same.

This is now our third Angry Birds game.  We have Angry Birds Space and Star Wars.  We began playing the game the way it was supposed to but then we ended up making our own structures with the kids.  This has helped the little guys figure out about how things balance, what parts you should hit to cause more blocks to fall, etc.

I didn't really appreciate the benefits of having an iPad stand until I tried this one.  This stand allows you to read text and watch videos (the stand allows you to switch from portrait to landscape and vice versa easily) at a more proper level when placed on a table.  I found it easier to read magazines and books compared to when I was just holding my iPad.

The assembly is quick and easy.  The fit is perfect for my iPad 2.  The stand feels sturdy too.  In addition, the stand can be adjusted into just about any position.  The stand allows you to swivel to your desired angle.  More importantly, it is easy to pop the iPad out of the stand when you need to bring your iPad somewhere.

My understanding is that this is the first 3D book for the Tag Reader system.  The 3D makes this book slightly more interesting, but I don't know how much the 3D enhances the learning experience.  In any case, just like most of the books for the Tag Reader, this book sparked the interest of my kids.  My youngest had the 3D glasses on and was reading away almost from the moment I opened the packaging.

The 3D glasses are the paper kind, which seem easy enough to tear/break.  You definitely have to be careful with these, specially because there is no place to store the 3D glasses properly.  The glasses came glued to the inside of the front cover, but once you use the glasses you don't have a place to slide them in to prevent them from being separated from the book.  We do have a Tag reader case in which we can put the books and the pen, but that only provides protection if the book/glasses are in the case and doesn't prevent misplacing the glasses once outside the case.

In general, I like the Tag Reader system.  It helped my eldest and now my youngest is enjoying it.  I think from an educational perspective it's an excellent device.  The books are fairly interesting and you get a wide selection of popular titles.

At first, I thought that this was going to be as useful as the Leap Reader, but it just came in a bulky case. Then I realized there's actually more to it. There are some additional activities that you can do besides reading. It's a fairly interesting concept. Aesthetically, the case doesn't look that nice. It looks very utilitarian. I think it's quite heavy for my 1st grader too. The content itself is up to Leap Frog standards, which is pretty good. The set comes with a starter book and two others. It's fairly simple to use. Once you install the software, you can easily do the rest.

My 3 year old son loves Thomas and this toy was just perfect.  Below are my three comments:

1. This toy was very easy to assemble and easy to move around.
2. My kid loves seeing how Thomas gets pulled up the incline.  This process also shows him how magnets work.  Because the magnet is not too strong, he has to set the trains up properly and hook the magnet correctly in order for Thomas and/or the cart to be pulled up.
3. The "stone cutter" didn't feel like it was well-made.  There's a button that Thomas runs through that drops the stone cutter from its original position, but when I try to pull it back up again it always feels like I'm going to break the thing or that the stone cutter won't hold its original position.

I bought the LG Blu Ray BD 370 player because it had Netflix streaming and wasn't as expensive as the alternatives.  Overall, this is an excellent Blu Ray player.

This is my first Blu Ray player, so I can't really make any comparison with other players.  However, I'm quite satisfied with the video quality, and there are some noticeable improvements over standard DVDs (although not a significant improvement - but this is not a player issue).  The upscaling when playing standard DVDs works well and is comparable to the upscaling of my Sony DVD.

One of the reasons why Netflix streaming was important to me was because my kid could get to watch a variety of cartoons over and over.  As his taste evolves fairly rapidly, I get to choose from a wide selection of children's programs available for streaming.  Also, unlike OnDemand on Comcast, some of the children's programs on Netflix are over an hour long, so you don't have to keep on coming back every half and hour to change the program.  Having the streaming feature on the Blu Ray player allows us to play the videos on our 46" LCD TV rather than on a 15" laptop screen.

I have also used the Netflix streaming feature to watch movies when we are in between the videos on our Netflix queue.  The quality of the Netflix streaming is pretty good even on regular videos.  The HD streaming is of even better quality, but your selection is much narrower.  The quality may be a function of a wired ethernet connection, but this Blu Ray player doesn't support Wi-Fi (most players that do would cost a lot more).

This player also has You Tube streaming and after the software update you gain access to something called Cinema Now or something like that.  The You Tube menus are not difficult to navigate and the quality of the videos is not too bad.  I don't use this feature that often.  Cinema Now allows you to purchase movies on-line and the movie will be streamed to your player.  I haven't tried this just because I have Netflix streaming, so I can't really comment on this feature.
These are really nice jeans.  The material is really soft and the quality appears to be really good.  The jeans were just a little large for my kid, but I'm sure he'll grow into it soon.

I didn't find anything special with this game.  The only good part is that it is easy to assemble.  My nine year old was able to do it all by himself.  Playing the game though was boring.  My kids were into this game for all of 10 minutes.  Maybe if you really liked baseball this would be a fun game.

I switched to a laser range finder instead of GPS apps because it would drain my phone battery too much (I actually ran out of battery while playing and didn't like the feeling of being disconnected from the electronic world). In any case, the Bushnell NEO is a good complement because it allows you to use a separate but small device to give you additional information instead of just knowing distances to certain objects and having to guess the rest. As for accuracy, the NEO is pretty good relative to my range finder. To be honest, I probably don't need that much precision anyway. So I would think the NEO would be good as a standalone device. Overall, this is a great device. The only thing that I didn't like is having to look behind the device to figure out what buttons I was pressing. I'm guessing that with more use I will get the hang of it.

Relative to most small umbrellas, the GustBuster is able to hold up (i.e., not flip over) to Chicago's winds and has kept me dry on many occassions.  In addition, the size makes it easy to carry by hand or in a messenger bag and it sure beats carrying a large golf umbrella.

The first half the book is stuff anyone with experience doing any serious sort of data analysis should already know. This also includes several  chapters on installing R and Python. If the reader needs all those chapters devoted to installing R and Python and the necessary, then there is almost no chance that that same reader will get anything out of this book. The second half of the book appears to cram many different statistical concepts into a few chapters and hope something sticks.

When the headset works, it is pretty convenient. Paring was easy. It was also easy to use.  The  sound quality is relatively good from both ends (mine and the person I'm talking to). The biggest problem I have with these is that it randomly drops the bluetooth connection with the phone even when the phone is less than a foot away.  This happens sporadically and cannot be repeated systematically (sometimes a whole day goes by without a single dropped connection), which makes it very annoying because you cannot predict when your connection will get dropped.  It appears that the unit shuts off when this happens and the call gets transferred to my cell phone handset, so your call isn't disconnected just the headset to phone connection.  After a few weeks, I ended up dumping this headset in favor of a different headset.

The lessons from this book should be followed by anyone that wants to improve their communication skills.  In my opinion, the most important point in this book is that one should be a good listener.  Only when you listen can you actually learn what your client or customer (or just about anybody) really means or wants.

There are also many other suggestions in this book, like avoiding non-words (e.g., uh, um) and hedge words.  In my opinion, some of the suggestions are easier said than done.  Specifically, many people are afraid of public speaking or presenting to a relatively large crowd that adding several other key thoughts may be overwhelming.  Therefore, I don't know how realistic one can get to attaining all the prescriptions in this book.  Nonetheless, I think that if one strives to master all the suggestions in this book (even though not perfecting all of them), one will definitely become a better communicator.

If you have to sit for hours, this is a high quality task chair that should make that task easier.  The seat is composed of some sort of fabric, which appears easy to clean.  The back is a mesh, which makes it breathable but allows sufficient support.  However, the back of the chair isn't as high as some other office chairs, but that is not a problem for me.  The arm rests are made of plastic, but appear to be well-built.  The package came in one box and assembly was relatively easy.  Overall, a pretty good task chair for everyday use.

users.query: I didn't measure out my room completely and was one tile short after I bought 4 packs of these. They look great in my workout room. I had to cut some down to size along the edges with a utility knife. It was quick and easy to install!

cands.text: This is my entryway rug. Took a day to flatten out but it has stood up to the abuse so far. This winter will be the true test.
I have stains on my floor board where my factory floor mats didn't cover. These things are big and designed perfectly to cover more surface area. Cannot see the stains if they're under the mat!
Small and light to hang up on the wall. Goes great with my nautical theme.
Will never own a vehicle without WeatherTech floor mats again. These things are awesome!
Ordered my exact shoe size 10.5 and I have a just a little wiggle room for my toes which is exactly what I wanted. These things are nice and tight to keep out the snow and your feet nice and dry!
Holy cow these are fancy! Upgrading from my cheap walmart pots and pans from my college days to these. Talk about being floored! I feel like a chef!

This has a lot of customization options and has a strong signal throughout the whole house (1600 sq ft). Gave me a few issues in the beginning with my signal dropping but after a week of making some changes, it has been going flawless for months since.
These came fast by mail. They look great and can't wait to put them on!
This thing is huge! It doesn't fit under my old cupboards but I plan on getting new cupboards someday so not that big of a deal!
Bought this for under my dining room table. I get compliments all the time on how "fancy" it is.
Inexpensive and does a darn good job! I'm going to need to buy some more so I don't have to wash them so often.
Goes great with my kitchen theme. Good for covering up bakery and for looks but not sure I would use for a hand towel, it's too nice!

Looks great in my nautical theme bathroom. The second hand was sticking when I first put batteries in it but after carefully tweaking it back into proper position, it appears to be keeping exact time so far.
Second pair of DC shoes that I bought. These things are comfy. I wear them all day at work. I always get compliments about my new kicks!
Second pair of DC shoes that I bought. These things are comfy. I wear them all day at work. I always get compliments about my new kicks!
Not sure what there is to say but I can say it looks great on my bathroom door. I get laughs from it.

I haven't actually used this yet but will update my status if I feel different. It appears to be really good quality and a nice sleek design. It stands pretty tall so be careful fitting it under your cupboards.
Cheap price but not cheap quality. Does a great job! I need to buy another set.
I love these shoe racks. I get asked all the time where I bought them. Highly recommend these to everyone. I bought two originally and bought another one after that.
These thing is fairly large. No issue fitting all of your bakery in it!
My pitt loves it. Sleeps in it everyday and still looks brand new after having it for many months! I do have a blanket on top of it so that helps any wear.
DOA. I heard the horror stories of them being bad and thought it wouldn't happen to me. Wrong!
I haven't used it yet but it's nice to know it's with my bike in case I ever do
Spendy, but really tied my nautical theme together. I recommend get the whole Avanti set.
Heavy, well constructed bookends. Looks great on my book shelf!

users.query: United Cutlery is noted for making replica blades, inexpensive and of low quality. It might look cool on the wall but for God's sake don't bet your life on it. Cold Steel and Condor make some really tough, usable, affordable machete's that will perform for you for years.

cands.text: United Cutlery is noted for making replica blades, inexpensive and of low quality. It might look cool on the wall but for God's sake don't bet your life on it. Cold Steel and Condor make some really tough, usable, affordable machete's that will perform for you for years.

What a beast! It is terrifyingly sharp. One thing I haven't seen anyone mention is that it is a chisel grind, sharpened only on one side. This should help with re sharpening.
The new steel they use is cons idered superior to S30V and other top metals. I do not like serrations because sometimes they snag and I would simply never be able to re sharpen it, lol.
I believe if you need this for self defense it would make your assailant think very hard about whether he wanted to get cut by it. I imagine the wound channel would be horrifying.
The handle texture makes it feel like it will stick to your hand, even if wet, thought we are not talking scratching your skin. Amazing texture.
The Triad Lock (check it out if you don't know what that is) is one of the best lock innovations since the lock back knife was invented. It puts the pressure from the blade onto a pin in the handle instead of on the lock bar, eliminating a possible failure point (where the lock bar bends because of pressure on it; I have seen this happen). This lock should be standard on every lockback blade.
One interesting comparison to the spyderco civillian (you can find direct "vs" reviews on YouTube) is that Spyderco has a recommendation right in the box to be careful with the fragile tip on its knife! No such worry with the cold steel version. Some of the other reviews seem to make out that this knife is much larger than the civillian but it is not (again, look at the videos). The Talon is slim and fits very unobtrusively in your pocket. If your clip is tight, this is not really a problem. Unscrew it from the handle and bend it a bit either way (tighter or looser) with some pliers and reattach it.
I apologize for the random way this review wanders around but I was just writing down things as they came to my mine, not making an essay
I recommend this knife highly and it is my current EDC (though I do have a Swiss army Tinker too). Please check out the knife laws in your state before you carry it because I am certain it would cause some raised eyebrows if a police officer saw it. It is only a 4 inch blade but it looks like 10 inches because of the intimidation factor 
If you have never used a knife with the assisted opening wave feature here is a basic guide to practice with. Put the knife deeply in your pocket and as far to the right as you can. When you want the blade open grasp both sides of the knife in the upper quarter or so, avoiding block in the blade, so basically just on both sides. Pull it out firmly back and I at about a 45 angle. You will feel the blade start to catch and just continue powering through and the blade will click open very satisfyingly. This may take a few tries to get the feel of it but once you do it feels wicked. When you do not want the blade do you open on its own grab the handle but also put your thumb on the blade and slowly pull it straight up, not to either side. If you pull it to the side or too fast, the blade will deploy. Sometimes it will deploy just enough to clip your finger nicely. Not deploying the blade can be as tricky as having it come out on you too. By the way I take no responsibility if you cut off your fingers or your uncle clems nose practicing this. Take it slow and steady until you feel very comfortable and then still exercise caution. I added this bit to help out but again, if you cut yourself or someone else, it is not my responsibility.

It's OK. I would classify it as a collector's piece only though. I hoped to EDC it for awhile but the handle guard feels clumsy and the weird blade droop (like a partially flaccid "member") make the knife feel strange and unwieldy. The fit and finish are fine and I understand these knives are supposed to be good investments, just don't expect to use it.

The LMF Mora knives are excellent and a real steal at the price. I actually purchased 3 of them; I have one for use and two for backup. I wanted to have a couple of backups in case the price goes up or they stop making the knife. Mora has a new product out that competes with this one so I am afraid they will stop making this knife and I really, really love it. I am a knife collector, lifelong, and I really recommend this knife. I just encountered this knife and it is excellent!

I bought two of these from the knife center of the internet (sorry Amazon ). I thought it was beautiful.
Then all the reviews of the blade breaking started. You can watch several on YouTube. Some have broken just by having been carried in a backpack...I used to go deep forest and you can't take a chance on a blade breaking for suspicious or random reasons, not related to misuse, in so many cases! I want to carry it and love the look but those pictures of broken blades are stuck in my head. I guess it will have to remain a contender...

This is a nice looking knife. Usually Damascus knives in this price range are pattern welded. It is more of a looker/wall hanger/conversation piece. I wouldn't take it out for any type of serious use. For what is is it looks like a nice knife. The pattern reminds me of the Tom Brown Tracker from Tops Knives.

Legal to carry anywhere and ready to go when you need it. I love this blade although I usually prefer full tang knives the look, feel, safety, and look make it my legal EDC. Get the "legal" part? It is really hard to find a blade you could protect yourself that isn't silly small. This <3 blade has a 5 or so inch reach! In Texas, San Antonio, ALL lock blade knives used to be illegal! Even a 1" blade was illegal though you could carry 5 1/2 " fixed blade. It was hard to find a knife for use and potential defense that didn't look insane or have a worthless folding blade (I cut myself enough as a kid to appreciate a lock blade (and choil). They finally got rid of the lock ban and now I can carry this, safe and secure.
Anyway, don't underestimate the quality and blade size. It's strong and beautiful, top quality all the way (though I wish it had a tri-ad type cold steel lock)
I bought this at another site but wanted to share my happiness with the blade. I am a normal user with no other incentive to post this beyond sharing a great find. I included a quick pic to show I actually own one.
(BTW, its razor sharp out of the box. I am surprised someone rated it dull...perhaps they didn't use the blade part? )

They fixed every problem with the original Ultimate Survivor Knife! This is a very nice package, esp. for a car emergency kit or emergency bag. I think it would be good for an EDC blade if your state allows it (mine doesn't). I really love this blade and it has so many nice bonus's like the fire starter, sharpener, whistle (yes, the whistle; if you are tired or hurt it can be very difficult to call out for help, if not impossible (imagine Titanic, the end where the girl is on the ice). A whistle can save your life instead of making you watch as someone walks close by but you are too tired to call out). I wouldn't hesitate to take this out camping. Check YouTube; people are trying to destroy this one, like they did the older version, and they can't! I read all the one star reviews and I think the people who wrote them know absolutely nothing about knives, or just hate the brand. Get one of these, you will not be sorry!

I bought one for a knife with a 4 1/2 inch blade that came with a lousy sheath ($150 knife!). This fit so well I immediately ordered another one for a old Marbles knife that the sheath was lost for. Perfect fit again! I literally could not be happier and recommend this product.
This is a great little hammer for around the house tasks. It has excellent balance and effortlessly drives nails. Recommended.

These cost a fraction of similar sets and are a decent , adjustable weight set for beginning arm workouts.
The smell? Well, they are iron, which rusts quickly. I imagine there is a coating that protects the dumbbells from rusting while they sit in storage waiting to be delivered to a customer. Guns and swords/knives have a similar coating on them for rust prevention. A good wash (and through dry) with dishwashing soap (for grease removal) should fix this problem.
I have just ordered the set, so I will amend this review after I use them, but after reading the reviews I figured some initial thoughts on the product may prove insightful. I am really pretty excited about finding a bargain like this on the same day I decide to start working out my arms again.
*quick edit* Yes, this is a great set. Get one while you still can.

If you have an average to large hand, welcome to heaven. I have purchased allot of mice, from logitech to steel series, from microsoft to razer, and this model is a perfect fit to my hand. I have a death adder, a diablo 3 (steel series), a WoW custom SS, a naga, etc., and all of these mice make my hand cramp after awhile. This mouse is a perfect fit to my hand. If my hand could sigh, it would, in luxury when I hold this mouse. Give it a try if most other mice feel uncomfortable in your hand. You don't need 10000 buttons or macros on a mouse; you do need a comfortable mouse for extended play.
Exactally what it looks like. It feeels a bit cheaply made, but it is! Functionality it is fine and dependable.

This keyboard is sold by apple for $149 and easily available for $99. I got mine with free two day shipping. Its a good keyboard and I have been using mine for months but I wouldn't suggest paying extra for nothing.
I guess the carbon/weight is the draw here? The price is beyond outrageous for the specs (video, RAM, processor, etc.)

Grim and dark, just like the book. Three headlines from the day I write this review: 1. North Korea readies its second missile launch to determine viability and range of a nuclear strike. 2. China hacks the USDoD, which contains nuclear launch codes and more. 3. The US readies a remote, robot controlled fighter plane that can fly faster than a normal fighter jet can and murder with greater efficiency.
Trillions of dollars spent on death. With the tech of today, if people could just get along, we could provide food and shelter, etc. for the entire world. Instead we work on better ways to kill each other. I think this movie portrays what is going to happen to the world and mankind. It is well deserved. Maybe the earth can somehow recover without the pestilence of man around to destroy everything.
BTW, if you wish to really "get" this movie you must watch it until the end. If you do not you will be missing the life affirming final message that Mr. McCarthy meant to be conveyed.

These plates are larger than the usual Corelle plates are. The coffe mugs are large mugs instead of small cups. I love Corelle for everyday usage because you can use the oven, microwave, convection oven, etc. without damaging the plates or cups. A+++

This is a beautiful and functional case. I think it would probably retail for about $100 at the Apple store! The only reason it doesn't have 5 starts is that it its a bit of a pain to fiddle with opening the case when you need to answer the phone, but the trade off is you get excellent screen protection.

This is a beautiful and functional case. It has that leather feel to it that no synthetic can match (buffalo leather here, I believe). It feels padded and substantial without being too heavy or clumsy. Every facet and feature of this case is superb. I have been buying cases the last few years, first for my older kindle reader, then two of the fire model. I have ended up a couple of times where I got a cheap product that I couldn't use, forcing me to return it. You would have to knock me out and pry this case out of my hands to get it back; it really is that nice. I have been using it for several months now, including a trip to Oregon and everyday use. It does not stain easily (I was kind of afraid it would) and requires only moderate care and cleaning. If their other products are as nice they will move to the #1 spot on my accessory list for the iPad. Get it, you won't be disappointed!

This is the best honey comb on Amazon, for the color, flavor, and quality. It is a few dollars more but worth it. I am just a honey comb lover, not affiliated with or paid by this company; I want you to find and enjoy the best quality honey comb. This is it!

I have owned it about a week and I really love it. It is easy to use and has a beautiful display. I love Kindle products and have owned one since the original Fire. This version is very light weight and has excellent sound. Some people have mentioned the speed. Yes, there is a slight delay...a couple of seconds. Whoop. For the price, $159, it cannot be beat. I also own a iPhone 6s Plus (only because I have it on contract at $1000) and of course it is faster, barely. Let me tell you, it is only a little faster than the Kindle! If I couldn't afford a iPad I would be fine with the Kindle. The weight of the devices are similar and the screen on the Kindle is bigger! Plus, the Kindle has stereo sound. There seems to be a recent (read Feb 2016) increase in speed. I am not sure why. I got another one of these for my daughter and it seems a bit faster. One small problem is that I now hear static in the headphones. I am working on a solution but if I don't get it, I will take off one star and post the problem here. I just cannot see you being disappointed with the Kindle and the people bashing on it are divorced from reality. The ads are VERY subtle and sometimes actually helpful, showing up only on the opening display for a moment or two! I highly recommend this device.

There is something grotesquely fascinating about this movie. I haven't really seen a movie that draws me back to watch it like this one does. It make you feel sick and guilty to watch it, but I am on my 3rd time, this time the unrated version. By the way, the unrated version only has bits and pieces but they make the overall film VERY worthwhile overall, adding to the impact of the movie. I think it is a gruesome masterpiece but seriously, if you can't take it, don't watch it! Especially don't watch it then cry because it's so horrible. I will warn you right now: it IS a horrible piece of film that will haunt you. You decide now if you want to see it, but don't complain that you didn't understand what you were getting into.
THere are better collections but for free this cannot be beat. A good introduction to the works of Edgar Allen Poe.

It could have worked but this is not worth watching. I usually like to give this type of low budget movie a chance but it was really bad; once the subtitles that you cannot disable, that take up 1/4 of the screen, started I was out (the beginning).

Not scary for one second. I thought this would be edgy and cool, and although it is enhanced by watching it on a computer, it isn't worth watching. Whatever you think it is, it probably isn't. It is just a computer screen with multiple screens. No thrills, no scares, nothing. I was so disappointed. For God's sake don't buy this like I did, anticipating from the trailer it would be good. It isn't.

users.query: I read them back to back and loved each book.  Mavis, the leader is so strong and sure of herself, yet she's vulnerable, too.  She directs a group of people, some really ungrateful, to safety and a new beginning.  The accomplishments of her group, the people we get to meet and interact with stay with you a long time after the last chapter.  When a character becomes ingrained, latches on to you, and you want to be with them again and again, that's the true sign of a great story.

cands.text: I enjoy a lot of different authors, different styles and if I like their last book I'll usually invest in their new one. There's not one of my favorites who haven't disappointed me with one of their stories.  It doesn't stop me from revisiting their work again, and I chalk it up everybody can't be great all the time.  Having said that I'll offer this -  I've never said this about any author - 100 percent of Harlan Coben's work I LOVE!  I have not read one of his books that's disappointed me or left me disappointed.  I devour his work, and Shelter is no exception.  I didn't want to read it, thinking it was a tween book, something for the young adult reader. But I had nothing left to read except Mickey Bolitar, and finally broke down and purchased it.  From first to last, I was sucked in, and it wasn't a kiddie kind of story!  It was full of mystery, suspense and tenderness. I say this each review, Harlan Coben,did it again!  I love his work and the world needs more, more, more, more!

The beginning of the series is outstanding, I plowed thru Books 1-3 with ease, page turners for sure!  Book 4 dragged a little, but Book 5 started out dull and kept going until I had to put it down.  I'm halfway thru it and eventually I'll finish it but I'm not in any hurry.

What I love most about Jacqueline Druga's writing is her ability to develop characters you care about and want to follow.  Also, her depictions of what it'll be like, the devastation, the fear, the confusion, all come across in her books.  It's what I think I'd feel in that situation.  When the Ashes Fall is another example of that, her characters are drawn as real people and you want them to be okay. But I didn't feel this one as much, I wanted her to go deeper into her characters and deeper into the devastation.  I wonder about the ashes not being harmful as they trudged thru them. Seems like it would make them sick.  I'm a fan and this is definitely worth the read.  I was not disappointed.
I enjoyed it, loved how they kept getting out of dangerous situations.  It's a good book and well worth the read.

I've read a lot of Jacqueline Druga's books and loved the majority of them.  From the reviews I thought this would be another great read.  I was mistaken.  Not by the storyline, not by the characters, but by the writing itself.  It was so juvenile I couldn't take it.  It felt forced and a lot of the descriptions were unnecessary. Here's what I mean, this is from the middle of the book:  'Rick smiled at Preston in the rear view mirror, jerking his head to the side to remove the hair from his laughing steel gray eyes.'  We've already established much earlier in the book that a) Rick as long hair, b) he also has gray eyes.  Why keep referring to it?  Want more?  Okay, they find old collectible guns on the property they purchased.  They take them to an antique dealer and sell them for a pretty good price.  That's established when they sell the weapons.  We got it.  Then, they get home and talk about the room where they found the guns. 'That room does seem to need some work now that we've sold all those old guns, doesn't it?, Darrell said.  Rick says, 'You've got that right.  Even I don't believe how much you got for those old relics.  They were amazing firearms for a collector of antiques, but you need some modern firepower that will protect your home and family from an invasion.'  Didn't we just have this conversation 5 pages ago?  It really isn't a bad storyline but I just can't take the writing style.  I gave up midpoint and think I'll read a comedy or two to take the bad taste out of my mouth.

Often you start a book and you don't like the beginning or you think the middle is stupid or your grossly disappointed at the ending.  Then you get a book you can't put down.  You don't want to put down.  Part 1 of Redaction was that for me.  I love this book because it was human.  When she talked about the neighborhood, you felt it, you were in it.  When she talked about the food or the lights or the fear, it was real, you could identify with the characters; they live next door, your relatives, and the people you've seen before but only to nod hello.  For me, Redaction was more human than most dystopian books I've read.  And when you achieve that in the story, you've done it all.

I've been hooked on Jacqueline Druga's books for a few months now, and started with The Silent Victor.  While I love dystopian tales I admit that my focus is more on HOW they survive vs. what actually happened to bring the world to an end.  Ms. Druga tells the story of this group of people, really a family, and she gives us the truth for each one of the characters.  The reactions and behaviors of these people propel the story to "must find out what happens next" status.  I couldn't put them down.  I've read all of them, up to The Ripple.  I gave this series 5 stars because I love the characters, BUT I will say by the Ripple I was getting disappointed by two key things.  Ellen's back and forth relationships, and the trying to "fix events" from the past. I've come to see Ellen as sort of a slut, and I don't understand why Frank and Dean continue to want her at all. I think she betrayed both of them over and over again.  Needless to say she is not one of my favorite.  And the time travel is just too weird.  It went from an end of the world story to a sci-fi tale.  I'll see what the next book brings because I'm invested in their outcome.  I just hope we don't continue to stray to far from reality, and that Frank and Dean meet real women who they can love and trust forever.

The number of positive reviews convinced me to start this series.  The first one, Breakers, had me 2nd guessing myself, it seems slow and had too much detail, but before I was half way, I was in love with the characters.  Mr. Robertson masterfully shaped each one of them so that you cared about their survival, cheered when they won, worried when they entered danger.  How these people survived - not together, really, but each on their own - was great story telling.  I will say - SPOILER ALERT - the loss of quite a few characters bothered me.  But it was realistic and the story went on.  My only problem is that I want more of them!

I love love love Jacqueline Druga's work. I wanted to be immersed in this one as I've been by her other books. Instead I was never absorbed in the story, never connected with the characters. The idea is great but it felt more like we skimmed the surface throughout.

I've been reading the Solomon and Lord series, and so I enjoy them.  They're not DEEP stories, they're light and airy, books you can breeze thru after reading the heavier stuff.  I like Solomon because he's good for a chuckle, he's friendly and open with people.  Are the characters memorable?  Well . . . mostly.  Solomon, his nephew, his father, the courtroom groupies, I enjoy.  The other half, Lord, is supposed to be the balance, the voice of reason, and she is.  It's just sometimes she's a little hard to take.
Sort of like the rest of the 'will they, won't they' couples we all know and love. But I like the main character, Stephen.  He's funny, shady, lovable, kind and hot headed.  It was a cute, easy read.

I wasn't sure about this series or the main character, Jack.  Halfway thru the book I still wasn't getting a feel for who she is, what she's about.  But the storyline was great, kept me turning pages to find out what happened.  Warning, it's very graphic, not for the faint-hearted.

Wow.  This is a very powerful, very moving story.  You love the children right away, and you feel for them right away.  The story moves from the first page and can't wait to see what happens next.  Each of the main characters are well developed, but there are a host of characters in the periphery of the book, and you care about them, as well.  I know this neighborhood, I know these neighbors.  What this family endured and how they clung to one another is real, it was real then and it's real right now.  What happens to a girl-child in a family, what makes someone abusive, what makes a mother turn away and sink so low?  It's all in there, you feel it on each page.  This was a great read, even with the abuse, this book touched me.

From the very first book I read of Ms. Cooper's I was hooked!  SOLD!  When you can open a book and get lost in the storytelling, you've got a real good book!  I don't read short stories normally, but J. California Cooper never disappoints and I never come away feeling there should have been more.  Her development of her characters is as real as true life.  I see these people, know them personally.  A Piece of Mine has been one of my favorite books for a very long time.

I've read all of Lisa Lutz's Spellman books - she is great!  No one comes up with the twists and turns and fun like a good Spellman book.  While I understand that Isabel is immature I did not see the need for her and Henry to part ways.  Their match was twisted from the beginning - him so straight-laced, she so not.  But the pair fit, she could count on him and he didn't try to change her.  No one wanted Isabel to get married and live happily ever after, although the idea of a Spellman wedding tickles my funny bone.  Breaking them up reminds me of my other favorite author, Janet Evanovich, who ruined Stephanie Plum with the back and forth crap of Joe and Ranger.  Isabel loved Henry, he loved her, Stephanie loved Joe, he loved her. Tell their story and leave their partners in place. They don't have to "live happily ever after" with all the trimmings - neither of these characters could pull that off.  But they could have a foothold in "happily".  Instead these women stand outside of any commitment, making us go back to the beginning with each new book.  I stopped reading Stephanie Plum because of it, and I hope I don't have to do the same with Isabel.  I mean, after all, who doesn't love every last one of the nut cases in the Spellman family?

I'm not going thru all the details - you've heard what this book is about a zillion times.  What I'll tell you about is getting thru it.  A friend, who doesn't consume books like I do, said this was a really good book.  It's been on my wish list forever, waiting for a price drop.  When I received it I tried reading the first few pages, shut it and texted my friend.  "R U Kidding Me?"  She said keep going, it gets better.  Eventually I went back and crawled thru the first chapters.  Then it was Off and Running!  I was hooked!  What a ride, what a story, what a mystery!  I can't figure it out, where it's going and what will happen next.  First I couldn't stand the wife, then I couldn't stand the husband!  To say both of them needed professional help is putting it mildly!  But it was a good read, a great ride - until the end.  The reason it's 4 stars instead of 5, since I did enjoy the book, is what was Gillian Flynn thinking with that ending!  Come on now, son!  I couldn't get over it.  In fact, thinking about it now has me heated!  I'm cool, I'm good.  Read Gone Girl, stick with it, and I promise the ride is worth it.

It was like going Home - pun intended.  How I missed these guys, all of them!  And Win!  I absolutely LOVE him!  He's the best character, the most interesting and I can't wait to find out more about him.  And this book had everybody, from the kids all the way down!  It was old home week.  Okay, for the story, Harlan Coben is a genius, point blank period.  He pulls you right in and doesn't let go until the last page, and by then you don't want him to let go.  This is really Win's story, although Myron is back playing a huge role (have I said I love these guys?!).  Two boys go missing for a decade and then suddenly there's a lead after years of nothing.  It sends Win on the chase, and he soon pulls in Myron, who pulls in the rest of the old gang.  Before you know it, it's like the agency is back in business and nobody's missed a beat.  Myron and Win aren't about to give up until they find the answers to what happened to the boys, now teenagers. Along the way they meet a treacherous fat man, who quickly learns what side to be on, and an old friend(?) comes back.  Truth, you can NEVER go wrong with Harlan Coben - never!  And his latest, Home, is all the proof you need.

I enjoy 'end of the world' stories.  I love reading how people adjust and survive, what they improvise, how they get along, or don't.  This is not that.  This book starts with an unbelievable tragedy, although I was expecting something worldwide,  Then we're catapulted into the future and whatever happened after 'the tragedy' is left to our imagination. Next, the character is approached by a strange man who whisks her away from everything, the man she loves, the family she adopted as her own, her friends, everything, for the chance to avenge the tragedy. She's put into 'the bat cave' where she receives remarkable abilities that help turn her into her very own superhero.  She can run faster than a speeding bullet, climb the tallest mountain, bend steel in her bare hands.  Pardon me, my attempt at cynicism.  Meanwhile, we go back and forth to the ones she left behind, all the torment and questions with no way to find answers.  I didn't find this to be dystopian, we didn't experience the tragedy, it was just there.  With the new found abilities, the bat cave, and the angst, I'd call this more of a fantasy.  Enigma Black is book one of the trilogy.  I'm not sure I'll try book two.

Talk about a page turner!!  You know when you start a book and immediately know it's going to be a good one?  This was it.  At first, I wasn't sure, but by page 5 I knew Jacqueline Druga had done it again!  This might not be for everyone but I absolutely loved how she used Revelations, and gave us 'real-time' situations.  Michael, Danny, Jessie, Harry, Dale and Jude - great characters, great story line, great premise.  The end of times - what happens?  God says He's had enough of us and decides to follow His Scripture. You would think the world would change seeing some of the signs listed in the Bible, but, I believe like real life, they don't.  The chaos, the devastation, the deaths, all of it is there and it's wonderfully told.  You're not preached at, there's no sermon about repenting, and the Bible's not quoted every other page. This book is about the characters, their families, how they connect and what happens to them during the end times.  It's fascinating, scary, and a great reminder!  Well done, once again, Ms. Druga.

For some reason I enjoy this Solomon guy immensely.  I said before he's funny and he's what makes the story shine.  So does the father and the nephew.  Not so much the love interest.  She's just a tad too rigid for me but not enough to make me stop reading the series.  Mr. Levine, keep them coming, please!

Jacqueline Druga writes about adults.  Her books are not about teenagers who accomplish magical feats to defend their world or any of that nonsense.  Druga writes about adults dealing with life changing situations and how they cope.  Her work is never technically laden with jargon only a scientist would understand.  Rather, her stories have you experiencing what it would BE like, what we would DO in the same situations.  She also writes characters you feel connected to, that you want to succeed, you want them to beat the disaster and make a new way.  Sealed In was a page turner; it was heart breakingly real, the families, their connections to one another, and the outsiders.  I love Druga's work, and Sealed In is another feather in her cap.

One of the review titles is "Not Evanovich", and that's very true!  But Spitfire has it's own good points, a few bad points, and a pretty predictable ending. It was an easy read, entertaining in it's lightness which helped advanced the storyline.  I will say that the murderer was a good surprise (I suspected but wasn't' really sure). The Yo Mama jokes were tiresome but I did like the strength of their friendship. Would I read another Sandoval book?  Probably, but Evanovich still comes first!

I love dystopian stories, and what made this one stand out were the characters.  Real people who were facing the end of life as they knew it.  It wasn't a lot of scientific jargon but more how people would react, things that would need to be done, true responses to the normal way of life.  Ms. Druga is a great storyteller, I loved the sequences of how the characters, how she built them to become more important to me, and to the story.  I was shocked at the deaths and amused at some of the naive behavior by a couple of the main characters.  The only reason I didn't give this 5 stars is because of one the main characters.  The Beginning Series is a keeper, and I don't want the series to end.

Leo is a hoot. And his 'assistants' are even better.  I read the stories looking for George and Nearly Normal Norman and the gang, but then I'm drawn into the mystery and how Leo will get out of the situation.  The point of a good story is to become lost in the telling of it.  If you become lost, you know you have a good book.  Cast In Stone isn't brilliant, but it's fun, and you want to know what happens, so for me, that's a good book.

A a, her son n her twin step children are safe locked away in a hotel. The CDC has set up a command center right outside n the military had the hotel surrounded.. Safe, yes. Prisoners, yes.  Okay, here's where Ms. Druga's talent shines. She writes HUMAN stories, not technically outlined fiction. U know what's going on, what 'problem' is but ur not left to interpret a bunch of scientific facts that slow down the story. She writes about the people, what they face, what they battle. She consistently creates survivors you come to care for, n some u don't. I love her work.

users.query: I am a size 40" waist and got these large size. they fit perfectly. the length of them was perfect as well. I prefer the longer style pants when playing. the knees are re-enforced for sliding and the material feels quality made. these are very comfortable. if you are larger than 40" waist I recommend that you go with xl size. these should fit anyone with 36-40" waist size. I am 5'8" and the length goes to my cleats. they are able to be hemmed if you want them shorter. good buy.

cands.text: belt is made quality. I have 40" waist and have to put belt on largest size and use second to last hole for it to fit. the elastic fits nicely. if you are larger than 40" waist I would not recommend this belt. the size fits perfectly in rawling baseball pants. would recommend for anyone with waist size 30-40".

The front pockets are good size so you don't have to worry about items falling out of them. The back pocket is big enough to hold wallet and has Velcro to keep it secure. Must buy.

I ordered 2 pair of these pants. They are very comfortable and fit great. They have pull string on them to adjust the waist if needed. The front pockets are good size so you don't have to worry about items falling out of them. The back pocket is big enough to hold wallet and has Velcro to keep it secure. Cargo pockets are nice size as well and also have Velcro to keep items secure. Must buy.

Can't go wrong with this belt. This is a 2" belt. Velcro adjustment with slip locks on them. I am 38 waist and still have plenty room to go bigger if needed. Hold all my accessories perfectly. Must buy

Got these as work shoes for my volunteer work. They fit perfect to size and are comfortable. Light weight and breath good keeping your feet cozy all day. Made with good materials. Everything about them is better than expected. Must buy.
The sizing is perfect. I am 5'8" and had no issues. Husband loves the outfit as well. Recommend black bra for underneath shirt though.
They fit perfect to size and are comfortable. Light weight and breath good keeping your feet cozy all day. Made with good materials. Everything about them is better than expected. Must buy.

Love this style. Couldn't find any bathing suits like this in local market. Amazon had great price. The length of the shorts are perfect. Go to just above the knee. I am 5'8" so I like that look. The waist fits good as well. Has pull string on the front but don't need to use it. It will com in hand when it stretches out over time though. Quality made. Must buy.

The best range pants ever designed. They are very comfortable and functional. Have multiple pockets to hold mags or spare ammo. Also come with built in mag pouch and another pocket for cell phone. I use the cell pocket to hold my multi tool and front sight post adjuster. Size was perfect and fit with no issues. They do run a little long.

Had to get new cleats. Old ones busted and couldn't wear my metal spike cleats I have. These fit true to size. I also wear ankle braces and didn't have to go up a half size like some other brands make you do. I stayed with Mizuno because of the quality of the product. They have good grip for infield and out field players. They are a 9 spike with multiple smaller spikes. The smaller spikes really help with grip in the grass and wet conditions. Because of the multiple spikes they do get a little clog when playing in rainy games from the clay. I play shortstop/second base and have no issues with grip fielding. They wear more likes tennis shoes than cleats. Very good padding and need one game to break in. If you are looking for a quality cleat at a budget price then these are the ones you need to get.

Got a good deal on these. They are a true set of 2. They run a little big so you might want to get one size smaller. I normally wear large but these are a little to large. Might return for a set of mediums. Both set are constructed very well. Can't go wrong with these gloves. Can be used by both novice and experienced players. Fast shipping as well.

Update 18 June 2013: already had to replace these batting gloves. Only lasted 6 games. The palm and finger area wore out very quickly on both sets. I have noticed the more I use them the more the bat was slipping. The material did not hold shape very well either. They were already a little big when I got them but they stretched out even more as I wore them. Constantly having to adjust the wrist strap throughout the game. Replaced them with a set of Mizuno techfire batting gloves. They are 100 times better. They also cost a little more but well worth it. If you are just a recreational player these might work for you since you get 2 sets but for league and tournament advanced players don't bother buying.

Very nice case. Love that it has the auto on/off feature when you close the cover. This save my daughters battery tremendously. The stand on the back is well constructed. Holds up the kindle with no problems at all. All the speakers slots and buttons match up perfectly with this case. Also has a spot to hold a stylus if you use one. Was so glad to find these on amazon. I use to get these at the local store all the time. Then they stopped carrying them. Check other places around town and still could not find. Very good price for these. I pay about $10 at local store for a pack of 12. Picked these up for $16 but got 24. Definitely worth the price and you will love the flavor. Must buy.

users.query: >I do the Jumble puzzle every day in the Kansas City Star, and now, when the paper is all read and puzzles done, I can still enjoy doing this popular puzzle. Fans of this will love this 3-book set.....97 puzzles in each one, which will keep you busy for many weeks and months to come.

cands.text: I bought this for a 7-year old boy for his birthday (at his request)  and gave it to him yesterday.......he and his 3 brothers immediately tackled putting it all together. Kept them busy for hours and hours......and they loved every minute of it. These LEGO sets are super cool.

>I got hooked on this show as I baby sitted 5 kids, ages 3-6.........they absolutely love it and watch it every day......as do I! So, as they prepared to leave for Florida today from Kansas, I bought this for them to watch in their van as they traveled. They are so excited......they had to watch one episode yesterday just as a preview.

  The series is actually quite entertaining.........I love Robbie Rotten and can't wait to see how he is foiled by the host of characters! But, from time to time, even this man is shown to have a soft side.

  Most importantly, the series focuses on certain values: for children to be happy and healthy, obey, learn and to be kind. All the live and puppet characters convey these things to the children.

  As a person who grew up on "Howdy Doody" in the 1950's, I like that quality of this show......values are extremely important.

This compliation of the Sundays in a single volume is the last. The Sundays are now integrated into the dailies, beginning with Volume 9. This volume has many great storylines and great art by Ray Moore and Wilson McCoy........very enjoyable.

I accidently came across all of the Tinkerbell figures for birthdays on the net, and thought they would make a treasured memory for a little Princess of mine, who recently celebrated her 5th birthday......but I wanted to go back and get her the entire series in retrospect. This figurine, like all in the series, are fantastically done. Any little girl who loves Tinkerbell will treasure these birthday figurines.

My nephew wanted this set for Christmas........I remember watching the series some when it was on TV........he wasn't alive then, but caught them in re-runs and fell for the series big time. He has watched the set twice since Christmas and is starting a 3rd run through! I thought the series was very original and action-packed with just the right amount of drama and suspense.

I really anticipated this volume, as I was once a big Golden Age comics collector and had many of the original issues. Now the author puts out a great product, providing a wealth of information on each Quality character, story synopses for many issues, writer and artist info, AND 9 great complete stories in full color. Is that great or what? Highly recommended.

Neil Sedaka is a cut above many performers, because he was a song writer and arranger as well. This particular collection looks at many sides of this great artist.......some well known classics, others strange to one's memory, as it covers many decades. Still, you will like this collection and only want more.

As a collector of the Captain Midnight series by Dyamite, and several months behind in my reading, I didn't realize that this volume was to fill in between two sections of the storyline. Was able to order it and read in its proper sequencing........for people who are reading the series, this book is invaluable to tie strings together before beginning the last story arc in the series. It could stand alone, but would leave the reader wondering what was going on at times.

Super nice set of salt and pepper shakers, ideal for use during the 4th of July or anytime to display your patriotism. Well made and functional, look great on my lazy susan with other 4th of July decor. You'll like them.

Merle Travis' style of finger-picking is still among the best today, and he widely imitated........he influenced people like Chet Atkins and Jerry Reed. These two albums found in this collection are among his best works, including many favorites of his loyal fans out there: such as Rockabye Rag, Blue Bell, Walking the Strings, and a few stirring religious numbers.
Bought this for a 7 year old "bug boy" I sit for for his birthday......he is fascinated by bugs of all types and loves using this net to capture prizes to be examined. Very practical and useful.

Another super collection in the this newspaper series, still featuring the superb writing of Lee Falk, and great art by newcomer Wilson McCoy (although the last storyline features art by both Ray Moore and Wilson McCoy). McCoy had his own flair for this strip, but the characters are still drawn very similar to Ray Moore's early work, which many find preferable. However, the tight, fast-paced stories and fluid art, keep one rivted to the strip. A must have.

Volume 1 of the anthology series highlights many of the tunes the group recorded that were never released on disc, tunes that other artists, like the Coasters, Buddy Holly, and others performed on disc. The group's interpretations are sometimes stunning and entertaining, sometimes down right great (like "How Do You Do It"), and sometimes very raw in their performance. But it's great to see how the group evolved over the months and years early on.

These tunes are followed by alternate and studio demo/takes from their very earliest albums, plus from "A Hard Day's Night".

Like Volume #2, this disc begins with a solo, at home made, John Lennon tune, "Free As a Bird", which the other three took, added more instrumentation and vocals to it, and came up with a groovy tune.

I bought this particular playset for a sweet 2-year-old toddler who loves Mickey Mouse........not only did he sit down and have hours of fun with this when he opened the package it came in, so did his four sibblings, ages 3-5. They all love Mickey-related toys and such, and this toy allows exploration with the child's imagination, as well as valuable hands-on dexterity activities. Now I have to go back and buy the additional items that are sold separately to round this set out.

Another great volume of the Phantom, this one containing the very last featuring artwork by Ray Moore, and in that one lone tale, both Moore and McCoy share art duties. The rest of the strips feature just Wilson McCoy artwork. Highly recommended for all Phantom fans out there. Really great story lines.

I bought this for a 6-year old boy who loves Batman and who is also learning how to tell time.....what a great combination this watch makes! It's sharp looking and helpful in helping him figure out the time.

For those familiar with Ernie Kovac's comedic genuis, this long awaited CD gathers together his classic Percy sketches as well as newer material not originally seen on TV. A big thumbs up to Edie Adams (Ernie's wife) for getting this collection put together and for making it available to those of us who remember Percy so well. Hopefully it can open the ears of others to enjoy the wild side of Ernie Kovacs.
Bought this for a boy who is a bug fanatic, and does he ever love this classic toy. Yours will too!

After having bought the 4 volumes of the Phantom Daily Strips, I really anticipated this first volume of the Sunday color strips, as I had never read any of them. Lee Falk and Ray Moore come through as usual with fantastic story and art that make this character so popular, even today, some 70+ years after his creation. All Phantom fans will drool over this volume and yell for more!

The 8th volume in this series provides superior writing by the likes of Don Cameron and Bill Finger, and superb art (for the most part) by Dick Sprang (the essential Batman artist) and Jerry Robinson. This material was published in the period just after WW2, and does feature a story each featuring the Joker, the Penguin and the Catwoman, and several "Adventures of Alfred" to boot.
There are tales illustrated by Win Mortimer (whose stiff, cardboard style I never cared for), and the team of Bob Kane and Ray Burnley (whose inks did nothing to enhance Kane's pencils). Still the stories carry themselves and the volume is of note because it does feature a variety of the artists who did Batman over the years.

This disc primarily centers around the groups' latter years of performing together, again featuring alternate takes, studio demos and the like, none of which made it on the final records that were released.

 Particularly noteworthy to me were the versions of "Maxwell's Silver Hammer", "I Will", "Ob-La-Di, Ob-la-Da", "Let it Be", and "Hey Jude", which vary greatly from the released versions, but which I immensely enjoyed anyway.

 Also the tune "Ain't She Sweet", found on an earlier disc and sung by John Lennon.....this version by Paul McCartney.

Another superb volume, a follow-up to the first volume, which includes the complete issues of the Green Lama magazine, #5-8, again featuring the mysterious hero, The Green Lama, written by editors Ken Crossen and Joseph Greene, and again illustrated by the superior Mac Raboy (with the help of Harry Anderson on one story).

Other features include Lt. Hercules, Rick Masters, Angus MacErc, the Boy Champions and more, written and illustrated by the likes of Horace Gold, Irving Tirman, George Roussos, Jerry Robinson, Mort Lawrence, and more.

Another must have volume to add to the first.

Another great release of the classic Shadow pulp novels, featuring two of the best this time around, both written by the unparalled Walter B. Gibson, including Gibson's classic "Golden Vulture", a re-write of the original novel by Lester Dent, and "Crime, Insured," considered to be Gibson's finest novel. You can't go wrong with this book.
