One have to put much faith to believe that the story could be true.
But who knows what really happens behind close doors...
Maybe it is not a work of fiction :)

I like this book, but it was worst than first two parts.
I am not exactly sure why.
The action seems to be swift enough but I wasn't able to read it at once - it was so tedious that I had to take breaks.

I usually don't like very much books with teenager characters.
For various reasons - such characters are not believable (come on, bunch o teenagers (in this case even 12 years old)  that act like old veterans, flying through universe, killing stealing etc.), and whole books are usually written for teenagers with usually has specific style and simplicity.
This case is no different, but fortunately the plot was interesting enough.
Big plus of this book is that it has an end - all main plots are closed, all mysteries are explained. There is second book in series, but you don't have to read it to know how the first ends.

This book definitely needs some cutting/editing/proof reading.
There are pages after pages on which something is going on, but after reading it you realize that the action didn't move on at all.
It would be much netter if author compress the action cutting at least hal of the book.
There is also very much sexuality, especially in first chapters which are filled with sex in maybe 50%?
Is it some kind of harlequin or s-f?
Not to mention that the action itself is very unbelievable.
To be honest I wasn't able to read more than one third of book. So maybe later is better.

This is very good story. It grabbed my attention and I really enjoyed reading it.
It consists of 3 connected storieswith the same characters.
It is about love and honor and how to cope with it in real life where there is no honor and everyone deceits everyone else.

The world as we know it has ended.
We never really find out how long ago (at least few generations, probably more than a century) or how (there is mentioned some kind of plaque).
After this Event group of survivors settled down on a sub-Antarctic island Kerguelen. During dozens of years this society managed to grow and even thrive. They virtually discovered seafaring again and set few island colonies over the world.
Out of nowhere "pirates" jumped. They started attacking Kerguelinian and their settlements without any obvious reason - attacking, destroying and kidnapping settlers.

This is the background and in that moment starts the action.

It is necessary to stand up against pirates, therefore Navy is created.
For start it is only one ship Navy, but still a Navy.
So during the story we witness creating the Navy, its first warship and accompany this first warship and its adventures, including few enemies encounters.

The story is interesting and quick paced, characters are nice. Battle descriptions are very addictive, alas some other part of book is a bit tedious and to wordy (especially first visit on Nosy Be).

There are plenty of inconsistencies, too
Some of them are:

- we never precisely find out why and what happened - nuclear war? meteor impact? - it is important in next one

- Kerguelans think that they are only one technology advanced people on the world. If that is true than it means that all technology advanced people had to gather after Catastrophe and travel to Kerguelen islands becoming their predecessors.

- if catastrophe was plaque than survivors would have gather in one place from all over the world and than travel to Kerguelen - impossible. If it was nuclear war that all would be from one place, not from all over the world so it is impossible, too. If people could prepare for this than they would choose better place to settle so the Catastrophe had to be quite quick. So it is just impossible that nowhere in the world lived another technological society. Yet the radios picked up nothing??  And all natives are described like very primitive peoples.

- why the h*** did those survivors settled on some small island near Antarctic??? There is no wood (all have to be imported), there is cold, windy, it is not friendly for crops or animals (chickens have to live in heated sheds). So why??? Especially that they are making settlements in much more friendly areas like Madagascar.
And how??
It is written than those survivors were from all over the world - Taiwan, France etc. They had to gather somewhere and travel expressly to Kerguelen islands. What sick mind would choose such island??

- why they don't want to settle on main land - only islands and only those uninhabited. There are plenty of ruins on main land so it would be much better to live near it and loot it than loot it and transport back to Antarctic. And there would be much more place to settle. And much better conditions. and resources like wood, coal, animals (food and work).

- they are able to build 100 meters (yes one hundred meter - 330 foots) long cargo ships using metal framework and plywood yet they are unable to produce larger amounts of small guns - 100 pieces for every seaman on first Navy ship is to expensive so most of them have only machetes!!!!. Yet - on Nosy Be 20 of those seamen (not gun experts) where able to produce 60 guns during two weeks.

- they are using boat with Stirling engine to tow big warship. Yet no one ever thought about building this engine into ship itself. OK it was the first warship and there was no enough time to adapt it.
But cargo ships also could extremely gain having such engine and still nobody never did it!!!

I won't mention custom of giving every sailor vodka every day or vodka being present at virtually every meal - what is it - WWII Russian army??

OK, lets not be to cruel and stop here.

The book describes peaceful society trying to survive in harsh conditions after all world being destroyed and almost everybody eradicated.
It should be lesson for everyone who survive. Lesson what hatred, animosities and cruelty could do to humanity.
Unfortunately evil enemy out of nowhere starts destroying everything this society build. It again leads to war, causalities, despair and destruction.
It creates a question about us - can we change? can we become better peoples? can we do it ourself or do we need total destruction of everything around us to trigger any changes? and are we able to learn on our mistakes?

I never read the first book in series.
This one however is quite good.
I like such techno-buble - that is advanced, seem to be realistic enough and is capable of changing the world.
And here there is new operating system capable of work directly inside brain using nano-something.
So everyone can connect to INTERNET directly in his had, do remarkable things like storing data or even modify his own neurotransmitters levels.
I believe such technology will be available in the future and it is nice to read how someone else thinks it could change the world.
What I didn't like was all that buddish, maybe it was important according to first book, but here it is out of place and for nothing, especially without knowledge of first book.

I can recommend this book.
It is quite long, so will last for a while.

The Lost World by Arthur Conan Doyle.

It is an old book - more than a century old. Its writing style is a bit different than in contemporary books, but it is not a flaw.
The story is interesting, action is quick paced, characters are OK.

For me there is only one problem with this book.
It is over century old and I suppose everyone have seen at least one film adaptation. So probably everybody knows what is this book about and what will happen next.
And that is my problem. I couldn't get really excited what will happen next because basically I have already knew :(

users.query: My main concern with using any sort of insecticide (slugicide) is one, that it works, and two, that it doesn't harm my pets or garden. The idea of sprinkling a pile of chemicals next to my lettuce plants just makes me a bit uneasy. This snail killer hits both marks: it is primarily made of sulfur and is rated to be fairly harmless (ok, it isn't going to win any organic, chemical-free gardening awards). My dogs have zero interest in the stuff, but the snails seem to be just the opposite... the devour it. I haven't seen a bunch of slug corpses lying around my yard, but I assume it is working because the plants that were formerly vanishing night by night are thriving and nibble-free again. Can't ask for much more than that.

cands.text: I sprinkled Dr. T's all around my gardens. I have chickens and dogs so I worry about using anything that can harm them. On the other hand, I want something that will kill slugs. I've tried other natural snail killers and I have always been disappointed. It seems that slugs and snails are just as indifferent to the natural killers as my dogs are. Dr. T's worked to kill the slugs. However, I am not sure if I would feel safe using it around my pets. When I use this I put a fence around the area so that my pets can't access it. That being the case, why not just use the cheap stuff and do the same thing?

I live in an older area with lots of ivy, fruit trees and thick bushes/trees. That means we inevitably have lots of rats roaming the neighborhood. The best traps out there that I've found (and I've tried them all), are the good old-fashioned snap traps. But I wanted to try this because it made me feel a little less guilty about catching rats (I hate that awful snap).

This worked ok, but not as well as snap traps (alas). One trap caught a rat early on, and it was stuck fast. The second trap seemed to have a rat visit it, but didn't catch anything. So far, 50% success rate. Since the rats escape my snap traps about 20% of the time, that's not quite as good, but not awful either. I'll keep trying with these, and they are a good alternative. Especially given that I have had 0% success with the balance traps that drop the rat into a bucket or the electric traps.

Gullet sticks are one of those things that are so popular these days, they can sometimes come from seriously shady sources. So I like knowing that my dogs aren't chewing on chemical-laden sticks. My dogs never met a bully stick they didn't like, so I was excited to try something a little different  - chances are that your dog will love them if they love bully sticks. They have a similar feel and look (and taste?).  I and Love and You sources from safe and healthy sources (as far as I can tell). These sticks stink - all bully sticks do, it is just part of chewing on the pizzle of a bull, and it seems like a gullet is no different. But they are such good treats - they last forever, they won't gum up and get stuck in your dog's throat/belly/intestine like rawhide can and they are great for strengthening teeth. I and Love and You's sticks are particularly good because they are a company that is open and transparent with buyers and located in the US. My dogs love these and so do I. My only wish is that they had  larger sticks for bigger/heavier chewers. They do have a 12" bully stick, though.

I keep hoping that someone will come along with an incredible applicator that will take all the mess and fuss out of flea application. Alas... Adams Plus Flea and Tick Control for Dogs is no better (and no worse) than the competitors. The applicator sort of works, it's a little messy, and I find that just using gloved hands works best (with this and all other flea treatments I've tried).

Once you get the product applied, though, it works great. The formula is made to address fleas and ticks at every life stage, and with the warmer winters and increased deer populations in my area, that's important. This works great at keeping the fleas at bay, and I haven't found a single tick yet.

So as long as you aren't purchasing this for the applicator, you will be satisfied with this product and so will your pooch.

I have used other Orb-3 products and loved them, so I had no hesitation trying the Orb03 antifoam. Because I have dogs and plenty of wildlife in my backyard, I hesitate to use chemicals in my pond. But foam and other issues can really make my pond look unattractive. So I love this product because it is everything you could possibly ask for: food grade, safe for animals, natural AND it WORKS! I have small pond, so this bottle will last me a long time, especially given that the bubbles stayed away for days (I added this several days ago and the bubbles have not returned). Plus, I don't have to worry when my dog sneaks a sip of pond water!

Hay fever, dogs, an old house under construction, life in a polluted city - I have all the uneasy breathing culprits, so I knew I would be putting this thing through its paces. I used this in my master bedroom (250 square feet) and I have been beyond happy.

The AeraMax comes with two filters - HEPA and carbon. It has a small footprint, which is nice in a small room, and it looks sleek and modern in the space. The interface is easy to use with straight-forward buttons that are very responsive. There is a night/day mode so you can have bright or low illumination depending on the ambient light, in addition to fan control, a lock and an alert that lets you know what level of purification the purifier is running at (high, med, low).

Very quiet, this is generally silent when it is running on low, but for those times that it kicks up into a higher gear, it sounds like a fan. It wouldn't be loud enough to wake you up, but it is definitely noticeable.

So how does it work? Amazing. I have noticed fewer allergies and it kicks into high gear whenever I do something that releases dust (spray my hair with dry shampoo, shake a rug, etc.) so I know it is working. I don't have a good way of testing fine particles, but the visible dust in the air is definitely reduced and I have noticed a change in air quality. I can't comment on whether this is good for babies, but for an adult, it is awesome.

I have 3 dogs and a big yard, so I know from mud and hair in my house. I need a vacuum that can tackle it all and that doesn't get full so fast I have to empty it a dozen times just to get the house down. The Bissell Cleanview is a great option for people like me.

CONS:
It doesn't pick up as well as my Oreck Upright - in fact, pretty much no other vacuum I've tried does, and none retains the suction that my Oreck has, even after 5 years. That said, it is pretty good. It gets my longer carpets and hardwoods with equal skill. I'd give it a 6 out of 10.
The power cord is SO SHORT! It is the shortest of any vacuum I've ever used. I also hate that it comes out of the base and has to attach to a little clip up near the handle.
The attachment hose is pretty short, too. The hose fits loose in its setting.
The power switch is really inconvenient to access.

PROS:
The bin on this is HUGE. It is the only bagless vacuum I've used that can tackle my whole house without needing emptying in the middle.
It disassembles easily to clean it or get any clogs out.
All of the attachments ride on the vacuum, so you don't have to store them off-vacuum.
The canister is super easy to empty and re-seat. It is very clear so you can easily see when it is time to empty.

For the money, this is a great vacuum. Though it doesn't pick up as well as my Oreck, the Oreck also doesn't have all the bells and whistles and isn't bagless, so you have to factor that in.

I'm new to the pond game, but as my pond has aged, it has gotten decidedly murky. I don't have fish, but I have plenty of plant life and it seems that perhaps things have gotten a bit off balance. The Orb3 enzymes, however, have gotten me back on track. I can see the bottom of my pond again after only a few days. I love that it works by naturally balancing the bacteria in my pond rather than clearing it out with chemicals, since I installed the pond to get a little bit of nature in my yard in the first place. I will update my review after a month or so in case things change, but right now, I would definitely recommend this.

For reference, I have a 10x10 pond with a sheet waterfall and a single pump and bubbler. I live in a dry climate, have no fish, but I do see the occasional frog. Wildlife loves to visit my pond and I have seen no negative effects so far, the birds and frogs continue to visit. My dogs also drink from the pond (despite my protests) and they seem no worse for the wear either.

If you have a murky or green pond, I would definitely recommend that you pick this up, it is well worth it.

I can't even tell you how many times I have grumbled to myself as I've had to switch between a nozzle and a sprinkler to keep the dry patches and gardens in my hard happy. I've even resorted to sort of wedging a spray nozzle between some rocks as a sort of rigged sprinkler when I was truly desperate. So this... this is so freakin smart, I can't believe it hasn't been done before.

So let's break this into its parts, because no matter how cool the combination may be, it isn't truly useful unless it is functional individually.

As a spray nozzle, it exceeds my expectations. It has a wide variety of spray functions, from mists, to rain to streams. All function as they should and when they should have pressure, they do, and when they should be soft and gentle, they are. So already, it is absolutely worth having just as a top notch nozzle.

Then there is the sprinkler function. Just flip out the wings and place it where you need it, and voila. This, too, works wonderfully. The wings are large enough and sit far enough apart that they hold the sprinkler in place, no rolling or shifting. The wings have a slight blade edge to them (it isn't sharp) to allow you to secure the sprinkler in place if you need to.

Taken as a whole, the whole thing is very sturdy, with metal and heavy plastic parts. The weight makes me so happy, because not only does it hold the sprinkler in place, but it is larger than the average nozzle, so it feels substantial and not like you have a toy attached to the end of your hose. It also has a filter in the handle so that you don't get clogged nozzle functions, which is the bane of my nozzle existence.

Absolutely excellent, from start to finish. This deserves an extra star.

I should warn you that my dog is not an objective resource when it comes to food - she will eat anything. Seriously. Every fall I have to defend my pumpkin patch because she will dive in and eat the pumpkins before the shells get too hard to get through. So I wasn't shocked that my dog loves it. But as for me, I give it four stars - it's not a high end kibble, but neither is it grocery-store quality. It doesn't have cheap fillers or artificial colors, which I appreciate, though it is a bit lower in protein (21%) than I prefer. The kibble is a nice size - smaller than a lot of other foods (about the size of a dime). The fact that the ingredient list is half of what most dog foods seem to be makes me happy and my dogs waste is firm and small on this food, which is good. Other mid-range foods can give her soft stools.

Because I can't let the last word in this review be "stools," I just want to reiterate that my dog loves the flavor and, for the price, I love it too.

My poor dogs (cocker spaniel and newfoundland) have terribly itchy skin, a gift from the dry climate and allergies, so I am always looking for something to keep them calm. Itchy skin is no fun at all. At the same time, I hate the chemical smell that most medicated shampoos have. But Fresh n Clean combines the power of medicated shampoo with the neutral odor I crave. My dogs are less itchy and a little goes a long way. I expect this bottle to last a good long time and when it is gone I will definitely be buying more because my dogs seem much less irritated, which makes all of us happy.

Kirschner is a skilled writer and she manages to breathe life into a character that could easily be overshadowed by her famous common-law husband.

Josephine Marcus Earp spent 50-years with Wyatt Earp (of OK Corral fame) but she rarely makes the Tombstone story. Kirschner remedies this oversight, painting the portrait of a complex, fascinating character that has been shrouded in myth and misunderstanding. Covering Josephine's youth through her death, Kirschner leaves nothing out, and the result is a story of an all-too-human woman making her way through history.

Inevitabley, Kirschner spends maybe too much time on Tombstone itself, which really didn't involve Josephine too much, but it is difficult to tell the story of the Earps without understanding the history that drove them. I was particularly fascinated by the Alaska years and Josephine's fight to control the Wyatt Earp story.

I really enjoyed this book despite the fact that I came into it expecting to hate it. There isn't anything new here - it basically boils down to eat food, not too much, mostly plants (thanks Michael Pollan!) and get your butt moving. But it is written in a conversational style and helps to remind you of the things that you should be doing.

There aren't any secrets in this book, just lots of solid, tried and true tips that most of us know but often ignore or forget. Definitely worth the read if you are looking for a fun, quick read to remind you how to get or stay healthy.

As a standard water filtering pitcher, this is great, but I seriously question its anti-bacterial capabilities. As a pitcher, I'd rate it 5 stars. As an anti-bacterial filter, just 1 star. Besides the matter of verifying the filter's efficacy, which I think other reviewers have covered nicely, I also noticed that a small amount of water seeps around the filter itself into the pitcher, which would mean that any bacteria in the water would be dripping into your filtered water. I'd hoped to use this to fill my neti pot and humidifiers, but I won't now since I am not sure that it can be trusted to be pure.

That said, it is a brilliant design, very modern looking and slim so it fits nicely in the fridge. As a filter, it gives me that fresh clean taste that I expect from a water filter. The large (8 cup) reservoir holds the water prior to filtering and then it is fed into the filter and down into the lower reservoir where your fresh water awaits. The filter is a snap to change and a little sliding piece tucked into the lid of the filter reminds you when it is time to change it up. It fills rather slowly, but since you can just top off the reservoir and let it do its thing, it is no big deal. A great pitcher at a great price, just don't rely on it to purify  your water.

It was a pretty safe bet that my dogs would love this stuff. I have yet to come across a Stella & Chewy product that they aren't crazy about. But my dogs are not crazy about their regular dry food, so having something that I can put on top as an enticement is so nice. The only bad thing is that they want to pick the mixers out and just ignore the rest of their food - it's that good.

Stella & Chewy reliably uses high quality ingredients that I feel comfortable giving my dogs. One of my dogs has a sensitive stomach, so I avoid giving her things that will upset her stomach. This doesn't cause any loose stools/vomiting and they LOVE the taste. Since I only put a scoop on top of their food and mix it in, it doesn't cost a fortune and I know my dogs are getting healthy food that they also love. I am a huge fan of Stella & Chewy, and this is another product that lives up to their excellent reputation.

Nutro makes a consistently good product that my dogs really enjoy. That said, it does contain a few ingredients I'd rather avoid, like wheat, coloring and corn starch, which aren't necessarily dangerous, but are definitely a sign of a cheap filler. That said, there are no by-products, no unhealthy ingredients and nothing that sets off alarm bells.

My dogs don't care about any of that, though. I've given them lots of gravy toppings on their food, and this seems to be their fav. I have one puppy and one not-quite a puppy, but I feed them both this food on top of their usual food as a treat, not as a meal. So far, no gas, no loose stools, no dryness or itchy skin. That's a big deal. I'd question some of the sources of the ingredients, since Mars isn't known for being exactly careful about their sources, but it also isn't nearly as expensive as some other foods, so it is a compromise.

As a treat, this is a great food that compromises between cost and quality.

This is an adorable toy and a lot of fun in the bathtub, kiddie pool or even right in the bowl. If your kid isn't ready for real pets, this is also a fun temporary substitute. Unfortunately, the fish is a bit hard to get the batteries into and they only last a couple of hours. I've been using rechargeable batteries because I can't imagine how much it would cost if your kid plays with this a ton.

The fish can only swim in circles, which makes it great in the bowl but a little silly in the tub. Nonetheless, we had fun with it and Lucky is even considered a must-have at bath time now - he is considered a friend. You can add fish tot he set if you want a fuller aquarium, but you'd better have a ton of batteries ready (or a set constantly on the charger). On the bright side, the kids love it and it has worked flawlessly in its non-stop swimming.

I feel bad for Valenti. The vitriolic spew that she must be receiving from both sides of the mommy wars (not my term) has got to be painful. If there is any topic out there sure to get blood boiling, it's parenting. And what Valenti has done in "Why Have Kids?" is sure to stir the pot even more.

In her book, Valenti explores the common truths and lies about being a parent - an in particular, being a mom. Each chapter addresses a different truth or lie, from the often repeated myth of "parenting is the hardest job in the world" to the truth that many mothers who fail to raise children as expected by society go to jail.

I found myself needing to look up statistics and sources a few times - hence the 4 stars - because Valenti doesn't include many sources. But the information that this book introduced is thought provoking, turning many assumptions on their heads.

Whether you are a parent, considering becoming a parent, or are simply concerned about the way that women are treated in the U.S., this is an excellent book. A great overview of the motherhood debate.

I used to get a monthly subscription box for my dogs. They LOVE the toys, but they always hated the treats, which drove me crazy, because the treats were very healthy! So I've been on the hunt for treats that are simple, healthy, and something that will motivate my dogs. Buckley Functional Immunity treats are the ticket! My dogs will climb out of bed for these and they are made with healthy ingredients that I don't feel guilty feeding to my pups. They actually smell like jerky, and they have a satisfying snap that my dogs seem to like.

I have no idea if this helps my dogs joints or skin or whatever - a small bag of treats probably won't make a difference in any dog's life - but over time if we keep buying them, maybe they will. They certainly didn't upset my dog's tummies and even if they don't improve my dog's health, the ingredients let me know that it won't hurt them. And, importantly, my dogs can't get enough of them.

I was pleasantly surprised by this book. I, perhaps unfairly, expected some lecturing and moralizing and general guilt-inducing from this book. Instead I got a well-written and very entertaining account of one woman's tale of testing the carnivorous waters. I think that vegetarians choosing to eat sustainable meat is a situation that is becoming more and more common and this book fills the void of discussion around this topic and it does it with flair and style.

There are a few studies mentioned in the book that lean towards eliminating meat and I didn't feel that they were balanced by studies stating the contrary, but this book isn't so much a debate about what you should do but a story about what the author experienced. I would highly recommend this book.

I am an adult woman and purchased these because they are cheaper than the adult version and my adult size is sold out everywhere. I was worried that they would be inferior quality or an odd fit, but no. They are perfect, just like the adult version but sized for small feet. These sneakers are a classic for a reason.

Invicta is one of those brands that marks its recommended price way, way up and then sells for far less - in this case, $90 down from $700. Knowing that you are purchasing a $90 watch rather than a $700 watch will go a long way in terms of managing your expectations.

This watch is NOT a diver's watch, it is a diver-looking watch. It is only water resistant to 100m and the bezel doesn't move. That said, I think it is a fun, modern looking watch. I generally prefer the look of a men's watch to women's, but if you have a smaller wrist, this watch will look MASSIVE. It is a solid, sturdy, and very, very large watch. I let my husband and brother try it on, and it even looked large on them. It isn't just the face that is large, it is the band as well, which is thick and wide. That's not a bad thing, just worth noting if you are a woman who likes to wear men's watches.

The matte, polyurethane band is a modern take and I really like the way it looks with a leather jacket, but it does tend to collect lint. The bold, inky black face is really fun, I love the large time markers. I find the bezel numbers to look a little overly large and cheap, but that is my main complaint about this watch. It doesn't feel as tight and solid as a high end watch, but it certainly feels much, much nicer than your average $100 watch.

Bottom line is that this a great looking modern watch with a trendy look.

Let's just get one thing out of the way first: I love the design of this book. Sure, it has all the requisite mouthwatering food photos. But it's also cheeky and fun. And has Acheson's original illustrations. I love it when cookbooks are fun to look at and not just informative. Still, that's not why you're here, so - onto the meat...

The Chef and the Slow Cooker starts out with a great intro that includes tips for making your food zing, along with some basic life philosophy for embracing the now (every cookbook worth its salt makes you a better person, right?). From there you jump into basics - the broths and stocks you will need as a base for many of the recipes, or, as Acheson calls them, the Jacuzzi for the main ingredient. Take my advice and make a few of these ahead of time to store - it will cut lots of time off your prep in the future.

From there we are off to the races with bean-based dishes. The White Bean Soup is DTF and I made it entirely in the slow cooker (no skillets or pans required). Then it's on to my personal favorite - the soups. Finally, a recipe for Pho that tastes like my favorite restaurant. Maybe better. And the Chicken Soup with Chiles, Coconut Milk and Lime... my mouth is watering thinking about it. Hang on, I have to go reheat my leftovers.

Right. So, then there is a chapter on veggie-based meals. I haven't tried any yet, but they look great (butter braised cabbage, spring stew, yum). Then there's seafood - if you don't put the Miso-braised salmon in your face ASAP, you will regret it for the rest of your life. Then on to the poultry. My husband made the Kimchi Chicken for dinner yesterday and it was out of this world. It was also stupid easy. The next chapter finally answers the question "Where's the beef" (it's here, in this book). I haven't tried any, yet, but my mouth waters just flipping through the chapter. Finally, we have pork and then lamb/goat, and ending with sweets.

Most of the recipes give you at least 4 hours of freedom, though a few are shorter or longer, so be sure to check how much free time each recipe gives you before you commit. There are also things you can do to cheat a little if you want to skip a step. For instance, the Hoppin' John calls for soaking peas overnight, but you could always use canned peas and cut down the prep time.

Some of the dishes - not all - call for a good some handling. These recipes are not all set-it-an- forget-it types, but rather, recipes that utilize a slow cooker to its maximum advantage. You can cut out some of the steps that take place outside of the slow cooker if you have an Instant-Pot type machine where you can sear right in the pot if you are looking to simplify. There are also lots of recipes that are just toss ingredients in and forget it, but if you ONLY want those types of recipes, I'd probably get one of the beginner-type slow cooker cookbooks. There are several awesome ones to choose from. This is targeted at a more gourmet audience.

The recipes are nothing like the standard slow fare out there and your guests will never believe you used that old crockpot from the '70s to make such amazing food. This isn't the standard mushy slow cooker fare of yore. There are, of course, the classics, like brisket, but jam? Beef cheeks with apple slaw? Lobster tacos? Poached eggs? Freakin' breakfast in the slow cooker? Oh yes.

The bottom line is this: this is a slow cooker recipe for the slightly more adventurous and for those who want a more elegant end product. It's a slow-cooker book from a Chef's perspective (as the book's title implies). The recipes are clear and easy to follow, but they sometimes include ingredients that may be harder to find and many of the recipes include some searing in a pan/chopping/prep before you dump everything into the slow cooker. Some even have some legwork during or after the cooking. The extra work gives you a far superior flavor, but if you only want to dump everything in without any prep, this book isn't your jam. If you are more of the type who loves to cook and has already mastered the basic slow-cooker recipes floating out there (or has been scarred by your mom's slow cooker meals from when you were a kid), pick this up yesterday.

As long as I don't have to say its name, I love this dog food. My dogs love it too.

I and love and you uses top-notch ingredients that are all natural and mostly sourced in the US. But even better, they also focus on sustainability, which isn't that common in dog food. Being grain free and free from fillers and artificial additives also takes this food to the next level. I challenge you to find another dog food with such a short list of identifiable ingredients: lamb, split peas, sweet potato, cabbage, eggs, flaxseed, banana, almond mean, spinach, alfalfa, kelp, ginger root, salt, and a few additives. It also has a good ration of protein to carbs and fat.

I found it easy to soften the food with a little warm water - cold water takes a little longer to mix in.

Whenever I switch to a new dog food, I always check recalls. I and love and you has never had a mandatory recall, but even better, they issued a voluntary recall once when they identified salmonella in one of their supply chains. Now that is an ethical company.

Of course, the final word comes down to my dogs: will they eat it? Absolutely, they love it, and it has made their skin and fur look better than ever.

users.query:
Ray Garton will not disappoint you this Halloween with this fictionalized account of Halloween 1974. As you've probably heard many times over, truth is stranger than fiction. Well, in this case it's more horrifying than fiction.

The '70s were a new era for kids. It was no longer safe to go trick or treating in your neighborhood. Find out just how awful it was in this quick bite of Halloween terror.

Highly recommended!

cands.text:
Halloween is my favorite holiday and I'm always on the lookout for great reading material on the subject. When I saw Lisa Morton and Ellen Datlow pop up as editors on a new Halloween anthology, you bet I checked on it. All I needed to see was the addition of John Little and I requested the book!

17 authors give it it their all, including Jonathan Maberry, Kate Jonez, and Eric Guignard. I'm only going to talk about a couple of my favorite stories by new authors I have never read.

JACK - by Pat Cadigan, I loved this story! It may have been my favorite in the collection by a previously unknown to me author. With 15 books behind them, I have no excuse. JACK is a wonderful tale of a watchful family.

DIRTMOUTH - by Stepthen Graham Jones, another winner for me. Wife died and is missed, maybe the family can remember the good times at their cabin.

SISTERS - by Brian Evenson was way fun rather than the typical scary story. It's impossible to say anything without spoiling. Just enjoy.

Like many anthologies not every story will strike everyone the same. For me, most of these were pretty darn good and averaged out to 4 stars. Recommended to all Halloween lovers!

This small collection of short stories is the perfect Halloween lovers read. It's not graphic and gory but subtle and extremely well written fiction of the darkest calibre. You can pull it out year after year and enjoy.

I hope you do.

Deliciously creepy, downright scary and practically perfect in every way. James Moore assembled his Halloween short stories in one volume.

If I had to say something negative about the book, it would be that it ran out of words and I had to stop reading. MORE, Mr. Moore, please!

Highly recommended!

For all the bad reviews, I really enjoyed this (very short) novella.  While it only took up half the space it claimed,  it was still a nice ghostly story.

What was causing ghosts to appear on Dean Evers new HDTV as watched his baseball games while relaxing in his new home in Florida?  Doctors, old partners and even his wife were showing up in the best seat in the house.

Some people find this novella to be slow moving, but baseball is slow moving to some compared to football.  I liked it.  I liked the ending.  It was definitely a creepy Stephen King ending.

Maybe it was a little pricy for such a short story, but do King fans really care?  I don't.

Ever read Magic by William Goldman? Do ventriloquist dummy's scare you/creep you out? Dolls, clowns and other inanimate objects scare me.

Tim Curran went outside the box with Puppet Graveyard.  You have never read a book like this before.  Trust me, you really haven't.  Tim had me squirming in my chair and after a certain scene, I simply stopped reading.  Just stopped, took a break and finished the book the next day.

I read a lot of horror.  I'm jaded.  Run of the mill horror books don't bother me.  You have been warned.  This is not for the faint of heart.

Do dolls bother you? Do mannequins freak you out just a bit? Tim Curran knows what scares and has written not a passage but a whole book of terror.

DOLL FACE starts out with a simple Twilight Zone-like premise that quickly degenerates into your worst nightmares come to life. This heartpounding, action-packed novel should be read when you are alone at home at night for best results. Have your local emergency number programmed into your phone and your doctor standing by...

You have been warned. I highly recommend this book if you want sleepless nights and awesome reading.

A copy of this book was provided by the publisher in exchange for my review.

I enjoyed this novel about monster hunters with a sense of humor. One of my favorite lines was "Since most people wouldn't accept the existence of the supernatural if it pooped in their Christmas pudding, the task falls to people like us."

There's a variety of supernatural entities in this book. Murder and mayhem ensue.  It's not really gross...well, do wormy pigeons bother you?  That was pretty interesting!

We also find that religious artifacts aren't the key to killing the paranormal. What is? Michael Boatman tells the tale in an easy to read style that I sped right through. He also left it open for sequels. I would love to read more.

If you're young and impressionable, this is bound to scare the crap out of you. Johnstone wrote some of the finest horror of the 80's and he didn't leave anything out of this one. A scary toy, insane family, and a whole lot of butchering goes on in this haunted house.

This is one of many William Johnstone books of horror that is being re-released by Kensington books - Lryical Underground. I plan to get every one. This is the horror that I love. It's well plotted and a satisfying read. While I wondered at the opening, I shouldn't have. It was all explained at the end.

And on another note, there are subjects brought up that are as pertinent today as they were then.

5 stars for Rockinghorse! Thank you to Kensington Books for my copy.

Advance Review Copy

Some of the best authors in the business contribute to this collection of dark horror that is sure to give you the shivers. Check 'em out: Gary Braunbeck, Willie Meikle, Joe Lansdale, Max Booth III, and the names go on and on. Joe and Max's stories were very dark - and very enjoyable. I'm used to them writing more humorous stories. Lucy Snyder's story was so good, such a great way to start the collection. John F.D. Taff is in there as well. I don't think he can tell a bad story.

Don't miss the foreword by Laird Barron! I tend to just skim forewords, but hey, it's Laird Barron. You'll want to read this one.

Yeah, there were a couple of stories that were just ok. That's the way it falls. But the great stories more than make up for that. Don't miss out on this one. It's awesome.

The story gets going in a Walmart with a screeching child in the candy aisle. Sounds like my Walmart. And while normally a day could only get better after that, there's nothing normal for the hero of our story. His day is definitely taking a downward plunge into an empty pool. As bad as things are, there are scenes you can't help but shake your head and laugh at - but then wipe that grin, things only get worse.

Phil and his son are nothing like you and your kid. Read this! It's awesome.

I got my copy as a member of KBP's Digital50.

4 3/4 stars

I'm not a person who normally likes ghost stories.  They tend to be silly or just gory/scary for no reason.  I also thought only Neil Gaiman could write a good ghost story followed by Stephen King. Now Neil is followed very closely in my mind by Bradley Convissar.

Why?  Not only is this a ghost story set in modern times, it has a message.  Like the old Twilight Zones and Star Trek:TOS, it makes you think and feel.  This is the second story that I've read by BC that affected me after I put it down and I couldn't go on to read another book.  As you can tell, I'm a cat person, but these dogs...if you're a dog person...read it!  You will be touched. I promise.

Why 4 3/4 stars?  The title. I judge a book by it's cover and title.  I passed this book up for the longest time without looking at it (I know what assume means) and thought it was literally a war book.  It brought to mind Iraq and Viet Nam.  So, I dropped a 1/4 only for that reason. I'm sorry that I did.

It's a great story.

Ok, so you know what the story is about. I don't need to tell you about that. What you need to know is Joe Hill can tell a story like nobody's business. If you're thinking, hey, he wrote that haunted suit book that I DNF and I haven't read him since, well, let me tell you I think that finishing THE FIREMAN might have left me speechless. The only thing I can think to say about THE FIREMAN is

WOW!

This is over 600 pages of pure storytelling. It's about people. You have plenty of time to get to know the people. You can love them, hate them, cry with them and laugh with them.

When I started this book I found myself reading way too fast. I could tell from the outset that it was a very good book. I forced myself to slow down and savor it. It took me 6 days to finish. I took my kindle everywhere and read in the car. It was an amazing experience drawing it out that way and I feel like I didn't miss anything.

The writing is exceptional., the storytelling second to none. Don't miss this one.

I received my copy from the publisher in exchange for a review.

I loved this book.  It's a story about people.  Yes, people. No zombie apocalypse to be found here, just people with all their foibles and messy ways.

Author Kelli Owen takes her time building the plot and the characters and then takes a sudden swan dive into the horror that we never see coming.  And when you do finally see the entire picture I'm quite sure that you'll be cringing and gasping just as much, if not more than I was.

I highly recommend you make this your next read.

Fantastic! 35 dark fiction stories from the publisher of Cemetery Dance. The title - A LONG DECEMBER - comes from the final story, actually a novella length piece about a serial killer. These stories are classic dark fiction, not necessarily horror, and show the influences of Robert Bloch and Richard Matheson among others. One story, which shall remain nameless (for your reading enjoyment!) clearly showed a Stephen King influence in a "what if?" kind of way.

I received my copy of A LONG DECEMBER from the publisher, Subterranean Press and highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys reading dark fiction.

Bleak and twisted are but two of the dark adjectives I will begin to use to describe this latest work by Jon Bassoff.  And work it was.  As he jumped from gruesome lobotomy to yet more gruesome bloody lobotomy I kept asking myself why I was subjecting myself to this type of horror.  Yes, I love psychological horror - anything that has to do with the mind can work for me.  This psychiatrist, crazy though he himself might be, could possibly be one to cure some psychoses in the brain.  Unfortunately, he couldn't tell that he was making matters worse.

I felt that Bassoff's writing was too slow for this story.  I kept putting the book away and reading others.  I think I went back at least a half dozen times  or more before I was able to get through all the very dark pages.  I was pleased that the writing up to par - he didn't play with style - if you like the subject, it was quite readable.  This just wasn't for me.

I received my copy of THE INCURABLES from the publisher.  You can buy yours by clicking the link above.

Like the wise man said, it's a love story. But it's a horror story as well.  The story is so well told - like all of Kelli Owen's tales - that you'll finish this with a sigh and a yearning for more.

Recommended reading.

I've read all of Toby Tate's horror/thriller books and just didn't know what to expect from this when he asked me to read and review it. I'm an old school SF fan. I prefer the 'classics'.

Well, Toby did not disappoint at all. His science was spot on. His fiction was exciting. His characters engaging. He reminded me somewhat of David Gerrold...and I consider that extremely high praise, indeed.

Chloe, as you saw from the description, is a genius 16 year old. Some may think because there is a 16 year old protagonist that this is a young adult book.  I don't think so. Both my husband and I (that cute old couple) enjoyed the book and plan on reading as many as are up to this standard.

I suggest you buy and read this asap!

The book is listed under horror, but it would be better filed under 'far right thumpin' deplorable readin''.

I look forward to reading anything that speaks of horror and carnivals, fairs, etc. You might get the impression that this would be a great read. Up to this book I loved all of Johnstone's horror books now being re-released. Let me tell you why I thought this one sucked.

The first couple of chapters set the stage for the story, the very long story. The much too long story. It appeared to me that the author really wanted to write a western. Whenever he didn't know where to go with the horror novel, he just kept writing...a western. I skimmed a full 10% at one point before he got back on track.

He kept repeating himself until I asked myself why I was still reading. Answer: I paid for this POS. Other things that made me scream: a description of a bumper sticker on a pickup truck: Nuke their ass and take the gas. upset at a 6 time child molester finally getting payback.

So, I finally reach 'Book 2' and 57% where a bible collection has begun and I decide that there are better books and my time would be better spent reading them. Originally I was going to be generous and go with two or three stars for the fun the horror portion of the book gave me. But lack of editing and all around idiocy and the light of day reminds me that that everyone pens a loser. So, 1 star. Sorry

No more zombies. Now we have second lifers. And there are such religious overtones in this book it made my head spin - somewhat like Regan in The Exorcist.  Now even the undead have rights. Oh, please.

This is a brilliant horror story, I mean sci-fi/social commentary short story that should scare the heck out of every thinking person during this election year in the US.

Very well done, Mr. Hicks. I highly recommend this.

NORTHWOODS is the sequel to THE BEAST OF BARCROFT.  Bill Schweigart brings his fantastic writing talents back into play, this time to the north woods of Wisconsin.  If you're looking for gore and action and an X-Files type storyline, look no further.  NORTHWOODS has the creatures you want also.

I enjoyed this very much. I hope you do also.  I received my copy from Random House/Hydra.

THE STEPMOTHER - always the evil one isn't she? I thought it was a retelling of the Snow White fairy tale, but imo, no, not so much. So, with my hopes dashed and yet another cast of unlikable characters (this is two in a row) I plodded through and nearly stopped reading this tale of a mousy woman who managed to snag a rich man after a whirlwind romance,

They both had kids, but we won't get into his not being called a wicked stepfather. They got married so quickly they never really got around to getting to know each other. And, there was the story. Finally it all began to come out about midway in the book. I'm glad I didn't give up, because it really did get convoluted. The author did not drop clues, she simply revealed as it suited her. To me that's not good writing. But it was an interesting storyline.

I received THE STEPMOTHER from Bookoutoure in exchange for my review. I gave it 3.5 stars, but rounded down.

The only genre more over-written than zombies is sparkly vampires. I don't read either one. They both normally lack any kind of of character development.  Severed wasn't any different. I really prefer character driven stories.

If you're into violence, however, this just might be the novel for you.
The problem with insanity is that no one understands it but the insane. This novella was stunning. It's obvious to me why it's an award winner. Well done, Craig. Brilliant work.

I filled it with mixed 50:1 ratio gas and two cycle oil, followed the starting directions exactly, and I was happy that it started right up. I let it run for a few minutes, shut it off, and let it rest for a while. I went to start it again already knowing that it runs, but this time I tried starting it the same way I start my other Homelite blower, a MightyLite, which is less involved and quite a bit different. Big mistake. I pulled and pulled and not even a burp.

Thinking I flooded it, I let it rest for about 15 minutes and tried starting it following the directions again, still nothing. I ended up taking out the spark plug and cleaning it, blowing air into the head through the spark plug hole, taking off the carb and blowing air into it, then put it all back together. Followed the directions to a T and what do you know, it started. Reluctantly at first but it started and ran great after that. Once it warmed up, I shut it off and immediately tried to start it without going through the whole process. I just left the choke off and the throttle about half way and after two pulls it started right up.

In summary, NO MATTER HOW YOU START OTHER SMALL ENGINES, FOLLOW THE DIRECTIONS GIVEN WITH THIS ONE EXAXTLY WHEN STARTING COLD. Once warmed up it should start without priming or using full choke. If it doesn't start after a couple of pulls, let it rest a few minutes then use the cold start procedure. Following this method I haven't had one problem with it starting.

As for the performance, is this the most powerful blower you can get? No. However, at $65 which is half the price of a new one and about 1/3 the price of a top of the line blower, is it better than using a broom or lugging a cord around? Heck yes! I'm very happy I bought this blower.

I originally had the same fire pit with a copper base but the screen finally met it's end. I was looking to just replace the mesh screen but they were just about as expensive as the whole unit, so I decided to purchase this Stainless Steel version. It is sturdy and attractive. It's nice to be able to just roll the screen up out of the way instead of having to lift off the screen and place it to the side as with most other fire pits.

Just a few notes. You will have to assemble the base and screen, and while it is not very difficult, it was a little trickier and more time consuming than I would've thought. Also, even though the bowl is stainless steel, a cover is a must. The screen will rust over time. One last tip is to drill a few small holes in the bottom of the bowl. This will keep you from having a mess in the bowl if it rains while letting the fire pit cool before you cover it.

Easy to use and fit the vehicle. Just cut it to size, heat the ends in boiling water and insert the metal tube in both ends. I think some small clamps should be included as well. I installed the fuel line and checked it and there were no leaks. VERY IMPORTANT! I did have an engine fire the next day. I'm not saying it was because of the fuel line as it was too far gone to tell the cause but it was in the same area. I would recommend that you maybe install some clamps and check it often for leaks.
These clamps aren't cheap but work much better than the standard clamps. Getting the right size is a little tricky but once you do, they hold the pipes nice and tight.

I use this for a key holder and am pretty rough with it. It last me about a month before the string can't take anymore. I'm a delivery driver and make about a 120 stops a day. If you use it for a badge reel or a key holder that you don't use as much as I do, it should hold up well. Good spring retraction.

Like others, I've tried those carpet pads that are supposed to keep rugs from slipping but was never satisfied. This stuff is great! No more slipping rugs and I can even vacuum the edges without them moving or lifting. I've even used it for the rugs on my hardwood floors without damage. If I need to remove the tape from the hardwood floor, I just use a hair dryer to heat the glue and remove the tape carefully.

Ever try hanging plastic dust barriers before sanding walls during remodeling? For one person to do it is not an easy task. This tape makes it so much easier. Again, heat the tape with a hair dryer and remove carefully to avoid damage to walls.

There are many other uses and will be buying more soon.
Bought this for my LG VX8300 phone and so far no problems. I have bought several other items with the Kingston brand and have been very satisfied.

I needed a hole saw to put in two round electrical boxes for exterior coach lamps. I was going through 3/4 waynescoat and did get the holes drilled but had drill from both inside and out. It definetly wasn't easy and had to stop once to straighten the saw as it bent once while sawing. It's cheaply made but will get the job done eventually with patience. If you need to make a lot of holes, or plan on using it often, I'd look elsewhere. If you're looking for multiple saw sizes for occasional light use, a handy case, and all for less than the cost of one top of the line hole saw, then this is it.

The heater bracket is pretty flimsy and made of thin steel, but for the price I could've lived with and fixed that. The next thing I noticed was the heat level knob was almost upside down. To see what levels I was setting, I had to either bend over and turn my head all the way to the side or sit on the ground. Still, for the price, probably would've kept it.

After lighting the burners on high and letting it run for a while I bent over to change the setting to medium and the burners went out. I tried it several times before deciding to return the heater. It's too bad to because they really pumped out some good heat on high. Maybe I just got a lemon but probably going to fork up a little more cash and get a better one.

The other reviews are mostly right, this is good if you only have a couple of doors to do. You have to do some modification and use longer screws to hold it in place. Also, take your time as this being plastic it tends to move some. So check your measuremnets and maybe mark the location on both side to make sure you're lined up right when drilling. You still need chisel and hammer for clean-up on the latch plate.

Even though it takes a little more time and effort than I thought, I think it's still is a good value for occasional use. I just wish this exact same kit would have been made in cast aluminum, it would have been worth paying a little more for. I haven't used the hinge plate template yet so I can't comment on that. I'll try to remember and update when I do.

The leaf blower starts and runs fine. I was a little disappointed in the blowing power though. I previously owned the Homelite Yardbroom 25cc and it seemed more powerful. It may be because the blower tube narrows on the end on the MightyLite. I did a little modification on the tube by cutting the end off and attaching some pvc tubing and a 90% elbow and it seems to work better. Haven't had a chance to test it thoroughly yet but the leaves are falling. I was kind of surprised at the packaging, there was none. Just put in a flimsy box which was pretty mangled.

Overall, for the price, I'm pretty satisfied. When it arrived I put the tube on, I had mixed gas already so I poured it in and it started right up.

This trimmer line is just what I needed. I have a Homelite gas trimmmer and it's a little tough getting it to snap in the plastic clips that hold the line when replacing it on the spool. It will go with some coercing though. Once you get it in, this is one tough line. It's thicker than the one recommended for the trimmer but it lasts a lot longer. I can blast weeds in rocks, roots, and wire fencing without it breaking. I also use it to edge the lawn. Just a side note, mine didn't come on a spool like the one pictured, it was in a molded plastic package.
