This exhuast hanger is just what the doctor ordered. I have an old Astro van that no matter how many times I readjusted and tightened the clamps the exhaust pipe kept creeping up and touched the rear fender. Put one of these babies on and problem solved! I also used it on my Mother's Olds Cierra that I originally tried those perforated metal band straps on. The vibrations from the exhuast would just be conducted through the strap and into the chassis. Plus, those thin perforated straps are thin and would bend and rust easily. This hanger is thicker but not to thick to be able to bend so it fits the angle you need. Also, the hard rubber piece in between the clamp and strap keeps the exhuast vibrations and noise from flowing through the rest of the car. They are a little pricey but well worth it.

Can't beat the price on this one. Most blades go for $7 to $10 a piece, so this pack was just what I was looking for. I've only used one blade so far, but it cuts as well as any other one I've used. I was a little worried it wouldn't fit my cheapo multi-tool from Harbor Freight but it worked. You just have to make sure to screw it down tighter that the HF blades.
Great music, great memories. If your looking at this your probably already a fan of the Stray Cats, so go ahead and get it. Favorite song is Rumble in Brighton.

This is more a review of Amazon than the antenna. I bought this as a gift but my Mother said she didn't need it that her channels now came in good. It came exactly as described, at a really good price, and free shipping.

This dimmer works well and fit a 60 year old small metal electrical box. Just know that the toggle is a little smaller than a normal one, so as to fit the dimmer slide into the toggle opening. The toggle seems like thinner plastic and does feel a little on the cheap side. I would have given it 5 stars if the plastic was better quality and the throw had a firmer feel.

I bought this hoping to get some nice video from old vhs tapes. The software is a little confusing but I was able to get it to work eventually. The quality is so so but I'm sure if I had time to play with it I could do better. Might be an okay product but it's not as easy as I thought.

users.query: I'm really enjoying this series however this book didn't hold my interest as much as the first three. I can't wait to see how the story ends in the next one.

cands.text: This book was not my favorite of the series so far. However, I did enjoy learning more about some of the secondary characters in the series. This book left me easy for the next one though. Can't wait.
I absolutely LOVE this series! I didn't want the book to end, so I read it again. I cannot wait for the next one to come out.
This was a fun quick read. Even though I predicted all of the plot twists I still found this book to be quite enjoyable. I'm not sure if I will be continuing the series though.
I thought this book was a good start to a series. I plan to read the next book, I just hope I like where the story goes from here.

I really liked this series a lot. I've read this twice now and it's just as good the second time around. It's full of action and excitement. There's even a couple of unexpected twists. I would definitely recommend this book.
I absolutely love this series. Eight books so far and the author still finds a way to keep me interested and guessing what will happen next.
After reading the first book in the series, I had to buy the second one right away. This book is just a good, if not better, than the last one.
I loved this book. I thought it was much better than the first one. Unlike the first book, I had no idea what was going to happen next. I can't wait to read the third book.

I absolutely loved this book. I could not put this book down. I read through it and started the next one immediately. This series has become one of my favorites. I'd definitely recommend this book and the rest o the series.
I really like this series. The characters are great and the author knows how to keep you guessing with just the right amount of plot twists in each book.

This book was ok.  I just didn't feel like I got to know the characters or really care about what happened to them. The concept was good, but the authors writing didn't make me feel like I could get lost in the story. I don't think that I'll be reading the rest of the series.
This series is great. Witch, just like all of the books so far, keep you guessing. I find myself wondering what can possibly happen next so I just have to read the next one right away.
A wonderful ending to a great series! I loved all the books so much I read them all in only three days, including the novella. I will definitely recommend this series.

Im not sure if the will be more books in this series or if it is a trilogy. But, this was a great ending to the series, if it is the end. I just loved the historical/dystopian/mythological twist in the story.

This is a great continuation of the series. You get to meet new characters and some old make a few appearances too. I love the dystopian/mythology woven into the story. I can't wait to read the next one.
I had this book for a while, I wish I would have read it sooner. This book was a good start of a series. I did feel like the characters moved a bit fast, but overall a good story.
This series just keeps getting better and better. The author really knows how to keep you guessing and I love that. I can't wait to see what happens in the last book.
I truly enjoyed this book. This was a great start to the series. The characters were written so well that I wanted to be friends with them all. I will enjoy reading the rest of the series.

A great continuation of the story. The book slowed it down a bit on the action, but it definitely did not disappoint. There was still quite a bit of action and we got to get more of a backstory on the characters. I can't wait to continue this series.
Good addition to the trilogy. I've read the trilogy at least three times and I'm happy to have another story of some of my favorite characters.

I loved this book! Cricket is extremely strong and holds on the her principles no matter how hard it is to do so. The characters were well developed with easy to relate personalities. The book leaves you wanting more but the story doesn't leave you feeling like nothing has been resolved.
I really enjoyed this book. I liked that we get to learn a bit more about everyone's background and how each character fits in. I can't wait to read the next one.

This was a wonderful, dark, and heart wrenching story. I felt so many emotions while reading this book. That is what makes the story so great, feeling everything the characters do as they are experiencing it. Bravo!

I love this series! Sienna has been through so much in her short time out of the box that I'm glad she manages to still have at least a little of herself left, I'm not sure I would. I hope that she holds on to that bit genuine goodness inside for what's to come. I can't put these books down. I will be starting the next one right away.
Wow. This was a great read, I couldn't put it down. It's full of action and plenty of twists and turns. I definitely recommend this book to anyone who likes a fast paced story and the Fae.

users.query: Eric doesn't just write about diversity, he lives it. "Not Like Me" is written as field guide for ministry and life reflecting several different voices from several different walks of life. Eric Bryant's heart for the "outsider" is clear and his call for "insiders" to branch out is compelling.

cands.text: In a day when it seems to be all about us, Brad reveals a contrarian view. He takes servant-leadership to a whole new level and combines the need for competency with the need for character. It's a fantastic read for leaders both in the marketplace and the church.

I love John's transparency and freedom to tell us how he failed--even in big ways. Anyone can brag about their successes. And critics can always tear down others because they never try anything new.

John Maxwell is successful because he keeps taking productive action steps. His newest book is chocked full of examples how to learn from your failures. And because we've all failed, we'll can all identify with the content. That is, if we're willing to admit we've failed.

Michael knows his stuff and he's willing to share it with us. Whatever level you're at, Platform will help you think bigger and reach farther. As one who's followed Michael for years, I've benefitted personally and professionally from his experience and insight. This new book is no exception. Thanks for all you do and more importantly who you are. I look forward to hearing you share more with John Maxwell at the upcoming Day about Books.

As a mentor to thousands of authors, speakers, and coaches it takes something special to catch my attention. Ive met people from every walk of life. And although everyone is uniquely created, Brian is definitely an outlier.

If you look at him on the outside, you might not be impressed. Hes an average guy. But its what he has on the inside that impresses me time and time again.

The guy is a ball of fire. Hes an action-taker and an unstoppable force. Hes insanely curious and committed to growthmore than most.

I think hes tremendously successful simply because he just won't quit. Some call it tenacity. Others call it grit. He doesnt believe in the word losing.

If I give him a challenge, he does it every time. Hes not afraid of failing or risking or believing. He takes imperfect action on a regular basis.

He does laps around people who trust in talent because Brian believes in something bettereffort.

Im honored to write his foreword. I believe in him and the value he brings. Although he might not be the most polished author who ever wrote a book, pay attention to him and his words. His content is gold and his approach to life is even more valuable.

If you can replicate even half of Brians enthusiasm you will 10x your impact.

This is your moment.
This is your legacy.

Its time to address your blinds pots and embrace a radical vision.

Lead U2 singer Bono writes the same song with a thousand different nuances and it gets better every time.

Best-selling author John C. Maxwell wrote the same book with a thousand different nuances and it too just got better.

Besides Maxwell's book reaching a whole new level, it might help you jump to your next level of leadership. As the world's #1 Leadership Guru, John brings you his best: stories, humor, truth, experience, and practical application.

In this book you'll learn the 5 levels of leadership:

1. Position--People follow because they have to.

2. Permission--People follow because they want to.

3. Production--People follow because of what you have done for the organization.

4. People Development--People follow because of what you have done for them personally.

5. Pinnacle--People follow because of who you are and what you represent.

More importantly, you'll face your own leadership gaps and the choice of jumping to your next level. In the words of Maxwell: "everything rises and falls on leadership: - including whether or not you reach your next level.

As someone who has seen Chris in action, attended his conferences, and witnessed his impact, I must say Chris' words are rooted in hope not hype. His work inspired me to start my own business and non-profit where I now Ignite Souls full-time. Thanks Chris for being a light to a sometimes dark world. Each of your books take us on a wild adventure. Even better, your words equip and empower us to create adventures of our own.

Mark shows us how we can make our work more than just toil.  With exceptional writing and keen insight, he demonstrates the possibility of us living out our OPUS everyday. Read this book and you'll sink your teeth into an alternative that could just change the way we work AND live.

Darren's new book is a work of art. It's packaged with intention, written with creativity, and presented with passion. I've listened to it 2 times, read it once, and attended the live event in Dallas, TX. Sure some of the content is basic for seasoned entrepreneurs, but how often we forget the basics and repeat "basic" mistakes. This is now a book I suggest to many of my clients just starting out so they know what's coming around the next turn. It's one of my top 3 reads in the last 24 months.

I found myself laughing out loud regarding the story about Space Mountain, cheering when Darren overcame the resistance with the water filters, and resonating when reading about the crabs. This book will fire you up with inspiration and then send you out with practical application to go make your entrepreneurial mandate a reality! Thanks Darren, Meredith, and the SUCCESS team.

I respect Chris Brogan. I like his tone, his style, his generosity. I've enrolled in his courses and he's clearly helped me go further in my business. His newest book is no different. Chris sees the world abnormally and he's not afraid to tell us how. Expect unconventional advice that gets results. Anticipate practical networking tips, like how to recall someone's name at a function, without embarrassing yourself or them. Read this book and you'll shake up your business in the best way.  Prepare to embrace your new labelfreak. Jump in with the rest of us...the waters is fine.

Are you caught up in chaos?

If so you're not alone, but thankfully you're in luck. In Mastering Chaos, author Robin Nickerson serves as your guide to help you push through your pain and into your potential. He is the founder of the APeX life companycreated to help individuals and organizations become the best me you can be.

When I met Robin, I knew I found a fellow Soul on Fire. I took time to discover his story:

Growing up with debilitating anxiety, depression, low self-esteem and limiting beliefs Robin struggled with fear, failure, and frustration. At the age of 19, after a business failure left him near bankruptcy, he became passionate about overcoming overwhelming loss and transformed his life.
Starting with only $100 by the age of 25 he was the owner of a thriving small business with $750,000 in annual sales. Now, after 18 years of experience as a business owner and student of personal transformation, he shares his experience of growth through adversity through his writing, training, and coaching. His passion is teaching others how to turn chaos into success.

Isnt it time you created a life full of meaning?

Imagine a place where fear, frustration, and confusion no longer sabotage you or your destiny.

If you hear a nagging voice telling you you're not doing your highest work
If you sense you're not fully utilizing your talents and abilities
If you feel you're not creating the most meaningful difference you can

Then Mastering Chaos is for you.

Robin distilled years of personal and professional lessons into this resource Mastering Chaos. Its a proven plan that helps you stop sabotaging your hierarchy of happiness because it shows you how to:

- Eliminate procrastination.
- Increase your ability to successfully reach your goals.
- Spike your creativity, intelligence, and resourcefulness.
- Overcome destructive emotions and habits.
- Create more meaning and purpose in your life.
- Develop more passion and persistence in your life.
- And much more

Blending a mix of stories, research and personal experience, Robin shares an entrepreneurial secret.

Its time to start your climb and discover that secret. What you find on the other side is well worth the effort.

The Big Adventure, has the power to ignite souls and awaken you to your true potential. When I wrote The Deeper Path I wanted to show people how to use their pain to create a deeper and more meaningful life. I met David Meyer while he was experiencing pain in his own life and his story resonated with me. He was passionate about helping people follow their purpose and pursue and their dreams.

This is rare because we often get caught up in living life that we forget about our dreams and slowly drift toward a future that is safe, predictable, and secure.

In The Big Adventure youll discover the most common regret of people dying is not going after their dreams. The dream to become a writer has been with David since he was a young boy. His book is a fulfillment of that dream

As you dive into the content I hope you ask the deep questions that will help you discover your own path. We never know what we are truly capable of until we find the courage to pursue our dreams and do what we love to do. When we find that courage within us we start living our own Big Adventure. This is your most exciting chapter to date.

Every now and then a book comes along that changes the way we think and talk about the legacy we want to leave on the world. With faith-inspired insights, this book reveals a creative path to extraordinary influence for all who refuse to let their deepest passions die within them.

Tim Brown is discontent with society's low expectation of young men. He's not about to let it slide. Instead, he provides a proven model and method to help young men break the mold and stand out for Jesus. An awesome read that will raise your expectations of what's possible.

William Vanderbloemen walks the walk. I've been impressed with his culture building strategies for well over a decade. In this book he gives us his proven blueprint. Save time, money, and pain with your own organization. Build your culture the right way.
A fantastic journey of faith and courage that reminds us of what we have forgotten: We are more than what we appear to be.

Ive been extremely blessed to work with authors and charitable leaders from around the world through my program Author Academy Elite. I cross paths with an incredible number of giving and generous individuals, but Ive always felt like there was a missing piece from the nonprofit sector.

We need someone who can cut through the bad advice, show nonprofit leaders how to overcome the fear of asking, and provide the path to free up our leaders so they can impact more lives. I believe that someone is here. Mary Valloni is an emerging thought leader on nonprofit fundraising.

Dont be left to figure it out on your own. Her insight and hands-on advice ensures you won't go it alone. I am especially excited about Fundraising Freedom because Mary shares her personal stories about how she has navigated the process so you know exactly what steps to take. Knowledge is only good if we implement the information and take action and Mary pushes you to do just that.

This book is about more than just raising money. Its about relationships. Its about creating a plan where lives are intertwined and it all leads back to fulfilling your vision for your cause. Securing financial gifts is just a result when you provide value to those you serve. The 7 Steps will guide you so you never have to question whats next. You will know exactly what the game plan is and youll have the freedom to make better decisions resulting in greater impact.

This content is clear and concise and an easy read for a new nonprofit leader, but it comes packed with content for a novice fundraiser as well. Most of us are guilty of appearing busy, but busy doesnt equal results. Mary wants you to see results and these steps will get you there.

Ive watched this book come together and Im excited for you because I know the words on the following pages will get you on the right path to fully fund your budget. I am passionate about igniting souls and I believe this content will spark a flame and ignite something incredible in nonprofits around the globe.

When I first met author Ana Donovitch, she told me she wanted her book to be different than most other books about trauma.

Now holding her finished book, she made good on that promise. Her stories are boldly transparent, showing all sides of her traumatic season of life. Its not what I expected; yes, theres despair and heartache, but also suspense, creativity and humor.

The story takes place on land and sea. Sail with Ana and youll discover the joy of living in the present reality and surviving the trauma of devastation. One thing is for sure. Ana has a heart to help the millions who are hurting from trauma, TBI, and PTSD. These are loaded labels for many but in Anas mind, each person has a name and a story:

 Each year trauma accounts for 41 million emergency department visits and 2.3 million hospital admissions across the nation.

 8% of Americans  24.4 million people  have PTSD at any given time. That is equal to the total population of Texas.

 Trauma injury accounts for 30% of all life years lost; cancer accounts for 16%, and heart disease accounts for 12%.

I know that for Ana her journey was arduous and long. This book reveals a process of personal healing and her quest to help others understand trauma.

Ana tells a story that captures your attention and curiosity. She weaves a storm that rages and refines. Ride the exhilarating winds of her past sailing adventures as the healing transformation unfoldsfeel the crisis, despair, the moments of humor, and overriding hope.

Her passage is certainly not a one-person affair; ripples radiate to families, friends, and workers. Her story calls out to those who are seeking direction for their own stormy dilemma. Trauma victims and their families will find additional reflections and resources in the back sections of the book.

Isnt it time you sailed a story of adventureone that changes your past and gives you hope for a brand new future.

Kary Oberbrunner

Melissa formatted this book in a way that's easy to digestdaily. Not only is it filled with amazing content, but it's also field-tested and time-tested. Melissa's words convey her contagious passion and deep purpose. She truly wants her readers to create the life of their dreams. Even better, she shows us the path to do so.

Few authors possess the gift of transporting readers into otherworldly regions, far away from the din and clamor this planet offers. In Home Behind the Sun, Tim and Jason serve as your tour guide, weaving their words, to lead you down unexplored pathways. Through your journeys, you'll discover a rich and robust Faiththe answer to your homesickness you've felt from the very beginning. - Kary Oberbrunner, author of Day Job to Dream Job and CEO of Igniting Souls and Redeem the Day

I met this author over the weekend and I was immediately impressed with his clarity, competence, and confidence. Marco knows his subject matter and he's generous enough to share it. A brilliant book by a brilliant author.

Every so often you hear a story that at first seems unbelievable.

Thats how I felt when I heard David and Kirstens story. To see them today, you wouldnt suspect the deep crisis that occurred a few years earlier. Yet when I heard the beginning of the story, I saw Gods redemption being lived out.

In Choosing a Way Out: When the bottom isn't the bottom, Kirsten Samuel walks us through the day that forever changed both of them. As you journey through the pages of their story, you will find hope that life can indeed be redeemed no matter how dark it seems.

Think you cant survive pornography addiction? In their story youll find hope, humility, forgiveness, and Gods redemptive work. You can overcome any stronghold and live with integrity once again.

Believe that depression means you will never experience joy again? Walk with the author as she uncovers the lies of her depression and discovers Gods Truth to eventually live in freedom and joy.

Convinced that your marriage cannot recover from the lies of the past? Discover anew, or maybe for the first time, the meaning of covenant and the hope found when we submit first to God and then to each other.

This book offers you a way out of the pit. It offers hope, not clichés. It presents truth from Gods Word, if you are willing to believe and apply it. It shows a way to find freedom from the prison of lies youve believed, if you are willing to embrace the pain, open yourself to Gods Word, and admit you are in need of healing, just like  your partner.

God will make all things new if we choose to walk through the pain.

Listen up guys.

These authors know their stuff.
And they write from a Biblical worldview.

As men we like to help solve problems.
Guess what?

These ladies are motivated to share the solutions to the problems that your wife might be dealing with.
Jill and Diana share their success stories and the places where they struggled.

This book is full of practical tips which will help women maintain balance in work AND home and woark AT home.
Thanks ladies for sharing your hearts and your wisdom.

High school is a deeply formational time. The choices we make in those early years set us on a path for the rest of our lives. Andy's heart to help young men comes through loud and clear on every page. His book serves as a guide to help teens to make wise choices and successfully navigate trials and temptations.

Living Forward starts out by addressing THE DRIFT.

The DRIFT is the tendency to arrive at destinations you don't consciously choose. The DRIFT is facing life in a reactive way and happens when youre:

1.) Unaware
2.) Distracted
3.) Overwhelmed
4.) Deceived

No one wakes up and says, Today I want to DRIFT. However, if you're not living a life according to design, then you're living a life according to DRIFT.

So how do you change direction and snap out of the DRIFT? Michael Hyatt and Daniel Harkavy reveal that the average person spends 5 hours researching and shopping for a new car. The average bride-to-be spends 40 days planning a three-hour wedding. However, the average person never spends 1 day planning his or her life.

Why?

The reality is most of us don't know how to plan our lives. Besides, it sounds daunting and out of reach.

Thankfully, Hyatt and Harkavy close the distance by demonstrating how to do a life plan. Even better, they provide examples of real Life Plans from real clients. These individuals come from a variety of backgrounds and life stages so readers of all kinds can relate.

The book is broken into 3 main parts: Understand Your Need, Create Your Plan, and Make it Happen. It literally walks you though the Life Plan process in a step-by-step fashion.

The Life Plan is facing life in a proactive way.

As you read this book youll answer 3 powerful questions:

1. How do I want to be remembered? This is your legacy.
2. What matters most to me? These are your priorities.
3. How do I get from where I am to where I want to be? This is your action plan.

Design your own Regret Free life by crafting your Life Plan.

The Life Plan creates clarity. It acts as a GPS.
The Life Plan creates courage. It acts as a filter.
The Life Plan creates commitment. It acts as a motivator.

Page 154 says it all, This may sound grandiose, but we are out to change the world. In Living Forward authors Hyatt and Harkavy do just that. They change the world one person at a time by challenging readers to create greatness one life plan at a time.

Living Forward is a fantastic tool to design the life you want and then clarify the steps you need to take to get there.

users.query: The Night Circus had points that dragged a bit for me, where I wished for more action and for events to unfold, but despite its slow motion, the book paints a gorgeous black and white picture of a magical traveling circus that you wish could be real. As the tents and acts are described, your mind wanders, trying to picture each little detail, and possibly how it could be accomplished sans magic, and before you know it you've read an entire page without really remembering any of the details and have to go back. I loved the wonder of the whole circus, and even though the reader knows that its really magic there, the circus attendees don't, and it leaves you trying to picture it the way the circus-goers view it. Really, what does happen when magic is introduced to an audience that doesn't believe it exists? How do they wrap their minds around it, and how do the performers hide the magic in plain sight? It was definitely a good read

cands.text: First off, I totally enjoyed the book. Certain parts tended to drag, but overall, I enjoyed the book. My biggest issue with it was the advertisement. The book description mentions various fantasy elements, like werewolves and witches, but I will say this now: there is no magic in this book. Fiction, yes. Fantasy, not so much. Still a good book, just don't be deceived by the description.

I absolutely love every book of this series. Great books for young readers. Magic, family, adventure, and though many people like to say its "like Harry Potter", its not, its a fantasy world unto itself that's just as intriguing and dynamic as the HP universe.

I am in love! This book was phenomenally good. Instead of diving into a European world of magic, where the terminology and ideas are familiar, we head into the wild Nigerian jungle of juju, and it was SO. MUCH. FUN. I loved the philosophy of education in this book, and the chittim and how it is earned and valued. I loved the setting of Nigeria. We need more books that take us to places other than the United States and England. I loved that all the characters were POC. I loved how our main character learns to embrace her self while others see her as inflicted with infirmity. I loved watching Sunny grow. If/when J.K. Rowling decides to write about her other wizarding schools, I hope her stories about Uagadou will have some sort of mention of Leopard Knocks His Foot. And if people thought the new Muggle term "No-Mag" was offensive, what on earth will they think of being called a Lamb? I need some Pepper Soup and Jollof rice and some good, sweet, milky tea.

I started this yesterday morning and finished at 1 AM, could NOT stop reading it! I started reading it because of the TV show trailer, and when I realized it was a book, I had to read it. To me, it was very reminiscent of the TV show Lost, where the author piled on mystery after mystery, things that couldn't possibly exist in the same realm (was it science and magic? aliens and alternate universes? okay, what is that thing, it just doesn't belong!) and it gets so convoluted that I was about to give up hope that he'd have an answer to everything (I thought I was going to get gypped in the same vein as I had with Lost) but the ending was an amazing twist that was completely unexpected for me! I can't wait for book 2, or the show.

The idea behind the book was great, I was really intrigued by the whole world the story was set in, but unfortunately we learn less about the world and focus all our time on the main character, Rhine. I spent too much of this book willing Rhine to get a spine and start taking action to fix the problems surrounding her, not just run away from them. Her whole escape plan was always "Run away!", no matter the situation nor how futile the attempt would be, her inevitable plan was simply "run away!". There were so many other options for her to get out of her given situation if she would just sit still a moment and think logically. The character just seemed utterly ridiculous to me, the daughter of two scholars being so reckless and unbending and completely unable to put a plan together just boggled my mind. I probably won't continue to the sequel unless someone can assure me it gets monumentally better...

Not as impressive as the first book in the series, but still a good read. I think I was mostly annoyed that it covers the same time period of events, just from a different person's perspective, but only from like, one more state away from the last story. I mean, they basically had the same things happen for them. I want to know what happened to people from say, the south, or some other country. I heard the first time around that they're all starving. There were some key differences that I enjoyed, like how since it was NYC, they were getting more assistance from the government than the girl from the first novel. But really, it was the same story, different family. Everything goes to pot, the end. I get that this is a lead into book three, where the two families meet, and I did enjoy it, I was just left wanting more by the end.

I did not expect to be such a fan of these books, but they are really good! You get interested based on the Cinderella plotline it seems to trail along after, but it truly does have its own world and the characters are so intriguing! Apparently books 3 and 4 come out in 2014 and 2015, and I just can't wait!! Haven't gotten this excited over a book series in awhile!

Everything moved SO. SLOW. I mean, they have the magic to grow flowers instantaneously, but I felt like I was watching and waiting for the flower of this book to bloom in real time. Magical realism is usually slow for me anyways, but this one seemed to drag. Beautiful story, beautiful book, but really, I think I took too long to get there.

This book was good at the start, had a good premise and got me really interested in the characters and the world they lived in. Then the excitement starts, and the book went all to hell. For like, the last 30% of the book, we get to sit and listen to the main character whine and fret and basically ruin the great beginning the author had built up. Her grand adventure takes place over the last third of the book and she goes nowhere and does nothing. I ended up skimming through the majority of that portion until the end. It was kind of a big let down.

My husband and I love cruising, and it was really cool to get an insider's view of what a cruise ship is like. The personal stories were funny and the characters he worked with are great. It was also interesting to read a lot of the facts about the cruise industry and Carnival in particular. Kinda sad to learn that the only pastimes the crew members have is alcohol and sex. Definitely won't be applying to work on a cruise ship anytime soon!

This book is so twisted and disturbing. I know this is Young Adult lit, and maybe a teen wouldn't be so disturbed over this book, but as an adult, a mother, and a human being, this book left me heartbroken and distraught over how a world like this could possibly happen (I should probably quit reading dystopian lit...)

What if your parents could unwind you? What type of child is chosen to be unwound? What about the kids who have no choice, despite how perfect they behave? What truly happens when you're unwound? So many questions, so many stories, so many points of view. My head was spinning, but this book is incredibly well written, and eventually (even if you think it'll never happen) all your questions will get answered. Hopefully. Supposedly. This world is so depressing.

Diving into book two, book one was too good to leave this place alone.

Not as amazing as the Legend series. I picked it up because I loved the whole Legend trilogy, and Marie Lu is a great writer, but just as with her Legend books, she seriously drags out the beginnings of books. It's not that she doesn't hook you, 'cause I was definitely interested and really like the book, but she just makes it seem so much longer than it needed to be. I felt the same way about the three Legend novels, but with all of her books, she at least ends really REALLY well. I'm definitely in for book two.

I was completely sucked into this book. I felt jittery and nervous and on edge for days after finishing it! I keep looking around the house, calculating my family's survival chances. This story was not only really well written, but it's got a very realistic human aspect. The main character is not all perfect and saving the world, she's very genuine to me. She makes mistakes, she's selfish, and she gets frustrated and angry over stupid things, like a typical teenage girl. And best of all, she keeps it real while the world ends around her. I also really loved the fact that the story is an "it's the end of the world!" story that does NOT involve aliens or zombies or humans destroying each other. It was just an unfortunate turn of events, and how do we now cope as a race trying to survive. I could not put this book down, it was an incredibly good read!

I preferred Graceling and Fire to this book. I feel like the action ran too slow for me, and Bitterblue herself was just so utterly clueless and lost, whereas in the other two books the female leads were so hardcore. I love the Graceling world, and Cashore's writing, but this book dragged a lot of the time for me.

For lovers of Daughter of Smoke and Bone, you will not be disappointed by the sequel! In fact, I quite believe the second book was better than the first. Where the first left us in the human world for the most part, only getting glimpses of the other world, book two has us travel back and forth between the two evenly, with more insight into the magic world. Karou is left to try and reconcile her two conscious selves, the Chimaera she was and the human she is. Akiva must find a way to atone for what he's done, all while believing he has once again lost Karou, to his own bad decisions. And Zusana is back, bringing much needed love and joy to a very bleak landscape.

Where book one had me begging for the answer of "What is going on with the teeth??" book two had me clamoring for "What is up with the thurible??" Laini Taylor weaves an amazing tale and truly brings both her worlds and her characters to life. I am on the edge of my seat for the third book, as I'm sure most fans are!

This book is stunning! Rachel Hartman has an incredible flair with words! This book may be considered young adult fantasy, but unlike many other YA authors, Hartman decided to up the game quite a bit and set us all to shame with her vocabulary. Any author who can slip the word "camelopardine" into a novel and have it just smoothly and elegantly fall into place is deserving of worldwide renown and acclaim. If her word usage doesn't make you fall in love with her writing, her graceful building of this dragon world will leave you spellbound. I was so won over by the way she wrote foreigners accents, they fit the visualizations of the characters and helped you place them in the world she created.

Hartman created an entirely new world that you slip into and just fall into step with, and everything about it just IS. Little explanation is needed on the various new terms of this world, such as "saar" or "Ker" or "ard", usage gets you along just fine (I know this for a fact as I discovered her handy glossary in the back only AFTER I had finished the whole book!) Character development is intense and deep, her characters are far beyond those simpletons who fall in love at first sight in so many other YA novels. This book was a spectacular look into the senseless prejudice of this dragon world, and how one young girl had to hide her true self from everyone because that prejudice is dual-sided. It speaks of the hardheadedness of previous generations and the hopefulness of the new, and really, it's so much like the real world, while being so very different. I was hooked from beginning to end and cannot wait for the sequel!

I'm not usually a fan of non-fiction, but this story was fantastic. Not only were his own personal experiences mind-blowing, but the facts about World War II that I learned about in this book (particularly about POW treatment, or how terrifying it was to be in the AAF period back in WWII) blew me away. Every few pages, I would stop and tell my husband "Did you know...?" Because of that, it took me a lot longer to read, but the book was spellbinding from beginning to end. So glad I picked it up!

I highly recommend this book and will be starting the next one right away!

This book was ok.  I wouldnt read it again though like i do with most books. it didn't leave me on my seat at all. nothing to really grip me.  kind of a let down. but good in its own way. give it a try.
I really enjoyed this book and didn't want to put down. There was good character development and the storyline was unique and new. Not usually a fan of romance triangles but I enjoyed this one.

users.query:

cands.text:

Introduction of some interesting characters for future books in this series has my interest piqued.

I will definitely read more by this author. Great introduction to her writing style.

Themes were dark but inferred opposed to detailed. A lot going on with this story but not overly bogged down with backstory. Read was easy and flowed relatively smoothly.

An erotic read that had me blushing on the train when I realised the guy next to me was reading along.

I really enjoyed the quirkiness of the female protagonist. Awkwardly funny and totally endearing.

Supporting characters added to the magic so much so that I've just purchased the entire three book series - yes I already own book one but I love a bargain.

I found the authors writing style engaging and easy to read. Nowhere near as smutty as my usual reads but thoroughly enjoyable.

First time read from this author. I'd read more if the price was right.

The writing style was fine. Pacing was a tad drawn out for my liking but easy to read. Editing and formatting were okay but could have been tighter.

Yeah not for me. Was not the plot but the telling of it. Felt like the author was still honing her craft. I found her voice to be immature.

Wrong felt so right. I enjoyed Ms. Ashton's first title. Her writing style is relaxed and easy to read. I read the story in one sitting and was entertained throughout.

Younger characters than I normally read but I enjoyed the twists and turns of this storyline. I had some issues with the timeline but that could just be me being an Aussie.
Read in one sitting.

I generally like my characters a little older than college age but i didn't find that the age of the characters detracted from the storyline.

The female protagonist having her life together was a win for me.

Psycho ex was a bit random.

Another FYM author ticked off my list. First time read for me of C.J. Duggan's work and I enjoyed the quick escape.

OTT plot but it worked a treat. Hotel nightmare to dream destination. Claire was sassy and Louis went from prick to prince.

Authors easy writing style kept me entertained and engaged. I will definitely read more by Ms. Duggan.

At times I found it totally over the top but I enjoyed the humour for the most part.

The author voice was not defined, it shifted throughout the read, it felt like too many elements to the story were tacked on with no real purpose.

None of the characters truly engaged me and at times it felt ... immature but it was a quick and easy read.

I was pleasantly surprised by Gable, book one in The Powers That Be series, as I prefer my couples a tad older but this college romance had me reading it in one sitting.

I found Ms. Bentley's writing style a comfortable read. Relationship development as well as sexy times.

I enjoyed the email exchanges, talk about luck of the draw on that one. Kind of random but they added a lot of vale IMO.

Gable and Scout's personalities although vastly different were a good match.

Looking forward to reading more in this series so much so I've already purchased, Zeke and Loch.

The series is growing in me. Book two while having some of the same traits was a little softer so I connected more with the characters.
Writing style is easy to read, editing okay, formatting in keeping with the series and chapter headings.
I ending up liking Alec's character much more than I thought I would. Still not sold on Casey's female protagonists though.
The most intriguing character of the series is up next, Kane. I'm already worried about if flu like symptoms.

Okay so there is a plot point that I totally did not see coming but when it did it made complete sense and that just doesn't tend to happen with me. So kudos.

Similar writing style as others works I've read from Ms. Douglas. A little too high school for my tastes but with a good amount of darkness to help balance it.

Female protagonist annoyed the heck out of me but the male lead and storyline got me passed that. Still left me with a tonne of unanswered questions though.

So I'm thinking I've read this book out of sequence as it felt like it missed the mark for me. The female protagonist was one dimensional and did little to win me as a reader over.

The ending may make sense in the series bigger picture but it left me scratching my head.

Editing could have been better. I'm in two minds about reading anything further of this series.

Beast I liked. Tilley not so much, she grated on my nerves the entire book. Lots going on in this book. Storyline starts quite simply then takes off in several different directions at once. Nothing wrong with the story just not my thing.

Off Side is the sweet love story of Ryan and Danny, two people from very different backgrounds.
A college romance, where ridiculous stereos types gone into play. An us (rich) against them (poor) with our two lover caught in the middle.
The character of Ryan, while his heart was pure, was a tad staid even his dialogue. The characterisation of his family was OTT and the was no real insight as to why he was different to his peers. I understand that this is a different genre but I've read other titles by Ms. Sawyer that I enjoyed far more.

Book 4 of The Blindfold Club series is Three Dirty Secrets and of the series this is my favourite ... So far.

The H appealed to me and while I found the h slightly annoying I thought they worked well as a couple.

A sizzling hot read that is sure to cause blushing if reading in public ... Especially on the train with a hot guy reading over your shoulder who gives you a cheeky wink as he gets off. I did like the fact that this couple owned their freak and there was no blushing from them.

Book 3 in the Fantasyland series really tied this series together. While books 1 and 2 had interconnections toward the end a book 3 built to it throughout.

This storyline had a real fairytale feel to it for me morse than the others in this series.

I really like the 'our world' Noc and look forward to seeing him more in Book 4.

I do have to say that the covers don't really do justice to the stories of this series - I'm a totally cover whore I admit it. So this is a series you shouldn't judge a book by its cover.

First time read for me of Ms. Madisons work and its a big hell yeah about hitting up some more of it.

FB teasers got me to buy the book and it sat on my kindle for a few months before I read the balls excerpt three times in one day and each time I snorted so it jumped to the top of my TBR list.

I enjoyed all of the characters in this title, even douchey hubby.

Lots of laugh at loud moments and a storyline that kept me engaged from start to finish. Read in one sitting I might add.

What a great read! I utterly enjoyed this book and had to think long and hard to pick something I didn't like about it. I managed in the character of Elec BUT I just purchased his book to find out the other half of the story.

I enjoyed the humour and general lightness Ms. Ward brought to the story given the serious undertones - emotional infidelity, medical condition, depression, hostile ex who used dogs as pawns.

The unconditional love of Damien and Chelsea was as sweet as it was hot. The rave reviews that have filled my FB timeline are justly deserved.

Well written, edited and formatted. A wonderful edition to any library.

Thus is a nifty little Bluetooth speaker. Good stereo sound, a little weak on the bass but that's to be expected given its size. The sound is very clear and pleasing, particularly when playing music. It's a significant upgrade from the ofttimes tinny, shallow sound from typical tablet speakers. Again, given its small size it won't fill a large room with resounding sound, but as a companion that can be taken on the road or carried from room to room it's more than loud and pleasing enough.

Update Jan. 4, 2016 - Have owned this speaker for well over a year and it's still going strong. The sound quality is still very good and it remains a solid performer. Speaking of solid, while I don't overly abuse it I do it move it around my apartment with me and have inevitably dropped it several times. The rubber body certainly keeps it well protected.

The lining runs the full length of the coat and is quite warm. The felt collar is removable and held on with buttons. So, this really is an all year round raincoat.

Very happy. I'm a stickler about clothes, and would recommend this coat to anyone.

users.query: This little book (and I mean little in size - not content) is wonderful.  Small enough to fit anywhere.  The patterns have a good selection.  Fancy socks, baby socks, plain socks and really funky socks.  This book is written in simple to understand instructions and really inspires you to make socks.  A must have for any sock knitter!

cands.text: This book will tell you more about socks then you ever thought you wanted to know.  History (with cool pictures), styles, techniques and just general information.  But, in the end this book tells you so much that you understand how to knit socks and you understand a lot of where the basics have come from.  Plus, the patterns that come with the book are fun and inspiring.  A great reference book for any knitter!
Fantastic knitting book.  I want to make everything in here.  The instructions are easy to understand and the patterns are well worth buying a whole book for!

This book is full of beautiful quick gifts.  What I like the most about this book is how it is sorted (by the length of time it takes an average knitter to finish a project).  I've found the patterns to be reasonable and easy to understand.  I have yet to really get "into" the book and test out a bunch of patterns.  But, from reading them it appears as if they are written well.

The only real downer with this book is the lack of "alternate" patterns.  I like a book to have patterns that are not just clothes or bags.  This book is missing that, but still worth getting.  I've actually given this book as a gift and it worked well for that too.

I was drawn to this book by the cover.  Cozy knits are always in fashion and normally so warm that during the winter months I'm enamored with them all.  I found the patterns in this book to be well organized, easy to read, and a nice assortment.  I don't like the number of scarf patterns (scarves to me are almost a waste to knit).  But, there are two jacket patters, slippers and sock patterns that are lovely!  This book would be great for any intermediate to advanced knitter.

This book is better and contains more than you could even imagine!  As far as sexy knits - this is by far the best book out there.  I know that knitting underwear might not be every ones cup of tea, but that book is filled with much much much more than just that.  Stockings, gloves, little sexy tops.  I found the patterns to be well described, easy to follow and for knitters of every level.  If you are looking for a timeless sexy knit book ... this would be it!

This is a wonderful little book with a few charms.  I have a rule that I only buy a book if there is something that I have to make out of it.  At least one item.  This book has a few.  There are some fun summer knits, chunkier fast knits, cables in very offset fashion, and everything fun flare French that you can imagine.

If you are into vintage knitted clothing you'll absolutely love this book!  I've found it to be full of patterns I want to make.  It isn't often that I get a book, open it up, and want everything.  Not just sort of want, urn for.  They are BEAUTIFUL!

For my accounts so far there are only a couple of pit-falls to this book.  1. Some of the patterns are VERY complicated and not easy to understand.  Trial and error seems to be the only way to find out if you are doing it correctly.  2. Even checking the gauge it seems like some of the patterns might be slightly off on how much yarn (as in length) is needed (especially if you buy a kit of yarn for a pattern from say knitpicks).  Even with the downfalls, the book is wonderful for advanced knitters.

I have wanted this book for the past couple of years.  It is out of print and I finally found a copy on Amazon.  I love it.  The patterns are amazing and so much fun.  You will not find a better clog sock book!

This is a wonderful little knitting book.  It has sweaters using ribbon, cotton, summer tops, winter knits, and men's knits.  The patterns are very easy to read.  The tomato sweater was done by someone in our knitting group and it knitted up very fast and came out amazing.  True to the pattern.  I would say that there are some basic knits in here that are missing a bit of imagination.  That would be my only complaint.

Wendy has always been one of my favorite knitting designers.  Her patterns are easy to read and always amazing.  This book is a compilation of some of the best patterns I seen out of her.  There are at least 10 sweaters or tops and a few hats that I need to make (which will always be in fashion).  And in the intro is one of the coolest things I've ever seen in a knitting book - how to make your very own duct tape double (to test out your knit wears).  She gives you lots of ideas on how to get your knitted items to fit correctly and the patterns are easy to read.  A must buy for any knitter!

This book is filled with easy weekend knits that cover the gamut.  Sometimes with these sorts of books there are a load of scarves, gloves, socks and hats.  Not with this book.  It has simple sweaters, ponchos, and home wears (and of course some gloves, socks, and hats).  Most of the patterns are also timeless classics.

The instructions are easy to read and follow (even for a novice).  The book has lovely pictures that show you the end product from many different angles.  The descriptions of non-standard stitches are amazingly clear.  You'll find yourself referencing this book whenever you need a quick gift.

This book offers some wonderful traditional Turkish socks.  Incredibly colorful and interesting, but not something you would wear every day.  I've found that I made one pair of socks out of this book (as a gift) - but I haven't made any others.

I may consider using these socks as Christmas Stocking Socks.

For some reason the cover of this book just turns me off.  I wasn't interested in it forever.  Until of course, I was at a bookstore thumbing through it.  I had to buy it.  There are some fantastic knits in there.  The Santa hat is a MUST make.  I plan to do it for this holiday.  There are also lovely, strange and totally enticing sweaters, socks and such.  The patterns also seem to pass the gamut of easy to quiet difficult and there is a section on gifts, knitted gift packaging and bows.

Even though I get the interweave magazine I bought this book.  I love the fact that the instructions, guides, and stitch examples are all in one place (sometimes I find it hard to find the exact stitch in old magazine).  This book also contains a handful of knitted sweaters that I'm going to have a make.  I'm not happy with the 3 shawl patterns that the book contains - but I can get over it since the rest of the patterns are all timeless classics!

A Good Yarn is the story of Lydia, the owner of a small yarn store in downtown Seattle.  The book starts off where I'm assuming "A Shop On Bloom Street" finished.  Although, I didn't read this book and can not say for sure.  Lydia has overcome a lot of problems in her life and finds happiness and joy in working in her store with her sister.

The story unfolds with Lydia starting a sock class.  The students that join are all in different places in their life and are so diverse that Lydia worries the class will never become friendly.  There is the young over weight high school student, a divorced librarian who has lost all of her money in a scam, and a newly divorced single mother of two who is trying to find not only her self, but also some semblance of life after marriage.

A Good Yarn is an uplifting story of female triumph and power.  I found the story to be slow to start, but once it got going I was very into it.  A lovely story!

I found this book to be very useful.  The pictures are helpful and the descriptions are meaningful.  I also LOVE the fact that there is a section on how to work out designs of your own.  Plus there is a good 20 pages on just different types of stitches that make really cool patterns.  I have not seen such a complete listing of these types of neat patterns in one place before. This is something that anyone could use.  To add to an already wonderful book this book gives great tips that even a seasoned kniter could use.

Yep.  Just so so.  Not terribly interesting on the knitting front and a bit too much politics for my liking.  I thought the characters were boring and made the assumption that all of us knitters are the same.  We are very much - NOT THE SAME.  I'm glad I didn't buy this book and it was a free copy.

I found this book to contain even more ideas/pattern and wonderful rugs than imaginable.  The pure selection of rugs is impressive.  Colorful rugs, cabled rugs, runners, circular ... you name it, and it is in the book.

What I find wonderful is that the explanations are great, the patterns are easy to follow, and there is a load of information about rugs themselves.  This book is great for knitters of all levels.  You'll wonder how you ever lived without this book (gifts in a flash).

Being a knitter and a murder mystery buff - I thought for sure this book would be right up my alley.  The story revolves around Kelly - a big city girl who comes home after her Aunt is killed.  She spends her time getting to know the locals, learning to knit and working to find her aunt's killer.  I was going to take the rest of the series off my wish list until I got to the end.  I do believe that this series has promise - but as a stand alone first novel it was missing a bit.  I believe the story could have used a good editor and a bit of character clean up.  There are way too many characters for my taste.  Still, the story did have twists and turns that kept me reading.  The book also comes with a recipe and a knitting pattern (in the back) - which I can't wait to try (I picked up the yarn this past weekend).

I've been a huge fan of Stefanie's for a while. Her first full book of patterns is filled with sweaters, fun tops, and amazing cover ups. I have found that her descriptions on how to fit tops is always well written and easy to understand.

The only major draw back (the minus one star for this book) is some of the out dated patterns. Some of them are so 80's I can't imagine anyone making them. This I find sad ... since I know that Stefanie is one of the hippest designers out there. I've read that her second book will be out next year. I just hope that it contains more of what I love from her (like the slightly showy wide necked sweater ... which I must start soon).

This rack is perfect.  It isn't too large.  It fits just enough pasta.  The pasta dries without sticking.  The wood is easy to clean and easy to put away (since it comes apart).  Perfect for home pasta making!

This is truly a supernatural romance novel.  Sometimes the romance is greater than the supernatural or visa-versa.  This book is a lovely blend of both.  Our story revolves around a new New Yorker, Jane, who meets a vampire, Rhy, while being assaulted by some jerk outside a bar.  Rhy has two brothers who are both vampires as well.  The story revolves around Rhy's love for Jane and his deep seeded issues with being a vampire.  I found this story gripping and heart wrenching at times.  You will want to know what happens with Jane and Rhy as soon as you pick up this book.

Jemima J is a wonderful summer read.  The story revolves around Jemima (a.k.a. JJ), a smart witty larger girl that finds comfort in food.  Jemima has a crush on a coworker, but would never dare tell him since she has never really had a boyfriend.  The turning point is when she learns about the internet and starts internet dating.  She has a friend digitally alter a photo of her to send to a man in California who wants her to visit.  This combined with her love interest leaving the newspaper where the work causes her to join a gym and basically stop eating.  Needless to say Jemima gets very small and that is where things become interesting.  The characters are written exceptionally well.  This is too much fun for chick-lit readers to miss!

I've done other puzzles by this manufacture and I really like them.  The pieces are nice and thick.  They stay together really well.  The animation is a bit of a let down - but I don't really do puzzles for that.  Overall this is a fantastic puzzle!

I think that color and design is very nice.  However, this particular shoe does not have good arch support and actually hurts your feet.  It is too high and no support for top half of the foot.
My grandson love his new AGPtEK 8GM MP3 Player.  I bought this so that my grandson could have music he's not old enough for a cell phone and I thought this would be the next best thing.

This a very nice leather hobo purse.  It has a lot of room and the leather was really soft.  I carry a lot in my purses and this purse has withstood whatever I have placed in it. I just might go back and order another one in a different color.  This leather hobo handbag is worth the money.

These face towels were nice and thick. I really liked the way they felt against my skin, soft.  I will be buying more of these face clothes, hand towels, & bath towels, rhey are really great quality towels.
These skirts were very nice and feel good and are very flattering to my figure.

users.query:
The MobileMate Micro Memory Card Reader I received works ok but, it did not contain the "Key ring and jewelry like necklace clasp for easy access"(lanyard) that was listed in the Technical Details.  For me it wasn't a big deal. I just reused one from an old SanDisk reader that had gotten broken.
Reading through the reviews there seems to be a LOT of inconsistency in what people are getting when they order this item. My order was "Fulfilled by Amazon"

I bought this because I had SD and microSD cards scattered all around the house and I wanted a convenient little case to put them together all in one place(a fire proof safe). This case works well for that purpose. I do not use it heavily, such as carrying it around with my notebook on trips, so I can't vouch for it's durability. Like I said I only use it to organize the SDs I have at home and only occasionally grab it to access one of the cards I've got stored in it.
