I bought this card at about $9 from amazon for mp3 storage. I've only used it in the deicated SD slot on my Lenovo T61p laptop and my Garmin Nuvi 780( I use the mp3 player feature on long trips). I have had no issues with this card.

I bought this card at about $9 from amazon for mp3 storage. I've only used it in the deicated SD slot on my Lenovo T61p laptop and my Garmin Nuvi 780( I use the mp3 player feature on long trips). I have had no issues with this card.

I needed an older small capacity CF card that uses the FAT file system for transferring firmware to an industrial controller.
I bought this card  and it worked great.

Fits the the wife's Core Prime very well and she says it looks like she has a new phone.
Looks like it should provide decent protection for the phone.

This is a great battery kit and includes ALMOST everything you need to replace the battery in your Garmin Nuvi 780.
The only thing missing from the kit is a piece of double-sided tape to secure the battery in place. I was able to reuse the really sticky tape from the original battery. You will need to make sure you have the Torx screw driver fully inserted into the screw and apply slight downward pressure as you remove the screws to prevent stripping them. The shell of the Nuvi is a little difficult to seperate(and put back together) but, watch the video provide or on Youtube and you should be ok.
Now I can program my Nuvi without having to plug it into the car adapter!
Bought for my son's LG OCtane and he's happy with it. Be aware that it is more of a hard plastic than "rubberized" but, it seems to protect the phone ok.

This is a great little hard protective case for the LG Octane. I purchased one for my wife. She wanted the purple to make her phone easy to find and not be confused with my son's.
Due to the way the Octane is constructed all of the cases, at least all of them that I've looked at or purchased,
rely on some small plastic tabs to attach the case to phone. If you drop your phone enough times on a hard surface
you will eventualy break these tabs off. The upside is your phone doesn't get scratched up or possibly broken.
So I find it well worth the $5.

Bought this as a gift for my son back in January. It appears to be durable because he carries it everywhere and it's held up well.
It's easy to transfer files to because it appears as an external USB storage device (drive) when connected to your PC via the supplied USB cable.
My son was very pleased with the ease of use and the sound quality but, he did ditch the earbuds that came with it and uses a higher quality set.
I deducted a star due to the lack of a microSD slot.

Pros:
Sturdy construction
Magnetic closures for the cover
Provides good protection
Has openings for all the things like microSD and charger  etc
Cons:
As others have pointed out the front cover is not fitted around the home button and it's easy to accidentally press it with the cover.
Flipping the cover to use it as a "kickstand" is a little touchy.
Bottom line:
Because it only cost $15 I cut a hole in the front cover to accommodate the home button we rarely use the "kickstand" function so it's not an issue.

As another review mentioned this shirt does not come with any sort of game code. At the time I bought the shirt there was no mention of a code in the description or in the photos.
I bought it for my son and he's very happy with it and it has held up well.
I bought this to replace my wife's lost mount for her nvi 750. I recieved the OEM(Garmin) replacement in OEM packaging. It fits and works fine.
I bought this to replace my wife's lost mount for her nvi 750. I recieved the OEM(Garmin) replacement in OEM packaging. It fits and works fine.

I bought this and put it on my Fuze almost 3 years ago and my Fuze still looks like new due to the great protection provided by the case. The clip seemed cheap and I never used it so I can't vouch for it. I also never found a use for the elastic band. I highly reccomend the case.

Pos: Nice long cord  and nice clip.
Cons: Microphone was dead on arrival and was returned to Amazon for a refund.
Note: Amazon rejected a previous review that contained some details about communication with the seller

These phones have been great. They have extremely long battery life, clear sound quality and very long range.  We can go outside anywhere in our yard and still be in range. The only casualty has been one handset that was left outside in the range for over a week. The call block feature is also great.

Pretty good sound quality with our Panasonic KX-TG6513B phone.
Unfortunately the headband is made of very thin plastic and was broken within a week of use.
I wish the headband was built of a thicker plastic and more durable.
I bought this to use as an backup image archive storage unit. I store backup images of all my home computers on this drive and the USB 3 speed is great when connected to my newer computers.

Oh yeah the theme song from Soul Train. Love it.
I also had a blast playing this song in marching band, it was always a crowd-pleaser!

This is not the exact cable that came with my Galaxy S5. The logos on the plugs are different, on the phone connector end the little bumps which indicate the top of the plug are not there and the cable is not nearly as flexible as the cable that came with the phone. They do come in what appear to be OEM boxes. So are they OEM? I can't say but so far I have been happy with them. The only reason I gave 4 stars instead of 5 stars is the stiffness of the cable. I would prefer it better if they were more flexible (like the one that came with the phone).

For $3 a piece with batteries they seem to be decent quality. As fate would have it my order arrived in the morning and that very afternoon a storm knocked out the our power. I passed these out to the wife and kids and everyone had their own flashlight for the night. They were pretty bright lights and the batteries held up pretty good. I didn't notice any bad smell on the ones I received.

I use this in a Canon SX210 IS to shoot Hi res video and Stills. It has ample room to store lots of video and pictures and the speed to keep up with the camera. It is also very fast when transferring files from the card in my PC's SD slot usually right around the 60MB/s rate.

I've been around computers and printers for a very long time and I've seen way too many printers ruined by "re-manufactured" Ink cartridges" or "do it yourself" refill kits. I always go with the genuine OEM cartridges for any printer and these are genuine Canon cartridges at a good price plus 50 sheets of photo paper thrown in.

users.query:
I'm not sure what to say about this.  It is an iPod dock that can be powered by a VERY large power brick, or 8xAA batteries.  It has a smalish remote which allows you to make selections on the iPod, pause/play, next/prev track, mute, vol up/down, bass boost and ROTATE.  The round grey button for Menu/up/down/ok needs to be pushed quite hard.  The center of the circle does nothing.  It is not a button.  Strange.  Why not make that "OK"?  Probably would infringe on an Apple patent or something.

The Rotate feature is why you would buy this instead of the litany of other iPod docks.  Push a button on the remote and the iPod turns 90 degrees counter-clockwise so you can watch a video in widescreen (if you have one of those iPods.)  This is kind of a cool gimmicky feature.  A button on the top turns off a backlight (the blue ring).  When on, the blue ring changes color when you rotate (to a lighter blue).

The sound quality on this is its largest flaw.  In a word, terrible.  You don't need to be much of a critic to know the sound is poor.  It reminds me of a transistor radio speaker from the 80s.  I'm pretty sure I can hear stereo sound.

The iPod connector also charges your iPod and there is a mini-plug in the back for a line-in (if you aren't using an actual ipod.)

It comes with a bunch of filler plates so all manner of iPods (with a standard iPod connector) will fit in the rotating mechanism.

I want to give it four stars, but the sound quality is so bad and the power brick is so large I can only justify three.  Oh, I almost forgot, you cannot use any type of iPod case with this thing - not even a super thin silicone case.  That settles it.  Three stars.

cands.text: I love the idea of iPods and have owned a few.  This one has only given me problems.  The battery does not hold a charge well and the hard drive has failed.  Apple warranty has expired so I am left to ebay parts repair.  I think the quality of this model is lacking and would not recommend buying it.  That said, iPods in general are great and there are many other alternatives now that work very well.  My 4GB Mini is still going strong.

I gave up waiting for the Squeezebox Touch to arrive so I bought this.  (There was a great deal on it online.)  I am very happy I did.  I cannot possibly explain all of the features in a review, so I won't try.  What I can tell you is that - once set up - it does everything it says it will.  I am able to stream music from the internet and my desktop iTunes to my living room sound system.  The remote works great (although sometimes it takes a moment for button presses to be recognized.)

I am not a wifi expert, but it does take a little tinkering to get it to work.  Logitech support is terrific if you run into trouble.

Overall, I am really happy with my purchase and give this a rare (for me) five star review.

I gave up waiting for the Squeezebox Touch to arrive so I bought this.  (There was a great deal on it online.)  I am very happy I did.  I cannot possibly explain all of the features in a review, so I won't try.  What I can tell you is that - once set up - it does everything it says it will.  I am able to stream music from the internet and my desktop iTunes to my living room sound system.  The remote works great (although sometimes it takes a moment for button presses to be recognized.)

I am not a wifi expert, but it does take a little tinkering to get it to work.  Logitech support is terrific if you run into trouble.

Overall, I am really happy with my purchase and give this a rare (for me) five star review.

This is a great keyboard and mouse combo.  Here are some things I didn't see in other reviews and are not in the description:

1) The left and right mouse buttons are fairly stiff - meaning you have to push them with some effort.  Maybe this will improve as the mouse is used more, but out of the box, I find myself having to re-click things I think I already clicked once

2) The left side of the keyboard has back and stop keys.  The top left of the keyboard has media player controls (play, pause, stop, rev, fwd).  Top right has, in order, mute, vol down, vol up, email, web, calculator.

3) The keyboard buttons are a bit mushy, but I like that.

4) The keyboard is full size, but doesn't take up a ton of desk real estate with extra surface area.

5) The photo on the Amazon page shows the receiver with a USB pass through - mine looks completely different from the photo - there is no USB pass-through.

6) The mouse is thin, so if you want something more substantial you might not be happy.

Overall, I really like this combo and it has the typical quality you would expect from Logitech. (I am a fan of their products.)  The software CD add some nice customization, and has web update features.

This is a really good product and I hope to use it for many years.

This is a nicely formed still/video camera.  It feel good in your hand and the buttons feel high quality.  The screen looks nice and the sound is reasonable for such a small device.  The software/firmware is absolutely abhorrent.  The whole point of this particular camera is that you can attach to a wifi hotspot and upload pictures/videos to various services, including picassa and facebook.  I simply could not get it to work.  I was able to connect to a wifi spot in my house, and log into my various services but each time it tried to upload a photo or video it returned an error asking me to "please try again later."  This happened across multiple services, mulitple different days, and over multiple different wifi connections.  Also, each time it needs to access the internet, it needs to reestablish the whole wifi connection anew.  Typing WAP passwords on the on-screen keyboard becomes very old very quickly.

I was able to eventually upload some photos and videos onto my computer using the simple pop-out USB connector (same as a flip video camera).  The videos had good sound, but the picture quality of both videos and photos left a lot to be desired.  Indoor photos looked very grainy (the "flash" is nearly useless).  Outdoor photos lacked vibrant color, though much better than indoor photos.

The battery seems to last a very long time - I did not encounter any low battery warnings after a full day of shooting photos and videos with limited flash usage.

All in all, this might be a great camera with a firmware upgrade and some major bug fixes.  However, as it exists now, I would not recommend it.

This is a great airplay system, assuming you want airplay and not Bluetooth. This uses your wifi so it works well when you want to move the speaker all around your house without regard to where the source is. Bluetooth would require it be within a few yards of the source.

Set up was pretty easy and the sound is what you would expect from a portable speaker. Not quite audiophile sound, but good enough for most informal needs. Background music. I had it drop out from time to time, but that was near the edge of my wifi range.

I have had at least a half dozen different Harmony remotes over the years.  This is an interesting concept, but go in with your eyes wide open what it is - and what it isn't.

My biggest problem is that it is an RF ONLY remote.  Whereas most Harmony RF remotes will also allow the remote to operate certain devices over IR, this does not.  Your iphone does not have an IR emitter and the simple handheld remote here does not have an RF emitter.  Thus, if you have a plasma on the wall and components inside a cabinet, this will not work.  The blasters inside the cabinet will not do anything for your plasma.  I get around this with my 900 because the 900 uses IR for my TV and RF for everything else.  It simply cannot be done with this.  Also, this only gives you one aux blaster, although there are ports for two.  This simply cannot work for my application.

Moving the setup to the phone and web is interesting.  I preferred the application, but it is just me being resistant to change.  My 900 settings moved over very easily with just a little necessary tweaking.

I don't like the lack of dedicated skip and review apart from FF and REW.

Be aware that this remote has a replaceable disk battery (looks like a quarter), but is not rechargeable.  Since it does not have a screen, it should last awhile.

Most (all?) of the buttons are dual purpose - with short and long hold options.  Thus, the three activities on the remote, are really six.

Big limitation if you have multiple wifi networks in your house.  The Harmony and your phone must be on the same wifi network.  My phone grabs whatever is strongest, so if it grabs a different one from the one the Harmony is attached to, I am out of luck.  Big annoyance.  Not sure why it is set up that way.

DISCLOSURE:  This item was sent to me through the Amazon Vine program.  Not sure why the usual banner is not automatically showing up.

I have four of these around my house.  The cameras are easy to configure on my network and they give a nice picture.  One star deduction because the sound is terrible - lots of background static.  Also, the base cannot be removed - it doesn't have a standard tripod mount in the back - which is odd.

The mydlink iphone app is only OK.  IP Cam Viewer is much better.

I have owned this for a few years at home and just bought another for my office at work.  The key response is great and the mouse feels terrific in the hand.  For some reason the feature buttons stoped working after a few months, but reinstalling the software seems to have fixed that.  Tilting the mouse wheel can browse back and forward.  There are enough other buttons on the keyboard to do everything you really need - especially mute the sound.  Battery life is reasonable and wireless range is all you should really need for a desktop set-up.  I am very happy with the purchase - so happy I bought another set-up for my office.

Big beautiful screen which is very responsive.  The only reason for the one star deduction is because the sound through the speaker is terrible.  Beyond bad.  It is not very loud and you cannot even really understand what it is saying. "OK Google" commands result in garbled answers.

The speaker for phone calls is fine.

The unit itself is awesome for what it is (other than the speaker).  It comes with a removable battery, but don't plan on changing it very often, because you will probably end up breaking the back - you have to pry open some thin plastic tabs to open the back and deal with the battery.

It comes with a usb wall wort and a micro-usb cable.

This can use multiple SIM cards and a micro SD card.

In case there is confusion, this is a 3-way switch.  It really meets a lot of needs.  It can be set auto on/timer off or push on/timer off.  The timer can be adjusted down to 1 min of inactivity.  All of the timer off settings also allow push off override (although if set to auto it will kick in if there is subsequent motion).  Installation is easy and there are real screw terminals, not pigtails that require nuts and take up lots of room in the box.

This is perfect for recessed lighting in a kid's bedroom.  The occupancy sensor makes sure that if your kid leaves the light on, they don't burn all day.

Unlike other switches that leave a lot of guesswork when programming, this uses digital programming - no dials hidden behind the faceplate.  Progamming can be adjusted without removing the faceplate.

Double tap brings the lights up to full strength.

Single tap brings the lights to the most recent dimmer setting.

30 seconds before the timer turns out the lights, they dim to 50% to give you the opportunity to move around and not be left in the dark.

The occupancy sensor has a near 180 degree field of view and we have not encountered any false triggers.  When sitting fairy still - such as typing on a computer - it might not sense the movement of your fingers.

Wish they offered this with a light sensor, so the auto on doesn't trigger when the room is lit with daylight.  Also wish they offered this as a z-wave model.

Wow.  Just.  Wow.

This case does an awesome job of doing only what it is supposed to.  It has a 3100 mah battery that give you almost two additional full charges (iphone 6).  It doesn't block any of the ports or buttons and the speakers sound fine with this.

Only two complaints -

1 - there is absolutely no excuse why the port on the bottom to charge the whole thing up is a micro-usb and not a lightning port
2 - the headphone jack is really recessed.  They give you an adapter to make it work, but that is a bit jeryrigged.

I highly recommend this as it is absolutely the best iphone battery case out there.  I only wish SOMEONE would make one that is lightning through and through.

This is a great switch for lights.  It is a single large push button (not a rocker) for on and off. The side has a dimmer up down with leds on the left to show you the dimmer level.  (Although there are six or seven led lights on the side, there are infinite levels of dimming.)  The remote also has a button for a "favorites" position to set the lights to a preset dim level.

The on and off both are accomplished with a fade in or fade out - which is a nice effect.

I am using two of these switches in different situations.  In one room the switch controls six recessed incandescent ceiling lights.  It works great and dims them very well from full bright down to barely on.

The switch does not claim to work with LED lights.  My second application has the switch controlling two wall sconces with medium base 8w (60w equivalent) LED dimmable bulbs.  Here, the switch works fine on full and down to about half strength.  Below half strength it causes the LED bulbs to flicker.  I suspect the bulbs simply are not getting enough power to stay lit.

Wiring and installation are pretty straight forward.  The switch has red, white, black, and greed leads leaving the switch.  It should be noted that the switch itself is pretty large and is a bit of a space hog in a cramped electrical box.  Four lead wires means four wire nuts.  I had to trim my wiring pretty substantially to get it all to fit well in the wall box.

The funky faceplate can be removed and used with a standard decora switchplate.  I'm using a two gang cover so the included cover did not work for me.

This is a decent basic bluetooth puck speaker.  It pairs fairly easily to your iphone (and reconnects each time).  It charges with a proprietary cable - not micro usb, which would have been MUCH more useful.  The music sound quality is OK but amplification is minimal.  Might be okay in a quiet bath, but the shower makes too much noise.  You can play/pause, skip, or reverse tracks.  You can also adjust volume up and down.

It is fairly useless for phone calls.  I can hear my phone ringing - so I know someone was trying to reach me while I am in the shower - but communication on either end is virtaully impossible.  I can somewhat make out what they are saying, but everything I say is garbled (the mic is terrible with no noise cancelling).

The instructions suffer from "Google translate" issues.  It is small and the battery seems to last a few hours.  There is no warning when the battery is getting low.

The back has a permanently attached large suction cup.

This is a must have if you have an Apple TV.  That remote is just too darn small and easy to loose.  We use this on our boat, where remotes get lost even more easily.  This fits perfectly and looks great.  It has a large double stick backing pad that adheres to the cabinet behind our sofa easily.

This is a very small speaker with very big sound.  It really is amazing how big it sounds with a fair amount of bass, but little mid-range.  It is not for autophiles, but most people will be pretty impressed with the sound.  It easily pairs via bluetooth with any smartphone or music source - not just iphones.  It was very easy to set up.  It has a charging base that you can leave the speaker on, or just lift it off take the speaker with you and use via battery.

My only complaint is that the sound, while big, has little separation for left and right channels.  I'm not sure, but it might just simplify the signal into a mono effect.  The speaker itself is the size of a child's sneaker, so it's not surprising that it does not create a large soundfield.

I think this is an excellent solution for anyone looking for a basic bluetooth speaker.  It does not give large stereo sound.  It does not support airplay.  The battery lasted several hours at moderate volume.

My 5 year old really wanted a cd player.  This is what we got her.  She is able to work it by herself.  I don't like the antiquated radio dial (turn to tune - not digital at all).  It has reasonable sound quality.  Even when turned to maximum volume (not especially loud) it doesn't have extreme distortion.  Good enough for what it is.  We leave it plugged in, so I can't comment on battery life.

This remote is simply awesome. I have been a long time Harmony owner - have had at least six earlier models (probably more). If you need the RF capabilities, this is the remote for you (otherwise, go for the Logitech Harmony Touch Universal Remote with Color Touchscreen - Black (915-000198)). This RF remote allows you to put all of your components in a closed cabinet and the remote transmits to a hub in the cabinet via radio waves (not line of sight) and the hub translates that into regular IR signals to your components. The function is the same as the Logitech Harmony 900 Rechargeable Remote with Color Touch Screen, which is the remote from which I upgraded. This new model is ages faster than the 900 was. There is zero lag between pushing the button and a response. You really can now flick from channel to channel without delay. The screen is gorgeous and I like the lighter feel of the remote. I wish the play, pause, stop, ff, rew buttons were below the screen. This will take some getting used to. Every hard button can be programmed for a long or short push with different responses for each. There is even a little vibrator (adjustable) that confirms the soft button pushes. This remote includes an IR transmitter right on the remote (not found on the Logitech 915-000194 Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone App and Simple Remote - Black), so you can have the remote use RF for some components and IR for others. (For example, my plasma on the wall cannot see the hub or any of the blasters, so I use IR from the remote to turn it on.) Complaints - - I don't like that the hub and your iphone need to be on the same wifi network for iphone to control things. The iphone app needs some work (ok, a lot of work) I wish there were more than two blaster ports on the back of the hub (my av cabinet has more than three shelves). The play, pause, stop, ff, rew buttons should be below the screen for easier use.

I hate this thing.  It is complete junk and does NOT work well at all.  If you live anywhere with more than three or four radio stations, you will experience inteference using this.  Save yourself the trouble and get something that wires directly into your radio via cable or cassette adapter.

The fatal flaw is that you are using this in a car and moving through different transmission areas.  There is no way you can stay on one station - any station - and not eventually have a problem.

The only reason I gave this two stars is that it charges your ipod.

I have two of these on my boat networked via NMEA2000 with a 700i receiver.  These work great to act as a nice remote, although I wish the screens were color.  My one star deduction is because it can be difficult to see which zone you are adjusting on the screen.  The contrast just isn't really great.  It is a very easily one wire installation.

As far as I am aware, this only works as a remote for Fusion electronics, but I think it would work as a NMEA repeater if you just wanted another depth gauge or something.
Great amp.  It is easy to hook up, uses a reasonable amount of power and gives great sound.  I use this on my boat in a protected location.

This really only works between a corded headset and a corded phone. It will not work with a 3.5mm earphone jack and it will not work if you just try to plug it straight into the wall.  It only works between a corded headset and a phone.  It also requires you to lift the handset off the cradle yourself to answer calls.  there is an accessory lifter, but that is extra.  The sound quality is adequate.  I found the headband comfortable, but none of the earpiece-only sizes was comfortable (I use an earpiece only one at work).

The corded phone must have a separate headset, not a clamshell phone where the headset also has buttons.

This is a trapizodial box with a zipper top.  There is a wire frame you must push down to get it to stand up.  (Hint: place it on a hard flat surface to get the wire sides to stay in place.)  There is a zipper across the top, handles on the sides and cynch straps on each side to tighten ____ (?) (I have no idea.)

Mine arrived incorrectly assembled.  The cynch straps ran outside the handles and made the handles unusable.  I looked at the picture on the box and realized the cynch straps were supposed to go inside the handles.  You can't unthread the cynch straps, but you can unhook them from the bottom attachment and re-run them.

The "clear" panel on top is not clear at all.  Translucent maybe.  No chance you can see what is inside.

The "non-skid" base is really not very effective at all - especially because the smooth fabric from the sides wraps around the bottom edges.

I really don't understand the purpose of this.  A cardbox would do the same thing.  In fact, it might do it better.  This has a trapizodial shape which is smaller on the bottom than the top. This greatly reduces your ability to put things in the bottom.  It also only has a central zipper, so you can't even open the whole thing up to put in tall items.

There are no internal dividers, and not even any tie down points around the outside to afix it to the floor of your trunk.

Essentially, you are buying a fairly ineffective box with a THULE logo on the outside.  I, for one, am not at all impressed with this product and do not recommend it.  Two stars - not one - because the fabric, zipper and overall assembly are pretty high end.

Three prong cable with angle plug - lays flat against the wall so you can push furniture right up against the wall.  It only blocks one of the two plugs.  It is white, but not stark white - more of an off-white.

I purchased this based on prior work by Karen Casey and also because I am currently retired and needed a boost to my morning. However, this doesn't do it. The "inspiration" just isn't there. Decent arch support, but not what I was expecting. For all the raving about this brand, I thought the arch would be far more sturdy and comfortable, but it just didn't do the trick. I have very low arches and need good support to keep my feet from turning in. Also, the toe hold pulls my toe away from my foot and that is unacceptable as it causes spasms for me to have my toes pulled apart and kept that way. There was no way to adjust that area to keep the toe in it's normal position so I had to return them. I have 65 year old feet and they need a good shoe after all the work they've done for me!
The color was way too radical for the style. I thought I could push it but it was just too much "hey look at my feet!" for me. I love Teva, always comfortable.

users.query: This is the first book I have read by this author.  I enjoyed the story of Marie and the choice she made to go undercover.  I would have loved to read the entire story in one sitting because it was hard to put down.  I can't wait to read the rest of the books in this series.

cands.text: I thoroughly enjoyed reading this book.  The story was fantastic and the characters were believable.  I even found myself crying at one point!  This was my first book by this author and I look forward to reading more.

This was such an enjoyable read!  I believe it is the author's debut novel and is so well written, I can't wait to read more from this author.  I loved the main characters and the whole premise of the story.  Growing up with sisters, Suzanne tired of receiving hand me downs.  So I love that she finds out that not all hand me downs are bad.  I appreciate the relatable story and the easy friendship that developed between Suzanne and the new principal.  I loved how the conflict between her and his family was handled.  I will certainly enjoy reading more from this author.
I received a copy of this book from the author, but the review is completely my own opinion.

This is a great collection of novellas.  I loved the variety of story lines.  Some of the authors were new to me, so it was fun to read their stories and see their styles.  I am interested in reading more by Darlene Franklin, as A Taste of Honey was my first taste of her writing.  I enjoyed reading about Edith and Grant and their renewed friendship.

I have read and enjoyed several of Angela Breidenbach's books and was not disappointed while reading her story which took place at the Chicago Fair in 1893.

I was happy to see a copy of this book front and center at my local Christian bookstore, so I hope others will pick it up and enjoy it also.

This is a great set of novellas. The first book, All About Mercie, was my introduction to this author and I immediately fell in love with the characters. The series is about Scottlyn, a 16 year old victim of rape and her decision to keep her baby. We follow Scottlyn through her pregnancy with the help of Diane, a widow who takes her in. The story continues in book 2 which delves into forgiveness as Scottlyn learns to allow Mercie's grandparents, the rapist's parents, into their lives. And the series ends with book 3, Scottlyn's wedding and attempt to reconcile with her own parents. I highly recommend this entire series. You will be drawn in to this wonderful story and fall in love with Scottlyn and her precious daughter, Mercie.
I absolutely loved this book and couldn't put it down.  It has a great plot, incredible conflict and rich characters.  I am looking forward to reading more from this author.

This was the first book I have read by Anna Zogg. I won a copy of this book and didn't know what to expect. It is a fantastic book!  The development of her characters and the world building were great!  I can't wait to read the next book in the series.
This was a fun read.  I loved all the characters and was drawn in by the rich descriptions. This was the first time I have read a book by this author, but it is not the last.

This book was absolutely delightful!  I enjoyed the story and the character development.  I identified with Molly in many ways, so this book was such a pleasure to read.  I even cried in a couple places. I would love to read more books by this author.  This is the third book in a series of books in which the stories reflect themes of Shakespearean plays.  Such an unusual and unexpected twist for Amish novels.

I received a copy of the book by the Book Club Network in exchange for an honest review.  All thoughts are my own.

This is the fourth book in the Women of Valley View series. It can stand alone, but I recommend reading Callie, which is where you first meet Samantha and her sister, Iris.

I loved delving further into Samantha's story and seeing how much she has matured. As with the rest of the stories in this series, I found myself immersed in the lives of the characters. Samantha has come a long way and I couldn't help but empathize with her and the struggles she had in her faith. Sam has made a great life for herself and her daughter. She is in a promising relationship, although she will not allow it to go any further until her boyfriend, Patrick, understands his need to allow Jesus to become his Lord and Savior. Things seem to be going well until Louis comes to town and forces himself back into her life and that of their four year old daughter. All of a sudden, Samantha is forced to make some very serious decisions.

There are some intense moments for sure, but they are lightened by the antics of this sweet and precocious four year old. You will fall in love with her and laugh along at her interactions with her invisible friend. Or is it her guardian angel?  You decide.

This is a quick, easy read about a Confederate spy during the Civil War.  I enjoyed this story about the daring young lady,  Sophie, and her desire to help the Confederate cause. Because it is a novella, it didn't go into much detail, bit it was such a fun read. I believe this is the first book i have read by this author and look forward to reading more.
I received a copy of this book from the publisher a d Bookfun.org but was not required to write a positive review. The opinions are my own.

This is the first time I have read a book by Patricia Bradley and I was not disappointed.  I love reading suspense/mystery and this was a great read.  Dr. Leigh Summerall and her son have come back to Logan Point to help her brother, but he has been murdered. There is plenty to keep you guessing in this story.  The author has done a great job of developing the story, plot, and characters.  Ben, who had a whirlwind romance with Leigh ten years earlier, is the Sheriff on the case.  The investigation is complicated by Ben' feelings for Leigh and a secret that may tear them apart.  Ben's father, who was the sheriff before Ben, may have important information,  but is unable to communicate due to a stroke he had after being shot. There is murder, illegal dog fights and gun trafficking and Ben needs to sort it all out in order to keep Leigh and  her son safe.  I highly recommend this book.
I received a copy of this book from The Book Club Network and the publishers in exchange for my honest review which I have given.

This was a fun book to read.  It is written for children ages 8-12, and I believe this would be most suitable for that age group,  though I certainly enjoyed reading it myself.  I have not read the first two books in the series.  While this one can stand alone, I think reading the first two would definitely be beneficial in learning who is who and being introduced to some of the spy lingo.  The series also builds on itself. I think this lends to a successful following of fans as we get to know May and follow her career as a K9 Spy.  This story centers around May the newest canine spy having just graduated from the spy academy.  The story is written in first person from May's point of view.  It is a fast paced adventure that will be enjoyed by all.

I received a copy of this book from the author in exchange for my honest review which I have given.

This is a fantastic book!  I have already recommended the the Friends and Horses series many times, and this latest book is another great read.  Kate and her friends find themselves trying to solve not one, but 3 different mysteries.  Miralee Ferrell has such a way of giving each character their own unique personality. I love how well she portrays Pete, Kate's autistic little brother, and Jake who has some fun quirks.  I love how the author effectively allows for the friends to gently point out to Jake when he has gone over the top without making fun of him.  There are some great lessons sprinkled throughout the entire book, but I especially love how in chapter 19 (I think it's 19)  where the kids learn how important it is to forgive even if you can't necessarily forget.

As with the other books in the series,  I highly recommend this one as well for any child between the ages of 9-13, or so.  I have not read the entire series, so believe each book can stand alone.  I can see where it would be beneficial to read all of them as it seems that each one may highlight a different friend a bit. However, the author has done a great job of weaving in a bit of history from previous books so that you get a feel of the background stories without rehashing it every time.
I received a copy of the book from the publisher.  The ideas expressed in this review are my own.

This third book in the Resolution series is another great read.  This book, though part of a series, can also stand alone.  Characters from previous books in the series also make an appearance.  Anika has had a rough life.  She was rescued from living with her alcoholic mother as a child and went to live with her aunt.  She desired to avoid making the same mistakes her mother made, but finds herself pregnant as a teenager and briefly turns to alcohol to escape.  The father of her baby has no desire to be a father and take responsibility, so encourages her to have an abortion.  Ani chooses to keep the baby and eventually moves to Resolution Island to make a new life for herself and her young son.  While there, the paternal grandfather sues for custody of her son.  She also meets an American who has travelled to Australia to fulfill the dying wish of his mother (another story in itself!) and has to face long buried attitudes and bitterness, before she can allow herself to love.  A murder, an illegal fishing ring, and the disappearance of her son add to the many twists to this beautiful story of love and forgiveness.  I highly recommend this book.  It does have some mature themes that would make this inappropriate for a younger audience.

I was given a copy of this book by the publisher and The Book Club Network in exchange for my honest opinion which I have given.

This was such a fun read!  I enjoyed every single page. The characters were so relatable.  It was such an encouragement to me that though this is fiction,  the message was real.  The truth will always win out.

This is the first book I have read by Carole Brown, but it will certainly not be the last.  I love a good mystery and this one delivered. From the first page I was caught up in the intrigue of this story about Tyrel, who was rejected as a soldier, but asked to serve his country as a spy during WWII.  The characters in this story were well developed.  This was definitely a page turner with enough twists to keep you guessing until the end.  I highly recommend this book and look forward to the next book in the series.

I received a copy of this book from the author in exchange for my honest review which I have given.

This is the second book in what I hope is a seies of several books in the Jericho Resistance series.  I recommend reading A Rebel in Jericho first so that you understand who Mercedes is and how she met John.  It is referenced several times in Twice Redeemed, but no details are given.  I thoroughly enjoyed reading this book and believe the characters are well-developed and relatable. There are a few surprises sprinkled throughout the story and lots of action to keep you turning the pages.  The inclusion of the topic of human trafficking is handled well.  I look forward to reading the next book.
I received a copy of this book from the author.  This review is completely my own.

This was a great read. A little bit of romance and a lot of suspense. The author did a great job of keeping my attention. I loved the characters.  I was impressed with how accurately she described the narcissistic traits of the villian in this story.

I really enjoyed Maggie Dove.  It was a great read and kept me interested until the surprise ending.  I loved Maggie and the honest look at grief. I felt the author did a great job of developing all the characters.  I will be reading more from this author.
I received a copy of this book from the Publisher in exchange for my honest review which I have given.

This was a great debut novel by Danele Rotharmel.  I couldn't put it down.  It was well written and the characters were real.  It had so many twists and turns that left you on the edge of your seat, definitely a page turner.  I have told my husband he needs to read this book, too.  I highly recommend this book to anyone who enjoys a great story.

I loved this book from the very first page. It is a different type of coming of age novel.  Misha is a young man that has been groomed from early childhood to become a Greek Orthodox priest.  He meets and falls in love with the beautiful Anastasia and his beliefs and life journey take on a whole new perspective.  I love the theme of unity in this novel which takes place in Russia toward the end of the Soviet regime.  Russia is about to change and so is the course of Misha's life and you will definitely enjoy the journey. I highly recommend this book.

I received a copy of this book from the publisher.  The opinions expressed in this review are my own.

What a great novella. It is part of a larger collection of novellas, but can be purchased individually on Amazon Kindle. Deborah has been taking care of her sick mother for over five years and waiting for the love of her life, Curt, to return. Curt left as an immature young man to pursue his life long dream of building furniture and woodworking against his father's wishes. A family tragedy brings Curt home, but can he and his father reconcile their differences and will he be be able to win back Deborah's trust?

I received a complimentary copy of this book in exchange for my honest review which I have given.

I loved this book.  It is a great story with beautiful illustrations.  This is a story of two children that spend a day with their Nana and learn a valuable lesson in giving.  I can't wait to try the recipe that is included.  I also appreciate the label templates included in the back to make our own jars for saving.  This is a story I will revisit many times with my boys.

I received a copy of this book fromthe author in exchange for my honest review which I have given.

This was an enjoyable read.  Monday Morning Joy is a contemporary romance written by Tia McCollors, who is a new to me author.  I most likely will read more of this series.  This book is about Rae who is a reporter for her town's struggling paper and is moving on after a broken engagement.  We also meet Malachi, a hometown hero and professional  baseball player nursing an injured shoulder who comes to Greensboro to hold a baseball camp for children.  Rae reluctantly agrees to write a story about Malachi, who has a reputation as a womanizer, and his charitable organization.  Malachi has found faith and new life, but finds it difficult to change his reputation.  This was an enjoyable read.  Since I live near Greensboro, I felt that I could relate to the characters and the southern culture.

I received a copy of this book from the Publisher. This review is my honest opinion.

I highly recommend this book.  The Peaceful Wife is written by April Cassidy, a blogger, part-time pharmacist and full time wife and mother.  She lays out biblical principles for having a good marriage.  I love that the focus is on the wife.  It is sometimes hard to remember our role as the wife in the home.  Biblical submission is often misunderstood and I feel that this author has effectively described it.  She also gives chapter after chapter of practical ways to implement this practice into your marriage to increase the love, respect and intimacy that may be missing.  I believe this is a great book for all wives and wives to be to read.

I received a copy of this book from the Publisher. This review is my honest opinion.

This drive is a wee bit different in appearance from the photo displayed on the Amazon page: the monitor light is red, not blue. That's really neither here nor there, but here's a something you do need to know. I was growing untrustworthy of a 750gb drive which was already 99% full anyway, so I bought this drive. Right away I started getting errors that this file or that was too large for the new drive. WTF? A little googling and investigating revealed the problem: the drive came formatted for the old FAT32 system which has maximum file sizes. As someone who shoots photos in RAW which are 12Mb big when shot on a 12Mb camera, and who also does a little video, the file size limitations prevented a lot of data from being transferred.

While the drive looks tough (and probably is) the first thing you should is reformat it to NTFS, the more modern file system which tolerates large files. It's simple and quick, but save yourself some grief: do it before you start putting data on it.

I haven't used the drive long enough to give it 5 stars, but I gave it 3 stars for the rather dumb idea of formatting it FAT32, forcing many of us to reformat the drive.

cands.text: This book is well-organized, well-written, and chock full of illustrations and examples. I can't imagine why anyone wouldn't enjoy this book. I even enjoy reading things I already knew! I gave a Kindle copy to my sister who's just learning photography.

Having acquired two Yongnuo 560 speedlites, I wanted a bag large enough to handle my Nikon D600 with a big Tamron 28-300mm zoom as well as the two speedlites. This bag fills the bill and has room left over for a flashmeter and a Hyperdrive Space external photo storage unit (reads various types of memory cards and stores the photos on a hard drive). There is plenty of space left over for smaller accessories, USB/Firewire cables, lens cloths, etc. If you have what may be about the same volume of gear you want to be able to carry in one bag, this could be the bag for you.

As for construction, it seems very well made.

If I have one complaint, they got creative with the padded part of the shoulder strap. Rather than being straight, it is shaped like a scallop. I have been unable to find a truly comfortable way of using it. So, if it proves a problem for you, do what i did: use the strap from your prior camera bag.

All in all, an excellent purchase with which I'm quite pleased.

I've been a professional photographer for 15 years and while I know many consider Photoshop the gold standard in photo editing, photo optimizing and repair, and artistic effects, I have always found the user interface poorly designed. It has a steep learning curve to do things which are easy in other software.

My two primary photo editing programs are JASC's by now ancient Paint Shop Pro version 7 and, until recently, Ulead's PhotoImpact 6. I say recently, because Corel bought the rights from Ulead and have put out an updated version, Corel PhotoImpact x3, which is in many ways a subtle improvement. I say "subtle" because anyone who has used Ulead's pre-Corel version will find Corel's version very familiar with little or no learning curve adapting to the upgrade.

Do I turn to Photoshop occasionally? Sure, but mostly for effects which are absent in other software or which Adobe does somewhat better. However, 99% of the time I use Paint Shop Pro (also bought by Corel, redesigned, and renamed Paint Shop Pro Xn with "n" standing for the latest version) but given a worse user interface in order to seem more modern and provide easy access to the many added features you're very unlikely to use).

If you were to have only one photo editing program, I'd recommend any version of PhotoImpact. If you have the money, get Corel's latest version. If you have budgetary restrictions, you can find PhotoImpact 6 here and there for only about $30.

I'm sure you've seen film or video of an icebreaker slowly slogging along as it breaks up the thick ice. That's how I felt as I plowed through this book. At about 1/3 of the way through I gave up. There are several reasons. The writer's style is dense, and although heavy on description, he has little talent for creating characters. Most of them are 2-dimensional cardboard characters of the Clue (game) variety, many of whom wouldn't be out of place in an Agatha Christie novel, though Mrs. Christie was a far better writer and vastly more economical writer. Every character is pretty much little more than a type. You have a British lord, a generic American President with generic advisors, generic intelligence officers in various governments. Yawn. The author has to learn to build his characters more on their thoughts and interactions with the other characters. Another problem is that 1/3 of the way through the book, there was/were no character or characters I either liked or found fascinating enough to force me to keep turning pages. At about the same time I got John Locke's Lethal People and was blown away by how quickly I got involved with his main character, Donovan Creed, a character who perfectly balances being fascinating and kind with being evil. Finally, I'm not a big fan of the huge paragraph style of writing, and Ruppert's book is riddled with very long paragraphs. Based on what I've told you, you might be thinking "Just my kind of book!" It's not mine. At $.99, I can't even say "worth every penny."

Others have explained that this pack is small. Well, they tell you it's a 20-liter pack. A little research will tell you that that's pretty small. It was just the right size for what I wanted, which was to take a sandwich, drink, and maybe jacket or sweater to work.

The problem isn't the size of the pack itself, it's that the shoulder straps are too short for an adult male like me. I'm not a terribly big guy. Just 5'10" with shoulders that are not in any way extra-wide and with the straps extended as far as they'd go, it was a real struggle to get it on. Sometimes the strap would pull through the buckle due to my efforts to get it on.

THIS SHOULD BE DESCRIBED AS A PACK FOR CHILDREN AND SMALL ADULTS!!!

About me: I'm a pro photographer and I wanted a knocking around camera that met several requirements. First, I wanted a camera that was relatively small. Second, I wanted one that's relatively lightweight. Third, I wanted one that was very "point and shoot." Fourth, I wanted quite a bit of zoom range, not 5x or even 10x, but much more. Fifth, I wanted a camera capable of taking very good photos. Finally, I wanted one that was cheap.

My work camera is a Nikon D600. This is technically more of a high-end "prosumer" camera than a true pro camera. That said, it gets the job done for me and the extra money spent on a true pro camera wouldn't provide any benefit to a guy who shoots pretty girls mostly indoors. If I shot sports or wanted a camera to take with me to the summit of Mt. Everest, I might spend two or three times as much, but the D600 has all the image quality of its much more expensive siblings and weighs less, which has become important to me. Even with the D600, I can have sore shoulders after 6 or 8 hours of continual shooting.

While my D600 could be put into Program or Auto mode and be used as a point-and-shoot and still take great photos, and while I had a wide-range (28-300mm) zoom, it didn't meet the other three requirements of being small, light in weight, and inexpensive.

My need was for a camera I could take with me all day without its weight wearing me out, without keeping me distracted as I manage all of its controls, and for a camera that wouldn't have me in tears if I dropped it or it was stolen. Let's face it: walking around with a D600 and a big lens is an invitation to have it taken at gunpoint!

I had been keeping my eyes open for just the right camera at a great price when I got an offer from one of the major discounters (not Amazon, sorry to say) offering the Nikon L310, factory refurbished, for just $99.99. I checked out the specs and the reviews and decided that this looked like a good bet. At just about $100, it would still be worth it even if was a bit disappointing.

I've had it for a little while now and I'm pretty pleased with it. Were I not a pro, I'd probably be totally happy with it, but I'll try to look at it from the point of view of the casual photographer who mainly takes personal, family, and vacation photos. Looked at that way, it's a great buy even at twice $99.99.

Getting back to my requirements and how it satisfies them...

Size: The L310 is quite small. Photos of it without something to give one a sense of scale tend to be a little misleading, since it looks kind of like a DSLR, but in truth it's about 60%-75% of a Nikon or Canon DSLR in physical dimensions.

Weight: The L310 weighs about a third what my D600 with its 28-300mm lens mounted weighs, much of that weight coming from the four AA batteries that power it. It's not so light that a strong breeze could blow it off a picnic table, though hurrican force winds might.

Ease of Use: For a pro, it's frustratingly easy. There is no (M)anual mode whatsoever. No (S)hutter Priority or (A)perture Priority modes, either. Every photo you take with it is either totally or mostly totally automatic. You can control ISO but most of your control actually comes down to choosing what program mode to use. And it has a lot of different program modes. Almost too many, I'd say. If anything, they overdid the program modes bit. Mostly, you'll be safe to just leave it in AUTO or EASY AUTO mode.

Zoom range: The L310 has a 21x optical zoom. This is fairly high. Other cameras have 24x or more, but 21x is a lot given that many cameras brag of having something like a 5x zoom. Of course, the problem as your zoom factor gets stronger is that the more zoom you use, the more camera wobble can screw up your shots making them soft or even blurred.

Quality of photos: It's a Nikon. The optics are good, the camera is well-designed, and so the photos are certainly plenty good for a camera in this range. This camera is about as thoroughly automatic as a camera can be. It's designed by some of the best camera and optics engineers in the world. How could the photos not be good?!!!

Price: I've already talked about the price. Like I said, I got a refurbished (=newish) one for near $100. Amazon and others are selling them new at $200 or so and that's still a very good price.

Now, I didn't get into resolution as a requirement, and let me tell you why. The L310 is 14.1 megapixel camera, which is more than you need if you are even thinking of a camera in this general range. To tell you the truth, you can get a good 8x10 photo from a 3 megapixel camera. The current trend toward selling 20+ megapixels is insane even in the pro category. Unless one is shooting a mural, 14 megapixels is much more than adequate. In fact, since the camera gives you the option of shooting smaller photos, I'd set the camera to take photos no larger than 2048z1536 (3 megapixels). For family or vacation photos, this is more than large enough. If you take a lot of 14.1 megapixel photos, it will chew up a lot of space on your hard drive, and before you know it you'll be buying external drives just to house all of your needlessly large photos. Also, the larger the photos you take, the sooner they'll fill up your memory card.

Anyway, in conclusion, for the everyday non-pro user who wants a camera that meets the primary requirements I listed in the beginning, you won't do a whole lot better for $200.

First, to those of you who have cats, my cat decided she liked to lay down on top of this bag and her 8 lb weight squished it to one side and made it impossible to get back into its proper shape again.

More generally, it's a design defect that the bottom straps aren't 1-1.5 inches longer. My pannier rack is 5.5 inches wide, fairly normal, and that left very very little strap with which to secure the bag. I ended up doing a workaround, which I won't describe because unless the platform on your rack is around 4 inches wide, you'll have much the same problem.

Saving a little money on straps earned Schwinn one star.

Everything was great except there was a collimation problem. In other words, I was seeing double because the two optical sides were not pefectly parallel to each other. I know this is a fairly common problem in binoculars and may be a manufacturing issue or something that can happen if the product receives rough treatment in shipping. I decided rather than chance receiving a second one with this issue, I'd go with a pair of Bushnell Perma-Focus 10x50's, which arrived today and I'm finding to be quite satisfactory. BTW, they (the Bushnell) IS permanently focused and focused quite well I must say. The only adjustment the Bushnell product required was to align the optics with the distance between my eyes, which is done by spreading the two sides further open or pressing them together.

It was too bad about the Alpen Pros because they were very handsome. I wish they had worked out. I gave three stars because I assume they usually are properly aligned. I just didn't want to take the chance.

I just got the machine and loaded the basic software  I need to use with it. It runs fine so far. However, You should know that the textured-looking surface isn't printed on the computer. The surface actually is textured. So far, my cat hasn't tried to sharpen her claws on it, but...fingers crossed.

UPDATE: I've had it for a week now and am pretty pleased with it. I failed to note in my original review what you don't get that you do get on many other laptops. There is no video out port other than the HDMI port. There is also no ExpressCard slot which is how you'd normally be able to add, for example, FireWire capability. You can forget that. This is probably not a major problem for most people, but you should know.

*****Be sure to read the update at the end*****

First impressions. This is one scary knife. Scary looking and scary sharp. It requires care in opening and closing because the first 45 degrees of blade travel (or last if you are closing the knife) are quite heavily spring loaded. When you close the knife and it reaches that angle...SNAP! Heaven forbid a finger tip is in the handle's opening because it will be laying on the floor. This is because, like so many Cold Steel knives, the blade is beyond just "scary sharp." I would almost say it is "unreasonably sharp."

I've used many knives for many years, and when you collect knives as I have, you cut yourself sometimes, but this knife is a frickin' guillotine! I have yet to try the wave opening, which can probably be done without much danger, but I will be doing 2-handed closing of this baby. I want full control of the blade during the closing procedure.

In place of the opening studs many folding knives have, the Talwar has a plate. Right now, the action is difficult. The resistance is too high for me to reliably open the blade, and if I don't succeed, there goes the blade snapping back into the handle! Hopefully no finger tips have wandered back into the groove. I'm getting a torx tool to loosen the blade a tad, but I fear what I'm up against is spring tension not tightness.

So much for the safety aspect.

Ergonomically, well, I've already mentioned the dangers of opening and closing. Otherwise, the knife is a dream. The G1 scales are very "grippy" (an expression another user used somewhere). The handle is also a grip. The first finger indent is very deep and won't ever let your hand slide forward onto the blade. But you can also grip it from the second indent, in which case the 4" blade becomes, in effect, a 5" blade due to 1" of additional reach.

About the blade, the tip is needle-sharp and because the shape of the knife has a lot of "belly," it's a good slicer as well. Stab or slash, it has all the piercing and cutting power you could ever need.

It's a flat grind and the blade is fairly thin overall compared to other knives. It's just gorgeous. And I love the satin finish better than the stone washed finish of other Cold Steel knives.

The blade is made of AUS8 steel which some purists will say is not the very best, but jeez this is a very common steel in sub-$100 knives, and in fact this one cost me less than $50! It may not be the best but when I consider the stupid-sharp edge on this knife, I can't complain.

This is one helluva knife, but a dangerous one for the owner as well as any attacker. Use with caution!

UPDATE: I emailed Cold Steel's customer service dept and explained my problem with the stiffness of the knife and, guess what? They sent me an email with a return label for sending them the knife so they could look at it, no cost to me.

Two weeks later a brand new Talwar 4 shows up and it's much easier to open. So, ignore that guy who claims he got such bad customer service from Cold Steel. He didn't sound very polite anyway. Antagonizing customer service people is never the best way to get them to help. Ask them to be your hero and by helping you get the value out of the product that you paid for.
Good combo printer/copier/scanner. Just isn't the quickest product on the market, but the price makes it a good buy if speed isn't all that important to you.

It's a beast, plain and simple. It looks as dangerous as it is without going overboard the way knives aimed at 15 year old boys do. My only criticism is that the screws holding the belt clip on came loose and one actually fell out. I'll have to contact CRKT customer service to get a replacement.
The prints look great. I've only used it for a week though, so 5 stars means "so far."

This is a sharp-looking watch and after three days, I can't say it's lost any time at all, even though automatic watches don't keep time nearly as accurately as good quartz watches.

It's smaller than one might think, making it a unisex watch, I suppose. It looks okay on my rather slim male wrist, but on the wrist of a guy with hands like catcher's mitts, it mioght look out of place.

The only reason it doesn't have 5 stars is that the watch band will soon need to be replaced, it is already starting to fray.
So far so good. Looks well made, does the job. If I still feel the same in a year, I may come back and give it the fifth star.
Very solidly built and the L/XLG size fits my really big head just fine.

I got the red and it's the most beautiful appliance in my kitchen. I was concerned because this is one of the kettles with a base. I assumed that the base was a heat plate and since I have a cat, that worried me. However, (and I know this is hard to believe)l the base doesn't get hot. Even more puzzling, neither does the bottom of the kettle. So, no burned paws on my kitty. If I had a wish, it would be that the temp control was analog so that I could dial in any temp I wanted rather than choosing between five (full boil and four others).

No mystery chunks or shreds floating in "gravy." No "pate" (oh so French). No grain or even vegetables (why would a cat want blueberries or potatoes?). It's shredded chicken that you could probably make fantastic tacos with. The only additions are vitamins and minerals lost in the canning process. My cat is like those described in most of the other reviews: she's crazy for it. Basically, when I open a can and she smells the chicken, she turns from a cat into a monkey and won't leave me alone until I put her dish down on the floor. Try it, your kitty will like it! Yes, it's more expensive than Friskies or 9 Lives. In my case, a day a week of Tiki Cat Puka Puka (or Koolina Luau which adds bits of egg) is a healthy treat. The other days it's a good brand of grain-free food. She never gets seafood. It's not good for cats ([...]).

Contrary to one prominent review, my knife arrived plenty sharp. (Maybe that review was taken as feedback.) BUT, let's face it: daggers aren't for slicing tomatoes or beefsteak. Rather, the whole point (pun intended) of a dagger is its stabbing power, and the point on this dagger is very sharp indeed. I'm giving it four stars simply because of the sheath. As has been speculated, a sharp knife might slice its way right through the stitching. I would have preferred a Kydex plastic sheath. Another problem with the sheath is that, at least on mine, the snap was very difficult to secure. A couple times I thought I had secured it, but it popped open. I have got the snap to where it's useful and reliableby simply using it over and over and over.

My cat seems to like it, but she tends to like foods for a while then go "meh" and walk away. My trouble with this product here is that I bought the same food in the same size for $9.99 at my local Petco.

If I could give half stars, it would be 4.5 stars, not 5.

The phone's body is quite nice. Unlike many other phones, the body is made of plastic with a rubbery feel to it. I often wonder if cell phones are so often made with a slick, slippery plastic in order to maximize the number of dropped phones and thus profits made on replacements. It has a certain amount of heft, which gives it a nice solid feel. It feels well made.

Because I wanted to migrate a phone number from Sprint to Virgin, the registration process was a bit more complicated than it might otherwise have been. I did have to make two calls from a friend's phone before I got it up and going, and while that was annoying, the Virgin employees assisting me spoke with a passably American accent, which was a nice change from so many other CS experiences I've had.

I used to own a small Virgin candy bar phone which I used to buzz people into my apartment building. It had its limitations. For example, I could only use Virgin ringtones. At the same time, I had the original HTC EVO 4G from Sprint, and it was a kick-ass phone. However, when I found myself hit hard by the recession I talked Sprint into switching me to one of their "dumb" phones on a cheaper plan to get me through to the end of the contract.

As my Sprint contract came to a close, I did a little research. Well, really, a LOT of research. When I research something I become possessed until I reach a decision. I told myself to be realistic about my needs and, as a result, one decision I made was that, while it would be nice to have a 4G phone, it would not be a deal killer to end up with 3G. I really don't use my phone enough for anything necessitating 4G.

I also told myself that at least for the time being I didn't want to be tied to a lengthy contract, so I decided to take a serious look at pay-as-you-go and prepaid phones/services. That pretty much eliminated the iPhone. Besides, my experience with the EVO taught me the Android interface, and I really felt that the Android market had all the apps I would ever need. No matter what you want, you typically end up with many 4 and 5 star choices.

When looking into plans, I did want as much unlimited service as possible, but if it would save me money, I would take a plan with limitations that would fit within my normal usage. In the end, I determined to give Virgin's 300 minutes + unlimited text/web a try for $35 a month. If I end up going over 300 minutes regularly, I'll go for the next step up which gives me 1200 minutes for $45 plus the unlimited text/web. I'm not a middle school girl, so there's no way in Hell I'll ever go over 1200 minutes.

Unlike the aforementioned minimalist Virgin phone, this more capable phone doesn't limit me to using Virgin's ringtones and wallpapers. I can choose from among the huge range of ringtones and wallpapers from sources like Zedge. I have loaded many Android apps and so far haven't found any that won't work. Of course, I filter them a bit based on some of the phone's limitations. One example: it has no forward facing camera. Neither does any other phone at anywhere near this phones $100 price range. Versus what I was paying before with sprint (about $70 a month) my savings on Virgin's $35 plan will pay for the phone in about three months!

One more thing, if you plan on storing much on the phone in terms of music and apps, you will probably want to replace the puny 2 gig MicroSD card with an 8 or 16 gig card.

I should, however, note that it can't play Flash graphics due to limitations in the processor speed and memory. You can, however, play Youtube videos and Youtube comes preinstalled on the phone.

This is a heck of a lot of phone for a mere $100. I can recommend it without reservation unless for some reason you absolutely must have 4G, a forward-facing camera, and/or Flash.

I love crayons, markers... I love crayola!

cands.text:
Anyone who knows me knows - i am a die hard sharpie loyalist! I have chisel tips, standard, fine point ... you name it I have it!

I got this set to add to my supply of sharpies based largely on the colors contained within it. The markers themselves, as fine points, allow for a smooth drawing and "coloring" of images as well as clear/crisp writing. In general the markers themselves when handled properly produce little to no bleed through - although i would be careful with the TYPE of paper you use them on to further minimize the possibility of bleed through.

This is one of two sets of sharpies that i have recently orderd - they are epic!

The fine point writes clearly, colors neatly and produces clean, crisp images/works when handeled properly. The storage container that the markers come in allow you to keep these markers neatly organized. While the markers themselves do not put through much if any bleed through - it is worth noting that you should be careful of what paper/material these are used on and adjust your handling of them accordingly to ensure that you get the intended result.

My Review: I love using chalkboard art labels to augment the handmade products I create particularly my sewing pin cushion jars or piggy banks; this set of 30 some labels works pretty well - nice even surface to them and liquid chalk shows up quite brightly on them.

Notes/Final Thoughts: If you intend whatever you put on the label to be permanent I would strongly suggest fully decorating the label, allow it to try and then apply a matte finish spray to it (to seal it) before applying it to something such as a mason jar as it will contain mess and allow you to control your design more thoroughly.

Disclaimer: I received a discounted or free product in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

This was my first use of chalk markers - I found them quite fun!

Don't expect smooth application (like ink markers) of the chalk liquid, have rag near by if you need to turn the dual tip (which was an added bonus - having a chisel and a rounded tip all in one!) and be patient... you may have to go over your work multiple times to achieve the desired effect.

The thing that frustrated me about this product however was the "priming" - I followed the directions to a T on the product packaging and found that it took me longer than implied (it doesn't state a time specifically but the implication is just mere minutes IMHO), approximately 20-25 minutes of shaking and pressure release to get liquid to fill the tip so the marker could be used as directed.

I got these cupcake liners because it was the biggest back for good price; they are quite nice - the tube they come in is handy when storing them while not in use. The variety of colors was a plus (although the "red" is more of a pink - which was a bit disappointing), each "section" (2 per color) seems that it should hold 25 liners.. however I found that my purple liners (at the top) were a few short, but the yellow liners made up for as there was a few extra of that color.

I have a small French lop bunny named Oreo - who became obsessed with the Christmas tree this year and was quite sad when we finally took it down... actually he became a bit irate to put it mildly. We realized that he liked the colored lights (at least that was the working theory) and got this light for him... it's small and quite compact ..... taking up very little space; the moment we turned it on Oreo started doing binkies (happy bunny jumping) in the cage. Ever since it has become a daily thing to turn the light on for my weird fur baby so he doesn't go rage bunny on the others in the cage... we will likely have to purchase another as I am sure it is not meant to be used as much/often as we use it to pacify Oreo lol
Good variety of colors - the drop bottles make it easy to use and even mix colors!

This was my first use of chalkboard paint and it was definitely a learning experience!

The consistency is slightly different from standard "2oz" acrylic paints - a bit more grainy maybe? The smell is also a bit ... noxious; I had windows open and opened more but apparently the ventilation was not quite good enough to prevent me from getting a "paint headache"... my fault though not the product.

Depending on the surface you are applying this too you may need to do more than one coat of paint - additionally I recommend ample drying time between coats and using any fixative finishes to achieve the best appearance.

Jack Williamson deserves to be remembered among the all-time science fiction greats.  With The Humanoid Touch, he revives the humanoids - robots whose Prime Directive is to protect Man from harm.  The Humanoids debuted in "With Folded Hands" in the late 1940s (which I've read) and in the novel The Humanoids (which I've not).  In The Humanoid Touch, a last bastion of humanity tries to hide from or fight against the inevitable humanoid advance.
Williamson's humanoids are provocative in every sense.  What happens when robots become too perfect, no matter how "benevolent" their intentions?  There is a latent horror throughout the book as the characters realize the humanoids are near.  Williamson succeeds in creating the aura of fear that Saberhagen hints at with his Berserkers, or Star Trek with the Borg.  Williamson's humanoids, however, are far more terrifying than either - who would have thought the words "At your service" could induce such spine-tingling horror?
The human characters more or less get in the way of the true protagonists, and here is where Williamson's skills perhaps aren't quite up to snuff.  The interaction and personal relationships between characters is not much more advanced than in his 1930s pulp sci-fi Legion series (a nevertheless fine read).  And the ending doesn't sit right; it's on the one hand too pat, and on the other too troubling - I can't say more without divulging spoilers.
All in all, however, this one ranks as a must read by all science fiction fans.  The humanoids are among sci-fi's greatest creations, easily the equal of Dune's Fremen or Asimov's psychohistory.  If you thought the Borg were creepy, you haven't seen anything until you've seen the humanoids.

cands.text:
Another serious case of mispackaging by Pocket.  The legend across the top of the cover declares "Captain Picard must keep a deadly weapon out of enemy hands!!"  The back of the book says Picard must stop all other races from acquiring superweapons.  And there is Jean-Luc's face on the cover.  All balderdash.  Picard plays but a minimal role, and these "superweapons" are nothing more than red herrings, declared such by Geordi LaForge during the first ten pages.  Instead, the hero of this one is none other than weenie extraordinaire Wesley Crusher.
It was with a somewhat nauseated feeling that I realized that Wesley was to play a major role in Balance of Power.  To my utter astonishment, not only did Wesley not bother me, I actually *enjoyed* him.  Ab Hugh has done a wonderful job bringing us a Wesley that is interesting and believable while staying remarkably faithful to the original.  Under his skillful pen (er, keyboard), we can actually appreciate Wesley's need to leave Starfleet and join the Traveler - and since the Wesley Joins the Traveler episode ranks among the worst, that is saying something.
The plot is entertaining if somewhat strained.  Other reviewers have complained about the implausibility of a high-stakes auction for what appears to be junk, but one can easily put that aside and enjoy a fun ride featuring two greedy Ferengi (sorry for the redundancy), the Grand Nagus, and, of course, Cadet Crusher.
I disagree with others who complained that the characters did not ring "true."  On the contrary, Balance of Power is the best Trek book I have read in a long, long time - the best at capturing the characters, the best at entertaining, and the best at keeping me interested until the very end.  It makes me regret giving out so many three stars to other Trek books.  If only they were all like this . . . .

With one exception, everyone who has reviewed The Gods Themselves has raved about the middle section, and rightly so.  In part two of The Gods Themselves, Asimov reaches a level of prosaic abilities he never achieved in any of his other works.  Asimov creates a strong emotional attachment between the reader and Odeen, Dua, and Tritt.  The effect he accomplishes has less to do with a well-designed alien culture than with a knack for showing the deepest feelings of these beings, feelings that are based on another culture but which we find ourselves relating to.
That we end up caring so much about Odeen, Dua, and Tritt, only makes the other two parts of the book that much more uninspiring.  The human characters, while not entirely cardboard, lack the depth of the aliens.  Mostly it's because of a stylistic change.  We see Odeen, Dua, and Tritt primarily through their own self-introspection.  The humans are developed entirely through dialogue; we are never given a peek into their heads and so, frankly, don't really care about them.
Parts one and three aren't terrible, but standing by themselves they are unmemorable.  Part two, however, deserves to be read by every fan of the creative imagination.
