I cried, squirmed, laughed, even jump out of my chair inresponse to many scenes & story twist.  I simply cannot put itdown.  I almost called in sick from work as I stayed up till dawnreading this darn book!  I agree with one of the reviewer here inAmazon, I was like a zombie at work too!  hehe...  I must say thoughthat the effort was pleasingly worth it.  I cannot even understand whythe avg rating here is only 4 1/2.  I say, it deserves more than justa 5... A 10 would be perfect!
Jennifer & Royce... both heartwarming couple!  Different yet perfect for one another.  Theirconfusions of love & hate made their love story riveting.  Trapbetween love & loyalty for country also made this story moreexciting.  Just when you begin to feel they start loving &trusting each other, situations/circumstances forces them to makechoices, which often times, lead them back to where they've started -hate & mistrust.  Really exhilarating....  Of course, love wins inthe end ... love set them both free!
I totally disagree with somereviews in regards to Jennifer being so "stupid" for notseeing his family & kin's faults.  For me, it is understandable& her loyalty for them actually makes me admire her more.  Itwould turn me off if she was easily swayed to give up her family &people without even trying... I say this book is more realistic! Yes,she's blind not to see the true color of her father... but regardlessof his mistakes, they are still her family.  She loves her father justlike any daughter would.  She also longed to be accepted & lovedby her people ever since she can remember & when they finally gaveher attention and recognition (which was his father's plan just tomanipulate her), it was difficult for Jennifer not to feel otherwise. Her choices, especially during the tournament made me squirm (i won'ttell what she did, don't want to ruin it for others...) Oh, but Icouldn't believe she did that!  I wasn't disgusted though, I feltsorry for her. I can tell it was a hard decision for her to make,however wrong it might be.  But this is where Judith McNaught reallyproved how she can touch her reader's soul by over turning this badchoice that Jennifer made. J.M.  wrote a wonderful come back at theend of this tournament (again, i won't tell...), which proved thatlove is far greater than pride and even life...  It is simply amazing!
Each page of this book contains many exciting scenes.  Amusingscenes: like the "THIS IS FORTY..." scene, her escaping fromcaptivity, the wedding & etc....  Heart warming scenes: WhenJennifer decided the fate of the boy who threw mudcake at her, WhenRoyce acknowledge her to his people, etc....  I can point outnumerous, numerous gestures in this book that really made my hearttwirl such as Jennifer kissing Royce's battle scars, standing in thebalcony together - sharing minds & dreams. There's more, lots more.... but I think it is best for the reader to find it out themselves. I can assure you, this book is really one of a kind.  The one youwouldn't want to miss.  If you are a romance book reader, YOU GATTAHAVE THIS ONE.

TRILOGY IN SEQUEL: The Pirate Prince.....The Princess......The Prince Charming
In addition to the EDITORIAL REVIEWS above: I specially admired the way Gaelen Foley created a make-believe Island of Ascension and molding it with the facts of history. It makes the history of Napoleon's family and his conquest, The Russian Czar's, French Revolution, Spanish Colonies and etc. more of an interesting read.  Although, this one was a bit slow and wordy in the beginning compared to the other two books in the series, it's still an entertaining read.  Educational and fun at the same time.
Darius Santiago: Definitely DARK and scarred hero.  He was introduce to us in the first book of the series, The Pirate Prince.  At that time, he was only 15 years old yet he's been through a lot of hardship.  Abused and enslaved.  However he was also characterized as a courageous and determined young man, who's also very loyal to King Lazar.  I was intrigued by his darkness so I was looking forward to read his own book.  Although, there was no detailed mention of what Darius went through during his slavery years in the hands of Malik (in The Pirate Prince), which I was looking forward to read,  I was still not disappointed by this book at all.  Oh, there's summary of his overall past, his tragedy years since childhood which made me feel for Darius.  It made me even admire his resistance and his disciplined manner.  He grew up quite, distant and secretive.  He concentrated on himself.  Worked hard on being the best in what he does.  He achieved everything that he thought mattered to him except deep down he needed something more... he needed love and Serifina. Despite his darksides, he is still an honorable man in most ways, that is why he had loved Sarifina for so long in secret.  He knows the Princess is off limit to him. The King had entrusted Serifina's safety over to him.  He is to guard her and not to have her for his own... He meant to keep the King's trust.
Meanwhile, The Princess Serifina: Beautiful, Rich, Royalty... not to mention KIND yet spoiled, carefree, impulsive, determined and a rebel with a cause... a very dangerous combination and a very irresistible one as well.  There is no self pity here for Serifina.  She knows what she wants then heads out to get it.  She isn't like some Princess story you normally would read who has a "pity-me-poor-little-rich-princess" attitude.  Nope, not Serifina.  She knows she is a Princess and she knows her station and her rank in life.  She would even use that valuable information to her advantage... and why not?  Call it selfish at times but that is what makes her more realistic in my eyes.  No martyrdom or overly good hearted Princess here either.  Serifina is unique and quite admirable.  I enjoyed her spunk, her witt and overall attitude.  She knows she wants Darius... so by treachery, seduction or even an honest-to-goodness confession, she meant to have him and she will.
Darius and Serifina's love story was truly an adventure. Pulse racing, heart stopping and heart warming all in one.  The reason why I didn't rate this book a five stars is 'cuz of the slow, wordy and repetitive information's.  Also, I would have prefer Lazar and Allegra to be more involved in their daughter's life.  It is admirable how they trusted Darius to care for Serifina's safety but it would have been a loving read to see both parents spend some quality time with her daughter.  Most specially a mother-daughter relationship scenes perhaps.  For both to talk about personal things such as love.  Considering Allegra was such a loving heroine in The Pirate Prince, who found true happiness and true love, I would have thought she would want the same for her daughter.  Both Allegra and Lazar had so much love in them in THE P.P that I expected more of them as parents.  For some reason their parenthood here became somewhat lacking.  Oh well, despite that small self-preferences, this book is totally entertaining.  It will capture not only your heart but your mind as well.  It will also lure you to read the next book of the series, The PRINCE CHARMING.  Don't wait, read the Ascension Trilogy and be 'awed' by this new Author.

users.query: This is a well-crafted book, melding the childhood relationship of two friends, the adult development of one of them (the narrator) who has trouble finding herself and her power in relationships, and fame in the worlds of dance and music. Relationships with their mothers and fathers are also important for both of the two friends. The narrator is a likable but frustrating character who seems too malleable. Her friend, her mother, and later her famous boss, have too much power over her, which is not a traditional gender submissiveness because the person with power also is a woman, and the narrator is uncomfortable with her malleability. Her lack of growth through much of the book is frustrating. Race also matters to the story as both the narrator and her friend are half black and half white, growing up in London housing projects. This is a good book for being pushed to take another perspective, and my feminist reading group had a great discussion of it. On the other hand, it is not really pleasant reading and can be slow going at times.

cands.text: I liked this book better after my book club discussed it.  The characters are memorable, although all are flawed. The author gives the reader access to their individual perspectives; yet, their persistence in doing things that have negative consequences makes them hard to like.  With few exceptions the relationships between any two people are difficult rather than supportive. The relationship between Don Chan and his daughter-in-law Esperanza is the most difficult of all the relationships. The narrative begins and ends with Don Chan, a widower of Chinese background who was an Invisible revolutionary in the Dominican Republic and who joins his sons family in NYC after his wife dies.  I had trouble deciding what the book is about: recent history of the Dominican Republic, the immigrant experience in NYC, love and family, hopes versus reality, probably all of these.  There are aspects of magical realism, especially in the fascinating character Hush who has special relationships with Don Chan, Esperanza, and her children Dallas and Bobby, and who engages in some unusual behaviors, such as eating the passages she especially likes from library books, which seems to have some parallel with Don Chans cutting out and keeping headlines from three newspapers each day. Esperanza is obsessed with the TV show Dallas, which she apparently believes to be true, and meets Bobby Ewing (Patrick Duffy) on the train. Readers who want every incident to be credible will be disappointed. Something is lacking in all of the characters' lives, which makes the book hard to read at times; but the author does hold out hope at the end.

This book interweaves the experiences of a teenage girl and an elderly woman whose childhoods at different times in very different places are parallel stories of abandonment, loneliness, and hardship.  Although the circumstances of these childhoods are unremittingly bleak, this is not a depressing book.  In fact, it is a lovely story of strong personalities ultimately persisting in spite of overwhelming odds.

I appreciate fiction that also educates.  In addition to an understanding of foster care from the child's perspective, I learned about an important but little-known piece of American history.  The title "Orphan Train" refers to trains run by charity organizations between 1854 and 1929 that moved over 200,000 orphaned or abandoned children from the east coast to the Midwest where they were supposed to find caring foster parents but often became little more than indentured servants.  The author portrays the leaders of this charitable effort as having low expectations for the children, and the children's lives as a series of dislocations outside their control.  Although the modern foster system has more protections and advocates for children, the child still lacks control and can only hope for a good placement.  One important theme of the book is "portaging," or what one carries from place to place when moving is necessary.

For this fine novel, Christina Baker Kline did extensive research on the orphan trains, foster/adoption protocols, and each of the locales (Ireland, Minnesota, and Maine) that play important roles in this book.  Her characters are convincing and memorable, the interplay of the two main characters' stories is well structured, and the book is highly involving--in fact, hard to put down.  I highly recommend it.

This book was originally published in 1928 by an author important in the Harlem Renaissance. Jessie Redmon Fauset explores the importance of race in peoples treatment and opportunities through the story of two sisters, Virginia who is obviously colored and Angela who appears white. The novel focusses on the latter who is conflicted between her desire to have the easier life of a white person and her need to stand up for her own people. Not to reveal too much of the plot, one of the many stages Angela goes through as a young woman is imagining that she could use a position as wife of a wealthy white man to help colored people. Not surprisingly, such a solution is not feasible given the racism of most of her white peers. Place is very important in this book, particularly neighborhoods in both Philadelphia and New York City and the opportunities represented by those neighborhoods. Angelas ability to enter at will into neighborhoods, restaurants, shops, jobs, and social situations only when she is thought to be white is the moral of this book subtitled A Novel Without A Moral.

The book has weaknesses in my opinion. To me, it moved slowly with too much description at places. The transitions in Angelas thinking about her choices sometimes seem to just happen rather than being understandable. The other characters are not developed well enough for their behavior to be predictable to the reader. The ending is unrealistic; it seemed to me to fit a romantic comedy film better than a novel of this weight. But, overall, this book is well worth reading for its sense of the time, revelations about white privilege, and insights provided by the contrasts between the lives of Virginia and Angela and Angela-when-thought-to-be-white and Angela-when-known-to-be-coloured.

This book is pleasant, easy reading even though there are very sad incidents.  The novel is told in the first person and begins with the protagonist struggling to find meaning in her work and life after her best friend dies.  She meets three other women, interesting characters who are making it on their own but with some gaps in their lives.  Unfortunately, Elizabeth Berg gives three of the four a solution that involves their being accepted by another person rather than developing their characters further as independent women.  I would have much preferred to see the women as their own salvation.  Their reliance on fortune telling in making their choices also got tiresome for me.  After each woman finds her solution, the rest of the book peters out and seems more like an epilogue.  I was ready to see how the characters took the steps they had initiated, but it seems like the author got tired and wrapped it up quickly.  The protagonist is a motivational speaker--what choices is the author trying to inspire in readers?

This book doesnt really need another review, but I want to add my vote for 5 stars.  This book deals with an important topic and allows the reader to empathize with the intertwined lives of two girls and then two women, a slave struggling to feel free (Handful) and a woman abolitionist (Sarah Grimk) rejecting the constraints placed on womens lives by her society.  Sarah Grimk and her younger sister Angelina are historical figures whose contributions to abolition and womens rights were huge but who are largely unknown; for me, that is one major contribution of the book.  The characters are beautifully drawn, and their struggles prompt the reader to consider her or his own issues of conscience versus safety.  There is ample suspense to keep the reader glued to the book, due to the dangers faced.  I found no flaw in the book.  Some reviewers have complained about Ophrahs notes; I inadvertently bought the Kindle version with the notes, but they were presented as footnotes, and I just didn't click on them.  I really appreciated the Authors Note in which Sue Monk Kidd clarifies where the book sticks closely to historical fact and where she deviated.  My version also had a discussion with the author, which I found valuable.  A wonderful book.

My version also had a discussion with the author, which I found valuable.  A wonderful book.

Evening Street shows a caring side of Bell Elkins rather than her investigative fierceness.  I thought the story was fine, although it couldn't really have the twists of a long piece of fiction; and I thought it ended kind of limply. It seemed too short because the Amazon site shows it as a novella that is 76 pages long; yet the last one-third of those pages are not Evening Street, but the start of a new novel, Sorrow Road. Ill buy Sorrow Road to read the whole things so I didn't intend to buy it now.

This is a well-crafted and thought-provoking book.  Readers might find it moves slowly if they focus on action in the plot--but it is not a simple book. I like it even better than I did originally after continuing to mull it over and discussing it with a book club. Each character's story is developed carefully; that choice on the author's part slows the "action," but the characters' stories gradually disclose Patchett's themes. This is a book about family: about the parent-child relationship, the sacrifices made by parents, the loyalty of their children, and the relationships of siblings. From the passing of a family heirloom to the adopted sons at the beginning of the book through the rest of the book to the very end, Patchett shows that family is not a matter of biological relationships.

There are many losses in this book, but it is moving rather than sad. The family becomes closer through the course of the book. Initially an outsider, Kenya becomes a redemptive figure pulling the family together. Another theme through the book is the invisibility of African-Americans, except Teddy and Tip, who are adopted by a prominent white family, and Kenya when she runs. Social inequality affects many characters' outcomes. Several characters have strong interests or obsessions. These obsessions, closely held secrets, and magical realism, through which some of the secrets are revealed to the reader, keep the book from being strictly realistic. But the lessons are real and beautifully told. Highly recommended.

This was a pretty good story, but it did not rival the classic 1981 Amanda Cross novel, Death in a Tenured Position. Kate Fansler is a more interesting and stronger character than Cynthia Kuhns protagonist Lila Maclean. The Amanda Cross novel (actually written by Carolyn Heilbrun, feminist professor at Columbia) was eye-opening in giving an insiders view of womens situation at an Ivy League institution in the late 1970s. Although Kuhn's novel describes problems that truly still exist for women in academe, they tend to exist now in subtler forms--Stonedale University seems behind the times in its open sexism and lack of official support for women. Some other aspects of the plot, such as a cousin, daughter, and brother of current or former Stonedale faculty members being hired and the chairs and chancellors open antagonism to the protagonist also seem improbable based on my experience in another exclusive school for those who didn't make it into the Ivy League but who were, according to their parents at least, exceptional nonetheless. However, intra-department hostility remaining after tenure and hiring decisions does seem realistic, and is essential to the plot of this book. Lilas daily work--teaching, grading, service, concerns about scholarship--played a natural part in the story and was described well. I had some trouble keeping track of all the English department members; Lila remembered their specialties and personalities more quickly than I could. I think fewer main characters could have been developed better, making the resolution of the mystery more convincing. Overall, the book did keep my interest, and I enjoyed reading it.

This is a beautiful book, with many memorable passages.  The unlikely friendship of Astrid and Veronika holds lessons for all who would be friends.  The reader is drawn into the gradually developing friendship and into the damaging past histories from which the two women need to be healed.

Linda Olssons prose has been described as luminous, and I found the presence and variations of light throughout the book to be magical.  I recommended this book to my feminist fiction reading group, and the members were very impressed with the writing and Astrid's and Veronikas friendship.  This is a favorite book that I keep returning to and giving to friends.

This lovely little book is about relationships among three people: the professor, his housekeeper, and her ten-year old son.  There are no other characters of significance except, somewhat mysteriously, the professor's sister-in-law.  The story is very focused--told from the perspective of just the housekeeper and dealing little with the characters' lives outside their relationships.  It could have been a bigger book if some side stories, such as the professor's relationship with his sister-in-law, had been developed; in fact, I found the inconsistencies in her behavior at the beginning and the end of the book disconcerting.  But the three main characters and their relationships are developed very well.  My initial reluctance to read a book in which mathematics and baseball play major roles was quickly forgotten as the story became real.  Readers who are into mathematics or baseball would really like this story, but I came to care about the topics like the housekeeper did; she came to appreciate these topics because they were passions of people she cared for and because they shared their passions so well.  All of the characters are good, kind people who are generally patient with each other.  The tension in the story is provided by the professor's lack of short-term memory, the housekeeper's need to make independent decisions about how best to deal with everyday emergencies and how to help him lead a "normal" life, and the unpredictability of a young boy.  Besides the professor's passion for and past knowledge of mathematics, his deep concern for children also provides continuities that bridge his memory gaps.  On one level, this book raises haunting questions about how each of us would deal with such a devastating disability or help a loved one do so.  On another level, it is a more universal story about how caring people brought together by circumstances can be a family.

This novel was chosen by my book club and, perhaps surprisingly, is my first Anne Tyler novel.  I note that some other reviewers found the characters, setting, or story too similar to some of Tyler's previous books to be engaging.  And, I don't imagine the book would appeal to a young person who has not developed an appreciation for the importance of memories or grappled with aging and dealing with in-laws and adult children, which are integral to this story. But I loved it! I am the age of the protagonists in the middle generation, Abby and Red, and found their story familiar and Tylers treatment of it comforting rather than depressing. The book begins and ends in the current time period but goes back to two earlier times.  Although people move from different locales and residences throughout the book in accord with their changing relationships and life situations, one special home is in the family for two generations and the book is practically organized around who lives in it. The story is told from the perspective of family members in three different generations. I think there is perspective in this book helpful for anyone who deals with a child or sibling who pulls at the family fabric, who struggles with what one gives up and gains with compromises to be a couple or part of a close family, who confronts their own or an aging parents restriction of options that come as health declines, or who comes from a background that doesnt quite fit with their current situation.

I bought this book because the price was reduced and it dealt with a mystery set in China. I also thought a Sisterhood" series would be interesting. However, I didn't finish it. I couldn't follow all the characters, male and female, and their roles in the group that apparently were based on past books in the series. There were several very violent encounters in the part I read, and the attitudes toward China and everything Chinese were very negative. Maybe it would have been more enjoyable if Id read previous books in the series, but I cant recommend it.

Another good story with further development of the main characters, archeologist Ruth Galloway and DCI Harry Nelson.  I really like Ruth, but she tends to fall into dangerous traps set by the perpetrators of crimes she is unraveling.  Although she was presented as a loner at the beginning of the first mystery (The Crossing Places) and still sees herself that way, Ruth tends to trust others until they display untrustworthiness, and her relationships with other continuing characters are a large part of the story.  In this novel, that includes her relationship with Nelson and their Druid friend Cathbad but also, importantly, her daughter Kate, as well as her best friend Shona, a visiting friend from Bosnia, the detective sergeants Clough and Johnson, and a number of archeologists.  Both she and Nelson struggle with their relationship with each other and their responsibilities to other characters; it seems impossible that they will find solutions in future installments that make them happy--but it seems likely they will continue to solve interesting crimes.

The Lowland has been described as a novel about two brothers, but it is also a novel about two marriages, and about the separate relationships of a daughter with her father and with her mother.  Different sections of the book are written from the perspectives of the four main characters.  The stories of the older brother/father Subhash and his daughter Bela are told chronologically for the most part; but the story of the wife/mother Gauri also flashes back to a critical incident in the Naxalite movement in Calcutta in the 1960s, where the story of the younger brother Udayan ended.  The novel is specifically linked to that historical movement and flows from that incident.

But the themes are not limited to that time or place or to Bengali immigrants to the United States.  Issues of the relationships between generations and the aging of parents and independence of children are universal.  One didn't have to grow up in Calcutta in the 1960s to struggle with how much to risk for social change or how to balance family against other desires and commitments.  The book also deals with constraints on women due to traditional expectations and with unconventional choices, still issues for many today.  These characters have major secrets; but we all worry about what to keep from our loved ones, to protect them or to protect ourselves.  In exploring the characters' relationships, Lahiri explores the definition of love and family.  Another universal is the natural environment, of which the reader is always aware.  As indicated by the book's title, the natural environment is crucial to the happenings in India, and the natural environment is more than background for the characters' lives in the United States as well.  To me, the book just feels real throughout.

This is mostly a sad novel and the reader might wish for more forgiveness from the characters.  But it didn't make me sad to read it--Lahiri makes these characters think continually about the right thing to do; and they try, even though they cannot always do it.  And it is a novel demonstrating resilience and healing.  Lahiri's prose is so beautiful and her insights so meaningful that it is worth it to walk along with these interesting characters for many years while they work their lives out.  Highly recommended.

You might think this topic would make for a depressing book, but it does not. The protagonist and several other characters are quite likable, and the protagonist's story and continued development throughout the novel are quite interesting. And there is an element of suspense. I read the book straight through. Readers will finish the book with a greater understanding of the dilemmas faced by abused women and why they often do not escape their situation. Excellent.

Rather than repeating information that is in other reviews, heres some encouragement to read this book.  It is a beautifully written and meaningful novel, but one might be reluctant to try it given the subject matter.  From the first paragraph, the reader knows this book will deal with one of lifes most tragic circumstances, the death of a child and its effect on her family.  I was reluctant to share the pain of that circumstance, but the book is somehow uplifting rather than depressing.  Ng provided relief from the painful current circumstance by flashbacks that included clues to the cause of Lydias death.  In her treatment of the past and present, Ng carefully unwrapped the personalities of each Lee family member including Lydia, the favorite child.  The reader can empathize with each of the major characters, and they exhibit growth in spite of, actually because of, the tragedy.  Having access to the thinking of each member of a particular interracial family in the late 1970s surprisingly gives the reader insight into much broader issues of parenting, marriage, gender, sexuality, being different, and prejudice.  As indicated by the title, lack of honest communication in relationships is central to the plot.  Ng leads the reader to consider both honesty and dependence-independence in relationships.  I found this book very valuable and highly recommend it.

I found the plot of this book so compelling that I had trouble putting it down.  The characters are well developed and move through interesting locales with potential disaster hanging over their heads.  As others have noted, the action is violent but not graphically so.  In fact, one objection to the book might be that it normalizes a violent lifestyle and makes a violent protagonist likable.  Personally, I found his likability and softening of perspective to be less than totally believable given where he started.  Without giving away the plot, I can say that some broad-brush aspects are predictable, but the specific investigation and threat to the protagonist have sufficient twists to keep the reader guessing and involved.  Overall, a good read.

Tenzing Norbu is a good guy with a complicated past.  He struggles to come to terms with the alternating and damaging parenting of his briefly married mother and father, an American hippie in Paris and a Tibetan Buddhist abbot in India.  It seems almost incredible that Ten ends up as a police detective and then private detective in Los Angeles.  Also, in spite of unhealthy parenting and rigid monastery training that encouraged lack of attachment, Ten is a good friend and forms new attachments to people almost too easily.  He also is un-monklike in being very attached to his car and his gun.  On the other hand, his Buddhist background centers him and is a theme throughout the book, including the running commentary of his assessment of his mental and physical state and need for moments of meditation.  It is a little hokey that some of his detective skills are supernatural, supposedly based on his training in the monastery.  Some reviewers have complained that the authors got some aspects of Tibetan life and Buddhist monasteries wrong; that is something they should correct in later installments of this series, which I hope they will continue for a long time.  I am interested in the exile of Tibetan Buddhists and in Los Angeles, so this was a happy juxtaposition for me as a reader.  I found the story involving and sufficiently complex to make a good mystery.  I look forward to reading more.

This story is set in Denmark and told in the voice of a precocious 14-year old boy, Peter, who often uses football (soccer) metaphors to make his points. The tale also involves his siblings, who have somewhat incredible talents, and a mystery about their parents disappearance. All three children believe their parents to be weird. In fact, the novel is populated with weird characters, but in a good way. It is a delightfully humorous read with underlying serious points about the universal truths of the worlds religions, about the effects of having a driving passion (an elephant for which one is the keeper), and about what it means to be truly free. If I had been holding a paper copy of the book, I would have underlined many of Peters insights. However, I was listening to an audio version while exercising or doing housework--so it just made me look forward to those activities. Complex plot, wonderful characters, funny, thought-provoking, suspenseful (but minimal violence)--I loved it!

Like all the Dr. Siri books, I found this installment, I Shot the Buddha, hard to put down from the moment I began reading until the surprising conclusion. I love spending time with Siri Paiboun and friends (and even his dog Ugly, who figures largely in this novel). And I admire Colin Cotterills imagination and ability to combine humor with a serious look at the shortcomings of Lao and Thai cultures in the 1970s. Cotterill also has an amazing ability to send Siri, Comrade Civilai, and Inspector Phosi and his wife Nurse Dtui off on different investigations that end up being connected in unexpected ways. However, I believe that complexity does not work as well in this book as in previous Dr. Siri books. There are more murders than the three mentioned in the blurb for this book and introduced in its first chapter. The three murders in the first chapter don't come back into the story for a while, so I had to keep looking back at the first chapter and using the Kindle search function to keep track of the murders. The second chapter begins two weeks earlier than the first, which is a tipoff that Cotterill will be playing with time in this novel, but that innovative attempt also makes the plot(s) harder to follow. Also unusual for mystery novels, Cotterill includes a mental health warning forewarning readers of his heavy use of supernatural elements. On the other hand, the last pages of the previous novel, Six and a Half Deadly Sins, are clarified by explanations in this novel. I encourage faithful readers of the Dr. Siri series to read this one as well, but I Shot the Buddha would not be a good place to begin an acquaintance with Siri Paiboun and friends. Three and a half stars.

This memoir describes American Linda Leaming's adjustment to a very different culture and a much simpler life.  How she came to love Bhutan would be an interesting story in itself.  But this book goes beyond explaining Leaming's adjustment.  It also describes the beautiful and severe natural environment and the beauty of the people and customs of this agrarian Buddhist society.  The contrast with American materialism is striking, both in terms of the day-to-day hardships of life in Bhutan and the shallowness of American priorities in the grand scheme of things.  The author describes her learning process and mistakes with humor, making the book very pleasant reading.  Rather than trying to be exhaustive, she details particular experiences; some readers might disagree with her choice of what it is important to describe.  And perhaps learning about Bhutan is less interesting to readers who never expect to be there.  I'll be visiting Bhutan in the near future, and i found her perspective and information very valuable.

The author of this memoir and her husband Tod (the guy with the beard) volunteered to teach in the mountains of Nepal, not far from the Everest Base Camp.  Their adventures with children, dogs, villagers, mountains, buses, and bureaucracy are told with humor and with affection for Nepal.  I read this memoir just after returning from Nepal and found it rang true, although Fiona's and Tod's living conditions were far more primitive and their experiences in Kathmandu more frustrating and chaotic than my own experiences protected by a tour guide.  I admired their determination.  Their learning experiences and adventures were interesting, and the book was easy reading.

I am typing a review that I am anxious to submit as this has to be one of my favorite purchases in a long time.  I had my daughters come out this past weekend to see if they wanted any of my old knives.  I no longer need any of them as these 4 will fill any need I could possibly have.

The first thing I sliced was tomatoes, green onions, and celery as I was making Taco Soup and this would be a good test of my new knives.
Well, let me tell you that this preparation was the easiest I've ever had and my only regret was that nobody was here to see the results of my efforts.  Well, efforts is not the right word because it didn't take any effort.  It was like I had an electric knife in my hand.  The green-handled one went through those tomatoes like cutting warm butter.  It was so easy!  Celery and onions were the same success.

Yesterday morning, though, I thought of a harder test.  I had a roll of sausage that had not been frozen and was in that pesky plastic wrapper.  I usually use my serrated knife cause it takes that to cut through the plastic.  Not this time...it cut through quickly with no effort of sawing back and forth as per usual.  I tried them also on fresh rolls that usually fold up when you try to cut them in half but didn't this time.

Do I sound pleased with these knives?  I am.  Best buy I've had in a long time.  I love them and I have them on my list of gifts to buy for loved ones.

I thought this was a perfect tool for my ice bucket.  I evidently lost my old one when I took ice to a pot luck dinner.  This is pretty to look at and has a firm grip on an ice cube.  I think the sharp knives I have are also made by this company and I love those also.

I doubt I would use  these tongs for serving food as they are hard to make both sides touch.  I could use them to pick a piece of meat out of soup to see if it was done or not but I think I'll stick to ice.

I thought the price was right and so is the appearance.  I might get another one to leave in the ice cube container in the freezer.  I certainly don't want strangers/friends using their hands there.  All in all, I am pleased.

I was pleased to get this knife this week and here is an honest opinion of same.  It is fairly heavy for a knife but it would make a great knife for scaling a fish or skinning an animal at night-hunting time.  The reason I say 'night' is that the flashlight (built in using  Triple AAA batteries) is extremely bright and if you shot a rabbit and wanted to clean it before packing in ice, this knife would be perfect.  I had a friend of mine test it who does fish and hunt a lot.  He loved the fact it had a light but thought the handle was rather large for his liking but he still thought it would be ideal for
sporting men.

I used it in the kitchen and thought it was quite sharp (I de-boned a chuck roast and then cut up the meat for stew)  but I still loved the whole
thing because of the flashlight part.  All in all, I would buy it for my Dad if he were still alive for as a child/young teen I went hunting with him a lot for squirrels and rabbits and he would have loved it.  That's as honest a review I can give as I'm female and this is a manly item, not a girly one.

I am an avid believer in soup and this cookbook is really a perfect addition to my bookcase of cookbooks.  I enjoy this type of cooking cause I can start it going long before I need it.  This makes my life much easier as I am a little old
senior citizen who believes in using leftover scraps to make soup and I don't mean scraps picked up from the floor.  I mean that leftover roast; the leftover peas and corn, etc.  There were some recipes in this book that I thought were great and many I had never tried before.  But those I tried made the book a great addition.  Try some soup for the July 4th cookout  or make pulled pork with a can of Dr. Pepper or my tonight''s dinner was Sauerkraut with pork ribs and new potatoes.  Slow cookers are what our parents needed and no one had invented them yet.  Hope you agree and say you do cause I love being right.

I am a rank beginner and I thought this book was good.  This is a great new hobby but not the cheapest one I ever saw.  However, with the help of the experts in these books, I have made some really pretty pieces.

Oh, my goodness..... what a pretty set of silverware.  I have a complete set of sterling silver and I'm telling you, these outshone those pieces.  The soup spoon is absolutely beautiful...so shiny, and just the right weight.  I can hardly wait to show my daughter who is looking for cutlery to get her daughter for Christmas.  These are pricey so maybe you might want to start with just two settings.  But what a great gift for someone just starting housekeeping.

The coffee spoon or it could be called a sugar spoon, is smaller than a regular teaspoon and I don't know how much.  It's also a little
shorter than my regular soup spoons.  But that's ok as the soup can double as a teaspoon cause I don't think it's as deep as my regular soup spoon.  And, as I stated above, you'll want to enjoy it yourself or show it off to company.

 I had not heard of Mepra company before I ordered these but I shall certainly shout their praises from now on if this is an example of their products.  I did a little research on them, though, and found out they have been around since 1947 bringing us three generations of Italian
tradition, design and lifestyle.  That's a long time and this set is not pricey compared to some sold in Italy.

THIS MEXICAN KITCHEN  DISH  is really pretty, with a cream/ivory inside and a colored (burgandy) top and bottom.  This IS NOT the least expensive piece of cookware I ever received but it has some very good points in its favor.  It is made of stoneware, microwave and dishwasher safe,
you can take right out of the oven to the table, and GORHAM (who made my silverware) is involved in this production,  and it's a 10" oval, pretty dish.  However, you could probably say the same thing about a casserole dish from the big box stores with the exception of Gorham.  From the picture, I thought it would be round and I could also use it for tortillos BUT it's oval and if I had looked closer, I would have known that from the title.

Now, if I were having company for a big Mexican fiesta, and I had other matching pieces, that would be very colorful and pretty.  If I ever get married again, I'd buy a lot of their product and use it often.  It is fairly heavy but not unmanageable.

I gave this 3 stars ONLY because of the cost.  It is a NICE AND PRETTY dish - just expensive.

This arrived today and it is so pretty.  I'm not even going to wait for Christmas to use it as I loved its shape and design.  All of my dishes (regular ones) and my special dishes are made by LENOX.  I love their beauty and durability.  Around $18 seems a little pricey for one glass so that might be a turn-off.  But, it is pretty and has a nice feel to it.  Would have been 5 star except for the price.

Well, I just got a surprise.  I received this order last week and immediately used it.  Then I sat down and wrote a great review because I loved the color and  weight of this really big salad bowl and the 4 smaller ones.  I was so happy with myself because I took the time to really give these some thought.  Well, a few minutes ago I was reviewing what I had bought and what I had been sent just for giving an honest review and the one for these bowls didn't appear anywhere.  But, it won't take but a minute to remember what I thought....maybe not in the same glowing words but certainly an honest opinion.  These bowls will be great to take on a July 4th picnic or
use for a bridge luncheon.  The latter is what I did first and the other 3 ladies thought the same as I did.  They were bright, shiny looked like fun (if you can call dishes fun).  But, we talked about them all through lunch and they wondered if they came in other colors.  Since I didn't 'choose' these, I didn't know, but had I chosen I would have picked this red.  The 'confetti' look fits the name of the dishes cause you see multi colors in the plastic (or it might be acrylic, I'm not sure) and it's festive, to say the least.  So, I'll say the last.  If you have a need for a set like this, you won't be wasting time nor money as they washed easily and looked like a party.  Try them!

This came this week and it is so cute.  I think my great grandson will like playing with it when he comes to see me.  I remember my own children playing with a MR. POTATO HEAD but not one as interesting as this one.  He will be three next month but naturally I think he is quite advanced for 3.  Of course, he could be just average but not to me.

This will keep him entertained when he's here and he is quite used to PLAYSKOOL as that is the brand I usually look for when buying toys for my three G-G kids.  You might be interested in knowing that PLAYSKOOL is part of the HASBRO Global company and they have been around since 1923.  Their mission is to make age appropriate toys for children.  Good Mission.

This came this week and it is so cute.  I think my great grandson will like playing with it when he comes to see me.  I remember my own children playing with a MR. POTATO HEAD but not one as interesting as this one.  He will be three next month but naturally I think he is quite advanced for 3.  Of course, he could be just average but not to me.

This will keep him entertained when he's here and he is quite used to PLAYSKOOL as that is the brand I usually look for when buying toys for my three G-G kids.  You might be interested in knowing that PLAYSKOOL is part of the HASBRO Global company and they have been around since 1923.  Their mission is to make age appropriate toys for children.  Good Mission.

This came at such a good time.  I was going to eat in our main dining room with some of the other residents (we live in a retirement community) as tonight was our POTLUCK dinner.  I sliced this thin and added crackers to the serving dish.  Everyone loved them!
I had sense enough to save some for me to eat tonight while I watched the programs taped earlier.

I tried them with Honey Mustard, regular mustard, dijon and horseradish mustard.  It was great with all.  I am going to try to order some more to put on my pizza I'll make for next week's potluck dinner.  This Vermont Smoke & Cure Smoked Pepperoni tasted so fresh and also just like it should taste....much softer than the kind you get in small packages at the grocery store.  This is a very small role of meat and I wished it had been bigger.  The slices were small....about the size of a sliced banana.

This item was much smaller than I thought it would be.  However, small or not, I think it would be an easy task for a young girl to have fun with this locket-making craft.  It's not expensive and easy to teach a little girl to do.  You never know, she might grow up to be a jewelry designer and she can look back and say this was her first toy that led to her success.

I gave this 3 stars because I didn't like the key chain.....no way to close it, in my mind.  Secondly, other than glue or tape there is no way to keep the 'little' things inside the locket.  If those negatives can be changed, I think it would be a 5-star purchase.  It was fun to do with my granddaughter (who is going on 4) and she actually did a lot of the 'making' of the locket.

This is an excellent table runner for Valentine's Day or simply because you love someone.  I have bought so many items for decorating my home for holidays from DII.  I live alone and it makes the condo feel lived in.

I put this over a white ruffled tablecloth just to see what it would look like and I was very pleased.  Time passes so fast when you become a Senior
Citizen so I have six months to wait to use it.  But I'm happy with it and have no negatives and don't think I will, as I have used DII holiday runners for other holidays.

I love this!  I used the divided space for napkins and silverware.  But the undivided space was what put my opinion over the top.  I live in a beautiful retirement village with a huge dining room downstairs.  However, there are times I just want to watch TV or fix my own dinner (it's not hard to get tired of mass-cooked food).  And, I eat in my den with my recliner and a tv tray.  I saw that I was making way too many trips back and forth and that was a downside of my alone time.

Now, I can carry everything but the food in an attractive carry-all caddy and it makes my mealtime happier.

This is a sturdy container, I like having just one handle instead of one on each end.  So, InterDesign gets my vote cause their product makes life easier for this old senior citizen.  Thank you, InterDesign, and thank you Amazon for choosing them as a vendor.

I live in a retirement village and I took this downstairs tonight to let everyone try it at dinner.  That way I get 23 opinions instead of just mine.  Fifteen thought it was great, 5 thought it was a little too spicy but still put it on their Philly Steak Hoagie and liked it and three thought it was too sweet but was good.

I thought it was tremendous.  I have never tasted Gochujang Sauce before but I use Tabasco a lot and sometimes the Sirachi Sauce (probably misspelled cause I don't want to go get the bottle to check it).  I also had the Philly Steak and french fries.  I dipped the FF in ranch and this and I loved it.  Then I poured it all over the Hoagie, added fresh onions and pickles and loved every bite of it.  It was neither too spicy or too sweet as I love all kinds of Asian sauces.  However, if it had soy sauce in it I didn't taste it but would have loved that added taste.  Of course, I now want to know what the original Gochujang sauce would taste like and I would also like to hear it pronounced....right now is call it Go chew jang.  And no matter how it's pronounced I shall add it to a lot of the things I eat regularly and will quickly need another bottle.  If this helped you at all, please check that it did.  If not, I hope you enjoy whatever you put it on.

WHAT A GREAT FIND!.  I had never heard of MINOR'S BEEF BASE until this past week.  I thought it might taste like bouillon cubes but I didn't find it that salty at all.  I make a great Taco Soup (that everyone loves) and I got out all the canned ingredients I use, opened them all up and put in my huge pot and THEN realized I didn't have any ground beef in the freezer.  What is a poor, old lady to do?  Then I remembered this beef base was delivered from dear old AMAZON and my soup was saved.  I didn't use much (I was expecting a powder) so I went easy on the amount at first.

Let me tell you, my taco soup has always been good but this batch was delightfully so.  I had made a lot so I could share with my friends here in the retirement village.  They, too, loved it.  My next step is to get the Chicken Base for my Tortilla soup--it's gotta be as good as the beef !

So impressed was I that off I went to Google to read more about this product and the company.  I was even more impressed when I say that the Nestle (and everything they make is good) bought out Mike Minor ten years after he started.  I don't know for how much.  I also saw that they make a base for Turkey Gravy, which I shall also get closer to Thanksgiving.  I am so glad that I had the opportunity to review this and hope you find this helpful before you purchase this product.

I got this Nutro 3 count Rotations Adult Dog Food earlier this week.  I haven't changed dog food in ages but it didn't seem my  Westie was eating as much as he usually does.  So when I saw this new (well, new to me) product, I thought I would give it a try.  My daughter lives one street from me and she has two weiner dogs (wasn't sure I could spell dachshund) that she often brings over and we take them to the dog park together.  When we got back, we decided to feed and water them and at the same time try the new dog food.  We had 3 different kinds to try.  It was so funny to watch because as if on cue, they each changed dishes.
Even my Maine Coon cat wanted to get into the act.  That wasn't figured into their thinking, so after a few growls, the cat walked away.  When the dogs finished, though, the cat licked each dish.  I doubted it would hurt him.

So, I gave this  4 stars as I seldom give 5.  I was happy to think my sweet Westie was getting a variety.  I had even considered buying more than one kind but didn't follow; through.  My dog isn't particularly a picky eater  but it wasn't just competition that
was on his mind with the other two cause since then he has relished each variety.  I shall continue to have this delivered by my Prime Account in a timely manner...with only a small dog, it should be quite a while.  This is 4 stars because I think it's more than his other food costs.  I'm going to check that out.  But this comes out to about  $4.17 a pound.  But, it's cheaper than still having my kids at home.

When I first saw this I thought it would be white - didn't think it would be clear acrylic.  I then sat down and thought of all the things I could do with....and there were a great many ideas floating in my head.  I wrote a really thorough review.  Somewhere near the end I must have left the computer or Heaven only knows what I did.  I actually thought I had sent it.  Today when I opened up my account I saw that no review had been submitted.

So, I'll put down in shorter order the uses, which first was cosmetics.  Then I thought of all my little jewelry findings that are so easy to lose; next came the very small tools used in jewelry making.  In the chance that I would bore you with ideas, I am going to suggest you think outside the box.....this box.  It is sturdy, pretty acrylic (heavy plastic, I can't tell which) and a mirror in the back of the lid.  Unfortunately, there is no clasp to make the lid stay down but that's OK unless you're thinking of traveling with it....then that might be a problem with no clamped lid.

I gave it 5 stars but some of you might think that's a little pricey for such a small box.  I plan on buying others for the ideas I came up with.  In my elder years I like things to be organized and within reach.....was not that way so much when my children were growing up.  Now I don't want to have to search for something or get down on my knees to find a box of something.  Just me, of course, but you'll also find other uses, I bet

I have to write this review right this minute.  I LOVED, LOVED, LOVED IT.  Such a good mystery - no,  make that a great adventure.  I haven't been this excited over an author since I read John Grisham's  first published book (The Firm) and David Balducci's first, Absolute Power.  I really seem to be able to predict future stars in the publishing world and when I find one, I want the whole world to enjoy what I enjoyed when I read those books.  This author ranks up there with the best of them in this genre of "mystery thriller psychological" books.

As far as I know, this is Mr. Palmer's first novel of this type.  I tried to look him up but only found other books with the same name that has written many books with locations  in the music world.  I don't know if they are the same writers or not as it is hard to get around one who writes about rock and roll and then writes this kind of book.  I'm still looking for the answer to that one.

The characters in this book are not one-dimensional....you can immediately relate to them.  The mystery synopsis you can read on the cover and I would hesitate to tell you any more because I would never want to spoil it for a reader.  Take my word for it...start it when you know you have free time ahead of you.  I could not put it down.....I even cancelled my bridge game to finish it.  This is going to be an excellent author to watch for in the coming years.  I received this book in return for an honest review and you can look at the reviews I have written and see that I don't rave, rave, rave over each and every one.  Actually, I've not too  often given 5 stars.  The book can be pre-ordered but doesn't come out until October.  If you only see the cover, read the hype on it and are now reading this, please take my word for it .... it is well-worth your time and money.  I LOVED IT.  Please write your review when you finish as I want to know how many of you felt as I did.  If you like books about our nation's capitol and how things are worked out behind closed doors and if you are even familiar with the political side of DC, Maryland and Virginia area, you will feel right at home.  No, I am not related to Mr. Palmer nor have I ever heard of him before.  I'm just telling ya........

Another great item from the AMAZON COLLECTION ..... this time it is Rose Gold Plated Sterling Silver Oval drop (or pendant).
This necklace would make a great graduation gift or a beautiful Mother's Day present.  It is as dainty as can be.  It's certainly not the biggest stone in the world but the color is beautiful.  It is a beautiful, sparkling red....not pink but actually red.  You could wear it constantly and just add your other necklace to it.  I have another one like this somewhat but blue and I loaned it to my darling little great granddaughter when she was going to have her picture taken.  She wanted to wear some of my jewwwee.  She has blue eyes that match that stone.

The price was great on this piece and I really think you will appreciate its beauty and daintiness.

I bought my husband a TUMI laptop piece a few years back and that was the first time I had seen a TUMI product, but certainly not the last time.
My better half carried that product wherever we went and he loved it.  He passed away in 2012 and now I carry it.  It continues to look like new and I ended up buying a larger, non-carry on suitcase and one in a Peony print in this VOYAGEUR SUPER LEGER  for my granddaughter when she
graduated from OSU.  You just cannot wear these products out..... and they stay so clean looking.

I gave this review item just 4 stars because of the price.  These are PREMIUM travel bags but they are pricey.  Of course, you'll never have to replace them (unless someone steals yours) and they live out their lives in great condition.  I made matching quilted covers for mine that are washable and protects from airport attendants who 'pitch' them around.  The 4 wheels make it easier to turn around and the weight is good for
lifting it up to overhead compartments.  I know TUMI will keep up the good work.

These bras fit just like I thought they would but I was prepared with extenders.  That made them fit like they are supposed to but I had a couple of negatives.  The strap adjuster is in the back so you have to guess as to whether you are getting it right.  The band wasn't as wide as I'd hoped for a larger sized body.  I took the wires out of one and it felt better.

The positives are the price for two and the two different colors.  I went to my lingerie drawer and saw that I have some other bras by CURVATION and they look like I've given them plenty of use.  The material did not seem the same caliber as the old ones; these do seem somewhat flimsier.

My 3-star review is not as good as I hoped it would be but I won't give up on the company as those in the drawer are O L D.

OFF-SEASON IS SMOKIN'!!!
Edit

Holy guacamole!  I'm a sucker for sports related romances, so I had gotten hooked on Roz Lee's baseball series.  (Check her out here: [...] ) Her fourth in the series just came out a few days ago & I picked it up last night.  H.O.T. !!!  OMG!  So the title is "Bases Loaded (Mustangs Baseball)", and apparently it refers to a "secret club" that these FICTIONAL major league ballplayers have created, where there is a sexual challenge put forth to women who are invited to participate -- and the result for those who make it through all (4) bases is some jewelry pierced into some... um... personal spots.

Anyway - this is the story of Antonio & Clare - Antonio is new to the Dallas Mustangs baseball club and Clare is a college music professor who moonlights as the baseball team's organist.  He catches sight of her at a fundraiser and realizes then & there that she is his soul-mate.  However, she is "curvy" and has massive self-esteem issues, so when he hits on her, she thinks he's being a bully & trying to humiliate her.  The resulting story is how he works through what he thinks are perverted needs for the woman who will bear his children, and she works through her body issues, as they fall in love.  Since it is the off-season, he has lots of free time in which to "woo" Clare.  The ultimate problem?  She wants to "run the bases" for his "Bases Loaded" sex club; he feels too possessive and they have constant clashes over this.  If you want to find out how it all shakes out... READ THE STORY!!!  (Disclaimer:  toy play, anal, m/m/m/f, light bondage.)

Okay, so I'm always a vocalist about digital book pricing, so I will say that this is very well priced for the amount of pages it has - WELL worth the money!!!  This isn't SOLELY sexually based; beyond the character growth of Clare learning to like herself as she is and to realize her inner AND outer beauty, there is a female bully (& don't we ALL know some absolute BITCH who just LIVES to make others feel like crap??!!!??) who threatens public humiliation of Clare and Antonio, which would result in the loss of his contract.  Lots of angst... lots of sex... lots of self-realization that beauty isn't all about Barbie dimensions!

Go read it.  It's awesome.  Just make sure the Partner or BOB is nearby - you may need their "assistance".  [wink]

PS:  Other great reads from this series -- please note that the first one is currently (6/30/13) FREE on Amazon!

cands.text:
I know Ive mentioned it before, but I have a thing for sports romances.  I don't know why.  It just is & I don't question it.  As such, this is the third Julie Brannagh football romance Ive read  coincidentally enough, it is the third one in her Love and Football series.  You might remember the info I posted on the first two books in the series  BLITZING EMILY and RUSHING AMY .  I simply adored them and must say that Julie Brannagh has done it again!  She has brought to the pages realistic characters  characters that youd really like to meet & strike up a friendship with  who don't claim perfection as they fumble their way to their HEA.  Cameron and Zach had a three day Vegas marriage and then found themselves separated for ten years due to family interference and lots of (wrong) assumptions.  Yes, the basic gist of this plotline has been done before  but Julie Brannagh finds a way to make it fresh and engaging, throwing in the realities of  the struggles women face in sports broadcasting, the unglamorous state of football training camp, and making a public relationship not be IN the public eye.

 Originally posted on Snarky Mom Reads and references a gifted book.

What better thing to do on Opening Day than to open up a baseball mystery book? Well, other than watching the game, of course!

This is a "cozy" sports mystery with a plucky heroine, hints of family trauma/drama, a cute neighbor/boyfriend, and sleazy "big business" practices that can't be ignored! Best of all - it gives you a perspective into some of the things that have tainted professional baseball - steroids, owner greed, etc... and makes you wish there were more folks like Cat out there to help keep it clean & get the focus off of baseball as merely a means to a profitable end, instead of the golden days of baseball.

This is a great start to what is explained as a trilogy of books revolving around Cat and her quest to pair reporting with her love of baseball. I look forward to starting on Curveball!

I received a copy of "Diamonds and Spurs" in exchange for an HONEST review.  I'm not familiar with the author, Melody Snow Malone.  I was also not aware at the time that this was the 9th in the "Callens Series" of books featuring menage relationships.  However, not knowing either of those things didn't affect my reading of this hot novella!  It reads well as a standalone book and I'm sure would also be a great addition to those who are invested in the series, because I'm sure that many of the folks mentioned are well-loved characters that everyone would be happy to get an update on!

The premise of "Diamonds and Spurs" is that the female lead, Mandy, has become aware her husband is engaged in illegal activities and she manages to get a divorce from him to escape.  She had prepared her plan and had a position waiting for her on a ranch to take women-only expeditions into the mountains.  While there, she meets Cameron & Vince, who just ended an engagement a month ago.  Accidents start to happen to Mandy, and the question becomes if it is her ex-husband trying to scare her so she doesn't testify against him... or if it's Cameron & Vince's ex-fiancee who is trying to eliminate Mandy as competition to get the men, and their money, back in her clutches.

Remember - this is a menage relationship, so you do get scenes of m/f/m -- but no m/m.  There's some spanking, toys, etc... and the sex scenes are really hot & inventive!  It's also nice to see Mandy shed her high society ways she had to adopt to fit in with her husband and return to her roots - which are country.  (This is where the concept of diamonds to spurs comes from -- one of her friends says at the end that she's gone from diamonds to spurs.)

While I've never read anything from this author or this series before (as I've mentioned) I really did enjoy it.  The character development was great; the sex scenes were hot; the descriptiveness of the dialogue was great... and quite frankly, the "mystery" of it all was very good & wasn't predictable!  Overall, I'd say this is a great buy for the price.  Great for the Kindle so you can "hide" it from the kids... and great to share with your favorite partner!

Krista and Ryan often see each other eating their lunches at the park; he thinks shes out of his league because shes dressed so classy, and she thinks hes out of her league because hes so hot & alpha.  He stops by her office to try to drum up business & she sees him coming out of her boss office  just hours before she finds her boss in the middle of a child pornography video ring and takes off running.  Only problem is that when her boss hires Ryan to find her, shes not sure whose side hes on  so shes afraid to lose her heart right along with her life.

The biggest surprise to me was that Id not heard of Anne Conley before, but Im glad I ran across this series (Id actually run across the 3rd book which is a recent release & figured Id start at the beginning.)  Ill be reading more, because this was a super read & the Pierce Securities guys are an interesting crew!

Originally posted on SnarkyMomReads
Snarky Scale: Yay, author!
Hit or Miss? Close to a bulls-eye!
Battery Powered? Hand fanning will do!
Re-read urge? I think Ill just pick up the next book in the series  there are two more after this one!

Its baseball season.  How is your favorite team doing?  Mine?  Not so great  which is why its so nice to read a great baseball-themed romance!  Chase is rehabbing at a minor league team (again, this was fun to read since weve had similar things happen here LOL!) and has a run-in with a die-hard fan well, a fan who is die-hard to hook up with him!  Her sister?  Just wants to get away with her dignity intact from the ballpark.  Instead, she gets away with the ball player!  The vast differences between Chase and Grey seem insurmountable, especially when he heads back to New York City to rejoin his major league team.  If you are a fan of spots (baseball) romances, this is a great choice for your TBR pile!

Originally posted on Snarky Mom Reads and may reference a gifted book.

Take me out to the ball park. Take me out to the game.

LINE DRIVE is the first hit of this baseball sports romance series and Mattie and Ashlynn end up with a home run of a love story!  Granted, there were some close calls in the 7th inning, but these batters end up finding the sweet spot on the bat and hitting it out of the park.  And Im done trying to be cutesie with baseball comments.  Okay, so this is a sweet sports romance between a do-gooder chef and a come back kid ball player who also bakes.  Erin Lindsey does a great job creating great environments in the ballpark and the kitchen  but most importantly, builds characters that are witty and you find yourself wishing you knew in real life.  This will be one baseball romance series youll want to keep your eye on for the next game from the Philadelphia Liberties!

For a novella, Cynthia Sax packs a LOT of character growth, extremely sexy scenes and emotional flashes into her story.  After reading this (copy provided for review purposes) I have to admit  I am OFF & RUNNING to find other Cynthia Sax works!  This loosely correlated story to Beauty and the Beast also offers many spots of humor

Employees raise their heads, spot Henley, and duck back down.

This happens again and again, the sigh hilariously funny.  Have you ever played that amusement-park game where the rodents pop out of holes and you have to whack them with a mallet? I ask.  Henley doesnt answer, his broad shoulders shaking.  Youre strong and fast.  I think youd be great at that game.  You could win me a stuffed bear or a giant plush unicorn.

A bark of laughter bursts from his lips.  Heads pop up.  Henley laughs even harder and I join in, his joy feeding mine.

Their unlikely romance while letting their love heal each others pain made this such an intriguing and gutsy read.  Itll also cause you to check the levels of your battery stash.  (Just sayin.)  Dont miss out on this one!

This was such a sweet romance featuring a small town, family-centric romance.  Liz is the overweight, ugly duckling that had a teenage crush on the older Ryan  and her life is defined by a moment titled The Humiliation.  It has caused her to be controlling about everything within her life.  On the flip side, Ryans Gran has survived a car accident and has realized that after playing it safe for 72 years, she needs to LIVE her life.  Ryan thinks that rigid Liz will be able to put a lid on Gran, so hires her to do some elder care over her summer teaching break.

If you enjoy stories based in small towns, with a sweet HEA based on childhood crushes coming true in adulthood  than this should be right up your alley!

Ive never made it a secret.  I freakn LOVE Eve Langlais!  Her heroines are sassy, the men stupidly sexy, and the shifter romances are always hot hot HOT!  This is the sixth book in the Freakin series but can easily be read as a standalone.  The sixth of the seven Grayson children finds his mate  but shes not buying what hes selling.  Patricia has already been mated and her mate died five years ago.  She cant imagine that shed have another mate  and not just one mate, but TWO more mates!

Patricia is trying to find a person who is killing shifters in prison.  She is assigned to a prison where Ricky has been installed undercover and she arrests Stu in order to have his hacking skills for the prison database.  Upon meeting both of them she realizes they are her mates.  Ricky intends to do the mating bite but Stu is willing to wait for Patricia to accept it.  In between this claiming struggle, there is the mystery of who is killing shifters  and trying to keep Stu & Ricky from becoming the next victims.

As usual when reading one of these Freakn Series books, I found myself gasping for air in between all the laughter inducing word play between characters.  If you're looking for a shifter romance that is fun, a bit suspenseful and incredibly smexyyou just cant go wrong with FREAKN COUGAR!

>Take home lesson for all the baddies?  Dont push a woman past her breaking point, because when she finds her escape, shell light your ass up.  Rayna has been kidnapped, watched her father killed, and has been mentally, physically and sexually abused for over three months.  When she finds an opportunity to escape, she kills her captor(s) and calls a friend of her fathers, Ox  who is the President of the Seven Deadlies MC.  He sends Fury to pick her up, and he arrives right after Rayna has blown up the MC Clubhouse with the dead / dying members inside.  Cause yanno, hell hath no FURY like WRATH.  Take one grieving MC member and one woman trying to find the new her, throw in a lot of bullets, hotter than hell insta-alpha-love, and youve got your first sin. WRATH.

Rebecca Zanetti is seriously just going onto my "auto buy" list.  She's been putting out some awesome stuff lately & I.  AM.  HOOKED!!!

Okay, if you want to read "Forgotten Sins", you'll have to do it via Kindle, because the paperback won't be out until January 2014.  (Hint:  Don't wait.)  Josie & Shane meet, have an explosive courtship, marry... and one day he simply disappears.  Years later, Josie gets a phone call to come pick up her husband from the hospital where he is after being found injured & suffering from amnesia.  Is he faking?  Why is he back in her life?  Who are all the dead men that keep showing up?  Well, read it & find out LOL!

This is the first of a series which I'm assuming will follow each of these "Sin Brothers" - all three (or is it four?!!!!??? hmmmmm.......) as they reclaim their lives and expose the bad guys... and find out what really happened to their dead (?) brother.  The suspense & intrigue is truly a blood pressure raiser... as are the (sex) scenes between husband & wife.  You'll find yourself needing a Kleenix as Shane & Josie try to figure out if their marriage is worth the effort based on the risk to her life.  Will they have a "happily ever after"?  Rebecca Zanetti has an incredible way of grabbing the reader and pulling them along for the ride with her characters, while simultaneously creating story arcs that come to a conclusion while still moving into the next story.  Speaking of the next story... here's hoping it is released... and SOON!!  (Her website implies it will be December.)

Check her out ( [...] ) - she has a bit of everything...  Romantic Suspense... Paranormal... and last but not least - COWBOYS.

"Making It Last" by Ruthie Knox is the latest installment in the Camelot, Ohio series.  This novella focuses once more on Tony & Amber, and the state of their marriage, ten years & three sons after the events in "How to Misbehave - A Novella (Camelot Series): A Loveswept Contemporary Romance".  I love this Camelot series, but I had a REALLY HARD TIME getting through this novella.  If it were any longer than its 151 pages I don't know what I would have done.  I actually had to stop several times & read some other things, then go back to it.  Did I do this because of the writing?  N.O.  I did it because of the STORY.  It was PAINFUL.  P.A.I.N.F.U.L.  Ruthie Knox just got right into this story, and into my heart as a reader, and TWISTED.  (I have to admit that I'm writing this first part before I have even finished the book, because, like I said - PAINFUL.  I needed a bit of a break.)  Anyone who has been in any sort of long term relationship can relate to this story... and as a Mom, I can REALLY relate.

Amber finds herself getting "lost" -- Tony is working long, hard hours and she is the consummate Mom (in the prior books she's mentioned driving kids to soccer practices, etc...) and spends all her energies on her husband and her kids.  Now that the youngest son is in school all day, she's starting to wonder - WHO AM I?!!!???  What happened to me?  Conversely, Tony is overwhelmed with fears about the home construction business in this economic downturn; not being able to cover payroll or his own mortgage payment; and concerns for his marriage, wife & children.  THIS IS REAL LIFE.  THIS is what Ruthie Knox does right.  While reading is escapism, and we all want the happy ending with the bluebirds singing at the end, some times it is just plain REFRESHING to know that other folks face the same fears; the same challenges; and that there can be a good resolution to it all.  If you're not in the mood for some reality with your romance, you might want to skip this one.  It can easily be read as a standalone - you don't need to have read the prior books, and it really does not have any "tie up loose ends" impact to it.  But man oh man - it is a STRONG read.  (Yes, I cried.  And I cried while I explained to The Man while I was crying.)

Well worth the price of admission.  Go check it out.

"Summer's Desire", by Kathleen Ball, is a 150+ page read for $4.99.  It's a "Cowboy Romance" - and a really fun one!  Summer is trying to leave her small town so she answers an ad to watch four boys for the new vet in town - not realizing that the four boys are actually bigger than her and aged 12-19!  So obviously, we all know that she & Holden, the vet (& oldest brother - not father) are going to fall in love. And should I mention that the cowboys are shirtless when she meets them?  'Nuff said.

Zach and Theresa have been best friends for 3 years and both have wanted more from the other but have been afraid  so yes, this is one of those lack of communication style love stories  but to cause further wrinkles, Zach is 3rd in the pack whereas Isabel is much more lower ranked.  The mating game comes about when the current alpha declares his intention to retire, leaving the pack alpha position to be determined between his second, Robert and Zach.  Problem is that Adam is about every ist in the book, and doesnt want the pack to go to Robert.  Things are manipulated to where it is up to Theresa to choose a mate, and the choice is between Robert or Zach  with the winner becoming the Alpha.  Theresa HAS to make a decision, or it will become a fight to the death which best friends Robert and Zach would like to avoid.  I have to say that I felt REALLY sorry for Robert as he basically needed to make the decision to place his career aspirations over his love life (theres a story there, but Im trying to avoid spoilers LOL!).

Im glad I decided to read a longer story from Melissa Snark (A CATS TALE was novella length) and I honestly will be checking out her backlist now!  (Not that having Snark as part of her name gives her an advantage or anything. <wink>)
