Let me start off this mostly negative review by saying that I do think Tyr is a very talented band... TECHNICALLY speaking, as they seem to have all the pieces down that would make up a great Viking metal band - Fantastic vocalist (honestly one of the very best I've ever heard), great production, full on bass, intense drumming, great guitar chops, great potential in their musical atmospheric techniques. The problem here, and what I've noticed in EVERY album from this band besides the latest, 'Northern Star,' is that the pieces simply aren't put together well or used to their fullest potential to make a memorable album. I honestly don't know what all these other reviewers are listening to, but if you're trying to convince me that this is one of the greatest metal albums ever created, I simply have to laugh at you, you most likely have no other metal albums in your entire collection.

I won't break down each song one by one, but on the whole this album mostly bored the life out of me, although I was able to see what kind of atmosphere the band was going for, the songs in the end just weren't very GOOD. I think the reason most people tend to fall in love with this band so quickly is because of the vocals - the guy's gifted with a very soothing natural voice, and when he puts it in song it has a very VERY epic and "viking" feel; this only is emphasized in the sections when the band sings together in unison for certain parts. The second track on the album is sung in their native tongue (a dialect of Norwegian) and the vocals in the song are produced to stand out, and if they were just sung with no instruments it might work, but the thing with heavy metal music is that you NEED some good guitar work to stand behind the vocals. ....the guitar work here (riffs and licks) is so overly simplified and sounds as if they just made it up as they went along, and just wanting everyone to hear their vocals more than anything else, the guitars really just taking a back seat.

There are 2 songs on this album that I decided to keep on my Ipod, because while they aren't masterpieces, they do have some pretty good choruses (which honestly feels more like luck than anything else). Still, even within these 2 songs the choruses are too few and far between, and mostly surrounded by more substandard guitar work (in the realm of creativity at least); I wish they would've just listened to these songs more and trimmed the fat off of them.

A masterpiece?? I don't think so, not even close. This is one of those albums that gets by on the band's image, cover art, lyrical themes, and bare bones vocal work (if this band had a different vocalist, I seriously think EVERYONE would hate this album)... but when it comes down to actual creative and engrossing songwriting, this album drags lazily and never makes any attempt to pick up the pace. If you're into bands like Ensiferum, Wintersun, Blind Guardian, or other melodic metal or viking metal bands, this album will do nothing for you. If you're curious to get into Tyr, I would strongly suggest only picking up their latest album - By The Light Of the Northern Star, which finally feels like the first album where the band finally decided to take more time into making good guitar-driven songs (it only took them 4 albums to finally get it somewhat right).

cands.text:
That statement might make fans pretty mad, but from what I've heard from Tyr and their previous 4 albums (Asgard, Eric the Red, Ragnarok, and Land) , this is the first one that seems to finally be giving metal fans what they really want to hear, and that is creative guitar-driven heavy metal. Or at least, getting more creative WITH their guitars and finally balancing them with their vocals.
Northern Star, to the metal veteran might just seem like your typical fare of Viking-themed music with really great vocal work. The lead vocalist in this band, if you haven't heard him yet, is one of the best vocalists in all of metal if you ask me. Not necessarily because he can hit great highs and lows (hence he's not a classically trained singer, because he actually never attempts to hit epic highs or gutteral lows and doesn't seem to have the ability to anyway), but because he's been gifted with a naturally powerful and melodic vocal tone, which translates well into singing for a metal band... although to be honest, he would fail at singing for any other genre of music, but might make a good career of doing voice-overs for books and such. Listen to some clips to see what I'm talking about. Anyway, the metal veteran with taste in melodic metal bands will see and hear the originality in a Viking metal band that decided they will not use harsh growling or death/screeching vocals. This is NOT Viking black metal, this is NOT Viking death metal, not even close; this is epic pulse-pounding Viking metal. This band doesn't mess with those other sub-genres because it wouldn't fit with the mountainous, cloudy skies and epic journeying atmosphere this band wants to create. This music isn't dark music at all, nor is it angry, it's actually very leaned towards heroism, bravery, victory and celebration.

What disappointed me about Tyr in previous albums is the, to put it bluntly, sheer BOREDOM I found in their songs; simply mediocre and lazy songwriting. All they seemed concerned about was their vocalist - he sounded great, so any sort of creativity with guitar work and atmosphere was put to the back seat. Sections dragged on, riffs were plain and flat, solos were just filler, choruses were unimaginative, lyrics were unintelligible, contrived and overly historical and metaphorical... I seriously have no idea why they still remained as popular as they did. Just name me ONE memorable hit Tyr has had in their past career... unlike other bands like Blind Guardian who wrote 'The Bard's Song' and Ensiferum's 'From Afar' and 'Old Man,' there is nothing that Tyr has written to banner themselves as a band that can contend with the greats. I don't mean to sound like their old music was absolutely unbearable, there were a FEW good songs (although even the good ones still dragged on in sections and were still overwrought with some of the same habits).

But that was former Tyr, now this album represents what I see as Tyr taking a new direction. I think they finally realized that they cannot leach off the melodic vocal tone of their singer anymore, and decided to finally write REAL guitar music that could contend and be well balanced with their lead singer, and in this album, unlike the other ones, has guitar music that will keep you just as interested in the music as the vocal work. Listen to it a few times, and the songs become more and more charming and addictive, it just takes a while, but this album does grow on you.
Lyrically the band even seems to be taking a new direction. Things are more comprehensive now, things flow better and are well paced. Some fans may think that the lyrical content was 'dumbed down' significantly from Tyr's historically intellectual roots, and maybe they have been, but if you're going to water down the lyrics and song themes to create better MUSIC, I'm all for it.
Most songs on this album follow a more direct flow of verse/chorus/verse/chorus, and that isn't always bad if a band is experimenting with a new direction; some bands work better with this formula and some bands are competent and talented enough to go beyond it. It's not a bad thing, as there are some bands who go the extra mile whose music is just simply worse than those who have more of a knack for a verse/chorus/verse/chorus formula, and vice versa - it's all a matter of personal ability. Creativity beats out technical chops any day. I don't care how many guitar notes you can hit in a second, if it's a boring lick or solo, I'm not interested. Perhaps Tyr can soon stretch their music to the former progressive attempts they used to make and actually write BETTER songs with it, but right now it seems they've decided to let go of those progressive stretches, and I say more power to them! This is their best album to date, and for any new fans I'd definitely recommend this one to pick up first.

As much as I hate to say it, Tyr is a band who has the image of musical prowess, but their past work has (to me at least) proven otherwise, and while it sucks for a band to have taken so many attempts to finally create a good and balanced album, this band is finally doing so. I am excited to hear new things from Tyr, as I feel this is a very good album and that there is simply not enough of it (it's actually rather short). I hope that for future albums they take this new appreciation for songwriting and try to advance it. Take Turisas and Ensiferum as examples if you have to, just keep putting out albums people can actually relate to!

This record definitely to me lost some of the industrial magic that made "Mind is a Terrible Thing" so creative. On the other hand though, the production on this record is a lot better and this really does sound more like Metal to me. The guitars thrash heavy and distorted, the bass will give you a whipping, and as usual Al Jourgeson's passion in his singing will help you to appreciate the anger behind all this music more. Overall, there's a lot more guitar playing on this one.
Yes, this record is definitly meatier then it's predecessor, but like the previous, it will not suite everyone. It's again a lot like the previous record, each song consists of about 2 guitar riffs, 3 at most and they just repeat over and over, although this record does have more variety in terms of its lyrics. This is just what Ministry's music is all about though, and even though most people will discard it by just saying "these guys have no talent, it's just the same thing over and over," the music is begging for you to look deeper, b/c even though it may not seem like there's much variety to each song, each song is VERY unique and it seems an equal amount of work went into each one. So that in turn tells me, No song could be released as a single, or EVERY song can be released as a single.
To those who have never heard anything my Ministry before, I'd highly recommend listening to "Mind is a Terrible Thing" FIRST at least 2 times, then that'll show you what this band is all about, what they're trying to express. If you end up liking it, then you can pick up "Psalm 69" and it'll be the same band, but experimenting with their own sound and musical idea further, and most likely you will like this one too.
Ministry is definitely very very original, and Al Jourgeson is definitly what I call an artist.

This is a band who's gotten a bad rap by most metal fans throughout the world, everyone just seems to write them off as the "cheesiest metal band ever." Blender magazine (corporate junk) made them one of the top 50 worst acts of all time. Gimme a break! I was hesitant to buy this at first but i wanted to see what all the fuss was about. I am more then happy with my purchase.
The opening track "wheels of fire" could really be compared to the opening track on Metallica's "Kill em All" debut. It's about riding your bike at night and not caring, the rebellious attitude that goes hand in hand with heavy metal music, just in with the Metallica line "no life till leather..." A fantastic way to open an album, the song is catchy, memorable, and will have your fist in the air in no time. The second track is really kind of egocentric, basically about how Manowar kills every other band out there, a good song, another fisterupper, but the lyrics you just gotta appreciate for their again, rebellious attitude. The third track is a pretty good ballad, but I've heard better. Good acoustic work... yes, they use ACOUSTICS! Although the vocals really weren't made for acoustic ballads. Next there's a bass guitar solo that's so fast and energetic it's amazing on "sting of the bumblebee." A fast high note bass guitar really does sound like a bee!
After this there seems to be a break in the album's attitude, which is a really cool thing, the songs "Crown and the Ring" and "Kingdom Come" are fantasy oriented power metal tracks, one which mostly sticks to keyboards and clean vocals, slows down but has a very epic stand-atop-a-cliff-with-sword-in-hand feel to it, creative and highly melodic.
Afterwards there's "Pleasure Slave" which starts out by hearing women having sex and loving it, it's a pretty sleazy sounding song and displays Manowar's love (or disrespect depending on which way you look at it) for sex and women, a surprise track which further enhances the variety of the record. Track 8 is somewhat mediocre but still decent, another hard hitting metal track. Track 9 is just an old man telling a boy a story, a fantasy tale of war an battle, which works as a good opener for the final amazing track "Blood of the Kings." Now this is a GREAT fantasy metal track, their use of choir type vocals during the chorus makes this one extremely catchy and melodic.
In the end i really have to say that this record emcompasses everything a passionate heavy metal band loves, whether it's fantasy, rebellious leather clad attitudes, sex, or a sensitive acoustic ballad, it all goes to show that these guys, though image wise are seen as idiots, really are imaginative, creative, sensitive and passionate human beings. This MUST be in EVERY metal fans collection, it's a classic!

This is the first progressive metal CD I've ever purchased (unless you consider Opeth progressive Metal). Anyway, I can see what all the hype is about in some ways. This record is filled with ultra-fast guitar work (solo's and riffs), keyboard melodies, classical violins, and melodic vocals. All of which, on this record anyway, work seemlessly well together on every track. This is most evident on the final 24 minute track "The Oddessy", which is split into 8 different parts but are blended together ingeniously. The whole thing is like a story, told by the singer through his lyrics and some parts break into instrumentals packed with more violin's, flutes, keyboard work, and guitar thrashes which almost take you away into this story. The first 3 tracks sound something like a melodic Ozzy Osbourne but when the 4th track "Accolades II" comes on, the classical elements introduce themselves brilliantly. I enjoyed this record a lot, I didn't love it, hence the 1 star taken off.
So why 4 stars? Well, even though all the songs aren't too long or too short, most falling into the 5-8 minute range, I still felt bored with a few of them, not at first, but I became bored after about 3 listens. The first 3 tracks for example are good in terms of instrument work, everything is fast and played flawlessly, but especially on the 2nd and 3rd track you feel you've heard it all after the 2nd chorus. It's almost like you have to be in the right mood to listen to this, it's not really just-a-pop-in-and-enjoy type of record. Either that or I'm just in a stale mood today but whatever. Track 4 is w/o a doubt the best on the album, even though I still felt they could've done more with the chorus and edited the mid guitar solo's a bit. Tracks 5,6 go back to the formula of the first 3 tracks- less classical, more melodic power metal, but are better songs. I take that back, track 6 is good, track 5 is a little boring. Track 7 is an 8 minute softer ballad with a great use of piano and symphonies, which becomes heavy and incorporates some really great classical music within, This song is awesome! Track 8 is a great ending like I said before with the 24 minute storyteller.
In conclusion, the only thing I can say about this is that it's a great prog metal album, incorporating great classical influences. Give this one a few listens, then stick it on the shelf and return back to it about a month later, just don't play it out because this album tends to do that easily.

I originally reviewed this album complaining of its cheesiness and lack of good guitar musicianship. I've recently replayed the disc after better understanding the whole Black Metal genre. I must say this is indeed a good album.
Dissection gives us a new "Storm of Lights Bane" album along w/ an EP of "Where Dead Angels Lie." I liked the SOLB part a lot better. This is really an album where you just have to sit alone, lay back and take it all in. It's not an album you can blast in your car to drive to. The album is just too dark and inaudibly produced for that. Now, probably the thing I couldn't stand most was the production. As with all Black metal album productions this one is raw and lacks low end. Because of this a lot of the great guitar melodies are hard to hear if there is any other sound being exposed to you (hence not driving while listening to this). It's a shame because some of the guitar riffs are so melodically enchanting most people won't hear them off the first listen and discard this as cheesy satan-wannabe metal. Yes, I know the raw production is a trademark of the black metal sound, but sometimes it becomes to annoying to take seriously (I guess that's why only certain people really "get" this music). Following along with the lyrics also helps while listening to this, as you can differentiate the choruses and verses. Like I said, b/c of production, a lot of it is hard to decipher. The first few songs on this one are REALLY good. It's the guitar riffs, they create such an absorbing dark atmosphere you can't help but be sucked in by it. As the album continues songs tend to become more redundent and uninspired. The vocals are typical high-reverb black raspy growls. They fit the music well though. The acoustic interludes aren't as bad as I complained of before, they're not Opeth quality, but still good.
Overall, I must say i did enjoy this the second time around and recommend it to anyone looking to get into the Black metal genre. Just remember to give it more then 1 or 2 shots and sit back and take it in w/ CD lyrics in hand, it'll be difficult to appreciate it any other way.

There's not much I can say about this disc that everyone else isn't already raving about. This is undeniably Metallica's Best record ever and most likely the greatest thrash Metal record ever created. Sure there are only 8 tracks on it, but each isn't a little old 3-5 minute song, each is around the 6-8+ minute range but are great all throughout. Kirk Hammett really shines on this one with the BEST guitar solo's I've ever heard in my life, they're just so fast, furious and pulse pounding, after 1 listen to this, you won't turn back from it.
I honestly cannot see any fan of REAL rock music not glowing about this record. When I say real rock I don't mean the Linkin' Park/Korn/Slipnot/Limp Bizkit crowd of Nu Metal. I'm talking the real deal. So if you're into thrash metal or any type of good rock music (I don't imagine you already owning this record), do yourself a favor and BUY THIS NOW! I GUARANTEE IT!!

The first thing fans will notice about Dragonland's 3rd album is their steering clear of more "medieval/middle earth" type atmosphere and going for a more straightforward (and unfortunately predictable) power metal sound in the vain of something that simply sounds like a stronger Sonata Arctica - exchanging songs of battle and middle earth war with songs about emotions and uplifted moods. This is unfortunate because I felt Dragonland was one of the very few bands who did the Middle Earth thing pretty well.
Now, the best thing I found on this album was its presentation - the instrumental chops are top notch, and the vocals are absolutely astounding, very on key, epic and passionate, you'll be hard pressed to find equally talented vocalists. Then there's the production, which is just perfect to say the least for a power metal album, I was floored by the album's presentation.... but just because an album comes off as pretty on the surface doesn't mean the songs are even all that good or memorable. Unfortunately, the majority of the songs on here just aren't, and while there are definitely few astounding moments, these parts that last only a few seconds aren't enough to sustain a 4 or 6 minute song. This makes for some very disappointing sections.
For example, the opener has easily have to have one of the best chorus's I've ever heard from a power metal song, so melodic and just perfect sounding, and after the 2nd verse the chorus is sung for the second time, then a pretty good bridge guitar solo goes... and goes, and goes until the song just ends, and I was left wondering why they didn't end the song with the epic chorus given it was SO GOOD! I asked myself "what were they thinking??" they just took this great song and hacked it into something so far below its potential it makes me wonder if they even have an EAR for their own music! This actally happens a couple of times throughout the album and it just sucks.
Overall, while it's pretty disappointing that Dragonland's leaving their Middle Earth sound, I can see their potential with their new direction, but I question how good of songwriters these guys actually are. In their history of work, they seem to hit some great highs but some epic lows. I still very much like this band anyhow, and highly recommend this album to anyone who's into melodic and uplifting power metal.

Slayer would be a great band if they just changed a few things about themselves. 1- Getting a lead singer that can actually sing, 2-structure their songs into some kind of organized format, 3-Put more variety into the music.
I first bought this CD b/c like everyone says it's "the greatest thrash CD ever!" When I opened the case I was HIGHLY disappointed to see that out of the 10 songs on this record, a whopping 8 were under 3 minutes long, and the other 2 were a mere 4 1/2 minutes long. I popped it in just to see "well, even though it's short, it might still be good." I was wrong. Sure they play fast as hell, and the guitarist can solo his head off with his lightning fast solo's, unfortunately the whole album feels unsolid, like a melted icecube, everthing just seems to fall everywhere and mix itself up too much. This in turn makes each song sound alike. The vocals are fast, the guitars are fast, the drums are fast, everything is so fast but not really that heavy, like let's say Metallica's "Master of Puppets" album, where the tempo was slower but songs had structure, it felt like it was going somewhere, and the songs were fuller, more bass. Another problem was the soloing itself. Sure it was fast, but it seems it was just there for the guitarist to boast his talent. The solo's didn't work WITH the music, rather, on top of it. After a chorus was over, the solo would start on top of a repeating riff behind it and stop, then the chorus or next verse would start. The solo's didn't lead into or away from the rest of the music, unlike handfuls of Metallica's music, where Kirk Hammett's solo's follow a structure. Last but not least, on top of everything else, the songs just had no rhythm or melody for that matter whatsoever. Isn't that what makes metal music good? Driving rhythems? Intelligent Melodics? Well, I guess in the world of arrogant metal, melody is for sissy's. I love Metal myself, but more in the talents of Metallica, Opeth, Type-o-Negative, Pantera, Blind Guardian and such. I gave this album 2 stars because even though I disliked it, I thought these guys can definitely play their instruments unlike a whole lot of bands out there, I'd just wish they'd pinpoint their talents and work together as a band, instead of just spreading it all over the place. If the album's half hour length doesn't turn you off, the abstracted noise probably will.

This is the first Nightwish record I picked up. After reading all the 5 star reviews on this website I thought it was worth checking out. And it is, but not paying full price for it. For anyone unfamiliar with this group, they're usually labeled as operatic/progressive metal. Though only progressive in a few areas. Upon first listen I really enjoyed Tarja's vocals. That girl can sing like no one else! The vocals fit the music very well (although the distortion level is tuned more to the likes of bands like Blind Guardian or Iron Maiden, not Metallica or Symphony X) though I would have liked to hear it a little harder at some parts. Even so, her opera style is something beautiful that should be heard. Anyways, enough with her voice. The music itself is where the CD is lacking. Why? B/c most of the riffs on this one sound too watered down and "mainstream" for my taste. I've heard that their previous album was a lot better, I'll be sure to pick it up in the near future. The guitar work is good at some parts though, every once in a while incorporating a good solo or riff here and there. The keyboard work is good too, although a little more bland then the guitar work. Still, this also is good at some given moments, most of the good melody one this album is found within the vocals. Overall, this whole album sounds like something Symphony X would've written during their very early years while still trying to get comfortable with their sound, but now it is something they've done over and mastered and progressed into something a lot better. It's good at given moments but not great, even my favorite song off the record was a little bland during the middle. It's basically a record you can use to introduce your pop/hip-hop loving g/f into good music, like metal. If you're a varied metal fan like myself and are into everything from progressive to death metal (not nu, i meant a real metal fan), don't be fooled by all the "oooh, aaahhhh" 5 star reviews on this page about this record, you'll be disappointed. hmmm, now if Tarja sung for symphony X, that'll be interesting. I'm becoming more familiar with the whole operatic progressive fantasy metal thing, so I'll be sure to check out bands like Tristania and Sonata Arctica in the near future. If you've got the money, try it out, you might like it.

Oh My God! An overhyped mediocre CD given a plethora of easy 5 star reviews?! Not on Amazon... NEVER!
Yes, my friends, here we have another overrated album which I don't hate, but don't really like either. Human Fortress's first album is a good intro to a competent band, but compared to all the other great power metal material, this CD just feels disposable. Let me try to explain why.
Human Fortress isn't the most original band in the world, mostly taking elements from such classic 80's bands like Iron Maiden and Dokken, with modern production and musical flares, but that is easily overlooked if you're an open-minded person. There are no epic symphonies or orchestras so all Rhapsody fans might not find it so interesting. I personally just want something that rocks, given if it is or isn't 100% original. Their guitar riffs are clean, and razorsharp w/ lots of guitar lick/lead use, unlike the thick power chord oriented type of sound from bands such as DreamEvil and Hammerfall. Vocals are clean, melodic, range testing and influence from vocalists like Bruce Dickenson are easily apparent. Songs are average length from about 4-6 minutes long. The main problem w/ this CD that I had was the mediocre and weak songwriting with most, not all songs.
We start on track 1 "Dragon's Lair" with lyrics about just that, there's moderatly fast basic guitar riffs and it's a good track due to its pitch shifts in vocals; a catchy, enjoyable song. Track 2 "Under Black age Toil" slows down a bit and has a chorus that i can see could be good for some, but to me just sounds too sensitive and cheesy (but when I'm in the mood I listen to it anyway cause it is a good song overall), and also very basic, like it could be on some cheesy made for TV movie soundtrack - a mood song.
Now on the third track is where this CD gets better, the song is great, and has a metal-horns-in-the-air feel that just grabs you during the chorus and one can't help but sing along to it; it has a great ending which slows down significantly giving way to what sounds like a melancholy and enchanting sitar followed by power chords and some fantasy dialogue, definitly the best song on the record (I have the chorus stuck in my head as I write this). The track also has good use of groovy and melodic keyboard work during the verses, which tend to give me a spacey feeling and hum later on. The fun continues on Track 4 "Divine Astronomy" in which the songwriting isn't as unpredictable and depthful as the last song, but the chorus is catchy and it's shifting in vocals tone and pitch make it a catchy and memorable track.
Things sink once again on track 5 who's chorus is just draggy and boring, and typical verses which just don't add anything new to the table. The track 6 instrumental is a one minute filler, and such a filler if I've ever heard one; simply a piano and guitar lick that repeats and bores. Track 7, "Amberdawn" - another mediocre song w/ a draggy chorus, nuff said. The ballad "Forgive and Forget" follows and is a lot slower than most power metal album ballads, it's simply a slow piano melody with a good verse and better chorus when the symphonics are introduced. Very melancholy and good (although it COULD be better). Track 9 - typical power metal song w/ yet another draggy chorus, overall not very interesting. Following this is a decent enough song w/ an ok chorus that some might find interesting, or maybe I'm just digging too deep to find good things to say about this album. The ending track is ok, and ends well with a guitar solo and good riff in the background, but the beef of the song isn't as interesting and is only good every once in a while, on top of that, the guitars were just too weak sounding, it was almost like they tuned down the bass knobs.
Overall, I found about 4 songs on this 11 track album to really be worth listening to, and 2 out of 4 worth owning. Most of the 2.5 star score is given b/c these guys can indeed play their intstruments well, but they need more time to really find themselves and write better and more interesting songs. This album has "learning debut" splattered all over it, but given time, I'm almost positive these guys will get better w/ upcoming material; because the potential these musicians show on this album is indeed great. But in the end, with this album, you'll be telling yourself that there's better stuff out there. Usually when I listen to it I never get past the first 4 songs, if that.

Blind Guardian's full length 4th album was the last record where Blind Guardian used a more Thrash/Speed metal approach to fantasy inspired metal rather then the Harmonious epic chorus structure of their 2 latest albums. Don't expect Slayer type Thrash metal though, not even close on this one. It is difficult to rate this record just because the good songs are flawed within themselves due to tacked on riffs and unneccessary solos. The chorus' aren't as epic as their latest 2 albums, so Kirsch's voice is mostly the only one you'll hear on this album, which isn't a big deal. Kirsch is the most passionate singer I've ever heard from any metal band; he just pours his heart out in EVERY song and we feel it just as much as he does.
The first 5 tracks are genuinely good songs, although as mentioned earlier, SOME parts within them drag on. For example, track 5 "Quest for Tanelorn" has a wonderfully melodic chorus, but the verses seem to be laden with uneven guitar riffs. A good song overall, though. Afterwards, you might find yourself skipping a few tracks as I have, most notably "Ashes to Ashes" and "Bard's Song-The Hobbit." Towards the end of the record we get 3 bonus tracks but really only 1 of them is good, another is just a demo version of an earlier track, not necessary.
Overall, this is worth the money if you're into Blind Guardian,but I still highly recommend their latest album "A Night at the Opera" on top of this one. Though I didn't enjoy this album as much it was still worth my money and I do pop it in every now and then, you really just have to give it more then 1 or 2 listens to get the music to grow on you because it eventually will. I still think these guys are one of the best in the world.

Blind Guardian's third album, although being far from their best, is still a good piece of fantasy inspired speed metal on its own. I would say from my current BG library this one ranks third behind the "Nightfall.." and "..Opera" albums. The music in a sum made me think of Metallica's "Ride the Lightening" guitars with BG type vocals-which I thought was evident for most, not all, songs.
The CD starts off well with the opener "Traveler In Time," a fun speed metal song with a multiple vocal chorus style as heard in BG's later albums, but just toned down in the term of epicness. The speed metal aspects that go for most of the record keep the songs grounded, to where it doesn't sound like pure Fantasy metal, but speed metal with fantasy flares sprinkled throughout. The next track is pretty similar to that of the first; speed metal verses with chorus style, um, choruses and whaling guitar solos, then we have a short instrumental with flares of shred guitar throughout, still fun.
Now these aren't some of the best songs ever written, but still a  fun time CD pop in every now and then. Track 4 "Lord of the Rings" was my favorite, another incredible BG ballad. It's just impossible for these guys to write a ballad that's anywhere below amazing, very melodic and enchanting.
The remainder of the album is mostly different takes and lyrics on the strong speed metal influence. Although I have to say that "Tommyknockers" is pretty silly sounding and a song you'll probably end up skipping. Track 9 is undoubtably one of the funnest metal songs ever written, one can't help but air guitar and sing along to it.
BG said in an interview that the reason they let go of the speed metal sound into their new harmonious sound is mostly because they've always tried writing songs like they have on their latest albums but just didn't have the musical ability, but as they grew older, they became more experienced and went to write songs w/ a sound they've always wanted. This is definitely apparent in this record, as both songwriting is good but not as grand as what they have recently, and Hansi's voice is most definitely not up to par to his passion of today's BG. He sounds somewhat wierd at certain parts, almost whaling like a hair-metal vocalist would- ugh. The bonus track is a good addition too. Overall this is better then their "Imaginations.." album, and just a plain ol' fun as hell record, although not the deepest thing you'll ever hear. The 4 stars means it's definitely worth buying IMO. I would say about 8/10 tracks on this are worth hearing. Pick this up if you're into BG or want to hear what their good old stuff sounded like.

Wow, the first mediocre power metal album I've gotten. I never thought that a genre that involves so much talent can release such a mediocre disc. Anyways, that said, let me tell you why I disliked "The Metal Opera" more then I liked it.
The whole record is like an hour long play, all these vocalists singing all these parts from different songs and with little interludes in between to round off the story. Sure, the idea's creative and enjoyable... for a broadway play. Not enjoyable for a album, not this one at least. Basically all the songs off this one never have anything to really GRAB you; no great melodies, no epic orchestra's, none of that. Sure there are some chorus's that are good (track 6 "Farewell" inperticular is a good song, reminicent of something you'd hear on Lord of the Rings) but none are within the Symphony X boat. Every song is linear, basic and pretty flat overall. Most chorus's only consist of singing the title of the song over and over. I can't stand songs like that. Very few choruses shine bleakly, like on "Avantasia," although they are pretty cheesy.
The vocals are pretty decent (although they don't sound too good, especially on track 11 "Inside" where the guy cracks at one part and made me squirm, they should've rerecorded that) which is why I gave this 2.5 stars instead of 1 or 2. Although, I did really enjoy the female vocals on track 6, but this is the only song she sings on, what a dissappointment!
The orchestrations you do find during the short interludes between the songs sound pretty weak too. Let's see, what else can I rant about? Well, that's pretty much it. I can describe this album in one word - flat.
It seems to me the whole project was made with good intentions but the writers seemed more intrested in the idea of a storyline throughout the record than with writing great songs. I don't see what all the raving is about on this webpage, these people obviously have never heard great power metal like Symphony X or Sonata Arctica. So if you're looking to get into this genre, DON'T start with this, and if you're already into the genre, still don't buy it, it's not worth it! Take if from someone who's heard great music to compare this too.

Equilibrium is a viking metal band from Germany mostly doing songs about epic battles and as [] would say, Germanic Tales. They are one of the most unique metal bands I've probably ever heard, sticking with the usual brand of guitars,bass,drums, keyboards that you'd expect from an atmospheric Viking Metal band, but creating an epic, fantastical and soaring sound that can only be best described as Epic Folk Viking Metal. Yes, also Folk metal, not so much in vocals, but mostly just in atmosphere.
Sagas is only their second album and truth be told it does not differ all too much from their first. Vocals are a mix of rasp growls as well as death growls, guitars and bass are mostly to the fast and fist-pumping pummeling nature (this band has yet to write any sort of slow ballet, and I doubt they ever will considering they can't seem to do clean vocals, but more on that in a bit), and drums follow suit. Keyboards are mostly the main star of Equilibrium's sound, and I mean that they go beyond guitars and even vocals. Equilibrium has a completely unmatched atmospheric keyboard tone that is always on play, creating atmospheres reminding you of vast terrains and epic landscapes, as well as going into sometimes danceable and "tropical" realms. This is almost a mix between metal and soundscape music, and it's not like anything I've ever heard from any atmospheric metal band. To many the keyboard lines may come off as somewhat goofy and playful at first (I can most closely describe them as a modernized version of Fintroll), but at the very least the band is experimenting, but also coming away with very dream-like keyboard overtones... although I should admit that this keyboarding technique is mostly utilized in their first album, but on the second the band seems to tone it down for a more streamlined metal sound (although the atmosphere I'm speaking of is definitely apparent). At times they also give off a more Celtic vibe, which is a great welcome, mostly considering that they're just plain creative and sound GREAT. Lots of it isn't just headbang inducing but also dance inducing, if you can believe that.

As good of an album I think this is, there was one thing that disturbed me both about this one as well as their last - the complete absence of clean and/or female vocals which, if done well, could make these bands one of the greatest in underground metal. The tone of the music itelf almost BEGS for it, but unfortunately, the continuous rasps and growls at times seem to be somewhat overdone, and to the casual metal fan, can come off as rather annoying on a few songs. If this band is reading this review, I would STRONGLY recommend injecting some clean vocals, as they not only would increase the epicness of their already profound sound, but also give them a more balanced and thematic presence. If this album had that, it would most likely be a 5 star review all the way.
Either way, this is a great and unique band that absolutely must be heard!

This was the first In flames disc I've purchased and upon first listen I wasn't too impressed. I felt the guitars too "noisy" and vocals too unoriginal. Anders Friden's screeching melodic yells and scratchy vocals to me sounded like a million other wannabe metal bands out there (not that In flames are wannabe's.) After a couple more listens I discovered what was beneath all that; great talent, great metal. People label In Flames as melodic death metal. I wouldn't really call it death metal, more like just metal, the melody doesnt really come from the vocals though but more from the brilliant genious guitar work. In Flames can seriously create some of the greatest guitar harmonics found in music today, and this album is full of them. A friend of mine once said In Flames should just be an instrumental band. I have to agree, but on the other hand, Friden's voice does match the music well after you've adjusted to it's sound and I don't think it would be the same without him. Ive spun this cd a lot of times by now and though I didn't like all the tracks, the ones that I do like, I love. There are 10 full length songs on this record (track 11 is a short guitar chord progression instrumental that isn't that good and too short to be considered a real song) each running about 3-5 minutes in length, nothing progressive or epic, although hearing them do that I'm sure would be amazing. I would say out of this 10, 6 or 7 at most are worth hearing (track 6 is worth the purchase alone as it is one of the best metal songs I've ever heard). Usually I would take off a star for only about half the record being good but of those songs I like, they're enough to be put aside on a separate record that would be an easy 5 stars. I've since purchased Colony and am looking towards getting The Jester Race which recieved amazing reviews. If you want to get into In Flames, this is a good disc to start out with, though I don't know if it's the best seeing as how I don't have them all, but it got me into them. If at first you don't like what you hear, give it another shot.

While definitely not as good as "Blackwater Park","My Arm's, Your Hearse" is definitely another hit on Opeth's list. It's probably up there with the likes of thier newer record "Still Life." I really can't say enough great things about band, they just can't seem to write a bad song!!
On "MAYH" Opeth takes a stab at thier harder side of music. This is not to say that the signiture acoustics aren't spread throughout this b/c they are, the record is prodomenintely harder. I never seem to enjoy Opeths harder stuff as much as I do their softer stuff but their both great pleasures to listen to. So why 4 stars instead of 5? Well, unlike "BP" and "SL" this record was overall more difficult to really get into. While a lot of their riffs, solo's, basslines,etc shine through, a couple of the songs feel a little uninspired and drawn out,such as the final track "Epilogue," an instrumental which while well played, isn't the most rhythmic guitar you've ever heard. Still decent though, not bad. Another thing I thought was strange were the entries into the next track. You really can't tell if you're going into a new track if not looking on your CD player or reading along witht the lyrics. On the upside of that, the whole thing sounds like one long song.
Other then that the rest of the record is more beautiful Black/Prog Metal that no real rock fan should be without. If you're turned off by growling vocals, I'd suggest giving an Opeth album a listen, and if it doesnt change your mind I GUARANTEE it will on about the 3rd or 4th CD spin. Another winner for THE most brilliant Metal Band alive, and one of THE GREATEST musical talents to ever walk Gods green Earth.

Porcupine Tree's latest album is the smooth, enchanting fix metal heads like myself need without feeling guilty. I've heard a few songs by them before this album (they have lots, and aren't all easily accessible), and they definitely are one of the most original bands in music history. Why? Well, Steve Wilson is just a musical genius, and the whole band came out with a album of HIGH variety, amazing creativity, hypnotic grooves, and progressive 70's flare. He can write extremely catchy songs with great longevity and replay value, and more intriguing tunes that put you in a trance, thus, a few more listens are necessary to appreciate them, but you'll be glad you did. The album sounds like a less technical RadioHead with a 70's influence.
I loved almost every song off this record, from their most catchiest to their most mellow to thier most technical and hypnotic. No instrument is ever overused; for example, the keyboard work isn't in every song, and only in those parts where it would be most effective, nothing is ever used to "save" a song from bordem like tons of other bands do. Also, no 2 songs sound alike. Every single one is distinctive and unique from the ones before and after it, yet still keeping the progressive rock roots in mind, which I should say is an INCREDIBLY difficult thing to achieve. You'll have to hear it to know what I mean. Although, from all the other PT stuff I've heard before, that's nothing new, all thier songs are very unique from one another. For example, with some songs I couldn't help but think of outer space, other parts made me feel like dancing like a hobbit, and others made me think of the seasons (if this makes any sense).
Anyway, with all this said, the reason I didn't give this a full 5 stars is only because there are 2 mediocre tracks on it. Track 10 just seems to go on forever and is one I tend to skip, track 11 is pretty good, mostly during the end but I won't listen to it all the time. Track 12 though ends the album BEAUTIFULLY. I don't know why, but the whole mood during that final masterpiece just makes you feel like you took a huge journey through the minds of these guys and are recalling every gorgeous second of it; a great ending.
Still, about 90% of this album is remarkable, and I highly recommend it to any metalhead or just plain rock music fan, or folk music for that matter. There's not many albums out there that make you listen to the whole thing and just word to yourself "niccce " once it's over. This is one of them. Buy this NOW!!

I purchased this disc after reading all the rave reviews on this webpage. People usually describe this band as Christian Black metal. I beg to differ. The overall style on this disc varies so much it's hard to catagorize. There really are only 1 or 2 songs at most on here that sound completely black metal. A lot this sounds like Nu-metal, yet a progressive nu-metal (if such a catagory exists), with elements of Power/progressive and Hardcore(like Hatebreed) metal and some black as said before.
A lot of people on this webpage tend to compare these guys to Opeth. The variety in their sound (clean and death/black growls, violins,acoustics etc) is reminicent and in the STYLE of Opeth, but the sound overall really isn't anything like Opeth. The Christianity aspect is only in the lyrics, but these guys aren't cheesy about it. It's not to the "worship God and Jesus and all your dreams with be fulfilled" level. A lot of it is dark sounding and morbid yet complementary to the Christian/Catholic religion.
Most of the songs on this 12 track (11 song) record are good. There are 2 instrumental which I adore. Track 5 "Meadows of Silence" is a gorgeous acoustic interlude which makes me think of nature in Autumn. Track 9 "Where Sleep is Rest" is more an electric guitar anthem ending in acoustic is also amazing. Almost like something Alice in Chains would write - overall a beautiful song.
The rest of the tracks sound mostly like black/death progressive guitar driven nu-metal songs. I say progressive because of the violin work and complex  experimental guitar riffs. I say nu-metal because most of the clean singing has a very nu metal sound to it (sometimes like taproot type clean singing, other times like Disturbed). Track 1 is a good album starter, kicking off with guitar, then violin , then both. Track 2 sounds a lot like track 1, also incorporating both guitar and violin work simultaneously. I'd give both songs a 3.5 out of 5. Track 3 is more like this but with an amazing guitar riff lead during the chorus, unfortunately, this chorus is only sung twice and after the 2nd time you might find yourself skipping to the next track because the song kind of drags afterwards. Track 4 "Embers" is the highlight, the best non-instrumental off the album. The clean singing is beautful and hard verses just as good. Track 5 I mentioned earlier. Track 6 "Shelters" is definitly a filler song. There's too much screaming and it's just plain boring. Track 7 and 8 are both great tracks also, incorporating more progressive twin guitar work with very melodic chords and vocals. Track 10 is really where the album ends for me-this track incorporates more gorgeous melodic clean vocals making this probably the 2nd best song off the album. Track 11 "Abandoned" is really a nothing track. Track 12 is really the only black metal sounding song on the album, this one too, is also a little boring.
As you can see any time I've tried to catagorize a style I used a lot of slashes. This is because this album pretty much covers everything. This band definitly has a unique sound so going into this thinking you're buying a Black Metal album is just wrong. This is probably about 30% black metal sounding. The rest is a strange yet satisfying mix of grunge,progressive,nu, and hardcore. These guys just seemed to have gotten together and said "let's make something that just plain f*****g sounds good, no matter what people catagorize this as," and out comes Undecieved by Extol - a very unusual yet talented band. If you're a metal fan, I can't see you not liking this album.

Being my first BN disc, I was sort of expecting one thing but got the other. BN's latest album is mostly a mixture of slow medieval medley's and some more modern light rock and flares of pop. Being predominantly angled towards a more middle ages approach in the reality sense and not in the fantasy sense, don't be expecting any atmospheric keyboard arrangements or lushful ambiences. This is all finger picked guitar/sitar driven music w/ softly sung female fronted vocals, and the occasional horns, flutes, etc. Coming from a heavy metal fan's perspective, this may seem a bit biased, but I could really appreciate any type of music, be it metal or classical (as long as it's not hip hop).
Well, there were some good moments on the album and I would say that out of 16 tracks (all approxiemately around the 3-5 minute mark) I really can only listen to about half the album when I'm in the mood for it, but when it's just for a quick spin, there are only about 3 really good songs on this. We start off pretty well w/ the opener "written in the stars" where Candice (lead vocals) opens up w/ slow singing for about a minute then giving way to a percussion-lead rhythm based song which is lacking somewhat in melody, but pulls off an OK job for opening an album. The Bob Dylan "Time are a-changin'" remake I very much enjoyed, but then again BN didn't write the song. A few mediocre tracks follow but eventually the title track "Fires at Midnight" is one that can be spun again and again granted the chorus w/ it's very beautiful main melody doesn't get on your nerves only b/c it is simply repeated 1 too many times w/in the song. This is easily the best track on the record. Good songs follow this track including the melodic and somber "Hanging Tree" and "Mid-winter's Night." I especially loved "Storm." it's fast and upbeat rhythms and chorus melody really gave this mostly soft and slow album some life - 2nd best track on the album and one I'm sure any folk rock fan will enjoy.
A few songs you really must take w/ a grain of salt, they are good (example: "All because of You") but may come off as a bit corny and poppish for those in the mood for something darker and more aggressive, but stil good songs nonetheless. There are also a couple of acoustic guitar driven soft instrumentals- one of which I enjoyed more than the other ("Praetorius"), kind of short to really appreciate though.
The ender "Village of the Sand" is another more upbeat song w/ poppish flares but still something that'll get your head moving -good song.
What brings this album down in my opinion is the sub-standard songwriting, lack of progression, predictability, and a handful of the songs on this album just being kind of boring and uninspired, like the phony sounding horns that feel tacked on a lot of times. The good songs on the album even have some sub-standard songwriting, but it's essentially their catchy yet undiverse melodies which luckily make them good. Lyrics are for the most part mediocre, typical and are repeated way too often in some songs, namely the title track. Track 4, "Home Again" has a medieval-pub-beer-in-hand type of chorus chant (sung by candice and a few background male singers) and would be a good song, well, in medieval times. I simply found it dry and plain. "Crowing of the King" has a faux horn in the main melody that's just too cheesy and bland to be any good, almost sounding like a childish nursery rhyme. In other words, very predictable.
Overall, this album has most good moments and skippable moments, but really nothing brilliant or mindblowing. This is one of those you have to listen to more than a few times to get into.
I did enjoy this disc but it's really more of something more or less you have to be in the mood for to play from start to end. I'm sure there are a lot of people out there who will love this disc, but they'd have to be really into folky music to. I guess I wanted more of something that'll create some sort of medieval/fantasy atmosphere, but istead what I got was something flatter and more down to earth than anything else. I've heard BN's earlier works to be more towards that inclination, so I won't close the book on them altogether, this album wasn't bad, just somewhat mediocre. If you wanna give this band a shot, I would suggest sampling this first.

There really isn't any other reason for me to be writing this review only to tell the poor souls who do not yet own this album that their is seriously something wrong with you. Live exploded onto the scene in the mid 90's once hits like "Selling the Drama", "I, Alone", and "Lightening Crashes" hit the airwaves. This was mainstream music, yes, but back then mainstream music wasn't anything to look down upon as it has sadly become now at the turn of the century. This mainstream music has depth, meaning, musical ability and most important of all, integrity.
This album is one of those rarities you really don't find much of anymore, an album you want to listen to all the way straight through and only repeat once it's over. Other albums of this nature include (for me anyway) "Blackwater Park" by Opeth, and "Master of Puppets" by Metallica.
The album kicks off great with Dam at Otter Creek, it's a slow and creepy song that works great as a lead-in to the rock and roll mayhem about to be ensued in the next few tracks. "Iris," and "Top" are my favorites off the album, as they are both deeply melodic and hypnotizing. Then again, every song on this one is very hypnotizing in it's flawless mixture of semi-progressive rock music and folk influence (I don't think you'll really find any traces of metal in here though). The hits just keep on hitting all the way through till the end. If there was any complaint I'd have about this album it's only that some of the songs are just too short. For example, "Waitress" I think is a great song, unfortunately, it only goes for about 2 and a half minutes. I think Live would do great with 6 and 7 plus minute songs.
That's about it though, otherwise there are no complaints at all, just applauds. This is the only album by Live I've heard though, as most of my money goes towards Metal CD's, but I'll have to pick up more from these guys soon. The bottom line is, BUY THIS.

Ok, *ignore* all the positive reviews on this board, these people are either mentally challenged or deaf. Long story short, I had a pretty good pair of Phillips in ear headphones where one side went bad so i needed a new pair. Got this pair at Best Buy and listened to it once on my Ipod and went right back to return them. Why? Well, apart from having a very weird in-ear design (it's just uncomfortable and feels like you're trying to stuff something bigger in your ear that's even supposed to fit there), and stupid outer speaker design (within decent volume on, everyone around you will be able to hear what you're listening to, given that there's literally a speaker on the OUTSIDE of each headphone that's supposedly supposed to bring sound "back in" - gimme a break!), the sound quality is just horrendous. Since these don't fit properly in anyone's ears and there isn't a filter mesh that the sound comes through, everything sounds muffled and distant, on top of that, the bass is absolutely horrendous, there is none to be found.
Here's some advice, if you're buying headphones for sound quality (which you should), pick up ones with a good wide frequency width. These are 16-20k Hz, whereas a Sony pair I picked up were a lot better at 6-23k Hz).
Just don't get these, if you're looking for GOOD in-ear headphones, don't go for any othese these ridiculous designs.

The DS rumble pack has it's good and fair points. Not really any bad points per se, so much as it is just a generally unknown and semi-useless add-on to your Nintendo DS. It's still a cute extra.

The game that currently comes packed with this rumble pack is Metroid Prime:Pinball (which can only now be purchased brand new at a fairly expensive price since it is out of print), but you can also purchase the rumble pack separately for use with any one of about, well, less than a handful of DS games.

The positives of this rumble pack is that it can give you a slight feedback to the game you're playing. The problem is, the feedback is barely noticeable if slightly annoying. Since you are using a handheld system that also requires the precision of a touch screen, the thing can only rumble so much or else just screw up your game entirely. This rumble gives a slight rumble at predetermined times but remember it is only slight, and can't even be felt all that much (I remember playing Metroid Pinball and wondering when the thing was gonna rumble, and was like "oh wait, that's it right there I guess, go figure"). On top of that, it emits a buzzing sound since it is so small. Remember the N64's rumble pack? That also made a sound since it was an outer attachment to the controller. Sure, the PS3 and Xbox controllers also rumble, but the difference there is that the rumble feature motors are already integrated into the build of the controller, thus the rumbling can be more forceful and at the same time controlled. I personally couldn't imagine playing a console game like my PS3 without the rumble feature. This outer attachment DS pack is already pretty lightweight, so it can only rumble so heavily (as opposed to the N64's pack which was fairly large). So since it is so small, how big of an electric motor can you actually fit in there? It's basically the exact same shape and build of a Game Boy Advance cartridge (since the pack plugs into the DS GBA slot). As you may already know, the GBA cartridges are very lightweight and slim. All in all, the pack's performance may be worth about the $5 it costs, but for some, it wouldn't even be worth that much.

The second biggest flaw with this attachment is the lack of games that actually support the rumble feature. Off the top of my head I can think of Metroid Prime:Pinball, Super Princess Peach, StarFox Command and Hotel Dusk Room 215. There may be a couple more but that is really where it ends. Granted, these games can very very easily be enjoyed just as much without this rumble pack (perhaps more even, but I'm curious to try StarFox with it; I am currently playing through Hotel Dusk and feel no desire to even give the rumble pack a shot, as I really like the game the way it is and feel a rumble would only make things feel silly). And these days, if anyone now owns a 3DS which doesn't even contain a GBA slot, it makes this rumble pack virtually obsolete. Why? Well, since gamers will now be playing those DS rumble pack games on their 3DS's anyway they will probably just sell their old DS's or just keep them to play their much older GBA games. And why shouldn't they? The 3DS games look and play BETTER on the 3DS than they do on a regular DS.
And don't count on this rumble pack to be some sort of collector's item. If people didn't care when it was released, I doubt they'll care in 10 years. I'd suggest to save your money and put it towards another cheap game.

RE5 has gotten a lot of slack for its rehashing of RE4 and controls that haven't been "updated" to the likes of Gears of War and Dead Space (action/adventure games that have evolved from 1st gen survival horror).
Yes, RE5 does *not* have a surprisingly creative story (there's one twist that RE fans will find ok, but nothing spellbinding), RE5 DOES carry 90% of the controls over from RE4 (which can seemingly feel problematic if you're accustomed to Gears of War type controls), and RE5 is in fact RE4 with a fresh coat of paint. Yes, all this is true. You cannot move while aiming or shooting, you cannot jump, the most agility you get is doing a 180 degree turn... but at the end of the day, the game is dang fun and enjoyable all the way through to the end. I found myself simply WANTING to come back to it, and most of the reason had nothing to do with how "up to date" the controls were or how agile my character was, or how similar it was to Gears of War and Dead Space. No, RE5 makes itself fun through the most subtle things that most people tend to overlook. In fact, I felt myself having more fun with this than I felt with Dead Space. ..but then again, I'm an RE veteran, and from what I gather, absolute newcomers to the series entirely simply won't "get" why this game controls the way it does.

RE5's characters are bulky, and have weight to them and their weapons; this can be noticed in the graphic detail, the movement and step sound effects (which are wonderful, the sound engineering and production of this game are top-notch). When your characters move, both their feet and gear clank, ruffle and footsteps match all the various types of terrain, which at first sounded a bit dramatic and overdone, but after about an hour or so into the game and it becomes second nature - the effects no longer are surprisingly loud but make this game feel all the more realistic. You'll pop in another game and notice the fact that it's NOT there and wish it was.
Graphically the game is ABSOLUTELY OUTSTANDING. Rarely will you see a graphical showing on the PS3 that is just as good. If I'm really picky I'd just have to say that the water effects could've been done a bit better, but as long as the sound engineering makes the water sound real, you could do without it looking perfect. Otherwise, characters and enemies are insanely detailed and precise, environments are perfectly lighted and texturized. Even in the smallest and most insignificant sections the producers still went the extra mile to give every single wall or area look as realistic as possible. Overall, the graphics, effects, explosions, etc are look stupendous.

Game length goes for 6 chapters or areas split into about 3 sections each. You'll come across areas with some vast amount of enemies, and while hey aren't zombies anymore, you'd really rather they not be. You can only do zombies for so many years before it becomes stale. No, just like RE4 these are humans infected by a virus, so the "zombies" are less like 'Night of the Living Dead' and more like murderous versions of '28 Days Later' type zombies. They run, they throw things, they yell, and later in the game lots of even use machine guns and weaponry. While this may seem silly to some, it definitely ups the challenge, and you'll definitely die a few times at some areas but overall the game doesn't punish the players too much. It is aware of its control scheme and understands how characters are only able to evade attacks in so many ways, so enemy attacks and behavior sort of "work" with that.
Weapon upgrading is enjoyable, taking down bigger baddies is fun, and you'll no longer need to solve any puzzles. No, this is a flat out action game. It's not scary in the way that the old RE games were, and it would be cool if for the next game the producers could do SOMETHING to bring back that old secluded and frightful "survival horror" vibe while still maintaining this same control scheme, camera work and character detail. I'd love to hear that eerie orchestral music once again and be scared to play the game in the dark... it's been too long since.
Unlockables are your standard fare and most RE fans will know what to expect, hasn't changed.

If there was something I'd change about this game it would be the aiming in some portions, but you never really run low on ammo as it seems to be everywhere, but it's a little disappointing that your inventory space feels somewhat limited, even if you have a partner who you can exchange and sort with. Most weapons are too expensive and lots of what you can buy you may not be able to until your second playthrough.

Overall I think RE veterans will very much enjoy this game and will look past the fact that it doesn't control like Gears of War. Newcomers will enjoy it if they give it a chance and take it for what it is.

I didn't do well in history in school because it was remembering a lot of useless information about things that didn't matter. I am sure I would have gotten an A+ if it would have been presented as interesting as this was. I won't soon forget what was presented about John Adams and the history that surrounds this story. Superb acting and more interesting than fiction ever was. Learning about others like Ben Franklin, John Quincy Adams, George Washington, Samuel Jackson just to name a few and the story of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, unlike the pictures I have seen, the Boston Massacre, well I could go on but this film inspired me and caused tears to well up in my eyes. I realize this was quick moving and not lingering on any one place in history for too long, except maybe being in France, I thought that was a lull in the action. but even that was interesting to learn about the French and their perspective on the American Revolution and Ben Franklin's escapades makes me wonder when he had time for inventions. I would like to see more history presented like this. A great job to say the least.
